[build-system]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs", "setuptools-scm!=9.0.0"]

[dependency-groups]
# A combination of dependencies useful for developers
dev = [
    { include-group = "test" },
    { include-group = "doc" },
    { include-group = "style" },
    { include-group = "rich" },
    "docstring_parser",
    "tox>=4",
    "tox-uv"
]
# Requirements necessary for building the documentation
doc = [
    "docutils>=0.17",
    "furo>=2024.8.6",
    # See https://github.com/jupyterlite/pyodide-kernel#compatibility
    "jupyterlite-pyodide-kernel>=0.8.0,<=0.9.0",
    "jupyterlite-sphinx>=0.23.0",
    "marimo>=0.12.0",
    "memory_profiler>=0.61",  # measuring memory during docs building
    "myst-parser>=3.0.1",
    "numpydoc>=1.8.0",
    "ruamel.yaml>=0.18.6",
    "sphinx>=7.4.7",
    "sphinx-copybutton>=0.5.2",
    "sphinx-design>=0.6.1",
    # sphinx-prompt<1.8.0 ships its package in a "sphinx-prompt" folder
    # that cannot be imported as "sphinx_prompt"
    "sphinx-prompt>=1.8.0",
    "sphinxcontrib-mermaid>=1.0.0",
    "sphinx-gallery>=0.18.0",
    "sphinxcontrib-bibtex>=2.6.3",
    "sphinxext-opengraph>=0.9.1",
    "templateflow>=25.0.0",
    "pyarrow>=13.0.0"  # mostly to avoid some warnings in pandas
]
min = [
    "joblib==1.5.0",
    "nibabel==5.2.0",
    "numpy==1.26.0",
    "pandas==2.3.0",
    "requests==2.33.0",
    # scikit-learn version 1.7.0 has a bug that prevents _repr_html_ to run
    # correctly
    # https://scikit-learn.org/stable/whats_new/v1.7.html#sklearn-base
    "scikit-learn==1.6.0,!=1.7.0",
    "scipy==1.12.0",
    "jinja2==3.1.6"
]
min_plotting = [
    { include-group = "min" },
    "kaleido==1.1.0",
    "matplotlib==3.8.0",
    "plotly==6.1.1"
]
# For prettier printing
rich = ["rich>=12.3.0"]
# Applying style guide
style = ['prek']
test = [
    { include-group = "test_common" },
    "coverage>=7.0.0",
    "lxml>=6.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=7.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.4.0",
    "pytest-xdist[psutil]>=3.8"
]
# For running unit and docstring tests
test_common = [
    "numpydoc>=1.8.0",
    "polars>=1.0.0",
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-csv>=3.0.0",
    "pytest-randomly>=4.0.0",
    "pytest-reporter-html1>=0.9.2,<0.9.4",
    "pytest-rerunfailures>=16.1",
    "pyarrow>=13.0.0"  # mostly to avoid some warnings in pandas
]
# Running test for free threaded python
# requires fewer extensions
test_free_threaded = [
    { include-group = "test_common" },
    "pytest-run-parallel>=0.8.2"
]
# For running baseline image comparison tests (requires matplotlib)
test_mpl = ["pytest-mpl>=0.18.0"]

[project]
authors = [{ name = "Nilearn developers" }]
classifiers = [
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: C",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Topic :: Software Development",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Operating System :: POSIX",
    "Operating System :: Unix",
    "Operating System :: MacOS",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14"
]
dependencies = [
    "joblib>=1.5.0",
    "nibabel>=5.2.0",
    "numpy>=1.26.0",
    "pandas>=2.3.0",
    "requests>=2.33.0",
    # sklearn 1.7.0 has a bug that prevents _repr_html_ to run correctly
    # https://scikit-learn.org/stable/whats_new/v1.7.html#sklearn-base
    # sklearn 1.9.0 creates sluggish HTML representation of estimators with many features
    # https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/34203
    "scikit-learn>=1.6.0,!=1.7.0,!=1.9.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.6",
    "scipy>=1.12.0",
    "packaging>=26.0.0"
]
description = "Statistical learning for neuroimaging in Python"
# Version from setuptools_scm
dynamic = ["version"]
license = "BSD-3-Clause"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
maintainers = [
    { name = "Bertrand Thirion", email = "bertrand.thirion@inria.fr" }
]
name = "nilearn"
readme = "README.rst"
requires-python = ">=3.11"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# keep plotly as a separate optional extra dependency because of its size
plotly = ["kaleido>=1.1.0", "plotly>=6.1.1"]
plotting = ["matplotlib>=3.8.0"]

[project.urls]
Changelog = "https://nilearn.github.io/stable/changes/whats_new.html"
Development = "https://github.com/nilearn/nilearn"
Discussions = "https://neurostars.org/tag/nilearn/19"
Homepage = "https://nilearn.github.io"

[tool.codespell]
builtin = "clear,rare,en-GB_to_en-US"
ignore-words = ".github/codespell_ignore_words.txt"
skip = "./.git,*.cff,*.bib,*/tmp,*.min.js,*.umd.js,localizer_behavioural.tsv,env,venv,./doc/auto_examples,./doc/modules/generated/*,./doc/_build,./maint_tools/*.html,./examples/*/results,AUTHORS.rst"

[tool.djlint]
blank_line_after_tag = "load,extends,include,endblock,set"
blank_line_before_tag = "load,extends,include,block,set"
format_css = true
ignore = "H030,H031,H037,H021,H006"
max_line_length = 79
use_gitignore = true

[tool.djlint.css]
indent_size = 5

[tool.djlint.per-file-ignores]
"doc/ci.jinja" = "H025"

[tool.doc8]
allow-long-titles = true
ignore-path = [
    "*/changes/*.rst",
    "*/modules/generated/*",
    "*/modules/generated_reports/*",
    "*/templates/*.rst",
    "doc/authors.rst",
    "doc/includes/*",
    "doc/modules/datasets.rst",  # to ignore mystparser error
    "AUTHORS.rst"
]
max-line-length = 120

[tool.hatch.build.hooks.vcs]
version-file = "nilearn/_version.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
exclude = [
    "nilearn/plotting/tests/baseline",
    "nilearn/maskers/tests/baseline",
    "nilearn/glm/tests/baseline",
    "nilearn/_estimator_checks",
    "nilearn/tests"
]
packages = ["nilearn"]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "nilearn"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
ignore_imports = [
    "nilearn.plotting.matrix.tests.* -> nilearn.glm.**",  # allowed in tests
    "nilearn.plotting.tests.* -> nilearn.glm.**",  # allowed in tests
    "nilearn.plotting.tests.* -> nilearn._utils.data_gen",  # allowed in tests
    "nilearn.plotting.matrix.* -> nilearn.glm.**",
    "nilearn.** -> nilearn.utils.tags"  # estimator tags are used by all layers
]
# ** utils:
# - can import from any lower layers
# - nilearn.utils.tags is a leaf module imported by all layers (see ignore_imports)
# ** glm, decoding, connectome, decomposition:
# - cannot import from each other
# - but can import from any lower layers
# ** mass_univariate:
# - can import from any lower layers
# ** maskers, image, surface, plotting, masking, datasets, reporting, interfaces:
# - can import from each other
# - can import from any lower layers
# ** signal:
# - can import from any lower layers
# TODO: not yet included are regions
layers = [
    "nilearn.utils",
    "nilearn.glm | nilearn.decoding | nilearn.connectome | nilearn.decomposition",
    "nilearn.mass_univariate",
    "nilearn.maskers : nilearn.image : nilearn.surface : nilearn.plotting : nilearn.masking : nilearn.reporting : nilearn.datasets : nilearn.interfaces",
    "nilearn.signal",
    "nilearn._base",
    "nilearn.nilearn_typing | nilearn.exceptions | nilearn._utils.versions"
]
name = "main architecture"
type = "layers"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
ignore_imports = [
    "nilearn.plotting.matrix.tests.* -> nilearn.glm.**",  # allowed in tests
    "nilearn.plotting.tests.* -> nilearn.glm.**",  # allowed in tests
    "nilearn.plotting.tests.* -> nilearn._utils.data_gen",  # allowed in tests
    "nilearn.plotting.matrix.* -> nilearn.glm.**",
    # additional on top of those of "main architecture"
    "nilearn.plotting.tests.test_img_comparisons -> nilearn._utils.data_gen",  # allowed in tests
    "nilearn.plotting.tests.test_img_comparisons -> nilearn.maskers",  # allowed in tests
    # TODO
    "nilearn.plotting.image.img_plotting -> nilearn.maskers",
    "nilearn.plotting.img_comparison -> nilearn._utils.masker_validation",
    "nilearn.plotting.img_comparison -> nilearn.maskers",
    "nilearn.image.image -> nilearn._utils.masker_validation"
]
layers = [
    "nilearn.glm",
    "nilearn.maskers",
    "nilearn.reporting",
    "nilearn.plotting"
]
name = "reporting"
type = "layers"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
forbidden_modules = [
    "nilearn.mass_univariate",
    "nilearn.reporting",
    "nilearn.plotting",
    "nilearn.maskers",
    "nilearn.image",
    "nilearn.surface",
    "nilearn.masking",
    "nilearn.datasets"
]
ignore_imports = [
    "nilearn.connectome.tests.test_connectivity_matrices -> nilearn.tests.test_signal",
    "nilearn.connectome.tests.test_group_sparse_cov -> nilearn._utils.data_gen"
]
name = "'nilearn.connectome' only imports from 'nilearn.signal'"
source_modules = ["nilearn.connectome"]
type = "forbidden"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
forbidden_modules = ["nilearn._utils.data_gen"]
name = "fixtures from 'nilearn.conftest' should not rely on data generated in 'nilearn._utils.data_gen'"
source_modules = ["nilearn.conftest"]
type = "forbidden"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
allowed_importers = ["nilearn.glm"]
name = "only 'nilearn.glm' imports from 'nilearn.mass_univariate'"
protected_modules = ["nilearn.mass_univariate"]
type = 'protected'

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
allowed_importers = [
    "nilearn.reporting",
    "nilearn.plotting",
    "nilearn.glm"  # TODO try to avoid
]
name = "assets only imported by reporting, plotting, glm"
protected_modules = ["nilearn._assets"]
type = "protected"

[tool.numpydoc_validation]
checks = [
    "all",
    "GL06",
    "GL07",
    "GL08",
    "SS01",
    "SS02",
    "SS03",
    "SS05",
    "ES01",
    "PR01",
    "PR02",
    "PR03",
    "PR04",
    "PR05",
    "PR07",
    "PR08",
    "PR09",
    "RT01",
    "RT02",
    "RT03",
    "RT04",
    "RT05",
    "YD01",
    "SA01",
    "SA02",
    "SA03",
    "SA04",
    "SS06",
    "EX01"
]

[tool.pyrefly]
# Errors already present in the code base are listed in the baseline file
# and are not reported, so only new errors fail the check.
# Regenerate it with: pyrefly check --update-baseline
baseline = "pyrefly-baseline.json"
baseline-format = "minimal"
baseline-matching-mode = "concise-description"
# Skip the bodies of unannotated functions and treat their return type
# as Any, as mypy did.
check-unannotated-defs = false
infer-return-types = "never"
preset = "legacy"
project-excludes = ["**/nilearn_cache/**/*", "**/nilearn/_version.py"]
project-includes = ["nilearn/**/*.py"]
python-version = "3.11"
replace-imports-with-any = [
    "IPython.*",
    "jinja2.*",
    "joblib.*",
    "kaleido",
    "matplotlib.*",
    "memory_profiler.*",
    "mpl_toolkits.*",
    "marimo.*",
    "nilearn._version",
    "numpydoc.*",
    "plotly.*",
    "polars.*",
    "pytest.*",
    "rich.*",
    "scipy.*",
    "sklearn.*",
    "statsmodels.*",
    "svg.*"
]

[tool.pyrefly.errors]
redundant-condition = "error"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# We do not run doctests systematically with "--doctest-modules".
# This is because some doctests outside of nilearn.plotting require matplotlib
# and would lead to import errors when run without the plotting dependencies.
addopts = "-ra --strict-config --strict-markers --showlocals --capture=no -v --template=maint_tools/templates/index.html"
doctest_optionflags = "NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE ELLIPSIS"
# see https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/capture-warnings.html#controlling-warnings
filterwarnings = [
    # ignoring warnings about using a non-interactive plotting backend
    'ignore:.*you are using the.*:UserWarning'
]
junit_family = "xunit2"
log_cli_level = "INFO"
log_level = "INFO"
markers = [
    # For tests that exceed the timeout allowed for each test.
    # Slow tests are run separately from the others in a different pytest invocation
    # with no timeout limit so that slow tests are only run if all "fasts" tests pass.
    # Also helps find tests that could point
    # to potential performance issues (in the code or in the test).
    "slow",
    "single_process",  # for test that require testing n_jobs>1 or that are flaky when used xdist testing parallelization
    "thread_unsafe",  # used by pytest-run-parallel: adding it here to avoid warning and not always install the extension
    "ai_generated",  # used by AI agents to flag tests they generate or modify
    "engines",  # used to specify engines for a test to be selected from available ones
    "mpl_image_compare"  # registered here so --strict-markers works without pytest-mpl installed
]
minversion = "8.0"
testpaths = ["nilearn"]
xfail_strict = true

[tool.ruff]
extend-exclude = ["doc/auto_examples/*", "nilearn/_version.py"]
include = [
    "pyproject.toml",
    "nilearn/**/*.py",
    "examples/**/*.py",
    "maint_tools/**/*.py",
    "doc/**/*.py"
]
indent-width = 4
line-length = 79

[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true
docstring-code-line-length = "dynamic"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"
quote-style = "double"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint]
dummy-variable-rgx = "^(_+|(_+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+?))$"
fixable = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "ARG005",
    "D105",
    "D205",
    "D301",
    "E741",
    "ERA001",
    "N803",
    "N806",
    "PERF203",
    "PLR2004",
    "PTH207",
    # Avoid linter rules conflicting with the formatter
    # https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules
    "COM812",
    "COM819",
    "E111",
    "E114",
    "E117",
    "Q000",
    "Q001",
    "Q002",
    "Q003",
    "W191"
]
# List of all the ruff rules (includes why the rule matters)
# https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/
select = [
    "ARG",
    "B",
    "C4",
    "C90",
    "D",
    "E",
    "ERA",
    "F",
    "FLY",
    "FURB",
    "I",
    "N",
    "NPY",
    "PERF",
    "PIE",
    "PTH",
    "PD",
    "PGH",
    "PLR",
    "RUF",
    "SIM",
    "TID",
    "UP",
    "W"
]
unfixable = []

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 23

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"**/{asv_benchmarks}/*" = ["TID"]
"**/{doc}/*" = ["B018", "D103"]  # 17 D103 errors to fix
"**/{examples}/*" = ["B018", "D103", "D400", "E402"]  # 13 D103 errors to fix
"__init__.py" = ["D104", "E402"]
"doc/conf.py" = [
    "I001"
]  # ignore sorting because this leads to conflict when running prek locally and in CI
"nilearn/**/tests/test_*" = ["D100"]
"nilearn/connectome/tests/test_connectivity_matrices.py" = [
    "D103"
]  # 30 errors to fix
"nilearn/datasets/func.py" = ["PTH211"]  # 1 error
"nilearn/datasets/tests/conftest.py" = ["D102"]
"nilearn/datasets/tests/test_atlas.py" = ["D103"]  # 24 errors to fix
"nilearn/datasets/tests/test_func.py" = ["D103"]  # 37 errors to fix
"nilearn/decoding/tests/test_decoder.py" = ["D103"]  # 26 errors to fix
"nilearn/glm/tests/test_contrasts.py" = ["D103"]  # 17 errors to fix
"nilearn/glm/tests/test_design_matrix.py" = ["D103"]  # 22 errors to fix
"nilearn/glm/tests/test_second_level.py" = ["D103"]  # 17 errors to fix
"nilearn/image/tests/test_image.py" = ["D103"]  # 37 errors to fix
"nilearn/image/tests/test_resampling.py" = ["D103"]  # 29 errors to fix
"nilearn/regions/tests/test_parcellations.py" = ["D103"]  # 15 errors to fix
"nilearn/regions/tests/test_region_extractor.py" = ["D103"]  # 20 errors to fix
"nilearn/regions/tests/test_signal_extraction.py" = ["D103"]  # 20 errors to fix
"nilearn/surface/tests/test_surface.py" = ["D103"]  # 44 errors to fix

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "numpy"

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#lint_pylint_max-args
max-args = 27
# https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#lint_pylint_max-branches
max-branches = 22
# https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#lint_pylint_max-returns
max-returns = 8
# https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#lint_pylint_max-statements
max-statements = 110

[project]
name = "qgc-tools"
version = "0.0.0"
requires-python = ">=3.10"

[dependency-groups]
scripts = [
  "packaging>=24",
  "defusedxml>=0.7.1",
  "lxml>=5",
  "fastcrc>=0.3",
  "httpx>=0.28",
  "jinja2>=3.1",
  "tomli>=2.0; python_version < '3.11'",
]
precommit = [
  "pre-commit",
]
test = [
  {include-group = "scripts"},
  "pytest",
  "jsonschema>=4.23",
  "jinja2",
  "pyyaml",
  "tomli>=2.0; python_version < '3.11'",
]
ci = [
  {include-group = "scripts"},
  "pre-commit",
  "meson",
  "ninja",
]
qt = [
  {include-group = "scripts"},
  "aqtinstall",
]
coverage = [
  {include-group = "scripts"},
  "gcovr",
]
terrain = [
  "numpy>=2",
  "pillow>=11",
  "rasterio>=1.4",
]
dev = [
  {include-group = "test"},
  {include-group = "lint"},
  {include-group = "build"},
  {include-group = "qt"},
  {include-group = "precommit"},
  "jinja2",
  "pyyaml",
  "pymavlink",
  "rust-just>=1.55.1",
  "tomli>=2.0; python_version < '3.11'",
]
build = [
  {include-group = "ci"},
  {include-group = "coverage"},
  "cmake>=3.28,<4",
]
lint = [
  {include-group = "scripts"},
  "ruff==0.16.5",
  "pyright==1.1.411",
  "import-linter>=2.0",
  "jsonschema>=4.23",
  "pyyaml>=6",
  "clang-format==23.1.0",
]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = []

[tool.uv.sources]
# Qt 6.12's split iOS SDKs and versioned extensions need miurahr/aqtinstall#1048; return to PyPI once released.
aqtinstall = { git = "https://github.com/miurahr/aqtinstall", rev = "6f0f842da47c744cdc814cd94da9828d934d7bf0" }

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["common", "analyzers", "generators", "qgc_tools", "setup", "terrain"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "common is a dependency-free foundation"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["common"]
forbidden_modules = ["analyzers", "generators", "qgc_tools", "setup", "terrain"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "tool packages are mutually independent"
type = "independence"
modules = ["analyzers", "generators", "terrain"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "shared domains do not import command entrypoints"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["qgc_tools"]
forbidden_modules = ["setup", "analyzers", "generators", "terrain"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

# Alternate-Django-version test matrix groups. Each is a real, independently-resolved
# environment (not a runtime `uv pip install` patch on top of `testing`) — see
# [tool.uv].conflicts below, which is required for these to coexist in one uv.lock at
# all. Currently unexercised: the CI matrices that would select one of these
# (migrations-check.yml, unit-tests.yml) only ever run with django-version: "pinned",
# which resolves independently via `testing`'s own (unconstrained-except-<6.0) Django
# requirement. If re-enabling that matrix dimension, add the matching fork to
# [tool.uv].conflicts for whichever combination gets exercised together.
django42 = [
    {include-group = "testing"},
    "django>=4.2,<4.3",
]
django52 = [
    {include-group = "testing"},
    "django>=5.2,<5.3",
]
ci = [
    "tox",
    "tox-uv",
]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = [] # explicit, not omitted -- uv's own default-groups fallback is ["dev"]
conflicts = [
    [
        { group = "django42" },
        { group = "django52" },
    ],
]

#  DO NOT EDIT constraint-dependencies DIRECTLY.
#  This list is managed by `edx_lint write_uv_constraints` and will be
#  overwritten the next time `make upgrade` is run.
#  - GLOBAL constraints: edit edx_lint/files/common_constraints.txt
#  - REPO-SPECIFIC constraints: edit [tool.edx_lint].uv_constraints in this file
constraint-dependencies = [
    "Django<6.0",
    "elasticsearch==7.9.1",
    "social-auth-app-django<=5.4.1",
    "social-auth-core<5.0.0",
    "pip<26.2.1",
    "celery>=5.2.2,!=5.6.1,<6.0.0",
    "django-oauth-toolkit==1.7.1",
    "django-stubs<6",
    "libsass==0.10.0",
    "numpy<2.0.0",
    "openedx-core<2",
    "path<16.12.0",
    "pymongo<4.4.1",
    "lxml==5.3.2",
    "xmlsec==1.3.14",
    "django-debug-toolbar<6.0.0",
    "sphinx-autoapi<3.6.1",
    "setuptools<82",
    "astroid==4.0.4",
    "edx-enterprise==8.17.0",
    "djangorestframework<3.18",
]
[tool.edx_lint]
uv_constraints = [
    # Date: 2025-10-07
    # Stay on LTS version, remove once this is added to common constraint
    "Django<6.0",
    # Date: 2026-01-13
    # We would normally pin celery to <6.0.0 to avoid auto-updating across a major
    # version boundary without more thorough testing. The reason it's currently also
    # pinned to !=5.6.1 is because of a celery bug related to the eta and countdown
    # parameters. This bug caused operational issues in MIT's deployment.
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/35280
    "celery>=5.2.2,!=5.6.1,<6.0.0",
    # Date: 2020-02-10
    # django-oauth-toolkit version >=2.0.0 has breaking changes. More details
    # mentioned on this issue https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/32884
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/35277
    "django-oauth-toolkit==1.7.1",
    # Date: 2024-07-19
    # Generally speaking, the major version of django-stubs must either match the major version
    # of django, or exceed it by 1. So, we will need to perpetually constrain django-stubs and
    # update it as we perform django upgrades. For more details, see:
    # https://github.com/typeddjango/django-stubs?tab=readme-ov-file#version-compatibility
    # including the note on "Partial Support".
    # Issue: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/35275
    "django-stubs<6",
    # Date: 2023-07-26
    # Our legacy Sass code is incompatible with anything except this ancient libsass version.
    # Here is a ticket to upgrade, but it's of debatable importance given that we are rapidly moving
    # away from legacy LMS/CMS frontends:
    # https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/31616
    "libsass==0.10.0",
    # Date: 2024-07-16
    # We need to upgrade the version of elasticsearch to at least 7.15 before we can upgrade to Numpy 2.0.0
    # Otherwise we see a failure while running the following command:
    # export DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=cms.envs.test; python manage.py cms check_reserved_keywords --override_file db_keyword_overrides.yml --report_path reports/reserved_keywords --report_file cms_reserved_keyword_report.csv
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/35126
    "numpy<2.0.0",
    # Date: 2023-09-18
    # Library is still in active development. Major versions require review
    # from openedx-maintainers. Minor and patch versions can roll out automatically.
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/35269
    "openedx-core<2",
    # Date: 2024-04-26
    # path==16.12.0 breaks the unit test collections check
    # needs to be investigated and fixed separately
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/35267
    "path<16.12.0",
    # Date: 2020-04-08
    # Adding pin to avoid any major upgrade
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/35265
    "pymongo<4.4.1",
    # Date: 2024-08-06
    # social-auth-app-django 5.4.2 introduces a new migration that will not play nicely with large installations. This will touch
    # user tables, which are quite large, especially on instances like edx.org.
    # We are pinning this until after all the smaller migrations get handled and then we can migrate this all at once.
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/37639
    "social-auth-app-django<=5.4.1",
    # Date 2026-07-02
    # social-auth-core 5.x changes the OAuth pipeline's post-login redirect
    # behavior, breaking common/djangoapps/third_party_auth's integration
    # tests (AzureAD/Google/LinkedIn/Twitter full-pipeline specs). Keep on
    # the 4.x line until that's investigated and fixed separately -- see the
    # social-auth-app-django pin above for a related, already-deferred
    # migration in this dependency family.
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/38841
    "social-auth-core<5.0.0",
    # Date 2025-01-08
    # elasticsearch==7.13.x is downgrading urllib3 from 2.2.3 to 1.26.20
    # https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-py/blob/v7.13.4/setup.py#L42
    # We are pinning this until we can upgrade to a version of elasticsearch that uses a more recent version of urllib3.
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/35126
    "elasticsearch==7.9.1",
    # Date 2025-05-09
    # lxml and xmlsec need to be constrained because the latest version builds against a newer
    # version of libxml2 than what we're running with.  This leads to a version mismatch error
    # at runtime.  You can re-produce it by running any test.
    # If lxml is pinned in the future and you see this error, it may be that the system libxml2
    # is now shipping the correct version and we can un-pin this.
    # Issue: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/36695
    "lxml==5.3.2",
    "xmlsec==1.3.14",
    # Date 2025-08-12
    # The newest version of the debug toolbar has a bug in it
    # https://github.com/django-commons/django-debug-toolbar/issues/2172
    # Pin this back to the previous version until that bug is fixed.
    "django-debug-toolbar<6.0.0",
    # Date 2026-01-13
    # Sphinx-autoapi changed the version of astroid it needs
    # but the newer version is not compatible with the current pylint version
    # which wants a newer version of astroid.  This can be removed once we're
    # building requirements with Python 3.12
    # https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/issues/37880
    "sphinx-autoapi<3.6.1",
    # Date 2026-03-02
    # setuptools 82.0.0 removed pkg_resources from its distribution, but fs (pyfilesystem2)
    # still uses pkg_resources for namespace package declarations. This constraint can be
    # removed once pyfilesystem2 drops its pkg_resources usage.
    # https://github.com/PyFilesystem/pyfilesystem2/issues/577
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/openedx-platform/issues/38068
    "setuptools<82",
    # Date 2026-03-02
    # The latest version of pylint pins back astroid to an older version.
    # This holdback is not caught in the docs requirements file and since both the docs
    # and testing file are required in the development.in file, we fail to compile
    # development.txt because of conflicting dependencies.
    #
    # Holding astroid back until pylint releases a new version that works with the latest
    # version of astroid.
    # https://github.com/openedx/openedx-platform/issues/38066
    "astroid==4.0.4",
    # Date: 2019-08-16
    # The team that owns this package will manually bump this package rather than
    # having it pulled in automatically. This is to allow them to better control its
    # deployment and to do it in a process that works better for them.
    "edx-enterprise==8.17.0",
    # Date: 2026-08-31
    # DRF 3.18.0 changes many=True validation errors from a list to a dict keyed by
    # item index, which breaks the error response shape of several write endpoints.
    # Issue for unpinning: https://github.com/openedx/openedx-platform/issues/39048
    "djangorestframework<3.18",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Note: The first file of settings found is used, there is no combining, so
# this file is only used for tests that don't find a pytest.ini file first.
# Details at https://docs.pytest.org/en/latest/reference/customize.html
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = "lms.envs.test"
addopts = "--nomigrations --reuse-db --durations=20 --json-report --json-report-omit keywords streams collectors log traceback tests --json-report-file=none"
# Enable default handling for all warnings, including those that are ignored by default;
# but hide rate-limit warnings (because we deliberately don't throttle test user logins)
# and field_data deprecation warnings (because fixing them requires a major low-priority refactoring)
filterwarnings = [
    "default",
    "ignore:No request passed to the backend, unable to rate-limit:UserWarning",
    "ignore::xblock.exceptions.FieldDataDeprecationWarning",
    # Remove default_app_config warning after updating Django to 4.2
    "ignore:.*You can remove default_app_config.*:PendingDeprecationWarning",
    "ignore:Instead access HTTPResponse.headers directly.*:DeprecationWarning:elasticsearch",
    # ABC deprecation Warning comes from libsass
    "ignore:Using or importing the ABCs from 'collections' instead of from 'collections.abc' is deprecated.*:DeprecationWarning:sass",
    "ignore:'etree' is deprecated. Use 'xml.etree.ElementTree' instead.:DeprecationWarning:wiki",
    # We sometimes use DeprecationWarning to enourage `.id` instead of `.pk` since there are some cases where we cannot
    # override the type of `.pk`, but we can always customize `.id` (e.g. using TypedBigAutoField). But we don't want to
    # see those warnings when Django is using `.pk` internally, which is fine.
    "ignore:Use \\.id instead:DeprecationWarning:django\\..*",
]
junit_family = "xunit2"
norecursedirs = ". .* *.egg build conf dist node_modules test_root cms/envs lms/envs openedx/envs"
python_classes = []
python_files = ["tests.py", "test_*.py", "tests_*.py", "*_tests.py", "__init__.py"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
# Skip gitignored directories (site/, .venv/, ...) when discovering files to check.
exclude_gitignore = true
# https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config_file.html
#### Additional opt-in checks of mypy.
# Disallows usage of types that come from unfollowed imports (anything imported from an unfollowed import is automatically given a type of Any).
disallow_any_unimported = true
# Disallows all expressions in the module that have type Any.
disallow_any_expr = false
# Disallows functions that have Any in their signature after decorator transformation.
disallow_any_decorated = false
# Disallows explicit Any in type positions such as type annotations and generic type parameters.
disallow_any_explicit = false
# Disallows usage of generic types that do not specify explicit type parameters.
disallow_any_generics = true
# Disallows subclassing a value of type Any.
disallow_subclassing_any = true

# Disallows calling functions without type annotations from functions with type annotations.
disallow_untyped_calls = true
# Disallows defining functions without type annotations or with incomplete type annotations.
disallow_untyped_defs = true
# Disallows defining functions with incomplete type annotations.
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
# Type-checks the interior of functions without type annotations.
check_untyped_defs = true
# Reports an error whenever a function with type annotations is decorated with a decorator without annotations.
disallow_untyped_decorators = true


# Warns about casting an expression to its inferred type.
# ty requires more casts than mypy currently.
warn_redundant_casts = false
warn_unused_ignores = true
# Shows errors for missing return statements on some execution paths.
warn_no_return = true
# Shows a warning when returning a value with type Any from a function declared with a non- Any return type.
warn_return_any = true
# Shows a warning when encountering any code inferred to be unreachable or redundant after performing type analysis.
warn_unreachable = true


# Prohibit equality checks, identity checks, and container checks between non-overlapping types.
strict_equality = true
# Extend the above to checks involving None.
strict_equality_for_none = true
# Enable additional checks that are technically correct but may be impractical in real code.
extra_checks = true
# Prevent automatic re-export of names imported from other modules to avoid accidental API exposure.
no_implicit_reexport = true
# Warn about unused '[mypy-<pattern>]' or '[[tool.mypy.overrides]]' config sections.
warn_unused_configs = true

# Additional opt-in error codes.
enable_error_code = [
  # Flag "type: ignore" comments without an error code.
  "ignore-without-code",
  # Flag methods overriding a parent method without the @override decorator.
  # TODO Enable once we depend on typing_extensions, as `typing.override`
  # requires Python 3.12.
  # "explicit-override",
  # Flag use of a deprecated feature.
  "deprecated",
  # Flag use of variables that may be undefined in some code paths.
  "possibly-undefined",
  # Flag boolean checks on types that are always truthy or always falsy.
  "truthy-bool",
  # Flag conditions and expressions that are always true or always false.
  "redundant-expr",
  # Flag redundant annotations of the self or cls parameter.
  "redundant-self",
  # Flag overrides of a mutable attribute with an immutable type, or vice versa.
  "mutable-override",
  # Flag use of typing.reveal_type without importing it.
  "unimported-reveal",
]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
# For test cases, we don’t need to annotate functions.
disallow_untyped_defs = false
# disallow_incomplete_defs = false
# warn_no_return = false

[tool.ty.rules]
# Opt-in soundness checks, disabled by default in ty.
# See https://docs.astral.sh/ty/reference/rules/.
# Casting to a type with no possible overlap is likely a mistake.
disjoint-cast = "error"
# Flag assignments, returns, and yields of `Any` values where a precise type is declared.
unsound-assignment = "error"
unsound-return-statement = "error"
unsound-yield = "error"

[tool.pyright]
# https://microsoft.github.io/pyright/#/configuration
pythonVersion = "3.11"
# "standard" adds cross-module checks mypy lacks, like TypedDict required-key access.
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
# Generated output of the docs build, also gitignored. Unlike ty and pyrefly,
# pyright does not respect .gitignore on its own.
exclude = ["site"]
executionEnvironments = [
  # Test code may access optional Draft.js keys directly, like anywhere else in tests.
  { root = "tests", reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess = "none" },
]

[tool.pyrefly]
# https://pyrefly.org/en/docs/configuration/
python-version = "3.11"
# Flag reassignment of ALL_CAPS constants.
treat-all-caps-as-final = true

[tool.pyrefly.errors]
# Enforce annotations on production code, like `disallow_untyped_defs` in mypy.
implicit-any = true
unannotated-return = true
# Flag TypedDict key accesses that may raise a KeyError, like pyright does.
not-required-key-access = true
# Additional checks, all currently passing.
# Flag stale "# pyrefly: ignore" comments.
unused-ignore = true
# Flag instantiation of abstract classes with unimplemented methods.
direct-abstract-base-instantiation = true

[[tool.pyrefly.sub-config]]
# Test code is exempt from the annotation requirements of production code,
# but is still checked, like with the mypy overrides above.
matches = "tests/**"

[tool.pyrefly.sub-config.errors]
implicit-any = false
unannotated-return = false
not-required-key-access = false

package com.flexpoker.archtest

import com.flexpoker.test.util.ArchUnitTestClass
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

@ArchUnitTestClass
class DomainBoundaryArchTests {

    @Test
    fun testDomainsDoNotRelyOnEachOther() {
        val chatRule = noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..chat..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("..login..", "..signup..", "..game..", "..table..")
        chatRule.check(classesUnderTest)

        val loginRule = noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..login..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("..chat..", "..signup..", "..game..", "..table..")
        loginRule.check(classesUnderTest)

        val signUpRule = noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..signup..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("..chat..", "..login..", "..game..", "..table..")
        signUpRule.check(classesUnderTest)

        val gameCommandRule = noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..game.command..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("..chat..", "..login..", "..signup..", "..table..")
        gameCommandRule.check(classesUnderTest)

        val tableCommandRule = noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..table.command..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("..chat..", "..login..", "..signup..", "..game..")
        tableCommandRule.check(classesUnderTest)
    }

    @Test
    fun testCommandSideIsInsulated() {
        val tableCommandRule = noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..table.command..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..table.query..")
        tableCommandRule.check(classesUnderTest)

        val gameCommandRule = noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..game.command..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..game.query..")
        gameCommandRule.check(classesUnderTest)
    }

}

# =============================================================================
# The architecture, made executable.
#
# Every rule below is a "fitness function": if the code violates the layering,
# `lint-imports` exits non-zero and (in CI / the TDD cycle) the build fails.
# A rule no test defends is a wish; these are defended.
#
# Run it:   uv run lint-imports
# =============================================================================

[importlinter]
root_package = myapp

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The central law, applied INSIDE every feature.
#
#    `containers` says "apply this layer order within each of these packages".
#    `layers` lists them OUTERMOST-first; a layer may import the layers BELOW it,
#    never above.
#
#    Read the order carefully — `service` is at the BOTTOM on purpose:
#      • api  imports service   (boundary calls the use case)        ✅
#      • repository imports service (the ADAPTER imports the PORT)   ✅  <- the key bit
#      • service imports NEITHER api nor repository                  ✅  <- THE law
#
#    The adapter (repository) importing the port (in service) is an INWARD
#    dependency even though, at runtime, the service CALLS the repository. That
#    inversion (control flows out, dependencies point in) is Dependency Inversion,
#    and it is why `service` — not `repository` — is the innermost layer here.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:feature-layers]
name = Inside each feature: api -> repository -> service (service never imports outward)
type = layers
containers =
    myapp.bugs
    myapp.users
layers =
    api
    repository
    service

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Pydantic schemas are boundary DTOs. They describe the wire, nothing more,
#    so the service/domain never depends on them (keeps Pydantic out of the core).
#
#    A `forbidden` contract is DIRECTIONAL: `source_modules` may not import
#    `forbidden_modules`. The rule we want is "service/repository must not import
#    schemas", so the service/repository modules are the SOURCE and schemas are
#    FORBIDDEN — not the other way around.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:schemas-are-dtos]
name = Pydantic schemas stay at the boundary (never imported by service or repository)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    myapp.bugs.service
    myapp.bugs.repository
    myapp.users.service
    myapp.users.repository
forbidden_modules =
    myapp.bugs.schemas
    myapp.users.schemas

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Features are islands. They do not import each other directly; if one ever
#    needs another, that goes through an explicit seam, not a sneaky import.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:features-independent]
name = Features do not import each other
type = independence
modules =
    myapp.bugs
    myapp.users

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. The shared kernel is depended UPON; it never depends DOWN on a feature.
#    Otherwise "shared" code would secretly couple to one feature.
#    (NB: this `shared/` folder is the cross-cutting kernel — NOT the architectural
#     "core"/domain, which lives inside each feature's service.py. See README §2.)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:shared-depends-on-no-feature]
name = shared (the cross-cutting kernel) depends on no feature
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    myapp.shared
forbidden_modules =
    myapp.bugs
    myapp.users

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Lazy/in-function imports are intentional here:
#   telemetry/* — gated behind the optional `telemetry` extra
#   cli/*       — deferred to keep `invana` CLI startup fast
#   server/app.py — lazy router + optional-server wiring at app build time
"src/invana/core/telemetry/*" = ["PLC0415", "PLW0603"]  # PLW0603: idempotent one-time provider init
"src/invana/cli/*" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/server/app.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# Optional/heavy SDKs imported lazily so they're only required when actually used:
#   core/events/services.py — opentelemetry (telemetry extra)
#   llm_providers/services — anthropic / openai SDKs + urllib, per-provider
#   llm/providers/*        — anthropic / claude-agent-sdk lazy-imported per provider (docs/for-developers/modules/agents/features/providers-and-models.md · docs/for-developers/modules/agents/features/providers-and-models.md)
"src/invana/core/events/services.py" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/core/events/managers/event.py" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/apps/llm_providers/ping.py" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/apps/llm/providers/*" = ["PLC0415"]
# The S12 nouns are mutually recursive by design (docs/for-developers/modules/work/spec.md): a Task is worked
# through a Thinking, a Thinking settles a Task, and an agent's lifecycle reads
# both. The cycle is the domain's, not an accident of layering, so the imports
# that close it are deferred to the call site — where the dependency is obvious
# — rather than papered over with a fifth module that exists only to be imported.
"src/invana/apps/agents/managers/agent.py" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/apps/work/managers/task.py" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/apps/sessions/managers/session.py" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/runtime/interpreter/loop.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# Task types share band 3 with `delegation` / `planning` / `services`, which import
# the catalogue: a top-level import would close the cycle.
"src/invana/plugins/core/llm/**" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/plugins/core/pure/**" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/invana/plugins/core/work_write/**" = ["PLC0415"]
# procrastinate is the optional `workers` extra; the queue imports it on first use.
"src/invana/plugins/queue.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# The MCP SDK is the optional `mcp` extra; the client imports it on first call.
"src/invana/plugins/mcp/client.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# Alembic revisions import the registry lazily so the seed and the runtime
# cannot drift; a top-level import would run at Alembic discovery time.
"src/invana/core/migrations/versions/*" = ["PLC0415"]
# starlette-admin ModelViews declare `fields`/`exclude_*` as plain class lists —
# the framework's documented API. RUF012 (ClassVar) doesn't apply.
"src/invana/server/admin/views.py" = ["RUF012"]
# Each module's own ModelView, now beside the code it describes
# (migration-plan §4.1). Same framework API, same exemption.
"src/invana/server/*/admin.py" = ["RUF012"]
# Test idioms: in-function imports (fixtures/locality) and partially-unpacked
# tuples (`schema, _ = ...`) are fine and intentional in tests.
"tests/**" = ["PLC0415", "RUF059"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter — the band rule (docs/for-developers/building-engine/migration-plan.md §3.2)
#
# Three contracts. Every allowance below is one of today's measured cycles or
# upward edges, named, with the refactor step that closes it. Removing an
# allowance is how a step is finished. A new allowance means the band map is
# wrong — change migration-plan.md first.
#
# 32 two-package cycles were measured (migration-plan §11). 13 of them — `modeller ↔
# {agents, auth, boards, events, graphs, llm_providers, projects,
# sessions, skills, thinking, work, workflows}` — closed at 1.2, when `Base` and
# the migrations moved into `core`. The remaining 19 are named below.
#
# `core/migrations/env.py` imports every model, because that is how alembic
# populates the metadata it autogenerates against. It is a script, not a module
# in the import graph — `migrations/` has no `__init__.py` — so the band rule
# neither sees it nor needs to.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "invana"

# 1 · core imports nothing from invana that is not core.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core is independent"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "invana.core",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "invana.graph",
    "invana.apps",
    "invana.runtime",
    "invana.plugins",
    "invana.server",
    "invana.cli",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # auth → graphs — `UserOut.graphs` embeds the caller's memberships in every
    # auth response, so the edge is a composition, not a stray import. It closes
    # with the `MembershipReader` protocol at migration-plan §17 step 7, not by moving
    # a function. refactor-plan.md "Why the membership check does not come out here".
    "invana.core.auth.managers.auth -> invana.apps.graphs.models",
    # events → agents — `EventStore.list_page` joins `Agent` to resolve an actor's
    # display name while paginating the audit list. It closes when the name is
    # captured at write (10.2), which is a behaviour change plus a backfill and is
    # deferred by migration-plan §17. refactor-plan.md "Why the event reader does not
    # come out here".
    "invana.core.events.querysets.event -> invana.apps.agents.models",
]

# 2 · the bands: edge → runtime → apps → graph engine → core. Downward only.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "bands"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "invana.cli : invana.server",
    "invana.activity",
    # Task types use the runtime's stream and governor; the runtime dispatches them.
    "invana.runtime : invana.plugins",
    "invana.apps",
    "invana.graph",
    "invana.core",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # core → apps: the same two edges as contract 1.
    "invana.core.auth.managers.auth -> invana.apps.graphs.models",
    "invana.core.events.querysets.event -> invana.apps.agents.models",
    # agents ↔ thinking · sessions ↔ thinking · skills ↔ thinking · work ↔ thinking ·
    # workflows ↔ thinking — the five genuine cycles: the runtime needs the envelope
    # and the plan; they need to open a run. RunOpener / EnvelopeCheck, refactor-plan §7.
    "invana.apps.sessions.schemas -> invana.runtime.schemas",
    "invana.apps.work.managers.task -> invana.runtime.services",
    "invana.apps.work.managers.task -> invana.runtime.managers",
    # graphs ↔ server · server ↔ thinking — the edge layer imported by domain
    # packages, for ActionResponse. migration-plan §17 step 5.
]

# 3 · apps are acyclic. Edges between apps are allowed; a cycle is not. Stated as
# an order, bottom to top; every upward edge is a named allowance.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "apps are acyclic"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "invana.apps.work",
    "invana.apps.task_plans",
    "invana.apps.explorer",
    "invana.apps.boards",
    "invana.apps.sessions",
    "invana.apps.agents",
    "invana.apps.skills",
    "invana.apps.govern",
    "invana.apps.llm",
    "invana.apps.llm_providers",
    "invana.apps.datasets",
    "invana.apps.standards",
    "invana.apps.semantic",
    "invana.apps.graphs",
    "invana.apps.modeller",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # graphs ↔ agents · graphs ↔ llm_providers · graphs ↔ skills —
    # graphs/services.py reaches up into three apps for the setup state.
    "invana.apps.graphs.managers.graph -> invana.apps.agents.managers",
    # llm ↔ llm_providers — split along the wrong seam. Folded at 2.2.
    "invana.apps.llm_providers.ping -> invana.apps.llm.providers.claude_agent_sdk",
    # projects ↔ work — same. Folded at 2.3.
    # agents ↔ sessions · agents ↔ work — agents/services.py reads sessions and tasks
    # to retire an agent safely.
    # llm → skills — one-way upward, no cycle: grounding offers skills.
    # The skills→agents pair closed at migration-plan §16 step 1: the routes
    # moved to `server/skills` and the usage read to `runtime/managers`.
    "invana.apps.llm.grounding -> invana.apps.skills.models",
    "invana.apps.agents.managers.agent -> invana.apps.work.models",
    "invana.apps.agents.managers.agent -> invana.apps.work.querysets",
    # Chains that leave the apps and come back. The same allowances as contract 2:
    # events ↔ agents (1.5), and sessions ↔ thinking, through which work and
    # workflows are reached.
    "invana.core.events.querysets.event -> invana.apps.agents.models",
]

[tool.setuptools]
zip-safe = false
include-package-data = true

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = [
    "src",
]
namespaces = false

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"*" = [
    "*.pyi",
]
napari = [
    "resources/fonts/*.ttf",
]
napari_builtins = [
    "builtins.yaml",
]


[tool.setuptools_scm]
write_to = "src/napari/_version.py"
fallback_version = "0.7.1.dev0"

[tool.check-manifest]
ignore = [
  ".circleci/continue_config.yml",
  ".cirrus.yml",
  ".pre-commit-config.yaml",
  "asv.conf.json",
  "codecov.yml",
  "Makefile",
  "src/napari/_version.py",  # added during build by setuptools_scm
  "tools/minreq.py",
  "tox.ini",
  "src/napari/_qt/qt_resources/_qt_resources_*.py",
  "*.pyi",  # added by make typestubs
  "binder/*",
  ".env_sample",
  ".devcontainer/*",
  "src/napari/resources/icons/_themes/*/*.svg"
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 79
extend-exclude = [
    "*vendored*",
    "*_vendor*",
]

fix = true

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "single"
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "F", "W", #flake8
    "UP", # pyupgrade
    "I", # isort
    "YTT", #flake8-2020
    "TC", # flake8-type-checing
    "BLE", # flake8-blind-exception
    "B", # flake8-bugbear
    "A", # flake8-builtins
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "ISC", # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "G", # flake8-logging-format
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "COM", # flake8-commas
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "INP", # flake8-no-pep420
    "PYI", # flake8-pyi
    "Q", # flake8-quotes
    "RSE", # flake8-raise
    "RET", # flake8-return
    "TID",  # flake8-tidy-imports # replace absolutify import
    "TRY", # tryceratops
    "ICN", # flake8-import-conventions
    "RUF", # ruff specyfic rules
    "NPY201", # checks compatibility with numpy version 2.0
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async
    "EXE", # flake8-executable
    "FA", # flake8-future-annotations
    "LOG", # flake8-logging
    "SLOT", # flake8-slots
    "PT", # flake8-pytest-style
    "T20", # flake8-print
]
ignore = [
    "E501", "TC001",
    "A003", # flake8-builtins - we have class attributes violating these rule
    "COM812", # flake8-commas - we don't like adding comma on single line of arguments
    "COM819", # conflicts with ruff-format
    "RET504", # not fixed yet https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2950
    "TRY003", # require implement multiple exception class
    "RUF005", # problem with numpy compatybility, see https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2142#issuecomment-1451038741
    "B028", # need to be fixed
    "PYI015", # it produces bad looking files (@jni opinion)
    "W191", "Q000", "Q001", "Q002", "Q003", "ISC001", # https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules
    "UP007", # temporary disable migrtion form Union[X, Y] to X | Y
    "UP045", # temporary disable migrtion from Optional[X] to X | None
    "TC006", # put types in quotes in typing.cast
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"src/napari/_vispy/__init__.py" = ["E402"]
"**/_tests/*.py" = ["B011", "INP001", "TRY301", "B018", "RUF012", "TID253"]
"src/napari/utils/_testsupport.py" = ["B011"]
"tools/validate_strings.py" = ["F401"]
"tools/**" = ["INP001", "T20", "LOG015"]
"examples/**" = ["ICN001", "INP001", "T20", "LOG015", "TID253"]
"**/vendored/**" = ["TID"]
"src/napari/benchmarks/**" = ["RUF012", "TID252", "TID253"]
"src/napari_builtins/**" = ["TID253"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-builtins]

; Declarative dependency-direction contracts for ``dataretrieval``.
;
; This file owns dependency-direction rules. ``tests/architecture_test.py``
; owns symbol-level claims, ``__all__`` surfaces, AST shape, positive imports,
; and package-wide cycle detection (see ADR 0003). The split is deliberate and
; the two do not overlap -- a rule enforced twice is a rule that gets updated
; once.
;
; Run with ``lint-imports`` (installed by the ``[metrics]`` extra).

[importlinter]
root_package = dataretrieval
; Contracts describe what runs, matching the AST suite. Type-checking imports
; document structural protocols and callback types without creating runtime
; dependency edges.
exclude_type_checking_imports = True

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Dependencies point toward stable policy (ADR 0003, ADR 0006)
type = layers
containers =
    dataretrieval
layers =
; The deprecated ``wateruse`` alias re-exports ``nwdc``, so it sits above the
; adapters rather than beside them. A compatibility facade may depend on the
; adapter it forwards to; nothing may depend on the facade.
    wateruse
    ngwmn | nldi | nwdc | nwis | streamstats | waterdata | wqp
    ogc
    utils
    _querying
    transport
    progress
; Response-format conventions sit above the pure leaves because they read the
; code tables, and below every adapter that shapes a response with them.
    _wqx
    _response_metadata | codes | combining | interruptions | rdb
    credentials
    configuration
    _configuration_core
    exceptions
; Pure dependency-free mechanisms sit together at the floor: none imports
; first-party code, so every layer can use them without reaching sideways or
; creating artificial dependencies among them.
    _ambient | _csv | _deprecation | _validation
; Every top-level module must be placed in the stack deliberately. A new
; top-level module fails this contract until someone decides where it sits.
exhaustive = True
exhaustive_ignores =
    _version

[importlinter:contract:configuration-core]
name = Only the configuration facade may import its private core
; Keep the extracted foundation private: adapters and other package modules
; continue to depend on dataretrieval.configuration, preserving all existing
; import paths and preventing parallel configuration interfaces.
type = protected
protected_modules =
    dataretrieval._configuration_core
allowed_importers =
    dataretrieval.configuration

[importlinter:contract:ogc-consumers]
name = Only NGWMN and Water Data consume the OGC subsystem (ADR 0003)
type = protected
; Read as: nothing outside this list may reach into OGC, directly or through a
; submodule. An allowlist rather than a denylist, so a new service module is
; refused by default instead of being silently permitted until someone
; remembers to add it.
;
; The root ``dataretrieval`` package is deliberately NOT an allowed importer.
; ``allowed_importers`` is matched with ``as_packages``, so naming the root here
; would make every module in the distribution an allowed importer and the
; contract could never fail. Its two real imports are listed as explicit
; exceptions below instead -- narrow, visible, and they fail if they go stale.
protected_modules =
    dataretrieval.ogc
allowed_importers =
    dataretrieval.ngwmn
    dataretrieval.waterdata
ignore_imports =
; The package __init__ re-exports the parallel-chunks context manager; it is
; part of the documented public surface, not a service reaching into OGC.
    dataretrieval -> dataretrieval.ogc.chunking

[importlinter:contract:ogc-facade]
name = Facade-only OGC consumers, never its internals (ADR 0007)
type = forbidden
; Listed per module rather than by package: most of ``waterdata`` (``ratings``,
; ``reference``, ``samples``, ``stats``, the package ``__init__``) legitimately
; imports ``ogc`` internals today, so only the modules that have earned the
; facade-only seam belong here.
source_modules =
    dataretrieval.ngwmn
    dataretrieval.waterdata.cql
; The wildcard is what makes this durable: a new ``ogc`` submodule is covered
; the day it is added, without editing this contract.
forbidden_modules =
    dataretrieval.ogc.**
; Direct imports only. Reaching an internal *through* the facade is the design,
; not a violation -- ``ngwmn -> ogc -> ogc.engine`` is how the seam is supposed
; to work, and the default (indirect included) forbids exactly that.
allow_indirect_imports = True

[importlinter:contract:ogc-internal-seams]
name = OGC internal seams (ADR 0003)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
; Feature shaping is downstream of execution. If shaping imports engine the
; subsystem gains a cycle and the schema fetch on an empty frame becomes
; reachable from request construction.
    dataretrieval.ogc.shaping
forbidden_modules =
    dataretrieval.ogc.engine

[importlinter:contract:ogc-utils]
name = OGC core does not depend on legacy utilities (ADR 0003)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    dataretrieval.ogc
forbidden_modules =
    dataretrieval._querying
    dataretrieval.utils

[importlinter:contract:nwis-quarantine]
name = Deprecated NWIS has no dependents (ADR 0005)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    dataretrieval._querying
    dataretrieval.codes
    dataretrieval.combining
    dataretrieval.credentials
    dataretrieval.exceptions

# Select rules: Pyflakes(F), pycodestyle(E,W), isort(I), pyupgrade(UP),
# flake8-bugbear(B), flake8-quotes(Q), flake8-simplify(SIM), flake8-tidy-imports(TID)
select = [
    "F", "E", "W", "I", "UP", "B", "Q", "SIM", "TID",
    "C90", # mccabe
    # A first-party import used only in annotations is not a runtime
    # dependency, and the project already says so twice: ``.importlinter`` sets
    # ``exclude_type_checking_imports = True`` ("Contracts describe what runs")
    # and ``tests/architecture_test.py`` skips ``TYPE_CHECKING`` blocks when it
    # asserts the module seams. TC001 makes the code agree with the policy
    # instead of leaving it to reviewer memory. TC002/TC003 (third-party and
    # stdlib) are a separate import-cost concern with no policy behind them
    # here, so they stay unselected.
    "TC001",
    "TC006", # quoted first argument to ``typing.cast``
    # Check broad exception handlers; retry policy distinguishes transient
    # from deterministic failures (ADR 0004). Progress display uses ``noqa``.
    "BLE001",
    # Check unused function parameters. ARG002-004 cover methods rather than
    # the function-based public interface; ARG005 also flags lambda parameters
    # required by callers.
    "ARG001",
    # Text-mode ``open()`` without ``encoding=`` uses the process locale,
    # which may not be UTF-8. Preview-only; recheck when upgrading Ruff.
    "PLW1514",
    # Require docstrings for public symbols. Other pydocstyle rules remain
    # disabled because their fixes can misformat indented ``Examples:`` text
    # as a section header.
    "D100", "D101", "D102", "D103", "D104",
    # A ``# noqa`` for a rule that no longer fires. Author note: ruff's fix
    # reads the rest of the line as the directive's description, so spell a
    # co-located suppression ``# noqa: X # pylint: disable=...``.
    "RUF100",
    # A blocking call inside ``async def`` stalls the whole event loop; the
    # suite awaits mocked transports, so a stalled loop still passes.
    "ASYNC",
    # Check pandas usage, including ``inplace=True``, and naive ``datetime``
    # operations that can cause time-zone ambiguity.
    "PD", "DTZ",
    # Zero findings today: comprehensions, lazy ``%s`` logging, no ``print`` in
    # a library, ``from __future__ import annotations``, retired numpy aliases.
    "C4", "LOG", "G", "T20", "FA", "NPY",
]
ignore = [
    "SIM105", # Use `contextlib.suppress(...)` instead of `try-except-pass`
    "SIM117", # Use a single `with` statement with multiple contexts
]

[tool.mypy]
# The package is fully annotated and passes ``mypy --strict``. The one
# remaining relaxation is ``ignore_missing_imports``: untyped third-party
# libraries (pandas, geopandas) are treated as ``Any`` instead of
# requiring stub packages. Dropping that — via pandas-stubs/types-requests and

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# The suite is offline by default. Every HTTP call is mocked (see
# ``tests/conftest.py``), so a push neither depends on USGS uptime nor spends
# someone's rate limit. The exception is the handful of tests marked ``live``,
# which exist precisely to notice when an upstream API changes shape -- a thing
# a mock can never tell us, because the mock is what would need updating.
# Deselecting them here rather than in the CI command keeps a local
# ``pytest tests/`` doing what CI does; run them with ``-m live``.

]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["dataretrieval"]
# Most of what this package gets wrong is a branch rather than a line.
branch = true
omit = [
  # Written by setuptools_scm at build time; absent from a source checkout.
  "dataretrieval/_version.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
# 98.97% displays as "99%", which would pass a ``fail_under = 99`` on rounding.
precision = 2
# A ratchet: raise it as coverage rises. Lower it only when a genuinely
# untestable path is added and excluding it would be dishonest.
fail_under = 98.9
# Anchored to the statement, so a pattern cannot match its own words in a
# comment or a string. Literal strings, because TOML rejects ``\s``.
exclude_also = [
  # Type-checking-only imports never execute.
  '^\s*if TYPE_CHECKING:',
  '^\s*@overload',
  # The suite installs the [test,nldi] extras, so an absent-dependency fallback

  '^\s*except ImportError',

]
maintainers = [
  { name = "xbbg contributors" },
]

  "Intended Audience :: Financial and Insurance Industry",
  "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
  "Topic :: Office/Business :: Financial",

  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.15",
  "Programming Language :: Rust",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]
dynamic = ["version"]
dependencies = [
  # 2.10.0 is the first release whose plugin discovery honours the
  # `narwhals.plugins` entry point registered below. On 2.0-2.9 the plugin is
  # never loaded, so converting an xbbg result raises
  # "TypeError: Expected pandas-like dataframe, Polars dataframe, or Polars
  # lazyframe, got: <class 'xbbg._core.ArrowTable'>". The old `>=2.0` floor
  # therefore advertised a combination that cannot work.
  "narwhals>=2.10.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Runtime stays minimal; extras opt into optional conversion/test surfaces.
#
# Every floor below is measured, not guessed: the `floors` CI job resolves this
# table with `--resolution lowest-direct` on Python 3.11 and runs the suite
# against it. Three of these were previously false claims:
#   * pandas 2.0.x declares no `numpy<2` bound, so a fresh resolve pairs it with
#     numpy 2.x and pandas then fails to import ("numpy.dtype size changed").
#     2.2.2 is the first release that supports numpy 2.

#     an Arrow PyCapsule object at all.
#   * narwhals below 2.10.0 ignores our plugin entry point (see above).
pyarrow = ["pyarrow>=22.0.0"]
pandas = ["pandas>=2.2.2,<4"]

polars = ["polars[timezone]>=0.20.4"]
duckdb = ["duckdb>=1.5.0"]

  "pytest>=8.4",

  "pytest-cov>=5.0",

  "pyarrow>=22.0.0",
  "pandas>=2.2.2,<4",
  "polars[timezone]>=0.20.4",
  # duckdb publishes no CPython 3.15 wheels yet, and its sdist is a full C++

package net.amygdalum.testrecorder.arch;

import static com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition.slices;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOptions;

public class ArchitectureTest {

	
	private static JavaClasses classes;

	@BeforeAll
	public static void beforeAll() throws Exception {
		classes = new ClassFileImporter()
			.importClasspath(new ImportOptions()
				.with(ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
				.with(location -> location.contains("/net/amygdalum/testrecorder/")));
	}

	@Test
	void testArchitecturalLayers() {
		layeredArchitecture()
			.layer("codeserializer").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.codeserializer")
			.layer("callsiterecorder").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.callsiterecorder")
			.layer("dynamiccompile").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.dynamiccompile")
			.layer("data").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.data")
			.layer("main").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder")
			.layer("configurator").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.configurator")
			.layer("runtime").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.runtime")
			.layer("profile").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.profile")
			.layer("extensionpoint").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.extensionpoint")
			.layer("serializers").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.serializers")
			.layer("generator").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.generator")
			.layer("deserializers").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.deserializers")
			.layer("builder").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.deserializers.builder")
			.layer("matcher").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.deserializers.matcher")
			.layer("evaluator").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.evaluator")
			.layer("values").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.values")
			.layer("types").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.types")
			.layer("fakeio").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.fakeio")
			.layer("util").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.util")
			.layer("asm").definedBy("net.amygdalum.testrecorder.asm")

			.whereLayer("codeserializer").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer() // only from outside module
			.whereLayer("callsiterecorder").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer() // only from outside module
			.whereLayer("dynamiccompile").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer() // only from outside module
			.whereLayer("data").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer() // reserved for future use
			.whereLayer("main").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
				"codeserializer",
				"callsiterecorder",
				"configurator",
				"generator")
			.whereLayer("configurator").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
				"main",
				"callsiterecorder")

# Contract 1 — the three-tier spine. Imports may only point downward.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Three-tier layering"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "alttprbot.presentation",
    "alttprbot.services",
    "alttprbot.repositories",
    "alttprbot.models",
]

# Contract 2 — the service and repository tiers must stay free of UI/transport
# libraries and of the presentation tier.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Core tiers must not import UI or presentation"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "alttprbot.services",
    "alttprbot.repositories",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "discord",
    "racetime_bot",
    "quart",
    "alttprbot.presentation",
]
allow_indirect_imports = "false"

# Contract 3 — the presentation tier must reach data only through services.
# Enforced (blocking in CI) as of the final migration phase: the direct-model
# import burn-down is complete.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Presentation must not import models directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "alttprbot.presentation",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "alttprbot.models",
]
# Direct-only: presentation may reach models transitively *through* services,
# but must not import alttprbot.models itself.
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

# Contract 4/5 — the REST API and the web BFF are independent presentation
# surfaces. Neither may import the other; sahasrahbot.py is the only place
# that wires them together (it imports both and registers the REST
# blueprints onto the web-owned Quart app).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "API presentation surface must not import the web surface"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "alttprbot.presentation.api",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "alttprbot.presentation.web",
]
allow_indirect_imports = "false"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Web presentation surface must not import the API surface"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "alttprbot.presentation.web",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "alttprbot.presentation.api",
]
allow_indirect_imports = "false"

# Contract 6 — presentation may reach repositories only transitively through
# services (mirrors contract 3's direct-only stance, and matches the edit-time
# hook in .claude/scripts/enforce_architecture.py).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Presentation must not import repositories directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "alttprbot.presentation",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "alttprbot.repositories",
]
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

# Contract 7 — shared util is bottom-tier plumbing: no upward imports, no
# UI/transport libraries. (alttprbot.models stays allowed: util/telemetry.py
# lazily imports it, and models is itself bottom-tier.)
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Shared util must stay bottom-tier"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "alttprbot.util",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "alttprbot.presentation",
    "alttprbot.services",
    "alttprbot.repositories",
    "discord",
    "racetime_bot",
    "quart",
]
allow_indirect_imports = "false"

# Contracts 8–12 — surface independence. Only the directions that are clean
# today are forbidden; racetime→discord, web→discord, and api→{discord,racetime}
# are by design (single process, live bot object) and stay allowed. api↔web is
# already covered by contracts 4/5.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Discord surface must not import sibling surfaces"

forbidden_modules = [

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Default ruff is `E4 + E7 + E9 + F`. We add:
# - `I`    (isort)              — import order, auto-fixable
# - `B`    (flake8-bugbear)     — likely-bug patterns (mutable defaults, etc.)
# - `UP`   (pyupgrade)          — modernise syntax to the target_version above
# - `RUF`  (ruff-specific)      — unused-noqa, ambiguous unicode, mutable class attrs, …
# - `SIM`  (flake8-simplify)    — `if x: True else: False` → `bool(x)`, etc.
# - `C4`   (flake8-comprehensions) — `list(x for x in y)` → `[x for x in y]`, …
# - `PERF` (perflint)           — avoid try/except in hot loops, etc.
# - `RET`  (flake8-return)      — unneeded `else` after `return`, redundant assigns
# - `PIE`  (flake8-pie)         — small wins (no-op `pass`, redundant `dict()` calls)
# - `T10`  (flake8-debugger)    — committed `breakpoint()` / `pdb` calls
# - `PGH`  (pygrep-hooks)       — blanket `# noqa` / `# type: ignore` without code
# - `EXE`  (flake8-executable)  — shebang/executable-bit consistency
# - `RSE`  (flake8-raise)       — `raise X()` style
# - `ICN`  (flake8-import-conventions) — standard import aliases (`numpy as np`)
# - `DTZ`  (flake8-datetimez)   — tz-naive `datetime.now()` / `utcnow()` bugs
# - `TID`  (flake8-tidy-imports) — banned modules / banned relative imports
# - `LOG`  (flake8-logging)     — `logging` module misuse
# - `G`    (flake8-logging-format) — f-strings inside `logging.x()` calls (defeats lazy-format)
# - `S`    (flake8-bandit)      — security (hardcoded creds, weak hashes, subprocess(shell=True), …)
# - `PTH`  (flake8-use-pathlib) — modernise `os.path.*` calls to `pathlib.Path`
# - `FURB` (refurb)             — modern Python idioms beyond UP/SIM/PIE/PERF
# - `W`    (pycodestyle warnings) — natural pair with `E`; trailing whitespace etc.
# - `FA`   (flake8-future-annotations) — consistent `from __future__ import annotations`
# - `YTT`  (flake8-2020)        — correct `sys.version` / `sys.version_info` checks
# - `A`    (flake8-builtins)    — shadowing built-in names
# - `ISC`  (flake8-implicit-str-concat) — accidental `"foo" "bar"` typos
# - `SLOT` (flake8-slots)       — require `__slots__` on `str`/`tuple`/`namedtuple` subclasses
# - `FLY`  (flynt)              — `"{}".format(x)` → f-string
# - `PYI`  (flake8-pyi)         — stub-hygiene rules (also fire on `.py`)
# - `TC`   (flake8-type-checking) — runtime-only imports out of `if TYPE_CHECKING:` blocks
# - `N`    (pep8-naming)        — class/function/variable naming consistency
# - `PLE0605`               — `__all__` must be a `list`/`tuple` (not a single str)
# - `PLW1510`               — `subprocess.run(...)` without `check=` swallows non-zero exits
# - `PLW2901`               — loop variable rebound inside the body (typo/bug class)
# - `PLW0108`               — `lambda x: f(x)` → just `f`
# - `PLW0603`               — `global` statement (code smell)
# - `PLR5501`               — `else: if …` → `elif` (auto-fixable)
# - `PLC0207`               — `.split()`/`.rsplit()` should use `maxsplit=` when only the first/last segment is used
# - `PLR1722`               — `sys.exit(0)` over `exit(0)` (interpreter-only alias)
# - `PLR1714`               — collapse repeated `x == "a" or x == "b"` into `x in {"a", "b"}`
# - `TRY002`                — don't `raise Exception(...)` (use a specific class)
# - `TRY004`                — type-check failures must `raise TypeError`, not `ValueError`
# - `TRY300`                — put the success-path under `else:` so `except:` only sees the dangerous bit
# - `TRY301`                — don't `raise` inside `try:` for an exception caught by the same `except:`
# - `BLE001` (flake8-blind-except) — catch-all `except Exception:`/bare `except:` (ratchet; see per-file-ignores)
select = [
    "E", "F", "I", "B", "UP", "RUF", "SIM", "C4", "PERF", "RET", "PIE",
    "T10", "PGH", "EXE", "RSE", "ICN", "DTZ",
    "TID", "LOG", "G",
    "S",
    "PTH",
    "FURB", "W", "FA", "YTT", "A", "ISC", "SLOT", "FLY",
    "PYI",
    "TC", "N",
    "PLE0605",
    "PLW1510", "PLW2901", "PLW0108", "PLW0603",
    "PLR5501", "PLC0207", "PLR1722", "PLR1714",
    "TRY002", "TRY004", "TRY300", "TRY301",
    "BLE001",
]

# `ruff format` (run via `make autoformat`) reflows whatever it can.
# E501 leftovers are content the formatter can't break (long string
# literals, URLs / shell commands inside f-strings, comments). Trust
# the formatter; don't fail CI on the unsplittable rest.
#
# RUF001/002/003 (ambiguous unicode in strings / docstrings / comments)
# exist to catch homoglyph attacks, not English typography. The project
# uses em/en-dashes deliberately and `ℹ` as a UI-hint glyph in CLI help
# output; flagging those is noise.
ignore = [
    "E501",
    "RUF001", "RUF002", "RUF003",
    # S603 (subprocess call without `shell=False`) and S607 (start
    # process with partial path) are over-eager for a project whose
    # CLI invokes `make` / `git` / `docker` / `ansible-playbook` from
    # PATH using list-form args. The list-form already prevents shell
    # injection (Python's `subprocess` does not parse argv[0] as a
    # shell command), and resolving every binary's absolute path in
    # the source would couple the code to the host filesystem layout.
    # The genuinely dangerous shell-injection patterns (`shell=True`)
    # are still caught by S602/S605.
    "S603", "S607",
    # PTH207 (`glob.glob` → `Path.glob`/`rglob`) and PTH208
    # (`os.listdir` → `Path.iterdir`) change the return shape:
    # `list[str]` → iterator of `Path`. Every call site needs per-site
    # review of how the result is consumed (string-path arithmetic,
    # `.startswith` / `.endswith` checks, plain string comparisons,
    # downstream APIs that require `str`). That work belongs to a
    # separate "iter-modernisation" follow-up commit, not this
    # use-pathlib pass.
    "PTH207", "PTH208",
    # SIM112 (capitalise env var names) conflicts with the deliberate
    # lowercase routing-knob surface: `make compose-deploy disable=x`
    # sets shell env `disable` via GNU Make's auto-export, and the
    # consumers read the same name. Forcing uppercase would split the
    # surface (`make … disable=x` writes lowercase, code reads
    # `DISABLE`) and break the make/env name parity.
    "SIM112",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Test code legitimately uses patterns flake8-bandit flags as security
# concerns in production code:
# - S101 (`assert`)             is the unittest idiom.
# - S102 (`exec`)               is used to load script-under-test by file path.
# - S105/S106 (hardcoded passwords) appear in fixtures / dummy creds.
# - S108 (hardcoded /tmp paths) appears in tempdir fixtures.
# - S110/S112 (try/except pass/continue) appear in cleanup helpers.
# - BLE001 (broad `except Exception`) is idiomatic in test fixtures /
#   cleanup helpers that must never abort the suite on teardown.
"tests/**" = ["S101", "S102", "S105", "S106", "S108", "S110", "S112", "BLE001"]

# Standalone scripts under ``roles/*/files/`` and ``utils/cert_utils.py``
# are exercised by test fixtures that monkey-patch the legacy ``os.*``
# surface (``os.makedirs``, ``os.stat`` with non-pathlib kwargs,
# ``patch.object(sut, "os")`` replacements). Converting these call
# sites to ``pathlib.Path`` would require rewriting every coupled
# test in lockstep — out of scope for the use-pathlib pass.
"roles/sys-ctl-rpr-container-hard/files/python/script.py" = ["PTH"]
"roles/sys-ctl-rpr-container-soft/files/python/script.py" = ["PTH"]

# BLE001 (flake8-blind-except) ratchet.
# Broad `except Exception:` is now selected project-wide so NEW code is
# gated. Standalone role scripts under ``roles/*/files/`` legitimately
# swallow-and-continue for resilience, so the whole tree is exempt. The
# production modules below predate the rule and are grandfathered pending
# a focused burn-down; they should shrink, not grow. New production files
# are gated. CodeQL (`py/empty-except`) still covers the empty-body case
# everywhere, including the exempt paths.
"roles/**" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/administration/deploy/container/command.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/administration/deploy/dedicated/apps.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/administration/deploy/dedicated/command.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/administration/deploy/development/inventory/legacy_resolver.py" = ["BLE001"]

"cli/administration/inventory/provision/credentials_generator.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/administration/inventory/provision/host_vars.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/administration/inventory/provision/services_disabler.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/administration/inventory/validate/loaders.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/contributing/mirror/sync/__main__.py" = ["BLE001"]
