"cli/meta/ci/roles/runtime/__main__.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/meta/j2/compiler/__main__.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/meta/roles/applications/all/__main__.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/meta/roles/applications/in_group_deps/__main__.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/meta/roles/applications/invokable/__main__.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/meta/roles/applications/type/__main__.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/meta/roles/lifecycle/__main__.py" = ["BLE001"]
"cli/meta/roles/services/called/__init__.py" = ["BLE001"]
"library/docker_bridge_gateway.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/filter/active_docker.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/filter/docker/service_enabled.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/filter/dotenv.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/filter/get/all/application_ids.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/filter/role_path_by_app_id.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/filter/split_postgres_connections.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/lookup/addon_env_flags.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/lookup/applications_current_play.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/lookup/image.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/lookup/email.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/lookup/prometheus_integration_active.py" = ["BLE001"]
"plugins/lookup/version.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/cache/base.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/nexus/list_apt_proxy_repos.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/roles/applications/in_group_deps.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/roles/applications/services/resources.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/roles/dependency_resolver.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/roles/validation/invokable.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/roles/validation/resources.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/templating/ansible.py" = ["BLE001"]
"utils/cert_utils.py" = ["PTH", "BLE001"]

# N999 (invalid module name) on Ansible-invoked role-level scripts
# whose filenames contain hyphens. Renaming to snake_case would break
# the Ansible meta references that source them via the literal path,
# so the hyphenated filename is locked in by the surrounding stack.

# `include_r` would be the canonical lowercase form per N806, but the
# matrix-deploy code consistently writes the round index as ``R`` in
# its formulas (``R if R < count else 0``) and the variable name
# ``include_R`` reads as "round R's include set" right next to those
# formulas. The uppercase R here is documentation, not a constant.
"cli/administration/deploy/development/deploy.py" = ["N806"]
"cli/administration/deploy/development/init.py" = ["N806"]
"cli/administration/deploy/development/inventory.py" = ["N806"]
"tests/unit/python/cli/administration/deploy/development/test_inventory.py" = ["N806"]

# Lazy-loaded class binding: ``ValueGenerator = _value_generator_cls()``
# rebinds the imported class inside the function. PEP 8 keeps the
# UpperCamelCase form for class identifiers, including local re-binds.
"plugins/filter/value_generator.py" = ["N806"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter — architectural import contracts (run via `lint-imports`,
# enforced by tests/lint/filesystem/python/test_import_contracts.py).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "cli"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# The dev/CI deploy package was repeatedly hit by CodeQL
# `py/unsafe-cyclic-import`. The fix split the env/arg helpers into the
# leaf module `env`, giving the load-time DAG compose -> common -> env.
# This layers contract locks that order in: a lower layer importing a
# higher one (i.e. a new cycle) breaks the build.
name = "cli.administration.deploy.development stays acyclic (compose -> common -> env)"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "cli.administration.deploy.development.compose",
    "cli.administration.deploy.development.common",
    "cli.administration.deploy.development.env",
]
# Type-checking-only / lazily-deferred back-references to `compose` do
# not run at import time, so they cannot form a load-time cycle.
ignore_imports = [
    "cli.administration.deploy.development.common -> cli.administration.deploy.development.compose",
]

[project]
  name = "ramses_rf"
  dynamic = ["version"]
  description = "A stateful RAMSES-II protocol decoder & analyser."
  readme = "README.md"
  authors = [
    {name = "Egbert Broerse", email = "dcc2@ebroerse.nl"}
  ]
  maintainers = [
    {name = "Egbert Broerse", email = "dcc2@ebroerse.nl"}
  ]
  license = "MIT"
  license-files = ["LICENSE*"]

  keywords = [
    "evohome",
    "honeywell",
    "resideo",
    "round thermostat",
    "ramses",
    "airios",
    "chronotherm",
    "climarad",
    "hometronics",
    "itho",
    "nuaire",
    "orcon",
    "sundial",
    "vasco",
  ]
  classifiers = [
    "Topic :: Home Automation",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  ]
  requires-python = ">=3.13"        # HA core >=3.14.2
  dependencies = [
    "aiofiles>=23.2.1",             # latest
    "colorlog>=6.9.0",              # latest
    "orjson>=3.9.0",                # added for Phase 2.1 Fat SQLite Backend
    "paho-mqtt>=2.1.0",             # latest
    "serialx>=1.8.2",               # Roadmap Item 9 / Issue #606 (HA container baseline; 1.8.1 fixed fd leak, Win32 race, USB string descriptors)
    "probatio >= 0.11.2"            # latest
  ]

#
[project.optional-dependencies]
zigbee = ["zigpy>=2.0.0"]           # ZigbeeTransport (Phase 3) — provided by ZHA inside HA

#
[project.urls]
  "Homepage" = "https://github.com/ramses-rf/ramses_rf"
  "Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/ramses-rf/ramses_rf/issues"
  "Wiki" = "https://github.com/ramses-rf/ramses_rf/wiki"
  "Contributing" = "https://github.com/ramses-rf/ramses_rf/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md"

#
[project.scripts]
  client = "ramses_cli.client:main"

#
### build-system #####################################################################

[build-system]
  requires = ["hatchling"]
  build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build]
  sources = ["src"]
  artifacts = ["examples/ser2net.yaml"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
  packages = ["src/ramses_rf", "src/ramses_tx", "src/ramses_cli"]

[tool.hatch.version]
  path = "src/ramses_rf/version.py"


#
### pytest ###########################################################################

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
  asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
  asyncio_mode = "auto"

  testpaths = [
    "tests/"
  ]

  # Kill hanging tests after 60 seconds
  # Without this, a hung test runs until GitHub Actions kills the job.
  timeout = 60
  # Continue collecting/running other tests after a timeout, don't abort
  # the entire session.
  timeout_method = "thread"

  # pytest-cov slows down our tests on GitHub Actions to 10 mins, so use coverage.py instead.
  # PyCharm might not hit a breakpoint. For debugging, disable -cov by adding:
  # –no-cov"

#
### coverage #########################################################################

[tool.coverage.run]
  core = "sysmon"  # essential setting for speed on GitHub < 11 secs instead of >12 mins
  branch = false  # true takes a lot longer and can't be combined with sysmon
#  patch = ["subprocess"]
  source = [
    "src",
    "tests"
  ]

[tool.coverage.report]
  # Regexes for lines to exclude from consideration
  exclude_also = [
    # Don't complain if tests don't hit defensive assertion code:
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
  ]
  format = "text"
  fail_under = 80  # total cov now 82%
  ignore_errors = true

[tool.coverage.html]
  directory = "coverage_html"

#
### mypy #############################################################################

[tool.mypy]
  files = [
    "client.py",
    "src",
    "tests"
  ]
  exclude = [
    "src/ramses_cli/utils",
    "tests/wip",
  ]

  # ### Import discovery...
  # - https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/command_line.html#import-discovery

  # ignore_missing_imports = true  # only used per-module
  # follow_imports = normal  # avoid skip/silent, prefer normal (default) over error

  # ### Strict typing (--strict) if all following are set to true (excl. ramses-rf)
  #  - https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/existing_code.html#introduce-stricter-options

  # # Config file & Configuring warning
  #  - https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/command_line.html#config-file

  # Start off with these
  warn_unused_configs = true
  warn_redundant_casts = true  # from: Configuring warning
  warn_unused_ignores = true  # from: Configuring warning

  # # Miscellaneous strictness flags
  #  - https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/command_line.html#miscellaneous-strictness-flags

  # Getting these passing should be easy
  extra_checks = true  # now incl.: strict_concatenate = true
  strict_equality = true

  # Strongly recommend enabling this one as soon as you can
  check_untyped_defs = true

  # allow_redefinition = false  # default is false
  no_implicit_reexport = true  # added by zxdavb

  # # Disallow dynamic typing...
  #  - https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/command_line.html#disallow-dynamic-typing

  # These shouldn't be too much additional work, but may be tricky to
  # get passing if you use a lot of untyped libraries
  disallow_subclassing_any = true
  disallow_untyped_decorators = true  # from: Untyped definitions and calls
  disallow_any_generics = true

  disallow_any_explicit = true  # TODO: extend to ramses_rf/ramses_cli (see override below)

  # # Untyped definitions and calls
  #  - https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/command_line.html#untyped-definitions-and-calls

  # These next few are various gradations of forcing use of type annotations
  disallow_untyped_calls = true
  disallow_incomplete_defs = true
  disallow_untyped_defs = true

  # # Configuring warnings
  #  - https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/command_line.html#configuring-warnings

  # This one can be tricky to get passing if you use a lot of untyped libraries
  warn_return_any = true

  disallow_any_unimported = true  # from: Disallow dynamic typing
  warn_no_return = true
  warn_unreachable = true

  # # None and Optional handling
  #  - https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/command_line.html#none-and-optional-handling

  no_implicit_optional = true


#

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = "debugpy.*"
  ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = "colorama.*"
  ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = "zigpy.*"
  ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = "homeassistant.*"
  ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = "ramses_tx.transport.zigbee.*"
  disable_error_code = [
    "unreachable",  # conditional imports inside try blocks
    "explicit-any",  # boundary shim around untyped zigpy/ZHA/HA objects
  ]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = "ramses_tx.transport.factory"
  disable_error_code = [
    "assignment",  # transport var reassigned between ZigbeeTransport and MqttTransport branches
  ]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = "tests_rf.*"

  disable_error_code = [
    "explicit-any",  #  mocks/fixtures legitimately carry Any
    "arg-type",  #     54
    "type-arg",  #     11
    "attr-defined",  #  duck-typed state/event attributes in fixtures
  ]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = "tests_tx.*"

  disable_error_code = [
    "explicit-any",   #  mocks/fixtures legitimately carry Any
    "attr-defined",   #  MagicMock assertions on typed callables
    "method-assign",  #  assigning MagicMock to methods in tests
    "assignment",     #  assigning MagicMock to None-typed fields
    "index",          #  Optional tuple indexing in test helpers
    "misc",           #  assigning to Final class attributes
    "union-attr",     #  accessing attrs on Any | None cluster mocks
    "arg-type",
    "type-arg",
  ]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = [
    "tests_cli.*",
    "utils.*",
    "wip.*",
  ]

  disable_error_code = [
    "explicit-any",  #  mocks/fixtures legitimately carry Any
    "arg-type",      #  plain strs for NewType'd ids in test calls
  ]

#
## ruff ##############################################################################

[tool.ruff]
  line-length = 79
  src = ["src", "tests"]
  target-version = "py312"


[tool.ruff.lint]
  select = [
    "ASYNC",   # flake8-async
    "B",       # flake8-bugbear
    "D",       # pydocstyle
    "E",       # pycodestyle
    "F",       # Pyflakes
    "I",       # isort
    "Q",       # flake8-quotes
    "SIM",     # flake8-simplify
    "TID251",  # flake8-tidy-imports (banned-api)
    "UP",      # pyupgrade
  ]
  ignore = [
    "ASYNC109",
    "ASYNC110",
    "B011",
    "D203",
    "D213",
    "E501",
    "SIM102",
    "SIM114",
    "UP040",
  ]

  # ASYNC109 - Async function with a timeout parameter
  # ASYNC110 - Use `asyncio.Event` instead of awaiting `asyncio.sleep` in a `while` loop
  # B011     - Do not call assert False since python -O removes these calls
  # D203     - 1 blank line required before class docstring (conflicts with D211)
  # D213     - Multi-line docstring summary should start at the second line (conflicts with D212)
  # E501     - Line too long
  # SIM102   - Use a single `if` statement instead of nested `if` statements
  # SIM114   - Combine `if` branches using logical `or` operator
  # UP040    - Type alias uses `TypeAlias` annotation instead of the `type` keyword


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions.extend-aliases]
  probatio = "vol"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-pytest-style]
  fixture-parentheses = false


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-quotes]
  inline-quotes = "double"


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
  "async_timeout".msg = "use asyncio.timeout instead"
  "pytz".msg = "use zoneinfo instead"


[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
  combine-as-imports = true
  force-sort-within-sections = false
  known-first-party = ["ramses_cli", "ramses_rf", "ramses_tx"]
  split-on-trailing-comma = true


[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
  "tests/*" = ["ASYNC", "D"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = [
    "ramses_rf",
    "ramses_tx",
    "ramses_cli"
]
ignore_type_checking_imports = true

# 1. Macro Level: CLI -> App -> Transport (OSI L1-L3 vs L4-L7)
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Macro Package Separation"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "ramses_cli",
    "ramses_rf",
    "ramses_tx",
]

# 2. ramses_rf: The Event-Driven CQRS Hierarchy
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ramses_rf CQRS Architecture Layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "ramses_rf.gateway",      # L7 Orchestrator / Facade (Top)
    "ramses_rf.pipeline",     # Async Event Bus (Reassembly, Decoder, Dispatcher, TopologyBuilder)
    "ramses_rf.systems",      # CQRS Read-Models (Systems / Zones)
    "ramses_rf.devices",       # CQRS Read-Models & Registry
    "ramses_rf.state",        # SSOT Database / Caches
    "ramses_rf.schemas",      # Pure DTO Validation
    "ramses_rf.messages",     # Immutable Event Envelopes
    "ramses_rf.routing",      # O(1) Routing Headers
    "ramses_rf.protocol",     # L7 Protocol Semantics (OpenTherm, Fingerprints)
    "ramses_rf.models",       # Pure Primitives / Enums / DTOs (Bottom)
]

# 3. CQRS Firewall: Entities cannot mutate topology or touch the pipeline
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "CQRS Read-Model Isolation"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "ramses_rf.devices",
    "ramses_rf.systems",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ramses_rf.pipeline",
    "ramses_rf.gateway",
]

# 4. ramses_tx: Pure L1-L3 Networking Stack
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ramses_tx Internal Stack Separation"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "ramses_tx.engine",
    "ramses_tx.protocol",
    "ramses_tx.transport",
    "ramses_tx.packet",
]

reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = "none"

package jp.glory.app.arch_unit

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.LayeredArchitecture
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.metrics.ArchitectureMetrics
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.metrics.MetricsComponents
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test


class ByLayerTest {
    companion object {
        const val basePackageName = "jp.glory.app.arch_unit"

        const val ktorLibrary = "Ktor Library"
        const val exposedLibrary = "Exposed Library"

        const val applicationBaseName = "Application Base"
        const val domainBaseLayerName = "Domain base"
        const val useCaseBaseLayerName = "UseCase base"
        const val webBaseLayerName = "Web base"

        const val moduleLayerName = "Module"
        const val domainLayerName = "Domain"
        const val useCaseLayerName = "UseCase"
        const val storeLayerName = "Store Adaptor"
        const val webLayerName = "Web Adaptor"

        val moduleNames = listOf("product")
    }

    @Test
    fun checkLayerDependency() {
        val basePackage = ClassFileImporter().importPackages(basePackageName)

        Architectures.layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .apply {
                defineLayers(this)

                defineKtorLibrary(this)
                defineExposedLibrary(this)

                defineBaseDomainLayerRule(this)
                defineBaseUseCaseLayerRule(this)
                defineBaseWebLayerRule(this)

                defineDomainLayerRule(this)
                defineUseCaseLayerRule(this)
            }
            .check(basePackage)
    }
    @Test
    fun calculateLakosMetrics() {
        val targetPackage = ClassFileImporter().importPackages(basePackageName)
            .getPackage(basePackageName)
            .subpackagesInTree
        val components = MetricsComponents.fromPackages(targetPackage)

        val metrics = ArchitectureMetrics.lakosMetrics(components)

        println("CCD: " + metrics.getCumulativeComponentDependency())
        println("ACD: " + metrics.getAverageComponentDependency())
        println("RACD: " + metrics.getRelativeAverageComponentDependency())
        println("NCCD: " + metrics.getNormalizedCumulativeComponentDependency())

    }

    @Test
    fun calculateComponentDependencyMetricsMetrics() {
        val targetPackage = ClassFileImporter().importPackages(basePackageName)
            .getPackage(basePackageName)
            .subpackagesInTree
        val components = MetricsComponents.fromPackages(targetPackage)
        val metrics = ArchitectureMetrics.componentDependencyMetrics(components)

        targetPackage.forEach {
            val targetName = it.name
            println("======================== Start $targetName ======================== ")
            println("Ce: " + metrics.getEfferentCoupling(targetName))
            println("Ca: " + metrics.getAfferentCoupling(targetName))
            println("I: " + metrics.getInstability(targetName))
            println("A: " + metrics.getAbstractness(targetName))
            println("D: " + metrics.getNormalizedDistanceFromMainSequence(targetName))
            println("======================== E n d $targetName ======================== ")
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun calculateMetrics() {
        val targetPackage = ClassFileImporter().importPackages(basePackageName)
            .getPackage(basePackageName)
            .subpackagesInTree
        val components = MetricsComponents.fromPackages(targetPackage)
        val metrics = ArchitectureMetrics.visibilityMetrics(components)

        targetPackage.forEach {
            val targetName = it.name
            println("======================== Start $targetName ======================== ")
            println("RV : " + metrics.getRelativeVisibility(targetName))
            println("======================== E n d $targetName ======================== ")
        }

        println("ARV: " + metrics.getAverageRelativeVisibility())
        println("GRV: " + metrics.getGlobalRelativeVisibility())
    }

    private fun defineLayers(architecture: LayeredArchitecture) {
        architecture.optionalLayer(ktorLibrary)
            .definedBy("io.ktor..")
        architecture.optionalLayer(exposedLibrary)
            .definedBy("org.jetbrains.exposed..")

        architecture.layer(applicationBaseName)
            .definedBy(basePackageName)
        architecture.layer(domainBaseLayerName)
            .definedBy("$basePackageName.base.domain..")
        architecture.layer(useCaseBaseLayerName)
            .definedBy("$basePackageName.base.usecase..")
        architecture.layer(webBaseLayerName)
            .definedBy("$basePackageName.base.adaptor.web..")

        architecture.layer(moduleLayerName)
            .definedBy(*createPackageIdentifiers("module"))
        architecture.layer(domainLayerName)
            .definedBy(*createPackageIdentifiers("domain"))
        architecture.layer(useCaseLayerName)
            .definedBy(*createPackageIdentifiers("usecase"))
        architecture.layer(storeLayerName)
            .definedBy(*createPackageIdentifiers("adaptor.store"))
        architecture.layer(webLayerName)
            .definedBy(*createPackageIdentifiers("adaptor.web"))
    }

    private fun createPackageIdentifiers(
        layerName: String
    ): Array<String> =
        moduleNames
            .map { "$basePackageName.$it.$layerName.." }
            .toTypedArray()

    private fun defineKtorLibrary(architecture: LayeredArchitecture) {
        architecture
            .whereLayer(ktorLibrary)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                webBaseLayerName
            )
    }

    private fun defineExposedLibrary(architecture: LayeredArchitecture) {
        architecture
            .whereLayer(exposedLibrary)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                webLayerName,
                storeLayerName
            )
    }

    private fun defineBaseDomainLayerRule(architecture: LayeredArchitecture) {
        architecture
            .whereLayer(domainBaseLayerName)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                domainLayerName,
                useCaseBaseLayerName,
                storeLayerName
            )
    }

    private fun defineBaseUseCaseLayerRule(architecture: LayeredArchitecture) {
        architecture
            .whereLayer(useCaseBaseLayerName)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                useCaseLayerName,
                webBaseLayerName
            )
    }

    private fun defineBaseWebLayerRule(architecture: LayeredArchitecture) {
        architecture
            .whereLayer(webBaseLayerName)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                applicationBaseName,
                webLayerName
            )
    }

    private fun defineDomainLayerRule(architecture: LayeredArchitecture) {
        architecture
            .whereLayer(domainLayerName)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                storeLayerName,
                moduleLayerName,
                useCaseLayerName
            )
    }

    private fun defineUseCaseLayerRule(architecture: LayeredArchitecture) {
        architecture
            .whereLayer(useCaseLayerName)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                applicationBaseName,
                moduleLayerName,
                webLayerName
            )
    }
}

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]

# into the pool before AddSerializedFile(). ruff must not strip or move those imports.

# deltalite's test suite bootstraps its harness/planner via sys.path (the package is a
# maturin-built extension living under rust/, not part of the Django app), so imports
# are necessarily lazy / post-path-insert (PLC0415, E402); the planner's small CLI
# prints its report (T201).

"posthog/settings/**" = ["F403", "F405"]

"manage.py" = ["PLC0415"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter: enforce internal product architecture
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["products", "owners_yaml"]
include_external_packages = true

# A Python distribution under packages/ is a leaf: it must install and run outside the
# monorepo venv, so it can import nothing from the app. tach resolves a uv distribution as
# third-party and cannot police that boundary. import-linter resolves by installed import
# name, so it can.

name = "packages/owners-yaml is a leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["owners_yaml"]
forbidden_modules = ["posthog", "ee", "products", "common", "django", "rest_framework"]

# The facade is the layer below presentation. A facade that imports its product's presentation
# inverts the layering (and drags DRF onto every consumer's import path); a facade that imports

# forced — without it import-linter rejects the wildcard modules as having shared descendants),
# so DRF reached through an internal module stays green: this enforces the layering norm, not a
# transitive guarantee. See products/architecture.md § Wiring couplings.

type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["products.*.backend.facade"]

    "products.*.backend.presentation",
    "rest_framework",
]

[tool.ty.rules]
# Import resolution - ty can't always find all modules/stubs
unresolved-import = "ignore"

# Django-related rules - ty doesn't support Django's metaprogramming yet
# See: https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/291
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"  # Django model fields, relationships, auto-generated attributes
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"  # Django querysets, managers, form fields
unknown-argument = "ignore"  # Django kwargs, queryset filters, manager methods
invalid-base = "ignore"  # Django model metaclasses (e.g., models.Model)
missing-argument = "ignore"  # Django auto-generated __init__, managers
too-many-positional-arguments = "ignore"  # Django metaprogramming signatures

# Dual mypy+ty — mypy still runs, so its artifacts are legitimate
redundant-cast = "ignore"  # casts needed by mypy that ty resolves
unused-type-ignore-comment = "ignore"  # type: ignore comments required by mypy
unused-ignore-comment = "error"  # default is warn, which does not fail CI; error keeps stale ty: ignore directives out

# Flags guards on stub and TypedDict types that runtime data does not honor
# (billing JSON, posthoganalytics.api_key, untyped access-control callers)
redundant-condition = "ignore"

# Django lazy imports and settings indirection
possibly-missing-submodule = "ignore"

# DRF serializer pattern — validate/update/create overrides are idiomatic
invalid-method-override = "ignore"
invalid-attribute-override = "ignore"  # Django manager/field overrides (e.g. `objects`)

# Conditional base classes (e.g. EnterpriseEventQuery | EventQuery pattern)
unsupported-base = "ignore"

# Protobuf generated code + Django lazy references
unresolved-reference = "ignore"

# Third-party library overload stubs (Anthropic SDK, Django, re, etc.)
no-matching-overload = "ignore"

# Framework metaclass magic — ty can't resolve dynamic callables
call-top-callable = "ignore"
call-non-callable = "ignore"

# Django querysets typed as `object` — ty can't narrow through managers
not-iterable = "ignore"

# `in` operator on Django/framework `object` types
unsupported-operator = "ignore"

# Subscript on `object`/`None` from unresolved Django types
not-subscriptable = "ignore"

# mypy already catches deprecations; ty is a fast preflight, not the authority
deprecated = "ignore"

# ty disagrees with mypy on some existing code — baselined, not suppressed.
# These rules catch real bugs in new code, so they stay enabled.
# invalid-type-form is the exception: generated code + ty limitations on valid patterns.
invalid-type-form = "ignore"

[[tool.ty.overrides]]
# Scanner schemas are built with create_model at runtime, so every kwarg looks extra to ty
include = ["products/replay_vision/backend/tests/test_scanners.py"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
pydantic-discarded-extra-argument = "ignore"

[project]
name = "npdoc2md"
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
]
description = "CLI utility for autogenerating markdown docs from numpy-style docstrings."

# Docstring parser did not correctly handle numpy docstrings,
# so for now install branch version from git with my fixes.
dependencies = [
    "docstring_parser@git+https://github.com/rr-/docstring_parser",
    "import-linter>=2.15",
]

dynamic = ["version"]
license.file = "LICENSE"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
[project.scripts]
npdoc2md = "npdoc2md.__main__:main"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "copier",
    "pipdeptree",
    "pre-commit",
    "pyright",
    "pytest",
    "pytest-cov",
    "ruff",
    "tox-direct",
    "types-mock",
    "import-linter",
]

[project.urls]
GitHub = "https://github.com/jwlodek/npdoc2md"

[[project.authors]] # Further authors may be added by duplicating this section
email = "jwlodek.dev@gmail.com"
name = "Jakub Wlodek"


[tool.setuptools_scm]
version_file = "src/npdoc2md/_version.py"

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
reportMissingImports = false # Ignore missing stubs in imported modules
reportMissingTypeStubs = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Run pytest with all our checkers, and don't spam us with massive tracebacks on error
addopts = """
    --tb=native -vv
    """
# https://iscinumpy.gitlab.io/post/bound-version-constraints/#watch-for-warnings
filterwarnings = "error"
# Doctest python code in docs, python code in src docstrings, test functions in tests
testpaths = "docs src tests"

[tool.coverage.run]
data_file = "/tmp/npdoc2md.coverage"

[tool.coverage.paths]
# Tests are run from installed location, map back to the src directory
source = ["src", "**/site-packages/"]

# tox must currently be configured via an embedded ini string
# See: https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/999
[tool.tox]
legacy_tox_ini = """
[tox]
skipsdist=True

[testenv:{pre-commit,type-checking,tests}]
# Don't create a virtualenv for the command, requires tox-direct plugin
direct = True
passenv = *
allowlist_externals =
    pytest

    "security-tools",

]

    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",

    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",

    "charset-normalizer~=3.1.0",

    "configupdater>=3.2,<4",
    # The floor stays below the CVE-2026-69247 fix (50.0.0) because sigstore
    # 4.1.0, the last release supporting Python 3.9, caps cryptography at < 47.
    "cryptography>=43.0.1,<51",
    "marshmallow>=3.18,<5",
    "marshmallow-dataclass>=8.7.0,<9",
    "oauthlib>=3.2.1,<4",

    "ruamel.yaml>=0.19,<0.20",
    "rich~=13.0",
    "sigstore>=4.0.0,<5",
    "typing-extensions~=4.14",

    "tomlkit>=0.13.3,<0.14",
    "filelock>=3.19.1",

]

# Import contracts for the monorepo: the root CLAUDE.md "Package Dependency
# Graph" as rules import-linter checks on every commit and every PR.
#
# Run with `python scripts/lint_imports.py` (the pre-commit hook of the same
# name runs it): the wrapper puts every package directory on sys.path, so the
# graph is built from THIS checkout's sources alone and no package has to be
# installed. Each contract is named after the sentence in the root CLAUDE.md
# it enforces; change the sentence and the contract together.
#
# An `ignore_imports` line is a baselined violation — debt the owner has
# seen, with the follow-up it waits for in the comment beside it. Never add
# one to make a new import pass; fix the import or change the rule. Paying
# a debt must delete its line in the same PR: an ignore whose import no
# longer exists is a hard error ("No matches for ignored import"), which
# the next unrelated commit would otherwise inherit.
#
# tests/test_import_contracts.py pins `root_packages` and the layers table
# to the packages on disk, so a new package cannot slip in unlisted.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    geecs_core
    geecs_data_utils
    geecs_schemas
    geecs_web_theme
    logmaker_4_googledocs
    geecs_analysis
    scan_analysis
    geecs_bluesky
    geecs_ca_gateway
    geecs_pva_gateway
    geecs_archiver
    geecs_log_triage
    geecs_scanner
    geecs_portal
    geecs_logbook
    geecs_mcp
include_external_packages = True
exclude_type_checking_imports = True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The shape of the graph
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Every edge points down this table and packages on one row never import
# each other, directly or through another package. A new edge in either
# direction is a graph change: update the root CLAUDE.md first.
[importlinter:contract:package-layers]
name = Package layers: edges point down the dependency graph; packages on one layer never import each other
type = layers
layers =
    geecs_scanner | geecs_mcp | geecs_portal | geecs_logbook
    geecs_bluesky | scan_analysis | geecs_ca_gateway | geecs_pva_gateway | geecs_archiver | geecs_log_triage
    geecs_analysis
    geecs_core | geecs_data_utils | geecs_schemas | geecs_web_theme | logmaker_4_googledocs

# Workspace root for the Netstead + corral monorepo.
#
# This file is NOT a publishable package — it carries the uv workspace
# declaration and shared development tooling configuration (ruff,
# pyright, import-linter, pytest, coverage) for all workspace packages.
#
# Distributable packages live in packages/, first-party Workbench plugins in plugins/ — see:
#   packages/corral/pyproject.toml         (generic engine)
#   packages/netstead/pyproject.toml       (GMNS-specific)
#   plugins/project-cards/pyproject.toml   (Workbench plugin "project cards": ProjectCard authoring)

[tool.uv.workspace]
# First-party plugins live in plugins/<name>, each its own workspace package that may import only
# netstead.workbench.plugins' public API (one import-linter contract per plugin, below).
members = ["packages/*", "plugins/*"]

[tool.uv.sources]
dbcorral = { workspace = true }
netstead = { workspace = true }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared dev tooling
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8",
    "pytest-cov>=5",
    "pytest-benchmark>=4",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
    # starlette>=1.7 TestClient requires httpx2 (plain httpx is deprecated there).
    "httpx2",
    "hypothesis>=6.100",
    "ruff>=0.5",
    "pyright>=1.1.370",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "pre-commit>=3.7",
]
docs = [
    "mkdocs>=1.6",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.5",
    "mkdocs-macros-plugin>=1.0",
    "mkdocs-mermaid2-plugin>=1.1",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.25",
    "mkdocs-autorefs>=1.0",
    "mkdocs-awesome-pages-plugin>=2.9",
    "mkdocs-section-index>=0.3",
    "mkdocs-glightbox>=0.4",
    "mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin>=1.2",
    "mkdocs-htmlproofer-plugin>=1.2",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ruff (replaces black + flake8 + isort)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"
# Only exclude vendored upstream content (no Python source in these
# directories). The previous `["netstead", "tests", "_archive"]` exclusion
# was for the legacy pre-monorepo tree and inadvertently matched the new
# package path `packages/netstead/netstead/`, skipping all of its source from
# lint. Path-scoped exclusions only.

    "packages/netstead/netstead/spec/0.95",
    "packages/netstead/netstead/spec/0.96",
    "packages/netstead/netstead/spec/0.97",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
    "I",    # isort
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify
    "RUF",  # ruff-specific
    "D",    # pydocstyle (Google convention)
]
ignore = [
    "D100",  # missing docstring in public module
    "D104",  # missing docstring in public package
    "D203",  # incorrect-blank-line-before-class
    "D213",  # multi-line-summary-second-line
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"**/tests/**" = ["D"]
"**/__init__.py" = ["D"]
"scripts/**" = ["E501", "D"]  # scripts have long inline strings + don't need full docstrings
# Typer CLI command signatures use `typer.Argument(...)` / `typer.Option(...)`
# in argument defaults — that's the idiomatic typer API. B008 (function call
# in default) is a false positive for this pattern, scoped to cli/ paths only.
"**/cli/**" = ["B008"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pyright (strict on corral; standard on netstead)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.pyright]
include = ["packages/corral/corral", "packages/netstead/netstead", "plugins/project-cards/netstead_project_cards"]
exclude = ["**/__pycache__", "**/_archive", "**/legacy"]
pythonVersion = "3.11"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"

[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "packages/corral/corral"
extraPaths = ["packages/corral"]

[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "packages/netstead/netstead"
extraPaths = ["packages/netstead", "packages/corral"]

[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "plugins/project-cards/netstead_project_cards"
extraPaths = ["plugins/project-cards", "packages/netstead", "packages/corral"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import-linter — enforce architectural boundaries
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rules:
#   - corral may not import from netstead
#   - netstead.clean / .server / .mcp are optional extras (no required import
#     of these from netstead core)
#   - Raw SQL strings outside corral.engines.ibis_engine are forbidden
#     (enforced separately by a ruff plugin / custom check; see ./scripts/lint_no_sql.py)

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["corral", "netstead", "netstead_project_cards"]
include_external_packages = false

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "corral must not depend on netstead"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["corral"]
forbidden_modules = ["netstead"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "netstead core must not require optional-extra submodules"
type = "forbidden"
# Source modules expand as the package grows; netstead.network etc. land in Phase 3.
source_modules = [
    "netstead.semantics",
    "netstead.scope",
    "netstead.indexes",
    "netstead.quality",
    "netstead.cli",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "netstead.clean",
    "netstead.server",
    "netstead.mcp",
    "netstead.osm",
    "netstead.reports",
    "netstead.map",
    # NB: netstead.graph is intentionally NOT forbidden — it is the graph/routing
    # *backend* (like netstead.indexes), which netstead.semantics (and, as the
    # unification proceeds, netstead.scope) import. Its scipy dep is lazily
    # imported and shipped via the [graph] extra.
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# The project cards plugin is written against the public plugin API only (Host, BaseAction, ActionSpec, ...), so it keeps
# working as netstead's internals move. netstead.workbench.plugins itself imports netstead internals: indirect
# imports through it are allowed; direct imports of anything else in netstead (or corral) are not.
name = "netstead-project-cards uses only the public plugin API of netstead"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["netstead_project_cards"]
forbidden_modules = ["netstead", "corral"]
ignore_imports = [
    "netstead_project_cards -> netstead.workbench.plugins",
    "netstead_project_cards.** -> netstead.workbench.plugins",
]
# The root pattern covers a future direct import in __init__.py; today only submodules import the API, so don't
# fail on an ignore that matches nothing.
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "none"
allow_indirect_imports = true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pytest
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
testpaths = ["packages/corral/tests", "packages/netstead/tests", "plugins/project-cards/tests"]
# importlib mode avoids module-name collisions when multiple packages each
# have a tests/__init__.py (otherwise both bind to "tests" and the second
# loses); also required for src-layout monorepos.
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--doctest-modules",
    "--import-mode=importlib",
    "--ignore=netstead",          # legacy tree (Phase 0 closeout removes)
    "--ignore=tests",           # legacy tree
    "--ignore=_archive",
    # Fixture BUILD scripts are one-shot data-prep (they hit OSM/Overpass and
    # run work at module scope), not library modules. Keep them out of the
    # --doctest-modules sweep so collection never imports them — otherwise a
    # live Overpass 504 fails CI at collection time. The fixture *accessor*
    # modules (__init__.py) still get collected.
    "--ignore-glob=*/fixtures/*/build.py",
    "--ignore-glob=*/fixtures/*/build_fixture.py",
    "--ignore-glob=*/fixtures/*/scripts/*.py",
    # Fast default tier. Full suite: add `-m ""` (a later -m overrides this one).
    # See "Running tests" in CONTRIBUTING.md.
    "-m",
    "not slow and not perf",
    # Under `-n auto` (pytest-xdist) keep each test file on one worker:
    # test_documented_python_contract shares a namespace across the blocks of
    # one doc page, so they must run in order in one process. No-op without -n.
    "--dist=loadfile",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    # duckdb >= 1.5 deprecated fetch_arrow_table() in favour of to_arrow_table();
    # the ibis-framework duckdb backend still calls the deprecated name until
    # its next minor release. Narrow ignore — DO NOT broaden to a blanket
    # `ignore::DeprecationWarning:ibis.*`, which would hide future ibis
    # deprecations affecting us and defeat the warning-as-error policy.
    # TODO(deps): drop when ibis-framework releases a duckdb backend that
    # uses to_arrow_table(); track at https://github.com/ibis-project/ibis
    "ignore:fetch_arrow_table.*:DeprecationWarning",
    # pytest-benchmark warns (at configure time, so "error" would abort the run)
    # that it disables itself under xdist. Expected with `-n auto`; the bench
    # workflow runs serially.
    "ignore:Benchmarks are automatically disabled because xdist plugin is active",
    # projectcard 0.3.3's utils.py has re.sub("[\ ]+", ...): compiling it warns, and "error" would turn that into
    # a SyntaxError at import (uv installs without bytecode, so CI always compiles it). Narrow: this message from
    # projectcard/utils.py only. Python 3.11 raises it as a DeprecationWarning, 3.12+ as a SyntaxWarning.
    # TODO(deps): drop when projectcard ships a raw string there.
    "ignore:invalid escape sequence:SyntaxWarning:.*projectcard.utils",
    "ignore:invalid escape sequence:DeprecationWarning:.*projectcard.utils",
]
markers = [
    "slow: end-to-end / multi-second tests; skipped by default, run with -m \"\" (full) or -m slow",
    "perf: performance regression bench; skipped by default, run with -m \"\" (full) or -m perf",
    "integration: cross-package integration",
    "live_llm: calls real LLM provider APIs; skipped unless NETSTEAD_LIVE_LLM=anthropic,openai,gemini,ollama (any subset)",
    "plugin_discovery: lets Session() discover installed Workbench plugin entry points (off by default in tests)",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Coverage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["packages/corral/corral", "packages/netstead/netstead", "plugins/project-cards/netstead_project_cards"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/_legacy/*",
    # Fixture build scripts are excluded from the doctest sweep (see pytest
    # addopts), so they are never imported under test — drop them from the
    # coverage denominator too, else the gate counts them as 0%.
    "*/fixtures/*/build.py",
    "*/fixtures/*/build_fixture.py",
    "*/fixtures/*/scripts/*.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@overload",
]
# Workspace-wide gate. Per-package gates are enforced separately in
# the Tests workflow (corral ≥86%, netstead ≥84%, project-cards ≥96%) so a
# regression in one package can't be masked by overshoot in another. Baseline
# measured 2026-05-26: combined 86%, corral 87%, netstead 85%; project-cards
# measured 2026-10-19: 97.7% —
# gates set one point below current (rounded down) to flag regressions
# immediately without flaking on stat-noise.
fail_under = 85

[importlinter]
root_package = _generics
include_external_packages = true

[importlinter:contract:1]
name = Private package can not import from public package
type = forbidden
source_modules = _generics
forbidden_modules = generics

; =============================================================================
; Import Linter — Architecture Guardrails for RDF Differ (component-first)
; =============================================================================
; Tier model: 0=core (commons), 1=foundation (diffing|reporting|loader), 3=api.
; Lower tiers must not import higher tiers; foundation peers must not import peers.
; Each component is internally layered: entrypoints > services > adapters > domain.
;
; LIVING ARTIFACT: groom this on every refactor / new component / rename. `(x)` =
; optional layer (skipped if absent); `a | b` = independent siblings at one tier.
; `make check-architecture` (poetry run lint-imports) gates it.

[importlinter]
root_package = rdf_differ
; required because the store-seam / domain-purity contracts forbid external libs
include_external_packages = True

; --- Tier hierarchy: api > (diffing | reporting | loader) > core ---------------
[importlinter:contract:tier-hierarchy]
name = Tier hierarchy: api > foundation(diffing|reporting|loader) > core
type = layers
layers =
    rdf_differ.api
    rdf_differ.diffing | rdf_differ.reporting | rdf_differ.loader
    rdf_differ.core

; --- Intra-component layers: entrypoints > services > adapters > domain --------
[importlinter:contract:component-layers]
name = Component layers: entrypoints > services > adapters > domain
type = layers
layers =
    (entrypoints)
    (services)
    (adapters)
    (domain)
containers =
    rdf_differ.api
    rdf_differ.diffing
    rdf_differ.reporting
    rdf_differ.loader

; --- core (commons) is inwards-looking: imports no business component ----------
[importlinter:contract:core-isolation]
name = core (commons) must not import business components
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    rdf_differ.core
forbidden_modules =
    rdf_differ.api
    rdf_differ.diffing
    rdf_differ.reporting
    rdf_differ.loader

; --- core layers are exhaustive (commons has no entrypoints) -------------------
[importlinter:contract:core-exhaustive]
name = core layers are exhaustive (no entrypoints)
type = layers
layers =
    (services)
    (adapters)
    (domain)
containers =
    rdf_differ.core
exhaustive = true

; --- Foundation peers must not import each other (tier 1 same-level) -----------
[importlinter:contract:foundation-peer-isolation-diffing]
name = Foundation peer isolation: diffing must not import peers
type = forbidden
source_modules = rdf_differ.diffing
forbidden_modules =
    rdf_differ.reporting
    rdf_differ.loader

[importlinter:contract:foundation-peer-isolation-reporting]
name = Foundation peer isolation: reporting must not import peers
type = forbidden
source_modules = rdf_differ.reporting
forbidden_modules =
    rdf_differ.diffing
    rdf_differ.loader

[importlinter:contract:foundation-peer-isolation-loader]
name = Foundation peer isolation: loader must not import peers
type = forbidden
source_modules = rdf_differ.loader
forbidden_modules =
    rdf_differ.diffing
    rdf_differ.reporting

; --- Domain purity: no domain layer may import an I/O framework ----------------
[importlinter:contract:domain-purity]
name = domain layers must not import I/O frameworks
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    rdf_differ.core.domain
    rdf_differ.diffing.domain
    rdf_differ.loader.domain
forbidden_modules =
    flask
    connexion
    celery
    click
    requests
    pyoxigraph
    eds4jinja2
    SPARQLWrapper

; --- DIP at the loader store seam (DEC-8) -------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:loader-services-store-seam]
name = loader.services must not import store/report libraries (DIP)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    rdf_differ.loader.services
forbidden_modules =
    pyoxigraph
    rdflib
    requests
    SPARQLWrapper
    eds4jinja2

; --- The GraphStorePort implementations must not import each other (DEC-8) -----
[importlinter:contract:store-adapter-independence]
name = store adapters are independent of each other
type = independence
modules =
    rdf_differ.loader.adapters.remote_sparql_store
    rdf_differ.loader.adapters.in_memory_stores

# Minimal pyproject.toml — Meaningfy standard (no-src, config-in-root).
# Only [project], [tool.poetry], [dependency-groups], [build-system] live here.
# Every TOOL is configured in its own dedicated root file:
#   ruff.toml · mypy.ini · pytest.ini · .coveragerc · .importlinter
#   .pre-commit-config.yaml · sonar-project.properties
# The single source of truth for the version is the root VERSION file; the build
# backend (hatchling) reads it directly, so there is no version to keep in sync here.

[project]
name = "rdf-differ"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Diff calculator for RDF datasets (SKOS/OWL aware) — REST API, UI, worker and CLI"
authors = [
    { name = "Meaningfy", email = "hi@meaningfy.ws" }
]
maintainers = [
    { name = "Meaningfy", email = "hi@meaningfy.ws" }
]
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
requires-python = ">=3.12,<4.0"
classifiers = [
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Natural Language :: English",
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
]
dependencies = [
    "click>=8.1,<9",
    "SPARQLWrapper>=2.0,<3",
    # Bounded by eds4jinja2 0.3.1's pins (rdflib ~=7.0, requests ~=2.31); widen here
    # to compatible ranges so resolution succeeds. Raise once eds4jinja2 relaxes them.
    "rdflib>=7.0,<8",
    "requests>=2.31,<3",
    # FastAPI entrypoints (EPIC api-ui-fastapi-modernization) — replaced Flask/connexion.
    "fastapi>=0.115,<1",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30,<1",
    "jinja2>=3.1,<4",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9,<1",
    "httpx>=0.27,<1",
    "itsdangerous>=2.1,<3",
    # werkzeug FileStorage is used by core/diffing adapters (upload handling).
    "werkzeug>=3,<4",
    "eds4jinja2>=0.3.1,<0.4",
    "shortuuid>=1.0,<2",
    "celery>=5.4,<6",
    "redis>=5,<6",
    "flower>=2.0,<3",
    "gunicorn>=22,<27",
    "pydantic (>=2.6,<3)",
    "pyoxigraph (>=0.4,<0.5)",
    "pyyaml (>=6,<7)",
]

[project.scripts]
rdf-diff = "rdf_differ.loader.entrypoints.cli:cli"

[dependency-groups]
# PEP 735 dependency groups.
dev = [
    "pre-commit==4.6.0",
]
test = [
    "pytest>=9,<10",
    "coverage>=7.5,<8",
    "pytest-cov>=6,<8",
    "pytest-bdd>=8,<9",
    "beautifulsoup4~=4.12.2",
]
lint = [
    "ruff==0.15.11",
    "mypy==1.20.2",
    "import-linter==2.11",
    "radon==6.0.1",
    "xenon==0.9.3",
]
docs = [
    "myst-parser~=2.0.0",
    "Sphinx~=7.1.2",
    "sphinxcontrib-apidoc~=0.4.0",
]
# Opt-in browser E2E. Not installed by default — `poetry install --with e2e` then
# `poetry run playwright install chromium`. See tests/e2e/README.md.
e2e = [
    "pytest-playwright~=0.5",
]

# Poetry is used here only for dependency management — the package is installed
# `--no-root` in Docker and never built/published via Poetry. Non-package mode lets
# Poetry skip its own version requirement; hatchling (the build backend) owns the
# version, reading it from the root VERSION file.
[tool.poetry]
package-mode = false

# Version is read from the root VERSION file (single source of truth).
[tool.hatch.version]
path = "VERSION"
pattern = "(?P<version>.+)"

# No-src layout: package the top-level package directly.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["rdf_differ"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.25"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# NOTE: intentionally no [tool.ruff], [tool.mypy], [tool.pytest], [tool.coverage]
# sections here — all tool config lives in dedicated root files (see header).

[importlinter]
root_package = eds4jinja2

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = eds4jinja2 cosmic layers
type = layers
layers =
    eds4jinja2.entrypoints
    eds4jinja2.services
    eds4jinja2.adapters
    eds4jinja2.models

[importlinter:contract:models-are-pure]

type = forbidden
source_modules =
    eds4jinja2.models
forbidden_modules =
    eds4jinja2.adapters
    eds4jinja2.services
    eds4jinja2.entrypoints

[importlinter:contract:adapters-only-models]
name = adapters import nothing above adapters
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    eds4jinja2.adapters
forbidden_modules =
    eds4jinja2.services
    eds4jinja2.entrypoints

# Standards-based packaging (PEP 517/518/621) with the setuptools backend.

# webhook_consumers.py is the one module core reads (through posthog.ingress.dispatch.loading)
# to register a product's inbound webhook consumers. Restricting what it may import gives the
# chain core -> webhook_consumers -> facade as two import edges, so a handler cannot reach
# product internals.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "webhook consumers must only import facade"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["products.*.backend.webhook_consumers"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "products.*.backend",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "products.**.backend.webhook_consumers -> products.**.backend.facade.**",
]

# The facade is the layer below presentation. A facade that imports its product's presentation
# inverts the layering (and drags DRF onto every consumer's import path); a facade that imports
# DRF is presentation in disguise. Only direct imports are checked (allow_indirect_imports is
# forced — without it import-linter rejects the wildcard modules as having shared descendants),
# so DRF reached through an internal module stays green: this enforces the layering norm, not a
# transitive guarantee. See products/architecture.md § Wiring couplings.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "facade must not import presentation or DRF"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["products.*.backend.facade"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "products.*.backend.presentation",
    "rest_framework",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    # TODO: existing violations — move the presentation-shaped code out of the facade, or the
    # facade-shaped code out of presentation, and drop the line
    "products.logs.backend.facade.retention_views -> products.logs.backend.presentation.views.retention_api",
    "products.managed_warehouse.backend.facade.api -> products.managed_warehouse.backend.presentation.views",
    "products.tasks.backend.facade.api -> products.tasks.backend.presentation.serializers",
    "products.billing_alerts.backend.facade.api -> rest_framework",
    "products.dashboards.backend.facade.api -> rest_framework",
    "products.experiments.backend.facade.api -> rest_framework",
    "products.feature_flags.backend.facade.api -> rest_framework",
    "products.tasks.backend.facade.api -> rest_framework",
    "products.tasks.backend.facade.client_provenance -> rest_framework",
]

# Contract files hold the data types other products read, so they stay free of Django, directly
# and through other product modules. Define a choices enum with posthog.enums.LabeledStrEnum or
# LabeledIntEnum instead of models.TextChoices. import-linter treats posthog as an external
# package, so Django reached through posthog.* is not visible here. See products/architecture.md
# § Contracts.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "facade contracts and enums must not import Django (use posthog.enums for choices)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "products.*.backend.facade.contracts",
    "products.*.backend.facade.enums",
    "products.*.backend.facade.types",
]
forbidden_modules = ["django"]
allow_indirect_imports = false

[tool.ty.rules]
# Import resolution - ty can't always find all modules/stubs
unresolved-import = "ignore"

# Django-related rules - ty doesn't support Django's metaprogramming yet
# See: https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/291
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"  # Django model fields, relationships, auto-generated attributes
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"  # Django querysets, managers, form fields
unknown-argument = "ignore"  # Django kwargs, queryset filters, manager methods
invalid-base = "ignore"  # Django model metaclasses (e.g., models.Model)
missing-argument = "ignore"  # Django auto-generated __init__, managers
too-many-positional-arguments = "ignore"  # Django metaprogramming signatures

# Dual mypy+ty — mypy still runs, so its artifacts are legitimate
redundant-cast = "ignore"  # casts needed by mypy that ty resolves
unused-type-ignore-comment = "ignore"  # type: ignore comments required by mypy
unused-ignore-comment = "error"  # default is warn, which does not fail CI; error keeps stale ty: ignore directives out

# Flags guards on stub and TypedDict types that runtime data does not honor
# (billing JSON, posthoganalytics.api_key, untyped access-control callers)
redundant-condition = "ignore"

# Django lazy imports and settings indirection
possibly-missing-submodule = "ignore"

# DRF serializer pattern — validate/update/create overrides are idiomatic
invalid-method-override = "ignore"
invalid-attribute-override = "ignore"  # Django manager/field overrides (e.g. `objects`)

# Conditional base classes (e.g. EnterpriseEventQuery | EventQuery pattern)
unsupported-base = "ignore"

# Protobuf generated code + Django lazy references
unresolved-reference = "ignore"

# Third-party library overload stubs (Anthropic SDK, Django, re, etc.)
no-matching-overload = "ignore"

# Framework metaclass magic — ty can't resolve dynamic callables
call-top-callable = "ignore"
call-non-callable = "ignore"

# Django querysets typed as `object` — ty can't narrow through managers
not-iterable = "ignore"

# `in` operator on Django/framework `object` types
unsupported-operator = "ignore"

# Subscript on `object`/`None` from unresolved Django types
not-subscriptable = "ignore"

# mypy already catches deprecations; ty is a fast preflight, not the authority
deprecated = "ignore"

# ty disagrees with mypy on some existing code — baselined, not suppressed.
# These rules catch real bugs in new code, so they stay enabled.
# invalid-type-form is the exception: generated code + ty limitations on valid patterns.
invalid-type-form = "ignore"

[[tool.ty.overrides]]
# Scanner schemas are built with create_model at runtime, so every kwarg looks extra to ty
include = ["products/replay_vision/backend/tests/test_scanners.py"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
pydantic-discarded-extra-argument = "ignore"

[project]
name = "igittigitt"
version = "2.2.8"
description = "A spec-compliant .gitignore parser and path filter, 100% git-compatible, with an include/whitelist mode and a streaming, memory-bounded CLI"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
    "wcmatch>=11.1",
    "pydantic>=2.14.1",
    "rich-click>=1.9.9",
    # Imported directly (adapters/cli/main.py), not only through rich-click.
    "click>=8.5.0",
    "lib_cli_exit_tools>=2.4.1",
    # 6.3.9: the version the [lib_log_rich] refusal (InvalidLoggingConfigError) is tested against.
    "lib_log_rich>=6.5.3",
    # Imported directly (adapters/logging/setup.py) to read the LOG_* lines of a .env.
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.4",
    "lib_layered_config>=7.1.9",
    "orjson>=3.13.0",
]
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "bitranox", email = "bitranox@gmail.com" }]
keywords = ["gitignore", "ignore", "glob", "wildmatch", "copytree", "cli", "filter", "whitelist"]
classifiers = [
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.15",
  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Environment :: Console",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]

# System packages required for CI runners (read by GitHub Actions workflow template)

system-dependencies-macos = []
system-dependencies-windows-pip = []
system-dependencies-windows-choco = []

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/bitranox/igittigitt"
Repository = "https://github.com/bitranox/igittigitt.git"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
  "pytest>=9.1.1",
  "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
  "hypothesis>=6.168.5",

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/igittigitt"]
include = [
    "src/igittigitt/py.typed",
    "src/igittigitt/adapters/config/defaultconfig.toml",
    "src/igittigitt/adapters/config/defaultconfig.d/*.toml",
]

# An allowlist, never a denylist: hatchling reads only the root .gitignore, so tracked working
# files and files hidden through .git/info/exclude or a nested .gitignore (session records,
# review notes, helper scripts) would ship. tests/test_packaging.py builds the sdist and
# refuses any other top-level entry.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
    "/src/igittigitt",
    "/tests",
    "/docs",
    "/README.md",
    "/LICENSE",
    "/CHANGELOG.md",
    "/pyproject.toml",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", "W",     # pycodestyle
  "F",           # pyflakes
  "I",           # isort
  "N",           # pep8-naming
  "UP",          # pyupgrade
  "B",           # bugbear
  "A",           # builtins shadowing
  "C4",          # comprehension simplification
  "C90",         # mccabe: cyclomatic complexity <= 10 (the house hard limit)
  "SIM",         # simplification
  "TCH",         # type-checking imports
  "RUF",         # ruff-specific
  "G",           # logging format (catches f-string in logger)
  "T20",         # print statements
  "PTH",         # pathlib preference
  "PLC", "PLE",  # pylint conventions/errors
  "S",           # flake8-bandit security checks
  "PERF",        # performance anti-patterns
  "ERA",         # eradicate dead/commented-out code
  "FBT",         # boolean trap (boolean positional args)
  "PLR",         # pylint refactor
  "PLW",         # pylint warnings
]
[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
# Pydantic resolves field annotations at runtime, so its base class must stay
# importable outside TYPE_CHECKING (else the TC00x autofix breaks model classes).
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Notebooks: unused imports are often intentional for side effects; print() is
# how a notebook shows output.
"notebooks/*.ipynb" = ["F401", "T201"]
# Tests: assert is standard, test fixtures have passwords, magic values are clearer inline, temp paths are
# fine, deferred imports exercise import/cache behaviour or avoid module-level fixture pollution
"tests/*.py" = ["T20", "S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "S311", "S603", "S607", "PLW1510", "FBT001", "FBT003", "PLR0913", "PLR2004", "C408", "PERF401", "PLC0415"]
# CLI: Click framework injects boolean params; commands have many options; the
# error boundary naturally has several return branches (PLR0911).
"src/igittigitt/adapters/cli/**/*.py" = ["FBT001", "FBT002", "PLR0913", "PLR0911"]
# Ports / config / memory adapters: many-parameter signatures by design.
"src/igittigitt/application/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/igittigitt/adapters/config/*.py" = ["PLR0913", "FBT001", "FBT002"]
"src/igittigitt/adapters/memory/*.py" = ["PLR0913", "FBT001", "FBT002"]
# Core engine: a ported, doctest-heavy module with an established public API.
# It deliberately uses os.path (not pathlib) so it never resolves symlinks, and
# keeps boolean-flag function signatures used by the doctests; both are by design.
"src/igittigitt/igittigitt.py" = [
  "SLF001", "PLR0913", "N818", "FBT001", "FBT002", "C408", "SIM108", "SIM113",
  "PTH100", "PTH111", "PTH123", "PTH207", "PLW2901", "PERF401", "T201",
]

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
extraPaths = [
  "src",
]

# `src` stays fully strict. Tests do legitimate white-box access of internal
# members (cache caps, the streaming token bound) and include a ported, loosely
# typed legacy suite; relax only the "unknown type" / private-usage rules there.
[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "tests"
reportPrivateUsage = false
reportUnknownVariableType = false
reportUnknownMemberType = false
reportUnknownArgumentType = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = ["--doctest-modules"]
doctest_optionflags = ["ELLIPSIS", "NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
markers = [
  "os_agnostic: test runs on every supported operating system",
  "os_windows: test exercises Windows-only behavior",
  "os_macos: test exercises macOS-only behavior",
  "os_posix: test exercises behavior requiring POSIX semantics",
  "os_linux: test exercises Linux-only behavior",
  "local_only: tests that require the local dev environment (external resources, script composition); skipped in CI",
  "integration: tests requiring external resources (SMTP, databases, APIs); run via 'bmk ti' or 'mktesti.sh'",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
parallel = false
# Use a temp directory for the coverage database to avoid SQLite locking
# issues on network-mounted filesystems. The {envtmpdir} placeholder is
# not supported by coverage.py, so we use an environment variable with
# fallback to a cross-platform temp location via the pytest_configure
# hook in tests/conftest.py. CI also sets COVERAGE_FILE via workflow env.
#
# For local development, the pytest hook automatically redirects to
# tempfile.gettempdir() before pytest-cov creates its Coverage() object.
# This static fallback catches edge cases where coverage is run directly.
data_file = "/tmp/.coverage.igittigitt"
source = ["src/igittigitt"]

[tool.coverage.report]
omit = [
  "tests/*",
]
fail_under = 80
show_missing = true

[tool.coverage.json]
output = "coverage.json"
pretty_print = true

[tool.clean]
# Patterns to remove when running `make clean`
patterns = [
  "**/__pycache__",
  ".hypothesis",
  ".import_linter_cache",
  ".pytest_cache",
  ".ruff_cache",
  ".pyright",
  ".mypy_cache",
  ".tox",
  ".nox",
  ".eggs",
  "*.egg-info",
  "build",
  "dist",
  "htmlcov",
  ".coverage",
  "coverage.xml",
  "codecov.sh",
  ".cache",
  "result",
  ".data_arch_violations.json",
]

[tool.git]
# Default git remote for push/release commands

[tool.scripts.test]
# Configuration for CI/CD test runner
pytest-verbosity = "-vv"
coverage-report-file = "coverage.xml"
src-path = "src"

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "igittigitt"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Core engine is independent of the CLI adapters"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "igittigitt.igittigitt",
  "igittigitt.conf_igittigitt",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "igittigitt.adapters",
  "igittigitt.application",
  "igittigitt.composition",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain is pure (no adapter/application/composition dependencies)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "igittigitt.domain",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "igittigitt.adapters",
  "igittigitt.application",
  "igittigitt.composition",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Clean Architecture layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
  "igittigitt.composition",
  "igittigitt.adapters",
  "igittigitt.application",
  "igittigitt.domain",
]

[tool.pip-audit]
# Empty on purpose: "pip-audit --skip-editable" is clean against the resolved dev
# tree, so nothing needs suppressing. An id listed here also swallows any FUTURE
# vulnerability filed under that same id, so an entry that no longer fires is a
# blind spot, not a leftover - add one only while a finding is live and unfixable,
# with the package, the fix version, and the condition to drop it again.
ignore-vulns = []

[tool.bashate]
# bashate style settings for .sh files (E003 excluded: indent handled by shfmt)
max-line-length = 120
ignores = ["E003"]

[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "1 day"
exclude-newer-package = {lib-cli-exit-tools = false, lib-layered-config = false, lib-log-rich = false}

; Importing constraints for layered layout of modules and packages.
; The goal is higher cohesion and lower coupling of components.
; https://import-linter.readthedocs.io/en/stable/contract_types.html
[importlinter]
root_package = kopf
include_external_packages = True
contract_types =
    conditional: _importlinter_conditional.ConditionalImportContract

[importlinter:contract:root-layers]
name = The root framework modules must be layered
type = layers
layers =
    kopf.on
    kopf._kits
    kopf._core
    kopf._cogs

[importlinter:contract:core-layers]
name = The internal core must be layered
type = layers
layers =
    kopf._core.reactor
    kopf._core.engines
    kopf._core.intents
    kopf._core.actions

[importlinter:contract:cogs-layers]
name = The internal cogs must be layered
type = layers
layers =
    kopf._cogs.clients
    kopf._cogs.configs
    kopf._cogs.structs
    kopf._cogs.aiokits
    kopf._cogs.helpers

[importlinter:contract:progress-storage]
name = Progress storages must be persistence settings
type = layers
layers =
    kopf._cogs.configs.configuration
    kopf._cogs.configs.progress
    kopf._cogs.configs.conventions

[importlinter:contract:diffbase-storage]
name = Diffbase storages must be persistence settings
type = layers
layers =
    kopf._cogs.configs.configuration
    kopf._cogs.configs.diffbase
    kopf._cogs.configs.conventions

[importlinter:contract:independent-storages]
name = Storage types must be unaware of each other
type = independence
modules =
    kopf._cogs.configs.diffbase
    kopf._cogs.configs.progress

[importlinter:contract:independent-aiokits]
name = Most asyncio kits must be unaware of each other
type = independence
modules =
    kopf._cogs.aiokits.aioadapters
    kopf._cogs.aiokits.aiobindings
    kopf._cogs.aiokits.aioenums
    kopf._cogs.aiokits.aiotoggles
    kopf._cogs.aiokits.aiovalues
    ; but not aiotasks & aiotime!

[importlinter:contract:ban-toolkits]
name = The internals must be unaware of user-facing toolkits
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    kopf._cogs
    kopf._core
forbidden_modules =
    kopf._kits

[importlinter:contract:indenpendent-toolkits]
name = The user-facing toolkits must be unaware of each other
type = independence
modules =
    kopf._kits.hierarchies
    kopf._kits.runner
    kopf._kits.webhooks

[importlinter:contract:allow-3rd-party]
name = 3rd-party clients must be explicitly allowed
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    kopf
forbidden_modules =
    pykube
    kubernetes
ignore_imports =
    kopf._core.intents.piggybacking -> pykube
    kopf._core.intents.piggybacking -> kubernetes
    kopf._cogs.helpers.thirdparty -> pykube
    kopf._cogs.helpers.thirdparty -> kubernetes

[importlinter:contract:secure-3rd-party]
name = 3rd-party clients must be secured by conditional imports
type = conditional
source_modules =
    kopf
conditional_modules =
    pykube
    kubernetes
    kubernetes_asyncio

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools", "setuptools-scm>=8.1"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "kopf"
description = "Kubernetes Operator Pythonic Framework (Kopf)"
keywords = ["kubernetes", "operator", "framework", "python", "k8s"]
authors = [{name = "Sergey Vasilyev", email = "nolar@nolar.info"}]
maintainers = [{name = "Sergey Vasilyev", email = "nolar@nolar.info"}]
license = "MIT"
readme = "README.md"
classifiers = [
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.15",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: CPython",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: PyPy",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
]
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "python-json-logger",   # 0.05 MB
    "jsonpatch",
    "iso8601",              # 0.07 MB
    "pyyaml",               # 0.90 MB
    "click>=8.2.0",         # 0.60 MB
    "aiohttp>=3.14.0",      # 7.80 MB
]
dynamic = ["version"]  # taken from git tags

[project.urls]
homepage = "https://kopf.dev/"
repository = "https://github.com/nolar/kopf"
documentation = "https://docs.kopf.dev/"

[project.scripts]
kopf = "kopf.cli:main"

[project.optional-dependencies]
full-auth = [
    "pykube-ng",            # 4.90 MB
    "kubernetes>=12.0.0",   # 40.0 MB (!)
]
uvloop = [
    "uvloop",               # 9.00 MB
    "uvloop>=0.18.0; python_version>='3.12'",
]
dev = [
    # NB: oscrypto is pinned for Ubuntu 24.04+ in dependency-group - read the details there.
    "oscrypto",             # 2.80 MB (smaller than cryptography: 8.7 MB)
    "certbuilder",          # +0.1 MB (2.90 MB if alone)
    "certvalidator",        # +0.1 MB (2.90 MB if alone)
    "pyngrok",              # 1.00 MB + a downloaded binary
]

[dependency-groups]
docs = [
    "sphinx>=9.0.0",
    "sphinx-autobuild",
    "sphinx-autodoc-typehints",
    "sphinx-copybutton",
    "sphinxcontrib-googleanalytics",
    "sphinx-llm>=0.1.4",
    "furo",
]
test = [
    "certbuilder",
    "certvalidator",
    "codecov",
    "coverage>=7.12.0",
    "freezegun",
    "kmock>=0.5",
    "looptime>=0.8",
    "pyngrok",
    "pytest>=9.0.0",
    "pytest-aiohttp",
    "pytest-asyncio",
    "pytest-cov",
    "pytest-mock",
    "pytest-timeout",
    "types-pyyaml",
    "types-setuptools",

    # Enforce the hotfix for Ubuntu 24.04 in CI. Otherwise, we are stuck in Ubuntu 22.04.
    # The bugfix is merged but not released: https://github.com/wbond/oscrypto/issues/78
    # Pinning this in the final operators is the decision of the operator developers,
    # including the protocols of accessing the repo or vendoring the dependency code.
    # The dev-mode dependency is used ONLY with a temporary insecure self-signed CA for simplicity,
    # and ONLY with Ubuntu 24.04+. Therefore, it is not pinned in the main dependencies (e.g., works fine in 22.04).
    # In the worst case, configure the operator with a self-signed CA made in the OpenSSL CLI.
    "oscrypto @ git+https://github.com/wbond/oscrypto.git@1547f535001ba568b239b8797465536759c742a3",
]
lint = [
    {include-group = "test"},
    "mypy==2.3.1",
    "import-linter",
    "isort",
    "pre-commit",
    # All extras — for proper type-checks of imports (only for linting, not for testing!).
    "kubernetes>=12.0.0",
    "kubernetes-asyncio>=12.0.0",
    "pykube-ng",
    "oscrypto",
    "certbuilder",
    "certvalidator",
    "pyngrok",
    "uvloop",
]
dev = [
    {include-group = "docs"},
    {include-group = "lint"},
    {include-group = "test"},
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
# The star is for the versions.py, which is gitignored in docker builds (somewhy).
include = ["kopf", "kopf.*"]

[tool.setuptools_scm]
version_file = "kopf/_cogs/helpers/versions.py"

[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "7 days"
# These packages are my own, if they are hacked, all my github is hacked anyway.
# MyPy is pinned, so the intent is explicit, no need for time constraints.
exclude-newer-package = { kmock=false, looptime=false, mypy=false }

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
packages = ["kopf"]
exclude = ['(^|/)test_.*\.py$']
python_version = "3.11"
exclude_gitignore = true
warn_unused_configs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pytest]
minversion = "9.0"
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
log_format = "%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s"
log_date_format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
addopts = ["--strict-markers", "--looptime"]

[tool.isort]
line_length = 100
multi_line_output = 11
balanced_wrapping = true
combine_as_imports = true
case_sensitive = true
known_first_party = ["kopf"]
filter_files = true
skip_glob = ["examples/*.py"]
