[project]
name = "abis-mapping"
version = "9.0.4"
description = "Provides templates and mappings to translate tabular data to ABIS rdf"
authors = [
    { name = "Gaia Resources", email = "dev@gaiaresources.com.au" }
]
dynamic = ["requires-python", "dependencies"]

[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core >= 2.0.0, <3"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"

[tool.poetry]
requires-poetry = ">=2.0.0, <3"

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.11"
rdflib = "==7.1.1"
python-slugify = "^8.0.4"
frictionless = { extras = ["excel"], version = "^5.18.1" }
python-dateutil = "^2.9.0.post0"
shapely = "^2.1.1"
pyproj = "^3.7.2"
pydantic = "^2.11.7"
pydantic-settings = "^2.10.1"
numpy = "^2.3.2"
attrs = "^25.3.0"

[tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies]
pytest = "^9.0.3"
pytest-cov = "^7.1.0"
pytest-mock = "^3.15.1"
mypy = "==1.17.1"
types-python-dateutil = "==2.9.0.20250809"  # keep version synced with actual library
ruff = "==0.12.9"
import-linter = "^2.4"
pandas = "^2.3.1"
pyshacl = "^0.30.1"
jinja2 = "^3.1.6"
mkdocs-material = "^9.6.17"
mike = "^2.1.3"
poethepoet = "^0.37.0"
jsonschema-markdown = "^2025.7.0"

[tool.poe.tasks]
lint = "ruff check"
lint-fix = "ruff check --fix-only"
lint-imports = "lint-imports"
format = "ruff format"
format-check = "ruff format --check --diff"
typecheck = "mypy tests/ abis_mapping/ docs/ scripts/"
generate-instructions = "./scripts/generate_instructions.sh"
generate-model-docs = "./scripts/generate_model_docs.sh"
generate-example-ttl-files = "python ./scripts/generate_example_ttl_files.py"
test = "pytest tests --cov=abis_mapping --cov=docs --cov-report=term-missing"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
filterwarnings = [
    # Treat any warnings in tests as errors.
    'error',
    # If certain warning should be allowed/ignored add them here.
    # https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/capture-warnings.html#controlling-warnings
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 120

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    # Default rules
    "E4", "E7", "E9", "F",
    # additional rules
    "B", # bugbear
    "A", # builtins
    "S", # bandit
    "G", # logging-format
    "RUF100", # unused suppressions
    "INP001", # no namespace packages
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Allow unused imports in __init__.py for re-exporting
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]
# Allow using assert in tests
"tests/*" = ["S101"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.importlinter]
# Import linter is a tool to enfore structure in a python program.
# See https://import-linter.readthedocs.io/en/stable/readme.html.
root_packages = [
    "abis_mapping",
    "docs",
    "scripts",
    "tests",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# The abis_mapping module must not depend on tests/scripts/docs modules.
name = "abis_mapping module independence"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["abis_mapping"]
forbidden_modules = ["tests", "scripts", "docs"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# The docs module must not depend on tests/scripts modules.
name = "docs module independence"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["docs"]
forbidden_modules = ["tests", "scripts"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# Enfore a layered structure in the "abis_mapping" module. Helps prevent circular imports.
# Modules in each layer can only import from modules in a lower layer.
# "foo | bar" means foo and bar are considered one layer, and must not import each other.
name = "abis_mapping structure"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true
containers = ["abis_mapping"]
layers = [
    # top-level modules
    "templates | documentation",
    # mid-level modules
    "base | plugins | vocabs",
    "models",
    # low-level modules
    "utils",
    "settings",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# Enforce a layered structure in the "tests" module.
name = "test structure"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true
containers = ["tests"]
layers = [
    # conftest is the top layer, fixtures declared here should be injected by pytest, not imported by tests.
    "conftest",
    # test modules are independant, should not import each other.
    "base | docs | models | plugins | templates | utils | vocabs",
    # low-level helpers.
    "helpers",
]

[importlinter]
root_package=src
include_external_packages=True

[importlinter:contract:1]
name=Utils Independence Contract
type=forbidden
source_modules =
    src.utils
forbidden_modules =
    <all-other>

[project]
name = "simple-secrets-manager"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Securely store and deliver tokens, passwords, API keys, and other secrets using HTTP API, Swagger UI, or Python Package."
authors = [
    { name = "Krishnakanth Alagiri", email = "39209037+bearlike@users.noreply.github.com" },
]
license = "CC0-1.0"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13,<4.0"
# Base install = only what the `ssm` / `ssm-cli` client actually imports.
# The Flask server and the reload sidecar pull their heavier deps via the
# `server` / `reload` extras so a CLI-only install stays lean.
dependencies = [
    "click>=8.1.8,<9.0.0",
    "rich>=13.9.4,<14.0.0",
    "requests>=2.32.3,<3.0.0",
    "keyring>=25.6.0,<26.0.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# OpenTelemetry event emission (the `ssm_telemetry` leaf). Pinned to one
# verified line (opentelemetry-python 1.43.0). We take the OTLP *HTTP*
# exporter on purpose — the umbrella `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp` drags in
# grpcio. `server` and `reload` layer these in via
# `simple-secrets-manager[otel]`; the CLI base stays otel-free (and
# `ssm_telemetry` degrades to a no-op when the extra is absent).
otel = [
    "opentelemetry-api==1.43.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk==1.43.0",
    "opentelemetry-semantic-conventions==0.64b0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.43.0",
]
# The Flask + flask-restx REST API server (`ssm_server`, `python -m ssm_server.main`).
server = [
    "flask-httpauth>4,<5",
    "flask-cors>=5.0.0,<6.0.0",
    "flask-restx>=0.5.1",
    "pymongo>4,<5",
    "loguru>=0.7.3,<0.8.0",
    # Typed cross-service reload contract (`ssm_contracts`) + OTel events, plus
    # the validated ServerSettings config (`pydantic-settings` also reads the
    # optional `.env`, replacing python-dotenv).
    "pydantic>=2.5,<3.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0,<3.0",
    "simple-secrets-manager[otel]",
]
# The `ssm-reload` container reloader sidecar (needs the Docker SDK).
reload = [
    "docker>=7.0.0,<8.0.0",
    # Typed cross-service reload contract (`ssm_contracts`) + OTel events, plus
    # the validated ReloadSettings config (`pydantic-settings`).
    "pydantic>=2.5,<3.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0,<3.0",
    "simple-secrets-manager[otel]",
]
# Everything, for a full local/dev checkout.
all = ["simple-secrets-manager[server,reload]"]

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/bearlike/simple-secrets-manager.git"
Issues = "https://github.com/bearlike/simple-secrets-manager/issues"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "ipykernel>=6.29.5,<7.0.0",
    "pytest>=8.3.5,<9.0.0",
    "ruff>=0.13.0,<0.14.0",
    "mypy>=1.17.1,<2.0.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0,<3.0",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77.0.3"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project.scripts]
ssm = "ssm_cli.main:cli"
ssm-cli = "ssm_cli.main:cli"
ssm-reload = "ssm_reload.runner:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
include = [
    "ssm_server*",
    "ssm_cli*",
    "ssm_reload*",
    "ssm_telemetry*",
    "ssm_contracts*",
    "ssm_projection*",
]
exclude = ["tests*"]

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = { attr = "ssm_cli.__version__" }

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 79
target-version = "py313"
exclude = [".venv"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# E/F = pycodestyle+pyflakes core; C901 = mccabe complexity; SIM102/PERF403 =
# targeted single rules; C4 = flake8-comprehensions (whole family passes clean).
# Deferred families (violations exist today, would need source edits owned by
# other work): I (import sort, 31), UP (pyupgrade, 97), B (bugbear, 2),
# SIM full (15). Enable them once those are fixed.
select = ["E", "F", "C901", "SIM102", "PERF403", "C4"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
ignore_missing_imports = true
# Both pass the whole tree today. Deferred (violations exist, need source
# edits): warn_unused_ignores (1: ssm_cli/auth.py redundant ignore) and
# check_untyped_defs (46, mostly untyped test bodies).
warn_redundant_casts = true
no_implicit_optional = true
exclude = [
    "^\\.venv/",
    "^build/",
    "^simple_secrets_manager\\.egg-info/",
]

# The reload sidecar is small and fully typed — hold it to the strict bar so it
# stays that way. Verified: `mypy --strict -p ssm_reload` is clean. NOTE: the
# `strict = true` meta-flag is not scopable in a per-module override (it leaks
# to every module), so the strict sub-flags are enumerated here instead.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "ssm_reload.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = true
disallow_any_generics = true
disallow_subclassing_any = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
no_implicit_reexport = true
strict_equality = true
check_untyped_defs = true
extra_checks = true

# --- import-linter: enforce the subproduct boundaries (dependencies flow
# inward). Run via `uv run lint-imports` / `make lint-imports`; wired into
# scripts/quality.sh after MyPy. ---
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = [
    "ssm_server",
    "ssm_cli",
    "ssm_reload",
    "ssm_telemetry",
    "ssm_contracts",
    "ssm_projection",
]

# `ssm_telemetry` (OTel events), `ssm_contracts` (the typed reload contract)
# and `ssm_projection` (the dotenv renderer + sinks) are LEAVES: the server,
# the CLI and the reloader import them across the HTTP boundary, so they must
# never import back into any app package or the reloader's hard isolation (and
# the inward dependency rule) would break.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ssm_telemetry is a leaf (imports no app package)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ssm_telemetry"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ssm_server",
    "ssm_cli",
    "ssm_reload",
    "ssm_contracts",
    "ssm_projection",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ssm_contracts is a leaf (imports no app package)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ssm_contracts"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ssm_server",
    "ssm_cli",
    "ssm_reload",
    "ssm_telemetry",
    "ssm_projection",
]

# The CLI and the reloader must render byte-identical env_file contents (compose
# hashes the file's CONTENTS), so the renderer is a leaf both import rather than
# a helper either one owns.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ssm_projection is a leaf (imports no app package)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ssm_projection"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ssm_server",
    "ssm_cli",
    "ssm_reload",
    "ssm_telemetry",
    "ssm_contracts",
]

# The reload sidecar talks only to the API over HTTP + the Docker socket; it
# must never import the server or CLI Python packages.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ssm_reload is independent of ssm_server and ssm_cli"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ssm_reload"]
forbidden_modules = ["ssm_server", "ssm_cli"]

# The CLI is a standalone HTTP client; it must not pull in the server or the
# reload sidecar.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ssm_cli is independent of ssm_server and ssm_reload"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ssm_cli"]
forbidden_modules = ["ssm_server", "ssm_reload"]

# Dependencies flow inward: the engines (domain layer) must not reach up into
# the API/HTTP layer. The one accepted edge is the leaf serialization util
# (to_iso / sanitize_doc / oid_to_str — pure functions, no Flask), which the
# engines legitimately reuse; everything else in ssm_server.api (the Flask app
# in api.core, the flask-restx resources) stays out of the engines.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ssm_server.engines does not depend on the API layer"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ssm_server.engines"]
forbidden_modules = ["ssm_server.api"]
ignore_imports = ["ssm_server.engines.* -> ssm_server.api.serialization"]

# Intended layering of src/ (import-linter, run by `qa.py check --name quality`; or just `lint-imports`).
# A layer may import the layers BELOW it, never above. `a | b` = same level, must not import each other;
# `a : b` = same level, may import each other (engine services around one shared core).
#
#   scenes | features        entry level: screens and plugins
#   ui                       widgets/HUD: used by scenes, never by the domain
#   gameplay | entities      domain
#   systems : effects : content : database    engine services
#   core                     infrastructure (constants, events, config) - imports nothing above it
#
# ignore_imports = the BASELINE: violations that exist today. The quality ratchet fails when this list grows or a
# new upward import appears; fix an edge, then delete its line (a stale line only warns, and the baseline count drops).
[importlinter]
root_packages =
    src
include_external_packages = False

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = layers
type = layers
layers =
    src.scenes | src.features
    src.ui
    src.gameplay | src.entities
    src.systems : src.effects : src.content : src.database
    src.core
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = warn
ignore_imports =
    # baseline: infrastructure imports the game (core -> scenes / database / entities)
    src.core.game_core -> src.scenes.scene_manager
    src.core.game_core -> src.database.db_core
    src.core.entity_manager -> src.entities.base_entity
    src.core.entity_manager -> src.entities.character
    src.core.entity_manager -> src.entities.enemy
    # baseline: entities import UI and gameplay (health bar, progression, hero drive)
    src.entities.character -> src.ui.health_bar
    src.entities.enemy -> src.ui.health_bar
    src.entities.character -> src.gameplay.progression
    src.entities.character -> src.gameplay.hero_drive
    # baseline: gameplay and entities are one level but import each other
    src.gameplay.world -> src.entities.enemy

package net.bestia.zone.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes
import net.bestia.zone.cartography.tile.MapTileService
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

/**
 * The map renderer runs inside the zone, but needs nothing from it: it draws a generated world. Kept that way,
 * so moving it to a module or a tile service of its own stays a move. `MapTileService` is the zone's adapter.
 */
class CartographyRendererRulesTest {

  private val renderer = arrayOf(
    "net.bestia.zone.cartography.render..",
    "net.bestia.zone.cartography.coverage..",
    "net.bestia.zone.cartography.tile..",
  )

  @Test
  fun `the map renderer depends only on itself and worldgen`() {
    val imported = ClassFileImporter()
      .withImportOption(ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests())
      .importPackages("net.bestia.zone.cartography")

    classes().that().resideInAnyPackage(*renderer)
      .and().doNotBelongToAnyOf(MapTileService::class.java)
      .should().onlyDependOnClassesThat().resideInAnyPackage(
        *renderer,
        "net.bestia.worldgen..",
        "java..",
        "javax.imageio..",
        "kotlin..",
        "org.jetbrains.annotations..",
        "io.github.oshai.kotlinlogging..",
      )
      .check(imported)
  }
}

package com.github.spanierm.archunitjunit5kotlin.onion

import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition.slices
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestInstance

@TestInstance(TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)
@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [OnionArchitectureTest::class])
internal class OnionArchitectureTest {
    @ArchTest
    val `there are no package cycles` =
            SlicesRuleDefinition.slices()
                    .matching("$BASE_PACKAGE.(**)..")
                    .should()
                    .beFreeOfCycles()

    @ArchTest
    val `the domain model does not have outgoing dependencies` =
            noClasses()
                    .that()
                    .resideInAPackage("$DOMAIN_MODEL_PACKAGE..")
                    .should()
                    .accessClassesThat()
                    .resideInAnyPackage("$DOMAIN_SERVICE_PACKAGE..", "$APPLICATION_PACKAGE..", "$ADAPTER_PACKAGE..")

    @ArchTest
    val `the domain does not access the application and adapters` =
            noClasses()
                    .that()
                    .resideInAPackage("$DOMAIN_PACKAGE..")
                    .should()
                    .accessClassesThat()
                    .resideInAnyPackage("$APPLICATION_PACKAGE..", "$ADAPTER_PACKAGE..")

    @ArchTest
    val `the application does not access the adapters` =
            noClasses()
                    .that()
                    .resideInAPackage("$APPLICATION_PACKAGE..")
                    .should()
                    .accessClassesThat()
                    .resideInAPackage("$ADAPTER_PACKAGE..")

    @ArchTest
    val `one adapter should not access another adapter` =
        slices()
                .matching("$ADAPTER_PACKAGE.(*)")
                .should().notDependOnEachOther()

    companion object {
        private val BASE_PACKAGE = OnionArchitectureTest::class.java.`package`.name

        private val DOMAIN_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.domain"
        private val DOMAIN_MODEL_PACKAGE = "$DOMAIN_PACKAGE.model"
        private val DOMAIN_SERVICE_PACKAGE = "$DOMAIN_PACKAGE.service"

        private val APPLICATION_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.application"

        private val ADAPTER_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.adapter"
    }
}

[tool.slotscheck]
# A module that fails to import is an error, not a silently skipped one.
strict-imports = true
require-superclass = true
require-subclass = true
# Every other class in the package is slotted (#3201). These are not, each for a reason
# a `__slots__` line would not fix. The pattern is verbose, so `#` carries the reasons.
exclude-classes = '''
  ^faststream\.specification\.(asyncapi\.v[0-9_]+\.schema|base|schema\.bindings\.http)
      # pydantic models: the fields live in BaseModel's own `__dict__` slot and the
      # AsyncAPI ones accept extra keys, so declaring `__slots__` would save nothing
| ^faststream\._internal\.configs\.(broker:BrokerConfig|endpoint:EndpointConfig|specification:SpecificationConfig)$
      # the config dataclass roots, and with them every broker config below. Python
      # 3.10 re-emits inherited fields into a `slots=True` subclass, doubling the
      # storage it is meant to save; safe again once 3.10 support is dropped
| ^faststream\._internal\.application:Application$
      # the user's application object, one per process; our CLI tests patch `app.run`
| ^faststream\._internal\.broker\.broker:BrokerUsecase$
      # one broker per process, and what suites mock: `patch.object(broker, "start")`
| ^faststream\._internal\.configs\.broker:ConfigComposition$
      # a `__getattr__` proxy: reads forward to the inner config, writes land here
| ^faststream\._internal\.endpoint\.subscriber\.mixins:ConcurrentMixin$
      # mixed into each broker's slotted subscriber; two slotted bases conflict
| ^faststream\.(kafka|confluent|redis)\.message:FakeConsumer$
      # the FAKE_CONSUMER singleton, whose methods tests patch on the instance
| ^faststream\.nats\.broker\.registrator:NatsRegistrator$
      # NatsRouter mixes it with BrokerRouter, a slotted sibling under Registrator
| ^faststream\.nats\.subscriber\.usecases\.basic:LogicSubscriber$
      # ConcurrentCoreSubscriber mixes TasksMixin in beside it; the lay-outs conflict
| ^faststream\.rabbit\.configs\.base:RabbitConfig$
      # mixed into two slotted dataclass configs; the lay-outs conflict
| ^faststream\._internal\.(broker\.(pub_base|registrator)|context|testing)[.:]
      # public objects user code constructs, receives or holds (messages, responses,
      # routers, test clients, context, ASGI, specification schema): slotting them is a
      # breaking change, so they are slotted in the 1.0 follow-up, which removes this
      # entry and the ones below it
| ^faststream\.asgi\.
| ^faststream\.(message\.message|response\.response|params\.no_cast):
| ^faststream\.specification\.schema\.
| ^faststream\.(kafka|confluent|mqtt|nats|rabbit|redis)\.(broker\.router|testing):
| ^faststream\.(kafka|confluent|mqtt|nats|rabbit|redis)\.(opentelemetry|prometheus)\.middleware:\w+Middleware$
| ^faststream\.middlewares\.acknowledgement\.middleware:AcknowledgementMiddleware$
| ^faststream\.(confluent\.configs\.broker:ConsumerBuilder|nats\.schemas\.schedule:Schedule|rabbit\.schemas\.channel:Channel)$
'''

#####################################################################
# Flags for UV compatibility
#####################################################################

[tool.uv]
managed = true
conflicts = [
    [
        { extra = "cu12" },
        { extra = "cu13" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "natten-cu12" },
        { extra = "natten-cu13" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "transformer-engine-cu12" },
        { extra = "transformer-engine-cu13" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "cu12" },
        { extra = "natten-cu13" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "cu12" },
        { extra = "transformer-engine-cu13" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "cu13" },
        { extra = "natten-cu12" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "cu13" },
        { extra = "transformer-engine-cu12" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "natten-cu12" },
        { extra = "transformer-engine-cu13" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "natten-cu13" },
        { extra = "transformer-engine-cu12" },
    ],
]

[tool.uv.extra-build-dependencies]
torch-sparse = ["torch"]
torch-cluster = ["torch"]
torch-scatter = ["torch"]
transformer-engine-torch = [{ requirement = "torch", match-runtime = true }]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "nvidia"
url = "https://pypi.nvidia.com"
explicit = true  # Only use for packages that explicitly specify this index

# Select PyTorch wheels from the same CUDA major version as RAPIDS and CuPy.
# These indexes apply to uv; pip users must select the wheel index explicitly.
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu130"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130"
explicit = true

# PyTorch 2.13 is the newest release with CUDA 12.9 wheels. CUDA 12.9 keeps
# Blackwell kernels and satisfies RAPIDS' nvJitLink>=12.9 requirement; later
# PyTorch releases publish CUDA 12 wheels only for CUDA 12.6, which stops at
# sm_90. Linux only: this index has no Windows wheels.
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu129"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129"
explicit = true

# NATTEN pre-built wheel indexes (flat HTML pages), split by CUDA version AND
# torch version.  The full path is required because natten encodes both CUDA
# and torch versions in local version identifiers (e.g. 0.21.7+torch2130cu126).
# Keep these URLs and the torch pins in the natten extras in sync: the binary
# extensions must use the same PyTorch ABI as the runtime.
# NATTEN publishes no CUDA 12.9 build; its CUDA 12.6 wheels run on the CUDA
# 12.9 PyTorch runtime but contain kernels only through sm_90.
# See https://natten.org/install/ for available builds.
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "natten-cu126-whl"
url = "https://whl.natten.org/cu126/torch2.13.0"
format = "flat"
explicit = true

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "natten-cu130-whl"
url = "https://whl.natten.org/cu130/torch2.13.0"
format = "flat"
explicit = true

[tool.uv.sources]
# When a CUDA 12 extra is active, torch/torchvision come from the CUDA 12.9
# index; with a CUDA 13 extra, they come from the CUDA 13.0 index. The NATTEN
# and Transformer Engine extras select the index too, so their CUDA binaries
# match PyTorch even without cu12/cu13. Every extra listed here must also
# declare torch and torchvision.
# When no CUDA extra is active (bare install), they come from PyPI.
# On macOS, CUDA extras should not be used (no GPU builds available).
torch = [
    { index = "pytorch-cu129", extra = "cu12" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu129", extra = "natten-cu12" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu129", extra = "transformer-engine-cu12" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu130", extra = "cu13" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu130", extra = "natten-cu13" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu130", extra = "transformer-engine-cu13" },
]
torchvision = [
    { index = "pytorch-cu129", extra = "cu12" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu129", extra = "natten-cu12" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu129", extra = "transformer-engine-cu12" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu130", extra = "cu13" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu130", extra = "natten-cu13" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu130", extra = "transformer-engine-cu13" },
]
cuml-cu13 = { index = "nvidia" }
cuml-cu12 = { index = "nvidia" }
pylibraft-cu13 = { index = "nvidia" }
pylibraft-cu12 = { index = "nvidia" }
nvidia-dali-cuda130 = { index = "nvidia" }
nvidia-dali-cuda120 = { index = "nvidia" }
# When natten-cu12 or natten-cu13 extras are active, pull natten from
# the pre-built wheel index instead of building from source via PyPI.
natten = [
    { index = "natten-cu126-whl", extra = "natten-cu12" },
    { index = "natten-cu130-whl", extra = "natten-cu13" },
]

# transformer-engine-torch is an sdist whose setup.py dynamically pins
# transformer_engine_cu{12,13} based on torch.version.cuda in the build
# environment.  Without this override, uv lock freezes whichever CUDA
# variant happened to be in the build env, which broke CI when PyTorch
# 2.12 flipped the PyPI default to cu130 (the cu13 binary then got
# pulled into a CUDA 12.8 runtime, producing missing libcublas.so.13
# errors at import time).  We provide the CUDA-agnostic subset of the
# dependencies here; the matching cuXX binary is pulled by the explicit
# transformer-engine-cu12 / transformer-engine-cu13 extras below.
# Static deps mirror TE 2.19's build_tools/pytorch.py::install_requirements().
[[tool.uv.dependency-metadata]]
name = "transformer-engine-torch"
requires-dist = [
    "torch>=2.1",
    "einops",
    "onnxscript",
    "onnx",
    "packaging",
    "pydantic",
    "nvdlfw-inspect",
    "nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.28.0",
]

#####################################################################

requires = ["hatchling>=1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"


[tool.hatch.version]
path = "physicsnemo/__init__.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["physicsnemo"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
exclude = [

    "/docs",
    "/examples",

]

#####################################################################
# Optional Dependency groups
#####################################################################

# These groups are self-referential.  So, they chain together as you
# move up the physicsnemo hierarchy.  A new extra dep in `physicsnemo/nn`
# will also be an extra dep in `physicsnemo/models`, but not the other
# direction.

[project.optional-dependencies]
# CUDA backend extras (mutually exclusive via [tool.uv] conflicts).
# Combine with feature extras, e.g. nvidia-physicsnemo[nn-extras,cu13].
# When neither is specified, torch comes from PyPI and no RAPIDS
# packages are installed.
cu13 = [
    "torch>=2.13.0",
    "torchvision>=0.28.0",
    "cuml-cu13>=26.8.0",
    "pylibraft-cu13>=26.8.0",
    # RAPIDS' stable Numba 0.64 dependency does not support NumPy 2.5.
    "numpy<2.5",
    # Keep CuPy and PyTorch on the same CUDA major version (cupy/cupy#9827).
    "cupy-cuda13x>=14.2.0",
    "nvidia-dali-cuda130>=2.3.0",
]
cu12 = [
    # PyTorch 2.14+ has no CUDA 12.9 wheels; see the pytorch-cu129 index.
    "torch>=2.13.0,<2.14",
    "torchvision>=0.28.0",
    "cuml-cu12>=26.8.0",
    "pylibraft-cu12>=26.8.0",
    "cupy-cuda12x>=14.2.0",
    "nvidia-dali-cuda120>=2.3.0",
]
# NATTEN pre-built wheel extras (mutually exclusive via [tool.uv] conflicts).
# Pair with the matching CUDA backend extra, e.g.:
#   uv sync --extra cu12 --extra natten-cu12
#   uv sync --extra cu13 --extra natten-cu13
# NATTEN 0.21.7 provides wheels for PyTorch 2.13, but not 2.14 yet.
# Without these extras, install NATTEN separately; see https://natten.org/install/.
natten-cu12 = [

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",

    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Information Analysis",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
]

# Core dependencies (essential for basic functionality)

    # Core scientific computing (lightweight)
    "numpy>=2.0",
    "matplotlib>=3.9.0",  # 3.9.x is the first series compatible with numpy>=2.0
    "networkx>=3.6.1",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    # scipy and scikit-learn moved to ml-ai optional group (all uses are deferred imports)
    # System monitoring and utilities
    "psutil>=5.8.0",
    # HTTP and async communication
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "aiohttp>=3.14.3",  # OpenRouter / Perplexity LLM providers; 3.14.3 patches PYSEC-2026-3545/46/47
    # Pygments: official fix for CVE-2026-4539 (AdlLexer ReDoS) — replaced git fork override
    "pygments>=2.20.0",
    # LLM stack (Step 13+); local Ollama + cloud APIs — defaults in ``llm/defaults.py`` / config
    "openai>=2.0",
    "ollama>=0.1.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.0",
    # Safe XML parsing (replaces stdlib xml.etree/minidom for untrusted input)
    "defusedxml>=0.7.1",
    # Active Inference ecosystem — pymdp 1.0.0 is the JAX-first rewrite
    # (see docs/pymdp/pymdp_1_0_0_alignment_matrix.md). Step 12 uses the new
    # Agent API: list[jax.Array] models, infer_states(empirical_prior=...),
    # infer_policies(qs), sample_action(q_pi, rng_key=...).
    # 1.0.4 is the supported release. It caps jax<0.11.1 pending a numpyro
    # fix, so it resolves on the py3.11 splits (jax 0.9.2); the py>=3.12
    # splits need jax>=0.11.1 for flax>=0.12.9 and ngclearn and stay on 1.0.3
    # until pymdp lifts that cap.
    "inferactively-pymdp>=1.0.4; python_full_version < '3.12'",
    "inferactively-pymdp>=1.0.3; python_full_version >= '3.12'",
    "equinox>=0.11.0",  # pymdp 1.0.0 Agent is an equinox Module
    "multimethod>=1.11",  # pymdp 1.0.0 dispatch
    # Step 12 execution backends (JAX, NumPyro, DisCoPy)
    # PyTorch ships in the dedicated ``torch`` extra: torch>=2.13.0 resolves
    # GHSA-rrmf-rvhw-rf47, lifting the previous lock exclusion. The bnlearn
    # package remains omitted from the default lock because its pgmpy
    # dependency pulls torch transitively.
    # Ceiling raised 0.11 -> 0.12 (2026-09-21) so the ngclearn extra can
    # resolve: ngclearn>=3.2.2 requires jax>=0.11.1. Probe receipts:
    # numpyro 0.22.0 + flax 0.12.x + equinox 0.13.x import on jax 0.11.2
    # (py3.12) and jax 0.10.2 (py3.11). pymdp 1.0.4 pins jax<0.11.1, so the
    # pymdp requirement above takes 1.0.4 on py3.11 and 1.0.3 (no jax upper
    # bound) on the python>=3.12 splits that carry ngclearn.
    "jax[cpu]>=0.7.0,<0.12",
    "jaxlib>=0.7.0,<0.12",
    # flax 0.12.6 calls jax.core.get_opaque_trace_state (removed in jax 0.11.0),
    # so the py>=3.12 splits (which resolve jax 0.11.2 for ngclearn) need
    # flax>=0.12.9 (first release compatible with jax 0.11.x); py3.11 splits
    # keep jax 0.9.2 and stay on flax <0.12.7.
    "flax>=0.7.0,<0.12.7; python_full_version < '3.12'",
    "flax>=0.12.9; python_full_version >= '3.12'",
    "optax>=0.1.0",
    "msgpack>=1.2.1",
    "numpyro>=0.22",  # 0.22.0 carries the jax-0.11.x compat fix; 0.20.x breaks on jax>=0.11
    "discopy>=1.1.0",
    # Interactive visualization (Step 9 advanced viz Plotly dashboards; steps 8/16)
    "pandas>=2.0",
    "plotly>=6.7.0",
    "seaborn>=0.12.0",
    "h5py>=3.8.0",
]

# Optional dependencies. The ``dev`` extra now keeps only genuinely
# optional-dependency test needs (mirroring named extras); universal dev
# tooling lives in the PEP 735 ``[dependency-groups]`` ``dev`` group below,
# installed by default via ``[tool.uv] default-groups``.
[project.optional-dependencies]
geo-infer = ["h3>=4.5.0,<5"]
dev = [
    # Stan executor driver library (same pin as the ``stan`` extra) so the dev

    "cmdstanpy>=1.2",

api = [

    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.23.0",

# Deep learning: transformer/scientific packages beyond core Step 12 backends.

# Import-linter boundaries (S2-33 Step 0, design §4.2 I5). TYPE_CHECKING
# blocks never execute at runtime, so they cannot break the lazy-facade
# invariant and are excluded from the static graph.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "gnn"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

# I1/I2: the ``gnn.utils`` facade stays light — it must not import any of its
# own submodules statically. Resolving re-exports happens at runtime through
# the PEP 562 ``__getattr__`` import map only.
# ``as_packages = false`` is load-bearing: with the default True, the
# forbidden contract skips any (source, forbidden) pair where one module is
# an ancestor of the other (importlinter ForbiddenContract overlap skip), and
# every facade-submodule pair is exactly that — the contract would never be
# able to fail. With False, the source is the exact ``gnn.utils`` module and
# the ``gnn.utils.*`` wildcard expands to every concrete submodule.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "utils facade stays lazy: no static submodule imports"
type = "forbidden"
as_packages = false
source_modules = ["gnn.utils"]
forbidden_modules = ["gnn.utils.*"]
# I5: concern packages must not import the facade (kills accidental cycles).
# Same overlap-skip rationale: every concern package is a descendant of
# ``gnn.utils``, so the default package semantics would skip every pair.
# Sources list each concern package (its own ``__init__``) AND its
# ``.*``-wildcard expansion (its leaf modules) as exact modules.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "concern packages never import the gnn.utils facade"
type = "forbidden"
as_packages = false
source_modules = [
    "gnn.utils.testing", "gnn.utils.testing.*",
    "gnn.utils.arguments", "gnn.utils.arguments.*",
    "gnn.utils.pipeline_orchestration", "gnn.utils.pipeline_orchestration.*",
    "gnn.utils.runtime_safety", "gnn.utils.runtime_safety.*",
    "gnn.utils.observability", "gnn.utils.observability.*",
    "gnn.utils.errors",
    "gnn.utils.config_io",
]
forbidden_modules = ["gnn.utils"]

# I5: the logging single-entry contract (SC-38). Every ``log_step_*`` /
# ``setup_step_logging`` consumer imports through the public
# ``gnn.utils.logging_utils`` entry; the implementation leaf
# ``gnn.utils.logging.logging_utils`` is imported only by the entry facade
# itself and by its own subpackage ``__init__`` (both pre-split tree), so
# those two edges are ignored here. The ``gnn.*`` wildcard expands to every
# concrete gnn module, so each (source, forbidden) pair is a real edge check;
# the default ``as_packages = True`` listing form (source ``gnn``) would be
# overlap-skipped for every pair because the leaf lives inside ``gnn``.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "logging single entry: only gnn.utils.logging_utils (and the gnn.utils.logging package itself) may import the implementation leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["gnn.*"]
forbidden_modules = ["gnn.utils.logging.logging_utils"]
ignore_imports = [
    # Entry facade re-exports the implementation leaf (pre-split tree).
    "gnn.utils.logging_utils -> gnn.utils.logging.logging_utils",
    # The logging subpackage __init__ imports its own leaf (pre-split tree).
    "gnn.utils.logging -> gnn.utils.logging.logging_utils",
]

[project]
name = "cvaugmentor"
version = "2.0.0"
description = "A package for augmenting images and videos for computer vision tasks"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
license = "MIT"
authors = [
    { name = "Ali Khalili Tazehkandgheshlagh", email = "ali.khalili.t98@gmail.com" },
]
keywords = [
    "augmentation",
    "computer-vision",
    "image-processing",
    "video-processing",
    "dataset",
    "clean-architecture",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Multimedia :: Graphics",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Image Processing",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
# NumPy is the compute substrate and Pillow is the codec floor, and both publish wheels
# for every platform this package targets. The accelerators are optional because OpenCV
# publishes none for Windows on ARM or for musl distributions, and a hard requirement
# there turns a pip install into a source build that cannot succeed (see decision 0053).
dependencies = [
    "numpy>=2",
    "pillow>=11",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# The fast paths. OpenCV carries the accelerated operations and ISA-L the accelerated
# deflate; without either, the adapters fall back to NumPy and stdlib zlib and stay correct.
fast = [
    "opencv-python-headless>=4.11",
    "isal>=1.7",
]
# Video has no fallback, because OpenCV is the only video codec here.
video = [
    "opencv-python-headless>=4.11",
]
all = [
    "cvaugmentor[fast,video]",
]

[dependency-groups]
# The accelerators are deliberately absent here. CI installs them for the accelerated job
# and withholds them for the fallback job, so both paths are executed rather than one being
# executed and the other asserted about (see decision 0053).
dev = [
    "hypothesis",
    "pytest",
    "ruff",
    "mypy",
    "import-linter",
]
# The API reference is published, not gated, so its tool is a group of its own rather than
# one more thing every contributor installs to run the suite (see decision 0058).
docs = [
    "pdoc>=15",
]

[project.scripts]
cvaugmentor = "cvaugmentor.facade.cli:main"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/AliKHaliliT/CVAugmentor"
Repository = "https://github.com/AliKHaliliT/CVAugmentor"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/cvaugmentor"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The showcase image is 3.4 MB and the README fetches it from GitHub by absolute URL, as
# the baseline requires of a published README, so shipping it would make the source
# distribution mostly picture for no reader's benefit.
exclude = ["util_resources"]

[tool.isort]
known_first_party = ["cvaugmentor"]
src_paths = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py314"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# The D codes check docstring presence only, never format, because the docstring rhythm is
# the house's own; the shape rules live in the README's Conventions section. PGH keeps every
# ignore honest: a suppression names the exact code it silences, never a blanket.
select = ["E", "F", "B", "UP", "Q", "PGH", "PERF", "C4", "S", "RET504", "D101", "D102", "D103", "D107"]
# The credential heuristics read any suggestive string as a possible secret, so they
# cannot decide their own question and may not gate. They leave the gating selection and
# run as advice instead, through `ruff check --select S105,S106 .`; decision 0025 carries
# the principle and AGENTS.md states what a warning obliges.
ignore = ["E501", "S105", "S106"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]
# A port's stub is a one-line signature; its documentation lives on each implementation.
"src/cvaugmentor/domain/interfaces/*.py" = ["D102"]
# Suites document themselves through case names and assertions (see docs/CONVENTIONS.md).
# A suite asserts for a living, and its fixtures carry throwaway credentials by design.
"tests/**" = ["D101", "D102", "D103", "D107", "S101"]

# import-linter machine-checks the Dependency Rule the same way ESLint carries the client
# style's layer rule. Locating the portions imports the package root once, which the
# library-citizenship rule (no import-time side effects) makes safe; everything after that
# is parsed rather than executed.
[tool.importlinter]
# The layer directories are bare namespace packages by convention, so they are listed as
# portions; a single "cvaugmentor" root would make grimp skip every directory with no __init__.py.
root_packages = [
    "cvaugmentor.adapters",
    "cvaugmentor.core",
    "cvaugmentor.domain",
    "cvaugmentor.facade",
    "cvaugmentor.services",
]
# External packages must be in the graph for a contract to forbid an SDK by name.
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The core stays inside the ports"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["cvaugmentor.domain", "cvaugmentor.services"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "cvaugmentor.facade",
    "cvaugmentor.adapters",
    # Stack binding: this project's imaging and compression libraries, kept out of the core by name.
    "PIL",
    "cv2",
    "numpy",
    "isal",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The Dependency Rule points one way"
type = "layers"
layers = ["cvaugmentor.facade", "cvaugmentor.services", "cvaugmentor.domain"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true
implicit_reexport = true

# Stack binding: this project's two accelerators ship no types.
# Both are optional at runtime and neither ships type information, so the checker is told
# they may be absent rather than every call site carrying an ignore.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["cv2.*", "isal.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# A deprecation warning is a removal notice at least two releases early, so it gates here
# rather than scrolling past unread. Any exception is a named ignore for one specific
# message with a reason beside it, never a blanket.
filterwarnings = ["error"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

name = "The adapter API is reachable without the TUI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "harlequin.adapter",
    "harlequin.autocomplete",
    "harlequin.catalog",
    "harlequin.config",
    "harlequin.crash",
    "harlequin.environment",
    "harlequin.exception",
    "harlequin.keymap",
    "harlequin.navigate",
    "harlequin.options",
    "harlequin.plugins",
    "harlequin.redact",
    "harlequin.ssh",
    "harlequin.transaction_mode",
    "harlequin_duckdb",
    "harlequin_sqlite",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "questionary",
    "textual",
    "textual_fastdatatable",
    "textual_textarea",
    "harlequin.app",
    "harlequin.colors",
    "harlequin.components",
    "harlequin.copy_widgets",
    "harlequin.keys_app",
    "harlequin.messages",
]
# import-linter reads the static graph, so it cannot see that these four are
# deferred into the function that needs them -- but a reader of this list can,
# and every one of them is a deliberate deferral with a comment at the import
# site. Any *new* route to Textual fails the contract instead of joining them.
# `tests/unit_tests/test_import_hygiene.py` is what proves the deferrals hold at
# run time.
ignore_imports = [
    "harlequin.exception -> harlequin.colors",       # pretty_print_warning()
    "harlequin.options -> harlequin.copy_widgets",   # to_widgets()
    "harlequin.options -> harlequin.colors",         # to_questionary()
    "harlequin.options -> questionary",              # to_questionary()
]


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

# The headless execution core, and the two modules that write its results out.
# It may reach `textual_fastdatatable.backend` -- that is where result
# normalization lives, and as of 0.16.1 it costs no Textual -- but nothing here
# may reach Textual itself or any part of the app. `harlequin.export` is in the
# list from both directions: it is what a headless caller writes a file with,
# and it is what the app's export dialog calls, so the dependency has to point
# that way and not back.
name = "The execution core is reachable without the TUI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "harlequin.export",
    "harlequin.layout",
    "harlequin.query",
    "harlequin.query_log",
    "harlequin.statements",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "questionary",
    "textual",
    "textual_textarea",
    "harlequin.app",
    "harlequin.colors",
    "harlequin.components",
    "harlequin.copy_widgets",
    "harlequin.keys_app",
    "harlequin.messages",
]
# the same deliberate deferrals the adapter-API contract lists, each with a
# comment at its import site; `harlequin.query_log` reaches the second three
# through `harlequin.redact`, which reads a profile's option declarations.
# tests/unit_tests/test_import_hygiene.py is what proves they defer.
ignore_imports = [
    "harlequin.exception -> harlequin.colors",       # pretty_print_warning()
    "harlequin.options -> harlequin.copy_widgets",   # to_widgets()
    "harlequin.options -> harlequin.colors",         # to_questionary()
    "harlequin.options -> questionary",              # to_questionary()
]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "error"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

# The whole point of shipping hsql as a second console script rather than a flag
# on `harlequin` is that this becomes a rule CI can check, instead of a
# discipline every contributor has to remember.
name = "hsql does not reach the TUI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["harlequin.hsql"]
# `locale_manager` is not a TUI module, but it is the one trap on this path:
# the IDE calls set_locale() so a human sees grouped digits, and output that
# varied with LC_ALL is output a caller cannot predict. hsql casts through
# duckdb instead, and must never reach the other thing.
forbidden_modules = [
    "questionary",
    "sqlfmt",
    "textual",
    "textual_textarea",
    "harlequin.app",
    "harlequin.cli",
    "harlequin.colors",
    "harlequin.components",
    "harlequin.config_wizard",
    "harlequin.copy_widgets",
    "harlequin.keys_app",
    "harlequin.locale_manager",
    "harlequin.messages",
]
# deferred into pretty_print_warning(), which nothing here calls; the run-time
# test in tests/unit_tests/test_import_hygiene.py is what proves it defers.
# the same deliberate deferrals the adapter-API contract lists, each with a
# comment at its import site. tests/unit_tests/test_import_hygiene.py is what
# proves they defer; a *new* route to Textual fails this contract instead.
ignore_imports = [
    "harlequin.exception -> harlequin.colors",       # pretty_print_warning()
    "harlequin.options -> harlequin.copy_widgets",   # to_widgets()
    "harlequin.options -> harlequin.colors",         # to_questionary()
    "harlequin.options -> questionary",              # to_questionary()
]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "error"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

# A warm session answers in about 20ms, almost all of which is the interpreter
# starting, so the client's import graph is the feature. `click` alone costs
# more than the round trip and `harlequin.config` more again -- so the three
# modules a session client loads reach for stdlib and each other, and nothing
# else. The run-time guards in tests/unit_tests/test_import_hygiene.py are what
# hold the stdlib half of the same rule, by counting modules.
name = "The warm-session client imports nothing it cannot afford"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "harlequin.hsql.client",
    "harlequin.hsql.protocol",
    "harlequin.hsql.session",
]
# `harlequin` covers its every submodule, so a stdlib-only one added later is
# on this list without anyone remembering to add it. The two exceptions are the
# other members of this contract's own source set.
forbidden_modules = [
    "click",
    "msgspec",
    "platformdirs",
    "pyarrow",
    "questionary",
    "textual",
    "textual_fastdatatable",
    "textual_textarea",
    "tomlkit",
    "wcwidth",
    "harlequin",
]
ignore_imports = [
    "harlequin.hsql.client -> harlequin.hsql.protocol",
    "harlequin.hsql.client -> harlequin.hsql.session",
]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "error"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

# Importing any harlequin.* submodule executes this package's __init__, so a
# single eager import there puts the whole TUI behind every consumer. The
# public names are resolved by a PEP 562 __getattr__ instead.
name = "The package root does not import either app"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["harlequin"]
forbidden_modules = ["harlequin.app", "harlequin.keys_app"]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "error"

"""

  "{major}.{minor}.{patch}-{pre_l}{pre_n}",

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter: enforce the trace-server / client import boundaries.
#
# Goal: the trace server (`weave.trace_server`) and the Weave client SDK
# (everything else under `weave`) must not import each other. `weave.shared`
# is the intentional neutral zone that both sides may import, and it imports
# neither. `weave.trace_server` now only holds deprecated aliases for
# `weave.shared`. TODO: drop it from these contracts when the last aliases are
# deleted, which happens together with `weave.shared`.
#
# No contract has an `ignore_imports` list: the direct cross-boundary imports
# are gone. Fix a new violation in the code rather than adding an ignore.
#
# `allow_indirect_imports = true` keeps each contract focused on *direct*
# imports, so every violation maps to a concrete `import` statement to fix.
# The `weave.shared` contract sets it to `false`: both sides import that
# package, so an indirect path out of it couples them just the same.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "weave"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Trace server must not import the Weave client SDK"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["weave.trace_server"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "weave.agent",
  "weave.chat",
  "weave.compat",
  "weave.conversation",
  "weave.dataset",
  "weave.durability",
  "weave.evaluation",
  "weave.flow",
  "weave.initialization",
  "weave.integrations",
  "weave.object",
  "weave.prompt",
  "weave.scorers",
  "weave.session",
  "weave.telemetry",
  "weave.trace",
  "weave.trace_server_bindings",
  "weave.type_handlers",

package org.codefreak.codefreak.arch

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures
import javax.inject.Named
import javax.persistence.ManyToMany
import javax.persistence.OneToMany
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = ["org.codefreak.codefreak"], importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class])
internal class ArchitectureTest {

  @ArchTest
  val `layer dependencies are respected` = Architectures
      .layeredArchitecture()
      .layer("Frontend").definedBy("org.codefreak.codefreak.frontend..", "org.codefreak.codefreak.graphql..")
      .layer("Auth").definedBy("org.codefreak.codefreak.auth..")
      .layer("Service").definedBy("org.codefreak.codefreak.service..")
      .layer("Persistence").definedBy("org.codefreak.codefreak.repository..")
      .layer("Config").definedBy("org.codefreak.codefreak.config..")
      .whereLayer("Frontend").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config")
      .whereLayer("Service").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Frontend", "Auth", "Config")
      .whereLayer("Persistence").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Service", "Auth", "Config")

  @ArchTest
  val `services are named correctly` = ArchRuleDefinition
      .classes()
      .that()
      .areAnnotatedWith(Service::class.java)
      .should()
      .haveNameMatching(".*Service")

  @ArchTest
  val `transactional methods are public` = ArchRuleDefinition
      .methods()
      .that()
      .areAnnotatedWith(Transactional::class.java)
      .should()
      .bePublic()
      .because("@Transactional on non-public methods is silently ignored")

  @ArchTest
  val `if an annotation exists in Spring and in Java, only one of them is used` = ArchRuleDefinition
      .noMethods()
      .should()
      .beAnnotatedWith(javax.transaction.Transactional::class.java)
      .orShould()
      .beAnnotatedWith(Named::class.java)

  @ArchTest
  val `List is not used as type for entity relations` = ArchRuleDefinition
      .noFields()
      .that()
      .areAnnotatedWith(OneToMany::class.java)
      .or()
      .areAnnotatedWith(ManyToMany::class.java)
      .should()
      .haveRawType(List::class.java)
}

readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
keywords = ["ai", "cli", "session", "codex", "claude"]
classifiers = [
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Topic :: Software Development",
]
dependencies = []

[project.scripts]
handoff = "handoff.cli:main"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=9",
    # Gates named in [tool.pytest.ini_options].required_plugins; the ini key
    # makes a missing plugin an error rather than a silently absent gate.
    "pytest-randomly",
    "pytest-timeout",
    "pytest-socket",
    # Module-graph and dependency-declaration gates (hk py-tests-scoped).
    "import-linter",
    "deptry",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/handoff"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = ["src", "tests", "README.md", "PORTING.md"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "9.0"                 # the strict_* ini keys below are unknown on pytest 8
pythonpath = ["src"]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# -ra: skips/xfails/teardown errors reach the summary (never -q here: it hides
# the pytest-randomly seed and the configfile: header). --disable-socket: a
# unit test that opens a socket fails instead of passing on someone's uptime.
addopts = "-ra --disable-socket"
strict_markers = true              # a typo'd mark is a collection error, not a no-op
strict_config = true               # a typo'd ini key is an error, not a warning
strict_xfail = true                # an xfail that passes is a failure, not an X
empty_parameter_set_mark = "fail_at_collect"  # an empty parametrize list fails, not skips
required_plugins = ["pytest-randomly", "pytest-timeout", "pytest-socket"]
timeout = 60                       # a hung test fails with a traceback
timeout_method = "signal"          # the thread method calls os._exit and drops the rest of the run
filterwarnings = [
    "error",                       # first: a forgotten await is only a RuntimeWarning otherwise
    # pytest-socket >= 0.8 warns inside SocketBlockedError.__init__, so under
    # "error" the UserWarning would replace the exception itself.
    "ignore:A test tried to use socket:UserWarning",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["handoff"]
# Cache is not concurrency-safe across parallel hk steps; the wrapper passes
# --no-cache so nothing is written.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "cli -> formats -> ir -> leaves"
type = "layers"
# The leaves (errors, _json, _ids) are independent siblings: `|` means none may
# import another.
layers = [
    "handoff.cli",
    "handoff.formats",
    "handoff.ir",
    "handoff.errors | handoff._json | handoff._ids",
]

[tool.deptry]
# DEP001 missing, DEP002 unused, DEP003 transitive, DEP004 dev dep in runtime code.
# stdlib-only package: every finding is a regression. Must run inside the
# project venv (uv run); a global shim guesses module<->distribution names.
# [dependency-groups] (PEP 735) is read natively, so DEP004 sees the dev group
# without extra keys.
known_first_party = ["handoff"]

# Import layering for the ingestion package — `make check_import_layers`.
#
# Layers run highest to lowest. A module may import its own layer (siblings are joined
# with `:`) or a lower one; importing a higher layer pulls that layer's whole subtree
# into every process below it, which is what makes `import metadata` expensive.
#
# ignore_imports records the imports that break this today, grouped by why. All of them
# are design debt to remove, whether or not they are function-local: deferring an import
# hides its cost, not the dependency. Fix one by guarding it with `if TYPE_CHECKING:` or
# resolving it through metadata.utils.importer — never by adding a line here. Entries that
# stop matching fail the run, so the list only shrinks.
#
# root_packages must list every namespace portion (directory without __init__.py):
# grimp will not find them under `metadata`, and an omitted one is silently unanalysed.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    metadata
    metadata.ingestion
    metadata.data_quality
    metadata.generated
    metadata.workflow
    metadata.applications
    metadata.automations
    metadata.cli
    metadata.clients
    metadata.config
    metadata.mixins
    metadata.models
    metadata.parsers
    metadata.pii
    metadata.readers
    metadata.sampler
    metadata.timer
    metadata.antlr

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Ingestion layers
type = layers
containers =
    metadata
layers =
    workflow : cli : automations : applications : sdk
    ingestion.source
    profiler : data_quality : sampler : pii : readers : parsers : great_expectations : ingestion.api : ingestion.lineage : ingestion.sink : ingestion.stage : ingestion.bulksink : ingestion.processor : ingestion.progress
    entity_resolution
    ingestion.ometa : ingestion.connections : ingestion.diagnostics : core : clients : config : utils : antlr : models : mixins : timer : domain
    generated
ignore_imports =
# Shared helpers that grew upwards: utils, mixins and config reach into the
# framework and into connectors, so importing any of them pulls those in.
    metadata.config.settings -> metadata
    metadata.mixins.pandas.pandas_mixin -> metadata.data_quality.validations.table.pandas.tableRowInsertedCountToBeBetween
    metadata.mixins.pandas.pandas_mixin -> metadata.readers.dataframe.models
    metadata.mixins.sqalchemy.sqa_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.source.connections
    metadata.utils.datalake.datalake_utils -> metadata.ingestion.source.database.column_helpers
    metadata.utils.datalake.datalake_utils -> metadata.parsers.json_schema_parser
    metadata.utils.datalake.datalake_utils -> metadata.readers.dataframe.models
    metadata.utils.datalake.datalake_utils -> metadata.readers.dataframe.reader_factory
    metadata.utils.db_utils -> metadata.ingestion.api.models
    metadata.utils.db_utils -> metadata.ingestion.lineage.models
    metadata.utils.db_utils -> metadata.ingestion.lineage.parser
    metadata.utils.db_utils -> metadata.ingestion.lineage.sql_lineage
    metadata.utils.db_utils -> metadata.ingestion.source.models
    metadata.utils.importer -> metadata.data_quality.validations.base_test_handler
    metadata.utils.importer -> metadata.ingestion.api.steps
    metadata.utils.logger -> metadata.data_quality.api.models
    metadata.utils.logger -> metadata.ingestion.api.models
    metadata.utils.logger -> metadata.ingestion.models.delete_entity
    metadata.utils.logger -> metadata.ingestion.models.life_cycle
    metadata.utils.service_spec.default -> metadata.data_quality.interface.sqlalchemy.sqa_test_suite_interface
    metadata.utils.service_spec.default -> metadata.data_quality.validations.runtime_param_setter.base_diff_params_setter
    metadata.utils.service_spec.default -> metadata.sampler.sqlalchemy.sampler
    metadata.utils.service_spec.service_spec -> metadata.data_quality.interface.test_suite_interface
    metadata.utils.service_spec.service_spec -> metadata.ingestion.api.steps
    metadata.utils.service_spec.service_spec -> metadata.sampler.sampler_interface
    metadata.utils.sqa_utils -> metadata.ingestion.source.database.column_type_parser
    metadata.utils.ssl_manager -> metadata.ingestion.source.connections
    metadata.utils.storage_metadata_config -> metadata.readers.file.config_source_factory
    metadata.utils.tag_utils -> metadata.ingestion.api.models
# The ometa client carries framework and connector types on its mixins, so every
# consumer of the client depends on them.
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.es_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.source.models
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.ingestion_pipeline_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.api.parser
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.lineage_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.lineage.models
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.lineage_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.lineage.parser
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.lineage_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.lineage.sql_lineage
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.patch_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.api.models
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.patch_mixin -> metadata.pii.types
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.patch_mixin -> metadata.sampler.entity_adapters
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.query_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.lineage.masker
    metadata.ingestion.ometa.mixins.user_mixin -> metadata.ingestion.api.common
# Feature packages bind directly to individual connectors instead of resolving them
# through the registry.
    metadata.data_quality.interface.sqlalchemy.unity_catalog.test_suite_interface -> metadata.ingestion.source.database.databricks.connection
    metadata.data_quality.validations.runtime_param_setter.base_diff_params_setter -> metadata.ingestion.source.connections
    metadata.ingestion.connections.test_connections -> metadata.ingestion.source.connections_utils
    metadata.ingestion.sink.metadata_rest -> metadata.ingestion.source.dashboard.dashboard_service
    metadata.ingestion.sink.metadata_rest -> metadata.ingestion.source.database.database_service
    metadata.ingestion.sink.metadata_rest -> metadata.ingestion.source.pipeline.pipeline_service
    metadata.sampler.messaging.kafka.sampler -> metadata.ingestion.source.messaging.kafka.connection
    metadata.sampler.pandas.burstiq.sampler -> metadata.ingestion.source.database.burstiq.client
    metadata.sampler.sqlalchemy.databricks.sampler -> metadata.ingestion.source.database.databricks.connection
    metadata.sampler.sqlalchemy.timescale.sampler -> metadata.ingestion.source.database.timescale.queries
    metadata.sampler.storage.gcs.sampler -> metadata.ingestion.source.storage.gcs.connection
    metadata.sampler.storage.s3.sampler -> metadata.ingestion.source.storage.s3.connection
# metadata.ingestion.models spans layers: custom_pydantic sits below the generated
# models while the rest of the package is framework-level.
    metadata.ingestion.models.custom_basemodel_validation -> metadata.utils.entity_link
    metadata.ingestion.models.custom_pydantic -> metadata.utils.secrets.secrets_manager_factory
    metadata.ingestion.models.patch_request -> metadata.ingestion.api.models
    metadata.ingestion.models.topology -> metadata.ingestion.source.**

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools~=70.3.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

# We will keep handling dependencies in setup.py
# since it helps us organize and isolate version management
[project]
name = "openmetadata-ingestion"
version = "2.0.0.0.dev0"
dynamic = ["readme", "dependencies", "optional-dependencies"]
authors = [
    { name = "OpenMetadata Committers" }
]
license = { file = "LICENSE" }
description = "Ingestion Framework for OpenMetadata"
requires-python = ">=3.10"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://open-metadata.org/"
Documentation = "https://docs.open-metadata.org/"
Source = "https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata"

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
readme = { file = ["README.md"] }

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["./src"]
exclude = ["tests*"]
namespaces = true

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"metadata.examples" = ["workflows/*.yaml"]
"_openmetadata_testutils" = ["data/**/*"]

    "src/metadata",

[tool.coverage.xml]

[tool.coverage.html]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]

    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "xdist_group(name): group tests to run on the same xdist worker"
]

# Skip tests that are known to fail or are not ready to run until issue #21736 is solved

[project.entry-points.pytest11]
pytest_openmetadata = "_openmetadata_testutils.pytest_openmetadata.plugin"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py310"
# Pin source roots so first-party isort detection is stable regardless of
# whether ruff is invoked from the repo root (pre-commit, CI) or from
# `ingestion/` (`make py_format_check`). Each path is listed twice — once
# relative to `ingestion/` (cwd for `make py_format_check`) and once with
# the `ingestion/` prefix (cwd is repo root for pre-commit hooks). Same
# pattern as `extend-exclude` below.
src = [
    "src",
    "ingestion/src",
    "../openmetadata-airflow-apis",
    "openmetadata-airflow-apis",
]
# Each excluded path is listed twice: once relative to the pyproject root
# (cwd = ingestion/) and once with the `ingestion/` prefix (for invocations
# from the repo root, e.g. `make py_format_check`). Without the prefixed form
# ruff's multi-root crawler races on extend-exclude matching and intermittently
# scans the generated/ tree.
extend-exclude = [
    "src/metadata/generated",
    "ingestion/src/metadata/generated",
    "build",
    "ingestion/build",
    "env",
    "ingestion/env",
    "../openmetadata-airflow-apis/build",
    "openmetadata-airflow-apis/build",
]

[tool.ruff.format]
# Black-compatible formatter; defaults match black output.

[tool.ruff.lint]
# ─── Selected rule families ──────────────────────────────────────────────
select = [
    # Style + correctness baseline
    "E",        # pycodestyle errors  — PEP 8 errors (whitespace, indent)
    "W",        # pycodestyle warnings — PEP 8 warnings (deprecated forms)
    "F",        # pyflakes             — unused vars/imports, undefined names
    "I",        # isort                — import grouping/ordering (auto-fix)
    "N",        # pep8-naming          — snake_case / PascalCase (replaces pylint C0103)
    "UP",       # pyupgrade            — modernize syntax for >=3.10

    # Likely-bug catchers
    "B",        # flake8-bugbear       — high-signal bug heuristics
    "C4",       # flake8-comprehensions — rewrite list/dict/set comps cleanly
    "C90",      # mccabe                — cyclomatic complexity cap per function
    "RET",      # flake8-return         — cleanup return-statement logic
    "SIM",      # flake8-simplify       — collapse trivial patterns
    "TRY",      # tryceratops           — better exception handling

    # Hygiene
    "PIE",      # flake8-pie            — small misc cleanups
    "ICN",      # flake8-import-conventions — enforce `import pandas as pd` etc.
    "T20",      # flake8-print          — no print/pprint (replaces print_checker plugin)
    "TC",       # flake8-type-checking  — move type-only imports under TYPE_CHECKING
    "TID",      # flake8-tidy-imports   — relative-import + banned-api (replaces import_checker plugin)
    "PTH",      # flake8-use-pathlib    — prefer pathlib over os.path
    "PERF",     # perflint              — common perf antipatterns

    # Pylint port (split intentionally)
    "PLE",      # pylint Errors         — real error rules from pylint
    "PLC",      # pylint Conventions    — style rules from pylint
    "PLW",      # pylint Warnings       — warning rules from pylint
    "PLR",      # pylint Refactor       — see ignore list for the noisy ones we drop

    # Ruff-specific
    "RUF",      # ruff-native rules     — Astral's own catches (incl. RUF100 unused-noqa)
]

# ─── Ignores: justify EVERY one ──────────────────────────────────────────
ignore = [
    # ── Formatter conflicts: enabling these creates oscillating fixes ──
    "E501",     # line-too-long           — `ruff format` handles wrapping
    "W191",     # tab-indentation         — `ruff format` handles whitespace
    "COM812",   # missing-trailing-comma  — fights with the formatter
    "ISC001",   # implicit-string-concat  — fights with the formatter

    # ── Star imports: real cleanup, separate refactor scope ──
    "F403",     # `from x import *`       — pervasive in connector __init__.py
    "F405",     # may-be-undefined        — cascade of F403; same scope decision

    # ── Bugbear taste calls ──
    "B008",     # function call in default arg — FastAPI/Typer Depends() pattern relies on this

    # ── Pyupgrade taste ──
    "UP015",    # redundant-open-mode     — explicit `open(p, "r")` is a readability call

    # ── RUF nits unsuited to our patterns ──
    "RUF005",   # iterable concat → unpack — Pydantic / SA models read better as concat
    "RUF022",   # `__all__` not sorted     — manual ordering communicates groupings

    # ── Simplify rules that are taste, not bugs ──
    "SIM108",   # use ternary              — often hurts readability for guard clauses
    "SIM114",   # combine-if-branches      — readability is the point of separate branches

    # ── Tryceratops nits ──
    "TRY003",   # long exception messages  — community consensus: skip
    "TRY400",   # use logger.exception over logger.error in except — the
                # codebase intentionally logs `logger.debug(traceback.format_exc())`
                # separately from the summary log line, splitting traceback
                # (debug-only) from the user-facing summary so production
                # log levels can filter independently. Forcing
                # `logger.exception` would conflate the two.

    # ── Perflint unavoidable cases ──
    "PERF203",  # try inside for-loop      — sometimes the only correct shape (row-by-row)

    # ── PLR complexity caps: noisy on connector dispatchers ──
    "PLR0904",  # too-many-public-methods
    "PLR0911",  # too-many-return-statements
    "PLR0912",  # too-many-branches
    "PLR0913",  # too-many-arguments
    "PLR0914",  # too-many-locals
    "PLR0915",  # too-many-statements
    "PLR0916",  # too-many-boolean-expressions
    "PLR0917",  # too-many-positional-arguments

    # ── PLR taste calls ──
    "PLR2004",  # magic-value comparison   — fires on every HTTP status, port number, retry count
    "PLR1711",  # useless-return None      — explicit-is-better-than-implicit defense
    "PLR2044",  # empty-comment            — too pedantic for the value

    # ── Lazy imports are a deliberate tool here, not a smell ──
    "PLC0415",  # import-outside-top-level — function-local imports keep heavy subtrees out
                # of import time; see .importlinter and tests/unit/test_import_cost.py
]

# Existing violations were grandfathered via `ruff check --add-noqa` during
# the pylint→ruff migration. Cleanup follow-up PRs should drop the noqas one
# rule at a time and fix the underlying issues.

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Re-exports are the whole point of __init__; F401/F403 are intended there.
"**/__init__.py" = ["F401", "F403"]
# Tests legitimately use assert; magic numbers and lazy imports are fine in test code.
# Each path listed twice — once relative to `ingestion/` (cwd for `make
# py_format_check`) and once with the `ingestion/` prefix (cwd is repo root
# for pre-commit hooks). Same pattern as `extend-exclude` above.
# `S101` (assert in test) is forward-looking — flake8-bandit (`S`) is not
# yet selected; the rule is no-op today but the entry stays so when `S`
# lands in a later stage tests don't immediately error out.
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC0415"]
"ingestion/tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC0415"]
# v2 CLI E2E framework uses relative imports by design (connector-centric
# layout — connectors live in subdirs and import from `..core.*` / `.connector`).
# `T201` (print) is allowed in the top-level conftest for the session-start
# posture banner. Path listed twice for the dual-cwd pattern above.
"tests/cli_e2e_v2/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC0415", "TID252", "T201"]
"ingestion/tests/cli_e2e_v2/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC0415", "TID252", "T201"]
# Auto-generated from JSON Schema — never edit, never lint.
"src/metadata/generated/**" = ["ALL"]
"ingestion/src/metadata/generated/**" = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = [
    "metadata",
    "ingestion",
    "_openmetadata_testutils",
    "airflow_provider_openmetadata",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Default 10 flags every connector yield_table; 15 is the common compromise.
max-complexity = 15

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Match the pylint config we replaced (max-args=7, max-public-methods=25)
# even though we ignored PLR0913/PLR0904 — devs running ruff-check locally
# still see the limits in any future per-file unignores.
max-args = 7
max-public-methods = 25

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# Banning relative imports keeps absolute paths everywhere (matches existing
# isort + import-checker plugin behaviour).
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
# Direct port of ingestion/plugins/import_checker.py — both prefixes are
# "build artifacts, don't depend on the layout of the source tree". Use
# the `metadata.` package directly.
"ingestion.src.metadata".msg     = "Use `metadata.` imports instead of `ingestion.src.metadata`."
"ingestion.build.lib".msg        = "Don't import build artifacts; use `metadata.` directly."

[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["src"]
stubPath = "stubs"
exclude = [
  "**/__pycache__",
  "src/metadata/generated/*",
  "src/metadata/__version__.py",
]

# Pin the analysis target to the lowest supported Python version so
# basedpyright catches forward-incompatible code (e.g. tomllib usage,
# PEP 695 generics) at type-check time. Runtime support across 3.10/3.11/
# 3.12 is verified separately by the unit-test matrix in py-tests.yml.
# Keep this in sync with `requires-python` above.
pythonVersion = "3.10"

# `standard` is the surveyed-2025-2026 production-default. `recommended`
# (basedpyright's default) enables `reportUnknown*` which is catastrophic
# on a 75-connector codebase with partially-typed third-party deps.
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
# Don't fail CI on warnings; only errors gate. Warnings are signals to
# tighten later via the ratchet plan below.
failOnWarnings = false

# Existing violations are grandfathered via .basedpyright/baseline.json
# (regenerate with `basedpyright -p ingestion/pyproject.toml --writebaseline`
# from the ingestion/ directory). New violations in any file fail CI.

# ── Real-bug catchers held to error ──────────────────────────────────────
# All of these are at `error` in `standard` defaults; restating to document
# intent and prevent a future `typeCheckingMode = "basic"` regression from
# silently dropping them.
reportPossiblyUnboundVariable = "error"
reportOptionalMemberAccess = "error"
reportAttributeAccessIssue = "error"
reportCallIssue = "error"
reportArgumentType = "error"
reportReturnType = "error"
reportAssignmentType = "error"
reportIncompatibleMethodOverride = "error"
reportInvalidTypeArguments = "error"

# ── Cheap promotions: real-bug rules that fire rarely ────────────────────
reportMatchNotExhaustive = "warning"
reportUnreachable = "warning"
reportInvalidCast = "warning"

# ── Stub-gap noise: explicitly off (matches `standard` defaults) ─────────
# These rules are "none" in standard mode by default. Restating them is
# documentation, not behavior change — it just makes the team's stance
# explicit so a future config refactor doesn't accidentally turn them on.
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "warning"
reportUnusedCallResult = "none"
reportImplicitStringConcatenation = "none"    # ruff already handles ISC001 conflict
reportUnannotatedClassAttribute = "none"      # fights with Pydantic patterns

# ── Project-specific waivers ─────────────────────────────────────────────
reportDeprecated = false                      # sqlalchemy 2.x deprecations;
reportMissingTypeStubs = false                # connector deps lack stubs; covered via allowedUntypedLibraries
reportAny = false                             # pandas/SA patterns produce intentional Any
reportExplicitAny = false                     # same
# @override was only added in python 3.12: https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.override
reportImplicitOverride = false                # we're at Python 3.10
# Cross-platform stub drift (macOS arm64 vs Linux x86_64) means a `# pyright: ignore`
# that is necessary on one platform may look unused on the other. Disable the
# unused-ignore warning so contributors can land platform-specific residuals
# without a back-and-forth flap between local and CI.
reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment = false
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = false        # Pydantic, Click, Typer, pytest fixture all trip it
reportPrivateUsage = false
reportImportCycles = false

# ── Allowed untyped libraries: scope Unknown noise to known boundaries ──
# When we ratchet `reportUnknown*` to `warning` later (see executionEnvironments
# scaffold below), these libraries stay silent — keeping focus on our own
# type debt rather than third-party stub gaps.
# Populate when promoting `reportUnknown*` rules to `warning` (see ratchet plan).
allowedUntypedLibraries = []

# ── Ratchet scaffold: enable subtree-by-subtree promotions later ────────
# Empty for now; uncomment + populate as well-typed subtrees are ready.
# Each block holds files under `root` to a stricter rule subset without
# affecting the rest of the codebase.
#
# Example progression:
#
# [[tool.basedpyright.executionEnvironments]]
# root = "src/metadata/data_quality"
# strict = true
#
# [[tool.basedpyright.executionEnvironments]]
# root = "src/metadata/utils"
# reportMissingParameterType = "error"

package io.github.jhipster.sample

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class ArchTest {

    @Test
    fun servicesAndRepositoriesShouldNotDependOnWebLayer() {

        val importedClasses = ClassFileImporter()
            .withImportOption(ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
            .importPackages("io.github.jhipster.sample")

        noClasses()
            .that()
                .resideInAnyPackage("io.github.jhipster.sample.service..")
            .or()
                .resideInAnyPackage("io.github.jhipster.sample.repository..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
                .resideInAnyPackage("..io.github.jhipster.sample.web..")
        .because("Services and repositories should not depend on web layer")
        .check(importedClasses)
    }
}

# Import layering for the ingestion package — `make check_import_layers`.
#
# Layers run highest to lowest. A module may import its own layer (siblings are joined
# with `:`) or a lower one; importing a higher layer pulls that layer's whole subtree
# into every process below it, which is what makes `import metadata` expensive.
#
# ignore_imports records the imports that break this today, grouped by why. All of them
# are design debt to remove, whether or not they are function-local: deferring an import
# hides its cost, not the dependency. Fix one by guarding it with `if TYPE_CHECKING:` or
# resolving it through metadata.utils.importer — never by adding a line here. Entries that
# stop matching fail the run, so the list only shrinks.
#
# root_packages must list every namespace portion (directory without __init__.py):
# grimp will not find them under `metadata`, and an omitted one is silently unanalysed.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    metadata
    metadata.ingestion
    metadata.data_quality
    metadata.generated
    metadata.workflow
    metadata.applications
    metadata.automations
    metadata.cli
    metadata.clients
    metadata.config
    metadata.mixins
    metadata.models
    metadata.parsers
    metadata.pii
    metadata.readers
    metadata.sampler
    metadata.timer
    metadata.antlr

name = Ingestion layers
