[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools~=70.3.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

# We will keep handling dependencies in setup.py
# since it helps us organize and isolate version management
[project]
name = "openmetadata-ingestion"
version = "2.0.0.0.dev0"
dynamic = ["readme", "dependencies", "optional-dependencies"]
authors = [
    { name = "OpenMetadata Committers" }
]
license = { file = "LICENSE" }
description = "Ingestion Framework for OpenMetadata"
requires-python = ">=3.10"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://open-metadata.org/"
Documentation = "https://docs.open-metadata.org/"
Source = "https://github.com/open-metadata/OpenMetadata"

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
readme = { file = ["README.md"] }

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["./src"]
exclude = ["tests*"]
namespaces = true

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"metadata.examples" = ["workflows/*.yaml"]
"_openmetadata_testutils" = ["data/**/*"]
"metadata.data_quality" = ["data/**/*"]

[project.scripts]
metadata = "metadata.cmd:metadata"

[project.entry-points.apache_airflow_provider]
provider_info = "airflow_provider_openmetadata:get_provider_config"

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["metadata"]
relative_files = true
branch = true
parallel = true

# Remap installed-package paths back to the source tree so that
# ``coverage combine`` (in a lightweight CI job without the package
# installed) produces paths that resolve to the checkout.
[tool.coverage.paths]
metadata = [
    "src/metadata",
    "*/site-packages/metadata",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
omit = [
    "*__init__*",
    "*/generated/*",
    "tests/*",
    "ingestion/src/*",
    "*/src/metadata/ingestion/source/database/sample_*"
]

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "ci-coverage.xml"

[tool.coverage.html]
show_contexts = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "xdist_group(name): group tests to run on the same xdist worker"
]

# Skip tests that are known to fail or are not ready to run until issue #21736 is solved
addopts = "--ignore=ingestion/tests/integration/sources/mlmodels/mlflow/test_mlflow.py"
[project.entry-points.pytest11]
pytest_openmetadata = "_openmetadata_testutils.pytest_openmetadata.plugin"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py310"
# Pin source roots so first-party isort detection is stable regardless of
# whether ruff is invoked from the repo root (pre-commit, CI) or from
# `ingestion/` (`make py_format_check`). Each path is listed twice — once
# relative to `ingestion/` (cwd for `make py_format_check`) and once with
# the `ingestion/` prefix (cwd is repo root for pre-commit hooks). Same
# pattern as `extend-exclude` below.
src = [
    "src",
    "ingestion/src",
    "../openmetadata-airflow-apis",
    "openmetadata-airflow-apis",
]
# Each excluded path is listed twice: once relative to the pyproject root
# (cwd = ingestion/) and once with the `ingestion/` prefix (for invocations
# from the repo root, e.g. `make py_format_check`). Without the prefixed form
# ruff's multi-root crawler races on extend-exclude matching and intermittently
# scans the generated/ tree.
extend-exclude = [
    "src/metadata/generated",
    "ingestion/src/metadata/generated",
    "build",
    "ingestion/build",
    "env",
    "ingestion/env",
    "../openmetadata-airflow-apis/build",
    "openmetadata-airflow-apis/build",
]

[tool.ruff.format]
# Black-compatible formatter; defaults match black output.

[tool.ruff.lint]
# ─── Selected rule families ──────────────────────────────────────────────
select = [
    # Style + correctness baseline
    "E",        # pycodestyle errors  — PEP 8 errors (whitespace, indent)
    "W",        # pycodestyle warnings — PEP 8 warnings (deprecated forms)
    "F",        # pyflakes             — unused vars/imports, undefined names
    "I",        # isort                — import grouping/ordering (auto-fix)
    "N",        # pep8-naming          — snake_case / PascalCase (replaces pylint C0103)
    "UP",       # pyupgrade            — modernize syntax for >=3.10

    # Likely-bug catchers
    "B",        # flake8-bugbear       — high-signal bug heuristics
    "C4",       # flake8-comprehensions — rewrite list/dict/set comps cleanly
    "C90",      # mccabe                — cyclomatic complexity cap per function
    "RET",      # flake8-return         — cleanup return-statement logic
    "SIM",      # flake8-simplify       — collapse trivial patterns
    "TRY",      # tryceratops           — better exception handling

    # Hygiene
    "PIE",      # flake8-pie            — small misc cleanups
    "ICN",      # flake8-import-conventions — enforce `import pandas as pd` etc.
    "T20",      # flake8-print          — no print/pprint (replaces print_checker plugin)
    "TC",       # flake8-type-checking  — move type-only imports under TYPE_CHECKING
    "TID",      # flake8-tidy-imports   — relative-import + banned-api (replaces import_checker plugin)
    "PTH",      # flake8-use-pathlib    — prefer pathlib over os.path
    "PERF",     # perflint              — common perf antipatterns

    # Pylint port (split intentionally)
    "PLE",      # pylint Errors         — real error rules from pylint
    "PLC",      # pylint Conventions    — style rules from pylint
    "PLW",      # pylint Warnings       — warning rules from pylint
    "PLR",      # pylint Refactor       — see ignore list for the noisy ones we drop

    # Ruff-specific
    "RUF",      # ruff-native rules     — Astral's own catches (incl. RUF100 unused-noqa)
]

# ─── Ignores: justify EVERY one ──────────────────────────────────────────
ignore = [
    # ── Formatter conflicts: enabling these creates oscillating fixes ──
    "E501",     # line-too-long           — `ruff format` handles wrapping
    "W191",     # tab-indentation         — `ruff format` handles whitespace
    "COM812",   # missing-trailing-comma  — fights with the formatter
    "ISC001",   # implicit-string-concat  — fights with the formatter

    # ── Star imports: real cleanup, separate refactor scope ──
    "F403",     # `from x import *`       — pervasive in connector __init__.py
    "F405",     # may-be-undefined        — cascade of F403; same scope decision

    # ── Bugbear taste calls ──
    "B008",     # function call in default arg — FastAPI/Typer Depends() pattern relies on this

    # ── Pyupgrade taste ──
    "UP015",    # redundant-open-mode     — explicit `open(p, "r")` is a readability call

    # ── RUF nits unsuited to our patterns ──
    "RUF005",   # iterable concat → unpack — Pydantic / SA models read better as concat
    "RUF022",   # `__all__` not sorted     — manual ordering communicates groupings

    # ── Simplify rules that are taste, not bugs ──
    "SIM108",   # use ternary              — often hurts readability for guard clauses
    "SIM114",   # combine-if-branches      — readability is the point of separate branches

    # ── Tryceratops nits ──
    "TRY003",   # long exception messages  — community consensus: skip
    "TRY400",   # use logger.exception over logger.error in except — the
                # codebase intentionally logs `logger.debug(traceback.format_exc())`
                # separately from the summary log line, splitting traceback
                # (debug-only) from the user-facing summary so production
                # log levels can filter independently. Forcing
                # `logger.exception` would conflate the two.

    # ── Perflint unavoidable cases ──
    "PERF203",  # try inside for-loop      — sometimes the only correct shape (row-by-row)

    # ── PLR complexity caps: noisy on connector dispatchers ──
    "PLR0904",  # too-many-public-methods
    "PLR0911",  # too-many-return-statements
    "PLR0912",  # too-many-branches
    "PLR0913",  # too-many-arguments
    "PLR0914",  # too-many-locals
    "PLR0915",  # too-many-statements
    "PLR0916",  # too-many-boolean-expressions
    "PLR0917",  # too-many-positional-arguments

    # ── PLR taste calls ──
    "PLR2004",  # magic-value comparison   — fires on every HTTP status, port number, retry count
    "PLR1711",  # useless-return None      — explicit-is-better-than-implicit defense
    "PLR2044",  # empty-comment            — too pedantic for the value

    # ── Lazy imports are a deliberate tool here, not a smell ──
    "PLC0415",  # import-outside-top-level — function-local imports keep heavy subtrees out
                # of import time; see .importlinter and tests/unit/test_import_cost.py
]

# Existing violations were grandfathered via `ruff check --add-noqa` during
# the pylint→ruff migration. Cleanup follow-up PRs should drop the noqas one
# rule at a time and fix the underlying issues.

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Re-exports are the whole point of __init__; F401/F403 are intended there.
"**/__init__.py" = ["F401", "F403"]
# Tests legitimately use assert; magic numbers and lazy imports are fine in test code.
# Each path listed twice — once relative to `ingestion/` (cwd for `make
# py_format_check`) and once with the `ingestion/` prefix (cwd is repo root
# for pre-commit hooks). Same pattern as `extend-exclude` above.
# `S101` (assert in test) is forward-looking — flake8-bandit (`S`) is not
# yet selected; the rule is no-op today but the entry stays so when `S`
# lands in a later stage tests don't immediately error out.
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC0415"]
"ingestion/tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC0415"]
# v2 CLI E2E framework uses relative imports by design (connector-centric
# layout — connectors live in subdirs and import from `..core.*` / `.connector`).
# `T201` (print) is allowed in the top-level conftest for the session-start
# posture banner. Path listed twice for the dual-cwd pattern above.
"tests/cli_e2e_v2/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC0415", "TID252", "T201"]
"ingestion/tests/cli_e2e_v2/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC0415", "TID252", "T201"]
# Auto-generated from JSON Schema — never edit, never lint.
"src/metadata/generated/**" = ["ALL"]
"ingestion/src/metadata/generated/**" = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = [
    "metadata",
    "ingestion",
    "_openmetadata_testutils",
    "airflow_provider_openmetadata",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Default 10 flags every connector yield_table; 15 is the common compromise.
max-complexity = 15

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Match the pylint config we replaced (max-args=7, max-public-methods=25)
# even though we ignored PLR0913/PLR0904 — devs running ruff-check locally
# still see the limits in any future per-file unignores.
max-args = 7
max-public-methods = 25

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# Banning relative imports keeps absolute paths everywhere (matches existing
# isort + import-checker plugin behaviour).
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
# Direct port of ingestion/plugins/import_checker.py — both prefixes are
# "build artifacts, don't depend on the layout of the source tree". Use
# the `metadata.` package directly.
"ingestion.src.metadata".msg     = "Use `metadata.` imports instead of `ingestion.src.metadata`."
"ingestion.build.lib".msg        = "Don't import build artifacts; use `metadata.` directly."

[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["src"]
stubPath = "stubs"
exclude = [
  "**/__pycache__",
  "src/metadata/generated/*",
  "src/metadata/__version__.py",
]

# Pin the analysis target to the lowest supported Python version so
# basedpyright catches forward-incompatible code (e.g. tomllib usage,
# PEP 695 generics) at type-check time. Runtime support across 3.10/3.11/
# 3.12 is verified separately by the unit-test matrix in py-tests.yml.
# Keep this in sync with `requires-python` above.
pythonVersion = "3.10"

# `standard` is the surveyed-2025-2026 production-default. `recommended`
# (basedpyright's default) enables `reportUnknown*` which is catastrophic
# on a 75-connector codebase with partially-typed third-party deps.
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
# Don't fail CI on warnings; only errors gate. Warnings are signals to
# tighten later via the ratchet plan below.
failOnWarnings = false

# Existing violations are grandfathered via .basedpyright/baseline.json
# (regenerate with `basedpyright -p ingestion/pyproject.toml --writebaseline`
# from the ingestion/ directory). New violations in any file fail CI.

# ── Real-bug catchers held to error ──────────────────────────────────────
# All of these are at `error` in `standard` defaults; restating to document
# intent and prevent a future `typeCheckingMode = "basic"` regression from
# silently dropping them.
reportPossiblyUnboundVariable = "error"
reportOptionalMemberAccess = "error"
reportAttributeAccessIssue = "error"
reportCallIssue = "error"
reportArgumentType = "error"
reportReturnType = "error"
reportAssignmentType = "error"
reportIncompatibleMethodOverride = "error"
reportInvalidTypeArguments = "error"

# ── Cheap promotions: real-bug rules that fire rarely ────────────────────
reportMatchNotExhaustive = "warning"
reportUnreachable = "warning"
reportInvalidCast = "warning"

# ── Stub-gap noise: explicitly off (matches `standard` defaults) ─────────
# These rules are "none" in standard mode by default. Restating them is
# documentation, not behavior change — it just makes the team's stance
# explicit so a future config refactor doesn't accidentally turn them on.
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "warning"
reportUnusedCallResult = "none"
reportImplicitStringConcatenation = "none"    # ruff already handles ISC001 conflict
reportUnannotatedClassAttribute = "none"      # fights with Pydantic patterns

# ── Project-specific waivers ─────────────────────────────────────────────
reportDeprecated = false                      # sqlalchemy 2.x deprecations;
reportMissingTypeStubs = false                # connector deps lack stubs; covered via allowedUntypedLibraries
reportAny = false                             # pandas/SA patterns produce intentional Any
reportExplicitAny = false                     # same
# @override was only added in python 3.12: https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.override
reportImplicitOverride = false                # we're at Python 3.10
# Cross-platform stub drift (macOS arm64 vs Linux x86_64) means a `# pyright: ignore`
# that is necessary on one platform may look unused on the other. Disable the
# unused-ignore warning so contributors can land platform-specific residuals
# without a back-and-forth flap between local and CI.
reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment = false
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = false        # Pydantic, Click, Typer, pytest fixture all trip it
reportPrivateUsage = false
reportImportCycles = false

# ── Allowed untyped libraries: scope Unknown noise to known boundaries ──
# When we ratchet `reportUnknown*` to `warning` later (see executionEnvironments
# scaffold below), these libraries stay silent — keeping focus on our own
# type debt rather than third-party stub gaps.
# Populate when promoting `reportUnknown*` rules to `warning` (see ratchet plan).
allowedUntypedLibraries = []

# ── Ratchet scaffold: enable subtree-by-subtree promotions later ────────
# Empty for now; uncomment + populate as well-typed subtrees are ready.
# Each block holds files under `root` to a stricter rule subset without
# affecting the rest of the codebase.
#
# Example progression:
#
# [[tool.basedpyright.executionEnvironments]]
# root = "src/metadata/data_quality"
# strict = true
#
# [[tool.basedpyright.executionEnvironments]]
# root = "src/metadata/utils"
# reportMissingParameterType = "error"

package no.nav.eessi.pensjon.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noMethods
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition.slices
import no.nav.eessi.pensjon.EessiPensjonJournalforingApplication
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestInstance


@TestInstance(TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)
internal class ArchitectureTest {

    private val root = EessiPensjonJournalforingApplication::class.qualifiedName!!
            .replace("." + EessiPensjonJournalforingApplication::class.simpleName, "")

    // Only include main module. Ignore test module and external deps
    private val classesToAnalyze = ClassFileImporter()
        .withImportOptions(listOf(
            ImportOption.DoNotIncludeJars(),
            ImportOption.DoNotIncludeArchives(),
            ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests())
        ).importPackages(root)

    @BeforeAll
    fun beforeAll() {
        // Validate number of classes to analyze
        assertTrue(classesToAnalyze.size in 100..250, "Sanity check on no. of classes to analyze (is ${classesToAnalyze.size})")
    }

    @Test
    fun `Packages should not have cyclic depenedencies`() {
        slices().matching("$root.(*)..").should().beFreeOfCycles().check(classesToAnalyze)
    }

    @Test
    fun `Check architecture`() {
        val root = "journalforing"

        // Root packages
        val eux = "eux"
        val config = "config"
        val listeners = "listeners"
        val oppgaveRouting = "journalforing bestemenhet"

        // Sub packages
        val pdf = "journalforing pdf"
        val pesysKlient = "listener pesys"
        val journalforing = "journalforing"
        val fagmodulKlient = "listener fagmodul"
        val journalpostKlient = "journalforing journalpost"
        val personidentifisering = "personidentifisering"
        val personidentifiseringHelpers = "personidentifisering helpers"

        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringOnlyDependenciesInAnyPackage(this.root)
                //Define components
                .layer(root).definedBy(this.root)
                .layer(eux).definedBy("${this.root}.eux")
                .layer(config).definedBy("${this.root}.config")
                .layer(journalforing).definedBy("${this.root}.journalforing")
                .layer(listeners).definedBy("${this.root}.listeners")
                .layer(oppgaveRouting).definedBy("${this.root}.journalforing.bestemenhet")
                .layer(pdf).definedBy("${this.root}.journalforing.pdf")
                .layer(fagmodulKlient).definedBy("${this.root}.listeners.fagmodul")
                .layer(journalpostKlient).definedBy("${this.root}.journalforing.journalpost")
                .layer(pesysKlient).definedBy("${this.root}.listeners.pesys")
                .layer(personidentifisering).definedBy("${this.root}.personidentifisering")
                .layer(personidentifiseringHelpers).definedBy("${this.root}.personidentifisering.helpers")
                //define rules
                .whereLayer(root).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
                .whereLayer(eux).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(listeners, journalforing, pdf) // Sed
                .whereLayer(config).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
                .whereLayer(journalforing).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(listeners)
                .whereLayer(listeners).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(root)
                .whereLayer(oppgaveRouting).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(journalforing)
                .whereLayer(pdf).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(journalforing)
                .whereLayer(fagmodulKlient).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(journalforing, eux, personidentifiseringHelpers)
                .whereLayer(journalpostKlient).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(journalforing)
                .whereLayer(pesysKlient).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(journalforing, listeners, oppgaveRouting)
                //Verify rules
                .check(classesToAnalyze)
    }

    @Test
    fun `avoid JUnit4-classes`() {
        val junitReason = "We use JUnit5 (but had to include JUnit4 because spring-kafka-test needs it to compile)"

        noClasses()
                .should()
                .dependOnClassesThat()
                .resideInAnyPackage(
                        "org.junit",
                        "org.junit.runners",
                        "org.junit.experimental..",
                        "org.junit.function",
                        "org.junit.matchers",
                        "org.junit.rules",
                        "org.junit.runner..",
                        "org.junit.validator",
                        "junit.framework.."
                ).because(junitReason)
                .check(classesToAnalyze)

        noClasses()
                .should()
                .beAnnotatedWith("org.junit.runner.RunWith")
                .because(junitReason)
                .check(classesToAnalyze)

        noMethods()
                .should()
                .beAnnotatedWith("org.junit.Test")
                .orShould().beAnnotatedWith("org.junit.Ignore")
                .because(junitReason)
                .check(classesToAnalyze)
    }
}

        # that dotted name in the measured process. _ioc.py/_tango_device_servers.py
        # (ophyd_async.epics/tango .testing/.demo) are deliberately run *by file
        # path* as standalone subprocess scripts - see their own docstrings - so
        # they load as `__main__`, not under their ophyd_async.* name, and the
        # package-name source spec alone can never match them. Path-based source
        # matches by file location instead, so it isn't fooled by that.
        "--cov=src",
        "--cov-report",
        "term",
        "--cov-report",
        "xml:cov.xml",
        { replace = "posargs", default = [
        ], extend = true },
    ],
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
lint.select = [

    "C4",      # flake8-comprehensions - https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#flake8-comprehensions-c4

]

]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# By default, private member access is allowed in tests

"tests/**/*" = ["SLF001", "S101", "D"]
"src/ophyd_async/testing/**/*" = ["SLF001", "S101"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "ophyd_async"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "All runtime modules are in layers"
type = "layers"
containers = ["ophyd_async"]
layers = ["fastcs", "epics | tango | sim", "plan_stubs", "core"]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = ["testing", "_version", "__main__", "_docs_parser"]

[build-system]

requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]

build-backend = "hatchling.build"


[tool.uv]
add-bounds = "exact"
cache-keys = [
  { file = "pyproject.toml" },
  { git = { commit = true, tags = true } },
]
package = true
trusted-publishing = "always"


[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# Last-resort sentinel: only used when a build sees neither a .git directory nor
# an expanded .git_archival.txt (e.g. an archive of a commit with no reachable
# tag). "0.0.0" reads clearly as "version could not be determined" rather than
# masquerading as a real early release. See .git_archival.txt + .gitattributes
# `export-subst` for the archive path that recovers the real tag-derived version.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"


[tool.hatch.build]
hooks.vcs.version-file = "src/chrome_version/_version.py"


[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "only-version"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true


[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The package uses a src layout, so the source tree lives under /src (not
# /chrome_version); including /src ships the actual modules -- and, for
# C-extension projects, the .pyx/.pxd sources needed to compile from the sdist.
include = ["/README.md", "LICENSE", "/src", "/tests"]


[tool.commitizen]
# Commit-authoring and message linting only. release-please owns version
# bumping, git tagging, and CHANGELOG.md (see .github/release-please-config.json),
# so the bump/tag/changelog settings are intentionally omitted here to avoid two
# tools competing over the same tags and changelog file.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# addopts = "-rXs --strict-config --strict-markers"
addopts = "-v --tb=short"
asyncio_mode = "auto"
filterwarnings = ["error"]
testpaths = ["tests"]
xfail_strict = true


[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
# Match `_version.py` wherever it resolves: `src/...` in editable dev installs and
# `.../site-packages/...` when tox/CI installs the built wheel or sdist. A
# `src/**`-only pattern silently misses the installed copy and reports it at 0%.
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
parallel = true
source_pkgs = ["chrome_version", "tests"]


[tool.coverage.paths]
# Unify coverage data across environments. tox installs the built wheel/sdist into
# each env's site-packages, so the same source file is measured under a different
# `.tox/<env>/.../site-packages/chrome_version` path per interpreter. Without
# remapping those back to the canonical `src/` tree, `coverage combine` keeps a
# separate copy per env and a version-gated line covered in one interpreter but not
# another is wrongly counted as missed — silently failing the `fail_under` gate.
# `tests` needs no remapping: it is never installed, so every environment measures
# it at the same repo-local path.
chrome_version = ["src/chrome_version", "*/site-packages/chrome_version"]


[tool.coverage.report]
# Untestable code is excluded per site with `# pragma: no cover`, not with blanket
# patterns here: a regex matching a `def` line excludes the *whole function body*,
# so a pattern like `def main\(` would silently un-measure any future `main()`
# with real logic (and did mask the tested GUI/TUI entrypoints). Pragmas carry the
# exclusion decision next to the code it affects. See ADR-008.
exclude_lines = ["no cov", "if __name__ == .__main__.:", "if TYPE_CHECKING:"]
fail_under = 99
# Patterns match both the `src/` (editable) and installed (`site-packages`)
# layouts (see [tool.coverage.run] omit).
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true


[tool.vulture]
# Framework-invoked handlers: Typer commands, FastAPI routes, FastStream
# lifecycle hooks, and the MCP tool dispatcher.
ignore_decorators = [
  "@app.command",
  "@app.get",
  "@app.after_startup",
  "@app.after_shutdown",
  "@server.call_tool",
]
# Public API surfaces vulture cannot see being used: ``main`` entry points are
# referenced only via pyproject scripts, ``model_config`` is consumed by
# pydantic-settings, ``logger`` is imported only by optional components, the MCP
# ``arguments`` parameter is mandated by the call_tool signature, the Textual
# names (CSS/compose/on_mount/title/BINDINGS) are invoked by the TUI framework,
# and ``pytestmark`` is consumed by pytest at collection time.
ignore_names = ["CONFIG_FILE_PATH", "logger", "main", "model_config"]
min_confidence = 60
paths = ["src", "tests"]


[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "chrome_version"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture"
type = "layers"
# Layers are listed high -> low: a layer may import lower layers but never a
# higher one. `cli` is the entrypoint layer (the ``chrome-version`` console
# script) and depends on `core`, the pure Chrome-detection logic; `core` must
# never import `cli`.
layers = ["chrome_version.cli", "chrome_version.core"]


[tool.ruff]
fix = true
output-format = "full"
preview = true
show-fixes = true
src = ["src", "tests", "examples"]
target-version = "py310"
unsafe-fixes = true


[tool.ruff.analyze]
detect-string-imports = true
preview = true


[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true
line-ending = "lf"
preview = true
skip-magic-trailing-comma = true


[tool.ruff.lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
# Two opinionated ruff 0.16 preview rules are disabled: RUF105 would rewrite the
# portable `# noqa` comments into ruff's own `# ruff: ignore` syntax (its docs note
# `# noqa` is needed for cross-tool compatibility), and RUF201 would rewrite every
# rule *code* in this config's selectors into long rule *names*. Both are stylistic.
ignore = ["COM812", "CPY", "FIX", "RUF105", "RUF201", "TD"]
logger-objects = ["logging_setup.logger"]
preview = true
select = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
# skip-magic-trailing-comma = true
split-on-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-copyright]
author = "Hasan Sezer Taşan <hasansezertasan@gmail.com>"


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"


[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 5


[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
ignore-overlong-task-comments = true


[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"


[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Recursive glob so nested test packages (tests/cli, tests/gui, ...) are covered.
# Tests legitimately use asserts/magic values, reach into package internals, and
# don't need return-value documentation on their fixtures and helpers.
# Tests also import `subprocess` (S404) to construct/assert on CalledProcessError.
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC2701", "DOC201", "S404"]
# Standalone example scripts: not an importable package (INP001) and they print
# their results to stdout by design (T201).
"examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001", "T201"]
# The Sphinx config is a standalone module, not part of an importable package.
"docs/conf.py" = ["INP001"]
# The console script deliberately writes results to stdout/stderr with print().
"src/chrome_version/cli.py" = ["T201"]
# Chrome detection shells out to the OS: `reg query` on Windows and the Chrome
# binary's `--version` on Linux/macOS, invoked via argv lists without a shell
# (S404/S603). The per-platform branching is inherent to the detection strategy,
# so the mccabe complexity ceiling (C901) is relaxed for this module.
"src/chrome_version/core.py" = ["C901", "S404", "S603"]


[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true


[tool.ruff.lint.ruff]
parenthesize-tuple-in-subscript = true


[tool.mypy]
files = ["src"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true


[tool.basedpyright]
exclude = [".venv"]
include = ["src/chrome_version"]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
venv = ".venv"
# venvPath is the directory *containing* the venv, not the venv itself; ".venv"
# here would make basedpyright look for ".venv/.venv". Use "." so both the venv
# and basedpyright's strict ruleset resolve the project's installed deps.
venvPath = "."


[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "tests"]
respect-ignore-files = false


[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.10"


[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true


[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.10"
project-includes = ["src"]

[tool.pylint.main]
# pylint runs as an always-on gate that deliberately overlaps ruff's PL* rules.
# Its canonical invocation is `pylint src`, so it never descends into tests; this
# ignore-paths is a defensive scope guard for broader invocations (`pylint .`,
# filename-passing hooks). Tests are linted by ruff, not pylint.
ignore-paths = ["^tests/.*$"]
# `.pyi` stubs (the c-extension type stub) are signature-only: their bodies are
# `...` and every parameter is unused by construction, so pylint's unused-argument
# check is a guaranteed false positive there. Stubs are type-checked by the
# type-checker gate, not pylint.
ignore-patterns = ['.*\.pyi$']

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
# Only formatter-owned checks, the docstring family, and too-few-public-methods
# are disabled so pylint is usable out of the box; everything else stays on.
disable = [
  "line-too-long",              # C0301 — ruff-format owns line length
  "missing-module-docstring",   # C0114
  "missing-class-docstring",    # C0115
  "missing-function-docstring", # C0116
  "too-few-public-methods",     # R0903 — trips dataclasses / config / Protocol classes
  "import-outside-toplevel",    # C0415 — components (cli->tui/gui/web, and each
  # component's own optional-dependency probe) are
  # deliberately lazy-imported so import-linter's
  # layering contract holds and optional extras
  # aren't required at import time.
  "try-except-raise", # W0706 — the generated TUI entry point
  # explicitly re-raises KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit
  # ahead of a broad `except Exception` to make the
  # "let these propagate" intent obvious to readers,
  # even though BaseException subclasses wouldn't be
  # caught by the Exception clause anyway.
  "duplicate-code", # R0801 — the component skeletons (gui/tui/mcp/
  # worker) are deliberately parallel: each fetches
  # package metadata and formats the same info block
  # the same way. That structural symmetry is a
  # feature of the scaffold, not copy-paste debt, and
  # R0801 cannot be suppressed inline at the call site.
]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10
max-positional-arguments = 10
max-branches = 20

[tool.tox]
# Python 3.15 is advertised (see the trove classifier) and exercised via
# `tox run -e 3.15`, but it is deliberately kept OUT of this blocking env_list
# while 3.15 is a prerelease: CI runs it as a separate non-blocking leg (see the
# `ci-prerelease` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml) so a prerelease regression
# never blocks a merge. Fold 3.15 into env_list once it reaches a stable release.
env_list = ["style", "3.14", "3.13", "3.12", "3.11", "3.10"]
requires = ["tox>=4"]


[tool.tox.env_run_base]
commands = [
  [
    "coverage",
    "run",
    "--module",
    "pytest",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
constrain_package_deps = true
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the tests under {base_python}"
env_tmp_dir = "{toxworkdir}/tmp/{envname}"
# Arms coverage-enable-subprocess so xdist/subprocess workers are measured too;
# `coverage run` plus `parallel = true` writes per-env data files that the CI
# `coverage combine` step merges.
set_env = { COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = "{tox_root}/pyproject.toml" }
extras = ["all"]

package = "wheel"

runner = "uv-venv-runner"
use_frozen_constraints = true
wheel_build_env = ".pkg"


[tool.tox.env.style]
base_python = ["3.10"]
commands = [
  ["ruff", "check", "--no-fix"],
  ["ruff", "format", "--check", "--diff"],
  ["mypy", "--python-version", "3.10"],
  ["mypy", "--python-version", "3.14"],
  ["basedpyright"],
  ["ty", "check"],
  ["pyrefly", "check"],
  ["zuban", "check", "src"],
  ["pylint", "src"],
  ["python", "-m", "slotscheck", "src"],
  ["lint-imports"],
  ["taplo", "lint", "*.toml"],
  # NOTE: kept in fix mode (not `--check`) because the rendered TOML is not yet
  # guaranteed taplo-formatted across every component combination. The `*.toml`
  # glob is non-recursive, so it scopes taplo to this project's own root TOML
  # (pyproject/prek/mise) without walking vendored `.tox`/`.venv`/site-packages
  # trees — no `.taplo.toml` exclude config needed. Making this a strict
  # `--check` gate is a follow-up that first requires the generated
  # pyproject/prek to be clean.
  ["taplo", "format", "*.toml"],
  ["typos", "--diff"],
  ["ec"],
  ["sphinx-lint", "docs"],
]
# `test` is included so the type checkers that scope tests (e.g. ty) can
# resolve pytest and other test-only imports.
dependency_groups = ["style", "test"]
description = "Run Checkers, Linters and Formatters"
# Optional components (web/gui/tui/mcp/worker) are only importable when their
# extra is installed; without this, pylint/mypy/etc. see import-error for any
# optional component present in this render.
extras = ["all"]
runner = "uv-venv-runner"


[tool.tox.env.prek]
commands = [["prek", "run", "--all-files"]]
dependency_groups = ["prek"]
description = "Run prek hooks"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-build]
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "html", "docs", "docs/_build/html"]]
extras = ["all"]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Build Docs"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-server]
commands = [["sphinx-autobuild", "docs", "docs/_build/html"]]
extras = ["all"]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Start the live-reloading docs server"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-linkcheck]
# On-demand link checker. Also run weekly (non-blocking) by docs-linkcheck.yml.
# Hits the network, so it is deliberately not part of the `style` env or PR CI.
commands = [
  [
    "sphinx-build",
    "-b",
    "linkcheck",
    "docs",
    "docs/_build/linkcheck",
  ],
]
extras = ["all"]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Check documentation for broken links"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"

[importlinter]
root_package = blast_furnace
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Presentation depends on application and domain
type = layers
layers =
    blast_furnace.presentation
    blast_furnace.application
    blast_furnace.domain

[importlinter:contract:inner]
name = Inner layers are framework independent

[build-system]

requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]

build-backend = "hatchling.build"


[tool.uv]
add-bounds = "exact"
cache-keys = [
  { file = "pyproject.toml" },
  { git = { commit = true, tags = true } },
]
package = true
trusted-publishing = "always"

[tool.uv.dependency-groups]
# Docs only ever build on the `.python-version` interpreter, never across the
# test matrix, so the group need not resolve down to the project's 3.10 floor.
# Without this the universal lock pins Sphinx and its extensions to the last
# releases that still support 3.10, and every Renovate bump past them fails
# with an unresolvable lock. 3.12 is the floor Sphinx 9.1 requires.
docs = { requires-python = ">=3.12" }


[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# Last-resort sentinel: only used when a build sees neither a .git directory nor
# an expanded .git_archival.txt (e.g. an archive of a commit with no reachable
# tag). "0.0.0" reads clearly as "version could not be determined" rather than
# masquerading as a real early release. See .git_archival.txt + .gitattributes
# `export-subst` for the archive path that recovers the real tag-derived version.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"


[tool.hatch.build]
hooks.vcs.version-file = "src/hwid/_version.py"


[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "only-version"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true


[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The package uses a src layout, so the source tree lives under /src (not
# /hwid); including /src ships the actual modules -- and, for
# C-extension projects, the .pyx/.pxd sources needed to compile from the sdist.
include = [
  "/README.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "/src",
  "/tests",
  "/docs/examples",
]


[tool.commitizen]
# Commit-authoring and message linting only. release-please owns version
# bumping, git tagging, and CHANGELOG.md (see .github/release-please-config.json),
# so the bump/tag/changelog settings are intentionally omitted here to avoid two
# tools competing over the same tags and changelog file.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# addopts = "-rXs --strict-config --strict-markers"
addopts = "-v --tb=short --doctest-glob=README.md"
# One marker per component, auto-applied by tests/conftest.py from each test's
# top-level tests/<dir>/. Enables `pytest -m web` locally and per-component CI
# jobs (issue #160, https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#per-component-markers-path-filtered-jobs-and-one-coverage-gate-per-component); `integration` (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/testing-strategy/#real-broker-integration-tests-testcontainers-locally-per-broker-ci-mechanism) is one axis of the scheme.
markers = [
  "core: core/shared component tests",
  "cli: CLI component tests",
]
filterwarnings = [
  "error",
]
# The project README is the deliberately small Markdown doctest surface. Other
# Markdown files can use illustrative snippets without becoming pytest inputs.
testpaths = ["tests", "README.md"]
doctest_optionflags = "ELLIPSIS IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"
xfail_strict = true


[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
# Match `_version.py` wherever it resolves: `src/...` in editable dev installs and
# `.../site-packages/...` when tox/CI installs the built (non-editable) wheel. A
# `src/**`-only pattern silently misses the installed copy and reports it at 0%.
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
parallel = true
# Store data-file paths relative to the project root so `.coverage` files produced
# on different runners/OSes merge in the `coverage-combine` CI job without
# absolute-path mismatches. Complements the `[tool.coverage.paths]` remap below
# (which unifies the src/ vs site-packages layouts). See https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#a-single-union-coverage-gate-across-the-whole-matrix.
relative_files = true
source_pkgs = ["hwid", "tests"]


[tool.coverage.paths]
# Unify coverage data across environments. tox installs the built wheel into
# each env's site-packages, so the same source file is measured under a different
# `.tox/<env>/.../site-packages/hwid` path per interpreter. Without
# remapping those back to the canonical `src/` tree, `coverage combine` keeps a
# separate copy per env and a version-gated line covered in one interpreter but not
# another is wrongly counted as missed — silently failing the `fail_under` gate.
# `tests` needs no remapping: it is never installed, so every environment measures
# it at the same repo-local path.
hwid = ["src/hwid", "*/site-packages/hwid"]


[tool.coverage.report]
# Untestable code is excluded per site with `# pragma: no cover`, not with blanket
# patterns here: a regex matching a `def` line excludes the *whole function body*,
# so a pattern like `def main\(` would silently un-measure any future `main()`
# with real logic (and did mask the tested GUI/TUI entrypoints). Pragmas carry the
# exclusion decision next to the code it affects. See ADR-008.
exclude_lines = ["no cov", "if __name__ == .__main__.:", "if TYPE_CHECKING:"]
fail_under = 99
# Patterns match both the `src/` (editable) and installed (`site-packages`)
# layouts (see [tool.coverage.run] omit).
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true


[tool.vulture]
# Framework-invoked handlers: Typer commands, FastAPI routes, FastStream
# lifecycle hooks, and the MCP tool dispatcher.
ignore_decorators = [
  "@app.command",
  "@app.get",
  "@app.after_startup",
  "@app.after_shutdown",
  "@server.call_tool",
  # A fixture used through ``@pytest.mark.usefixtures("name")`` -- or from
  # another test module -- is only ever named in a string, which vulture cannot
  # see. Unused fixtures are caught properly by ``pytest --dead-fixtures`` in
  # the tox ``style`` env, so this delegates rather than suppresses.
  "@pytest.fixture",
]
# Public API surfaces vulture cannot see being used: ``main`` entry points are
# referenced only via pyproject scripts, ``model_config`` is consumed by
# pydantic-settings, ``logger`` is imported only by optional components, the MCP
# ``arguments`` parameter is mandated by the call_tool signature, the Textual
# names (CSS/compose/on_mount/title/BINDINGS) are invoked by the TUI framework,
# and ``pytestmark``/``pytest_*`` (conftest hooks) are consumed by pytest at
# collection time.
ignore_names = ["CONFIG_FILE_PATH", "logger", "main", "model_config", "pytest_*", "collect_ignore_glob"]
min_confidence = 60
paths = ["src", "tests"]


[tool.deptry]
# `known_first_party` is explicit because the tox `deps` env installs the built
# wheel, so without it deptry reads the project's own imports as a third-party
# transitive dependency (DEP003). Add further `per_rule_ignores` entries for the
# project's own findings, e.g. DEP003 for a package only importable through
# another declared one, or DEP002 for an optional import guarded by try/except.
# See https://deptry.com/rules-violations/.
# Excluded: the Sphinx config, the build hook (its imports belong to
# `[build-system].requires`, not the runtime dependencies), the benchmarks and the
# worker probe script (neither ships in the wheel; pytest and anyio come from
# the dev tooling).
extend_exclude = [
  "docs/conf.py",
  # Standalone Poetry demo projects with their own manifests; they do not ship in
  # the wheel, so their imports (typer) are not this project's dependencies.
  "examples",
]
known_first_party = ["hwid"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# tools/build_docs.py imports `packaging`, pinned in the `docs` group for that
# script alone, so deptry reads it as a misplaced dev dependency.
DEP004 = ["packaging"]


[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "hwid"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture with independent components"
type = "layers"
# Layers are listed high -> low: a layer may import lower layers but never a
# higher one. Modules joined by ` | ` on one line are independent SIBLINGS that
# may not import each other. `cli` is the orchestrator layer — the
# `hwid` console root, whose subcommands launch the other
# components (web/gui/tui/mcp/worker) via lazy imports — so it sits ABOVE the
# independent component group, which sits above `core`, which sits above the leaf
# `utils`.
#
# `exhaustive` makes the contract fail when a subpackage of
# `hwid` is not named in `layers` — so a new top-level
# subpackage is a deliberate architecture decision (add it to a layer here)
# rather than something that silently accretes at the package root. Feature code
# belongs inside an existing layer; see "Package structure" in `AGENTS.md`. The
# `exhaustive_ignores` entries are the non-layer foundations: the metadata and
# hatch-vcs version modules and the `python -m` dispatcher.
containers = ["hwid"]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = [
  "__main__",
  "__metadata__",
  "_version",
]
layers = [
  "cli",
  "core",
  "utils",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered core internals"
type = "layers"
# hwid's own layering inside `core`, high -> low. `app` (the version/info
# payload the CLI renders) and `resolution` (the HWID resolution logic) are
# independent siblings. `resolution` sits above `impl` (the per-platform
# backends darwin/linux/win32); `app` sits above the logging stack
# (`logging_setup` -> `config` -> `dirs`). `exceptions` is a leaf.
containers = ["hwid.core"]
layers = [
  "app | resolution",
  "logging_setup | impl",
  "config | exceptions",
  "dirs",
]


[tool.ruff]
fix = true
output-format = "full"
preview = true
show-fixes = true
src = ["src", "tests", "examples", "docs/examples"]
target-version = "py310"
unsafe-fixes = true


[tool.ruff.analyze]
detect-string-imports = true
preview = true


[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true
line-ending = "lf"
preview = true
skip-magic-trailing-comma = true


[tool.ruff.lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
# Two opinionated ruff 0.16 preview rules are disabled: RUF105 would rewrite the
# portable `# noqa` comments into ruff's own `# ruff: ignore` syntax (its docs note
# `# noqa` is needed for cross-tool compatibility), and RUF201 would rewrite every
# rule *code* in this config's selectors into long rule *names*. Both are stylistic.
ignore = ["COM812", "CPY", "FIX", "RUF105", "RUF201", "TD"]
logger-objects = ["hwid.core.logging_setup.logger"]
preview = true
select = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
# skip-magic-trailing-comma = true
split-on-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-copyright]
author = "Hasan Sezer Taşan <hasansezertasan@gmail.com>"


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"


[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 5


[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
ignore-overlong-task-comments = true


[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"


[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Recursive glob so nested test packages (tests/cli, tests/gui, ...) are covered.
# Tests legitimately use asserts/magic values, reach into package internals, and
# don't need return-value documentation on their fixtures and helpers.
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC2701", "DOC201"]
# hwid's examples are standalone scripts in dash-named directories (not importable
# packages), so the package-name and implicit-namespace rules do not apply.
"examples/**/*.py" = ["N999", "INP001"]
# Documentation examples are importable modules tested by
# ``tests/test_docs_examples.py``; they are not application packages.
"docs/examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001"]
# The platform backends shell out to native OS tools (powershell, system_profiler,
# dmidecode) to read the hardware UUID -- running these fixed commands is the
# intended mechanism, not an oversight. darwin/win32 use ``shell=True`` for their
# pipelines (S602); linux runs argv-form (no shell) so its timeout kills sudo
# directly, which is what S603 flags. All commands are fixed literals, no input.
"src/hwid/core/impl/*.py" = ["S404", "S602", "S603"]
# The Sphinx config is a standalone module, not part of an importable package.
"docs/conf.py" = ["INP001"]
# The docs warning-allowlist gate is a standalone script (not an importable
# package) whose whole job is to print GitHub `::error::` annotations to stdout.
"docs/check_warnings.py" = ["INP001", "T201"]
# The versioned-docs build orchestrator is a standalone CLI script under tools/,
# not part of an importable package (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/docs-versioning/#docs-publish-only-the-current-version-and-carry-older-built-versions-forward-from-gh-pages).
"tools/build_docs.py" = ["INP001"]


[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true


[tool.ruff.lint.ruff]
parenthesize-tuple-in-subscript = true


[tool.mypy]
files = ["src", "docs/examples"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true


[tool.basedpyright]
exclude = [".venv"]
include = ["src/hwid", "docs/examples"]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
venv = ".venv"
# venvPath is the directory *containing* the venv, not the venv itself; ".venv"
# here would make basedpyright look for ".venv/.venv". Use "." so both the venv
# and basedpyright's strict ruleset resolve the project's installed deps.
venvPath = "."


[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "tests", "docs/examples"]
respect-ignore-files = false


[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.10"


[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true


[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.10"
project-includes = ["src", "docs/examples"]

[tool.pylint.main]
# pylint runs as an always-on gate that deliberately overlaps ruff's PL* rules.
# Its canonical invocation is `pylint src docs/examples`, so it never descends into tests; this
# ignore-paths is a defensive scope guard for broader invocations (`pylint .`,
# filename-passing hooks). Tests are linted by ruff, not pylint.
ignore-paths = ["^tests/.*$"]
# `.pyi` stubs (the c-extension type stub) are signature-only: their bodies are
# `...` and every parameter is unused by construction, so pylint's unused-argument
# check is a guaranteed false positive there. Stubs are type-checked by the
# type-checker gate, not pylint.
ignore-patterns = ['.*\.pyi$']

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
# Only formatter-owned checks, the docstring family, and too-few-public-methods
# are disabled so pylint is usable out of the box; everything else stays on.
disable = [
  "line-too-long", # C0301 — ruff-format owns line length
  "missing-module-docstring", # C0114
  "missing-class-docstring", # C0115
  "missing-function-docstring", # C0116
  "too-few-public-methods", # R0903 — trips dataclasses / config / Protocol classes
  # C0415 — the cli->tui/gui/web dispatch, and each component's own heavy or
  # platform-conditional import (tkinter, uvicorn, the worker's uvloop probe),
  # are deliberately lazy so import-linter's layering contract holds and a
  # framework is only imported when the code path that needs it actually runs.
  # Textual is the exception: the TUI imports it at module scope so `InfoApp`
  # can be defined there and driven by the headless pilot (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/testing-strategy/#interactive-components-expose-injected-driver-seams-so-headless-ci-measures-everything-but-the-blocking-call).
  "import-outside-toplevel",
  # W0706 — the generated TUI entry point explicitly re-raises
  # KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit ahead of a broad `except Exception` to make the
  # "let these propagate" intent obvious to readers, even though BaseException
  # subclasses wouldn't be caught by the Exception clause anyway.
  "try-except-raise",
  # R0801 — the component skeletons (gui/tui/mcp/worker) are deliberately
  # parallel: each fetches package metadata and formats the same info block the
  # same way. That structural symmetry is a feature of the scaffold, not
  # copy-paste debt, and R0801 cannot be suppressed inline at the call site.
  "duplicate-code",
  # C0414 — `from x import y as y` is the PEP 484 explicit re-export idiom that
  # strict mypy/pyright need to see `get_hwid` as part of the public API of
  # `hwid` and `hwid.core`; pylint reads it as a redundant alias.
  "useless-import-alias",
]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10
max-positional-arguments = 10
max-branches = 20

[tool.typos.files]
# copier records `_commit` as a `git describe` string (`v1.2.3-4-g<hash>`) when
# the template is rendered from an untagged ref, and a fragment of the hex hash
# can read as a misspelled word, failing the check on a hash nobody chose. The
# file is machine-written with no prose to check. The prek hook passes
# `--force-exclude`, so the exclusion holds there as well as in `tox -e style`.
extend-exclude = [
  ".copier-answers.yml",
]

[tool.tox]
# The ``worker`` env is intentionally omitted: it starts a broker-bound process
# and would hang/fail under ``tox run`` in CI (where no broker is available).
# The worker is covered by its pytest TestBroker suite; run it on demand with
# ``tox -e worker`` when a broker is up (e.g. inside the devcontainer).
env_list = [
  "style",
  # Inline ``>>>`` snippets are part of the tested-documentation contract,
  # so run them in the default CI ``tox run`` invocation.
  "docs-doctest",
  "cli",
  "3.14",
  "3.13",
  "3.12",
  "3.11",
  "3.10",
]
requires = ["tox>=4"]


[tool.tox.env_run_base]
commands = [
  [
    "coverage",
    "run",
    "--module",
    "pytest",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the tests under {base_python}"
env_tmp_dir = "{toxworkdir}/tmp/{envname}"
# Arms coverage-enable-subprocess so xdist/subprocess workers are measured too;
# `coverage run` plus `parallel = true` writes per-env data files that the CI
# `coverage combine` step merges.
set_env = { COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = "{tox_root}/pyproject.toml" }
# Non-editable: `uv sync --no-editable` builds the project and installs it into
# site-packages, the layout `[tool.coverage.paths]` remaps and the per-component
# coverage gates measure (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#per-component-markers-path-filtered-jobs-and-one-coverage-gate-per-component).
package = "wheel"
# Every env installs from uv.lock (`uv sync --locked`), so tox tests and lints
# the exact versions the lockfile pins. The plain `uv-venv-runner` resolves the
# project's own dependencies fresh on every env creation (tox's
# `use_frozen_constraints` never reaches its `uv pip install`), so a newer
# release could float in and clash with a pinned tool such as semgrep.
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.style]
base_python = ["3.10"]
commands = [
  [
    "ruff",
    "check",
    "--no-fix",
  ],
  [
    "ruff",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.10",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.14",
  ],
  # Style runs once on Linux, so explicitly sweep platform-gated branches that
  # mypy would otherwise prune as unreachable on the host platform.
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "win32",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "darwin",
  ],
  [
    "basedpyright",
  ],
  [
    "ty",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "pyrefly",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "zuban",
    "check",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "pylint",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "python",
    "-m",
    "slotscheck",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "lint-imports",
  ],
  # Rules-database SAST. Deliberately style-env-only (like ty/pyrefly/zuban) and
  # not a prek hook: semgrep keeps no on-disk rule cache, so a pre-commit hook
  # would make a registry request on every `git commit`. The ruleset is named
  # explicitly rather than `--config auto` so rule selection does not depend on
  # language auto-detection; it is still fetched from the registry, which is why
  # this cannot be vendored (see https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/lint-orchestration/#semgrep-runs-in-the-style-env-against-a-named-registry-ruleset-never-vendored). `--error` makes findings blocking;
  # silence a false positive with a trailing `# nosemgrep: <rule-id>`.
  [
    "semgrep",
    "scan",
    "--config",
    "p/python",
    "--error",
    "--metrics=off",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "taplo",
    "lint",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  # A strict `--check` gate, not fix mode: a generated file that taplo would
  # rewrite fails its own CI on first push and drifts on every `copier update`.
  # `.taplo.toml` disables array auto expand/collapse so the shipped layout is
  # the canonical one regardless of which components are enabled. The `*.toml`
  # glob is non-recursive, so it scopes taplo to this project's own root TOML
  # (pyproject/prek/mise/taplo) without walking vendored `.tox`/`.venv`/
  # site-packages trees — no `.taplo.toml` exclude config needed.
  [
    "taplo",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  [
    "typos",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "ec",
  ],
  [
    "sphinx-lint",
    "docs",
  ],
  # Collects (does not run) the suite and flags fixtures that are never used --
  # cheap, deterministic, and a natural fit next to the other whole-program
  # analyzers above (lint-imports, slotscheck).
  [
    "pytest",
    "--dead-fixtures",
  ],
]
# `test` is included so the type checkers that scope tests (e.g. ty) can
# resolve pytest and other test-only imports.
dependency_groups = ["sast", "style", "test"]
description = "Run Checkers, Linters and Formatters"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


# On-demand and CI-only (not in env_list, like `integration`): the `deps` job in
# ci.yml runs it and `check` aggregates that job. `test` is included so deptry
# and creosote can resolve the project's own test-only imports. creosote needs
# the installed distributions to map import names, which the lock runner provides.
[tool.tox.env.deps]
commands = [
  [
    "deptry",
    ".",
  ],
  [
    "creosote",
    "--deps-file",
    "pyproject.toml",
    "--section",
    "project.dependencies",
    # Without this creosote skips imports inside functions, so a dependency used
    # only through a lazy import (the worker's uvloop) is reported as unused.
    "--include-deferred",
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["deps", "test"]
description = "Check dependency hygiene (deptry, creosote)"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.prek]
commands = [["prek", "run", "--all-files"]]
dependency_groups = ["prek"]
description = "Run prek hooks"
# The hooks that need the project call `uv run --locked`, which syncs it (and the
# groups they name) into this env through the runner's UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT;
# installing the wheel here too would only be swapped for that install each run.
package = "skip"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-build]
# Write the warning stream to a file (`-w`) instead of `-W` turning the first
# warning into a hard error, then let docs/check_warnings.py own the pass/fail:
# it diffs the emitted warnings against the docs/expected_warnings.txt allowlist,
# failing on both unexpected new warnings and expected ones that vanished.
commands = [
  ["sphinx-build", "-w", "docs/_build/warnings.txt", "-b", "html", "docs", "docs/_build/html"],
  ["python", "docs/check_warnings.py"],
]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Build Docs"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
# Keep build log output unbuffered/ordered. Reproducible builds pin Sphinx's
# "today"/copyright to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, which the CI docs steps
# (docs-preview.yml, release.yml) export from the last commit date before
# invoking sphinx-build directly. Local `tox` runs deliberately do NOT export
# it: an empty value ("{env:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:}") is *present but blank*, which
# breaks hatchling's get_reproducible_timestamp (`int("")`), so we leave it
# unset locally and conf.py falls back to the current year.
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-server]
# ``--ignore`` the machine-generated ``docs/_generated/`` tree: ``conf.py``
# rewrites it on every Sphinx build, so watching it would make each rebuild
# trigger the next in an endless live-reload loop.
commands = [["sphinx-autobuild", "--ignore", "*/_generated/*", "docs", "docs/_build/html"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Start the live-reloading docs server"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-doctest]
# ``literalinclude`` keeps complete examples in tested Python modules; this
# separate builder executes the occasional ``>>>`` snippet that belongs inline
# with prose.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "doctest", "docs", "docs/_build/doctest"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Run documentation doctests"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-linkcheck]
# On-demand link checker. Also run weekly (non-blocking) by docs-linkcheck.yml.
# Hits the network, so it is deliberately not part of the `style` env or PR CI.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "linkcheck", "docs", "docs/_build/linkcheck"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Check documentation for broken links"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }

[tool.tox.env.cli]
commands = [
  [
    "hwid",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
      "version",
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
description = "Run the CLI application."
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"

[importlinter]
# Run from backend/ with: PYTHONPATH=app uv run lint-imports
include_external_packages = True
root_packages =
    modules
    core

# Layer rules (ORM ownership, transport delegation, persistence purity, outbound
# reach through a published surface, dependency direction) are enforced by
# ``tests/architecture/test_module_boundaries.py::TestLayerRules``. They are stated
# there once, by file role, because contracts here match exact module names: a
# qualified stem (``pipeline_service``) escaped them and every flat module needed
# its own copy. What stays below is what import-linter is good at: external
# packages, the platform direction, and named design seams.

[importlinter:contract:auth-boundary]
name = Auth boundary: non-auth must not import auth internals directly
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules.users
    modules.activities
    core
    modules.followers
    modules.garmin
    modules.gears
    modules.health
    modules.notifications
    modules.server_settings
    modules.strava
    modules.websocket
forbidden_modules =
    modules.auth._internal
    modules.auth.*.crud
    modules.auth.*.*.crud

# The substrate is the external ``jasil`` package, which enforces its own
# ports-and-adapters direction and its own no-domain rule upstream. Which part of
# it application code may touch is still this repository's rule, but it cannot be
# stated here: import-linter rejects a subpackage of an external package as a
# forbidden module. It lives in ``tests/architecture/test_jasil_boundary.py``.

# The same rule one layer up, for ``core``: the platform never reaches into the
# domain to ask what work exists. Each module declares its own ``scheduled_jobs``,
# and the composition root (``main``) hands the collected list to
# ``start_scheduler``.
# One exception is recorded here so it is reviewed rather than assumed:
# ``core.middleware`` reads the server-settings SCHEMA (a data shape, not
# behaviour) to type the settings it stamps onto the request.
[importlinter:contract:core-not-domain]
name = Core must not import domain modules
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    core
forbidden_modules =
    modules
ignore_imports =
    core.middleware -> modules.server_settings.schema

[importlinter:contract:redis-owned-by-platform]
name = Only the platform Redis capability may import redis
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules
    core
forbidden_modules =
    redis

# A layers contract (not a denylist) that states the substrate's internal direction
# once: the composition root (container) sits above the adapters (backends), which sit
# above the ports (providers) and the event envelope (events). Higher layers may import
# lower ones, never the reverse — so a port importing an adapter (the ports-and-adapters
# inversion the forbidden contracts above do NOT catch) is rejected here.
# The substrate's internal layering is an import contract in the ``jasil``
# repository, verified on its releases rather than on ours.

# The whole activities module is provider-agnostic, not just its core. Strava and
# Garmin depend on activities — they parse a provider payload and hand it to the
# ingestion seam — and activities must not depend on them back, or neither side
# could be built, tested or extracted without the other.
#
# The direction is one-way, via three seams activities owns and providers plug
# into:
#   * ``activity_ingestion.provider_registry`` — a provider registers a fetch
#     callable at startup; the refresh path names no provider.
#   * ``activity_ingestion.contracts.BulkImportSource`` — a provider export
#     subclasses it (``modules.strava.bulk_import_source``) instead of the base
#     class branching on ``strava_activities``.
#   * ``GarminSource.gear_id`` — the provider resolves its own synced gear and
#     passes the id, so enrichment only answers "and if not, what is the default?".
#
# Stating the rule over the whole module means a new sub-package inherits it
# instead of having to be added to a list.
[importlinter:contract:activities-provider-agnostic]
name = The activities module must not import a provider — providers register with it
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules.activities
forbidden_modules =
    modules.strava
    modules.garmin

# The activities core (activity/) is parsing-agnostic: it exposes the typed
# ParsedActivity contract + ingestion_service.store_parsed_activity, but never
# imports a file parser. All format knowledge lives in the sibling
# activity_ingestion/ package, which produces the contract and calls the core.
# Direct imports only (allow_indirect_imports): the rule is that the core must
# not reach for a parser directly, not that it must avoid transitive shared
# dependencies. The provider half of this boundary is the module-wide
# ``activities-provider-agnostic`` contract above.
[importlinter:contract:activities-parsing-boundary]
name = Activities core must not import file parsers
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules.activities.activity
forbidden_modules =
    modules.activities.activity_file_import

# The ingestion PIPELINE is provider-agnostic, the same way it is already
# format-agnostic. It owns "validate -> parse -> enrich -> store -> retain" and nothing
# about where a file came from: the export specifics (which duplicate listings to
# skip, what metadata to apply, the sidecar photos) are answered by the source object it
# is handed. ``contracts.py`` is deliberately NOT in scope here: defining the seam a
# provider export subclasses *is* its job.
# Superseded in the provider dimension by ``activities-provider-agnostic`` above;
# kept because it also forbids the pipeline reaching for the *parsers*, which is a
# different rule with the same shape.
[importlinter:contract:ingestion-pipeline-format-agnostic]
name = The ingestion pipeline must not import a parser directly — the registry resolves one
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules.activities.activity_ingestion.upload_entry_service
    modules.activities.activity_ingestion.provider_entry_service
    modules.activities.activity_ingestion.bulk_import_service
    modules.activities.activity_ingestion.service
    modules.activities.activity_ingestion.contracts
forbidden_modules =
    modules.activities.activity_file_import

# The file parsers (activity_file_import/) are PURE: bytes -> parsed dict/Activity, with no
# db, privacy, gear, provider, or exercise-title-crud coupling. Domain
# resolution (default/Garmin gear, privacy defaults, exercise-title persistence)
# lives in the sibling activity_ingestion/ enrichment seam, which legitimately
# owns db + provider knowledge — so a parser is unit-testable with bytes alone. The parsers may still import the activities SCHEMAS (activity.schema /
# activity_exercise_titles.schema / activity_workout_steps.schema) — data shapes, not crud.
[importlinter:contract:activity-file-import-purity]
name = Activity file parsers must be pure (no db / domain / provider / crud / HTTP imports)
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules.activities.activity_file_import
forbidden_modules =
    modules.gears
    modules.users
    modules.garmin
    modules.strava
    modules.activities.*.crud
    modules.activities.*.*.crud
    sqlalchemy
    fastapi

# The activities module performs no raw network egress. Reverse geocoding goes
# through the platform GeocodingProvider, with the SSRF host checks (OWASP A10)
# in core.network where a future outbound integration inherits them. This
# contract is what keeps egress code out of the domain: an outbound call from
# activities must be added as a platform provider.
# Note: ``urllib`` is deliberately not listed. import-linter cannot forbid a
# single subpackage of an external/stdlib package, and activities legitimately
# uses ``urllib.parse`` for URL decoding — banning the parent would reject that
# too. The HTTP clients actually in use here are covered.
[importlinter:contract:activities-no-raw-egress]
name = The activities module must not make raw network calls
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules.activities
forbidden_modules =
    requests
    httpx
    socket
    staticmap

# Data migrations are historical orchestration, but that does not grant them
# unrestricted access to every package implementation. Each package exposes the
# exact legacy operations it supports through ``migration_service.py``; those
# adapters are for app/migrations only and must never become a general-purpose
# domain dependency.
[importlinter:contract:activities-migration-surfaces-are-private]
name = Activity migration services are consumed only by application migrations
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules
    core
forbidden_modules =
    modules.activities.*.migration_service

# Provider modules describe users data with the read schemas the users CRUD actually
# returns, never the ORM models: the runtime value is already a DTO, so naming the
# ORM classes would only keep a users-ORM import alive inside Strava/Garmin.
[importlinter:contract:providers-no-users-orm]
name = Provider modules must not import the users ORM models
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    modules.strava
    modules.garmin
forbidden_modules =
    modules.users.users_integrations.models
    modules.users.users_privacy_settings.models

[project]
name = "endurain"
version = "0.20.0-beta2"
description = "Endurain API for the Endurain app"
authors = [{name = "João Vitória Silva", email = "joao@endurain.com"}]
# readme intentionally omitted — internal app, not published to PyPI
requires-python = ">=3.13,<4.0"
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.141.1",
    "uvicorn>=0.53.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.3",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.54",
    "apscheduler>=3.11.3",
    "requests>=2.34.2",
    "stravalib>=2.6.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.32",
    "gpxpy>=1.6.2",
    "tcxreader>=0.4.11",
    "alembic>=1.20.0",
    "joserfc>=1.7.5",
    "fitdecode>=0.11.0",
    "numpy>=2.5.3",
    "geopy>=2.5.0",
    "pydantic-core>=2.46.5",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.15.0",
    "garminconnect>=0.3.16",
    "websockets>=17.1",
    "timezonefinder>=9.0.0",
    "psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.3.6",
    "user-agents>=2.2.0",
    "pydantic[email]>=2.13.5",
    "pyotp>=2.10.0",
    "qrcode[pil]>=8.2",
    "psutil>=7.2.2",
    "python-magic>=0.4.27",
    "pwdlib[argon2,bcrypt]>=0.3.1",
    "authlib>=1.8.0",
    "httpx2>=2.13.0",
    "itsdangerous>=2.2.0",
    "slowapi>=0.1.10",
    "safeuploads[fastapi]>=1.1.1",
    "nh3>=0.3.7",
    "aiofiles>=25.1.0",
    "staticmap>=0.5.7",
    # Pinned below the next minor: JASIL is pre-1.0 and documents breaking
    # changes on minor versions.
    "jasil[fastapi,geocoding,jobs,migrations]>=0.6.1,<0.7.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Extra pulled in for multi-node (`distributed`) deployments: Redis-backed
# shared state / event bus and S3-compatible object storage. The default image
# (`uv export --no-dev`) ships neither, so `local` deployments stay lean.
distributed = [
    "boto3>=1.43.98",
    "redis>=8.1.0",
    "jasil[redis,s3]>=0.6.1,<0.7.0",
]

[dependency-groups]
typecheck = [
    "mypy>=2.3.1",
    "types-requests",
    "types-psutil",
    "types-qrcode",
    "types-aiofiles",
    "types-Authlib",
]
lint = [
    "ruff>=0.16.8",
]
test = [
    "httpx2>=2.13.0",
    "faker>=40.39.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.168.0",
    "import-linter>=2.15",
    "pytest>=9.1.1",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4.0",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "boto3>=1.43.98",
    "redis>=8.1.0",
]
dev = [
    "hatch>=1.18.1",
    {include-group = "lint"},
    {include-group = "test"},
    {include-group = "typecheck"},
]
docs = [
    "mkdocs-material>=9.7.7",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=1.0.6",
    "mkdocs-redirects>=1.2.3",
    "mkdocs-swagger-ui-tag>=0.8.1",
]

[tool.uv]
required-version = "0.12.24"
exclude-newer = "30 days"
# jasil is first-party (endurain-project) and published through PyPI Trusted
# Publishing with PEP 740 attestations, so it is exempt from the quarantine the
# cutoff applies to third-party releases. Every other dependency keeps it.
exclude-newer-package = { jasil = false }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pypi"
url = "https://pypi.org/simple"
explicit = true

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["app"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
only-include = ["app"]

[tool.hatch.envs.default]
type = "virtual"
path = ".venv"

[tool.hatch.envs.default.scripts]
lint = "ruff check . --fix"
format = "ruff format ."
lint-check = "ruff check ."
format-check = "ruff format --check ."
test = "pytest"
typecheck = "mypy"
validate = ["lint", "format", "test", "typecheck"]
check = ["lint-check", "format-check", "test", "typecheck"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["app"]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
addopts = "--tb=short --strict-markers --cov --cov-report=term-missing"
markers = [
    "postgres: needs a disposable PostgreSQL database (TEST_DATABASE_URL); skipped when it is unset",
    "distributed: runs real API and worker processes against disposable PostgreSQL, Redis and S3 (TEST_DATABASE_URL, TEST_REDIS_URL, TEST_S3_ENDPOINT_URL); skipped unless all are set",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:slowapi.*",
