# Import contracts for src/ag. AUTHORITATIVE for the import rules of the package; the
# architecture document describes it and defers to it.
#
# Run: lint-imports   (from the repository root, with the project installed editable)
#
# Built against the import-rule table of the accepted tree, one contract per row and named
# by row number so the file can be read against that table. Row 14 needs two contracts and
# row 16 needs one per adapter and port, so there are more than eighteen sections.
#
# EVERY CONTRACT HAS BEEN BROKEN ONCE ON PURPOSE with a throwaway probe module, and the
# failure recorded in the pull request that added it. Do the same for a new contract:
# over a nearly empty tree a contract passes whether or not its names are right.
#
# WHAT IMPORT-LINTER 2.15 DOES WITH A NAME THAT DOES NOT EXIST (probed):
#   - it refuses to run for a missing module in `source_modules`, `protected_modules`,
#     `allowed_importers`, `modules` (independence) and a non-optional layer;
#   - it accepts, silently, a missing module in `forbidden_modules`, an optional layer
#     in parentheses, and a wildcard that matches nothing.
# So the modules named in the first group exist as docstring-only placeholders, and the
# names in the second group are covered by the break-it-once evidence only. A typo in a
# `forbidden_modules` entry passes forever; check the spelling against the tree.
#
# ALLOW-LISTS ARE WRITTEN AS `protected`, NOT `forbidden`, wherever the rule is "only X
# may import Y": a forbidden list enumerates today's packages and admits tomorrow's.
# Where a rule is "may import only these modules of a package" (rows 4, 8, 14, 15), the
# contract forbids the whole package and lists the allowed imports under
# `ignore_imports`, so a new module is denied until it is added here on purpose. Those
# contracts set `unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = none` because the allowed imports
# do not exist yet.

[importlinter]
root_package = ag
include_external_packages = True


# --- Row 1 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:row-01-package-stack]
name = Row 1: the package stack; every package under ag has a layer
type = layers
containers =
    ag
layers =
    orchestrator
    runtime
    generalization
    lineage | staging
    adapters
    ports
    core
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores =
    observability


# --- Row 2 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `exhaustive` is not in the table; it is here so that a new module under
# ag/generalization has to be given a layer, which is what keeps row 11's list complete.
[importlinter:contract:row-02-domain-layers]
name = Row 2: the layers inside ag.generalization
type = layers
containers =
    ag.generalization
layers =
    registry
    pipelines
    operations
    helpers
    tuning | errors | sources | products | classification_rules
exhaustive = true


# --- Row 3 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:row-03-core-is-pure]
name = Row 3: ag.core imports nothing else in ag
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.core
forbidden_modules =
    ag.ports
    ag.adapters
    ag.lineage
    ag.staging
    ag.observability
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.generalization


# --- Row 4 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:row-04-ports-import-four-core-modules]
name = Row 4: ag.ports imports four ag.core modules and nothing else in ag
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.ports
forbidden_modules =
    ag.core
    ag.adapters
    ag.lineage
    ag.staging
    ag.observability
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.generalization
ignore_imports =
    ag.ports -> ag.core.handles
    ag.ports.** -> ag.core.handles
    ag.ports -> ag.core.types
    ag.ports.** -> ag.core.types
    ag.ports -> ag.core.injection
    ag.ports.** -> ag.core.injection
    ag.ports -> ag.core.errors
    ag.ports.** -> ag.core.errors
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = none


# --- Row 5 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extended in slice 1a with the value modules: the three Protocols stay independent of
# each other, so what they share (fields and values, the predicate algebra, the geometry
# value type, the port errors) sits below them, and the toolbox that bundles them above.
# `row_shape` and `columns` join the bottom line when they land.
[importlinter:contract:row-05-port-layers]
name = Row 5: the layers inside ag.ports; the three Protocols stay independent
type = layers
containers =
    ag.ports
layers =
    toolbox
    cartographic_ops
    geometry_ops | table_ops | graph_ops
    predicates
    geometry | attributes | errors


# --- Row 6 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:row-06-adapters-chosen-at-the-top]
name = Row 6: only a composition root imports ag.adapters
type = protected
protected_modules =
    ag.adapters
allowed_importers =
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator


# --- Row 7 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `_shared` and `errors` are left out of the list on purpose: every adapter may import them.
[importlinter:contract:row-07-adapters-are-independent]
name = Row 7: adapter packages do not import each other
type = independence
modules =
    ag.adapters.arcpy
    ag.adapters.fakes
    ag.adapters.networkx
    ag.adapters.storage
    ag.adapters.cluster


# --- Row 8 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The narrower rule, that only session.py runs a tool, touches arcpy.env or names a
# vendor exception, is not an import rule. The stub in stubs/arcpy_constrained/ and a static scan
# enforce it (docs/contributing/toolchain.md).
[importlinter:contract:row-08-vendor-libraries]
name = Row 8: a vendor library is imported only by its adapter
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag
forbidden_modules =
    arcpy
    networkx
    shapely
    boto3
    minio
    google
ignore_imports =
    ag.adapters.arcpy -> arcpy
    ag.adapters.arcpy.** -> arcpy
    ag.adapters.networkx.graph_ops -> networkx
    ag.adapters.** -> shapely
    ag.adapters.** -> boto3
    ag.adapters.** -> minio
    ag.adapters.** -> google
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = none


# --- Row 9 -------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:row-09-staging-is-runtimes-alone]
name = Row 9: only ag.runtime imports ag.staging
type = protected
protected_modules =
    ag.staging
allowed_importers =
    ag.runtime


# --- Row 10 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One allowed importer while `mint` is reached through the Toolbox.
[importlinter:contract:row-10-lineage-is-runtimes-alone]
name = Row 10: only ag.runtime imports ag.lineage
type = protected
protected_modules =
    ag.lineage
allowed_importers =
    ag.runtime


# --- Row 11 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# sources and products importing each other is row 2's business (they are independent
# siblings there); a module may not be both a source and a forbidden module here.
[importlinter:contract:row-11-identity-modules-are-leaves]
name = Row 11: sources and products import only ag.core
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.generalization.sources
    ag.generalization.products
forbidden_modules =
    ag.ports
    ag.adapters
    ag.lineage
    ag.staging
    ag.observability
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.generalization.registry
    ag.generalization.pipelines
    ag.generalization.operations
    ag.generalization.helpers
    ag.generalization.tuning
    ag.generalization.errors
    ag.generalization.classification_rules


# --- Row 12 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Follows indirect imports on purpose: ag.core.locations, graph, selection, policy,
# planning and validation each import one of the two, so they are ruled out as well.
[importlinter:contract:row-12-operations-know-no-data-objects]
name = Row 12: operations and helpers never see a DataObject (ADR-0003)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.generalization.operations
    ag.generalization.helpers
forbidden_modules =
    ag.core.data_objects
    ag.core.pipeline
    ag.generalization.sources
    ag.generalization.products


# --- Row 13 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Redundant with rows 6, 9 and 10; kept because this is the message a domain developer
# should read.
[importlinter:contract:row-13-domain-stays-below-the-framework]
name = Row 13: domain code never imports the framework above the ports
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.generalization
forbidden_modules =
    ag.adapters
    ag.staging
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.lineage


# --- Row 14 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:row-14a-observability-is-a-leaf]
name = Row 14a: ag.observability imports only stdlib and ag.core.types
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.observability
forbidden_modules =
    ag.core
    ag.ports
    ag.adapters
    ag.lineage
    ag.staging
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.generalization
ignore_imports =
    ag.observability -> ag.core.types
    ag.observability.** -> ag.core.types
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = none

[importlinter:contract:row-14b-no-ambient-context-in-declarations]
name = Row 14b: no context accessor in ag.core or in pipelines
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.core
    ag.generalization.pipelines
forbidden_modules =
    ag.observability.context


# --- Row 15 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Direct imports only. The orchestrator imports ag.generalization.registry, which
# imports pipelines, which import operations for their declarations, and operations
# import ports; a contract that followed indirect imports would fail on that legal chain.
[importlinter:contract:row-15-orchestrator-schedules-and-touches-no-pod]
name = Row 15: ag.orchestrator imports no pod-side code
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.orchestrator
forbidden_modules =
    ag.generalization.operations
    ag.adapters.arcpy
    ag.staging
    ag.ports
ignore_imports =
    ag.orchestrator -> ag.ports.cluster
    ag.orchestrator.** -> ag.ports.cluster
    ag.orchestrator -> ag.ports.archive
    ag.orchestrator.** -> ag.ports.archive
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = none
allow_indirect_imports = true


# --- Row 16 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One contract per adapter and port. The wildcard picks up a new group module by itself.
[importlinter:contract:row-16-arcpy-geometry-ops-groups]
name = Row 16: arcpy geometry_ops group modules are independent
type = independence
modules =
    ag.adapters.arcpy.geometry_ops.*

[importlinter:contract:row-16-arcpy-table-ops-groups]
name = Row 16: arcpy table_ops group modules are independent
type = independence
modules =
    ag.adapters.arcpy.table_ops.*

[importlinter:contract:row-16-arcpy-cartographic-ops-groups]
name = Row 16: arcpy cartographic_ops group modules are independent
type = independence
modules =
    ag.adapters.arcpy.cartographic_ops.*

[importlinter:contract:row-16-memory-geometry-ops-groups]
name = Row 16: memory geometry_ops group modules are independent
type = independence
modules =
    ag.adapters.fakes.memory.geometry_ops.*

[importlinter:contract:row-16-memory-table-ops-groups]
name = Row 16: memory table_ops group modules are independent
type = independence
modules =
    ag.adapters.fakes.memory.table_ops.*

[importlinter:contract:row-16-memory-cartographic-ops-groups]
name = Row 16: memory cartographic_ops group modules are independent
type = independence
modules =
    ag.adapters.fakes.memory.cartographic_ops.*


# --- Row 17 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The last two layers are optional because each adapter has one of them.
[importlinter:contract:row-17-adapter-layers]
name = Row 17: adapter layers: port packages, support, _base, session or store
type = layers
containers =
    ag.adapters.arcpy
    ag.adapters.fakes.memory
layers =
    geometry_ops | table_ops | cartographic_ops
    support
    _base
    (session)
    (store)


# --- Row 18 ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Narrower than row 6, and both apply: an import from ag.runtime.compose passes row 6
# and fails here.
[importlinter:contract:row-18-fakes-for-the-local-runner-only]
name = Row 18: only ag.runtime.local imports ag.adapters.fakes
type = protected
protected_modules =
    ag.adapters.fakes
allowed_importers =
    ag.runtime.local

# TEMPLATE — layer contracts for the executable companion.
#
# Run: lint-imports   (from this directory)
#
# On promotion this file moves to the repository root beside `src/ag/` and the
# `root_packages` line is the only thing that changes.
#
# WHY A LINTER AND NOT A CONVENTION. `ag.sources` and `ag.products` are only useful as
# leaves. One convenience import — a source module reaching into a pipeline for a
# constant — makes them a cycle, and the property they exist for ("read one file and
# see everything entering the project") is gone silently. A docstring saying "leaf
# module" is not enforcement; this is.
#
# NOT YET EXPRESSIBLE: the vendor-import contracts of 03-architecture §4.2 - "arcpy
# appears in exactly one module", and the same for networkx and shapely. Those need
# `adapters/` to have content; the `ports/` rows below are now real.

[importlinter]
root_package = ag

[importlinter:contract:identity-modules-are-leaves]
name = sources and products import nothing but core
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.sources
    ag.products
forbidden_modules =
    ag.operations
    ag.pipelines
    ag.staging
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.tuning
    ag.helpers

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = the package stack, top to bottom
type = layers
layers =
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.runtime
    ag.pipelines
    ag.operations
    ag.staging
    ag.ports
    ag.core

[importlinter:contract:ports-are-a-boundary]
name = a port knows nothing above or beside it
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.ports
forbidden_modules =
    ag.adapters
    ag.operations
    ag.pipelines
    ag.staging
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.sources
    ag.products
    ag.core.pipeline
    ag.core.data_objects

# The next two are ALLOW-LISTS, not forbidden lists, because that is how
# 03-architecture §4.1 states the rule: `adapters/` is imported by the composition
# roots, `staging/` by `runtime/` only. A forbidden contract enumerates today's
# packages and silently admits tomorrow's - add `ag.reporting` next year and it may
# import an adapter with nothing complaining. `protected` inverts that: a new package
# is denied until someone adds it here on purpose.

[importlinter:contract:adapters-are-chosen-only-at-the-top]
name = only a composition root chooses an adapter
type = protected
protected_modules =
    ag.adapters
allowed_importers =
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
broken_contract_guidance =
    An adapter is chosen, not depended on. Take the port as a parameter and let
    runtime/ or orchestrator/ decide which implementation to pass - that is what
    keeps the dependency arrow pointing at the contract. 03-architecture §4.1.

[importlinter:contract:staging-is-runtimes-alone]
name = only runtime reaches the staging layer
type = protected
protected_modules =
    ag.staging
allowed_importers =
    ag.runtime
broken_contract_guidance =
    staging/ owns local paths, workspaces and transfers - pod concerns. An operation
    that reaches it has learned where it is running, which is the ignorance the whole
    declaration model depends on. orchestrator/ is excluded too: it schedules pods and
    never touches a pod's disk. 03-architecture §4.1.

[importlinter:contract:core-is-pure]
name = core imports nothing above it
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.core
forbidden_modules =
    ag.sources
    ag.products
    ag.operations
    ag.pipelines
    ag.staging
    ag.runtime
    ag.orchestrator
    ag.ports
    ag.adapters
    ag.helpers
    ag.observability

[importlinter:contract:operations-know-no-data-objects]
name = an operation never sees a DataObject
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ag.operations
forbidden_modules =
    ag.core.data_objects
    ag.core.pipeline
    ag.sources
    ag.products

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

# The Python target (docs/contributing/python-version.md) is stated by four settings that
# always change together: `requires-python` here, `[tool.pyright] pythonVersion`,
# `[tool.ruff] target-version` and `.python-version`.
[project]
name = "ag"
version = "0.0.0"
description = "Cartographic generalization behind a port and adapter boundary."
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = []

# The one place tool versions are stated. Every hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml runs its
# tool through `uv run --locked --extra dev`, and CI does the same, so nothing else pins a
# version. uv resolves these into uv.lock, which is committed and written only by uv
# (docs/contributing/toolchain.md). Set up with `uv sync --extra dev`;
# `pip install -e ".[dev]"` is the fallback, which is why this is a standard extra rather
# than a `[dependency-groups]` table (`pip install --group` needs pip 25.1) and why no
# uv-specific table exists here.
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "ruff==0.16.8",
    "pyright==1.1.399",
    "import-linter==2.15",
    "pytest==9.1.1",
    "pre-commit==4.6.2",
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

# Ruff is the one formatter and linter for the whole repository. `force-exclude` keeps the
# exclusion in force when a file is passed explicitly, as an editor does; the example
# pipelines are excluded while they are inert, and the exclusion goes when they go live;
# the template the new code is lifted from, module by module, and the staging scripts are
# excluded because neither ships and both are deleted; Markdown is excluded because ruff
# would otherwise reformat the Python examples inside documents. Patterns are root-anchored (`dir/**`, `./file.py`): a bare name would match that name
# anywhere in the tree, `src/ag/generalization/` included.
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
force-exclude = true
extend-exclude = [
    "tests/fixtures/example_pipelines",
    "docs/refactor/template_code/**",
    "docs/refactor/temp/**",
    "*.md",
]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "F",       # pyflakes
    "E9",      # io and syntax errors
    "I",       # isort (import order and grouping)
    "SLF001",  # private member access; scoped to ag/generalization below
]

# SLF001 catches reach-through such as `tb.geometry._port`, which no import contract can
# see. It applies to the domain code only.
#
# The legacy packages are linted, with two rules held back: F401 and I001 have autofixes
# that remove or reorder imports, and the legacy convention is side-effect imports, so they

# Strict over the new code only, by path: the legacy packages and tests_legacy/ are outside
# the include list, and `strict` names the checked roots so that a legacy file opened in
# an editor is analysed in standard mode, not strict. The example pipelines are excluded
# while they are inert; the exclusion goes when they go live. `extraPaths` lets the static
# tests import the scripts under tools/ the way pytest does, and makes `src` resolve as
# local source rather than as the installed library, which strict mode would otherwise
# ask stubs for.
[tool.pyright]
include = ["src", "tests", "tools"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    "tests/fixtures/example_pipelines",
]
extraPaths = ["tools", "src"]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
strict = ["src", "tests", "tools"]
pythonVersion = "3.13"

# The constrained ArcPy stub (stubs/arcpy_constrained/, non-tool names only) applies to
# these two roots and nowhere else. An execution environment's extraPaths outranks the
# interpreter's site-packages, so the constraint holds whichever interpreter an editor has
# selected. The stub is never placed at `typings/`: pyright treats that directory as the
# global stubPath and would apply the stub to every file in the repository, legacy
# packages included (docs/contributing/toolchain.md).
[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "src/ag/adapters/arcpy"
extraPaths = ["stubs/arcpy_constrained"]

[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "tests/support/arcpy"
extraPaths = ["stubs/arcpy_constrained"]

[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "."
extraPaths = ["tools", "src"]

# The marker and the collection roots, and nothing else: no default `addopts`.
# `testpaths` keeps a bare `pytest` away from the legacy tests, the template and the
# staging scripts under docs/, which import ArcPy or are not part of this suite.
# tests/conftest.py gives the marker the same behaviour everywhere: without ArcPy a bare
# run skips marked tests, and `-m arcpy` fails the session instead of reporting green.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = [
    "arcpy: needs ArcPy; runs under an ArcGIS Pro Python environment. Skipped when ArcPy is absent; with `-m arcpy` and no ArcPy the session fails.",
]
testpaths = [
    "tests/unit",
    "tests/static",
    "tests/conformance",
    "tests/goldens",
    "tests/invariance",
    "tests/smoke",
]

# Architecture contracts, checked by `make lint-imports` (import-linter).
#
# Type-checking-only imports are excluded: a `TYPE_CHECKING` reference does not
# create a runtime dependency, and treating it as one produces false positives
# (most of this package's apparent import cycles are type-only).
#
# `ignore_imports` entries are an explicit, reviewable debt list, not an excuse
# list: each one is a dependency that exists today. Adding a NEW violation makes
# CI fail, which is the point. Remove entries as the dependencies are resolved;
# do not add entries to silence a new one without discussion.

[importlinter]
root_package = evalscope
include_external_packages = False
exclude_type_checking_imports = True

# Benchmarks are plugins loaded on demand via evalscope/benchmarks/_index.json.
# Nothing in the core may import them back, otherwise touching any core module
# drags all ~240 adapter modules (and datasets/nltk/openai) into the process.
[importlinter:contract:core-does-not-import-benchmarks]
name = core layers must not import benchmark adapters
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    evalscope.api
    evalscope.evaluator
    evalscope.report
    evalscope.metrics
    evalscope.models
    evalscope.perf
forbidden_modules =
    evalscope.benchmarks

# evalscope/api/metric/semantics.py declares the intended direction: the catalog,
# baseline table, alias manifest and resolver under evalscope.metrics.semantics
# import the contract module, "never the other way round". The entries below are
# the places that still go the other way.
# evalscope.report is deliberately NOT forbidden here: building a Report is part
# of the DataAdapter contract, so api -> report is by design.
[importlinter:contract:api-does-not-depend-on-implementations]
name = api must not depend on metrics / benchmarks implementations
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    evalscope.api
forbidden_modules =
    evalscope.metrics
    evalscope.benchmarks
ignore_imports =
    evalscope.api.benchmark.meta -> evalscope.metrics.semantics.legacy_identity
    evalscope.api.benchmark.adapters.text2image_adapter -> evalscope.metrics.semantics
    evalscope.api.benchmark.adapters.text2image_adapter -> evalscope.metrics.semantics.naming
    evalscope.api.mixin.llm_judge_mixin -> evalscope.metrics
    evalscope.api.mixin.llm_judge_mixin -> evalscope.metrics.semantics.naming
    evalscope.api.metric.scorer -> evalscope.metrics.semantics.naming
    evalscope.api.metric.metric -> evalscope.metrics.vision.t2v_metrics.constants

# Perf field semantics currently live under metrics.semantics and read the perf
# constants, which is the one edge from the eval stack into the perf subsystem.
[importlinter:contract:metrics-does-not-depend-on-perf]
name = metrics must not depend on perf
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    evalscope.metrics
forbidden_modules =
    evalscope.perf
ignore_imports =
    evalscope.metrics.semantics.perf -> evalscope.perf.utils.perf_constants

# utils is meant to be a leaf helper collection: evalscope/utils/__init__.py only
# lazily exposes leaf modules. The entries below are modules that sit in utils but
# depend on the top of the stack (the docs pipeline) or on api types
# (multi_choices, whose Choices objects are constructed at runtime).
[importlinter:contract:utils-is-a-leaf-layer]
name = utils must not depend on api / metrics / report / config
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    evalscope.utils
forbidden_modules =
    evalscope.api
    evalscope.metrics
    evalscope.report
    evalscope.config
ignore_imports =
    evalscope.utils.multi_choices -> evalscope.api.evaluator
    evalscope.utils.doc_utils.benchmark_stats -> evalscope.api.benchmark.statistics
    evalscope.utils.doc_utils.benchmark_stats -> evalscope.api.messages
    evalscope.utils.doc_utils.benchmark_stats -> evalscope.api.messages.chat_message
    evalscope.utils.doc_utils.benchmark_stats -> evalscope.api.registry
    evalscope.utils.doc_utils.benchmark_stats -> evalscope.config
    evalscope.utils.doc_utils.generate_dataset_md -> evalscope.api.benchmark
    evalscope.utils.doc_utils.generate_dataset_md -> evalscope.api.benchmark.adapters
    evalscope.utils.doc_utils.generate_dataset_md -> evalscope.api.registry

# The perf subsystem is independent of the eval stack. Its only current path into
# the report layer runs through utils.multi_choices, which is covered above.
[importlinter:contract:perf-is-independent-of-the-eval-stack]
name = perf must not depend on benchmarks / report / evaluator
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    evalscope.perf
forbidden_modules =
    evalscope.benchmarks
    evalscope.report
    evalscope.evaluator
ignore_imports =
    evalscope.utils.multi_choices -> evalscope.api.evaluator

; §II Protocol-boundaries as a machine contract (#234).
; Since #238 the code is an installed package `kinozal_scraper`; grimp builds the
; graph from that single root_package (src on sys.path via the editable install /
; pytest pythonpath=["src"]). grimp is static/AST, so the `__main__` wiring blocks
; never execute during analysis.
;
; NOTE on granularity: the Protocol classes (Storage/Notifier/Enricher) live in
; the SAME module as their concrete impls (sheets_storage holds both `Storage`
; and `SheetsStorage`). So a module-level contract cannot express "orchestrators
; import only Protocol modules" — these contracts pin dependency *direction*
; instead. A stricter protocol-only contract needs a Protocol-extraction refactor
; (out of scope, see #234).

[importlinter]
root_package = kinozal_scraper

[importlinter:contract:pipeline-layers]
name = Pipeline dependency direction (§II)
type = layers
layers =
    kinozal_scraper.kinozal_pipeline | kinozal_scraper.github_popular_pipeline | kinozal_scraper.steam_pipeline | kinozal_scraper.github_trending_pipeline | kinozal_scraper.soldout_pipeline
    kinozal_scraper.sheets_storage | kinozal_scraper.telegram_notifier | kinozal_scraper.gemini_enricher
    kinozal_scraper.generic_pipeline

[importlinter:contract:adapter-no-auth]
name = Service adapters take ready clients, not credentials (§II)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    kinozal_scraper.sheets_storage
    kinozal_scraper.telegram_notifier
    kinozal_scraper.gemini_enricher
forbidden_modules =
    kinozal_scraper.kinozal_auth

# independent `:`) because they import each other by design (di.bootstrap wires
# _services.run_action into the registry, which _services then resolves). `impls/` is
# intentionally OUT of the layered stack: domain.py imports a default impl
# (impls.process_executor), so impls cannot sit cleanly above domain — see
# docs/part-a-rationale.md OPEN QUESTIONS. PENDING HUMAN SIGN-OFF.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "er-layered"
name = "ER layered architecture"
type = "layers"
containers = ["finecode_extension_runner"]
layers = [
    "er_server",
    "services",
    "_services : di",
    "domain",
]

# er_errors.py is the ER's shared exception vocabulary, used by both the top infra layer
# (er_server.py, which legitimately talks JSON-RPC) and mid-layers (e.g.
# impls/project_action_runner.py). It must depend only on itself and the standard
# library — an exception here that imports a transport package to carry a wire-protocol
# detail couples the shared vocabulary to one specific protocol. Scoped to er_errors.py
# rather than the full `domain` layer because domain.py has a separate, pre-existing,
# already-flagged exception (it imports impls.process_executor — see the er-layered
# contract's note above); that is an unrelated question this contract does not attempt to
# resolve.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "er-errors-purity"
name = "ER shared exception vocabulary depends only on itself and the standard library"
type = "domain_purity"
domain_modules = ["finecode_extension_runner.er_errors"]

# WM server internal stack. Source: docs/guides/wm-server-internals.md layer diagram

id = "wm-subsystems-layered"
name = "WM client subsystems sit above the WM server core"
type = "layers"

    "wm_server",
]


# The WM server core must not import its client subsystems (explicit forbidden form of the
# direction enforced above). Verified no such imports exist today.

# ignored `finecode.runner.runner_client` (no such module) and `lsp_server.lsp_server`;

# errors.py and domain.py are wm-layered's pure-data bottom in the sense that matters
# here: they only ever hold data types and exceptions, with no legitimate reason to
# reference infrastructure. context.py is deliberately excluded even though wm-layered
# groups it with them — WorkspaceContext is the WM's shared *mutable* state and by design
# holds live handles to running infrastructure (e.g. runner_io_thread: AsyncIOThread,
# ws_projects_extension_runners: dict[..., ExtensionRunnerInfo]). wm-layered's grouping is
# about import *direction* (doesn't import upward); this contract is about *purity*
# (references nothing but itself + stdlib) — those are different properties that happen to
# coincide for errors.py/domain.py but not for context.py.

# it catches ANY future infrastructure dependency automatically, rather than needing this
# contract updated every time a new one is introduced. A domain exception that imports a
# transport package (to carry e.g. a wire-protocol code) couples the domain to one specific
# protocol and makes the exception meaningless outside that boundary — that mapping belongs
# at the actual dispatch boundary (wm_server.py), which is already infrastructure-aware. See

    "finecode.wm_server.errors",
    "finecode.wm_server.domain",
]
# Pre-existing debt, out of scope for the contract that introduced this rule — real

package org.gotson.komga.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption

import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.gotson.komga.Application
import org.springframework.stereotype.Controller
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController

@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [Application::class], importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class NamingConventionTest {
  @ArchTest
  val servicesShouldNotHaveNamesContainingServiceOrManager: ArchRule =
    noClasses()
      .that()
      .resideInAnyPackage("..domain..service..", "..application..service..")
      .should()
      .haveSimpleNameContaining("service")
      .orShould()
      .haveSimpleNameContaining("Service")
      .orShould()
      .haveSimpleNameContaining("manager")
      .orShould()
      .haveSimpleNameContaining("Manager")
      .because("it doesn't bear any intent")

  @ArchTest
  val controllersShouldBeSuffixed: ArchRule =
    classes()
      .that()
      .areAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java)
      .or()
      .areAnnotatedWith(Controller::class.java)
      .should()
      .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Controller")
}

# This "runtime" dependency group refers to dependencies that already
# exist in AWS Glue's runtime. We don't need to install these in the
# container.
#
# It is best to keep the dependencies here in sync with what's on Glue's
# documentation.
# https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-python-libraries.html#glue-modules-provided
[tool.poetry.group.runtime.dependencies]
aws-glue-libs = { git = "https://github.com/awslabs/aws-glue-libs.git", rev = "master" }
pyspark = "3.3.0"

[tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies]
pytest-randomly = "^3.15.0"
pytest-cov = "^5.0.0"
pre-commit = "^3.7.1"
import-linter = "^2.0"
ruff = "^0.5.4"
mypy = "^1.11.0"
pytest = "^8.3.1"


[tool.poetry.group.deploy.dependencies]
aws-cdk-lib = "^2.149.0"
cdk-nag = "^2.28.163"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
output-format = "full"
respect-gitignore = true
target-version = "py310"
exclude = ["snapshots", ".venv", ".ipynb_checkpoints"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
  # Line too long
  "E501",
  # pydocstyle
  "D",
  # Missing type annotation for `self` in method
  "ANN101",
  # To Do comments
  "TD002",
  "TD003",
  "FIX002",
  # Conflicts with ruff format
  "COM812",
  "ISC001",
]
# Allow unused variables when underscore-prefixed.
dummy-variable-rgx = "^(_+|(_+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+?))$"

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 7

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"**/test_*" = ["S101", "ANN", "PT", "PD"]

[tool.mypy]
packages = "glueetl"
python_version = "3.10"
show_error_codes = true
pretty = true
strict = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
implicit_reexport = true
explicit_package_bases = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "*.tests.*"
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_untyped_calls = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = ["--import-mode=importlib"]
filterwarnings = [
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
  "ignore::FutureWarning:.*pyspark.*",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
omit = ["**/test_*.py"]

[tool.coverage.report]
skip_empty = true
exclude_also = [
  "def __repr__",
  "if self.debug:",
  "if settings.DEBUG",
  "raise AssertionError",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  "if 0:",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
  "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
  "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["cdk", "glueetl"]
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Jobs and deployment code should not import from each other"
type = "independence"
modules = ["glueetl", "cdk"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Glue Job scripts should not use CDK"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["glueetl"]
forbidden_modules = ["aws_cdk"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "CDK code should follow layers architecture"
type = "layers"
layers = ["cdk.stacks", "cdk.constructs"]

# Virtual workspace root for the rAPIdy family. Published artifacts live in packages/*.
[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["packages/*"]

[tool.uv.sources]
rapidy-core = { workspace = true }

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "hypothesis>=6,<7",
    "ruff>=0.8,<1.0",
    "mypy>=1.14,<2.0",
    "pytest>=8.0,<9.0",
    "pytest-aiohttp>=1.0.5",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.0,<2.0",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0,<7.0",
    "pytest-httpserver>=1.0.8",
    "import-linter>=2.0,<3.0",
]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = ["dev"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["rapidy", "rapidy_client", "rapidy_core"]
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy_core stays independent from consumers"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy_core"]
forbidden_modules = ["rapidy", "rapidy_client"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy server does not import rapidy_client"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy"]
forbidden_modules = ["rapidy_client"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy_client does not import rapidy server"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy_client"]
forbidden_modules = ["rapidy"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy testing dependencies stay in rapidy.testing"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy"]
forbidden_modules = ["anyio", "httpx"]
ignore_imports = [
    "rapidy.testing.client -> anyio",
    "rapidy.testing.client -> httpx",
    "rapidy.testing.sse -> anyio",
    "rapidy.testing.sse -> httpx",
    "rapidy.testing.websocket -> anyio",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy server consumes Dishka through rapidy_core"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy"]
forbidden_modules = ["dishka"]
ignore_imports = ["rapidy.depends -> rapidy_core.di"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy generic validation stays ASGI-runtime free"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "rapidy.endpoint_handlers.attr_containers",
    "rapidy.endpoint_handlers.validation",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "rapidy.application",
    "rapidy.middlewares",
    "rapidy.request",
    "rapidy.response",
    "rapidy.routing",
    "rapidy.serve",
    "rapidy.websockets",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy_client: yarl only in _models"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy_client"]
forbidden_modules = ["yarl"]
ignore_imports = ["rapidy_client._models -> yarl"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy_client: foundation layering (_models > errors > _redaction)"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "rapidy_client._models",
    "rapidy_client.errors",
    "rapidy_client._redaction",
]
ignore_imports = ["rapidy_client.errors -> rapidy_client._models"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "httpx2/httpcore2 localized to transports.httpx (rule 5.1.1)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "rapidy_client._models",
    "rapidy_client._content",
    "rapidy_client._redaction",
    "rapidy_client._clock",
    "rapidy_client.errors",
    "rapidy_client.testing.chaos",
]
forbidden_modules = ["httpx2", "httpcore2"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rapidy_client: _models does not runtime-import config (rule 5, one-way)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy_client._models"]
forbidden_modules = ["rapidy_client.config"]
ignore_imports = ["rapidy_client._models -> rapidy_client.config"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "schema layer stays transport-free (rule 3, section 5.1)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy_client.schema"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "rapidy_client._client",
    "rapidy_client._pipeline",
    "rapidy_client.transports",
    "httpx2",
    "httpcore2",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "client DI uses only rapidy_core DI facade"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["rapidy_client.di"]
forbidden_modules = ["dishka"]
ignore_imports = ["rapidy_client.di -> rapidy_core.di"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "wsproto localized to ws.py (rule 5.1.1)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "rapidy_client._models",
    "rapidy_client._content",
    "rapidy_client._redaction",
    "rapidy_client._clock",
    "rapidy_client.errors",
    "rapidy_client.config",
    "rapidy_client._pipeline",
    "rapidy_client._client",
    "rapidy_client.sse",
    "rapidy_client.observability",
    "rapidy_client.transports.httpx",
    "rapidy_client.transports",
    "rapidy_client.testing.chaos",
]
forbidden_modules = ["wsproto"]
ignore_imports = [
    "rapidy_client._client -> rapidy_client.ws",
    "rapidy_client.sse -> rapidy_client._typed",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import-linter: enforce hexagonal architecture boundaries
#
# Layer dependency rules (→ = "may import from"):
#   domain  → (nothing)
#   ports   → domain
#   core    → domain, ports
#   adapters → domain, ports, core
#   metrics → domain, ports  (presentation layer, no core or adapter deps)
#
# The sole exception is core.applications — the composition root that wires
# concrete adapters into the core.  All 4 allowed imports are listed below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["pgqueuer"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain must not import from adapters, core, or metrics"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pgqueuer.domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["pgqueuer.adapters", "pgqueuer.core", "pgqueuer.metrics"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Ports must not import from adapters, core, or metrics"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pgqueuer.ports"]
forbidden_modules = ["pgqueuer.adapters", "pgqueuer.core", "pgqueuer.metrics"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Core must not import from adapters or metrics"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pgqueuer.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["pgqueuer.adapters", "pgqueuer.metrics"]
ignore_imports = [
    # applications.py is the composition root — it wires concrete adapters.
    "pgqueuer.core.applications -> pgqueuer.adapters.drivers.asyncpg",
    "pgqueuer.core.applications -> pgqueuer.adapters.drivers.psycopg",
    "pgqueuer.core.applications -> pgqueuer.adapters.persistence.queries",
    "pgqueuer.core.applications -> pgqueuer.adapters.inmemory",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Metrics must not import from adapters or core"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pgqueuer.metrics"]
forbidden_modules = ["pgqueuer.adapters", "pgqueuer.core"]

		.haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Manager")
		.should()

		.areAssignableTo(Service::class.java)
		.should()
		.haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Service")
		.because("they should be easy to find")

		.haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Service")

		.haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Intent")

		.beAssignableTo(Intent::class.java)

		.areAnnotatedWith(IntentHandler::class.java)

		.bePrivate()
		.because("only the framework is supposed to invoke these methods")

}

[tool.ruff.lint]
ignore = [
    "COM812",  # ignore trailing comma errors due to older Python versions
    "PD011",   # ignore .values usage since ruff assumes it's a Pandas DataFrame
    "PLR0913", # ignore too many arguments in function definitions
    "PLW1514", # allow Path.open without encoding
    "RET505",  # allow `else` blocks
    "RET506",  # allow `else` blocks
    "S311",    # allow standard pseudo-random generators
    "TC001",   # ignore imports used only for type checking
    "TC002",   # ignore imports used only for type checking
    "TC003",   # ignore imports used only for type checking
    "FIX002",  # Allow TODO comments
    "FIX004",  # Allow HACK comments
]
select = [
    # Rules reference: https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/

    # Code Style / Formatting
    "E",      # pycodestyle: checks adherence to PEP 8 conventions including spacing, indentation, and line length
    "W",      # pycodestyle: checks adherence to PEP 8 conventions including spacing, indentation, and line length
    "A",      # flake8-builtins: prevents shadowing of Python built-in names
    "C",      # Convention: ensures code adheres to specific style and formatting conventions
    "COM",    # flake8-commas: enforces the correct use of trailing commas
    "ERA",    # eradicate: detects commented-out code that should be removed
    "I",      # isort: ensures imports are sorted in a consistent manner
    "ICN",    # flake8-import-conventions: enforces import conventions for better readability
    "N",      # pep8-naming: enforces PEP 8 naming conventions for classes, functions, and variables
    "NPY",    # NumPy: enforces best practices for using the NumPy library
    "PD",     # pandas-vet: enforces best practices for using the pandas library
    "PT",     # flake8-pytest-style: enforces best practices and style conventions for pytest tests
    "PTH",    # flake8-use-pathlib: encourages the use of pathlib over os.path for file system operations
    "Q",      # flake8-quotes: enforces consistent use of single or double quotes
    "TCH",    # flake8-type-checking: enforces type checking practices and standards
    "TID",    # flake8-tidy-imports: enforces tidy and well-organized imports
    "RUF022", # flake8-ruff: enforce sorting of __all__ in modules

    # Code Structure / Complexity
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions: improves readability and performance of list, set, and dict comprehensions
    "C90", # mccabe: checks for overly complex code using cyclomatic complexity
    "ISC", # flake8-implicit-str-concat: prevents implicit string concatenation
    "PIE", # flake8-pie: identifies and corrects common code inefficiencies and mistakes
    "R",   # Refactor: suggests improvements to code structure and readability
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify: simplifies complex expressions and improves code readability

    # Code Security / Bug Prevention
    "ARG",   # flake8-unused-arguments: detects unused function and method arguments
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async: identifies incorrect or inefficient usage patterns in asynchronous code
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear: detects common programming mistakes and potential bugs
    "BLE",   # flake8-blind-except: prevents blind exceptions that catch all exceptions without handling
    "E",     # Error: detects and reports errors in the code
    "F",     # Pyflakes: detects unused imports, shadowed imports, undefined variables, and various formatting errors in string operations
    "INP",   # flake8-no-pep420: prevents implicit namespace packages by requiring __init__.py
    "PGH",   # pygrep-hooks: detects deprecated and dangerous code patterns
    "PL",    # Pylint: comprehensive source code analyzer for enforcing coding standards and detecting errors
    "RSE",   # flake8-raise: ensures exceptions are raised correctly
    "S",     # flake8-bandit: detects security issues and vulnerabilities in the code
    "SLF",   # flake8-self: prevents incorrect usage of the self argument in class methods
    "T10",   # flake8-debugger: detects the presence of debugging tools such as pdb
    "T20",   # flake8-print: detects print statements left in the code
    "UP",    # pyupgrade: automatically upgrades syntax for newer versions of Python
    "W",     # Warning: provides warnings about potential issues in the code
    "YTT",   # flake8-2020: identifies code that will break with future Python releases

    # Code Documentation
    "FIX", # flake8-fixme: detects FIXMEs and other temporary comments that should be resolved
]

[tool.ruff.lint.extend-per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = [
    "S101",    # asserts allowed in tests
    "ARG",     # Unused function args allowed in tests
    "PLR2004", # Magic value used in comparison
    "TCH002",  # No import only type checking in tests
    "SLF001",  # enable private member access in tests
    "S105",    # allow hardcoded passwords in tests
    "S311",    # allow standard pseudo-random generators in tests
    "PT011",   # allow generic exceptions in tests
    "N806",    # allow uppercase variable names in tests
    "PGH003",  # allow general ignores in tests
    "S106",    # allow hardcoded passwords in tests
    "PLR0915", # allow complex statements in tests
]
"scripts/**/*.py" = [
    "T201",    # print statements are allowed
    "INP001",  # scripts/ is not a package
    "S603",    # scripts invoke external programs like git by design
    "S607",    # scripts resolve external programs from PATH on purpose
]
"contrib/**/*.py" = [
    "T201",    # print statements are allowed
    "INP001",  # contrib/ is not a package
]
"tests/js/**/*.py" = [
    "INP001",  # Node test helpers live beside package.json, not as a Python package
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["guidellm", "tests"]


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "guidellm"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Enforce import layers"
type = "layers"
containers = ["guidellm"]
layers = [
  "__main__",
  "cli",
  "entrypoints",
  "benchmark | mock_server",
  "data | backends",
  "scheduler",
  # utils/extras/schemas can interdepend so treat
  # them as one layer and check with a separate rule
  "utils : extras : schemas",
  "logger",
  "settings",
]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = ["version"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Check acyclic siblings on utility modules"
type = "acyclic_siblings"
ancestors = [
    "guidellm.utils",
    "guidellm.schemas",
    "guidellm.extras",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

type = "forbidden"

  "guidellm.scheduler",
  "guidellm.backends",
  "guidellm.schemas",
  "guidellm.schemas.**",
]

  "datasets",
  "transformers",
  "torch",
  "numpy",
]

    "guidellm.mock_server",
]

]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter — enforces the layered architecture documented in
# unique_toolkit/experimental/README.md. Contracts are scoped to the
# experimental/ subpackage; the rest of the toolkit keeps its existing
# (un-layered) shape until modules graduate into the new layout.
#
# Run:  uv run poe check-imports   (or: uv run lint-imports)
#
# Rules encoded below:
#   1. integrations → resources → _internal   (layers)
#   2. components → resources → _internal   (layers; peer of integrations)
#   3. components never import integrations (keeps orchestration framework-agnostic)
#   4. primitive resources are mutually independent
#   5. primitives never import facades (dependency direction inside resources/)
#   6. facades compose primitives only — never unique_sdk / components / integrations
#   7. components never call unique_sdk directly (go through a resource)
#   8. each integrations/<framework>/ stands alone — enabled when real modules land
#
# Imports under ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` are excluded from the graph (see
# ``exclude_type_checking_imports``) so type-only imports (e.g. ``unique_sdk``)
# do not violate layer/forbidden contracts. Runtime imports are still enforced.
#
# Preference rules from the README that are NOT machine-enforced (import-linter
# is pass/fail, not tiered): integrations prefer facades over primitives;
# integrations importing components is "discouraged but allowed".
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["unique_toolkit"]
include_external_packages = true
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "experimental: integrations stack (integrations → resources → _internal)"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.integrations",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental._internal",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "experimental: components stack (components → resources → _internal)"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.components",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental._internal",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "experimental: components never import integrations"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["unique_toolkit.experimental.components"]
forbidden_modules = ["unique_toolkit.experimental.integrations"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "experimental: primitive resources are independent"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.user",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.group",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.content_folder",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.scheduled_task",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "experimental: primitives never import facades"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.user",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.group",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.content_folder",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.scheduled_task",
]
forbidden_modules = ["unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.facades"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "experimental: facades never import other facades"
type = "independence"
modules = ["unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.facades.*"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "experimental: facades compose primitives only"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["unique_toolkit.experimental.resources.facades"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "unique_sdk",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.components",
    "unique_toolkit.experimental.integrations",
]
# Facades legitimately reach `unique_sdk` transitively through primitive
# resources (that's the whole point). This flag restricts the check to
# *direct* `import unique_sdk` statements inside facade modules.
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "experimental: components never call unique_sdk directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["unique_toolkit.experimental.components"]
forbidden_modules = ["unique_sdk"]
# Components are allowed to reach `unique_sdk` indirectly through a
# resource or an existing toolkit service; the rule only bans a *direct*
# `import unique_sdk` inside a component module.
allow_indirect_imports = true

# Uncomment and populate once concrete integrations exist under
# unique_toolkit/experimental/integrations/<framework>/.
# [[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# name = "experimental: integrations are mutually independent"
# type = "independence"
# modules = [
#     "unique_toolkit.experimental.integrations.openai",
#     "unique_toolkit.experimental.integrations.langchain",

# --- Silenced rules ---
# Any-cascade: all triggered by untyped third-party code; fixing requires
# sprinkling `Any` everywhere which defeats the purpose.
reportAny = "none"

reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"

reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportUnknownLambdaType = "none"

reportUnannotatedClassAttribute = "none"

reportDeprecated = "none"

# Third-party libraries that ship no type stubs.
reportMissingTypeStubs = "none"

# Structural: circular imports require architectural refactoring.
reportImportCycles = "none"

# Style preferences.

reportCallInDefaultInitializer = "none"

# Intentional patterns: callers often discard return values on purpose.
reportUnusedCallResult = "none"
reportUnusedParameter = "none"

# Toolkit legitimately accesses SDK-internal symbols.
reportPrivateUsage = "none"
reportPrivateLocalImportUsage = "none"

[tool.pixi.pypi-dependencies]
esm = { path = ".", editable = true }

[tool.pixi.tasks]
build-wheel = "python -m pip wheel --no-deps -w dist ."
upload-wheel = "python -m twine upload --repository pypi"

[tool.pixi.feature.dev.dependencies]
matplotlib = "*"
numpy = ">=2.0.0,<2.4"
pre-commit = "*"
pytest = "*"
pytest-cov = "*"
pytest-xdist = "*"
seaborn = "*"
ty = "==0.0.49"

[tool.pixi.feature.dev.pypi-dependencies]
# DockQ is optional at runtime. Keep the NumPy 2-compatible fork in the dev
# environment for tests without publishing its direct URL in package metadata.
dockq = { git = "https://github.com/nrontsis/DockQ.git", rev = "ba4df5adaad7c77fd60851d0b7b05f2b77061ba2" }

[tool.pixi.feature.dev.tasks]
lint-all = "pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure"
cov-test = "pytest -v --junitxml=pytest.xml --cov=esm"

[tool.pixi.feature.fused]
platforms = ["linux-64"]

[tool.pixi.feature.fused.pypi-dependencies]
flash_attn = { url = "https://github.com/evolutionaryscale/wheels/releases/download/py312-pt211-cu13-sm80-90/flash_attn-2.7.4.post1-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl" }
xformers = { url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130/xformers-0.0.35-py39-none-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl" }
cuequivariance-torch = ">=0.8.1"
cuequivariance-ops-torch-cu13 = ">=0.8.1"

# `gpu` stays on 3.12: the prebuilt flash_attn wheel in `fused` is cp312-only.
[tool.pixi.environments]
default = {features = ["py312"], solve-group = "default"}
dev = {features = ["dev", "py312"], solve-group = "default"}
gpu = {features = ["dev", "fused", "py312"], solve-group = "default"}
dev-py313 = {features = ["dev", "py313"], solve-group = "py313"}
dev-py314 = {features = ["dev", "py314"], solve-group = "py314"}

[tool.ruff]
extend-include = ["*.ipynb"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Enable Pyflakes (`F`) and a subset of the pycodestyle (`E`), sort imports ('I')
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "I"]
ignore = [
    # allow variable == False (tensors should do this)
    "E712",
    # allow assigning of lambdas
    "E731",
    # Allow ambiguous variables, e.g. we use O for oxygen
    "E741",
    # Ignore errors from jaxtyping hints
    # https://docs.kidger.site/jaxtyping/faq/#flake8-or-ruff-are-throwing-an-error
    "F722",
    # TODO: Fix the few offenders in a follow up PR
    "E721",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
split-on-trailing-comma = false
known-third-party = ["wandb"]

[tool.ruff.format]
skip-magic-trailing-comma = true
docstring-code-format = true
docstring-code-line-length = "dynamic"

[tool.isort]
known_third_party = ["wandb"]

[tool.ty.src]
# gitignore-style globs. Skip notebooks, tests, and the Modal-app tutorial whose deps
# (modal, abnumber) and dynamic decorators aren't resolvable in the lint env.
exclude = [
    "**/*.ipynb",
    "**/*_test.py",
    "**/test_*.py",
    "**/tests/",
    "**/conftest.py",
    "cookbook/tutorials/binder_design.py",
]

[tool.ty.rules]
# Strict LSP override-compatibility checking that pyright `basic` never enforced; low
# value for duck-typed ML code.
invalid-method-override = "ignore"
# flash_attn resolves only where it's installed (a GPU environment); the ignores it
# requires there read as unused/redundant in this CPU lint env where it's absent.
unused-ignore-comment = "ignore"
unused-type-ignore-comment = "ignore"

[tool.ty.analysis]
# ty can't introspect optional/compiled deps absent from this lint env (flash_attn is
# GPU-only; zstd is a C-extension), so it falsely reports them unresolved. Treat as Any
# rather than disabling unresolved-import, so genuinely-broken first-party imports still
# surface.
replace-imports-with-any = [
    "biotite.database",
    "biotite.database.**",
    "biotite.structure",
    "biotite.structure.**",
    "biotite.sequence.align",
    "biotite.sequence.align.**",
    "scipy.spatial",
    "transformer_engine",
    "transformer_engine.**",
    "transformer_engine_torch",
    "xformers",
    "xformers.**",
    "cuequivariance_torch",
    "cuequivariance_torch.**",
    "flash_attn",
    "flash_attn.**",
    "zstd",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "esm"

[importlinter]
include_external_packages = True
root_packages =
    domain
    application
    infrastructure
    presentation

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Dependencies point inward only
type = layers
layers =
    presentation
    infrastructure
    application
    domain

[importlinter:contract:domain-is-framework-free]
name = The domain layer knows about no framework
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    domain
forbidden_modules =
    litestar
    sqlalchemy
    pydantic
    httpx
    redis
    faststream
    aio_pika
    alembic
    prometheus_client
    opentelemetry

[importlinter:contract:application-is-framework-free]
name = The application layer knows about no framework
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    application
forbidden_modules =
    litestar
    sqlalchemy
    httpx
    redis
    faststream
    aio_pika
    alembic
    prometheus_client

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = [
    "src/application",
    "src/domain",
    "src/infrastructure",
    "src/presentation"
]

[project]
name = "backend-template"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Ory Hydra login & consent provider: OIDC/OAuth2, RBAC, TOTP 2FA, sessions, audit log, transactional outbox"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    "alembic>=1.18.4",
    "asyncpg>=0.31.0",
    "bcrypt>=5.0.0",
    "faststream[cli,rabbit]>=0.6.7",
    "greenlet>=3.4.0",
    "litestar[opentelemetry]>=2.22.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.30.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.51b0",
    "pyjwt>=2.13.0",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.49",
    "pyotp>=2.9.0",
    "redis>=5.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.6",
    "aiosmtplib>=5.1.2",
    "dishka>=1.10.1",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30.0",
    "prometheus-client>=0.26.0",
]

# Security floors for packages nothing here depends on directly. Each was flagged by
# `pip-audit` in CI; the version is the advisory's fix release. Constraints rather than
# dependencies, because this project should not claim to import them -- they arrive via
# uvicorn/faststream (click), httpx/anyio (idna) and alembic (mako).
[tool.uv]
constraint-dependencies = [
    "click>=8.3.3",   # PYSEC-2026-2132
    "idna>=3.15",     # PYSEC-2026-215
    "mako>=1.3.12",   # PYSEC-2026-2617
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "basedpyright>=1.39.2",
    "ruff>=0.15.11",
    "pytest>=9.0.3",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "faker>=30.0.0",
    "import-linter>=2.15",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = "-v --tb=short"
markers = [
    "integration: needs a real Postgres (skipped unless testcontainers is available)",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src"]
branch = true
omit = ["*/migrations/*"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
exclude_also = [
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "\\.\\.\\.$",
]

[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["src", "tests"]
ignore = ["**/migrations"]
typeCheckingMode = "all"
stubPath = "stubs"

[[tool.basedpyright.executionEnvironments]]
# Tests lean on fakes, fixtures and MagicMock doubles, which "all" reports as Unknown-typed
# noise. Everything else stays on, so genuine type errors in tests are still caught.
root = "tests"
reportUnknownMemberType = false
reportUnknownArgumentType = false
reportUnknownVariableType = false
reportUnknownParameterType = false
reportUnknownLambdaType = false
reportMissingParameterType = false
reportMissingTypeArgument = false
reportAny = false
reportExplicitAny = false
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = false
reportUnusedCallResult = false
reportPrivateUsage = false
# A pytest fixture is never called by name, and a test may request one purely for its side
# effect; both read as "unused" to a type checker but are how the framework works.
reportUnusedFunction = false
reportUnusedParameter = false

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py314"
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "F",      # pyflakes
    "E", "W", # pycodestyle
    "I",      # isort
    "N",      # pep8-naming
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "B",      # bugbear
    "S",      # bandit
    "ASYNC",  # async antipatterns
    "DTZ",    # naive datetimes
    "C4",     # comprehensions
    "SIM",    # simplify
    "RET",    # return
    "ARG",    # unused arguments
    "PIE",    # misc lints
    "PERF",   # performance
    "PTH",    # pathlib
    "TID",    # tidy imports
    "EM",     # exception messages
    "TRY",    # tryceratops
    "A",      # builtin shadowing
    "RUF",    # ruff-specific
]
ignore = [
    "TRY003",  # long messages live on our exception classes' `detail`, not at the raise site
    "EM101",   # ditto: domain errors take the message as a dataclass field
    "EM102",
    "TRY300",  # `return` in `try` is fine and often clearer than an `else:` block
    "RUF001",  # Cyrillic look-alikes are intentional in comments
    "RUF002",
    "RUF003",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = [
    "S101",    # assert is the point
    "S105", "S106",  # test fixtures carry obviously fake secrets
    "ARG001", "ARG002",  # fakes must match the port signature
    "SLF001",
]
"src/infrastructure/db/sqlalchemy/migrations/**" = ["ALL"]
# `path`, `guards`, `dependencies` are Litestar's declarative class attributes; annotating
# them as ClassVar contradicts the framework's own typing of Controller.
"src/presentation/http/controllers/**" = ["RUF012"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["domain", "application", "infrastructure", "presentation"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "parents"

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "single"
docstring-code-format = true

package org.goafabric.calleeservice.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition
import org.goafabric.calleeservice.Application
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration
import org.springframework.web.service.annotation.HttpExchange

@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [Application::class], importOptions = [DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class AdapterRulesTest {
    @ArchTest
    val adapterName: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.methods().that()
        .areMetaAnnotatedWith(HttpExchange::class.java)
        .should().beDeclaredInClassesThat().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Adapter")
        .allowEmptyShould(true)

    @ArchTest
    val declarativeClientShouldBeUsed: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses().that()
        .areNotAnnotatedWith(Configuration::class.java)
            .and().areNotAnnotatedWith(SpringBootApplication::class.java)
        .should()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .haveFullyQualifiedName("org.springframework.web.client.RestClient")
        .orShould().dependOnClassesThat()
        .haveFullyQualifiedName("org.springframework.web.client.RestTemplate")
        .orShould().dependOnClassesThat()
        .haveFullyQualifiedName("org.springframework.web.reactive.function.client.WebClient")
        .`as`("Only use the declarative REST Client, as otherwise native image support is broken")
        .allowEmptyShould(false)


    @ArchTest
    val declarativeClientShouldUserCircuitBreaker: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.methods().that()
        .areMetaAnnotatedWith(HttpExchange::class.java)
        .should()
        .beDeclaredInClassesThat()
        .areMetaAnnotatedWith("io.github.resilience4j.circuitbreaker.annotation.CircuitBreaker")
        .allowEmptyShould(true)
}

package org.goafabric.calleeservice.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.Location
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition
import org.goafabric.calleeservice.Application
import org.springframework.aot.hint.RuntimeHintsRegistrar
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.condition.ConditionalOnProperty
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration
import org.springframework.context.annotation.ImportRuntimeHints
import kotlin.jvm.java

@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [Application::class], importOptions = [DoNotIncludeTests::class, ApplicationRulesTest.IgnoreCglib::class])
class ApplicationRulesTest {
    @ArchTest
    val reflectionShouldBeAvoided: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses()
        .that()
        .areNotAnnotatedWith(Configuration::class.java)
        .and()
        .doNotImplement(RuntimeHintsRegistrar::class.java)
        .and()
        .haveSimpleNameNotContaining("AuditTrailListener").and().resideOutsideOfPackage("..persistence.entity..")
        .should()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .resideInAPackage("java.lang.reflect")
        .orShould()
        .callMethod(Class::class.java, "forName", String::class.java)
        .orShould()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .haveFullyQualifiedName("org.springframework.util.ReflectionUtils")
        .orShould()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .haveFullyQualifiedName("org.springframework.beans.BeanWrapperImpl")
        .orShould()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .haveFullyQualifiedName("jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidator")
        .orShould()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .areAnnotatedWith(ConditionalOnProperty::class.java)
        .because("Reflection breaks native image support");


    @ArchTest
    val aspectsNeedRuntimeHint: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that()
        .areAnnotatedWith("org.aspectj.lang.annotation.Aspect").should()
        .beAnnotatedWith(ImportRuntimeHints::class.java)
        .allowEmptyShould(true)
        .because("Aspects need a Reflection RuntimeHint with MemberCategory.INVOKE_DECLARED_METHODS")

    @ArchTest
    val librariesThatAreBanished: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses()
        .should()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .resideInAPackage("com.google.common..")
        .orShould()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .resideInAPackage("org.apache.commons..")
        .because("Java 21+ and Spring cover the functionality already, managing extra libraries with transient dependencies should be avoided")

    @ArchTest
    val onlyAllowedLibraries: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .should()
        .onlyDependOnClassesThat()
        .resideInAnyPackage(
            "org.goafabric..",
            "java..",
            "javax..",
            "jakarta..",
            "org.springframework..",
            "org.slf4j..",
            "com.fasterxml.jackson..","tools.jackson..",
            "org.flywaydb..",
            "org.hibernate..",
            "org.mapstruct..",
            "io.github.resilience4j..",
            "io.micrometer..",
            "org.springdoc..",
            "net.ttddyy..",

            "io.swagger.v3..",
            "com.github.benmanes.caffeine..",
            "com.azure.storage.blob..",
            "software.amazon.awssdk..", "io.awspring.cloud..",

            "org.javers..",
            "com.nimbusds.jwt..",
            "tools.jackson.databind.jsontype..",

            "org.aspectj..",
            "io.opentelemetry..",

            "kotlin..",
            "kotlinx..",
            "org.jetbrains.annotations.."
        )
        .because("Only core and allowed libraries should be used to avoid unnecessary third-party dependencies")

    @ArchTest
    val componentNamesThatAreBanished: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses()
        .that().haveSimpleNameNotContaining("Mapper")
        .should()
        .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Impl")
        .andShould()
        .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Management")
        .because("Avoid filler names like Impl or Management, use neutral Bean instead")

    @ArchTest
    val asyncIsBanished: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.noMethods().should()
        .beAnnotatedWith(org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Async::class.java)
        .because("Using Async leads to ThreadLocals being erased, Exceptions being swallowed, Resilience4j not working and possible Concurrency Issues in General")

    @ArchTest
    val flywayJavaMigrationsAreBanished: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses().should().dependOnClassesThat()
        .resideInAnyPackage("org.flywaydb.core.api.migration..")
        .because("Flyway Java Migrations should not be used, complex import logic should go to a separate batch, simple ones with a simple Java class if aware of the consequences")

    class IgnoreCglib : ImportOption {
        override fun includes(location: Location): Boolean {
            return !location.contains("$$") && !location.contains("EnhancerByCGLIB")
        }
    }
}

package org.goafabric.calleeservice.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.base.DescribedPredicate
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClass
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchCondition
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ConditionEvents
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures
import org.goafabric.calleeservice.Application

@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [Application::class], importOptions = [DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class PersistenceRulesTest {
    @ArchTest
    val layerAreRespectedWithPersistence: ArchRule = Architectures.layeredArchitecture()
        .consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers()
        .ignoreDependency(
            JavaClass.Predicates.simpleNameStartingWith("DemoDataImporter"),
            DescribedPredicate.alwaysTrue()
        )

        .layer("Controller").definedBy("..controller")
        .layer("Logic").definedBy("..logic..")
        .layer("Persistence").definedBy("..persistence..")

        .whereLayer("Controller").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
        .whereLayer("Logic").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controller")
        .whereLayer("Persistence").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Logic")
        .allowEmptyShould(true)

    @ArchTest
    val classesExtendingRepositoryShouldEndWithRepository: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that().areAssignableTo("org.springframework.data.repository.Repository")
        .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Repository")
        .because("all classes extending Repository should end with 'Repository' in their name")
        .allowEmptyShould(true)


    @ArchTest
    val logicAnnotatedWithTransactional: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that().areAssignableTo("org.springframework.data.repository.Repository")
        .should(object : ArchCondition<JavaClass?>("Repository used") {
            override fun check(item: JavaClass?, events: ConditionEvents) {
                ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
                    .that().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Logic")
                    .should().beAnnotatedWith("org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional")
                    .because("Logic Classes should be annotated with @Transactional")
                    .check(ClassFileImporter().importPackagesOf(Application::class.java))
            }
        }
        ).allowEmptyShould(true)
}
