/**
 * The import graph, read as a graph rather than as text.
 *
 * Twenty-one bespoke audits live in `scripts/`, twelve thousand lines of them,
 * and not one asks a question about the shape of the module graph. Grepping
 * `scripts/` and every `tests` directory under `packages` and `apps` for
 * `circular|cycle` on 2026-08-06 returns four lines: two are prose about the
 * traditional text's arithmetic, one is a comment about a hanging test, and the
 * fourth — `packages/engine/tests/runnable.test.ts:152`, "terminates on a
 * cycle, because modules import each other" — asserts that a walker does not
 * hang on a two-file cycle in a tree the test builds in memory. Not one of them
 * asks whether THIS repository has a cycle. No test anywhere asserts that a
 * package may not reach an app. That is the class this file covers, and it is
 * the reason it exists: not a tool that replaces a sweep, but a reader for
 * something nobody was reading. **Nothing is deleted for this file. There was
 * nothing to delete.**
 *
 * dependency-cruiser 18.1.1, installed as a root devDependency on 2026-08-06,
 * run as `bun run depcruise` — which is `node_modules/.bin/depcruise`, the
 * local binary, for a reason given at length below.
 *
 * ---
 *
 * THE TWO GRAPHS, MEASURED 2026-08-06 over `packages apps`, with the options
 * this file sets (`node_modules` not followed, `node_modules|dist|data`
 * excluded). Both numbers are this tool's own `summary.totalCruised` and
 * `summary.totalDependenciesCruised`, read out of `--output-type json`.
 *
 *     graph                              modules  dependencies  violations
 *     ---------------------------------  -------  ------------  ----------
 *     RUNTIME   tsPreCompilationDeps:false    333           902           0
 *     TYPE-AWARE tsPreCompilationDeps:'specify' 335          968           9
 *
 * Those four counts are a SNAPSHOT and they drift, faster than one might think:
 * three test files landed in this tree between the first cruise run while this
 * file was being written and the last, taking the runtime graph from 329/887 to
 * 333/902 in under twenty minutes. Nothing is asserted against them. The
 * companion test's threshold is walked off the disk on every run precisely so
 * that no check in this repository depends on a number in a comment.
 *
 * The runtime graph is what this config cruises and what the rules below are
 * enforced over. It is green today, on every rule, and it went in green
 * deliberately: a rule that is red the day it is written is a rule somebody
 * turns off, and a rule that has only ever been green can still only go red for
 * the reason it was written down.
 *
 * The two graphs differ by two modules and sixty-six dependencies, and that gap
 * has been stable across every pair of runs measured today. The two
 * extra modules are `grammy/types` and `scripts/lib/spillover.d.mts` — both
 * reachable only through a type position, so neither exists at run time. The
 * sixty-six extra edges are `import type` and `import { type X }`: real to
 * `tsc`, absent from the emitted JavaScript.
 *
 * That difference is not a detail. It is the whole disagreement between the two
 * readings, and it is what the nine type-aware violations are made of:
 *
 *   1 type-only cycle    apps/bot/src/commands.ts <-> apps/bot/src/render.ts
 *   6 tests -> apps      packages/{engine,journal}/tests into apps/* (below)
 *   2 tests -> other app apps/mobile/tests/{contrast,fields}.test.ts into
 *                        apps/miniapp/src/contrast.ts
 *
 * ---
 *
 * WHY THE RUNTIME GRAPH, AND WHY madge WAS REJECTED FOR THIS REPOSITORY.
 *
 * madge is the obvious tool for "find me the cycles" and it is the wrong one
 * here, measured rather than argued. madge 8.0.0, installed into a scratch
 * directory outside this tree on 2026-08-06 so that nothing was added to this
 * repository to run it:
 *
 *     $ madge --extensions ts,tsx --circular packages apps
 *     Processed 338 files (1.6s) (1 warning)
 *     x Found 1 circular dependency!
 *     1) apps/bot/src/commands.ts > apps/bot/src/render.ts
 *     $ echo $?
 *     1
 *
 * It exits 1. On correct code. `apps/bot/src/render.ts:12` is
 *
 *     import type { Room } from './commands';
 *
 * — a type-only import, erased before anything runs. There is no cycle at run
 * time; `commands.ts` imports `render.ts` and `render.ts` imports nothing back.
 * madge does not distinguish the two, so the only finding it has ever produced
 * over this tree is a false one, and a check that cries wolf on correct code is
 * one somebody deletes rather than obeys. dependency-cruiser with
 * `tsPreCompilationDeps: false` does not report it, because the edge is not in
 * the graph it builds — the distinction is made by construction, not by an
 * exemption entry, which is why there is no exemption entry for it below.
 *
 * RETRACTED, and left here rather than removed. An earlier pass recorded that
 * `madge --ts-config` *crashes* in this repository. Re-run on 2026-08-06 at
 * madge 8.0.0 against `apps/bot/tsconfig.json`, both over `apps/bot/src` and
 * over `packages apps`, it does not crash: it completes and prints the same
 * single false cycle. Assume the crash was a different madge or a different
 * tsconfig; it is not reproducible here and is not a reason to reject the tool.
 * The false cycle above is, and it is the only reason needed.
 *
 * AND THE TWO READERS WERE PUT SIDE BY SIDE ON THE SAME PLANTED FAULT, because
 * "madge is wrong about `render.ts`" is one file's word against another's until
 * somebody makes the fault on purpose. Two temporary probes were written into
 * `packages/engine/src` on 2026-08-06 and deleted the moment each run finished:
 *
 *   - `zz-cycle-probe.ts` importing a value from `zz-cycle-probe-b.ts` and
 *     `zz-cycle-probe-b.ts` importing a value back. A REAL runtime cycle.
 *     dependency-cruiser: exit 1, `no-circular`, the cycle printed as a path.
 *     madge: exit 1, two cycles found — the probe and its standing false one.
 *     Both readers name it. Agreement.
 *   - The same two files with one edge changed to `import type`. Nothing else
 *     touched. dependency-cruiser: `v no dependency violations found (335
 *     modules, 903 dependencies cruised)`, exit 0 — correct, because after
 *     erasure nothing cycles. madge: still `Found 2 circular dependencies`,
 *     exit 1.
 *
 * The difference between the two tools is exactly the difference between those
 * two runs, and it is not a matter of taste: one of them goes red on code that
 * has no defect, and this repository has written down at length why a check
 * that cries wolf is one people delete rather than obey.
 *
 * ---
 *
 * WHY `bun run depcruise` AND NEVER `npx --yes dependency-cruiser`.
 *
 * This is this repository's own favourite defect — a check nobody can run reads
 * exactly like a check that passes — and dependency-cruiser produces it by
 * default, in its own output, with the reassuring half first. dependency-cruiser
 * needs a resolvable `typescript` to parse TypeScript at all. Run through
 * `npx --yes`, from a directory where `typescript` does not resolve, against
 * this very config and this very tree:
 *
 *     $ npx --yes dependency-cruiser --config .../.dependency-cruiser.mjs \
 *         --output-type err-long <leela>/packages <leela>/apps
 *     v no dependency violations found (11 modules, 5 dependencies cruised)
 *
 *     !! missing-typescript-transpiler: dependency-cruiser detected a TypeScript
 *        environment, but not a compatible TypeScript compiler ...
 *        it's likely to have missed TypeScript sources and dependencies.
 *     $ echo $?
 *     0
 *
 * **Eleven modules of three hundred and thirty-three, a green tick, and exit 0.**
 * The reason is printed, and it is printed BELOW the tick — a human skims the
 * first line, CI reads the exit code, and neither of them ever learns that
 * ninety-seven per cent of the tree went unread. The same command run from the
 * repository root, where `typescript@5.6.3` resolves, cruises the full graph.
 * So the failure is not "the tool is broken"; it is "the tool silently agrees
 * with you when it cannot see anything", which is worse.
 *
 * Two things follow, and both are in the tree rather than in this paragraph:
 *
 *   - The root script pins the local binary. `bun run depcruise` resolves
 *     `depcruise` from `node_modules/.bin`, beside the `typescript` this
 *     repository installs.
 *   - The exit code is not trusted on its own. THE COUNT GUARD in
 *     `packages/journal/tests/a-package-that-needs-an-app.test.ts` re-runs this
 *     cruise as JSON and asserts that the number of modules cruised is at least
 *     the number of `.ts`/`.tsx` files on disk under every workspace's `src`
 *     directory, counted by walking the disk rather than written down.
 *     Sixty-nine files today, three hundred and thirty-three modules cruised;
 *     the eleven-module run above fails it. A green tick over an empty graph is
 *     the failure mode this whole wiring is built around.
 *
 * ---
 *
 * THE BOUNDARY NO MANIFEST DECLARES, and the reason it is not forbidden here.
 *
 * Six edges run from a package's test suite into an application's source. They
 * are deliberate — they are cross-surface agreement tests, the mechanism by
 * which four surfaces are held to one answer — and forbidding them would be
 * deleting the thing they protect. They are also completely undeclared: not one
 * of the manifests below names the app it needs.
 *
 *   packages/engine/tests/one-question-two-surfaces.test.ts
 *       -> apps/miniapp/src/view.ts
 *       -> apps/mobile/src/game.ts
 *   packages/journal/tests/between-the-surfaces.test.ts
 *       -> apps/bot/src/take-in.ts
 *       -> apps/bot/src/take-out.ts
 *       -> apps/miniapp/src/journal-file.ts
 *       -> apps/mobile/src/journal.ts
 *
 * So the two source packages are **packages/engine** and **packages/journal**,
 * and the three apps they reach are **apps/miniapp**, **apps/mobile** and
 * **apps/bot**. `packages/journal/package.json` declares exactly one workspace
 * dependency, `@leela/engine`, and its suite cannot run without three
 * applications on disk. `packages/engine/package.json` declares no workspace
 * dependency at all, and its suite cannot run without two. A person cloning
 * this repository and running `cd packages/journal && vitest run` on the
 * strength of the manifest is running something the manifest does not describe.
 *
 * There is no `ignore` entry for these edges and there is no rule forbidding
 * them. Instead the statement above is mandatory: the companion test derives
 * the set of such edges from this tool's JSON, on every run, and fails unless
 * every source package and every app it reaches is named in this doc-comment.
 * Add a seventh edge into a fourth app and the test goes red until this
 * paragraph says so. The set is derived; it is not a list somebody remembered
 * to update.
 *
 * The two `apps/mobile/tests -> apps/miniapp/src` edges are the same shape one
 * surface over and are recorded above for completeness. They are not covered by
 * the guard, which asks only about packages, and saying so is cheaper than
 * pretending otherwise.
 *
 * ---
 *
 * WHAT IS ENFORCED. Two rules, both green on the day they were written, both
 * over the runtime graph.
 */
export default {
  forbidden: [
    /**
     * A cycle at RUN TIME. Not a cycle in the type graph — see the madge
     * paragraph above: `apps/bot/src/commands.ts` and `apps/bot/src/render.ts`
     * form one in the type graph and it is harmless, because
     * `render.ts:12` is `import type`. `tsPreCompilationDeps: false` keeps that
     * edge out of the graph entirely, so this rule cannot fire on it and needs
     * no exemption to avoid doing so.
     *
     * MEASURED zero violations over 333 modules and 902 dependencies on the day
     * it went in. A runtime cycle in an ES-module graph is a module that reads a
     * binding from a neighbour that has not finished evaluating, which is
     * `undefined` at exactly one point in the program and correct everywhere
     * else — a defect that survives review, survives a typecheck, and shows up
     * as a crash on one code path.
     */
    {
      name: 'no-circular',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        'A module that depends on itself through its neighbours, at run time. ' +
        'Type-only edges are not in this graph, so a type-only cycle is not a ' +
        'violation here and does not need excusing.',
      from: {},
      to: { circular: true },
    },

    /**
     * A library reaching into an application. `packages/*` are the shared
     * layers — engine, content, journal, db, ai, contracts — and `apps/*` are
     * the four surfaces built on top of them. The arrow only ever points one
     * way, and nothing until now said so.
     *
     * MEASURED zero violations on the day it went in, which is the whole
     * point: this is a direction that is correct today and that one convenient
     * import would reverse. A package that imports from an app cannot be
     * published, cannot be tested without that app, and drags a Telegram
     * client or a React Native screen into whatever else consumes it.
     *
     * `src` only. Test suites are deliberately excluded — six of them cross
     * this line on purpose, they are listed in the header, and the companion
     * test makes that listing mandatory rather than optional. Forbidding them
     * here would mean writing an exemption list for correct code, which is the
     * shape this repository keeps finding rot in.
     */
    {
      name: 'no-package-src-to-app',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        'packages/*/src must not import from apps/**. The dependency runs from ' +
        'app to library and never back. Tests are out of scope on purpose; see ' +
        'the header of this file.',
      from: { path: '^packages/[^/]+/src/' },
      to: { path: '^apps/' },
    },
  ],

  options: {
    /**
     * THE RUNTIME GRAPH. `false` means edges are read from the source as it
     * will be executed: `import type` and `import { type X }` are not
     * dependencies, because they are erased before anything runs. Setting this
     * to `'specify'` builds the type-aware graph instead — 335 modules, 968
     * dependencies, 9 violations, all nine of them measured and explained in
     * the header, and none of them a defect. Changing this line therefore turns
     * a green gate red without any code changing, which is why the number it
     * produces is written down above rather than left to be rediscovered.
     */
    tsPreCompilationDeps: false,

    /**
     * Third-party packages are edges, not territory. Following them would drag
     * grammy, react-native and expo into the graph, which answers no question
     * asked here and costs minutes. Without this, a cruise over `packages apps`
     * does not finish inside two minutes on this machine.
     */
    doNotFollow: { path: 'node_modules' },

    /**
     * `data/` is `packages/content/data` — twenty-three generated JSON files,
     * one per language, produced by `scripts/build-content.mjs`. They are
     * imported, so the tool sees them, and they are not modules anybody can
     * write a cycle through. `dist/` is build output. Excluding both is the
     * difference between 333 modules and 367, and none of the 34 is source
     * anybody edits.
     */
    exclude: { path: '(^|/)(node_modules|dist|data)/' },
  },
};

[tool.importlinter]

# libraries and shared; libraries use shared; shared uses nothing above it.
root_packages = [
    "cli",
    "experiment",
    "analysis_cli",
    "dashboard",
    "routing",
    "prediction",
    "infra",
    "analysis",
    "shared",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Entry point over apps over libraries over shared"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "cli",
    "experiment | analysis_cli | dashboard | routing",
    "prediction",
    "infra | analysis",
    "shared",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "One loader for run artifacts"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["shared.artifacts"]
# `dashboard` belongs here: it reads the same artifacts as analysis, and reading the
# files itself is what let a storage-format change break it silently. Its direct read
# was the deferred work this contract was written around; it now goes through the loader.
allowed_importers = ["experiment", "analysis", "analysis_cli", "dashboard"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 120
extend-exclude = ["archived", ".venv", "results"]

# F841: unused-variable (matplotlib bar assignments, debug vars in analysis scripts)

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"apps/routing/tests/*.py" = ["F841"]
"apps/prediction/tests/*.py" = ["F841"]
"apps/analysis/analysis_cli/*.py" = ["F841"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"


[tool.ty.src]
# The archived/ snapshot is a frozen pre-refactor copy of the codebase: its diagnostics
# are history, not work, and they are the only reason the type check used to be a
# manual-stage hook. Excluding it lets ty gate commits on code that is actually live.
exclude = ["archived/**"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Modern layout per the pytest docs: several packages carry their own tests/
# directory, and the default prepend import mode lets the first one imported claim
# the name "tests". importlib derives a unique name from the path instead, with the
# one trade-off that test modules must not import each other (they don't).
addopts = "--import-mode=importlib --strict-markers -m 'not live'"
testpaths = ["apps", "libs"]
markers = [
    "live: touches the real k3d clusters and Docker; run explicitly with -m live, never while an experiment is running",
]
# A hung test fails instead of stalling a measurement window. The live tier opts out
# per module; those runs are minutes long by nature.
timeout = 120
norecursedirs = ["archived", ".*", "build", "dist", "node_modules", "venv", "{arch}"]
timeout_method = "signal"

[tool.mutmut]
# Scope, not a repo-wide gate: these are the modules where a mutation would restore a
# bug this refactor removed. Run with `uv run mutmut run`. The tests directory is the
# repo root so a mutant is judged by the whole hermetic suite rather than by one
# package's tests — the modules under test are consumed from three packages.
paths_to_mutate = [
    "libs/shared/shared/artifacts.py",
    "apps/experiment/experiment/tuning/workload_analysis.py",
    "apps/routing/routing/algorithm/registry.py",
]
tests_dir = "."

root_package = src

name = Layered architecture
type = layers

    src.delivery
    src.infrastructure
    src.application
    src.domain
rules =
    src.delivery -> src.infrastructure
    src.infrastructure -> src.application
    src.application -> src.domain

# Contratos de arquitectura (import-linter) - Fase 0 monolito modular.
#
# Objetivo: ratchet de dependencias. Las violaciones actuales se permiten via
# baseline (ignore_imports) y CI falla ante NUEVAS dependencias prohibidas.
# Cada PR posterior que corte una dependencia debe borrar su linea del baseline
# (import-linter falla si una linea de ignore_imports no matchea ningun import).
#
# Alcance Fase 0: imports directos (allow_indirect_imports = True). El tooling de
# soporte (debug_queries, benchmarks) y los tests se excluyen para enfocarse en
# runtime; se ampliara cobertura en fases posteriores.
#
# Limitacion conocida: import-linter/grimp solo analiza paquetes regulares (con
# __init__.py). Los namespace packages sin __init__.py (p. ej. historial.services)
# quedan fuera del grafo y no se chequean por ahora.
#
# Como correr localmente:
#   python -m venv .venv-arch
#   .venv-arch\Scripts\pip install -r requirements/arch.txt   (Windows)
#   $env:PYTHONPATH = "src/backends;src/backends/kernel;src/backends/dispositivos"; .venv-arch\Scripts\lint-imports
# o via Docker:
#   docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/sisoc" -w /sisoc -e PYTHONPATH=/sisoc/src/backends:/sisoc/src/backends/kernel:/sisoc/src/backends/dispositivos python:3.11.15-slim-bookworm \

[build-system]
requires = [ "poetry-core>=1.0.0",]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"

[tool.poetry]
name = "carvera-controller-community"
description = "Community developed controller for the Carvera CNC"
version = "0.0.0"
license = "GPL-2.0"
readme = "README.md"
authors = [ "Carvera-Community",]
[[tool.poetry.packages]]
include = "carveracontroller"

[[tool.poetry.packages]]
include = "scripts"

[[tool.poetry.source]]
name = "pypi-public"
url = "https://pypi.org/simple/"

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "<3.14,>=3.9"
Kivy = "^2.3.1"
certifi = ">=2017.4.17"
pyserial = "^3.5"
pyquicklz = "^1.4.1"
hid = "^1.0.7"
ezdxf = "^1.3.0"

[tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies]
pyinstaller = "^6.11.0"
pyinstaller-versionfile = ">=2.1.1,<4.0.0"
ruamel-yaml = ">=0.18.6,<0.20.0"
cython = "^3.1.2"
toml = "^0.10.2"
virtualenv = ">=20.31.2,<22.0.0"
buildozer = "^1.5.0"

[tool.poetry.group.test.dependencies]
pytest = "^8.0"
pytest-timeout = "^2.3"
Pillow = "^11.0"

[tool.poetry.group.lint.dependencies]
ruff = ">=0.8,<0.17"
mypy = "^1.13"
import-linter = "^2.1"
pre-commit = "^4.0"

[tool.poetry.group.ios-dev.dependencies.kivy-ios]
git = "https://github.com/Carvera-Community/kivy-ios.git"
branch = "pr-643-fix-custom-recipes"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
timeout = 60

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py39"
line-length = 120
extend-exclude = [
    ".buildozer",
    "build",
    "dist",
    # Platform packaging assets are generated or consumed by external build
    # tools rather than imported by the Python application.
    "assets/packaging/**",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E9",    # syntax and indentation errors
    "W292",  # final newline
    "I",     # import ordering
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear correctness checks
    "C4",    # comprehension simplifications
    "SIM",   # non-controversial simplifications
    "RET",   # return consistency
    "UP",    # Python-version-aware modernization
    "FA100", # future annotations needed by typing aliases
    "FA102", # future annotations needed by PEP 604 syntax
    "F821",  # undefined names
    "F822",  # undefined names in __all__
    "F823",  # local variable referenced before assignment
    "F811",  # duplicate definitions
    "F541",  # f-strings without placeholders
]
ignore = [
    "B007",   # Kivy callbacks and parser loops often carry descriptive unused names
    "B904",   # exception chaining is useful but noisy across hardware/protocol paths
    "RET503", # many Kivy callbacks intentionally return None implicitly
    "RET504", # assignment-before-return is left to local readability
    "SIM102", # nested UI-state conditionals are often clearer in the Kivy shell
    "SIM105", # broad exception suppression appears in hardware/UI integration paths
    "SIM108", # if/else assignments are often clearer for command-building code
    "SIM115", # explicit file handles are used in long-running UI and transfer flows
    "UP031",  # percent formatting is used heavily in command strings
]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.9"
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
# The application contains dynamic Kivy widgets and runtime-bound ids, so the
# package baseline checks imports, name resolution, and typed call sites without
# requiring annotations everywhere.
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
disallow_untyped_calls = false
disallow_subclassing_any = false
disallow_any_generics = false
disable_error_code = [
    "var-annotated",
]
# Addon packages expose Kivy plugin surfaces with runtime-bound ids and
# controller objects. They are linted and tested, while package-level mypy
# focuses on the controller application and shared modules.
exclude = [
    '^carveracontroller/addons/',
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["carveracontroller"]
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture: ui depends on machine, never reversed"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "carveracontroller.ui",
    "carveracontroller.machine",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Machine layer is Kivy-free"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["carveracontroller.machine"]
forbidden_modules = ["kivy"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# E402 is checked incrementally like other existing debt. Entry points with
# intentional import ordering retain their local, reviewable suppressions.
# F401 is allowed only in __init__.py barrel files for intentional re-exports.
# Structural gates. These constrain shape, not style: function size, branch count,
# parameter count, dead code and import direction. They are enforced as a ratchet
# against a baseline (existing violations are tolerated, new ones are not), so the
# thresholds below state the standard rather than describing the current tree.
extend-select = [
  "I",      # keep import checks active when judging unused noqa directives
  "PGH003", # blanket type: ignore hides unrelated type errors
  "PGH004", # noqa must name the suppressed rule
  "RUF100", # obsolete noqa directives
  "PT011",  # broad pytest.raises needs a distinguishing message
  "PT012",  # setup inside pytest.raises can satisfy the wrong expectation
  "BLE001", # broad catches require review of isolation/recovery responsibility
  "UP006",
  "UP007",
  "UP035",
  "UP037",
  "UP045",
  "C901",    # function is too complex
  "PLR0911", # too many return statements
  "PLR0912", # too many branches
  "PLR0913", # too many arguments
  "PLR0915", # too many statements
  "B",       # flake8-bugbear: likely bugs
  "ARG001",  # unused function argument — the signature is lying
  "ARG002",  # unused method argument
  "ARG003",  # unused class-method argument
  "ARG004",  # unused static-method argument
  "SIM",     # redundant control flow
  "RET",     # redundant return flow
  "ERA",     # commented-out code
  "FBT001",  # boolean trap: positional bool parameter
  "FBT002",  # boolean trap: positional bool default
]
# Deliberately excluded:
#   FBT003  reports the call site rather than the API that caused it; FBT001/FBT002
#           already carry that signal at the definition.
#   ARG005  fires on callback-shaping lambdas (`lambda raw: ...`) where the ignored
#           parameter is dictated by the caller's signature, not by this code.
#   TID252  all 680 hits are `from ..x import y` inside a package, which is this
#           repo's deliberate convention. Import DIRECTION is a real concern, but it
#           is import-linter's job (see .importlinter), which judges the dependency
#           edge rather than the syntax used to write it.

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 12

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 6

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"scripts/start_server.py" = ["UP"]
"lib/zcu_tools/qick_remote/pyro.py" = ["UP"]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]
# Fixtures legitimately take many parameters and accept ones they only activate;
# `assert False` (B011) is a normal marker for a branch a test asserts is unreachable.
"tests/**" = ["PLR0913", "ARG001", "ARG002", "FBT001", "FBT002", "B011"]

[tool.pyright]
include = ["lib", "zcu_lab", "tests", "scripts", "mcp_servers", "tools", "migrations"]
executionEnvironments = [
  { root = "zcu_lab", extraPaths = ["lib", "."] },
  { root = "lib", extraPaths = ["lib", "."] },
  { root = "scripts", extraPaths = ["lib", "."] },
  { root = "mcp_servers", extraPaths = ["lib", "."] },
  { root = "migrations", extraPaths = ["lib", "."] },
  { root = "tools", extraPaths = ["lib", "tools", "."] },
  # Resolve production packages before same-named test packages.
  { root = ".", extraPaths = ["lib", "tools", "tests"] },
]
# strict, minus the rules whose diagnostics are produced by untyped third-party
# packages (qick, pyvisa, scqubits, qtpy) rather than by this repository. Measured
# on lib/: the reportUnknown* family is 59% of strict output and is almost entirely
# third-party in origin; with it disabled every remaining diagnostic is own-code.
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
# Missing optional-profile packages remain visible debt in the ratchet; missing
# imports and missing third-party stubs are different diagnostics.
reportMissingImports = "error"
reportMissingTypeStubs = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownLambdaType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "none"
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = "none"
reportUntypedBaseClass = "none"
# Ruff owns unused imports (F401, with __init__.py barrels exempted); a second
# authority on the same rule would only disagree about the barrels.
reportUnusedImport = "none"
# reportPrivateUsage stays ON everywhere, including tests. In lib/ its 327 hits are
# encapsulation breaks across module boundaries, which is the signal this gate
# exists to surface. In tests/ its 2663 hits are tests reaching into internals,
# which the test contract (tests validate observable behaviour and Interfaces)
# already forbids; the ratchet drains them rather than the config hiding them.
#
# Pre-existing override that narrows strict; a candidate for removal as the ratchet
# drains.
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = "none"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# tools/ is listed so tests import a check by name, the same way running it
# directly or loading it from another check does; see tools/_support.py.
pythonpath = [".", "tools"]
# Tests live under tests/ (project convention). Scoping collection here keeps
# pytest from walking into scratch/ helper scripts (named test_*.py with plain
# helper functions like test(label, ...) that pytest would mis-collect as cases).
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Import test modules by their full path-derived name. This keeps equal basenames
# in unrelated test domains isolated in both serial and xdist collection.
# Pin the temporary-file root to the invoking worktree so no caller has to create
# a basetemp parent first. `uv run --directory <worktree>` fixes the cwd, so parallel
# lanes stay isolated. pytest clears this directory at session start.
# Installing the quality group must not randomize ordinary collection or runs.
# Diagnostics opt in explicitly with `pytest -p randomly --randomly-seed=<seed>`.
# Ticket checks omit slow tests. Before land review, CLI -m "" includes all tests;
# -m slow selects only the slow subset, not the full suite.
addopts = "--import-mode=importlib --basetemp=.pytest-tmp --strict-markers --strict-config -p no:randomly -m 'not slow'"

  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:matplotlib.*",

]

  "requires_loopback: integration tests that bind or connect a real loopback socket",
  "slow: expensive validation reserved for pre-land review (see tests/README.md)",
  # Capability markers. A module declares what it uses; tools/check_test_capabilities.py

  "requires_subprocess: tests that spawn a real child process",
  "uses_wall_clock: tests that sleep instead of synchronising on an event",
]

# DDD layering contract (docs/ddd-refactor-plan.md:184-193, epic #137 / S10).
#
# Scope: this enforces the *internal* hyperion layering (who may statically
# import whom). The complementary "lite core pulls no heavy third-party"
# guarantee is enforced separately by tests/test_import_graph.py and S10's
# no-extras smoke job -- NOT here -- because `haversine` soft-imports `numpy`
# and hyperion.domain.geo carries a TYPE_CHECKING `import numpy`, so an
# external-package contract would false-positive on numpy. Hence
# include_external_packages stays False (default): contracts are graph-internal.
#
# Deprecation-shim modules (hyperion.entities, hyperion.typeutils,
# hyperion.infrastructure.*, the hyperion.catalog namespace shim) are
# intentionally NOT layer-constrained: they exist only to redirect old import
# paths to the new locations and are removed in 2.0. They resolve relocated
# concretes lazily via importlib (no static edge) but a couple carry
# TYPE_CHECKING edges into hyperion.data by design.
#
# `allow_indirect_imports = True` on contracts 2-5 keeps them *direct-import*
# checks: the S8 design has ports.{queue,cache,schema_registry,secrets}
# lazily delegate to hyperion.composition (which then imports an adapter inside
# a config branch), so ports -> composition -> adapters is an intentional
# *indirect* chain. Direct-edge enforcement is what code review reasons about;
# the transitive lite promise is covered by test_import_graph.py + smoke jobs.

[importlinter]
root_package = hyperion
include_external_packages = False

# Rule 1 -- domain is pure: no inward dependency on any other hyperion layer
# (only stdlib / pydantic / dateutil / lite-core hyperion.{log,dateutils,
# asyncutils,config,typeutils} are allowed, which this contract does not
# constrain). Strict: indirect chains are caught too.
[importlinter:contract:domain-isolation]
name = domain depends on nothing but lite core
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    hyperion.domain
forbidden_modules =
    hyperion.ports
    hyperion.adapters
    hyperion.application
    hyperion.data
    hyperion.composition
    hyperion.catalog
    hyperion.infrastructure

# Rule 2 -- ports depend only on domain (+ lite core). They may lazily
# delegate to the composition root (S8 from_config), so hyperion.composition
# is deliberately NOT forbidden here.
[importlinter:contract:ports-isolation]
name = ports do not reach into adapters/application/data/catalog
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    hyperion.ports
forbidden_modules =
    hyperion.adapters
    hyperion.application
    hyperion.data
    hyperion.catalog
allow_indirect_imports = True

# Rule 3 -- the application tier (hyperion.application + the Catalog
# orchestration module hyperion.catalog.catalog) may import domain/ports but
# never adapters. Scoped to hyperion.catalog.catalog, not the whole
# hyperion.catalog package, because catalog/__init__.py (S9 lazy namespace)
# and catalog/schema.py (S6 deprecation shim) are intentionally NOT
# layer-constrained (see header). Documented carve-out: Catalog uses the avro
# serializer adapter directly (S5; Catalog stayed at hyperion.catalog rather
# than moving to application/).
[importlinter:contract:application-no-adapters]
name = application/catalog never import adapters (except the avro serializer)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    hyperion.application
    hyperion.catalog.catalog
forbidden_modules =
    hyperion.adapters
ignore_imports =
    hyperion.catalog.catalog -> hyperion.adapters.serialization.avro
allow_indirect_imports = True

# Rule 4 -- adapters may import domain/ports + their backend's third-party,
# but never the application tier nor the composition root (rule 6 corollary).
[importlinter:contract:adapters-no-up]
name = adapters do not import application/catalog/composition
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    hyperion.adapters
forbidden_modules =
    hyperion.application
    hyperion.catalog
    hyperion.composition
allow_indirect_imports = True

# Rule 5 -- hyperion.data is a leaf validation-stack adapter package: no live
# layer may import it (only data/ itself and tests).
[importlinter:contract:data-isolation]
name = data is not imported by any live layer
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    hyperion.domain
    hyperion.ports
    hyperion.application
    hyperion.adapters
    hyperion.composition
    hyperion.catalog
forbidden_modules =
    hyperion.data
allow_indirect_imports = True

# Rule 6 -- composition.py is the ONLY module allowed to import from both
# hyperion.ports and hyperion.adapters and construct adapters from config.
# This is enforced by construction via the conjunction of rules 2-5: nothing
# but composition (and the documented Catalog->avro carve-out) imports
# hyperion.adapters, so no extra contract is required.

[tool.ruff.format]
# Ruff 0.16 formats Python code blocks inside Markdown by default. Our docs use
# illustrative fragments (bare kwargs, partial function bodies), which the
# formatter rewrites into misleading full-module style — so keep .md as authored.
exclude = ["*.md"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Ruff 0.16 replaced the old E4/E7/E9/F default with a curated 413-rule set
# (partial-prefix subsets across ~35 groups). We inherit that default instead of
# pinning: new defaults from future ruff versions are adopted on upgrade, and
# anything we can't pass goes into `ignore` below with a reason.
extend-select = [
    # The pre-0.16 pycodestyle baseline, no longer part of ruff's defaults.
    "E4", "E7", "E9",
    # Full isort (defaults only carry I001).
    "I",
    # Blocking subprocess/os calls in async defs; adopted pre-0.16 but not in
    # the curated default set.
    "ASYNC240", "ASYNC250",
]
ignore = [
    # Broad `except Exception` is deliberate resilience in a tool-execution
    # platform: agent/tool failures must degrade, never crash the run loop.
    "BLE001",
    # The whole repo (credit system, pricing, tools, tests — 300+ sites)
    # uniformly uses the str constructor for Decimal (`Decimal("100")` and
    # `Decimal("0.0001")` alike). FURB157 would rewrite only the int-valued
    # ones, splitting the style in financial code.
    "FURB157",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
# FastAPI's parameter markers are designed to be called in defaults.
extend-immutable-calls = [
    "fastapi.Body",
    "fastapi.Depends",
    "fastapi.File",
    "fastapi.Path",
    "fastapi.Query",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# One-off ops/migration scripts run interactively from a shell; blocking I/O,
# prompts on the event loop, and naive local timestamps are fine there
# (scripts/ is likewise out of scope for deptry and basedpyright).
"scripts/*" = ["ASYNC", "LOG015", "DTZ"]
# Nested `with patch(...)` stacks mirror decorator stacking and read better
# than one parenthesized mega-with; naive datetimes are fine for fixture data;
# silently swallowed exceptions in best-effort test cleanup are fine too.
"tests/*" = ["SIM117", "DTZ", "S110", "S112"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
force-single-line = false
known-first-party = ["intentkit"]
known-local-folder = ["app"]
section-order = ["future", "standard-library", "third-party", "first-party", "local-folder"]

[tool.deptry]

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import io.reflectoring.buckpal.archunit.HexagonalArchitecture
import kotlin.test.Test

class DependencyRuleTests {

    @Test
    fun `domain layer does not depend on application layer`() {
        noClasses()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("io.reflectoring.buckpal.account.domain..")
            .should()
            .dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("io.reflectoring.buckpal.account.application..")
            .check(ClassFileImporter().importPackages("io.reflectoring.buckpal.."))
    }

    @Test
    fun `validate registration context architecture`() {
        HexagonalArchitecture.boundedContext("io.reflectoring.buckpal.account")
            .withDomainLayer("domain")
            .withAdaptersLayer("adapter")
            .incoming("in.web")
            .outgoing("out.persistence")
            .and()
            .withApplicationLayer("application")
            .services("service")
            .incomingPorts("port.in")
            .outgoingPorts("port.out")
            .and()
            .withConfiguration("configuration")
            .check(ClassFileImporter().importPackages("io.reflectoring.buckpal.."))
    }

}

[importlinter]
# Flat service: no multi-level services hierarchy (see balancer/tournament
# conversions). These three contracts are the ones that actually fail on
# a regression — SQL in rpc, domain growing a session, services importing rpc.
root_packages =
    src
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:rpc-no-sql]
name = RPC transport owns no SQLAlchemy
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    src.rpc
forbidden_modules =
    sqlalchemy

[importlinter:contract:domain-is-pure]
name = domain/ stays free of sessions and transport
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.domain
forbidden_modules =
    src.services
    src.rpc
    src.core.db
    sqlalchemy

[importlinter:contract:services-dont-import-rpc]
name = services never import rpc
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.services
forbidden_modules =
    src.rpc

[importlinter]
# Enforces the layering the 2026-08-20 OOP refactor established
# (docs/plans/2026-08-20-app-service-oop-repositories.md).
#
# Layer shape per domain:
#   src/rpc/<x>.py            transport: decode, gate, one service call. No SQL.
#   services/<d>/flows.py     class <D>Service + singleton — orchestration, cache, mapping
#   services/<d>/service.py   class <D>Queries  + singleton — analytical SQL only
#   services/<d>/_mappers.py  sync ORM -> DTO functions
#   shared.repository         CRUD, flush-only
#
# NB: this file previously used TOML table syntax (`[[importlinter.contracts]]`)
# in an INI-parsed file, so `lint-imports` aborted with
# "section '' already exists" and enforced nothing. Rewritten as INI.

root_packages =
    src

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 1: layered hierarchy inside src.services.
#
# Layers (high -> low):
#   - achievements: aggregates user/encounter/tournament behaviour
#   - dashboard, user: cross-domain read APIs
#   - hero, map, statistics, workspace: leaf/core domains
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:services-layers]
name = src.services layered hierarchy
type = layers
layers =
    achievements
    dashboard | user
    hero | map | statistics | workspace
containers =
    src.services
ignore_imports =
    # ---- Known debt: map -> hero ----
    src.services.map.service -> src.services.hero.queries
    src.services.map.service -> src.services.hero.service

    # ---- Known debt: lower layers reaching into user ----
    src.services.map.service -> src.services.user.service


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 2: the transport layer owns no data access.
#
# rpc/*.py decodes parameters, gates permissions and calls one service. It must
# never reach a query class or a repository directly — that is what put SQL and
# `session.commit()` into rpc/{users_admin,catalog_aliases,audit,binary}.py in
# the first place.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:rpc-goes-through-services]
name = RPC transport must orchestrate via services, never query classes
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    src.rpc
forbidden_modules =
    src.services.user.queries
    src.services.hero.queries
    src.services.statistics.queries
    src.services.achievements.queries

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 3: private mappers / query packages stay inside their domain.
#
# Each consumer of tournament-flow data owns its own queries + mappers. A third
# consumer gets its own, so the consumers can evolve independently.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:user-privates]
name = user/ private modules belong to user/
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    src.services.dashboard
    src.services.statistics
    src.services.hero
    src.services.map
    src.services.workspace
forbidden_modules =
    src.services.user.queries
    src.services.user._mappers

[importlinter:contract:achievements-privates]
name = achievements/ private modules belong to achievements/
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    src.services.user
    src.services.dashboard
    src.services.statistics
    src.services.hero
    src.services.map
    src.services.workspace
forbidden_modules =
    src.services.achievements._mappers

[tool.uv]
dev-dependencies = [
    "pytest<8.0.0,>=7.4.3",
    "mypy<2.0.0,>=1.8.0",
    "ruff<1.0.0,>=0.2.2",
    "pre-commit<4.0.0,>=3.6.2",
    "types-passlib<2.0.0.0,>=1.7.7.20240106",
    "coverage<8.0.0,>=7.4.3",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    # Runs the quota gate's Lua for real in unit tests: the all-or-nothing
    # two-scope charge is the one piece of this codebase that only a Redis
    # script interpreter can verify.
    "fakeredis[lua]>=2.38",
]

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["shared", "app-service", "identity-service", "discord-service", "parser-service", "balancer-service", "tournament-service", "analytics-service", "stream-service"]

[tool.uv.sources]
shared = { workspace = true }

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
exclude = ["venv", ".venv", "alembic"]

[tool.ty.environment]
# Point ty at the workspace venv so it resolves `shared` (editable install)
# and all third-party packages.
python = ".venv"
python-version = "3.14"
# Roots for import resolution:
# - "." so `shared/` resolves as `shared`
# - each service dir so `from src.xxx` works inside that service
root = [
    ".",
    "app-service",
    "identity-service",
    "parser-service",
    "tournament-service",
    "balancer-service",
    "discord-service",
    "analytics-service",
    "stream-service",
]
extra-paths = [
    ".",
    "app-service",
    "identity-service",
    "parser-service",
    "tournament-service",
    "balancer-service",
    "discord-service",
    "analytics-service",
    "stream-service",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py314"
line-length = 120
exclude = ["alembic"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",  # pycodestyle errors
    "W",  # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",  # pyflakes
    "I",  # isort
    "B",  # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
#    "ARG001", # unused arguments in functions
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long, handled by black
    "B008",  # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "W191",  # indentation contains tabs
    "B904",  # Allow raising exceptions without from e, for HTTPException
    "F403", # 'from module import *' used; unable to detect undefined names
    "F405", # may be undefined, or defined from star imports (companion to F403; aggregators re-export via `*`)
    "UP046", # non-pep695 generic class — hold off on PEP 695 syntax (pydantic generics)
    "UP047", # non-pep695 generic function — hold off on PEP 695 syntax
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Test modules legitimately set env vars / sys.path before importing app code.
"**/tests/**" = ["E402"]
# Aggregator __init__.py files re-export via `*` in a hand-crafted dependency
# order (e.g. `hero` before `achievement`, which consumes `HeroRead`). Import
# sorting (I001) would reorder them alphabetically and break circular-import
# avoidance, and re-exports look like unused imports (F401).
"**/__init__.py" = ["I001", "F401"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
# Preserve types, even if a file imports `from __future__ import annotations`.
keep-runtime-typing = true

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# Treat these as first-party so `shared.*` isn't grouped with stdlib/third-party.
known-first-party = ["shared", "src"]

[tool.coverage.run]
# Per-service suites run with --parallel-mode + --source, then `coverage combine`
# merges them. relative_files keeps paths portable across the matrix/checkout.
relative_files = true
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/alembic/*",
    "*/.venv/*",
    "*/migrations/*",
    "*/scripts/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = false

[project]
name = "geoparquet-io"
version = "1.7.0"
description = "Fast I/O and transformation tools for GeoParquet files"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [
    { name = "Chris Holmes", email = "cholmes@9eo.org" }
]
keywords = ["geoparquet", "geospatial", "parquet", "gis", "io"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: GIS",
]
dependencies = [
    "click>=8.0.0",
    "click-plugins>=1.1.1",  # Plugin system for extending CLI
    "pyarrow>=23.0.1",  # PYSEC-2026-113 fix
    # Floor at 1.5.5: it is the DuckDB release the 'geography' community
    # extension is published for, so S2 (`gpio add s2`, `gpio partition s2`)
    # works on every supported version rather than only some of them (#737).
    # The floor also has to stay above 1.5.1, which applies the selection vector
    # twice in TRY() under conditional execution (duckdb/duckdb-spatial#858):
    # TRY() over a blob segfaults and over a fixed-width type can silently
    # return another row's value, crashing geometry repair on ordinary
    # extractions (#737) and why core/geometry_repair.py counts invalid
    # geometry in layers (#645).
    #
    # 1.5.6 raises the floor past a 1.5.5 regression where ST_Read_Meta
    # segfaults on a JSON file GDAL cannot open as a vector layer (an array of
    # records, a {"data": [...]} wrapper), killing `gpio convert` with no
    # message (#1102, duckdb/duckdb-spatial#860). The 'geography' extension is
    # published for 1.5.6 too, so the S2 guarantee above still holds.
    #
    # The <1.6 cap is unchanged from #778. Keeping it is what makes the S2
    # claim above hold: community extensions are built per DuckDB release, so
    # if 1.6 ships before 'geography' is published for it, an uncapped range
    # would let `uv sync` pull a DuckDB that silently breaks S2. Lift it in a
    # deliberate step once 1.6 exists and the extension is published for it.
    "duckdb>=1.5.6,<1.6",
    "pandas>=1.0.0",
    "fsspec>=2023.9.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "pystac>=1.9.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.0.0",  # Required for pystac validation
    "psutil>=5.9.0",
    "obstore>=0.8.2",
    "aiohttp>=3.13.4",  # Required by fsspec for HTTP/HTTPS support (CVE-2026-* fixes)
    "s3fs>=2023.9.0",  # Required by fsspec for S3 support
    # Resolves the full AWS credential chain (SSO, assume-role, credential_process,
    # instance metadata) for object-store writes and copies (#865). Already present
    # transitively via s3fs -> aiobotocore; declared here because gpio imports it.
    # boto3 is deliberately not used: botocore alone carries the chain.
    # Floor is the feature floor, not uv.lock's 1.43.0: aiobotocore pins
    # botocore<1.43.1, so a >=1.43.0 floor would pin every user to one release.
    "botocore>=1.34.0",
    "geoarrow-pyarrow>=0.1.0",  # Required for CRS handling in Parquet native geo types
    "pyproj>=3.0.0",  # Required for CRS handling and PROJJSON generation
    "mercantile>=1.2.0",  # Required for quadkey generation
    "pmtiles>=3.0.0",  # Required for reading/writing PMTiles archive metadata (pyramid bands)
    "httpx>=0.25.0",  # Required for ArcGIS REST API requests (http2 disabled due to ArcGIS compatibility)
    "owslib>=0.29.0",  # Required for OGC Web Feature Service (WFS) extraction
    # Security: explicit constraints for transitive dependencies
    "requests>=2.33.0",  # CVE-2026-25645 fix
    "lxml>=6.1.0",  # CVE-2026-41066 fix
    "idna>=3.15",  # CVE-2026-45409 fix
    "urllib3>=2.7.0",  # PYSEC-2026-141, PYSEC-2026-142 fix
    "msgpack>=1.2.1",  # GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964 fix (transitive via CacheControl)
    "multidict>=6.9.1",  # CVE-2026-104874 fix (transitive via aiohttp)
]

[project.scripts]
gpio = "geoparquet_io.cli.main:main"

[project.urls]

"Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/geoparquet/geoparquet-io/issues"
"Documentation" = "https://geoparquet.io/"

    "xenon>=0.9.3",

[tool.uv]
# Keep transitive msgpack (pulled via pip-audit -> cachecontrol) above the
# GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964 fix so `uv lock --upgrade` cannot reintroduce it.
constraint-dependencies = ["msgpack>=1.2.1"]

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["geoparquet_io"]
# Include markdown skill files in wheel
artifacts = ["geoparquet_io/skills/*.md"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests", "docs/guide"]
pythonpath = ["."]
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_functions = "test_*"
# Coverage flags deliberately absent: a plain `uv run pytest` should be fast and
# green. Instrumenting every run (including every spawned subprocess) cost 39-49%
# on single-file dev runs, and a partial run can never clear the whole-suite floor,
# so the default local invocation always exited 1 on a gate that measured nothing.
# The floor is enforced where it is meaningful — the one COVERAGE_JOB leg in
# .github/workflows/tests.yml passes --cov=geoparquet_io --cov-report=term-missing
# --cov-report=xml over the whole fast suite, reads [tool.coverage.report]
# fail_under below as the floor, and feeds Codecov plus the 90% diff-cover gate.
# Locally, opt in with:
#   uv run pytest --cov=geoparquet_io --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=0
# (--cov-fail-under=0 is required on a subset: [tool.coverage.report].fail_under
# re-arms the floor on any --cov run, which a partial run can never clear.)
addopts = [
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--strict-markers",
    # The geoparquet-testing submodule ships its own pytest suite; never collect it.
    "--ignore=tests/data/geoparquet-testing",
]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "network: marks tests requiring network access (deselect with '-m \"not network\"')",
    "integration: marks end-to-end integration tests; runs in the fast suite unless also marked slow/network (see tests/e2e/test_integration_lane.py)",
    "corpus: tests against the official geoparquet-testing corpus (requires git submodule)",

]

# The group modules split out of "geoparquet_io.cli.main" inherited its blanket
# suppression. Narrowed to the two codes they actually emit (17 errors: add 4,
# extract 5, partition 8 — benchmark now emits none) so any OTHER type error in
# this new layer is reported. The cause is not the CLI wrappers: Click hands a
# command `float | None` / `tuple[float, ...] | None` where the core function it
# calls is annotated `int | None` / a fixed-length tuple, i.e. core annotations
# narrower than their implementations. Widening those annotations removes the
# need for this override entirely — tracked in a follow-up issue.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.add",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.extract",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.partition",
]
disable_error_code = ["arg-type", "index"]

# Same story for the "check" group, moved out of "geoparquet_io.cli.main" by
# #920: it inherited that module's blanket suppression, so these 7 errors were
# never reported and this override only keeps them that way. Narrowed to the
# four codes it actually emits (union-attr 4, arg-type 1, index 1, misc 1) so
# any OTHER type error in the module is still reported. Two independent causes,
# neither introduced by the move: `check_spatial_order` is annotated
# `float | dict | None` while every caller treats the `return_results=True`
# result as a dict (union-attr/index/arg-type), and `check bbox --fix` defines
# `bbox_fix_func` once per branch with different keyword defaults (misc).
# Fixing them belongs with the rest of the CLI typing cleanup, not here.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.check",
]
disable_error_code = ["arg-type", "index", "misc", "union-attr"]

# contourrs pins numpy>=2.5.3, whose stubs use PEP 695 `type` statements that
# mypy's python_version = "3.10" target refuses to parse — and duckdb's stubs
# import numpy, so on a Python >= 3.12 venv every mypy run loads them and dies
# on numpy's own files (the 3.11 CI meta leg resolves numpy 2.4.6 and never
# saw this). Skipping types numpy as Any, the same footing as any unstubbed
# dependency; `follow_imports` alone is not enough because mypy always follows
# .pyi stubs unless follow_imports_for_stubs is set too.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["numpy"]
follow_imports = "skip"
follow_imports_for_stubs = true

[tool.mutmut]
source_paths = ["geoparquet_io/"]
# Fast tests only: slow/network tests are nondeterministic (live third-party
# servers) and far too slow to run once per mutant. --no-cov drops the coverage
# overhead and stops [tool.coverage.report].fail_under from failing every mutant.
# NOTE: mutmut 3 runs pytest in-process and IGNORES a `runner` setting;
# extra args must go in pytest_add_cli_args.
# `not meta` is what keeps the tooling meta-tests out: they spawn `uv run ...`
# subprocesses against the project, and from mutmut's mutants/ cwd that would
# resolve/install the MUTATED package — meaningless for mutation score and
# fatal to the run. It replaces the per-file --ignore list those tests used to
# need. test_import_linter.py is not in the meta lane (it is a fast unit test
# of the contract config) but shells out the same way, so it keeps its ignore.
pytest_add_cli_args = [
    "--no-cov",
    # --tb=short (not --tb=no): a failure in mutmut's single-process stats
    # phase must show WHERE it failed. --tb=no once hid a cwd-related crash
    # (tests that chdir break mutmut's trampoline) and made nightly red with
    # no diagnosable reason. See the tests/ chdir guard in .pre-commit-config.
    "--tb=short",
    "-m", "not slow and not network and not meta",
    "--ignore=tests/test_import_linter.py",
]
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = ["tests/"]
# Everything the test suite reads relative to the repo root must also exist
# inside mutmut's mutants/ tree (tests import scripts.*, and the meta-tests
# validate ADRs, CLAUDE.md, workflows, and config files).
also_copy = [
    "scripts/",
    "context/",
    ".github/",
    ".pre-commit-config.yaml",
    ".pip-audit-ignores",
    "CLAUDE.md",
]

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", ".venv", "docs"]
skips = [
    "B608",  # SQL injection false positives: DuckDB is an embedded OLAP database;
             # all SQL queries use internally-derived column names (from schema detection),
             # not untrusted user input. Parameterised queries are not supported for
             # column/table identifiers in DuckDB's Python API.
    "B110",  # try/except/pass: all instances are intentional (race-condition guards for
             # DuckDB extension installation, optional cleanup, optional metadata ops).
    "B112",  # try/except/continue: intentional in iteration over optional schema columns.
    "B404",  # subprocess import: used only in the benchmark module to call ogr2ogr.
    "B603",  # subprocess without shell=True: ogr2ogr call in benchmark with a fixed argv list.
    "B607",  # partial executable path: ogr2ogr relies on PATH, which is standard practice.
    "B105",  # hardcoded password: false positive on an ArcGIS token endpoint URL constant.
    "B101",  # assert used: single internal logic guard (assert overall_bounds is not None).
]

[tool.commitizen]
name = "cz_conventional_commits"
version = "1.7.0"
version_files = ["pyproject.toml:^version"]
tag_format = "v$version"
# Off: the changelog is generated from merged pull requests by
# scripts/release_notes.py (see .claude/skills/release/), which writes the
# house style. Letting cz regenerate it from commit subjects would fight that,
# and would overwrite the reviewed section with a second, unreviewed one.
update_changelog_on_bump = false
changelog_file = "CHANGELOG.md"
major_version_zero = true

[tool.vulture]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["geoparquet_io", "tests"]
sort_by_size = true
verbose = false

[tool.codespell]
# site/ (zensical build) and mutants/ (mutmut working tree) are gitignored
# build artifacts; scanning them made test_codespell_passes fail on any
# machine that had built docs or run mutation testing locally.
# *.csv and *.geojson are sample data, not prose: real-world place names and
# addresses carry their own misspellings, which are data to be preserved
# verbatim, not mistakes to be fixed.
#
# Skipping by extension, not by directory, because a directory pattern does not
# work here. codespell matches each candidate against its basename and against
# the path string it walked, and a whole-repo run walks from "." - so
# "tests/data/*" never matches "./tests/data/canonical/places.csv" and skips
# nothing at all. (That entry was dead config and has been removed; the tree it
# claimed to exclude has been spell-checked all along, and passes.) Matching by
# extension also keeps prose that lives beside the data - notably
# tests/data/canonical/README.md - checked, which a working directory skip
# would have swallowed.
skip = ".git,*.lock,*.parquet,*.json,*.csv,*.geojson,geoparquet-testing,.venv,uv.lock,site,mutants"
ignore-words-list = "nd,ot,crs,inout,hel,bu"
check-filenames = true

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["geoparquet_io"]
# Branch coverage on: the line figure hid partial branches -- an `if` whose body
# ran and whose fall-through never did. Two consumers see the difference: the
# fail_under floor below now measures the COMBINED line+branch figure, and the
# diff-cover gate in tests.yml counts a partial branch on a changed line as
# uncovered -- but only because it is passed --branch-coverage; without that
# flag diff-cover ignores the condition data coverage.xml carries.
branch = true
omit = [
    "geoparquet_io/__init__.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
# Trailing ratchet: the floor sits two points under the measured full-fast-suite
# number (89.243% on 2026-09-13, `-m "not slow and not network and not meta"`),
# so it catches real regressions without flaking on run-to-run noise. When the
# measured number moves up, raise the floor to follow it (measured minus two,
# rounded down); never lower it to admit a regression. The move is one command,
# `uv run python scripts/coverage_floor.py --apply`, which re-measures and
# rewrites this value, the dated figure above, and the prose that repeats it
# (see ADR-0006). This is the ONE place the number lives: pytest-cov reads it
# on the CI coverage leg because COV_ARGS passes no --cov-fail-under, and
# tests/test_coverage_job.py asserts that stays so (and that branch = true
# stays on, since turning it off would silently turn this into a looser
# line-only floor).
#
# That measured number is the COMBINED line+branch figure, because
# [tool.coverage.run] branch = true. It is several points under the line figure
# - re-measure, don't convert, when you next move this.
#
# pytest-cov rounds the total to a whole number before comparing, so the exit
# status enforces "> floor - 0.5", while its summary line compares unrounded;
# in that half-point band the log says FAIL and the job passes. Cosmetic, but
# read the exit status, not the line.
fail_under = 87
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "geoparquet_io"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "core-no-click"
name = "Core modules must not import Click"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["geoparquet_io.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["click"]
# benchmark_suite lazily imports __version__ from package root, which transitively
# imports cli.main -> click. This is acceptable since the import is version-info only.
ignore_imports = [
    "geoparquet_io.core.benchmark_suite -> geoparquet_io",
]
# Alert when ignored patterns no longer match any actual imports (stale ignores)
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "warn"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "api-no-cli"
name = "API modules must not import CLI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["geoparquet_io.api"]
forbidden_modules = ["geoparquet_io.cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "commands-no-cli-main"
name = "Command group modules must not import cli.main"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["geoparquet_io.cli.commands"]
forbidden_modules = ["geoparquet_io.cli.main"]
# Same transitive edge core-no-click already ignores: benchmark_suite imports
# __version__ from the package root, whose __init__ re-exports cli.main. The
# import is version-info only and the _get_version indirection behind it is dead
# weight — removing it drops this ignore. Tracked in a follow-up issue.
ignore_imports = [
    "geoparquet_io.core.benchmark_suite -> geoparquet_io",
]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "warn"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "commands-independent"
name = "Command group modules must not import each other"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.add",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.benchmark",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.check",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.convert",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.extract",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.inspect",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.partition",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.pmtiles",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.process",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.publish",
    "geoparquet_io.cli.commands.sort",
]
# See commands-no-cli-main above: the same benchmark_suite -> package-root edge
# would otherwise route every group into every other group through cli.main.
ignore_imports = [
    "geoparquet_io.core.benchmark_suite -> geoparquet_io",
]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "warn"

# The common.py split (#1010, #1066, #1083). Layers are listed top to bottom; a
# module may import anything below it and nothing above it, directly or through
# any other module -- function-level imports count, so a deferred import cannot
# be used to sneak a back-edge past this contract. `|` separates siblings that
# must stay independent of each other; `:` separates siblings that may import
# each other (the metadata readers below the split are a pre-existing tangle
# -- crs_utils <-> duckdb_metadata, geo_metadata -> geometry_detection -> ...
# -- that the split did not create and this contract does not pretend to fix).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "core-common-split-layers"
name = "The common.py split is layered: nothing imports upward through it"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    # The stage-C residue: get_parquet_metadata, add_computed_column, the SQL
    # geometry-type helpers, auto-version resolution, bounds. It imports the
    # whole stack below; nothing below may import it.
    "geoparquet_io.core.common",
    # The two write funnels; the only module that needs both geo-block builders.
    "geoparquet_io.core.write_funnels",
    # The geo block for an Arrow table / for a written file. Independent by
    # construction (#1010): neither reaches the other.
    "geoparquet_io.core.arrow_geo_metadata | geoparquet_io.core.derive_geo_from_file",
    "geoparquet_io.core.bbox_structure",
    # file_type: what kind of GeoParquet a file is. parquet_writer: the write
    # facade's three decisions (#990). Neither needs the other.
    "geoparquet_io.core.file_type | geoparquet_io.core.parquet_writer",
    # The geo-metadata readers. geo_metadata owns the WKB type-code tables that
    # arrow_geo_metadata and derive_geo_from_file consume, which is why it sits
    # below both of them.
    "geoparquet_io.core.geo_metadata : geoparquet_io.core.crs_utils : geoparquet_io.core.duckdb_metadata : geoparquet_io.core.geometry_detection",
    # Leaves.
    "geoparquet_io.core.duckdb_utils : geoparquet_io.core.arrow_types : geoparquet_io.core.compression : geoparquet_io.core.sizing",
]
# Each ignored edge is a deferred import of a stage-C resident that has not
# moved out of common.py yet (#1010's "Stages C and D" table). Deleting the
# resident's block from common.py removes the edge, and the `error` alerting
# below then fails the build until its line here is deleted too -- the ignore
# list is meant to shrink to nothing, never to grow.
ignore_imports = [
    # geometry_type_sql: compute_geometry_types_via_sql, zm_suffix_sql, ...
    "geoparquet_io.core.geo_metadata -> geoparquet_io.core.common",
    "geoparquet_io.core.write_strategies.arrow_streaming -> geoparquet_io.core.common",
    "geoparquet_io.core.write_strategies.disk_rewrite -> geoparquet_io.core.common",
    # version_resolution: _resolve_auto_version, resolve_geoparquet_version_from_file
    "geoparquet_io.core.parquet_writer -> geoparquet_io.core.common",
    # add/computed_column: add_computed_column
    "geoparquet_io.core.constants -> geoparquet_io.core.common",
]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "error"

package skillmanagement.domain.employees

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOptions
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestInstance
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS
import skillmanagement.test.UnitTest

@UnitTest
@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)
internal class DomainArchitectureTests {

    private val options = ImportOptions()
        .with(DoNotIncludeTests())

    private val basePackage = this::class.java.packageName

    @Test
    fun `no cyclic dependencies between packages`() {
        SlicesRuleDefinition.slices()
            .matching("(**)")
            .should().beFreeOfCycles()
            .check(classesOf(basePackage))
    }

    @Test
    fun `sub domains boundaries are respected`() {
        Architectures.layeredArchitecture()
            .layer("root").definedBy(basePackage)
            .layer("metrics").definedBy("$basePackage.metrics..")
            .layer("model").definedBy("$basePackage.model..")
            .layer("searchindex").definedBy("$basePackage.searchindex..")
            .layer("tasks").definedBy("$basePackage.tasks..")
            .layer("usecases").definedBy("$basePackage.usecases..")
            .whereLayer("metrics").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("model").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("root", "searchindex", "tasks", "usecases")
            .whereLayer("searchindex").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("tasks").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("usecases").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("tasks")
            .check(classesOf(basePackage))
    }

    private fun classesOf(vararg packages: String): JavaClasses =
        ClassFileImporter(options).importPackages(*packages)
}

[project]

[tool.mypy]

[tool.importlinter]

[tool.pdm]

package-dir = "src"

[project.scripts]
run-bot = "{{cookiecutter.package_name}}.__main__:main"
