    "jsonschema>=4.23,<5",
]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = "all"

# Layer boundaries, checked by `lint-imports` (task check:imports).
# A layer may import the layers below it, never the ones above:
# - application sees infrastructure directly (no full hexagon, by decision)
# - infrastructure implements the application ports structurally, so it
#   needs nothing from application; the port vocabulary lives in domain
# - domain imports only the standard library
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "boosty_downloader"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layers: cli -> application -> infrastructure -> domain"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "boosty_downloader.cli",
    "boosty_downloader.application",
    "boosty_downloader.infrastructure",
    "boosty_downloader.domain",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# auto mode: every async test runs under asyncio without a manual mark.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Bare `pytest` runs unit and e2e (local server) tests. Integration tests
# need live credentials and the canary needs the network: an explicit path
# argument (task test:api, task test:canary) overrides this.
testpaths = ["test/unit", "test/e2e"]
# -ra: show the reason for every skip/xfail in the summary.
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers"
# The dev tools in scripts/ have unit tests too (scripts/api_schema).
# test/ holds the shared test helpers (support/).
pythonpath = ["scripts", "test"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["boosty_downloader"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "7.0"
testpaths = ["api/tests"]
asyncio_mode = "strict"
# test_schema_contract.py (Lot 3, PLAN_SOLIDITE_TECHNIQUE.md) fuzzes the whole
# API surface via Schemathesis — even clamped, a full pass takes ~10-15
# minutes (95 operations x heavy simulation compute), which would triple the
# normal ~3min test job. It has its own workflow (schemathesis.yml) and is run
# there via `pytest api/tests/test_schema_contract.py -o addopts=""` — naming
# the file explicitly bypasses this --ignore (it only affects directory
# discovery, confirmed live), so that invocation still collects it.
#
# test_engine_benchmarks.py (Lot 8.1, PLAN_SOLIDITE_TECHNIQUE.md) is ignored
# for a different reason: pytest-benchmark disables its timing machinery when
# pytest-xdist is active (confirmed — "Benchmarks are automatically disabled
# because xdist plugin is active"), and backend-ci-cd-pipeline.yml runs this
# suite via `-n auto`. Running the file there doesn't silently no-op though —
# confirmed live, every test crashes with AttributeError ('NoneType' object
# has no attribute 'stats') since the benchmark fixture's .stats never gets
# populated. It has its own blocking CI step, invoked explicitly without
# -n auto (see
# backend-ci-cd-pipeline.yml's "Engine perf ceilings" step and the module
# docstring for the full design rationale).
addopts = "--cov=api --cov-report=term --cov-report=html --cov-fail-under=90 -v --ignore=api/tests/test_schema_contract.py --ignore=api/tests/test_engine_benchmarks.py"
# Test integrity (phase 11b): a mistyped marker (`@pytest.mark.skipp`) is an
# error instead of a silently ignored decoration (strict_markers), and
# an xfail test that starts passing fails the run (xfail_strict), so a fixed
# bug can't hide behind a stale xfail. A test that is genuinely nondeterministic
# opts out explicitly with `strict=False` and a reason (test_polity_vllm_live.py).
# Ini keys, not addopts: they hold under `-o addopts=""` (fast-gate, local runs).
strict_markers = true
xfail_strict = true
# behavior("ELE-01", ...): the docs/spec/behaviors.md invariants a test checks;
# test_behavior_catalogue.py keeps the catalogue and the markers in step.
markers = [
    "behavior(*ids): the docs/spec/behaviors.md invariant IDs this test checks",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["api"]
# Branch data: diff-cover --branch-coverage (backend-ci-cd-pipeline.yml) fails a
# changed line whose branch was only taken one way (an `if` whose `else` no test
# reaches), which line coverage alone counts as covered. It also makes the
# fail_under total below combine lines and branches.
branch = true
omit = ["api/tests/*"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
precision = 0
fail_under = 90

# Linting (replaces flake8 as of Lot 1 of PLAN_SOLIDITE_TECHNIQUE.md — same
# ~100x speedup and broader rule catalogue Ruff is known for, kept OUT of
# scope here: this is a faithful swap, not a coverage expansion). Deliberately
# narrow, matching the .flake8 config this replaces exactly: only F (pyflakes
# — unused imports/vars, undefined names, f-string mistakes) is selected.
# Syntax errors are reported by Ruff unconditionally, regardless of `select`,
# so there's no equivalent of flake8's E9 to configure. The cosmetic E/W
# pycodestyle codes stay OFF on purpose: the codebase uses a column-aligned
# style those checks dislike and they carry no correctness signal — the exact
# reasoning the replaced .flake8 documented for its own narrow `select`.
# (The old .flake8 also ignored F824 — Ruff has no F824 rule at all, so
# there's nothing to carry over.)
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
extend-exclude = [
    ".vulture_whitelist.py",  # same exclusion the old .flake8 had — its
                              # bare names are deliberately "undefined",
                              # that's how vulture's whitelist mechanism works.
    "*.ipynb",  # flake8 never linted notebooks at all (no native support);
                # Ruff does by default, which is real *new* coverage, not
                # parity — out of scope for a faithful swap. Revisit
                # separately if notebook linting is ever wanted.
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["F", "NPY002"]   # NPY002: legacy np.random.* singleton calls
# Test integrity (CI hardening plan, phase 11b): api/tests is linted too, and
# these rules catch a test that can pass without checking anything -- a bare
# comparison or expression that asserts nothing (B015, B018), `assert False`
# (B011, PT015), a pytest.raises with no expected exception or so broad any
# ValueError passes (PT010, PT011), raises/warns blocks that swallow more than
# one statement (PT012, PT031), a closure that sees a later loop value (B023),
# an assert inside `except` (PT017) and unittest-style asserts (PT027).
# Enabled for test code only: see per-file-ignores below.
extend-select = ["B011", "B015", "B018", "B023", "PT010", "PT011", "PT012", "PT015", "PT017", "PT027", "PT030", "PT031"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# The test-integrity rules above apply to tests only; the rest of the codebase
# keeps its existing rule set (enabling B018/B023 there is a separate decision).
"!{api/tests/**,scripts/**/tests/**}" = ["B011", "B015", "B018", "B023", "PT010", "PT011", "PT012", "PT015", "PT017", "PT027", "PT030", "PT031"]
# These two tests drive the legacy global RNG on purpose, to prove the engine
# never reads or reseeds it.
"api/tests/test_no_global_rng.py" = ["NPY002"]
"api/tests/test_seeded_rng_isolation.py" = ["NPY002"]

# Unused/undeclared dependency detection (Lot 2, PLAN_SOLIDITE_TECHNIQUE.md —
# knip's Python equivalent). Scoped to api/ — fast_api_voter/scripts/ holds
# the polity LLM test harness and acceptance scripts, a self-contained tool
# area with its own dependency footprint (e.g. scipy, used only there), not
# part of the application's own dependency contract this is meant to police.
[tool.deptry]
ignore_notebooks = true  # Electors simulation.ipynb — exploration, not the app.
extend_exclude = [
    "scripts/",    # see above.
    "api/tests/",  # deptry's own docs: dev-only code should be excluded from
                   # scanning entirely, not detected — a test file importing
                   # pytest/hypothesis directly isn't a "misplaced dependency"
                   # (DEP004), it's exactly where a dev dependency belongs.
]

# deptry can't derive this one from the PyPI name on its own: the package
# installs into the nested opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi namespace
# path (see api/core/tracing.py's import) rather than a flat opentelemetry_
# instrumentation_fastapi module — without this mapping it wrongly reports
# DEP002 ("defined as a dependency but not used"), confirmed via its own
# "Assuming the corresponding module name..." warning during Lot 13's
# CODE_AUDIT.md refresh.
[tool.deptry.package_module_name_map]
"opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi" = "opentelemetry"

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# Each of these is a real, deliberate case deptry's static import-scanning
# can't see, not an unfixed finding — see PR that introduced this section for
# the investigation behind each one:
DEP002 = [
    "python-dotenv",  # never `import dotenv` directly; used internally by
                       # pydantic-settings' `SettingsConfigDict(env_file=...)`.
    "uvicorn",         # not `import`ed by api/ or api/tests/ (also excluded
                       # above) — invoked as a CLI process (Dockerfile CMD /
                       # workflow `run:` steps), never as a library.
]
DEP003 = [
    "starlette",  # imported directly in api/main.py, but deliberately left as
                  # fastapi's transitive pin rather than a second explicit one
                  # — see requirements.txt's fastapi line, which already
                  # tracks starlette's CVE-fixed versions through fastapi's
                  # own pin. A separate starlette== pin would just be a second
                  # place that pin can drift out of sync.
]

# Second static-analysis opinion alongside mypy (Lot 6.2, PLAN_SOLIDITE_
# TECHNIQUE.md — informational only, not a gate; see scripts/audit.sh
# --quality). "standard" (not "strict"/"all"): basedpyright's stricter modes
# propagate `Unknown` far more aggressively than `mypy --strict` and drown
# the signal — e.g. ~15k warnings from z3-solver alone lacking type stubs.
# api/tests/ excluded to match mypy.ini's own `exclude = (tests)` scope, so
# the two tools are compared on the same code, not different codebases.
[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["api"]
exclude = ["api/tests"]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
pythonVersion = "3.14"
# mypy.ini's `plugins = pydantic.mypy` understands `Field(default, ge=, ...)`
# and `Field(default_factory=SomeModel)` as providing real defaults;
# basedpyright's PEP 681 (dataclass_transform) support doesn't fully resolve
# that overload combination and reports phantom missing-argument/type errors
# on otherwise-correct pydantic models — a known, documented baseline
# (~32 findings, all verified false positives), not something to chase to
# zero. See PLAN_SOLIDITE_TECHNIQUE.md §6.2 for the full breakdown.

# Dead-code detection (informational only — see CODE_AUDIT.md for the
# rationale and how this feeds scripts/audit.sh / CI). min_confidence=80 keeps
# the signal-to-noise ratio usable: below that threshold Enum members and
# FastAPI/pydantic decorated handlers dominate the output as false positives.
# The whitelist (.vulture_whitelist.py) is passed as an extra PATH argument
# on the command line, e.g. `vulture api/ .vulture_whitelist.py --config ...`
# — vulture has no config key for it.
[tool.vulture]
min_confidence = 80
ignore_decorators = [
  "@*.get", "@*.post", "@*.put", "@*.patch", "@*.delete", "@*.websocket",
  "@field_validator", "@model_validator", "@validator",
]
exclude = ["api/tests/"]

# Python modernization (Lot 6, PLAN_SOLIDITE_TECHNIQUE.md — informational
# only, see scripts/audit.sh --quality). 145 findings, 77 of them the same
# `dict(x)`/`list(x)` -> `.copy()` idiom (FURB123) — a real, if tiny, perf
# win on a CPU-bound engine (`.copy()` skips the general dict/list
# constructor's type dispatch) but purely mechanical, so left as a baseline
# to fix incrementally rather than a one-shot mass edit across ~30 files.
[tool.refurb]
python_version = "3.14"

[tool.mutmut]
# Score de mutation du moteur de vote. Le fichier a longtemps porté 177 lignes
# de commentaire pour 52 de config : l'historique complet (pourquoi la sélection
# de tests est dérivée et non curée à la main, la panne numpy 2.4+ / mutmut
# 3.7.0 qui a tenu le job rouge 17 jours, pourquoi le correctif 3.8.0 a triplé
# le nombre de mutants sans que ce soit une régression, et pourquoi le plancher
# reste à 70 %) vit maintenant dans
# docs/exploration/EXP-015-mutmut-mutation-testing-scope.md.
#
# Ne restent ici que les notes qui expliquent une clé à son point d'usage.
source_paths = [
    "api/engine/utils/simulation_ranked_utils.py",
    # The cardinal half of the engine-parity harness. Both files are locked
    # against the TS client by voter-app's playgroundVoting.parity.test.ts, so
    # both deserve the same "do the tests actually assert, or just execute?"
    # check — mutating only the ordinal half left half the invariant unmeasured.
    "api/engine/utils/simulation_score_utils.py",
    # 11 of 15 workers here are numpy-free and now have direct-call tests
    # (test_theory_pure.py) that mutmut's auto-detection can select — see
    # EXP-015 for why. The 4 numpy-touching workers are not
    # covered here; they stay excluded pending confirmation numpy itself
    # doesn't retrigger the in-process reload failure.
    "api/domain/theory/workers.py",
]
# mutmut's mutants/ working copy only contains source_paths + also_copy —
# our tests live at api/tests/ (not the top-level tests/ mutmut assumes by
# default), and pytest needs the rest of the api/ package (schemas, routes,
# __init__.py chain) importable too. also_copy runs before mutation
# application, so re-copying the source_paths file here is harmless.
also_copy = ["api/"]
# Skip lines the coverage report already shows as unexercised — mutants there
# are guaranteed, uninteresting survivors (we already know from --cov-report
# that nothing asserts on them); this keeps the baseline focused on "did a
# covered line's mutation actually get caught".
mutate_only_covered_lines = true
# -o addopts= strips pyproject's `--cov-fail-under=90` (and -v) for mutmut's
# own pytest runs: mutmut selects a small per-mutant test subset via
# dependency tracking, so that subset's coverage is always far below the
# repo-wide 85% floor — without this override, every mutant run would exit
# non-zero on the coverage gate regardless of whether the mutant was
# actually caught, corrupting the kill/survive signal (same footgun as the
# quick local `-o addopts=""` pattern documented in CLAUDE.md).
pytest_add_cli_args = ["-o", "addopts="]
# EVERY test file that imports either source_paths module directly and does NOT
# touch FastAPI/TestClient/numpy (the in-process re-exec incompatibility above).
# Derived, not hand-curated — regenerate with:
#   for p in api/tests/test_*.py; do
#     grep -qE "simulation_(ranked|score)_utils" "$p" || continue
#     grep -qE "TestClient|from fastapi|import numpy|from api\.main" "$p" && continue
#     echo "$p"
#   done
#
# The previous list held 12 + 2 files out of the 80 in api/tests/, and its own
# KNOWN CAVEAT flagged nine functions (condorcet, two_round, plurality, approval,
# minimax, copeland, nanson, baldwin, kemeny) as having "no dedicated test file
# in the list above". They all had one — it just wasn't selected. So the score
# was partly measuring this list rather than the tests. Widening it to 25 files
# moved the run from 58.9% to 64.2% (714 → 621 survivors) with no test written.
#
# Regenerated again after test_anonymity.py + test_cardinal_orphans.py were
# added (the 13-rule tie-break fix): the measured score barely moved on that
# PR (64.2% → 63.2%, despite fixing 13 real bugs and adding 96 tests) because
# this list is hand-curated, not auto-discovered, and neither new file had
# been added to it — the exact tests written to catch the tie-break bugs never
# ran under mutmut at all.
#
# It drifted a third time (6 matching files missing, test_borda.py among them,
# so Borda's own tests never ran against Borda's mutants). The list is now
# locked to the rule above by api/tests/test_mutmut_selection.py: a file the
# rule selects must be listed here or named, with its reason, in that test's
# EXCLUDED (the benchmarks, and the two whole-engine suites too slow to run
# per mutant).
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = [
    "api/tests/test_anonymity.py",
    "api/tests/test_anti_plurality.py",
    "api/tests/test_approval.py",
    "api/tests/test_baldwin.py",
    "api/tests/test_ballot_dict_format.py",
    "api/tests/test_benham.py",
    "api/tests/test_black.py",
    "api/tests/test_borda.py",
    "api/tests/test_bucklin_cumulative.py",
    "api/tests/test_cardinal_batch.py",
    "api/tests/test_cardinal_orphans.py",
    "api/tests/test_condorcet.py",
    "api/tests/test_copeland.py",
    "api/tests/test_dowdall.py",
    "api/tests/test_gibbard_satterthwaite.py",
    # Property-based suites: the most effective mutant killers in the selection,
    # and both were previously left out.
    "api/tests/test_hypothesis_condorcet.py",
    "api/tests/test_hypothesis_monotonicity.py",
    "api/tests/test_irv_coombs_elimination.py",
    "api/tests/test_kemeny_young.py",
    "api/tests/test_literature_counterexamples.py",
    "api/tests/test_minimax.py",
    "api/tests/test_nanson.py",
    "api/tests/test_plurality.py",
    "api/tests/test_positional_score.py",
    "api/tests/test_ranked_pairs_random_ballot.py",
    "api/tests/test_raynaud.py",
    "api/tests/test_river.py",
    "api/tests/test_schulze_beatpath.py",
    "api/tests/test_smith_irv.py",
    "api/tests/test_split_cycle.py",
    "api/tests/test_star_runoff_tie.py",
    "api/tests/test_tally_ties_by_name.py",
    "api/tests/test_theory_pure.py",
    "api/tests/test_tie_lot.py",
    "api/tests/test_two_round.py",
    "api/tests/test_workers_behavioral.py",
]

# Makes the voter-api skill's documented layering blocking instead of just
# written down (Lot 2, PLAN_SOLIDITE_TECHNIQUE.md — see .claude/skills/
# voter-api/SKILL.md's "Layering (never short-circuit it)" section, which
# this contract enforces verbatim). A "layers" contract forbids any import
# from a layer back up into one listed above it; api.routes may import
# api.domain and api.engine, api.domain may import api.engine, never the
# reverse. api.core/api.schemas/api.sockets are deliberately not covered —
# the skill only documents routes -> domain -> engine, and sockets already
# has its own distinct (and legitimate) shape, calling api.engine directly
# for its narrower live-stream use case.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["api"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layering: routes -> domain -> engine"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "api.routes",
    "api.domain",
    "api.engine",
]

# Performance anti-patterns on the CPU-bound simulation engine (Lot 6,
# PLAN_SOLIDITE_TECHNIQUE.md — informational, see scripts/audit.sh
# --quality). Everything except loop-invariant-statement disabled: that one
# rule alone fires ~1,600 times on this codebase's dense per-voter/per-
# candidate loops, the overwhelming majority on expressions pylint can't
# prove are actually invariant across iterations (attribute lookups,
# subscripts on mutable containers) -- real signal-to-noise ratio too low
# to be useful at the whole-repo scale; left disabled rather than drowning
# the handful of other, much rarer and much more concrete perflint checks
# (unnecessary-list-cast, incorrect-dictionary-iterator, use-list-copy, ...).
[tool.pylint.main]
load-plugins = ["perflint"]

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
disable = ["all"]
enable = [
    "unnecessary-list-cast", "incorrect-dictionary-iterator",
    "loop-global-usage", "memoryview-over-bytes", "dotted-import-in-loop",
    "use-tuple-over-list", "use-list-comprehension", "use-list-copy",
    "use-dict-comprehension", "loop-try-except-usage",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "fuellib"
version = "3.0.8a3"
description = "FuelLib: A Python library for Group Contribution Method (GCM) calculations of fuel properties"
readme = "README.md"
license = {text = "BSD-3-Clause"}
authors = [
    {name = "NLR", email = "david.montgomery@nlr.gov"},
]
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"
keywords = ["fuel", "thermodynamics", "group-contribution", "properties"]

# =============================================================================
# Import Linter Configuration
# =============================================================================
# Enforces architectural boundaries to maintain clean code structure.
# Run with: lint-imports (or tools/lint_imports.bat)
# =============================================================================

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    mcp_workspace
    tests
root_package_paths =
    src
    .
include_external_packages = True
# Match tach's ignore_type_checking_imports, so an annotation-only import is not
# reported as a dependency. The flag applies at graph-build time, so it governs
# all nine contracts - including the six library-isolation ones and the
# subprocess ban, which depend on external edges (include_external_packages).
# Trade-off: a forbidden library import hidden inside a TYPE_CHECKING guard
# would no longer be flagged. Nothing changes today - the only upward
# TYPE_CHECKING imports in src/ are base_branch's two, and no module
# type-checking-imports github/git/mcp/requests/subprocess outside its allowed
# home.
exclude_type_checking_imports = True

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: Layered Architecture
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensures dependencies flow in one direction:
#   main -> server -> file_tools -> (no internal dependencies)
#
# Why this matters:
# - Prevents circular dependencies
# - Keeps entry point (main) as thin orchestration layer
# - Server focuses on MCP protocol, delegates to file_tools
# - File tools are independent, reusable utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:layered_architecture]
name = Layered Architecture
type = layers
layers =
    mcp_workspace.main
    mcp_workspace.server
    mcp_workspace.server_reference_tools
    mcp_workspace.checks
    mcp_workspace.file_tools | mcp_workspace.github_operations | mcp_workspace.reference_projects
    mcp_workspace.git_operations | mcp_workspace.workflows
    mcp_workspace.config | mcp_workspace.constants | mcp_workspace.utils | mcp_workspace._ssl

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: MCP Library Isolation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 'mcp' package should only be imported by main.py and server.py.
# File tools should remain MCP-agnostic for reusability.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: PyGithub Library Isolation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 'github' package should only be used by github_operations module.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:pygithub_isolation]
name = PyGithub Library Isolation
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    mcp_workspace
forbidden_modules =
    github
ignore_imports =
    mcp_workspace.github_operations.* -> github
    mcp_workspace.github_operations.** -> github

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: Requests Library Isolation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 'requests' library should only be used by github_operations module.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:requests_isolation]
name = Requests Library Isolation
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    mcp_workspace
forbidden_modules =
    requests
ignore_imports =
    mcp_workspace.github_operations.* -> requests
    mcp_workspace.github_operations.** -> requests

[importlinter:contract:mcp_library_isolation]
name = MCP Library Isolation
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    mcp_workspace
forbidden_modules =
    mcp
ignore_imports =
    mcp_workspace.server -> mcp
    mcp_workspace.server_reference_tools -> mcp

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: GitPython Library Isolation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 'git' package should only be used by git_operations module.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:gitpython_isolation]
name = GitPython Library Isolation
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    mcp_workspace
forbidden_modules =
    git
ignore_imports =
    mcp_workspace.git_operations.* -> git

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: Structlog Library Isolation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structured logging should only be configured in log_utils.
# Other modules should use standard logging.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:structlog_isolation]
name = Structlog Library Isolation
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    mcp_workspace
forbidden_modules =
    structlog

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: Python JSON Logger Isolation
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# python-json-logger should only be used via mcp_coder_utils (external).
# No direct imports allowed from mcp_workspace.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:pythonjsonlogger_isolation]
name = Python JSON Logger Isolation
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    mcp_workspace
forbidden_modules =
    pythonjsonlogger

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: Subprocess Ban
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Production code must not use subprocess directly.
# Use GitPython for git operations instead.
# Note: mcp_coder_utils.subprocess_runner/streaming are banned via tach.toml
# (not listed in depends_on for any production module).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:subprocess_ban]
name = Subprocess Ban (use GitPython instead)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    mcp_workspace
forbidden_modules =
    subprocess
ignore_imports =
    mcp_workspace.git_operations.verification -> subprocess

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: Source Code Independence from Tests
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Production code should never import from test modules.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:no_test_imports_in_source]
name = Source Code Independence from Tests
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    mcp_workspace
forbidden_modules =
    tests

[dependency-groups]
# Workspace-only compensation for `[tool.uv] override-dependencies` (#2378).
# The override strips anthropic's `docstring-parser` requirement from every uv
# resolution so it cannot shadow pydoclint's `docstring-parser-fork`, which owns
# the same top-level `docstring_parser` module. In a sync that also has `full`
# the fork arrives via pydoclint, but `uv sync --extra ai` on its own would then
# install neither and `anthropic.lib.tools` would raise ModuleNotFoundError.
# This group puts the fork back for exactly those syncs, and no call site has to
# ask for it: `[tool.uv] default-groups` below lists `ai-runtime` alongside
# `dev`, so a plain `uv sync --extra ai` already carries the fork. `ai-review.yml`
# and `scripts/ci/run-ai-contract-tests.sh` therefore pass no `--group` flag.
#
# It is deliberately NOT on the published `ai` extra: the override is a uv
# workspace setting that pip never reads, so shipping the fork in wheel metadata
# would make `uv pip install 'lintro[ai]'` (README, docs/configuration.md) pull
# two distributions that own `docstring_parser`. lintro itself imports neither.

[tool.ruff.lint]

  "COM",

  "D",

# Structural thresholds (issue #2291). Ratchet plan: max-complexity 15 -> 12 -> 10.

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.black]
line-length = 88
target-version = ["py311", "py312", "py313", "py314"]
exclude = "/(\n    \\.git\n    | \\.venv\n    | venv\n    | build\n    | dist\n    | __pycache__\n    | test_samples\n    | node_modules\n)/\n"

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["test_samples"]
# Suppression policy (see issue #1026):
#   - Global skips are reserved for rules that are genuinely universal noise
#     across the whole codebase and cannot be meaningfully scoped.
#   - Subprocess rules (B404/B603/B607) are NOT skipped globally: subprocess is
#     the core execution mechanism, but each call site must be reviewed and
#     suppressed inline with a justification, e.g.
#       ``subprocess.run(...)  # nosec B603 - resolved binary, shell=False, no user shell input``
#   - Use a file-top / per-call-site ``# nosec Bxxx - <specific reason>`` rather
#     than a broad global skip whenever the rule can apply to new code.
skips = [
  "B101", # assert_used — pytest and test helpers rely on ``assert`` across all of tests/; genuinely universal, cannot be scoped meaningfully
  "B108", # hardcoded_tmp_directory — ``/tmp`` appears in fixtures and temp-path examples throughout tests; universal noise
]

[tool.lintro]
line_length = 88

# Warn-level module-size gate (issue #1052). Guards against the recurring
# oversized-module pattern. Non-blocking today: existing violators are
# baselined so the gate is green on merge. Ratchet plan: refactor the baselined
# modules below the threshold, remove them from `baseline`, then lower
# `threshold` in steps (800 -> 700 -> 600). See lintro/utils/module_size.py.
[tool.lintro.module_size]
enabled = true
threshold = 800
baseline = ["lintro/cli_utils/commands/doctor.py"]
exclude = [
  "test_samples/",
  "node_modules/",
  ".venv/",
  "venv/",
  "dist/",
  "build/",
  "__pycache__/",
  ".lintro/",
  "tests/",
]

[tool.lintro.pip_audit]
# Advisory ids pip-audit ignores on this repository's own requirements.
# Every id here must also be a time-boxed [[IgnoredVulns]] entry (by id or
# alias) in .osv-scanner.toml, which carries the reason and the expiry;
# tests/unit/test_pip_audit_ignores.py fails when one is missing or expired.
# GHSA-84m7-p3x7-pcfv / CVE-2026-59951: mcp 1.29.0, pinned exactly by semgrep;
# see the osv entry. Drop both together once semgrep's pin moves.
ignore_vulns = ["CVE-2026-59951", "GHSA-84m7-p3x7-pcfv"]

# Duplicate-code ratchet gate (issue #2293). pylint's `duplicate-code` checker
# runs on the per-tool packages only, so the copy-pasted definition template
# cannot grow back after #2311 factored it out. `include` lists every
# `lintro/tools/<tool>` package, so a new tool joins the gate by being added
# here alongside its package. pylint has no per-finding
# baseline, so the ratchet is a count: `duplicate_code_baseline` is the number
# of R0801 blocks present when the gate landed, and the run fails when the
# count is higher. Lower this number in the PR that removes duplication; never
# raise it, and lower `MAX_ALLOWED_DUPLICATE_CODE_BASELINE` in
# tests/unit/test_duplicate_code_baseline.py in the same commit — that test
# asserts this value is `<=` the ceiling recorded there, so leaving the ceiling
# behind would silently allow the baseline to climb back. #2311 drove the count
# to 0, so the gate is now zero-tolerance: any new clone set in the per-tool
# packages fails the run. The live guard stays `<=` so a pylint/astroid build
# that reports a phantom finding is the only way this can move, and the fix is
# to delete the duplication. See lintro/utils/duplicate_code.py.
[tool.lintro.pylint]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
# The offline eval harness (#2147) is repo-only tooling, not a package: its
# root has to be on the search path for ``review_matrix`` imports to resolve.
mypy_path = ["evals/review-efficacy"]
# Pin the incremental cache to one location (#2297). A bare ".mypy_cache" is
# mypy's default and is still resolved against the process cwd, so it would
# not stop an invocation started outside the repo root from scattering a cache
# into that subdirectory. $MYPY_CONFIG_FILE_DIR expands to the directory
# holding this file, which anchors the cache to the repo root from any cwd.
# .gitignore keeps them untracked either way; this stops them being created.
cache_dir = "$MYPY_CONFIG_FILE_DIR/.mypy_cache"
strict = true
ignore_missing_imports = false
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_unused_configs = true
explicit_package_bases = true
namespace_packages = true
exclude = [
  "^test_samples/",
  "^node_modules/",
  "^dist/",
  "^build/",
  "^\\.venv/",
  "^venv/",
  "^env/",
  "^__pycache__/",
  "^\\.lintro/",
]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["assertpy"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["mcp", "mcp.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]

  "tests.utils.*",

  "tests.scripts.*",

[tool.uv]
# pydoclint (the `full` extra) depends on `docstring-parser-fork`; anthropic (the
# `ai` extra) depends on `docstring-parser`. Both distributions install the same
# top-level `docstring_parser` package, so an environment carrying both ends up
# with one shadowing the other — pydoclint then dies on import with
# `cannot import name 'DocstringYields' from 'docstring_parser.common'`, and
# `lintro chk` reports it as skipped rather than failed, silently dropping the DOC
# gate. No version pin helps: those symbols exist only in the fork. CI's dogfood
# job installs `full` alone, but the published `ai` Docker image and any local
# `--extra full --extra ai` sync need both, so drop anthropic's requirement and
# let the fork own the module (#2378). See the `ai-runtime` dependency-group
# above for the ai-without-full case. The
# fork is a superset of upstream, and anthropic touches only
# `docstring_parser.parse` / `.Docstring` in its optional `@beta_tool` helper,
# which the fork provides and lintro does not use. `uv.lock` must therefore
# resolve `docstring-parser-fork` and no `docstring-parser`;
# `tests/unit/test_docstring_parser_override.py` fails if that ever regresses.
override-dependencies = ["docstring-parser ; sys_platform == 'never'"]

# `ai-runtime` joins `dev` as a default group so *every* uv sync carries the
# fork, including `uv sync --extra ai` with no flags. Requiring callers to pass
# `--group ai-runtime` coupled them to this file: `ai-review.yml` runs under
# `pull_request_target`, which takes the workflow from the base branch while
# checking out `base.sha`, so a flag and a group landing together still skew
# apart whenever a checked-out base predates them. Defaulting the group removes
# the coupling — there is no call site to keep in step (#2378).
default-groups = ["dev", "ai-runtime"]

constraint-dependencies = [
  # Security fix: TOCTOU vulnerability in directory creation (dependabot alert #4)
  "virtualenv>=20.36.1",
  # High-severity transitive remediation (issue #1118). These advisories flow
  # through the `mcp` extra / default dev group (mcp -> pyjwt[crypto],
  # starlette, python-multipart) and twine (urllib3). None are core runtime
  # deps, but we force the patched versions so no shipped extra carries a
  # known high-severity vulnerability. Semgrep is no longer in this graph
  # (#2104); its tree lives in requirements-semgrep.txt.
  # pyjwt: crit-header handling / RFC 7515 violation
  # (GHSA-xgmm-8j9v-c9wx, supersedes prior >=2.12.1 for GHSA-... alert #26)
  "pyjwt>=2.13.0",
  # starlette: multipart/form parsing DoS
  # (GHSA-82w8-qh3p-5jfq, GHSA-wqp7-x3pw-xc5r)
  "starlette>=1.3.1",
  # cryptography: OpenSSL-backed high-severity advisory (GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf);
  # PKCS#7 Bleichenbacher oracle (GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5)
  "cryptography>=50.0.1",
  # python-multipart: parser resource-exhaustion DoS
  # (GHSA-5rvq-cxj2-64vf, GHSA-pp6c-gr5w-3c5g)
  "python-multipart>=0.0.30",
  # urllib3: redirect / pool-manager high-severity advisories
  # (GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc, GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j)
  "urllib3>=2.7.0",
]

# import-linter (#2289; contracts from #2290). `root_package` lets
# `lint-imports` build lintro's import graph; the two contracts below declare
# the package layering the re-alignment roadmap (#2288) refactors towards.
#
# RATCHET RULE (binding). Every `ignore_imports` entry is a violation that
# exists today, annotated with the issue that will delete it. An entry may be
# **deleted, never added**, and the list may only shrink. A PR that closes a
# cycle deletes its entries in the same PR. If a change would need a new entry,
# the change is wrong: turn the dependency around instead. Moving a
# module-level import into a function body is **not** a fix — `import-linter`
# counts function-body imports, and so does `scripts/ci/import_matrix.py`,
# whose two-way cycle count `tests/unit/test_import_boundaries.py` pins.
# Exception: a new tool package records its three
# `-> lintro.plugins.{base,protocol,registry}` edges under #2410, which owns the
# `lintro.plugins` / `lintro.tools` cycle: discovery in `lintro.plugins` imports
# `lintro.tools`, while the plugin base-class edge runs the other way.

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "lintro"

# Contract 1 (#2290): the AI subsystem is an optional extra, so `lintro chk`
# must load without it. Sources are every top-level package except the four
# that are allowed to reach into it: `ai` itself and the `mcp`, `cli_utils` and
# `api` entry points.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core-does-not-import-ai"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "lintro.config",
  "lintro.deps",
  "lintro.enums",
  "lintro.exceptions",
  "lintro.formatters",
  "lintro.licenses",
  "lintro.models",
  "lintro.parsers",
  "lintro.plugins",
  "lintro.profiling",
  "lintro.tools",
  "lintro.utils",
  "lintro.watch",
]
forbidden_modules = ["lintro.ai"]
# Explicit rather than relying on import-linter's default: a stale entry must
# fail the contract, otherwise the baseline could shrink on paper only.
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "error"
ignore_imports = [
  # 4 edges owned by #2312
  "lintro.utils.doctor_report -> lintro.ai.doctor_checks",  # owned by #2312
  "lintro.utils.doctor_report -> lintro.ai.interface",      # owned by #2312
  "lintro.utils.execution.advisory -> lintro.ai.config",    # owned by #2312
  "lintro.utils.output.sarif.document -> lintro.ai.models", # owned by #2312
  # 11 edges owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.definition -> lintro.ai.availability", # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.definition -> lintro.ai.budget",       # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.definition -> lintro.ai.config",       # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.definition -> lintro.ai.exceptions",   # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.definition -> lintro.ai.interface",    # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.definition -> lintro.ai.paths",        # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.definition -> lintro.ai.providers",    # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.engine -> lintro.ai.budget",           # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.engine -> lintro.ai.config",           # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.engine -> lintro.ai.invoke",           # owned by #2331
  "lintro.tools.idiom_review.engine -> lintro.ai.providers.base",   # owned by #2331
]

# Contract 2 (#2290): the target layering, highest layer first. Packages on one
# line are independent siblings and may not import each other.
#
# #2290 specified an `execution` layer above `plugins | tools`, declared as the
# module paths it occupies today (`utils.tool_executor`,
# `utils.async_tool_executor`, `utils.execution`). `import-linter` rejects a
# contract whose layers share descendants ("Modules have shared descendants"),
# so `lintro.utils` and `lintro.utils.execution` cannot both be layers. Those
# modules therefore stay inside the `utils` layer, which is the stricter of the
# two readings; #2312 lifts them into a real `lintro.execution` package and
# adds the layer then.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "layers"
type = "layers"
containers = ["lintro"]
layers = [
  "cli_utils | mcp | api",
  "ai",
  "watch | profiling",
  "plugins | tools",
  "config",
  "formatters | parsers",
  "utils",
  "models",
  "enums",

# pylint (#2292). Only the duplicate-code (R0801) checker is enabled: every
# other pylint check either duplicates ruff/mypy or contradicts this repo's
# style, so `disable = ["all"]` keeps the tool to the one job lintro has no
# other checker for. `jobs = 0` fans the run out across all cores; the
# similarity checker implements pylint's map/reduce protocol, so R0801 is
# still detected across workers. pylint is not enabled in
# `.lintro-config.yaml` yet — that lands with the baseline in #2293, where
# the intended paths are `lintro` and `tests`.
[tool.pylint.main]
disable = ["all"]
enable = ["duplicate-code"]
jobs = 0

[tool.pylint.similarities]
min-similarity-lines = 12
ignore-comments = true
ignore-docstrings = true
ignore-imports = true

[tool.pydoclint]
style = "google"
arg-type-hints-in-docstring = false
arg-type-hints-in-signature = true
check-return-types = false
check-arg-order = true
skip-checking-short-docstrings = true
allow-init-docstring = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_functions = "test_*"
timeout = 120
timeout_method = "thread"
# The AI provider layer is async end to end (issue #722); auto mode runs
# plain `async def test_*` functions without per-test decorators.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
markers = [
  "docker_only: mark test as requiring Docker or Docker-specific dependencies",
  "slow: mark test as slow running (use @pytest.mark.timeout(300) if needed)",
  "timeout: override default timeout for slow tests",
  "integration: mark test as integration test",
  "unit: mark test as unit test",
  "generated_questions: run the once-per-run review question pass (#2720) instead of the review suite's default rubric-only opt-out",
  "verification: run the per-round verification pass (#2728) instead of the review suite's default unverified opt-out",
  "cli: mark test as CLI test",
  "utils: mark test as utility test",
  "formatters: mark test as formatter test",
  "markdownlint: mark test as markdownlint specific",
  "html_validate: mark test as html-validate specific",
  "hadolint: mark test as hadolint specific",
  "prettier: mark test as prettier specific",
  "yamllint: mark test as yamllint specific",
  "ruff: mark test as ruff specific",
  "actionlint: mark test as actionlint specific",
  "pytest: mark test as pytest specific",
  # Tiered AI CLI contract tests (issue #1614). Tier 1 reads only --version
  # and --help, so it is free and can gate every change; tier 2 makes a real
  # call, so it spends quota and is opt-in via LINTRO_CONTRACT_TIER2=1.
  "contract_tier1: free flag-surface check against an installed agent CLI",
  "contract_tier2: real-invocation smoke test that spends provider quota",
]
# No --maxfail here on purpose (issue #2295): a red run must report every
# failure, not just the first few.
addopts = [
  "--strict-markers",
  "--durations=10",
  "--tb=short",
  "--showlocals",
  "-v",
]
filterwarnings = ["ignore:Couldn't import C tracer"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["lintro", "lintro_build"]
branch = true
omit = ["lintro/ascii-art/*", "*/__main__.py"]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 81
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
exclude_also = ["if TYPE_CHECKING:", "raise NotImplementedError", "@overload"]

package com.mycompany.myapp

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class ArchTest {

    @Test
    fun servicesAndRepositoriesShouldNotDependOnWebLayer() {

        val importedClasses = ClassFileImporter()
            .withImportOption(ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
            .importPackages("com.mycompany.myapp")

        noClasses()
            .that()
                .resideInAnyPackage("com.mycompany.myapp.service..")
            .or()
                .resideInAnyPackage("com.mycompany.myapp.repository..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
                .resideInAnyPackage("..com.mycompany.myapp.web..")
        .because("Services and repositories should not depend on web layer")
        .check(importedClasses)
    }
}

package com.bmarques.springarchunitmvcexample

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired
import org.springframework.stereotype.Repository
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service

class ArchUnitAnnotationCheckTest {

    private var importedClasses: JavaClasses? = null

    @BeforeEach
    fun setup() {
        importedClasses = ClassFileImporter()
                .withImportOption(ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
                .importPackages("com.bmarques.springarchunitmvcexample")
    }

    @Test
    fun `Field injection not should be use with Autowired annotation`() =
        ArchRuleDefinition.noFields()
                .should().beAnnotatedWith(Autowired::class.java)
                .check(importedClasses)

    @Test
    fun `Repository classes should have spring repository annotation`() =
        ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..repository..")
                .should().beAnnotatedWith(Repository::class.java)
                .check(importedClasses)

    @Test
    fun `Service classes should have spring service annotation`() =
        ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..service..")
                .should().beAnnotatedWith(Service::class.java)
                .check(importedClasses)
}

# catches subtle correctness issues.

[project]
name = "aionto-sdk"
version = "0.1.0rc5"
description = "Aion Python SDK — A2A server, authoring toolkits and the aion CLI"
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
authors = [{ name = "Terminal Research Team", email = "support@terminal.exchange" }]
# No upper bound: this is the wheel's Requires-Python, and Poetry refuses a
# dependency whose Python range is narrower than the installing project's
# (^3.12, the default there, means <4.0). The one bound the tree does carry
# sits on litellm, below, as a marker.
requires-python = ">=3.12"

# The base install: aion.core, aion.api, aion.mcp endpoints and the CLI shell.
# Everything the server needs to breathe - a database, an ASGI stack, the
# a2a-sdk server extras - lives in [server] instead, so `pip install aionto-sdk`
# stays small enough to be worth doing.
#
# asyncclick and keyring are here rather than in [server] because `aion --help`
# has to work in a base install: without a console entry point there is nothing
# left to print the hint about which extra to install.
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.11.3",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.3.4",
    # 1.2.0 is the first release whose load_dotenv() honours
    # PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED, the switch the `aion` CLI documents for skipping a
    # project's `.env` and the test suites rely on: libraries the frameworks
    # bring call load_dotenv() on import, and only the switch stops them.
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.0",
    # Two reasons this is not 6.0. PyYAML 6.0 ships no wheel for any
    # interpreter this project supports and its sdist does not build on 3.12,
    # so the floor that was written here could never have been installed at
    # all; and google-adk, whose floor the adk extra sets, asks for
    # >=6.0.2 itself. Checked by the `floors` CI job, which installs the
    # bottom of every range below and resolves them together.
    "PyYAML>=6.0.2,<7.0.0",
    # Published, an exact pin conflicts with whatever the installing project
    # already has; the upper bound stays on the minor because aion.server
    # reaches into a2a-sdk's internals. The floor is the release the server's
    # overrides follow: the terminal-state UnsupportedOperationError, the
    # keyset ListTasksCursor, Authorization from a push config's
    # authentication, the stored config set_info returns, and the cluster
    # mode (VersionedTaskStore, TaskEventStream) the server runs on
    # PostgreSQL.
    "a2a-sdk>=1.2.2,<1.3.0",
    # Ariadne's custom operations use graphql-core's 3.2 AST contract.
    # Keep runtime installs aligned with the generator, including without dev extras.
    "gql[websockets]==4.0.0",
    "graphql-core==3.2.13",
    "PyJWT>=2.9.0,<3.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.28.1,<0.29.0",
    "websockets==15.0.1",
    "asyncclick>=8.0.1.2,<9.0.0",
    "keyring>=25.0.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
server = [
    "SQLAlchemy>=2.0.0,<3.0.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0,<2.0.0",
    "psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.1.12,<4.0.0",
    "greenlet>=3.0.3,<4.0.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.23.2",
    "fastapi>=0.115.2",
    "python-logstash-async>=4.0.1,<5.0.0",
    # The only release of asgi-proxy-lib is a pre-release, and pip will not
    # pick one up from an unbounded specifier - hence the exact pin.
    "asgi-proxy-lib==0.2a0",
    # This block is "a2a-sdk[http-server,telemetry,encryption]", written out.
    # It cannot be written that way: Poetry's solver (2.4.1) fails on a package
    # that appears plain in [project.dependencies] and bracketed in more than
    # one extra, and a2a-sdk is exactly that - base, because aion.core builds on
    # its types, and extras-carrying, because aion.server needs its server side.
    # These five are what those three extras of a2a-sdk 1.2 pull in; they are
    # pinned to a2a-sdk's own constraints and held in place by the upper bound
    # on a2a-sdk itself.
    "starlette",
    # 1.6.5 is the oldest release where the separator the JSON-RPC
    # dispatcher and the A2A 0.3 adapter set on a response after building it
    # is honored; below it
    # events go out CRLF-delimited, which HTTP tunnels mangle. Found by the
    # `floors` CI job (tests/unit/server/core/test_jsonrpc_dispatcher.py).
    "sse-starlette>=1.6.5",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.33.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.33.0",
    "cryptography>=43.0.0",
]
langgraph-authoring = [
    # The floor is langchain's, not a guess: langchain 1.0.0 requires
    # langgraph>=1.0.0,<1.1.0, so the pair `langgraph 0.6.0` + `langchain
    # 1.0.0` this range used to allow has no solution and nobody could ever
    # have installed it. The `floors` CI job is what now says so.
    "langgraph>=1.0.0,<2.0.0",
    # Not our dependency: langgraph-prebuilt comes with langgraph, and each
    # langgraph release names the prebuilt range it goes with. Only the floor
    # is ours, so that the `floors` job pairs langgraph 1.0.0 with prebuilt
    # 1.0.0. One pairing langgraph allows does not work: every langgraph below
    # 1.1.3 accepts `langgraph-prebuilt<1.1`, and prebuilt 1.0.9 and later
    # import `ExecutionInfo`, which langgraph.runtime has from 1.1.3 on. A
    # project that holds langgraph below 1.1.3 has to hold prebuilt below
    # 1.0.9 as well; an upper bound here cannot say that without also keeping
    # out the prebuilt that langgraph 1.2 requires. tests/unit/langgraph/
    # test_framework_imports.py and the dist-smoke langgraph-server
    # environment are what fail when a resolution pairs the two wrongly.
    "langgraph-prebuilt>=1.0.0",
    "langchain>=1.0.0,<2.0.0",
    "langchain-mcp-adapters>=0.1.11,<0.4.0",
    "langchain-openai>=1.1.7,<2.0.0",
]
adk-authoring = [
    # 1.27.1, not lower: the server imports `ensure_part` from
    # google.adk.artifacts.base_artifact_service, which 1.27 introduced, and
    # 1.27.0 itself is yanked. Found by the `floors` CI job.
    "google-adk>=1.27.1,<3.0.0",
    # Not our dependency: google-adk 1.27 imports GEN_AI_INPUT_MESSAGES from
    # the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions 0.58b0, which come with
    # opentelemetry 1.37, while declaring `opentelemetry-*>=1.36.0`. At 1.36
    # importing google.adk fails. Drop these two lines once a google-adk
    # release we allow declares the version it imports from.
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.37.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.37.0",
    # aion_lite_llm() builds on ADK's LiteLlm, which imports litellm directly.
    # litellm declares <3.15 in every release we allow. Without the marker that
    # bound would become the SDK's, and Poetry then refuses every project
    # declaring ^3.12. With it, a 3.15 interpreter gets the extra minus litellm
    # and aion_lite_llm() raises ImportError saying so. Drop the marker as soon
    # as litellm supports 3.15.
    "litellm>=1.93,<2.0; python_version < '3.15'",
    # The server builds on google-adk's MCP toolset, which needs mcp. google-adk
    # 1.x depends on it directly; 2.x moved it into its `mcp` extra. The range
    # is the one google-adk states for it.
    "mcp>=1.24,<3.0.0",
]

# The composite extras below are written out in full rather than as
# self-references ("aionto-sdk[langgraph-authoring,server]"). poetry-core emits
# a self-reference correctly and pip resolves it, but Poetry's own solver
# (2.4.1) asserts on any self-referential extra of the root project, which
# takes `poetry install -E ...` - the way this repository is developed - off
# the table. The cost is that a dependency added to a component extra has to be
# added to the composites too; scripts/packaging/check.py is where that drift
# gets caught, by asserting the set relations these unions are supposed to have.
langgraph-server = [
    # aionto-sdk[langgraph-authoring]
    # See [langgraph-authoring] for why the floor is 1.0.0 and not 0.6.0.
    "langgraph>=1.0.0,<2.0.0",
    # See [langgraph-authoring]: only the floor is ours.
    "langgraph-prebuilt>=1.0.0",
    "langchain>=1.0.0,<2.0.0",
    "langchain-mcp-adapters>=0.1.11,<0.4.0",
    "langchain-openai>=1.1.7,<2.0.0",
    # aionto-sdk[server]
    "SQLAlchemy>=2.0.0,<3.0.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0,<2.0.0",
    "psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.1.12,<4.0.0",
    "greenlet>=3.0.3,<4.0.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.23.2",
    "fastapi>=0.115.2",
    "python-logstash-async>=4.0.1,<5.0.0",
    "asgi-proxy-lib==0.2a0",
    "starlette",
    "sse-starlette>=1.6.5",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.33.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.33.0",
    "cryptography>=43.0.0",
    # its own
    "langgraph-checkpoint-postgres>=2.0.0,<4.0.0",
]
# No external dependencies of its own beyond the union: an alias, so the four
# framework extras read the same way at the install line.
adk-server = [
    # aionto-sdk[adk-authoring]
    # See [adk-authoring] for the google-adk floor and the opentelemetry pair.
    "google-adk>=1.27.1,<3.0.0",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.37.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.37.0",
    # See [adk-authoring] for the marker.
    "litellm>=1.93,<2.0; python_version < '3.15'",
    # See [adk-authoring]: google-adk 2.x keeps mcp in an extra.
    "mcp>=1.24,<3.0.0",
    # aionto-sdk[server]
    "SQLAlchemy>=2.0.0,<3.0.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0,<2.0.0",
    "psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.1.12,<4.0.0",
    "greenlet>=3.0.3,<4.0.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.23.2",
    "fastapi>=0.115.2",
    "python-logstash-async>=4.0.1,<5.0.0",
    "asgi-proxy-lib==0.2a0",
    "starlette",
    "sse-starlette>=1.6.5",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.33.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.33.0",
    "cryptography>=43.0.0",
]

[project.scripts]
aion = "aion.cli.cli:cli"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/Terminal-Research/aion-python-sdk"
Repository = "https://github.com/Terminal-Research/aion-python-sdk"

[tool.poetry]
packages = [{ include = "aion", from = "src" }]
include = ["src/aion/cli/bin/*"]
# Every subpackage carries its README beside the code, for whoever reads the
# repository. A distribution is not that reader: the package page is the root
# README, and these ten would just be files nobody opens inside site-packages.
exclude = ["src/aion/**/README.md"]

# The range this repository's own lock resolves under - not published, that
# is requires-python above. It cannot be open-ended: Poetry will not lock a
# project whose Python range exceeds a dependency's, and grpc-interceptor
# (under google-adk) declares <4.0. Written as ^3.12 it is what a consumer
# project declares by default, so the two ranges agree.
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = ">=3.12,<4.0"

[tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies]
pytest = ">=8.0.0"
pytest-asyncio = ">=0.24"
pytest-cov = ">=7.1.0"
# `make tests-unit` spreads the unit suite over worker processes; UNIT_WORKERS
# in the Makefile sets how many.
pytest-xdist = ">=3.6.0"
# The unit suite runs with no network beyond this machine: tests/conftest.py
# lets a unit test connect to localhost only, so a call that would reach a live
# service fails the test instead of reaching it.
pytest-socket = ">=0.7.0"
import-linter = ">=2.0"
# Development-only: the generated GraphQL client is committed, so nothing at
# install time needs the code generator.
ariadne-codegen = { version = "==0.19.0", extras = ["subscriptions"] }
twine = ">=6.0.0"
# Both belong to the scenario suite under tests/scenarios: Jinja2 renders the
# `aion.yaml` each deployment variant is started from, and pytest-timeout is
# what stops a scenario whose server never answers from holding the run.
Jinja2 = ">=3.1.0,<4.0.0"
pytest-timeout = ">=2.3.1"
# `make tests-floors` builds its environment with uv: `--resolution
# lowest-direct` is the one thing Poetry's solver cannot do. A tool, not a
# library - nothing under src/ or tests/ imports it.
uv = ">=0.12.0"

# The ten libs used to keep the layers apart by accident: a lib's venv simply
# had no code from the layers above it. One project, one venv, so the rule has
# to be written down and checked. The order below is the one the code already
# has - it was read off the imports, not imposed on them.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "aion"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layers"
type = "layers"
# Top to bottom: each layer may import the layers under it and nothing above.
# Names joined by "|" share a rank and, by the same rule, may not import each
# other - that is what keeps the LangGraph and ADK sides from growing a
# dependency on one another.
#
# aion.proxy sits above aion.server rather than beside it: the proxy reads the
# server's settings and its port reservations. aion.db sits above the authoring
# packages so that "authoring never touches the database" is a layer fact and
# not only the forbidden contract below.
layers = [
    "aion.cli",
    "aion.langgraph.server | aion.adk.server",
    "aion.proxy",
    "aion.server",
    "aion.db",
    "aion.langgraph.authoring | aion.adk.authoring",
    "aion.mcp",
    "aion.api",
    "aion.core",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Authoring never imports server machinery"
type = "forbidden"
# Implied by the layer order above, and stated separately anyway: this is the
# property published wheels are sold on - an authoring extra installs without a
# database, an ASGI stack or the CLI - and it should fail by name when broken.
source_modules = ["aion.langgraph.authoring", "aion.adk.authoring"]
forbidden_modules = ["aion.server", "aion.proxy", "aion.db", "aion.cli"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]
# No global warning filter. A blanket `ignore::DeprecationWarning` would hide
# exactly the signal tests/unit/server/test_sdk_override_parity.py exists to
# catch: an a2a-sdk extension point announcing its replacement one release
# before it moves. Silence a specific warning at the test that provokes it.
markers = [
    # One marker per suite, put on by tests/conftest.py from the directory an
    # item lives in - tests/unit, tests/integration, tests/scenarios - so that
    # no module can forget one or claim another. The Make targets run by
    # directory; the markers are there for combining with `-m`.
    "unit: runs on any developer machine with nothing set up; `make tests-unit`",
    "integration: needs PostgreSQL, or a real process tree to signal; `make tests-integration`",
    "scenario: drives a real `aion serve` over A2A; `make tests-scenarios`, never `make tests-unit`",
    # `command` and `variant` say what one scenario drives and where; the
    # scenario matrix is built out of them.
    "command(key): the command from tests/scenarios/commands.py this scenario drives; skipped where frameworks.UNSUPPORTED names the pair",
    "variant(name): the deployment template under tests/scenarios/configs this scenario runs against",
    "divergence(key): the guarantee this scenario asserts, as frameworks.DIVERGENCES names it when an adapter does not hold it yet",
    "event_router: this scenario asserts which handler the SDK's event router picked; skipped where frameworks.NO_EVENT_ROUTER names an adapter that has no router",
    "capability(key): the framework feature this native scenario drives; skipped where frameworks.NATIVE_UNSUPPORTED names the pair",
    # One marker per scenario suite; `make tests-scenarios TAGS=...` selects on
    # them. The "scenario suite -" prefix is what scripts/scenarios_matrix.py
    # reads to tell a suite from the markers above.
    "smoke: scenario suite - agent answers at all: card, health, help, echo",
    "streaming: scenario suite - chunked replies, ephemeral typing, unary send",
    "events: scenario suite - event order, ids, outbox, get_task agreement",
    "terminal_states: scenario suite - COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, INPUT_REQUIRED",
    "interrupts: scenario suite - INPUT_REQUIRED and resume",
    "errors: scenario suite - failures that must stay reported, not crash the server",
    "artifacts: scenario suite - artifact and card emission",
    "files: scenario suite - inline file parts: stored, rejected, or passed through",
    "extensions: scenario suite - extension activation and payload delivery",
    "daemon: scenario suite - daemon extension identity and environment",
    "authentication: scenario suite - bearer tokens: required, verified, and naming the caller",
    "config: scenario suite - aion.yaml configuration and deployment variants",
    "lifecycle: scenario suite - cancel, concurrency, push notifications, startup",
    "contexts: scenario suite - Context extension: list, read and delete conversations",
    "toolkits: scenario suite - toolkit plugins: a turn translated into A2A, a refusal before the task exists, a cancel",
    "persistence: scenario suite - needs POSTGRES_TEST_URL; survives a server restart, migrates an empty database",
    "distributed: scenario suite - needs POSTGRES_TEST_URL; two servers over one database",
    "native: scenario suite - an ordinary framework agent on its own path: model, tools, memory, no Aion API",
]

[tool.ariadne-codegen]
schema_path = "graphql/schema.graphql"
queries_path = "graphql/queries.graphql"
target_package_path = "src/aion/api/gql/generated"
client_name = "GqlClient"
async_client = true
enable_custom_operations = true
opentelemetry_client = true
plugins = ["ariadne_codegen.contrib.extract_operations.ExtractOperationsPlugin"]

[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core>=2.0.0"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"

name = "pymotivaxmc2"
version = "0.8.0"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# NOTE: no direct-URL (git+https) dependencies here. PyPI rejects any package
# whose published metadata carries a direct reference, so the py-dev-gates gate
# tool is NOT listed: CI installs it via the droman42/py-dev-gates composite

[project]
name = "pipefy-mcp-server"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "MCP server that exposes Pipefy's GraphQL API."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    # Pinned to the 2.0 patch line rather than opened to <3, because two of the
    # surfaces this package builds on are outside what SemVer covers: the
    # MCPServer(middleware=[...]) list, which upstream marks provisional, and the
    # Tool.run patch behind the argument-validation envelope. A minor release can
    # move either with no signal, and nothing in CI resolves past the lock to
    # catch it. Patch releases are accepted; widening to a new minor is a
    # deliberate change that re-tests both surfaces. The floor is 2.0 because the
    # server imports mcp.server.mcpserver, which no 1.x release has.
    "mcp[cli]==2.0.*",
    # Workspace resolves versions in dev; PyPI releases stage these wheels alongside CLI/MCP (see release workflow).
    "pipefy-auth==0.5.4-beta.1",
    "pipefy-infra==0.5.4-beta.1",
    "pipefy==0.5.4-beta.1",
    "pydantic>=2.13.4,<3",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.8.1",
    # Declared even though `mcp` already pulls it, because this package imports
    # starlette directly: the `Starlette` return type of wire_hosted_observability,
    # and the `Request` annotation the runtime and the identity resolvers take. An
    # SDK release that drops or vendors starlette would break those imports with no
    # bound to catch it. The floor is what the SDK resolves today; the `<2` cap keeps
    # a major starlette release a deliberate upgrade, which the SDK's own floor
    # (`starlette>=0.27` on Python < 3.14) would not.
    "starlette>=1.3.1,<2",
    # Declared for the same reason as starlette: `run_server` imports uvicorn and
    # builds a `Config`/`Server` pair on the `--transport http` path. `mcp` requires
    # it too, but under a `sys_platform != 'emscripten'` marker, so the transitive
    # guarantee is conditional. The floor is what resolves today; the `<1` cap keeps
    # a major uvicorn release a deliberate upgrade.
    "uvicorn>=0.34.0,<1",
]

# Intra-package layering, enforced by import-linter (run `uv run lint-imports`
# from this directory). Ruff's TID251 above guards the inter-package direction;
# this guards the direction within pipefy_mcp. The rationale and the layer model
# live in docs/architecture.md.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "pipefy_mcp"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Inward-only layers: composition root > adapters > core > auth > settings"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "pipefy_mcp.server",
    "pipefy_mcp.tools",
    "pipefy_mcp.core",
    "pipefy_mcp.auth",
    "pipefy_mcp.settings",
]

# Hosted per-user safety: settings reachable from the tool layer are
# process-global — under the remote profile they are shared across concurrent
# callers, so such a read may only ever make a per-deployment decision, and each
# one is reviewed onto ignore_imports (direct or via a core helper; the contract
# checks transitive chains). The line and its rationale live in CLAUDE.md
# ("Process-global configuration and the single-backend assumption").
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Tools read no process-global settings"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pipefy_mcp.tools"]
forbidden_modules = ["pipefy_mcp.settings"]
ignore_imports = [
    # Reviewed: permission_denied_enrichment_timeout_seconds, a deployment
    # tuning knob, not a per-user decision.
    "pipefy_mcp.tools.graphql_error_helpers -> pipefy_mcp.settings",
    # Reviewed: unified_envelope, a per-deployment response-shape flag applied
    # identically to every caller.
    "pipefy_mcp.core.tool_error_envelope -> pipefy_mcp.settings",
    # Reviewed: the composition root builds the runtime from settings at
    # startup. The runtime holds no Settings tree — it exposes only the two
    # curated per-deployment booleans it resolves at construction (is_remote,
    # unified_envelope), never settings.* — so tool code reaching the runtime
    # off the lifespan context has no import-free path to the Settings tree.
    # Reviewed per-deployment reads elsewhere still go through the
    # import exceptions listed here.
    "pipefy_mcp.core.runtime -> pipefy_mcp.settings",
    # Reviewed: imports the Settings type for startup identity resolution.
    # StartupIdentity receives settings from the composition root and
    # RequestScopedIdentity resolves from the request bearer — no call-time
    # global read. Reached transitively via core.runtime.
    "pipefy_mcp.auth.session_identity -> pipefy_mcp.settings",
    # Reviewed: reads McpSettings.host and the transport allowlist at startup
    # for bind-safety / DNS-rebinding config — per-deployment, not a per-user
    # decision. Reached transitively via core.runtime.
    "pipefy_mcp.core.transport_security -> pipefy_mcp.settings",
]

# Next ratchet (disabled): lock the domain as framework-free once it has a home.
# The pure domain is still scattered: the error/success envelope lives in
# core/tool_error_envelope.py and the payload builders under tools/, with no single

[project]
name = "pyforge-marshal"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Deterministic BMAD-loop supervisor: wraps bmad-loop with gates-as-objects, run supervision, landing, fleet status, and adapter portability."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "rxm7706" }]
# Marshal's own direct dependencies (architecture Stack table) -- declared
# here rather than inherited transitively from bmad-loop, even though
# PyYAML/tomlkit/psutil also happen to resolve in-environment via
# bmad-loop's own flattened noarch recipe. jsonschema is entirely new
# surface (envelope + journal schema validation). Story 1.7 makes bmad-loop
# itself a declared runtime dependency: adapters/harness_bmadloop.py now
# lazily imports bmad_loop.adapters.multiplexer/profile,
# bmad_loop.bmadconfig, and bmad_loop.sprintstatus (inside the relevant
# HarnessPort methods, never at module top level) to back `marshal
# preflight`'s harness/adapter/story-feed checks (AD-19). The range matches
# AD-3/Story 1.9's planned conda pin -- pre-1.0, so the upper bound excludes
# a minor bump that could rename/remove any of the modules this module reads.
# 2026-09-26: cap widened <0.12 -> <0.13 after bmad-loop 0.12.0 was verified --
# the four lazily-imported modules are still shipped and the marshal suite
# passes against 0.12.0 (DW-marshal-bmad-loop-0-12-cap-2026-09-26).
dependencies = [
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    # <0.13.3 matches this repo's own environment cap (root pixi.toml pins
    # tomlkit "<0.13.3" for an unrelated dependency, dagster-dg-core) --
    # architecture Stack table: "do not assume >=0.13.3 features" here either.
    "tomlkit>=0.13,<0.13.3",
    "psutil>=7.2.2",
    "jsonschema>=4.25",
    "bmad-loop>=0.11.0,<0.13",
    "pyforge-core",
    # Story 10.1: Genesis's template engine (architecture Stack table,
    # AD-52). Imported nowhere but seed/engine/copier.py (P-02, proven by
    # tests/meta/test_p02_copier_sole_ownership.py).
    "copier>=9.17,<10",
    "packaging>=24.0",
]

[project.scripts]
marshal = "pyforge.marshal.cli.main:main"
# Story 18.1 (FR-153/FR-154): PATH-relative MCP server for per-home
# `.mcp.json` registration via policy `mcp_servers` (AD-43). Never an
# absolute path — `marshal init` renders the basename into the home.
marshal-mcp = "pyforge.marshal.mcp.server:main"

# Story 26.1: today's loop runner is the default plugin on the shared
# S-32.1 group. Do not add a parallel pyforge.marshal.hooks group.
[project.entry-points."pyforge.core.hooks"]
bmad-loop = "pyforge.marshal.adapters.harness_bmadloop:BmadLoopHarness"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/pyforge"]

# Story 22.8: ship the packaged session-harness CLI profiles (FR-193 CAP-8)
# as data files inside the package tree. Story 19.3's own coverage-floors
# force-include (coverage_thresholds.toml) left this block 2026-09-20 (doctor
# Story 24.1, spec-coverage-gate-independence CAP-1/CAP-2): the gate module
# and its thresholds file both moved outside every pyforge.<station>
# package -- scripts/coverage_gate.py and docs/governance/coverage-thresholds.toml.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"src/pyforge/marshal/data/harness_profiles" = "pyforge/marshal/data/harness_profiles"
"src/pyforge/marshal/data/bmad_loop_plugins" = "pyforge/marshal/data/bmad_loop_plugins"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Story 1.4: tests/integration/test_init_worktree.py is a real end-to-end
# `marshal init` provision + re-run against a throwaway temp git repo --
# dominated by real `git worktree add` subprocess calls, too slow for the
# default pyforge-marshal-test task (pixi.toml passes -m "not slow" there)
# to stay a sub-minute loop. Mirrors pyforge-warden's identical convention.
markers = ["slow: dominated by real git/subprocess calls, not part of the default pyforge-marshal-test task"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["pyforge.marshal"]
# subprocess/os/time and bmad_loop are all external to root_packages --
# import-linter requires this flag before it will validate a forbidden
# contract naming an external module.
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "AD-4: core is pure -- no I/O, subprocess, clock, or adapters"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pyforge.marshal.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["subprocess", "os", "time", "pyforge.marshal.adapters"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "AD-3: only adapters/harness_bmadloop.py may reference bmad_loop"
type = "forbidden"
# Deliberately excludes pyforge.marshal.adapters as a whole package from
# source_modules -- see architecture.md's "Import-linter contract scope
# gap" design note: including it would also forbid harness_bmadloop.py
# itself, the one module this contract must let import bmad_loop. A future
# adapter module that wrongly imports bmad_loop is NOT caught by this
# contract until that module's own story adds it to source_modules.
# pyforge.marshal.coverage_gate (Story 19.3 / FR-131) is REMOVED from this
# list 2026-09-20 (doctor Story 24.1, spec-coverage-gate-independence CAP-1):
# the evaluator moved to scripts/coverage_gate.py, outside every
# pyforge.<station> package, so this contract has nothing left to say about
# it -- a station's own AD-3 seam cannot forbid a module the station no
# longer ships.
source_modules = [
    "pyforge.marshal.cli",
    "pyforge.marshal.core",
    "pyforge.marshal.data",  # Story 93.1 bmad-loop plugin payloads (no bmad_loop imports)
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_supervisor",
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_verify",  # Story 22.3 / FR-193 CAP-3 dispatch gate runner
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_verification_journal",  # Story 22.17 shared dispatch-verification journal payloads
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_land",  # Story 22.4 / FR-193 CAP-4
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_land_finalize",  # Story 22.4 finalize subprocess dispatch land composer
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_land_heal",  # Story 28.20 / CAP-4 mechanical land heal
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_fleet_supervisor",  # Story 22.7 / FR-193 CAP-7 campaign supervisor
    "pyforge.marshal.mcp",
    "pyforge.marshal.ports",
    "pyforge.marshal.scope",  # Story 20.6 / FR-190 CAP-1 verify_scope primitive
    "pyforge.marshal.seed",
    "pyforge.marshal.supervisor",
]
forbidden_modules = ["bmad_loop"]
# Story 1.7: import-linter's default (false) checks INDIRECT chains too, so
# the moment harness_bmadloop.py gained a real `import bmad_loop...` (Story
# 1.10 only ever rendered a vendored template -- no such import existed
# until this story), the pre-existing cli.config -> harness_bmadloop edge
# (Story 1.10's write_policy_toml wiring) became a "cli imports bmad_loop"
# violation under strict/transitive checking, even though cli.config never
# writes that import itself. AD-3's own wording ("only ... may invoke the
# harness binary, import its package") is about DIRECT import authorship,
# not about whether a caller may use harness_bmadloop.py's public API (the
# whole point of the seam) -- true regardless of indirect-checking, so this
# flag makes the contract's enforcement match its stated intent rather than
# loosen it: cli/core/ports/seed/supervisor still may never themselves write
# `import bmad_loop`.
# Story 18.1: mcp/ added to source_modules — the FastMCP surface must not
# import bmad_loop either (thin CLI wrappers only).
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "AD-9: the supervisor has no control channel back to cli"
type = "forbidden"
# Story 3.4: the supervisor is a separate OS process that observes a run
# from outside and never trusts session self-report (AD-9) -- a session
# can never disable, silence, or reconfigure its own supervisor. The
# session's own front door (cli/) already has no code path back into a
# separate OS process's internals; this contract makes that absence
# structural rather than an unenforced convention. Deliberately the
# mirror image of the AD-3 contract above (which lists `supervisor` in
# ITS OWN source_modules, forbidding supervisor -> bmad_loop): this one
# forbids the other direction, supervisor -> cli.
source_modules = ["pyforge.marshal.supervisor"]
forbidden_modules = ["pyforge.marshal.cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "AD-9: the dispatch supervisors have no control channel back to cli"
type = "forbidden"
# Story 22.7 added the fleet-drain CAMPAIGN supervisor to this contract
# rather than minting a sixth: it is the same discipline over the same
# seam. Its own module docstring asserts "this module imports no
# pyforge.marshal.cli module" -- it drives the campaign the way an operator
# would, by running the published `marshal factory drain --once` command
# through the ProcessPort seam, so the claim needs teeth, not prose (the
# same reasoning the Story 8.4 contract below records).
source_modules = [
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_supervisor",
    "pyforge.marshal.dispatch_fleet_supervisor",
]
forbidden_modules = ["pyforge.marshal.cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Story 8.4 review finding: regions never imports model.manifest (avoids a package cycle)"
type = "forbidden"
# seed/model/manifest.py already imports FROM seed/regions/markers.py

# regions/apply.py's own module docstring already asserts this in prose

# gives that claim teeth, matching this repo's own established preference
# for mechanical enforcement over docstring-only claims (AD-61's fs.py
# meta-test precedent: "so the guard cannot be routed around").
source_modules = ["pyforge.marshal.seed.regions"]
forbidden_modules = ["pyforge.marshal.seed.model.manifest"]
