# A group here earns its place only when something has to be present in the project
# *environment*. Every rhiza gate provisions its own tooling on the fly — `uv run
# --with pytest --with pytest-cov ...` in the `test` target, `--with ty` in
# `typecheck`, `--with interrogate` in `docs-coverage`, `uvx pre-commit` in `fmt` —
# so a tool named by a `--with` flag must NOT be declared: the declaration only
# duplicates the pin (and can conflict with it, as `pytest-benchmark==5.2.3`
# pinned by the `benchmark` target would).
#
# Two things do qualify: a library the test suite imports under a gate that does
# not inject it, and an import deptry resolves in DEPTRY_FOLDERS (src + book).
dev = [
    "pandas>=2.2.3",       # required by quantstats (comparison tests only — not a runtime dependency)
    "pyarrow>=22.0.0",     # polars' .to_pandas() (used all over tests/test_migration) imports it; polars declares it only under [pyarrow]
    "yfinance==1.7.0",
    "quantstats==0.0.86",  # reference implementation used in test_quantstats.py for metric validation
    # starlette's TestClient needs an HTTP client present; starlette declares one only under [full].
    # starlette>=1.2 prefers httpx2 and warns on plain httpx, but the lowest-direct job resolves
    # fastapi's floor, whose starlette (<1.2) knows only httpx -- so both stay declared.
    "httpx2>=2.13.1",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "marimo>=0.23.6",      # book/ notebooks import it and deptry scans MARIMO_FOLDER — DEP001 without this
]
test = [
    # pytest itself is injected by every pytest-backed target, but stays declared so
    # a bare `uv run pytest tests/...` works. Most of its plugins are not: cov, html,
    # mock, xdist, benchmark and pygal all arrive via `--with`.
    "pytest>=8.0",
    # pytest.ini sets a global `timeout = 60`, and `benchmark`, `hypothesis-test` and
    # `stress` run pytest WITHOUT injecting this plugin — without it they warn
    # "Unknown config option: timeout" and a hanging test hangs forever.
    "pytest-timeout>=2.0",
    # Imported by tests that `make test` collects, and `make test` injects neither.
    # hypothesis in particular is reached through pytest.importorskip, so dropping it
    # would not fail the suite — it would silently skip the property tests.
    "hypothesis>=6.150.0",
    "syrupy>=4.9.1",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
    # Declared here IN ADDITION to the `mpl` extra, and neither declaration is redundant:
    #   * The extra is what `uv sync --all-extras` installs. benchmark-pr.yml runs
    #     exactly that, without --all-groups, and uv's default group
    #     set is `dev` only — so without the extra that job runs the suite with
    #     matplotlib absent.
    #   * The group is what a bare `uv sync && uv run pytest` installs.
    # Either gap has the same consequence, and it is NOT a skip: coverage is measured
    # directory-scoped over src/, so an unimported src/jquantstats/_plots/_mpl/*.py is
    # reported at 0% rather than dropping out of the report — a hard failure against
    # `fail_under = 100`, with a misleading message. That is why there is no
    # `pytest.importorskip("matplotlib")` anywhere; contrast test_kaleido.py, where the
    # dependency genuinely can be absent because it needs a Chrome subprocess.
    "matplotlib>=3.9",
]
# There is no `lint` group: nothing resolves one from the project environment. ruff runs
# through the pre-commit hooks `make fmt` executes via uvx, and import-linter — which
# enforces the [tool.importlinter] contracts — runs as one of those hooks, as
# `uv run --with import-linter lint-imports`.


# Build system configuration
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# Supplies the `version` that [project] declares dynamic, from `git describe`. Two
# consequences worth knowing:
#   * The build needs the tag to be visible. hatch-vcs does not fail without it -- it
#     falls back to a dev version like 0.11.1.dev3+g<sha> -- so rhiza_release.yml checks
#     the built distribution's filename against the tag, and its checkout uses
#     fetch-depth: 0. An sdist carries the resolved number in PKG-INFO, so building from
#     one needs no git.
#   * Between tags the local version is the *next* patch as a dev release
#     (guess-next-dev, the default), which is why nothing pins a fallback-version here:
#     a wrong-looking version must surface as a release failure, not as a plausible
#     constant.
[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"

# Configuration for wheel build
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/jquantstats"]

# Configuration for what files to include in the build
[tool.hatch.build]
include = [
    "LICENSE",    # Ensure the LICENSE file is included in your package
    "README.md",
    "src/jquantstats",
    "src/jquantstats/py.typed",
]

# Bandit security linter configuration
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["src/tests"]  # Exclude test directories from security scanning

# Settings for the rhiza-task CLI, which replaced the synced make layer in rhiza
# v1.4.0. Every value below was carried over from a file that release deleted
# (`.rhiza/make.d/*.mk`, `.rhiza/.env`, the old Makefile); each one differs from the
# CLI default, so dropping it would quietly weaken a gate rather than fail loudly.
[tool.rhiza-task]
# Was COVERAGE_FAIL_UNDER in .rhiza/make.d/custom-env.mk. The CLI default is 90.
# `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 100` above does NOT cover this: the `test`
# task passes `--cov-fail-under` on the command line, which outranks the config
# file. Without this line the suite may drop to 90% coverage and still go green.
coverage_fail_under = 100

# Was TYPECHECKER in .rhiza/make.d/python.mk. The CLI default is `ty` alone, so
# omitting this would stop running mypy --strict entirely. Note this is also
# stricter than the make layer was: the old shell `case` let mypy's exit status
# win, so a `ty` failure could pass. Both must now succeed.
typechecker = "both"

# Was MARIMO_FOLDER in .rhiza/.env. The CLI default is `docs/notebooks`, which does
# not exist here — the notebooks live under book/. Without this, `marimo-validate`
# finds nothing to check and the notebooks stop being verified, and the folder also
# drops out of the deptry scan (taking the `marimo` dev dependency with it).
marimo_folder = "book/marimo/notebooks"

# Was RHIZA_CHECKS_VERSION in .rhiza/make.d/quality.mk, consumed as
# `pytest-rhiza==$(RHIZA_CHECKS_VERSION)`. The CLI default resolves
# `pytest-rhiza @ git+…@v0.2.0`, older than what this repo needs.
#
# 0.6.0 is the floor, not a routine refresh: it is the release whose pyproject
# check learned that `[project].version` may be *derived* from the VCS. Up to and
# including 0.2.1 the check reads a written number unconditionally, so against the
# `dynamic = ["version"]` above it fails three ways — `version` missing from the
# required-[project]-fields list, "" failing the semver regex, and
# `Version("")` raising InvalidVersion while comparing against the latest tag. All
# three are artefacts of the checker, not of this repo.
pytest_rhiza = "pytest-rhiza==0.6.0"

# Replaces `DEPTRY_FOLDERS += api` from the old Makefile. v1.4.0 removed that
# accumulator and now *derives* the deptry folder set — source_folder plus
# marimo_folder — with no setting to extend it. The `deps` task appends
# `deptry_ignore` to deptry's argv after those folders, and deptry takes multiple
# roots positionally, so a bare path here restores the previous scope exactly.
#
# This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: without it deptry never sees api/, and
# `ci / deps` fails with `DEP002 'fastapi' defined as a dependency but not used`.
# Suppressing that with a per_rule_ignores entry would have been the weaker fix —
# it would also stop flagging fastapi if api/ ever really stopped importing it.
deptry_ignore = ["api"]

# Deliberately NOT set, each because it already matches the CLI default — listing
# them anyway is how a redundant line becomes the one someone edits:
#   source_folder ("src"), tests_folder ("tests"), uv_sync_args
#   ("--all-extras --all-groups"), license_fail_on ("GPL LGPL AGPL"),
#   book_output ("_book"), zensical_version (">=0.0.36"), paper_folder
#   ("docs/paper").
# Also deliberately unset:
#   mkdocs_extra_packages  the old Makefile set `--with 'mkdocstrings[python]'`,
#                          which is now the default. Naming the setting REPLACES
#                          the default list, so restating it invites someone to
#                          append a package and silently drop mkdocstrings.
#   license_ignore_packages  marimo.mk appended `docutils`; rhiza-task adds it
#                            itself whenever the marimo tasks are registered.
#   ci_os_matrix  .rhiza/.env documented leaving this unset on purpose so
#                 rhiza_ci.yml can pick the matrix per caller. Pinning it here
#                 would defeat that for every consumer.
#   layers / rhiza_checks  both derived — layers from the manifests present
#                          (pyproject.toml -> "python"), and the check set from
#                          layers, which still yields all five checks the make
#                          accumulators built up.
# Not settings at all: PROJECT_NAME_EXTRA and LOG_LEVEL from custom-env.mk were
# cosmetic and have no CLI equivalent.

# Ignore specific dependency issues.
#
# DEP002 flags a declared dependency with no import site. The three below have
# none by design, so the ignore records a fact rather than hiding a gap:
#   kaleido           - Plotly's static image-export backend. Selected at runtime
#                       by plotly.io, never imported by us.
#   uvicorn           - ASGI server for api/app.py. Invoked as a command
#                       (`uvicorn api.app:app`), not imported.
#   python-multipart  - parses multipart/form-data for FastAPI's Form/UploadFile.
#                       Imported by Starlette, never by us.
# fastapi is deliberately absent: api/ is part of the deptry scan (see
# `deptry_ignore` under [tool.rhiza-task] above — it was the Makefile's
# DEPTRY_FOLDERS line before rhiza v1.4.0), so its import there is observed
# directly.
[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
DEP002 = ["kaleido", "uvicorn", "python-multipart"]

# Package to module name mapping
[tool.deptry.package_module_name_map]
jinja2 = "jinja2"
numpy = "numpy"
plotly = "plotly"
polars = "polars"
pandas = "pandas"
scipy = "scipy"
kaleido = "kaleido"
fastapi = "fastapi"
uvicorn = "uvicorn"
yfinance = "yfinance"
quantstats = "quantstats"
marimo = "marimo"
hypothesis = "hypothesis"
narwhals = "narwhals"
python-multipart = "python_multipart"
pyarrow = "pyarrow"
httpx = "httpx"
httpx2 = "httpx2"
matplotlib = "matplotlib"

# Coverage configuration
[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 100
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",  # type-only imports are never executed at runtime
    "@overload",  # overload stubs have no runtime body
]


# Interrogate docstring coverage configuration
[tool.mypy]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["plotly.*", "scipy.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.interrogate]
fail-under = 100
ignore-init-method = true
ignore-magic = true
ignore-overloaded-functions = true

# Test-layout parity (rhiza check_test_layout): tests here are organised by
# behaviour under tests/test_jquantstats/… rather than mirroring src/ 1:1, and
# per-module coverage is guaranteed by the 100% line+branch pytest gate above
# (a stronger guarantee than file-mirroring). Opt out of the 1:1 mirror rule.
[tool.check_test_layout]
enforce = false
# Keep this string free of a literal `%`: tools that read [tool.*] tables through
# configparser (radon, for one) treat it as interpolation syntax and crash outright.
reason = "Tests are organised by behaviour under tests/test_jquantstats/; per-module coverage is guaranteed by the full line-and-branch pytest coverage gate rather than 1:1 file mirroring."

# Kept even though there is no longer a version in this file to rewrite, because its
# *presence* is what `/rhiza:release` reads to tell "this repo declares where its version
# lives, and it is the tag" from "this repo declares nothing" -- the second of which makes
# the command stop. Deliberately carries no `current_version`: bump-my-version then
# derives the current version from the newest matching tag, which is the same fact
# hatch-vcs builds from, so the two cannot drift. This is the shape rhiza's `go-core` and
# `rust-core` bundles ship for exactly the same reason.
#
# There is no `[[tool.bumpversion.files]]` entry, and adding one would be the mistake:
# every location that used to hold the number is now derived from the tag, so a file
# listed here could only reintroduce the drift this change removed.
[tool.bumpversion]
allow_dirty = false
# The release flow commits and tags itself, so that the regenerated changelog lands in
# the bump commit rather than in a second one after the tag.
commit = false
tag = false

# Architectural import contracts (import-linter), run as a pre-commit hook and so
# covered by `make fmt`. These encode the layering that src/jquantstats/_protocol.py
# describes in prose: the analytics subpackages annotate against the structural
# Protocols and must never reach for the concrete Data / Portfolio classes.
#
# Type-checking-only imports are excluded, because `if TYPE_CHECKING: from ..data
# import Data` is exactly the sanctioned pattern here — it costs nothing at
# runtime and forms no import cycle. Only real runtime imports are contract
# violations.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "jquantstats"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

# NOTE on the pyplot ban: it deliberately is NOT an import-linter contract.
# import-linter rejects `matplotlib.pyplot` with "subpackages of external packages are
# not valid" — it can only forbid whole external distributions, and forbidding
# `matplotlib` outright would ban the renderer itself. The ban is enforced instead by
# tests/test_jquantstats/test__plots/test_no_pyplot.py, which scans the source tree,
# plus a runtime leak-detector fixture. See that module for the reasoning.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "analytics subpackages must not import the concrete Data/Portfolio at runtime"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "jquantstats._stats",
    "jquantstats._plots",
    "jquantstats._reports",
    "jquantstats._utils",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "jquantstats.data",
    "jquantstats.portfolio",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the Data reshape mixin must not import Data"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["jquantstats._data_reshape"]
forbidden_modules = ["jquantstats.data"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the Portfolio mixins must not import Portfolio or Data at runtime"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "jquantstats._portfolio_attribution",
    "jquantstats._portfolio_base",
    "jquantstats._portfolio_constructors",
    "jquantstats._portfolio_cost",
    "jquantstats._portfolio_nav",
    "jquantstats._portfolio_transform",
    "jquantstats._portfolio_turnover",
    "jquantstats._portfolio_units",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "jquantstats.data",
    "jquantstats.portfolio",
]

[importlinter]
root_package = local_rag_backend

[importlinter:contract:core-base-layering]
name = Core domain/ports/services must not depend on infra/http/composition
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    local_rag_backend.core
forbidden_modules =
    local_rag_backend.infrastructure
    local_rag_backend.http
    local_rag_backend.composition

[importlinter:contract:use-cases-layering]
name = Use cases must not depend on infra/http/composition
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    local_rag_backend.core.use_cases
forbidden_modules =
    local_rag_backend.infrastructure
    local_rag_backend.http
    local_rag_backend.composition

[importlinter:contract:http-routers-boundary]
name = HTTP routers must not import concrete infrastructure adapters
type = forbidden
# Routers use composition for wiring; concrete adapter imports remain forbidden.
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    local_rag_backend.http.routers
forbidden_modules =
    local_rag_backend.infrastructure.persistence
    local_rag_backend.infrastructure.retrieval
    local_rag_backend.infrastructure.llms
    local_rag_backend.infrastructure.embeddings
    local_rag_backend.infrastructure.ingestion

[importlinter:contract:transport-independence]
name = HTTP and CLI transports should stay independent
type = independence
modules =
    local_rag_backend.http
    local_rag_backend.cli_commands

[importlinter:contract:public-integrations-boundary]
name = Public integrations must not depend on transports or composition
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    local_rag_backend.integrations
forbidden_modules =
    local_rag_backend.cli_commands
    local_rag_backend.composition
    local_rag_backend.http

name = Plugins never import each other's internals (consts only)

modules =

    dropbot_status_and_controls

ignore_imports =
    # Rule: a plugin's own consts module (topics/constants/message schemas)
    # is the one thing siblings may import from it.
    ** -> *.consts
    # microdrop_application is itself a plugin (MicrodropPlugin), but two
    # of its submodules are genuinely shared infrastructure by design, not
    # plugin-private business logic: `helpers` (the Redis app-globals
    # accessor + experiment-directory lookup, used repo-wide) and the
    # `dialogs` subpackage (a self-contained messaging-dialog library,
    # AGENTS.md: "User-facing errors go through
    # microdrop_application.dialogs.pyface_wrapper ... never a raw
    # QMessageBox"). Everything else in microdrop_application (menus.py,
    # plugin.py, task.py, views/, preferences*, touch_assist/) stays
    # plugin-private; existing cross-plugin uses are itemized as debt below.
    ** -> microdrop_application.helpers
    ** -> microdrop_application.dialogs
    ** -> microdrop_application.dialogs.**

    # pluggable_protocol_tree registers the PROTOCOL_COLUMNS Envisage
    # extension point (see its plugin.py docstring); its interfaces,
    # models.column/quick_action/row/display_state/compound_column,
    # views.columns.*, builtins.*_column, execution.*, session and
    # services.preferences ARE the declared public API for plugins that
    # contribute protocol columns (dropbot_protocol_controls,
    # volume_threshold_protocol_controls, portable_dropbot_protocol_controls,
    # video_protocol_controls, protocol_quick_action_tools, device_viewer).
    # Treated like a consts surface: importable by everyone. This does NOT
    # cover the opposite direction — pluggable_protocol_tree importing a
    # specific leaf plugin's internals is a real violation, itemized below.
    ** -> pluggable_protocol_tree.**

    # Issue #611 (PR #658) — dropbot_tools_menu's self-test dialogs render
    # from the backend's self_tests model directly instead of a message.
    dropbot_tools_menu.self_test_dialogs -> dropbot_controller.models.self_tests

    # module directly instead of via consts/messages ---
    logger_ui.preferences -> microdrop_application.preferences
    device_viewer.preferences -> microdrop_application.preferences_dialog
    dropbot_preferences_ui.preferences -> dropbot_controller.preferences
    dropbot_protocol_controls.protocol_columns.voltage_column -> dropbot_controller.preferences

    # --- Seeded debt: mocks/tests reaching into the real plugin's models ---
    mock_dropbot_controller.consts -> dropbot_controller.models.self_tests
    mock_dropbot_status.message_handler -> dropbot_controller.models.shorts

    # --- Seeded debt: other direct model/service/interface reach-ins ---
    portable_dropbot_controller.services.portable_dropbot_electrodes_mixin_service -> electrode_controller.models
    # opendrop_controller/services was invisible to grimp (no __init__.py) until
    # #679; reuses electrode_controller's pydantic request model directly
    # instead of via consts, same shape as the portable_dropbot_controller
    # reach-in above.
    opendrop_controller.services.opendrop_electrodes_mixin_service -> electrode_controller.models
    electrode_controller.plugin -> dropbot_controller.interfaces.i_dropbot_control_mixin_service
    # electrode_controller/services was likewise invisible until #679. Durable
    # fix: move IDropbotControlMixinService out of dropbot_controller.interfaces
    # into peripheral_device_controller_base, the shared base both plugins'
    # controllers already subclass, instead of siblings importing it directly.
    electrode_controller.services.electrode_disable_service -> dropbot_controller.interfaces.i_dropbot_control_mixin_service
    electrode_controller.services.electrode_state_change_service -> dropbot_controller.interfaces.i_dropbot_control_mixin_service
    volume_threshold_protocol_controls.protocol_columns.volume_threshold_column -> dropbot_protocol_controls.services.force_math
    volume_threshold_protocol_controls.demos.vt_test_harness -> dropbot_protocol_controls.services.force_math

package org.muellners.finscale.core

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class ArchTest {

    @Test
    fun servicesAndRepositoriesShouldNotDependOnWebLayer() {

        val importedClasses = ClassFileImporter()
            .withImportOption(ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
            .importPackages("org.muellners.finscale.core")

        noClasses()
            .that()
                .resideInAnyPackage("org.muellners.finscale.core.service..")
            .or()
                .resideInAnyPackage("org.muellners.finscale.core.repository..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
                .resideInAnyPackage("..org.muellners.finscale.core.web..")
        .because("Services and repositories should not depend on web layer")
        .check(importedClasses)
    }
}

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class ArchUnitTest {

    @Test
    fun controllerはuseCaseに依存する() {

        val javaClasses = ClassFileImporter().importPackages("com.daisuzz.samplethymeleaftodo")

        val rule: ArchRule = layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer("Controller").definedBy("..presentation..")
            .layer("UseCase").definedBy("..usecase..")
            .whereLayer("Controller").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("UseCase").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controller")
        rule.check(javaClasses)
    }
}

# Reference import-linter config for Python (Django/LangChain) projects.
# Enforces DIP mechanically: application code (views/services) must NOT import
# the ORM (models) directly, bypassing the service layer.
# Instantiate as .importlinter in your project root and run: lint-imports

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    app

[importlinter:rule:DjangoModelsNotImportedFromViews]
source_modules =
    app.views
    app.api
forbidden_modules =
    app.models
message = |
    DIP violation: views/api must not import ORM models directly.
    Route through a service in app.services instead.

[importlinter:rule:NoInfraFromDomain]
source_modules =
    app.domain
forbidden_modules =
    django.db
    sqlalchemy
    langchain
message = |
    DIP violation: domain layer must not depend on infrastructure (DB/ORM/framework).

[importlinter]
# IMPORTANT: every package directory under src/ MUST contain an __init__.py.
# Without it, grimp drops the package from the import graph and every contract
# passes as a false-green (this masked the violations now baselined below).
#
# The ignore_imports lists freeze the pre-existing layering debt so CI blocks any
# NEW cross-layer import. The domain-isolation contract has no baseline and must
# stay clean. Shrink the other baselines as the debt is inverted behind ports.

    src

    "resend==2.30.1",

    "langgraph==1.2.8",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["import-linter>=2.0"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]

[tool.coverage.run]
omit = [
    # Development and testing utilities
    "src/api/middleware/dev_auth_bypass.py",
    # No-logic DTOs / models (exclude from coverage gate)
    "src/api/schemas/*",
    "src/api/schemas/**",
    "src/domain/model/*",
    "src/domain/model/**",
    "src/infra/database/models/*",
    "src/infra/database/models/**",
    # Database infrastructure
    "src/infra/database/migration_manager.py",
    "src/infra/database/uow_async.py",
    # External service integrations
    "src/infra/services/pinecone_service.py",
    "src/infra/services/firebase_auth_service.py",
    "src/infra/services/ai/openai_chat_service.py",
    "src/infra/websocket/connection_manager.py",
    # Operational infrastructure (batch jobs, health checks)
    "src/api/routes/v1/health.py",
    # Standard exclusions
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*.py",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/venv/*",
    "*/.venv/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]
show_missing = true
precision = 2

# import-linter contracts live in ./.importlinter (import-linter reads it in
# preference to this file). Run `lint-imports` — also a CI step — to check the
# architecture boundaries. NOTE: every package dir under src/ must contain an
# __init__.py, or grimp drops it from the graph and contracts pass as false-greens.

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 88
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # pyflakes
    "I",      # isort
    "B",      # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
]
ignore = [
    "E501",   # line too long (handled by formatter)
    "E402",   # module level import not at top (main.py loads dotenv first)
    "B008",   # function calls in argument defaults (FastAPI Depends)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["src"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest==9.1.0",
    "pytest-asyncio==1.4.0",
    "pytest-cov==7.1.0",
    "pytest-mock==3.15.1",

    "UP", # pyupgrade
    "SIM",# flake8-simplify
    "S",  # flake8-bandit: security checks (AST-based)
    "N",  # pep8-naming
    "T10",# debugger
    "T20",# print
    "RET",# flake8-return
    "ERA",# eradicate commented-out code
    "PT", # flake8-pytest-style: pytest style correctness
    "FAST",# FastAPI specific best practices
    "ARG",# flake8-unused-arguments: unused function/method arguments
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Migrations are often generated/edited by tooling; keep Ruff UP strict for
# app code, but ignore pyupgrade modernization suggestions inside migrations.
"db/migrations/**" = ["UP", "ERA", "S101", "S608"]
# sqlite adapters build SQL from static schema-derived column lists.
"db/adapters/sqlite/**" = ["S608"]
# Tests intentionally use `assert` for invariants and expected failures.
"**/tests/**" = ["S101", "S105", "S108", "S310", "S608", "ARG001", "ARG002", "ARG003", "ARG005", "B008", "PT011", "PT012", "SIM117"]

"scripts/**" = ["S101", "S105", "ARG001", "ARG002", "ARG003", "ARG005", "B007", "ERA001", "S603", "S607", "S608", "S108", "S110", "S310", "SIM102", "T20"]

"simulation/api/schemas/simulation.py" = ["S101"]

package org.muellners.finscale.identity

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class ArchTest {

    @Test
    fun servicesAndRepositoriesShouldNotDependOnWebLayer() {

        val importedClasses = ClassFileImporter()
            .withImportOption(ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
            .importPackages("org.muellners.finscale.identity")

        noClasses()
            .that()
                .resideInAnyPackage("org.muellners.finscale.identity.service..")
            .or()
                .resideInAnyPackage("org.muellners.finscale.identity.repository..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
                .resideInAnyPackage("..org.muellners.finscale.identity.web..")
        .because("Services and repositories should not depend on web layer")
        .check(importedClasses)
    }
}

package org.muellners.finscale.multitenancy

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class ArchTest {

    @Test
    fun servicesAndRepositoriesShouldNotDependOnWebLayer() {

        val importedClasses = ClassFileImporter()
            .withImportOption(ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
            .importPackages("org.muellners.finscale.multitenancy")

        noClasses()
            .that()
                .resideInAnyPackage("org.muellners.finscale.multitenancy.service..")
            .or()
                .resideInAnyPackage("org.muellners.finscale.multitenancy.repository..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
                .resideInAnyPackage("..org.muellners.finscale.multitenancy.web..")
        .because("Services and repositories should not depend on web layer")
        .check(importedClasses)
    }
}

# manage.py vive en gotogym/ (no en la raiz del repo, donde esta este

# Permisivo a proposito, no por backlog pendiente (el backlog inicial de

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter: deterministic layer-dependency contracts (arch-checker, feat-008).
# Runner sets PYTHONPATH=backend:services/siem-service so Grimp can locate the
# `app` and `siem_service` source roots (neither is pip-installed as a package);
# `siem_contracts` is resolved from the editable workspace install.
# Invoked via `make check` and the pre-commit hook. Rationale per contract is in
# doc/tech/arch-checker.md (the invariant registry).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["app", "siem_service", "siem_contracts"]
# Required so the "no fastapi in domain" contracts can name an external package.
include_external_packages = true

# Backend layered architecture (doc/tech/backend.md § Правила вызовов).
# Higher layers may import lower ones; the reverse is forbidden. This catches
# repositories/storage/models → services/api and services → api. `repositories`
# and `storage` are independent siblings (`|`) at the same level: repositories
# are ORM-CRUD, storage is swappable-backend abstractions (BlobStorage,
# TraceStore) — neither imports the other. The single known localized exception
# (services/mcp_server.py → api/schemas) is allow-listed.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Backend layers: api > services > repositories|storage > models"
type = "layers"
containers = ["app"]
layers = ["api", "services", "repositories | storage", "models"]
ignore_imports = [
    # Known localized exception (backend.md § Правила вызовов): the MCP service
    # imports its request schema against the layer direction, without a cycle.
    "app.services.mcp_server -> app.api.schemas.mcp_servers",
]

# API must reach data/agent only through the service layer. A plain layers
# contract permits api → repositories/storage (downward skip), so the
# prohibition is expressed separately and scoped to api/routes — api/deps.py
# legally wires repositories/storage for DI.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Backend: api/routes must not import repositories, storage or agent directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.api.routes"]
forbidden_modules = ["app.repositories", "app.storage", "app.agent"]
# Only direct imports are violations: api → repositories/storage/agent *through
# the service layer* is the sanctioned path, so indirect chains must be allowed.
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
ignore_imports = [
    # R1 — pre-existing API→Repository violations, backlog (feat-008 report).
    # Removing an entry resurfaces the violation once the route is refactored.
    "app.api.routes.settings -> app.repositories.settings",
    "app.api.routes.mcp_servers -> app.repositories.mcp_server",
    "app.api.routes.feedback -> app.storage.trace_store",
]

# ORM models stay pure: no transport, no infra clients (conventions.md § Схема БД).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Backend: models must not import infra"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.models"]
forbidden_modules = ["app.infra"]

# Transport must not leak into the domain (conventions.md § Обработка ошибок →
# «доменные исключения, не транспорт»). Services/repositories/storage/agent
# raise AppError, never fastapi.HTTPException — so they must not import
# fastapi at all.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Backend: domain layers must not import fastapi (no transport leak)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "app.services",
    "app.repositories",
    "app.storage",
    "app.agent",
    "app.models",
]
forbidden_modules = ["fastapi"]
# Only a *direct* `import fastapi` in a domain module is a transport leak; the
# indirect chain via the allow-listed mcp_server → api.schemas import is fine.
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "SIEM: domain layers must not import fastapi (no transport leak)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "siem_service.services",
    "siem_service.repositories",
    "siem_service.pipeline",
    "siem_service.correlation",
    "siem_service.domain",
]
forbidden_modules = ["fastapi"]
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

# SIEM domain is the bottom of the stack — imports nothing internal upward
# (siem-service.md § Layered Architecture, "infra/domain не вверх").
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "SIEM: domain must not import upward"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["siem_service.domain"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "siem_service.api",
    "siem_service.services",
    "siem_service.pipeline",
    "siem_service.correlation",
    "siem_service.repositories",
    "siem_service.infra",
]

# SIEM infra is a utility package: configured clients, no upward dependency.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "SIEM: infra must not import upward"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["siem_service.infra"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "siem_service.api",
    "siem_service.services",
    "siem_service.pipeline",
    "siem_service.correlation",
    "siem_service.repositories",
]

# Workers and data access never reach the presentation layer (api > workers/data).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "SIEM: services/pipeline/correlation/repositories must not import api"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "siem_service.services",
    "siem_service.pipeline",
    "siem_service.correlation",
    "siem_service.repositories",
]
forbidden_modules = ["siem_service.api"]

# Shared contracts are a leaf library — they must not depend on either service
# (conventions.md § Структура проекта; packages/ are imported, never import back).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Packages: siem-contracts must not import service code"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["siem_contracts"]
forbidden_modules = ["app", "siem_service"]

# DEP002 (declared but not imported): every entry below is intentionally pinned even though
# nothing imports it directly, so deptry cannot see the usage:
#   - cryptography: used by the Cython-compiled comic_utils.get_panel_bytes Fernet decrypter;
#     its .pyi stub hides the runtime `from cryptography.fernet import Fernet` from deptry.

#     the build pipeline, not via a direct top-level import in the reader.
#   - docutils/docutils-stubs/types-docutils: docutils runtime + type-check-only stub packages.

    "better-exceptions",
    "certifi",
    "click",
    "colorama",
    "cryptography",
    "docutils",
    "docutils-stubs",
    "filetype",
    "idna",
    "kivy-deps-angle",
    "kivy-deps-glew",
    "kivy-deps-sdl2",
    "kivy-garden",
    "numpy",
    "pygments",
    "pyobjc-core",
    "pyobjc-framework-cocoa",
    "pypiwin32",
    "pytz",
    "pywin32",
    "six",
    "types-docutils",
    "tzdata",
    "urllib3",
    "win32-setctime",
]

  "filelock>=3.16,<5.0",

  "python-dotenv>=1.0,<2.0",

    # pathlib preference — codebase intentionally mixes os.path/Path
    "PL100", "PL101", "PL103", "PL105", "PL107", "PL108", "PL109",
    "PL110", "PL111", "PL112", "PL113", "PL116", "PL117", "PL118",
    "PL119", "PL120", "PL123",
    "E800",  # eradicate: section comments flagged as code
    # --- reviewed during the 2024 lint sweep; not actionable here ---
    "PIE786", "PIE799", "PIE790",  # broad-except is the documented policy
    "T201", "T000",               # print/TODO are legitimate in a CLI tool
    "G200", "G201", "G100",       # logging style — exception() already used
    "LOG005", "LOG014",
    "TRY003", "TRY101", "TRY202", "TRY300", "TRY301", "TRY401",

    "DOC301", "LN001", "LN002",   # docstring/length plugins
    "SCS100", "SCS109",           # secure-coding-style preference
    "ISC004",                     # implicit concat style
    "SIM105",                     # remaining suppress() candidates are noqa'd
    "E402",                       # lazy imports are a deliberate pattern
]

# Standalone bandit is the canonical Python SAST pass (flake8's S rules
# are disabled so findings are not double-reported).
# Skips: B104 hardcoded bind-all (the config layer binds 0.0.0.0
# intentionally behind profiles; BIND_HOST validation lives in
# core/config.py), B311 random (secrets module is used for tokens),
# B310 urllib open (all outbound HTTP goes through the pinned
# security.http_client wrapper), B101 assert (pytest-style asserts in
# service code are intentional contract checks), B110
# try/except/pass (alerts/metrics export paths deliberately never
# raise), B404 subprocess import (the platform adapters' job),
# B105/B107 credential-name heuristics (variable names, not values),
# B603/B607 subprocess-without-shell/partial-path (the real risk is
# B602 shell=True, which stays enabled).
skips = ["B104", "B311", "B310", "B101", "B110", "B404",

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = ["no.nav.klage"], importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class LayeredArchitectureTest {
    private fun kabalApiLayeredArchitecture(): Architectures.LayeredArchitecture =
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer(
                "Controllers",
            ).definedBy(
                "no.nav.klage.oppgave.api.controller..",
                "no.nav.klage.dokument.api.controller..",
                "no.nav.klage.innsyn.api.controller..",
                "no.nav.klage.kaptein.api.controller..",
            ).layer("ApiMappers")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.api.mapper..", "no.nav.klage.dokument.api.mapper..")
            .layer(
                "View",
            ).definedBy(
                "no.nav.klage.oppgave.api.view..",
                "no.nav.klage.dokument.api.view..",
                "no.nav.klage.innsyn.api.view..",
                "no.nav.klage.kaptein.api.view..",
            ).layer(
                "Services",
            ).definedBy(
                "no.nav.klage.oppgave.service..",
                "no.nav.klage.dokument.service..",
                "no.nav.klage.innsyn.service..",
                "no.nav.klage.kaptein.service..",
            ).layer("Repositories")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.repositories..", "no.nav.klage.dokument.repositories..")
            .layer("Clients")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.clients..", "no.nav.klage.dokument.clients..")
            .layer("Config")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.config..", "no.nav.klage.dokument.config..")
            .layer("Domain")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.domain..", "no.nav.klage.dokument.domain..")
            .layer("Eventlisteners")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.eventlisteners..", "no.nav.klage.dokument.eventlisteners..")
            .layer("Util")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.util..", "no.nav.klage.dokument.util..")
            .layer("Exceptions")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.exceptions..", "no.nav.klage.dokument.exceptions..")
            .layer("Gateway")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.oppgave.gateway", "no.nav.klage.dokument.gateway")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForControllers: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Controllers")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForApimappers: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("ApiMappers")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config", "Services")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForView: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer(
                "View",
            ).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Services", "Config", "ApiMappers", "Exceptions", "Util", "Domain", "Gateway")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForServices: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Services")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Config", "Eventlisteners", "ApiMappers", "Gateway", "Clients")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForPersistence: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Repositories")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Services", "Controllers", "Config", "Eventlisteners", "ApiMappers")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForClients: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Clients")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                "Services",
                "Repositories",
                "Config",
                "Controllers",
                "Util",
                "ApiMappers",
                "Gateway",
                "Eventlisteners",
            )

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForEventlisteners: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Eventlisteners")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config", "Services", "Domain")
}

]
classifiers = [

    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Database",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
]
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "click>=8.3.0",
    "rich-click>=1.9.0,<2.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "jinja2>=3.0.0",
    "pydantic==2.13.5",
    "packaging>=23.2",
    # EXACT pin: ruff is the generated-code formatter (core/codegen/formatter.py
    # runs `ruff format` over the output tree), so its version is part of LHP's
    # reproducible-output contract. An unbounded floor let CI float to 0.15.x,
    # which preserves a blank line after a multi-line `def` that 0.13.3 strips —
    # drifting generated bytes vs the e2e baselines. Bump deliberately, then
    # regenerate baselines with the new version.
    "ruff==0.13.3",
    "networkx>=3.6.0",
    # FLOOR >=28: sqlglot 28.0.0 made the Databricks parser EMIT the (already
    # existing) exp.Stream node for `FROM STREAM` / `stream(...)`, above the wrapped
    # table; 26.x/27.x emit exp.Anonymous INSIDE exp.Table instead. Note the class
    # exists on both, so hasattr() is not a version probe.
    # core/dependencies/sql_extraction.py supports only the >=28 shape, deliberately
    # — no version gating, so one LHP version yields one deterministic dependency
    # graph. Below 28 the opaqueness rule silently stops firing and edges get
    # invented from string literals and nested wrapper calls.
    # Bounded ceiling: extracted SQL dependency edges feed hash-pinned e2e
    # baselines; bumps stay deliberate (characterization diff + baseline regen).
    # Note .github/dependabot.yml ignores semver-major, so ceiling widenings arrive
    # as constraint changes needing manual review, never auto-merge.
    "sqlglot>=28,<31",
]

# the hash-stable fixture tree and pollutes e2e baseline directory comparisons.

    # name happens to match pytest's class-collection heuristic. The
    # constructor signature differs from a test class so pytest already
    # skips it; suppress the informational warning.

    # whose name happens to match pytest's class-collection heuristic. It has

[tool.ruff]
# This block governs LHP's OWN repo tooling: ruff is the single linter +
# formatter + import-sorter for src/ and tests/. ``target-version`` /
# ``line-length`` are TOP-LEVEL keys (not under ``[tool.ruff.format]``, which
# holds only format options like ``quote-style``).
# NOTE: this is unrelated to the generated-output formatting pass. That pass
# (``core/codegen/formatter.py``) runs ``ruff format`` inside the USER's project
# dir and passes its config EXPLICITLY, so this repo config never leaks into
# generated bytes — generated formatting stays deterministic and LHP-controlled.
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 88
# ``force-exclude`` makes the excludes below win even when a file is passed
# EXPLICITLY (as pre-commit does with the changed-file list) — defense-in-depth
# so the hash-stable generated baselines are never linted/formatted.
force-exclude = true
extend-exclude = [
    "tests/fixtures",             # hand-written + import_manager fixtures (incl. invalid_syntax.py)
    "tests/e2e/fixtures",         # generated E2E baselines — NEVER format (hash-stable)
    "tests/baselines",            # generated DLT baselines (reference dp/spark globals → F821)
    "tests/performance/baselines",
    "src/lhp/templates/init_sample",  # packaged sample-project data — notebook-source .py referencing spark/dbutils globals; never lint/format
    # docs fixture projects — generated/ code is byte-exact generator output that docs
    # literalinclude (only fixtures listed in tests/docs/test_docs_fixture_drift.py are
    # drift-checked); hand-written fixture inputs are excluded too. Never lint/format.
    "docs/_fixtures",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Constitution rules stay enforced via family selects:
#   B ⊃ B904 (§7.3) · TRY ⊃ TRY400 (§7.2) · RUF ⊃ RUF013 (§7.4)
select = ["E", "W", "F", "C901", "I", "B", "C4", "RET", "PIE", "RUF", "TRY"]
ignore = [
    "E203",    # whitespace before ':' — the formatter owns this
    "E501",    # line length — the formatter wraps; long strings/URLs stay exempt (as before)
    "W291",    # trailing whitespace — formatter owns code lines; residual cases are intentional whitespace inside test-data string literals
    "W292",    # no-newline-at-end-of-file — the formatter owns this
    "W293",    # whitespace on a blank line — the formatter owns this
    "ISC001",  # implicit-str-concat — conflicts with `ruff format`
    "RUF002",  # ambiguous-unicode in docstrings — noise
    "RUF003",  # ambiguous-unicode in comments — noise
    "RUF059",  # Tier-2 (deferred): unused-unpacked-variable
    "RUF012",  # Tier-2 (deferred): mutable-class-default vs Pydantic models
    "TRY002",  # raise-vanilla-class — noisy
    "TRY003",  # long-message-outside-class — conflicts with ErrorFactory rich messages
    "TRY300",  # consider-else — noisy
    "TRY301",  # raise-within-try — noisy
]
# `×` (MULTIPLICATION SIGN) is intentional in the CLI warning rollup count
# suffix (e.g. "×2288") and its tests; permit just that confusable rather than
# disabling RUF001 wholesale.
allowed-confusables = ["×"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 40   # RATCHET — target 10; lower as functions are refactored (see CHANGELOG)

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]

# argument defaults, which B008 (function-call-in-default-argument) flags. These
# calls are sentinels, not mutable defaults — exempt them. (webapp routers.)
extend-immutable-calls = [
    "fastapi.Depends",
    "fastapi.Query",
    "fastapi.Header",
    "fastapi.Path",
    "fastapi.Body",
    "fastapi.File",
]

name = "webapp-uses-public-api"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lhp.webapp"]
forbidden_modules = ["lhp.core", "lhp.parsers", "lhp.generators", "lhp.bundle", "lhp.models", "lhp.presets", "lhp.utils", "lhp.cli"]
# Only flag DIRECT imports — transitive chains through ``lhp.api`` are by
# design (the public API is the one allowed bridge into domain modules per
# §5.3). ``lhp.webapp`` imports ``lhp.api`` / ``lhp.errors`` directly; the
# domain modules it reaches are all behind that public surface.
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

# LHP top-down layering. ``generators`` sits ABOVE ``core`` because the
# per-action generators inherit from ``BaseActionGenerator`` in
# ``lhp.core.registry`` — those 17 former carve-outs are now legal downward
# edges and have been removed. To make this hold, ``core`` was decoupled from
# ``generators`` (the reverse edge): ``python_file_copier`` moved into ``core``
# and ``ActionRegistry`` is now populated by ``lhp.generators.registration``
# (wired in at the composition root) instead of importing the families.
# ``presets`` and ``parsers`` are core's DEPENDENCIES, so they sit BELOW
# ``core`` (``presets`` above ``parsers`` because ``presets`` imports it);
# ``errors`` sits below ``models`` because ``models`` imports ``errors``.
# ``lhp.api`` is a single public surface above ``core``; ``core`` no longer
# imports ``api`` (ValidationService returns the internal ``ValidationError``
# and ``BaseWarningCollector`` lives in ``core/_interfaces.py``). See the
# "Layering contract redesign V2" CHANGELOG entry for the full rationale.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "LHP top-down layering"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "lhp.cli",
    "lhp.webapp",
    "lhp.api",
    "lhp.bundle",
    "lhp.generators",
    "lhp.core",
    "lhp.presets",
    "lhp.parsers",
    "lhp.models",
    "lhp.telemetry",
    "lhp.errors",
    "lhp.utils",
]

# §13.5 — subprocess workers never emit telemetry, so no domain package may
# reach the client; instrumentation is composed at the edges (CLI, webapp, api).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Only CLI, webapp and api may import telemetry"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lhp.core", "lhp.models", "lhp.parsers", "lhp.presets", "lhp.generators", "lhp.bundle", "lhp.utils", "lhp.errors"]
forbidden_modules = ["lhp.telemetry"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Models must not depend on higher layers"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lhp.models"]
forbidden_modules = ["lhp.cli", "lhp.bundle", "lhp.core", "lhp.generators", "lhp.parsers", "lhp.presets", "lhp.api"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Utils must depend only on stdlib (and at most models)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lhp.utils"]
forbidden_modules = ["lhp.cli", "lhp.bundle", "lhp.core", "lhp.generators", "lhp.parsers", "lhp.presets", "lhp.api"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

type = "independence"
modules = ["lhp.generators.load", "lhp.generators.transform", "lhp.generators.write", "lhp.generators.test"]
# The families never import each other directly. They are wired into the core
# ``ActionRegistry`` from ``lhp.generators.registration`` (the composition

[tool.mutmut]
# Mutation spot-checks (scripts/ci/mutation.sh module) — see that script for how
# the pieces fit. Key repo integration points:
# - Single-process pytest: the repo pytest.ini addopts carry -n 4 (xdist),
#   but mutmut's trampoline stats are collected by in-process pytest plugins
#   (pytest_runtest_teardown) — xdist workers run the tests where the
#   collector does not exist, so no test ever associates with a mutant.
# - also_copy: the mutants/ dir isolates mutated files, but tests/conftest
#   imports the whole app at collection; a full copy keeps imports resolving.
# - The script swaps source_paths + pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection to
#   the module + its test file per run; stats then executes only that file.
# - mutate_only_covered_lines is deliberately OFF everywhere: its coverage
#   pass unloads every module imported during the stats run, and numpy (and
#   other C extensions) cannot be re-imported in the same process.
source_paths = ["app"]
also_copy = ["app", "tests", "scripts"]
# The diff-driven scoping in scripts/ci/mutation.sh module stamps
# `# pragma: no mutate` onto every unchanged line; mutmut's AST visitor only
# honors that comment on simple statement lines and standalone comments, so
# interior lines of multi-line statements still got mutated. The pattern
# matcher keys on line CONTENT, which catches every stamped line — this is
# what actually makes the scoping work (unchanged lines produce no mutants).
do_not_mutate_patterns = ["# pragma: no mutate"]
# Per-mutant timeout = timeout_constant + timeout_multiplier * stats_time.
# The default constant (1s) is sized for fast local machines; on the 2-core
# CI runner each mutant pays ~25-30s of fresh-process startup (python + app
# import + collection) that the stats phase does not capture, so the default
# timeout races the startup and every mutant reads as a timeout. The constant
# buys that startup headroom.
timeout_constant = 60.0
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = []
pytest_add_cli_args = ["-p", "no:xdist", "-o", 'addopts=-m "not composio and not model_onboarding and not schemathesis" --strict-markers -p no:opik -p no:langsmith_plugin -p no:schemathesis --timeout=300']

# coverage.py does not read pytest.ini (only .coveragerc, setup.cfg, tox.ini,
# pyproject.toml), so the [coverage:*] sections that used to live there were
# never applied — the CI lane passed --cov-fail-under explicitly, which is why
# nobody noticed. relative_files is required at DATA-COLLECTION time: the two
# test lanes write coverage on self-hosted runners and the combine job runs
# wherever it lands; absolute runner paths there fail with "No source for code".
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["app"]
relative_files = true
omit = ["app/patches.py", "app/static/*"]

[tool.coverage.paths]
source = ["app", "*/apps/api/app"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
fail_under = 80
exclude_lines = ["pragma: no cover", "if TYPE_CHECKING:", "if __name__ == .__main__.:"]

# An app boot and a pytest process both pay every import these low modules
# reach. Constants and config are leaves by definition, and app.utils is shared
# by models that every test worker loads at collection; letting any of them
# reach the model stack cost ~1.5s per process (app.constants.llm imported the
# langchain-typed llm types; app.utils.timezone imported RunnableConfig to
# annotate one parameter). Run it with `lint-imports --no-cache` from apps/api:
# grimp's on-disk cache drops function-scope imports, so a cached run sees a
# SUBSET of the graph and can go green on a violation the CI lane catches.
#
# Every ignore_imports entry below is ONE direct edge with a reason. grimp reads
# the AST, so it cannot tell a deliberately deferred function-scope import from
# a module-scope one and counts both; those entries say so. Listing edges one at
# a time rather than by wildcard is what keeps the contracts able to fail: a NEW
# import from any of these packages is still red.
# KNOWN HOLE, stated rather than hidden: app/services/ has no __init__.py, and
# grimp only walks directories that are real packages — so nothing under
# app.services is in the graph and no chain THROUGH a service is analysed.
# "app.services" is therefore absent from the forbidden lists below (naming a
# module grimp cannot see is an error, not a check). Adding the __init__.py
# makes ruff's isort re-classify `mcp` as third-party for the six modules under
# app/services/mcp/, and reformatting those files trips the PLR complexity
# ratchet on grandfathered debt this change did not create. Worth revisiting
# with that debt, not alongside it. Direct imports out of app.constants /
# app.config / app.utils are all still checked, which is where the measured
# cost actually came from.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["app"]
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "app.constants is a leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.constants"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "app.agents",
  "app.api",
  "app.db",
  "langchain_core",
  "langchain",
  "langgraph",
  "transformers",
]
ignore_imports = [
  # Same leaf-prompt edge the app.config contract exempts below: the chain from
  # a constant runs through oauth_config into plain prompt-text modules.
  "app.config.oauth_config -> app.agents.prompts.memory_prompts",
  "app.config.oauth_config -> app.agents.prompts.subagent_prompts",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "app.config is a leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.config"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "app.agents",
  "app.api",
  "app.db",
  "langchain_core",
  "langchain",
  "langgraph",
  "transformers",
]
ignore_imports = [
  # The per-plan limit tables are keyed by PlanType; the enum lives on the
  # payment model, which is what makes the table and the subscription agree.
  "app.config.rate_limits -> app.models.payment_models",
  # token_repository is a Postgres repository that has always lived under
  # config/ — misfiled, not config reaching downwards. Moving it is a separate
  # change with its own blast radius.
  "app.config.token_repository -> app.db.postgresql",
  "app.config.token_repository -> app.models.db_oauth",
  # app/agents/prompts/ is prompt TEXT — plain string modules with no imports of
  # their own. The oauth config names each integration's prompts; the edge is to
  # a leaf that only happens to live under app/agents/.
  "app.config.oauth_config -> app.agents.prompts.memory_prompts",
  "app.config.oauth_config -> app.agents.prompts.subagent_prompts",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "app.utils never pulls the model stack"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.utils"]
forbidden_modules = ["langchain_core", "langchain", "langgraph", "transformers"]
ignore_imports = [
  # Utils that genuinely manipulate LangChain messages/runnables or a LangGraph
  # runtime — for these the import IS the work.
  "app.utils.agent_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.chat_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.embedding_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.file_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.mcp_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.multimodal -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.notes_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.research_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.workflow_utils -> langchain_core",
  # Their whole job is a langchain value: stream_utils reshapes AIMessage,
  # todo_vector_utils builds Document. The type IS the input, so there is no
  # shared piece to move down into a leaf.
  "app.utils.stream_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.todo_vector_utils -> langchain_core",
  "app.utils.workflow_utils -> langgraph",
  "app.utils.integration_checker -> langgraph",
  "app.utils.integration_checker -> app.models.agent_models",
  "app.utils.composio_hooks.gmail_hooks -> app.models.agent_models",
  "app.utils.composio_hooks.reddit_hooks -> app.models.agent_models",
  "app.utils.composio_hooks.twitter_hooks -> app.models.agent_models",
  "app.utils.device_onboarding -> app.models.agent_models",
  # Reaches a langchain-typed model directly; the stack is below that edge.
  "app.utils.workflow_utils -> app.models.agent_models",
  # Utils that call the LLM client / vision helpers / tool registry outright —
  # same family as the langchain_core entries above, one hop further out.
  "app.utils.agent_utils -> app.agents.tools.core.registry",
  "app.utils.chat_utils -> app.agents.llm.chatbot",
  "app.utils.file_utils -> app.agents.llm.client",
  "app.utils.file_utils -> app.agents.llm.vision",
  "app.utils.image_utils -> app.agents.llm.vision",
  "app.utils.profile_card -> app.agents.llm.client",
  "app.utils.research_utils -> app.agents.llm.client",
  "app.utils.notes_utils -> app.db.chroma.chromadb",
  "app.utils.todo_vector_utils -> app.db.chroma.chromadb",
  "app.utils.stream_publishers -> app.models.stream_events",
  "app.utils.agent_utils -> app.models.stream_events",
  "app.utils.canvas_vector_utils -> app.db.chroma.chromadb",
  "app.utils.embedding_utils -> app.db.chroma.chromadb",
]
