# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 1: domain-is-clean
#
# The domain layer must not import from any outer layer or from CLI/UI
# frameworks (argparse, etc.).  This is the strictest contract — any new
# violation here is a clean-architecture regression.
#
# NOTE: allow_indirect_imports = True is required because import-linter
# resolves the root `orb` package as an intermediate node when any domain
# module does `from orb.domain...`.  The root orb/__init__.py re-exports
# SDK/bootstrap symbols which transitively touch outer layers, creating
# false positives on every domain file.  Direct-only enforcement is the
# correct policy here.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:domain-is-clean]
name = Domain layer is clean (no outer-layer imports)
type = forbidden
source_modules = orb.domain
forbidden_modules =
    orb.application
    orb.infrastructure
    orb.interface
    orb.providers
    orb.monitoring
    orb.cli
    argparse
allow_indirect_imports = True
# No baseline ignore_imports needed: the only domain argparse violation
# (provider_cli_spec_port) was moved to orb.providers.base in this branch (E2).
# Any future argparse-in-domain import is now a real CI failure.


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 2: application-no-infra-concretes
#
# The application layer must not import from infrastructure concretes,
# provider implementations, or monitoring adapters.  It may only depend on
# domain (pure) and its own cross-cutting application interfaces.
#
# All A1/A2/A3 baseline violations have been fixed by Epic E4 / ticket #1358:
#   A1 — TemplateDTO moved to orb.application.dto.template
#   A2 — same fix as A1
#   A3 — MetricsCollector now injected via MetricsPort
#
# The circuit-breaker resilience leak has also been inverted: the orchestration
# service now depends on orb.application.ports.resilience_port (a
# CircuitBreakerPort protocol + CircuitBreakerOpenError base) and the
# infrastructure strategy/exception are wired in via the DI bootstrap.  No
# app→infra resilience import remains, so no ignore is needed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:application-no-infra-concretes]
name = Application layer does not import infrastructure concretes
type = forbidden
source_modules = orb.application
forbidden_modules =
    orb.infrastructure
    orb.providers
    orb.monitoring
allow_indirect_imports = True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 3: infrastructure-no-upward
#
# The infrastructure layer must not import from the interface/CLI layers.
# It adapts domain ports to external systems; it must not depend on the
# presentation/CLI tier.
#
# I1 baseline violation has been fixed by Epic E4 / ticket #1358:
#   I1 — console_adapter inverted: it now owns Rich logic and cli/console.py
#        delegates downward to the adapter (cli → infrastructure, correct).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:infrastructure-no-upward]
name = Infrastructure layer does not import upward layers
type = forbidden
source_modules = orb.infrastructure
forbidden_modules =
    orb.interface
    orb.cli
allow_indirect_imports = True

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=80.9.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "orb-py"
version = "1.8.5"
description = "Open Resource Broker (ORB) — dynamic cloud resource provisioning via CLI and REST API"
readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [
    {name = "Open Resource Broker Maintainers", email = "open-resource-broker-maintainers@lists.finos.org"},
]
maintainers = [
    {name = "Open Resource Broker Maintainers", email = "open-resource-broker-maintainers@lists.finos.org"},
]
keywords = [
    "aws",
    "azure",
    "gcp",
    "kubernetes",
    "ec2",
    "hostfactory",
    "symphony",
    "slurm",
    "hpc",
    "cluster",
    "cloud",
    "infrastructure",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Natural Language :: English",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Topic :: System :: Clustering",
    "Topic :: System :: Distributed Computing",
]
requires-python = ">=3.10"

dependencies = [
    # Core dependencies (always needed, never provider-specific)
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0.0",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.0",
    "urllib3>=2.8.0", # Security: Fix CVE-2025-66471, CVE-2025-66418, CVE-2026-21441,
    # CVE-2026-97687, CVE-2026-97688, CVE-2026-97689
    # Security: Fix GHSA-ffc3-869f-jxw9 (critical), GHSA-9j54-fg26-wv3r,
    # GHSA-w2cx-738m-mc7w, GHSA-9v7f-9g4p-ffgj, GHSA-p4g4-x82p-q773,
    # GHSA-r6x4-923q-g947 (high), GHSA-jwrc-g2q2-pq5p, GHSA-8wjv-2p76-3863,
    # GHSA-hxm8-2xgr-2p9m, GHSA-2gx3-rcp4-g85q, GHSA-w6j9-cwv2-h6wq,
    # GHSA-42vr-xj54-vc7v (medium)
    "PyJWT>=2.15.0",
    "cryptography>=46.0.5", # Security: Fix CVE-2026-26007
    "filelock>=3.20.1", # Security: Fix CVE-2025-68146 race condition
    "requests>=2.31.0",
    "PyYAML>=6.0.0", # Exported API (lazy-loaded)
    "jsonschema>=4.17.0",
    # AWS provider deps — currently in core for backward compatibility.
    # The canonical install path going forward is `pip install orb-py[aws]`,
    # which already works today.  When the second provider lands these will
    # move to the [aws] extra and a major-version bump will signal the
    # breaking change for operators who installed without extras.
    "boto3>=1.42.21",
    "botocore>=1.42.21",
    "psutil>=5.9.0", # Required by the system health check (CPU/memory)
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# ── Storage extras ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SQL storage strategy — includes Alembic for schema migration support.
# Install with: pip install orb-py[sql]
sql = [
    "alembic>=1.13",
]

# ── Provider extras ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# AWS provider — explicit opt-in alias for the AWS deps currently in core.
# Pinning the same versions keeps `pip install orb-py[aws]` resolving identically
# to the bare install and future-proofs operator install commands for the day
# AWS deps move out of core.
aws = [
    "boto3>=1.42.21",
    "botocore>=1.42.21",
]

# Modern Kubernetes provider — explicit opt-in extra.  Install with:
#   pip install orb-py[k8s]
# Only the SDK client is required here; everything else (jinja2, watchdog,
# alembic etc.) is legacy-plugin baggage and stays in the [k8s-legacy] extra.
k8s = [
    "kubernetes",
]

# Azure provider runtime dependencies. Install with:
#   pip install orb-py[azure]
azure = [
    "azure-core>=1.38.2",
    "azure-identity>=1.25.2",
    "azure-mgmt-compute>=37.2.0",
    "azure-mgmt-network>=30.2.0",
    "azure-mgmt-resource>=25.0.0",
    "azure-mgmt-resource-subscriptions>=1.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
]
# GCP provider. Install with:
#   pip install orb-py[gcp]
gcp = [
    "google-cloud-compute>=1.14.0",
    "google-auth>=2.23.0",
    # Imported directly for exception translation and retry predicates
    # (compute_client.py, exceptions.py, single_vm_handler.py), not just
    # pulled in transitively by google-cloud-compute.
    "google-api-core>=2.17.0",
]

# Meta-extra: all currently implemented providers
all-providers = [
    "orb-py[aws]",
    "orb-py[azure]",
    "orb-py[k8s]",
    "orb-py[gcp]",
]

# Legacy k8s HostFactory plugin — heavy deps gated behind optional extra.
# Install with: pip install orb-py[k8s-legacy]
k8s-legacy = [
    "kubernetes",
    "boto3>=1.42.21",
    "jinja2>=3.1.0",
    "typing-extensions",
    "watchdog",
    "rich>=13.3.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0.0",
    "tenacity",
    "prometheus-client>=0.17.0",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.0",
    "pg8000",
    "alembic",
    "fastapi>=0.128.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.24.0",
]

# ── Feature extras ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reflex web UI — the wheel ships a pre-built SPA bundle in ``orb/ui/_static/``
# so end users do NOT need Node/Bun at runtime (only builders running
# ``dev-tools/package/build_ui.sh`` do).  Pin to 0.9.x: earlier versions
# lack ``api_transformer`` and the React Router 7 build layout our
# rxconfig/api-transformer assumes.
# Install with: pip install orb-py[ui]
ui = [
    "reflex>=0.9,<0.10",
]

# CLI enhancements (colored output)
cli = [
    "rich>=13.3.0",
    "rich-argparse>=1.0.0",
]

# API server (for REST API mode)
api = [
    "fastapi>=0.128.0",
    "starlette>=0.49.1", # Security: Fix CVE-2025-62727, CVE-2025-54121, CVE-2024-47874
    "uvicorn>=0.24.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.0",
]

# Model Context Protocol server. The 2.x line registers low-level server
# handlers through constructor callbacks instead of decorators.
mcp = [
    "mcp>=2.3,<3",
]

# OTel API only — for embedders that want instrumentation without the SDK weight.
# Libraries should depend on [otel]; applications depend on [monitoring].
otel = [
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.20.0",
]

# Monitoring & observability (provider-neutral — no boto3 instrumentation here)
monitoring = [
    "orb-py[otel]",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.41b0,<1.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.41b0,<1.0",
    # Click span-per-command instrumentation (programmatic, not CLI-wrapper)
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-click>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    # OS-level CPU/memory/GC/thread gauges (replaces dead memory_usage_bytes/cpu_usage_percent)
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-system-metrics>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    # Log-record trace_id/span_id injection for log-trace correlation
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    "prometheus-client>=0.17.0",
    "psutil>=5.9.0",
]

# AWS-specific monitoring (botocore/boto3 instrumentation; requires [aws])
monitoring-aws = [
    "orb-py[aws,monitoring]",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-botocore>=0.64b0,<1.0",
]

# All optional runtime features (providers + features + UI).  This is the
# "give me everything a user could run" extra.  It deliberately includes `ui`
# (reflex) so `pip install orb-py[all]` yields a fully-functional install incl.
# the embedded web UI.  NOTE: `ui` conflicts with the `ci`/`dev` dependency
# groups (reflex→click>=8.2 vs semgrep→click<8.2), so never combine
# `--extra all` with `--group ci`/`--group dev`; use `--no-dev` when syncing it.
all = [
    "orb-py[cli,api,mcp,sql,monitoring,monitoring-aws,all-providers,ui]",
]

# ── Test extras ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# AWS test dependencies — moto + response mocking
test-aws = [
    "orb-py[aws]",
    "moto[ec2,iam,ec2instanceconnect,autoscaling,ssm,dynamodb,sts,sqs,sns]>=5.1.19,<6.0.0",
    "responses>=0.24.0,<1.0.0",
    "requests-mock>=1.11.0,<2.0.0",
]

# Azure SDK packages imported directly by the Azure tests. These overlap with
# the runtime extra because the tests assert behavior using real SDK exception
# and model types, but the test group does not install unrelated runtime SDKs.
test-azure = [
    "azure-core>=1.38.2",
    "azure-identity>=1.25.2",
    "azure-mgmt-compute>=37.2.0",
    "azure-mgmt-resource>=25.0.0",
    "azure-mgmt-resource-subscriptions>=1.0.0",
]

# GCP provider tests use Compute SDK models and google-api-core exceptions.
test-gcp = [
    "orb-py[gcp]",
]

# Kubernetes test dependencies — kmock is an in-process HTTP-level K8s API mock.
# Tests point the real kubernetes SDK client at the kmock URL so the full
# client stack is exercised without a live cluster.
test-k8s = [
    "orb-py[k8s]",
    "kmock>=0.7",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# pip compatibility shim for [dependency-groups] (PEP 735)
#
# pip does not yet support PEP 735 dependency-groups.  The authoritative dev
# dependency list lives in [dependency-groups] below.  This optional-dep keeps
# `pip install -e ".[dev]"` working by combining two things:
#
#   1. orb-py[all] — the full runtime surface (providers, api, ui, monitoring,
#      sql, cli).  pip resolves extras, so runtime deps need NOT be re-listed
#      here; referencing [all] avoids a hand-maintained mirror of them.
#   2. The CI/dev TOOLCHAIN (ruff, pytest, mkdocs, pip-audit, …).  These live only
#      in [dependency-groups] — which pip cannot read — so they must be mirrored
#      here until pip gains PEP 735 support.
#
# tests/unit/test_pyproject_dev_extra.py guards that this shim still covers the
# whole dev dependency-group, so the toolchain mirror can't silently drift.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
dev = [
    # Full runtime surface — including the UI, which [all-providers] omits.
    "orb-py[all]",
    # --- toolchain from dependency-groups.lint ---
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
    "pathspec>=0.11.0",
    # --- toolchain from dependency-groups.typecheck ---
    "pyright>=1.1.408,<2.0.0",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0.12.12,<7.0.0",
    "types-python-dateutil>=2.8.19.14,<3.0.0",
    "kubernetes-stubs-elephant-fork>=36.0.2,<37.0.0",
    "tomli>=2.0.0,<3.0.0",
    # --- toolchain from dependency-groups.arch ---
    "import-linter>=2.0,<3.0.0",
    # --- toolchain from dependency-groups.test (runtime test deps not in [all]) ---
    "pytest>=7.4.3,<10.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0,<8.0.0",
    "pytest-env>=1.1.1,<2.0.0",
    "pytest-mock>=3.12.0,<4.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.21.1,<2.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.2.0,<3.0.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.3.1,<4.0.0",
    "pytest-html>=4.1.1,<5.0.0",
    "pytest-benchmark>=5.1.0,<6.0.0",
    "coverage>=7.3.2,<8.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "httpx2>=2.13,<3",
    "moto[all]>=5.1.19,<6.0.0",
    "responses>=0.24.0,<1.0.0",
    "requests-mock>=1.11.0,<2.0.0",
    "joserfc>=1.6.1",
    "werkzeug>=3.1.6",
    # Security: Fix CVE-2026-76217, CVE-2026-76218, CVE-2026-76219,
    # CVE-2026-76220, CVE-2026-76222, CVE-2026-78675, CVE-2026-78676,
    # CVE-2026-78677, CVE-2026-78678, CVE-2026-78679, CVE-2026-87817,
    # CVE-2026-87819, GHSA-jm78-9fvv-mhgr (high), GHSA-59cr-6r3x-644w (medium)
    "gitpython>=3.1.62",
    "watchdog",
    "tenacity",
    "pg8000",
    "kmock>=0.7",
    # --- toolchain from dependency-groups.docs ---
    "mkdocs>=1.5.0,<2.0.0",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.1.0,<10.0.0",
    "mkdocstrings>=0.22.0,<2.0.0",
    "mkdocstrings-python>=1.1.0,<3.0.0",
    "mkdocs-gen-files>=0.5.0,<1.0.0",
    "mkdocs-literate-nav>=0.6.0,<1.0.0",
    "mkdocs-section-index>=0.3.0,<1.0.0",
    "mike>=1.1.0,<3.0.0",
    # --- inlined from dependency-groups.security ---
    "pip-audit>=2.6.1,<3.0.0",
    "cyclonedx-bom>=4.0.0,<8.0.0",
    "lxml>=6.1.0",
    # semgrep is intentionally excluded from this shim (as in the security group):
    # workflows pin and install their own version to avoid version drift.
    # --- inlined from dependency-groups.build ---
    "build>=1.0.3,<2.0.0",
    "wheel>=0.41.3,<1.0.0",
    "setuptools>=80.9.0",
    # --- dev-only tools (not in any CI group) ---
    # Security: Fix CVE-2024-53899 (command injection), CVE-2026-102925,
    # CVE-2026-102930, CVE-2026-102937, CVE-2026-102938
    "virtualenv>=21.7.13",
    "pre-commit>=3.5.0,<5.0.0",
    "bump2version>=1.0.1,<2.0.0",
    "python-semantic-release>=10.0.0,<11.0.0",
    "line-profiler>=4.1.1,<6.0.0",
    "memory-profiler>=0.61.0,<1.0.0",
    "py-spy>=0.3.14,<1.0.0",
    "py-cpuinfo>=9.0.0,<10.0.0",
    "ipdb>=0.13.13,<1.0.0",
    "ipython>=8.16.1,<9.0.0",
    "radon>=6.0.1,<7.0.0",
    "pip-tools>=7.3.0,<8.0.0",
    "twine>=4.0.0",
    "git-changelog>=2.6.0,<3.0.0",
]

[dependency-groups]
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authoritative dev dependency definitions (PEP 735).
# Use: `uv sync --group dev` or `uv sync --group ci`
# The [project.optional-dependencies] ci/dev sections above are pip shims
# that mirror these lists for `pip install -e ".[dev]"` compatibility.
#
# Per-job groups (each maps to one CI job):
#   lint      — ruff + pathspec (lint-ruff, auto-format jobs)
#   typecheck — pyright + type stubs (lint-pyright job)
#   arch      — import-linter (arch-validation job; pyyaml via project deps)
#   test      — pytest stack + all test dependencies (all test legs)
#   docs      — mkdocs stack (docs job)
#   security  — pip-audit/cyclonedx (security-pip-audit job)
#   build     — build + wheel (build-and-package job)
#
# Umbrella groups (keep local dev + --all-groups unchanged):
#   ci        — includes all sub-groups above (same resolved set as before)
#   dev       — includes ci + local-dev tools
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- per-job sub-groups ---

lint = [
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
    "pathspec>=0.11.0",  # For gitignore pattern matching in dev-tools
]

typecheck = [
    "pyright>=1.1.408,<2.0.0",
    # pyright type-checks the whole src/orb tree, so it needs every runtime
    # dependency the code imports (fastapi, kubernetes, alembic, opentelemetry,
    # rich, jinja2, starlette, prometheus-client, click, ...) importable — not
    # just type stubs.  Pull the full runtime via the `all` extra; this group is
    # synced standalone (--no-default-groups --group typecheck) so `all`'s ui
    # extra does not clash with the ci/dev groups.
    "orb-py[all]",
    # Type stubs (augment the runtime packages above)
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0.12.12,<7.0.0",
    "types-python-dateutil>=2.8.19.14,<3.0.0",
    "kubernetes-stubs-elephant-fork>=36.0.2,<37.0.0",
    # For pyproject.toml parsing in dev scripts (Python < 3.11)
    "tomli>=2.0.0,<3.0.0",
]

arch = [
    "import-linter>=2.0,<3.0.0",  # Architecture layer-boundary enforcement
    # pyyaml is available via project [dependencies] (always installed with the project)
]

test = [
    # Testing Framework
    "pytest>=7.4.3,<10.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0,<8.0.0",
    "pytest-env>=1.1.1,<2.0.0",
    "pytest-mock>=3.12.0,<4.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.21.1,<2.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.2.0,<3.0.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.3.1,<4.0.0",
    "pytest-html>=4.1.1,<5.0.0",
    "pytest-benchmark>=5.1.0,<6.0.0",
    "coverage>=7.3.2,<8.0.0",
    # Test dependencies for API and template tests
    "fastapi>=0.128.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",  # Required by FastAPI TestClient
    "jinja2>=3.1.0",
    # MCP server tests exercise the official SDK, so the test surface needs it.
    "mcp>=2.3,<3",
    "httpx2>=2.13,<3",  # HTTP client of the MCP SDK; the transport tests drive it directly
    # AWS Testing
    "moto[all]>=5.1.19,<6.0.0",
    "responses>=0.24.0,<1.0.0",
    "requests-mock>=1.11.0,<2.0.0",
    # Security overrides for vulnerable transitive deps pulled in by test tooling
    "joserfc>=1.6.1",
    "werkzeug>=3.1.6",
    # Security override for python-semantic-release's vulnerable gitpython
    # (GHSA-956x-8gvw-wg5v, GHSA-2f96-g7mh-g2hx, GHSA-v396-v7q4-x2qj argument
    # injection; GHSA-rwj8-pgh3-r573 os.path.expandvars in polish_url)
    # Security: Fix CVE-2026-76217, CVE-2026-76218, CVE-2026-76219,
    # CVE-2026-76220, CVE-2026-76222, CVE-2026-78675, CVE-2026-78676,
    # CVE-2026-78677, CVE-2026-78678, CVE-2026-78679, CVE-2026-87817,
    # CVE-2026-87819, GHSA-jm78-9fvv-mhgr (high), GHSA-59cr-6r3x-644w (medium)
    "gitpython>=3.1.62",
    # k8s-legacy extra deps — required for tests/integration/k8s_legacy/
    "kubernetes",
    "watchdog",
    "tenacity",
    "pg8000",
    "uvicorn>=0.24.0",
    "prometheus-client>=0.17.0",
    "alembic>=1.13",
    # OpenTelemetry stack — so pyright resolves guarded optional imports and
    # observability tests exercise the real SDK path
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.41b0,<1.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.41b0,<1.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-botocore>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-click>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-system-metrics>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging>=0.64b0,<1.0",
    # k8s HTTP-level mock server (test-only, not shipped with the package)
    "kmock>=0.7",
]

docs = [
    "mkdocs>=1.5.0,<2.0.0",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.1.0,<10.0.0",
    "mkdocstrings>=0.22.0,<2.0.0",
    "mkdocstrings-python>=1.1.0,<3.0.0",
    "mkdocs-gen-files>=0.5.0,<1.0.0",
    "mkdocs-literate-nav>=0.6.0,<1.0.0",
    "mkdocs-section-index>=0.3.0,<1.0.0",
    "mike>=1.1.0,<3.0.0",
]

security = [
    "pip-audit>=2.6.1,<3.0.0",
    "cyclonedx-bom>=4.0.0,<8.0.0",
    # Security override for lxml (CVE-2026-41066) — transitive via cyclonedx-bom + pip-audit
    "lxml>=6.1.0",
    # semgrep is intentionally excluded: the workflow pins and installs its own
    # version via pip (semgrep==<pinned>) to avoid version drift with this group.
]

build = [
    "build>=1.0.3,<2.0.0",
    "wheel>=0.41.3,<1.0.0",
    # Matches [build-system].requires: python -m build --no-isolation (used
    # by build.sh) reuses this environment's packages for the build backend
    # instead of provisioning its own, so setuptools must be present here too.
    "setuptools>=80.9.0",
]

# --- umbrella groups (preserve --all-groups / local dev-install behaviour) ---

# CI Dependencies: umbrella that includes all per-job sub-groups.
# Resolved package set is identical to the former flat ci group.
ci = [
    {include-group = "lint"},
    {include-group = "typecheck"},
    {include-group = "arch"},
    {include-group = "test"},
    {include-group = "docs"},
    {include-group = "security"},
    {include-group = "build"},
]

# Dev Dependencies: Additional dev tools (includes all CI deps)
dev = [
    {include-group = "ci"},
    "virtualenv>=21.7.13",  # Security: Fix CVE-2024-53899, CVE-2026-102925,
    # CVE-2026-102930, CVE-2026-102937, CVE-2026-102938
    "pre-commit>=3.5.0,<5.0.0",
    "bump2version>=1.0.1,<2.0.0",
    "python-semantic-release>=10.0.0,<11.0.0",
    "line-profiler>=4.1.1,<6.0.0",
    "memory-profiler>=0.61.0,<1.0.0",
    "py-spy>=0.3.14,<1.0.0",
    "py-cpuinfo>=9.0.0,<10.0.0",
    "ipdb>=0.13.13,<1.0.0",
    "ipython>=8.16.1,<9.0.0",
    "radon>=6.0.1,<7.0.0",
    "pip-tools>=7.3.0,<8.0.0",
    "twine>=4.0.0",
    "git-changelog>=2.6.0,<3.0.0",
]
[project.scripts]
orb = "orb.run:cli_main"

[project.entry-points."orb.providers"]
aws = "orb.providers.aws.provider_plugin:AWSPlugin.register_plugin"
azure = "orb.providers.azure.provider_plugin:AzurePlugin.register_plugin"
gcp = "orb.providers.gcp.provider_plugin:GCPPlugin.register_plugin"
k8s = "orb.providers.k8s.provider_plugin:K8sPlugin.register_plugin"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/finos/open-resource-broker"
Documentation = "https://finos.github.io/open-resource-broker/"
Repository = "https://github.com/finos/open-resource-broker"
"Bug Reports" = "https://github.com/finos/open-resource-broker/issues"

[tool.uv]
conflicts = [
    [
        { group = "ci" },
        { extra = "ui" },
    ],
    [
        { group = "dev" },
        { extra = "ui" },
    ],
]
# Overrides pin transitive deps across every resolution split (including
# the ``ui``-only one that isn't reachable through the ``ci`` group's own
# ``lxml>=6.1.0`` override).  GHSA-vfmq-68hx-4jfw affects lxml 5.x.
# cyclonedx-python-lib>=11 switches its jsonschema extra from [format]
# (which pulls GPL-3.0-only rfc3987) to [format-nongpl] (which uses the
# Apache-2.0 rfc3987-syntax instead).  Without this override the ui-only
# conflict split resolves cyclonedx-bom's transitive dep to 9.1.0.
override-dependencies = [
    "lxml>=6.1.1",
    "cyclonedx-python-lib>=11.0.0",
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-dir]
"" = "src"

[tool.setuptools]
include-package-data = true

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"*" = ["py.typed"]
"orb.config" = ["default_config.json"]
"orb.api.assets" = ["*.png"]
"orb.providers.aws.config" = ["*.json"]
"orb.ui" = ["rxconfig.py", "_static/**/*", "_static/*"]
"orb.k8s_legacy.alembic" = ["alembic.ini", "script.py.mako"]
"orb.k8s_legacy.alembic.versions" = ["*.py"]
"orb.k8s_legacy.tests.resources" = ["*.yml", "*.tpl"]
"orb.infrastructure.scheduler.slurm.scripts" = ["*.sh", "*.bat"]

[tool.setuptools.data-files]
"orb_scripts" = ["src/orb/infrastructure/scheduler/hostfactory/scripts/*.sh", "src/orb/infrastructure/scheduler/hostfactory/scripts/*.bat", "src/orb/infrastructure/scheduler/slurm/scripts/*.sh", "src/orb/infrastructure/scheduler/slurm/scripts/*.bat"]  # keep in sync with .project.yml build.package_root



[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests", "src/orb/k8s_legacy/tests"]
norecursedirs = [
    "tests/providers/aws/live",
    # k8s live tests require a real cluster; the parallel ci-tests-providers
    # target passes -m "not serial" which would deselect every test if
    # live/conftest.py's pytest_collection_modifyitems hook is allowed to run
    # (it bulk-stamps serial on all collected items in the session).  Excluding
    # this subtree from auto-discovery mirrors the aws/live pattern and keeps
    # the parallel leg collecting only the mocked/unit/contract tests.  The
    # serial ci-tests-providers-serial target points pytest at the path
    # explicitly so live tests are still reachable when --run-k8s is passed.
    "tests/providers/k8s/live",
    # Legacy k8s regression tests require a live cluster + kubeconfig; their
    # conftest calls `delete_pods_in_namespace()` at collection time, which
    # crashes in headless CI without a real kube context.  Run them
    # explicitly with `pytest src/orb/k8s_legacy/tests/regression`.
    "src/orb/k8s_legacy/tests/regression",
]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
asyncio_mode = "strict"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
junit_family = "legacy"
# Coverage flags are NOT set here: CI drives coverage via makefiles/common.mk
# (PYTEST_COV_ARGS), passed explicitly by each ci-tests-* target.  Keeping --cov
# out of addopts means a bare `pytest` run is not instrumented (faster, no need
# for --no-cov everywhere) while CI coverage is unchanged.
addopts = "--tb=short --strict-markers --disable-warnings"
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
]
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests",
    "integration: Integration tests",
    "e2e: marks end-to-end tests",
    "mcp: MCP server tests",
    "slow: Slow running tests (docker builds, stress loops, subprocess spawning)",
    "aws: Tests requiring AWS credentials",
    "manual_aws: Live AWS integration tests that must be run manually with --run-manual-aws",
    "rest_api: REST API integration tests",
    "application: Application layer tests",
    "architecture: Architecture compliance tests",
    "domain: Domain layer tests",
    "infrastructure: Infrastructure layer tests",
    "patterns: Design pattern tests",
    "providers: Provider implementation tests",
    "performance: Performance benchmark tests",
    "provider_contract: Part of the provider contract test suite",
    "simulator_limitation: Assertion weakened due to known simulator gap",
    "requires_real_provider: Skipped unless --run-real-provider flag passed",
    "moto: Tests using moto-mocked AWS (no real credentials required)",
    "live: Tests requiring real AWS credentials (enabled with --live or --run-aws)",
    "sdk: Tests exercising the ORBClient SDK interface",
    "cli: marks CLI integration tests",
    "benchmark: marks benchmark/performance tests",
    "api: marks API tests",
    "security: marks security tests",
    "serial: forces serial execution (use ``-n0`` or filter with ``-m 'not serial'`` under xdist)",
    "k8s_live: Live Kubernetes integration tests (require a real cluster — pass --run-k8s to enable)",
    "timeout: Per-test wall-clock timeout (requires pytest-timeout; value in seconds)",
]
# Provider-specific fake credentials live in
# tests/providers/<name>/mocked/conftest.py.  The global pytest-env block
# intentionally does not set cloud credentials so live suites (any
# provider, any auth mechanism) inherit the operator's real environment.
env = []

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/orb"]
branch = true
omit = [
    # Test files that live under src/ are not production source.
    "*/tests/*",
    # Thin process entrypoints / daemon lifecycle: not meaningfully unit-tested
    # (exercised via subprocess/integration, not the coverage-uploading legs).
    "src/orb/__main__.py",
    "src/orb/run.py",
    "src/orb/interface/server_daemon.py",
    # Reflex UI render trees + entrypoints: these are declarative rx.* component
    # definitions that only execute through the Reflex compile step and a running
    # server, so they are exercised by the ui-smoke leg (boot + curl each page)
    # and the compile build, NOT by pytest.  Unit-testing render trees yields
    # brittle structural assertions with no bug-catching value.  The Reflex-
    # agnostic UI logic (state, api client, cell formatters, column defs,
    # component helpers) IS unit-tested under tests/ui/ and stays in the report.
    # This mirrors the src/orb/ui pyright exclusion (Reflex Var[T] unions
    # produce ~50 false positives per component).
    "src/orb/ui/pages/*",
    "src/orb/ui/app.py",
    "src/orb/ui/rxconfig.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
ignore_errors = true
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "pragma: nocover",
    "def __repr__",
    "def __str__",
    "if self.debug:",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if 0:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
    "pass",
    "raise ImportError",
    "except ImportError:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "\\.\\.\\.$",
]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"
title = "Open Resource Broker Coverage Report"

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 100
exclude = [
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".hg",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    # Legacy k8s plugin is in maintenance mode; it predates the root ruff config
    # and uses mypy/tox for type-checking.  Exclude it from the enforced ruff
    # scan to avoid spurious CI failures on code that isn't being actively evolved.
    "src/orb/k8s_legacy",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# ENFORCED: These rules fail CI (replace black/isort/flake8).  S (flake8-bandit)
# is enforced too — see makefiles/ci.mk's ci-quality-ruff target, which runs it
# as a separate pass scoped to src/ (not the whole repo).
select = ["E", "W", "F", "I"]
# OPTIONAL: These warn but don't fail CI (replace pylint functionality)
extend-select = ["N", "UP", "B", "PL", "C90", "RUF", "S"]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # Line too long (handled by formatter)
    "S311",  # Standard pseudo-random generator use - no crypto/token generation uses random in this codebase
    "PLR0913",  # Too many arguments
    "PLR0912",  # Too many branches
    "PLR0915",  # Too many statements
    "PLR2004",  # Magic value used in comparison - acceptable in tests
    "PLR0911",  # Too many return statements - acceptable for complex logic
    "PLW2901",  # Loop variable overwritten - acceptable pattern
    "PLW0603",  # Using global statement - acceptable for singletons
    # Non-critical violations that don't break functionality
    "C901",   # Function complexity - doesn't break functionality
    "E402",   # Module imports not at top - acceptable in scripts/tests
    "E712",   # Equality comparisons to True - style preference
    "E721",   # Type comparisons - style preference
    "B009",   # getattr with constant — used intentionally after hasattr guards for duck-typing
    "B007",   # Unused loop variables - cosmetic
    "B904",   # Missing exception chaining - important but large effort
    "B024",   # Abstract base class without abstract methods - design choice
    "B023",   # Function definition does not bind loop variable - acceptable pattern
    "B019",   # lru_cache on methods - acceptable for performance
    "B004",   # hasattr callable check - acceptable pattern
    "I001",   # Import block formatting - handled by formatter
    "N818",   # Exception naming conventions
    "N802",   # Function naming conventions
    "N804",   # First argument of class method should be cls — false positive with Pydantic @model_validator
    # Pyupgrade and modernization - non-critical style issues
    "UP006",  # Use built-in types for type annotations - style preference
    "UP024",  # Replace aliased errors - style preference
    "UP035",  # typing.Dict is deprecated - style preference
    "UP045",  # Use X | None for type annotations - style preference
    "RUF013", # PEP 484 prohibits implicit Optional - style preference
    "RUF059", # Unpacked variable is never used - acceptable in tests
    "RUF012", # Mutable class attributes should use ClassVar - design choice
    "RUF022", # __all__ is not sorted - style preference
    "RUF006", # Store reference to asyncio.create_task - acceptable pattern
    "RUF005", # Consider unpacking instead of concatenation - style preference
    "RUF003", # Comment contains ambiguous character - style issue
    "PLW1508", # Invalid type for environment variable default - acceptable
    "PLW0602", # Using global but no assignment - acceptable pattern
    "PLW1641", # Object does not implement __hash__ - design choice
    "PLC0415", # Import should be at top-level - used to avoid circular imports
    "PLC0414", # Import alias does not rename - acceptable pattern
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pep8-naming]
# Treat Pydantic decorators as classmethod-like so N805 ("first arg should be self")
# does not fire on @field_validator / @model_validator(mode="before"/"after") methods.
classmethod-decorators = [
    "classmethod",
    "pydantic.field_validator",
    "pydantic.model_validator",
    "validator",          # pydantic v1 compat
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = [
    "PLC0415",  # Allow conditional imports in tests for optional dependencies
    "N803",     # Allow PascalCase argument names (e.g. StateClass helper)
    "N806",     # Allow PascalCase local names for dynamically-constructed test subclasses
    "S",        # flake8-bandit: assert, dummy credentials/tokens, subprocess and
                # tmp-file patterns are normal test-harness code, not production risk
]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["orb"]
known-third-party = ["mcp"]
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
pythonPlatform = "Linux"
include = ["src/orb"]
exclude = [
    ".venv", "build", "dist",
    # Legacy k8s plugin code predates pyright adoption and uses mypy.
    # The package is in maintenance mode pending the modern k8s provider;
    # type-checking is gated separately via ruff + the legacy tox config.
    "src/orb/k8s_legacy",
    # Reflex uses a symbolic reactive Var[T] system where component props
    # can accept either raw Python values OR Vars that resolve at render
    # time.  Reflex's own type stubs are conservative and pyright flags
    # every legal Var/value union as a mismatch (e.g. `color_scheme=` on
    # rx.badge, `.contains()` on Var[str]).  Type-safety of the UI is
    # gated by the Reflex compile step + runtime pytest suite; running
    # pyright over generated Reflex APIs produces ~50 false positives
    # per component that do not indicate real bugs.  Exclude the UI
    # tree; Reflex-agnostic Python (state.py, api.py) is small and
    # covered by tests.
    "src/orb/ui",
]
extraPaths = ["src"]
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
reportMissingImports = true
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportUnusedVariable = true
reportUnusedImport = true
reportPrivateUsage = false
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

[tool.semantic_release]
version_toml = ["pyproject.toml:project.version"]
version_variables = [".project.yml:version"]
build_command = "make semantic-release-build"
# Extra files to fold into the tagged release commit.  The build_command
# (make semantic-release-build) stamps these to NEW_VERSION before PSR stages
# and commits, so the vX.Y.Z tag is self-contained: it carries the bumped Go SDK
# MinCompatibleVersion and the version-stamped OpenAPI spec.  This is what lets
# `go get .../sdk/go@vX.Y.Z` resolve a version.go that matches the tag, with no
# separate post-tag chore(sdk/go) commit polluting the next release's range.
assets = [
    "sdk/go/orb/version.go",
    "sdk/spec/openapi.json",
]
major_on_zero = true
allow_zero_version = true
tag_format = "v{version}"
commit_parser = "conventional"

[tool.semantic_release.branches.main]
match = "(main|master)"
prerelease_token = "rc"
prerelease = false

[tool.semantic_release.branches.release]
match = "release/.*"
prerelease_token = "rc"
prerelease = false

[tool.semantic_release.branches.feature]
match = "fix/.*|feature/.*"
prerelease_token = "alpha"
prerelease = true

[tool.semantic_release.changelog]
exclude_commit_patterns = [
    '''chore(?:\([^)]*?\))?:.+''',
    '''ci(?:\([^)]*?\))?:.+''',
    '''refactor(?:\([^)]*?\))?:.+''',
    '''style(?:\([^)]*?\))?:.+''',
    '''test(?:\([^)]*?\))?:.+''',
    '''build\((?!deps\):.+)''',
    '''Initial [Cc]ommit.*''',
]

[tool.semantic_release.changelog.default_templates]
changelog_file = "CHANGELOG.md"
output_format = "md"

[tool.semantic_release.commit_parser_options]
minor_tags = ["feat"]
patch_tags = ["fix", "perf"]
# Major bumps come from a "!" or a BREAKING CHANGE footer (conventional-commit
# rule). The conventional parser has no major_tags option; a "release:" commit
# is a trigger marker only and contributes nothing to the computed bump — the
# size is decided by the feat/fix/breaking commits in the range.
default_bump_level = 2

[tool.semantic_release.remote]
name = "origin"
type = "github"

[tool.semantic_release.publish]
dist_glob_patterns = ["dist/*"]
upload_to_vcs_release = true

[importlinter]
root_package = reference_service
# Load-bearing: required whenever a `forbidden` contract's forbidden_modules
# list names a third-party package (fastapi, starlette below). Without this,
# lint-imports refuses to run at all rather than silently skipping the check.
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:domain-independence]
name = Domain imports no other layer and no web or database framework
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    reference_service.domain
forbidden_modules =
    reference_service.api
    reference_service.services
    reference_service.infrastructure
    reference_service.container
    reference_service.main
    fastapi
    starlette
    sqlalchemy
    asyncpg
    opentelemetry
    httpx
    stamina
    redis
    aioboto3

[importlinter:contract:services-independence]
name = Services import neither api nor infrastructure
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    reference_service.services
forbidden_modules =
    reference_service.api
    reference_service.infrastructure
    reference_service.container
    reference_service.main
    fastapi
    starlette
    sqlalchemy
    asyncpg
    opentelemetry
    httpx
    stamina
    redis
    aioboto3

[project]
name = "reference-service"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "The PyFr reference service."
authors = [{ name = "Emad Mokhtar", email = "311636+EmadMokhtar@users.noreply.github.com" }]
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.115",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.32",
    "pydantic>=2.9",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.6",
    # Read directly by scripts/generate_config_docs.py, to pull the `Ge`/
    # `Gt`/`Le` constraint objects a `Field(ge=..., le=...)` puts in
    # `FieldInfo.metadata` (Verified Fact 5). A hard dependency of pydantic
    # itself at every version pydantic>=2.9 above resolves to, so this
    # floor constrains nothing new -- it only makes that script's own
    # import honest about what it uses rather than borrowing it
    # transitively through pydantic.
    "annotated-types>=0.4",
    # Read directly by scripts/generate_config_docs.py, to recognise the
    # `PydanticUndefined` sentinel a `default_factory` field reports as its
    # `.default` (Verified Fact 2). Same story as annotated-types above:
    # pydantic-core is pinned exactly per pydantic release, so 2.23.2 is
    # what pydantic>=2.9 itself already requires at minimum -- not a new
    # constraint, just an honest import.
    "pydantic-core>=2.23.2",
    "structlog>=24.4",
    "orjson>=3.10",
    # Capped below 2.1 on purpose. opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy
    # declares `sqlalchemy<2.1.0` (still true in 0.66b1). Against SQLAlchemy
    # 2.1 it logs a DependencyConflict and attaches nothing, so no query
    # ever produces a database span. Raise this cap in the same change that
    # raises the instrumentation's own cap.
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.52,<2.1",
    "asyncpg>=0.31",
    # Traces, metrics and logs. The API/SDK/exporter line and the
    # instrumentation line version SEPARATELY and always will: 1.44 for the
    # first, 0.65b0 for the second. The `b` is upstream's, not a typo — the
    # instrumentation packages are permanently beta-versioned.
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.44,<2",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.44,<2",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.65b0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.65b0",
    # Garbage collection, memory and thread counts for the runtime dashboard.
    # Its defaults emit both the current metric names and their deprecated
    # `process.runtime.cpython.*` duplicates plus whole-host `system.*`
    # series; observability/metrics.py passes an explicit config instead.
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-system-metrics>=0.65b0",
    # Supplies the LoggingHandler that bridges the standard logging
    # module to OTLP. The one in opentelemetry-sdk is deprecated as of
    # 1.44.0 and warns on construction, which filterwarnings=["error"]
    # turns into a test failure; the SDK's own message names this
    # package as the replacement.
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging>=0.65b0",
    # The shared outbound client (spec 12, item 5). A runtime dependency
    # from M3 on, not a test helper: infrastructure/http/client.py is
    # production code.
    "httpx>=0.28",
    # Bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Chosen over
    # writing one: stamina is asyncio-native, typed, and wraps tenacity,
    # which has solved retry budgets and jitter properly for years. The
    # circuit breaker beside it IS hand-written, because no maintained
    # asyncio implementation exists — see the plan's Verified Fact 15.
    "stamina>=26.1",
    # Outbound spans for the payment call. Closes the first row of the M2
    # plan's "deliberately does not include" table.
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-httpx>=0.65b0",
    # The cache client. redis-py's own asyncio interface (redis.asyncio) —
    # aioredis was merged into it years ago and is archived, so there is no
    # separate async package to choose. Used ONLY by
    # infrastructure/cache/, which is the one place allowed to import it.
    "redis>=8.1",
    # The S3-compatible object store client. aioboto3 wraps aiobotocore,
    # which wraps botocore: one adapter serves MinIO, Amazon S3, Cloudflare
    # R2, Ceph and Backblaze B2, distinguished only by endpoint_url (spec
    # 9.1). boto3 itself is synchronous and would block the event loop on
    # every call.
    "aioboto3>=15.5",
    # Spans for Redis commands. Same 0.65b0 line as every other
    # opentelemetry-instrumentation-* dependency above; the `b` is
    # upstream's permanent beta versioning, not a typo. Wired up in
    # observability/otel.py's instrument_redis, called unconditionally
    # from main.py's lifespan whenever telemetry is enabled.
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-redis>=0.65b0",
    # NO opentelemetry-instrumentation-botocore dependency here, on
    # purpose — it was tried and removed, not merely never added. Task 12
    # measured, rather than assumed, whether that instrumentor sees
    # aioboto3's async S3 calls at all: it patches
    # `botocore.client.BaseClient._make_api_call`, but `aioboto3` runs on
    # `aiobotocore`, whose `AioBaseClient` shadows that exact method with
    # its own async override, so the instrumentor's patch is never on the
    # call path. Instrumenting, then running ListBuckets, CreateBucket,
    # PutObject and GetObject through a real `aioboto3.Session` against
    # MinIO produced zero spans, even though `is_instrumented_by_opentelemetry`
    # reported True and every call itself succeeded — see the Task 12
    # report for the full transcript. Re-adding this dependency without
    # re-verifying against a current aiobotocore release would silently
    # reintroduce a store adapter whose spans never appear, which is worse
    # than no instrumentation: a dashboard built against it would read as
    # "S3 calls are always fast" rather than "S3 calls are not observed".
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.3",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.24",
    "hypothesis>=6.112",
    "mypy>=1.13",
    "ruff>=0.7",
    "import-linter>=2.1",
    "pre-commit>=4.0",
    # Decides this project's version and writes its changelog at a release
    # (.github/workflows/release.yml), and checks every commit message
    # (.pre-commit-config.yaml). Pinned exactly, and pinned HERE only: the
    # version that numbers each release must be one version, in one file
    # Dependabot updates. Every caller runs it through `uv run --locked cz`.
    "commitizen==4.19.0",
    # Alembic is NOT a migration tool in this project — golang-migrate owns the
    # schema (spec D12), and there is deliberately no alembic/ directory and no
    # alembic_version table. It is installed for exactly one job: its
    # compare_metadata() function is the comparison engine behind the
    # model/schema drift gate in tests/integration/test_schema_drift.py. Deleting
    # this dependency silently removes that gate. See Task 9 of the M1 plan.
    "alembic>=1.19",
    "testcontainers[postgres,redis,minio]>=4.15",
    # Imported at module scope by testcontainers.community.minio (its first
    # line is `from minio import Minio`), so collection fails without it.
    # The production adapter uses aioboto3 and never imports this — it is
    # purely a test-container dependency.
    "minio>=7.2",
    # Reads ops/prometheus/rules/*.yml in the SLO gate (tests/unit/
    # test_slo_rules.py), so the PromQL and the Python constants cannot
    # drift. Available transitively through pre-commit today; depended on
    # explicitly because a gate must not rest on someone else's transitive
    # dependency.
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0",
    "schemathesis>=4.26",
    "pytest-recording>=0.13",
    "mutmut>=3.7",
]

# The documentation site (docs/, mkdocs.yml). Its own group so `uv sync`
# for the service does not install a static-site generator.
docs = [
    # Capped below 2.0: MkDocs 2.0 removes the plugin system entirely, with
    # no migration path, which would break mkdocs-material and the docs
    # build outright.
    "mkdocs>=1.6,<2",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/reference_service"]

[tool.uv]
# Never resolve to a pre-release unless a requirement names one. uv's
# default mode (`if-necessary`, since uv 0.12.3) tries stable versions
# first and then falls back to a pre-release when no stable version fits

# package in its hint.

# (see the `0.65b0` floors above). Under `explicit` a pre-release is only
# allowed where a first-party requirement carries the marker; the direct
# dependencies above carry their own, and these constraints carry it for
# the four packages that arrive only transitively. A constraint changes
# nothing for a package that is not in the graph, so this list is the
# same for every answer set. A new instrumentation package that drags in
# another beta-only transitive dependency fails `uv lock` with that
# package's name in the hint: add it here.
constraint-dependencies = [
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation>=0.65b0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-asgi>=0.65b0",
    "opentelemetry-semantic-conventions>=0.65b0",
    "opentelemetry-util-http>=0.65b0",

[tool.commitizen]
# The release workflow runs `cz bump` with this table: it reads the
# Conventional Commits since the last tag, decides the bump, writes
# CHANGELOG.md and tags. `just changelog` and `just next-version` preview
# both without changing anything.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"
# Writes BOTH [project].version above and the matching [[package]] entry in
# uv.lock. `pep621` writes only the first, which leaves the lock file stale
# and fails the uv-lock hook -- inside the release workflow, after the tag
# has already been pushed.
version_provider = "uv"
tag_format = "v$version"
update_changelog_on_bump = true
changelog_file = "CHANGELOG.md"
# Pre-1.0: a breaking change bumps the MINOR number (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0)
# rather than jumping to 1.0.0. Semver puts no compatibility promise on
# the major number below 1.0.0, and 1.0.0 should be a deliberate decision
# about stability, not a side effect of the first `feat!:`.
major_version_zero = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "-q --strict-markers --strict-config -m 'not integration and not contract'"
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
markers = [
    # Anything needing a container. Excluded from the default run by the `-m`
    # in addopts above, so `just test` stays a few seconds and needs no Docker.
    # `just test-integration` selects them back in with `-m integration`.
    "integration: requires a running Docker daemon",
    # Schemathesis over ASGI. Deselected by default for the same reason
    # `integration` is — it is slow — and for one worse reason that is
    # specific to it: its ASGI transport leaves anyio memory object
    # streams unclosed, and `filterwarnings = ["error"]` below turns the
    # resulting ResourceWarning into a PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning.
    # That warning fires whenever the garbage collector reaches the
    # stream, so pytest blames whichever test happens to be running then.
    # Verified: with tests/contract/ in the default selection, the whole
    # suite failed on tests/api/test_errors.py — a test that passes on its
    # own and has nothing to do with contracts. `just test-contract` runs
    # this tier on its own, where the filter in tests/contract/conftest.py
    # contains the damage.
    "contract: schemathesis conformance against the committed contract",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",

    # control until Starlette itself moves. Narrow and specific on

    # one instead of surfacing it. Note the category: StarletteDeprecationWarning

# The whole package, then narrowed below. Pointing source_paths straight
# at domain/ and services/ instead would leave the package unimportable
# inside mutmut's copy, because api/ and main.py would be missing.
source_paths = ["src/reference_service"]

# Mutate business logic only. Mutating adapters produces a long tail of
# survivors about error paths nobody asserts on, and a signal nobody
# trusts is worse than no signal (spec 8.1).
only_mutate = [
    "src/reference_service/domain/*",
    "src/reference_service/services/*",
]

# mutmut runs the suite inside a `mutants/` COPY of the project, and that
# copy contains source_paths, tests/ and a fixed list of lock files —
# nothing else. Without `ops`, M2's tests/unit/test_dashboards.py fails
# with "mutants/ops/grafana/dashboards not found".

# it hashes.

#

# are slow: mutmut injects `from mutmut import ...` into every module it
# mutates, so M0's tests/unit/test_layer_purity.py — which asserts that
# domain/ imports nothing but pydantic and the standard library — FAILS
# inside the copy, reporting mutmut itself as a third-party import. The
# alternative, adding mutmut to that gate's allow-list, would weaken a
# real M0 gate in ordinary runs to satisfy a tool. A gate that checks the
# SHAPE of the tree can never kill a mutant in the first place, so
# excluding it costs nothing.

    "tests/unit/test_order.py",
    "tests/unit/test_order_service.py",
    "tests/unit/test_domain_errors.py",
    "tests/unit/test_memory_repository.py",
    "tests/api/test_orders.py",

    # (services/receipt.py), added alongside the two files above and left
    # out of this list by the same mistake this comment is now here to
    # prevent repeating — without them mutmut reports every mutant in
    # both files as "no tests", which is not a mutation SCORE, it is the
    # mutation gate never running against a financial document's renderer
    # at all. tests/api/test_receipts.py is the receipt-endpoint analogue
    # of tests/api/test_orders.py above.

    "tests/api/test_receipts.py",
]

# The floor, as a percentage of mutants killed. Measured 85.3% (64/75 killed)
# in M3 Task 14 (2026-09-09), after the payments code (domain/payments.py,
# PlaceOrder's authorise-then-save call) pushed the score up from the plan's
# original baseline of 87.9% (51/58 killed), which predated that code and
# was stale by then.
#
# Recomputed again in M4 (2026-09-10), as this comment's own instruction
# below requires whenever a milestone adds substantial domain or services
# code -- M4 added three such files (domain/receipt_render.py,
# services/receipt.py, plus the test-selection entries above). The rerun
# gave 87.3% (48/55 killed), which is what is now current.

readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [

    # what pydantic>=2.9 itself already requires at minimum -- not a new
    # constraint, just an honest import.
    "pydantic-core>=2.23.2",
    "structlog>=24.4",
    "orjson>=3.10",
{%- if cookiecutter.database == "postgres" %}
    # Capped below 2.1 on purpose. opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy
    # declares `sqlalchemy<2.1.0` (still true in 0.66b1). Against SQLAlchemy
    # 2.1 it logs a DependencyConflict and attaches nothing, so no query
    # ever produces a database span. Raise this cap in the same change that
    # raises the instrumentation's own cap.
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.52,<2.1",
    "asyncpg>=0.31",
{%- endif %}
    # Traces, metrics and logs. The API/SDK/exporter line and the
    # instrumentation line version SEPARATELY and always will: 1.44 for the
    # first, 0.65b0 for the second. The `b` is upstream's, not a typo — the
    # instrumentation packages are permanently beta-versioned.
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.44,<2",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.44,<2",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.65b0",
{%- if cookiecutter.database == "postgres" %}
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.65b0",
{%- endif %}
    # Garbage collection, memory and thread counts for the runtime dashboard.
    # Its defaults emit both the current metric names and their deprecated
    # `process.runtime.cpython.*` duplicates plus whole-host `system.*`
    # series; observability/metrics.py passes an explicit config instead.
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-system-metrics>=0.65b0",
    # Supplies the LoggingHandler that bridges the standard logging
    # module to OTLP. The one in opentelemetry-sdk is deprecated as of
    # 1.44.0 and warns on construction, which filterwarnings=["error"]
    # turns into a test failure; the SDK's own message names this
    # package as the replacement.
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging>=0.65b0",
    # The shared outbound client (spec 12, item 5). A runtime dependency
    # from M3 on, not a test helper: infrastructure/http/client.py is
    # production code.
    "httpx>=0.28",
    # Bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Chosen over
    # writing one: stamina is asyncio-native, typed, and wraps tenacity,
    # which has solved retry budgets and jitter properly for years. The
    # circuit breaker beside it IS hand-written, because no maintained
    # asyncio implementation exists — see the plan's Verified Fact 15.
    "stamina>=26.1",
    # Outbound spans for the payment call. Closes the first row of the M2
    # plan's "deliberately does not include" table.
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-httpx>=0.65b0",
{%- if cookiecutter.cache == "redis" %}
    # The cache client. redis-py's own asyncio interface (redis.asyncio) —
    # aioredis was merged into it years ago and is archived, so there is no
    # separate async package to choose. Used ONLY by
    # infrastructure/cache/, which is the one place allowed to import it.
    "redis>=8.1",
{%- endif %}
{%- if cookiecutter.object_storage == "s3" %}
    # The S3-compatible object store client. aioboto3 wraps aiobotocore,
    # which wraps botocore: one adapter serves MinIO, Amazon S3, Cloudflare
    # R2, Ceph and Backblaze B2, distinguished only by endpoint_url (spec
    # 9.1). boto3 itself is synchronous and would block the event loop on
    # every call.
    "aioboto3>=15.5",
{%- endif %}
{%- if cookiecutter.cache == "redis" %}
    # Spans for Redis commands. Same 0.65b0 line as every other
    # opentelemetry-instrumentation-* dependency above; the `b` is
    # upstream's permanent beta versioning, not a typo. Wired up in
    # observability/otel.py's instrument_redis, called unconditionally
    # from main.py's lifespan whenever telemetry is enabled.
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-redis>=0.65b0",
{%- endif %}
{%- if cookiecutter.object_storage == "s3" %}
    # NO opentelemetry-instrumentation-botocore dependency here, on
    # purpose — it was tried and removed, not merely never added. Task 12
    # measured, rather than assumed, whether that instrumentor sees
    # aioboto3's async S3 calls at all: it patches
    # `botocore.client.BaseClient._make_api_call`, but `aioboto3` runs on
    # `aiobotocore`, whose `AioBaseClient` shadows that exact method with
    # its own async override, so the instrumentor's patch is never on the
    # call path. Instrumenting, then running ListBuckets, CreateBucket,
    # PutObject and GetObject through a real `aioboto3.Session` against
    # MinIO produced zero spans, even though `is_instrumented_by_opentelemetry`
    # reported True and every call itself succeeded — see the Task 12
    # report for the full transcript. Re-adding this dependency without
    # re-verifying against a current aiobotocore release would silently
    # reintroduce a store adapter whose spans never appear, which is worse
    # than no instrumentation: a dashboard built against it would read as
    # "S3 calls are always fast" rather than "S3 calls are not observed".
{%- endif %}
]

    "tests/unit/test_memory_repository.py",
    "tests/api/test_orders.py",
    # M4: render_receipt (domain/receipt_render.py) and GetReceipt
    # (services/receipt.py), added alongside the two files above and left
    # out of this list by the same mistake this comment is now here to
    # prevent repeating — without them mutmut reports every mutant in
    # both files as "no tests", which is not a mutation SCORE, it is the
    # mutation gate never running against a financial document's renderer
    # at all. tests/api/test_receipts.py is the receipt-endpoint analogue
    # of tests/api/test_orders.py above.
    "tests/unit/test_receipt_render.py",
    "tests/unit/test_get_receipt.py",
    "tests/api/test_receipts.py",
]

# The floor, as a percentage of mutants killed. Measured 85.3% (64/75 killed)
# in M3 Task 14 (2026-09-09), after the payments code (domain/payments.py,
# PlaceOrder's authorise-then-save call) pushed the score up from the plan's
# original baseline of 87.9% (51/58 killed), which predated that code and
# was stale by then.
#
# Recomputed again in M4 (2026-09-10), as this comment's own instruction
# below requires whenever a milestone adds substantial domain or services
# code -- M4 added three such files (domain/receipt_render.py,
# services/receipt.py, plus the test-selection entries above). The rerun
# gave 87.3% (48/55 killed), which is what is now current.
#
# The floor stays at 80, deliberately below the current 87.3%, by roughly
# the cushion the current gap gives: about four survivors -- 48/55 killed
# can drop to 44/55 = 80% before the gate fails. That cushion exists so the
# next message-only survivor (raise ValueError("...") -> raise
# ValueError(None)) does not fail the build and pressure whoever hits it
# into asserting on prose. Raise this floor when the score improves for a
# real reason; never lower it to make a build pass. Recompute both the
# measured score and this floor whenever a milestone adds a substantial
# amount of domain or services code -- that is exactly what made the 87.9
# baseline stale enough to need the M3 update, and the 85.3 measurement
# stale enough to need this one.
mutation_threshold_percent = 80

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
files = ["src", "tests"]
warn_unused_configs = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
ignore_missing_imports = true

# Strict where the business logic lives. Lenient in infrastructure and api,
# where third-party type stubs are imperfect and strictness only produces
# `# type: ignore` comments rather than safety.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["{{ cookiecutter.package_name }}.domain.*", "{{ cookiecutter.package_name }}.services.*"]
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_any_generics = true
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_reexport = true
warn_return_any = true

# Backend tooling config. Ruff is the lint/format layer; the house rules Ruff
# cannot express - file, endpoint and test length, and the repository pattern -
# live in backend/tests/backend_linter.py. `make back-lint` runs all three, and
# the import contracts at the end of this file.
#
# Ruff finds this file by walking up from each file it checks, so it governs
# everything under backend/ no matter which directory the gate is invoked from.
# The rule set is prototipo-atem's, minus what does not fit here (see below).

[tool.ruff]
# Matches backend/Dockerfile (python:3.14-slim) and the CI interpreter, so
# pyupgrade never emits syntax the deployed interpreter lacks.
target-version = "py314"
line-length = 100
# venv/__pycache__ are not ours. alembic IS linted here - only the dead-code
# gate skips it, because alembic calls its modules by name convention.
extend-exclude = ["venv", ".venv", "__pycache__"]

# The package root is the repository, one level up: imports read
# `from backend.core...`, so ruff has to look for `backend/` from there or
# isort files every first-party import as third-party.
src = [".."]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# F   - pyflakes: dead imports, unused locals, undefined names.
# E/W - pycodestyle correctness (E501 line length is the formatter's job).
# B   - flake8-bugbear: real footguns (mutable defaults, except-pass, ...).
# I   - isort: one import order, so a diff never argues about it.
# UP  - pyupgrade: modern syntax only (`list[str]`, `str | None`).
#
# The families below each encode a rule this code keeps, or a bug it had -
# chosen by what they find, not by how many exist:
# ASYNC  - blocking calls inside `async def`: a free guard for an app that is
#          async end to end. It cannot see a blocking call
#          behind a library (google-auth's certificate fetch was one, fixed by
#          hand in core/security.py), so it is a floor, not a proof.
# DTZ    - naive datetimes. core/clock.py's rule, mechanised: every moment is
#          timezone-aware UTC.
# BLE    - blind `except Exception` that swallows. A handler names what it
#          expects; one that re-raises is not flagged.
# G, LOG - logging calls: arguments, not f-strings (the message is built only
#          when the record is emitted, and one template groups one event), and
#          no misuse of the logging module itself.
# TRY400 - `logger.error` inside `except` drops the traceback; `.exception`
#          keeps it. Only this one of the tryceratops rules: the rest are about
#          exception-message style.
# FAST   - FastAPI idioms: `Annotated[..., Depends(...)]` rather than a default
#          value, so a dependency reads the same in a route and in a test.
# ISC    - implicit string concatenation. In a list or tuple it is how a
#          missing comma merges two items silently (ISC004) - and prompts and
#          seed data are long lists of strings.
# RUF    - Ruff's own: implicit Optional, mutable class defaults, unsorted
#          `__all__`, `noqa` comments that no longer silence anything.
# PT     - pytest idioms: one fact per `assert` (a failure names which one),
#          `pytest.raises` narrowed by `match`.
# T20    - `print`: the app logs. Command-line tools are exempt below.
#
# Not selected, on purpose: SIM (style: its hits were nested `if`s and the
# word lists in services/language/common_words.py, which read better as the
# split strings they are); S (bandit: 750 hits, all `assert` in tests); ANN, D
# (annotation and docstring coverage are the type checker's and the reader's
# business); ARG (FastAPI dependencies are unused arguments by design).
select = [
  "F", "E", "W", "B", "I", "UP",
  "ASYNC", "DTZ", "BLE", "G", "LOG", "TRY400", "FAST", "ISC", "RUF", "PT", "T20",
]
# E501: line length is enforced by the formatter, not as a lint error.
# UP042: rewriting `class X(str, Enum)` as `StrEnum` is a behaviour change -
#        `str(member)` and f-strings go from "Kind.MEMBER" to "member", which
#        reaches responses and stored values. Off until someone migrates on
#        purpose.
ignore = ["E501", "UP042"]
# Ruff calls these fixes unsafe; here they are not, and marking them safe is
# what lets `make back-fix` apply them, so back-fix still fixes exactly what
# back-lint checks:
# FAST002 - it is unsafe because moving `= Depends(x)` into `Annotated` changes
#           the parameter's default. FastAPI resolves both forms identically,
#           and nothing here calls a route function directly.
# PT018 stays unsafe - and so is fixed by hand: its fix drops a trailing comment.
extend-safe-fixes = ["FAST002"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Command-line tools: printing is their output, and each reports whatever
# failed - a Gemini call, a file it cannot parse - instead of dying with it.
# The app has neither excuse.
"tools/**" = ["T20", "BLE001"]
"**/__main__.py" = ["T20"]
"tests/backend_linter.py" = ["T20", "BLE001"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# See `src` above: without this, `backend.*` is sorted as a third-party import.
known-first-party = ["backend"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
# FastAPI's dependency markers are meant to be called in argument defaults -
# that is the framework idiom, not the B008 footgun.
extend-immutable-calls = [
  "fastapi.Depends",
  "fastapi.Query",
  "fastapi.Path",
  "fastapi.Body",
  "fastapi.Header",
  "fastapi.Cookie",
  "fastapi.Form",
  "fastapi.File",
  "fastapi.Security",
]

[tool.ruff.format]
# LF, as the repository's .gitattributes checks every text file out: the
# formatter pins what git already guarantees.
line-ending = "lf"

# The layer boundaries, as import contracts `make back-lint` checks with
# import-linter. It builds the import graph of backend/ - every `import`, direct
# or through other modules - and fails when an edge a contract forbids exists.
# A contract is only as good as its reason, so each one carries it; and none
# carries an exemption list: when real code breaks a contract, the code moves.
#
# What is NOT here, on purpose: whether an endpoint may call a repository
# directly or must go through a service. That question is open with the user
# (#211); until it is answered, api/ -> repositories/ is neither allowed nor
# forbidden by a contract.
[tool.importlinter]
# google.genai is a root package so the SDK is a node of its own. Left external,
# the graph squashes it to `google`, which google-auth's sign-in shares.
root_packages = ["backend", "google.genai"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# core/ is the floor: settings, the clock, the database engine, security
# helpers. Everything builds on it; if it imported a layer above, that layer
# could not be imported without it, and the floor would have a ceiling.
name = "core/ imports no other layer"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["backend.core"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "backend.models",
  "backend.repositories",
  "backend.schemas",
  "backend.services",
  "backend.api",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# The database layer answers queries; what to do with the answer is a service's
# or an endpoint's business. A repository reaching up is a rule hidden in a
# query, where nobody looking for the rule will find it.
name = "models/ and repositories/ never import services/ or api/"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["backend.models", "backend.repositories"]
forbidden_modules = ["backend.services", "backend.api"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# "Gemini writes content; arithmetic decides what appears" (CLAUDE.md).
# Selection, the Rasch rating, pacing, the generation decision, where the right
# option sits, and who the nightly run serves are arithmetic: none of them may
# reach a Gemini call, not even through another module (import-linter follows
# indirect imports too).
name = "the arithmetic never reaches Gemini"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "backend.services.lessons",
  "backend.services.jobs.nightly_decision",
]
forbidden_modules = ["backend.services.gemini"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# The Gemini layer returns content - typed results a caller turns into rows.
# Building ORM rows there made the prompt code decide what the database holds.
name = "the Gemini layer writes content, never rows"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["backend.services.gemini"]
forbidden_modules = ["backend.models", "backend.repositories"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# One typed door to the SDK: services/gemini/client/ holds the client,
# the retry, the guard and the call, and every use case goes through it. The
# tests are the other importer: they fake the SDK's client and errors.
name = "only services/gemini/client/ imports google.genai"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["google.genai"]
allowed_importers = ["backend.services.gemini.client", "backend.tests"]

# pytest. It lives beside ruff, and is found the same way: `make
# back-test` names backend/tests, and pytest looks for its config from there
# upward, so this file is the config and backend/ the rootdir.
#
# Everything here fails rather than warns. As a warning, a misspelt marker
# (`@pytest.mark.lvie`) runs its test in the default suite, and an un-awaited
# coroutine passes.
[tool.pytest]
minversion = "9.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Every `async def test_` is an asyncio test; no decorator needed.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# strict_markers, strict_config, strict_xfail and strict_parametrization_ids.
strict = true
# The worktree is mounted into a container that runs as the invoking user: a
# cache directory there is litter nobody reads.
addopts = ["-p", "no:cacheprovider"]
markers = [
  "live: calls the real Gemini/YouTube APIs and spends quota; lives in tests/live/ and nowhere else, and runs only with --live (#176). `live(calls=N)`: the billed calls it may make, 1 unless it says",
  "db: reaches the run's Postgres. Applied by tests/conftest.py to every test that uses the test_db fixture, never by hand; `-m 'not db'` runs the rest with no database",
]
# Every warning is an error, except two a dependency raises on import, which we
# cannot fix and which say nothing about our code. Each is pinned to the module
# that raises it, so the same deprecation in our code still fails.
filterwarnings = [
  "error",
  "ignore:'_UnionGenericAlias' is deprecated:DeprecationWarning:google.genai.types",
  "ignore:'asyncio.iscoroutinefunction' is deprecated:DeprecationWarning:slowapi.extension",
]

# Coverage, measured by every full `make back-test` and floored: the run
# fails when the app's coverage drops under `fail_under`. The floor is the
# measured total when it was set, less a point of slack, so it catches a
# feature landing untested, not a refactor moving lines around. Raise it when
# the total rises; never lower it to make a red run green. A selected run
# (`make back-test K=...`) covers a slice and is not measured.
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["backend"]
omit = ["backend/tests/*"]
branch = true
# Outside the mounted worktree: the container discards it, CI does not care.
data_file = "/tmp/goalgetter-backend.coverage"

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 90
skip_covered = true
show_missing = true

# The type gate: `make back-types`. mypy rather than pyright, for three
# reasons. It rejects an explicit `Any` (`disallow_any_explicit`), which is the
# rule this gate exists for and which pyright has no setting for. It is a pip
# package that runs in the backend image with no network, where pyright is a
# Node program its pip wrapper downloads on first run. And it has the Pydantic
# plugin, so a model's constructor is checked field by field.
#
# `strict` on everything under backend/: every function annotated, generics
# spelled out - a bare `dict` or `list` fails (`disallow_any_generics`), and an
# explicit `Any` fails - and `dict[str, Any]` with it. What remains is judgement:
# data crossing a layer is a Pydantic model, a dataclass or a TypedDict, not a dict.
# Strict is affordable because the whole backend passes it, with the narrow
# exceptions below.
#
# The cache lives in .mypy_cache at the repository root (gitignored): cold, the
# whole backend with its libraries takes ~40 s; warm, a couple of seconds.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true
disallow_any_explicit = true
warn_unreachable = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
# backend/ has namespace packages (no __init__.py in several folders), and its
# imports read `backend.x`: modules are named from the repository root.
explicit_package_bases = true
mypy_path = "$MYPY_CONFIG_FILE_DIR/.."
# google-auth ships no annotations: calling it is allowed, and what it answers
# is turned into a typed value on the spot (core/security.py).
untyped_calls_exclude = ["google.oauth2"]

# Two libraries with no annotations and no stubs, each imported by one command-line
# tool (disposable_database.py, deadcode.py): what they answer is untyped there.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["psycopg2", "vulture", "vulture.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# `make gemini`'s menu is a table of use cases whose functions all take
# different arguments, so an entry's arguments are `Any` to the table; the
# test beside it checks each entry's arguments against its function's own
# signature (tests/test_tools/test_gemini_cli.py). Only that rule is off.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["backend.tools.gemini_cli"]
disallow_any_explicit = false

# Tests are held to a looser standard. Their bodies are still checked - an
# argument of the wrong type, or too many of them, fails - but a test need not
# annotate its own functions, fixtures or the lists that record calls; it may
# replace a method to patch it; and it reads an Optional it just wrote without
# narrowing it first, because a None there is a failure the assert reports anyway.
# And it may assert what the types already say, since a test exists to check it.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["backend.tests.*"]
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
disallow_untyped_calls = false
disallow_untyped_decorators = false
disallow_any_explicit = false
disallow_any_generics = false
warn_return_any = false
warn_unreachable = false
disable_error_code = ["var-annotated", "union-attr", "method-assign", "index"]

[tool.pydantic-mypy]
# A model built with a field it does not have, or a value of the wrong type,
# fails here and not at runtime.
init_forbid_extra = true
init_typed = true
warn_required_dynamic_aliases = true

# Ruff: All-in-one linter with comprehensive rule sets
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 88

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "I",   # isort-compatible import sorting (via ruff)
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "S",   # bandit security
    "T20", # flake8-print
    "ARG", # flake8-unused-arguments
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
]
ignore = [
    "E501", # line too long, handled by ruff format
    "B008", # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "S101", # assert_used (for tests)
    "S106", # hardcoded_password_funcarg
    "T201", # print statements (for init.py and scripts)
    "S603", # subprocess.run without check=True
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*" = ["S101", "S311", "E501", "ARG002", "S105", "S602", "S603"]
"examples/**/*" = ["T201", "E501"]
"src/ezqt_app/cli/**/*" = ["T201", "E501", "S603"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# ✅ TYPE CHECKING TOOLS
# Static type analysis with minimal and comprehensive modes
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Ty: Type checking with minimal configuration
[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.11"
root = ["src", "src/ezqt_app"]

[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src/ezqt_app/**/*.py"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
]
respect-ignore-files = true

[tool.ty.terminal]
output-format = "full"
error-on-warning = false

[tool.ty.rules]
# Ignore PySide6 stub issues (isValid, setIcon, setText overloads)
no-matching-overload = "ignore"

# Pyright: Comprehensive type checking with detailed reporting
[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.11"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
include = ["src/ezqt_app"]
extraPaths = ["src"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "**/node_modules",
    "**/.*",
]
reportMissingImports = true
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportUnusedImport = true
reportUnusedClass = true
reportUnusedFunction = true
reportUnusedVariable = true
reportDuplicateImport = true
reportOptionalSubscript = true
reportOptionalMemberAccess = true
reportOptionalCall = true
reportOptionalIterable = true
reportOptionalContextManager = true
reportOptionalOperand = true
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = false
reportUntypedClassDecorator = false
reportUntypedBaseClass = false
reportUntypedNamedTuple = false
reportPrivateUsage = false
reportConstantRedefinition = true
# Disabled: Qt widgets intentionally override methods with properties
reportIncompatibleMethodOverride = false
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = true
reportInconsistentConstructor = true

# 🧭 IMPORT LINTER CONTRACTS

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["ezqt_app"]
# Note: import-linter 2.x ne supporte pas source_paths (feature pending PR #323).

name = "layer dependency flow"
type = "layers"
