]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🧪 TESTING & COVERAGE TOOLS
# Test execution, coverage analysis, and test configuration
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Pytest: Test runner with markers and coverage configuration
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "7.0"
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--cov=src/ezqt_app",
    "--cov-report=term-missing",
    "--cov-report=html",
    "--cov-report=xml",
    "--cov-fail-under=70",
    "--tb=short",
    "--color=yes",
    "--durations=10",
    "--maxfail=5",
]
console_output_style = "progress"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "robustness: marks tests as robustness tests",
    "unit: marks tests as unit tests (default)",
    "qt: marks tests requiring Qt runtime",
    "wizard: marks tests related to RichWizard",
    "config: marks tests related to ConfigurationManager",
    "cli: marks tests related to CLI",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/ezqt_app"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/site-packages/*",
    "*/.pytest_cache/*",
    "*/.benchmarks/*",
    "*/.vscode/*",
    "*/.egg-info/*",
    "*/.hooks/*",
    "setup.py",
    "build/*",
    "dist/*",
    ".venv/*",
    "venv/*",
    "htmlcov/*",
    "coverage.xml",
    ".coverage",
    "docs/*",
    "examples/*",
    "_temp/*",
    # CLI entry points: tested via e2e/smoke tests, not unit tests
    "src/ezqt_app/cli/*",
    # Fichier auto-généré par Qt Resource Compiler (données binaires, pas de logique utilisateur)
    "*/shared/resources/base_resources.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
# Lines to exclude: comments, abstractions, unreachable code
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "if self.debug:",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if 0:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
    "if platform.system\\(\\) == \"Windows\":",
    "except ImportError:",
]
show_missing = true
precision = 2
fail_under = 70

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🔒 SECURITY TOOLS
# Code security scanning and vulnerability detection
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Bandit: Security linter for identifying common security issues
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = [
    "tests",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "venv",
    ".venv",
    ".hooks",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    ".tmp",

]
skips = ["B101", "B601"]

[importlinter]
root_package = src

[contract:no-tests-in-src]
name = Application code must not import the test suite.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src
forbidden_modules =
    tests

# PRD-211 — In-repo topology discipline (Phase 2 Wave 4).
#
# Thesis T2 measured Automatos as a healthy modular monolith: only ~3.0% of
# imports are true feature-to-feature coupling; ~80.5% is the shared kernel.
# The verdict — "stay a monolith, harden the boundaries in-repo" — is only a
# claim until it is enforced. This `independence` contract makes the NEXT new
# lateral edge between feature modules fail loud in CI, at zero runtime cost.
#
# Rule in words: no feature module (orchestrator/modules/*) may import another
# feature module EXCEPT through the permitted routing layer (modules.tools or
# the api package). modules.tools is excluded by the routing wildcard below;
# `api` lives outside the `modules` root package and is therefore never a node
# in this graph (routing through it is inherently invisible to the contract).
#
# This is a RATCHET, not a refactor: every lateral edge that exists on the
# branch tip today is carried as an explicit `ignore_imports` so the contract
# is GREEN now. It forbids the next edge, it does not demand today's edges be
# removed (that is a held CLAUDE.md §12 option, not this PRD).
#
# To re-trace the baseline after intentional coupling changes, rebuild it from
# grimp: build_graph("modules") -> direct edges where both endpoints are
# distinct feature modules. Do not hand-edit blindly.

[importlinter]
root_package = modules
include_external_packages = False

[importlinter:contract:feature-module-independence]
name = Feature modules must not import each other (route via modules.tools or api)
type = independence
modules =
    modules.agents
    modules.attachments
    modules.codegraph
    modules.context
    modules.coordination
    modules.documents
    modules.intake
    modules.knowledge
    modules.memory
    modules.nl2sql
    modules.policy
    modules.rag
    modules.search
    modules.socials
    modules.voice
    modules.widgets
    modules.workflows
ignore_imports =
    modules.tools.** -> modules.**
    modules.agents.factory.agent_factory -> modules.attachments.resolver
    modules.agents.factory.agent_factory -> modules.context
    modules.agents.factory.agent_factory -> modules.memory.memory_tool
    modules.agents.services.agent_platform_tools -> modules.codegraph

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Visualization",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Typing :: Typed"
]
# 3.12 floor: this is what `zarr>=3.2` below requires — zarr 3 needs Python
# >=3.11 in every release and >=3.12 from 3.2 on. The two move together, so
# lowering this floor means lowering the zarr pin with it. No ceiling: 3.13 and
# 3.14 are supported too (see the classifiers above and the CI matrix).
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "numpy>=2.0",
    # zarr-python 3. Luxar WRITES zarr format 3 on disk by default and reads
    # both formats (see `luxar._zarr_compat`); 2.18 could not read a v3 store at
    # all, and the 3.x pin also lifts the transitive caps the old `zarr<3.0`
    # forced on anndata and napari.
    "zarr>=3.2,<4",
    # A DIRECT dependency, not just zarr's transitive one, because the floor is
    # load-bearing for the compressor policy. zarr's format-3 `BloscCodec` hands
    # numcodecs the SERIALIZED BYTE buffer, so the element width is lost unless
    # it can forward `typesize` — which it only does for numcodecs >= 0.16
    # (numcodecs #713). Below that floor the byte shuffle
    # `luxar.encoding.compression` measured for multi-byte integer codes becomes
    # a silent no-op: the metadata still records `typesize: 2, shuffle: shuffle`
    # while the chunk is compressed as if typesize were 1. Measured on a
    # 200k-point scene, that cost 12.5% of the chunk bytes — more than the delta
    # filter was introduced to win. Nothing raises, and only format 3 is
    # affected (a format-2 array is handed the typed array itself), which is why
    # `test_zarr_compat.py::test_format_3_blosc_actually_applies_the_byte_shuffle`
    # asserts on the stored BYTES rather than on the recorded configuration.
    "numcodecs>=0.16",

    "typer>=0.19,<1.0",
    # A DIRECT dependency, not just typer's transitive one: the `luxar demo`
    # catalogue renders through `rich.console`/`rich.text` (see
    # `luxar.cli.demo_render`), so a future typer that drops or vendors rich
    # must not silently break the demo listing.
    #
    # Today typer pins `rich>=13.8`, so THAT is the floor a resolver actually
    # picks; 13.0 is the independent minimum this package needs on its own, and
    # is the version the whole `demo_render` API surface was verified against
    # (Console(soft_wrap=), Text.rstrip/pad_right/cell_len, Console.capture).
    # It only becomes load-bearing if typer's own requirement goes away.
    "rich>=13.0",
    "fastapi>=0.111,<1.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.27,<1.0",
    # Both halves of the remote-control channel need this: the hub in
    # `luxar serve --control` is served through uvicorn's WebSocket support, and
    # `luxar.control.Viewer` drives a viewer with `websockets.sync.client`.
    # `uvicorn[standard]` happens to pull it in today, but depending on a
    # transitive for an import we make ourselves is how a working install turns
    # into an ImportError the moment that extra is repackaged. The sync client
    # arrived in websockets 13.
    "websockets>=13,<18",
    "arbol>=2025.2.27.2",
    "ansicolors>=1.1.8",
    # >=2.32.4 for GHSA-9hjg-9r4m-mvj7: below it, a redirect could leak the
    # .netrc credentials for the ORIGINAL host to the redirect target.
    "requests>=2.32.4",
    "aiohttp>=3.9.0",
    "fsspec>=2023.1.0",
    "xxhash>=3.0.0",
    "hilbertcurve>=2.0.5",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.1"

Changelog = "https://github.com/royerlab/luxar/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Upper bounds are intentional. IMPORTANT: the optional prebuilt CUDA extension
# (cuda_splatting_backend*.so, `make build-cuda`) is compiled against a specific
# torch ABI — after any torch upgrade you MUST rebuild it, or it fails to import
# (fitting then falls back to the NVRTC runtime-compiled kernels, which have no
# ABI coupling). The `<3.0` torch cap guards against a silent major-version jump
# that would break the prebuilt .so.
gsplats = [
    "scipy>=1.9.0,<2.0",
    "torch>=2.2.0,<3.0",
    # The native CPU splatting kernels (luxar.gsplats.models.gsplats.cpu),
    # JIT-compiled at runtime from these wheels: CPU-only installs need no C++
    # toolchain. Optional at runtime -- without it CPU fits use the PyTorch
    # renderer. >=0.60 for `numba.parallel_chunksize` and Python 3.12+ wheels.
    "numba>=0.60"
]
# `test` extends `gsplats`; `dev` extends `test`. This keeps scipy/torch (and
# their bounds) defined in exactly one place — no hand-copied drift.
test = [
    "luxar[gsplats]",
    "pytest>=7.4.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
    # SPIKE: parallel test execution, to measure whether obsidian's 16 cores
    # can beat GitHub's per-leg VMs on the python matrix.
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5.0",
    # Exercise the custom root-level hatch_build.py hook directly in tests.
    "hatchling>=1.27",
    "hypothesis>=6.0",
    # The ORACLE for the hand-rolled QR encoder in `luxar.cli._qr`, which the
    # exported scene folder needs because that folder has nothing installed.
    # A decoder, deliberately, not another encoder: comparing two encoders
    # only proves they agree, and the first version of ours produced symbols
    # that were the right size with the right patterns and would not scan.
    # Test-only -- nothing at runtime imports it.
    "zxing-cpp>=2.2",
    # `fastapi.testclient` (test_cli_integration.py) is a re-export of
    # starlette's TestClient, which refuses to import without httpx. It reached
    # the DEFAULT env transitively via a `dev` dependency, so the omission was
    # invisible there — but the `test` matrix envs got no httpx at all and died
    # during collection ("Interrupted: 1 error during collection", which pytest
    # then reports with a ZERO exit status). Declared here, next to the pytest
    # deps it belongs with, rather than left to a transitive.
    "httpx>=0.27"
]
dev = [
    "luxar[test]",
    # Pinned to a minor series because ruff is now a GATE, not just a helper:
    # `hatch run lint` runs `ruff format --check`, so a formatter change in a new
    # ruff turns CI red on an unrelated PR, at a moment nobody is thinking about
    # ruff. `>=0.1.0` also let every machine resolve a different formatter.
    # Keep in lockstep with `.pre-commit-config.yaml`'s ruff-pre-commit `rev`,
    # or the hook and the gate disagree about the same file.
    "ruff>=0.16,<0.17",
    # Pinned because mypy's bundled typeshed defines what all three typing gates
    # accept; a new minor can otherwise turn an unrelated change red. The floor
    # must include Python 3.14's stdlib types.
    "mypy>=2.4,<2.5",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0.12",
    "pre-commit>=3.3.0",
    "bandit[toml]>=1.7.5",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    # grimp is import-linter's Rust-backed graph engine, pinned here so its
    # upgrades are reviewed explicitly. Version 3.16 initially omitted the
    # macOS arm64 wheel for standard CPython 3.14, forcing a source build that
    # needs rustc >= 1.94, but upstream backfilled the 3.16 and 3.17 wheels on
    # 2026-09-11. The ceiling remains the review guard rather than a wheel fix.
    "grimp<3.18",
]
io = [
    "tifffile>=2023.1.0",
    # tifffile decodes deflate TIFFs itself, but LZW/JPEG/zstd TIFFs and
    # OME-TIFFs can need imagecodecs. Without it, tifffile raises a codec
    # error or tries an unavailable zstd fallback on Python < 3.14.
    "imagecodecs>=2023.1.0",
    "imageio>=2.31.0",
]
demos = [
    "pandas>=1.5.0",
    "pyarrow>=13.0.0",
    "networkx>=3.0",
    "umap-learn>=0.5.0",
    "scikit-image>=0.19.0",
    "scipy>=1.15.0,<2.0",
    "tifffile>=2023.1.0",
    "imagecodecs>=2023.1.0",
    "moderngl>=5.8",
    "sentence-transformers>=2.2.0",
    "Pillow>=9.0.0",
    # The `<0.13` ceiling is GONE: it existed only because anndata 0.13 requires
    # zarr>=3.1, which was unsatisfiable under the old `zarr>=2.16,<3.0` pin.
    # Luxar is on zarr 3 now, so 0.13+ resolves cleanly. Mirrored by
    # INSTALL_SPECS in luxar.demos._dependencies.
    "anndata>=0.10.0",
    "cellxgene-census>=1.0.0",
    "esm>=3.0.0",
    "h5py>=3.0.0",
    "astropy>=6.0.0",
    "astroquery>=0.4.7",
    "mrcfile>=1.4.0",
    "nibabel>=5.0.0",
    "pyshp>=2.3.0",
    # scikit-image ships only a handful of sample images in its wheel; cells3d
    # and kidney are FETCHED, and skimage's fetcher is pooch. Without this pin
    # the cells3d/kidney demos fail on a cold cache even though `luxar[demos]`
    # installed scikit-image — pooch was reaching them only as an accidental
    # transitive of some other package's extra.
    "pooch>=1.6.0",
    # KMeans fallback in demo_protein_embeddings_cafa5. Arrives transitively via
    # umap-learn today; pinned because a demo imports it directly.
    "scikit-learn>=1.0",
    # `--show-roundtrip` diagnostic plots in the gsplat demos.
    "matplotlib>=3.5.0",
    # Pure-Python NEXRAD Level II decoder (metpy.io.Level2File) for
    # demo_gsplats_4d_nexrad_supercell. The >=1.6.3 floor is LOAD-BEARING:
    # metpy declares only `numpy>=1.20.0`, so a resolver would happily pair
    # metpy 1.5.x with Luxar's core `numpy>=2.0` and break at runtime;
    # 1.6.3 is the release that added NumPy 2.0 support. It does not drag zarr
    # in either: metpy pulls xarray, but only xarray's CORE requirements
    # (numpy/packaging/pandas) — zarr lives in the `xarray[io]` extra, which
    # nothing here requests. A clean install resolves to metpy 1.7.1 + numpy
    # 2.5.1 + xarray with no extra zarr constraint at all.
    # Mirrored by INSTALL_SPECS in luxar.demos._dependencies.
    "metpy>=1.6.3,<2.0",
]
docs = [
    "sphinx>=7.0.0",
    "sphinx-rtd-theme>=1.3.0",
    "myst-parser>=2.0.0"
]
# Bridge fitted Gaussian splats into the Royer-lab tracking ecosystem
# (luxar.gsplats.interop.tracksdata). tracksdata is a clean PyPI dependency —
# the >=...rc lower bound lets pip resolve the current pre-release. napari is for
# the optional demo viewer. Keep this publish-safe: no git/direct references.
tracksdata = [
    "tracksdata>=0.1.0rc5",
    # The `<0.8` ceiling is GONE. napari 0.8's optional-base extra requires
    # zarr>=3.0.8, which the old `zarr<3.0` pin could not satisfy; the resolver
    # then backtracked napari into 2018-era sdist-only releases whose setup.py
    # imports the long-removed setuptools.Feature, and every CI env-create failed
    # (2026-07-14). On zarr 3 that conflict is gone, so the floor moves up to the
    # release that wanted zarr 3 in the first place.
    "napari[pyqt6]>=0.8",
]

# CLI entry point
[project.scripts]
luxar = "luxar.cli:app"

# numcodecs discovers codecs by entry point (group "numcodecs.codecs", name ==
# codec_id): with luxar merely INSTALLED, vanilla `zarr.open(...)` resolves the
# luxar_delta_v1 filter without any `import luxar` — third-party Python readers
# of delta-filtered stores just work. (Importing luxar.encoding still registers
# it eagerly; this is the no-import fallback numcodecs loads lazily.)
[project.entry-points."numcodecs.codecs"]
luxar_delta_v1 = "luxar.encoding._encoders.delta_codec:LuxarDelta"

# The format-3 twin of the entry point above, for the same reason: a vanilla
# `zarr.open(...)` on a format-3 delta store resolves the codec without any
# `import luxar`. zarr 3 has its OWN registry and its own entry-point group
# ("zarr.codecs"), so being registered with numcodecs buys nothing here —
# and `numcodecs.zarr3`, the wrapper that would have bridged them, is
# deprecated. Same codec NAME under both groups: one wire format, one
# TypeScript twin, two plumbings.
[project.entry-points."zarr.codecs"]
luxar_delta_v1 = "luxar.encoding._encoders.delta_codec:LuxarDeltaV3"

# ---------------------------------------------
# Hatch Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------

# Version management
[tool.hatch.version]
path = "packages/luxar/src/luxar/__init__.py"

# Build configuration
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["packages/luxar/src/luxar"]
# The viewer dist is bundled into standard wheels via force-include below.
# Run `make build-viewer` before `hatch build` to populate it. The custom hook
# keeps this strict for release wheels but overrides the force-include for
# editable builds, where cli/utils.py resolves the viewer from the source tree.
#
# Native launcher binaries (cli/_launchers/*) and icon assets
# (cli/_launcher_assets/*) are inside the package and ride along
# automatically when present at build time. Run `make build-launchers`
# before `hatch build` to populate the binaries.
exclude = [
    # Drop dotfiles that ride along with package directories — they
    # are only meaningful in the source tree.
    "**/.gitignore",
    "**/.gitkeep",
    # Demo data (~450 MB of Git-LFS catalogs/zarrs/parquets) must NOT ship in
    # the wheel: it blows past PyPI's 100 MB per-file limit, and in CI (no
    # `git lfs pull`) it would otherwise ship as broken ~130-byte pointer files.
    # Demo *scripts* stay; the data is fetched/regenerated separately.
    "**/demos/data/**",
    # Multiscale-decomposition research demos are source-tree-only (kept for
    # development; not part of the installed package surface).
    "**/gsplats/multiscale/demos/**",
    # gsplats/demos and gsplats/seeds/demos are the same category: standalone
    # research/dev scripts (not in the public `luxar demo` registry, and they
    # execute a fit at import time), so they stay source-tree-only too.
    "**/gsplats/demos/**",
    "**/gsplats/seeds/demos/**",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.hooks.custom]
path = "hatch_build.py"

# The README-as-long-description hook (see `dynamic` under [project]).
[tool.hatch.metadata.hooks.custom]
path = "hatch_build.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"packages/luxar-viewer/dist" = "luxar/_viewer_dist"

# NOTE: the wheel is the ONLY published distribution artifact, and the sdist
# below is deliberately not uploaded (publish.yml builds with `-t wheel` and
# asserts no tarball is staged).
#
# This note used to say a source-only install produced a "degraded package"
# missing the viewer. That is wrong, and optimistically so: the wheel build
# hook RAISES when packages/luxar-viewer/dist/index.html is absent
# (hatch_build.py), and the sdist does not carry that directory, so building a
# wheel from the sdist fails outright. Measured — `python -m build --wheel` on
# the unpacked sdist dies with FileNotFoundError. So `pip install --no-binary`
# does not yield a reduced package, it fails, and publishing the sdist would
# only offer users an artifact that cannot be installed.
#
# The target is kept configured rather than deleted on purpose: hatchling
# builds an sdist by DEFAULT, so removing this section would produce a larger
# one, not none. Source provenance lives in the Git tag and the archived
# record, not on PyPI.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
packages = ["packages/luxar/src/luxar"]
include = [
    "/packages/luxar/src/luxar",
    "/hatch_build.py",
    "/README.md",
    "/ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md",
    "/CITATION.cff",
    "/LICENSE",
    "/CHANGELOG.md"
]
exclude = [
    "*.pyc",
    "__pycache__",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".mypy_cache",
    "htmlcov",
    # See wheel-target note: demo data is too large for PyPI and is LFS-tracked.
    "**/demos/data/**",
]

# Development environments
[tool.hatch.envs.default]
# Inherit the dev toolchain + gsplats (scipy/torch with their version caps) from
# the project's optional-dependency groups so versions live in ONE place.
# `dev` → `test` → `gsplats`, so this pulls pytest/cov/ruff/mypy/pre-commit/
# bandit + scipy/torch transitively.
features = ["dev"]
# `installer = "uv"` was evaluated (it would cut the cold first create from
# ~20 min of pip resolution) and NOT adopted: uv-built envs ship no `pip`, and
# the Makefile (`install-dev`, `setup-cuda`'s CUDA-torch swap, `build-cuda`'s
# ninja), the CUDA build hints and `luxar demo deps --install` all run
# `pip install` inside this env. Adopt it only together with moving those to
# `uv pip` (or adding `pip` to this env's dependencies).
dependencies = [
    # Apple Silicon optimization (not a project optional-dependency)
    "mlx>=0.29.0; sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'",
    # Demo / figure deps used by examples (a subset of the `demos` group)
    "scikit-image>=0.19.0",
    "tifffile>=2023.1.0",
    "imagecodecs>=2023.1.0",
    # Keep demo-only GL deps out: every CI Python leg builds this env, and
    # moderngl/glcontext ship no CPython 3.14 wheels. Run the GL tests with
    # `hatch run demos:pytest packages/luxar/src/luxar/demos/tests/test_clay_renderer.py`.

    # Ceiling lifted with the zarr 3 migration; see the tracksdata group note.
    "napari[all]>=0.8",
    "pandas>=1.5.0",
    "pyarrow>=13.0.0",
    "networkx>=3.0",
    "umap-learn>=0.5.0",
    "sentence-transformers>=2.2.0",
    "Pillow>=9.0.0",
    # Manuscript figure generation
    "matplotlib>=3.5.0",
    "drawsvg>=2.0.0",
]

# Pin BLAS/OpenMP to one thread, mirroring `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
#
# torch and numpy default `num_threads` to the core count, so every one of the
# thousands of sub-millisecond tensor ops in the LOD/merge/decimate paths pays a
# 16-way fork-join barrier. The signature is `sys` time exceeding `user` time.
# Measured A/B/A on gsplats/lod/tests/test_decimate.py (31 tests, same 31 passed
# each arm), back to back, CPU = user+sys:
#     pinned 9.5 s  ->  unpinned 54.0 s  ->  pinned 10.7 s
# with `sys` alone going 0.8 s -> 38.1 s -> 0.7 s. At whole-suite scale the
# unpinned serial run spent 2334 s user against 3342 s sys.
#
# CI has set these since the self-hosted runner landed. Its original `-n 4`
# benchmark took the suite from 45.5/44.0/47.5 min to 15.8/16.6/16.9 for the
# SAME 6261 passed / 288 skipped and 86.44% coverage; CI now uses `-n 2` to fit
# the runner's 12 GiB memory cap. Neither thread pinning nor process parallelism
# buys the same result alone. The thread pin did not reach `hatch run test`, the
# documented pre-push gate, until now.
#
# Set here rather than in conftest.py so the pin also reaches the subprocesses
# some tests spawn (`luxar gsplat fit --tile`, the `-j 2` worker pools), and so
# an ad-hoc `hatch run pytest <file>` — the documented way to run one test file
# — is pinned too, not just the `test` script.
#
# The env-var scope is the WHOLE environment, though, so it also reaches
# `hatch run python demo_x.py`, `hatch run luxar gsplat fit --device cpu` and
# the benchmark scripts, where one thread is the wrong default and a
# single-threaded CPU baseline would flatter every GPU comparison. Hence
# `{env:NAME:1}`: an explicitly exported value WINS, so
#     OMP_NUM_THREADS=16 MKL_NUM_THREADS=16 hatch run luxar gsplat fit ... --device cpu
# runs at full width while an unqualified `hatch run` stays pinned. Both
# variables, not just OMP: this torch takes its intra-op count from MKL, so
# overriding OMP alone still gives `torch.get_num_threads() == 1`.
# `luxar gsplat fit`/`cal` on CPU widen torch to min(physical cores, 8) for the
# command whenever torch still has one thread, including when an OMP-only
# export did not raise it (LUXAR_CPU_THREADS=N overrides, 0 disables; the
# test conftest sets 0) — see
# luxar/gsplats/utils/cpu_threads.py.
[tool.hatch.envs.default.env-vars]
OMP_NUM_THREADS = "{env:OMP_NUM_THREADS:1}"
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS = "{env:OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS:1}"
MKL_NUM_THREADS = "{env:MKL_NUM_THREADS:1}"
NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS = "{env:NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS:1}"

# `test` runs the FULL suite (incl. `slow`) — the authoritative pre-push gate,
# run locally before every push. `test-cov` (coverage + the 89% gate) runs on every
# ci.yml push to dev and dispatch, plus the dedicated non-cancelling coverage.yml
# workflow; PR runs use `test-nocov` (same subset, no instrumentation) so a PR does
# not pay the coverage cost (see ci.yml/coverage.yml).
# Both deselect `slow` so the 1-core GitHub runner stays well under the job timeout;
# the heavy CPU-fitting tests (content-fit CLI, tiled/progressive fitting) still
# run locally and their code stays covered by fast unit tests (coverage holds
# above the 89% gate).
[tool.hatch.envs.default.scripts]
# `-n ... --dist loadfile` on the two LOCAL-ONLY scripts. Override the worker
# count with LUXAR_PYTEST_JOBS.
#
# `loadfile` is not optional. Plain `-n N` (`--dist load`) scatters individual
# tests across workers, which rebuilds every module- and class-scoped fixture
# ONCE PER WORKER — and `gsplats/tests/conftest.py` exists precisely to share
# two expensive fits, taking that directory "from ~14 min to ~1 min without
# removing any assertion". Scattering would hand that back and could make the
# suite slower. `loadfile` pins a whole file to one worker, which preserves
# those fixtures and sidesteps ordering concerns entirely.
#
# 6, not `auto`: several `slow` tests spawn their own subprocess pools (`-j 2`,
# `jobs_per_gpu=2`) sized at `os.cpu_count() // 2`, so `auto` would multiply
# 16 workers by up to 8 child jobs. Pairs with the thread pin in `env-vars`
# above — ci.yml's note is explicit that neither works without the other.
test = "pytest -n {env:LUXAR_PYTEST_JOBS:6} --dist loadfile --max-worker-restart=0 {args:packages/luxar/src/luxar packages/luxar/examples/tests stats scripts/gallery/tests scripts/tests}"
# NOT parallelised here: this is the script CI runs, and ci.yml already injects
# `-n 2 --dist loadfile` via PYTEST_ADDOPTS on the 16-core self-hosted box while
# deliberately keeping the 2-core hosted runners serial (four workers importing
# torch/napari/scipy OOM-killed the runner agent there). Hardcoding `-n` would
# override that per-machine choice from the wrong place. Set PYTEST_ADDOPTS
# yourself for a fast local coverage run.
test-cov = "mkdir -p coverage/python && pytest -m 'not slow' --cov=luxar --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html {args:packages/luxar/src/luxar packages/luxar/examples/tests stats scripts/gallery/tests scripts/tests}"
# `test-nocov` is the per-PR fast path: the SAME `-m 'not slow'` subset and paths
# as `test-cov`, but without `--cov` instrumentation (the dominant cost of the job).
# ci.yml runs it on `pull_request`; pushes to dev keep the 89% gate under the
# protected `python-tests (3.12)` context, and coverage.yml starts a per-commit
# advisory run that newer dev pushes cannot cancel.
test-nocov = "pytest -m 'not slow' {args:packages/luxar/src/luxar packages/luxar/examples/tests stats scripts/gallery/tests scripts/tests}"
test-cov-all = "mkdir -p coverage/python && pytest -n {env:LUXAR_PYTEST_JOBS:6} --dist loadfile --max-worker-restart=0 --cov=luxar --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html {args:packages/luxar/src/luxar packages/luxar/examples/tests stats scripts/gallery/tests scripts/tests}"
# `scripts/benchmarks` remains explicit as a safety net if the anchored
# `/benchmarks/` ignore rule ever regresses to matching nested directories.
format = [
    "ruff format packages/luxar/src scripts scripts/benchmarks stats hatch_build.py",
    "ruff check --fix packages/luxar/src scripts scripts/benchmarks stats hatch_build.py"
]
lint = [
    # Project-wide targets keep the gate implementations and supporting Python
    # tooling under E/W/F/I checks too; package-only CI left them unchecked.
    "ruff check packages/luxar/src scripts scripts/benchmarks stats hatch_build.py",
    # Formatting was enforced ONLY by an opt-in pre-commit hook, which sees just
    # the staged files — so 10 Python files had drifted unformatted in the tree
    # with nothing to notice (audit A12-04). Checked here so `hatch run lint`
    # and CI ask the identical question.
    "ruff format --check packages/luxar/src scripts scripts/benchmarks stats hatch_build.py",
    "check-complexity",
    "check-lint-ratchet",
    "type-check",
    "type-check-darwin",
    "type-check-py314"
]
type-check = "mypy packages/luxar/src/luxar/ scripts/ci_queue_scan.py scripts/check_cadence_liveness.py"
# Cross-platform fixes must work in both passes: use dynamic lookup as in
# `gsplats/utils/device.py` or file-scope `warn-unreachable=False` as in
# `gsplats/models/gsplats/metal/__init__.py`; a bare ignore fails on the host.
type-check-darwin = "mypy --platform darwin --cache-dir .mypy_cache/darwin packages/luxar/src/luxar/ scripts/ci_queue_scan.py scripts/check_cadence_liveness.py"
# The floor decides whether an ignore is necessary. A newer typeshed may make a
# floor-required ignore redundant, so the additive ceiling pass must not police it.
type-check-py314 = "mypy --python-version 3.14 --no-warn-unused-ignores --cache-dir .mypy_cache/py314 packages/luxar/src/luxar/ scripts/ci_queue_scan.py scripts/check_cadence_liveness.py"
security = "bandit -r packages/luxar/src/luxar -c pyproject.toml --severity-level medium --confidence-level medium -q"
# Enforce layer direction: the full `Subpackage layering` stack, plus the three
# narrower `forbidden` contracts.
check-imports = "lint-imports"
# Keep that contract honest: assert the declared order is still the measured
# minimum, and that its dated debt list has not GROWN. import-linter refuses an
# ignore matching nothing, so it already stops the list rotting; this stops a new
# violation being waved through by appending a line.
check-layer-order = "python scripts/check_layer_order.py {args}"
# Assert Python, viewer, and citation metadata describe the same release.
check-versions = "python scripts/check_version_consistency.py"
# Regenerate the Python + TS format-contract projections from contract.yaml.
gen-contract = "python scripts/gen_format_contract.py"
# Assert the committed projections match format-contract/contract.yaml.
check-contract = "python scripts/gen_format_contract.py --check"
# Regenerate the remote-control wire constants for Python, TypeScript AND
# Go from control-contract/contract.yaml. Three implementations have to
# agree, and the third ships inside a native binary nobody rebuilds when a
# Python constant changes.
gen-control-contract = "python scripts/gen_control_contract.py"
# Assert the committed control-contract projections match the YAML.
check-control-contract = "python scripts/gen_control_contract.py --check"
# Regenerate demos/data_manifest.json from the demos/data tree. The per-file
# sha256 comes from the git-LFS pointers / file bytes, so no git-lfs binary is
# required (and CI, which checks out pointers only, can still run this). Any
# hosted_sha256 is carried forward from the committed manifest — it describes the
# Zenodo artifact, which has no source on disk.
gen-data-manifest = "python scripts/gen_data_manifest.py"
# Assert the committed demo-data manifest matches the tree.
check-data-manifest = "python scripts/gen_data_manifest.py --check"
# Synchronize the four live documentation sites with the demo registry and the
# focused-example glob. Historical changelog counts are intentionally excluded;
# concurrent stale branches may still need to rerun this after the first merges.
# README catalogue section counts remain guarded by the renderer pytest.
sync-demo-counts = "python scripts/sync_demo_counts.py"
# Assert those committed counts match their derivation sources.
check-demo-counts = "python scripts/sync_demo_counts.py --check"
# Audit built demo scenes when present; a checkout without generated scenes is
# a read-only no-op. The underlying gate is unit-tested in the Python suite.
check-demo-ladders = "python scripts/check_demo_ladders.py {args}"
# Built scenes must carry the citation their demo declares. The source-level
# gate (test_credited_demo_wires_citation) cannot see what reached disk: a
# rebuild from a checkout predating the wiring ships an uncredited store and
# nothing complains. Also a no-op without built scenes.
check-scene-credits = "python scripts/check_scene_credits.py {args}"
# Ratchet ruff's C901 against scripts/complexity_baseline.json: existing debt is
# tolerated, while new, worsened, moved, or paid-down entries fail until the
# baseline is refreshed.
check-complexity = "python scripts/check_complexity.py {args}"
# Inspect a BUILT wheel: package completeness against the source tree, the
# pyproject excludes honoured, no Git-LFS pointer stubs, no member over PyPI's
# 100 MB limit, the wheel ITSELF under that limit, viewer dist bundled.
# Deliberately NOT in `check-static` — it
# needs `hatch build` to have run, and `make build-viewer` before that. CI runs
# it in `wheel-viewer`, where the dist already exists.
#   make build-viewer && hatch build && hatch run check-wheel dist/luxar-*.whl
check-wheel = "python scripts/check_wheel.py {args}"
# Ratchet ruff's defect-bearing rules (flake8-bugbear + blind-except + RUF012)
# against scripts/lint_baseline.json. It has the same shape as check-complexity
# for the same reason: 641 pre-existing violations across 334 file/rule keys
# mean the rules cannot go into `[tool.ruff.lint] select` without a large,
# behaviour-changing sweep. Paid-down entries fail until the baseline is refreshed.
check-lint-ratchet = "python scripts/check_lint_ratchet.py {args}"
# Compile-check the shipped CUDA/Metal sources -- no GPU, no linking, just
# `-fsyntax-only` / `metal -c` / `nvcc -cuda`. First no-GPU compile gate over
# ~3,900 lines of native code that rides into the wheel; it immediately caught
# both build paths pinning a C++ standard below what torch demands, which stopped
# compiling at all. Every toolchain is optional and reported as SKIP when
# absent (a Linux box has no `metal`, a Mac has no `nvcc`), so it is safe in
# `check-static`; CI passes `--require` for the toolchains its runner has, so a
# skipped arm cannot pass for a run one.
check-native = "python scripts/check_native_compiles.py {args}"
# Everything in `check` EXCEPT the test suite. `make check-all` runs this, so
# that `make test-all` is the single place the Python tests execute — following
# the documented pre-commit checklist used to run the whole suite twice (once
# via `test-all`, then again with coverage at the tail of `check`).
check-static = [
    "format",
    "lint",
    "check-imports",
    "check-layer-order",
    "check-versions",
    "check-contract",
    "check-control-contract",
    "check-data-manifest",
    "check-demo-counts",
    "check-demo-ladders",
    "check-scene-credits",
    "check-native",
    "security"
]
# The complete gate: static checks plus the coverage-measured suite. Kept for
# release prep and for anyone who wants one command that verifies everything.
check = [
    "check-static",
    "test-cov"
]

# Black and isort configuration removed - using ruff instead

[tool.mypy]

# Strict mode settings

# Additional strict checks beyond basic strict mode

warn_redundant_casts = true

warn_no_return = true
warn_unreachable = true

extra_checks = true

# Error reporting

show_error_context = true
pretty = true
color_output = true

# Paths

# Additional type checking features
check_untyped_defs = true
disallow_any_generics = false  # Too strict for numpy/zarr usage
disallow_any_unimported = false  # Too strict for external libraries
disallow_any_expr = false  # Too strict for numpy usage
disallow_any_decorated = false  # Too strict for decorators
disallow_any_explicit = false  # Allow explicit Any when needed
disallow_subclassing_any = false  # Too strict for external libraries

# Function signature checks
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = true

# None/Optional handling
no_implicit_optional = true
strict_optional = true

# zarr 3 SHIPS type stubs, where 2.18 shipped none. That is a welcome change but
# not a free one: `Group.__getitem__` is typed as a wide union
# (`Array | Group | int | float | str | bytes | generic | NDArrayLike`), because a
# key may address either kind of node. So idiomatic Luxar chains like
# `root["fitting"]["config"].attrs` no longer type-check — 415 errors appear, 359
# of them in just `gsplats/io/migrate.py` and `io/reader.py`, essentially all of
# the shape "union member has no attribute .attrs" or "str is not a valid index".
#
# Adopting those stubs properly means narrowing at every access, which is a real
# improvement (a wrong node type would become a clear error instead of an
# AttributeError deep in a walk) but a substantial, independently-reviewable piece
# of work. It is deliberately NOT bundled into the format-neutral library upgrade.
# `follow_imports = "skip"` keeps zarr's types as `Any`, exactly as they were under
# 2.18's `ignore_missing_imports`, so this preserves the previous status quo rather
# than relaxing anything. Remove the `follow_imports` line to pick the work up.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["zarr.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true
follow_imports = "skip"

# Per-module options for external dependencies
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "arbol.*",
    "numcodecs.*",
    "typer.*",
    "fastapi.*",
    "uvicorn.*",
    "requests",
    "requests.*",
    "napari",
    "napari.*",
    "numpy.*",
    "numba",
    "numba.*",
    "scipy",
    "scipy.*",
    "metal_splatting_backend",
    "setuptools",
    "torch.utils.cpp_extension",
    "matplotlib",
    "matplotlib.*",
    "colorcet",
    "colorcet.*",
    # Optional `tracksdata` extra (luxar.gsplats.interop.tracksdata) and its
    # polars dependency — not installed in the mypy/CI env.
    "tracksdata",
    "tracksdata.*",
    "polars",
    "polars.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# tifffile >= 2025.3 uses `type X = ...` (PEP 695) which mypy rejects
# as a syntax error, aborting the entire check. Skip it entirely.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "tifffile",
    "tifffile.*",
]
follow_imports = "skip"

# The `# type: ignore[misc]` on the numba.njit decorators is needed when
# numba is installed (typed decorator -> untyped-decorator error) but is

    "luxar.io._ordering.curves.morton",
    "luxar.io._ordering.curves.hilbert",
    "luxar.gsplats.models.gsplats.cpu.kernels",

# Relax strict rules for test files. ignore_errors is kept on:
# narrowing it surfaces ~540 mypy hits, mostly noise from intentional
# negative tests passing wrong types into validation functions to verify
# rejection, and from MockGaussianSplatFitter (a duck-typed stand-in for

    # etc.); remove this if one ever needs to.
    "-p", "no:napari",
]

    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",

[tool.coverage.run]
data_file = "coverage/python/.coverage"
source = ["packages/luxar/src/luxar"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",                              # test code, not shipped logic
    "*/luxar/demos/*.py",                     # *.py is load-bearing: root demos omitted, nested _support measured
    "*/luxar/demos/_support/_umap_utils.py",  # optional umap-extra paths are not available in core CI
    "*/luxar/demos/_support/runtime/device.py", # hardware-gated CUDA/MPS detection branches
    # Demo helpers split out of luxar/demos/ by #2079; same rationale as the
    # demos omit above. This exact set is asserted by demos/tests/
    # test_demo_import_spelling.py::test_coverage_omits_only_the_split_demo_utilities,
    # which compares the "/utils/" patterns here for EQUALITY -- adding or
    # removing one fails that test by design.
    "*/luxar/utils/colors.py",
    "*/luxar/utils/scenes.py",
    "*/gsplats/**/demos/*",                   # research demos (run-on-import; compile-smoke-tested only)
    "*/gsplats/models/gsplats/cuda/*",        # hardware-gated CUDA extension
    "*/gsplats/models/gsplats/metal/*",       # hardware-gated Metal extension
]

[tool.coverage.report]
# Each entry is a REGEX that coverage.py searches against every physical
# line, and a hit inside a multi-line statement is attributed to that
# statement's FIRST line -- so an unanchored word excludes the whole clause
# it lands in. `"pass"` used to be here unanchored: a `passes` substring in a
# Typer `help=` string, or a `*_per_pass` parameter name inside a multi-line
# `def`, silently deleted the entire function body. Measured blast radius
# before anchoring: 76 files / ~1102 statements, including all of
# `run_fit_volume` (the `luxar gsplat fit` entry point), `lod_recipe`,
# `fit_progressive_gaussian_splats` and `run_batch_submit`. Anchor anything
# added here.
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "^\\s*def __repr__",
    "^\\s*def __str__",
    "^\\s*raise AssertionError",
    "^\\s*raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "^\\s*if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "^\\s*pass\\s*$",
]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
# Held just under measured so the gate actually gates. This is the floor for
# `hatch run test-cov` -- the `-m 'not slow'` subset CI runs (ci.yml) -- NOT the
# full suite, which measures higher. Measured 91.58% on 2026-09 after anchoring
# the exclude_lines regexes and dropping the `*/__init__.py` omit (42,847
# statements, up from 41,347 when a stray "pass" substring was deleting whole
# function bodies from the denominator).
#
# The ~2.5 pt margin is deliberate, not slack, and matters MORE now that PRs skip
# coverage entirely (`test-nocov`): the gate is measured after merge by ci.yml's
# push-to-dev `python-tests` legs, NOT on the introducing PR. A regression can
# therefore ride a green PR onto `dev` before the protected 3.12 leg catches it.
# coverage.yml also runs one non-cancelling 3.12 observation per dev commit, but its
# context is advisory until repository protection requires it. Full-matrix
# dispatches add 3.13/3.14, so a floor tuned tight to one interpreter can still
# redden `dev`. Re-measure with `hatch run test-cov` before raising.
fail_under = 89

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "coverage/python/htmlcov"

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "luxar"
# Exclude annotation-only imports guarded by `if TYPE_CHECKING:`. This keeps the
# eight deferred `ZarrWriterProtocol` imports from #2526 out of the runtime graph.
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# THE layering contract. Until this landed, import-linter declared three
# `forbidden` contracts and reported them kept over 1,026 files -- green, while
# the graph carried ten mutually-cyclic subpackage pairs (audit A1-01).
#
# ## Why this order
#
# Chosen by measurement, not taste. `scripts/check_layer_order.py` scores every
# ordering of the seven ambiguous middle packages by how many production edges
# point UP the stack; this one is the minimum at 33. `cli`/`demos` are
# unambiguously the top (201 and 343 outgoing edges against 2 and 6 incoming)
# and the five zero-outgoing packages the bottom, so only the middle was in
# question. Re-run that script after any structural change; it prints the top
# orderings and the exact edges each would violate.
#
# The count alone did not settle `gsplats`: above `core`/`io` and below both
# score within one edge of each other. It sits BELOW because of what the edges
# ARE -- `core -> gsplats` is the scene graph consuming the splat DATA MODEL
# (`gsplat_data`, `tree`, `lift`, `utils.trils`), which is a consumer reaching
# down, while `gsplats -> io` is `gsplats.io.save_gsplats` reaching into the
# private `luxar.io._compiler` tree, which is the same debt A1-03 removed from
# `core`. Ordering it the other way would have declared that debt to be the
# architecture.
#
# ## The ignore list is DATED DEBT, not design
#
# 33 edges, measured 2026-09-05. Every one is a layering violation someone
# should eventually remove, and the two large groups are one job each:
#
#   gsplats -> io    (17)  mostly `gsplats.io.*` reaching into `io._compiler`;
#                          the residue A1-03 left behind (see #2526).
#   gsplats -> core  (10)  mostly `core.group.partition` / `core.group.compositing`
#                          -- shared helpers that belong lower, same species as
#                          the validators A1-03 moved to `luxar.validation`.
#
# import-linter REFUSES an `ignore_imports` entry that matches nothing, while
# `check-layer-order` pins a high-water mark of 33. Delete an edge from the code,
# its ignore here, and lower that constant; the list can shrink but not grow.
# That property is why a seeded contract is worth having now rather than a
# perfect one later.
name = "Subpackage layering"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "luxar.cli",
    # A user-facing driver, peer of the CLI: it imports nothing inside luxar
    # today (stdlib plus `websockets`), and sits above `core` so the typed
    # snapshot/patch dataclasses the spec anticipates can be adopted without
    # moving the layer.
    "luxar.control",
    "luxar.environment",
    "luxar.demos",
    "luxar.io",
    "luxar.core",
    "luxar.gsplats",
    "luxar.encoding",
    "luxar.validation",
    "luxar.utils",
    "luxar.typing_utils",
    "luxar.colormaps",
    "luxar.mesh",
    "luxar.shading",
    "luxar._zarr_compat",
    "luxar._process",
]
# Layers contracts report indirect chains too. The `luxar` package root
# re-exports the public API, so imports of that hub need explicit exemptions
# below; direct cross-layer imports remain governed by the declared order.
ignore_imports = [
    # Colocated tests drive higher layers on purpose -- a `core` test may load
    # the compiler. The contract targets production code, matching the three
    # contracts below.
    "luxar.**.tests.** -> luxar.**",
    "luxar.**.tests.** -> luxar",
    "luxar.tests.** -> luxar.**",
    "luxar.tests.** -> luxar",
    # `luxar/__init__.py` re-exports the whole public API, so ANY module that
    # imports the package root reaches every layer through it. That is the
    # public API working; a layers contract that called it a fault would be
    # unusable. Only the root itself is exempted -- a direct
    # `luxar.utils.x -> luxar.demos.y` still fails.
    "luxar.utils.** -> luxar",
    # gsplats -> io (17)
    "luxar.gsplats._data.io_adapter -> luxar.io.reader",
    "luxar.gsplats.batch.merge_orchestrator -> luxar.io.volume",
    "luxar.gsplats.batch.slurm_gen -> luxar.io.ome_zarr",
    "luxar.gsplats.fitting.sorting -> luxar.io.ordering",
    "luxar.gsplats.io -> luxar.io.ordering",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.load_gsplats -> luxar.io._compiler.gsplat_tree",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.migrate -> luxar.io._compiler.gsplat_tree",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.save_gsplats -> luxar.io._compiler.finalize.amplitude_window",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.save_gsplats -> luxar.io._compiler.finalize.hashing",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.save_gsplats -> luxar.io._compiler.gsplat_assembly",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.save_gsplats -> luxar.io._compiler.gsplat_tree",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.save_gsplats -> luxar.io._ordering.gsplats",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.save_gsplats -> luxar.io.ordering",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.save_gsplats -> luxar.io.reader",
    "luxar.gsplats.lod._substitutive.warm_start -> luxar.io.ordering",
    "luxar.gsplats.lod.annotate -> luxar.io._compiler.gsplat_tree",
    "luxar.gsplats.preprocessing.denoise_pipeline -> luxar.io.volume",
    # gsplats -> core (10)
    "luxar.gsplats._data.composition -> luxar.core.group.partition",
    "luxar.gsplats.batch.merge_orchestrator -> luxar.core.group.partition",
    "luxar.gsplats.doctor.checks -> luxar.core.dimensions",
    "luxar.gsplats.doctor.checks -> luxar.core.group.partition",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.load_gsplats -> luxar.core.group.compositing",
    "luxar.gsplats.io.save_gsplats -> luxar.core.group.compositing",
    "luxar.gsplats.lod.recipes -> luxar.core.group.lod.group",
    "luxar.gsplats.lod.recipes -> luxar.core.group.partition",
    "luxar.gsplats.restride -> luxar.core.group.partition",
    "luxar.gsplats.tree -> luxar.core.group.lod.group",
    # demos -> cli (1)
    "luxar.demos.demo_gsplats_3d_flylight_mcfo_63x_brain -> luxar.cli",
    # gsplats -> demos (1)
    "luxar.gsplats.demos.demo_3d_celegans_culling -> luxar.demos",
    # typing_utils -> validation (1)
    "luxar.typing_utils -> luxar.validation.types",
    # utils -> core (1)
    "luxar.utils.scenes -> luxar.core.dimensions",
    # utils -> demos (1)
    "luxar.utils.scenes -> luxar.demos.demo_lorenz",
    # utils -> io (1)
    "luxar.utils.scenes -> luxar.io.compiler",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain layers must not import the CLI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "luxar.gsplats",
    "luxar.io",
    "luxar.core",
    "luxar.encoding",
    "luxar.mesh",
    "luxar.shading",
]
forbidden_modules = ["luxar.cli"]
# CLI-behaviour tests colocated under domain packages legitimately import the
# CLI (they drive/monkeypatch CLI commands); ignore test-module edges only, so
# the contract still catches any production domain -> CLI import.
ignore_imports = [
    "luxar.**.tests.** -> luxar.cli.**",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# `io` sits ABOVE `core`: the compiler reads core's domain types (Dimensions,
# transforms, the compositing constants), while core only ever NAMES
# `ZarrWriterProtocol` -- a Protocol io implements. So core -> io is a back-edge,
# and it was a real one: five function-local imports reached from
# `core.group.compositing` and `core.group.gsplats_pipeline.from_io` into the
# PRIVATE `io._compiler` tree (audit A1-03).
#
# Being function-local is what made it invisible. mypy does not follow deferred
# imports for cycle purposes and neither existing contract looked at this pair,
# so a mutual dependency between the two largest packages was carried for months
# with every gate green. The shared pre-write validators now live in
# `luxar.validation.writing`, below both.
#
# DIRECT edges only, matching the utils contract below. An indirect chain here
# is not a layering fault: `luxar.core.tests.test_scene_structure` reaches io
# through `luxar.utils.scenes`, and any module that imports the `luxar` package
# root reaches it through `luxar/__init__.py`. Both are the public API working
# as intended. The fault A1-03 found -- and the one this contract exists to
# refuse -- is core NAMING io itself.
#
# `exclude_type_checking_imports` (set above) keeps the eight annotation-only
# `ZarrWriterProtocol` imports out of scope. Those are the dependency inversion
# working: core declares the Protocol it needs, io implements it.
name = "core must not import io"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["luxar.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["luxar.io"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    # Colocated tests drive the compiler on purpose; the contract targets
    # production code, matching the convention of the CLI contract above.
    "luxar.core.tests.** -> luxar.io",
    "luxar.core.tests.** -> luxar.io.**",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Shared utils must not import leaf packages"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["luxar.utils"]
forbidden_modules = ["luxar.gsplats", "luxar.demos", "luxar.cli"]
# Direct edges only: utils legitimately reaches gsplats through luxar.io and
# luxar.typing_utils, which is the layering working rather than a back-edge.
allow_indirect_imports = true
# The scenes edge is permanent: the public scene helpers stay in utils.
ignore_imports = [
    "luxar.utils.tests.** -> luxar.**",
    "luxar.utils.scenes -> luxar.demos.demo_lorenz",
]

[tool.bandit]
# Exclude tests and the demo scripts: demos are example programs that download
# public datasets (urlopen B310) and load their own pickled artifacts (B301) —
# not shipped library code paths, so they are out of scope for the gate.
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "test_*.py", "demos"]
skips = ["B101"]  # Skip assert_used test

[tool.ruff]
# Ruff replaces black, isort, flake8, and more
line-length = 88
target-version = "py312"

# Exclude directories
exclude = [
    ".git",
    "__pycache__",
    "build",
    "dist",
    ".eggs",
    "*.egg",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    ".tox",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".pytest_cache",
    "htmlcov",
    "node_modules",
    # Generated by scripts/gen_format_contract.py; formatting owned by the
    # generator (see `hatch run check-contract`), not ruff.
    "packages/luxar/src/luxar/typing_utils/_format_contract.py",
    # Likewise, from scripts/gen_control_contract.py.
    "packages/luxar/src/luxar/cli/_control_contract.py",
]

# The FORMATTER is Python-only. Ruff 0.16 also formats Python code blocks inside
# Markdown, which means `hatch run format` (and therefore `make check-all`)
# silently rewrites the code samples in 33 package READMEs — measured, not
# hypothetical. Those samples are prose: the rewrite collapses a deliberately
# multi-line teaching example onto one 88-column line and re-quotes it, which is
# a documentation decision rather than a formatting one.
#
# Two things follow from excluding them, both wanted. `make check-all` stops
# surprising anyone with a 33-file README diff, and `ruff format --check`
# becomes gateable in CI (see the `lint` script) instead of red on arrival.
# The linter is unaffected — it never read Markdown.
[tool.ruff.format]
exclude = ["*.md"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Enable various rule sets - start with essential ones
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # pyflakes
    "I",      # isort
]

# Ignore specific rules to match previous tools' behavior
ignore = [
    "E501",   # line too long (handled by formatter)
]

# B007 treats every name matching this regex as an intentional dummy. Keep
# ruff's default explicit because it is part of the ratchet's settings fingerprint.
dummy-variable-rgx = "^(_+|(_+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+?))$"

# Per-file ignores
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # imported but unused
# Each demo declares a DEMO_META literal right after its docstring (read via
# AST by luxar.demos.registry, never imported), so imports follow it.
"**/demos/demo_*.py" = ["E402"]  # module-level import after DEMO_META block

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["luxar"]

# The `B` (flake8-bugbear) and `BLE` (flake8-blind-except) families plus RUF012
# are enforced as a RATCHET by `scripts/check_lint_ratchet.py`, not by `select`
# above — see that script's module docstring for why (641 pre-existing
# violations across 334 file/rule keys, and B905's fix changes behaviour). This
# setting exists so the ratchet baselines real defects only:
# `typer.Option(...)` / `typer.Argument(...)` in a parameter default is the
# documented Typer idiom, evaluated once at import ON PURPOSE, and it accounted
# for ALL 83 B008 findings in the tree. Declaring the two calls immutable takes
# B008 to zero, so the ratchet gates it at zero and a genuine mutable default
# elsewhere still fires. It also covers B006, which reads the same list.
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
extend-immutable-calls = ["typer.Option", "typer.Argument"]

# C901 (the rule this limit feeds) is intentionally NOT in `[tool.ruff.lint]
# select`: ruff has no baseline mechanism, so a bare `select` entry would fail
# on all 195 pre-existing violations, and the only ruff-native suppression
# (`per-file-ignores`) is file-granular and would blind the guard to new
# offenders in those files. Instead `scripts/check_complexity.py` selects C901
# explicitly and ratchets it against `scripts/complexity_baseline.json`, so THIS
# value is what the gate enforces for new code. Run `hatch run check-complexity`.
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

# Product-owned import-linter config (not synced). Fleet-required settings: docs/quality.md
#
# Inventory (top-level middleware.* portions / intended roles) — issue #482:
#   middleware.shared      — ConfigWrapper, API models, tracing, security helpers
#   middleware.api_client  — HTTP client for API consumers (optional)
#   middleware.api         — FastAPI app, business_logic, arc_store, document_store, worker
#   middleware.tools       — omitted (no installable portion under middleware/tools/src)
#
# Cross-portion rules mirror openspec/principles.md (Module Dependency Rules):
#   api may → shared, api_client; shared ↛ api|api_client; api_client may → shared, ↛ api.
# Encoded as `forbidden` (not `independence` between api/api_client — api→api_client is allowed).
#
# PEP 420: grimp cannot use ancestors = middleware (namespace). Ancestors are the
# installed portions instead — same contract type acyclic_siblings as the fleet template.
# Do not add a path-mutating middleware/__init__.py (Import policy).

[importlinter]
exclude_type_checking_imports = True
root_packages =
    middleware.api
    middleware.api_client
    middleware.shared

[importlinter:contract:middleware-acyclic-siblings]
name = middleware sibling packages must be acyclic
type = acyclic_siblings
ancestors =
    middleware.api
    middleware.api_client
    middleware.shared

[importlinter:contract:shared-isolation]
name = shared must not import api or api_client
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    middleware.shared
forbidden_modules =
    middleware.api
    middleware.api_client

[importlinter:contract:api-client-not-api]
name = api_client must not import api
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    middleware.api_client
forbidden_modules =
    middleware.api

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    src

# ============================================================
# Contract 1: レイヤー階層契約
#   domain < utils < BC群 < orchestration/api
#   上位レイヤーが下位レイヤーを参照するのは合法。逆は禁止。
#
# src.domain は型とポートのみを持つ共有カーネルであり、src.domain.types 以外を
# 一切 import しない真の最下層。2026-09-22 の設計判断でこれを恒久的な位置づけとした
# （docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-22-db-ownership-decoupling-design.md §3）。
#
# src.infrastructure は意図的に layers へ載せていない。
#   src/infrastructure/* -> src.market_data（アダプタが BC を参照）
#   src/backtest/*, src/reporting/*, src/quality/* -> src.infrastructure
# とパッケージ単位で循環しているため、層に追加した時点で契約が落ちる。
# 循環の解消は別 Issue とする。
#
# ignore_imports は両契約とも未使用（例外 0 件が現状）。
# 例外を追加する際は必ずレビューを経ること。
# ============================================================
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Layered architecture (domain < utils < BC < orchestration/api)
type = layers
layers =
    src.api | src.orchestration
    src.backtest | src.prediction | src.trading | src.reporting | src.watchlist | src.market_data | src.rule_engine | src.quality | src.screening
    src.utils
    src.domain

# ============================================================
# Contract 2: BC 独立性契約
#   Bounded Context 同士は相互参照禁止（将来的解消が前提）。
#   ignore_imports に追加する際は必ず理由コメントを付けること。
#
# 違反分類ロードマップ:
#   [A] reporting → prediction/watchlist は解消済み（対象の import が存在しない）
#   [B] market_data/watchlist/prediction → reporting、backtest → prediction/market_data も
#       解消済み（対象の import が存在しない）
#
# [C] prediction.rule_signal_pipeline → trading/backtest は rule_engine BC (#340) で解消済み
# [D] backtest → screening は PR-8 (screening port wiring) でポート経由に反転し解消済み
#
# 現状: ignore_imports は両契約とも 0 件。これが目標状態であり、
# 新規に追加する場合は必ずレビューを経ること（恒常的な 0 件維持が前提）。
# ============================================================
[importlinter:contract:independence]
name = BC independence (BCs must not import each other)
type = independence
# 間接依存（A -> 非 BC モジュール -> B）も検査する。かつて utils.db が prediction.db を
# importlib で再輸出していたため allow_indirect_imports = True で無効化していたが、
# Phase 4c（2026-09-22 設計書）でプロキシを撤去し有効化した。
modules =
    src.backtest
    src.prediction
    src.trading
    src.reporting
    src.watchlist
    src.market_data
    src.rule_engine
    src.quality
    src.screening

# ============================================================
# Contract 3: domain purity 契約
#   src.domain は src.domain 自身以外の src.* を一切 import しない。
#
# Contract 1（layers）は src.domain が src.utils・BC群・src.api/src.orchestration より
# 下位にあることは証明するが、src.infrastructure については何も証明しない。
# src.infrastructure は BC 群との間でパッケージ単位の循環があり（Contract 1 のコメント参照）、
# 意図的に layers 契約へ載せていないため、"layers" という型ではこの性質を表現できない。
# そのため forbidden 型の独立した契約として domain の純粋性のみを直接検証する。
#
# ignore_imports は未使用（例外 0 件が現状）。
# 例外を追加する際は必ずレビューを経ること。
# ============================================================
[importlinter:contract:domain-purity]
name = domain purity (src.domain imports nothing outside itself)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.domain
forbidden_modules =
    src.api
    src.orchestration
    src.infrastructure
    src.utils
    src.backtest
    src.prediction
    src.trading
    src.reporting
    src.watchlist
    src.market_data
    src.rule_engine
    src.quality
    src.screening

# We aren't as strict about code quality in notebooks and scripts
lint.per-file-ignores."src/{scripts,notebooks}/**" = [
  "ANN",     # Annotations
  "ARG001",  # Unused function arguments
  "B018",    # "Useless" expressions are used for displaying cell outputs
  "BLE001",  # OK to catch blind exceptions
  "D",       # Documentation
  "E501",    # Line length
  "FBT",     # Defensive programming techniques for function definitions are overkill
  "INP001",  # __init__.py not applicable for standalone scripts anyway
  "PLR0913", # OK to have functions with many arguments in scripts and notebooks
  "S101",    # Asserts fine in scripts and notebooks
  "T201",    # Prints fine in scripts and notebooks
]
lint.per-file-ignores."tests/**" = [ "INP" ]
lint.per-file-ignores."tests/**/*.py" = [
  "ANN201",  # We don't need return type annotations in tests
  "D",       # We don't need docstrings in tests
  "FBT001",  # Fine for fixtures
  "INP",     # Tests don't need __init__.py files
  "PLR0913", # When we use fixtures, our test functions can have many arguments
  "S101",    # Using assert is fine in tests
  "SLF001",  # Accessing private members is sometimes necessary in tests
]
lint.allowed-confusables = [ "ℹ", "–", "σ" ]
lint.flake8-builtins.strict-checking = true
lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api."pytz".msg = "'zoneinfo' should be preferred to 'pytz' when using Python 3.9 and later, see https://tonkintaylor-sonarqube.azurewebsites.net/coding_rules?open=python%3AS6890&rule_key=python%3AS6890"
lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-module-level-imports = [
  "branca",
  "folium",
  "geopandas",
  "matplotlib",
  "mpl_toolkits",
  "pandas",
  "scipy",
  "skimage",
  "tqdm",
]

lint.flake8-type-checking.quote-annotations = true
lint.flake8-type-checking.runtime-evaluated-base-classes = [ "pydantic.BaseModel" ]
lint.flake8-type-checking.strict = true
lint.pydocstyle.convention = "google"

[tool.codespell]
ignore-regex = [ "[A-Za-z0-9+/]{100,}" ]
ignore-words-list = [ "..." ]

[tool.deptry]
extend_exclude = [ "src/notebooks", "src/scripts", "src/archive" ]
experimental_namespace_package = true

[tool.pyproject-fmt]
keep_full_version = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = [ "tests" ]
norecursedirs = [ "tests/assets", "src/notebooks", "src/scripts", "src/archive", ".hypothesis" ]
addopts = [
  "-m not hypothesis",
  "--import-mode=importlib",
  "-ra",
  "--strict-config",
  "--strict-markers",
]
markers = [
  "hypothesis: test is a Hypothesis test and does not run on CI",
  "folium: test requires folium package",
  "matplotlib: test requires matplotlib package",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = [ "src" ]
omit = [ "*/pytest-of-*/*", "*/_version.py", "src/archive/*" ]
relative_files = true

[tool.coverage.report]
ignore_errors = true
show_missing = true
exclude_lines = [
  # Don't complain if tests don't hit defensive assertion code:
  "raise AssertionError",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  "AbstractMethodError",
  # Don't complain if non-runnable code isn't run:
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
  "if 0:",
  # Don't complain about missing debug-only code:
  "def __repr__",
  "if self\\.debug",
  # Don't complain about abstract methods, they aren't run:

]

[importlinter]
root_package = lobster
include_external_packages = True

# =============================================================================
# Layer Contract: Core -> Agents direction
# =============================================================================
# Agents depend on core, but core must NOT import from agents.
# This enforces the plugin architecture boundary.
[importlinter:contract:core-agents-layers]
name = Core must not import agents (agents depend on core)
type = layers
layers =
    lobster.agents
    lobster.services
    lobster.tools
    lobster.core
    lobster.config

# =============================================================================
# Forbidden Contract: No domain libraries in core
# =============================================================================
# Core must not import domain-specific bioinformatics libraries.
# These libraries belong in agent packages (lobster-transcriptomics, etc.)
[importlinter:contract:no-domain-deps-in-core]
name = Core must not import domain-specific libraries
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    lobster.core
    lobster.config
forbidden_modules =
    scanpy
    pydeseq2
    cyvcf2
    leidenalg
    scrublet
    scvi
    torch
    igraph

# =============================================================================
# Independence Contract: Core modules loosely coupled
# =============================================================================
# Core modules should not have circular dependencies.
# Each can depend on shared infrastructure but not on each other.
[importlinter:contract:core-independence]
name = Core modules are loosely coupled
type = independence
modules =
    lobster.core.runtime.data_manager
    lobster.core.component_registry
    lobster.core.queues.download_queue

# =============================================================================
# Layers Contract: Core subpackages respect layering
# =============================================================================
# Higher layers can import from lower layers, but not vice versa.
# notebooks -> provenance -> governance -> queues -> runtime
[importlinter:contract:core-subpackage-layers]
name = Core subpackages respect layering
type = layers
layers =
    lobster.core.notebooks
    lobster.core.provenance
    lobster.core.governance
    lobster.core.queues
    lobster.core.runtime

package pl.cloudbox.kotlinapp.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchUnitRunner
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestInstance
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import pl.cloudbox.kotlinapp.ClientBalanceApp


@RunWith(ArchUnitRunner::class)
@TestInstance(TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)
@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [ClientBalanceApp::class])
internal class LayerBoundariesTest {

    @ArchTest
    val `Repository layer should has no dependency with higher layers` =
        noClasses()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("$REPOSITORY_PACKAGE..")
            .should()
            .dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("$SERVICE_PACKAGE..", "$ENDPOINT_PACKAGE..")


    @ArchTest
    val `Endpoint layer should not access repository layer` =
        noClasses()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("$ENDPOINT_PACKAGE..")
            .should()
            .accessClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("$REPOSITORY_PACKAGE..")


    @ArchTest
    val `Any layer should not access endpoint layer` =
        noClasses()
            .that()
            .resideInAnyPackage("$REPOSITORY_PACKAGE..", "$SERVICE_PACKAGE..")
            .should()
            .accessClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("$ENDPOINT_PACKAGE..")


    companion object {
        private val BASE_PACKAGE = ClientBalanceApp::class.java.`package`.name
        private val SERVICE_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.service"
        private val REPOSITORY_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.repository"
        private val ENDPOINT_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.endpoint"
    }
}

# (es ist unser Code), verlangt aber eine Umsortierung in rund fünfzig

# dauerhaft gelber Job wäre wertlos. src/core war der Anfang; storage und auth
# kamen mit #54/#53 dazu und waren von Beginn an sauber.

python_version = "3.10"

# --- Schichten als Vertrag (import-linter) -------------------------------------
# CLAUDE.md sagt seit langem in Prosa, was wohin gehört. Ein Import, der das
# verletzt, fällt aber niemandem auf — er funktioniert ja. Diese Verträge machen
# daraus einen roten Job, der den konkreten Pfad nennt.
#
# Bewusst `forbidden`-Verträge statt einer strengen Schichtung: die echten
# Aufwärts-Abhängigkeiten (die AppFactory *baut* die Oberflächen) sind damit
# benannte Ausnahmen mit Begründung, statt die Schichtung unmöglich zu machen.
#
# Gleich beim ersten Lauf hat der Linter zwei Importe gefunden, die ein `grep`
# über die Dateiköpfe nicht sieht: **verzögerte Importe innerhalb von
# Funktionen**. Genau dafür ist er da.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = [
    "core", "config", "security", "storage", "auth",
    "wiki", "rss", "tts", "stt", "ui", "api", "email_adapter", "evals", "bench",
]

# Der Guard wird von Wiki, RSS, Streamer und API gerufen — er darf nichts davon
# kennen. Sonst entsteht ein Kreis, und schlimmer: eine Regel, die sich am
# Aufrufer orientiert, ist keine Regel mehr.
#
# `config` fehlt in der Liste bewusst: `_load_texts` holt die Meldungstexte per
# Lazy-Import, wenn der Aufrufer keine mitgibt. config ist selbst ein Blatt,
# also keine Schichtverletzung — aber es ist die einzige erlaubte Abhängigkeit,
# und deshalb steht sie hier statt in jemandes Kopf.
forbidden_modules = [
    "core", "storage", "auth", "wiki", "rss",
    "tts", "stt", "ui", "api", "email_adapter", "evals", "bench",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

[tool.uv]
# R2 из спецификации: arq 0.28 (апрель 2026) заявляет redis<6, а проект на redis-py 8.1. Эмпирически
# они совместимы (enqueue, дедупликация по job_id, повторы, отложенный запуск; два
# DeprecationWarning, см. filterwarnings ниже), поэтому пин arq снят. Тест
# tests_v2/integration/test_arq_compat.py сторожит эту связку при обновлениях зависимостей.
override-dependencies = ["redis>=8.1,<9"]

[tool.hatch.version]
path = "src/messunjerr/__init__.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
# В src/ рядом лежит код v0.1 (пакет `src`); в сборку попадает только новый пакет.
packages = ["src/messunjerr"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- pytest
# В backend/ лежит pytest.ini от v0.1, поэтому тесты v2 запускаются с `-c pyproject.toml`
# (Makefile, dev.ps1 и CI делают это сами).
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests_v2"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"
asyncio_default_test_loop_scope = "session"
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers --strict-config --import-mode=importlib"
markers = [
    "integration: нужны PostgreSQL и Redis (см. tests_v2/integration/conftest.py)",
    "offline: тест из tests_v2/stand, которому сам стенд не нужен (без STAND_BASE_URL не пропускается)",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    # arq 0.28 пользуется параметрами redis-py, объявленными устаревшими в 5.0.1 и 6.0 (см. [tool.uv]).
    "ignore:Call to '__init__' function with deprecated usage of input argument/s 'retry_on_timeout'.*:DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore:Call to deprecated close\\. \\(Use aclose\\(\\) instead\\).*:DeprecationWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["messunjerr"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_also = ["if TYPE_CHECKING:", "raise NotImplementedError", "\\.\\.\\."]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- ruff
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py313"
src = ["src", "tests_v2"]
# Код v0.1 (src/auth, src/posts, ...) и его тесты живут до S13 и линтером не проверяются.
include = ["pyproject.toml", "src/messunjerr/**/*.py", "tests_v2/**/*.py", "migrations/**/*.py"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W", "F", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "A", "C4", "ASYNC", "PT", "SIM", "RUF",
    "S", "T20", "TID", "PIE", "RET", "PERF", "DTZ", "ISC", "ICN", "LOG", "G", "FBT",
]
ignore = [
    "E501",    # длину строк держит форматтер; длинные русские комментарии допустимы
    "RUF001",  # кириллица в строках, комментариях и докстрингах: так задумано
    "RUF002",
    "RUF003",
    "RET504",
    "FBT001",  # булевы позиционные аргументы допустимы в небольших внутренних функциях
    "FBT002",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests_v2/**" = ["S101", "S105", "S106", "S311", "S608", "PLR2004", "FBT003"]
"migrations/**" = ["S608", "N999"]
"src/messunjerr/core/dbinit.py" = ["S608"]
"src/messunjerr/cli.py" = ["T201"]  # командная строка печатает результат в stdout
"tests_v2/stand/probe.py" = ["T201"]  # программа, а не тест: итог нагрузки идёт в stdout

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["messunjerr"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- pyright
[tool.pyright]
include = ["src/messunjerr", "tests_v2", "migrations"]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false

[importlinter]
root_package = apps
# external packages are analysed too: the contract below is about DRF and django.http
include_external_packages = True

# Slices depend downwards only: a slice may import the slices below it and never the
# ones above it.  Slices on the same line are independent of each other.  Upward
# interaction goes through domain events (apps.core.events) and the lecture-content
# registry (apps.courses.extensions), never through imports.
#
# apps.seeding is development tooling (demo data, local database setup).  It sits on
# top of everything, may import any slice and is imported by none.
[importlinter:contract:slices]
name = Slices depend downwards only
type = layers
layers =
    apps.seeding
    apps.insights | apps.notifications
    apps.certificates
    apps.assessments | apps.messaging
    apps.learning
    apps.billing | apps.content
    apps.courses
    apps.accounts
    apps.core

# Inside a slice: HTTP adapters call services, services use selectors, everything
# ends up in the models.
[importlinter:contract:inside-slices]
name = Inside a slice: api -> services -> selectors -> models
type = layers
containers =
    apps.accounts
    apps.assessments
    apps.billing
    apps.certificates
    apps.content
    apps.core
    apps.courses
    apps.insights
    apps.learning
    apps.messaging
    apps.notifications
layers =
    (api)
    (services)
    (selectors)
    (models)

# The domain code does not know HTTP: a service raises ServiceError (apps.core.api.errors), a
# selector returns querysets or plain values, a model holds data and rules.  The HTTP adapters
# (api/) translate; nothing below them imports the framework's request or response types.
[importlinter:contract:no-http-in-the-domain]
name = services, selectors and models know nothing about HTTP
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    apps.accounts.services
    apps.accounts.models
    apps.assessments.services
    apps.assessments.selectors
    apps.assessments.models
    apps.billing.services
    apps.billing.selectors
    apps.billing.models
    apps.certificates.services
    apps.certificates.selectors
    apps.certificates.models
    apps.content.models
    apps.core.models
    apps.courses.services
    apps.courses.selectors
    apps.courses.models
    apps.insights.services
    apps.insights.selectors
    apps.insights.models
    apps.learning.services
    apps.learning.selectors
    apps.learning.models
    apps.messaging.services
    apps.messaging.selectors
    apps.messaging.models
    apps.notifications.services
    apps.notifications.models
forbidden_modules =
    rest_framework
# only direct imports: apps.core.api.errors itself builds on DRF and is allowed everywhere.
# (django.http is a subpackage of an external package, which this contract type cannot name;
# ruff bans it outside the HTTP adapters, see TID251 in ruff.toml)
allow_indirect_imports = True

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract: Layered Architecture
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensures dependencies flow downward through the architecture:
#   cli -> workflows -> llm -> utils -> config
#
# Why this matters:
# - Prevents circular dependencies between modules
# - Keeps the CLI as a thin presentation layer
# - Ensures workflows orchestrate but don't leak into infrastructure
# - Maintains utils as reusable, independent components
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:layered_architecture]
name = Layered Architecture
type = layers
layers =
    mcp_coder.cli | mcp_coder.icoder
    mcp_coder.workflows
    mcp_coder.workflow_steps
    mcp_coder.services | mcp_coder.checks
    mcp_coder.workflow_utils
    mcp_coder.llm | mcp_coder.prompt_manager
    mcp_coder.prompt_sources | mcp_coder.prompt_parsing
    mcp_coder.prompts
    mcp_coder.install
    mcp_coder.utils
    mcp_coder.mcp_tools_py | mcp_coder.mcp_workspace_git | mcp_coder.mcp_workspace_github
    mcp_coder.config | mcp_coder.constants
ignore_imports =
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.ui.app
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.services.llm_service
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.core.app_core
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.core.event_log
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.core.log_inventory
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.env_setup

    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.permissions.approval
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.permissions.gateway
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.permissions.skill_frame
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.core.command_registry
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.skills
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.core.commands.info
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.core.commands.color
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.core.commands.display
    mcp_coder.cli.commands.icoder -> mcp_coder.icoder.ui.widgets.session_picker

# Contract: External Service Integrations Independence
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Removed: github_operations no longer exists as a local module.
