[tool.pyrefly]
# Docs: https://pyrefly.org
project-includes = [ "dmr", "dmr_pytest.py", "tests", "typesafety" ]
min-severity = "warn"
preset = "strict"

[tool.pyrefly.errors]
implicit-any-attribute = false
implicit-any-empty-container = false
implicit-any-lambda = false
unused-ignore = true


[tool.pyright]
# Docs: https://microsoft.github.io/pyright/#/configuration
venv = ".venv"
venvPath = "."
strict = [ "dmr/**/*", "dmr_pytest.py", "typesafety/**/*" ]
include = [ "dmr", "dmr_pytest.py", "tests", "typesafety" ]
exclude = [
  # It has a lot of ugly code:
  "dmr/internal/django.py",
]


[tool.ty.src]
# Docs: https://docs.astral.sh/ty/reference/configuration
include = [ "typesafety/" ]

[tool.ty.analysis]
strict-literal-narrowing = true
strict-generic-narrowing = true
# `ty` has its own error codes for `# type: ignore`
respect-type-ignore-comments = false


[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# pytest config: http://doc.pytest.org/en/latest/customize.html
# PYTHONPATH configuration:
# `docs` is here, so `.rst` doctests can import `examples.*`
# the same way our sphinx extension does:
pythonpath = [ "django_test_app", "docs" ]
# Extra options:
addopts = [
  # pytest-xdist is only applied to some envs, not all tests
  "--strict-config",
  "--strict-markers",
  "--doctest-modules",
  "--doctest-glob=*.rst",
  "--doctest-glob=README.md",
  # Output:
  "--tb=short",
  # Coverage:
  "--cov=dmr",
  "--cov=django_test_app",
  "--cov=tests",
  "--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered",
  "--cov-report=html",
  "--cov-report=xml",
  "--cov-branch",
  "--cov-fail-under=100",
  # Tracecov:
  "--tracecov-format=text,html,markdown",
  "--tracecov-fail-under-operations=100",
  "--tracecov-fail-under-examples=100",
  # TODO: set value to 100
  "--tracecov-fail-under-parameters=90",
  "--tracecov-fail-under-keywords=95",
  "--tracecov-fail-under-responses=50",
  # Ignores benchmarks:
  "--ignore=benchmarks/",
  # Ignores docs:
  "--ignore=docs/conf.py",
  "--ignore=docs/examples/",
  "--ignore=docs/tools/",
  "--ignore=docs/_build/",
  # Ignores typesafety tests:
  "--ignore=typesafety/assert_type",
  # Ignores optional deps:
  "--ignore=dmr/plugins/msgspec",
  # Ignores compiled:
  "--ignore=dmr/_compiled",
]
# Strict `@xfail` by default:
xfail_strict = true
# Fail on warnings:
filterwarnings = [ "error" ]
# pytest-asyncio configuration:
# https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/configuration.html
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Django options:
# https://pytest-django.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = "server.settings"
# pytest-timeout configuration:
# https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-timeout
timeout = 20
timeout_method = "thread"


[tool.coverage.run]
# Covdefaults: https://pypi.org/project/covdefaults
plugins = [ "covdefaults" ]


[tool.slotscheck]
# https://slotscheck.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration.html
strict-imports = true
require-subclass = true
exclude-slots = '''
(
  dmr\.streaming\.sse\.metadata:(SSEvent|_SSEventSlots)\._serialize
  |dmr\._compiled\.negotiation:_MediaTypeHeader
)
'''
exclude-modules = '''
(
  dmr\.security\.jwt\.blocklist
  |dmr\.security\.django_session\.views
  |dmr\.security\.jwt\.views
  |dmr\.security\.jwt\.concrete_views
  |dmr\.security\.token\.views
  |dmr\.security\.token\.concrete_views
  |dmr\.security\.token\.app
  |dmr\.internal\.model_fields
  |dmr\.internal\.endpoint
)
'''

[project]
name = "dotfiles"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Cross-platform dotfiles with comprehensive tooling and documentation"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [
    # httpx's successor rather than a typosquat of it: same author, developed at
    # pydantic/httpx2 under BSD-3. The name alone reads as one, which is why it is
    # said here — and `request()` in github_release.py delegates a security
    # property to it, popping `Authorization` on a cross-origin redirect so the
    # GitHub PAT never reaches the CDN an asset download lands on.
    "httpx2>=2.9.1",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "structlog>=25.0.0",
    "typer>=0.12.0",
]

[project.scripts]
dotfiles = "dotfiles.main:app"
packages = "dotfiles.declaration:cli"


# ---------- Tool Configurations ---------- #


[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = [".git", ".mypy_cache", ".pytest_cache", ".ruff_cache", ".venv", "tests"]
skips = ["B113", "B311"]


[tool.codespell]
skip = '*.css.map'
# Each of these is a name or literal, not prose: ags and noice are tools
# (Aylur's GTK Shell, folke/noice.nvim), fpr is gpg's fingerprint record field,
# te is a `<leader>te` keybinding, afterall is a test-framework hook, notin is
# the `ast.NotIn` comparison node.
ignore-words-list = "astroid,aNULL,ANULL,anull,ags,noice,fpr,te,afterall,unparseable,notin"
check-filenames = true
check-hidden = true
builtin = "clear,rare"
uri-ignore-words-list = "*"


[tool.coverage.run]
parallel = true
branch = true
source = ["install", "src/dotfiles"]
omit = []
# Without these a test that drives the CLI through `python -m dotfiles.main`
# measures nothing: `commands/manage.py::update` read 0% while
# `tests/cli/test_update.py` was exercising it against real git repositories.
# pytest-cov 7 dropped its own subprocess support in favor of them.
#
# `subprocess` puts the serialized config in the environment, which the .pth file
# coverage ships into site-packages reads at interpreter start. `parallel` above
# is what gives each of those children a data file of its own.
#
# `_exit` and `execv` are the two ways this package leaves a process without
# running the atexit that saves the data — `update` ends `--reinstall` at
# `os._exit`, and `edit` hands the process to $EDITOR.
patch = ["subprocess", "_exit", "execv"]

[tool.coverage.paths]
install = ["install"]
dotfiles = ["src/dotfiles"]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 70
show_missing = true
exclude_lines = [
  "pragma: no cover",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
  "@abstractmethod",
  # A Protocol body and a bare NotImplementedError stub are unreachable by
  # construction, so counting them leaves statements no test can ever take and a
  # percentage that cannot reach itself. Anchored, because a NotImplementedError
  # carrying an argument is a real refusal a caller turns into a Refusal, and
  # `registry.py:163` is one that tests/install/test_provider_seams.py drives.
  "^\\s*\\.\\.\\.$",
  "raise NotImplementedError$",
]


[tool.docformatter]
recursive = true
in-place = true
exclude = [".git", ".mypy_cache", ".venv", "build", "dist"]
wrap-summaries = 140
wrap-descriptions = 140
close-quotes-on-newline = true
blank = false


# The layering `lint-imports` enforces, read by the pre-commit hook of the same
# name and by tests/install/test_layering.py.
#
# Each layer may import everything below it and nothing above it, directly or
# through any number of hops. The hops are what the contract is for: no single
# import in the violations it has closed was wrong on its own, and every one of
# them was a chain.
#
# A module not named here is unconstrained, and a route through one still breaks a
# layer pair as surely as a direct import does. So the modules a closed cycle ran
# through are named alongside its ends: `session` carried `registry -> session ->
# resolve`, `context` is what broke it, and `evidence` is why `context` imports
# under `TYPE_CHECKING`. Left out, a cycle between any two of those three reads
# green — `evidence` importing `registry` back is measured and reported by the
# list below, and was not by a list naming only the ends.
#
# `resources` is the one that cannot join, and the reason is structural rather
# than a choice. A layer covers the package and every descendant, so naming it
# pulls in `resources.packages`, which imports `registry` — while
# `resources/__init__.py` is imported *by* `registry` and sits under it. That is
# three broken pairs: `resources` against `session`, against `registry`, and
# `evidence` against `resources`. Splitting the resource vocabulary out of
# `resources/__init__.py` is what would let it in.

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "dotfiles"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture"
type = "layers"
# `resolve` sits above `registry` because `resolve()` walks `registry.PROVIDERS`.
layers = [
    "dotfiles.main",
    "dotfiles.commands",
    "dotfiles.reconcile",
    "dotfiles.engine",
    "dotfiles.session",
    "dotfiles.resolve",
    "dotfiles.registry",
    "dotfiles.context",
    "dotfiles.evidence",
    "dotfiles.catalog",
    "dotfiles.paths",
]


[tool.mypy]
pretty = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
check_untyped_defs = false
warn_return_any = false
# `mypy .` sees two files named conftest.py and, with no __init__.py anywhere
# under tests/, maps both to the module `conftest`. Deriving the name from the
# path instead makes them tests.conftest and tests.e2e.conftest. Adding
# __init__.py would fix mypy and break pytest, which resolves `harness` by
# putting the first directory without one on sys.path.
explicit_package_bases = true
# `src` is what resolves `dotfiles.*` to the package. Without it, and with
# ignore_missing_imports on above, every intra-package import is an unresolved
# name that becomes `Any` — so `mypy .` reports success having checked nothing
# across a module boundary. `tests/e2e` resolves bare `harness`, matching the
# pythonpath below.
#
# `tests` cannot be a third entry, which is why `matrix.harness`, `mutation`,
# `relay`, `runlogs` and `shells` are still `Any` here. It maps tests/conftest.py
# to `conftest`, where tests/e2e already maps tests/e2e/conftest.py, and mypy
# aborts the whole crawl on a duplicate module.
mypy_path = ["src", "tests/e2e"]

# `standard` replaces the per-rule opt-outs repos used to accumulate; basedpyright
# defaults to `recommended`, which turns every one of them back on. Named
# `pyright` so both basedpyright and Pylance read it.

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
analyzeUnannotatedFunctions = true  # or pylance stops analyzing in vscode

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
markers = [
    "e2e: reaches the real network or a real HOME; opt in with --e2e",
    "docker: installs a whole machine in a container; opt in with --docker",
    "interpreter(name): drives a shell this machine may not have; --require-interpreters makes its absence fatal",
    "replants: spawns its own pytest per mutant, so it costs minutes of CPU; opt in with --replants",
    "measures_requests: drives the real syspkg.requested; the autouse stub in tests/resources/test_system.py stands aside",
]
# So `harness` imports the same way from tests/e2e and from the root conftest,
# rather than relying on pytest inserting the test file's directory. `tests` is
# here for `mutation`, whose modules import each other and are also run as a
# command — the Taskfile sets PYTHONPATH for that half.
pythonpath = ["tests/e2e", "tests"]
verbosity_assertions = 2


[tool.refurb]
ignore = [
    "FURB184",  # Allow separate assignment and assertion in tests for readability
]


[tool.ruff]
line-length = 140
exclude = [
    ".git",
    "__pycache__",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".vscode",
    ".venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "single"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"
docstring-code-format = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify
    "I",    # isort
    "ICN",  # flake8-import-conventions
    # flake8-bandit by rule, never as the family. Most of what the family
    # reports is a subprocess call made on purpose, and silencing that takes an
    # ignore list that grows with every project.
    "S102",  # exec
    "S113",  # an HTTP request with no timeout, which can hang forever
    "S301",  # pickle, which runs code from the bytes it loads
    "S307",  # eval
    "S324",  # md5 or sha1 used for security
    "S501",  # TLS certificate verification turned off
]
ignore = [
    "SIM108",  # ternary operator — often less readable
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
force-single-line = true

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions]
banned-from = ["datetime", "pyspark.sql.functions", "pyspark.sql.types"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions.extend-aliases]
datetime = "dt"
sqlalchemy = "sa"
"pyspark.sql.functions" = "sf"
"pyspark.sql.types" = "st"
dataclasses = "dc"

[tool.forge]
# Keys the shared toolchain standard owns, written by its generator.
# Dropping one from the template removes it here on the next sync; a key absent
# from this list belongs to the project and is never touched. Do not hand-edit.
managed = [
    ["ruff", "line-length"],
    ["ruff", "format", "quote-style"],
    ["ruff", "format", "indent-style"],
    ["ruff", "format", "skip-magic-trailing-comma"],
    ["ruff", "format", "line-ending"],
    ["ruff", "format", "docstring-code-format"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "select"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "ignore"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "isort", "force-single-line"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "flake8-import-conventions", "banned-from"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "flake8-import-conventions", "extend-aliases", "datetime"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "flake8-import-conventions", "extend-aliases", "dataclasses"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "flake8-import-conventions", "extend-aliases", "sqlalchemy"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "flake8-import-conventions", "extend-aliases", "pyspark.sql.functions"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "flake8-import-conventions", "extend-aliases", "pyspark.sql.types"],
    ["ruff", "lint", "per-file-ignores", "__init__.py"],
    ["mypy", "pretty"],
    ["mypy", "ignore_missing_imports"],
    ["mypy", "check_untyped_defs"],
    ["mypy", "warn_return_any"],
    ["pyright", "typeCheckingMode"],
    ["pyright", "analyzeUnannotatedFunctions"],
    ["codespell", "check-filenames"],
    ["codespell", "check-hidden"],
    ["codespell", "builtin"],
    ["codespell", "uri-ignore-words-list"],
    ["pytest", "ini_options", "verbosity_assertions"],
    ["pytest", "ini_options", "minversion"],
    ["pytest", "ini_options", "testpaths"],
]
# Dependencies held at the version the pre-commit hook runs, in every group
# and extra that names them, so a local run and CI cannot disagree.
pinned = ["ruff"]

[dependency-groups]
# The pre-commit hook runs `uv run mypy`, so mypy has to resolve from this
# environment: without it the command falls through to the uv *tool* mypy, whose
# venv has no pip, and the hook's own `--install-types` then dies fetching the
# stubs below. Declaring them is what makes the hook deterministic per machine.
dev = [
    "mypy>=1.10.0",
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    # tests/mutation/subset.py imports it directly, and a transitive dependency
    # of pytest-cov is not a declaration — docs/learnings/undeclared-transitive-dependency.md
    # is what that costs. The floor is the version carrying `patch`.
    "coverage>=7.10.6",
    "pytest-cov>=7.0.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5.0",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0.12",
    # A dependency rather than a `uv tool`, because `lint-imports` resolves the
    # package it measures off the Python path — outside the project environment
    # it exits with `Could not find package 'dotfiles' in your Python path`. That
    # is also what puts the console script beside `sys.executable`, which is how
    # tests/install/test_layering.py spawns it.
    "import-linter>=2.14",
    "ruff==0.17.1",
]

# mkdocs is a repo concern, not a runtime one: `uv tool install` deploys this
# package to a machine that never builds the site.
docs = [
    "markdown>=3.10",
    "mkdocs>=1.6.1",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.6.23",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.30.1",
    "pygments>=2.19.2",
    "pymdown-extensions>=10.16.1",
]

[tool.uv]
# pre-commit's mkdocs-strict hook, deploy-docs.yml and install/ops/docs.sh all
# run a bare `uv run mkdocs`, so the docs group has to be synced by default.
default-groups = ["dev", "docs"]

[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-name = "dotfiles"

[build-system]
# Wider than a single minor series on purpose: the uv doing the build is the one
# `install.sh` just installed, which is whatever astral publishes at bootstrap
# time or whatever version the offline bundle happened to capture. A pin narrow
# enough to name one series warns on every fresh machine.
requires = ["uv_build>=0.9.13,<0.13.0"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

# Tool configurations have been moved to config/ directory:
# - ruff.toml: Linting and formatting rules
# - bandit.toml: Security scanning configuration
# - .coveragerc: Test coverage thresholds and exclusions
# - tool.ty below: Type checking configuration

# ty is the sole type checker, enforced in CI and pre-commit.
[tool.ty.src]
include = ["roadmap", "tests"]
# These fixture trees are synthetic "roadmap" packages used only for the
# architecture checker's AST scan; they are never actually imported, so
# ty's import resolution has nothing real to check them against.
exclude = ["tests/policy/fixtures/architecture"]

[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.12"

[tool.ty.rules]
unresolved-import = "error"
unresolved-reference = "error"
invalid-argument-type = "error"
invalid-assignment = "error"
invalid-return-type = "error"
possibly-missing-attribute = "error"
unresolved-attribute = "error"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = "--tb=short --strict-markers -n auto --maxfail=3 --strict-config -ra"
filterwarnings = [
    "error::ResourceWarning",
    "error::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning",
]
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests (fast, no filesystem operations)",
    "integration: Integration tests (slower, with filesystem operations)",
    "filesystem: Tests that require real filesystem operations",
    "slow: Slow tests that may be skipped in CI",
    "performance: Performance-focused tests",
    "mock_scanning: Tests with mocked repository scanning operations",
    "no_xdist: Tests that should not run in parallel (disables xdist parallelization)"
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle (Error)
    "W",    # pycodestyle (Warning)
    "F",    # Pyflakes
    "I",    # isort (importの並び替え)
    "D",    # docstrings (ドキュメンテーション文字列のチェック)
    "UP",   # pyupgrade (新しいPython構文への更新)
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear (バグの可能性が高いコードを検出)
    "C4",   # flake8-comprehensions (不要な内包表記の書き換え)
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify (よりシンプルな書き方へのリファクタリング)
    "PTH",  # flake8-use-pathlib (os.pathの代わりにpathlibを推奨)
    "RUF",  # Ruff固有のルール
    "PERF", # perflint (パフォーマンス関連の改善提案)
    "PL",   # Pylint (コード品質向上)
    "N",    # pep8-naming (命名規則)
    "RET",  # flake8-return (return文の改善提案)
]

ignore = [
    "PLR2004", # マジックナンバーの使用 (コード生成プロジェクトでは許可)
    "T201",    # print文の使用 (デバッグ用途で使用)
    "PLR0913", # 引数が多すぎる (AST処理で必要)
    "PLR0912", # 分岐が多すぎる (AST処理で必要)
    "PLR0915", # 文が多すぎる (AST処理で必要)
    "PLR0911", # 戻り値が多すぎる (AST処理で必要)
    "PERF203", # try-except内でのループ (必要な場合がある)
    "RUF002",  # docstring内の日本語文字 (日本語プロジェクトのため許可)
    "RUF003",  # comment内の日本語文字 (日本語プロジェクトのため許可)
    "E501",    # 行が長すぎる (コード生成で長いテンプレートが必要)
    "D104",  # __init__.py のdocstring (CA構造で多数の空__init__.pyが必要)
    "D105",  # __repr__ 等のmagic methodのdocstring
    "D107",  # __init__ のdocstring (クラスdocstringで代替)
    "D400",
    "D413",
    "D415",
    # 競合するdocstringルールを無効化
    "D203",    # incorrect-blank-line-before-class (D211と競合)
    "D213",    # multi-line-summary-second-line (D212と競合)
    "RUF001",  # docstring内の日本語文字 (日本語プロジェクトのため許可)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"**/__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # 未使用import (re-exportの場合)
"mb_scanner/domain/entities/sarif.py" = ["N815"]  # SARIF標準フォーマットのcamelCaseを維持
"mb_scanner/adapters/cli/**/*.py" = ["B008"]  # typer.Optionをデフォルト引数で使用 (Typerの正しい使い方)
"mb_scanner/domain/ports/**/*.py" = ["D102"]  # Protocolメソッドはクラスdocstringで代替
"mb_scanner/adapters/repositories/**/*.py" = ["D102"]  # Protocol実装のメソッドはインターフェース定義を参照
"tests/**/*.py" = ["D101", "D102", "D103"]  # テストのクラス/メソッド/関数の docstring 強制は過剰

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# プロジェクト内のモジュールを正しく認識
known-first-party = ["mb_scanner"]
# 標準ライブラリ、サードパーティ、ファーストパーティの順に並び替え
force-sort-within-sections = true

[tool.ruff.format]
# Ruffのフォーマッターに関する設定 (Blackとほぼ互換)
# -----------------------------------------------
# 文字列のクォートをダブルクォートに統一する。
quote-style = "double"
# インデントにスペースを使う。
indent-style = "space"
# 改行コードをLFに統一する。
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# pytestの設定
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
# テスト実行時の追加オプション
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",  # 未定義のマーカーを警告
    "--tb=short",        # トレースバックを短縮表示
    "--disable-warnings", # 警告を無効化（必要に応じて削除可能）
]
# カスタムマーカー（必要に応じて追加）
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
# カバレッジ測定対象のソースディレクトリ

# 除外するファイル・ディレクトリ

]

[tool.coverage.report]

    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "if self.debug:",
    "if settings.DEBUG",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if 0:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
exclude = [
    ".venv",
    "**/__pycache__",
    "mb-analyzer",            # TypeScript 側の node_modules 等を対象外に

    "**/node_modules",
]
stubPath = "stubs"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false

# テストディレクトリ専用の設定
# テストコードではMock、fixture、parametrizeなど型推論が難しいケースが多いため、
# 以下のチェックを緩和している:
# - reportPrivateUsage: テストではprivateアクセスが必要な場合がある
# - reportUnknown*: Mock、fixture等で型が不明になりやすい
# - reportArgumentType: parametrizeや辞書アンパック時の型不一致を許容
executionEnvironments = [
    { root = "tests", reportPrivateUsage = "none", reportUnknownMemberType = "none", reportUnknownArgumentType = "none", reportUnknownVariableType = "none", reportMissingParameterType = "none", reportUnknownParameterType = "none", reportArgumentType = "none", reportUnknownLambdaType = "none" }
]

# ================================
# CONTRATOS DE ARQUITECTURA (import-linter)
# ================================
# Se comprueban en el CI (workflow "Architecture & API Contract") y en local con:
#   lint-imports
#
# Qué protegen, y de dónde sale cada regla:
# - Capas: dentro de cada módulo, infrastructure puede importar application y
#   domain; application solo domain; domain nada de las otras dos. Es la regla del
#   CLAUDE.md "los casos de uso nunca importan de infrastructure" (refactor del
#   16 nov 2025), que hasta ahora solo se comprobaba en revisión.
# - Dominio puro: el dominio no conoce FastAPI, SQLAlchemy ni Pydantic.
# - Entre módulos se comparte dominio (p. ej. MatchFormat), nunca infraestructura:
#   cada módulo define sus propios decoradores de persistencia. Los imports
#   INDIRECTOS se permiten porque todos pasan por src.config.dependencies, la
#   composition root, que es el único sitio donde se ensambla todo.
# - Dominio y aplicación no importan esa composition root. Sí pueden leer
#   configuración (src.config.settings, csrf_config).
#
# Si un contrato falla, la salida dice qué import lo rompe. No se relaja el
# contrato sin decidirlo: añadir una excepción es una decisión de arquitectura.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    src
include_external_packages = True

type = layers

# Curated false-positive allowlist — every entry is reachable, just not via a plain
# in-module read that deadcode's static analysis can follow:
ignore_names = [
    # Documented-but-unused config allowlist (informational; validator ignores unknown keys).
    "FOREIGN_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS",
    # Attribute assignments on stdlib objects deadcode can't attribute to a definition.
    "check_hostname",   # ssl.SSLContext.check_hostname
    "verify_mode",      # ssl.SSLContext.verify_mode
    # @dataclass wire-format fields: populated from Claude Code / upstream JSON+YAML and

    "is_local_install",        # InstallContext (read via ctx.is_local_install in cli.py)
    "last_audited",            # UpstreamEntry (manifest schema field)
    "transcript_path",         # StatusData (Claude Code statusline stdin schema)

    "twine>=3.1.1",
    "gitpython>=3.1.0",
    "requests-cache>=0.9.2",
]
dev = [
    "ruff",
    "check-manifest>=0.42",
    "pre-commit>=2.9.0",
    "pydantic[dotenv]",
    "napari[testing]",
]
build = [
    "ruff",
    "pyqt5",
]

[project.entry-points.pytest11]
napari = "napari.utils._testsupport"

[project.entry-points."napari.manifest"]
napari_builtins = "napari_builtins:builtins.yaml"

[project.scripts]
napari = "napari.__main__:main"

[tool.setuptools]
zip-safe = false
include-package-data = true
license-files = [
    "LICENSE",
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
namespaces = false

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"*" = [
    "*.pyi",
]
napari_builtins = [
    "builtins.yaml",
]


[tool.setuptools_scm]
write_to = "napari/_version.py"

[tool.check-manifest]
ignore = [
  ".cirrus.yml",
  ".pre-commit-config.yaml",
  "asv.conf.json",
  "codecov.yml",
  "Makefile",
  "napari/_version.py",  # added during build by setuptools_scm
  "tools/minreq.py",
  "tox.ini",
  "napari/_qt/qt_resources/_qt_resources_*.py",
  "*.pyi",  # added by make typestubs
  "binder/*",
  ".env_sample",
  ".devcontainer/*",
  "napari/resources/icons/_themes/*/*.svg"
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 79
exclude = [
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".pants.d",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "buck-out",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    "venv",
    "*vendored*",
    "*_vendor*",
]

fix = true

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "single"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "F", "W", #flake8
    "UP", # pyupgrade
    "I", # isort
    "YTT", #flake8-2020
    "TCH", # flake8-type-checing
    "BLE", # flake8-blind-exception
    "B", # flake8-bugbear
    "A", # flake8-builtins
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "ISC", # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "G", # flake8-logging-format
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "COM", # flake8-commas
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "INP", # flake8-no-pep420
    "PYI", # flake8-pyi
    "Q", # flake8-quotes
    "RSE", # flake8-raise
    "RET", # flake8-return
    "TID",  # flake8-tidy-imports # replace absolutify import
    "TRY", # tryceratops
    "ICN", # flake8-import-conventions
    "RUF", # ruff specyfic rules
    "NPY201", # checks compatibility with numpy version 2.0
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async
    "EXE", # flake8-executable
    "FA", # flake8-future-annotations
    "LOG", # flake8-logging
    "SLOT", # flake8-slots
    "PT", # flake8-pytest-style
    "T20", # flake8-print
]
ignore = [
    "E501", "TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003",
    "A003", # flake8-builtins - we have class attributes violating these rule
    "COM812", # flake8-commas - we don't like adding comma on single line of arguments
    "COM819", # conflicts with ruff-format
    "SIM117", # flake8-simplify - we some of merged with statements are not looking great with black, reanble after drop python 3.9
    "RET504", # not fixed yet https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2950
    "TRY003", # require implement multiple exception class
    "RUF005", # problem with numpy compatybility, see https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2142#issuecomment-1451038741
    "B028", # need to be fixed
    "PYI015", # it produces bad looking files (@jni opinion)
    "W191", "Q000", "Q001", "Q002", "Q003", "ISC001", # https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"napari/_vispy/__init__.py" = ["E402"]
"**/_tests/*.py" = ["B011", "INP001", "TRY301", "B018", "RUF012"]
"napari/utils/_testsupport.py" = ["B011"]
"tools/validate_strings.py" = ["F401"]
"tools/**" = ["INP001", "T20"]
"examples/**" = ["ICN001", "INP001", "T20"]
"**/vendored/**" = ["TID"]
"napari/benchmarks/**" = ["RUF012", "TID252"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-quotes]
docstring-quotes = "double"
inline-quotes = "single"
multiline-quotes = "double"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# Disallow all relative imports.
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party=['napari']
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions]
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions.extend-aliases]
# Declare a custom alias for the `matplotlib` module.
"dask.array" = "da"
xarray = "xr"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# These follow standard library warnings filters syntax.  See more here:
# https://docs.python.org/3/library/warnings.html#describing-warning-filters
addopts = ["--maxfail=5",  "--durations=10",  "-ra", "--strict-markers", "--strict-config"]
console_output_style = "count"
minversion = "8"
# log_cli_level = "INFO"
xfail_strict = true
testpaths = ["napari", "napari_builtins"]


# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.
# napari deprecation and future warnings should NOT go in here.
# instead... assert the warning with `pytest.warns()` in the relevant test,
# That way we can clean them up when no longer necessary
filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:ipykernel",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",
  "ignore:Accessing zmq Socket:DeprecationWarning:jupyter_client",
  "ignore:pythonw executable not found:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:data shape .* exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE:UserWarning",
  "ignore:For best performance with Dask arrays in napari:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:numpy.ufunc size changed:RuntimeWarning",
  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",
  "ignore:Alternative shading modes are only available in 3D, defaulting to none",
  "ignore:distutils Version classes are deprecated::",
  "ignore:There is no current event loop:DeprecationWarning:",
  "ignore:(?s).*Pyarrow will become a required dependency of pandas:DeprecationWarning",  # pandas pyarrow (pandas<3.0),
  # TODO: remove once xarray is updated to avoid this warning
  # https://github.com/pydata/xarray/blame/b1f3fea467f9387ed35c221205a70524f4caa18b/pyproject.toml#L333-L334
  # https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/8939
  "ignore:__array__ implementation doesn't accept a copy keyword, so passing copy=False failed.",
]
markers = [
    "examples: Test of examples",
    "disable_qthread_start: Disable thread start in this Test",
    "disable_qthread_pool_start: Disable strarting QRunnable using QThreadPool start in this Test",
    "disable_qtimer_start: Disable timer start in this Test",
    "disable_qanimation_start: Disable animation start in this Test",
    "enable_console: Don't mock the IPython console (in QtConsole) in this Test",
]

[tool.mypy]
files = "napari"
# This file triggers an internal mypy error, so exclude collection
# TODO: fix this
exclude = "napari/utils/events/_tests/test_evented_model\\.py"
plugins =  "numpy.typing.mypy_plugin, pydantic.mypy"
ignore_missing_imports = true
hide_error_codes = false
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
disable_error_code = [
  # See discussion at https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2427;
  # mypy cannot run type checking on method assignment, but we use
  # that in several places, so ignore the error
  'method-assign'
]
# see `$ qtpy mypy-args` and qtpy readme. This will be used by `tox -e mypy`
# to properly infer with PyQt6 installed
always_false=['PYSIDE6', 'PYSIDE2', 'PYQT5']
always_true=['PYQT6']


# gloabl ignore error

module = [

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Block import from qt module in napari.layers"
type = "layers"
layers = ["napari.qt","napari.layers"]
ignore_imports = [
    "napari.plugins._npe2 -> napari._qt._qplugins",
    # TODO: remove once npe1 deprecated
    "napari._qt.qt_main_window -> napari._qt._qplugins",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Block import from qt module in napari.components"
type = "layers"
layers = ["napari.qt","napari.components"]
ignore_imports = [
    "napari.plugins._npe2 -> napari._qt._qplugins",
    # TODO: remove once npe1 deprecated
    "napari._qt.qt_main_window -> napari._qt._qplugins",
]

  "setuptools >= 69",
  "setuptools_scm[toml]>=8"
]

    "Environment :: X11 Applications :: Qt",
    "Intended Audience :: Education",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: BSD License",
    "Programming Language :: C",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.9",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Visualization",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Information Analysis",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Bio-Informatics",
    "Topic :: Utilities",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Operating System :: POSIX",
    "Operating System :: Unix",
    "Operating System :: MacOS",

requires-python = ">=3.9"
dependencies = [

    "app-model>=0.2.8,<0.3.0",
    "cachey>=0.2.1",
    "certifi>=2018.1.18",

    "jsonschema>=3.2.0",
    "lazy_loader>=0.2",
    "magicgui>=0.7.0",

    "napari-svg>=0.1.8",
    "npe2>=0.7.6",

    "numpy >=1.22.2, <2 ; python_version < '3.10'",
    "numpydoc>=0.9.2",
    "pandas>=1.3.0",
    "Pillow>=9.0",
    "pint>=0.17",
    "psutil>=5.0",
    "psygnal>=0.5.0",
    "pydantic>=1.9.0",
    "pygments>=2.6.0",

[tool.setuptools]
zip-safe = false
include-package-data = true
license-files = [
    "LICENSE",
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
namespaces = false

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"*" = [
    "*.pyi",
]
napari_builtins = [
    "builtins.yaml",
]


[tool.setuptools_scm]
write_to = "napari/_version.py"

[tool.check-manifest]
ignore = [
  ".cirrus.yml",
  ".pre-commit-config.yaml",
  "asv.conf.json",
  "codecov.yml",
  "Makefile",
  "napari/_version.py",  # added during build by setuptools_scm
  "tools/minreq.py",
  "tox.ini",
  "napari/_qt/qt_resources/_qt_resources_*.py",
  "*.pyi",  # added by make typestubs
  "binder/*",
  ".env_sample",
  ".devcontainer/*",
  "napari/resources/icons/_themes/*/*.svg"
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 79
exclude = [
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".pants.d",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "buck-out",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    "venv",
    "*vendored*",
    "*_vendor*",
]

fix = true

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "single"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "F", "W", #flake8
    "UP", # pyupgrade
    "I", # isort
    "YTT", #flake8-2020
    "TCH", # flake8-type-checing
    "BLE", # flake8-blind-exception
    "B", # flake8-bugbear
    "A", # flake8-builtins
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "ISC", # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "G", # flake8-logging-format
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "COM", # flake8-commas
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "INP", # flake8-no-pep420
    "PYI", # flake8-pyi
    "Q", # flake8-quotes
    "RSE", # flake8-raise
    "RET", # flake8-return
    "TID",  # flake8-tidy-imports # replace absolutify import
    "TRY", # tryceratops
    "ICN", # flake8-import-conventions
    "RUF", # ruff specyfic rules
    "NPY201", # checks compatibility with numpy version 2.0
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async
    "EXE", # flake8-executable
    "FA", # flake8-future-annotations
    "LOG", # flake8-logging
    "SLOT", # flake8-slots
    "PT", # flake8-pytest-style
    "T20", # flake8-print
]
ignore = [
    "E501", "TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003",
    "A003", # flake8-builtins - we have class attributes violating these rule
    "COM812", # flake8-commas - we don't like adding comma on single line of arguments
    "COM819", # conflicts with ruff-format
    "SIM117", # flake8-simplify - we some of merged with statements are not looking great with black, reanble after drop python 3.9
    "RET504", # not fixed yet https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2950
    "TRY003", # require implement multiple exception class
    "RUF005", # problem with numpy compatybility, see https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2142#issuecomment-1451038741
    "B028", # need to be fixed
    "PYI015", # it produces bad looking files (@jni opinion)
    "W191", "Q000", "Q001", "Q002", "Q003", "ISC001", # https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"napari/_vispy/__init__.py" = ["E402"]
"**/_tests/*.py" = ["B011", "INP001", "TRY301", "B018", "RUF012"]
"napari/utils/_testsupport.py" = ["B011"]
"tools/validate_strings.py" = ["F401"]
"tools/**" = ["INP001", "T20"]
"examples/**" = ["ICN001", "INP001", "T20"]
"**/vendored/**" = ["TID"]
"napari/benchmarks/**" = ["RUF012", "TID252"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-quotes]
docstring-quotes = "double"
inline-quotes = "single"
multiline-quotes = "double"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# Disallow all relative imports.
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party=['napari']
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions]
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions.extend-aliases]
# Declare a custom alias for the `matplotlib` module.
"dask.array" = "da"
xarray = "xr"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# These follow standard library warnings filters syntax.  See more here:
# https://docs.python.org/3/library/warnings.html#describing-warning-filters
addopts = ["--maxfail=5",  "--durations=10",  "-ra", "--strict-markers", "--strict-config"]
console_output_style = "count"
minversion = "8"
# log_cli_level = "INFO"
xfail_strict = true
testpaths = ["napari", "napari_builtins"]


# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.
# napari deprecation and future warnings should NOT go in here.
# instead... assert the warning with `pytest.warns()` in the relevant test,
# That way we can clean them up when no longer necessary
filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:ipykernel",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",
  "ignore:Accessing zmq Socket:DeprecationWarning:jupyter_client",
  "ignore:pythonw executable not found:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:data shape .* exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE:UserWarning",
  "ignore:For best performance with Dask arrays in napari:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:numpy.ufunc size changed:RuntimeWarning",
  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",
  "ignore:Alternative shading modes are only available in 3D, defaulting to none",
  "ignore:distutils Version classes are deprecated::",
  "ignore:There is no current event loop:DeprecationWarning:",
  "ignore:(?s).*Pyarrow will become a required dependency of pandas:DeprecationWarning",  # pandas pyarrow (pandas<3.0),
  # TODO: remove once xarray is updated to avoid this warning
  # https://github.com/pydata/xarray/blame/b1f3fea467f9387ed35c221205a70524f4caa18b/pyproject.toml#L333-L334
  # https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/8939
  "ignore:__array__ implementation doesn't accept a copy keyword, so passing copy=False failed.",
  "ignore:pkg_resources is deprecated",
  "ignore:Deprecated call to `pkg_resources.declare_namespace"
]
markers = [
    "examples: Test of examples",
    "disable_qthread_start: Disable thread start in this Test",
    "disable_qthread_pool_start: Disable strarting QRunnable using QThreadPool start in this Test",
    "disable_qtimer_start: Disable timer start in this Test",
    "disable_qanimation_start: Disable animation start in this Test",
    "enable_console: Don't mock the IPython console (in QtConsole) in this Test",
]

[tool.mypy]
files = "napari"
# This file triggers an internal mypy error, so exclude collection
# TODO: fix this
exclude = "napari/utils/events/_tests/test_evented_model\\.py"
plugins =  "numpy.typing.mypy_plugin, pydantic.mypy"
ignore_missing_imports = true
hide_error_codes = false
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
disable_error_code = [
  # See discussion at https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2427;
  # mypy cannot run type checking on method assignment, but we use
  # that in several places, so ignore the error
  'method-assign'
]
# see `$ qtpy mypy-args` and qtpy readme. This will be used by `tox -e mypy`
# to properly infer with PyQt6 installed
always_false=['PYSIDE6', 'PYSIDE2', 'PYQT5']
always_true=['PYQT6']


# gloabl ignore error
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
  '*._tests.*',
  '*.experimental.*',
  '*._vendor.*',
  '*.benchmarks.*',
  'napari_builtins.*'
]

# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.

filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:ipykernel",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",
  "ignore:Accessing zmq Socket:DeprecationWarning:jupyter_client",
  "ignore:pythonw executable not found:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:data shape .* exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE:UserWarning",
  "ignore:For best performance with Dask arrays in napari:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:numpy.ufunc size changed:RuntimeWarning",
  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",
  "ignore:Alternative shading modes are only available in 3D, defaulting to none",
  "ignore:distutils Version classes are deprecated::",
  "ignore:There is no current event loop:DeprecationWarning:",
  "ignore:(?s).*Pyarrow will become a required dependency of pandas:DeprecationWarning",  # pandas pyarrow (pandas<3.0),
  # TODO: remove once xarray is updated to avoid this warning
  # https://github.com/pydata/xarray/blame/b1f3fea467f9387ed35c221205a70524f4caa18b/pyproject.toml#L333-L334
  # https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/8939
  "ignore:__array__ implementation doesn't accept a copy keyword, so passing copy=False failed.",
]
markers = [
    "examples: Test of examples",
    "disable_qthread_start: Disable thread start in this Test",
    "disable_qthread_pool_start: Disable strarting QRunnable using QThreadPool start in this Test",
    "disable_qtimer_start: Disable timer start in this Test",
    "disable_qanimation_start: Disable animation start in this Test",
    "enable_console: Don't mock the IPython console (in QtConsole) in this Test",
]

[tool.mypy]
files = "napari"
# This file triggers an internal mypy error, so exclude collection
# TODO: fix this
exclude = "napari/utils/events/_tests/test_evented_model\\.py"
plugins =  "numpy.typing.mypy_plugin, pydantic.mypy"
ignore_missing_imports = true
hide_error_codes = false
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
disable_error_code = [
  # See discussion at https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2427;
  # mypy cannot run type checking on method assignment, but we use
  # that in several places, so ignore the error
  'method-assign'
]
# see `$ qtpy mypy-args` and qtpy readme. This will be used by `tox -e mypy`
# to properly infer with PyQt6 installed
always_false=['PYSIDE6', 'PYSIDE2', 'PYQT5']
always_true=['PYQT6']

module = [

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError()",
    "except ImportError:",
    "^ +\\.\\.\\.$",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
parallel = true
omit = [
    "*/_vendor/*",
    "*/_version.py",
    "*/benchmarks/*",
    "napari/utils/indexing.py",
    "**/add_layer.py_tmpl"
]
source = [
    "napari",
    "napari_builtins",
]

[tool.coverage.paths]
source = [
    "napari/",
    "D:\\a\\napari\\napari\\napari",

]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "napari"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Forbid import PyQt and PySide"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = "napari"
forbidden_modules = ["PyQt5", "PySide2", "PyQt6", "PySide6"]
ignore_imports = [
    "napari._qt -> PySide2",
    "napari.plugins._npe2 -> napari._qt._qplugins",
]

name = "Block import from qt module in napari.layers"
type = "layers"
layers = ["napari.qt","napari.layers"]

    "napari.plugins._npe2 -> napari._qt._qplugins",

    "napari._qt.qt_main_window -> napari._qt._qplugins",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

    "napari.plugins._npe2 -> napari._qt._qplugins",

# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.

filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors

  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",

  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",

    "YTT", #flake8-2020
    "TCH", # flake8-type-checing
    "BLE", # flake8-blind-exception
    "B", # flake8-bugbear
    "A", # flake8-builtins
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions

    "G", # flake8-logging-format
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "COM", # flake8-commas
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "INP", # flake8-no-pep420
    "PYI", # flake8-pyi
    "Q", # flake8-quotes
    "RSE", # flake8-raise
    "RET", # flake8-return
    "TID",  # flake8-tidy-imports # replace absolutify import
    "TRY", # tryceratops
    "ICN", # flake8-import-conventions
    "RUF", # ruff specyfic rules

]

    "E501", "TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003",

    "COM819", # conflicts with ruff-format

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# These follow standard library warnings filters syntax.  See more here:
# https://docs.python.org/3/library/warnings.html#describing-warning-filters
addopts = ["--maxfail=5",  "--durations=10",  "-ra", "--strict-markers", "--strict-config"]
console_output_style = "count"
minversion = "8"
# log_cli_level = "INFO"
xfail_strict = true
testpaths = ["napari", "napari_builtins"]


# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.
# napari deprecation and future warnings should NOT go in here.
# instead... assert the warning with `pytest.warns()` in the relevant test,
# That way we can clean them up when no longer necessary
filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:ipykernel",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",
  "ignore:Accessing zmq Socket:DeprecationWarning:jupyter_client",
  "ignore:pythonw executable not found:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:data shape .* exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE:UserWarning",
  "ignore:For best performance with Dask arrays in napari:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:numpy.ufunc size changed:RuntimeWarning",
  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",
  "ignore:Alternative shading modes are only available in 3D, defaulting to none",
  "ignore:distutils Version classes are deprecated::",
  "ignore:There is no current event loop:DeprecationWarning:",
  "ignore:(?s).*Pyarrow will become a required dependency of pandas:DeprecationWarning",  # pandas pyarrow (pandas<3.0),
]

    "examples: Test of examples",
    "disable_qthread_start: Disable thread start in this Test",
    "disable_qthread_pool_start: Disable strarting QRunnable using QThreadPool start in this Test",
    "disable_qtimer_start: Disable timer start in this Test",
    "disable_qanimation_start: Disable animation start in this Test",
    "enable_console: Don't mock the IPython console (in QtConsole) in this Test",
]

console_output_style = "count"
minversion = "8"

xfail_strict = true

# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.

filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules

# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.

filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors

  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",

  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",

    "disable_qtimer_start: Disable timer start in this Test",

package no.nav.klage.kaka

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = ["no.nav.klage.kaka"], importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class LayeredArchitectureTest {
    private fun kakaApiLayeredArchitecture() =
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer("Controllers")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.kaka.api")
            .layer("View")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.kaka.api.view")
            .layer("Services")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.kaka.services..")
            .layer("Repositories")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.kaka.repositories..")
            .layer("Config")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.kaka.config..")
            .layer("Domain")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.kaka.domain..")
            .layer("Util")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.kaka.util..")
            .layer("Exceptions")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.kaka.exceptions..")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForControllers: ArchRule =
        kakaApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Controllers")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForView: ArchRule =
        kakaApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("View")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Services", "Config")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForServices: ArchRule =
        kakaApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Services")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Config")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForPersistence: ArchRule =
        kakaApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Repositories")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Services", "Controllers", "Config")
}

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "F", "W", #flake8
    "UP", # pyupgrade
    "I", # isort
    "YTT", #flake8-2020
    "TCH", # flake8-type-checing
    "BLE", # flake8-blind-exception
    "B", # flake8-bugbear
    "A", # flake8-builtins
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "ISC", # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "G", # flake8-logging-format
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "COM", # flake8-commas
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "INP", # flake8-no-pep420
    "PYI", # flake8-pyi
    "Q", # flake8-quotes
    "RSE", # flake8-raise
    "RET", # flake8-return
    "TID",  # flake8-tidy-imports # replace absolutify import
    "TRY", # tryceratops
    "ICN", # flake8-import-conventions
    "RUF", # ruff specyfic rules
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async
    "EXE", # flake8-executable
    "FA", # flake8-future-annotations
    "LOG", # flake8-logging
    "SLOT", # flake8-slots
    "PT", # flake8-pytest-style
]
ignore = [
    "E501", "TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003",
    "A003", # flake8-builtins - we have class attributes violating these rule
    "COM812", # flake8-commas - we don't like adding comma on single line of arguments
    "COM819", # conflicts with ruff-format
    "SIM117", # flake8-simplify - we some of merged with statements are not looking great with black, reanble after drop python 3.9
    "RET504", # not fixed yet https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2950
    "TRY003", # require implement multiple exception class
    "RUF005", # problem with numpy compatybility, see https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2142#issuecomment-1451038741
    "B028", # need to be fixed
    "PYI015", # it produces bad looking files (@jni opinion)
    "W191", "Q000", "Q001", "Q002", "Q003", "ISC001", # https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# These follow standard library warnings filters syntax.  See more here:
# https://docs.python.org/3/library/warnings.html#describing-warning-filters
addopts = ["--maxfail=5",  "--durations=10",  "-ra", "--strict-markers", "--strict-config"]
console_output_style = "count"
minversion = "8"
# log_cli_level = "INFO"
xfail_strict = true
testpaths = ["napari", "napari_builtins"]


# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.
# napari deprecation and future warnings should NOT go in here.
# instead... assert the warning with `pytest.warns()` in the relevant test,
# That way we can clean them up when no longer necessary
filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:ipykernel",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",
  "ignore:Accessing zmq Socket:DeprecationWarning:jupyter_client",
  "ignore:pythonw executable not found:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:data shape .* exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE:UserWarning",
  "ignore:For best performance with Dask arrays in napari:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:numpy.ufunc size changed:RuntimeWarning",
  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",
  "ignore:Alternative shading modes are only available in 3D, defaulting to none",
  "ignore:distutils Version classes are deprecated::",
  "ignore:There is no current event loop:DeprecationWarning:",
  "ignore:(?s).*Pyarrow will become a required dependency of pandas:DeprecationWarning",  # pandas pyarrow (pandas<3.0),
]
markers = [
    "examples: Test of examples",
    "disable_qthread_start: Disable thread start in this Test",
    "disable_qthread_pool_start: Disable strarting QRunnable using QThreadPool start in this Test",
    "disable_qtimer_start: Disable timer start in this Test",
    "disable_qanimation_start: Disable animation start in this Test",
    "enable_console: Don't mock the IPython console (in QtConsole) in this Test",
]

# Module boundary contracts -- ADR-004 (docs/adr/004-modular-monolith.md).
#
# "Do not rely on human discipline: discipline slips at 11pm in week 3."
#
# Run:  uv run lint-imports
# A CI failure here means an import crossed a boundary. There are no temporary exemptions.
#
# ASCII ONLY in this file. import-linter reads it with ConfigParser using the *locale*
# encoding (cp1252 on a default Windows install), so a single Vietnamese character makes
# the whole run fail with a UnicodeDecodeError instead of reporting contracts.
# Same rule as packages/*/alembic.ini. Vietnamese explanations live in the modules'
# docstrings, which are Python source and therefore always UTF-8.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    shared
    edge
    central
    simulator
    pipeline
include_external_packages = False

# -- 1. `shared` must not know about application code ------------------------
# It carries the event contract that BOTH edge and central import. A dependency back
# into either one would be a cycle across the store/central boundary.
[importlinter:contract:shared-is-independent]
name = shared does not depend on edge or central
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    shared
forbidden_modules =
    edge
    central

# -- 2. edge <-> central: two systems, joined only by HTTP + the event contract ----
[importlinter:contract:edge-central-separate]
name = edge and central are independent (joined via HTTP + shared.events only)
type = independence
modules =
    edge
    central

# -- 3. POS <-> Loyalty boundary (ADR-004 rules 1 and 2) ---------------------
# `pos` may only reach `loyalty` through edge.loyalty.api. It must never touch
# loyalty's inner layers, and never query loyalty's tables.
#
# allow_indirect_imports: only DIRECT imports are forbidden. The chain
# pos -> edge.loyalty.api -> edge.loyalty.domain is legitimate -- going through the
# public door is exactly what ADR-004 asks for. Forbidding indirect chains too would
# forbid api.py from doing its job.
[importlinter:contract:pos-not-into-loyalty-internals]
name = pos reaches loyalty only through edge.loyalty.api
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    edge.pos
forbidden_modules =
    edge.loyalty.domain
    edge.loyalty.application
    edge.loyalty.adapters
allow_indirect_imports = True

[importlinter:contract:loyalty-never-into-pos]
name = loyalty never imports pos (one-way dependency)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    edge.loyalty
forbidden_modules =
    edge.pos

# -- 4. `reporting` is a read layer; it must not drive write use cases -------
[importlinter:contract:reporting-is-read-only]
name = reporting does not import the application layer of pos/loyalty
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    edge.reporting
forbidden_modules =
    edge.pos.application
    edge.loyalty.application

# -- 5. Layering inside each module: domain is pure, it knows no infrastructure ----
[importlinter:contract:pos-layers]
name = pos -- adapters > application > domain
type = layers
layers =
    edge.pos.adapters
    edge.pos.application
    edge.pos.domain

[importlinter:contract:loyalty-layers]
name = loyalty -- adapters > application > domain
type = layers
layers =
    edge.loyalty.adapters
    edge.loyalty.application
    edge.loyalty.domain

# -- 6. Sync worker is transport only; it must not learn any business logic ---
# It reads the outbox and POSTs it. It never interprets an event's content.
[importlinter:contract:sync-is-transport-only]
name = sync worker is a transport layer, it holds no business logic
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    edge.sync
forbidden_modules =
    edge.pos
    edge.loyalty
    edge.reporting

# -- 7. The simulator is a CLIENT of the system under test (docs/18 sec 8) -----
# It drives the edge over HTTP like a real till. If it imported edge/central code, a
# test would prove the simulator, not the system. The audit reads Postgres directly --
# that is the tester's privilege, not a shortcut into application code.
# Virtual mode (docs/18 sec 3) is the one allowed exception, and only for PURE code:
# edge.sync.client + edge.sync.backoff (so a virtual store pushes and backs off exactly
# like the real worker) and edge.pos.domain / edge.loyalty.domain (pricing and points,
# so a virtual store cannot compute a second, drifting price). Everything with a DB,
# HTTP server, settings or use case stays forbidden.
[importlinter:contract:simulator-is-a-client]
name = simulator imports only pure edge code, never central
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    simulator
forbidden_modules =
    central
    edge.main
    edge.settings
    edge.health
    edge.web
    edge.ops
    edge.reporting
    edge.sync.worker
    edge.pos.adapters
    edge.pos.application
    edge.loyalty.adapters
    edge.loyalty.application
    edge.loyalty.api

[importlinter:contract:nothing-imports-simulator]
name = shared, edge and central never import the simulator
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    shared
    edge
    central
forbidden_modules =
    simulator

# -- 8. The data pipeline (S4/S5, docs/17) is standalone --------------------------
# It also runs inside the Airflow image, which has its own pinned dependency set
# (data_platform/requirements.txt). Importing application code would drag FastAPI,
# SQLAlchemy and pydantic-settings into that image. It reads central Postgres with SQL,
# like any other analytical consumer.
[importlinter:contract:pipeline-is-standalone]
name = pipeline does not import shared, edge, central or simulator
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    pipeline
forbidden_modules =
    shared
    edge
    central
    simulator

[importlinter:contract:nothing-imports-pipeline]
name = application code never imports the pipeline
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    shared
    edge
    central
    simulator
forbidden_modules =
    pipeline

[tool.uv]

# ───────────────────────────── ruff ─────────────────────────────
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100
src = ["packages", "tests"]
extend-exclude = ["store", "central/dags", "central/scripts", "crawl_data"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W",      # pycodestyle
    "F",           # pyflakes
    "I",           # isort
    "N",           # pep8-naming
    "UP",          # pyupgrade
    "B",           # bugbear
    "C4",          # comprehensions
    "DTZ",         # ⚠️ flake8-datetimez — cấm datetime naive (quy ước: timestamptz UTC)
    "ASYNC",
    "S",           # bandit
    "RUF",
]
ignore = [
    "S101",        # assert — cần cho pytest
    "B008",        # Depends() trong default arg là idiom FastAPI
    # Codebase viết docstring/comment bằng tiếng Việt (CLAUDE.md §Quy ước) — ×, —, ⚠️,
    # dấu nháy kiểu Việt... là chữ hợp lệ, không phải lỗi gõ nhầm ký tự la-tinh nhìn giống.
    "RUF002",      # ambiguous unicode character trong docstring
    "RUF003",      # ambiguous unicode character trong comment
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S105", "S106", "S107", "S311"]
"packages/*/migrations/versions/*" = ["E501"]
# Pipeline ghép SQL từ đặc tả bảng khai báo trong code (`pipeline/tables.py`) và giá trị do
# chính nó sinh (đường dẫn file, token) qua `clickhouse.quote()` — không có đầu vào người dùng.
"packages/pipeline/*" = ["S608"]
# Script vận hành: việc của nó là gọi docker/alembic/lệnh ops cố định qua tiến trình con.
"infra/bootstrap.py" = ["S603", "S607"]
"infra/store_backup.py" = ["S603", "S607", "S608"]
# Bộ đối soát ghép SQL ClickHouse từ UUID đã qua `uuid.UUID()` và store_id đã lọc dấu nháy.
"packages/simulator/audit.py" = ["S608"]
# Bảng khai báo panel/rule (một dòng mỗi mục, chuỗi mô tả dài): dòng dài là dữ liệu, không phải code.
"infra/observability/build_*.py" = ["E501"]
# Diễn tập cảnh báo ghép SQL từ tên partition / UUID mà chính nó vừa đọc từ DB test.
"tests/scenarios/test_alert_drills.py" = ["S608"]
# Script đo tải/khối lượng: gọi lệnh cố định qua tiến trình con, SQL là hằng của bộ truy vấn lớp C
# và tên database do chính script đặt.
"infra/loadtest/*.py" = ["S603", "S607", "S608", "E501", "ASYNC221", "ASYNC240"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["shared", "edge", "central", "simulator", "pipeline"]

# ───────────────────────────── mypy ─────────────────────────────
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["packages", "tests", "infra/bootstrap.py", "infra/store_backup.py", "infra/alert_watch.py", "infra/loadtest"]
strict = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
warn_unreachable = true
# `files` đã giới hạn ở packages + tests, nên v1 (`store/`, `central/`) nằm ngoài tầm quét.

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Không có stub/py.typed nhưng mypy VẪN suy được kiểu đúng từ mã nguồn .py của chúng
# (uuid7() -> UUID, PasswordHasher().hash() -> str) — chỉ cần tắt lỗi "không tìm thấy stub".
module = ["testcontainers.*", "uuid6.*", "argon2.*", "asyncpg.*", "redis.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# opentelemetry-instrumentation-* khác: mypy đọc được mã nguồn .py KHÔNG chú thích kiểu
# của chúng và báo "no-untyped-call" ở chế độ strict — `ignore_missing_imports` không tắt
# được lỗi này (nó chỉ tắt lỗi "không tìm thấy stub"). `follow_imports = "skip"` buộc mypy
# coi cả cây import là `Any`, đúng ý định: các gói instrumentation không phải code của ta.
module = ["opentelemetry.*", "pyarrow.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true
follow_imports = "skip"

# ───────────────────────────── pytest ─────────────────────────────

    "slow: chạy > 30s",

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]

dependencies = [
    # Core data validation & config
    "pydantic>=2.7.1",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0.0",

    # Storage stack (md-first three-piece set)
    # Upper bound: 0.35.0 embeds lance-rust v9 (large storage/encoding jump, not
    # yet stable-released). 0.32-0.34 carry a compaction offset-overflow regression
    # (lance-format/lance#7653); we run 0.34.0 safely via the with_position=False
    # FTS workaround. Do not float past 0.34.x until 0.35 has been validated under
    # sustained churn (bounded + reclaimable index dir, no compaction crash) — see
    # docs/cascade_runbook.md. Never widen this floor back below 0.34 (older lance
    # cannot read v8 data).
    "lancedb>=0.34.0,<0.35.0",    # Vector + BM25 + scalar filter (Arrow-based)
    # Floor, not a new package: lancedb pulls pyarrow in anyway. 25.0.1 stops
    # the per-value `import pytz` attempt in to_pylist() (24 walked sys.path
    # for every tz-aware timestamp) and materialises rows without a Scalar
    # per element; 25.0.0 lacks the latter and has a mimalloc exit crash.
    "pyarrow>=25.0.1",
    "aiosqlite>=0.20.0",          # Async SQLite driver (used by SA async engine)
    "sqlmodel>=0.0.22",           # ORM (Pydantic + SQLAlchemy 2.0 async)
    "alembic>=1.13.0",            # SQLite schema migrations
    "greenlet>=3.0",              # Required by SQLAlchemy async

    # LLM & embedding (one provider per file pattern)
    # <3: openai 3.x (2026-09-24) moved to the httpx 1.0 pre-release line and its
    # client raises AttributeError on every request; 2.x is what the lock tests.
    "openai>=1.0.0,<3",

    # Markdown / file system
    "PyYAML>=6.0",                # YAML frontmatter parsing
    "watchdog>=4.0.0",            # Cross-platform file system events (cascade daemon)

    # Web framework (entrypoints/api)
    "fastapi>=0.104.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.7",    # Required by FastAPI for Form / UploadFile endpoints
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.24.0",

    # Observability (core/observability)
    "structlog>=24.0.0",
    "prometheus-client>=0.20.0",

    # CLI + TUI
    "typer>=0.12.0",
    # click is a transitive dep of uvicorn today, but our CLI raises
    # ``click.exceptions.Abort`` directly (e.g. tests that inject aborts)
    # and typer 0.15+ vendored a copy of click under ``typer._click`` — so
    # the two classes are DIFFERENT even though users only ever see
    # ``typer.Abort``. We depend on the standalone click package so
    # ``click.exceptions.Abort`` stays importable and both classes are
    # covered in the Ctrl-C catch (see backfill exit-130 path).
    "click>=8.1",
    "textual>=8.2.7",

    # Tokenization (BM25 Chinese support)
    "jieba>=0.42.1,<1.0",

    # OME (Offline Memory Evolution) async scheduler & file I/O
    "apscheduler>=3.10.4,<4.0",   # async strategy scheduler chassis
    "portalocker>=2.8.2",          # cross-platform file lock for single-engine guard
    # Windows only: the MSVC C++ runtime (msvcp140.dll et al.) that greenlet's
    # wheel links against and a stock Windows does not ship. It lands in
    # sys.prefix; everos/__init__.py registers that dir with the DLL loader.
    "msvc-runtime>=14.44; sys_platform == 'win32'",
    "watchfiles>=0.21.0",          # native fs watcher for config hot reload
    "anyio>=4.0",                  # Async file I/O (anyio.Path, to_thread.run_sync) for the markdown layer

    # Algorithm library (everalgo monorepo, published on PyPI).
    "everalgo-user-memory==0.4.0",
    "everalgo-agent-memory==0.4.0",
    "everalgo-rank==0.4.1",
    "everalgo-knowledge==0.1.1",

    # everalgo's own transitive layer, pinned to what this repo's uv.lock —
    # and therefore the whole test suite — actually resolves. The packages
    # above declare it as `>=0.2.0,<2.0.0`, treating a 0.x line as if a major
    # bump were the only breaking one, so a fresh `pip install everos` picks
    # up releases the suite has never run against. That is not theoretical:
    # everalgo-boundary 0.3.0 added a third required field to the public
    # `DetectionResult` NamedTuple while everalgo-agent-memory 0.4.0 still
    # builds it with two, so `POST /add` answered 500 on a default
    # (`memorize.mode = "agent"`) install of 1.2.3 while every local suite
    # stayed green on the locked 0.2.1. Raise these deliberately, together
    # with a run of the release smoke against a PyPI-resolved install.
    "everalgo-boundary==0.2.1",
    "everalgo-core==0.3.0",
    "everalgo-clustering==0.2.1",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
multimodal = ["everalgo-parser[svg]>=0.2.1"]  # [svg] bundles cairosvg → SVG works by default
# Native OpenTelemetry tracing export. Optional — EverOS never imports these
# unless [observability] is enabled. Install with: pip install everos[otel]
otel = [
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.27.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.27.0",

"Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/EverMind-AI/EverOS/issues"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/everos"]

# ``env.template`` lives at src/everos/templates/env.template and is
# auto-included via ``packages``. ``everos init`` reads it through
# ``importlib.resources``. No force-include needed.

# sdist uses an include-whitelist (not exclude) so we don't accidentally ship
# things like CLAUDE.md, .claude/, CI configs, or IDE settings. New top-level
# files default to NOT-shipped — you have to opt them in here.
#
# exclude is kept as belt-and-suspenders for build artefacts that CI generates
# inside the project tree (UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache in .gitlab-ci.yml).
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
    "/src",
    "/tests",
    "/docs",
    "/pyproject.toml",
    "/README.md",
    "/QUICKSTART.md",
    "/CHANGELOG.md",
    "/CONTRIBUTING.md",
    "/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md",
    "/SECURITY.md",
    "/ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md",
    "/CITATION.md",
    "/LICENSE",
    "/NOTICE",
    "/config.example.toml",
]
exclude = [".uv-cache", ".venv"]

[project.scripts]
everos = "everos.entrypoints.cli.main:app"

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Tooling
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = ["src_old"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "SIM", "ASYNC", "RUF"]
ignore = [
    "RUF001",  # ambiguous Unicode in strings (intentional × – symbols)
    "RUF002",  # ambiguous Unicode in docstrings
    "RUF003",  # ambiguous Unicode in comments
    "RUF012",  # mutable class attribute default (SQLModel requires this)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# The four dataset adapters hold the answer and judge prompts as multi-line string
# literals, copied byte-for-byte from each benchmark's reference harness. Rewrapping one
# changes what the model is shown and so changes the score, which is the opposite of what
# this code is for. Every long line in these four files is inside such a literal --
# nothing outside one is exempted, and no other file under benchmarks/ is.
"benchmarks/adapters/locomo.py" = ["E501"]
"benchmarks/adapters/longmemeval.py" = ["E501"]
"benchmarks/adapters/subtlememory.py" = ["E501"]
"benchmarks/adapters/evermembench.py" = ["E501"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
addopts = "-v --tb=short -m 'not slow and not live_llm'"
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    # tzlocal (via APScheduler, imported by the OME engine): a container with no
    # /etc/timezone and no /etc/localtime warns and falls back to UTC. Under `error`
    # that aborts COLLECTION for every test that imports the app -- measured at 50
    # files here -- so `make test` fails on a clean container for a reason unrelated
    # to any test. The fallback is already what this project wants: the display
    # timezone comes solely from EVEROS_MEMORY__TIMEZONE, never from the OS (see
    # .claude/rules/datetime-handling.md), so tzlocal's guess is never read.
    "ignore:Can not find any timezone configuration:UserWarning",
    # jieba 0.42.1: unescaped backslashes in regex strings (upstream
    # unmaintained; no fix available).  Python 3.12 emits
    # SyntaxWarning for invalid escape sequences.
    "ignore:invalid escape sequence:SyntaxWarning",
    # aiosqlite teardown: connection-worker thread and Connection.__del__
    # raise after pytest closes the event loop.  Upstream issue
    # (aiosqlite + pytest-asyncio); we cannot fix their lifecycle.
    "ignore:Exception in thread.*_connection_worker_thread:pytest.PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning",
    # aiosqlite + asyncio teardown: Connection.__del__ and
    # BaseEventLoop.__del__ fire after pytest closes the event loop.
    # Upstream lifecycle issue; we cannot fix their cleanup order.
    "ignore:Exception ignored.*:pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning",
]
markers = [
    "slow: runs that take >=10s (regardless of dependency); CI default excludes these. Run with `pytest -m slow`.",
    "live_llm: requires real LLM / embedder / reranker credentials from .env; burns tokens. CI default excludes. Run with `pytest -m live_llm`.",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/everos"]
branch = true
omit = ["**/__init__.py"]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 80
show_missing = true
exclude_lines = [
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "pragma: no cover",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["everos"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "everos.entrypoints",
    "everos.service",
    "everos.memory",
    "everos.infra",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Subpackage internals are private"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["everos.service", "everos.memory", "everos.entrypoints"]
# `**` matches any descendant (writer.py, reader.py, sub.foo.bar, ...).
# Public API must be reached via the subpackage `__init__.py`.
forbidden_modules = [
    "everos.infra.persistence.markdown.**",
    "everos.infra.persistence.lancedb.**",
    "everos.infra.persistence.sqlite.**",
    "everos.infra.persistence.index.**",
    "everos.infra.persistence.records.**",
    "everos.infra.persistence.milvus.**",
]
# `forbidden` contracts run a *transitive closure* — any path from a
# source module to a forbidden module fails the check, even when the
# source only imports the subpackage top-level. The whitelist below
# carves out **intra-subpackage wiring**: each storage subpackage's
# own ``__init__.py`` imports its own ``tables`` / ``repos`` / manager
# children to assemble the public API surface that outer layers reach.
# These edges are normal Python package wiring, *not* a privacy
# breach — without these ignores, even a legitimate
# ``from everos.infra.persistence.sqlite import X`` would be punished
# because the transitive scan walks one hop further into the package.
#
# Direct imports from outer layers into a subpackage internal module
# (e.g. ``from everos.infra.persistence.sqlite.tables import X`` written
# in ``service`` or ``entrypoints``) remain blocked — that edge is not
# in this whitelist.
#
# One edge below is *not* intra-subpackage wiring: ``lancedb -> records``.
# ``records/`` holds the table declarations every index backend reads
# (TABLE_NAME / BM25_FIELDS / PRIMARY_KEY); it is the one shared schema
# module inside ``persistence/`` (docs/architecture.md, dependency table).
ignore_imports = [
    "everos.infra.persistence.sqlite -> everos.infra.persistence.sqlite.tables",
    "everos.infra.persistence.sqlite -> everos.infra.persistence.sqlite.repos",
    "everos.infra.persistence.sqlite -> everos.infra.persistence.sqlite.sqlite_manager",
    "everos.infra.persistence.lancedb -> everos.infra.persistence.records",
    "everos.infra.persistence.lancedb -> everos.infra.persistence.lancedb.repos",
    "everos.infra.persistence.lancedb -> everos.infra.persistence.lancedb.lancedb_manager",
    "everos.infra.persistence.markdown -> everos.infra.persistence.markdown.mds",
    "everos.infra.persistence.markdown -> everos.infra.persistence.markdown.writers",
    "everos.infra.persistence.markdown -> everos.infra.persistence.markdown.readers",
    "everos.infra.persistence.index -> everos.infra.persistence.index._provenance",
    "everos.infra.persistence.index -> everos.infra.persistence.index.predicate",
    "everos.infra.persistence.index -> everos.infra.persistence.index.protocols",
    "everos.infra.persistence.index -> everos.infra.persistence.index.router",
    "everos.infra.persistence.index -> everos.infra.persistence.index.schema",
    # The facade and the router select the engine at call time; the Milvus
    # import is function-level so pymilvus stays an optional extra, but the
    # transitive scan still walks it.
    "everos.infra.persistence.index -> everos.infra.persistence.milvus",
    "everos.infra.persistence.index.router -> everos.infra.persistence.milvus",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# The facade and the router resolve a configured backend, so they import the
# engine packages by design. The port definitions must not: the moment protocols or
# schema knows a concrete engine, "portable" stops being checkable and the
# next adapter inherits whatever leaked in. This is the rule that keeps the
# split from eroding -- moving files alone does not stop anyone moving them
# back.
name = "Derived-index ports know no concrete backend"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "everos.infra.persistence.index.protocols",
    "everos.infra.persistence.index.schema",
    "everos.infra.persistence.predicate",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "everos.infra.persistence.lancedb",
    "everos.infra.persistence.milvus",
    "everos.core.persistence.lancedb",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "OME does not depend on memory/service/entrypoints or sibling infra subpackages"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["everos.infra.ome"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "everos.infra.persistence",
    "everos.memory",
    "everos.service",
    "everos.entrypoints",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "ruff>=0.8.0",
    "pytest>=8.4.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.1.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.0.0",
    "pytest-rerunfailures>=15.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "pre-commit>=4.0.0",
    "ipdb>=0.13.13",
    "pyinstrument>=5.0.0",
    # Tracing tests must actually run (no skip-when-absent), so the optional
