    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.27.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.27.0",
    "pymilvus>=3.0.0",
]

package no.nav.klage.search

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = ["no.nav.klage.search"], importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class LayeredArchitectureTest {
    fun kabalApiLayeredArchitecture() =
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer("Controllers")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.api.controller")
            .layer("ApiMappers")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.api.mapper")
            .layer("View")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.api.view")
            .layer("Services")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.service..")
            .layer("Repositories")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.repositories..")
            .layer("Clients")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.clients..")
            .layer("Config")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.config..")
            .layer("Domain")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.domain..")
            .layer("Util")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.util..")
            .layer("Exceptions")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.exceptions..")
            .layer("Gateway")
            .definedBy("no.nav.klage.search.gateway")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForControllers: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Controllers")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForApimappers: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("ApiMappers")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Config", "Services")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForView: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("View")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Services", "Config", "ApiMappers")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForServices: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Services")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Config", "ApiMappers", "Clients")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForPersistence: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Repositories")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Services", "Controllers", "Config", "ApiMappers")

    @ArchTest
    val layerDependenciesAreRespectedForClients: ArchRule =
        kabalApiLayeredArchitecture()
            .whereLayer("Clients")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Services", "Repositories", "Config", "Controllers", "Util", "ApiMappers", "Gateway")
}

[project]
name = "bitranox_template_py_lib"
version = "2.0.2"
description = "Template for backward compatible python libs with registered cli commands"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
    "lib_cli_exit_tools>=2.4.1",
    "rich-click>=1.9.9",
    "rtoml>=0.14.0",
]
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "bitranox", email = "bitranox@gmail.com" }]
keywords = ["logging", "rich", "cli", "terminal", "ansi"]
classifiers = [
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.15",
  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Environment :: Console",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]

# System packages required for CI runners (read by GitHub Actions workflow template)
# Format: "apt_package_name" for Ubuntu, future: {"apt": "...", "brew": "...", "choco": "..."}
[tool.ci]
system-dependencies-ubuntu = []
system-dependencies-macos = []
system-dependencies-windows-pip = []
system-dependencies-windows-choco = []
os = ["ubuntu-latest", "windows-latest", "macos-latest"]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/bitranox/bitranox_template_py_lib"
Repository = "https://github.com/bitranox/bitranox_template_py_lib.git"
Issues = "https://github.com/bitranox/bitranox_template_py_lib/issues"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
  "pytest>=9.1.1",
  "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
  "ruff>=0.17.0",
  "pyright[nodejs]>=1.1.414",
  "bandit>=1.9.4",
  "build>=1.6.1",
  "hatchling>=1.32.4",
  "twine>=7.0.0",
  # codecov-cli is disabled, not dropped: it requires click<8.3.0, which drags click back to
  # 8.2.1 - the version with CVE-2026-7246 (command injection in click.edit(), fixed in 8.3.3).
  # Nothing else here caps click, so with this line active the audit gate goes red on every
  # clean install. Leaving it off costs nothing: CI uploads coverage via codecov/codecov-action,
  # not this CLI, and "bmk codecov" resolves codecovcli from PATH and only warns when absent.
  # Re-enable once codecov-cli relaxes its click<8.3.0 pin.
  # "codecov-cli>=11.2.6",
  # Transitive CVE pins
  "click>=8.5.0",  # CVE-2026-7246
  "pip-audit>=2.10.1",
  "textual>=8.2.8",
  "import-linter>=2.15",
  "pydantic>=2.14.1",
  "setuptools>=84.0.0",
  "rtoml>=0.14.0",
]

[project.scripts]
bitranox_template_py_lib = "bitranox_template_py_lib.cli:main"
bitranox-template-py-lib = "bitranox_template_py_lib.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = [
    "hatchling>=1.32.4",
]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/bitranox_template_py_lib"]
include = ["src/bitranox_template_py_lib/py.typed"]

# An allowlist, never a denylist: hatchling reads only the root .gitignore, so tracked working
# files and files hidden through .git/info/exclude or a nested .gitignore (session records,
# review notes, helper scripts) would ship. tests/test_packaging.py builds the sdist and
# refuses any other top-level entry.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
    "/src/bitranox_template_py_lib",
    "/tests/*.py",
    "/docs",
    "/README.md",
    "/LICENSE",
    "/CHANGELOG.md",
    "/pyproject.toml",
]

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 160
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", "W",     # pycodestyle
  "F",           # pyflakes
  "I",           # isort
  "N",           # pep8-naming
  "UP",          # pyupgrade
  "B",           # bugbear
  "A",           # builtins shadowing
  "C4",          # comprehension simplification
  "C90",         # mccabe: cyclomatic complexity <= 10 (the house hard limit)
  "SIM",         # simplification
  "TCH",         # type-checking imports
  "RUF",         # ruff-specific
  "G",           # logging format (catches f-string in logger)
  "T20",         # print statements
  "PTH",         # pathlib preference
  "PLC", "PLE",  # pylint conventions/errors
  "S",           # flake8-bandit security checks
  "PERF",        # performance anti-patterns
  "ERA",         # eradicate dead/commented-out code
  "FBT",         # boolean trap (boolean positional args)
  "PLR",         # pylint refactor
  "PLW",         # pylint warnings
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# ignore the "unused import sys" in the jupyter notebook - which we need (it is a linter hickup)
"notebooks/*.ipynb" = ["F401"]
# Tests: assert is standard, test fixtures have passwords, magic values are clearer inline, temp paths
# are fine. PLC0415: local/deferred imports are a deliberate test idiom - some tests import inside the
# test body to exercise import-time and cache behaviour, so moving them to module top would defeat intent.
"tests/*.py" = ["S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "T20", "PLR2004", "PLR0913", "FBT001", "FBT003", "PLC0415"]

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
extraPaths = [
  "src",
]
exclude = [
  "scripts/menu.py",
  ".venv*",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = ["--doctest-modules"]
doctest_optionflags = ["ELLIPSIS", "NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
markers = [
  "os_agnostic: test runs on every supported operating system",
  "os_windows: test exercises Windows-only behavior",
  "os_macos: test exercises macOS-only behavior",
  "os_posix: test exercises behavior requiring POSIX semantics",
  "os_linux: test exercises Linux-only behavior",
  "local_only: test only runs in local development environments (skipped in CI)",
  "integration: tests requiring external resources (SMTP, databases, APIs); run via 'make testintegration'",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
parallel = false
data_file = ".coverage.unit"
source = ["src/bitranox_template_py_lib"]

[tool.coverage.report]
omit = [
  "tests/*",
]
fail_under = 85
show_missing = true

[tool.coverage.json]
output = "coverage.json"
pretty_print = true

[tool.clean]
# Patterns to remove when running `make clean`
patterns = [
  "**/__pycache__",
  ".hypothesis",
  ".import_linter_cache",
  ".pytest_cache",
  ".ruff_cache",
  ".pyright",
  ".mypy_cache",
  ".tox",
  ".nox",
  ".eggs",
  "*.egg-info",
  "build",
  "dist",
  "htmlcov",
  ".coverage",
  "coverage.xml",
  "codecov.sh",
  ".cache",
  "result",
]

[tool.git]
# Default git remote for push/release commands
default-remote = "origin"

[tool.scripts.test]
# Configuration for CICD test runner
pytest-verbosity = "-vv"
coverage-report-file = "coverage.xml"
src-path = "src"

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "bitranox_template_py_lib"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# The first project-wide gate was Ruff's default error-focused families while
# the historical lint backlog was retired. It has been widened to add the two
# families that catch defects this project actually cares about:
#
#   B — flake8-bugbear: real bugs, not style.
#   S — flake8-bandit: the security lane.
#
# Widening them wholesale would have meant a ~700-line sweep across hundreds of
# files, which is exactly the broad refactor CONTRIBUTING tells us not to do.
# So each family is enabled with today's backlog pinned in `ignore` below. The
# point is the ratchet: every *other* rule in B and S is now enforced, so a new
# `eval`, `exec`, `shell=True`, `verify=False`, or `yaml.load` cannot land
# unnoticed, and each ignored rule can be retired one at a time in its own
# reviewable commit.
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "B", "S"]

ignore = [
    # --- deliberate, not backlog ------------------------------------------
    # `assert` in library code. Audited 2026-09-02: every one narrows a type
    # behind a pydantic model validator or an `if ... raise` immediately above
    # it. Verified empirically too — the 11,248-test research-agent suite run
    # under PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1 (all asserts stripped) produces a byte-identical
    # failure set. None of them is a fail-closed gate.
    "S101",
    # Suspicious URL open. All 18 sites use pinned literal hosts (NCBI
    # eutils, PhysioNet with a pinned redirect handler, Tavily).
    "S310",
    # "Hardcoded password". All 10 are parse tokens and environment variable
    # *names*, not values.
    "S105",
    # Subprocess without shell=True. The step runner deliberately builds
    # argument vectors and never passes a shell string.
    "S603",
    "S607",

    # --- backlog, pinned; retire one rule per commit ----------------------
    "B905",  # 187 — zip() without an explicit strict=
    "B023",  # 45  — closures over a loop variable; audited, all are invoked
             #       within the same iteration, so none currently misfires
    "B008",  # 38  — function call in a default argument
    "B007",  # 31  — unused loop control variable
    "B904",  # 24  — raise without `from` inside except; hurts diagnosability
    "B028",  # 3   — warnings.warn without stacklevel
    "S110",  # 133 — try/except/pass. This is the silent-swallow pattern the
             #       2026-09 audit is about; retiring it is its own project.
    "S112",  # 82  — try/except/continue, same family
    "S608",  # 54  — SQL built by string interpolation (DuckDB, internal)
    "S324",  # 9   — sha1/md5 used as content keys, not as a MAC
    "S314",  # 6   — ElementTree on PubMed responses
    "S108",  # 5   — literal /tmp in the sandbox subprocess environment
    "S311",  # 2   — random used for sampling, not for secrets
    "S301",  # 2   — the two sanctioned pickle sites, both opt-in gated
    "S104",  # 1   — a comparison against "0.0.0.0", not a bind
    "S106",  # 1   — an argument named `token` that carries a receipt id
]

package com.hhkbdev.khreact

import com.tngtech.archunit.base.DescribedPredicate.alwaysTrue
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClass.Predicates.belongToAnyOf
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture

@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [KhReactApp::class], importOptions = [DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class TechnicalStructureTest {
    @ArchTest
    val respectsTechnicalArchitectureLayers = layeredArchitecture()
        .layer("Config").definedBy("..config..")
        .layer("Web").definedBy("..web..")
        .optionalLayer("Service").definedBy("..service..")
        .layer("Security").definedBy("..security..")
        .layer("Persistence").definedBy("..repository..")
        .layer("Domain").definedBy("..domain..")
        .whereLayer("Config").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
        .whereLayer("Web").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config")
        .whereLayer("Service").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Web", "Config")
        .whereLayer("Security").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config", "Service", "Web")
        .whereLayer("Persistence").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Service", "Security", "Web", "Config")
        .whereLayer("Domain").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Persistence", "Service", "Security", "Web", "Config")
        .ignoreDependency(belongToAnyOf(KhReactApp::class.java), alwaysTrue())
        .ignoreDependency(
            alwaysTrue(),
            belongToAnyOf(
                com.hhkbdev.khreact.config.ApplicationProperties::class.java
            )
        )
}

description = "Polynomial And NURBS Toolkit"

requires-python = ">=3.11, <3.15"
license = "MIT"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
authors = [{ name = "Pablo Antolin", email = "pablo.antolin@epfl.ch" }]
keywords = [

  "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
  "Programming Language :: Python",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering",
]
# Always-on runtime dependencies. Optional features (MPI, METIS partitioning,
# visualization) live in `[project.optional-dependencies]` and are opt-in.
dependencies = [
  "numpy>=1.26,<3",
  "scipy>=1.15,<2",  # 1.15 added BarycentricInterpolator's `rng`, which Lagrange tabulation needs to be reproducible
  "numba>=0.63,<0.66",  # 0.66.0 broke mypy's view of get_num_threads/config.NUMBA_NUM_THREADS
  "threadpoolctl>=3.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
mpi = [
  "mpi4py>=3.1,<5",
]
metis = [
  "pymetis>=2025.2",
]
viz = [
  "pyvista>=0.43,<1",
]
docs = [
  "sphinx>=7.2,<8",
  "furo>=2024.1",
  "myst-parser>=2.0,<3",
  "linkify-it-py>=2.0,<3",
  # matplotlib is used only by the 2-D plots in the tutorial scripts (not by pantr
  # itself, whose rendering is pyvista-based); pinned here so the gallery always builds.
  "matplotlib>=3.7,<4",
  # Sphinx-Gallery executes the `tutorials/` scripts and embeds their output; pyvista
  # renders the 3-D scenes off-screen and the trame stack (+ nest_asyncio2)
  # exports them as interactive vtk.js widgets. On headless builders docs/conf.py
  # starts Xvfb and VTK renders via Mesa software GL (RTD installs them through
  # `.readthedocs.yaml`; GitHub's ubuntu-latest ships them).
  "sphinx-gallery>=0.15,<1",
  "sphinx-design>=0.5,<1",
  # Bibliographic citations ({cite} roles + the References page bibliography).

# import-linter contracts — executable encoding of .claude/FRAGO.md IMPORT_RULES (L102-127).
#
# Phase 0: REPORT-ONLY baseline.
#   The codebase currently violates several of these contracts (known dependency
#   cycles maintained via lazy imports). Running `lint-imports` will report a
#   non-zero violation count — this is EXPECTED. The violation count is the
#   technical-debt baseline, not a CI gate. See scripts/check_arch.sh, which runs
#   the linter with `|| true` so CI does not fail on the baseline. Phase 7 will
#   flip this to enforced once the cycles are surgically removed.
#
# Source-of-truth: .claude/FRAGO.md "### 模块边界" IMPORT_RULES dict.

[importlinter]
root_package = frago

# --- browser/ subsystem boundaries -------------------------------------------

[importlinter:contract:browser-root]
name = browser/ NEVER imports server/, cli/, recipes/
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.browser
forbidden_modules =
    frago.server
    frago.cli
    frago.recipes

[importlinter:contract:browser-cdp]
name = browser/cdp/ NEVER imports server/, cli/, recipes/, browser/extension/
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.browser.cdp
forbidden_modules =
    frago.server
    frago.cli
    frago.recipes
    frago.browser.extension

[importlinter:contract:browser-extension]
name = browser/extension/ NEVER imports server/, cli/, browser/cdp/, browser/backends/
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.browser.extension
forbidden_modules =
    frago.server
    frago.cli
    frago.browser.cdp
    frago.browser.backends

[importlinter:contract:browser-backends]
name = browser/backends/ NEVER imports server/, cli/, recipes/
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.browser.backends
forbidden_modules =
    frago.server
    frago.cli
    frago.recipes

# --- recipes/ ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Split from the former single bundled `recipes` contract into two independent
# contracts so each edge can be judged KEPT/BROKEN on its own:
#   - recipes-server: the reverse cycle to be removed (KEPT once Phase 3 lands).
#   - recipes-browser: the open_url runtime lazy import — a PERMANENT known
#     exception per FRAGO.md, long-term BROKEN/tolerated, NOT a cycle-removal goal.

[importlinter:contract:recipes-server]
name = recipes/ NEVER imports server/, cli/ (reverse cycle, removed by Phase 3)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.recipes
forbidden_modules =
    frago.server
    frago.cli

[importlinter:contract:recipes-browser]
name = recipes/ NEVER imports browser/ (open_url runtime lazy — permanent known exception, tolerated long-term)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.recipes
forbidden_modules =
    frago.browser

# --- agent_driver/ -----------------------------------------------------------
# agent_driver ↔ server is an invisible pure-lazy bidirectional cycle (both
# directions have zero top-level imports, kept alive only by function-body lazy
# imports). This contract makes that hidden cycle visible. Initially BROKEN
# (baseline expansion, report-only); becomes KEPT after Phase 4 lands.

[importlinter:contract:agent_driver]
name = agent_driver/ NEVER imports server/, cli/ (pure-lazy cycle with server, removed by Phase 4)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.agent_driver
forbidden_modules =
    frago.server
    frago.cli

# --- viewer/ -----------------------------------------------------------------
# viewer is a server-dependent frontend feature layer (analogous to cli):
# viewer→server is a LEGAL forward dependency, so NO forbidden→server contract is
# set for it. Only the reverse-to-cli edge is forbidden (expected KEPT).

[importlinter:contract:viewer]
name = viewer/ NEVER imports cli/ (viewer→server is legal, not forbidden)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.viewer
forbidden_modules =
    frago.cli

# --- lower layers: session/, init/ -------------------------------------------

[importlinter:contract:session]
name = session/ NEVER imports server/, cli/ (pure lower layer — eager, zero reverse imports)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.session
forbidden_modules =
    frago.server
    frago.cli

[importlinter:contract:init]
name = init/ NEVER imports server/, cli/
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    frago.init
forbidden_modules =
    frago.server
    frago.cli

# --- big-picture direction: only what FRAGO.md actually states ---------------
# FRAGO.md 明确规定的方向只有 cli > server（cli 可 import server，反向禁止）。
# 下层（recipes/session/init）彼此的相对顺序 FRAGO.md 未定义，故 NEVER 在此
# 强加全序——它们对 server/cli 的"禁止反向"已由上面各 forbidden 契约覆盖。
# 在 FRAGO.md 补出下层排序之前，这里不编码未声明的规则（避免把"未定规则"伪装成债务）。

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Layered dependency direction (cli > server, per FRAGO.md)
type = layers
layers =
    frago.cli
    frago.server

    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "ARG", # flake8-unused-arguments
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
]

# pytest 用函数参数声明 fixture 依赖，不少 fixture 只要副作用（如 mock_home
# 打桩家目录、isolated_config 改配置路径），用例体里并不引用它。那是依赖声明，
# 不是「忘了用的参数」，在测试目录里只会制造噪音。
#
# ARG002 是方法参数、ARG001 是函数参数：同一件事，取决于用例写成类方法还是模块级
# 函数。原先只挡了 ARG002，是因为当时的用例都是类方法；模块级用例一多，同样的
# fixture 声明就开始报错。ARG005 同理——monkeypatch 的替身 lambda 必须保持与被替换
# 函数一致的签名，用不上的形参是契约的一部分，不是冗余。

    terok.cli | terok.tui
    terok.lib.domain
    terok.lib.orchestration
    terok.lib.core
    terok.lib.integrations

# ── Cross-package boundaries (tach can't do this) ────────────────
#
# ``protected`` contracts: "module X may ONLY be imported by modules Y, Z".
#
# Every sibling-wheel import funnels through a single adapter in
# ``terok.lib.integrations`` — that adapter is the *only* allowed
# importer.  A new ``from terok_sandbox import …`` anywhere else is a
# CI failure: route it through the adapter instead (and extend the
# adapter's re-export surface if the symbol is new).

[importlinter:contract:sandbox-boundary]
name = terok_sandbox access restricted to the integrations adapter
type = protected
protected_modules = terok_sandbox
allowed_importers =
    terok.lib.integrations.sandbox

[importlinter:contract:executor-boundary]
name = terok_executor access restricted to the integrations adapter
type = protected
protected_modules = terok_executor
allowed_importers =
    terok.lib.integrations.executor

[importlinter:contract:clearance-boundary]
name = terok_clearance access restricted to the integrations adapter
type = protected
protected_modules = terok_clearance
allowed_importers =
    terok.lib.integrations.clearance

[importlinter:contract:shield-boundary]
name = terok_shield access restricted to the integrations adapter
type = protected
protected_modules = terok_shield
allowed_importers =
    terok.lib.integrations.shield

# Import Linter Configuration for Troostwatch
# See https://import-linter.readthedocs.io/
#
# These contracts enforce the layered architecture described in docs/architecture.md.
# Run with: lint-imports (or python -m importlinter)
# Note: This is an INI configuration file, not Python code.

[importlinter]
root_package = troostwatch
include_external_packages = False


# =============================================================================
# Contract 1: Domain layer is pure (no infrastructure dependencies)
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:domain-purity]
name = Domain layer must not import infrastructure
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    troostwatch.domain
forbidden_modules =
    troostwatch.infrastructure
    troostwatch.services
    troostwatch.app
    troostwatch.interfaces


# =============================================================================
# Contract 2: Services cannot import from interfaces/app
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:services-no-interfaces]
name = Services must not import from interfaces or app
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    troostwatch.services
forbidden_modules =
    troostwatch.interfaces
    troostwatch.app


# =============================================================================
# Contract 3: CLI should not import infrastructure directly
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:cli-no-infrastructure]
name = CLI must not import infrastructure directly
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli
forbidden_modules =
    troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories
    troostwatch.infrastructure.http
allow_indirect_imports = True
ignore_imports =
    # Allowed adapters that bridge CLI to infrastructure
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.context -> troostwatch.infrastructure.http
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.context -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.context -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.context -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories.base
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.images -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.context_helpers -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.auth -> troostwatch.infrastructure.http
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.debug -> troostwatch.infrastructure.diagnostics.debug_tools
    troostwatch.interfaces.cli.bid -> troostwatch.infrastructure.http


# =============================================================================
# Contract 4: API routes should use services, not infrastructure
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:api-no-infrastructure]
name = API must not import infrastructure directly
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    troostwatch.app.api
forbidden_modules =
    troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories
    troostwatch.infrastructure.http
allow_indirect_imports = True
ignore_imports =
    # dependencies.py is the designated wiring module
    troostwatch.app.dependencies -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories
    troostwatch.app.api -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories.images
    troostwatch.app.dependencies -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db
    troostwatch.app.api -> troostwatch.infrastructure.db.repositories.images


# =============================================================================
# Contract 5: Infrastructure cannot import from higher layers
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:infrastructure-isolation]
name = Infrastructure must not import from services or interfaces
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    troostwatch.infrastructure
forbidden_modules =
    troostwatch.services
    troostwatch.interfaces
    troostwatch.app


# =============================================================================
# Contract 6: Layered architecture (informational)
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Layered architecture
type = layers
layers =
    interfaces
    app
    services
    domain
containers =
    troostwatch

## pyproject.toml for the Troostwatch package

# This file follows the [PEP 621](https://peps.python.org/pep-0621/) specification for
# Python project metadata.  It describes the Troostwatch package as it exists
# today at version 0.7.1.  The project scrapes auction data from the
# Troostwijk website, stores it in a SQLite database, calculates bidding
# exposure and provides several command‑line interfaces.

[build-system]
# Setuptools is used to build the package; a recent version is required for
# PEP 621 and pyproject support.  Wheel is included to generate a wheel
# distribution when building.
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
# Basic metadata.  The name should be unique on PyPI if you intend to
# publish the package; change this if a different name is needed.
name = "troostwatch"
# The version number is the single source of truth; read at runtime via importlib.metadata.
version = "0.7.1"
# A short, one‑line summary of what the project does.
description = "Scrape Troostwijk auctions, track bids, analyse exposure and view results via a CLI."
# A longer description taken from the README file.  When distributed, this
# ensures that the README renders correctly on package indexes.
readme = "README.md"
# The minimum Python version required.  Troostwatch uses modern type hints
# and dataclasses, so Python 3.11 or newer is recommended. Python 3.14 is
# supported when available.
requires-python = ">=3.14"
# The project’s license.  If you intend to publish, replace with the
# appropriate SPDX identifier or a license file.
license = { text = "MIT" }
# Contact information for the authors/maintainers.  Replace the email address
# with an appropriate contact if known.  Multiple authors can be listed.
authors = [
  { name = "Jochem", email = "jochem@example.com" },
]

# Runtime dependencies.  Only include external packages that are actually
# required for the package to function.  Click is used for the CLI entry
# points; BeautifulSoup and requests are suggested for future HTML parsing and
# HTTP fetching.  Rich provides colourful tables and progress bars for
# improved command‑line output.  These versions are kept broad so they will
# resolve correctly on most systems.
dependencies = [
  "click>=8.3",
  "beautifulsoup4>=4.14",  # for robust HTML parsing
  "requests>=2.32",        # HTTP client (alternative to urllib)
  "rich>=14.0",            # fancy CLI output (tables, colours)
  "aiohttp>=3.13",         # async HTTP client for concurrent fetching

    {name = "Theta AI Team", email = "developer@thetahealth.ai"},
]
# The PyPI storefront line: keep it in step with the README's opening lines.
description = "Self-hosted AI health data engine: lab reports, wearables and genetics in one standardized record, with answers that cite their sources."
readme = "README.md"
# 3.12+ is a hard floor, not a preference: the codebase uses PEP 701 f-strings
# (nested same-type quotes, e.g. utils/config/config.py), which are a SyntaxError
# on 3.11 — the package cannot even be imported there.
requires-python = ">=3.12"
# What people actually search PyPI for; the vocabulary names are the moat.
keywords = [
    "health", "health-data", "FHIR", "LOINC", "SNOMED", "wearables",
    "lab-reports", "genomics", "MCP", "agent", "AI", "LLM",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Healthcare Industry",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Medical Science Apps.",
]
# Constraint policy (this is a LIBRARY): floors only. An upper cap needs a
# reproduced breakage documented next to it — unjustified caps just create
# resolver conflicts downstream.
#
# ── Why base is one line ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# This project ships in two forms and they want opposite things. The PyPI
# package is a LIBRARY and wants to be small enough that nobody has to think
# about it. The Docker application is a PRODUCT and wants everything in the
# box. Until 1.3.0 the pyproject described only the second: base carried the
# whole ① Collect extraction stack and three LLM SDKs, so a consumer who wanted
# ② Translate — offline name → LOINC, UCUM units — installed 93 packages and
# 245 MB, of which mirobody itself was 29 MB.
#
# That was not merely wasteful. `mcp>=2.0.0` in base made the package
# UNINSTALLABLE alongside `langchain-mcp-adapters` (which caps `mcp<2.0.0`),
# and the downstream fix was to override this file's metadata in the consumer's
# lockfile — i.e. the contract was wrong enough that using the library required
# lying about it.
#
# So: base is what `resolve()` and the vocabulary modules actually need, which
# is numpy and nothing else (measured — `import mirobody.engine` pulls zero
# third-party packages; numpy is imported inside `OfflineResolver.__init__`).
dependencies = [
    # ② Translate. `_bundle` and `_strtab` read the shipped offset arrays with
    # it, and the resolver builds its lookup orders from them. It went
    # undeclared for a long time and worked only because pandas (since
    # removed) happened to pull it in, i.e. `mirobody resolve` depended on a
    # transitive accident.
    "numpy",
]

[project.scripts]
# The single entry point, source checkout and PyPI install alike:
# `mirobody serve|worker|parse|resolve`, or `python -m mirobody …` where a
# console
# script may not survive (compose persists site-packages but not the venv's
# bin/). Replaces the former repo-root main.py / main_worker.py, which were
# not shipped in the wheel — a PyPI install had no way to start the server.
mirobody = "mirobody.cli:main"
# The stdio MCP server alone, for `uvx --from mirobody mirobody-mcp`; the same
# as `mirobody mcp`, which is what the MCP Registry entry (server.json) runs.
mirobody-mcp = "mirobody.mcp.stdio:main"

# ── Extras: one bracket a human types, one bucket the image installs ─────────
#
# The test for whether something deserves an extra is not "is it a separable
# concern" — it is "will somebody choose it". 1.2.2 had six extras and exactly
# one of them was ever installed by anything: `requirements.txt` reads
# `-e .[agents]`, one line, no choice. `[server]` was referenced nowhere and
# could not usefully be installed alone anyway (`mirobody serve` and `worker`
# both refuse without the agent layer). `[cn]` was referenced nowhere at all,
# and was not an axis: it bundled an object-storage backend with an LLM vendor
# SDK under a country name, while their siblings (aws.py, the OpenAI/Anthropic/
# Gemini clients) sat in `[server]` and base. `storage/factory.py` iterates
# `AbstractStorage.__subclasses__()` — aws and aliyun are peers in the code and
# were split by geography only in the packaging.
#
# Three runtime extras remain, one per question (plus [test] for working on it):
#
#   [parse]  do you also want to read documents?   <- the one real choice
#   [agent]  the agent harness as a library, without the server (1.4.0)
#   [app]    everything; this is what the image installs
[project.optional-dependencies]
# ① Collect, single-file surface: `mirobody parse labs.pdf` — a lab report in,
# standardized LOINC readings out, one model key, no database and no server.
# The extraction formats and the model clients are one extra rather than two
# because `parse` needs both and nothing else needs either: an extraction
# backend with no model cannot read a scan, and the client factory exists to
# feed the extractor.
#
# `mirobody parse` checks for this extra up front and prints what to install,
# the same way `serve`/`worker` already do for the agent layer — see
# `cli._require_extra`.
parse = [
    # Documents. Every entry here is imported by name somewhere under
    # mirobody/; a package that only *typed* a file (rarfile, py7zr — archives
    # are recognised, never opened), a second library for a job one already
    # does (pypdf beside pypdfium2 + pdfplumber), or a
    # 68 MB dependency for two functions (pandas, for turning a sheet into
    # text) has been removed — see CHANGELOG 1.4.0.
    # The one PDF library: text layer AND page rendering (`documents/extract.py`).
    "pypdfium2>=4.30.0",
    "Pillow>=11.1.0",
    # `.xlsx` read directly (file_abstract_extractor.py); the pre-2007 binary
    # `.xls` is not supported, and never was — the old xlrd fallback was not
    # installed either.
    "openpyxl>=3.1",
    # Word and PowerPoint. Both read only the modern zip-based formats, which is
    # exactly the honest boundary: `.docx`/`.pptx` are supported, and legacy
    # binary `.doc`/`.ppt` stay OUT of `SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS` rather than being
    # accepted and then refused after the upload — which is what they used to do.
    "python-docx>=1.1",
    "python-pptx>=1.0",
    # The engine's own model access, via direct SDKs. The agent FRAMEWORK stack
    # (LangChain, deepagents) is a different thing and lives in [app].
    "azure-identity>=1.15.0",  # Azure OpenAI WIF token provider (utils/config/llm.py)
    "openai>=2.11.0",
    # `_build_anthropic` did a bare `import anthropic` that only resolved
    # because langchain-anthropic dragged it in, so configuring an Anthropic key
    # without the agent layer failed at client construction.
    # Floor at 1.5, and deliberately no upper cap: the newest SDK is where the
    # newest models are supported. 1.x REMOVED `temperature`, `top_p` and
    # `top_k` from the messages API, which turned every extraction call into a
    # TypeError before a request was built — so `backends_anthropic` filters
    # parameters against the installed signature rather than a hardcoded list,
    # and the next removal costs a DEBUG line instead of an outage.
    "anthropic>=1.5",
    # Floor at 2.0: the Interactions API server dropped the legacy turn-list
    # schema (breaking change, May 2026) and now requires the 2.x 'steps' schema,
    # which only the >=2.0 SDK can send/parse. No upper cap.
    "google-genai>=2.0.0",
    # `utils/config` is on the parse path (the client factory reads config), and
    # it needs these three.
    "python-dotenv",
    # Uses only the modern YAML() API (utils/config/config.py); load+dump of
    # the real config.yaml verified on 0.19, so no upper cap.
    "ruamel.yaml>=0.17",
    "cryptography",
    # `utils/net.fetch_bounded`, the bounded downloader a library consumer
    # fetches caller-supplied URLs with.
    "aiohttp",
    # `utils/http.py` is built on Starlette's Request/Response and
    # `utils/__init__` re-exports them, so importing anything under utils needs
    # it. (FastAPI is a web *framework* and stays in [app].)
    "starlette",
    "pydantic",
    # `utils/prompts.py` — the strict Jinja renderer every prompt package uses.
    "jinja2",
]

# ③a The agent layer as a LIBRARY: the harness middleware (fault containment,
# retry governance, invalid-call repair, prompt caching), the virtual-filesystem
# backends, the checkpointer, the LLM client factory, `hitl`, the prompt renderer,
# and the tool surface (`mirobody.mcp.tool` publishes the same tools an MCP client
# sees; its schemas come from the `mcp` SDK). A consumer that runs its own
# deepagents agent installs this and nothing else — no HTTP server, no object
# stores, no mail. `mirobody.mcp.service` (serving those tools over HTTP) is [app].
agent = [
    # The checkpointer (langgraph-checkpoint-postgres) and the file-system
    # projections talk to Postgres directly.
    "psycopg[binary]",
    # 3.2 is the first with `check=`, which replaces a connection a Postgres
    # restart killed instead of failing the request that drew it.
    "psycopg[pool]",
    "psycopg-pool>=3.2",
    "jinja2",
    # `utils/config` — the client factory, the checkpointer and the registry
    # read configuration through it. `mirobody.utils` itself resolves its
    # re-exports lazily, so importing one helper (`utils.sse`, `utils.prompts`,
    # …) pulls none of this.
    "ruamel.yaml",
    "python-dotenv",
    "cryptography",
    # `utils/net.fetch_bounded` (see [parse]).
    "aiohttp",
    # Model clients: the two families the shipped config.yaml uses. Every other
    # family is one `pip install` away and NOT declared here: `init_chat_model`
    # imports a provider package lazily and names it in the error when it is
    # missing. So a deployment that configures `llm_type: anthropic` (deepagents
    # brings langchain-anthropic anyway), a Vertex-hosted model
    # (`langchain-google-vertexai`, which drags the 170 MB
    # `google-cloud-aiplatform` behind it) or an Azure OpenAI WIF login
    # (`azure-identity`, which [parse] carries) adds that one package — instead
    # of every install carrying all of them for a configuration it never has.
    # `langchain_community` was declared and never imported; gone.
    # 1.4.0 is deepagents 0.7.14's floor.
    "langchain>=1.4.0",
    "langchain-openai>=1.4.3",
    # 4.2.4 relaxed its google-genai cap to <3.0.0 (earlier 4.x pinned <2.0.0,
    # which would block the google-genai>=2.0 required by [parse]).
    # 4.4.0 is the version verified to round-trip Gemini 3.x's
    # `thought_signature` through a tool loop (see `gemini-flash` in
    # config.llm.yaml). No upper cap: newer packages support newer models, and
    # the one time a floor without a verified lower bound bit us, `anthropic`
    # 1.x had silently removed `temperature` from `messages.create`.
    "langchain-google-genai>=4.4.0",
    # Floor at 0.7.5. 0.7 is where the BackendProtocol settled: the deprecated
    # `*_info` / `grep_raw` shims are gone (we never used them), `glob`/`grep`
    # take `path: str | None`, `grep` gained a `max_count` cap that
    # CompositeBackend splits across mounts, and `delete` arrived as an optional
    # protocol method (PgFilesystemBackend does not implement it; the tool is
    # excluded by name — see agent/agent.py `_EXCLUDED_NATIVE_TOOLS`).
    # NOTE 0.7 also DROPPED `TodoListMiddleware` from the default middleware
    # stack, so `write_todos` no longer exists unless a caller adds it back.
    # the agent intentionally does not — see agent/agent.py `_build_agent`.
    # Floor raised to 0.7.14 on 2026-09-16; the API this repository binds
    # (`create_deep_agent`, `HarnessProfile`, the backends, `get_model_provider`)
    # is byte-identical across 0.7.5..0.7.14, and 0.7.14 pulls langchain 1.4.
    "deepagents>=0.7.19",
    # In-process JS/TS interpreter middleware — the agent's code sandbox, with
    # no external sandbox service or key. 0.3.7 is deepagents 0.7.14's floor
    # for its own `quickjs` extra.
    "langchain-quickjs>=0.3.7",
    # Conversation memory: the agent graph is compiled with an AsyncPostgresSaver
    # keyed on thread_id = session_id, so LangGraph replays the real message
    # objects. This replaced a hand-rolled rebuild of history from persisted UI
    # chunks (the deleted chat/history_replay.rebuild_canonical_messages) —
    # see agent/checkpointer.py.
    "langgraph-checkpoint-postgres>=3.1.2",
    # Floor at 2.0 for two reasons, both verified against the installed source
    # rather than release notes:
    #   1. 2.0.0 is the first release implementing protocol revision 2026-07-28
    #      (DiscoverRequest/Result, InputRequiredResult/MRTR, CacheHint);
    #      1.29.0 tops out at 2025-11-25.
    #   2. Its `func_metadata` generates our tool inputSchemas. The hand-rolled
    #      parser it replaced got Literal, Enum, bare dict and Annotated wrong.
    # NOTE `mcp.server.fastmcp` was REMOVED in 2.0 (it is `mcp.server.mcpserver`
    # now), and the third-party `fastmcp` package does not yet import against
    # 2.0 at all (`McpError` was renamed `MCPError`), so it is not an option.
    "mcp>=2.0.0",
]

# ③ Everything — the HTTP/chat/MCP server, its stores, and the agent layer.
# `requirements.txt` is `-e .[app]` and that is the only thing that installs
# it: `docker compose` mounts the checkout and pip-installs from it, so PyPI is
# not a deployment path and this extra never asks anyone to choose a backend.
# Both object stores and every model vendor go in, unconditionally — oss2 is
# 0.3 MB and aioboto3 0.2 MB, and a decision point costs more than that.
app = [
    "mirobody[parse]",
    "mirobody[agent]",
    # HTTP surface.
    "fastapi",
    "python-multipart",
    "uvicorn",
    # Stores.
    "sqlalchemy",
    # SQLAlchemy declares greenlet only under platform markers and extras, so
    # its async engine can be missing it on an otherwise-correct install.
    "greenlet",
    # Object storage — `storage/factory.py` tries every AbstractStorage
    # subclass and falls back to local, so which one is a config question at
    # runtime, never an install-time one.
    "aioboto3",
    "oss2",
    # boto3 is the SYNC half of `utils/config/llm.py::_build_bedrock`, and it
    # was never declared anywhere: it arrived transitively via aioboto3, which
    # is the same class of bug as the undeclared python-multipart / starlette /
    # anthropic before it. Named here so it stops being an accident.
    "boto3",
    # Identity and mail.
    "pyjwt",
    "webauthn>=2.0.0",
    "mandrill",
    # OAuth1 — among the shipped providers, only Garmin still speaks it.
    "requests-oauthlib",
]

# The suite a clone runs. CI's first job is `pip install -e '.[test]'` followed
# by `pytest -q`, which is how a minimal install that aborts at collection is
# caught; without this extra that job installs numpy and exits 127 on a missing
# pytest, which is what happened when `indicator-build` was deleted beside it.
test = ["pytest", "pytest-asyncio", "pytest-sugar", "import-linter", "ruff", "build"]


[project.urls]
"Homepage" = "https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody"
"Bug Reports" = "https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/issues"
"Source" = "https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["mirobody", "mirobody.*"]
# `mirobody/tests/` is the part of the suite in git: the resolver score the
# README publishes, the cross-language identity checks a terminology
# contributor runs, the server's security gates, and `test_skills.py`, the
# public evidence for the agent skills. The build backend ships only that evidence module and prunes the
# checkout-only gates; `scripts/check_wheel_data.py` enforces the split.
#
# Everything else lives in a gitignored `tests/` at the repo root, so the local
# regression suite can be thorough without becoming public API. That rule was
# briefly dropped on `refactor/deep-agent-only` and 92 test files reached the
# public remote; `.gitignore` carries the account.

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"mirobody" = [
    # PEP 561: without this marker every type checker ignores the annotations
    # in this package entirely, so a consumer gets `Any` for `Resolution`,
    # `ParsedQuantity` and everything else no matter how well typed it is.
    "py.typed",
    "**/*.md",
    "**/*.sql",
    "**/*.json",
    "**/*.yaml",
    "**/*.jinja",
    "**/*.so",
    # ── engine data bundles (Git LFS) ────────────────────────────────────────
    # These are not optional extras: `mirobody.engine.resolve` — the front door
    # of ② Translate, and the one line the README leads with — reads
    # res/loinc/fhir_loinc_bundle.tar.gz and res/loinc/aliases_src/*.tsv
    # at import time. Until 1.0.62 only *.bin was listed here, so every published
    # wheel shipped an engine that could not resolve anything. Keep .gz/.npy/.tsv
    # in this list; scripts/check_wheel_data.py enforces it at build time.
    "**/*.bin",
    "**/*.gz",
    # Public, small genotype examples ship with the testing toolbox; keep
    # these globs narrow so a raw personal upload cannot enter a wheel.
    "testing/genomics/*.vcf",
    "testing/genomics/*.txt",
    "testing/genomics/*.csv",
    "testing/genomics/*.bgz",
    "testing/genomics/*.zip",
    # The read-only dbSNP site index is queried on genotype import.
    "**/*.sqlite3",
    # res/ucum/ucum-essence.xml: UCUM's own table, verbatim (its NOTICE says why).
    "**/*.xml",
    "**/*.npy",
    "**/*.tsv",
    "**/*.NOTICE",
    "**/*.html",
    "**/*.htm",
    "**/*.js",
    "**/*.css",
    "**/*.png",
    "**/*.jpg",
    "**/*.jpeg",
    "**/*.svg",
    "**/*.ico",
]
# NOTE: there is deliberately no [tool.setuptools.exclude-package-data] here.
# It does not work against the broad `**/*.bin` / `**/*.npy` includes above —
# setuptools keeps files the include globs matched — and a stanza that looks
# like it prunes 28 MB while pruning nothing is worse than none. The pruning
# lives in scripts/build_backend.py::_BUILD_ONLY_DATA (wheel) and MANIFEST.in
# (sdist), and scripts/check_wheel_data.py fails the build if it stops working.

# (The web client's static assets live at repo-root frontend/ — outside the
# package on purpose. A pip install serves API + MCP; the UI comes from a
# checkout (Docker/source) or the hosted client at mirobody.ai. This is what
# took the wheel from ~57MB of which 8MB was JavaScript, to engine + data only.)

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = {attr = "mirobody.__version__"}

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
disable_test_id_escaping_and_forfeit_all_rights_to_community_support = true
# Collect bare `async def` tests via pytest-asyncio (already in the [test]
# extra). Without this the async tests fail with "async def functions are not
# natively supported" on every machine.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Two roots. `mirobody/tests/` holds the gates that ship: the resolver
# benchmark the README scores itself against, cross-language identity and the
# server's security gates. `tests/` is the local regression
# suite and is gitignored: internal quality control that can be as detailed as
# it needs to be without becoming part of the project's public surface. It is simply absent from a clone, and
# pytest skips a testpath that does not exist. (Historical note: the README
# once documented a tests/ directory along with `-m mcp` / `-m chat` and other
# markers, none of which existed — following it produced "0 tests collected".)
testpaths = ["mirobody", "tests"]
# Scratch and artifact directories are never test roots. `out/` in particular
# holds review artifacts that may include a full clone of this repo — recursing
# into one collides every test module with its twin ("import file mismatch").
norecursedirs = [".*", "build", "dist", "node_modules", "out", "frontend", "__pycache__"]
markers = [
    "needs_db: requires a live PostgreSQL (deselect with -m 'not needs_db')",
    "needs_llm: calls a real model provider and costs money",
]

# ── Architectural boundary, machine-enforced (run: lint-imports) ─────────────
#
# The engine follows the langchain / langchain-core layering: the DATA ENGINE
# (① Collect: collect · ② Translate: translate, plus the shared utils/user/mcp/task
# infra) must stay importable without any agent framework, while the AGENT
# LAYER (③ Agent: agent, server) is the only place LangChain and friends
# may appear. These contracts turn that rule from a convention into a CI check.
# import-linter parses function-local imports too, so lazy imports can't sneak
# a violation past it.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["mirobody"]
# Required for contracts that forbid EXTERNAL packages (the langchain family).
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "engine is agent-framework-free (the langchain-core rule)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    # The LIBRARY — what `pip install mirobody` ships and a consumer imports.
    "mirobody._bundle",
    "mirobody._strtab",
    "mirobody.engine",
    "mirobody.lexical",
    "mirobody.kernel",
    "mirobody.kernel.citations",
    "mirobody.kernel.connect",
    "mirobody.kernel.events",
    "mirobody.kernel.evidence",
    "mirobody.kernel.meds",
    "mirobody.kernel.memory",
    "mirobody.kernel.metrics",
    "mirobody.kernel.ops",
    "mirobody.kernel.query",
    "mirobody.kernel.overlay",
    "mirobody.kernel.quality",
    "mirobody.kernel.series",
    "mirobody.kernel.sink",
    "mirobody.kernel.tools",
    "mirobody.units",
    "mirobody.kernel.decoders",
    "mirobody.value_scale",
    "mirobody.zh_fold",
    "mirobody.translate",
    # The rest of the engine.
    "mirobody.collect",
    "mirobody.documents",
    "mirobody.utils",
    "mirobody.user",
    "mirobody.task",
    "mirobody.mcp",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "langchain",
    "langchain_core",
    "langchain_openai",
    "langchain_anthropic",
    "langchain_google_genai",
    "langgraph",
    "deepagents",
    "langchain_quickjs",
]
# (The former router seam is gone: pulse/router moved to server/routers, where
# importing the agent layer is legal. The engine list needs no exemptions here.)

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the library layer stands alone (the numpy-only rule)"
# What makes `dependencies = ["numpy"]` true, and the only way to keep it true.
# These modules are everything a default `pip install mirobody` is for, and
# every import they add is a package somebody who only wanted `unit_family` has
# to download. They may import each other and nothing else in this package —
# `mirobody.utils` alone would put starlette, ruamel, aiohttp and cryptography
# back in base.
#
# `mirobody.engine` is deliberately NOT in this list: `parse_file` reaches into
# `utils.llm`, which is the [parse] extra, and does so inside the function so
# `resolve` never pays for it. That seam is the exception that needs the rule
# written down. `mirobody.translate` codes through the engine and inherits
# the same exemption; it is held to the agent-framework rule above instead.
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "mirobody._bundle",
    "mirobody._strtab",
    "mirobody.lexical",
    "mirobody.kernel",
    "mirobody.kernel.citations",
    "mirobody.kernel.connect",
    "mirobody.kernel.events",
    "mirobody.kernel.evidence",
    "mirobody.kernel.meds",
    "mirobody.kernel.memory",
    "mirobody.kernel.metrics",
    "mirobody.kernel.ops",
    "mirobody.kernel.query",
    "mirobody.kernel.overlay",
    "mirobody.kernel.quality",
    "mirobody.kernel.series",
    "mirobody.kernel.sink",
    "mirobody.kernel.tools",
    "mirobody.units",
    "mirobody.kernel.decoders",
    "mirobody.value_scale",
    "mirobody.zh_fold",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "mirobody.agent",
    "mirobody.engine",
    "mirobody.mcp",
    "mirobody.collect",
    "mirobody.documents",
    "mirobody.server",
    "mirobody.task",
    "mirobody.user",
    "mirobody.utils",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the library layer is stdlib + numpy (third-party packages are forbidden)"

    "mirobody.kernel",

    "mirobody.kernel.connect",
    "mirobody.kernel.events",
    "mirobody.kernel.evidence",
    "mirobody.lexical",
    "mirobody.kernel.meds",
    "mirobody.kernel.memory",
    "mirobody.kernel.metrics",
    "mirobody.kernel.ops",
    "mirobody.kernel.overlay",
    "mirobody.kernel.quality",
    "mirobody.kernel.query",
    "mirobody.kernel.series",

# ── Lint gate (run: ruff check mirobody) ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# Narrow on purpose: every rule here is either a real defect class (F: undefined
# names, unused imports/variables, duplicate definitions; B905: a zip that
# silently truncates; B006: a mutable default) or a modernisation the 3.12 floor
# makes unambiguous (UP: PEP 585/604 annotations, datetime.UTC). Style rules
# that would generate churn without catching anything (import sorting, line
# length, quote style) are deliberately absent — add one only with the diff that
# applies it.
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 120
extend-exclude = ["frontend"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Narrow by design, and every addition below earns its place by catching a class
# of DEFECT rather than a style preference:
#   B    flake8-bugbear — late-binding closures, mutable defaults, mutable
#        class attributes. B904 and B007 are ignored below.
#   ISC  implicit string concatenation — the missing comma in a list literal.
#   PLE  pylint errors. PLE0604 is excluded below: it cannot see through a
#        dynamically built `__all__`, which is how the lazy (PEP 562) packages
#        here export.
#   RUF100  a `noqa` that no longer suppresses anything. A stale one silently
#        swallows the NEXT finding on that line.
#   C4, PIE  comprehension and simplification defects, three findings between them.
#   TID  a relative import that leaves its directory (TID252, at ruff's default
#        `parents` level; plain `from .sibling` stays legal). See CLAUDE.md:
#        the same dependency was being spelled two ways, so grep stopped
#        answering "who imports kernel".
select = [
    "E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "UP",
    "B", "ISC", "C4", "PIE", "PLE", "RUF100",
    "RET505", "RET507", "PLW0602", "TID",
]
ignore = [
    "B007",   # unused loop variable. `for k, v in d.items()` when only `v` is read
              # names the key for a reader even when the code does not use it;
              # rewriting it to `.values()` is churn, not a fix. (owner, 2026-09-08)
    "B904",   # `raise ... from` inside `except`. It only changes what a traceback
              # PRINTS ("during handling of the above" vs "direct cause"), and the
              # original is in the chain either way — not worth 33 mechanical
              # edits across the tree. (owner, 2026-09-08)
    "E402",   # imports after code: three routers register models before importing helpers on purpose
    "E701",   # `if x: return` one-liners in the strtab/bundle readers
    "E741",   # `l` as a variable in a few tight loops
    "UP042",  # (str, Enum) -> StrEnum: the enum values are persisted wire strings; not worth the diff
    "PLE0604",  # `__all__` built with `*_EXPORTS`: the lazy packages compute it, and
                # the linter cannot prove the members are strings.
]
# NOT selected, each for a reason, so the next person does not re-litigate it:
#   G004 (1,110 findings) f-string in a log call. Worth doing — lazy formatting
#        and the PHI policy both want %-style — but 1,110 mechanical edits would
#        bury any real change in the same commit. Its own PR.
#   DTZ  (68) `datetime.now()` without a tz. DELIBERATE here: `series_data.time`,
#        the device point buffer, is a NAIVE LOCAL wall clock and the aggregation
#        pass is built on that (th_observation itself stores timestamptz with its
#        zone). Selecting DTZ would ask us to break the buffer's contract to
#        satisfy a linter.
# TID252 was listed here as "relative imports are used throughout by choice".
# Reversed 2026-09-14 on measurement, not taste: numpy nests deeper than we do
# with zero parent-relative imports, fastapi likewise, and nothing in an
# eighteen-library sample reached the four dots this package had. It is selected
# above now. import-linter still guards the layering; TID252 keeps the edge
# visible to a reader.

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
# FastAPI declares a parameter's SOURCE in its default: `file: UploadFile =
# File(...)`, `user = Depends(auth)`. B008 is right about mutable defaults in
# general and wrong about this framework's entire calling convention.
extend-immutable-calls = [
    "fastapi.File", "fastapi.Form", "fastapi.Body", "fastapi.Query",
    "fastapi.Path", "fastapi.Header", "fastapi.Cookie", "fastapi.Depends",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Package __init__ files re-export for their consumers; every import there is
# "unused" to a linter and load-bearing to the package.
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]

[project]
name = "graphknows"
description = "Agentic memory: knowledge-graph ingestion + hybrid retrieval, llm-free or ontology-guided"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
authors = [{ name = "Tamás Mákos", email = "tamasmakos@gmail.com" }]
keywords = [
    "memory",
    "knowledge-graph",
    "agents",
    "retrieval",
    "rag",
    "ontology",
    "mcp",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
]
dynamic = ["version"]
dependencies = [
    # Batteries-included: `pip install graphknows` gives a fully working memory
    # service (local extraction, embeddings, analytics, parsers) that also serves
    # MCP out of the box — and, with a key and `Memory(mode="llm_assisted")`, the
    # LLM decoder too. Both modes are the contract surface, so neither sits behind
    # an extra; only the injectable RDF/OWL stack (`ontology`) and the optional
    # adapters do.
    "pydantic>=2.7.0",
    # env_file loading in settings.py needs python-dotenv, but pydantic-settings
    # already requires it unconditionally (not behind an extra) — no separate
    # declaration needed here.
    "pydantic-settings>=2.2.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "numpy>=1.26.0",
    "dateparser>=1.2.0",
    # extraction (llm_free) + embeddings
    # `gliner` (not just gliner2) is required: entities/gliner_model.py loads
    # knowledgator/gliner-relex-large-v1.0 through `from gliner import GLiNER`.
    # It is NOT a transitive dependency of gliner2 — omitting it breaks the
    # default llm_free extraction path with ModuleNotFoundError on first ingest.
    "gliner>=0.2.26",
    # Capped below 2.0: gliner2 2.0.0 moved peft/torch/transformers/safetensors
    # out of the base install and behind a `local` extra, so `pip install gliner2`
    # imports fine but cannot load a model ("No module named 'peft'"), and
    # `gliner2[local]` pins transformers<5 which this resolution cannot satisfy.
    # The cap also makes the Dockerfile's lock-free `uv pip install ".[assisted]"`
    # agree with uv.lock, which pins 1.3.1.
    "gliner2>=0.1.0,<2",
    "spacy>=3.7.0",
    "sentence-transformers>=3.0.0",
    # Imported DIRECTLY by embedder.py, gliner_model.py and
    # _gliner2_verifier.py — not merely pulled in by sentence-transformers.
    # Relying on the transitive edge means a sentence-transformers release that
    # drops or re-pins any of them silently breaks us. The Dockerfile also
    # installs torch from an explicit index (CPU by default), which needs the
    # constraint declared here to resolve consistently.
    "torch>=2.4.0",
    "transformers>=4.44.0",
    "huggingface-hub>=0.24.0",
    # BM25 sparse channel in retrieval/retriever.py. Was undeclared and
    # therefore absent, so `except ImportError` silently degraded the channel to
    # a tf-style scorer — a fused retrieval source that looked live and was not.
    "rank-bm25>=0.2.2",
    # WordNet/FrameNet lookups in the default (llm_free) relation path:
    # ingestion/extraction/relations/_lingfeatures.py and frames/framenet.py.
    # Core, not eval-only — those call sites guard LookupError (missing *corpus*),
    # which does not catch the ModuleNotFoundError raised by a missing *package*.
    "nltk>=3.10.2",  # PYSEC-2026-3726 fixed in 3.10.2
    # plug-and-play MCP server. Capped below 2.0: that release removed
    # `mcp.server.fastmcp`, which graphknows.server.mcp imports, so the server
    # raises BrokenInstallError on import. The cap is here rather than in the
    # lock because the image installs with `uv pip install ".[assisted]"` — it
    # resolves from THESE constraints and never reads uv.lock, so a lock pin is
    # silently ignored on every rebuild.
    "mcp>=1.0.0,<2",
    # The LLM decoder (`Memory(mode="llm_assisted")`). Core, not an extra: the
    # mode is part of the contract surface, and an extra that gates half of that
    # surface is a documentation bug waiting to happen (ADR 0003). `llm_free`
    # installs carry them unused — the cost of the swap, accepted deliberately.
    # `litellm` is declared beside dspy because the decoder imports it directly
    # (typed retry signals, the model-map registration that makes structured
    # output reach the provider), not only through dspy.
    "dspy>=3.2.1",
    "litellm>=1.85.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Injectable RDF/OWL ontology: what the release image installs
# (`deploy/Dockerfile`), what the dev image and CI sync, and what the five
# ontology MissingExtraError call sites name.
#
# `networkx` sits beside rdflib for graphknows.symbolic.ontology.rdf: projecting a
# folder of RDF needs a multigraph with parallel predicate-keyed edges, and the
# label-keyed taxonomy needs cycle detection and a topological order. Both are
# imported inside functions behind a MissingExtraError guard, so a base install
# pulls neither.
#
# The `assisted` extra is GONE (ADR 0003): dspy and litellm are core, because
# `llm_assisted` is part of the contract surface. `pip install
# 'graphknows[assisted]'` now fails; RDF users want `graphknows[ontology]`.
ontology = ["rdflib>=7.0.0", "networkx>=3.0"]
# Framework adapter. Genuinely optional — nothing in the core paths imports it,
# and it is lazily imported behind a MissingExtraError guard. The `langchain`
# extra was removed with its adapter: `GraphKnowsRetriever` had zero importers
# (no test, example, eval, or docs page) and raised a bare ImportError, so the
# extra it named guarded nothing.
langgraph = ["langgraph>=0.2.0"]
# Langfuse tracing for the LangGraph example. Nothing in the library imports it
# — the example builds the callback only when LANGFUSE_* is set.
#
# `langfuse>=3` is not cosmetic: the 2.x SDK imports `langchain.callbacks`,
# which langchain 1.x deleted, so 2.x cannot be used with any current langchain.
# The `langchain` meta-package is a real requirement, not a transitive one —
# langfuse's integration imports it directly and raises if it is absent, and
# langchain-openai/langgraph alone pull only langchain-core.
observability = ["langfuse>=3.0", "langchain>=1.0"]

# Every extra named by a MissingExtraError call site MUST appear above;
# `MissingExtraError.KNOWN_EXTRAS` and tests/test_packaging.py enforce it. For a
# missing *core* dependency raise BrokenInstallError instead — there is no
# extra to install, and suggesting one is a dead end.

[dependency-groups]

    # permit the violation. A gate that documents its own bypass is not a gate.
    "import-linter>=2.11",

    # environment member, not an ephemeral `uvx` call like pip-audit/zizmor: it
    # matches imported module names against the *installed* distributions, so
    # it has to see this project's own resolved environment to work at all.
    "deptry>=0.25.0",
]
eval = [
    "datasets>=2.19.0",
    "pandas>=2.2.0",
    "pytest>=8.0.0",

    # dependency — see [project.dependencies]. Declaring it here too was what
    # let the Docker image satisfy a production import from a dev-only group.
]

[tool.uv]
# Floors on TRANSITIVE packages, to clear advisories the dependency audit
# (`scripts/gate.sh`, `.pip-audit-ignore`) reports against the resolved runtime
# set. They are constraints, not dependencies: graphknows imports neither, so
# declaring them in [project.dependencies] would be a lie deptry rightly flags —
# a constraint only says "if something pulls this in, not below this version".
#
# Both entered the audited set when dspy and litellm became core (ADR 0003): the
# audit exports the runtime closure, which used to exclude them with the extra.
# Drop a line once the puller's own floor overtakes it.
constraint-dependencies = [
    "aiohttp>=3.14.3",   # litellm; PYSEC-2026-3545/3546/3547
    "json-repair>=0.60.1",  # dspy; GHSA-xf7x-x43h-rpqh
]

[tool.deptry]
# `known_first_party`: deptry guesses local modules by iterating the *contents*
# of the scanned root, so when the root passed on the command line is the
# package directory itself (`deptry graphknows`, required below to keep
# evaluation/'s legitimate eval-group imports out of scope) it never adds
# "graphknows" itself to that guessed set — every internal `import graphknows`
# / `from graphknows import ...` line then reads as DEP003 (a transitive
# dependency). Declaring it here is the documented escape hatch, not a
# workaround for a real drift.
known_first_party = ["graphknows"]

# First run (27 Aug 2026) of `uv run deptry graphknows --config pyproject.toml`
# on this environment (`uv sync --group dev`, no optional extras installed)
# reported exactly four DEP002 (unused dependency) findings and nothing else:
#   - python-dotenv  ([project.dependencies] — genuinely unimported anywhere
#     under graphknows/; removed (#218) — pydantic-settings already requires
#     it unconditionally for env_file loading)
#   - scipy          ([project.dependencies] — zero references under
#     graphknows/ despite the dependency comment claiming a direct import;
#     removed (#218))
#   - langfuse        (`observability` extra — deliberate, ignored below)
#   - langchain       (`observability` extra — deliberate, ignored below)
# No DEP003/DEP004 findings this run.
#
# Verified against deptry's own docs (https://deptry.com/usage/, v0.25.1):
# [project.dependencies] / [project.optional-dependencies] are extracted as
# regular dependencies, and groups under [dependency-groups] are extracted as
# *development* dependencies BY DEFAULT — no group config needed. Development
# dependencies are exempt from the unused-dependency rule (DEP002). So the
# `dev` and `eval` groups need no `pep621_dev_dependency_groups` entry here;
# that setting is deprecated in favour of `--optional-dependencies-dev-groups`,
# which concerns [project.optional-dependencies] extras, not PEP 735 groups —
# writing it would be a no-op on a deprecated option. This is what makes
# DEP004 (a dev-group package that a shipped module imports) fire out of the
# box, which is the actual class of defect this gate exists to catch: nltk
# sat in the `eval` group while graphknows/ imported it, breaking a plain
# `pip install graphknows` while the container stayed green because
# Dockerfile installs `--group dev --group eval` (see #204).

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
DEP002 = [
    # 27 Aug 2026: `observability` extra. [project.optional-dependencies]'s own
    # comment says it: nothing in the library imports langfuse/langchain, the
    # LangGraph example builds the tracing callback only when LANGFUSE_* env
    # vars are set. Deliberately unused by graphknows/ itself. Remove this
    # entry once the extra is either imported somewhere in graphknows/ or
    # dropped.
    "langfuse",   # 27 Aug 2026
    "langchain",  # 27 Aug 2026
]

[tool.bandit]
skips = ["B101"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = "--import-mode=importlib"
# pytest.ini used to take precedence over this table, so this setting was never
# applied — async tests only ran because each carried an explicit
# @pytest.mark.asyncio. Now that pytest.ini is gone, it actually binds.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
pythonpath = ["."]
markers = [
    "integration: marks tests that require live infrastructure (ArcadeDB) — excluded from CI unit test run",
    "unit: marks pure unit tests with no infrastructure dependencies",
    "slow: marks tests that build or install a real artifact (minutes, not seconds)",

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"
# The agent harness is tracked (so its rules survive a clone) but it is not this
# package's code: these are vendored skill helpers, and scripts/gate.sh lints
# `graphknows evaluation tests` only. Without this the pre-commit hook — which has no
# path scope of its own — holds a third-party skill to graphknows' docstring rules.
extend-exclude = [".claude"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "I",    # isort
    "D",    # pydocstyle
    "C90",  # mccabe complexity
    "N",    # naming
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear — likely bugs, mutable defaults, loop-var capture
    "BLE",  # blind except — catches `except Exception:` without variable binding
    "TRY",  # tryceratops — exception anti-patterns
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify — boolean traps, redundant conditions
    "ERA",  # eradicate — commented-out dead code
    "RUF",  # Ruff-specific rules
    # Silent-swallow detectors. This repo's recurring defect is not a crash, it
    # is code that runs, passes and does nothing: a BM25 channel that scored
    # with a fallback, a reranker that was a no-op, a verifier score computed
    # and discarded. Every one hid behind a swallowed exception.
    "S110",  # try-except-pass
    "S112",  # try-except-continue
]
ignore = [
    "E501",   # line too long — formatter handles this
    "D100",   # missing docstring in public module — enforced per-file
    "D104",   # missing docstring in public package
    "D105",   # missing docstring in magic method (__aenter__, __aexit__, etc.)
    "D107",   # missing docstring in __init__
    "D203",   # one-blank-line-before-class — conflicts with D211
    "D213",   # multi-line-summary-second-line — conflicts with D212
    "TRY003",  # long messages outside exception class — too strict for this codebase
    "TRY301",  # abstract raise to inner function — style choice, not a bug
    # BLE001 (blind except) stays off, measured rather than assumed: it fires at
    # 67 sites across 23 files, every one an I/O boundary (ArcadeDB HTTP, torch
    # model loads, MCP transport) where the set of raisable exceptions is not
    # enumerable and narrowing would turn a degraded path into a crash. Turning
    # it on buys 67 `noqa` comments and no defect. S110/S112 below are the half
    # of this that IS a defect — caught and did nothing — and are enforced.
    "BLE001",
    "SIM108",  # ternary — readability preference
    "ERA001",  # commented code — false positives on intentional examples
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# TRY002: test doubles legitimately raise bare Exception to simulate a backend
# failure — inventing an exception class per mock side-effect adds noise, not safety.
"tests/*" = ["D", "S101", "B017", "E402", "N806", "SIM102", "UP038", "TRY002"]
"scripts/*" = ["D103"]
"evaluation/**" = ["D", "C901", "UP038", "RUF034"]
# TODO(tech-debt): add docstrings and refactor complexity in the files below
"**/rdf_parser.py" = ["C901"]
"**/storage/arcadedb/*.py" = ["D102", "C901"]  # data-access layer — docstrings deferred
"**/retrieval/agentic.py" = ["C901"]  # ReAct loop complexity is inherent
"**/framenet/framenet.py" = ["C901"]  # FE assignment is one dependency-parse pass
# Pre-existing complexity, exempted rather than refactored under a gate-hardening
# change: both are single linear passes over a parse tree / a section, and
# splitting core extraction to satisfy a metric is churn with defect risk.
"**/parsers/base.py" = ["C901"]  # _split_large_section: one section scan (15)
# RUF059 flags unused names in tuple unpacking. Test fixtures return a fixed
# tuple and each test binds all of it positionally while using a subset; the
# alternative is index arithmetic, which is worse to read in a failing test.
"tests/**" = ["RUF059"]
# SIM905's autofix expands the compact whitespace-delimited stopword block into
# ~100 lines of one word each. An inline noqa is impossible — the diagnostic
# lands on the `"""` line, where the directive becomes string content.
"**/extraction/entities/hygiene.py" = ["SIM905"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"

disable_error_code = ["misc"]

# Only the two low-signal annotation codes stay off. `union-attr` and

forbidden_modules =
    bioetl.application
    bioetl.composition
    bioetl.infrastructure
    bioetl.interfaces

[importlinter:contract:application-independence]
name = Application layer must not import from infrastructure or composition
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    bioetl.application
forbidden_modules =
    bioetl.composition
    bioetl.infrastructure
    bioetl.interfaces

[importlinter:contract:infrastructure-independence]
name = Infrastructure layer must not import from application, composition or interfaces
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    bioetl.infrastructure
forbidden_modules =
    bioetl.application
    bioetl.composition
    bioetl.interfaces

[importlinter:contract:composition-no-interfaces]
name = Composition layer must not import from interfaces
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    bioetl.composition
forbidden_modules =
    bioetl.interfaces

[importlinter:contract:interfaces-no-direct-infrastructure]
name = Interfaces layer must not import infrastructure directly
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    bioetl.interfaces
forbidden_modules =
    bioetl.infrastructure
allow_indirect_imports = True

# Dependency Injection Constraints (docs/00-project/RULES.md §1)
# Application layer must not directly instantiate infrastructure classes

[importlinter:contract:no-direct-instantiation-in-application]
name = Application layer must not directly import concrete infrastructure classes
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    bioetl.application
forbidden_modules =
    # Concrete adapter implementations
    bioetl.infrastructure.adapters.chembl
    bioetl.infrastructure.adapters.pubchem
    bioetl.infrastructure.adapters.uniprot
    bioetl.infrastructure.adapters.pubmed
    bioetl.infrastructure.locking.memory_lock
    bioetl.infrastructure.checkpoint.local_checkpoint
    bioetl.infrastructure.quarantine.unified

# Note: interfaces -> composition -> infrastructure is allowed through
# composition-owned entrypoints, while direct interfaces -> infrastructure
# imports are forbidden by interfaces-no-direct-infrastructure.
# The core hexagonal constraints are enforced by:
# - Domain must not import other layers
# - Application must not import infrastructure or composition
# - Infrastructure must not import application or interfaces
