# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hexagon layering
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read bottom-up: a layer may import anything BELOW it and nothing above.
#
#   shared kernel   cross-cutting vocabulary every layer may speak: logging,
#                   the error taxonomy, protocol constants, the SDK shim, the
#                   vendored task wire (ADR-015). No I/O, no policy.
#   domain          entities, value objects, policies, ports.
#   application     use cases, command/query handlers, sagas, read models.
#   infrastructure  adapters. The root-level modules on this line are adapters
#                   that never moved into the package: metrics is a Prometheus
#                   registry, http_client and stdio_client are transports,
#                   retry/gc are runtime machinery.
#   delivery        HTTP/MCP surfaces and the facade.
#
# The split of the root-level modules is the point of this contract rather than
# a detail. Folding all 14 into the shared kernel would have been a shorter
# file and would have legitimised `domain -> metrics` and
# `domain.contracts.launcher -> http_client` -- a port importing its own
# adapter. Those are the leaks the contract exists to make visible.
#
# Component packages (auth, approvals, compliance, bootstrap,
# observability) carry their own internal layering and are deliberately out of
# scope here; exhaustive = False keeps them unconstrained rather than
# pretending this contract governs them.

[importlinter:contract:hexagon]
name = Hexagon: shared kernel < domain < application < infrastructure < delivery
type = layers
layers =
    mcp_hangar.server : mcp_hangar.fastmcp_server : mcp_hangar.facade
    mcp_hangar.infrastructure : mcp_hangar.metrics : mcp_hangar.http_client : mcp_hangar.stdio_client : mcp_hangar.retry : mcp_hangar.gc
    mcp_hangar.application
    mcp_hangar.domain
    mcp_hangar.logging_config : mcp_hangar.lock_hierarchy : mcp_hangar.redactor : mcp_hangar.errors : mcp_hangar.protocol : mcp_hangar.context : mcp_hangar._sdk_compat : mcp_hangar.tasks_wire : mcp_hangar.negotiation : mcp_hangar.observability : mcp_hangar.trusted_hosts
exhaustive = False

# The debt ledger. Every line is an edge that exists today and should not.
# It may shrink; tests/unit/test_import_contracts.py caps it so it cannot grow.
#
# It went 33 -> 9. What cleared did so because the edge turned out to be held
# up by code that could not run: a port that was never wired, a fallback beside
# an injected dependency, a deprecation shim with no callers. Measuring first
# was what found those -- three of the "cycle avoidance" imports avoided no
# cycle at all, and grimp said so in a second.
#
# The nine that remain are NOT of that kind, and the difference is worth
# stating so the next pass does not mistake churn for progress:
#
#   * application -> metrics (2) + observability.tracing -> metrics.
#     Services instrumenting themselves. A port per counter would turn
#     IMetricsPublisher into a god interface; `metrics` is an adapter (it has a
#     scrape endpoint behind it), so moving it into the shared kernel is
#     relabelling, not repair. cost_handler CLEARED: CostReportGenerated now
#     carries the mcp_server / tool / cost_model dimensions (schema v2), so the
#     metrics adapter can reconstruct the counter from the event and the
#     application layer no longer writes one directly. No upcaster was needed --
#     the change is additive and v1 rows genuinely lack the dimensions, so
#     passthrough plus empty defaults is the honest reading of old data.
#     The tracing one is a third case again: tracing.py is dual, half
#     ambient-span accessors that logging_config legitimately needs and half
#     OTLP exporter setup. Splitting those two apart is the honest fix and is a
#     673-line module's worth of work.
#
#   * context -> domain.value_objects.identity. The kernel's contextvar carrier
#     needing a domain type. Moving IdentityContext down would put a validated
#     domain concept (CallerIdentity enforces an invariant) in the kernel;
#     moving the contextvar up into domain puts a runtime mechanism in a
#     value-objects module and rewrites 41 import sites. Accepted for now
#     BECAUSE both available moves are worse than the edge, not because nobody
#     looked.
#
#   * domain.model.mcp_server -> infrastructure.launchers, and
#     domain.services -> application.read_models.tool_projection. The aggregate
#     constructing its own launchers despite IMcpServerLauncher existing, and a
#     domain service reaching into an application read model. These two look
#     like the ones that cleared -- worth measuring next.
#
#   * application.event_handlers.detection_handler -> server.api.sessions
#     CLEARED. It was the only application -> delivery edge, and it was three
#     problems in three lines: a function-local import, hiding a reach past the
#     underscore into another module's private state, in the wrong layer. The
#     suspended-session store was never route code -- it is a bounded TTL cache,
#     i.e. an adapter -- so it moved to infrastructure behind
#     ISessionSuspensionRegistry and the handler is handed the same instance the
#     routes use.
#
#   * infrastructure.truncation.manager -> server.tools.batch.models. A shared
#     DTO living in the delivery layer; likely wants to move down rather than
#     be inverted.
#
ignore_imports =
    mcp_hangar.application.commands.handlers -> mcp_hangar.metrics
    mcp_hangar.application.commands.load_handlers -> mcp_hangar.infrastructure.runtime_store
    mcp_hangar.application.discovery.discovery_orchestrator -> mcp_hangar.metrics
    mcp_hangar.application.mcp.tooling -> mcp_hangar.fastmcp_server.asgi
    mcp_hangar.context -> mcp_hangar.domain.value_objects.identity
    mcp_hangar.domain.model.mcp_server -> mcp_hangar.infrastructure.launchers
    mcp_hangar.domain.services -> mcp_hangar.application.read_models.tool_projection
    mcp_hangar.infrastructure.truncation.manager -> mcp_hangar.server.tools.batch.models
    mcp_hangar.observability.tracing -> mcp_hangar.metrics

[project]
name = "mcp-hangar"
version = "2.31.0"
description = "Policy enforcement plane for MCP: every tool call ends in a verdict. Self-hosted, MIT."
readme = "README.md"
license = {text = "MIT"}
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    {name = "Marcin Pyrka", email = "marcin@mcp-hangar.io"}
]
keywords = ["mcp", "model-context-protocol", "llm", "ai", "security", "policy-enforcement", "tool-poisoning"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
    "Topic :: System :: Systems Administration",
]
dependencies = [
    # Pinned EXACTLY, not merely bounded. This pin is a contract with the SDK, and
    # what it protects against is a wrong wire, not an ImportError.
    #
    # Why exact: `_sdk_compat` shims SDK internals (`_lowlevel_server`,
    # `add_request_handler`, `MCPError`, `HANDSHAKE_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS`), the front
    # door installs its own `tools/list` and `tools/call` handlers, and the relay
    # registers `tasks/*` methods the SDK deliberately does not carry in
    # `SPEC_CLIENT_METHODS`. Any of those can change between two SDK releases
    # without a failing import, and 2.3.0 proved it: it stopped running the
    # `tools/list` handler before dispatch and asked `get_tool_input_schema`
    # instead, so every `Mcp-Param-*` check on a projected tool was silently
    # skipped (#1791) -- a deny that did not deny.
    #
    # How to move it: run the weekly canary against the candidate (#1793), then
    # the full integration tier, the relay smoke (`task-relay-smoke.yml`, by
    # dispatch) and the conformance workflow. A failure there is the pin doing its
    # job. Move `mcp` and `mcp-types` together to the same version, and raise the
    # floors in `scripts/check_dependency_floors.py` that the move implies.
    #
    # The v1 line on `main` solves the same class of problem with `>=1.28.1,<2`
    # (#561): both branches must be unable to follow the SDK somewhere their
    # code does not run. Do not widen either to match the other.
    "mcp==2.3.0",
    "mcp-types==2.3.0",  # v2 split protocol-types dist (imported directly as mcp_types); paired with mcp
    "structlog>=24.0.0",
    # Mirrors the floor `mcp==2.3.0` declares; we inherit it rather than choose it.
    # Declared at the same value so the metadata cannot claim an install that the
    # resolver can never produce (see scripts/check_dependency_floors.py).
    "pydantic>=2.12.0",
    # Capped below 1.0: httpx 1.0 drops `httpx.AsyncClient`, which this code
    # uses everywhere. Unbounded, `pip install --pre mcp-hangar` -- the install
    # the v2-preview docs recommend -- resolves httpx to 1.0.dev3 and the
    # gateway dies at startup. Same class as the `mcp` cap (#561): a dependency
    # allowed to walk into a major this code does not run on.
    "httpx>=0.25.0,<1",
    "prometheus-client>=0.19.0",
    # Security floors: pip leaves an already-installed version alone while it
    # satisfies the constraint, so a floor is what an existing environment keeps.
    # pyjwt 2.13.0 fixes CVE-2026-48522/48523/48524/48525/48526 and CVE-2026-32597;
    # 48524 and 48525 are pre-auth DoS on the JWKS path (`get_signing_key_from_jwt`).
    # 2.14.0 fixes PYSEC-2026-4140 and 4142..4152 (4145: an HMAC/asymmetric
    # allow-list accepts a non-canonical PEM public key as the HMAC secret);
    # 2.15.0 fixes PYSEC-2026-4141.
    # `[crypto]` because JWKS RS256/ES256 needs it; it arrived only via `mcp` before.
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.15.0",
    # 50.0.0 fixes CVE-2026-69247; 49.0.0 fixes CVE-2026-69248/69249.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    # not imported directly; arrives via mcp/httpx/starlette. 4.14.2 fixes
    # GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6 (TLSStream IDNA 2003 host name encoding) and
    # GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp (process-pool workers blocked on undrained stderr).
    "anyio>=4.14.2",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "docker>=7.1.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19.0",
    "typer>=0.12.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "questionary>=2.0.0",
    # not imported directly; declared to raise the floor inherited via mcp/starlette
    # (mcp alone asks for >=0.0.9). 0.0.31 fixes CVE-2026-53537..53540.
    "python-multipart>=0.0.31",
    "protobuf>=6.33.5",
    "jcs>=0.2.1",
    "click>=8.3.3",  # security floor: PYSEC-2026-2132 (click.edit() command injection); transitive via typer
    # not imported directly; uvicorn needs a WebSocket library to upgrade a
    # connection, and without one `/api/ws/events` answers 404 (#1676). Only the
    # Dockerfile installed it before. 16.0 is the first release with Python 3.14
    # wheels, above uvicorn[standard]'s own >=13.0 and every known advisory (<9.1).
    "websockets>=16.0",
]
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.0.3",  # security floor: CVE-2025-71176 (tmpdir handling)
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",  # first release that admits pytest 9 (the pytest floor above)
    "pytest-timeout>=2.2.0",
    "pytest-benchmark>=5.1.0",
    # Parallel runs: CI passes `-n auto --dist loadfile` (see ci-core.yml).
    "pytest-xdist>=3.6.0",
    # Pinned, not a floor: this is the version CI lints with. A floor would let
    # every machine resolve a different ruff, which is how a rule that fires
    # locally stays invisible in CI. Dependabot bumps it (uv ecosystem), and CI
    # follows automatically because it installs from here.
    "ruff==0.17.0",
    "import-linter==2.15",
    "mypy>=1.8.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.90.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.20.0",
    # The discovery security check's HTTP client (security_validator.py). In a
    # deployment the kubernetes extra brings it; without it here the check is
    # skipped in every test run and its tests can only skip (#1756). Security
    # floor: the deps-floor-audit job refuses anything older than 3.14.4.
    "aiohttp>=3.14.4",
]
# The kubernetes discovery source imports this. Until now it was declared
# nowhere -- not a dependency, not an extra, not in the image -- so the source
# could not be constructed on any supported install: bootstrap took the
# ImportError path, logged `discovery_source_unavailable` and discovered
# nothing, while the guide, the cookbook and the config reference all described
# a working feature. `docker` is a base dependency, so its source always worked;
# this is the same standing for kubernetes.
# The fuzzing harnesses under `fuzz/`. Markered, not bare: atheris publishes
# manylinux x86_64 wheels for CPython 3.12-3.14 ONLY, so an unconditional entry
# would break `uv sync --all-extras` on this project's own 3.11 baseline and on
# every macOS machine. The invariants the harnesses assert live in
# `fuzz/invariants.py`, which imports nothing from atheris and is replayed by
# the normal test suite everywhere.
fuzz = ["atheris>=3.1.0; sys_platform == 'linux' and python_version >= '3.12' and platform_machine == 'x86_64'"]
kubernetes = ["kubernetes>=29.0.0"]
# 1.35 is the lowest release that installs beside the core dependencies:
# `opentelemetry-proto` requires `protobuf<6` through 1.34.x, and the core
# requires `protobuf>=6.33.5` (`mcp` alone already needs the API at >=1.28).
opentelemetry = [
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.35.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.35.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp>=1.35.0",
]
# The PostgreSQL stores import psycopg2 -- see `database_common.PostgresConnectionFactory`.
# This extra declared `asyncpg`, which appears nowhere in `src/` outside a docstring,
# so `pip install mcp-hangar[postgres]` installed a library nothing imports and left
# the driver unable to start (#779). Same failure shape as the kubernetes extra (#770),
# harder to notice because the extra existed and was merely wrong.
postgres = [
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9.9",
]
# The truncation continuation cache's redis driver imports this (#1008). Same
# class as [postgres]: cluster-only, off the base install AND off `full` so a
# laptop stays small; the published image installs it (see Dockerfile).
redis = [
    "redis>=5.0.0",
]
full = [
    "fpdf2>=2.8.0",
]
[project.scripts]
mcp-hangar = "mcp_hangar.server.cli:cli_main"
[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://mcp-hangar.io"
Documentation = "https://mcp-hangar.io/docs/getting-started/quickstart"
Repository = "https://github.com/mcp-hangar/mcp-hangar"
[build-system]
# hatchling is PINNED. 1.32.1 (published 2026-09-16) loads a builder plugin
# chain whose binary builder imports the `hatch` CLI package
# (`hatchling/builders/binary.py`: `from hatch.plugin.manager import
# PluginManager`). That package is NOT present in the isolated build env that
# `hatch build` and `python -m build` each create from this `requires` list, so
# every build path died with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hatch'` --
# the Docker image, the `build` CI job, `make build-core` and the release
# workflow. 1.32.0 is unaffected. See #1513.
#
# This one pin covers every path because all of them resolve the backend from
# this list. Before lifting it, check that a newer hatchling no longer imports
# `hatch` at plugin-load time, then prove it with `docker build .` and the
# `build` job -- not with a local `pip install`, which has `hatch` on hand and
# therefore cannot reproduce the failure.
requires = ["hatchling==1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
[tool.hatch.build]
exclude = ["/.github/brand"]
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/mcp_hangar"]
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"src/mcp_hangar/py.typed" = "mcp_hangar/py.typed"
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The sdist ships what it takes to build and test the project from source, and
# nothing that is an artefact of having built it here. `scripts/` stays because
# the test suite imports it (`tests/unit/test_api_route_inventory.py` reads
# `scripts.dump_api_routes`), so dropping it would ship a tests/ directory that
# cannot run; `examples/` stays because the quickstart points at
# `examples/rugpull/` (#1193).
exclude = [
    ".github/brand",
    ".clusterfuzzlite",
    ".grimp_cache",
    ".import_linter_cache",
    "coverage.json",
]
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"
extend-exclude = ["packages/operator", "site", "dist"]
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP", "B", "BLE001", "C4", "C90", "SIM"]
ignore = [
    "B007",
    "B011",
    "B017",
    "B024",
    "B027",
    "B904",
    "C401",
    "C416",
    "N806",
    "N818",
    "SIM102",
    "SIM103",
    "SIM105",
    "SIM108",
    "SIM110",
    "SIM117",
    "SIM118",
]
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Cyclomatic complexity ceiling for NEW code. Everything above it today carries an
# explicit `# noqa: C901` naming its current score -- 16 functions, listed by
# `ruff check src --select C901`. That list is a debt ledger, not wallpaper: it is
# short enough to read, and each entry is visible to whoever next opens the
# function.
#
# 15 rather than mccabe's default 10 because 10 would have baselined 54 functions,
# and a 54-entry noqa list stops being read. Anything above 15 is indefensible in
# review, so the gate bites real monsters while leaving ordinary code alone.
#
# The rule: never add a noqa here. Lower the ceiling, or split the function.
max-complexity = 15

# Mypy strictness migration in progress (TASK-P1-5).
# Phase 1: baseline strictness with per-module debt overrides (DONE).
# Phase 2: clean union-attr + attr-defined site by site.
# Phase 3: enable disallow_untyped_defs, drop all per-module overrides.
# Goal: zero overrides + strict = true by 2026-Q4.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = false
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false      # TODO(mypy-phase-3): enable
disallow_incomplete_defs = false   # TODO(mypy-phase-3): enable
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
show_error_codes = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
# disable_error_code intentionally absent -- per-module overrides below
# carry the technical debt explicitly. Goal: zero per-module overrides
# by 2026-Q4 (tracked in the issue tracker; see TODO(mypy-phase-3) above).
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "docker.*",
    "yaml.*",
    "prometheus_client.*",
    "kubernetes.*",
    "psycopg2.*",
    "opentelemetry.*",
    "watchdog.*",
    "aiohttp.*",
    "httpx.*",
    "structlog.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.coverage.run]
# branch = true lives HERE, not only on the command line, for two reasons.
# 1. The decision-path floors are BRANCH numbers. A floor compared against
#    statement-only data silently passes a lower bar than it claims.
# 2. Modes do not mix: combining a statement-mode .coverage with a branch-mode
#    run raises `coverage.exceptions.DataError: Can't combine branch coverage
#    data with statement data` as a pytest INTERNALERROR. Making every run
#    branch-mode removes the mixed state entirely.
branch = true
relative_files = true

[tool.coverage.report]
# Deliberately NO fail_under. coverage.py's threshold is GLOBAL -- there is no
# per-file setting -- so a single number would have to be low enough for the
# weakest module in the tree, which is exactly the modules that need the
# strongest guarantee. Per-module floors live below and are checked by
# scripts/check_decision_coverage.py.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision-path coverage floors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A module is a DECISION PATH when a wrong branch produces a wrong allow/deny:
# authorization, human consent, egress and tool-access policy, supply-chain
# digest pinning. An untested branch there is a security defect, not a style
# complaint, so these modules get a floor and the rest of the tree does not.
#
# Values are combined line+branch coverage as MEASURED on this branch, rounded
# down -- not an aspirational 90. A gate that is red the day it lands teaches
# people to skip it; this one is green on arrival and catches regressions from
# the first commit. Raising a floor is the unit of progress
# (`check_decision_coverage.py coverage.json --bump` locks in what was gained).
#
# Floors are measured on the Python the GATE runs (3.11 in the decision-coverage
# job), not on a developer's interpreter. Branch-arc counts differ between CPython
# versions: server/tools/batch/executor.py measures 85.38 on 3.13 and 85.06 on
# 3.11, so a floor taken from 3.13 failed CI on arrival. When a floor moves, take
# the number from the CI job -- or the lower of the two if you have both.
#
#   server/tools/batch/executor.py at 84.5 -- deliberately below what anyone
#     measures locally. The module runs work on a thread pool with timeouts and
#     single-flight de-duplication, so a handful of branches fire or not
#     depending on scheduling. Measured: 85.38 three times on CPython 3.13,
#     85.06 twice on 3.11, and 85.06 then 84.75 on two CI runs of the same
#     tree. Local is reproducible; a loaded shared runner is not. The floor sits
#     under the lowest observed CI value rather than under the local one, so the
#     gate reports a real regression instead of the runner's mood.
#     Pinning those branches with deterministic tests would let this rise again.
#
# Two entries are visible debt rather than a target:
#   approvals/persistence/sqlite_approval_repository.py at 87.0 -- the store
#     holding approval state, tenant scoping and the arguments hash. Unit tests
#     use a fake repository; the real SQL of `transition` is exercised by the
#     multi-process race test (#1794) and the CLI resolve tests (#1778).
#   domain/value_objects/tool_access_policy.py at 84.2 -- _CompositePolicy's
#     merge and approval-list handling, i.e. the consent-preservation logic.
#   server/tools/batch/executor.py at 85.3 -- the invoke path, including the
#     455-line _execute_call_inner.
[tool.decision_coverage]
# How far a floor may sit below reality before it stops being a ratchet.
drift_allowance = 3.0

[tool.decision_coverage.floors]
  "application/tasks/governed_task_store.py" = 89.8
  "application/tasks/tool_pin_context.py" = 94.4
  "approvals/api/routes.py" = 90.0
  "approvals/bootstrap.py" = 98.3
  "approvals/commands/resolve.py" = 96.7
  "approvals/delivery/event_stream.py" = 100.0
  "approvals/delivery/noop.py" = 100.0
  "approvals/hold_registry.py" = 100.0
  "approvals/models.py" = 97.9
  "approvals/pending.py" = 100.0
  "approvals/persistence/sqlite_approval_repository.py" = 87.0
  "approvals/service.py" = 96.1
  "auth/commands/handlers.py" = 99.2
  "auth/infrastructure/middleware.py" = 96.9
  "auth/infrastructure/opa_authorizer.py" = 100.0
  "auth/infrastructure/rbac_authorizer.py" = 98.8
  "auth/roles.py" = 100.0
  "domain/policies/egress_l7.py" = 98.6
  "domain/services/digest_computation.py" = 100.0
  "domain/services/digest_validator.py" = 100.0
  "domain/services/task_consent.py" = 92.7
  "domain/services/task_digest_guard.py" = 97.7
  "domain/services/task_ownership.py" = 97.9
  # 94.1 -> 96.0 when tests/unit/test_config_policies_are_adopted_in_one_step.py
  # drove the reload's policy swap and provenance paths (#1424): 97.38 measured

  "domain/services/ui_resource_guard.py" = 100.0

  # 88.7 -> 92.7 because the two security regression files moved from

  "server/api/middleware.py" = 92.8
  "server/api/route_permissions.py" = 100.0
  # The two chokepoints that confine a tenant-scoped grant: which tenant a

  "domain/events/tenancy.py" = 100.0

  # approval-gate terminal path (#1274): 91.49 measured on 3.11, so 87.4 sat

  # run-to-run swing noted above. 89.0 -> 89.5 when

; Import-Linter contracts for the Agent Brain monorepo.
; See docs/plans/2026-05-28-mcp-uds-transport-design.md §9.
;
; Layering: server (bottom) → uds → mcp → cli (top).
; Server must have no upward deps. UDS may only touch server.models.
; MCP must never call server internals — always via HTTP/UDS API.
; CLI may consume uds + server.models.
;
; Enforced at the repo root via `task check:layering`.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    agent_brain_server
    agent_brain_uds
    agent_brain_mcp
    agent_brain_cli
include_external_packages = False

[importlinter:contract:server-has-no-upward-deps]
name = server has no upward deps
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    agent_brain_server
forbidden_modules =
    agent_brain_uds
    agent_brain_mcp
    agent_brain_cli

[importlinter:contract:uds-touches-only-server-models]
name = uds touches only server.models
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    agent_brain_uds
forbidden_modules =
    agent_brain_server.services
    agent_brain_server.api
    agent_brain_server.indexing
    agent_brain_server.storage
    agent_brain_mcp
    agent_brain_cli

[importlinter:contract:mcp-never-calls-server-internals]
name = mcp never calls server internals
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    agent_brain_mcp
forbidden_modules =
    agent_brain_server.services
    agent_brain_server.api
    agent_brain_server.indexing
    agent_brain_server.storage
    agent_brain_server.config
    agent_brain_server.providers
    agent_brain_server.runtime
    agent_brain_server.storage_paths
    agent_brain_server.job_queue
    agent_brain_cli

[importlinter]
root_package = app
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[importlinter:contract:1]
name = Enforce Layered Architecture (Routers -> Services -> Models)
type = layers
layers =
    routers
    services
    schemas
    models
containers = app
# Models and Schemas are foundational (at the bottom).
# Services can import Models/Schemas.
# Routers can import Services/Models/Schemas.
# BUT Models/Schemas cannot import Services or Routers.
# Services cannot import Routers.

    "ruff",
    "import-linter",
]
# Mutation testing is neither a test nor a lint dependency: only the
# scheduled mutation workflow installs it (alongside ".[test]").
mutation = [
    "mutmut",
]

[project.scripts]
sanity-gravity = "sanity_gravity.cli.main:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["sanity_gravity*"]

# Mutation testing (mutmut 3.x; keys verified against 3.7: the 2.x
# names paths_to_mutate/tests_dir/runner are deprecated or gone).
# Scope, first pass: the code the new guards claim to protect - domain/
# is the identity grammar; core/registry.py owns tag parsing + the tier
# filter that feeds every CI matrix. plugins/ joins on a later pass.
# The whole package is copied (imports must resolve inside mutants/)
# but only the scoped files grow mutants.
[tool.mutmut]
source_paths = ["sanity_gravity"]
only_mutate = [
    "sanity_gravity/domain/*",
    "sanity_gravity/core/registry.py",
]
# Never the integration suite: a docker-bound run turns minutes into an
# overnight job and imports flakiness as "survived".
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = ["tests/unit"]
# mutmut copies tests/ and pyproject.toml on its own; everything else
# the unit suite reads from the repo root must tag along or the mutant
# runs diverge from the real suite: pytest.ini (suite config), plugins/
# (manifests the registry discovers), sandbox/ (layer Dockerfiles the
# planner stats), .github/ (workflow files the matrix/packaging guards
# parse), CONTRIBUTING.md and the READMEs (docs contract), sanity-cli
# (the launcher the reporter parity test execs).
also_copy = [
    "pytest.ini",
    "plugins/",
    "sandbox/",
    ".github/",
    "CONTRIBUTING.md",
    "README.md",
    "README_ja.md",
    "README_zh-TW.md",
    "sanity-cli",
]

# Architecture contracts, executable via lint-imports (CI lint job) and
# embedded in the unit suite (tests/unit/test_architecture.py). Config
# lives here rather than in a separate .importlinter INI: pyproject is
# already the single config surface (ruff, mutmut), the packaging
# contract tests parse it with tomllib, and import-linter reads
# [tool.importlinter] natively.
#
# Every ignore_imports entry is frozen debt: the list may only shrink.
# import-linter errors on unmatched ignores by default, so a retired
# edge forces its line to be deleted - the ratchet is self-enforcing.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["sanity_gravity"]
include_external_packages = true
# Type-only imports are not runtime coupling: domain/capability.py
# imports PluginRegistry under TYPE_CHECKING purely for annotations.
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "domain imports nothing internal (and no process/OS access)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["sanity_gravity.domain"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "sanity_gravity.cli",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs",
    "sanity_gravity.hooks",
    "sanity_gravity.compose",
    "sanity_gravity.infra",
    "sanity_gravity.core",
    "sanity_gravity.effects",
    "sanity_gravity.plugins",
    "sanity_gravity.events",
    "subprocess",
    "os",
    "sys",
]
# No ignore_imports: this contract is debt-free and must stay that way.
# It is the load-bearing one - Tag/Naming/plan stay value objects that a
# property test can hammer with no docker daemon anywhere in scope.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "layering: cli on top, domain at the bottom"
type = "layers"
containers = ["sanity_gravity"]
layers = [
    "cli",
    "verbs",
    "hooks",
    "compose",
    "infra",
    "core",
    "effects",
    "plugins",
    "domain",
]
# Frozen debt, re-derived from the tree at contract birth (31 edges;
# 15 retired when colors/registry - pure downward-importing services
# that only accidentally lived under cli/ - moved to core/). Every
# remaining entry is a lower layer reaching up for CLI-shaped services;
# the io split migration retires the 13 cli.io edges. Entries are exact
# module-to-module edges, never wildcards: a new module importing
# upward must show up as a red build, not slip through a glob.
ignore_imports = [
    # verbs -> cli (12)
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.build -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.check -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.ide -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.open -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.proxy -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.pull -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.shell -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.status -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.sync -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.test_suite -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.up -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.upgrade -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    # hooks -> verbs (2): function-local imports dodging the runtime
    # import cycle, not the design one - exactly what this pins.
    "sanity_gravity.hooks.lifecycle -> sanity_gravity.verbs.lifecycle",
    "sanity_gravity.hooks.snapshot -> sanity_gravity.verbs.lifecycle",
    # compose -> cli (1)
    "sanity_gravity.compose.generators -> sanity_gravity.cli.io",
    # plugins -> core (1)
    "sanity_gravity.plugins.registry -> sanity_gravity.core.eventbus",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "only the process boundary may import subprocess"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["sanity_gravity"]
forbidden_modules = ["subprocess"]
ignore_imports = [
    # By design (not debt): core.proc IS the boundary this contract
    # protects; ide/shell hand the terminal to an interactive
    # `docker exec -it` and need the raw TTY-inheriting call.
    "sanity_gravity.core.proc -> subprocess",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.ide -> subprocess",
    "sanity_gravity.verbs.shell -> subprocess",
    # Frozen debt: SystemRuntime still shells out directly; it retires
    # when the action runtime is rebased onto core.proc.
    "sanity_gravity.effects.actions -> subprocess",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100
extend-exclude = [".venv", "workspace", "sanity_gravity.egg-info"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Deliberately narrow for the first pass: correctness-flavored rules
# only, and the tree is clean under them - a red here is a real finding,
# not baseline noise. E501 (line length) stays out until a separate
# formatting-only commit; mixing reflows into behavior changes destroys
# diff reviewability.
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]
ignore = [
    "B008",  # function call in default arg - not a pattern this repo misuses
    "B905",  # zip() strict= is a per-site semantic decision, not a sweep
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests legitimately import for side effects and shadow builtins in fixtures.
"tests/**" = ["F811"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["sanity_gravity"]

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    selfhealing

[importlinter:contract:no-top-level-self-import]
name = Internal modules must not import from top-level selfhealing
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    selfhealing.core
    selfhealing.services
    selfhealing.adapters
    selfhealing.interfaces
    selfhealing.settings
forbidden_modules = selfhealing

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
include = ["shopping*", "myproject*"]
exclude = ["tests*", "htmlcov*", "staticfiles*", "media*"]

# ==========================================
# Black Configuration (Code Formatting)
# ==========================================
[tool.black]
line-length = 127
target-version = ['py312']
exclude = '''
/(
    \.git
  | \.venv
  | venv
  | env
  | __pycache__
  | migrations
  | staticfiles
  | media
  | htmlcov
  | \.backup
)/
'''

# ==========================================
# isort Configuration (Import Sorting)
# ==========================================
[tool.isort]
profile = "black"
line_length = 127
skip_glob = ["*/migrations/*", "venv/*", "env/*", "htmlcov/*"]
known_django = ["django"]
known_third_party = [
    "rest_framework",
    "celery",
    "redis",
    "mptt",
    "allauth",
    "dj_rest_auth",
    "drf_spectacular"
]
known_first_party = ["shopping", "myproject"]
sections = ["FUTURE", "STDLIB", "DJANGO", "THIRDPARTY", "FIRSTPARTY", "LOCALFOLDER"]

# ==========================================
# pytest Configuration
# ==========================================
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = "myproject.settings.test"
python_files = ["tests.py", "test_*.py", "*_tests.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*", "*Tests", "*TestCase"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = """
    -n auto
    --dist=loadscope
    --cov=shopping
    --cov=myproject
    --cov-report=html
    --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered
    --cov-fail-under=70
    --tb=short
    --strict-markers
    -m 'not load_test and not manual and not concurrency and not performance and not auth_race and not payment_race and not order_race and not point_race and not return_race and not heavy and not slow and not e2e and not requires_redis and not requires_db and not flaky'
"""
# selfhealing coverage는 별도 repo에서 측정 (https://github.com/gotoUSA/selfhealing-python)
testpaths = ["shopping/tests", "tests"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "unit: marks tests as unit tests (fast, no external deps)",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests (requires full infrastructure)",
    "performance: marks tests as performance tests",
    "load_test: load test related (excluded by default in CI)",
    "manual: manual/debugging tests (excluded by default in CI)",
    "concurrency: concurrency tests (race condition verification)",
    "auth_race: authentication related race condition tests",
    "payment_race: payment related race condition tests",
    "order_race: order related race condition tests",
    "point_race: point related race condition tests",
    "return_race: return related race condition tests",
    "heavy: high-load stress tests (optionally excluded in CI)",
    "schema: OpenAPI schema-based contract tests (Schemathesis)",
    "stateful: Stateful API workflow tests (state transition verification)",
    "fuzz: Fuzz tests - Hypothesis/Schemathesis based random input verification",
    "negative: Negative tests - proper error handling for invalid inputs",
    "security: Security tests - SQL Injection, XSS, SSTI attack defense verification",
    "chaos: Chaos engineering tests - fault injection and recovery verification",
    "compound: Compound failure tests - multiple failure modes simultaneously",
    # Self-Healing Test Tiers (Reference: docs/testing/SELF_HEALING_TEST_MATRICES.md)
    "tier1: Fast unit tests for PR validation (< 2 min, no external deps)",
    "tier2: Integration tests for merge to main (< 10 min, requires DB/Redis)",
    "tier3_chaos: Chaos engineering tests for nightly runs (< 30 min)",
    "tier4_load: Load and stress tests for releases (< 2 hours, dedicated runner)",
    # Self-Healing Domain Markers
    "tenant_aware: Multi-tenancy isolation tests (R-001)",
    "cost_sensitive: Cost-aware recovery tests (R-002)",
    "requires_redis: Tests requiring Redis connection",
    "requires_celery: Tests requiring Celery worker",
    "requires_db: Tests requiring database connection",
    "flaky: Tests with known flakiness (quarantined from CI)",
]
filterwarnings = [
    # Ignore dj-rest-auth deprecation warnings (library internal, cannot fix)
    "ignore:app_settings.USERNAME_REQUIRED is deprecated:UserWarning:dj_rest_auth.registration.serializers",
    "ignore:app_settings.EMAIL_REQUIRED is deprecated:UserWarning:dj_rest_auth.registration.serializers",
    # Ignore factory_boy deprecation warning (library internal)
    "ignore:.*_after_postgeneration will stop saving the instance.*:DeprecationWarning:factory.django",
    # Ignore coverage warnings from pytest-xdist parallel execution
    "ignore:No data was collected:coverage.exceptions.CoverageWarning",
    "ignore::coverage.exceptions.CoverageWarning",
    # Ignore CovReportWarning from pytest-cov
    "ignore::pytest_cov.plugin.CovReportWarning",
]

# ==========================================================================
# Test Logging: WARNING 이상만 출력하여 테스트 가독성 확보.
# 디버깅이 필요하면: SELFHEALING_TEST_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG pytest ...
# ==========================================================================
log_level = "WARNING"
log_cli_level = "WARNING"

# pytest-env: Set environment variables before test execution
# Resolves PostgreSQL cp949 encoding issue on Windows
[tool.pytest_env]
PGCLIENTENCODING = "UTF8"
PYTHONIOENCODING = "utf-8"
SELFHEALING_TEST_LOG_LEVEL = "WARNING"

# ==========================================
# coverage Configuration
# ==========================================
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["shopping", "myproject"]
omit = [
    "*/migrations/*",
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*.py",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/venv/*",
    "*/env/*",
    "manage.py",
    "myproject/wsgi.py",
    "myproject/asgi.py",
    "load_tests/*",
]
branch = true
# Parallel testing support (pytest-xdist)
parallel = true
concurrency = ["thread", "multiprocessing"]
# Explicitly set data file path
data_file = ".coverage"
# Do not retain existing data during parallel execution (measure fresh each time)
relative_files = true

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "def __str__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

# ==========================================
# radon Configuration (Code Complexity)
# ==========================================
[tool.radon]
exclude = "*/migrations/*,*/tests/*,*/__pycache__/*,*/venv/*"
cc_min = "C"  # Show complexity C or above (A=1-5, B=6-10, C=11-20, D=21-30, E=31-40, F=41+)

# ==========================================
# bandit Configuration (Security Analysis)
# ==========================================
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "migrations", "venv", "env", "htmlcov", "load_tests"]
skips = ["B101", "B311"]  # B101: assert usage, B311: random (non-security use)
targets = ["shopping"]

# ==========================================
# vulture Configuration (Dead Code Detection)
# ==========================================
[tool.vulture]
exclude = ["*/migrations/*", "*/tests/*", "venv/", "env/", "htmlcov/"]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["shopping"]
sort_by_size = true

# ==========================================
# mutmut Configuration (Mutation Testing)
# ==========================================
# Not yet introduced in this project
# Will be introduced after core logic stabilization

[importlinter]
root_package = yamlgraph

[importlinter:contract:three-layer]
name = Three-layer architecture (Presentation → Logic → Side Effects)
type = layers
# `:` (colon) = non-independent siblings: free imports within the same layer.
# `|` (pipe)  = independent siblings: no cross-imports within a layer.
# We use `:` so that logic modules can freely import each other while still
# being blocked from importing up into cli (Layer 1).
layers =
    yamlgraph.cli
    yamlgraph.compile : yamlgraph.node_factory : yamlgraph.executor : yamlgraph.linter : yamlgraph.routing : yamlgraph.graph_cache : yamlgraph.schema_loader : yamlgraph.data_loader : yamlgraph.discovery : yamlgraph.executor_async : yamlgraph.interactive_tool : yamlgraph.mermaid_export
    yamlgraph.tools : yamlgraph.models : yamlgraph.utils : yamlgraph.config : yamlgraph.constants : yamlgraph.storage : yamlgraph.contrib : yamlgraph.executor_base : yamlgraph.error_handlers : yamlgraph.verification : yamlgraph.loop_detector

[importlinter:contract:linter-llm-free]
# Judgement (2026-06-24, FR-588): the linter is a pure, offline, deterministic
# AST/YAML analyzer. It must never make an LLM call — no API keys, no network,
# no non-determinism inside a tool that runs in pre-commit and CI. An LLM-scored
# complexity metric (FR-588) lives in a standalone command, never wired into the
# linter. This contract forbids any linter module from importing the executor or
# LLM-factory layer directly. The single legitimate transitive bridge —
# checks_semantic imports loop_detector for cycle detection (FR-658 extraction);
# loop_detector is a pure utility with no executor/LLM dependencies.
name = Linter stays LLM-free (no executor or LLM-factory imports)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    yamlgraph.linter
forbidden_modules =
    yamlgraph.executor
    yamlgraph.executor_async
    yamlgraph.executor_base
    yamlgraph.utils.llm_factory

[importlinter:contract:fsm-contrib-ownership]
# FR-755 ruling C: the FSM bridge is a supported repeating pattern but not
# part of core framework API surface. Freeze this ownership boundary by
# preventing core modules from importing yamlgraph.utils.fsm directly.
name = core modules do not import yamlgraph.utils.fsm
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    yamlgraph.cli
    yamlgraph.compile
    yamlgraph.node_factory
    yamlgraph.executor
    yamlgraph.executor_async
    yamlgraph.executor_base
    yamlgraph.linter
    yamlgraph.routing
    yamlgraph.graph_cache
    yamlgraph.schema_loader
    yamlgraph.data_loader
    yamlgraph.discovery
    yamlgraph.interactive_tool
    yamlgraph.tools
    yamlgraph.models
    yamlgraph.storage
    yamlgraph.verification
    yamlgraph.loop_detector
forbidden_modules =
    yamlgraph.utils.fsm

[importlinter]
root_package = src

[importlinter:contract:layered_architecture]
name = Enforce src layering
type = layers
layers =
    src.interfaces
    src.pipeline
    src.engine
    src.core

[importlinter:contract:shared_is_layer_neutral]
name = Shared must not import layer packages
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.shared
forbidden_modules =
    src.interfaces
    src.adapters
    src.pipeline
    src.engine
    src.core

; The console reads through `Command.invoke` or not at all. The layers contract
; above permits `interfaces -> pipeline`, so this is the one place the rule can
; be stated. `allow_indirect_imports` is required, not a loophole: the web
; package imports the command layer, which imports pipeline, and that chain is
; the whole point -- what must not exist is a DIRECT reach past it, which is how
; the previous browser UI grew a second read path and then drifted from the CLI.
[importlinter:contract:web_reads_through_the_command_layer]
name = The console must not reach past the command layer
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.interfaces.web
forbidden_modules =
    src.pipeline
    src.engine
    src.core
allow_indirect_imports = True

; Dispatching work and doing it are different jobs, and the layers contract
; above cannot say so -- `interfaces -> engine` is legal, so Azure code reaching
; into the solver reads as ordinary layering. It had: `share.py` imported the
; checkpoint manifest's FILENAME from `engine.solver.storage`, which is a string
; the node wrapper also needs and cannot get that way (stdlib-only, and
; `shared -> engine` is forbidden) -- so the same literal was spelled four
; times. The name now lives in `shared.records`, which already declares the
; artifact, and this keeps the edge from coming back the next time cloud code
; needs to know something about a run's contents.
[importlinter:contract:cloud_dispatches_work_it_does_not_do]
name = Azure dispatch must not reach into the solver
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.interfaces.cloud
forbidden_modules =
    src.engine
    src.core

; The dependency INVERSION, and the reason `src/adapters/` exists as a name.
; The work declares what it needs as a Protocol under `src.shared.ports` and
; never learns which adapter satisfies it; the composition root is the only
; place that knows. Without this contract `adapters/` is just a folder, and
; `pipeline` importing psycopg would pass.
[importlinter:contract:the_work_does_not_know_its_adapters]
name = The work must not import what it talks to
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.pipeline
    src.engine
    src.core
forbidden_modules =
    src.adapters

; The other half, and they are a PAIR -- changing one without the other leaves a
; one-way door open. Generalises `cloud_dispatches_work_it_does_not_do` below,
; which can say this for `interfaces.cloud` alone and CANNOT say it for
; `interfaces.gtowizard`, whose HTTP client and engine-reaching player are one
; package. Splitting that is what makes this statable for every adapter.
;
; Why not `type = independence`: listing pipeline/engine/core and adapters as
; independent would also sever `pipeline -> engine`, which IS the layering.
; Why not the layers contract's `|` sibling delimiter: it would make adapters and
; pipeline mutually unreachable but still permit `adapters -> engine`, since
; engine sits in a layer BELOW. Only a forbidden pair says both things.
[importlinter:contract:an_adapter_does_not_do_the_work]
name = Adapters must not reach into the pipeline or the solver
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.adapters
forbidden_modules =
    src.pipeline
    src.engine
    src.core

; THE ONE HERE THAT IS ABOUT CORRECTNESS, not tidiness. `reference/` holds
; textbook implementations -- tabular CFR, exact BR, LBR -- that are tractable
; only at Kuhn/Leduc scale and exist to PROVE the production estimators right:
; `restricted_hunl.py` validates the vectorised public-tree engine against
; `reference/best_response.py` to 1e-9. An oracle that imported the thing it
; validates would make that agreement circular, and the test would still pass.
[importlinter:contract:the_oracles_are_independent_of_what_they_validate]
name = Reference implementations must not import the estimators they check
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.pipeline.evaluation.reference
forbidden_modules =
    src.pipeline.evaluation.estimators
    src.pipeline.evaluation.ledger
    src.pipeline.services

; An estimator produces a number; the ledger decides how one is written down and
; which tier it may be compared against. Keeping the arrow one-way is what lets
; a new estimator be added without touching the record, and what stops a scorer
; from quietly depending on how it will be filed. (The reverse edge exists and
; is fine: `ledger/tiers.py` reads `lbr/config.py` to derive a tier.)
[importlinter:contract:an_estimator_does_not_know_how_it_is_recorded]
name = Estimators must not import the ledger
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.pipeline.evaluation.estimators
forbidden_modules =
    src.pipeline.evaluation.ledger
    src.pipeline.services

; The play server loads a finished blueprint and answers questions about it.
; Training is the one thing it must never do -- it runs on a box sized to serve,
; deallocates itself when idle, and a training import there is either dead
; weight at load time or an accident waiting on a shared filesystem.
[importlinter:contract:serving_is_not_training]
name = The play server must not import training
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.interfaces.blueprint
forbidden_modules =
    src.pipeline.training

[importlinter:contract:training_and_evaluation_are_independent]
name = Training and evaluation must not import each other
type = independence
modules =
    src.pipeline.training
    src.pipeline.evaluation

; Building a blueprint AND READING ONE -- `grid`/`paths` merged in from the
; former `analysis/` -- are what training, evaluation and anything serving a run
; for reading all start from, so it must depend on none of them. It lived under
; `training` while training was the only builder, and the cost was that every
; other consumer reached across the independence contract above to get at it.
; Stated only in a docstring this would drift back within a release; the two
; imports that would restore the old arrangement are exactly what this forbids.
[importlinter:contract:blueprint_construction_is_foundational]
name = Building a blueprint must not depend on what consumes one
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.pipeline.blueprint
    src.pipeline.abstraction
forbidden_modules =
    src.pipeline.training
    src.pipeline.evaluation
    src.pipeline.services
    src.interfaces

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "A",    # builtin shadowing
    "ARG",  # unused arguments
    "B",    # bugbear: likely bugs (B905 = zip without strict=)
    "BLE",  # blind except -- deliberate ones carry `# noqa: BLE001 -- <why>`
    "C4",   # comprehension / literal misuse
    "DTZ",  # naive datetimes -- the ledger already has a naive-local-time era
    "E",
    "F",
    "FLY",  # static join -> f-string
    "G",    # logging format
    "I",
    "ICN",  # import naming conventions
    "INT",  # gettext
    "ISC",  # implicit string concat
    "LOG",  # logging misuse
    "N",
    "PERF", # obvious perf smells
    "PGH",  # blanket noqa / type: ignore with no code
    "PIE",
    "PLC0415", # import inside a function -- deliberate ones carry `# noqa: PLC0415 -- <why>`
    "PLW1510", # subprocess.run without check= -- a swallowed exit code, again
    "PT",   # pytest style
    "PTH",  # os.path -> pathlib
    "Q",    # quote style
    "RET",
    "RSE",  # raise X() -> raise X
    "RUF",
    "SIM",
    "SLF",
    "SLOT", # __slots__ misuse
    "TC",   # annotation-only import -> `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (see flake8-type-checking)
    "TID",  # tidy imports
    "UP",
    "W",
]
ignore = [
    "RUF001",
    "RUF002",
    "RUF003",
    # G004 (f-string in a log call) does not pay for itself here: every such
    # line uses `{n:,}` formatting, which %-style cannot express, so the lazy
    # form would be `logger.info("%s rows", f"{n:,}")` -- worse to read, and
    # these are once-per-checkpoint lines, not a hot path. The rest of G still
    # catches real misuse (string concat / .format() in a log call).
    "G004",
    # ERA001 cannot tell a worked example from dead code, and this codebase
    # explains its arithmetic in comments: "# e_i = (u0 + u1) / 2" reads as
    # commented-out code to it. All four hits were false positives.
    "ERA001",
]

# TC assumes an annotation is never evaluated at runtime, and pydantic breaks
# that: it resolves field annotations to build the model, so a name hidden
# behind TYPE_CHECKING is a startup crash rather than a lint. Declared rather
# than left to inference -- the payload contract and the config schemas should
# not depend on a ruff version continuing to guess right. Two other runtime
# readers of annotations are NOT covered and must be added here if one ever
# appears in a moved import: a FastAPI route signature (request parsing is
# derived from it) and any dataclass reached by `get_type_hints`.
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
# Both resolve their annotations at RUNTIME, so TC would move an import
# these classes need. SQLAlchemy is not theoretical: deferring `datetime`
# raises `MappedAnnotationError: Could not resolve all types within mapped
# annotation` at import, not at first use.
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel", "sqlalchemy.orm.DeclarativeBase"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"*.py" = ["E501"]
# Tests are full of deliberately-unused arguments: monkeypatch stand-ins that
# must match a real signature, and fixtures requested for their side effect.
# PLC0415 is off here because a test module ships nothing, and importing inside
# a test is how you import the module under test AFTER monkeypatching what it
# reads at import time, or keep a heavy optional dependency off the collection
# path (`conftest.py::requires_card_abstraction`).
"tests/**/*.py" = ["SLF001", "ARG001", "ARG002", "ARG005", "PLC0415"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "timeout: test timeout in seconds",
]
# `-n auto` because the suite is dominated by a handful of genuinely expensive
# tests: 57 `slow`-marked ones carry 6m25s of the wall clock and the other ~2400
# are nearly free. Re-measured 08-24 at 2453 tests -- serial 12m22s full / 4m12s
# fast gate, across 12 workers 6m25s / 58s.
#
# Only the FAST GATE parallelises (4m12s -> 58s). The full suite does not, and
# the 6m25s is not a scheduling result: ONE test, `test_every_seven_card_hand`,
# runs 6m00s of it by itself. No worker count moves that floor -- splitting that
# test is the only thing that would.
#
# `--dist load` (the default) is what wins: `loadfile`/`loadscope` would pin a
# whole slow file to one worker and set the floor there, and `worksteal`
# measured no better. Do NOT add `--maxschedchunk=1` -- finer scheduling
# measured SLOWER, because these tests are CPU-bound and oversubscribing them
# costs more than the packing saves.
#
# To debug one test, `-n0` turns it off: worker startup and interleaved output
# are pure cost when there is nothing to parallelise.
addopts = "-v -n auto --durations=15"
# 60s, raised from 5 on 08-25. The old floor's rule was "if one flakes, mark
# THAT test, never raise this" -- and its evidence was 0 failures in 10 `-n auto`
# runs. That was measured on a quiet box. This one now carries several agent
# sessions at once, and the floor was found to be a load meter: three separate
# cohorts, ~20 distinct tests across nine files, each failing under `-n auto`
# and every one passing serially. Measured margins were 1.2-1.9x, not the 5x
# claimed (`test_unknown_scorer_rejected` 4.11s; three more at 2.6-2.9s).
#
# Twenty annotations would have been chasing it. A gate whose red carries no
# information is worse than no gate, so the budget is now sized for its real
# job -- catching a HANG -- and creeping slowness is surfaced by `--durations`
# above, which reports without failing. Explicit per-test marks of 30-180s
# still work and still win; nothing about them changes.
timeout = 60
timeout_func_only = true

[dependency-groups]
# Development, testing, and code quality tools
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.0.2",
    "ruff>=0.16.4",
    # Pinned exactly: `ty` is pre-1.0 and moves fast enough that a lockfile
    # refresh can swap the type gate underneath a commit. Raising it is a triage
    # pass rather than a version bump -- 0.0.12 -> 0.0.74 was 73 diagnostics --
    # so it moves when someone means it to.
    "ty==0.0.74",
    "pre-commit>=4.5.1",
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12.20250915",
    "types-tqdm>=4.67.0.20250809",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.4.0",
    "httpx>=0.28.0",
    "import-linter>=2.10",
    "deptry>=0.24.0",
    "vulture>=2.14",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
    "hypothesis>=6.140",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src"]
# Workers are separate processes; without this they report nothing.
concurrency = ["multiprocessing"]
parallel = true

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_also = [
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
    "\\.\\.\\.$",
]

[tool.uv]
preview = true

[tool.uv.extra-build-dependencies]
eval7 = ["Cython"]

; import-linter contracts — Pawrrtal backend
;
; Mirrors the layer ordering defined in `.sentrux/rules.toml`. Sentrux's OSS
; build only evaluates 4 of the 17 rules in that file; this config plugs the
; gap by enforcing the layered architecture and the frontend↔backend
; boundary that Pro-only sentrux rules cover.
;
; Layer ordering: top of the list is the highest in the stack (the
; consumer). Modules in a higher layer can import from any lower layer but
; never from a higher one. Modules separated by `:` share the same layer
; and may import each other (non-independent siblings). The `|` separator
; means independent siblings — same level, but cannot import each other.
;
; Run:    cd backend && uv run lint-imports
; CI:     `.github/workflows/sentrux.yml` runs both sentrux + import-linter
;         on every PR to development/main.

[importlinter]
root_package = app
; `frontend` is treated as an external package by import-linter (it's not
; a Python module). The boundary contract below needs it visible to the
; resolver so it can be marked forbidden.
include_external_packages = True

; --- Contract 1: layered architecture (mirrors sentrux fe/be layers) ------

; `backend/main.py` is a sibling launcher (not under `app/`), so it can't sit
; inside the `app` container. It's a leaf — nothing imports it — so it
; doesn't need its own contract. The cli package below covers the rest of
; the be-entry layer.

[importlinter:contract:backend-layers]
name = Backend layered architecture (sentrux mirror)
type = layers
containers =
    app
layers =
    cli : infrastructure.app_factory : infrastructure.router_registry : infrastructure.startup : infrastructure.shutdown
    chat : conversations : agents : providers : tools : lcm : workspace : projects : governance : integrations : schemas
    models : governance_models : lcm_models : mcp_models
    infrastructure.auth : infrastructure.database : infrastructure.lifecycle : infrastructure.logging : infrastructure.middleware : infrastructure.models
; `app.channels` is intentionally NOT in any layer here yet:
; `channels/base.py` + `channels/registry.py` are generic adapter interfaces,
; while the concrete Telegram / Google Chat adapters still own surface-specific
; route, command, and delivery behavior. Keep tightening those seams in focused
; follow-ups rather than misrepresenting the package as layer-pure.
;
; `app.infrastructure.event_bus` and `app.infrastructure.observability` are
; also intentionally unlayered during this cleanup: both still bridge runtime
; orchestration, provider events, and persistence side effects. Split those
; modules in focused follow-ups before adding them to a lower-level layer.
;
; PR #223 extracted `Base` into `app.db_base`, breaking the legacy
; `app.db -> app.models` cycle that previously needed grandfathering here.
;
; Stack A (PRs #208–#225) landed several modules that read ORM
; rows / call CRUD directly — pragmatic for governance/audit pipelines that
; need to write audit_event/cost_ledger rows in-process. Grandfathered here
; so this contract doesn't block onward work; each entry should be flattened
; (e.g. inject a Protocol the caller satisfies, or move the side-effect into
; the api/crud layer) in a follow-up. Pattern mirrors `EXEMPT_FUNCTIONS` in
; `scripts/check-nesting.py`.
ignore_imports =
    ; Exporters (markdown / html / json) previously imported the
    ; ``Conversation`` + ``ChatMessage`` ORM rows directly. They now
    ; take ``ConversationLike`` + ``MessageLike`` Protocols from
    ; ``app.conversations.exports.types`` and stay layer-pure. (Cluster A
    ; flatten — exporters → models — has landed.)
    app.governance.audit -> app.models
    app.governance.cost_tracker -> app.models
    app.agents.scheduling.scheduler -> app.models
    app.infrastructure.event_bus.handlers -> app.workspace.crud
    ; LCM (Stack B / PRs #186–#196) owns three ORM tables
    ; (lcm_summaries, lcm_summary_sources, lcm_context_items) and must
    ; read/write them directly to assemble context, compact leaves, and
    ; condense same-depth summaries.  Same shape as the governance and
    ; exporter grandfathers above — flatten in a follow-up (e.g. inject
    ; a Protocol the caller satisfies, or move the side-effect into the
    ; api/crud layer).
    app.lcm -> app.models
    app.lcm.condense -> app.models
    app.tools.lcm_describe -> app.models
    app.tools.lcm_grep -> app.models
    app.tools.lcm_expand_query -> app.models
    ; LCM Retrieval Lab (PR #258 / issues #251–#256) extends the same
    ; substrate — observability, ranked search, eval harness, semantic
    ; retrieval — and must read the same ORM tables (now plus
    ; lcm_embeddings).  Grandfathered alongside the older LCM entries
    ; until the entire LCM stack is flattened in one pass.
    app.lcm.embeddings -> app.models
    app.lcm.evals -> app.models
    app.lcm.observe -> app.models
    app.tools.lcm_search -> app.models

; --- Contract 2: the legacy db ↔ models cycle is the one cycle sentrux
; allows (max_cycles = 1). Pin it explicitly so any *new* cycle fails CI. -

[importlinter:contract:no-other-cycles]
name = No new import cycles outside the known db ↔ models pair
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.chat
    app.conversations
    app.agents
    app.providers
    app.tools
    app.lcm
    app.workspace
    app.projects
    app.governance
    app.integrations
forbidden_modules =
    app.main
    app.cli
allow_indirect_imports = False
ignore_imports =
    ; (none — entry points should never be imported by lower layers)

; --- Contract 3: nothing in the codebase should import `frontend.*`.
; The frontend lives in a sibling directory and is not a Python package, so
; this contract is largely a safety net for accidental tooling glue. -----

[importlinter:contract:no-frontend-imports]
name = Backend must not import the frontend
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app
forbidden_modules =
    frontend

; --- Contract 4: provider adapters must not depend on channel adapters. ----

[importlinter:contract:providers-must-not-import-channels]
name = Providers must not import channels
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.providers
forbidden_modules =
    app.channels

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Strict ruleset. Each family adds a class of catch:
#   E, W    = pycodestyle errors/warnings
#   F       = pyflakes (unused imports, undefined names)
#   I       = isort (import sorting)
#   N       = pep8-naming (consistent naming conventions)
#   B       = flake8-bugbear (real bugs: mutable defaults, etc.)
#   A       = flake8-builtins (don't shadow builtins)
#   C4      = flake8-comprehensions (idiomatic comprehensions)
#   C90     = mccabe complexity (function complexity cap)
#   UP      = pyupgrade (modernize syntax for target Python)
#   SIM     = flake8-simplify (collapse redundant patterns)
#   ASYNC   = flake8-async (async/await footguns)
#   PERF    = perflint (avoid known-slow patterns)
#   PL      = pylint (subset)
#   PT      = flake8-pytest-style (idiomatic pytest)
#   PTH     = flake8-use-pathlib (prefer pathlib over os.path)
#   RET     = flake8-return (clean control flow on returns)
#   RUF     = ruff-specific (latest catches)
#   S       = flake8-bandit (security: hardcoded secrets, weak crypto, eval, etc.)
#   T20     = flake8-print (no stray print statements)
#   TID     = flake8-tidy-imports (banned-imports + relative-import policy)
#   TRY     = tryceratops (exception-handling antipatterns)
#   D       = pydocstyle (docstrings on public API — matches project rule)
select = [
    "E", "W", "F", "I", "N", "B", "A", "C4", "C90", "UP", "SIM", "ASYNC",
    "PERF", "PL", "PT", "PTH", "RET", "RUF", "S", "T20", "TID", "TRY", "D",
]
# Ruff's ``PLC2701`` (Pylint preview) would catch the cross-module
# private-import pattern described in
# ``.cursor/plugins/pawrrtal/rules/clean-code/python-module-privacy.mdc`` (issue #283).
# Today the codebase has ~124 existing violations (mostly tests
# importing module-level test helpers) so enabling the rule would
# fail CI on every PR.  The rule is documented for human + agent
# review; mechanical enforcement is a follow-up sweep, not this PR.
# When enabling: add ``"PLC2701"`` to ``select`` above and turn
# ``preview = true`` + ``explicit-preview-rules = true`` on.
ignore = [
    "E501",     # line length — handled by formatter, soft cap only
    "D100",     # missing module docstring (too noisy on small modules)
    "D104",     # missing docstring in __init__.py
    "D107",     # missing docstring in __init__ method (covered by class docstring)
    "D203",     # incompatible with D211 (no blank line before class)
    "D213",     # incompatible with D212 (multi-line summary on first line)
    "PLR0913",  # too many args — FastAPI handlers regularly need many deps
    "B008",     # function call in default arg — required for FastAPI Depends()
    "TRY003",   # long exception messages — over-prescriptive
    "TRY300",   # else-after-try — clearer to keep return inline for short paths
    "TRY301",   # raise within try — sometimes clearer for explicit re-raise
    "RET504",   # unnecessary assignment before return — assignment often aids readability
    "S101",     # assert in tests is fine (per-file ignore covers tests; this catches asserts in app code only)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = [
    "D",       # tests don't need docstrings on every fn
    "PLR2004", # magic numbers in test data are fine
    "S101",    # assert is the whole point of pytest
    "S105",    # hardcoded password strings (test fixtures)
    "S106",    # hardcoded password (function arg)
    "S108",    # /tmp paths in test scenarios are fine
    "PT018",   # compound asserts in tests are fine if they're checking related state
    "PLC0415", # lazy/in-fn imports in tests are intentional: avoid module-load
               # side effects, isolate `importlib.reload` cases, and let fixtures
               # set env before the SUT is bound. Hoisting defeats those patterns.
]
"tests/conftest.py" = ["D", "E402"]   # sys.path manipulation must come before imports
"main.py" = ["E402"]                  # allow early logging configuration before other imports
"alembic/**" = ["D", "E", "I", "S"]   # migrations are auto-generated
"app/cli/**" = [
    "T20",   # CLI scripts legitimately use print
    "S603",  # subprocess calls in CLI are operator-driven, not user-input
    "S607",  # `git` and similar trusted binaries on PATH are intentional
]
"tests/test_alembic_postgres_upgrade.py" = [
    "S603",  # spawns the real `alembic` CLI (via sys.executable -m) on purpose:
             # the advisory-lock DDL-rollback bug only reproduces through a real
             # env.py connection lifecycle, not an in-process call. URL is built
             # from a test-controlled scratch DB name, not external input.
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Cap cyclomatic complexity. Functions above this should be split.
max-complexity = 12

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# "parents" allows same-package relative imports (from .base import X) but
# bans parent-traversing ones (from ..foo). The all-relative ban produced
# 12 violations in legitimate intra-package imports.
ban-relative-imports = "parents"

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["app"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

# --- pytest -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Pinned to ``tests/`` so pytest never wanders into the vendored codex SDK's
# own test suite (``backend/vendor/codex/sdk/python/tests/``), which depends
# on the codex binary being available and fails in our CI environment.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
norecursedirs = ["vendor", ".venv", "node_modules", "__pycache__", "*.egg-info"]
filterwarnings = [
    # google-genai defines an aiohttp.ClientSession subclass at import time.
    # aiohttp emits this deprecation from aiohttp.client before Pawrrtal code
    # can influence the SDK internals; keep the filter exact so first-party
    # warnings still surface.
    "ignore:Inheritance class AiohttpClientSession from ClientSession is discouraged:DeprecationWarning",
]

# --- mypy: static type checker ---------------------------------------------
# Strict-ish defaults. Project rule forbids cast(Any, ...), so we want mypy
# to surface real type holes rather than letting them slip through.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
strict = true
# Targeted relaxations — strict mode is too loud against FastAPI/SQLAlchemy
# ecosystems where many third-party annotations are still incomplete.
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = false  # FastAPI/pytest decorators trip this
# Required because ``app.models`` and ``app.api.models`` both end with ``models.py``
# — without explicit package bases, mypy can't disambiguate them.
explicit_package_bases = true
# Optional provider SDKs live behind plugin/provider boundaries; local stubs
# let strict checks run when a worktree has not initialized every SDK.
mypy_path = ".:typestubs:vendor/codex/sdk/python/src"
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
exclude = [
    "alembic/versions/",
    "workspaces/",
    ".venv/",
    # Vendored submodules (e.g. backend/vendor/codex) follow their own
    # type conventions; mypy treats them as authoritative for the SDK
    # surface but the SDK's example scripts + ad-hoc tests are noisy.
    "vendor/",
    # Agentic tooling / editor metadata directories.
    "\\.agents/",
    "\\.claude/",
    "\\.cursor/",
    "\\.pi/",
    "\\.opencode/",
    "\\.crush/",
    "\\.codex/",
    "\\.beans/",
    "\\.zed/",
    "\\.vscode/",
    "\\.sentrux/",
    # Provider image translation is not implemented for every host yet.
    "tests/test_provider_images.py",
]
files = ["app", "tests", "main.py"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = false  # test fixtures are fine without explicit types

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Vendored Codex Python SDK (``vendor/codex/sdk/python``) is on ``mypy_path``
# so ``import openai_codex`` resolves, but the generated sources are not held
# to Pawrrtal's strict gate.
module = "openai_codex.*"
follow_imports = "skip"

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Third-party packages without complete type stubs.
# xai_sdk ships generated protobuf classes without a ``py.typed`` marker;
# mypy can't follow the .pyi files the SDK omits.  The provider does its
# own narrow type-checking at the seam.
module = ["sqlalchemy_utils.*", "mcp.*", "markitdown.*", "xai_sdk.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# google-auth ships ``py.typed`` but its service_account credential
# constructors are still untyped (``from_service_account_file`` returns
# ``Any``), so strict-mode ``disallow_untyped_calls`` / ``warn_return_any``
# fire at the call site. This module is the single, narrow boundary that
# touches google-auth; relax those two checks here only, rather than
# scatter inline ignores. Everything else in the module stays strict.
module = "app.channels.google_chat.auth"
disallow_untyped_calls = false
warn_return_any = false


# --- bandit: security scanner ------------------------------------------------
# Catches hardcoded secrets, weak crypto, shell injection, unsafe deserialization.
# Ruff already covers most flake8-bandit (S) rules during lint, but bandit's
# AST-based checks find a few extras that ruff doesn't yet implement.
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = [
    "tests",
    ".venv",
    "alembic/versions",
    "workspaces",
    "app/cli",  # CLI subprocess calls are operator-driven; ruff S-rules with per-file ignore handles them
    # Agentic tooling / editor metadata directories.
    ".agents",
    ".claude",
    ".cursor",
    ".pi",
    ".opencode",
    ".crush",
    ".codex",
    ".beans",
    ".zed",
    ".vscode",
    ".sentrux",
]
skips = [
    "B101",  # assert_used — covered by ruff S101 with its own per-file ignore policy
]

# Without `explicit_package_bases`, mypy collapses `app/api/channels.py`
# and `app/channels/__init__.py` into a single ``channels`` module name
# and aborts with "duplicate module" before checking anything else.
# Naming the package roots makes mypy resolve them as `app.api.channels`
# and `app.channels`, which are distinct.

# =============================================================================

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "typer.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "kombu.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "amqp.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# =============================================================================
# ruff
# =============================================================================
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 88
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # Pyflakes
    "I",      # isort
    "B",      # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "ARG",    # flake8-unused-arguments
    "SIM",    # flake8-simplify
    "TCH",    # flake8-type-checking
    "PTH",    # flake8-use-pathlib
    "RUF",    # Ruff-specific
    "PGH004", # blanket noqa (always name the rule)
    "D",      # pydocstyle
    "C90",    # mccabe complexity
    "PLR0911", # too many return statements
    "PLR0912", # too many branches
    "PLR0915", # too many statements
    "PLR0917", # too many positional arguments (make extra params keyword-only)
    "BLE",    # blind except (allowed only with `# noqa: BLE001  <reason>`)
    "ERA",    # commented-out code
    "RET",    # flake8-return
    "PT",     # flake8-pytest-style
    "PLR0402", # manual from-import
    "PLR1711", # useless return
    "PLR1714", # repeated equality comparison
    "PLR5501", # collapsible else-if
]
# Baseline: code that predates the rules above carries a per-line
# `# noqa: <codes>` (added with `ruff check --add-noqa`), to be removed by
# refactors. Don't add bare noqa comments: a new one needs a reason after the
# codes, e.g. `# noqa: BLE001  fire-and-forget: ...`. RUF100 (via "RUF") flags
# any noqa that no longer suppresses anything, so the baseline only shrinks.
ignore = [
    "E501",   # Line too long (handled by formatter)
    "D100",   # Missing docstring in public module
    "D104",   # Missing docstring in public package
    "D107",   # Missing docstring in __init__
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# pylint defaults, written down so the limits are visible
max-branches = 12
max-returns = 6
max-statements = 50
max-positional-args = 5

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["stemtrace"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["D", "ARG"]  # No docstrings required in tests
"examples/**/*.py" = ["ARG001", "D417"]  # bind=True tasks have unused self

# =============================================================================
# import-linter (architecture boundaries, see CONTRIBUTING.md)
# =============================================================================
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "stemtrace"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core is independent of library, server and transports"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["stemtrace.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["stemtrace.library", "stemtrace.server", "stemtrace.transports"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core uses no broker, Celery or web libraries"

    "amqp",
    "celery",
    "fastapi",
    "httpx",
    "kombu",
    "redis",
    "starlette",

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
