type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["stemtrace.transports"]
forbidden_modules = ["stemtrace.library", "stemtrace.server"]

# =============================================================================
# pytest
# =============================================================================
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "-m", "not e2e",  # Exclude E2E tests by default (run with: pytest -m e2e)
]
markers = [
    "integration: requires running services (Redis, Celery)",
    "e2e: end-to-end tests (slow, requires Docker)",
    "slow: tests that take > 1 second",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:celery.*",
    # Starlette 1.x TestClient prefers httpx2 but still supports httpx.
    "ignore:Using `httpx` with `starlette.testclient` is deprecated",
]
asyncio_mode = "auto"

# =============================================================================
# coverage
# =============================================================================
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/stemtrace"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "src/stemtrace/server/__main__.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "^\\s*\\.\\.\\.\\s*$",  # Protocol method stubs (a bare `...` body line)
    "class.*Protocol.*:",
]

[importlinter]
root_package = deeptutor

[importlinter:contract:core-purity]
name = Core contains values and protocols only
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    deeptutor.core
forbidden_modules =
    deeptutor.app
    deeptutor.api
    deeptutor.runtime
    deeptutor.services

[importlinter:contract:no-api-backimports]
name = Runtime and service layers do not import API adapters
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    deeptutor.runtime
    deeptutor.services
    deeptutor.knowledge
    deeptutor.learning
    deeptutor.multi_user
    deeptutor.capabilities
    deeptutor.agents
forbidden_modules =
    deeptutor.api
ignore_imports =
    deeptutor.learning.tests.** -> deeptutor.api.**

[importlinter:contract:app-adapter-direction]
name = Application does not import API adapters
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    deeptutor.app
forbidden_modules =
    deeptutor.api

# Python project configuration for DeepTutor
# This file configures Black, Ruff, and other Python tools

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "deeptutor"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "An agent-native intelligent learning companion with multi-agent collaboration and RAG"
# Python 3.14 is supported by the core app now that compiled base dependencies
# such as FAISS publish compatible wheels. Keep a forward cap so a future
# interpreter is not advertised before the compiled dependency stack is ready.
# Individual optional integrations may carry tighter markers below.
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.15"
readme = "README.md"
license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}
dependencies = [
    # Core runtime
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.0",
    "openai>=1.30.0",
    "tiktoken>=0.5.0",
    "aiohttp>=3.9.4",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "requests>=2.32.2",
    "ddgs>=9.9.1",
    "nest_asyncio>=1.5.8",
    "tenacity>=8.0.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0.0",
    "packaging>=24.2",
    "jsonschema>=4.20.0,<5.0.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19.0",
    "typer>=0.9.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "prompt_toolkit>=3.0.36",
    "pyte>=0.8.1",  # in-memory terminal emulator: scrape Claude Code's /model TUI on sync
    # MCP client. Core rather than a `partners`-only extra (issue #792): the
    # default chat/tool surface includes configurable MCP servers, so a plain
    # install must be able to connect them without an optional extra.
    "mcp>=1.26.0,<2.0.0",
    "pageindex>=0.2.10,<0.3.0",
    # Partner channel QR onboarding (WeChat, WeCom, Feishu). Same reasoning as
    # `mcp` above: scan-based onboarding is part of the default partner setup
    # surface, it is pure Python with no compiled or system dependencies, and
    # without it the browser renders no code at all — the operator sees a
    # button that does nothing, with no error to explain why.
    "qrcode>=7.4.0,<9.0.0",
    # IANA time zone database for `zoneinfo`. Windows ships none, so without
    # it every named zone (even "UTC") is unknown there and usage statistics,
    # practice reviews and cron schedules reject every timezone they are given.
    # On Linux/macOS `zoneinfo` keeps preferring the system database.
    "tzdata>=2024.1",
    # Full app dependencies included by default for `pip install deeptutor`.
    "anthropic>=0.30.0",
    "dashscope>=1.14.0",
    "perplexityai>=0.1.0",
    "oauth-cli-kit>=0.1.1",
    "llama-index>=0.14.12",
    # The current BM25 integration pins PyStemmer <3, whose 2.x line has no
    # Python 3.14 wheels. Skip it there so ordinary installs never require a C
    # compiler; the retriever already falls back to vector search when absent.
    "bm25s>=0.3.14,<0.4.0",  # Legacy page lookup without optional PyStemmer
    "llama-index-retrievers-bm25>=0.7.1,<0.8.0; python_version < '3.14'",
    # FAISS vector store: vectorized ANN retrieval that replaces SimpleVectorStore's
    # brute-force per-query scan for large knowledge bases (issue #552). The
    # pipeline imports it lazily and falls back to SimpleVectorStore if absent.
    "llama-index-vector-stores-faiss>=0.4.0,<1.0.0",
    "faiss-cpu>=1.8.0,<2.0.0; python_version < '3.14'",
    "faiss-cpu>=1.12.0,<2.0.0; python_version >= '3.14'",
    "PyMuPDF>=1.26.0",
    "Pillow>=10.0.0",
    "numpy>=1.24.0,<3.0.0",
    "arxiv>=2.0.0",
    "python-docx>=1.1.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.0",
    "python-pptx>=1.0.0",
    "pypdf>=4.0.0",
    "pdfplumber>=0.11.0",
    "reportlab>=4.0.0",
    "defusedxml>=0.7.1",
    "youtube-transcript-api>=1.2.0,<2.0.0",
    "fastapi>=0.100.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.24.0",
    "websockets>=12.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.6",
    "bcrypt>=4.0.0",
    "python-jose[cryptography]>=3.3.0",
    "pocketbase>=0.12.0",
    "redis>=5.0.0,<7.0.0",
    "loguru>=0.7.3,<1.0.0",
    "json-repair>=0.57.0,<1.0.0",
    "croniter>=6.0.0,<7.0.0",
    # Process-tree memory readings and Windows MinerU worker ownership.
    "psutil>=5.9.0,<8.0.0",
    "pywin32; sys_platform == 'win32'",  # MinerU Job Object ownership
]

[project.scripts]
deeptutor = "deeptutor_cli.main:main"
deeptutor-export-frontend-contracts = "deeptutor.api.contracts.export:main"

# CodeBuddy chat works over HTTP with the login state the IDE plugin / CLI
# already stores. This extra adds the Agent SDK (a ~130 MB bundled headless
# CLI) for in-app browser login and CLI-driven agent tools.
# Upper-bounded on purpose: the provider probes the SDK for its turn-limit
# and permission-mode kwargs, and a minor bump that renames them would make
# every options build fail — codebuddy_provider fails closed with a clear
# message rather than running the agent unrestricted. The floor tracks the
# published series: there is no 0.1.24 on PyPI (0.1.x stops at 0.1.19), so the
# old `>=0.1.24,<0.2` range was unsatisfiable and any resolver rejected it.
# Not in `all` — it vendors a ~130 MB headless CLI and chat works over plain

# Optional document-parsing engines for the shared parse layer
# (deeptutor/services/parsing). MinerU is an external CLI / hosted API and is

# absent engine simply reports unavailable in Settings → Document Parsing.
parse-markitdown = ["markitdown[all]>=0.1.7"]
# Docling's base package intentionally leaves some format backends as extras.
# Install all input-format dependencies so DeepTutor can honor the complete
# upstream format list. Legacy Office needs LibreOffice and video needs ffmpeg
# on the host in addition to these Python packages.
parse-docling = [
    "docling[xbrl]>=2.123.1",
    "docling-slim[format-iwork,format-opendocument,format-video]>=2.123.1",
]
# Current PyMuPDF4LLM includes CPU-only layout/OCR and image extraction on its
# public conversion path. Keep it upgradeable so format and layout gains land

parse-pymupdf4llm = ["pymupdf4llm>=1.28.2"]
parse-liteparse = ["liteparse>=2.14.2"]
parse = [
    "deeptutor[parse-markitdown]",
    "deeptutor[parse-docling]",
    "deeptutor[parse-pymupdf4llm]",
    "deeptutor[parse-liteparse]",
]

    "mistune>=3.0.0,<4.0.0",
    "nh3>=0.2.18,<1.0.0",

# Math Animator addon (Manim). Mirrors requirements/math-animator.txt.

math-animator = ["manim>=0.19.0"]

# GraphRAG knowledge-base engine (microsoft/graphrag). Optional, heavy
# (LiteLLM + lancedb + graspologic) and kept out of `all` so it stays a
# deliberate opt-in. The pipeline imports lazily and the adapter targets the
# 3.x API (see services/rag/pipelines/graphrag/engine.py). Every graphrag 3.x
# release is capped at python <3.14; the `python_version` marker mirrors that
# so on 3.14+ the extra resolves to a no-op instead of an unsatisfiable hard
# dep — otherwise pip backtracks deeptutor to the last extra-free version
# (1.4.5) and silently downgrades. Floor is 3.0.1 (3.0.0/3.0.3 were yanked).
graphrag = ["graphrag>=3.0.1,<4.0.0; python_version < '3.14'"]

# Built-in LightRAG provider. The exact release is intentional: the adapter
# isolates a private source-resolver seam and locks it with smoke tests.
# MinerU remains an independently selected DeepTutor parser and is not a
# transitive dependency of this extra.
rag-lightrag = ["lightrag-hku==1.5.7"]

# Optional cross-encoder reranker for the default LlamaIndex engine. The
# sentence-transformers/torch stack is heavy and model-dependent, so it stays
# out of `all`; retrieval lazily falls back to embedding-only ranking when the
# package or configured model is unavailable.
rag-rerank = ["sentence-transformers>=3.0.0,<6.0.0; python_version < '3.14'"]

# Optional request screening (rate limit, IP allow/deny lists, attack-pattern

# Everything: server + partners + non-E2EE matrix + math-animator + dev tools.
all = [
    "deeptutor[partners]",
    "deeptutor[matrix]",
    "deeptutor[math-animator]",
    "deeptutor[dev]",
    "deeptutor[video-learning]",

[tool.setuptools]
include-package-data = true

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = {attr = "deeptutor.__version__.__version__"}

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
include = ["deeptutor*", "deeptutor_cli*"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
# Runtime data shipped inside the deeptutor package: prompt YAMLs (loaded by
# PromptManager from PACKAGE_ROOT/deeptutor/.../prompts/*.yaml), markdown
# templates (builtin SKILL.md files, vision_solver prompts), and helper shell
# scripts. Without these, ``pip install deeptutor`` ships a wheel missing
# every agent prompt and capability fails at first use.
deeptutor = [
    "**/*.yaml",
    "**/*.yml",
    "**/*.md",
    "**/*.json",
    "**/*.sh",
    "**/*.j2",
    "**/*.jinja",
]
deeptutor_cli = ["**/*.md"]
deeptutor_web = ["**/*", ".next/**/*"]

# ============================================
# Black code formatter configuration
# ============================================
[tool.black]
line-length = 100
target-version = ['py311', 'py312', 'py313', 'py314']
include = '\.pyi?$'
extend-exclude = '''
/(
  # Exclude directories
  \.eggs
  | \.git
  | \.hg
  | \.mypy_cache
  | \.tox
  | \.venv
  | venv
  | _build
  | buck-out
  | build
  | dist
  | __pycache__
  | node_modules
  | \.next
)/
'''

# ============================================
# Ruff linter and formatter configuration
# ============================================
[tool.ruff]
# Target Python version
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Enable only foundational lint rules (intentionally relaxed)
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors (语法错误)
    "F",   # pyflakes (未使用的导入、变量等)
    "I",   # isort (import 排序)
    # Keep only essential checks; other rules stay relaxed
]

extend-select = [
    "B006",  # Do not use mutable data structures for argument defaults
]

# Ignore specific rules (keep the lint profile relaxed)
ignore = [
    "E501",  # Line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",  # Do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "PLR0911", # Too many return statements
    "PLR0912", # Too many branches
    "PLR0913", # Too many arguments
    "PLR0915", # Too many statements
    "PLR2004", # Magic value used in comparison
    "TRY003", # Avoid specifying long messages outside exception class
    "T201",  # print found (allowed for debugging scripts)
    "E722",  # Do not use bare except (kept relaxed for legacy paths)
    "E402",  # Module level import not at top of file (kept relaxed)
    "PLC0415", # import should be at top-level (kept relaxed)
    "PTH123", # open() should be replaced by Path.open() (standard open allowed)
    "PTH103", # os.makedirs() should be replaced by Path.mkdir() (os.makedirs allowed)
    "PTH118", # os.path.join() should be replaced by Path (os.path.join allowed)
    "EM101",  # Exception must not use a string literal
    "EM102",  # Exception must not use an f-string literal
    "TRY002", # Create your own exception
    "TRY300", # Consider moving this statement to an else block
    "DTZ005", # datetime.now() called without tz argument
    "RET504", # Unnecessary assignment before return
    "PLW2901", # for loop variable overwritten by assignment target
    "F841",  # Local variable assigned but never used
    "ERA001", # Found commented-out code (kept relaxed)
]

# Exclude patterns
exclude = [
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".git-rewrite",
    ".hg",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".nox",
    ".pants.d",
    ".pyenv",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".pytype",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    ".vscode",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "buck-out",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    ".next",
    "out",
    "venv",
    "__pycache__",
]

# Allow autofix for all enabled rules
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = []

# Allow unused variables when underscore-prefixed
dummy-variable-rgx = "^(_+|(_+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+?))$"

[tool.ruff.format]
# Use double quotes for strings
quote-style = "double"
# Indent with spaces
indent-style = "space"
# Respect magic trailing comma
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
# Automatically detect the appropriate line ending
line-ending = "auto"

# ============================================
# Ruff import sorting (isort replacement)
# ============================================
[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["deeptutor", "deeptutor_cli", "scripts"]
force-sort-within-sections = true
split-on-trailing-comma = true

# ============================================
# Ruff per-file-ignores
# ============================================
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Allow longer lines in test files
# F401: Allow unused imports for availability checks in tests
"**/test_*.py" = ["E501", "PLR2004", "F401"]
"**/__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # Allow unused imports in __init__.py

# ============================================
# Ruff mccabe complexity
# ============================================
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

# ============================================
# Pytest configuration
# ============================================
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests", "deeptutor/learning/tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
markers = [
    "asyncio: mark async tests that require pytest-asyncio",
    "integration: requires explicitly configured external services",
    "redis_integration: requires DEEPTUTOR_TEST_REDIS_URL",
    "real_llm_resolver: exercises LLM config resolution itself, so it keeps the real resolver",
]
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--disable-warnings",
    "--tb=short",
    "--import-mode=importlib",
]

# ============================================
# MyPy type checking configuration
# ============================================
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
# Relaxed type checking for gradual adoption
pretty = false
show_error_context = false
warn_return_any = false
warn_no_return = false
show_error_codes = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
follow_imports = "silent"
# Disable strict checks that generate too many errors
check_untyped_defs = false
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
no_implicit_optional = false

# Module-specific overrides
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
ignore_errors = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "deeptutor.tools.*"
ignore_errors = true  # Some tools may have dynamic imports

# ============================================
# Bandit security linting configuration
# ============================================
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "scripts"]
# B101=assert, B311=random, B403/B404=pickle/subprocess imports
# B110=try_except_pass (intentional for non-critical error handling)
# B104=hardcoded_bind_all_interfaces (required for server binding)
# B112=try_except_continue (intentional for iteration)
# B105=hardcoded_password_string (false positive on empty string initialization)
# B301=pickle (used for internal embedding cache, not untrusted data)
# B501=request_with_no_cert_validation (opt-in via env var for dev/testing)
# B603=subprocess_without_shell_equals_true (controlled execution)
# B202=tarfile_unsafe_members (already using safe_members filter)
skips = ["B101", "B311", "B403", "B404", "B110", "B104", "B112", "B105", "B301", "B501", "B603", "B202"]

[project]
name = "skyward"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Execute Python functions on cloud compute with a simple decorator"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = {text = "MIT"}
authors = [{name = "Gabriel Francisco"}]
keywords = ["cloud", "distributed", "gpu", "serverless", "compute"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Framework :: AsyncIO",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]

# What a bare node needs: it runs the worker and nothing else.
dependencies = [
    "casty>=0.30.2",
    "cloudpickle>=3.1",
    "loky>=3.5",
    "lz4>=4.3",
    "msgspec>=0.19",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# What the SDK needs to reach a control plane — any control plane, including one
# running in the same process.
client = [
    "httpx>=0.28",
]
# The live terminal dashboard, and `sky app`. Without it the pool still prints
# its log, one line at a time — the extra buys the pinned panel and the screen,
# not the ability to watch.
tui = [
    "rich>=13.7",
    "textual>=8.2.8",
]
# What the daemon needs and the node does not. A machine rented by the hour
# should not be waiting on a web framework it will never serve with.
server = [
    "httpx>=0.28",
    "litestar>=2.13",
    "piccolo[sqlite]>=1.0",
    "asyncssh>=2.22.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.30",
    # Uvicorn serves a WebSocket only if one of these is importable, and falls back
    # to refusing the upgrade if neither is. The browser console's terminal is a
    # WebSocket, so without this the daemon serves the page and not the thing on it.
    "websockets>=13",
    # The daemon mints a certificate authority per compute and signs its members.
    # The node only reads the three files it is handed, so this stops here.
    "cryptography>=42",
    # `sky server interface set` names an interface, and the daemon listens on the
    # addresses it has when it starts; the standard library cannot list them.
    "psutil>=5.9",
]
# Three adapters need an sdk of their own; the other twelve speak plain HTTP
# through httpx. An adapter whose sdk is absent is not registered, so `server`
# buys the daemon and these buy the clouds it can reach.
aws = [
    "aioboto3>=13.0.0",
]
gcp = [
    "cryptography>=42",
]
salad = [
    "salad-cloud-sdk>=0.9.0a17",
    "websockets>=13",
]
providers = [
    "skyward[aws,gcp,salad]",
]
# The `sky` command. A node installs skyward to run a function and has no
# business acquiring an argument parser to do it.
cli = [
    "cyclopts>=3.0",
    # `sky run` reads a script's requires-python, which is a PEP 440 specifier.
    "packaging>=24",
]
# A local Jupyter whose kernel runs on a compute (`skyward.notebook`). Client
# side only: jupyter-client and traitlets are what the provisioner imports, and
# ipykernel is what the machine launches — the image needs it, this does not.
notebook = [
    "jupyter-client>=8.0",
    "traitlets>=5.0",
    "ipykernel>=6.0",
]
# The user-facing object storage module (`skyward.storage`). Its S3 client is
# imported lazily, so the dependency is only needed when a Storage is opened.
storage = [
    "aioboto3>=13.0.0",
]
# `sky mcp`: the daemon as tools an AI assistant calls, over the Model Context
# Protocol. The command is the CLI's, so it carries the CLI and the client along.
mcp = [
    "skyward[client,cli]",
    "mcp>=2.3",
]
# Everything skyward ships, for the machine that is developing against it rather
# than running one job.
all = [
    "skyward[client,server,cli,tui,notebook,storage,providers,mcp]",
]

[project.scripts]
sky = "skyward.cli:app"

[project.entry-points."jupyter_client.kernel_provisioners"]
skyward = "skyward.core.notebook.provisioner:SkywardKernelProvisioner"

    "local: features that need nothing but this process",
    "sanity: provider sanity tests (real cloud, real GPUs)",
    "aws: AWS provider tests",
    "runpod: RunPod provider tests",
    "vastai: VastAI provider tests",
    "verda: Verda provider tests",
    "gcp: GCP provider tests",

]

[dependency-groups]

    "skyward[all]",
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.25",
    "pytest-cov>=7.0.0",
    "pytest-describe>=3.2",
    "pytest-sugar>=1.1.1",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.4.0",
    "pyright>=1.1",
    "ruff>=0.9",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "jax>=0.8.2",
    "keras>=3.13.0",
    "scikit-learn>=1.8.0",
    "types-aioboto3[ec2,pricing]>=15.5.0",
]
docs = [
    "mkdocs-material>=9.5",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.27",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "skyward"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Folders are layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "skyward.cli",
    "skyward.core",
    "skyward.server",
    "skyward.providers",
    "skyward.worker",
    "skyward.shared | skyward.api",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # The embedded transport: the client hosts the daemon in-process when asked to.
    "skyward.core.client -> skyward.server.http.app",
    # The joblib backend runs client-side only; the import is lazy and a node never reaches it.
    "skyward.worker.plugins.joblib -> skyward.core.function",
]

[tool.uv]
# casty is ours; opt it out of the global 7-day exclude-newer quarantine.
exclude-newer-package = { casty = "0 seconds" }

[importlinter]
root_package = faultmaven

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 1: Service Layer Independence
# ============================================================================
# Services should not directly import from each other
# Service dependencies are injected via the DI container.
[importlinter:contract:1]
name = Service layer independence
type = independence
modules =
    # Legacy services migrated to modules:
    #   auth_service, user_service → modules/auth/domain/services/
    #   case_service → modules/case/domain/services/case_service.py
    #   evidence_artifact_service, file_storage_service → modules/evidence/domain/services/
    # Preprocessing moved to modules/preprocessing (Domain Service pattern)
    faultmaven.modules.preprocessing
    # Analytics moved to infrastructure/observability (cross-cutting metrics)
    # Knowledge services (vertical slice module)
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge.domain.services.knowledge_service

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 2: Services Cannot Import API Layer
# ============================================================================
# API layer depends on services, not the other way around
# This prevents circular dependencies and maintains proper layering
#
# Violation: Service importing from API is a critical architectural error
[importlinter:contract:2]
name = Services cannot import API layer
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.services
forbidden_modules =
    faultmaven.api

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 3: Models Cannot Import Services
# ============================================================================
# Models are data structures; they should not import business logic
# This prevents circular dependencies between models and services
[importlinter:contract:3]
name = Models cannot import services
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.models
forbidden_modules =
    faultmaven.services

# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION NOTES
# ============================================================================
# Phase 3 Week 13: Baseline and Enforcement
# - Establish current violation baseline
# - Enable CI/CD enforcement to prevent NEW violations
# - Focus on critical architectural boundaries
# - Do NOT fix all violations yet (that's Week 14-18)
#
# Phase 3 Week 14-15: DI Container Refactoring
# - Tighten Contract 1 (service independence)
# - All service dependencies via DI
#
# Phase 3 Week 16-18: Vertical Slice Extraction
# - Add contracts for module boundaries
# - Extract modules/auth, modules/case, modules/knowledge, etc.
# - Each module self-contained with router, service, models, tests
# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 4: Knowledge Module Layer Boundaries
# ============================================================================
# Enforce clean architecture within the Knowledge module vertical slice
# Layers are listed from highest to lowest dependency level:
# - API layer (highest) can depend on Domain and Infrastructure
# - Domain layer (middle) can depend on Infrastructure
# - Infrastructure layer (lowest) cannot depend on higher layers
# Exception: Infrastructure CAN import Domain models (repositories need models)
[importlinter:contract:4]
name = Knowledge module layer boundaries
type = layers
layers =
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge.api
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge.domain
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge.infrastructure
ignore_imports =
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge.infrastructure.persistence.knowledge_item_repository -> faultmaven.modules.knowledge.domain.models.knowledge_item

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 5: Case Module Layer Boundaries
# ============================================================================
# Enforce clean architecture within the Case module vertical slice
[importlinter:contract:5]
name = Case module layer boundaries
type = layers
layers =
    faultmaven.modules.case.api
    faultmaven.modules.case.domain
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure
ignore_imports =
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.postgresql_hybrid_case_repository.* -> faultmaven.modules.case.domain.models.*
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.postgresql_hybrid_case_repository.* -> faultmaven.modules.case.domain.owned_models.*
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.case_repository -> faultmaven.modules.case.domain.models.*
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.case_repository -> faultmaven.modules.case.domain.owned_models.*
    # The cross-enterprise metadata reader builds CaseMetadata, whose derived
    # fields come from the domain rules a loaded case applies (ADR-012 D9).
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.case_metadata_reader -> faultmaven.modules.case.domain.models.*
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.sqlite_case_repository.* -> faultmaven.modules.case.contracts
    # sqlite_case_repository -> owned_models.* ignore removed in storage redesign
    # 2026-04 phase 2: the standalone evidence path was deleted and those imports
    # no longer exist, so import-linter flags the ignore entry itself.
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.sessionless_case_repository -> faultmaven.modules.case.contracts
    faultmaven.modules.case.contracts -> faultmaven.modules.case.domain.models.*
    faultmaven.modules.case.contracts -> faultmaven.modules.case.domain.owned_models.*

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 6: Auth Module Layer Boundaries
# ============================================================================
# Enforce clean architecture within the Auth module vertical slice
# Re-enabled with ignores for infrastructure → domain model imports (repositories need models)
[importlinter:contract:6]
name = Auth module layer boundaries
type = layers
layers =
    faultmaven.modules.auth.api
    faultmaven.modules.auth.domain
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure
ignore_imports =
    # session_repository ignore removed in storage redesign 2026-04 phase 3 —
    # the SQL session repository was deleted (auth sessions are Redis-only).
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.repositories.oauth_code_repository -> faultmaven.modules.auth.contracts
    # ITokenRevocationStore interface defined in jwt_token_generator (should be in contracts)
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.stores.token_revocation_store -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.services.jwt_token_generator
    # SSO adapter implements the ISSOIdentityProvider port defined in contracts
    # (same DIP pattern as oauth_code_repository above). ADR-015.
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.sso.workos_provider -> faultmaven.modules.auth.contracts
    # SSO org-mapping adapter implements the ISSOOrgMappingRepository port
    # defined in contracts (same DIP pattern as above). #869.
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.repositories.sso_org_mapping_repository -> faultmaven.modules.auth.contracts
    # SSO personal-tenant adapter implements the ISSOPersonalEnterpriseRepository port
    # defined in contracts (same DIP pattern as above). #1045.
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.repositories.sso_personal_enterprise_repository -> faultmaven.modules.auth.contracts

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 7: Agent Module Layer Boundaries
# ============================================================================
# Enforce clean architecture within the Agent module vertical slice
# Re-enabled after Gap #15/#16 fixes (removed infrastructure imports from domain layer)
[importlinter:contract:7]
name = Agent module layer boundaries
type = layers
layers =
    faultmaven.modules.agent.api
    faultmaven.modules.agent.domain
    faultmaven.modules.agent.tools
ignore_imports =
    # Indirect chain: tools → (various shared modules) → models → agent.domain.models.agentic
    # The shared models package re-exports agent domain models for backward compatibility.
    # This is a transitive dependency, not a direct layer violation.
    faultmaven.models -> faultmaven.modules.agent.domain.models.agentic
    faultmaven.models.api -> faultmaven.modules.agent.domain.models.agentic

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 8: Evidence Module Boundaries (storage redesign 2026-04 phase 2)
# ============================================================================
# The standalone evidence path was deleted in phase 2 — the Evidence module's
# api/ package is gone entirely, and domain/ now contains only the
# FileStorageService plus compatibility re-exports. Evidence itself is
# case-tied and owned by the Case module. The original layer contract
# (api → domain) is therefore moot; we keep a forbidden-import contract to
# prevent Evidence from importing from Case infrastructure directly.
[importlinter:contract:8]
name = Evidence module must not import Case infrastructure
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.evidence
forbidden_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 9: Report Module Layer Boundaries
# ============================================================================
# Enforce clean architecture within the Report module vertical slice
[importlinter:contract:9]
name = Report module layer boundaries
type = layers
layers =
    faultmaven.modules.report.api
    faultmaven.modules.report.domain

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 10: Auth Module - Other Modules Use Contracts Only
# ============================================================================
# Other modules must only import from auth module's contracts.py, not from
# internal implementation (domain, infrastructure, api).
# This enforces the module boundary and prevents coupling to auth internals.
#
# TEMPORARY EXCEPTIONS:
# - Legacy compatibility layers (faultmaven.models, faultmaven.models.auth)
#   are allowed to import from auth.domain for backward compatibility
# - TYPE_CHECKING imports in contracts.py are allowed
# TODO: Remove these exceptions by migrating all imports to use contracts.py DTOs
[importlinter:contract:10]
name = Other modules use auth contracts only
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.case
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge
    faultmaven.modules.evidence
    faultmaven.modules.agent
    faultmaven.modules.report
forbidden_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.auth.domain
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure
    faultmaven.modules.auth.api
allow_indirect_imports = false
ignore_imports =
    faultmaven.models -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.models.session
    faultmaven.modules.auth.contracts -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.models.auth
    faultmaven.modules.auth.contracts -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.models.user
    faultmaven.modules.auth.contracts -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.models.rbac
    faultmaven.infrastructure.llm.router -> faultmaven.models
    # Container is the composition root - allowed to wire all module internals
    faultmaven.container.providers.services -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.services.*
    faultmaven.container.providers.services -> faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.repositories.*
    faultmaven.container.providers.services -> faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.stores.*
    faultmaven.container.providers.infrastructure -> faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.stores.*
    faultmaven.container.providers.infrastructure -> faultmaven.infrastructure.auth.*
    # The shared API-layer auth dependency, newly visible now that
    # faultmaven/api is a real package. Every module's routes depend on it to
    # authenticate a request — that is what it is for — and it is not one of the
    # five modules this contract governs: it is the application's auth wiring.
    # Its own use of auth internals is therefore not a module reaching across a
    # boundary, and without these three "module X has an authenticated route"
    # reads as "module X imports auth.domain".
    faultmaven.api.v1.auth_dependencies -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.**
    faultmaven.api.middleware.auth -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.**
    faultmaven.api.v1.auth_dependencies -> faultmaven.container

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 11: No Direct Database Access to Auth Tables
# ============================================================================
# Other modules MUST NOT directly access auth module's database tables.
# All access must go through IOAuthService or IOAuthCodeRepository contracts.
# This enforces database-per-module boundaries.
[importlinter:contract:11]
name = No direct database access to auth tables
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.case
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge
    faultmaven.modules.evidence
    faultmaven.modules.agent
    faultmaven.modules.report
forbidden_modules =
    # The PACKAGE, not a hand-listed set of modules. The list named
    # `token_repository`, which no longer exists, and missed the two SSO
    # repositories added since — a rule that silently stops covering what it
    # was written to cover. Every repository here reads auth tables, which is
    # exactly what this contract forbids other modules from doing.
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.repositories
allow_indirect_imports = false
ignore_imports =
    # Container is the composition root - allowed to wire all module internals
    faultmaven.container.providers.services -> faultmaven.modules.auth.domain.services.*
    faultmaven.container.providers.services -> faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure.repositories.*
    # Reaching the container is reaching everything it wires, and every module's
    # authenticated route reaches it through the shared API auth dependency.
    # Contracts 10, 12 and 13 each needed this once faultmaven/api became a real
    # package. This contract has the same source modules and the same indirect
    # semantics, and passes today only because the one chain that gets here ends
    # on an edge already ignored above.
    faultmaven.api.v1.auth_dependencies -> faultmaven.container

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 12: Domain Services Cannot Bypass Case Contracts
# ============================================================================
# Per module-organization-design.md:
# - Evidence, Agent, Report are Domain Services (NOT vertical modules)
# - They should use Case module's contracts (ICaseRepository)
# - They should NOT import directly from Case infrastructure
[importlinter:contract:12]
name = Domain Services use Case contracts not infrastructure
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.evidence
    faultmaven.modules.agent
    faultmaven.modules.report
forbidden_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure
allow_indirect_imports = false
ignore_imports =
    # Container is the composition root - allowed to wire infrastructure
    faultmaven.container.providers.infrastructure -> faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.sessionless_case_repository
    faultmaven.container.providers.infrastructure -> faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure.case_repository
    # Reaching the container is reaching everything it wires. Same composition-root
    # rationale as the two lines above; newly visible because faultmaven/api is a
    # real package now.
    faultmaven.api.v1.auth_dependencies -> faultmaven.container

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 13: Other Modules Use Case Contracts Only
# ============================================================================
# Per module-organization-design.md:
# - Case module owns evidence, reports, and agent execution data
# - Other modules must import these models from Case contracts
# - Case contracts re-exports models for cross-module use
# Note: Evidence, Agent, Report can still have domain/models for backward compat
#       but they re-export from Case contracts
# Re-enabled: faultmaven/api now has an __init__.py, so it is a regular package
# and its modules appear in the import graph. While it did not, this contract was
# unfalsifiable, which is why it was commented out rather than left to pass.
[importlinter:contract:13]
name = Other modules use Case contracts for shared models
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.services
    faultmaven.api
    faultmaven.core
forbidden_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure
allow_indirect_imports = false
ignore_imports =
    # A composition root, wiring implementations: allowed to name the container
    # because selecting implementations is the job. Same rationale as the
    # container entries on contracts 11 and 12.
    faultmaven.api.v1.auth_dependencies -> faultmaven.container

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 14: Preprocessing Module Uses Case Contracts Only
# ============================================================================
# Preprocessing is a Domain Service that depends on shared Case models
# (notably EntityType for entity profiles). It must import these through
# faultmaven.modules.case.contracts, not from case.domain.* or
# case.infrastructure.*. The contracts module re-exports the relevant
# symbols (EntityType is available at case.contracts:512).
#
# Originally enforced informally by code review; tightened after a system
# review surfaced 5 entity extractors importing EntityType directly from
# case.domain.models (commit-ref: fix/data-pipeline-review-highs).
[importlinter:contract:14]
name = Preprocessing uses Case contracts not domain or infrastructure
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.preprocessing
forbidden_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.case.domain
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure
# Indirect imports allowed: case.contracts itself re-exports from
# case.domain.models, and models.api transitively reaches it through
# agent/case domain models. Direct preprocessing → case.domain or
# case.infrastructure imports are still blocked, which is the contract
# we actually need.
allow_indirect_imports = true

# ============================================================================
# CONTRACT 15: Providers Do Not Reach Into Module Internals
# ============================================================================
# faultmaven.providers is cross-cutting: config.tenant_context resolves a
# provider, so EVERY module reaches this package. That makes it the widest
# blast radius in the tree — a provider that imports one module's internals
# makes every other module a transitive importer of them, which is exactly how
# `providers.tenancy` came to couple all five modules to `auth.domain`.
#
# It had no rule of its own until now because it had no __init__.py: grimp
# never put it in the graph, so a contract naming it could not have failed.
# The tenancy violation was only ever visible transitively, through chains that
# happened to start at one of the five modules.
[importlinter:contract:15]
name = Providers do not reach into module internals
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    faultmaven.providers
forbidden_modules =
    faultmaven.modules.auth.domain
    faultmaven.modules.auth.infrastructure
    faultmaven.modules.case.domain
    faultmaven.modules.case.infrastructure
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge.domain
    faultmaven.modules.knowledge.infrastructure
    faultmaven.modules.evidence.domain
    faultmaven.modules.agent.domain
    faultmaven.modules.report.domain
allow_indirect_imports = false

[project]
name = "faultmaven"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "AI-powered troubleshooting copilot for incident investigation"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = {text = "FSL-1.1-ALv2"}
authors = [
    {name = "FaultMaven Team", email = "team@faultmaven.com"}
]
keywords = ["troubleshooting", "incident-response", "ai", "investigation", "observability"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: System Administrators",
    "License :: Other/Proprietary License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: System :: Monitoring",
    "Topic :: System :: Systems Administration",
]

# ============================================================================
# CORE DEPENDENCIES (Standalone)
# Lightweight installation for local development and self-hosting
# Uses SQLite, local file storage, in-memory sessions
# ============================================================================
dependencies = [
    # Core FastAPI and server
    "fastapi>=0.115.8",

    "starlette>=1.3.1",
    "uvicorn>=0.28.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.30",  # >=0.0.30: multipart DoS (unbounded header / quadratic parse) fixes
    "sse-starlette>=2.0.0",

    # LLM Framework (REQUIRED - core functionality)

    # aiohttp (infrastructure/llm/providers/fireworks_provider.py).
    "openai>=1.0.0",
    "anthropic>=0.25.0",
    "tiktoken>=0.5.0",

    # Database (SQLite in base, PostgreSQL drivers in cloud)
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19.0",

    # Core utilities and validation
    # >=2.10: the floor every patched litellm release declares. The old
    # <2.10 ceiling pinned litellm to 1.83.0 and held ten proxy-server
    # advisories open (fm#904); <3 stays a deliberate major boundary.
    "pydantic>=2.10,<3",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.3.0",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    # [speedups]: aiodns/c-ares keeps DNS resolution off the shared thread

    # with BGE-M3 encode work); >=3.14: request-smuggling/parse GHSA fixes
    "aiohttp[speedups]>=3.14.0",
    "aiofiles>=23.2.1",
    # Floor raised past CVE-2026-63374 / CVE-2026-64847 (both fixed in 4.14.2).
    # The lockfiles are what pip-audit reads, but a consumer resolving from this
    # file directly — or any future re-resolution — would otherwise be free to
    # select 4.13.0 again and reintroduce both advisories with CI still green.
    "anyio>=4.15.1",
    "requests>=2.31.0",
    "PyJWT>=2.15.1",  # >=2.13.0: GHSA key-confusion (HS256 forgery) fix; >=2.14.0: CVE-2026-102274 / GHSA-w6j9-cwv2-h6wq (JWK-set parsing; not reachable here, pinned to keep the audit clean); >=2.15.1: floor = lock pin (#1518)
    # RS256 JWT keys; >=50.0.0: PKCS#7 EnvelopedData Bleichenbacher oracle
    # (GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5). Reachable only once workos 10.1.1 relaxed its
    # own cryptography~=49.0 pin — the two floors move together.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    "bcrypt>=4.0.0",
    "email-validator>=2.0.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.1",
    "typing-extensions>=4.12.2",
    "tenacity>=8.3.0",

    # Logging (structured logging for all editions)
    "structlog>=24.1.0",
    "python-json-logger>=2.0.7",

    # Knowledge base and embeddings (ChromaDB + sentence transformers)
    "chromadb>=1.0.0",
    # Floored at the release the lockfiles pin and the image is built with.
    # The security floor is 5.6.0: below it, loading a model from a path that
    # exists on local disk runs that directory's Python even with
    # trust_remote_code=False (CVE-2026-68770 / GHSA-jhr6-gm9c-rqjv). 6.x is a
    # major release (transformers>=5, huggingface-hub>=1.3); `model_cache`
    # uses only the constructor and `encode`, and BGE-M3 vectors are
    # byte-identical on 5.4.1 and 6.1.0.
    "sentence-transformers>=6.1.0",
    # Transitive via sentence-transformers, floored here for two GHSAs it
    # is the only lever on: torch <=2.12.1 is itself vulnerable
    # (GHSA-rrmf-rvhw-rf47), and torch 2.11's `setuptools<82` pin held the
    # graph below the patched setuptools 83.0.0 (GHSA-h35f-9h28-mq5c).
    # 2.13.0 drops the cap to `setuptools>=77.0.3`. The Dockerfile installs
    # the CPU wheel at whatever version the lockfile pins — it reads the pin
    # rather than repeating it, so there is nothing here to keep in step.
    "torch>=2.13.0",
    # Transitive via sentence-transformers, floored here for the same reason:
    # below 5.10.0, `save_pretrained` writes files at paths taken from a Hub
    # repo's `chat_template` keys, so a malicious repo escapes the save
    # directory (CVE-2026-9856 / GHSA-xrqw-3rrv-vx5w).
    "transformers>=5.10.0",
    # >=6.14.2: inline-image infinite-loop GHSA fixes; >=6.15.0:
    # CVE-2026-71852; >=6.16.1: three denial-of-service advisories — outline
    # retrieval and XForm extraction blow up on crafted files
    # (GHSA-23w6-3w8w-8484, GHSA-763m-79hh-57f2) and TreeObject.insert_child
    # can loop forever (GHSA-jp53-mhqp-8xcg). Reached from evidence upload.
    "pypdf>=6.19.0",
    "python-docx>=1.1.2",

    # Data processing and analysis
    "numpy>=1.26.4,<2",
    "pandas>=1.5.0",
    "pandas-stubs>=2.0.0",
    "pylogrus>=0.1.2",
    "scikit-learn>=1.5.0",
    "pyod>=2.0.1",
    # >=5.29.6: GHSA-7gcm-g887-7qv7 + GHSA-8qvm-5x2c-j2w7 fixes. <6 is a
    # deliberate major-version boundary (the locked consumers allow 6.x per
    # their metadata) — lift it deliberately when a 6.x need arises.
    "protobuf>=5.29.6,<6",
    # Transitive (spacy / thinc / torch import it at runtime), floored here
    # because nothing else in the graph moves it: >=83.0.0 patches
    # GHSA-h35f-9h28-mq5c. torch 2.11's `setuptools<82` used to cap it.
    "setuptools>=83.0.0",
    # Transitive (requests and kubernetes; botocore and sentry-sdk in the
    # cloud lockfile), floored here because none of them requires the
    # patched release: >=2.8.0 fixes target-server TLS settings applied to an
    # HTTPS proxy connection (CVE-2026-97687), an infinite loop on chunked
    # Deflate responses (CVE-2026-97688) and an unbounded chunk-size line
    # buffered into memory (CVE-2026-97689).
    "urllib3>=2.8.0",

    # Web utilities
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.12.3",
    "tavily-python>=0.7.0",

    # Document processing
    "python-frontmatter>=1.0.0",

    # Background task scheduling
    "apscheduler>=3.10.4",

    # In-process Redis (standalone deployment: API-compatible Redis without external server)
    "fakeredis[lua]>=2.21.0",
]

]

]

[tool.coverage.report]

    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",

    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "@abc.abstractmethod",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# THIS LIST IS THE GATE. CI (`code-quality` in .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml) and
# the ruff pre-commit hook both run bare `ruff check faultmaven/ tests/`, with no
# `--select`, so what is written here is exactly what is enforced. Never pass
# `--select` on a command line: it REPLACES this list rather than narrowing it,
# which is how the previously declared set (E, W, F, I, B, C4, UP, G) came to be
# published for months without ever running — `faultmaven/` and `tests/` carry
# 10,275 violations of it (ruff 0.9.10, measured at cfbc9e23e).
#
# The set below is what `faultmaven/` and `tests/` actually pass today:
#   E9    syntax / IO errors — the file does not parse
#   F63   comparison mistakes (`is` on literals, invalid `==` types)
#   F7    misplaced statements (`break` outside a loop, etc.)
#   F82   undefined names — a NameError waiting for the right branch
#   F811  a name redefined before its first use: the earlier definition is dead
#         and never runs. Added here with the sweep that made it pass, which
#         turned up four real defects: ten DI getters in `_container_impl.py`
#         shadowed by later definitions of the same names, and a duplicate
#         `TitleResponse` whose required `view_state` the live route never
#         passes — the published one is the second.
#   I     import sorting (ruff replaced isort here in #179)
#
# E9,F63,F7,F82 is not a chosen set: it is GitHub's starter-workflow flake8 line
# (`flake8 . --count --select=E9,F63,F7,F82`), added in 2025 and translated
# verbatim into ruff by #179, whose recorded rationale concerns which PATHS are
# linted, not which rules. Widening it is a correction, not a re-litigation —
# but widen it one rule at a time, with the sweep that makes the tree pass in
# the same PR, so this list never again names something that is not enforced.
select = [
    "E9",    # pycodestyle: syntax/IO errors
    "F63",   # pyflakes: invalid comparisons
    "F7",    # pyflakes: misplaced statements
    "F82",   # pyflakes: undefined names
    "F811",  # pyflakes: redefinition of an unused name (dead definition)
    "I",     # isort: import sorting
]
# Inert while the set above stays narrow (none of these is selected). Kept so
# that widening `select` does not also have to rediscover these decisions.
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",  # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "C901",  # too complex
]

# NOTE: Error logging standard (not currently enforceable by linter):
# All logger.error() and logger.critical() calls within exception handlers
# MUST include exc_info=True or use logger.exception()
# See docs/operations/monitoring/logging-policy.md for details

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Every path named here must exist — tests/unit/test_lint_config_is_live.py
# asserts it. Two entries (faultmaven/agent/doctrine.py,
# faultmaven/data_processing/log_processor.py) named files deleted long ago and
# went unnoticed because nothing ever resolved them.
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # Allow unused imports in __init__.py
"test_*.py" = ["F401", "F811"]  # Redefinition is the pytest-fixture idiom
"conftest.py" = ["F401"]  # Allow unused imports in conftest files
"faultmaven/main.py" = ["F841"]  # Allow unused variables (dependency injection)


[tool.black]
line-length = 88
target-version = ["py311"]
include = '\.pyi?$'

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = false
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false
ignore_missing_imports = true
show_error_codes = true
check_untyped_defs = false
warn_no_return = false
warn_unreachable = false
no_implicit_optional = false
ignore_errors = true
warn_unused_ignores = false
# No `files` key. It named faultmaven/session_management.py and
# faultmaven/agent/tools/web_search.py — neither has existed for a long time, so
# a bare `mypy` could not even start ("cannot read file ... No such file or
# directory") while the config looked configured. Nothing in CI runs mypy, and
# `ignore_errors = true` above means it reports nothing anyway (measured: `mypy
# faultmaven` spends 2m05s to print "no issues found in 472 source files"). So
# rather than point the key at a real path and publish a second no-op that reads
# as a gate, the key is removed: run `mypy <paths>` explicitly. Giving mypy
# teeth — dropping `ignore_errors`, picking a scope, wiring a CI job — is its
# own change, not this one.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "pandas.*",
    "sklearn.*",
    "numpy.*",
    "yaml.*",
    "mcp.*"
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    domain
    application
    infrastructure
include_external_packages = True

# =============================================================================
# Contract 1: Domain layer independence
# The domain layer is the core of the application and must have no dependencies
# on application services, infrastructure, or any framework (Django).
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:domain-layer-independence]
name = Domain layer must not import from application or infrastructure
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    domain
forbidden_modules =
    application
    infrastructure
    django
    rest_framework

# =============================================================================
# Contract 2: Application layer independence
# The application layer orchestrates use cases but must not depend on
# infrastructure implementations. It should only depend on domain and its own
# port interfaces.
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:application-layer-independence]
name = Application layer must not import from infrastructure
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    application
forbidden_modules =
    infrastructure
    django
    rest_framework

# =============================================================================
# Contract 3: Aggregate isolation - Cart
# The Cart aggregate must not import from other aggregates.
# Cross-aggregate coordination happens in the application layer.
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:cart-aggregate-isolation]
name = Cart aggregate must not import from other aggregates
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    domain.aggregates.cart
forbidden_modules =
    domain.aggregates.product
    domain.aggregates.order

# =============================================================================
# Contract 4: Aggregate isolation - Product
# The Product aggregate must not import from other aggregates.
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:product-aggregate-isolation]
name = Product aggregate must not import from other aggregates
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    domain.aggregates.product
forbidden_modules =
    domain.aggregates.cart
    domain.aggregates.order

# =============================================================================
# Contract 5: Aggregate isolation - Order
# The Order aggregate must not import from other aggregates.
# =============================================================================
[importlinter:contract:order-aggregate-isolation]
name = Order aggregate must not import from other aggregates
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    domain.aggregates.order
forbidden_modules =
    domain.aggregates.cart
    domain.aggregates.product

[project.urls]
"Homepage" = "https://github.com/graphrag/graphrag"
"Bug Reports" = "https://github.com/graphrag/graphrag/issues"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
include = ["src*"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
addopts = "-v --tb=short"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",   # Pyflakes
    "I",   # isort
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",  # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["src"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]

# Dependency floor policy
# ------------------------
# Every floor below carries an intent tag. Bump rules:
#   * `CVE fix`           — floor exists to dodge a known CVE; never lower it.
#   * `security hardening` — non-CVE security improvement (defaults, audits); bump freely upward.
#   * `breaking change floor` — version where an upstream breaking change settled in our favour.
#   * `runtime requirement` — required for the language/server/protocol version we run.
#   * `feature floor`     — code in this repo calls APIs added at this version.
#   * `baseline`          — chosen as the current modern release at the time of pinning; safe to bump.
# When raising a floor, document the new tag inline; do not delete prior context.
dependencies = [
    # Extracted, mountable in-repo blocks (uv workspace members under packages/).
    # The host mounts each block's router via ``tribunal_<id>.get_router()``.
    "tribunal-widget",
    "tribunal-short-links",
    "tribunal-reviews",
    "tribunal-lead-capture",
    "tribunal-offers",
    # FastAPI + ASGI
    # CVE fix: fastapi 0.109.1+ vendors python-multipart fix for CVE-2024-24762 (Content-Type ReDoS).
    # CVE fix: fastapi >=0.136 pulls starlette >=0.47.2, which patches CVE-2025-54121 (multipart DoS).
    "fastapi>=0.136.1",
    # baseline: matches httptools/h11 wheels available for Python 3.12+; ASGI lifespan parity with starlette 0.47+.
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.47.0",
    # runtime requirement: lower bound only — fastapi pins the effective upper. Kept explicit so a future
    # fastapi downgrade cannot silently drag in pre-CVE-2025-54121 starlette. Real floor is fastapi's.
    # CVE fix: starlette 1.0.1 patches GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr / PYSEC-2026-161 (BadHost: missing Host-header
    # validation poisons request.url.path, bypassing path-based security checks). Do not lower below 1.0.1.
    "starlette>=1.0.1",
    # WebSocket client (Grok realtime, audio streaming)
    # feature floor: websockets 14 introduced the new asyncio API used in app/websockets/voice_bridge.py.
    "websockets>=14.0",
    # YAML (scenario/config loaders)
    # baseline: 6.0 dropped Python 2 support and is the long-standing LTS line.
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    # Database
    # feature floor: SQLAlchemy 2.0.49 carries the AsyncSession.scalars()/Row.tuple typing fixes we rely on.
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.49",
    # runtime requirement: 0.30 is the first release with full PostgreSQL 17 protocol support.
    "asyncpg>=0.30.0",
    # feature floor: pgvector 0.3 ships the SQLAlchemy ``Vector`` type + asyncpg codec used by
    # the hybrid knowledge retrieval vector arm (app/models/knowledge_chunk.py + retrieval_service).
    "pgvector>=0.3.6",
    # feature floor: Alembic 1.18 added async migration env autogenerate fixes used by our env.py.
    "alembic>=1.18.4",
    # runtime requirement: greenlet 3.1+ required by sqlalchemy[asyncio] on Python 3.12.
    "greenlet>=3.1.0",
    # Redis
    # breaking change floor: redis-py 5→7 dropped sync-style decode params and reworked async pubsub.
    # We rely on the 7.x async cluster client semantics in app/db/redis.py; do not downgrade below 7.4.
    "redis>=7.4.0",
    # Validation
    # CVE fix: pydantic 2.13.4 patches the serialize_as_any regression chain from 2.12 (no CVE, but
    # corrupted output qualifies as data-integrity); also required for Python 3.14 forward-compat.
    # breaking change floor: 2.12 changed model_fields_set behaviour for extras; our schemas assume 2.13+.
    "pydantic>=2.13.4",
    # runtime requirement: pydantic-settings 2.14 aligns with pydantic 2.13's CoreSchema changes.
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14.1",
    # security hardening: 2.2 added stricter IDN/RFC 6531 validation used by app/schemas/contact.py.
    "email-validator>=2.2.0",
    # Authentication & Encryption
    # CVE fix: pyjwt 2.13.0 patches PYSEC-2026-175/177/178/179 (JWT verification/decoding flaws);
    # do not lower below 2.13.0. Prior baseline: 2.8 first shipped the typed Algorithm enum we import
    # in app/core/security.py.
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.13.0",
    # security hardening: 23.1 hardened the default Argon2id parameters (mem cost, parallelism).
    "argon2-cffi>=23.1.0",
    # baseline: bcrypt 4.x rewrote to Rust; 4.0 is the floor that ships pre-built wheels for 3.12/3.13.
    "bcrypt>=4.0.0",
    # CVE fix: python-multipart 0.0.28 is the latest 0.x patch carrying the CVE-2024-24762 ReDoS fix
    # (originally landed in 0.0.7). Newer 1.x is gated by upstream FastAPI; do not lower.
    "python-multipart>=0.0.28",
    # HTTP Client
    # feature floor: httpx 0.28 made the `proxies=` → `proxy=` rename and is the floor openai 2.x assumes.
    "httpx>=0.28.0",
    # OpenAI
    # feature floor: openai 2.36 is the first SDK with the Realtime API shape we use in app/services/ai/.
    # breaking change floor: 2.x dropped the legacy openai.ChatCompletion module our codebase no longer uses.
    "openai>=2.36.0",
    # feature floor: typed LLM outputs with retryable validators.
    "pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==1.39.0",
    # Logging
    # feature floor: structlog 24.4 added the `EventRenamer` processor used by app/core/logging.py.
    "structlog>=24.4.0",
    # Utilities
    # baseline: 8.13 ships up-to-date carrier/region metadata.
    "phonenumbers>=8.13.0",
    # baseline: resend 2.30.1 is the SDK release matching the current Resend API surface we call.
    "resend>=2.30.1",
    # security hardening: svix 1.93 ships the rotated signature-verification defaults; older versions
    # accepted weaker HMAC parameters.
    "svix>=1.93.0",
    # security hardening: beautifulsoup4 4.14 includes the parser hardening for nested-tag stack overflow.
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.14.3",
    # Audio resampling (anti-aliased sample rate conversion)
    # feature floor: soxr 0.5 added the Float32 numpy-array signature we pass from the voice bridge.
    "soxr>=0.5.0",
    # Statistics (bandit A/B testing)
    # runtime requirement: numpy 1.26 is the first release with wheels for Python 3.12.
    "numpy>=1.26.0",
    # runtime requirement: scipy 1.12 dropped distutils and is the floor compatible with numpy 1.26+/3.12.
    "scipy>=1.12.0",
    # ML (TF-IDF similarity for IVR loop detection)
    # baseline: scikit-learn 1.5 is the floor that supports numpy 2 / Python 3.12.
    "scikit-learn>=1.5.0",
    # CVE fix: cryptography >=46.0.7 patches CVE-2026-39892 (non-contiguous buffer overflow); >=46.0.6
    # patches CVE-2026-34073 (X.509 name-constraint bypass); >=46.0.0 patches CVE-2026-26007 (ECC
    # subgroup attack via SECT curves). 48.0.0 is the current stable that bundles all three plus
    # OpenSSL 3.5.x. Do not lower below 46.0.7 under any circumstance.
    "cryptography>=48.0.0",
    # runtime requirement: stdlib `audioop` was removed in Python 3.13; this is the PyPI backport.
    "audioop-lts>=0.2.1 ; python_full_version >= '3.13'",
    # feature floor: stripe 15.1 carries the 2025-09 API version pinned in app/services/billing/.
    "stripe>=15.1.0",
    # security hardening: sentry-sdk 2.60 dropped a leaky breadcrumb path for FastAPI form data.
    "sentry-sdk[fastapi]>=2.60.0",
    # feature floor: 7.1 added the `inprogress_name` arg we configure in app/main.py.
    # runtime requirement: 8.0.0 ported the instrumentator to Starlette v1 (its 7.x line pins
    # starlette<1.0.0, which would otherwise cap us below the GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr fix). Keep in lockstep
    # with the starlette>=1.0.1 floor above.
    "prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator>=8.0.0",
    # feature floor: tenacity 9.1 introduced the typed `retry_if_exception_type` overloads used in
    # app/services/telephony/telnyx_sms.py.
    "tenacity>=9.1.4",
    # runtime requirement: OpenTelemetry 0.62b1 (1.41.x) is the matched pre-1.0 contrib series — all
    # five `opentelemetry-instrumentation-*` packages must move in lockstep with the SDK to avoid
    # ABI mismatches at import time. Bump them as a group.
    "opentelemetry-distro>=0.62b1",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.62b1",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-httpx>=0.62b1",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.62b1",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-redis>=0.62b1",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp>=1.41.1",
    # baseline: pybreaker 1.4 is the first release with typed async support used in our circuit-breaker
    # wrapper around outbound Telnyx calls.
    "pybreaker>=1.4.1",
    "ez-pixel>=0.1.0",
    # Knowledge ingestion (RAG): token-aware chunking + document text extraction.
    # feature floor: tiktoken 0.8 is the first release shipping the cl100k_base wheels for
    # Python 3.12/3.13 used by the token-aware splitter in app/services/knowledge/chunking.py.
    "tiktoken>=0.8.0",
    # feature floor: pypdf 5.1 is the maintained pure-Python PDF parser used for text extraction
    # in app/services/knowledge/text_extraction.py (supersedes the unmaintained PyPDF2 line).
    "pypdf>=5.1.0",
    # feature floor: python-docx 1.1 carries the typing + lxml fixes used for .docx text extraction
    # in app/services/knowledge/text_extraction.py.
    "python-docx>=1.1.2",
    "aiortc>=1.15.0",
]

# harmless. Scaffold a member with ``scripts/blocks/scaffold_backend_block.py``.
# See ``docs/blocks/BACKEND_BLOCK_PATTERN.md``.
[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["packages/*"]

# Resolve extracted block distributions from the in-repo workspace rather than

# Aragora layered-architecture import contract (import-linter / grimp).
# ============================================================================
# Five mission layers, ordered top (highest) to bottom (lowest). A module may
# import from its own layer or any layer below it, but NEVER from a layer above
# it (per architecture.md section 2):
#
#   interface       server, cli, mcp, gateway, bots, channels, integrations,
#                   connectors, __main__, approvals, client, extensions,
#                   webhooks
#   application     workflow, pipeline, nomic, swarm, gauntlet, goals,
#                   implement, modes, verticals, autonomous, broadcast, canvas,
#                   spectate, analytics, audit, control_plane, golden, inbox,
#                   marketplace, services, skills, stores, computer_use,
#                   coordination, export, markets, plugins, prompt_engine,
#                   receipts, workspace, brief_engine, codex, compat, essay,
#                   factory, fixtures, gti, harnesses, hooks, ideacloud,
#                   interrogation, missions, onboarding, operations, ops, pdb,
#                   playbooks, policy, prediction, ralph, reports, review,
#                   scheduler, schedulers, sync, trail, triage, worktree
#   domain          debate, agents, memory, knowledge, ranking, reasoning,
#                   evidence, evaluation, explainability, learning, ml,
#                   advocates, analysis, audience, blockchain, compliance,
#                   container, core, deliberation, documents, embeddings,
#                   epistemic, evolution, genesis, heterogeneity, insights,
#                   introspection, metrics, moderation, prompts, pulse,
#                   replay, reputation, rlm, routing, templates, tools,
#                   tournaments, training, uncertainty, verification,
#                   visualization, work
#   infrastructure  storage, resilience, events, observability, security,
#                   queue, db, caching, billing, backup, migrations, cache,
#                   deletion_coordinator, fabric, maintenance, monitoring,
#                   performance, resilience_config, resilience_patterns,
#                   runtime, sandbox, streaming, telemetry, transcription,
#                   auth, logging_config, notifications, persistence, privacy,
#                   rbac, tenancy
#   foundation      api_errors, config, core_types, exceptions, errors, utils,
#                   protocols, types, __version__, _lazy_imports,
#                   core_protocols, docs_only, http_client, models,
#                   serialization, task_brief, topic_handler, topic_spec,
#                   topics, type_protocols, shared
#
# Siblings within a layer are colon-separated (":"), i.e. non-independent: they
# may import one another freely; only the cross-layer direction is enforced.
#
# This is an *adoption* contract: main currently has many upward imports and
# 139 mutual cycles (measured 2026-10-04 with TYPE_CHECKING imports excluded;
# ratchet in scripts/baselines/import_cycles_baseline.json), so the contract
# cannot pass clean at adoption. Enforcement
# is shrink-only via scripts/ci/check_import_contracts.py, which freezes the
# current violation set into scripts/baselines/import_contracts_baseline.json
# and fails only on NEW violations (fail-on-new). Bottom layers
# (foundation, infrastructure) are driven to zero in P4a.
#
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# module_tiers cross-check (VAL-P0-006)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every layer assignment above was cross-checked against aragora/module_tiers.yaml
# (first on 2026-06-12, last on 2026-10-12). Outcome: 0 discrepancies. All 166
# layered names resolve to a real top-level module in the local source tree, and
# every top-level module is layered; the 143 that are directory packages all
# appear in module_tiers.yaml (21 core, 94 integrated, 25 experimental, 3
# deprecated: metrics, operations and schedulers, deprecated re-export shims
# kept until they are retired), and the 23 that are single-file modules (for
# example __main__, api_errors, core_types, exceptions, errors, cache,
# container, golden, http_client, logging_config) are real importable modules
# that module_tiers.yaml does not track because it enumerates package
# directories only (not a discrepancy). The one module_tiers entry that is not
# layered, live, is the Next.js frontend: it has no __init__.py, so it is not a
# Python module. Tranches add names only by appending them to the existing
# layer lines.
# Because the discrepancy count is zero, no operator Decision line is required.
# ============================================================================

[importlinter]
root_package = aragora
# Imports guarded by `if TYPE_CHECKING:` create no layer edge; runtime imports at
# any scope still do. import-linter accepts only the spellings True/true here.
exclude_type_checking_imports = True

[importlinter:contract:aragora-layers]
name = Aragora layers: interface > application > domain > infrastructure > foundation
type = layers
containers =
    aragora
ignore_imports =
    # Authorized P4a exception seam: preserve the VAL-P4A-005 lazy fallback; sanctioned by VAL-P4B-004(b)/(c).
    aragora.exceptions -> aragora.connectors.exceptions
    # Authorized P4a exception seam: preserve the VAL-P4A-005 lazy fallback; sanctioned by VAL-P4B-004(b)/(c).
    aragora.exceptions -> aragora.server.handlers.exceptions
    # Authorized one-release compatibility shim; TODO remove when aragora.utils.redis_cache is retired.
    aragora.utils.redis_cache -> aragora.caching.redis
    # Sanctioned M3 seam (architecture B8): aragora.exceptions mirrors the control-plane exception types through its lazy __getattr__.
    aragora.exceptions -> aragora.control_plane.exceptions
layers =
    server : cli : mcp : gateway : bots : channels : integrations : connectors : __main__ : approvals : client : extensions : webhooks
    workflow : pipeline : nomic : swarm : gauntlet : goals : implement : modes : verticals : autonomous : broadcast : canvas : spectate : analytics : audit : control_plane : golden : inbox : marketplace : services : skills : stores : computer_use : coordination : export : markets : plugins : prompt_engine : receipts : workspace : brief_engine : codex : compat : essay : factory : fixtures : gti : harnesses : hooks : ideacloud : interrogation : missions : onboarding : operations : ops : pdb : playbooks : policy : prediction : ralph : reports : review : scheduler : schedulers : sync : trail : triage : worktree
    debate : agents : memory : knowledge : ranking : reasoning : evidence : evaluation : explainability : learning : ml : advocates : analysis : audience : blockchain : compliance : container : core : deliberation : documents : embeddings : epistemic : evolution : genesis : heterogeneity : insights : introspection : metrics : moderation : prompts : pulse : replay : reputation : rlm : routing : templates : tools : tournaments : training : uncertainty : verification : visualization : work
    storage : resilience : events : observability : security : queue : db : caching : billing : backup : migrations : cache : deletion_coordinator : fabric : maintenance : monitoring : performance : resilience_config : resilience_patterns : runtime : sandbox : streaming : telemetry : transcription : auth : logging_config : notifications : persistence : privacy : rbac : tenancy
    api_errors : config : core_types : exceptions : errors : utils : protocols : types : __version__ : _lazy_imports : core_protocols : docs_only : http_client : models : serialization : task_brief : topic_handler : topic_spec : topics : type_protocols : shared

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    app

[importlinter:contract:layered_architecture]
name = Layered Architecture
type = layers
layers =
    app.api
    app.modules
    app.infrastructure
    app.lib

[importlinter:contract:services_use_orchestrators]

[importlinter:contract:lib_no_modules]
name = Library layer cannot depend on domain modules
type = forbidden

    app.lib

    app.modules
