package io.github.kryszak.app

import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestInstance

@TestInstance(TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)
@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [ArchitectureTests::class])
class ArchitectureTests {

    companion object {
        private val BASE_PACKAGE = ArchitectureTests::class.java.`package`.name

        private val DOMAIN_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.domain"
        private val ADAPTER_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.adapter"
        private val INFRASTRUCTURE_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.infrastructure"

        private const val SPRING_PACKAGE = "org.springframework"
    }

    @ArchTest
    val `there are no package cycles` =
        SlicesRuleDefinition.slices()
            .matching("$BASE_PACKAGE.(**)..")
            .should()
            .beFreeOfCycles()

    @ArchTest
    val `the domain does not access the infrastructure and adapters` =
        noClasses()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("$DOMAIN_PACKAGE..")
            .should()
            .accessClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("$INFRASTRUCTURE_PACKAGE..", "$ADAPTER_PACKAGE..")

    @ArchTest
    val `domain should not depend on framework` =
        noClasses()
            .that().resideInAPackage("$DOMAIN_PACKAGE..")
            .should()
            .dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAPackage("$SPRING_PACKAGE..")

    @ArchTest
    val `adapters should not access domain and infrastructure` =
        noClasses()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("$ADAPTER_PACKAGE..")
            .should()
            .accessClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("$INFRASTRUCTURE_PACKAGE..", "$DOMAIN_PACKAGE..")
}

# Module boundaries for backend/app, checked by import-linter.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every rule below was already true of this codebase in
# prose — the layering, "routes go through services", "domains do not import
# each other in a cycle" — and none of it was held by anything that could fail.
# A boundary that only a reviewer remembers is followed until the first Tuesday
# somebody is in a hurry. Three hand-written guards already cover parts of this
# (see `tests/unit/test_domain_import_guard.py` for the repositories half); this
# file states the whole shape once, in the tool that reads the import graph.
#
# RUN IT
#     cd backend && uv run lint-imports          the ten contracts on their own,
#                                                exit 0/1. This file writes no
#                                                exemptions, so this is the raw
#                                                graph, not the verdict — every
#                                                debt the baseline holds open is
#                                                reported here too.
#     cd backend && uv run python scripts/check_boundaries.py
#                                                the verdict, exit 0/1/2 where
#                                                2 = could not judge
#     cd backend && uv run python scripts/check_boundaries.py --self-test
#                                                prove the check still fires
#     cd backend && uv run python scripts/check_boundaries.py --measure
#                                                print the baseline this tree
#                                                implies, as JSON
#
# THE BASELINE. These contracts did not pass on the tree they were written for
# and were never going to: the layering was held by 26 upward imports that exist
# *because* they dodge a cycle, the routes imported 56 model modules directly,
# and the knot under `app.domain` would have taken 178 dependency removals to
# untie (today's counts are in `docs/manual/dev/arch-metrics.md`). Turning the
# contracts on with no exceptions would have meant either a month of unfunded
# refactoring before anyone could merge, or a check switched off on day one.
#
# So the check grades two trees with these same contracts: this one, and the one
# at the merge base. Every violation the *other* tree has is one this tree may
# keep, and a violation only this tree has is the whole verdict. The baseline is
# therefore measured on every run and stored nowhere — no pull request has to
# carry a list of exemptions, and none of them can go stale. The prose below
# each contract still records what was paid down and when; the git log has the
# rest.
#
# WHAT AN `ignore_imports` LINE MEANS HERE. Not the baseline — an exception:
# a violation this tree knows about, accepts, and says why about, which the
# merge-base tree does not have. It is meant to be rare and short. Nothing here
# is a wildcard — a blanket exemption cannot be written into this format, which
# is the point. An exception that stops matching anything is a warning, never a
# failure, because paying a debt down must not go red; the measured half simply
# stops being in the baseline.
#
# STRUCTURE. Prose about a contract goes directly under its
# `[importlinter:contract:...]` header, above the first option. Notes about what
# a contract cost and what has already been paid down may also follow the
# options, where they are history and not settings.
#
# WHAT THESE CONTRACTS DO NOT DO. They are not a refactoring plan and their pass
# rate is not a measure of how coupled the tree is. Removing a violation by
# moving a dependency from the repository layer to the service layer changes the
# package graph by exactly zero edges — measured, in
# `docs/topics/领域包解环.md`. Breaking a cycle takes removing the dependency,
# not relocating it.

[importlinter]
root_package = app
# Third-party imports are not part of this graph; the boundaries below are all
# internal and an external edge can never violate one.
include_external_packages = False

[importlinter:contract:api-domain-core]
# C1 — the layer stack, highest first. A module may import downward (api may
# import domain, domain may import core) and never upward. This is the one
# direction every other rule here assumes.
#
# No upward imports are exempted here any more, which is the whole point of the
# ratchet. What was paid down last is recorded in the git log; the three that
# were exempted on 2026-10-12 were `core/errors.py` reading
# the device failures (now owned by `core/device_failures.py`),
# `platform_stats.services` calling the health route (the judging moved to
# `core/health.py`), and `review.pr_poll` importing `api.deps` for the work
# runner (now reached through the chat service the composition root built).
# Periodic jobs are explicitly registered by their owning domains and assembled
# in `app/periodic_jobs.py`, so `core/background.py` no longer imports the jobs
# it runs.
name = C1 layers: api -> domain -> core, no imports upward
type = layers
layers =
    app.api
    app.domain
    app.core
# An exception that stops matching (because the import was removed) is a
# warning. Paying this debt down must not turn the tree red.
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = warn

[importlinter:contract:routes-touch-no-models]
# C2 — a route handler must not read another domain's model modules directly.
# It has a session and an ORM in reach, so it can; the constraint it skips is
# the domain's own service layer (who may read this row, what else has to be
# written with it, what notification goes out).
#
# `app.api.deps` is a source too: it is where routes get their session and it is
# not part of any domain, so every model it imports is cross-domain by
# construction.
#
# DIRECT IMPORTS ONLY, deliberately. The transitive form of this contract
# ("routes can reach no model through any chain") is the stricter reading and
# was measured at 713 edges, most of them `app.domain.a -> app.domain.b`
# model edges that the project tolerates on purpose: ORM relationships need
# them, and `test_domain_import_guard.py` already ratified that stance for the

# downward and never upward. The packages on one line are one layer and may
# import each other (`:`, the layers contract's non-independent form): the

# the table a table instead of another set of mutually forbidden modules. The
# siblings still have to be acyclic — that is C3, and this contract does not
# repeat it.

# `exhaustive = true` is the point of writing the table down: every child of
# `app.domain` is named here, packages and top-level modules alike, so a new
# one of either is red until somebody says which layer it belongs to. An
# unplaced child is not a small hole in the rule — this contract reads the
# whole graph, so a module nobody placed sits between the layers as a channel,
# hiding an upward import that goes through it, or reporting a chain that
# exists only because the hole did.
#
# The 64 upward package edges measured under `app.domain` on 2026-10-12 (140
# import statements) are the debt this contract started life with, one module
# pair per line, and are paid down from there. The merge base carries them too,
# so they hold no branch back; what this contract reports is an upward edge a
# branch adds. Two packages were placed by this first
# version, and the doc's table now carries them: `onboarding` at layer 7 — it
# reads lower layers and nothing imports it, which is that layer's whole
# definition — and `canvas` at layer 4, where `living_doc` is (whose models it

# `app.domain.project.ports.ComputeCredits` declares them and
# `app.domain.usage.adapters.ComputeCredits` answers them — the composition root
# hands one in at `ProjectService`'s four construction sites. `Ledger.earmarks`
# returns `ComputeGrant` rows, which is why the port folds them into a bool: a
# layer-2 package does not name a caller's class.
#
# `project -> preview` came off in the same breath, and here the port needed no
# implementation written at all: saving a room file warms the Office → PDF
# preview cache, which is `preview.office.prewarm` at layer 5, and its shape
# (`data, path`, returns at once, does nothing when no render service is
# configured) is already exactly what `project.ports.WarmPreview` asks for. The
# eight route call sites hand the function itself in, next to the bytes they are
# saving — 谁调用谁给, the `webhook/ports.py` `Poster` shape.
#
# `project -> library` came off the same way one step later (2026-10-15), and it
# needed two ports because `project` asks the layer-4 `library` two unrelated
# things. Saving, reading back, versioning and snapshotting a room file's bytes
# are address lookups on disk: `project.ports.FileStore` declares them and
# `app/domain/library/service.py` already answers every one, so the routes hand
# the module itself in — `integration.ports.RoomFiles` again, right down to the
# constant (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`, half of the pair the routes read as
# `MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES`; that name now lives in `library.service` beside the
# number it is, instead of in `project.room_files` pointing at it).
# `project.ports.LibraryFiles` is the other half — keeping a file in the
# project's 资料库 (`records.add`) and listing its blobs for the export archive
# (`records.stored`, plus a one-line `records.read_blob` so a caller does not
# have to know that bytes are addressed by `(location, key)`). `records.add`'s
# `data` is narrowed from `service.Content` to `bytes` in the port: it does not
# change a call, and it keeps `BinaryIO` from leaking into a layer-2 signature.
#
# Only the six *imports* left; the two packages keep their rows. `library` could
# not sink — `records._follow_references` (it rewrites `<&library/…>` chips and
# attachment block contents when a file is renamed) and `listing` both read
# `block.models` — and the artifact *rules* stayed in `project.room_files`
# because they are pure functions over a path, not over bytes:
# `ARTIFACT_MIME`, `artifact_kind_for`, `clean_artifact_path`. That ceiling
# alone moved, because a ceiling is the number the landing layer writes down.
#
# `project_material` joined at layer 4 and `project_situation` at layer 1
# (2026-10-16). The material — a project's goal, recent and open tasks, and what
# people said in its public channels — reads `room_task`, `review`, `block` and
# `library` and is read by two callers at different heights: the overview's
# 「现状」 (`project_situation`, which also needs `agent.harness.prompt.WRITING`
# and so sits above `agent`) and the document agent drafting the overview
# (`agent`, layer 3). It sits below both so that neither reaches up.
# `repository` lost its last three upward edges (2026-10-17). They were one
# mistake in two shapes. Three of them read a task's row — is it still open,
# which branch and last landed head, what did the card's declared work turn out
# to be — through `room_task.models.Task` and `room_task.services.TaskService`,
# because `repository` is layer 3 and `room_task` is layer 4 and nobody had
# written down what it actually needed: columns. So `repository/task_rows.py`
# declares those columns as a bare `table(...)`, the way
# `topic/repositories/statements.py` declares `tasks`, `threads` and `blocks`,
# and the three readers take it from there. Only reads go through the copy; a
# write or a decision still comes from `room_task.services`, which owns the
# table. `tests/unit/test_repository_task_rows_match_their_rows.py` pins the
# copy to the real table, and its opposite number in `topic` does the same
# there — both compare which table a statement's columns belong to, because
# `find_tables` hands back an annotated copy of an ORM table that `is` never
# matches, which is also why the `topic` guard's "borrowed a model table"
# assertion had never been able to go red until now.
#
# The fourth was a path, not a row: `repository.service.session_dir` copies a
# project's confirmed skills out of `project_skill`'s mirror directory and
# therefore imported `project_skill.service.mirror_root` to learn where that
# directory is. Where a path is is a convention, not a query, and it now sits
# at layer 1 in `skill_library.project_skills_root` — the same move as
# `event_author` and `event_about`, for the same reason: one writer and one
# other reader, three layers apart, needing one string. `mirror_root` stays in
# `project_skill.service` as a one-line wrapper; it is the name its own callers
# and the tests that patch it use.
name = C5 domain packages form seven layers, dependencies point down
type = layers
layers =
    platform_stats : feature_stats : dashboard : project_progress : project_situation : onboarding : account
    routine : task_quiet : admin : room_cleanup
    agent : agent_instance : machine : device : local_fs : shell : site : preview : assistant : delivery
    block : thread : pin : mentions : room_task : task : review : living_doc : documents : library : deliverables : memory : feedback : space : groups : questions : answers : comments : discussion : materials : project_skill : search : docs_site : canvas : web_snippet : project_material : voice

    identity : user : team : project : topic : membership : topic_membership : authz : policy : invite : passkey : oauth : agent_type : agent_credential : ci_activity
    common : day_windows : conversation : idempotency : addressing : delivery_events : run_record : session_record : attachment : avatars : textfile : service_keys : backend_log : frontend_log : tag : legal : skill_library : notice_meta : shell_catalog : presentation_meta : review_note_codes : project_material_rows : event_about : event_author : project_permissions : reads : repositories

[tool.ruff.lint]
# DTZ and A003 are here because a hand-rolled guard was doing half of each job
# worse. DTZ (flake8-datetimez) catches the half our own rule never covered —
# `datetime.now()` with no tzinfo at all, as opposed to `.replace(tzinfo=None)`
# stripping one that was there; both produce the same silent UTC shift against
# TIMESTAMPTZ columns, and only the second was ever checked. A003 replaces that
# guard's builtin-shadowing rule outright, and covers every builtin rather than
# the four someone thought to list. Both were verified to report zero on the
# tree at the time they were switched on, so neither arrives with a backlog.
#
# A001/A002 (variable and argument shadowing) are deliberately NOT selected: 12
# existing sites, and `id`/`type` as a parameter name is idiomatic enough that
# the rule would cost more attention than it saves.
#
# Layout is fixed, never judged: import order (I) is applied by the pre-commit
# `ruff-format` hook together with `ruff format`, and line length (E501) is left
# to the formatter. RUF100 reports a `# noqa` that suppresses nothing, so
# `ruff check --fix` deletes it instead of a test keeping count of them.
select = ["E", "F", "UP", "B", "DTZ", "A003", "RUF100"]
# UP042 wants `class X(str, Enum)` → `class X(StrEnum)`. That is NOT behaviour-
# preserving: `str(member)` returns "X.MEMBER" for (str, Enum) but the raw value
# for StrEnum, which silently changes serialization/logging output. The existing
# (str, Enum) pattern is valid and intentional across the merged tree, so we keep
# it rather than risk a subtle behaviour change for a stylistic modernization.
ignore = ["UP042", "E501"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# A test that pins behaviour to a fixed instant writes `datetime(2026, 1, 1)`,
# and demanding a tzinfo on each of those 44 sites buys nothing — that value is
# never compared against a stored one, it IS the expectation. DTZ005 stays on
# even here: `now()` without a tz is the same latent bug in a test as in app
# code, since it lands in a TIMESTAMPTZ column and reads back shifted. Three of
# those were live in the contract data factory when this rule was switched on.
"tests/**" = ["DTZ001"]

# A migration on main is immutable (.claude/rules/migrations.md), so its
# now-inert `# noqa` comments stay as they were written.
"alembic/versions/*" = ["RUF100"]

# FastAPI's dependency-injection markers are CALLED in parameter defaults
# (`x = Depends(dep)`, `q = Query(...)`) — that's the framework's idiom, not the
# B008 "mutable/expensive default" anti-pattern. Whitelist them so B008 flags
# only genuine call-in-default mistakes. (Without this the merged tree shows ~636
# false positives, all fastapi.Depends/Query/Body/File.)
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
extend-immutable-calls = [
    "fastapi.Depends",
    "fastapi.Query",
    "fastapi.Body",
    "fastapi.Path",
    "fastapi.Header",
    "fastapi.Cookie",
    "fastapi.Form",
    "fastapi.File",
    "fastapi.Security",
    # our own DI marker, used exactly like fastapi.Depends in route defaults
    "app.auth.checker.require_permission",
]

[tool.pyright]
# Type-check the application source only. Tests deliberately pass SimpleNamespace
# / Mock ducks where typed objects are declared, and scripts/ are one-off spikes —
# holding either to strict typing yields hundreds of false positives with no
# app-correctness value. (Project standard: pyright zero errors in app code.)
include = ["app"]
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
pythonVersion = "3.13"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
anyio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Collection assigns three layers before CI partitions them across runners.
# Nothing writes these on a test: pytest_collection_modifyitems derives the layer
# from where the test lives and what its fixture closure reaches for. A test
# that declares one of these itself aborts the collection; a test that declares
# none has one added, and there is no third case, because that hook's
# `_layer_of` always answers with one of the three.
#
# Registered because the hook adds them by name and --strict-markers refuses an
# unregistered one even from there. What the flag is actually for is the other
# direction: a marker written on a test and registered nowhere is an error
# ("'bogus' not found in `markers` configuration option") instead of a
# decoration that silently does nothing, which is what @pytest.mark.asyncio had
# been here for as long as it existed — pytest-asyncio is not installed — and
# why those two had to go in the same commit that turned this on. It also
# catches a hand-written layer marker whose name is mistyped past the hook's
# own check. It does not read `-m` expressions: `-m puree` deselects the whole
# suite and exits 5, so a typo there is a red step, never a quiet green one.
markers = [
    "pure: no Postgres, no ASGI app — runs on a machine with nothing but Python",
    "contract: one side of a seam real and the other a double",
    "integration: real Postgres, real alembic, real ASGI app",
    # Not a layer: the tests that assert something is read — or happens —
    # exactly once: a request's SQL round trips, a batch that must not go per
    # row, a one-shot effect. Added by `pytest_collection_modifyitems` from the
    # file's name or its code, never written by hand; `pytest -m reads_once` is
    # the way to list them.
    "reads_once: asserts that a thing is read or happens exactly once, not once per row",
]
addopts = ["--strict-markers"]
# A wedged test must name itself. Without this, one test that never returns
# looks exactly like a slow suite: the run produces progress dots, then
# nothing, and CI kills the job at its own ceiling — so the log ends with a
# row of dots and no test name anywhere in it. That has now happened three
# times, and each one cost twenty minutes of the box's single runner to learn
# nothing at all.
#
# 300s only ends a test that never finishes. How long a finished test may take
# is a separate, much tighter check per layer (`_LAYER_CEILING_S` in
# tests/conftest.py), reported as that test's failure.
#
# The 300 s timeout applies locally too, deliberately: the same silence is just as unreadable
# on a laptop, and pytest-timeout stands down on its own under a debugger.
timeout = 300
# A signal can interrupt anyio's run_until_complete without cancelling the
# async test. Fixture teardown then queues behind that still-running test and
# hangs before the timeout report reaches CI. Dump the stack and exit the
# worker instead; xdist reports the crashed test. A local run, on a scheduler
# that hands out one case at a time, keeps going; CI's --dist loadfile ends the
# shard at the loss (scripts/ci_evidence), where the lost case cannot be
# retried either.
timeout_method = "thread"
# Keep a test's tmp_path only when it failed. Every passing test's directory
# used to stay until pytest's three-run rotation, which is how 13 GB of them
# filled the dev box's 32 GB /tmp tmpfs (docs/infrastructure.md).
tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed"

# pyproject.toml — Unifideck plugin (py_modules/unifideck/)
#
# This config currently only carries the ruff settings. It lives at
# the package root so ``ruff check .`` from any subdirectory of the
# package picks it up automatically. If the upstream repo has a
# pyproject.toml at the repo root, merge the [tool.ruff*] sections
# into it and delete this file.

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100

# ── Why both ``exclude`` AND ``force-exclude`` ────────────────────
# ``extend-exclude`` only applies when ruff walks the filesystem
# itself. CI gates that pass explicit file paths — ``pip-audit``
# expanding ``defaults/python/**/*.py``, ``mypy --strict`` on a glob,
# pre-commit hooks feeding the staged file list, or
# ``ruff check defaults/python/`` invoked directly from a workflow —
# bypass that filter entirely.
#
# Setting ``force-exclude = true`` makes ruff honour these patterns
# even when files are passed by name. Combined with the catch-all
# patterns below, the audit scope becomes "backend Python only"
# regardless of how ruff is invoked.
#
# Patterns live in ``exclude`` (not ``extend-exclude``) so they
# replace, not merge with, ruff's defaults — keeping the resolved
# list short and predictable.
force-exclude = true
exclude = [
    # ─── Ruff defaults we still want to keep ─────────────────────
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".git-rewrite",
    ".hg",
    ".ipynb_checkpoints",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".nox",
    ".pants.d",
    ".pyenv",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".pytype",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    ".vscode",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "buck-out",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    "site-packages",
    "venv",
    "env",
    "__pycache__",
    "*.egg-info",
    # ─── Vendored 3rd-party libraries ────────────────────────────
    # Pinned upstream code. CVE exposure is tracked via
    # ``requirements.txt`` + ``pip-audit``; ruff style/complexity
    # findings on this code are upstream choices that produce only
    # noise here. A previous full-scope audit returned 24 K issues
    # in the vendor tree, 0 actionable.
    #
    # Patterns are listed three ways to defeat invocation-path
    # ambiguity:
    #   * bare name             — matches dirs at the search root
    #   * `**/<name>/`         — matches the dir anywhere under root
    #   * specific full paths   — for the Decky Loader install layout
    "pip",
    "pip-*",
    "**/pip",
    "**/pip-*",
    "requests",
    "**/requests",
    "urllib3",
    "**/urllib3",
    "aiohttp",
    "**/aiohttp",
    "websockets",
    "**/websockets",
    "idna",
    "**/idna",
    "charset_normalizer",
    "**/charset_normalizer",
    "certifi",
    "**/certifi",
    "cryptography",
    "**/cryptography",
    "jsonschema",
    "jsonschema_specifications",
    "**/jsonschema",
    "**/jsonschema_specifications",
    "vdf",
    "**/vdf",
    "steamgrid",
    "**/steamgrid",
    "yaml",
    "**/yaml",
    "_yaml",
    # ─── Decky Loader vendor layouts ─────────────────────────────
    # Decky drops vendored deps into one of these depending on the
    # plugin version; all three are out of audit scope.
    "defaults/python",
    "defaults/python/*",
    "**/defaults/python",
    "**/defaults/python/*",
    "python_modules",
    "python_modules/*",
    "**/python_modules",
    "**/python_modules/*",
    "**/site-packages",
    "**/_vendor",
    "**/_vendor/*",
    "**/vendored",
    "**/vendored/*",
    "**/dist-info",
    "**/*.dist-info",
    # ─── Frontend ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # The TS/React layer has its own ESLint pipeline. Any ``.py``
    # under ``frontend/`` would be a packaging accident, not audit
    # territory.
    "frontend",
    "frontend/*",
    # ─── Docs build output ───────────────────────────────────────
    "docs/_build",
    "docs/_build/*",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Rule selection — distilled from the audit sessions. Keep
# everything that has historically caught a real bug, drop the
# rules that produce only style noise or false positives in this
# codebase.
select = [
    "F",      # Pyflakes (undefined names, unused imports, dead code)
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings (whitespace, EOF)
    "I",      # isort (import sorting)
    "N",      # pep8-naming
    "UP",     # pyupgrade (modern syntax)
    "B",      # bugbear (real bugs)
    "A",      # builtins shadowing
    "C4",     # comprehensions
    "DTZ",    # datetime timezone (caught 4 naive-datetime bugs)
    "T10",    # debugger
    "EXE",    # executable shebangs
    "ISC",    # implicit string concat
    "ICN",    # import conventions
    "PIE",    # misc anti-patterns
    "PT",     # pytest
    "Q",      # quotes (consistency)
    "RET",    # return statements (caught the launcher/bootstrap cascade bug)
    "SIM",    # simplify
    "TID",    # tidy imports
    "TC",     # type-checking
    "ARG",    # unused args
    "ERA",    # eradicate (commented-out code)
    "PL",     # pylint
    "TRY",    # try-except antipatterns
    "RUF",    # ruff-specific
    "S",      # bandit (security)
    "ASYNC",  # async pitfalls (caught the proton_service blocking-IO bug)
    "C90",    # mccabe complexity
]

ignore = [
    # ─── Documentation ───────────────────────────────────────────
    # Docstrings are tracked separately (Google-style coverage tooling
    # in the docstrings PR). Don't let ruff churn on D-rules.
    "D",
    # Type annotations: the codebase uses ``from __future__ import
    # annotations`` everywhere, ruff's ANN advice doesn't apply
    # consistently.
    "ANN",
    # ─── Formatter territory ─────────────────────────────────────
    # Formatter rules (long lines, trailing commas) belong to the
    # formatter, not the linter.
    "COM",
    "E501",
    # Boolean positional args (FBT) — many call sites already use
    # ``flag=True`` keyword form, and the rule fires too eagerly on
    # legitimate APIs.
    "FBT",
    # ─── pathlib migration (PTH) — deferred to Sprint C ──────────
    # The PTH family (use pathlib over os.path) stays ignored
    # pending its own dedicated migration pass, exactly as the
    # quality.yml gate documents. Re-selecting it prematurely
    # surfaced ~37 os.path findings across the cloud-save and
    # Ubisoft-prefix code that belong to that future sweep, not a
    # PR-blocking gate today. Graduate to ``select`` when Sprint C
    # lands the migration.
    "PTH",
    # ─── Refactor opinions ───────────────────────────────────────
    # PLR* are mostly "too many X" advisory thresholds. Useful at
    # design time, noisy in maintenance.
    "PLR",
    # PLC0415 forbids imports below the module top — we use lazy
    # imports intentionally to break circular-import chains in the
    # store layer.
    "PLC0415",
    # ─── TRY opinions ────────────────────────────────────────────
    # TRY003 (long messages) is taste. TRY300 (use else after try)
    # forces a style we don't follow. TRY301 (abstract raise) fires
    # on raise-from idioms.
    "TRY003",
    "TRY300",
    "TRY301",
    # ─── Mutable class attributes ────────────────────────────────
    # RUF012 fires on dataclass ``field(default_factory=list)``
    # which is the correct pattern.
    "RUF012",
    # ─── Bandit false-positive zone ──────────────────────────────
    # S101 (assert): we use asserts as runtime invariants in launcher
    # code, not as test scaffolding.
    "S101",
    # S603 (subprocess without shell=False): default is already
    # shell=False; the rule has no signal.
    "S603",
    # S607 (partial paths in subprocess): the binaries we exec are
    # resolved via ``which`` upstream or are intentional plain names
    # (``pgrep``, ``pkill``, ``xdg-settings``).
    "S607",
    # ─── BLE001 — broad-except in best-effort boundaries ─────────
    # The codebase deliberately catches ``Exception`` at every I/O,
    # network, CDP, subprocess, and plugin-SDK boundary so that one
    # flaky operation can't crash a launch. Every site logs the
    # exception (audited in the cleanup pass: 151 sites, 100% logged
    # at warning or debug level). The pattern is a feature, not a
    # bug; converting it to per-exception handlers would be a large
    # refactor with no clear payoff.
    "BLE001",
    # ─── Pytest discipline ───────────────────────────────────────
    # This is not a pytest project (tests live elsewhere). Drop the
    # PT rules so they don't fire on test fixtures we don't ship.
    "PT",
    # ─── Docstring micro-rules ───────────────────────────────────
    # RUF002 fires on intentional Unicode in docstrings (× for
    # multiplication, ≤/≥ in math notation, en-/em-dashes in prose).
    # The codebase deliberately uses these as typographic conventions
    # in docstrings; the rule has no signal here.
    "RUF002",
    # Same rationale extends to comments — ``× 100ms`` etc.
    "RUF003",
    # ─── Subprocess audit false positives ────────────────────────
    # S310: urllib audit for ``http://`` URLs. Every flagged site is
    # one of: a localhost CDP debugging port, a Steam-internal
    # 127.0.0.1 service, or an explicit user-controlled config URL
    # — never a default external endpoint over plain HTTP.
    "S310",
    # ─── Comment classification noise ────────────────────────────
    # ERA001 flags "commented-out code" but every site flagged in
    # this codebase is a doc-comment (worked example, RFC quote, or
    # a snippet of code shown to explain the surrounding logic), not
    # actual commented-out logic. We rely on git history for dead
    # code, not ruff.
    "ERA001",
    # ─── ARG family false positives ──────────────────────────────
    # ARG001/002/005 fire on unused lambda / method args that exist
    # to match a callback signature (asyncio.to_thread, asyncio
    # callbacks, mixin contracts where subclasses ignore the arg).
    # Removing the arg would change the callable's shape and break
    # the consumer. The rule has no signal in this codebase.
    "ARG001",
    "ARG002",
    "ARG005",
    # ─── Type-checking-import cosmetics ──────────────────────────
    # TC001-006 enforce TYPE_CHECKING-guarded imports. The codebase
    # uses ``from __future__ import annotations`` everywhere, which
    # makes all annotations strings — there is no runtime benefit to
    # moving the imports under TYPE_CHECKING and the noise drowns
    # out actionable hints.
    "TC001",
    "TC002",
    "TC003",
    "TC005",
    "TC006",
    # ─── Style/preference rules ──────────────────────────────────
    # SIM rules are mostly style preferences (use of contextlib.suppress
    # for ignored exceptions, ternaries vs if/else, etc). They don't
    # catch bugs; they enforce one author's taste.
    "SIM102",  # nested if can be combined
    "SIM105",  # use contextlib.suppress
    "SIM108",  # use ternary
    "SIM115",  # use context manager for open
    "SIM117",  # combine `with` blocks
    # ─── PLW0603 — module-level singletons ───────────────────────
    # Every flagged site is a deliberate module-level cache or
    # singleton pattern: lazy CDP-client init, SSL context cache,
    # Steam owned-games TTL cache, locale-config import cache.
    # Process-wide singletons are the correct shape for these,
    # and the ``global`` keyword is the only way to update them
    # from inside a function. Rule has no signal here.
    "PLW0603",
]

# Per-file overrides for cases where a whole rule should be skipped
# inside one directory rather than peppering the file with noqa.
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Type re-export modules: F401 is the expected pattern.
"**/__init__.py" = ["F401"]
# S105 false-positives (event-name constants and _DEFAULT_TOKEN_FILE
# paths matching the "_TOKEN_" substring) are handled by inline
# ``# noqa: S105`` directives in the affected files (events.py +
# stores/{gog,microsoft}/config.py). Per-file-ignores were removed
# in lot-async109 because some CI configurations bypass them, which
# would let S105 fire on the CI side while silencing it locally —
# inline noqa converges both paths.

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# Treat ``unifideck`` as the first-party namespace so its imports
# group correctly relative to stdlib/3rd-party.
known-first-party = ["unifideck"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Align ruff's C901 (cyclomatic) threshold with the project-wide
# complexity policy enforced in .github/workflows/complexity.yml
# (flake8 --max-complexity=15) and mirrored in .flake8. Ruff
# defaults to 10, which would make the ruff gate *stricter* than
# the documented bar and flag functions the complexity workflow
# considers in-policy. 15 is the single source of truth.
max-complexity = 15

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# mypy — same scope as ruff
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# mypy honours ``files`` and ``exclude`` settings under
# ``[tool.mypy]``. The CI gate runs ``mypy py_modules/unifideck/``
# from the repo root; that explicit-path invocation would
# *otherwise* descend into any vendored deps under the package
# unless we filter them here. The exclude regex mirrors the ruff
# exclude list above — same scope, different tool.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
# We list the package as ``files`` so a bare ``mypy`` invocation
# without arguments still type-checks the right tree.
files = ["py_modules/unifideck"]
# Regex (not glob!) — mypy's exclude uses Python's ``re.search``.
# Each alternative is a path fragment that disqualifies the file.
exclude = '''(?x)(
    /__pycache__/
    | /\.ruff_cache/
    | /\.mypy_cache/
    | /build/
    | /dist/
    | /defaults/python/
    | /python_modules/
    | /site-packages/
    | /_vendor/
    | /vendored/
    | \.dist-info/
    | /pip/
    | /requests/
    | /urllib3/
    | /aiohttp/
    | /websockets/
    | /idna/
    | /charset_normalizer/
    | /certifi/
    | /cryptography/
    | /jsonschema/
    | /vdf/
    | /steamgrid/
    | /yaml/
    | /frontend/
)'''

# Strict mode (matches the project's mypy invariant).
strict = true
warn_unused_configs = true
warn_unreachable = true
# Don't follow imports into excluded dirs.
follow_imports = "silent"

# ``attr`` / ``attrs`` / ``rpds`` ship ``.pyi`` stubs that mypy
# reads transitively when ``jsonschema`` and friends pull them in.
# Their stubs trigger 13 generic-type-arg and variance errors that
# originate inside the stubs themselves — nothing actionable from
# our side. ``ignore_errors = true`` silences them without
# changing ``follow_imports``, so dependents of these modules
# (jsonschema, etc.) keep their type info intact. Placed AFTER the
# strict-mode flags so TOML scoping doesn't pull them into the
# per-module override (a mistake that previously turned a 13-error
# fix into a 1300-error regression by losing strict-mode for the
# entire tree).
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["attr", "attr.*", "attrs", "attrs.*", "rpds", "rpds.*"]
ignore_errors = true

# ``legendary`` (the Epic CLI) is bundled as a GitHub-release binary at
# build time, NOT a pip dependency — its ``py_modules/legendary`` tree is
# gitignored, so it is PRESENT locally but ABSENT in CI's checkout. Without
# this override mypy diverges by environment: locally it resolves the
# untyped module (``no-untyped-call``), in CI it can't find it at all
# (``import-not-found``), and any ``type: ignore`` that fixes one fails as
# ``unused-ignore`` in the other. ``follow_imports = "skip"`` +
# ``ignore_missing_imports`` force it to ``Any`` either way, so the cloud-save
# fallback that calls ``legendary.core.LegendaryCore`` type-checks identically
# in both. (Only ``cloud_save/epic_strategy.py`` imports it.)
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["legendary.*"]
follow_imports = "skip"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ``Xlib`` is in the same category as ``legendary`` above, one step further
# removed: it is not a dependency of this plugin at all. It rides inside the
# bundled umu zipapp, which the gamescope window tagger puts on ``sys.path``
# for the length of one import. It is therefore absent from CI, absent from
# the dev venv, and present only at runtime on a device — so the same
# environment-divergence argument applies, and ``types-python-xlib`` would
# be a dependency added for a module we do not ship.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["Xlib.*"]
follow_imports = "skip"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# pytest — test suite at the repo root
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Layout convention (cf. "Test coverage companion v1.0", section
# "Naming conventions") :
#
#   tests/unit/<sub_package>/test_<source_file>.py
#
# So ``py_modules/unifideck/core/cache_manager.py`` is mirrored
# by ``tests/unit/core/test_cache_manager.py`` — drop the
# ``py_modules/unifideck/`` prefix, keep the rest of the path,
# prepend ``test_`` to the basename.
#
# ``testpaths`` is set to ``tests`` (relative to the repo root)
# so that a bare ``pytest`` invocation walks the right tree.
# This matches the CI commands :
#   * ``.github/workflows/tests.yml`` — runs ``pytest tests/``
#   * ``.github/workflows/complexity.yml`` — runs ``pytest tests/unit/_tooling/``
#
# Historical note : an earlier version of this config pointed
# at ``py_modules/unifideck/tests`` (in-package). That layout
# was abandoned in favour of root-level ``tests/`` so the test
# tree doesn't ship inside the plugin zip (Decky bundles
# ``py_modules/`` whole) and so the coverage companion's
# mirror convention is enforceable by CI without a path
# rewrite step.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
# The plugin package lives in ``py_modules/unifideck/`` (a
# non-src, non-installed layout dictated by Decky Loader). It
# is never ``pip install``-ed, so without help ``import
# unifideck`` fails under CI — locally it only worked because
# PYTHONPATH was exported by hand. ``pythonpath`` (pytest >= 7,
# guaranteed by ``minversion = 8.0``) prepends this dir to
# ``sys.path`` at collection time, making the package importable
# everywhere pytest runs (CI, local, pre-commit, IDE) with no
# external env var or editable install. This is the canonical
# fix for non-src layouts and replaces the manual PYTHONPATH.
pythonpath = ["py_modules"]
# Strict markers/config keep test scaffolding honest : a typo
# in a marker name fails the suite instead of silently being a
# no-op. ``no:cacheprovider`` disables the .pytest_cache dir
# which is pure noise in CI runners.
#
# Strict warnings (added 2026-05): the suite must run with
# **zero warnings**. ``filterwarnings = ["error", ...]``
# promotes every warning to an error so a Deprecation/Runtime
# warning introduced by a dependency bump or a sloppy test
# fails the suite instead of scrolling past unnoticed. Because
# pytest reads this file everywhere (CI, local, pre-commit,
# IDE), the rule holds for every contributor, not just CI.
#
# ``ignore::ResourceWarning`` is the single, explicit
# allow-list entry. Those warnings ("unclosed file") originate
# in application/dependency code (config readers), are out of
# scope for the test suite, never surface in normal runs, and
# promoting them would fail CI for reasons unrelated to test
# correctness. Any test that legitimately needs to assert on a
# specific warning uses the ``filterwarnings`` marker, which
# overrides these globals locally.
#
# ``-ra`` prints a short summary of every non-pass outcome
# (skips, xfails) so they stay visible in CI logs — the
# companion tests.yml turns a non-zero skip count into a hard
# failure (pytest has no native "error on skip").
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "-ra",
    "-p", "no:cacheprovider",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    "ignore::ResourceWarning",
]
asyncio_mode = "auto"

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["py_modules/unifideck"]
# Mirror the exclusion list as omit patterns — coverage.py uses
# fnmatch syntax (not regex like mypy, not glob like ruff).
omit = [
    "*/defaults/python/*",
    "*/python_modules/*",
    "*/site-packages/*",
    "*/_vendor/*",
    "*/vendored/*",
    "*/*.dist-info/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/frontend/*",
]

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Tools whose scope is NOT controlled from this file
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# These tools take their config from separate root-level files.
# They each need their own scope filter to avoid auditing vendored
# deps. Left out of this file because mixing their TOML sections
# here would split ownership of those tools' configuration.
#
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# 1. ``flake8`` — reads ``.flake8`` (or ``setup.cfg [flake8]``).
#    flake8 does NOT honour pyproject.toml: this is why ruff's
#    ``[tool.ruff] exclude`` doesn't stop flake8 from descending
#    into ``py_modules/urllib3/``, ``py_modules/vdf/``, etc.
#    The companion ``.flake8`` file in this repo mirrors the
#    vendored exclusions and the complexity ceilings below.
#    Note that flake8 has no ``force-exclude`` — explicit-path
#    invocations (``flake8 py_modules/urllib3/foo.py``) bypass
#    the exclude list. Make sure CI invokes flake8 on
#    ``py_modules/unifideck/`` (or the repo root with the walk
#    relying on ``.flake8`` exclusions), never on a path inside a
#    vendored dir.
#
# 2. ``pip-audit`` — reads ``requirements.txt`` directly. Already
#    scoped correctly: we list only the 4 direct runtime deps
#    (``aiohttp``, ``websockets``, ``cryptography``, ``jsonschema``),
#    not the transitive vendor tree. No config change needed.
#
# 3. ``import-linter`` — reads ``.importlinter`` at the repo root.
#    Contracts there must ignore packages they don't own. The
#    canonical scope filter for that file is:
#
#       [importlinter]
#       root_packages =
#           unifideck
#       include_external_packages = False
#
#    ``include_external_packages = False`` is the equivalent of
#    ``force-exclude`` for this tool: it stops the linter from
#    descending into ``site-packages``/``defaults/python``/
#    ``python_modules`` when resolving imports.
#
# 4. ``vulture`` (dead-code finder, if used in CI) — scope via
#    ``--exclude defaults/python,frontend,python_modules`` on the
#    command line, or a ``vulture.toml`` next to ``pyproject.toml``.
#
# 5. GitHub Actions workflows — make sure every linter invocation
#    runs ``py_modules/unifideck`` (or the package root) as its
#    working directory rather than the repo root, OR passes
#    ``py_modules/unifideck`` as the explicit path argument. With
#    ``force-exclude = true`` set above, even a bad CI invocation
#    can't accidentally lint vendored code through ruff — but
#    flake8 (no force-exclude) and mypy honour their own
#    ``exclude`` only during directory walking, so the same care
#    applies.


# ─── vulture ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Dead-code finder. Run via ``vulture py_modules/unifideck/``.
#
# ``min_confidence = 80`` filters out the noisy 60%-confidence
# class-method/attribute/property reports. The remaining
# 80%-100% reports flag functions/variables/imports that are
# genuinely unreferenced statically.
#
# WHY 60% IS NOISY HERE: this codebase relies on three patterns
# vulture cannot resolve statically:
#
# 1. RPC methods on ``*RPCMixin`` classes are invoked from JS by
#    the Decky bridge (no Python caller). Every public coroutine
#    on a mixin looks "unused" to vulture.
#
# 2. Event-handler methods named ``_on_<event>`` are subscribed
#    dynamically via ``bus.subscribe(handler.method)`` rather
#    than called by name. They look unused even though every
#    one fires on its corresponding event.
#
# 3. Dataclass attributes (``Result.metadata``, ``Game.appid``,
#    ``SyncStats.bytes_transferred`` etc.) are read from
#    serialised JSON on the JS side or from SQL row factories,
#    again invisible to vulture's static walk.
#
# Together these account for 200+ of the 220 60%-confidence
# reports. Raising the threshold catches the real dead code
# (the single 100%-confidence ``resync_artwork`` parameter
# triaged in lot-vulture) without drowning in noise.
[tool.vulture]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["py_modules/unifideck"]
exclude = [
    "defaults/python/",
    "python_modules/",
    "frontend/",
    "node_modules/",
    "**/__pycache__/",
]
# Pattern-level ignores for symbols vulture sees as orphan but
# that the framework / RPC bridge / event bus invoke dynamically.
# Patterns use glob-style matching (``*`` matches any substring).
ignore_names = [
    "_on_*",          # event handlers subscribed via bus
    "_*RPCMixin*",    # RPC mixin classes invoked from JS
]

[importlinter]

[importlinter:contract:layered]
name = Ouro three-layer architecture

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

# L3 freeze (2026-04-25): these thresholds are frozen at the post-R7 high-water mark.
# Raising them in the future requires explicit justification recorded in
# docs/ratchet/SUPPRESSIONS.md, the same way per-line noqa entries are tracked.
# Current near-the-line offenders are listed in SUPPRESSIONS.md.
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Wave R7c raised default 10 → 22 to accommodate dispatch tables and the
# build-pipeline phase functions. C0a-e + C1a-d drove every offender in
# core/ and electrical/builder_phases.py back below the default threshold;
# C1e drops the threshold to 18 — the new peak in src/, held by
# CircuitBuilder.build (electrical/builder.py:921). The remaining 7 C901
# violators between 12 and 18 (svg_path match dispatch + the four add_*
# /build methods on CircuitBuilder) are tier-C2 territory.
max-complexity = 18

# L3 freeze (2026-04-25): these thresholds are frozen at the post-R7 high-water mark.
# Raising them in the future requires explicit justification recorded in
# docs/ratchet/SUPPRESSIONS.md, the same way per-line noqa entries are tracked.
# Current near-the-line offenders are listed in SUPPRESSIONS.md.
[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Schematika builders/factories legitimately take many kwargs (positional-only
# identity + many keyword-only flags).  Raised from ruff default 5 → 8 in Wave
# R3. C2d-1/2/3 bundled all ≥8-arg functions into option dataclasses; C2d-4
# returns the threshold to ruff's default of 8.
max-args = 8
# Wave R7c: PLR0911/PLR0912/PLR0915 threshold relaxations.
# max-returns raised from 6 → 10: translate() and _render_page() are
# singledispatch/match-style dispatch functions where each branch must return
# independently; merging returns would worsen readability.
# Wave C0a: lowered from 10 to 6 (translate + _render_page now use match/case
# with single final return; behavior-compatible refactoring achieved the goal).
max-returns = 6
# Wave R7c raised default 12 → 22; C0b extracted the SVG path parsers and
# C1a-d extracted the four build-pipeline phase functions. C1e drops the
# threshold to 13 — the new peak in src/, held by parse() in core/svg_path.py
# (inherent 10-arm match dispatch on PathCommand) and add_symbol/add_spdt in
# electrical/builder.py (tier C2).
max-branches = 13
# Wave R7c raised default 50 → 70; C0c rewrote _rotate_path_d (was 70+ stmts)
# to a one-liner and C1a-d collapsed the four build-pipeline phases into
# 3-5 line orchestrators. C1e drops the threshold to 51 — the new peak in
# src/, held by CircuitBuilder.build (electrical/builder.py:921; tier C2).
max-statements = 51

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401", "F403", "I001"]  # isort disabled for all __init__.py: deliberate import orders avoid circular imports (electrical: system.system first; catalog: errors -> device -> registry -> cables); F403 OK because shims declare __all__ (Wave L3a / L1)
# Inline Typst code in string literals has long lines
"src/schematika/rendering/typst/compiler.py" = ["E501"]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["E501"]
# tests/** ignores:
#   D    — no pydocstyle on test fixtures/asserts
#   ARG  — fixture/subclass params aren't always used
#   PLR2004 — "magic value" comparisons are the whole point of assertions
#   PLR0913 — parametrised fixtures legitimately take many args
#   S101 — asserts are pytest's assertion mechanism, not a security risk
#   S108 — /tmp paths in tests are deliberate test fixtures, not real temp-file creation
#   S314 — ET.fromstring() parses our own renderer output, not untrusted data
#   ANN  — annotation completeness is a library-API concern; pytest fixtures and
#          assertions don't benefit from `-> None` / `*args: object` noise (Wave T4a)
"tests/**" = ["D", "ARG", "PLR2004", "PLR0913", "S101", "S108", "S314", "ANN"]
# examples/** are demonstration scripts; same rationale as tests/** for ANN (Wave T4a).
"examples/**" = ["ANN"]
# test_transform.py exercises SVG path commands (M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, Z)
# whose uppercase letters are part of the grammar — test names mirror them.
"tests/unit/test_transform.py" = ["N802"]
# Wave R5 — IEC/PLC naming in tests
"tests/unit/test_pcb_adapter.py" = ["N806"]      # F1/T1/_F1 are IEC fuse/terminal designators
"tests/unit/test_plc_resolver.py" = ["N806", "N817"]  # PLC identifiers and import aliases
"tests/unit/test_terminal_type.py" = ["N817"]    # T alias for Terminal in IEC context
"src/schematika/**/__init__.py" = ["D104"]
# mcp/server.py is a sandboxed code executor; it intentionally catches all
# user-raised exceptions (Exception) to return structured error strings.
# S102: exec() is the explicit mechanism for executing user-submitted Python code
# in the MCP sandbox — there is no alternative, and this is intentional.
"src/schematika/mcp/server.py" = ["BLE001", "S102"]
# test_builder.py mock_symbol helper uses an intermediate variable for clarity;
# fixing RET504 would require test body changes (blocked per wave R6 spec).
"tests/unit/test_builder.py" = ["RET504"]

[tool.ty.src]
exclude = [

[tool.mutmut]
# Mutation testing config — target the two files slated for refactor.
# Kill-rate floor: see docs/baselines/<date>/mutmut_results.txt.
# Runner uses .venv python directly (skip `uv run` cold-start overhead per mutant)

package com.bernardomg.association.test.architecture.rule;

import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.fields;

import java.time.Instant;

import com.bernardomg.framework.testing.architecture.predicates.IsJpaAnnotatedClass;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule;

public class EntityRules {

    /**
     * JPA entities should only use Instant for date/time.
     */
    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule jpa_entities_should_only_use_instant = fields().that()
        .areDeclaredInClassesThat(new IsJpaAnnotatedClass())
        .and()
        .areNotStatic()
        .and()
        .areNotFinal()
        .should()
        .haveRawType(Instant.class)
        .orShould()
        .notHaveRawType(java.util.Date.class)
        .andShould()
        .notHaveRawType(java.sql.Date.class)
        .andShould()
        .notHaveRawType(java.time.LocalDate.class)
        .andShould()
        .notHaveRawType(java.time.LocalDateTime.class)
        .andShould()
        .notHaveRawType(java.time.ZonedDateTime.class)
        .andShould()
        .notHaveRawType(java.time.Year.class)
        .andShould()
        .notHaveRawType(java.time.YearMonth.class)
        .andShould()
        .notHaveRawType(java.time.MonthDay.class)
        .because("Only java.time.Instant is allowed for representing date/time in entities.");

}

        // Profile modules

# name = "httpx stays out of the pure center"
# type = "protected"
# protected_modules = ["httpx"]
# allowed_importers = ["calfkit.providers", "calfkit.adapters"]

# import-linter contracts -- the Python analog of a build-graph "no cycles"
# + visibility rule. Guards the layering established when the three
# lazy-import cycles were removed (build_isolation_env -> subenv, the CUDA
# IPC cache -> _ipc_shared, the worker pool -> pool). Run: `lint-imports`.
#
# IMPORTANT: keep this passing WITHOUT relying on function-body imports as an
# escape. A cycle re-broken by moving an import into a function body is still
# a cycle -- fix the layering instead. (import-linter analyses top-level
# imports; a reviewer must reject new in-function cross-module imports.)

[importlinter]
root_package = comfy_env

[importlinter:contract:isolation-acyclic]
name = isolation modules form no import cycles
type = independence
# These modules must not import each other in a way that forms a cycle.
# Stated as independence between the leaves and the layers above them.
modules =
    comfy_env.isolation.subenv
    comfy_env.isolation.tensor_utils

[importlinter:contract:nothing-imports-wrap]
name = wrap is the top orchestrator -- nothing under isolation imports it
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    comfy_env.isolation.pool
    comfy_env.isolation.metadata
    comfy_env.isolation.subenv
    comfy_env.isolation.tensor_utils
    comfy_env.isolation.workers.subprocess
    comfy_env.isolation.workers._ipc_parent
    comfy_env.isolation.workers._ipc_shared
forbidden_modules =
    comfy_env.isolation.wrap
# The public facade (isolation/__init__ re-exports register_nodes from wrap)
# is the ONE legitimate top-level reference; exempt it so the contract
# checks DIRECT module imports, not the package-init re-export chain.
ignore_imports =
    comfy_env.isolation -> comfy_env.isolation.wrap

[importlinter:contract:transport-leaf]
name = the transport leaf (_ipc_shared) imports nothing from comfy_env
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    comfy_env.isolation.workers._ipc_shared
forbidden_modules =
    comfy_env.isolation.wrap
    comfy_env.isolation.pool
    comfy_env.isolation.metadata
    comfy_env.isolation.workers.subprocess
    comfy_env.isolation.workers._ipc_parent
    comfy_env.isolation.tensor_utils

[importlinter:contract:package-layers]
name = comfy_env packages form a one-way dependency graph
type = layers
# Top imports down, never up. config / debug / settings / pixi are universal
# leaves (imported everywhere) and are deliberately NOT listed -- the layers
# contract only constrains the modules named here.
layers =
    comfy_env.isolation
    comfy_env.install
    comfy_env.packages
    comfy_env.environment
    comfy_env.detection
ignore_imports =
    # The root package __init__ is the public facade, so `import comfy_env`
    # anywhere routes through it. Exempt those facade edges so the contract
    # checks DIRECT module imports, not facade-routed ones (the same reason
    # isolation/__init__ -> wrap is exempt below).
    #
    # Only the edges the pruned facade actually has. import-linter treats an
    # ignore that matches nothing as an error, so a stale entry here fails the
    # whole run -- and with it publish.yml, which is `needs: test`. The facade
    # reaches environment via its SUBMODULES (environment.setup,
    # environment.cache), which is a different edge, and no longer touches
    # packages at all.
    comfy_env -> comfy_env.isolation
    comfy_env -> comfy_env.install
    # register_serializer is re-exported from a module four levels down, so the
    # facade edge is to that module -- NOT to `comfy_env.isolation`. An ignore
    # matches one exact edge, so the line above does not cover this one, and
    # without it every subpackage that touches the facade looks like it imports
    # isolation.
    comfy_env -> comfy_env.isolation.workers._ipc_shared

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = isolation dependency layers point one way
type = layers
# Top imports down; never the reverse.
layers =
    comfy_env.isolation.wrap
    comfy_env.isolation.metadata
    comfy_env.isolation.pool
    comfy_env.isolation.workers.subprocess
    comfy_env.isolation.workers._ipc_parent
    comfy_env.isolation.workers._ipc_shared
ignore_imports =
    comfy_env.isolation -> comfy_env.isolation.wrap

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = ["inc.evil"], importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class])

    @ArchTest
    val controllersShouldNotTalkToRepositories: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses()
        .that()
        .resideInAPackage("..web..")
        .should()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .resideInAnyPackage("..repo..")

    @ArchTest
    val loggingLibraryShouldBeUsedInsteadOfSystemOut = GeneralCodingRules.NO_CLASSES_SHOULD_ACCESS_STANDARD_STREAMS
        .because("The preferred way of logging is via a logging library like logback")

        .that()
        .areInterfaces()

        .haveNameMatching(".*Repository")
        .and()
        .areAssignableTo(org.springframework.data.repository.Repository::class.java)
        .should()
        .beAnnotatedWith(Repository::class.java)

    @ArchTest
    val jpaRepositoriesClassNameMustHaveRepositorySuffix: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that()
        .areInterfaces()
        .and()
        .areAssignableTo(org.springframework.data.repository.Repository::class.java)
        .should()
        .haveNameMatching(".*Repository")

    @ArchTest
    val servicesClassNamesMustHaveServiceOrServiceImplSuffix: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that()
        .areAnnotatedWith(Service::class.java)
        .should()
        .haveNameMatching("(.*ServiceImpl)|(.*Service)")

    @ArchTest
    val controllerClassNamesMustHaveControllerOrControllerImplSuffix: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that()
        .areAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java)
        .should()
        .haveNameMatching("(.*ControllerImpl)|(.*Controller)")

    @ArchTest
    val restControllersAreInTheControllerPackage: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that()
        .areAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java)
        .should()
        .resideInAPackage("..web.rest")

    @ArchTest
    val servicesAreInTheServicePackage: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that()
        .areAnnotatedWith(Service::class.java)
        .should()
        .resideInAPackage("..service.impl")

    @ArchTest
    val repositoriesAreInTheRepositoryPackage: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that()
        .areAnnotatedWith(Repository::class.java)
        .should()
        .resideInAPackage("..repo")

    @ArchTest
    val jpaEntitiesAreInTheModelPackage: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.classes()
        .that()
        .areAnnotatedWith(Entity::class.java)
        .should()
        .resideInAPackage("..model")

    @ArchTest
    val controllersShouldNotTalkToJpaEntities: ArchRule = ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses()
        .that()
        .areAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java).or().areAnnotatedWith(Controller::class.java)
        .should()
        .dependOnClassesThat()
        .areAnnotatedWith(Entity::class.java)

    @ArchTest
    val noFieldInjection = GeneralCodingRules.NO_CLASSES_SHOULD_USE_FIELD_INJECTION
}

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/Alberto-Codes/gepa-adk"
Documentation = "https://alberto-codes.github.io/gepa-adk/"
Repository = "https://github.com/Alberto-Codes/gepa-adk"
Issues = "https://github.com/Alberto-Codes/gepa-adk/issues"
Changelog = "https://github.com/Alberto-Codes/gepa-adk/releases"

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build>=0.9.22,<0.14.0"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[tool.uv]
constraint-dependencies = [
    # GHSA-7wc2-qxgw-g8gg: Authlib < 1.6.7 vulnerable
    "authlib>=1.6.7",
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "testpypi"
url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple/"
publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"
explicit = true

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88  # Formatter target
target-version = "py312"
exclude = [".uv-cache", ".venv", "__pycache__", "*.egg-info"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Sonar-adjacent rule set shared with quantfit (#354): pycodestyle, isort,
# pydocstyle, bugbear, simplify, pyupgrade, ruff, pylint, mccabe, tryceratops,
# perflint, bandit and logging-format.
extend-select = ["E402", "E501", "I", "D", "B", "SIM", "UP", "RUF", "PL", "C901", "TRY", "PERF", "S", "G"]
# Exception messages built at the raise site carry the context; a custom
# exception class per message is noise.
ignore = ["TRY003"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 12  # buffer under the SonarQube threshold of 15

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 7  # matches Sonar S107

[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
max-line-length = 100  # Linter threshold (allow some flexibility)

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Test names carry the scenario, so a docstring restating them is noise.
# Tests assert with bare `assert` (S101), pass fixture credentials (S106),
# seed fake randomness (S311), compare against literal expected values
# (PLR2004) and import inside a test to isolate module state (PLC0415).
# S105: the hits are literal "password"/"token"/"secret" values that the
# redaction tests feed in or assert on, plus one enum member named PASS.
# RUF012: every hit is a fixed class-level default on a test fake or stub,
# not shared production state.
"tests/**/*.py" = [
    "S101", "S105", "S106", "S311", "PLR2004", "PLC0415", "RUF012",
    "D100", "D101", "D102", "D103", "D104",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# `scripts` is named so local and CI runs classify the gate modules alike.
known-first-party = ["gepa_adk", "scripts"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
docstring-code-format = true
docstring-code-line-length = "dynamic"

# Ty type checker configuration (ty 0.0.18)
# Remaining overrides are for genuine ty limitations with dynamic types and test patterns
[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "tests"]
exclude = [
    "scripts/",    # Utility scripts - not production code
]

# `.claude/hooks/` holds the session guards. It forms no package, so name
# it as a search path to let its tests import it.
[tool.ty.environment]
extra-paths = [".claude/hooks"]

# Override for test files - relax rules for dynamic types, negative-path tests, and Optional guards
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["tests/**"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
# Tests for deserialize_schema() access attributes on dynamically created BaseModel subclasses
# ty can't know the runtime type has these fields - confirmed by passing tests
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
# Tests deliberately pass wrong types to verify error handling (e.g., string instead of class)
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"
# Tests subscript content.parts which ty sees as Optional — runtime asserts guard this
not-subscriptable = "ignore"
# Tests use `in` on Optional fields — runtime asserts guard this
unsupported-operator = "ignore"
# Tests deliberately assign to frozen/read-only attributes inside pytest.raises,
# and monkey-patch Protocol attributes with mocks
invalid-assignment = "ignore"
# Tests deliberately pass extra kwargs to Pydantic models to verify they are discarded/rejected
pydantic-discarded-extra-argument = "ignore"
# ADK 2.x deprecates Sequential/Loop/ParallelAgent (still the supported gepa-adk path
# until the graph-API port) - Issue #346
deprecated = "ignore"

# ADK 2.x deprecation bridge - Issue #346
# workflow.py and api.py construct Sequential/Loop/ParallelAgent, deprecated in ADK 2.x
# in favor of google.adk.workflow. They remain the supported path until the graph-API
# port (epic #337 Phase B); remove this override when it lands.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = [
    "src/gepa_adk/adapters/workflow/**",
    "src/gepa_adk/adapters/evolution/multi_agent.py",
    "src/gepa_adk/api.py",
]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
deprecated = "ignore"

# Override for examples with dynamic schema execution
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["examples/schema_evolution_example.py"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
# deserialize_schema() returns type[BaseModel] but actual class has dynamic fields
# ty can't resolve attributes on dynamically created types - this is expected
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# import-linter
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "gepa_adk"
include_external_packages = true
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Hex architecture layers"
type = "layers"
# `utils` sits between `ports` and `domain`: utils imports domain
# (`events.py`, `schema_utils.py`), and neither domain nor ports imports utils.
# The default selection strategies sit in `ports.defaults`, so both the
# engine and the adapters may import them under ADR-000; no layer
# exception is needed.
layers = [
    "gepa_adk.adapters",
    "gepa_adk.engine",
    "gepa_adk.ports",
    "gepa_adk.utils",
    "gepa_adk.domain",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "No external SDK in domain/ports/engine/utils"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "gepa_adk.domain",
    "gepa_adk.ports",
    "gepa_adk.engine",
    "gepa_adk.utils",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "google",
    "litellm",
]

# The layers contract above lets adapters import engine; ADR-000 does not.
# This contract closes that gap. It replaced the boundaries shell script (#533).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Adapters do not import engine"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "gepa_adk.adapters",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "gepa_adk.engine",
]

# `json` and `pathlib` stay allowed: the domain uses them for the canonical
# hash, the serialisability check and `checkpoint_path` coercion, not file IO.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain is IO-free"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "gepa_adk.domain",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "os",
    "io",
    "logging",
    "httpx",
    "subprocess",
    "socket",
    "sqlite3",
    "shutil",
    "tempfile",
]

[tool.docvet]
fail-on = ["enrichment", "freshness", "coverage", "griffe", "presence"]
# `.claude/hooks/` holds session guards that are not part of the
# `gepa_adk` package, so package-relative docstring checks do not apply.
extend-exclude = [".claude"]

[tool.docvet.enrichment]
# ruff D417 requires *args/**kwargs to be documented; include them in
# docvet's signature-vs-Args agreement check so the two don't conflict.
exclude-args-kwargs = false
# Document **kwargs inline in Args (ruff D417 convention) rather than in
# a separate Other Parameters section.
require-other-parameters = false

[tool.docvet.presence]
min-coverage = 100.0

[tool.hatch.envs.default.scripts]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Coverage
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# pytest-cov reads `fail_under` from here when no `--cov-fail-under` is
# passed, so the pre-push hook and CI share one floor.
[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 85
show_missing = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests - fast, isolated",
    "contract: Contract tests verifying interface compliance",
    "integration: Integration tests with real databases",
    "slow: Slow-running tests (execution, API calls)",
    "api: Tests that make real API calls to external services (Gemini, Ollama, etc.) - excluded by default",
    "requires_ollama: Tests requiring local Ollama service",
    "requires_gemini: Tests requiring Gemini API (video, native planning)",
]
# `.claude/hooks/` holds the session guards. It forms no package, so put it
# on the import path for its tests, matching `[tool.ty.environment]`.
# `.` lets `tests/conftest.py` import `tests.fixtures` at load time; there is no
# `tests/__init__.py`, so pytest only puts `tests/` on the path, not the root.
pythonpath = [".claude/hooks", "."]
# Exclude API tests by default to avoid accidental quota usage.
# `--strict-markers` turns a marker typo into an error instead of a
# silently deselected test; `--strict-config` does the same for unknown
# ini keys.
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--showlocals",
    "-m",
    "not api",
]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Deprecation warning strategy: treat all warnings as errors, explicitly ignore third-party issues.
# Each ignored warning MUST have a tracking issue. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full process.
# Pattern: "ignore:message_regex:WarningClass:module_regex"
filterwarnings = [
    # Treat all warnings as errors by default - new warnings will fail CI
    "error",
    #
    # === Third-party warning ignores (each with tracking issue) ===
    #
    # Pydantic v2 deprecation warnings from LiteLLM/ADK - Issue #118
    # Upstream uses Pydantic v1 patterns; remove when they migrate to v2
    "ignore:.*PydanticDeprecatedSince20.*:DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore:.*Pydantic.*serialization.*:UserWarning",
    "ignore:.*Pydantic.*serializer.*:UserWarning",
    "ignore::UserWarning:pydantic.*",
    "ignore:.*Pydantic.*:UserWarning",
    "ignore:^deprecated$:DeprecationWarning:pydantic.*",  # Generic "deprecated" from pydantic internals
    "ignore:^deprecated$:DeprecationWarning:google.adk.*",  # Pydantic deprecated field in ADK RunConfig - Issue #125
    #
    # ADK 2.x deprecation bridge - Issue #346
    # google-adk 2.x deprecates Sequential/Loop/ParallelAgent in favor of google.adk.workflow,
    # and BaseAgentConfig (config now loaded via reflection). The 1.x-style classes remain the
    # supported gepa-adk path until the graph-API port (epic #337 Phase B) lands.
    "ignore:BaseAgentConfig is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore:SequentialAgent is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore:LoopAgent is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore:ParallelAgent is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
    #
    # Google genai SDK aiohttp subclassing - Issue #118 (bundled with Pydantic/ADK issues)
    # google.genai._api_client subclasses aiohttp.ClientSession which is deprecated
    "ignore:Inheritance class.*from ClientSession is discouraged:DeprecationWarning",
    #
    # ADK experimental feature warnings - Issue #119
    # We intentionally use experimental ADK features (ADR-014); these are informational
    "ignore:.*adk.*\\[EXPERIMENTAL\\].*:UserWarning",
    "ignore:.*adk.*experimental.*:UserWarning",
    #
    # LiteLLM async cleanup warnings - Issue #120
    # Known upstream bugs: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/8831, #14276
    "ignore:coroutine.*was never awaited:RuntimeWarning",
    #
    # Async test cleanup warnings (unclosed sockets/event loops) - Issue #120
    # Common with async tests using LiteLLM/ADK; not actionable in test code
    "ignore::ResourceWarning",
    "ignore::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning",
    #
    # Misc third-party async cleanup warnings - Issue #120
    "ignore:.*tracemalloc.*:UserWarning",
    "ignore:enable_cleanup_closed.*:DeprecationWarning",
    #
    # === gepa-adk internal deprecations ===
    #
    # evolve_sync() deprecated in favor of run_sync() — Story 2.6
    "ignore:evolve_sync\\(\\) is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
]

[project]
name = "mandari"
version = "0.11.0"
description = "Mandari Insight - Kommunalpolitische Transparenz"
readme = "README.md"
license = { text = "AGPL-3.0-or-later" }
# Obergrenze = neueste Python-Version, mit der Image und CI laufen. uv sperrt für den ganzen Bereich; ohne Grenze
# müsste jede gesperrte Version schon Wheels für künftige Python-Versionen haben. Beim Wechsel des Basis-Images
# anheben und `uv lock` ausführen.
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"
authors = [{ name = "Sven Konopka" }]

# Einzige Quelle der direkten Abhängigkeiten; die gesperrten Versionen stehen in uv.lock (Image, CI, pip-audit
# und SBOM lesen sie von dort). Nach jeder Änderung hier: `uv lock` in diesem Verzeichnis.
dependencies = [
    # Gemeinsame OParl-Typen (lokales Paket ../shared, siehe [tool.uv.sources])
    "mandari-oparl",

    # Django 6.1. Die nächste Feature-Version wird von Hand gehoben (zusammen mit django-stubs); Dependabot
    # liefert hier nur Patch-Versionen, siehe `ignore` in .github/dependabot.yml.
    "django>=6.1,<6.2",
    "django-htmx>=1.19.0",
    "django-cotton>=2.7.2",
    "django-vite>=3.2.0",
    "django-ninja>=1.7.1",
    "django-unfold>=0.40.0",
    "whitenoise>=6.7.0",

    # Database
    "psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.2.0",  # pool: Verbindungspool statt langlebiger Verbindungen (#257)
    "dj-database-url>=2.2.0",

    # Ingestor integration (needed for Django sync daemon)
    # Das Image führt den Ingestor-Code aus /ingestor selbst aus (Abgleich aus dem Admin, manage.py sync_daemon).
    # [asyncio] zieht greenlet ausdrücklich: Ab SQLAlchemy 2.1 kommt es nicht mehr von selbst mit, und ohne
    # greenlet scheitert der Abgleich. Obergrenze: Die Nebenversion folgt dem Ingestor und wird von Hand gehoben
    # (Dependabot: `ignore`), nachdem sie dort geprüft ist.
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.36,<2.1",
    "asyncpg>=0.30.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.6.0",
    "rich>=13.9.0",

    # Cache & Sessions
    "redis>=5.2.0",

    # Environment
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.0",
    # Zeitzonendaten unabhängig vom Betriebssystem des Images (Django verlangt das Paket nur unter Windows)
    "tzdata>=2026.1",

    # Search: Client-Hauptversion = Server-Hauptversion (docker-compose.yml), deshalb die Obergrenze
    "elasticsearch>=8.12.0,<9",

    # AI / HTTP
    "httpx>=0.28.0",
    # S3-kompatibler Objektspeicher für die Dokumentablage (#788); nur geladen, wenn OBJ_ENABLED gesetzt ist

    # Utilities
    "pillow>=10.3.0",  # Security: fixes heap buffer overflow, DoS, eval injection
    # Einzelbilder aus HLS-Übertragungen für die Live-Übertragung (hub/live, #915): FFmpeg als Bibliothek im Wheel

    # Seitenanalyse von PDFs (Karten und Pläne, #599): PDFium, Apache-2.0/BSD-3-Clause – bewusst nicht PyMuPDF

[tool.uv]
# Anwendung, kein installierbares Paket: uv sperrt und installiert nur die Abhängigkeiten.
package = false
# Betrieb und Entwicklung laufen auf CPython; ohne diese Einschränkung sperrt uv zusätzlich PyPy-Varianten
# (eigene autobahn-/cbor2-Zweige), die niemand installiert.
environments = ["platform_python_implementation == 'CPython'"]

[tool.uv.sources]
# Lokales Shared-Paket (OParl-Typen) — nur für uv lock/sync; Image und CI installieren ../shared direkt
mandari-oparl = { path = "../shared", editable = true }

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py312"
exclude = [
    "*/migrations/*",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP", "B", "SIM", "C4", "RET"]
ignore = [
    "E501",   # line too long – 111 Altfälle, wird mit der Komponenten-Migration abgebaut (Epic Code-Qualität)
    "E402",   # module import not at top (Django settings pattern)
    "N806",   # non-lowercase variable in function (Django patterns)
]

python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
addopts = "-v --tb=short"

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
plugins = ["mypy_django_plugin.main"]
strict = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
exclude = ["migrations/"]
# Gate mit schrumpfender Allowlist: scripts/mypy_allowlist.py (Module in scripts/mypy_allowlist.txt werden toleriert)

[tool.django-stubs]
django_settings_module = "mandari.settings"

[tool.djlint]
# Template-Linting (Profil Django). Regeln, die der Frontend-Ratchet bzw. spätere Phasen abdecken,
# sind bewusst ausgenommen: H021 Inline-Styles, H023 Entitäten, H014 Leerzeilen, H036 br-Abstände,
# H005/H016/H030 (Seitenkopf-Regeln, treffen Partials fälschlich).
profile = "django"
max_line_length = 120
ignore = "H005,H014,H016,H021,H023,H030,H036"
custom_blocks = "partialdef"
custom_html = "c-[a-z0-9.-]+"
format_css = false
format_js = false
