[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "I",   # isort (déjà activé pré-F — gardé)
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "ANN", # flake8-annotations
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async
    "TID", # flake8-tidy-imports (Phase F : interdit `from . import …`
           # relatifs au-delà du package et bannit certains imports)
]
ignore = [
    "ASYNC240",  # pathlib dans async OK — on est sur asyncio, pas trio/anyio
]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# Interdit les imports relatifs au-delà du package (RÈGLE 1 du CDC §2.2).
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# src/jarvis/interfaces/voice/agent.py (ex-voice_agent.py) contient 13
# __import__("jarvis.capabilities.tools.X") en lambdas (CDC §B.2 anticipation
# des migrations tools). Le namespace allongé fait dépasser E501. Reformatage
# propre prévu en F.1.3 (ruff TID + I).
# E402 : `from jarvis.kernel.paths import PROJECT_ROOT` doit venir après
# `load_dotenv` qui s'exécute au top — résolu en C avec une vraie composition root.
"src/jarvis/interfaces/voice/agent.py" = ["E501", "E402"]
# src/jarvis/app.py : le bloc qui force l'encodage UTF-8 de stdout/stderr DOIT
# s'exécuter avant tout import (sinon une ligne de log non-cp1252 crashe le
# démarrage sous Windows, cf. jarvis.ps1 run). Ce code-avant-imports volontaire
# déclenche E402 sur tous les imports suivants.
"src/jarvis/app.py" = ["E402"]
# scripts/doc_helper/write_overviews.py est un generateur one-shot dont le corps
# est presque entierement de la prose Markdown dans des f-strings : phrases longues
# et lignes de tableau `| ... | ... |`, qu'on ne peut pas couper sans casser le
# rendu du document genere. Les vraies regles (E402, B005, imports) sont
# respectees ; seule la longueur de ligne est exemptee.
"scripts/doc_helper/write_overviews.py" = ["E501"]
# tests/test_settings_consumers.py utilise `Any` dans des Spy classes qui
# capturent des kwargs arbitraires des constructeurs patchés (AsyncOpenAI,
# AsyncAnthropic, httpx.AsyncClient). Typer ces kwargs précisément demanderait
# de répliquer leur signature exacte — inutile pour un test gardien.
"tests/test_settings_consumers.py" = ["ANN401"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.importlinter]
# `root_packages` (pluriel) — `config/` à la racine est un namespace DATA
# (JSON/YAML) avec quelques modules Python loaders historiques. On le déclare
# dans le graphe pour que la RÈGLE 4 puisse interdire son import depuis
# `jarvis.*` — sinon `config` reste hors-graphe et la règle est invisible.
# Cf. F.7 : closure du shim racine survivant à audit_imports + import-linter
# (3e gate fantôme après C8 et B4a).
root_packages = ["jarvis", "config"]

# Le contrat de couches strict (`type = "layers"`) n'exprime pas correctement
# la topologie du projet (cf. CDC §2.2) parce que :
#   - `app.py` et `interfaces/voice/agent.py` doivent tous deux appeler
#     `bootstrap.build()` (2 entry-points = 2 process) ; ils ne sont pas
#     un layer unique au-dessus des autres ;
#   - `app.py` doit importer les routers `interfaces.api.*` pour les
#     monter, mais voice/agent n'a pas besoin de routers ;
#   - les 4 sous-packages L1 (providers, capabilities, analytics, hardware)
#     ne s'importent pas entre eux (RÈGLE 2).
# Solution : 4 contrats `forbidden` qui encodent fidèlement les 3 RÈGLES
# du CDC + la fermeture explicite du shim racine `config/` (RÈGLE 4).
# Le "layering" implicite tombe directement de cette table d'interdictions.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "RÈGLE 1 — Kernel indépendant"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["jarvis.kernel"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "jarvis.engine",
    "jarvis.providers",
    "jarvis.capabilities",
    "jarvis.interfaces",
    "jarvis.app",
    "jarvis.bootstrap",
    "jarvis.analytics",
    "jarvis.hardware",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "RÈGLE 2 — Providers/Capabilities/Analytics/Hardware n'importent que kernel"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "jarvis.providers",
    "jarvis.capabilities",
    "jarvis.analytics",
    "jarvis.hardware",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "jarvis.engine",
    "jarvis.interfaces",
    "jarvis.app",
    "jarvis.bootstrap",
]
# Résidus connus tolérés : tools plugin instanciés par skills utilisateur
# sans DI possible, et un type Agent passé en signature. Voir BACKLOG
# Phase G "fermer RÈGLE 2 strict".
ignore_imports = [
    "jarvis.capabilities.tools.subagent -> jarvis.engine.agent",
    "jarvis.capabilities.tools.subagent -> jarvis.engine.mission.backends.rpc",
    "jarvis.capabilities.tools.subagent -> jarvis.engine.mission.backend_factory",
    "jarvis.capabilities.skills.lab -> jarvis.engine.mission.docker_executor",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "RÈGLE 3 — Engine n'importe que kernel"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["jarvis.engine"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "jarvis.providers",
    "jarvis.capabilities",
    "jarvis.interfaces",
    "jarvis.app",
    "jarvis.bootstrap",
    "jarvis.analytics",
    "jarvis.hardware",
]
# Plugin Fusion 360 instancié à la demande dans worker_agent quand un step
# nomme `fusion_360` — l'import est lazy et annoté `# lazy: plugin`.
ignore_imports = [
    "jarvis.engine.mission.worker_agent -> jarvis.capabilities.tools.fusion",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# Le shim racine `config/` est un namespace DATA — JSON/YAML qui restent à la
# racine du repo (décision Q1). Les loaders Python associés vivent dans
# `jarvis.kernel.*` et lisent les fichiers via `kernel.paths.CONFIG_DIR`
# (absolu). Aucun module sous `jarvis.*` ne doit importer `config.*` :
# le `from config.X import …` est l'ancien namespace pré-B.3 qui a survécu
# trois gates (audit_imports lazy-only, import-linter root_package="jarvis"
# uniquement). B9 cold-install l'a attrapé en juin : sur clone neuf, le
# wheel n'embarque que `src/jarvis/` et l'app ne boote pas. F.7 ferme.
name = "RÈGLE 4 — Aucun module sous jarvis.* n'importe le shim racine `config/`"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "jarvis.kernel",
    "jarvis.providers",
    "jarvis.capabilities",
    "jarvis.analytics",
    "jarvis.hardware",
    "jarvis.engine",
    "jarvis.interfaces",
    "jarvis.app",
    "jarvis.bootstrap",
]
forbidden_modules = ["config"]

[tool.mypy]
# Scope strict : kernel + test de conformité des Protocols (CDC §F.1.3bis).
# Le reste du codebase (46k lignes) reste à typer en chantier séparé.
files = [
    "src/jarvis/kernel",
    "tests/unit/kernel/test_contracts_conformance.py",
]
python_version = "3.11"
strict_optional = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false
no_implicit_optional = true
ignore_missing_imports = true

type = layers

    datarax.pipeline.pipeline
    datarax.pipeline.host_stage | datarax.pipeline.iteration | datarax.pipeline.materialization
    datarax.pipeline.run_configuration | datarax.pipeline.run_units
    datarax.pipeline.epochs | datarax.pipeline.dag_call | datarax.pipeline.read_plan | datarax.pipeline.placement
    datarax.pipeline.host_workers

[importlinter:contract:tfds-sources]

    datarax.sources.tfds_streaming_source

    datarax.sources._tfrecord

[importlinter:contract:decoded-copy]

    _files
    _units
    _layout

[importlinter:contract:disk-sources]

type = layers
layers =
    datarax.sources.decoded_copy
    datarax.sources.streaming_disk_source
    datarax.sources._disk_provenance

description = "Differentiable data pipelines for JAX/Flax NNX: HuggingFace, TFDS and ArrayRecord sources, augmentation stages, scan-based epochs, exact mid-epoch resume"

name = "datarax"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Platform-specific installation:
# - Linux with GPU: pip install datarax[all]
# - macOS (Apple Silicon): pip install datarax[all-macos]
# - macOS/Linux CPU-only: pip install datarax[all-cpu]
all = ["datarax[cuda12,data,dev,docs,test,wandb]"]
all-cpu = ["datarax[data,dev,docs,test,wandb]"]
all-macos = ["datarax[data,dev,docs,metal,test,wandb]"]
automation = [
  # Local cloud orchestration dependencies (benchmarks/automation/vast_orchestrator.py)
  "skypilot[vast]>=0.11,<0.12",
  "click<8.3", # SkyPilot 0.11.x launch incompatibility with click>=8.3
  # vastai-sdk 1.0+ removed VastAI.api_key_access which sky/adaptors/vast.py
  # uses for credential validation; pin to the 0.2.x line until SkyPilot
  # 0.12 upgrades its adapter. Bounce the SkyPilot API daemon
  # (`sky api stop`) after upgrading these so the new adapter is loaded.
  # The 0.2.x line pins aiohttp==3.10.1 (35 open advisories); every 1.x release
  # of the underlying `vastai` package pins cryptography==49.0.0 instead, which the
  # cryptography>=50 constraint below refuses, so neither line is clean.
  "vastai-sdk>=0.2.6,<0.3",
  # Required by benchmarks.export when the orchestrator's --analyze step
  # imports benchmarks.cli locally (the remote VM gets matplotlib via the
  # benchmark extra; the local box only installs `automation`).
  "matplotlib>=3.8"
]
# benchmark extra is separate — it pulls in 12 Linux-only frameworks (DALI, PyTorch, Ray, etc.)
# Install explicitly: pip install datarax[benchmark]
benchmark = [
  # Peer frameworks for comparative benchmarking (Section 14.2 of benchmark report)
  # Tier 1: JAX ecosystem (Grain already in base deps)
  "jax-dataloader>=0.1", # jax-dataloader — minimal JAX-native loader
  "tensorflow-datasets>=4.9.10", # tf.data adapter; CIFAR-10 is read through TFDSEagerSource
  "protobuf>=6.31.1", # tensorflow-metadata 1.21 is generated for 6.31.1; protobuf 5 fails its import
  # Tier 2: High-performance leaders
  "nvidia-dali-cuda120>=1.0; sys_platform == 'linux'", # NVIDIA DALI — GPU-native data loading + augmentation (Linux/CUDA only)
  "spdl>=0.1", # Meta SPDL — thread-based data loading
  "torch>=2.0,<2.11", # PyTorch DataLoader baseline (<2.11 for CUDA 12 wheels; 2.11+ pulls libcudart.so.13)
  "torchvision>=0.15,<0.26", # torchvision transforms + batch JPEG decode (paired with torch <2.11)
  "torchaudio>=2.0,<2.11", # paired with torch (avoid the 2.11 CUDA-13 transitive dep)
  # Tier 2: Cloud/streaming
  "mosaicml-streaming>=0.7", # MosaicML StreamingDataset — MDS format
  "webdataset>=0.2", # WebDataset — TAR-based streaming
  # Tier 3: Specialized
  "litdata>=0.2", # Lightning LitData — cloud streaming
  "ray[data]>=2.9", # Ray Data — distributed actor-based
  "datasets>=2.21", # Hugging Face Datasets (>=2.21 for pyarrow 15+ compat)
  "pyarrow>=21", # >=21 for pa.json_ (datasets 4+) and macOS-14 arm64 wheel stability
  "deeplake>=4.0", # Deep Lake — AI database
  # Benchmark infrastructure
  "matplotlib>=3.8", # Plotting for benchmark reports
  "tabulate>=0.9", # Table formatting for reports
  "rich>=13.0", # Rich terminal output for benchmark runners
  # benchmarks/cli.py imports click at module level, and the nightly workflow runs it as
  # `from benchmarks.cli import main`. click was declared only under `automation`, which
  # was harmless while the nightly installed every extra and load-bearing the moment
  # automation became a conflicting extra. It stays in `automation` as well, pinned <8.3
  # there for SkyPilot, because the orchestrator invokes benchmarks.cli locally; the two
  # declarations never resolve together because the extras conflict by construction.
  "click>=8.1" # benchmarks/cli.py

# Note: FFCV requires system OpenCV (libopencv-dev) — install separately via:

  # Complete CUDA development environment

  "datarax[cuda12,dev]"

  "tensorflow>=2.20.0",
  "tensorflow-datasets>=4.9.10",
  "protobuf>=6.31.1" # tensorflow-metadata 1.21 is generated for 6.31.1; protobuf 5 fails its import

wandb = ["calibrax[wandb]>=0.1.14"]

[tool.bandit]
# Note: bandit excludes tests/scripts/examples because security scanning focuses on
# production code. .pre-commit-config.yaml does NOT exclude these — pre-commit hooks
# (ruff, pyright, formatting) intentionally run on all code including tests.
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "scripts", "examples", "documents", "custom_modes", "notebooks", "example_data"]
# B101: assert_used - Assert statements are the idiomatic way to write pytest tests
# They are safe in test files as pytest rewrites them for better error messages
# B110: try_except_pass - Used intentionally for optional statistics collection
skips = ["B101", "B110"]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"
skip_covered = false
skip_empty = false

[tool.coverage.paths]
source = [
  "src",
  "*/datarax/src"
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
  "pragma: no cover",
  "def __repr__",
  "if self.debug:",
  "if settings.DEBUG",
  "raise AssertionError",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  "if 0:",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
  "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
  "raise ImportError"
]
# Adjusted for large codebase with focused testing approach
fail_under = 80
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
omit = ["*/tests/*", "*/conftest.py", "*/__pycache__/*", "*/scripts/*", "*/examples/*", "*/benchmark/*", "*/example_data/*"]
parallel = true
relative_files = true
source = ["src"]

[tool.coverage.xml]

environment_file = ".datarax.env"

[tool.deptry.package_module_name_map]

[tool.mypy]
# This project uses pyright as its type checker (see [tool.pyright] below).
# mypy is NOT configured and will produce false positives due to JAX/Flax/NNX
# type stubs. Do not use mypy --strict for audit purposes.
follow_imports = "skip"

[tool.pydoclint]
allow-init-docstring = true
arg-type-hints-in-docstring = false
# Instance attributes are documented under Attributes per the Google style; pydoclint would
# compare them with class-level attributes only.
check-class-attributes = false
# Annotations are the source of truth for types; docstrings carry the prose.
check-return-types = false
check-yield-types = false
# `# noqa: DOC...` is read from the def line, where propagated exceptions are annotated.
native-mode-noqa-location = "definition"
skip-checking-short-docstrings = true
style = "google"

[tool.pylint."messages_control"]
# NNX modules require nnx.Variable as direct attrs; config dataclasses map 1:1
# to parameters. Default max-attrs=7 is too restrictive for this domain.
max-args = 10
max-attributes = 12

[tool.pyright]
exclude = ["example_data", ".deprecated", "**/__pycache__", "**/.venv"]
include = ["src", "tests", "examples", "scripts", "benchmarks"]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
# JAX/Flax/NNX ecosystem requires these specific suppressions due to
# dynamic attribute access patterns and type stub limitations.
reportFunctionMemberAccess = false
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = false
# Benchmarks depend on many optional adapters/frameworks that are intentionally
# not required in every dev environment or pre-commit hook env.
reportMissingImports = false
# tensorflow lives in the tfds extra, which setup.sh does not install; pyright checks its uses
# against the stubs it bundles either way, so a stub without a source is information.
reportMissingModuleSource = "information"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
# The checkpoint package was rewritten in 0.1.6 and holds the full standard.
strict = ["src/datarax/checkpoint"]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config --verbose --tb=short --color=yes --durations=10 --cov=src/ --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html --cov-fail-under=80 --timeout=300 --json-report --json-report-file=temp/test-results.json --json-report-indent=2"
cache_dir = ".pytest_cache"
# Additional settings
console_output_style = "progress"
filterwarnings = [
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:pkg_resources.*",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:jax.*",
  "ignore:jax.interpreters.xla.pytype_aval_mappings is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
  "ignore::pytest.PytestCollectionWarning:cannot collect test class 'TestFileAnalysis'",
  "ignore::pytest.PytestCollectionWarning:cannot collect test class 'TestStructureAnalyzer'",
  # CUDA-related warnings (automatically handled by conftest.py)
  "ignore::UserWarning:jax._src.xla_bridge",
  "ignore:.*cuSPARSE.*",
  "ignore:.*CUDA-enabled jaxlib.*",
  # TODO: Fix Orbax checkpoint warnings - need to provide proper sharding info when restoring
  "ignore:Sharding info not provided when restoring.*:UserWarning:orbax.*",
  "ignore:Sharding info not provided when restoring.*:UserWarning",
  # Resource warnings from checkpoint operations (cleanup issues, not functional failures)
  "ignore:unclosed <socket.socket.*:ResourceWarning",
  "ignore:unclosed event loop.*:ResourceWarning",
  # Ignore all ResourceWarnings during testing (they don't affect functionality)
  "ignore::ResourceWarning"
]
log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"
markers = [
  "tfds: marks tests that read the TFDS fixture or prepared datasets (CI long-running job)",
  "hf: marks tests that require huggingface datasets to be installed",
  "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
  "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
  "unit: marks tests as unit tests",
  "benchmark: marks tests as performance benchmarks (requires pytest-benchmark)",
  "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests",
  "performance: marks tests as performance tests",
  "contract: marks tests as contract tests"
]
# Minimum version
minversion = "6.0"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_functions = "test_*"
# Main pytest configuration
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.pytest-benchmark]
compare = ["last", "base"]
disable_gc = true
histogram = "histogram.svg"
min_rounds = 5
min_time = 0.1
save = "benchmark-results"
save_data = true
warmup = true
warmup_iterations = 3

[tool.pytest_env]
# D: prefix = set as default only (don't override existing env vars)
JAX_ENABLE_X64 = {skip_if_set = true, value = "0"}
JAX_SKIP_CUDA_CONSTRAINTS_CHECK = {skip_if_set = true, value = "1"}
# Ray 2.53's uv runtime_env hook detects uv-managed venvs and tries to
# recreate them for workers — but the new venv lacks ray itself, causing
# workers to crash silently and from_numpy()/iter_batches() to hang.
RAY_DATA_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS = "1"
RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV = "0"
TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL = {skip_if_set = true, value = "1"}
XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION = {skip_if_set = true, value = "0.75"}
XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE = {skip_if_set = true, value = "false"}

[tool.ruff]
extend-include = ["*.ipynb"]
line-length = 100
# Only src/ is searched for first-party packages. The default also searches the repository
# root, where a generated directory (wandb/, site/, temp/) would be read as a package and its
# import sorted into the first-party block on the machine that has it and the third-party block
# everywhere else. The root-level packages are named in known-first-party instead.
src = ["src"]
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.format]
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"
quote-style = "double"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint]
# pydoclint's DOC codes appear in `# noqa` comments on def lines.
external = ["DOC"]
# Add W291, W292, W293 to fixable to handle whitespace issues
fixable = ["I001", "F401", "E", "W", "W291", "W292", "W293", "F841"]
ignore = [
  "E402", # Module level import not at top of file
  "E721", # Do not compare types directly
  "E741", # Ambiguous variable name
  "F722", # Forward annotation syntax error
  "W391", # Blank line at end of file
  "E203", # Whitespace before ':'
  # UP035 — fixed: imports now use collections.abc
  "RUF005", # Consider using unpacked tuple instead of concatenation
  # --- Documented exemptions from the adopted rule set ---
  "ANN401", # `Any` is legitimate for JAX pytree leaves and dynamic data payloads
  "TRY003", # inline exception messages are the established, readable style here
  "TRY300", # return-in-`else` restructuring adds no safety to guard-heavy flow
  "TRY004", # state/checkpoint validation intentionally raises ValueError for structural incompatibility
  "PLR2004", # magic-value comparisons pervade numeric/array/scientific code
  "SIM102", # collapsing nested `if`s reduces readability in guard-heavy validation
  "SIM108" # ternary-over-if is not always clearer in these branches
]
# Adopt the shared SWE guide's rule set. C90 (mccabe, max-complexity=10) is active:
# every library function is at or below rank B. ANN401/TRY003/etc. exemptions above.
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "W", "ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "D", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "SIM", "T20", "TRY"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
extra-standard-library = []
known-first-party = ["benchmarks", "datarax", "tests"]
lines-after-imports = 2
order-by-type = false

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Rule 2 (SRP/KISS): cyclomatic complexity ceiling. Functions above this must be
# decomposed; matches the radon rank-B boundary and the xenon --max-absolute B gate.
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"benchmarks/**" = ["ANN", "C90", "D", "T20", "PLR", "B", "SIM", "TRY", "ARG", "RET", "PTH", "E501"]
"examples/**" = ["ANN", "C90", "D", "T20", "PLR", "B", "SIM", "TRY", "ARG", "RET", "PTH", "E501"]
"scripts/**" = ["ANN", "C90", "D", "T20", "PLR", "B", "SIM", "TRY", "ARG", "RET", "PTH", "E501"]
# buffer_sampler's nested jax.lax.cond branch closures have structurally-enforced,
# pyright-inferred return types; per-closure annotations add noise, not safety.
"src/datarax/samplers/buffer_sampler.py" = ["ANN202", "ANN001"]
# Tests, examples, benchmarks, and scripts keep baseline correctness rules
# (E/F/I/W/UP) but are exempt from production-only strictness — examples and
# benchmarks legitimately use print(), and none ship as library API.
"tests/**" = ["ANN", "C90", "D", "PLR", "B", "SIM", "TRY", "ARG", "RET", "PTH"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Datarax exposes configuration-heavy scientific entrypoints. Keep the threshold
# explicit and bounded so PLR0913 remains active for accidental API sprawl.
max-args = 13

[tool.substrax.compute]
backend = "modal"

[tool.substrax.compute.backends.modal]
outputs_volume = "datarax-compute-outputs"

# R53: an NCCL all-reduce on two GPUs after a TFDS read, eager or streamed, with no TensorFlow
# in the process (tests/sources/test_tfds_collective.py). The control runs the same program with TensorFlow
# imported first, which breaks JAX's NCCL collectives.
[tool.substrax.compute.jobs.tfds-nccl]
env = {DATARAX_TEST_JAX_PLATFORMS = "cuda,cpu", DATARAX_TFDS_FIXTURE_DIR = "/tmp/tfds_fixture", NCCL_DEBUG = "WARN"}
extras = ["cuda12", "data", "dev", "test", "tfds"]
resources = {accelerator = {count = 2, kind = "L40S"}, cpu = 8, memory_mib = 32768}
runtime = {platforms = ["cuda"], preallocate = false, xla_flags = ["--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true"]}
task_timeout_seconds = 900
timeout_seconds = 2700

# Tasks run in table order and the table is kept sorted, so their names carry the order.
[tool.substrax.compute.jobs.tfds-nccl.commands]
1-fixture = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_fixture", "/tmp/tfds_fixture"]
2-program = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_collective", "/tmp/tfds_fixture"]
3-stream-program = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_collective", "/tmp/tfds_fixture", "--stream"]
4-collective = ["python", "-m", "pytest", "tests/sources/test_tfds_collective.py", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", "--no-cov", "-rs", "-v"]
5-control = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_collective", "/tmp/tfds_fixture", "--import-tensorflow"]
6-stream-control = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_collective", "/tmp/tfds_fixture", "--stream", "--import-tensorflow"]

[tool.uv]
# The automation extra is benchmark tooling: skypilot[vast] and vastai-sdk, used only
# by benchmarks/automation/ and imported nowhere under src/. vastai-sdk pins
# aiohttp==3.10.1 exactly and the extra pins click<8.3. uv resolves ONE universal
# lockfile across every extra, so those two pins governed the aiohttp and click that
# ordinary installs and CI received, putting 37 advisories into an audit of
# .[dev,test,data], which does not include automation at all.
# Declaring the conflict lets uv fork the resolution: automation keeps aiohttp 3.10.1
# and click 8.1.8, everything else gets 3.14.3 and 8.5.0.
conflicts = [
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "benchmark"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "cuda-dev"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "tfds"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "data"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "dev"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "docs"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "examples"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "cuda12"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "metal"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "test"}]
]
# Floors for transitively-reached packages carrying advisories, raised here because no
# direct dependency declares them. Same mechanism the sibling repositories use.
constraint-dependencies = [
  "cryptography>=50" # PYSEC-2026-3552, PKCS#7 EnvelopedData decryption oracle
]
python-preference = "only-managed"

# Configure for GPU package installation
[tool.uv.pip]
find-links = ["https://storage.googleapis.com/jax-releases/jax_cuda_releases.html"]

typing = [
    "celery-types==0.23.0",
    "mypy",
    "pandas-stubs>=2.3.0.250703",
    "numpy-typing>=1.1.1",
]
tools = ["mypy-clean-slate", "deptry", "import-linter"]

[tool.mypy]
# disallow_any_unimported = true
# disallow_any_expr = true
# disallow_any_decorated = true
disallow_any_explicit = true
# disallow_any_generics = true
# disallow_subclassing_any = true
strict = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
disable_error_code = "unused-ignore"
exclude = [
    "^mcr_meeting/app/db/migrations(/.*)?$",
    "^notebooks(/.*)?$",
] # MyPy uses regex for exclusion rather than glob patterns

[tool.pydantic-mypy]
init_forbid_extra = true
init_typed = true
warn_required_dynamic_aliases = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# This ignore type check on untyped imported modules.
module = [
    "jiwer",
    "ffmpeg",
    "num2words",
    "pyannote.*",  # pyannote.core / pyannote.metrics, used by the ASR evaluations
    "soundfile",
    "docxtpl.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
# T20:  flake8-print -> No print statements
# I:    isort -> Sorted imports
# G:    flake8-logging-format -> logging format
# UP:   pyupgrade -> PEP approved code conventions
# TID252: flake8-tidy-imports -> No relative imports
extend-select = ["T20", "I", "G", "UP", "TID251", "TID252"]
logger-objects = ["loguru.logger"]

ignore = ["UP017", "UP008", "UP028", "UP046"]

exclude = ["scripts/**", "notebooks/**"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"logging".msg = "Use loguru instead of stdlib logging"
"requests".msg = "Use httpx instead of requests"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
env_override_existing_values = 1
env_files = ["../.env.local.docker", "../.env", "../.env.local.testing"]
markers = [
    "integration: exercises a live external dependency; skips when unreachable",
]

[tool.deptry]
extend_exclude = ["scripts/**", "notebooks/**"]

[tool.deptry.package_module_name_map]
"ffmpeg-python" = ["ffmpeg"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter — enforce the target architecture from CLAUDE.md.
#
#   1. `layers` (closed-by-default) encodes the vertical call chain: nothing below
#      use_cases may import api or use_cases.
#   2. `domain` is I/O-less — it may not (directly) import db/infrastructure or any
#      legacy layer. (Kept as a `forbidden` contract rather than `|`-independent layers
#      because the ORM models import `db.db`, so every layer reaches db *indirectly*
#      and layers contracts have no direct-only mode.)
#   3. use-cases must not import each other (share via use_cases._shared).
#   4. use-cases must not reach into the legacy layers.
#
# `ignore_imports` lists the KNOWN legacy edges still to migrate — the debt ledger.
# It only shrinks: unmatched ignores raise an error, so removing an edge forces
# removing its entry. `models` / `schemas` / `exceptions` are the shared kernel and
# are left out of the layering.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "mcr_meeting"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Call chain: api > use_cases > {domain, db, infrastructure}"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "mcr_meeting.app.api",
    "mcr_meeting.app.use_cases",
    "mcr_meeting.app.domain : mcr_meeting.app.db : mcr_meeting.app.infrastructure",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "domain is I/O-less (no db/infrastructure/legacy)"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = true
source_modules = ["mcr_meeting.app.domain"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "mcr_meeting.app.db",
    "mcr_meeting.app.infrastructure",
    "mcr_meeting.app.services",
    "mcr_meeting.app.client",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Use-cases must not import each other"
type = "independence"
modules = ["mcr_meeting.app.use_cases.*"]
# Shared business operations live in use_cases._shared and may be imported by
# any use-case (see CLAUDE.md). Independence still holds between use-cases.
ignore_imports = [
    "mcr_meeting.app.use_cases.* -> mcr_meeting.app.use_cases._shared.**",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Use-cases must not depend on legacy services/client"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = true
source_modules = ["mcr_meeting.app.use_cases"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "mcr_meeting.app.services",
    "mcr_meeting.app.client",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]

# (see docs/plans/lint-hardening.md). RUF carries the ruff-specific rules,
# including RUF100 (unused `# noqa`) which keeps suppressions honest.
select = [
    "E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP", "B", "SIM", "S", "RUF",
    # Part 2 (lint-hardening-part-2): async footguns, logging correctness,
    # banned-api (money ≠ Float), implicit str-concat, f-strings, raise-from,
    # pylint errors, comprehensions, pie, return consistency, private access,
    # perf anti-patterns.
    "ASYNC", "G", "LOG", "TID", "ISC", "FLY", "RSE", "PLE",
    "C4", "PIE", "RET", "SLF", "PERF",
]
ignore = [
    # Prose in two languages uses typographic dashes and quotes on purpose.
    "RUF001",
    "RUF002",
    "RUF003",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
# Money and amounts are stored as Numeric/Decimal (ADR precision 15, scale 2),
# never as binary floats — a Float column silently loses cents. The only
# legitimate float column is a 0..1 similarity score (payee_merge), which keeps
# a documented `# noqa: TID251`.
"sqlalchemy.Float".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not Float (floats lose cents). A genuine non-money float (e.g. a 0..1 score) needs an explicit noqa."
"sqlalchemy.REAL".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not REAL."
"sqlalchemy.Double".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not Double."
"sqlalchemy.FLOAT".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not FLOAT."
"sqlalchemy.types.Float".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not Float."
"sqlalchemy.types.FLOAT".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not FLOAT."
"sqlalchemy.types.REAL".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not REAL."
"sqlalchemy.types.Double".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not Double."
"sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.FLOAT".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not FLOAT."
"sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.REAL".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not REAL."
"sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.DOUBLE_PRECISION".msg = "Amounts must be Numeric/Decimal, not DOUBLE_PRECISION."

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# FastAPI uses Depends/Query in argument defaults — B008 is a false positive there.
"src/kaleta/api/**" = ["B008"]
# main.py pins NICEGUI_STORAGE_PATH with stdlib before importing nicegui.
"src/kaleta/main.py" = ["E402"]
# Demo data is not a security boundary: `random` is the right generator here.
"src/kaleta/seeders/**" = ["S311"]
# Tests assert, use fixture passwords, spawn the app under test and bind
# 0.0.0.0 for the e2e server — none of which is production code. Tests also

# Operator scripts: demo password, subprocess calls, benchmark randomness.
"scripts/**" = ["S105", "S310", "S311", "S603", "S607"]

# Deliberately NOT enabled here (deferred to their own chore): `warn_unreachable`,
# `truthy-bool` and `redundant-expr`. On this codebase they almost only surface
# the "declared non-optional but runtime-optional" gap — SQLAlchemy relationships

package dev.upaya.shf

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.junit.Test
import java.time.OffsetDateTime
import java.time.ZonedDateTime


class DateArchTest {

    @Test
    fun `OffsetDateTime only be used for database`() {
        val importedClasses = ClassFileImporter().importPackages("dev.upaya.shf");

        val myRule: ArchRule = noClasses()
            .that()
                .resideOutsideOfPackage("dev.upaya.shf.data.session_data.datastore..")
            .should()
                .accessClassesThat()
                .haveFullyQualifiedName(OffsetDateTime::class.java.name)
            .orShould()
                .accessClassesThat()
                .haveFullyQualifiedName(ZonedDateTime::class.java.name)
            .because("we only need offsets when storing in database")

        myRule.check(importedClasses);
    }
}

# Public-mirror variant of the root pyproject, pruned to the packages and paths
# that sync.

name = "imbue"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Monorepo for Imbue projects"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    # ty is held at 0.0.39: the later 0.0.x releases report a different set of
    # diagnostics on this tree, including a change in how
    # [tool.ty.environment] extra-paths resolves scripts/. Lift the cap in the
    # change that works through them. MIND-301.
    "ty>=0.0.39,<0.0.40",
    "click>=8.0.0",
]

[tool.uv]
# Supply-chain cooldown: uv ignores any package uploaded after this timestamp
# when resolving, so we only adopt releases public long enough for malware to
# surface. scripts/release.py advances it to 2 weeks before each release, and
# only ever forward. This only buys a detection delay; it can't catch a
# compromise that stays undetected past the window.
exclude-newer = "2026-09-02T00:00:00Z"

[tool.uv.sources]
imbue-common = { workspace = true }
overlay = { workspace = true }

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["libs/*", "apps/*"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pre-commit>=4.2.0",
    "ruff~=0.12.8",
    "pytest>=9.0",
    "pytest-cov>=7.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3.0",
    "pytest-split>=0.9.0",
    # really just for debugging slow tests
    "pytest-profiling",
    "line-profiler",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "semver>=3.0",
    "tomlkit>=0.12.0",
    "imbue-common[dev]",
    "shellcheck-py>=0.10.0",
    # In-memory AWS service mocks for unit tests (S3 state-bucket round-trips).
    "moto[s3]>=5.0",
    # Validates the generated /api/schema OpenAPI document in minds tests.
    "openapi-spec-validator>=0.7",
]

# Shared pytest settings (markers, filterwarnings, coverage report config)
# are centralized in:
#   libs/imbue_common/imbue/imbue_common/conftest_hooks.py
# The settings below remain here because they are read from pyproject.toml
# before any hooks run: addopts, coverage.run, inline-snapshot, timeout_func_only.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Only timeout the test function itself, not fixtures. This is required because
# --timeout-method=signal sends SIGALRM which kills the entire xdist worker process
# if it fires during fixture setup/teardown (especially the session-scoped cleanup).
timeout_func_only = true
# Use xunit1 format to enable record_xml_attribute fixture for consistent classnames
junit_family = "xunit1"
pythonpath = [
  "apps/*",
  "libs/*",
]
testpaths = [
  "test_meta_ratchets.py",
  "apps/*",
  "libs/*",
  "scripts",
]
addopts = [
  "--cov=imbue.mngr",
  "--cov=imbue.imbue_common",
  "--cov=imbue.resource_guards",
  "--cov=imbue.overlay",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_claude",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_autocompact",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_opencode",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_antigravity",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_codex",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_pi_coding",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_pair",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_schedule",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_ttyd",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_tutor",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_kanpan",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_usage",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_claude_usage",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_opencode_usage",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_pi_coding_usage",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_codex_usage",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_recursive",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_latchkey",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_notifications",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_file",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_forward",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_imbue_cloud",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_docker",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_lima",
  "--cov=imbue.skitwright",
  "--cov=imbue.minds",
  "--cov=imbue.concurrency_group",
  "--cov=imbue.modal_proxy",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_wait",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_robinhood",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_vps",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_vultr",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_aws",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_ovh",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_gcp",
  "--cov=imbue.mngr_azure",
  # NOTE: no --cov-report/--coverage-to-file here. Per-run coverage reports
  # are expensive to generate (they walk every measured file) and are only
  # useful interactively, so the local recipes that want them
  # (just test-unit / test-integration) pass those flags explicitly. Keeping
  # them out of addopts lets offload CI batches disable them entirely with
  # `--cov-report=` (pytest-cov only treats the empty value as "clear all
  # reports" when it is the sole --cov-report given) while still writing the
  # raw .coverage data file that CI combines for the coverage gates.
  "--durations=20",
  "--timeout=10",

]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["imbue"]
parallel = true
concurrency = ["multiprocessing", "thread"]
# sys.monitoring (PEP 669) is ~3x lower overhead than the default C tracer on
# Python 3.12, which matters for import-heavy workloads (pytest collection
# and short-lived batch processes are dominated by module imports). Requires
# Python >= 3.12 and is incompatible with branch coverage, dynamic contexts,
# and greenlet/eventlet/gevent concurrency -- none of which we use. On older
# Pythons coverage warns and falls back to the default core.
core = "sysmon"
omit = [
    "*_test.py",
    "test_*.py",
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/conftest.py",
    # Test utility modules contain helpers only used by tests
    "*/testing.py",
    "*/utils/plugin_testing.py",
    "*/conftest_hooks.py",
    "*/ratchet_testing/*",
    # Shared Sentry error-reporting machinery is mostly runtime integration glue
    # (live sentry_sdk wiring, the custom HTTP transport's network paths, the
    # threaded S3 uploader); its pure logic is unit-tested and the whole thing is
    # exercised end-to-end by the processes that call setup_sentry.
    "*/imbue_common/sentry/*",
    # Modal provider plugin requires network access for testing
    "libs/mngr_modal/imbue/mngr_modal/*",
    # Docker provider requires a Docker daemon for testing
    "libs/mngr_docker/imbue/mngr_docker/instance.py",
    "libs/mngr_docker/imbue/mngr_docker/volume.py",
    "libs/mngr_docker/imbue/mngr_docker/leaked_container_sweep.py",
    # Lima provider requires Lima/QEMU for full integration testing
    "libs/mngr_lima/imbue/mngr_lima/instance.py",
    "libs/mngr_lima/imbue/mngr_lima/limactl.py",
    # Mind deploy modules run on Modal and require infrastructure to test
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/deploy/cron_runner.py",
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/deploy/remote_runner.py",
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/deploy/verification.py",
    # Minds telegram/supertokens integrations require external services to test
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/telegram/credential_extractor.py",
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/telegram/bot_creator.py",
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/telegram/injector.py",
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/desktop_client/supertokens_routes.py",
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/desktop_client/tunnel_token_injection.py",
    # Minds Docker state-container teardown shells out to the `docker` CLI and
    # needs a real daemon -- exercised via a docker-marked test, not offload.
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/envs/docker_cleanup.py",
    # Minds deployment_tests importable helpers are exercised only by the
    # minds_deployment / minds_services pytest suites against real cloud,
    # which are excluded from `just test-offload`. No path through the
    # standard test run reaches these files.
    "apps/minds/imbue/minds/deployment_tests/*",
    # mngr_claude keychain sync requires a real macOS keychain to test
    "libs/mngr_claude/imbue/mngr_claude/resources/sync_keychain_credentials.py",

    "libs/mngr_schedule/imbue/mngr_schedule/implementations/modal/verification.py",
    # don't bother with anything in scripts
    "scripts/*",
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clean-architecture layering enforcement (Phase 0 #C2 / SAD §13.2).
#
# Layers (innermost first):
#   1. domain:         pure entities, value objects, repository interfaces
#   2. application:    use cases; depends on domain only
#   3. infrastructure: SQLAlchemy models, mappers, concrete repos
#   4. api:            FastAPI routes/schemas; orchestrates application layer
#
# Allowed: outer → inner. Forbidden: inner → outer.
# `core` and `shared` are leaf utilities: no inbound restrictions in v1.
#
# Run: `uv run lint-imports`
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "app"
include_external_packages = false

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain is pure"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.domain"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "app.application",
    "app.infrastructure",
    "app.api",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Application depends only on domain (and core/shared utilities)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.application"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "app.infrastructure",
    "app.api",
]
# Tech debt: to remove in Phase 1 (lifecycle collapse) when the
# password-set-token use case is restructured to depend on a domain repository
# interface, with the concrete implementation injected from infrastructure.
ignore_imports = [
    "app.application.use_cases.tenant_use_cases -> app.infrastructure.repositories.password_set_token_repository",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "API routes do not import infrastructure directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.api.routes"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "app.infrastructure",
]
# `app.api.dependencies` is the FastAPI composition root: by design it wires
# infrastructure repositories into routes via Depends(...). The transitive
# edge routes -> dependencies -> infrastructure is the intended pattern.
# The grandfathered direct edges below are existing tech debt; remove them in
# Phase 1 (entity boilerplate + lifecycle collapse) and Phase 2 alongside the
# new entity work. Adding *new* direct edges must fail CI.

package org.redbee.archunit

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures

private const val ADAPTERS = "Adapters"
private const val APPLICATION = "Application"
private const val USECASE = "UseCase"
private const val PORT_IN = "Port In"
private const val SHARED = "Shared"

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = ["org.redbee"], importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class LayeredArchitectureTest {

    @ArchTest
    val layer_dependencies_are_respected: ArchRule = Architectures.layeredArchitecture()
        .layer(ADAPTERS).definedBy("org.redbee.adapter..")
        .layer(APPLICATION).definedBy("org.redbee.application..")
        .layer(USECASE).definedBy("org.redbee.application.usecase")
        .layer(PORT_IN).definedBy("org.redbee.application.port.in")
        .layer(SHARED).definedBy("org.redbee.shared..")
        .whereLayer(APPLICATION).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(ADAPTERS, SHARED)
        .whereLayer(ADAPTERS).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(USECASE, SHARED)
        .whereLayer(USECASE).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(PORT_IN, SHARED)
}

# ── Hinweise ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Für Multi-App-Repos: Jede App als eigenes Layer eintragen
# Exceptions mit ignore_imports statt Regeln aufweichen
# Bei False Positives: --debug für Details

/**
 * The pass order, as the places a module can sit in, earliest first (#1443).
 *
 * `docs/architecture/README.md` §1: at run time a pass takes only the artifact
 * the pass just before it returned (#1991), and "a module may import code or
 * types from a lower-numbered pass in its own layer, or from any earlier
 * layer, and nothing else." This file enforces the second half: which
 * modules may import which. `src/cli/__tests__/PassChain.test.ts` checks
 * the first. So each place below may reach every place before
 * it and none after
 * it, and one rule per place says so. The rules are generated from this list
 * rather than written out because the order is ONE fact: written as pairs it
 * was eight hand-authored rules, each naming one later root, and a pair nobody
 * wrote -- 1.1 reading 1.2, PARSE reading WRITE -- was simply allowed.
 *
 * Two places are not passes. `TranspileState` (with the `ICodeGenApi` slot it
 * holds) is the per-file working state 2.2 and 2.3 both write, so it sits
 * after 2.1 -- an analyzer reaching it read whatever the previous file or RUN
 * left there, which is how #1430 suppressed E0427 and #1432 let a signed
 * subscript reach generated C at exit 0 (#1456) -- and before 2.2. And
 * `CodeGenWalker` drives 2.2 and 2.3 for one file, so it sits after 2.3. Both
 * are directly under `TRANSPILE/` by the owner's ruling on #1443, which
 * README §1 records.
 *
 * One edge into a later place is ruled, and `mayRead` names it. 1.1 lexes a
 * `.cnx` file to find its includes with 1.2's `CNextLexer`, so it and the
 * parser agree on what a comment hides (#1745, owner ruling 2026-09-30,
 * option A: discovery decides which files get parsed, so no `ParsedFile`
 * exists yet when it asks). The lexer only: the parser stays forbidden, and
 * `scripts/__tests__/pass-order.test.ts` checks both.
 *
 * Each rule is `reachable: true`: a layer boundary is a claim about what a
 * module can END UP depending on, not about who wrote the import (#1297,
 * asserted by `scripts/__tests__/layer-rules.test.ts`). `__tests__` is
 * excluded: a test that runs two passes -- which is what the pipeline does --
 * must name both.
 *
 * They replace `parse-cannot-import-render`, `parse-cannot-import-transpile`,
 * `declare-cannot-import-resolve`, `analyze-cannot-import-plan`,
 * `analyze-cannot-import-render`, `analyzers-cannot-reach-codegen-state`,
 * `plan-cannot-import-render` and `state-cannot-import-output`, each of which
 * forbade one later place this list now forbids with all the others.
 */
const PASS_ORDER = [
  {
    rule: "1-1-discover",
    path: "^src/cnx/PARSE/1-Discover/",
    mayRead: "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/grammar/CNextLexer\\.ts$",
  },
  { rule: "1-2-parse", path: "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/" },
  { rule: "1-3-declare", path: "^src/cnx/PARSE/3-Declare/" },
  { rule: "1-4-resolve", path: "^src/cnx/PARSE/4-Resolve/" },
  { rule: "2-1-analyze", path: "^src/cnx/TRANSPILE/1-Analyze/" },
  {
    rule: "transpile-state",
    path: "^src/cnx/TRANSPILE/(TranspileState\\.ts$|types/)",
  },
  { rule: "2-2-plan", path: "^src/cnx/TRANSPILE/2-Plan/" },
  { rule: "2-3-render", path: "^src/cnx/TRANSPILE/3-Render/" },
  { rule: "codegen-walker", path: "^src/cnx/TRANSPILE/CodeGenWalker\\.ts$" },
  { rule: "3-1-write", path: "^src/cnx/WRITE/1-Write/" },
];

const passOrderRules = PASS_ORDER.slice(0, -1).map((place, index) => ({
  name: `${place.rule}-reads-no-later-pass`,
  comment:
    `${place.path} may reach only the places before it in PASS_ORDER. ` +
    "See the comment on PASS_ORDER.",
  severity: "error",
  from: { path: place.path, pathNot: "__tests__" },
  to: {
    path: PASS_ORDER.slice(index + 1).map((later) => later.path),
    ...(place.mayRead === undefined ? {} : { pathNot: place.mayRead }),
    reachable: true,
  },
}));

/**
 * What counts as holding a parse tree -- the one definition, read by both
 * `parse-tree-sites` (the inventory) and `parse-tree-confined-to-parser` (the
 * ruling, #1932).
 */
const PARSE_TREE_TYPES = [
  "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/.*grammar/",
  "node_modules/antlr4ng/",
  // The sanctioned carriers. `IParsedFile` is documented as the way a
  // pass takes the tree "instead of re-parsing", and `IParsedFile["tree"]`
  // IS `ProgramContext` -- so a module reaches the tree through this hop
  // while naming neither the grammar nor the runtime, and the count stays
  // flat as the coupling grows. Measured: a probe in `state/` holding
  // `IParsedFile["tree"]` left the gate at 141 and exit 0, while the same
  // probe spelled `ParserRuleContext` failed loudly. The guard was
  // catching the honest spelling and missing the recommended one.
  // #1445 box 2 removed `IDeclaredFile` from this alternation with the
  // type itself. It was 1.3's apparent artifact and held
  // `parsed: IParsedFile`, so importing it reached the tree in one hop
  // -- exactly what naming the carriers here was for. Its `symbols`
  // half had no reader, so it was a bundle whose only live content was
  // the re-export.
  "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/types/IParsedFile\\.ts$",
  // #1957: the 1.2 parser that RETURNS a tree. A module calling it holds the
  // tree as a value -- `CNextSourceParser.parse(src).tree` -- while naming no
  // grammar type, so without this it was counted by neither rule. #1991:
  // `HeaderParser` left the list when it began returning lowered syntax.
  "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/CNextSourceParser\\.ts$",
];

/**
 * #1932 box 2: the shared helpers that hold a parse tree. Each is allowed only
 * because every caller is 1.2 Parse, so each is also a `to` of
 * `parse-tree-confined-to-parser`: a later pass importing one fails exactly as
 * if it had imported the grammar. #1991: `OverflowBehaviorUtils` left the list
 * when it stopped taking a parse context.
 */
const PARSE_TREE_HELPERS = ["^src/cnx/utils/ParserUtils\\.ts$"];

/** @type {import('dependency-cruiser').IConfiguration} */
module.exports = {
  forbidden: [
    ...passOrderRules,
    {
      name: "collectors-build-names-from-scopes",
      comment:
        "#1285/#1357: qualified names are built from a scope REFERENCE, through " +
        "ScopeUtils, never from a scope NAME string. Four collectors used to " +
        "flatten `scope.name` and join one level, which is correct only while " +
        "the grammar admits no nested scopes -- a coincidence, not a decision. " +
        "Importing QualifiedCName here is how that comes back, so it fails the " +
        "build rather than review. " +
        "#1357 widened this from the collectors seam to every directory that " +
        "measurably needs nothing from QualifiedCName: parser, preprocessor and " +
        "data, 42 files against the original 7. It stops there because an " +
        "import-level rule is all-or-nothing, and codegen and analysis " +
        "legitimately decode names (split, isQualified, toCppQualified) and " +
        "build whole paths (fromParts). What THEY must not do is a call SHAPE, " +
        "not an import, so it is gated by `npm run scope-joins:check` against " +
        "docs/architecture/scope-join-sites.md instead.",
      severity: "error",
      from: {
        path: [
          "^src/cnx/PARSE/3-Declare/cnext/collectors/",
          "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/",
          "^src/cnx/PARSE/1-Discover/",
        ],
      },
      to: {
        path: "^src/cnx/utils/QualifiedCName\\.ts$",
      },
    },

    // ==========================================================================
    // General Best Practices
    // ==========================================================================

    {
      name: "nothing-after-1-1-discovers",
      comment:
        "#1444 box 4. §1: 'After 1.1, nothing may discover a file.' No pass " +
        "after 1.1 Discover reaches one of its modules, except the types of " +
        "its artifact (`types/`): a later pass may read an earlier pass's " +
        "artifact, and running its primitives again is the re-discovery " +
        "#1435 and #1672 removed. The host roots (`cli/`, `lib/`) construct " +
        "the port and the run, and are not passes. `reachable` because a " +
        "helper is as good a route as a direct import: at `b000ecdd8` all 35 " +
        "violations came from 5 direct edges, 2.1 and render reaching " +
        "discovery's text and classification helpers.",
      severity: "error",
      from: {
        path: "^src/cnx/(PARSE/[234]-|TRANSPILE/|WRITE/)",
        pathNot: "__tests__",
      },
      to: {
        path: "^src/cnx/PARSE/1-Discover/",
        pathNot: "^src/cnx/PARSE/1-Discover/types/",
        reachable: true,
      },
    },
    {
      name: "header-language-is-judged-once",
      comment:
        "#1844. A header's language is judged once, on the text a C compile " +
        "meets. It was judged in Stage 2 instead, on the raw text when warm " +
        "and the preprocessed text when cold, so a run passed cold and failed " +
        "warm (#1851). Since #1713 that text is the compile of the run's " +
        "target, so 1.2 judges it, once 1.2 has chosen the target (owner " +
        "ruling 2026-10-16). Only `HeaderSources` runs the language checks.",
      severity: "error",
      from: {
        pathNot: [
          "__tests__",
          "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/HeaderSources\\.ts$",
          "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/detect(Cpp|Assembly)Syntax\\.ts$",
        ],
      },
      to: {
        path: "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/detect(Cpp|Assembly)Syntax\\.ts$",
      },
    },
    {
      name: "header-sources-are-settled-once",
      comment:
        "#1844 review. `header-language-is-judged-once` lets `HeaderSources` " +

        "`HeaderSources.settle` would judge every header a second time, on " +
        "text of its own choosing, and the rule would pass. Only 1.2's " +

      severity: "error",
      from: {
        pathNot: [
          "__tests__",
          "^src/cnx/PARSE/2-Parse/(HeaderReading|HeaderSources)\\.ts$",
        ],
      },

      },
    },

      name: "artifact-types-name-no-discovery-module",
      comment:

      severity: "error",
      from: {

        pathNot: [
          "__tests__",
          "^src/cnx/PARSE/1-Discover/types/IRunAnchor\\.ts$",
        ],
      },

        pathNot: "^src/cnx/PARSE/1-Discover/types/",
        reachable: true,

      name: "nothing-after-resolve-derives-cross-file-facts",
      comment:
        "#1447's definition of done. `docs/architecture/README.md`: \"After 1.4, " +

        'from Program, which is complete before 2.1 begins." ' +
        "Stated as an import rule, that is: a pass after 1.4 may depend on the " +
        "TYPE `IProgram` -- which lives in `src/cnx/types/`, reachable by " +
        "every layer -- and never on `4-Resolve/` itself. Importing the builder " +
        "or a deriver is how a later pass recomputes what 1.4 authored, which " +
        "is the failure the ownership rule exists to prevent, and it is exactly " +
        "the shape the `externalScopeTypes` seed had before #1472. " +
        "`reachable` because re-derivation arrives through a helper as easily " +
        "as directly (#1297).",
      severity: "error",
      from: {

        // main, and `^src/transpiler/output/` a second. Both are gone rather

        // this comment said while the arm above it did exactly that (#1589
        // review).

        pathNot: "__tests__",

      to: { path: "^src/cnx/PARSE/4-Resolve/", reachable: true },
    },

      severity: "error",
      from: {

      },
      to: {
        path: "^src/cnx/PARSE/4-Resolve/DeferredTypes\\.ts$",
      },
    },
    {
      name: "shared-contracts-cannot-import-a-pass",
      comment:

        "this file both call the " +
        "place EVERY layer may depend on, and until now that was prose with " +
        "nothing behind it. A contract that imports a pass root drags the pass " +
        "into every layer that names the contract -- transitively and " +
        "invisibly, because the importer names only the type. " +
        "#1452 broke it twice: `IAssignmentContext` gained a " +

    // narrow it again later.

    // would have silently taken 63 modules out of every rule at once (#1297 one
    // level up), and `TRANSPILE` had to be spelled out because the filesystem is
    // case-sensitive. Cruising everything cannot acquire either failure.
  },

# --- Contract 1: dependency direction ---
# Each layer may import any layer strictly below it. Same-layer siblings
# (grouped with `|`) may not import each other. `orchestration` sits above
# everything -- it's the one documented exception to "apps never import
# each other" (see the allocations<->timetable problem in the modular
# monolith plan), and nothing is allowed to import it back.

type = layers
# identity.admin registers a StudentSubjectEnrollmentInline on StudentExtraAdmin
# (Django admin inlines require a real model class, not a DTO) -- an upward
# read from the foundation layer, same class of "presentation layer needs a
# real model instance" exception already granted to services.py call sites
# elsewhere in this file. Tracked, not a design change: the inline belongs
# conceptually to students, but Django's admin API ties it to the parent
# model's ModelAdmin, which lives with StudentExtra in identity.
# apps.finance.views -> orchestration.tasks: finance's invoice-generation endpoint dispatches

    apps.identity.admin -> apps.students.models
    apps.finance.views -> orchestration.tasks

    apps.analytics

    apps.allocations | apps.staff | apps.attendance | apps.assignments | apps.messaging | apps.finance
    apps.students
    apps.academics
    apps.identity
    apps.core | apps.content

# The facade is the layer below presentation. A facade that imports its product's presentation
# inverts the layering (and drags DRF onto every consumer's import path); a facade that imports
# DRF is presentation in disguise. Only direct imports are checked (allow_indirect_imports is
# forced — without it import-linter rejects the wildcard modules as having shared descendants),
# so DRF reached through an internal module stays green: this enforces the layering norm, not a
# transitive guarantee. See products/architecture.md § Wiring couplings.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "facade must not import presentation or DRF"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["products.*.backend.facade"]

]

[tool.ty.rules]
# Import resolution - ty can't always find all modules/stubs
unresolved-import = "ignore"

# Django-related rules - ty doesn't support Django's metaprogramming yet
# See: https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/291
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"  # Django model fields, relationships, auto-generated attributes
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"  # Django querysets, managers, form fields
unknown-argument = "ignore"  # Django kwargs, queryset filters, manager methods
invalid-base = "ignore"  # Django model metaclasses (e.g., models.Model)
missing-argument = "ignore"  # Django auto-generated __init__, managers
too-many-positional-arguments = "ignore"  # Django metaprogramming signatures

# Dual mypy+ty — mypy still runs, so its artifacts are legitimate
redundant-cast = "ignore"  # casts needed by mypy that ty resolves
unused-type-ignore-comment = "ignore"  # type: ignore comments required by mypy
unused-ignore-comment = "error"  # default is warn, which does not fail CI; error keeps stale ty: ignore directives out

# Django lazy imports and settings indirection
possibly-missing-submodule = "ignore"

# DRF serializer pattern — validate/update/create overrides are idiomatic
invalid-method-override = "ignore"
invalid-attribute-override = "ignore"  # Django manager/field overrides (e.g. `objects`)

# Conditional base classes (e.g. EnterpriseEventQuery | EventQuery pattern)
unsupported-base = "ignore"

# Protobuf generated code + Django lazy references
unresolved-reference = "ignore"

# Third-party library overload stubs (Anthropic SDK, Django, re, etc.)
no-matching-overload = "ignore"

# Framework metaclass magic — ty can't resolve dynamic callables
call-top-callable = "ignore"
call-non-callable = "ignore"

# Django querysets typed as `object` — ty can't narrow through managers
not-iterable = "ignore"

# `in` operator on Django/framework `object` types
unsupported-operator = "ignore"

# Subscript on `object`/`None` from unresolved Django types
not-subscriptable = "ignore"

# mypy already catches deprecations; ty is a fast preflight, not the authority
deprecated = "ignore"

# ty disagrees with mypy on some existing code — baselined, not suppressed.
# These rules catch real bugs in new code, so they stay enabled.
# invalid-type-form is the exception: generated code + ty limitations on valid patterns.
invalid-type-form = "ignore"

include = ["products/replay_vision/backend/tests/test_scanners.py"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
pydantic-discarded-extra-argument = "ignore"

# =============================================================================
# Both contracts are RATCHETS: they freeze the cross-layer imports that exist

# fails CI. Shrink the ignore lists over time; never grow them without an
# architectural decision.
[tool.importlinter]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "pipeline must not import api (frozen exceptions only)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pipeline"]
forbidden_modules = ["api"]
ignore_imports = [
    # Theo/Lyra research runs inside the API container and reuses its
    # service singletons (Qdrant, embeddings, Redis, Discord webhook).
    "pipeline.connectors.cache -> api.cache",

    "pipeline.lyra.handlers.cross_pollination -> api.services.lyra_embeddings",
    "pipeline.lyra.theo_research_index -> api.services.lyra_embeddings",
    # Publish/correct run in the API image and drop its cached research responses.
    "pipeline.lyra.theo_publishing -> api.cache",
    "pipeline.lyra.theo_sources -> api.services.lyra_tools",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "api may only use sanctioned pipeline module families"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["api"]
forbidden_modules = ["pipeline"]
ignore_imports = [
    # Shared DB layer — the one crossing CODE_AUDIT.md D5 always allowed.
    "api.** -> pipeline.database",
    # Sanctioned families (status 2026-08-05): research pipeline runs
    # in-process, renderers/utils/normalizers are shared code.
    "api.** -> pipeline.config",
    "api.** -> pipeline.connectors",
    "api.** -> pipeline.connectors.**",
    "api.** -> pipeline.lyra.**",

    "api.** -> pipeline.news_visibility",
    # IndexNow announcer, called right after publish/unpublish commits
    # (2026-09-17); the orchestrator step lives on the pipeline side.
    "api.** -> pipeline.indexnow",
    # Umami read layer and its pure analysis — both under pipeline/ so the
    # Lyra image (which has no api/ tree) can run the digest.
    "api.** -> pipeline.stats_analysis",

]

# =============================================================================
# Ruff Configuration (Linting & Formatting)
# =============================================================================
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100
exclude = [
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "__pycache__",
    ".git",
    "node_modules",
    "ancient-nerds-map",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "I",    # isort
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",   # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "S",    # flake8-bandit (security)
]
ignore = [
    "E501",   # Line too long (handled by formatter)
    "E402",   # Module level import not at top (needed for load_dotenv pattern)
    "E722",   # Bare except (used intentionally in connector error handling)
    "E741",   # Ambiguous variable name
    "F401",   # Unused imports (managed manually)
    "S101",   # Assert usage (OK in tests)
    "S104",   # Binding to all interfaces
    "S110",   # try-except-pass (intentional in connectors)
    "S112",   # try-except-continue (intentional in connectors)
    "S310",   # Suspicious URL open (we fetch URLs by design)
    "S314",   # Suspicious XML element tree (we parse XML feeds)
    "S324",   # Insecure hash MD5 (used for checksums, not security)
    "S603",   # Subprocess without shell=true
    "S607",   # Start process with partial path
    "S608",   # Hardcoded SQL (intentional in data pipeline)
    "B008",   # Function call in default argument (OK for FastAPI Depends)
    "B023",   # Function uses loop variable (intentional closures)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/*" = ["S101", "S106"]  # Allow asserts + dummy credentials in tests
"scripts/*" = ["S602", "S603", "S607"]  # Allow subprocess in scripts

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["api", "pipeline"]

# =============================================================================
# Pyright Configuration
# =============================================================================
[tool.pyright]
# The remediation census lives under scripts/remediation/ as an importable package
# (`census`) that is loaded by inserting scripts/remediation on sys.path, because a
# dependency installs a top-level package named `scripts` into site-packages which
# shadows this repo's scripts/ directory (see tests/scripts/test_funnel_report.py).
# Without this extraPath the type checker cannot resolve `from census import model`,
# even though the import is correct at runtime. It only widens the search path; it
# does not change which files are checked.
#
# `scripts` is needed as well because tests/remediation/test_wave0_scoping.py imports the
# top-level module `audit_enrich`, which sits directly in scripts/. No CI job type-checks
# scripts/ or tests/ - the gate is `mypy api/` - so this only affects local tooling.
extraPaths = ["scripts/remediation", "scripts"]

# =============================================================================
# Pytest Configuration
# =============================================================================
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
addopts = [
    "-v",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--tb=short",
    # Live-LLM contract tests hit the real MiniMax API (Follow-up-Ticket 3,
    # 2026-08-05) — excluded by default so a normal test run doesn't burn
    # quota or crawl/hang under quota pressure from a concurrent research
    # run. Run them explicitly with `-m live_llm`.
    # (pytest takes the LAST `-m` value when it appears more than once, so a
    # command-line `-m live_llm` overrides this addopts-injected default —
    # no need to edit this file to opt in for one run.)
    "-m",
    "not live_llm",
]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "unit: marks tests as unit tests",
    "live_llm: makes a real call to the MiniMax API — deselected by default, run with -m live_llm",
]

# =============================================================================
# Coverage Configuration
# =============================================================================
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["api", "pipeline"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/migrations/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]
show_missing = true
fail_under = 50  # Start with 50%, increase over time

# Product-owned import-linter config (not synced). Fleet-required settings: docs/quality.md
#
# Inventory (top-level middleware.* portions) — issue #209:
#   middleware.sql_to_arc  — converter (entry, orchestration, mapping, upload)
#   middleware.api_client  — Middleware API client (git dep from advanced_middleware_api)
#   middleware.shared      — ConfigWrapper / shared utilities (git dep)
#
# Intended dependency direction (openspec/principles.md Module Dependency Rules):
#   sql_to_arc → api_client → shared
# Converter may depend on shared and api_client; libs must not depend upward into sql_to_arc.
#
# PEP 420: grimp cannot use ancestors = middleware (namespace). Ancestors / root_packages
# are the installed portions. Do not add a path-mutating middleware/__init__.py (Import policy).

[importlinter]
exclude_type_checking_imports = True

    middleware.sql_to_arc
    middleware.shared
    middleware.api_client

[importlinter:contract:middleware-acyclic-siblings]
name = middleware sibling packages must be acyclic
type = acyclic_siblings
ancestors =
    middleware.sql_to_arc
    middleware.shared
    middleware.api_client

[importlinter:contract:sql-to-arc-layers]
name = sql_to_arc may depend on api_client and shared; libs must not depend upward
type = layers
layers =
    middleware.sql_to_arc
    middleware.api_client
    middleware.shared

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Surface the slowest tests so regressions in test latency stay visible
# (core pytest CLI flags, so strict_config=true is unaffected).
#
# --max-worker-restart=1 is load-bearing, not tuning. `timeout_method =
# "thread"` force-exits the whole worker PROCESS when a test blocks past
# `timeout` below, and xdist's default policy is to spawn a replacement
# worker. The crashing test is reported failed and its remaining queue is
# redistributed, but xdist's default restart budget is 4x the node count. A
# run with repeated worker crashes can therefore burn many full `timeout`
# intervals before it stops. Allow one replacement so a single crashed
# worker does not abort the rest of the suite, while a second crash ends the
# run instead of starting a long replacement cycle.
# Tests that call live provider APIs, provision external services, or fork the
# current pytest process run only when explicitly selected. This keeps bare
# pytest non-billable and avoids forking pytest's own helper threads.
addopts = '--durations=15 --durations-min=1.0 --max-worker-restart=1 -m "not integration_live and not integration_external and not serial"'
testpaths = ["tests"]
strict_markers = true
strict_config = true
# Safety net: no single test should run for minutes. A hung test
# (e.g. an await on an event/future that never fires) is force-failed
# by pytest-timeout instead of blocking the whole suite indefinitely,
# and faulthandler dumps the stuck stack just before the timeout fires.
timeout = 60
timeout_method = "thread"
faulthandler_timeout = 55
markers = [
    "integration_local: local integration tests with no live services; may use subprocesses/filesystem",
    "integration_socket: tests requiring localhost socket bind/connect permissions",
    "integration_live: tests requiring live provider/API endpoints, API keys, and optional provider extras",
    "integration_external: tests requiring external local binaries, SDKs, or services without live provider API credentials",
    "serial: tests that must not run inside an xdist worker, such as direct os.fork coverage",
    "slow: long-running end-to-end tests; opt in with '-m slow'",
    "contract: provider, protocol, or bridge contract tests",
    "latency: latency measurement or latency SLO tests",
    "stress: load, soak, or high-volume validation tests",
    "release: release-gate validation tests",
    "flaky: quarantined intermittent test; requires linked issue, owner, and review date",
    "allow_task_leak: async test intentionally leaves background tasks beyond the test body",
    "guard: docs/onboarding/prose guard test — scans Markdown, docstrings, routes, or generated blocks rather than exercising product runtime; excluded from the fast dev loop but always run in `just test`/`check` and in the guard-* lanes.",
    "provider_openai: OpenAI provider coverage",
    "provider_deepgram: Deepgram provider coverage",
    "provider_elevenlabs: ElevenLabs provider coverage",
    "provider_cartesia: Cartesia provider coverage",
    "surface_stt: STT surface coverage",
    "surface_tts: TTS surface coverage",
    "surface_agent: agent bridge surface coverage",
    "surface_transport: transport surface coverage",
    "surface_vad: VAD surface coverage",
    "agent_bridge: agent bridge contract or live coverage",
    "provider(name): generic provider metadata for custom provider filtering",
]

# Import Linter (`uv run lint-imports`) turns the package's layering prose into
# machine-enforced contracts. Wired into `just lint`, ci.yml's lint job, and a
# repo-local pre-commit hook so the contracts are enforced everywhere at once.
# `exclude_type_checking_imports` keeps `if TYPE_CHECKING:` edges out of scope.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "easycat"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

# Configuration (construction) and planning (preview) are peers, not layers:
# ``easycat.planning`` must not import ``easycat.config`` (importing
# ``easycat.config`` pulls ``_factory`` and therefore ``Session``, which would
# make the side-effect-free planner drag the whole construction path in), and
# ``easycat.config`` must not import ``easycat.planning`` (the planner is the
# diagnostic projection *over* configuration). The pure decisions both make live
# in the stdlib-only leaf ``easycat._pipeline_decisions``, below both.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Configuration and planning do not import each other"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "easycat.config",
    "easycat.planning",
]
# `easycat.planning.selection` (the shared load -> plan -> coded-issue boundary
# `easycat plan` / `easycat doctor` / `VoiceServer` share) legitimately loads a
# manifest, and `ProjectManifest.to_easyconfig` holds a function-local
# `easycat.config` import so a manifest can be turned into a session config.
# That edge belongs to the PROJECT layer, not to planning: nothing on the
# planning path calls `to_easyconfig` (the planner reads a `VoiceProfile`
# directly, precisely so it never constructs an `EasyConfig`), and
# `tests/planning/test_boundary.py` proves at runtime that importing
# `easycat.planning` pulls no `easycat.config._factory`. Ignore the single
# manifest -> config edge rather than the planning -> project one, so a DIRECT
# planning -> config import is still a broken contract.
ignore_imports = [
    "easycat.project.manifest -> easycat.config",
]

# STT / TTS / VAD are independent provider families with no direct cross-imports.
# transports/telephony are DELIBERATELY excluded: they are genuinely
# bidirectionally coupled (twilio_media.py <-> telephony.dtmf), so an
# independence contract over them would fail on real, intended coupling.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "STT / TTS / VAD provider families stay independent"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "easycat.stt",
    "easycat.tts",
    "easycat.vad",
]
# The WebRTC transport is a leaf: server / cli / debugger must not DIRECTLY
# depend on it. `allow_indirect_imports` scopes the contract to direct imports,
# so legitimate lower-layer coupling (config wiring transports) does not red the
# build. Each `ignore_imports` entry is a real current direct edge grandfathered
# so the contract lands green; shrink this list as QS6's convergence removes
# edges — never grow it (mirrors the C901 grandfather convention).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "server / cli / debugger do not depend on transports.webrtc"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "easycat.server",
    "easycat.cli",
    "easycat.debugger",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "easycat.transports.webrtc",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    # Per-offer routes legitimately construct the peer transport lazily.
    "easycat.server.webrtc_routes -> easycat.transports.webrtc",
]

# Orchestration direction: SessionManager owns the Sessions that drive the
# pipeline, which in turn wraps the transport providers, so the transport layer
# must never import back up into SessionManager. Standalone multi-session server
# helpers live in easycat.server and leave provider modules focused on transport
# mechanics. (A fuller Session -> Stages
# spine is deliberately NOT modelled here: `events` and `config` both import
# `session.actions` as a shared leaf, which is intentional, permanent
# architecture rather than a ratchetable violation.)
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Transport providers do not import the SessionManager orchestrator"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "easycat.session_manager",
    "easycat.transports",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Bundle archive loader does not import the bundle facade"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "easycat.debug._bundle_loader",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "easycat.debug.bundle",
]

# `validation.latency` is the documented outward-facing facade. Internal
# validation code imports focused domain leaves directly so the facade cannot
# regress into a god module or create cycles between policy and orchestration.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Validation internals do not depend on the public latency facade"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "easycat.validation._environment",
    "easycat.validation._failure_classification",
    "easycat.validation._lane_harness",
    "easycat.validation._latency_artifacts",
    "easycat.validation._latency_baseline",
    "easycat.validation._latency_budgets",
    "easycat.validation._latency_models",
    "easycat.validation._latency_runner",
    "easycat.validation._latency_selectors",
    "easycat.validation._live_runner",
    "easycat.validation._release_runner",
    "easycat.validation._reliability_policy",
    "easycat.validation._runner_support",
    "easycat.validation._slice_runner",
    "easycat.validation.reliability",
]

    "easycat.validation.latency",
]

# The app composer owns optional-dependency loading and route assembly. Route
# leaves depend on source/domain helpers directly and must not reach back into
# the server facade, which would recreate the monolithic dependency direction.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Debugger route leaves do not import the server facade"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "easycat.debugger._core_routes",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "easycat.debugger.server",
]
