package com.tj.boilerplate.coreapi.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition.slices
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class ArchitectureTest {
    private val importedClasses: JavaClasses =
        ClassFileImporter()
            .withImportOption(ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
            .importPackages(ROOT_PACKAGE)

    @Test
    fun `레이어 의존은 정방향(상위 → 하위)만 허용한다`() {
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers()
            .layer(CORE_API)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.coreapi..")
            .layer(DOMAIN)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.domain..")
            .layer(STORAGE)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.storage..")
            .layer(CLIENTS)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.clients..")
            .layer(MODULES)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.modules..")
            .layer(COMMON)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.common..")
            // 진입 모듈은 최상위 — 아무도 의존하지 못한다
            .whereLayer(CORE_API)
            .mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            // domain 은 진입 모듈에서만 접근(storage·clients 는 domain 을 역참조 ❌)
            .whereLayer(DOMAIN)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(CORE_API)
            // storage 는 domain 을 통해서만(진입 모듈의 직접 참조 ❌)
            .whereLayer(STORAGE)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(DOMAIN)
            // 외부 API 는 진입 측 조율층에서만(domain 의 외부 I/O ❌)
            .whereLayer(CLIENTS)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(CORE_API)
            // 횡단 기술 기능은 진입 모듈·domain 에 더해 storage 도 사용한다(컬럼 암복호를 위한 crypto 참조).
            // clients 는 제외 — 실제 참조가 생길 때 근거와 함께 열어준다(미리 열면 규칙이 아무것도 막지 않는다)
            .whereLayer(MODULES)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(CORE_API, DOMAIN, STORAGE)
            // common 은 leaf — 모든 레이어가 참조 가능하나 common 자신은 아무도 의존하지 않는다
            .whereLayer(COMMON)
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(CORE_API, DOMAIN, STORAGE, CLIENTS, MODULES)
            .withOptionalLayers(true)
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `JPA 엔티티는 storage 레이어에만 존재한다`() {
        classes()
            .that()
            .areAnnotatedWith("jakarta.persistence.Entity")
            .or()
            .areAnnotatedWith("jakarta.persistence.MappedSuperclass")
            .should()
            .resideInAPackage("..storage..")
            .allowEmptyShould(true)
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `Spring Data Repository 는 storage 레이어에만 존재한다`() {
        classes()
            .that()
            .areAssignableTo("org.springframework.data.repository.Repository")
            .should()
            .resideInAPackage("..storage..")
            .allowEmptyShould(true)
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `common 은 leaf — 다른 레이어를 의존하지 않는다`() {
        noClasses()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("$ROOT_PACKAGE.common..")
            .should()
            .dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("..coreapi..", "..domain..", "..storage..", "..clients..", "..modules..")
            .allowEmptyShould(true)
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `레이어 간 순환 의존이 없다`() {
        slices()
            .matching("$ROOT_PACKAGE.(*)..")
            .should()
            .beFreeOfCycles()
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    companion object {

[project]
name = "bmk"
version = "3.22.0"
description = "Build, test and release runner for Python projects: keep the Makefile, drop the shell. Cross-OS, uv-based, one self-updating Makefile."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
# bmk declares its whole toolchain here, by design: it ships no [dev] extra, because the
# tools ARE the product. Keep the groups below - an undifferentiated list is how `textual`
# (orphan of a TUI deleted in 3.0.0) and `twine` (never invoked in bmk's entire history) sat
# here unnoticed, dragging 22 transitive packages into every install. Before adding a line,
# say which group it belongs to; if it fits none, it does not belong here.
dependencies = [
    # --- imported by bmk's own code ---------------------------------------------------
    "rich-click>=1.9.9",           # the CLI surface
    "click>=8.5.0",                # imported directly in cli/main.py for cli.main(obj=...) and in
                                   # commands/config.py (click.exceptions), not only via rich-click;
                                   # ALSO the CVE-2026-7246 floor, so this line is load-bearing
                                   # twice over - do not remove it as "just a pin"
    "lib_cli_exit_tools>=2.4.1",
    "lib_log_rich>=6.5.4",          # 6.4.2: validate_config, the check config --profile runs,
                                   # refuses exactly what init() refuses
    "lib_layered_config>=7.2.0",
    "btx_lib_mail>=4.5.0",         # send-email / send-notification (SecretStr password + Transport seam)
    "pydantic>=2.14.1",            # the pipeline-overlay and email schemas
    "orjson>=3.13.0",              # JSON: PyPI responses, CLI output
    "rtoml>=0.14.0",               # TOML read (stdlib tomllib does not exist on our 3.10 floor)
    "tomlkit>=0.15.1",             # TOML round-trip EDIT: preserves comments when bmk writes back
    "httpx2>=2.13.1",               # PyPI version lookups
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.4",        # reads CODECOV_TOKEN from .env, and the LOG_* lines of a .env
                                   # in adapters/logging/setup.py
    "filelock>=4.1.0",              # the cross-process lock serialising venv provisioning
                                   # (adapters/stagerunner/venv.py). It already arrived here
                                   # TRANSITIVELY via pip-audit -> cachecontrol[filecache], which is
                                   # far too fragile a provenance for something bmk imports: drop
                                   # pip-audit and the lock vanishes. bmk's deps stage keeps this
                                   # floor at the latest release. What the code actually uses is
                                   # FileLock + Timeout, an API far older than this floor, so the
                                   # floor is "current", not a hard requirement. It is NOT held up
                                   # by ReadWriteLock (3.21): that one is SQLite-backed, and this
                                   # repo already relocates a SQLite file off network mounts in
                                   # tests/conftest.py because network filesystems do not give
                                   # SQLite the locking semantics it needs - so a lock file that
                                   # can land on such a mount must not be built on it
    "packaging>=26.3",             # PEP 440 parsing/ordering of the PROJECT's own version in
                                   # domain/version.py (release gate, bump, plugin sync), and the
                                   # Requires-Python specifiers and markers the dependency update
                                   # checks a release against. Already arrives transitively via
                                   # build/hatchling/pip-audit/pytest; declared because bmk imports
                                   # it, not because it was missing

    # --- invoked as tools, never imported ---------------------------------------------
    # These look unused to an import scan. They are not: each one is a stage. The
    # distribution name and the executable differ for several - import-linter ships
    # `lint-imports`, shellcheck-py ships `shellcheck`, shfmt-py ships `shfmt`.
    "ruff>=0.17.1",
    "pyright[nodejs]>=1.1.414",    # [nodejs] bundles Node, so no system Node is required
    "bandit>=1.9.4",
    "pip-audit>=2.10.1",
    "import-linter>=2.15",
    "shellcheck-py>=0.11.0.1",
    "shfmt-py>=4.2.0",
    "bashate>=2.1.1",
    "pytest>=9.1.1",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",           # a pytest PLUGIN, activated by CI's --cov flags
    "hypothesis>=6.168.5",         # property tests in bmk's own suite
    # NEVER floor this at exactly 1.5.1: PyPI yanked that release (upstream shipped unintended
    # breaking changes), and a yanked release is invisible to a range resolve, so a >=1.5.1 floor
    # has ZERO candidates and makes bmk itself uninstallable - which bricked `make` fleet-wide
    # once already. 1.6.0 is a real unyanked release, so this floor resolves. The rule is about
    # the yanked version, not about staying low: check a candidate is unyanked before moving it.
    "build>=1.6.1",

    # --- neither imported nor invoked, and here on purpose -----------------------------
    # `python -m build` resolves the backend from [build-system].requires into its own
    # ephemeral venv, which pip-audit never sees - pip-audit audits the project's real .venv.
    # Declaring hatchling again HERE is what puts it in the audited env, so a future hatchling
    # CVE is actually caught. Not redundant with [build-system].
    "hatchling>=1.32.4",
    # A transitive of pip-audit, floored for CVE-2025-66471, CVE-2025-66418, CVE-2026-21441.
    # bmk never imports urllib3; httpx2 is its HTTP client. This is a floor, not a choice of
    # library, so "replace it with httpx2" is not a thing that can be done.
    "urllib3>=2.8.0",

    # --- deliberately absent ------------------------------------------------------------
    # twine: bmk never uploads to PyPI itself. `release` tags, pushes and calls `gh release`;
    # the publish is pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish in the release workflow. twine was declared
    # here for years and invoked nowhere - `git log -S twine` over src/ finds no commit that
    # ever wired it up. Removing it also removed keyring and the jaraco-* chain, which is why
    # the jaraco-context CVE floor went with it: that package only ever arrived via twine, and
    # a pin here INSTALLS a package rather than merely bounding it.
    #
    # textual: orphan of scripts/menu.py, a TUI deleted in the 3.0.0 rewrite. Zero imports.
    #
    # codecov-cli is disabled, not dropped: it requires click<8.3.0, which drags click back to
    # 8.2.1 - the version with CVE-2026-7246 (command injection in click.edit(), fixed in 8.3.3).
    # Nothing else here caps click, so with this line active the audit gate goes red on every
    # clean install. Leaving it off costs nothing: CI uploads coverage via codecov/codecov-action,
    # not this CLI, and "bmk codecov" resolves codecovcli from PATH and only warns when absent.
    # Re-enable once codecov-cli relaxes its click<8.3.0 pin.
    # "codecov-cli>=11.3.1",
]
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "bitranox", email = "bitranox@gmail.com" }]
keywords = [
  # What it is for. These were missing, so bmk advertised itself as a general task
  # runner while nothing works without a pyproject.toml: wrong audience found it, and
  # the right one could not.
  "python", "pyproject", "uv", "pytest", "makefile", "make",
  # What it does.
  "build", "test", "release", "task-runner", "cli", "devops", "ci", "coverage",
  "stagerunner", "custom-commands", "automation",
]
classifiers = [
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Environment :: Console",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]

system-dependencies-ubuntu = []
system-dependencies-macos = []
system-dependencies-windows-pip = []
system-dependencies-windows-choco = []
os = ["ubuntu-latest", "windows-latest", "macos-latest"]

[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "7 days"
exclude-newer-package = {btx-lib-mail = false, lib-cli-exit-tools = false, lib-layered-config = false, lib-log-rich = false, ruff = "2026-10-15T15:23:19Z"}

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/bitranox/bmk"
Repository = "https://github.com/bitranox/bmk.git"
Issues = "https://github.com/bitranox/bmk/issues"

[project.scripts]
bmk = "bmk.entry:main"
mk = "bmk.entry:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"



[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
# `bmk_selfcheck` is a second TOP-LEVEL module on purpose, so the deployed Makefile can run
# it as `python -m bmk_selfcheck` without importing `bmk` (whose __init__ costs 0.7s and is
# the very thing the check audits). `packages` cannot carry a lone module, hence the
# only-include/sources pair - which is exactly what `packages = ["src/bmk"]` desugars to.
only-include = ["src/bmk", "src/bmk_selfcheck.py", "src/bmk_toollock.py"]
sources = ["src"]
include = [
    "src/bmk/py.typed",
    "src/bmk/adapters/config/defaultconfig.toml",
    "src/bmk/adapters/config/defaultconfig.d/*.toml",
    "src/bmk/makefile/Makefile",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", "W",     # pycodestyle
  "F",           # pyflakes
  "I",           # isort
  "N",           # pep8-naming
  "UP",          # pyupgrade
  "B",           # bugbear
  "A",           # builtins shadowing
  "C4",          # comprehension simplification
  "SIM",         # simplification
  "TCH",         # type-checking imports
  "RUF",         # ruff-specific
  "G",           # logging format (catches f-string in logger)
  "T20",         # print statements
  "PTH",         # pathlib preference
  "PLC", "PLE",  # pylint conventions/errors
  "S",           # flake8-bandit security checks
  "PERF",        # performance anti-patterns
  "ERA",         # eradicate dead/commented-out code
  "FBT",         # boolean trap (boolean positional args)
  "PLR",         # pylint refactor
  "PLW",         # pylint warnings
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
# Pydantic resolves field annotations at runtime (model validation, serialization),
# so the TC00x autofix must not move BaseModel field-type imports into TYPE_CHECKING.
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Notebooks: unused imports are often intentional for side effects.
# F821: `_exit_code` is injected by IPython, so ruff cannot see it defined.
# S101: the asserts on it ARE the CI gate - `allow_errors=False` cannot see a
#       failing `!cmd`, so without them a broken command leaves the run green.
"notebooks/*.ipynb" = ["F401", "F821", "S101"]
# Stage helpers: CLI-style utilities with subprocess calls, print output, and magic values
"src/bmk/adapters/stagerunner/helpers/*.py" = ["T20", "S101", "S603", "S607", "E501", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR2004"]
# Tests: assert is standard, test fixtures have passwords, magic values are clearer inline, temp paths are fine
# PLR0917: unittest.mock.patch stacks inject mocks POSITIONALLY in decorator (bottom-up) order,
# so the flagged test functions cannot be made keyword-only without breaking the injection.
# PLC0415: deferred imports are a deliberate test idiom here - several tests import inside
# the test body to exercise import/cache behaviour, or to import a module under test lazily
# via a fixture.
"tests/*.py" = [
    "T20", "S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "S603", "S607", "E501", "ERA001",
    "FBT001", "FBT003", "PLC0415", "PLR0913", "PLR0917", "PLR2004", "PLW1510",
]
# CLI: Click framework injects boolean params; commands have many options
"src/bmk/adapters/cli/**/*.py" = ["FBT001", "FBT002", "PLR0913"]
# Protocols/adapters: many-param signatures by design
"src/bmk/application/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/bmk/adapters/config/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/bmk/adapters/email/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/bmk/adapters/memory/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/bmk/adapters/stagerunner/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
# git_ops runs git (partial path, on PATH) and prints user-facing commit/push output
"src/bmk/adapters/stagerunner/git_ops.py" = ["PLR0913", "T201", "S603", "S607"]
# venv runs uv and git (partial paths, on PATH) and prints user-facing provisioning output;
# the untrack notice in particular must reach the user, since it stages index deletions
"src/bmk/adapters/stagerunner/venv.py" = ["PLR0913", "T201", "S603", "S607"]
# The tool-env guard: its stderr messages ARE the user-facing signal (an unexplained
# multi-minute wait and a hang look identical to a person), and running the wrapped
# upgrade argv is the whole job. Stdlib-only by design, so it cannot route through click.
"src/bmk_toollock.py" = ["T201", "S603"]
# The CLI entry point prints one line when bmk's own environment was replaced mid-run.
# It must reach stderr even when the failure came from a spawned tool rather than an
# exception, so it cannot go through the normal error-rendering path.
"src/bmk/adapters/cli/main.py" = ["T201"]

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
extraPaths = [
  "src",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = ["--doctest-modules"]
doctest_optionflags = ["ELLIPSIS", "NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
markers = [
  "os_agnostic: test runs on every supported operating system",
  "os_windows: test exercises Windows-only behavior",
  "os_macos: test exercises macOS-only behavior",
  "os_posix: test exercises behavior requiring POSIX semantics",
  "os_linux: test exercises Linux-only behavior",
  "local_only: tests that require the local dev environment (external resources, script composition); skipped in CI",
  "integration: tests requiring external resources (SMTP, databases, APIs); run via 'make testintegration'",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
parallel = false
# Use a temp directory for the coverage database to avoid SQLite locking
# issues on network-mounted filesystems. The {envtmpdir} placeholder is
# not supported by coverage.py, so we use an environment variable with
# fallback to a cross-platform temp location via the pytest_configure
# hook in tests/conftest.py. CI also sets COVERAGE_FILE via workflow env.
#
# For local development, the pytest hook automatically redirects to
# tempfile.gettempdir() before pytest-cov creates its Coverage() object.
# This static fallback catches edge cases where coverage is run directly.
data_file = "/tmp/.coverage.bmk"
source = ["src/bmk"]

[tool.coverage.report]
omit = [
  "tests/*",
]
fail_under = 80
show_missing = true

[tool.coverage.json]
output = "coverage.json"
pretty_print = true

[tool.clean]
# Patterns to remove when running `make clean`.
# Not the project venv: bmk provisions and syncs it, and `push` cleans right after
# `test`, so listing it would delete the venv bmk just built and force a full
# re-resolve next command. Delete a venv by hand when you want it gone.
patterns = [
  "**/__pycache__",
  ".hypothesis",
  ".import_linter_cache",
  ".pytest_cache",
  ".ruff_cache",
  ".pyright",
  ".mypy_cache",
  ".tox",
  ".nox",
  ".eggs",
  "*.egg-info",
  "build",
  "dist",
  "htmlcov",
  ".coverage",
  "coverage.xml",
  "codecov.sh",
  ".cache",
  "result",
  ".data_arch_violations.json",
]

[tool.psscriptanalyzer]
# PSScriptAnalyzer rules to exclude when linting .ps1 files
exclude-rules = [
  "PSAvoidUsingWriteHost",              # intentional: stagerunner colored console UI
  "PSUseBOMForUnicodeEncodedFile",      # BOM-less UTF-8 is the modern standard
  "PSUseUsingScopeModifierInNewRunspaces",  # false positive: param() + -ArgumentList in Start-Job
]

[tool.bashate]
# bashate style settings for .sh files (E003 excluded: indent handled by shfmt)
max-line-length = 120
ignores = ["E003"]

[tool.git]
# Default git remote for push/release commands
default-remote = "origin"


[tool.scripts.test]
# Configuration for CICD test runner
pytest-verbosity = "-vv"
coverage-report-file = "coverage.xml"
src-path = "src"

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "bmk"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain is pure (no adapter dependencies)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "bmk.domain",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "bmk.adapters",
  "bmk.composition",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Clean Architecture layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
  # Composition wires adapters - can import everything
  "bmk.composition",
  # Adapters implement ports - can import application and domain
  "bmk.adapters",
  # Application defines ports - can import domain
  "bmk.application",
  # Domain is pure - bottom layer
  "bmk.domain",
]

[tool.pip-audit]
# Known vulnerabilities to ignore (environment-level packages, not project dependencies).
# Currently empty: both audit targets (project .venv and bmk's tool venv) are clean, and
# the pip_audit stage now force-upgrades pip to the latest in the audited interpreter, so
# the former pip CVEs cannot recur. Add an entry (with an inline note) only if a real,
# unfixable env-only CVE is flagged.
ignore-vulns = []

[tool.bandit]
# Skip warnings for subprocess usage in _shared.py and commit_cmd.py  -  these modules
# intentionally execute external scripts (test runners, git) as part of core functionality.
skips = [
  "B404",  # Consider possible security implications associated with subprocess module
  "B603",  # subprocess call - check for execution of untrusted input
  "B607",  # Starting a process with a partial executable path (git, shell scripts)
]

package com.github.arch

import com.github.arch.option.DoNotConfigPackageOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture

@AnalyzeClasses(
    packages = ["com.github.ryebot"],
    importOptions = [
        ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class,
        ImportOption.DoNotIncludeJars::class,
        ImportOption.DoNotIncludeArchives::class,
        DoNotConfigPackageOption::class,
    ]
)
class LayerCheckTest {

    @ArchTest
    fun `레이어간 의존성을 확인한다`(importedClasses: JavaClasses) {

        val layerArch = layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            // 레이어
            .layer("Api").definedBy("..api..")
            .layer("Application").definedBy("..application..")
            .layer("Domain").definedBy("..domain..")
            .layer("Client").definedBy("..client", "..client.(error|model)..")
            .layer("Repository").definedBy("..repository..")
            // 의존관계
            .whereLayer("Api").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("Application").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Api")
            .whereLayer("Domain").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Application")
            .whereLayer("Client").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Domain")

        layerArch.check(importedClasses)
    }
}

    # stores keep matching), reranker orderings are unchanged, and worker peak

    "pycozo[embedded]==0.3.0; sys_platform != 'linux' or platform_machine != 'aarch64'",

[project]
name = "quantbox"
version = "0.17.0"

# The base install is what the CORE layer imports (ADR-0010 decision 4,
# TOM-1451): a client install (robo) gets core and nothing else. A library a
# core module does not import belongs in an extra below. This file is the one
# owner of every list; docs point here.
dependencies = [
  "pandas>=2.3.3",
  # The floor is the lowest numpy the suite was run on, not the lock's version:
  # the full suite passes on 1.26.4 and on 2.1.3 (TOM-1451). No core code needs
  # numpy 2. A client caps numpy below 2.2 (robo), so do not raise it lightly.
  "numpy>=1.26.4",
  "scipy>=1.15.3",
  "pyarrow>=25.0.1",
  "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
  "jsonschema>=4.26.0",
  "statsmodels>=0.15.0",
  "pandas-market-calendars>=5.4.0",
  "typer>=0.27.2",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Per-audience extras (ADR-0010). Without one, a module that needs it raises
# MissingExtraError naming it, on import or on use; it never fails bare.
# [data]: the data-source clients (datasources, market_cap, the duckdb store).
data = ["duckdb>=1.5.5", "httpx>=0.28.1", "pycoingecko>=3.2.0", "requests>=2.34.2"]
# [research]: the research layer's libraries (reports need plotly) plus [data].

# [trade]: the venue clients brokers and publishers import. requests is
# declared, not borrowed from ccxt: the Binance-futures and Hyperliquid brokers
# import it for their Telegram notices.
trade = ["ccxt>=4.5.81", "httpx>=0.28.1", "requests>=2.34.2"]
# The vectorbt backtest engine (quantbox.bt, adapters.vectorbt, run_vectorbt,
# engine: vectorbt, quantbox.sweep sweep/run_grid). Without it those raise
# MissingExtraError naming this extra; everything else imports (TOM-1334).
vectorbt = ["vectorbt>=1.0.0", "numba>=0.67.0"]
ibkr = ["ib_insync"]
binance = ["python-binance"]
ccxt = ["ccxt>=4.5.81"]
ml = ["scikit-learn>=1.7.2"]
simulation = ["arch>=8.0"]
viz = ["matplotlib>=3.10.9", "seaborn>=0.13.2"]
full = ["quantbox[data,research,trade,vectorbt,ibkr,binance,ccxt,ml,simulation,viz]"]

[build-system]

    # [research] (which includes [data]) is what the old base install carried
    # beyond core: the suite exercises datasources, the store and reports.

    "pytest>=9.1.1",

    "slow: takes multiple seconds — relocated to CI by the pre-push hook, never weakened. Run via `pytest -m slow`.",
]

[tool.importlinter]
# THE LAYER MAP (ADR-0010, TOM-1451). These contracts are its one owner: docs,
# tests and scripts/check_no_vectorbt.sh read it from here (scripts/layer_map.py).
# Layers, in import order: core < plugins < research, trade. A layer imports only
# the layers below it; research and trade never import each other.
#
# Each layer is the `source_modules` of its contract. tests/test_layer_map.py
# fails when a module under src/quantbox is in no layer or in two, and when a
# contract's `forbidden_modules` is not exactly the layers above its source.
#
# Why `forbidden` contracts, not one `layers` contract: the layers interleave in
# the package tree (quantbox.engine is core, quantbox.engine.vectorbt research;
# quantbox.plugins.builtins is core, its siblings are plugins, research or trade;
# the root package and the plugins.pipeline namespace hold several layers). A
# `layers` contract treats each entry as a package with all its descendants, so
# it cannot state that. Here `as_packages = false`: an entry is one module, and
# `X.**` adds every module below X.
root_package = "quantbox"
include_external_packages = true

[tool.commitizen]
name = "cz_conventional_commits"
version = "0.17.0"
version_files = [
    "pyproject.toml:version",
    "src/quantbox/__init__.py:__version__",
    # uv.lock is deliberately NOT listed. `uv.lock:version` looks right and is a
    # trap: cz rewrites EVERY line matching the pattern, and other packages share
    # the string that gets rewritten — `dill` has historically shared ours, so
    # listing uv.lock would silently rewrite dill's pin during a bump and corrupt
    # the lockfile (verified against the installed updater in review of #147).
    #
    # Keep literal X.Y.Z numbers OFF any comment line that also contains the word
    # cz matches on. This very comment was rewritten by the 0.4.2 bump — it ended
    # up reading "a 0.4.2 -> 0.4.2 bump", the trap it warns about, demonstrated
    # on itself. Hence the placeholders.
    #
    # The lock is refreshed by `/ship` instead: it runs `uv lock` after the bump
    # and includes the result in the bump commit itself, so no separate step and
    # no helper script. That refresh is best-effort (it warns and continues if
    # `uv` is absent or the resolve fails); `.github/workflows/lockfile-check.yml`
    # is what turns a missed refresh into a red check.
]
update_changelog_on_bump = true
# ANNOTATED, always. WITHOUT this setting cz creates a LIGHTWEIGHT tag, and
# `git push --follow-tags` pushes only annotated ones. A lightweight tag therefore never leaves the machine while the
# push reports success; on 2026-07-28 that surfaced three steps later as
# `uv lock` failing with "couldn't find remote ref refs/tags/v0.4.1".
#
# Set HERE rather than relying on the caller passing --annotated-tag, so the
# safe behaviour does not depend on anyone remembering a flag.
annotated_tag = true
tag_format = "v$version"
ignored_tag_formats = ["rb-$version", "rb-*"]
major_version_zero = true

; Executable form of the layering rules in AGENTS.md. Run by `pdm check` via `lint-imports`.
; A broken contract means a dependency direction drifted — fix the direction, do not add an exemption.

[importlinter]
root_package = backend
include_external_packages = True

; Higher layers may import lower ones; never the reverse.
;   api            - transport; translates HTTP to use cases
;   minecraft      - sits above application because it implements the delivery/bridge PORTS
;                    defined there; nothing in application knows minecraft exists
;   application    - use cases; depends downward on infrastructure directly
;   infrastructure - database, redis, smtp, s3_storage, security, auth, http_client
;   config         - settings only, imports nothing
;   errors         - shared error kernel, imported by every layer, imports nothing
; exhaustive=True: a new top-level backend package must be placed in this hierarchy
; (or explicitly ignored) before it can be merged.
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Layered architecture
type = layers
containers = backend
layers =
    api
    minecraft
    application
    infrastructure
    config
    errors
exhaustive = True
exhaustive_ignores =
    di
    cli
    workers

; The layers contract puts minecraft above application because it implements ports the
; application layer defines — that is the position every driven adapter gets, and today
; minecraft is the only one. But position alone would let it reach ANY application module,
; so the permitted surface is enumerated here: ports, their DTOs and their errors, nothing
; else. Extending this list is a deliberate, reviewable act; a listed import that no longer
; exists fails the contract, so the list cannot rot.
[importlinter:contract:adapter-surface]
name = Adapters reach the application layer only through its ports
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    backend.minecraft
forbidden_modules =
    backend.application
ignore_imports =
    backend.minecraft.** -> backend.application.luckperms_bridge
    backend.minecraft.** -> backend.application.game_role_grants.delivery.adapter
    backend.minecraft.** -> backend.application.game_role_grants.delivery.models
    backend.minecraft.** -> backend.application.game_role_grants.delivery.errors

; The layers contract only governs backend modules, so the kernel's third-party
; dependencies are pinned separately: errors carries vocabulary, not machinery.
[importlinter:contract:error-kernel]
name = The error kernel stays free of transport, ORM and settings machinery
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    backend.errors
forbidden_modules =
    fastapi
    sqlalchemy
    pydantic_settings

; backend.di is deliberately outside the layers contract: the composition root knows every
; module by design. What must hold is that only entrypoints reach for it.
[importlinter:contract:composition-root]
name = Only entrypoints import the composition root
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    backend.api.routers
    backend.api.dependencies
    backend.api.schemas
    backend.application
    backend.infrastructure
    backend.minecraft
    backend.config
    backend.errors
forbidden_modules =
    backend.di

# ComfyUI 端点定义不经声明式运行时（docs/adr/0081）：两种 kind 的定义不同构，共用的只有诊断载体、
# 诊断翻译与 kind 常量三件事。comfyui 一侧一旦够到声明式的模板引擎、取值路径或它的校验实现，就是把
# 「JSON in/out + 提交 / 轮询」的假设搬进节点图这一侧，保存期与填值期从此各说各话。反向也不许：
# 分派表在 endpoint_definition.validator，它 import comfyui.validator 是唯一允许的方向。
# comfyui 一侧有两处：定义契约与保存期判定在 arcreel_market_core.comfyui，客户端、执行与两条调用通道
# 在 lib.custom_provider.comfyui。连间接依赖一起查：它们用到的调用通道运行支持
# （lib.backends.backend_runtime）与视频契约（arcreel_market_core.video_backend_contract）都够不到声明式运行时。
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ComfyUI 端点实现不依赖声明式运行时"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lib.custom_provider.comfyui", "arcreel_market_core.comfyui"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "lib.custom_provider.declarative_backend",
    "arcreel_market_core.endpoint_definition.validator",
    "arcreel_market_core.endpoint_definition.template_engine",
    "arcreel_market_core.endpoint_definition.response_extractor",
    "arcreel_market_core.endpoint_definition.jsonpath_subset",
]

# arcreel_market_core 是最底层：市场源工具与端点定义校验器被市场源仓库的 CI 与官方服务单独安装，
# 装不到 ArcReel 应用的其余部分。子包需要应用侧能力（翻译目录、共享 HTTP 客户端）时由调用方以参数
# 注入，主仓依赖子包，反向一律不许。
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "arcreel_market_core 不依赖主仓"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["arcreel_market_core"]
forbidden_modules = ["lib", "server"]

# arcreel_catalog_core 同为最底层：目录数据的格式与校验器被目录数据仓库的 CI 单独安装，
# 只依赖标准库，主仓依赖子包，反向一律不许。
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "arcreel_catalog_core 不依赖主仓"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["arcreel_catalog_core"]
forbidden_modules = ["lib", "server", "arcreel_market_core"]

# 路线中立层不得依赖某一条具体路线的子包。违约条目类型（draft_violation）、草稿信封
# （draft_quarantine）、正式 script_plan 的路径与写禁表（episode_paths）、已登记引用名的
# 构造入口（reference_catalog）对 drama / narration / reference_video 一视同仁，任一处
# import lib.script.reference_video 都是把三条路线共用的机制绑在其中一条上。
# lib.script.script_review 不在列：它另有一条 lib.script.reference_video.duration_migration 的依赖（参考
# 生视频专属的时长收编），纳入就要加 baseline 掩盖，那等于让契约声明一件它此刻并不成立的事。
# lib.script.script_references 同理不在列：它按设计依赖 lib.script.reference_video.text_parser——「引用名落在
# 载荷哪些位置」里有一类是正文的 @[名称] 记号，识别它的解析器只此一份。
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "路线中立层不依赖参考生视频子包"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "lib.script.draft_violation",
    "lib.script.draft_quarantine",
    "lib.episode.episode_paths",
    "lib.references.reference_catalog",
]
forbidden_modules = ["lib.script.reference_video"]

# 视频请求事实是两条视频路线共用的求值入口（docs/adr/0086），不得直接 import 参考生视频子包。
# 本契约只检查直接依赖，不检查经 lib.config.resolver → lib.project.project_manager 的间接项目加载链。
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "视频请求事实不依赖参考生视频子包"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lib.generation.video_request_facts"]
forbidden_modules = ["lib.script.reference_video"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# 核心库与服务端的分界（website/docs/dev/architecture.md「核心库与服务端的分界」）：核心库是领域逻辑与
# 基础设施，服务端是交付层与多入口共用的用例编排，依赖只能由服务端指向核心库。核心库需要服务端的
# 能力时（如生成 Worker 的任务执行器与续跑执行器），由应用装配处（server/app.py）注入。
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "核心库不依赖服务端"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lib"]
forbidden_modules = ["server"]

# 核心库不知道 HTTP 的存在：请求级的语言解析、依赖注入等框架胶水归服务端（server.i18n 等）。
# 只查核心库自己写下的 import——经由服务端间接够到框架的链已由上一条契约拦住。

[tool.deptry]
# 扫描范围与 basedpyright 的 include 对齐：核心库、服务端、迁移基础设施、脚本与测试。
# exclude 是 deptry 默认值去掉 tests（测试的 import 也要参与依赖卫生判定）再补上 worktree 目录。

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# DEP002（声明了但无 import）——全部是靠 entry point / 后端注册被运行时加载的插件，
# 源码里不会出现 import。
DEP002 = [
    "aiosqlite",        # SQLAlchemy 的 sqlite+aiosqlite 异步驱动
    "asyncpg",          # SQLAlchemy 的 postgresql+asyncpg 异步驱动
    "python-multipart", # Starlette 解析 multipart/form-data 的后端
    "socksio",          # httpx 的 SOCKS 代理传输后端
    "lxml",             # BeautifulSoup 的 lxml / lxml-xml 解析器后端
    "mutmut",           # 变异测试 CLI，源码不 import 它；变异后的模块只在 mutants/ 副本里 import
    "pytest-testmon",   # pytest 插件，经 entry point 加载；按改动选测试，用法见 docs/agents/testing.md
]
# DEP004（import 了 dev 依赖）——tests/ 与 scripts/ 在扫描范围内，deptry 无法按目录区分
# dev 与生产文件，故逐项列出它们正当 import 的测试框架包；其余 dev 依赖仍受本规则守护。
DEP004 = [
    "pytest",         # 测试框架
    "_pytest",        # pytest 的内部模块，根 conftest 复用其选择参数解析器
    "pytest_asyncio", # pytest 的 asyncio 插件，测试内直接用 @pytest_asyncio.fixture（本规则按模块名匹配）
    "respx",          # httpx 的测试替身
    "blockbuster",    # 事件循环阻塞检测，tests/blocking_guard 护栏的拦截点来源
]

# 变异测试（mutmut 3.7.0）。不进 dev 依赖，按需 `uv run --with mutmut==3.7.0 mutmut run`。
# 变异得分是信号不是闸门：不为杀死变异体补写测试，只用存活 mutant 筛选待审查的测试。
[tool.mutmut]
# 操作流程（跑一批、超时复核、三层验收、已知陷阱）见 docs/testing/mutmut-runbook.md；这里只写配置项的取舍。
# 必须显式写：不写时 mutmut 只推断出 lib/，漏掉 server/
source_paths = ["lib", "server"]
# 按批次填写待变异模块；留空则变异 source_paths 全域（一轮数小时，不实用）
# only_mutate = ["lib/speech/speech_rate.py"]
# tests.mutmut_plugin 给每个 mutmut 会话一个私有 basetemp，让并行子进程收尾时不再竞争共享根下的软链；
# 它只在这里加载，本地与 CI 的 pytest 不带它。
# tests/integration/lib/generation/test_task_failure_capability.py 里三个用例用 ast 扫 lib/ server/ 源码里的 capability code
# 字面量并与登记表比对；mutants/ 里的源文件同时含全部字符串 mutant 变体（XXcodeXX / CODE），扫描必报「未登记」，
# stats 阶段直接失败。凡读源码文本而非 import 模块的用例都要这样按 nodeid --deselect，不整文件 --ignore：
# 同文件其余用例是 bound_reason / collapse_cascade_reason / 级联渲染的行为测试，其中部分路径由它们独家覆盖，
# 整文件排除会让 lib/generation/task_failure.py 的真变异体记成存活。
# 只排除扫描用例同样只会多出假存活：它们独家能杀的只有 code 字面量的变体，而各 backend 用例都断言 exc.code。
pytest_add_cli_args = [
    "-p",
    "tests.mutmut_plugin",
    "--deselect=tests/integration/lib/generation/test_task_failure_capability.py::test_capability_codes_registered_no_drift",
    "--deselect=tests/integration/lib/generation/test_task_failure_capability.py::test_no_unscannable_capability_construction_sites",
    "--deselect=tests/integration/lib/generation/test_task_failure_capability.py::test_capability_construction_sites_supply_every_template_param",
]
# pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection 不设：走全量 testpaths。仅 tests/unit 快 5.5 倍，
# 但存活集合约 45% 是假存活，复核每个都要跑一次全量套件，总账反而更贵。
# timeout_multiplier / timeout_constant 保持默认（15 / 1.0），不要调小。
# 预算按关联用例的运行时长外推，调小只会让慢用例上的真存活记成超时（⏰），每个都得新进程复核。
also_copy = [
    "agent_runtime_profile",
    "alembic",
    "alembic.ini",
    "scripts",
    "skills",
    "skills-lock.json",
    "public",
    ".github",
    "frontend/src",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Layered architecture contract — enforces docs/layered-agent-architecture.md
# (L1 lowest -> L15 highest). Upper layers may import lower; lower must NOT
# import upper. Authoritative package->layer mapping lives in that doc.
#
# Coverage: every top-level magi.* package is enumerated in `layers` below
# (bootstrap is the sole exception — it IS the composition root). When adding a
# new top-level package, place it in the ordering, or CI cannot see its edges.
#
# Adoption model: BASELINE + RATCHET.
#   * The ignore_imports list below is a frozen snapshot of pre-existing
#     cross-layer imports (originally 115 edges as of 2026-05-31; ratcheted
#     down since). CI is GREEN today.
#   * Do NOT add new entries. Any *new* lower->upper import fails CI.
#   * The list should only ever SHRINK. Delete an entry once the underlying
#     import is removed; never grow it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Magi L1-L15 layered architecture
type = layers
containers =
    magi
layers =
    transport | ipc
    outreach
    commands
    api | chat | channels
    chat_preview
    delivery
    timeline
    agent
    context
    user_profile
    awareness
    personality
    system_suggestions
    mcp
    tools
    skills
    memory
    llm
    speech
    plugins
    control
    notifications
    runtime_trace
    events
    i18n
    config
    hooks
    location
    media
    scheduler | identity
    db
    core
    utils
    availability
ignore_imports =
    # == Composition root (NOT debt; structural & permanent) ==================
    # core.container is the DI container: wiring every layer is its purpose.
    magi.core.container -> magi.**
    # Any import of bootstrap/ is composition-root wiring; bootstrap/ is the
    # outer assembly boundary, intentionally outside the numbered layer stack.
    magi.** -> magi.bootstrap.**
    #
    # == KNOWN DEBT BASELINE (frozen 2026-05-31; ratchet down, never up) ======
    # Buckets include historical tools/skills->agent, L14 api/chat/channels
    # sibling edges, runtime_trace->events, and other ratcheted-down legacy
    # edges. Retired buckets include awareness->timeline and transport chat
    # notifications. The L7 tools<->skills sibling cycle was broken:
    # `tools` is now ordered above `skills` and the `skills -> tools.registry`
    # arms were inverted via ToolRegistryPort.
    # ChatExecutionCoordinator RELOCATED from magi.agent.task_agents.chat.coordinator
    # to magi.chat.task_agent.coordinator (P2 Task 6, chat-driver descent). The old
    # agent->channels delivery edge and its chat->channels relocation are retired;
    # chat now receives a channel-owned delivery dispatcher by injection.
    magi.api.routers.commands -> magi.commands
    magi.api.routers.memory.dependencies -> magi.chat

[importlinter:contract:plugin-isolation]
name = Plugin implementations depend on SDK only, never host layers
type = forbidden
# Direct-only on purpose: the first hop from any plugin module to a host
# module is always a direct edge, so the boundary is still fully enforced.
# Without this, transitive chains through bootstrap/ (the composition root,
# which imports every layer) would flood the contract with false positives
# — the same reason the layers contract exempts bootstrap.
allow_indirect_imports = true
# NOTE: magi.plugins is intentionally excluded — it is the host-side L4
# plugin registration/management layer (manager, installation, registry_client),
# governed by the layers contract, NOT plugin-implementation code.
source_modules =
    magi.tools.builtin
    magi.tools.code_agent
    # magi.skills excluded (Phase 5): it is the HOST skill-execution engine
    # (runner/subagent/loader/indexer), host integration code like magi.mcp and
    # magi.plugins — NOT plugin-implementation content. The third-party skill
    # *content* plugins contribute is dynamically loaded and runtime-guarded.
forbidden_modules =
    magi.agent
    magi.chat
    magi.api
    magi.transport
    magi.channels
    magi.timeline
    magi.context
    magi.memory
    magi.personality
    magi.llm
    magi.events
    magi.control
ignore_imports =
    # == KNOWN DEBT BASELINE (frozen 2026-05-31; ratchet down, never up) ==
    # Plugin->host edges that exist today. Do NOT add entries; only delete
    # them as the underlying import is removed during later migration phases.
    # Some edges also violate the layers contract and appear in BOTH baselines;
    # when an import is removed, delete it from BOTH ignore_imports lists.
    #
    # BASELINE = 0 as of Phase 5 Task 3: the last plugin->host edge
    # (magi.tools.builtin.agent_tool -> magi.agent.workers) was removed when
    # agent_tool was relocated to magi.agent.runtime_tools and host-registered
    # via the composition root. Do NOT add new entries here.

version = "0.1.30"
description = "Local-first AI agent with personality, memory, and temporal awareness"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "Magi Contributors" }]
keywords = ["ai", "agent", "llm", "memory", "desktop"]

[importlinter:contract:server-layers]
name = Server layers (legacy edges are explicit)
type = layers
containers = server
# Highest to lowest. Assembly and API ownership follow the current graph;
# jobs/cadlink coordinate each other, while registry selects solver adapters.
# Pipes require independent siblings; colons permit sibling collaboration.
layers =
    __main__
    app : cli
    updates
    diagnostics
    exports | design_io | source_editor
    jobs : cadlink
    engines
    solver
    mesh
    preview
    integration
    design
    charts | drivers | settings | workspace | protocol
    platform
    contracts
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores =
    # Test modules are clients of production packages, not runtime layers.
    tests
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = error
# Exact module edges only: never widen these to wildcard package exceptions.
# Remove an edge when its dependency is extracted into a lower layer.
ignore_imports =
    # cadlink -> exports: existing upward dependency.
    # Legacy use: geometry_hash_for_design.
    server.cadlink.intake.ingest -> server.exports.geometry_identity
    # Legacy use: WgLinkExportRequest, _base_name, _export_wglink_sync.
    server.cadlink.onshape.api -> server.exports.api
    # cadlink -> updates: existing upward dependency.
    # Legacy use: UPDATE_RESTART_PENDING.
    server.cadlink.api -> server.updates.restart
    # design -> cadlink: existing upward dependency.
    # Legacy use: CadLink.
    server.design.textcfg -> server.cadlink.identity
    # design -> jobs: existing upward dependency.
    # Legacy use: SolveOptions.
    server.design.solve_block -> server.jobs.models
    # engines -> jobs: existing upward dependency.
    # Legacy use: PolarConfig.
    server.engines.dryrun -> server.jobs.models
    # integration -> jobs: existing upward dependency.
    # Legacy use: SolveRequest.
    server.integration.provenance -> server.jobs.models
    # jobs -> updates: existing upward dependency.
    # Legacy use: RestartApproval, UPDATE_RESTART_PENDING.
    server.jobs.api -> server.updates.restart
    # Legacy use: RestartApproval.
    server.jobs.runtime.core -> server.updates.restart
    # mesh -> cadlink: existing upward dependency.
    # Legacy use: AS_MODELLED, spec_axis, spec_matrix.
    server.mesh.imported -> server.cadlink.interpretation.solver_frame
    # Legacy use: source_physical_name.
    server.mesh.imported -> server.cadlink.wglink_protocol
    # mesh -> solver: existing upward dependency.

    server.mesh.api -> server.solver.symmetry

    # Legacy use: canonical_source_role.
    server.solver.metal -> server.cadlink.roles

    server.solver.warmup -> server.engines.registry

    # Legacy use: DriveChannel.

    # Legacy use: DriveChannel.

# Product-owned import-linter config (not synced). Fleet baseline: docs/quality.md.
#
# Inventory (top-level middleware.* portions / intended roles) — issue #302 / #155:
#   middleware.shared / middleware.api_client — shared libs (git deps)
#   middleware.contracts                    — plugin-facing errors / NiceHttpClient / Plugin
#   middleware.payload                      — PayloadKind / DataMapper / RDF mappers (no plugin deps)
#   middleware.parsing                      — DiscoveryResult / PayloadParser registry (may use contracts)
#   middleware.harvester                    — orchestrator; imports plugins + payload + parsing + contracts
#   middleware.inspire                      — INSPIRE/CSW plugin
#   middleware.linked_data                  — sitemap/HTML JSON-LD plugin (shim→generic during migration)
#   middleware.generic                      — Protocol + shared pipeline (consumes parsing)
#   middleware.oai_pmh                      — OAI-PMH / Scythe plugin (consumes parsing + payload)
#
# PEP 420: grimp raises NamespacePackageEncountered for package `middleware`, so
# `ancestors = middleware` (fleet template) cannot run here. Ancestors are the
# installed portions instead — that still uses contract type `acyclic_siblings`
# and checks cycles among each portion's children.

[importlinter]
exclude_type_checking_imports = True
root_packages =
    middleware.api_client
    middleware.contracts
    middleware.generic
    middleware.harvester
    middleware.inspire
    middleware.linked_data
    middleware.oai_pmh
    middleware.parsing
    middleware.payload
    middleware.shared

[importlinter:contract:middleware-acyclic-siblings]
name = middleware sibling packages must be acyclic
type = acyclic_siblings
ancestors =
    middleware.api_client
    middleware.contracts
    middleware.generic
    middleware.harvester
    middleware.inspire
    middleware.linked_data
    middleware.oai_pmh
    middleware.parsing
    middleware.payload
    middleware.shared

# payload MUST NOT depend on harvester, parsing, contracts, or protocol plugins.
[importlinter:contract:payload-isolation]
name = payload must not import harvester, parsing, contracts, or protocol plugins
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    middleware.payload
forbidden_modules =
    middleware.harvester
    middleware.contracts
    middleware.inspire
    middleware.linked_data
    middleware.generic
    middleware.oai_pmh
    middleware.parsing

# contracts MAY import payload; MUST NOT import harvester, parsing, or plugins.
[importlinter:contract:contracts-isolation]
name = contracts must not import harvester, parsing, or protocol plugins
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    middleware.contracts
forbidden_modules =
    middleware.harvester
    middleware.parsing
    middleware.inspire
    middleware.linked_data
    middleware.generic
    middleware.oai_pmh

# parsing MAY import contracts + payload; MUST NOT import harvester or plugins.

name = parsing must not import harvester or protocol plugins
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    middleware.parsing
forbidden_modules =

    middleware.inspire
    middleware.linked_data
    middleware.generic
    middleware.oai_pmh

# Protocol plugins must not import each other, except the documented temporary
# linked_data → generic discovery/parser/pipeline shims (principles.md).

name = inspire must not import linked_data, generic, or oai_pmh
type = forbidden

[tool.pyright]
venv = ".venv"
venvPath = "."
reportUnusedVariable = false
reportUnusedImport = false
reportMissingImports = false

[tool.ruff]
lint.select = [
  "F",   # flake8
  "E",   # pycodestyle errors
  "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
  "B",   # flake8-bugbear
  "N",   # PEP 8 naming conventions
  "C",   # McCabe complexity
  "T",   # Print found todos
  "UP",  # upgrade syntax
  "ANN", # type annotations
  "S",   # security issues
  "DTZ", # datetime timezone issues
]

lint.ignore = [
  "ANN204", # Missing type annotation for special methods
  "E501",   # line too long
  "C901",   # function too complex
  "ANN401", # Any type
  "W293",   # blank line contains whitespace
  "W291",   # trailing whitespace
]

"test*" = [
  "S101",   # disable security issues for tests

]

[tool.mypy]

disallow_untyped_decorators = true

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["ai_framework"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ai_framework layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "ai_framework.application",
    "ai_framework.providers",
    "ai_framework.tools",
    "ai_framework.session",
    "ai_framework.attachments",
    "ai_framework.memory",
    "ai_framework.migrations",
    "ai_framework.tool_loop",
    "ai_framework.protocols",
    "ai_framework.entities",
]

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    services
    adapters
    lib
    domain
    models
    host
    bootstrap
include_external_packages = True

# The host is the process, not a layer of the application. It owns the port, the
# protocol and the lifetime, and it reaches none of the code it hosts — the
# composition root hands it a dispatcher and an event sink, and it asks them
# nothing about what is behind them.
[importlinter:contract:host-hosts-nothing-it-knows]
name = The host must not import the application it hosts
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    host
forbidden_modules =
    services
    adapters
    bootstrap
    domain

# ...and the other direction, which is the half that rots without a check. The
# first service that wants to send an event would reach in here for the sink,
# and from then on the composition root would no longer be the only place that
# knows a transport exists. ``main.py`` and ``check.py``, the two entry points,
# are the modules allowed to know, and neither is a package, so nothing in this
# list can name them.
[importlinter:contract:nobody-imports-the-host]
name = Only the entry point may import the host
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    services
    adapters
    bootstrap
    domain
    lib
    models
forbidden_modules =
    host

# Services must not import concrete adapters (Protocols are OK). Forbid the
# ``adapters`` root package wholesale, not a hand-enumerated denylist: services
# depend only on Protocols (defined in ``services/protocols/``), so they have
# zero legitimate adapter imports. A denylist rots — the old 8-module list had
# silently stopped covering ``adapters.repositories.*`` and ~15 other modules
# (#985). The completeness of the sibling ``service-independence`` list is
# guarded by ``scripts/check_service_independence_contract.py``.
[importlinter:contract:no-adapter-impl-in-services]
name = Services must not import concrete adapter implementations
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    services
forbidden_modules =
    adapters

# Adapters must not import services
[importlinter:contract:no-services-in-adapters]
name = Adapters must not import services
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    adapters
forbidden_modules =
    services

# Utilities (lib/) must not import services, adapters, or domain
[importlinter:contract:utilities-independence]
name = Utilities must not import services, adapters, or domain
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    lib
forbidden_modules =
    services
    adapters
    domain

# Domain is pure compute — no dependencies on any other internal layer.
# Services, adapters, lib, and models are all forbidden. Anything domain
# needs from "shared utilities" (e.g. ISO timestamp parsing) lives inside
# domain itself.
[importlinter:contract:domain-independence]
name = Domain must not import services, adapters, lib, or models
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    domain
forbidden_modules =
    services
    adapters
    lib
    models

# Domain is pure compute, stdlib + self only. ``_vendor`` hosts vendored
# third-party packages and is the only entry point for non-stdlib code
# into the codebase; banning it from domain enforces the CP doctrine
# that domain has no external runtime dependencies.
[importlinter:contract:domain-stdlib-only]
name = Domain must not import vendored third-party packages
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    domain
forbidden_modules =
    _vendor

# Models must not import services, adapters, domain, or lib
[importlinter:contract:models-independence]
name = Models must not import services, adapters, domain, or lib
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    models
forbidden_modules =
    services
    adapters
    domain
    lib

# Services must not import stdlib I/O, concurrency, or non-deterministic
# primitives directly. Real I/O belongs behind adapters; time, uuid, and
# async sleep come from Protocols (Clock, UuidGen, Sleeper) so services
# stay deterministic under test. ``time`` and ``uuid`` are banned now
# that every service has been migrated onto the injection seam — the
# UuidGen Protocol returns ``str`` so even ``services/protocols.py``
# does not need to import ``uuid``.
#
# ``urllib.request`` is intentionally omitted: import-linter rejects
# subpackage names for forbidden external modules, and banning the
# whole ``urllib`` parent would also lock out ``urllib.parse`` /
# ``urllib.error`` which services legitimately need.
#
# ``datetime.now()`` and ``asyncio.sleep()`` are call-level — see #303
# for a custom check that complements this import-level guardrail.
[importlinter:contract:no-stdlib-io-in-services]
name = Services must not import stdlib I/O or concurrency primitives
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    services
forbidden_modules =
    random
    subprocess
    threading
    requests
    time
    uuid

# Services must be independent of each other
[importlinter:contract:service-independence]
name = Services must not import other services
type = independence
modules =
    services.achievements
    services.active_core_resolver

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# E14263 AG1 intent (RAISE-14696): adapters must not import from session layer.
# AG1 detected auth-related symbols fanning out across module boundaries without
# an aggregator. This contract enforces that adapter implementations (filesystem,
# jira, etc.) remain caller-independent — they must not depend on session state,

# from adapters or session, which prevents the fan-in coupling CAND-17 was designed to detect

forbidden_modules = ["onnxruntime"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# RAISE-16340 (Epic RAISE-16334, O7) — the raise_cli 5-layer model.
#
# Allowed import direction, outermost first:
#     cli  ->  services  ->  domain  ->  adapters  ->  core
#
# Modules on the same line are joined with `:` (non-independent siblings):
# intra-layer imports are ALLOWED. This contract polices the *direction of
# travel between layers*, not coupling inside one. Intra-layer independence
# where it actually matters is already enforced by the ADR-001 Foundation
# Independence and E14263 contracts above.
#
# The map is PARTIAL by design. Top-level subpackages not listed here are not
# checked; they get added as they are classified (see the "still being
# classified" list in packages/raise-cli/ARCHITECTURE.md). A partial map that
# enforces what we know beats a complete one that is never turned on.
#
# TWO PLACEMENTS DIVERGE FROM THE EPIC SKETCH, on gemba evidence:
#   * `adapters` sits BELOW domain, not above services. It has a fan-in of 17
#     top-level packages because it holds the ports (`adapters.protocols`,
#     `adapters.models`) alongside the implementations. Everything that speaks
#     to an external system depends on those ports. Placing it at the edge
#     would need 41 extra waivers to describe imports that are not actually
#     wrong. Splitting ports from implementations is RAISE-16339, and this
#     placement is revisited then.
#   * `mcp` is in the core tier, not a peer of `cli`. `raise_cli.mcp` is the
#     bridge/registry/schema infrastructure (fan-in 6: cli, adapters, pipeline,
#     session, worktree; fan-out 1). The MCP *server* entry point lives in
#     `raise_cli.pipeline.mcp_server`, not here. This confirms the premise of
#     governance/adrs/v1/adr-042-mcp-infrastructure-layer.md.
#
# Rationale for import-linter over tach (the epic sketched tach): import-linter
# was already a dev dependency carrying four contracts and its `layers` type
# expresses this model directly. Two enforcement tools for one concern is waste.
# See governance/adrs/adr-2026-08-19-cli-layer-model-enforcement.md.
#
# Enforced by: `uv run lint-imports` locally, `guard:import-contracts`
# (.gitlab-ci.yml) and the `arch` job (.github/workflows/ci-raise-cli.yml) in CI.
# Specified by: packages/raise-cli/tests/pkg_meta/test_layer_contract.py
name = "RAISE-16340 raise_cli 5-layer model"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "cli",
    "pipeline : worktree : backlog : docs : reliability : skills : release_preflight : release_version : calibration : compliance : quality : self_update : hooks : output : fleet : onboarding : work_item",
    "gates : session : memory : distillation : governance : work_events : cartridges : doctor",
    "adapters",
    "config : storage : schemas : compat : exceptions : cwd_binding : telemetry : graph : mcp : _agent_session : discovery : core : portfolio : dev : developer_profile : project_config : hook_bus : embeddings",
]
containers = ["raise_cli"]
# WAIVER REGISTRY — the frozen stock of layer violations as of RAISE-16340.
#
# This list may only SHRINK except via enrollment waivers (ADR-2026-08-21).
# Enrollment: a package first classified into the contract may carry pre-existing
# violations as enrollment waivers — raise MAX_WAIVERS in the SAME commit,
# tag the entry with the enrolled package name, and cite a remediation story.
# Regression waivers (new code violating a boundary) are always forbidden.
#
# The ceiling is asserted by test_waivers_are_a_shrinking_ratchet in
# packages/raise-cli/tests/pkg_meta/test_layer_contract.py — lower MAX_WAIVERS
# there when you delete an entry here.
ignore_imports = [
    # --- Back-imports into `cli`. Owned by RAISE-16337 (cli/ dependency
    # inversion). Pinned per-import, not wildcarded, so no NEW module may reach
    # up into cli even while these six survive.
    "raise_cli.session.bundle_data -> raise_cli.cli.main",
    "raise_cli.gates.governance.skill_cli_refint_gate -> raise_cli.cli.main",
    "raise_cli.pipeline.mcp_tools_docs -> raise_cli.cli.commands._resolve",
    "raise_cli.pipeline.mcp_tools_backlog -> raise_cli.cli.commands._resolve",
    "raise_cli.pipeline.mcp_server -> raise_cli.cli.commands.connect",
    "raise_cli.pipeline.mcp_tools_story -> raise_cli.cli.commands.session",
    # --- Boundary-level debt discovered by this story. One entry per violated
    # boundary; each is removed wholesale when that boundary is repaired.
    # core -> domain: telemetry emits work events instead of the reverse.
    "raise_cli.telemetry.** -> raise_cli.work_events.**",
    # core -> domain/adapters: storage reaches up into memory and adapters.
    "raise_cli.storage.** -> raise_cli.memory.**",
    "raise_cli.storage.** -> raise_cli.adapters.**",
    # domain -> services: gates orchestrate service-tier modules.
    "raise_cli.gates.** -> raise_cli.docs.**",
    "raise_cli.gates.** -> raise_cli.pipeline.**",
    "raise_cli.gates.** -> raise_cli.release_preflight",
    "raise_cli.gates.** -> raise_cli.release_version",
    "raise_cli.session.** -> raise_cli.worktree.**",
    # --- doctor enrollment — RAISE-16981: pipeline_coverage_gate imports doctor,
    # which imports pipeline.loader for coverage checks and worktree.provision
    # for workspace readiness checks.
    "raise_cli.doctor.** -> raise_cli.pipeline.**",
    "raise_cli.doctor.** -> raise_cli.worktree.**",
    # --- S3 enrollments (ADR-2026-08-21 enrollment waivers, pre-existing debt).
    # graph→cartridges remediated by RAISE-16457; hooks×3 remediated by RAISE-16455.
    # --- RAISE-16509 removals: W11/W8/W9 remediated — distillation→pipeline,
    # session→self_update, developer_profile→adapters removed.
]

[tool.poe.tasks.typecheck]
help = "Strict type check with zuban"

[tool.poe.tasks.pycroscope]
help = "Semi-static analysis with pycroscope"

[tool.poe.tasks.imports]
help = "Check the import layering with import-linter"

[tool.poe.tasks.hooks]
help = "Run every pre-commit hook on all files"

help = "Run all the checks to do before a commit"
sequence = ["lint", "format", "typecheck", "pycroscope", "imports", "hooks"]

[tool.poe.tasks.test]
help = "Run the test suite (extra arguments go to pytest)"
cmd = "pytest"
executor = { group = "test" }

help = "Run the GUI tests headless (installs the gui extra)"

help = "Serve the docs site locally with live reload"

[tool.poe.tasks.docs-build]

executor = { group = "docs" }

[tool.poe.tasks.docs-deploy]
help = "Build the docs and deploy them to docs.tagger.photo (needs Node and Cloudflare env vars)"

    { ref = "docs-build" },

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
indent-width = 4
target-version = "py314"
fix = true
unsafe-fixes = false

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "CPY001", # missing-copyright-notice: this project has no copyright-header policy
    "D203",   # one-blank-line-before-class
    "D212",   # multi-line-summary-first-line
    "D413",   # blank-line-after-last-section
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"**/tests/{test_*.py,conftest.py}" = [
    "S101",   # Allow assert in tests
    "S105",   # Allow hardcoded password in strings in tests
    "S106",   # Allow hardcoded password in function calls in tests
    "ARG001", # Allow unused arguments in tests (for pytest fixtures)
    "INP001", # No __init__.py needed — pytest uses --import-mode=importlib
    "TC001",  # Keep imports at runtime in tests; the import-cost the TC rules guard is irrelevant
    "TC002",  # here, and a TYPE_CHECKING block for a test's own framework import reads oddly.
    "TC003",
]
# The whole point of these tests is characters that look like each other but are not, so the rule
# that warns about exactly that has nothing to add here.
"**/tests/test_script_guard.py" = [
    "RUF001", # Ambiguous unicode characters are the subject under test
]
"**/__init__.py" = [
    "D104", # Allow empty __init__.py files
]
"packaging/**" = [
    "INP001",  # Build scripts, not an importable package
    "T201",    # print() is the right channel for build-time progress
    "S603",    # subprocess with fixed, trusted args (iconutil)
    "S607",    # ditto
    "PLC0415", # Intentional in-function imports (selftest probes; lazy Qt launch)
    "F401",    # selftest imports modules only to confirm they were bundled
]
# The telemetry dashboard is a marimo notebook: every cell is a `def _(dep, ...)` whose parameters
# are dependencies marimo injects from other cells, and imports live inside a cell by design. That
# shape trips a fixed set of rules that do not apply to notebook code.
"telemetry/dashboard.py" = [
    "ANN001",  # Cell params are marimo-injected dependencies, not annotated call arguments
    "ANN202",  # Every cell is an unannotated `def _(...)`
    "PLR0913", # A cell takes one param per dependency; marimo controls the signature
    "PLR0917", # Same: positional dependency params, not a call-site design choice
    "PLC0415", # marimo requires imports inside a cell so it can track them reactively
    "N803",    # COLORS flows between cells as a param; the name must match its definition
    "N806",    # COLORS is a palette constant, but a marimo cell is a function
    "S608",    # SQL is built from int-coerced window sizes against a read-only token; the free-form
    #            console runs user SQL by design. No untrusted interpolation reaches a write path.
]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
force-wrap-aliases = true
lines-after-imports = 2

[tool.docformatter]
# Reflow docstrings to the project's 100-column width. `pre-summary-newline` keeps the summary on the
# second line to match the active D213 (the D212 alternative is ignored above). The pre-commit hook
# passes `--in-place`; a bare `docformatter src` only prints a diff. A couple of files are excluded
# from the hook (see prek.toml for which and why).
recursive = true
wrap-summaries = 100
wrap-descriptions = 100
pre-summary-newline = true

# docstring-reflow wraps the prose paragraphs docformatter leaves alone (it mistakes "word: text"
# for a field list). Same width, so the two tools never rewrite each other.
[tool.docstring-reflow]
wrap-length = 100

[tool.zuban]

disallow_untyped_defs = true
warn_unreachable = true
python_executable = ".venv/bin/python"

[tool.pycroscope]
# Directory to analyze (relative to pyproject.toml) and the import root for the src layout
paths = ["src/photo_tagger"]
import_paths = ["src"]

# Output one issue per line, easier to scan and grep.
output_format = "concise"

# Checks
possibly_undefined_name = true
unused_variable = true
value_always_true = true
use_fstrings = true
missing_return_annotation = true
missing_parameter_annotation = true
suggested_parameter_type = true
suggested_return_type = true
incompatible_override = true
missing_generic_parameters = true

# See https://github.com/JelleZijlstra/pycroscope/issues/499
internal_error = false

# Tests intentionally use loose typing and assert helpers that pycroscope would flag as suggestions
[[tool.pycroscope.overrides]]
module = "tests"
missing_return_annotation = false
missing_parameter_annotation = false
suggested_parameter_type = false
suggested_return_type = false

# The gui package (the Qt shell) is excluded from pycroscope wholesale via a file-level
# `# static analysis: ignore` header in each of its modules, because the lint job does not install
# the [gui] extra and pycroscope cannot import PySide6. See the note in gui/__init__.py.

[tool.bandit]
# packaging/ and telemetry/ are dev tooling (like tests/), not shipped app code. packaging/'s only
# flagged use is a fixed-args iconutil call; telemetry/dashboard.py builds read-only Analytics SQL
# from int-coerced window sizes (B608 false positives). ruff still covers both via per-file-ignores.
exclude_dirs = [".git", ".venv", "__pycache__", "tests", "packaging", "telemetry"]

[tool.bandit.assert_used]
skips = ['tests/test_*.py']

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--durations=10",
    "--import-mode=importlib",
    "--random-order",
    "--numprocesses=logical",
    "--dist=load",
    "--tb=short",
    "--verbose",
    "--cov=src/photo_tagger",
    "--cov-branch",
    "--cov-report=term-missing",
    "--cov-report=xml:reports/coverage.xml",
    "-m",
    "not integration",
]
markers = [
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests; deselect with '-m \"not integration\"'",
]
# Warnings are errors: a new DeprecationWarning from a dependency bump (the exact thing Renovate
# ships) must fail the suite instead of scrolling past. Add targeted `ignore::...` entries here
# when a third-party warning is genuinely not actionable.
filterwarnings = ["error"]

[tool.coverage.run]
# The PySide6 desktop window and its Qt event loop cannot run under the headless
# CI suite (no display, and the [gui] extra is intentionally not installed there).
# Its testable, Qt-free logic lives in the gui_state package, which is covered normally;
# the gui package is the widget/event-loop shell, exercised manually and by the
# offscreen-guarded tests in test_gui.py when PySide6 is present.
omit = ["src/photo_tagger/gui/*"]

# See https://github.com/seddonym/import-linter

[importlinter]
root_package = server
include_external_packages = True
exclude_type_checking_imports = True


[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Layered architecture of our project
type = layers

containers =
  server.apps.*

layers =
  (urls) | (admin)
  (views) | (htmx) | (api)
  (tasks)
  (infra)
  (models)
  (logic)


[importlinter:contract:apps-independence]
name = All apps must be independent
type = independence

modules =
  server.apps.*

ignore_imports =
  # This is hack we have to use due to models relations
  server.apps.*.admin -> server.apps.*.models
  # Pipeline services need prompts/assets models; deferred runtime imports
  server.apps.pipelines.services.prompt_renderer -> server.apps.prompts.models
  server.apps.pipelines.services.asset_writer -> server.apps.assets.models
  # Pipeline stages use generation provider clients (generation is a client
  # library whose sole consumer is pipeline stages — cross-app by design)
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.research -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.research -> server.apps.generation.clients.search
  # Channel research agent uses generation clients (same provider-library pattern)
  server.apps.channel_research.agent -> server.apps.generation.clients.search
  server.apps.channel_research.agent -> server.apps.generation.clients.dataforseo
  server.apps.channel_research.agent -> server.apps.generation.clients.youtube_search
  # Channel research agent uses NexLev as its YouTube data provider
  # (same provider-library pattern as the generation clients above)
  server.apps.channel_research.agent -> server.apps.nexlev.services
  server.apps.channel_research.logic.value_objects -> server.apps.nexlev.logic.value_objects
  server.apps.channel_research.selectors -> server.apps.nexlev.logic.value_objects
  server.apps.channel_research.tasks -> server.apps.nexlev.services
  server.apps.channel_research.tasks -> server.apps.nexlev.logic.value_objects
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.outline -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.script -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.scene_breakdown -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.visual_prompts -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.visual_anchors -> server.apps.generation.clients.fal
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.image_gen -> server.apps.generation.clients.fal
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.tts -> server.apps.generation.clients.elevenlabs
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.motion -> server.apps.generation.clients.fal
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.clip_transcribe -> server.apps.generation.clients.elevenlabs
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.music_plan -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.thumbnail -> server.apps.generation.clients.fal
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.metadata -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.narrative_qc -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_queries -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  # Footage search stage drives the stock provider registry, the AI fallback,
  # asset persistence, and ffprobe validation of downloaded media.
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_search -> server.apps.generation.clients.fal
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_search -> server.apps.generation.clients.llm
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_search -> server.apps.generation.clients.stock.base
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_search -> server.apps.generation.clients.stock.registry
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_search -> server.apps.assets.models
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_search -> server.apps.rendering.ffmpeg
  # Footage prep stage normalizes sourced media (video trim/loop or Ken
  # Burns) into scene segments, same asset/ffmpeg dependencies as above.
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_prep -> server.apps.assets.models
  server.apps.pipelines.stages.footage_prep -> server.apps.rendering.ffmpeg
  # Pipeline stages save assets and reference AssetKind from the assets app

package com.fabridinapoli.kotlinorms.architecturetest

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class HexagonalArchitectureTest {

    private val importedClasses = ClassFileImporter()
        .withImportOption(DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
        .importPackages("com.fabridinapoli.kotlinorms")

    @Test
    fun `domain should depend on domain only`() {
        classes()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("..domain..")
            .should()
            .onlyDependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage(
                "..domain..",
                "java..",
                "javax..",
                "org.jetbrains..",
                "kotlin..",
                "arrow.."
            )
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `application services should not depend on infrastructure`() {
        classes()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("..application..")
            .should()
            .onlyDependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage(
                "..domain..",
                "..application..",
                "java..",
                "javax..",
                "org.jetbrains..",
                "kotlin..",
                "arrow.."
            )
            .check(importedClasses)
    }
}
