[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["autoskillit"]
# Exclude imports made inside `if TYPE_CHECKING:` guards from all contracts.
# This is critical for execution/headless.py, which imports pipeline types only
# inside TYPE_CHECKING blocks to avoid circular imports at runtime.
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

# Contract IDs below use IL-NNN (three-digit serial numbers, e.g. IL-001).
# These are NOT import layer levels (IL-0 through IL-3).
# IL-002 = config's contract; IL-2 = the recipe/migration/fleet import layer.

# IL-001 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: IL-0 (core) is the foundation layer; it must have zero upward imports to
# remain independently testable and importable outside the autoskillit package.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-0 core has no autoskillit upward imports"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["autoskillit.core"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "autoskillit.config",
    "autoskillit.pipeline",
    "autoskillit.execution",
    "autoskillit.workspace",
    "autoskillit.recipe",
    "autoskillit.migration",
    "autoskillit.server",
    "autoskillit.cli",
]

# IL-002 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: IL-1 config resolves settings from layered sources; allowing it to import
# pipeline/execution/recipe would create hidden initialization-time coupling that
# breaks independent layered testing.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-1 config imports only IL-0"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["autoskillit.config"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "autoskillit.pipeline",
    "autoskillit.execution",
    "autoskillit.workspace",
    "autoskillit.recipe",
    "autoskillit.migration",
    "autoskillit.server",
    "autoskillit.cli",
]

# IL-003 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: pipeline/ holds cross-session gate and audit state; importing from IL-2
# (recipe, migration) would create initialization-order coupling and prevent IL-1
# packages from being tested in isolation without a full IL-2 import graph.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-1 pipeline does not import IL-2 or IL-3"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["autoskillit.pipeline"]
# EXCEPTION: autoskillit.config is intentionally omitted from the
# forbidden_modules list. pipeline.context.ToolContext owns
# AutomationConfig as the DI wiring point — see the docstrings on
# pipeline/context.py and pipeline/__init__.py. The coupling is safe
# because config/ depends only on IL-0 (enforced by IL-002), so no
# cycle is possible. This exception is asserted by
# tests/arch/test_import_linter_contracts.py
#     ::test_il003_pipeline_config_exception_documented.
forbidden_modules = [
    "autoskillit.execution",
    "autoskillit.workspace",
    "autoskillit.recipe",
    "autoskillit.migration",
    "autoskillit.server",
    "autoskillit.cli",
]

# IL-004 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: execution/ manages subprocess lifecycle; it must not import config,
# pipeline, workspace, recipe, migration, server, or cli to remain a leaf IL-1 service
# that can be tested without spinning up the full autoskillit stack.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-1 execution imports only IL-0"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["autoskillit.execution"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "autoskillit.config",
    "autoskillit.pipeline",
    "autoskillit.workspace",
    "autoskillit.recipe",
    "autoskillit.migration",
    "autoskillit.server",
    "autoskillit.cli",
]

# IL-005 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: workspace/ manages cloning and skill resolution; importing from config
# or pipeline would introduce a circular risk since config and pipeline both may
# depend on workspace for path resolution.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-1 workspace imports only IL-0"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["autoskillit.workspace"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "autoskillit.config",
    "autoskillit.pipeline",
    "autoskillit.execution",
    "autoskillit.recipe",
    "autoskillit.migration",
    "autoskillit.server",
    "autoskillit.cli",
]

# IL-006 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: recipe/ is an IL-2 service that orchestrates validation over workspace
# artifacts; importing config, pipeline, execution, migration, server, or cli
# would conflate recipe semantics with runtime session management.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-2 recipe imports only IL-0 and workspace"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["autoskillit.recipe"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "autoskillit.config",
    "autoskillit.pipeline",
    "autoskillit.execution",
    "autoskillit.migration",
    "autoskillit.server",
    "autoskillit.cli",
]

# IL-007 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: migration/ must not import config or pipeline to stay independently
# runnable as a schema-upgrade step without a live pipeline context.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-2 migration does not import IL-3 or config"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["autoskillit.migration"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "autoskillit.config",
    "autoskillit.pipeline",
    "autoskillit.server",
    "autoskillit.cli",
]

# IL-008 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: The four IL-1 peers (config, pipeline, execution, workspace) form an
# independent service tier. Lateral imports between them create hidden coupling
# that prevents each package from being tested and deployed in isolation. The
# independence contract makes this boundary machine-verifiable and surfaces any
# future regression immediately via lint-imports.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-1 siblings are independent of each other"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "autoskillit.config",
    "autoskillit.pipeline",
    "autoskillit.execution",
    "autoskillit.workspace",
]
# EXCEPTION: autoskillit.pipeline.context may import autoskillit.config.
# pipeline.context.ToolContext owns AutomationConfig as the DI wiring point.
# config/ depends only on IL-0 (IL-002), so no cycle is introduced.
# This exception mirrors the one already documented in IL-003.
ignore_imports = [
    "autoskillit.pipeline.context -> autoskillit.config",
]

# IL-009 | Lens: module-dependency | DS-001
# Rationale: fleet is IL-2 — imports IL-0 (core) only; workspace allowed for path utilities
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IL-2 fleet does not import IL-3 or most IL-1 peers"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["autoskillit.fleet"]
forbidden_modules = [
    # EXCEPTION: autoskillit.workspace is intentionally absent from this list.
    # fleet may import workspace solely for path-lookup utilities (e.g., worktree paths).
    # This is a deliberate, narrow allowance — do not expand workspace use in fleet
    # beyond path utilities without updating this contract and the rationale comment above.
    "autoskillit.config",
    "autoskillit.pipeline",
    "autoskillit.execution",
    "autoskillit.migration",
    "autoskillit.recipe",
    "autoskillit.server",
    "autoskillit.cli",
]

    cad_dxf_agent.llm

    cad_dxf_agent.models

# inspect_ai discovers third-party model providers via the `inspect_ai`
# entry-point group (importlib.metadata). When the [audit] extra is
# installed and `inspect eval` runs, inspect_ai loads each entry-point
# in this group (`ep.load()`) — that import triggers our
# `evals/petri/__init__.py:register()`, which registers
# `GeodeModelAPI` so `--model-role target=geode/<base>` resolves.
#
# PR #6 (2026-05-14) — multiple names point to the same module so that
# inspect_ai's ``ensure_entry_points(package=<prefix>)`` finds a matching
# ep regardless of which provider prefix appears in the model id. The
# fast-path matches ep.name == prefix (no full-load fallback needed), so
# ``openai-codex/gpt-5.5`` resolution loads ``evals.petri`` and
# its top-level ``register_codex()`` runs before the model lookup retries.
# Python's import system de-dupes the module so all registrations run
# exactly once per process.
#
# Reference: inspect_ai/_util/entrypoints.py:ensure_entry_points
[project.entry-points.inspect_ai]
geode_audit = "evals.petri"
geode = "evals.petri"
openai-codex = "evals.petri"
openai-platform = "evals.petri"

# v0.52 phase 6 — process binding 강제 (B2/B8 재발 방지)
# CLI/agent/server/channels 사이의 직접 import 를 정적 차단한다.
# 위반 시 `lint-imports` 실패 → CI 에서 PR merge 차단.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["core", "evals", "evolve"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "CLI must not import server/messaging (process boundary)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["core.cli"]
forbidden_modules = ["core.server", "core.messaging"]
# ``core.wiring`` is the legal outer-composition layer. This contract rejects
# CLI-owned process imports while allowing injected capabilities to traverse
# that composition boundary.
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Agent stays pure (no CLI/server)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["core.agent"]
forbidden_modules = ["core.cli", "core.server"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Server may host agent but never CLI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["core.server"]
forbidden_modules = ["core.cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Messaging integration is capability-pure (no process imports)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["core.messaging"]
forbidden_modules = ["core.cli", "core.server", "core.agent"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Runtime does not import evaluation or evolution"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["core"]
forbidden_modules = ["evals", "evolve"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Evaluation does not import evolution"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["evals"]
forbidden_modules = ["evolve"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Runtime tool handlers stay capability-neutral"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["core.tools.handlers"]
forbidden_modules = ["core.agent", "core.cli", "core.server", "core.ui"]
# This ownership rule targets direct imports; existing transitive core-tool
# dependencies remain governed by their owning layer contracts.
allow_indirect_imports = true

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100
# S-2 (2026-06-11) — "tests" removed from src roots: with the test tree on
# the source-mirror convention, tests/core/<pkg>/ made ruff's first-party
# resolver see a second `core.*` package under the tests root and silently
# flipped isort grouping for function-body import blocks.
src = ["core", "evals", "evolve", "scripts"]
extend-exclude = [
    ".geode",        # runtime config + skill scripts (not part of codebase)
    ".claude",       # Claude Code session artifacts
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Rule families:
#   E/F/W   pycodestyle + pyflakes baseline
#   I       isort
#   UP      pyupgrade — pin to py312 idioms
#   B       flake8-bugbear — common gotchas
#   SIM     flake8-simplify
#   S       flake8-bandit subset (overlaps bandit; keep both for dual coverage)
#   N       pep8-naming
#   C4      flake8-comprehensions
#   C901    mccabe cyclomatic complexity (per-function)
#   PLR     pylint refactor (max-args/branches/returns/statements)
#   TID     flake8-tidy-imports — banned APIs (TID251), relative imports (TID252)
#   RUF     ruff-specific
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "S", "N", "C4", "C901", "PLR", "TID", "RUF"]
ignore = [
    "S101",   # assert — used extensively in tests and fixture validation
    "S311",   # non-cryptographic random — intentional in data generator
    "N806",   # non-lowercase variable — FIXTURE_MAP, COMMAND_MAP patterns
    "N803",   # invalid argument name — LangGraph callback signatures
    "RUF001", # ambiguous unicode char in string — Korean/English mixed project
    "RUF002", # ambiguous unicode char in docstring
    "RUF003", # ambiguous unicode char in comment
    "RUF012", # mutable class default — Pydantic models handle this
    "RUF059", # unused unpacked variable — LangGraph stream event destructuring
    # PLR rule subset — informational rather than actionable for the current codebase:
    "PLR2004", # magic-value comparison — too noisy on score thresholds, status codes
    "PLR0904", # too-many-public-methods — incompatible with Pydantic / Typer command classes
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "S105", "S106", "S310", "B017", "E501", "PLR0915", "PLR0912", "PLR0913"]
"core/agent/bash_tool.py" = ["S602"]  # shell=True is intentional for agentic bash tool
# Manim visualization scripts use long literal vector / score lists; line-length not
# enforced on this path (mirrors the tests/** allowance).
"scripts/visualizations/**.py" = ["E501"]
# Generated terminal art: one long truecolor-ANSI string literal per pixel row.
"core/ui/geodi_art.py" = ["E501"]
# Generated inline-image data: one long base64 PNG string literal.

# Exact ceiling witnesses and symbol overrides are owned by
# docs/architecture/exception-debt.toml. CI probes Ruff one point below each
# value, rejects unregistered symbols, and requires this value to fall whenever
# the measured maximum falls.
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 52

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 23
max-branches = 51
max-returns = 18
max-statements = 207

# TID251 — banned imports with educational error messages (LangGraph pattern).
# Symbol-level guardrail complementary to import-linter (which is module-level
# layer enforcement). Use for transitional moves, deprecated aliases, and
# specific anti-pattern symbols outside import-linter's contract scope.
#
# Convention: keep the .msg short and uniform — `Moved to <new.path> (v<X.Y.Z> step <N>).`
# The "domain-free-core refactor" context is documented in CHANGELOG and
# docs/architecture/domain-free-core-audit.md; the ban message should be
# scannable, not explanatory.
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests"]
skips = ["B101", "B105", "B110", "B311", "B404", "B603", "B607"]

# deptry — dependency drift detection (unused/missing/transitive imports vs pyproject.toml).
# Run via `uv run deptry .` — see CI lint job.
[tool.deptry]
extend_exclude = [
    "tests",
    ".claude",
    ".geode",
    "scripts",
]
known_first_party = ["core", "evals", "evolve"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# DEP001 — imported module is provided by an opt-in external benchmark checkout,
# not by GEODE's default dependency set.
DEP001 = [
    # tau2-bench is installed under artifacts/eval/harnesses/tau2-bench by the
    # benchmark_harness plugin when live tau2 measurement is requested.
    "tau2",
    # MCPMark harness modules resolve via MCPMARK_ROOT sys.path insertion in
    # evals/benchmarks/mcpmark/runner.py; opt-in checkout, absent by default.
    "src",
    "pipeline",
]

# DEP002 — declared as dep but not imported anywhere by deptry's static scan.
# All entries below are confirmed-needed:
#   openai-agents: kept for Responses-API runtime path even when no static
#       import exists in core/ today; removing it would break the optional
#       agents harness when re-enabled. Re-evaluate if/when that surface
#       is fully retired.
#   Pillow: imported as `PIL` from core/tools/computer_use.py (desktop extra).
DEP002 = [
    "openai-agents",
    "Pillow",
    # `inspect-petri` is loaded via inspect_ai's evaluation harness
    # (its `audit` task is referenced as `inspect_petri/audit` from the
    # CLI), not by direct import in our code. The [audit] extra still

# Pillar 2 of the testing-foundation-sprint (parent ticket 86b9ve0wa,
# this Bit 86b9ve0yt). Declares structural import-layer contracts that
# import-linter enforces in CI via the `lint-imports` step in
# .github/workflows/test.yml + deploy.yml. Contracts intentionally
# reflect REALITY on current main, not aspirations — running
# `lint-imports` from the repo root must pass on the commit that
# ships this file.
#
# Each contract uses the `forbidden` type (source_modules cannot reach
# forbidden_modules in the import graph). grimp resolves the package
# tree from `root_package = bot` below.
#
# AC item "No module imports `from bot._impl import *`" is enforced
# separately by tests/contracts/test_no_impl_star_import.py — import-linter sees
# star imports as regular imports of the source module, indistinguishable
# from `import bot._impl` for graph purposes, so the wildcard ban needs
# AST-level detection.

[importlinter]
# D1.1 (ticket 86b9ypn49, 2026-05-16) — Data Corpus collector/ scaffolding.
# Singular `root_package = bot` flipped to plural `root_packages = bot, collector`
# so grimp walks BOTH packages and the new `collector-no-bot` forbidden
# contract below has source-modules to scan. Without the plural flip, the
# new contract would silently no-op (no edges to forbid because grimp wouldn't
# see collector/ at all). Pinned by tests/contracts/test_collector_no_bot_imports.py
# ::test_importlinter_root_packages_is_plural_form (configparser-level check
# that the singular key is absent and both `bot` + `collector` appear in the
# plural list).
#
# D1.1.5 (ticket 86b9zdhz2, 2026-05-16) — extended with `kalshi_wire` for
# the shared transport library (RSA-PSS auth + WS connect/reconnect/subscribe
# protocol + bronze envelope). Same plural-list requirement: without listing
# `kalshi_wire`, grimp wouldn't walk it and the two new `kalshi_wire-no-*`
# forbidden contracts would silently no-op. Pinned by
# tests/contracts/test_kalshi_wire_no_bot.py
# ::test_importlinter_root_packages_includes_kalshi_wire.
#
# D2.1 (ticket 86b9zkpc6, 2026-05-17) — extended with `coinbase_wire` for
# the Coinbase-side shared transport library (HMAC-SHA256 auth + WS
# connect/reconnect + bronze envelope). Sub-Bit of the 86b9zkkv4 D2.x
# umbrella. Same plural-list requirement as kalshi_wire: without listing
# `coinbase_wire`, grimp wouldn't walk it and the two new
# `coinbase_wire-no-*` forbidden contracts would silently no-op. Pinned by
# tests/contracts/test_coinbase_wire_no_bot_imports.py
# ::test_importlinter_root_packages_includes_coinbase_wire.
#
# D3.0 (ticket 86b9zxc6t, 2026-05-18) — extended with `silver` for the
# off-VPS silver ETL layer (dbt-style DuckDB normalization reading bronze
# JSONL.zst chunks from S3 and writing partitioned Parquet to
# `silver/v1/<source>/utc_date=...`). First Bit of Phase 2 (Silver).
# Same plural-list requirement: without listing `silver`, grimp wouldn't
# walk it and the two new `silver-no-*` forbidden contracts would
# silently no-op. Pinned by
# tests/contracts/test_silver_no_bot_imports.py
# ::test_importlinter_root_packages_includes_silver.
root_packages =
    bot
    collector
    kalshi_wire
    coinbase_wire
    silver
# Bit 12.3 (Sprint 12, 2026-05-11): required for the bot-no-torch
# and bot-no-pandas contracts, which name EXTERNAL packages (torch,
# pandas) as forbidden_modules. Without this flag, import-linter

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sprint 6 (Bits 6.1 + 6.2 + 6.3) extracted VolatilityEngine,
# ProbabilityEngine, and CalibrationEngine into bot/engines/. The original

name = bot.feeds.* must not import bot.engines.*

forbidden_modules =

# Contract 4 — helpers leaf rule
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bit 3.2 extracted bot/helpers/ as the leaf-most subpackage: helpers

# IMPORTANT — implementation note: import-linter's `forbidden` contract

# contract generalizes to ALL bot.* modules. torch is reachable
# transitively via scripts/cal_mlp/integration.py (NOT under bot/), so
# the contract correctly allows that path. Bit 12.3 (Sprint 12,
# 2026-05-11).
[importlinter:contract:bot-no-torch]
name = bot.* must not import torch directly (cal_mlp/integration.py is the single torch entry point)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    bot
forbidden_modules =

# Per kb/decisions/data-corpus-architecture.md §5 (collector process shape)
# + §10 (bot-isolation contract mechanism #5), the collector/ package MUST
# contain zero `bot.*` imports — the structural enforcement of the
# isolation invariant "collector failure ⇒ bot keeps trading; bot failure
# ⇒ collector keeps capturing."
#
# Listing `bot` (not `bot.X` for each subpackage) in forbidden_modules
# covers every bot.* subpackage via grimp's package-tree resolution —
# any `from bot[.X] import …` or `import bot[.X]` edge from any collector
# module fails the contract.
#
# v1 stance (D0.3 §5 paragraph 6): if a future collector submodule
# genuinely needs an auth/etc. utility that bot/ also uses, DUPLICATE
# the minimum (~20 LOC for RSA-PSS-SHA256) rather than introduce the
# first cross-package coupling. Re-evaluate at D1.5 if drift becomes a
# problem. No ignore_imports carve-out at D1.1.
#
# Peer-pinned by tests/contracts/test_collector_no_bot_imports.py
# (AST defense-in-depth + negative-injection mutation test that
# verifies lint-imports actually catches a forbidden edge).
[importlinter:contract:collector-no-bot]
name = collector.* must not import bot.* (D0.3 bot-isolation contract)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    collector
forbidden_modules =
    bot

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 9 — kalshi_wire must not import bot (pure-transport leaf)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D1.1.5 (ticket 86b9zdhz2, 2026-05-16) — Per the 2026-05-16 AMENDMENT to
# kb/decisions/data-corpus-architecture.md §5 (which SUPERSEDED §5 ¶6+7
# after external-advisor pivot), `kalshi_wire/` is the shared transport
# library consumed by BOTH bot/feeds/kalshi.py AND collector/ws_connection.py.
# The "two sides of the same coin" symmetry requires that the wire layer
# is bot-state-free: reaching into bot/ would couple the collector's view
# to bot-specific machinery (orderbook cache, schema probes, blacklist).
#
# Listing `bot` (not `bot.X` for each subpackage) covers every bot.X
# subpackage via grimp's package-tree resolution — any `from bot[.X]
# import …` or `import bot[.X]` edge from any kalshi_wire module fails.
#
# Sibling-package status (NOT a `bot/` subpackage) makes this contract
# enforceable structurally — `kalshi_wire/` lives at repo-root next to
# `bot/` and `collector/`.
#
# Peer-pinned by tests/contracts/test_kalshi_wire_no_bot.py (AST
# defense-in-depth + negative-injection mutation test that verifies
# lint-imports actually catches a forbidden edge).
[importlinter:contract:kalshi_wire-no-bot]
name = kalshi_wire.* must not import bot.* (pure-transport leaf)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    kalshi_wire
forbidden_modules =
    bot

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 10 — kalshi_wire must not import collector (pure-transport leaf)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D1.1.5 (ticket 86b9zdhz2, 2026-05-16) — Sister contract to
# `kalshi_wire-no-bot`. The dependency arrow is consumer → wire, never
# wire → consumer:
#
#     bot.feeds.kalshi        ─┐
#                              ├─→ kalshi_wire
#     collector.ws_connection  ┘
#
# A `kalshi_wire → collector` edge would invert the layering, couple the
# wire library to the bronze-archival pipeline, and break the symmetry
# that makes the advisor's "two sides of the same coin" actually work.
#
# Peer-pinned by tests/contracts/test_kalshi_wire_no_collector.py.
[importlinter:contract:kalshi_wire-no-collector]
name = kalshi_wire.* must not import collector.* (pure-transport leaf)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    kalshi_wire
forbidden_modules =
    collector

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 11 — coinbase_wire must not import bot (pure-transport leaf)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D2.1 (ticket 86b9zkpc6, 2026-05-17) — sub-Bit of the 86b9zkkv4 D2.x
# Coinbase WS bronzing umbrella. Mirrors the D1.1.5 `kalshi_wire-no-bot`
# pattern for the Coinbase wire surface. `coinbase_wire/` is the shared
# transport library that will (post-D2.1.5 body) be consumed by BOTH
# `bot/feeds/coinbase.py` AND `collector/coinbase_archiver.py` (the
# future D2.2 archiver). The "two sides of the same coin" symmetry
# requires that the wire layer is bot-state-free: reaching into bot/
# would couple the collector's view of the Coinbase wire to bot-specific
# machinery (cross-exchange feed cache, blacklist, schema probes).
#
# D2.1 ships SCAFFOLDING ONLY — empty stub `coinbase_wire/__init__.py`
# + `auth.py` + `ws_client.py`. The contract is pinned NOW so the body
# implementer at D2.1.5 cannot accidentally introduce a bot.* edge.
#
# Listing `bot` (not `bot.X` for each subpackage) covers every bot.X
# subpackage via grimp's package-tree resolution — any `from bot[.X]
# import …` or `import bot[.X]` edge from any coinbase_wire module fails.
#
# Sibling-package status (NOT a `bot/` subpackage) makes this contract
# enforceable structurally — `coinbase_wire/` lives at repo-root next
# to `bot/`, `collector/`, and `kalshi_wire/`.
#
# Peer-pinned by tests/contracts/test_coinbase_wire_no_bot_imports.py
# (AST defense-in-depth + negative-injection mutation test that
# verifies lint-imports actually catches a forbidden edge).
[importlinter:contract:coinbase_wire-no-bot]
name = coinbase_wire.* must not import bot.* (pure-transport leaf)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    coinbase_wire
forbidden_modules =
    bot

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 12 — coinbase_wire must not import collector (pure-transport leaf)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D2.1 (ticket 86b9zkpc6, 2026-05-17) — Sister contract to
# `coinbase_wire-no-bot`. Mirrors the D1.1.5 `kalshi_wire-no-collector`
# pattern. The dependency arrow is consumer → wire, never wire → consumer:
#
#     bot.feeds.coinbase           ─┐
#                                   ├─→ coinbase_wire
#     collector.coinbase_archiver   ┘
#
# A `coinbase_wire → collector` edge would invert the layering, couple
# the wire library to the bronze-archival pipeline, and break the
# symmetry that makes "two sides of the same coin" actually work.
#
# Peer-pinned by tests/contracts/test_coinbase_wire_no_collector.py.
[importlinter:contract:coinbase_wire-no-collector]
name = coinbase_wire.* must not import collector.* (pure-transport leaf)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    coinbase_wire
forbidden_modules =
    collector

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 13 — silver must not import bot (pure off-VPS ETL surface)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D3.0 (ticket 86b9zxc6t, 2026-05-18) — First Bit of Phase 2 (Silver).
# Plan doc: `kb/decisions/d3-0-silver-foundations-plan.md`.
#
# `silver/` is the dbt-style normalization layer that reads bronze JSONL.zst
# chunks from S3 (via DuckDB's S3 connector + `read_json`) and writes typed
# Parquet to `silver/v1/<source>/utc_date=YYYY-MM-DD/`. It runs OFF the bot
# VPS (operator Mac via launchd nightly @ 02:00 local, per the D0.3 §13
# off-VPS-compute decision) and consumes ONLY bronze + silver state.
#
# A `silver → bot` edge would (a) require Python paths from the bot VPS
# to be reachable on the ETL host, (b) couple analyst-tier queries to
# trading-state internals, (c) break the same isolation discipline that
# kalshi_wire / coinbase_wire / collector enforce in the bronze tier.
#
# Pinned by tests/contracts/test_silver_no_bot_imports.py.
[importlinter:contract:silver-no-bot]
name = silver.* must not import bot.* (pure off-VPS ETL surface)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    silver
forbidden_modules =
    bot

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 14 — silver must not import collector (pure off-VPS ETL surface)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D3.0 (ticket 86b9zxc6t, 2026-05-18) — sister contract to `silver-no-bot`.
#
# Silver reads bronze via DuckDB's S3 connector (`read_json('s3://...')`),
# NOT via collector's writer/uploader code. The two have parallel views of
# bronze format (D0.3 §2 envelope is the shared contract), but neither
# imports the other. A `silver → collector` edge would couple the ETL
# layer to the bronze-archival pipeline and invert the medallion
# direction-of-flow (bronze produces; silver consumes; silver does not
# loop back to the producer).
#
# Peer-pinned by tests/contracts/test_silver_no_bot_imports.py
# ::test_importlinter_declares_silver_no_collector_contract.
[importlinter:contract:silver-no-collector]
name = silver.* must not import collector.* (pure off-VPS ETL surface)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    silver
forbidden_modules =
    collector

# Bit 1.1 of repo modularization plan (kb/decisions/repo-modularization-plan-may05.md).
# Sprint 1 shipped this file as tooling-only metadata (py-modules+packages
# explicit-empty). Sprint 2 Bit 2.1a renamed bot.py → bot/_impl.py and 2.1b
# made the bot/ package installable via [tool.setuptools.packages.find] below.

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=64", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "kalshi-bot"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Cryptocurrency prediction market trading bot for Kalshi (15-minute crypto windows + observation engines)."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.9,<4"
# Runtime deps. Mirror requirements.txt EXACTLY (bidirectional) —
# tests/unit/test_pyproject.py asserts the symmetric difference is empty so the
# two cannot drift. requirements.txt remains the CI / VPS install path
# (see .github/workflows/test.yml + start.sh); pyproject deps are the
# packaging-tool view of the same set.
dependencies = [
    "requests",
    "websocket-client",
    "websockets",
    "cryptography",
    # D1.2 (ticket 86b9ypn66, 2026-05-16) — Data Corpus bronze archiver.
    # zstandard is the in-process compressor for the rotation handler
    # in collector/writer.py::BronzeWriter._rotate (zstd level 6 per
    # kb/decisions/data-corpus-architecture.md §7; operator-side bulk
    # re-compression may use level 9-19 at silver-tier backfill time).
    # Chosen over shell-out to the `zstd` binary because: (a) testable
    # without subprocess mocking, (b) avoids fork+exec overhead per
    # rotation (~50/hr × 18 conn-channels at full peak), (c) explicit
    # version pin shipped via this file. Required by collector/ ONLY;
    # bot/ continues to have zero zstd touchpoints (rotate_journals.sh
    # shells to the binary, but it's a bash script not a bot/ module).
    "zstandard",
    # P1-A (ticket 86ba1pqqx, 2026-05-20) — orjson replaces stdlib json
    # in collector/writer.py::BronzeWriter.write (3-5× faster, returns
    # bytes directly, releases GIL identically). Required by collector/
    # write path; not used elsewhere. Without this entry the pyproject↔
    # requirements.txt drift check (tests/unit/test_pyproject.py::
    # test_pyproject_runtime_deps_match_requirements_txt) fails.
    "orjson",
    "scipy",
    "numpy",
    "lightgbm",
    "scikit-learn",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Install with: pip install -e .[dev]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8",
    # Ruff 0.5 introduced the [tool.ruff.lint] table; <0.5 silently no-ops
    # on the `select` list because it expected the deprecated top-level form.
    # Pin floor + cap < 1 to track the 0.x release line until ruff stabilizes.
    "ruff>=0.6,<1",
    "tomli; python_version < '3.11'",
    # Pillar 1 of the testing-foundation-sprint: griffe powers the public-API
    # contract snapshot at tests/contracts/public_api.json (consumed by
    # tests/contracts/test_public_api_snapshot.py). Adds a structural gate
    # for the bot.* public surface; complements (does not replace) the
    # per-Bit AST source-grep tests in test_*_extraction.py (which check
    # _impl.py source content + runtime identity that griffe can't see).
    #
    # PINNED TIGHTLY: griffe's serialization changed substantially between
    # 1.0 (slash-separated paths, ~5,200 entries) and 1.14 (dot-separated
    # paths, ~3,700 entries). The same source produces wildly different
    # snapshots across the 1.x range. Pin to a single minor (1.14.x) so
    # the snapshot is stable; bump deliberately when a new minor ships.
    "griffe>=1.14,<1.15",
    # Pillar 2 of the testing-foundation-sprint: import-linter declares
    # layering contracts in `.importlinter` and the `lint-imports` CLI
    # fails on violation. The contract surface (engines/fetchers/feeds/
    # helpers boundaries + the documented Bit 6.2 ignore_imports carve-out
    # for the probability.py late-binding) is wired into CI as a blocking
    # gate alongside pytest in test.yml + deploy.yml.
    #
    # Pin floor at 2.5 (the version that landed on PyPI when Pillar 2
    # shipped — same self-test discipline as griffe). Cap < 3 to track
    # the v2.x release line; bump deliberately when v3 ships and the
    # ignore_imports / forbidden contract syntax has been reverified.
    "import-linter>=2.5,<3",
    # Pillar 3 of the testing-foundation-sprint: equivalence harness for
    # bot/engines/ extractions. Three deps:
    #   * hypothesis powers property-based tests with hand-written
    #     strategies (engine inputs are tightly bounded; polyfactory
    #     would generate impossible inputs without heavy filtering).
    #   * pytest-regressions provides num_regression for numeric
    #     snapshots with built-in tolerance + NaN handling. Chosen over
    #     syrupy (which is heavier and overkill for primarily-numeric
    #     engine outputs).
    #   * pyarrow reads tests/fixtures/engine_inputs.parquet. Already
    #     listed under [ml] for cal_mlp paths; duplicated here so the
    #     equivalence suite installs without the full ml extra.
    #
    # Same pinning discipline as griffe/import-linter: floor at the
    # version that landed when the Pillar shipped, cap below the next
    # major. Snapshot stability + property-test reproducibility across
    # the entire pin range is what's load-bearing here.
    "hypothesis>=6.100,<7",
    "pytest-regressions>=2.5,<3",
    "pyarrow>=14,<22",
    # pytest-regressions.num_regression requires pandas at call time
    # (DataFrame is the on-disk snapshot format). Listed here even
    # though pandas is also under [ml] — dev installs without ml
    # would otherwise crash the equivalence suite at fixture-call
    # time with a ModuleNotFoundError chain that's two layers deep.
    "pandas>=2,<3",
    # Pillar 5 of the testing-foundation-sprint: tiered suite + testmon
    # incremental runs + mutmut mutation-survival baseline.
    #
    # pytest-testmon: skips tests unaffected by a code change. Backs
    # `make test-affected` (≈sub-second when nothing relevant moved).
    # Pinned to 2.x — 1.x had a different cache layout (.testmondata
    # vs .testmon).
    "pytest-testmon>=2.1,<3",
    # pytest-clarity: improves assert-failure diff rendering. Loaded
    # automatically when installed (no addopts entry needed). Pinned
    # to 1.x — stable for years, the v2 milestone hasn't shipped yet
    # so a `<2` cap is the next bump-trigger.
    "pytest-clarity>=1,<2",
    # mutmut: mutation-testing harness. Pillar 5 runs a one-time
    # baseline against bot/engines/{volatility,probability}.py to
    # grade the equivalence harness's effectiveness. Pinned to 2.x —
    # 3.x is a rewrite with a different config schema and runner
    # contract; stay on 2.x until the 3.x ergonomics settle.
    "mutmut>=2.4,<3",
    # Bit-5 (CI perf umbrella 86b9zjtzk): parallel test execution on
    # the integration tier via `pytest -n auto --dist=loadfile`.
    # `--dist=loadfile` keeps all tests in one file on the same worker
    # so module-scoped fixtures + intra-file shared state stay coherent.
    # Pinned to 3.x — current major; cap at <4 to require deliberate
    # bump on any future 4.x release.
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5,<4",
    # Bit-9 (CI perf umbrella 86b9zjtzk, ticket 86b9zkk5j, 2026-05-17):
    # hash-balanced test sharding so the post-Bit-5+7 integration-tier
    # job (the long pole at ~2:08 wall) splits into 2 concurrent GH
    # jobs running ~half the test corpus each. pytest-shard adds
    # `--shard-id=N --num-shards=M` flags that hash test IDs evenly
    # across N shards. Stable across runs (same test always lands in
    # same shard) so xdist + shard compose deterministically.
    # 0.1.x pinned floor — only published series; cap <2 to require
    # deliberate bump on any future 1.x release.
    "pytest-shard>=0.1.2,<2",
]
# ML extras used by cal_mlp + analysis paths. Not required for the live bot
# loop, so kept optional.
ml = [
    "torch",
    # pandas + pyarrow pinned to the same major-range bands as `[dev]`
    # (Pillar 3) so a user installing only `[ml]` doesn't end up on a
    # different pandas/pyarrow than the equivalence suite was tested
    # against — silent skew between extras is a drift class we don't
    # need.
    "pandas>=2,<3",
    "pyarrow>=14,<22",
]

# Scope setuptools' flat-layout discovery to the bot/ + collector/ packages.
# Without `include`, setuptools >=64 walks the repo root and finds 9 sibling
# top-level Python-identifier directories besides bot/ (agent_docs/, analysis/,
# data/, kb/, models/, ops/, reports/, research/, templates/ — none have
# __init__.py but PEP 420 namespace discovery treats them as packages anyway;
# scripts/, tests/, build/, dist/, venv/ etc. are filtered by setuptools'
# curated _EXCLUDE list). With multiple top-level candidates, setuptools
# aborts `pip install -e .` with PackageDiscoveryError("Multiple top-level
# packages discovered in a flat-layout"). The Bit 1.1 hand-off note's claim
# that flat-layout discovery "picks up bot/ correctly" only held in a
# pristine bot-only repo; this repo has many sibling dirs.
#
# `include = ["bot", "bot.*", "collector", "collector.*", "kalshi_wire",
# "kalshi_wire.*"]`: fnmatch-matches each parent package + every subpackage.
# The "bot.*" / "collector.*" / "kalshi_wire.*" patterns require a literal
# dot so they don't match the bare parent names — both patterns are needed
# for each package. D1.1 (ticket 86b9ypn49, 2026-05-16) added the collector
# entries when the Data Corpus initiative shipped the collector/ top-level
# package. D1.1.5 (ticket 86b9zdhz2, 2026-05-16) added the kalshi_wire entries
# when the 2026-05-16 AMENDMENT to D0.3 §5 introduced the shared transport
# library (sibling to bot/ and collector/, consumed by both, zero bot.* /
# collector.* imports per the `kalshi_wire-no-bot` + `kalshi_wire-no-collector`
# .importlinter contracts). D2.1 (ticket 86b9zkpc6, 2026-05-17) added the
# coinbase_wire entries when the sub-Bit of the 86b9zkkv4 D2.x Coinbase WS
# bronzing umbrella introduced the Coinbase-side wire library (sibling to
# bot/, collector/, kalshi_wire/; pure-transport leaf per the new
# `coinbase_wire-no-bot` + `coinbase_wire-no-collector` .importlinter
# contracts; D2.1 ships SCAFFOLDING ONLY with empty stub bodies — D2.1.5
# lands the HMAC + WSClient body).
# `namespaces = false`: defense-in-depth — gates discovery on __init__.py
# existence so a future include-pattern broadening can't silently sweep in
# a PEP 420 namespace dir.
# Pinned by tests/unit/test_pyproject.py::test_pyproject_packages_find_scoped_to_bot_and_collector_and_wire.
[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["bot", "bot.*", "collector", "collector.*", "kalshi_wire", "kalshi_wire.*", "coinbase_wire", "coinbase_wire.*"]
namespaces = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Ported verbatim from the deleted pytest.ini. Pytest prefers pytest.ini over
# pyproject.toml when both exist — see test_pytest_ini_removed for the guard
# that prevents it from coming back.
testpaths = ["."]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "integration: marks integration tests",
    "smoke: marks quick smoke tests for CI",
    "fragile: marks tests that verify code structure via string matching (non-blocking in CI)",
    "serial: test must run in a single worker — CPU/timing sensitive under pytest-xdist (Bit-5)",
]
# List form (not space-split string) is shell-safe — pytest splits the
# string on whitespace, so a future flag value with a space would silently
# misroute.
addopts = ["--tb=short", "--ignore=venv"]

# Pillar 5: mutmut configuration. One-time baseline run against the
# extracted engines (Bits 6.1+6.2) to grade the equivalence harness
# (Pillar 3) — every surviving mutant is a hole in the test suite.
#
# `paths_to_mutate` is intentionally narrow. bot/_impl.py is huge,
# slow to mutate, and the equivalence harness doesn't pin it directly;
# revisit once more of _impl is extracted into typed engines. Helpers
# (bot/helpers/) are leaf utilities and can fold in later.
#
# `runner` points at the equivalence suite — that's the sole consumer
# of these engines' public surface in Pillar 3. Using -x for fail-fast
# keeps each mutant cycle fast (~3s for the equivalence pass × ~hundreds
# of mutants = ~1-2h on Mac).
#
# The two late-binding `from bot import _impl as _bot_impl` shims
# inside `ProbabilityEngine.compute()` and `counterfactual_prob()`
# (Bit 6.2 — see `kb/decisions/bit-6.2-shipped-may09.md` for why
# the imports are inside method bodies rather than at module top)
# are NOT excluded here: mutmut 2.x's AST walker skips `import_name`
# and `import_from` nodes by design — there's no operator/literal/
# comparison to flip on an import statement, so no mutants are
# generated. The invariant is "method-body import statements".
# Specific line numbers and mutmut source-file refs are intentionally
# omitted because Bit 6.3 (CalibrationEngine extraction) and any
# future mutmut bump would shift them.
#
# If a future mutmut version starts mutating imports, revisit by
# either (a) adding `# pragma: no mutate` inline (touches
# bot/engines/probability.py) or (b) adding a regex-based skip in
# this section.
# `paths_to_mutate` is a TOML list rather than a comma-separated string:
# mutmut 2.5.1's `split_paths` (mutmut/__main__.py:320) filters with
# `Path(p).exists()` and does NOT strip whitespace, so a cosmetic edit
# to the string form (e.g., "a.py, b.py" with one space) silently drops
# the second entry. The list form sidesteps the whitespace fragility
# entirely. Pinned by `tests/unit/test_pyproject.py::test_pyproject_mutmut_targets_engines`.
[tool.mutmut]
paths_to_mutate = ["bot/engines/volatility.py", "bot/engines/probability.py"]
runner = "python3 -m pytest -x tests/equivalence/test_volatility_engine.py tests/equivalence/test_probability_engine.py"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py39"
# Don't fight existing line lengths in bot/_impl.py / dashboards. Sprint 1 is
# "ruff runs and reports", not "ruff is clean".
line-length = 120
# Patterns are unanchored — they match a directory of that name at any
# depth. That's what we want here: `kb/` should be excluded wherever it
# appears. Ruff's defaults already cover venv/.venv/dist/build/.ruff_cache/
# .pytest_cache/__pycache__/.git — don't relist.
# `research/` deliberately NOT excluded — autoresearch (per
# kb/decisions/autoresearch-design-may05.md) ships Python under research/
# and we want it linted when it lands.
# Regression: tests/unit/test_pyproject.py::test_extend_exclude_actually_excludes
# verifies these patterns are functional, not just declarative.
extend-exclude = [
    ".smart-env",
    "kb",
    "kb-research",
    "agent_docs",
    "models",
    "data",
    "reports",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Lenient per Bit 1.1 spec. Pycodestyle errors (E) + Pyflakes (F) only;
# import sorting (I), naming (N), bugbear (B), etc. deferred until later
# sprints. Goal here is "ruff check . exits with a count", not a clean repo.
select = ["E", "F"]
ignore = []
# Sprint 1 spec: "don't fix yet". Empty fixable list neutralizes
# `ruff check . --fix` so a contributor (or IDE-on-save) can't silently
# mutate bot/_impl.py, which is sacred per CLAUDE.md. Future sprints can flip
# this once targeted cleanup is in scope.
fixable = []

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests routinely have unused imports (fixtures via side-effect) and long
# assertion strings. Don't drown the signal in test noise.
# Bit 1.5 consolidated root test_*.py files into tests/regression/, so
# the legacy `test_*.py` pattern (originally a second entry alongside
# `tests/**`) was dropped. The repo-root invariant is enforced by
# tests/unit/test_no_root_test_files.py.
"tests/**" = ["E501", "F401", "F811"]
"conftest.py" = ["E501", "F401", "F811"]
# research/scratch/ is reference-only space (Bit 1.5 landed dead-code
# HAR files there with `pytest.skip(allow_module_level=True)` followed
# by imports — i.e., E402 by design). The autoresearch comment under
# `[tool.ruff]` (research/ NOT extend-excluded) targets *active*
# research code that ships under research/<topic>/, not scratchpads.
# Adding E402 here on top of the standard tests-style trio because the
# skip-then-import pattern is the whole point of the file.
"research/scratch/**" = ["E402", "E501", "F401", "F811"]

[importlinter]
root_packages = uon

[importlinter:contract:1]
name = Cross-Domain Independence (No Lateral Imports)
type = independence

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
include = ["tracertm*"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "-vv",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--tb=short",
    "-p",
    "asyncio",
]
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests (fast, no external dependencies)",
    "integration: Integration tests (database, file system)",
    "e2e: End-to-end tests (full CLI workflows)",
    "cli: CLI command tests",
    "slow: Slow tests (>1s execution time)",
    "agent: Agent coordination tests (concurrent operations)",
    "asyncio: Async tests (mark for async tests)",
    "performance: Performance and load tests",
    "property: Property-based tests using Hypothesis",
    "benchmark: Benchmark tests for performance measurement",
    "smoke: Minimal critical-path checks",
    "chaos: Chaos/resilience tests (connection failures, resource exhaustion)",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning",
    "ignore::pytest.PytestAssertRewriteWarning",
    "ignore::RuntimeWarning",
]

[tool.pytest_asyncio]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/tracertm"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/migrations/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/site-packages/*",
]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
fail_under = 90
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "except (ImportError|Exception|ModuleNotFoundError).*:",
    "except ImportError:",
    "except Exception:.*# (test )?fallback",
]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

[tool.interrogate]
# Docstring coverage; used by pre-commit and `interrogate` CLI. Keep in sync with .pre-commit-config.yaml.
fail-under = 85
path = ["src/"]
exclude = ["tests", "build", "dist", ".venv"]
ignore-init-module = true
ignore-init-method = true

[tool.bandit]
# Security linter; complements ruff S rules and semgrep. Run: bandit -r src/
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "build", "dist", ".venv", "ARCHIVE"]
skips = ["B101"]  # assert_used: allow in tests (tests excluded); optional in dev
severity = "medium"
confidence = "medium"

[tool.ruff]
# Ruff output format: use --output-format=grouped for file-grouped output
# This groups issues by file for easy processing by agents (easier to fix)
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
preview = true
# Vendored/archived/third-party code: do not lint.
extend-exclude = ["ARCHIVE", "ARCHIVE/**", "cairosvg", "default"]
# Skip ARCHIVE even when a file under ARCHIVE is passed directly (e.g. by IDE).
force-exclude = true

[tool.ty]

[tool.ty.src]
# Exclude vendored/archived code, scripts, optional TUI/vault, and tests that use optional deps or conditional types.
include = ["src", "tests"]
exclude = [
    "ARCHIVE",
    "ARCHIVE/**",
    "ARCHIVE/CONFIG/default",
    "backend/tests",
    "cli",
    "cli/tests",
    "frontend/disable",
    "scripts",
    "scripts/**",
    "src/tracertm/vault",
    "src/tracertm/vault/**",
    "tests/unit/validation/test_dataframe_schema_validation.py",
]
respect-ignore-files = true

# Component storage: SyncEngine/SyncQueue/SyncStateManager use mocks (MockDBConnection, SimpleNamespace); method shadowing in test_sync_queue.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = [
    "tests/component/storage/test_sync_engine_errors.py",
    "tests/component/storage/test_sync_queue.py",
]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"
invalid-assignment = "ignore"

# Root conftest: optional router/textual imports, Base fallback, router/registry fixtures when module missing.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["conftest.py", "tests/conftest.py"]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
unresolved-import = "ignore"
invalid-assignment = "ignore"
call-non-callable = "ignore"

# E2E and fixtures: project.id/item.id are UUID; service/repo APIs expect str.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["tests/e2e/**", "tests/fixtures.py"]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"

# Integration workflows: sync Session passed to ProjectRepository (expects AsyncSession in type hint).
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["tests/integration/workflows/**"]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"

# MCP tests: optional auth APIs (_build_static_verifier, CompositeTokenVerifier), fastmcp ToolError/parse_scopes; parse_scopes return type.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["tests/mcp/**"]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
unresolved-import = "ignore"
unknown-argument = "ignore"
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"
unsupported-operator = "ignore"

# Performance tests: optional locust/psutil; UUID->str for item_service; result may be None before .id.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["tests/performance/**"]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
unresolved-import = "ignore"
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"
possibly-missing-attribute = "ignore"

# item_specs router: response models (EARSAnalysisResponse, QualityScoreResponse, MerkleProofResponse, VersionChainResponse, ContentAddressResponse, etc.) and router construction are out of sync; optional request bodies; redundant cast for adjacency/item_metadata.

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
missing-argument = "ignore"
unknown-argument = "ignore"
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"
invalid-parameter-default = "ignore"
invalid-return-type = "ignore"
redundant-cast = "ignore"

# API main router: complex runtime validation and dynamic payloads.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["src/tracertm/api/main.py"]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"
no-matching-overload = "ignore"
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
possibly-missing-attribute = "ignore"
invalid-assignment = "ignore"

# GitHub handlers: repository interfaces and webhook models are dynamically typed.

include = ["src/tracertm/api/handlers/github.py"]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]

include = ["src/tracertm/observability/**"]
[tool.ty.overrides.rules]

unresolved-attribute = "ignore"

include = ["src/tracertm/repositories/**", "tracertm/repositories/**"]

  "D203",
  "D213",
  # The formatter owns line length.
  "E501",
  # The __all__ lists are grouped by domain with comments; a sort would destroy the grouping.
  "RUF022",

  "TRY003"

  "ANN",
  "ARG",
  "B",
  "C4",
  "C90",
  "D",
  "E",
  "F",
  "I",
  "N",
  "PIE",

  "PT",

  "RUF",

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Examples are narrative walkthroughs: they print, and their main functions are long.
"examples/*" = ["C901", "PLR0915", "T20"]
# Development scripts report on stdout.
"scripts/*" = ["T20"]
# The CLI's output is print by design.
"src/calibrax/cli/*" = ["T201"]
# Test factories are keyword-only builders with one parameter per field.
"tests/*" = ["D", "PLR0913", "PLR2004", "S101"]
# Local stubs for untyped libraries spell names as the library does (NVML's camelCase).
"typings/*" = ["N"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]

# Architecture fitness functions — Sprint 2.3.
#
# Run with `lint-imports`. CI gate is per-PR. Violations either get
# fixed or explicitly waivered in `.importlinter-waivers.yaml`.
#
# Contract authoring guide:
#   * Layered: top depends on layers below it, never sideways or up.
#   * Forbidden: list importer/imported pairs.
#   * Independence: a set of modules that may NOT import each other.
#
# Reasoning per contract is in the comment block above each.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    cognithor

# ── Layered architecture ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Higher layers may import lower; never sideways. Each layer is one
# rung. Channels sit at the top because they're entry points; security
# sits below everything because it's policy that all layers consult.

[importlinter:contract:1]
name = Cognithor layered dependencies
type = layers
layers =
    cognithor.channels
    cognithor.gateway
    cognithor.crew
    cognithor.skills
    cognithor.mcp
    cognithor.video : cognithor.evolution : cognithor.identity : cognithor.kanban : cognithor.leads : cognithor.packs
    cognithor.memory : cognithor.audit : cognithor.db
    cognithor.core
    cognithor.security
    cognithor.config : cognithor.utils
exhaustive = false
ignore_imports =
    # Logging is allowed cross-layer because it's pure utility.
    cognithor.utils.logging -> *
    # Security needs to read config but not the other way.
    cognithor.security -> cognithor.config

# ── Forbidden: packs may not touch security internals ──────────────────
# A pack should declare its tool-risks in its manifest; the loader
# enforces them. Packs reaching into security.* would let a malicious
# pack bypass the Gatekeeper layer.

[importlinter:contract:2]
name = Packs cannot import security internals
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    cognithor.packs
forbidden_modules =
    cognithor.security.permission_scope
    cognithor.security.cost_ledger
    cognithor.security.fingerprint
    cognithor.security.cloud_escalation
    cognithor.security.trust_bundle

# ── Forbidden: channels cannot reach into Crew internals ───────────────
# Channels invoke crew via the public API surface. Going around it
# means a channel could observe partial Crew state and re-implement
# sequencing the wrong way.

[importlinter:contract:3]
name = Channels use only Crew public surface
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    cognithor.channels
forbidden_modules =
    cognithor.crew.guardrails
    cognithor.crew.delegation
    cognithor.crew.replay_internals
allow_indirect_imports = true

# ── Forbidden: tests cannot import from src/ via relative paths ────────
# The repo allows `from cognithor.x import y` (absolute). Relative
# imports across the src/ boundary cause editable-install drift.

[importlinter:contract:4]
name = No src-relative imports in tests
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    tests
forbidden_modules =
    src
    src.cognithor

# ── Independence: video pipeline tools must not depend on each other ───
# The 5 video tools (compose, compose_explainer, compose_social_cut,
# caption_overlay, render) should each be self-contained so they can
# be swapped or A/B-tested individually.

[importlinter:contract:5]
name = Video MCP tools are independent
type = independence
modules =
    cognithor.mcp.video_tools
    cognithor.video.skills
    cognithor.video.renderer_base
    cognithor.video.renderers

# ── Forbidden: no direct vllm-orchestrator from non-routing/non-API ────
# Only the API layer + the routing module should drive the
# orchestrator. Anyone else stops or starts the container is a bug
# waiting to happen.

[importlinter:contract:6]
name = vllm_orchestrator only used by routing + API
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    cognithor.crew
    cognithor.skills
    cognithor.packs
    cognithor.evolution
    cognithor.kanban
forbidden_modules =
    cognithor.core.vllm_orchestrator

# ── Forbidden: mcp tools must not import channels ──────────────────────
# Tools are pure functions of inputs; if they need channel context
# it's via Gatekeeper-mediated parameters.

[importlinter:contract:7]
name = MCP tools cannot import channels
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    cognithor.mcp
forbidden_modules =
    cognithor.channels

# ── Forbidden: gateway should not depend on individual MCP tool modules ─
# Gateway dispatches via the registry. Hardcoded imports of specific
# tools mean a missing optional extra crashes the whole gateway boot.

[importlinter:contract:8]
name = Gateway uses MCP via registry, not direct imports
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    cognithor.gateway
forbidden_modules =
    cognithor.mcp.browser
    cognithor.mcp.media
    cognithor.mcp.video_tools
allow_indirect_imports = true

# `packages` discovery — Hatch walks the package tree and includes all files,
# not just .py. The earlier explicit `force-include` of the templates
# directory caused PyPI to reject the wheel with "Duplicate filename in local
# headers" because the same files landed twice (once via packages, once via
# force-include). Keep it out — packages alone is correct.

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"

]

    # starlette uses deprecated multipart import — third-party, can't fix

    # asyncio transport cleanup after event loop is closed (Windows + Linux)
    "ignore:Exception ignored in.*Transport:pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning",
    # Mock artifacts: coroutines created by AsyncMock but never awaited
    "ignore:coroutine .* was never awaited:RuntimeWarning",
]

target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]
# Crew scaffolder templates are Jinja2 source trees, not Python packages —

    "RUF002",  # Ambiguous EN DASH in docstrings
    "RUF003",  # Ambiguous EN DASH in comments
    "RUF012",  # Mutable class defaults — dataclass pattern, harmless

    "SIM103",  # Needless bool — style preference

private const val CONTROLLER_LAYER = "Controller"
private const val REPO_LAYER = "Repo"
private const val SERVICE_LAYER = "Service"

@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [ActiveRecordApp::class])
class ActiveRecordArchTest {
    @ArchTest
    val correctLayering: ArchRule = layeredArchitecture()
        .consideringAllDependencies()
        .layer(CONTROLLER_LAYER).definedBy(CONTROLLER_PACKAGE)
        .layer(SERVICE_LAYER).definedBy(SERVICE_PACKAGE)
        .layer(REPO_LAYER).definedBy(REPO_PACKAGE)
        .whereLayer(CONTROLLER_LAYER).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
        .whereLayer(SERVICE_LAYER).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(CONTROLLER_LAYER)
        .whereLayer(REPO_LAYER).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(SERVICE_LAYER)

    @ArchTest
    val repositoryInheritance: ArchRule = classes()
        .that()
        .resideInAPackage(REPO_PACKAGE)
        .should()
        .beInterfaces()
        .andShould()
        .beAssignableTo(Repository::class.java)

    @ArchTest
    val onlyImplementRepoInRepoPackage: ArchRule = classes()
        .that()
        .resideOutsideOfPackage(REPO_PACKAGE)
        .should()
        .notBeAssignableTo(Repository::class.java)

    @ArchTest
    fun noDomainLeakage(importedClasses: JavaClasses) {
        val dtoPredicate = object : DescribedPredicate<JavaClass>("be either a standard collection or a DTO") {
            override fun test(t: JavaClass): Boolean {
                return when {
                    t.packageName == DTO_PACKAGE -> true
                    t.packageName == "java.lang" && t.isAssignableTo("void") -> true
                    t.isAssignableTo(Collection::class.java) -> true
                    else -> false
                }
            }
        }

        val dtoAnnotationRule = classes()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage(DTO_PACKAGE)
            .should()
            .notBeAnnotatedWith(Entity::class.java)

        val domainAnnotationRule = classes()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage(DOMAIN_PACKAGE)
            .should()
            .beAnnotatedWith(Entity::class.java)
            .orShould()
            .beEnums()

        val returnTypeRule = methods()
            .that()
            .arePublic()
            .and()
            .areDeclaredInClassesThat()
            .areAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java)
            .should()
            .haveRawReturnType(dtoPredicate)

        assertAll(
            { dtoAnnotationRule.check(importedClasses) },
            { domainAnnotationRule.check(importedClasses) },
            { returnTypeRule.check(importedClasses) },

    }

[project.scripts]
rigplane = "rigplane.cli:main"
# Deprecated alias of `rigplane` — prints DeprecationWarning then forwards.

[project.optional-dependencies]
# `audio` and `bridge` extras are kept as no-op aliases for backwards
# compatibility — `opuslib`, `sounddevice`, and `numpy` are now part of
# the core dependencies (#1090). New users should run `pip install rigplane`.
audio = []
bridge = []
scope = [
    "pillow>=10.0",
]
dsp = ["scipy>=1.11"]
webrtc = ["aiortc>=1.9"]
tls = ["cryptography>=41.0"]

# system (`python3-soapysdr` on Debian/Raspberry Pi OS) or a SoapySDR build.
# The extra is a feature marker for the SDR IQ source; it adds no packages
# and runtime dependencies are unchanged.
sdr = []
# Dev/build-only: pydantic drives the public-state JSON-Schema → TypeScript
# codegen (MOR-881). It must NEVER enter the runtime `dependencies` above —
# core stays zero-runtime-dep. Only the conformance test and the
# `scripts/gen_state_types.py` generator import it; `state_schema.py` is never
# imported on the live request path.
# `jsonschema` drives the consumer-driven contract (CDC) runner (MOR-883):
# `scripts/run_consumer_contracts.py` validates the real producer artifacts
# against consumer-authored expectations. Like `pydantic`, it is DEV/CI-only and
# must NEVER enter the runtime `dependencies` above — core stays zero-runtime-dep.

dev = ["pytest", "pytest-asyncio", "pytest-cov", "pytest-timeout", "pytest-xdist", "ruff", "mypy", "pydantic>=2.13,<3", "jsonschema>=4.0"]

    "pydantic>=2.13,<3",
    # Dev/build-only — drives the MOR-883 consumer-driven contract runner.
    # NOT a runtime dependency (core stays zero-runtime-dep).
    "jsonschema>=4.0",
    # Dev/test-only — imported only by the property tests under tests/property.

strict = true
follow_imports = "skip"

# Codegen-only contract schema (MOR-881). Under the global ``follow_imports =

[tool.mutmut]
# Weekly mutation-testing trend job. The whole src/ tree is
# copied into mutants/ so imports stay intact; only_mutate restricts

# Top-level test-support and rig-profile data; without these the copied

# Per-mutant pytest invocation: -x -q -p no:cacheprovider. The selection

[project]
name = "luxury-lakehouse"
version = "0.5.124"
description = "Serverless soccer analytics platform built on Databricks Lakebase"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.11"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
dependencies = [
    # Core ingestion dependencies (must work on Databricks serverless Python 3.10)
    # NOTE: pandas and numpy are pre-installed on Databricks serverless runtime.
    # Do NOT pin them here — version conflicts break the Python kernel.
    "requests>=2.33.0",
    "requests-cache>=1.2.0",
    # Transitive dep (requests, httpx, anyio). Pinned to >=3.15 to resolve
    # CVE-2026-45409 (idna 3.11 vulnerability).
    "idna>=3.15",
    # Transitive dep (mlflow + fsspec[http] via huggingface-hub/datasets/torch). Pinned to
    # >=3.14.3 to resolve CVE-2026-34993 + CVE-2026-47265 (aiohttp < 3.14.0), the
    # CVE-2026-54273..54280 batch (aiohttp 3.14.0, fixed in 3.14.1), and
    # PYSEC-2026-3545 (fixed 3.14.3) + PYSEC-2026-3546 / PYSEC-2026-3547 (fixed 3.14.2)
    # in one bump — 3.14.3 is the lowest version clearing all three.
    "aiohttp>=3.14.3",
    # Transitive dep (httpx/starlette → anyio; pulled forward to 4.12.1 by the silly-kicks 4.120.0
    # re-lock via ruthless-efficiency 0.6.0). Floored to >=4.14.2 to resolve CVE-2026-63374 +
    # CVE-2026-64847 (anyio < 4.14.2). The lakehouse uses anyio only transitively (httpx async
    # transport); 4.14.2 is the lowest version clearing both.
    "anyio>=4.14.2",
    # Transitive dep (mlflow-skinny → fastapi). Floored to >=1.3.1 to resolve
    # CVE-2026-48818 + CVE-2026-48817 + CVE-2026-54283 + CVE-2026-54282 (starlette < 1.x
    # web-server vulnerabilities). fastapi (>=0.46.0, no ceiling) accepts the starlette 1.x
    # major; the lakehouse uses mlflow as a tracking client only (no server/gateway), so the
    # starlette web-server paths are never exercised. uv kept 0.52.1 only because the 1.x line
    # released after the last lock; the floor forces the upgrade.
    "starlette>=1.3.1",
    # Transitive dep (google-auth -> databricks-sdk -> mlflow-skinny; also directly).
    # Floored to >=50.0.0 to resolve GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf (cryptography < 48.0.1),
    # PYSEC-2026-3553 + PYSEC-2026-3554 (fixed 49.0.0), and PYSEC-2026-3552 (needs >=50.0.0).
    #
    # The >=50 floor became reachable only once full `mlflow` was dropped for
    # `mlflow-skinny` (see the [mlflow] extra + ADR-027, 2026-08-31 amendment): full
    # mlflow capped `cryptography<50` (3.15.x -> `cryptography>=43,<50`), which made
    # 49.0.0 the prior ceiling and left PYSEC-2026-3552 unresolvable (it was ignored
    # in .pip-audit-ignores.yml). mlflow-skinny carries no cryptography pin, so the
    # floor now resolves and that ignore is REMOVED — a genuine fix, not a suppression.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    # Transitive dep (mlflow / databricks-sdk / distributed). Floored to >=1.2.1 to resolve
    # GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964 (msgpack < 1.2.1).
    "msgpack>=1.2.1",
    # Transitive dep (dbt-core, flask/taipy, typer). Floored to >=8.3.3 to resolve
    # PYSEC-2026-2132 (click < 8.3.3). No parent caps click, so the floor is satisfiable.
    "click>=8.3.3",
    # Transitive dep (matplotlib / taipy). Floored to >=12.3.0 to resolve the PYSEC-2026-2253,
    # -2254, -2255, -2256, -2257 batch (pillow < 12.3.0) in one bump. No parent caps pillow.
    "pillow>=12.3.0",
    # Transitive dep (dbt-core). Floored to >=0.6.0 to resolve PYSEC-2026-3696 / -3697 / -3698 /
    # -3699 (sqlparse < 0.6.0 parsing vulnerabilities), all fixed in 0.6.0.
    "sqlparse>=0.6.0",
    # Workflow framework (card parsing + validation)
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    # HF Hub (cost tracking, dataset publishing, model weight sync)
    "huggingface_hub>=1.5.0",
    # Floored to >=3.1.51 to resolve GHSA-2f96-g7mh-g2hx / -v396-v7q4-x2qj /
    # -956x-8gvw-wg5v (gitpython < 3.1.51).
    "gitpython>=3.1.58",
    "pygments>=2.20.0",
]

"src/ingestion/refresh_synced_tables.py" = ["BLE001"]  # CLI error accumulator
"src/ingestion/sync_hf_costs.py" = ["BLE001"]  # per-item HF parse loop (best-effort)
"src/ingestion/statsbomb.py" = ["BLE001"]  # per-match fetch best-effort (logs with traceback, records failure)

"src/ingestion/tracking_metadata.py" = ["BLE001"]  # per-match XML/kloppy parse best-effort
"src/ingestion/dbt_runner.py" = ["BLE001"]  # SDK token resolution (prints + re-raises)

"hf_taipy_app/src/admin_api.py" = ["BLE001"]  # background refresh thread — logs via logger.exception

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["analytics", "evolve", "ingestion", "shared", "workflows"]

[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
reportMissingImports = "warning"  # pyspark only available in Databricks runtime
# PyTorch re-exports public API (randint, zeros, allclose, etc.) from C
# extensions via __init__.py; pyright stubs can't model this correctly and
# flag torch.randint as "not exported from module torch". Disable globally
# rather than adding 284 inline suppressions across torch test files.
reportPrivateImportUsage = "none"
# Test files under src/tests/ insert scripts/ and hf_taipy_app/src/ onto
# sys.path at runtime to import scripts + Taipy modules that are NOT part
# of any installed Python package. Declaring those directories as extraPaths
# lets pyright resolve the same imports statically; without this, every
# such test file generates reportMissingImports warnings (160 warnings
# across 10 test files pre-fix, empirically measured 2026-04-17). Session-45
# memory flagged this as a deferred warning on `test_grant_synced_table_permissions.py`;
# the fix generalises to every sys.path-insert test file at once.
extraPaths = [
    "scripts",
    "hf_taipy_app/src",
    # src/tests is a pytest package (has __init__.py); intra-test helper
    # imports use the short name (``from coverage_utils import ...``) which
    # pytest resolves because the package root is inserted onto sys.path
    # automatically at collection time. Listing it here lets pyright
    # resolve the same imports statically; otherwise every test that uses
    # a shared helper under src/tests/ emits reportMissingImports.
    "src/tests",

# (target/, logs/) and local cache (.user.yml) that aren't needed at runtime.
# dbt_packages/ IS needed at runtime for macro resolution and is bundled.

# D59: force ``dbt_project/dbt_packages/`` into the sdist even though it is
# gitignored. ``uv build`` (no flag) builds sdist then extracts it into a temp
# dir and builds the wheel from that extracted tree. Without this entry the
# sdist omits dbt_packages (gitignored → VCS-aware exclusion), the wheel's
# force-include then fails with FileNotFoundError: Forced include not found,
# and every caller of ``uv build`` breaks (CI, manage_space.py, deploy.sh).

# wheel's force-include finds it at the expected location during extraction.

# reads the source tree in place, but we keep this parallel config so plain

# --- uv configuration ---
[tool.uv]
# Security floors on TRANSITIVE dependencies live here — NOT in
# [project.dependencies] — so the project's declared deps stay limited to what we
# actually import. constraint-dependencies apply a floor across the whole
# resolution without creating a phantom direct dependency. This is the canonical
# home for "vulnerable transitive package, fix version exists" (per the CVE-floor
# convention). Direct-dep CVEs are floored inline in [project.dependencies].
constraint-dependencies = [
    # CVE-2026-59885 + CVE-2026-59886 (pyasn1 < 0.6.4). Transitive via the
    # cryptography / pyOpenSSL / databricks-sdk auth chain — no direct import.
    "pyasn1>=0.6.4",
    # PYSEC-2026-2151 (flask < 3.1.3). The Space resolves flask 3.1.1 because taipy-rest 4.1.1
    # caps it at <=3.1.1; taipy-rest 4.1.0 does not, so this floor takes 4.1.0 instead. Measured
    # 2026-08-11 and re-verified 2026-08-12: 136 packages before and after, nothing added or
    # removed, and only taipy-rest + apispec + apispec-webframeworks move — none of which appear
    # anywhere in hf_taipy_app/ (they arrive solely as transitives of the taipy metapackage, and
    # the Space is a GUI app that never touches the REST layer).
    # This is the D5 carve-out: a backwards move accepted as the measured, named, bounded price
    # of a security fix.
    #
    # This constraint binds the DEPLOY-TIME compile, not uv.lock — the lock already resolves
    # flask 3.1.3 / taipy-rest 4.1.0. It therefore does NOT fix production on its own; only the
    # next deploy does (Task 5b).
    "flask>=3.1.3",
    # PYSEC-2026-3032 + PYSEC-2026-3033 (python-engineio < 4.13.2) and PYSEC-2026-3042
    # (python-socketio < 5.16.2). These two floors exist BECAUSE of the flask floor above.
    #
    # Measured 2026-08-12 against the deployed Space: flask>=3.1.3 forces taipy-rest 4.1.0, and
    # that older taipy-rest caps python-engineio at 4.13.1 and python-socketio at 5.16.1 — both
    # vulnerable. An UNCONSTRAINED compile takes 4.13.4 / 5.16.4, which are fixed. So taking the
    # flask fix alone would have *caused* three advisories to persist that a plain redeploy would
    # have cleared: 9 of 12 fixed instead of 12.
    #
    # All three floors resolve together: 136 packages, taipy-rest still 4.1.0, nothing added, and
    # only the typer chain (typer, shellingham, annotated-doc) drops — verified unimported by
    # hf_taipy_app (the only matches were incidental byte sequences inside .pyc files).
    #
    # The D5 change manifest did NOT catch this: it measures movement RELATIVE TO PRODUCTION, so a
    # package sitting still at a vulnerable version is invisible to it.
    "python-engineio>=4.13.2",
    "python-socketio>=5.16.2",
    # CVE-2026-104851 (fsspec < 2026.6.0): NOT floored here — `datasets` caps fsspec<=2025.3.0, and
    # the newer `datasets` that would lift the cap requires pyarrow>=21, which taipy-core caps at
    # <19 (ResolutionImpossible). Carried as a justified ignore in .pip-audit-ignores.yml (BLOCKED).
    # CVE-2026-104874 (multidict < 6.9.1). Transitive via aiohttp / yarl (the HF/http async stack).
    "multidict>=6.9.1",
    # PYSEC-2026-4114 (oauthlib < 4.0.0): NOT floored here — databricks-sql-connector hard-caps
    # oauthlib>=3.1.0,<4.0.0 across every available version, so the 4.0.0 floor is unsatisfiable
    # (ResolutionImpossible). Carried as a justified ignore in .pip-audit-ignores.yml (BLOCKED).
    # PYSEC-2026-4175 + PYSEC-2026-4176 + PYSEC-2026-4177 (urllib3 < 2.8.0). Transitive via
    # requests / the HTTP stack — no direct import.
    "urllib3>=2.8.0",
    # CVE-2026-102598 (werkzeug < 3.1.9). Transitive via flask (already floored >=3.1.3); flask 3.1.x
    # requires werkzeug>=3.1, so 3.1.9 is in-range.
    "werkzeug>=3.1.9",
    # PYSEC-2026-4011/-4012/-4013/-4014 (virtualenv < 21.7.13). DEV-only transitive via pre-commit;
    # 21.7.13 is the lowest version clearing all four.
    "virtualenv>=21.7.13",
]

# Taipy-GUI 4.1.2 caps flask-socketio <5.5, but Flask 3.1.3 (pinned by the
# PYSEC-2026-2151 floor above) made RequestContext.session a read-only property.
# flask-socketio <5.5.1 still assigns `ctx.session = ...` directly, raising
# `AttributeError: can't set attribute 'session'` on EVERY Socket.IO connect —
# Taipy delivers page content over that websocket, so the app rendered blank in
# production from the 2026-08-12 D5 CVE deploy (which introduced the flask>=3.1.3
# floor) until this override. Fixed upstream in flask-socketio 5.5.1 (the
# `_session` compatibility branch). Taipy-GUI 4.1.2 uses only stable SocketIO APIs
# (SocketIO(), .on, .run, .async_mode, .wsgi_server), so its <5.5 cap is
# conservative and safe to lift here. Keeping flask>=3.1.3 preserves the CVE fix.
# Verified: 5.4.1 reproduces the exact prod traceback, 5.6.1 connects cleanly.
# See ADR-083. Requires hf_taipy_app/Dockerfile to install with --no-deps
# (plain `pip install -r` fails ResolutionImpossible against taipy-gui's cap).
override-dependencies = [
    "flask-socketio>=5.5.1",
]

# taipy requires sqlalchemy>=2.0; dbt-databricks requires sqlalchemy<2.0.
# These extras are separate deployment targets that never coexist in a single env.
conflicts = [
    [
        { extra = "taipy-app" },
        { extra = "dbt" },
    ],
    [
        { extra = "dbt" },
        { extra = "sdk" },
    ],
]

[[tool.uv.index]]

    # PYSEC-2026-196 (pip < 26.1.2 vulnerability). Durable pin per the idna/pyjwt

    "pip>=26.2",

]

[tool.uv.sources]

greenhouse-server = { workspace = true }
greenhouse-cli = { workspace = true }

[tool.uv]
default-groups = ["dev"]
# Transitive pins, not imported by greenhouse code. mcp: >=1.28.1 clears PYSEC-2026-3481/3482/3483;
# <2 because fastapi-mcp 0.4.0 (latest) constructs `mcp.server.lowlevel.Server(name, version)`, which

    "pytest-cov>=5.0",

    "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
    "ruff>=0.16.3",
    "time-machine>=2.15",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# A hung test fails with a traceback after 5 min instead of eating the CI job (slowest golden test ~40 s locally).
timeout = 300
pythonpath = ["libs/greenhouse-core", "libs/greenhouse-server", "libs/greenhouse-cli", "tests"]
# fastapi-mcp 0.4.0 (types.py) calls the deprecated BaseModel.__get_pydantic_core_schema__ at import; nothing to fix
# on our side until it is replaced or fixed upstream (#119). Any other warning stays visible.
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore:The `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` method of the `BaseModel` class is deprecated:pydantic.warnings.PydanticDeprecatedSince211",
]
markers = ["dotenv: keep Settings' real `.env` loading (tests/conftest.py disables it for every other test)"]

[tool.mypy]

# generated Alembic revisions are frozen history and stay out of scope.
files = ["libs/greenhouse-core", "libs/greenhouse-server", "libs/greenhouse-cli", "tests"]
exclude = ["/migrations/versions/"]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
follow_imports = "silent"
# The workspace packages ship no py.typed, so without this their imports resolve through the
# editable .pth files as "missing" and silently become Any. Source paths make them typed.
# tests/ is on the path because the tests import their helpers from the rootdir (`from fake_data import …`,
# `from server.conftest import …`); explicit_package_bases names each test module by that root.
mypy_path = ["libs/greenhouse-core", "libs/greenhouse-server", "libs/greenhouse-cli", "tests"]
explicit_package_bases = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Third-party packages with neither stubs nor py.typed — the only untyped imports. Targeted,
# so a new untyped dependency fails loudly instead of silently becoming Any.
module = ["tinytuya", "tinytuya.*", "apscheduler.*", "fastapi_mcp", "fastapi_mcp.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"
src = ["libs/greenhouse-core", "libs/greenhouse-server", "libs/greenhouse-cli", "tests"]
# tests/ is a rootdir-import tree (`from fake_data import …`, `from server.conftest import …`); an
# __init__.py would make pytest import those modules a second time under a `tests.` name.
namespace-packages = ["tests"]
# Frozen Alembic history: generated DDL that is never edited (AGENTS.md, Key facts).
extend-exclude = ["libs/greenhouse-core/greenhouse_core/migrations/versions"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Every stable rule. The only ignores are rules that cannot hold together with something we keep;
# each one names what it conflicts with.
select = ["ALL"]
extend-select = [
    # Preview rules opted in by full name (explicit-preview-rules): size limits that agree with
    # scripts/sizecheck.py, enforced since before the ALL switch.
    "PLR0904",  # too-many-public-methods
    "PLR0914",  # too-many-locals
    "PLR0917",  # too-many-positional-arguments
    "PLR1702",  # too-many-nested-blocks
]
ignore = [
    "COM812",  # conflicts with ruff format (trailing commas are the formatter's call)
    "ISC001",  # conflicts with ruff format (implicit string concatenation on one line)
    "CPY001",  # a per-file copyright header; the licence lives once in LICENSE
]
# Preview refines two stable rules: BLE001 accepts a handler that logs the exception or re-raises, S310
# accepts literal http(s) URLs. With explicit-preview-rules, no other preview rule turns on by itself.
# Preview behaviour may change between ruff releases; the version is pinned in uv.lock and
# .pre-commit-config.yaml.
preview = true

# Frozen user-facing text (MCP tool descriptions, CLI help, TUI renders) uses the en dash and ×.
