# Import Linter Configuration
# Enforces module boundaries for the backend TypeScript code

[importlinter]
package_root = backend/src
exclude_patterns = ["**/node_modules/**", "**/__mocks__/**", "**/*.test.ts", "**/*.spec.ts"]

[[importlinter.rules]]
name = "domain-layer-dependencies"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    {name = "modules", = ["^backend/src/modules"]},
    {name = "features", = ["^backend/src/features"]},
    {name = "utils", = ["^backend/src/utils"]},
    {name = "config", = ["^backend/src/config"]},
]

# Modules can depend on features, utils, and config
# Features can depend on utils and config
# Utils can depend on config
# Config should have no internal dependencies

# Import Linter Configuration
# Enforces module boundaries and architectural layering

[importlinter]
ignore_package_patterns = ["^@types/", "^@mock/"]

# Define the dependency constraints between packages
[importlinter.constraints]
[[importlinter.packages]]
 name = "modules"
 from_constraints = {"min_version": "1.0.0"}

[[importlinter.packages]]
 name = "features"
 from_constraints = {"min_version": "1.0.0"}

[[importlinter.packages]]
 name = "config"
 from_constraints = {"min_version": "1.0.0"}

[[importlinter.packages]]
 name = "utils"
 from_constraints = {"min_version": "1.0.0"}

# Define allowed dependencies
# features can import modules but not vice versa
# config can only import from utils
# utils can import from modules and features
[[importlinter.rules]]
 name = "no_cross_package_imports"
 definition = "Enforce architectural layering"
 constraints = [
   {"from": "features", "to": "modules", "allowed": true},
   {"from": "modules", "to": "features", "allowed": false},
   {"from": "config", "to": "modules", "allowed": true},
   {"from": "config", "to": "features", "allowed": false},
 ]

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    platform_django
include_external_packages = True

# =============================================================================
# Contract 1: Infrastructure cannot import business modules
# =============================================================================
# core is the lowest-level module. It must not import from any business domain
# modules.
[importlinter:contract:infrastructure-isolation]
name = Infrastructure cannot import business modules
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    platform_django.core
forbidden_modules =
    platform_django.users

# =============================================================================
# Contract 2: Users module internal layers (api -> services/selectors -> models)
# =============================================================================
# This is the gate that keeps a write out of a view: api and views may call
# services and selectors, and never the reverse. A selector that imports a
# service, or a service that imports a view, fails the build.
#
# tasks is parenthesised because the module ships no Celery task — an optional
# layer keeps its position in the hierarchy declared for the project that adds
# one, without the contract failing on a file that does not exist yet.
[importlinter:contract:users-internal-layers]
name = Users module internal layers
type = layers
layers =
    api
    views
    (tasks)
    services
    selectors
    models
containers =
    platform_django.users

# =============================================================================
# Contract 3: The API viewset may not reach the ORM
# =============================================================================
# The layers contract above gates direction — a selector importing a service
# fails. It cannot, on its own, catch a write reimplemented inside a view: a
# view that queries or saves imports nothing a layers contract forbids. This
# does. The viewset has no legitimate reason to name the model, so a query or a
# save placed back in it fails the build.
#
# allow_indirect_imports keeps this about the viewset's own code. Reaching the
# model *through* a selector, a service or a serializer is the point of those
# layers; only a direct import here is the defect.
#
# platform_django.users.views is deliberately not covered. Django's DetailView
# and UpdateView take `model = User` as a class attribute, so the same rule
# there would forbid the framework's own idiom.
[importlinter:contract:api-views-do-not-query]
name = The users API viewset does not touch the ORM directly
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    platform_django.users.api.views
forbidden_modules =
    platform_django.users.models
allow_indirect_imports = True

# ==== pytest ====
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "6.0"
addopts = "--ds=config.settings.test --reuse-db --import-mode=importlib"
python_files = [
    "tests.py",
    "test_*.py",
]
# Setting this replaces pytest's defaults, so ".*" has to be restored by hand.
# Without it, and without "worktrees", a run at the repository root collects every
# worktree's copy of conftest.py and pluggy rejects the duplicate registration.
norecursedirs = [".*", "node_modules", "worktrees", "build", "dist", "*.egg"]

# ==== Coverage ====
[tool.coverage.run]
include = ["platform_django/**", "libs/*/src/**"]
omit = ["*/migrations/*", "*/tests/*"]
plugins = ["django_coverage_plugin"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
skip_empty = true
show_missing = true
precision = 2

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

# ==== mypy ====
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
check_untyped_defs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_configs = true
plugins = [
    "mypy_django_plugin.main",
    "mypy_drf_plugin.main",
]

exclude = ["libs/.*/tests/"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Django migrations should not produce any errors:
module = "*.migrations.*"
ignore_errors = true

[tool.django-stubs]
django_settings_module = "config.settings.test"

# ==== django-migration-linter ====
# The default rule set already treats backward-incompatible operations — DROP or
# RENAME of a column or table, ADD NOT NULL without a default, ALTER of a column
# type — as errors, and data-migration hygiene as non-blocking warnings. That is
# the split we want, so no `--warnings-as-errors`.
[tool.django_migration_linter]
# `sites` migrations live under platform_django/contrib/sites via
# MIGRATION_MODULES; the linter cannot resolve that shimmed path.
exclude_apps = ["sites"]

# ==== djLint ====
[tool.djlint]
blank_line_after_tag = "load,extends"
close_void_tags = true
# allauth's {% slot %}/{% endslot %} isn't a builtin django tag
custom_blocks = "slot,element"
format_css = true
format_js = true
# TODO: remove T002 when fixed https://github.com/djlint/djLint/issues/687

include = "H017,H035"
indent = 2
max_line_length = 119
profile = "django"

[tool.djlint.css]

[tool.djlint.js]

# === Per-part stage helpers isolation (generalized, stage-axis discipline per AGENTS.md) ===
# AVOIDED PATCHWORK: consolidated from inbound-stages-entrypoints-only, cross-part-stage-helpers-isolation, outbound-per-part-helpers-local, streaming-primitives-local, adapters-no-legacy-stage-shims, transport-result-public-surface, etc.
# One broad contract instead of many narrow ones.
# Enforces: HELPERS per part (focused extract inside the stage, compose, no god modules or cross-duplication), public entrypoints only for adapters, local _* helpers.
# Covers ADR-073 (stage as primary axis + thin adapters) + ADR-059 (port boundaries, no direct concretions in application layers).
# Reduces contract count and maintenance. See root AGENTS.md Core for usage.

[importlinter:contract:per-part-stage-helpers-isolation]
name = Per-part stage helpers/entrypoints isolation (HELPERS per part): locals (_*, router etc) not bypassed or crossed; adapters/shared use public surfaces only (ADR-073 + AGENTS.md)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    factory.adapters.shared
    factory.adapters.shared.inbound
    factory.adapters.telegram
    factory.adapters.discord
    factory.adapters.web
    factory.adapters.omp
    factory.adapters.clipool
    factory.adapters.nats
    factory.adapters
    factory.core
    factory.nats
    factory.llm
    factory.infrastructure
    factory.bootstrap
    factory.dashboard
    factory.agents
    factory.commands
    factory.monitoring
    factory.obs
    factory.integrations
forbidden_modules =
    # inbound internals (bypass targets; public entrypoints like pipeline/attachment_ingest/prebuilt_parser/wire_* /context allowed for adapters)
    factory.inbound.router
    factory.inbound.session_builder
    factory.inbound.dispatcher
    # outbound per-part _helpers (must stay local)
    factory.outbound._emitter_run
    factory.outbound._placeholder_lifecycle
    factory.outbound._reasoning_accum
    factory.outbound._streaming_state
    factory.outbound._tool_recap
    # streaming primitives (compose at consumer sites only; no god usage)
    factory.streaming.event_emitter
    factory.streaming.state_machine
    factory.streaming.parser
    # legacy stage shims (adapters must not re-introduce; shims belong in stages)
    factory.adapters.shared._shared_streaming_emitter
    factory.adapters.shared._shared_streaming
    # transport public surface (Result etc); consume only via factory.transport (not _result god module)
    factory.transport._result
ignore_imports =
    # Transitional / current composition sites for per-part helpers (to be drained via stage axis cleanup).
    # These are the "bypass" or direct _/internal uses caught by the generalized contract.
    # Debt tracked under axial review / quality-debt (consistent with ADR-048 transition ignores).
    factory.adapters.shared.inbound.pipeline -> factory.inbound.dispatcher
    factory.adapters.shared.inbound.pipeline -> factory.inbound.router
    factory.adapters.shared.inbound.pipeline -> factory.inbound.session_builder
    factory.adapters.discord.discord_formatter -> factory.outbound._reasoning_accum
    factory.adapters.telegram.telegram_formatter -> factory.outbound._reasoning_accum
    factory.core.cli.cli_streaming_parser -> factory.streaming.event_emitter
    factory.core.cli.cli_streaming_parser -> factory.streaming.state_machine
    factory.core.processors.stream_processor -> factory.streaming.event_emitter
    factory.core.processors.stream_processor -> factory.streaming.state_machine
    factory.core.processors.stream_close -> factory.streaming.state_machine
    factory.core.processors.stream_text -> factory.streaming.state_machine
    factory.core.processors.stream_tool -> factory.streaming.state_machine
    # Only transport internals reach the private _result (public surface enforcement)
    factory.transport.nats_request_response -> factory.transport._result
    factory.transport.http_transport -> factory.transport._result
    factory.transport.worker_pool_client -> factory.transport._result
allow_indirect_imports = true

[importlinter:contract:stage-purity]
name = Stage purity (inbound/outbound/streaming/transport/nats): no llm/nats/bootstrap bleed into stages + sqlite (outer infra/adapters/bootstrap covered by shared-modules-upper-boundary generalization). Enforces ADR-073 + engineering-standards. Consolidated from multiple purity contracts.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    factory.inbound
    factory.outbound
    factory.streaming
    factory.transport
    factory.nats
forbidden_modules =
    factory.llm
    factory.bootstrap
    aiosqlite
    sqlite3
ignore_imports =
    # nats has direct sqlite for pipeline.db (legacy or specific); other stores use the no-sqlite contract. Transitional for stage-purity generalization.
    factory.nats.pipeline.db -> sqlite3
allow_indirect_imports = true
# Covers ADR-073 (axial stage decomposition: stages as primary axis, thin adapters, no cross duplication) and parts of ADR-059 (inward dependencies for application layers).
# Generalized from transport-plumbing-purity, outbound-stage-purity, streaming-primitives-purity, stages-no-infrastructure, etc. to avoid patchwork.
# Outer bans in shared-modules-upper-boundary. Cross-stage in shared-modules-independence.

venv = ".venv"
# ── Permanent policy ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# reportPrivateUsage: Python's _name is a convention (advisory), not access
# control. Pyright enforcing it generates false positives on tightly-coupled
# partner modules, stdlib internals, and white-box test access — none of which
# represent real violations. Enforced by code review, not by the type checker.
reportPrivateUsage = "none"
#
# reportUnusedFunction: Decorator-registered callables (Discord app_commands,
# Telegram update handlers, asyncio task targets) are not statically reachable.
# Confirmed by manual audit 2026-03-23: all 48 src hits are dynamic registrations
# or private module helpers called through the module's public entry point.
reportUnusedFunction = "none"
# ── Wave 4 (#411) — config loading migrated to Pydantic ──────────────────────
# Rules still suppressed: cascading errors from non-config dict[str, Any] in
# business logic, LLM drivers, and tests (~3,165 hits total). Config sites
# are now fully typed. Re-enable incrementally in follow-up issues.
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "none"
reportUnknownLambdaType = "none"
reportMissingTypeArgument = "none"

[tool.ruff]
src = ["src", "tests", "packages/roxabi-nats/src", "packages/roxabi-nats/tests", "packages/roxabi-contracts/src", "packages/roxabi-contracts/tests", "packages/roxabi-blobs/src", "packages/roxabi-blobs/tests", "packages/roxabi-satellite/src", "packages/roxabi-satellite/tests"]

  "azure_blob_worm_staging: requires Azure Blob Storage with immutability policy. Env: AMA_STAGING_BLOB_WORM=1.",

  "axe_a11y: axe-core a11y assertions (delegated to pnpm test:a11y in CI).",
  "unit: fast in-process tests with no external deps (Spec 036 / F-A10 / T223)",
  "contract: contract tests proving schema / API parity (Spec 036 / F-A10 / T223)",
  "e2e: end-to-end tests requiring deployed infra (Spec 036 / F-A10 / T223)",
  "load: load / stress harnesses (Spec 036 / F-A10 / T223)",
  "spec007_isolation: required simulation tenant-isolation behavioral release gate.",
]

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Spec-032 Stream 1 — Code-quality gates (FR-Q01..FR-Q05).
# These tools mirror the CI gates in .github/workflows/ci.yml and .pre-commit-config.yaml.
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["apps", "packages"]
branch = true
omit = [
  "*/tests/*",
  "*/__init__.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
precision = 2
exclude_lines = [
  "pragma: no cover",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = false
warn_return_any = false
files = ["apps", "packages"]
exclude = "(^|[/\\\\])tests([/\\\\]|$)"
explicit_package_bases = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["tests.*"]
ignore_errors = true

# Import-linter rules (FR-Q02). Keep narrow and provable; expand as the codebase matures.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["apps", "packages"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "agents do not depend on api"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["apps.agents"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.api"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ingestion does not depend on api"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["apps.ingestion"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.api"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "domain does not depend on apps"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["packages.domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps"]

# NOTE: packages/prompts/ is a YAML-asset directory (no Python module), so it
# has no imports to lint. Re-add a contract here only if Python code is added
# under packages/prompts/.

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Spec-039 / Two-Path Rule (SC-007, plan §"Two-Path Rule").
# Production code MUST NOT import the simulator package, and runtime code MUST
# NOT import the seed package directly (seed records flow through the loader).
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "simulator_not_imported_by_production"
type = "forbidden"
# Enumerate production source modules sibling-wise so the forbidden
# simulator subtree is NOT itself a descendant of the source set
# (otherwise import-linter aborts with "Modules have shared descendants").
# Only modules with a real ``__init__.py`` are listed (import-linter
# refuses unknown modules).
source_modules = [
  "apps.api.app.auth",
  "apps.api.app.clients",
  "apps.api.app.domain",
  "apps.api.app.models",
  "apps.api.app.observability",
  "apps.api.app.repositories",
  "apps.api.app.schemas",
  "apps.api.app.validators",
  "apps.api.app.services.eval",
  "apps.api.app.services.governance",
  "apps.agents",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "apps.api.app.services.simulation.feeds",
  "apps.api.app.services.simulation.replay",
  "apps.api.app.services.simulation.generators",
]
# ``ignore_imports`` is intentionally omitted — the feeds/replay/generators
# sub-packages do not yet contain inter-module imports, so an unused-ignore
# entry would itself cause ``lint-imports`` to fail with
# "No matches for ignored import …". Re-add per-edge ignores here only when
# such imports legitimately exist (Phase 5+).

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "seed_not_imported_by_runtime"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "apps.api",
  "apps.agents",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "packages.domain.src.domain.seed",
]
# Pre-existing reference-data bootstrap services that intentionally import
# ``packages.domain.src.domain.seed.bootstrap`` for one-shot in-process
# warm-up. These were merged before spec-039 and are NOT regressions to
# fix here; track via plan §"Two-Path Rule — known acceptable callers".
ignore_imports = [
  "apps.api.app.services.governance_registry -> packages.domain.src.domain.seed.bootstrap",
  "apps.api.app.services.organisation_intelligence_service -> packages.domain.src.domain.seed.bootstrap",
  "apps.api.app.services.outcome_evaluator_service -> packages.domain.src.domain.seed.bootstrap",
  "apps.api.app.services.preparedness_analysis_service -> packages.domain.src.domain.seed.bootstrap",
  "apps.api.app.services.seed_service -> packages.domain.src.domain.seed.bootstrap",
]

# Правила зависимостей, проверяемые CI.
#
#   pip install import-linter
#   lint-imports --config .importlinter
#
# Каждый контракт снабжён строкой причины. Контракт без причины — кандидат на
# удаление: значит никто уже не помнит, что он защищает.
#
# Файл написан на целевую структуру из docs/components.md и переезжает в неё
# вместе с кодом: контракт раскомментируется в том же коммите, что и модуль под
# ним. Из трёх границ ЭТАП 0 (docs/current-state.md, §2) две уже стали
# целевыми — httpx заперт в core.adapters, SQL в core.repos, — а третья умерла
# вместе с каталогом bot/services/.
# Остальное закомментировано до появления пакетов `web` и `worker` —
# import-linter падает на несуществующем модуле, а не пропускает его.
#
# **Контрактов стало меньше, и это не ослабление.** На коммите 22 одиннадцать
# временных правил вокруг `core.usecases` заменились одной строкой в
# `core-siblings-are-independent` — она запрещает строго больше, включая
# обратное направление, которого временные правила не запрещали вовсе.
# Проверено переносом: семь мутаций, которые ловили снесённые правила (и две,
# которых они не ловили), ломают контракт и сейчас.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    bot
    core
#    web                  ← раскомментировать, когда появится кабинет
#    worker               ← раскомментировать, когда появится воркер
include_external_packages = True


# ============================================================================
# Границы, которые держатся в текущем дереве. Работает сегодня.
# ============================================================================

[importlinter:contract:only-adapters-speak-http]
name = httpx живёт только в core.adapters
# Причина: §2 документа — «ни bot, ни web, ни worker не импортируют httpx».
# Сеть должна быть подменяема в тестах одной заменой реализации порта.
#
# Целевая формулировка, достигнутая переносом: список исключений таял по одному
# на коммит и закончился вместе с каталогом bot/services. Раньше правило
# называлось «httpx живёт только в bot.services».
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    bot
    core.domain
    core.config
    core.i18n
    core.texts
    core.usecases
    core.ports
forbidden_modules =
    httpx
# Правило про прямой импорт: хендлеру нельзя открывать сокет, а дотянуться до
# сети через адаптер — это и есть архитектура. Без этой строки контракт ломается
# на цепочке bot.stock -> core.adapters.keycrm.client -> httpx, то есть ровно на
# том, ради чего затевался перенос.
allow_indirect_imports = True

[importlinter:contract:only-repos-touch-db]
name = SQL и драйвер БД живут только в core.repos
# Причина: сохранить границу, которая держалась с самого начала (весь SQL в
# одном модуле), и не дать транзакции растечься по хендлерам и джобам.
#
# Целевая формулировка, достигнутая переносом. Раньше правило называлось
# «aiosqlite живёт только в bot.db» и несло исключение под этот модуль;
# исключение ушло вместе с самим модулем.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    bot
    core.domain
    core.config
    core.i18n
    core.texts
    core.adapters
    core.usecases
    core.ports
forbidden_modules =
    aiosqlite
    sqlalchemy
    asyncpg
# Ровно те же грабли, что и с httpx: без этой строки контракт ломается на
# цепочке bot.handlers.common -> core.repos.users -> aiosqlite. Правило про
# прямой импорт — хендлеру нельзя открывать соединение, а ходить в базу через
# репозиторий это и есть архитектура.
allow_indirect_imports = True

# Третий контракт ЭТАП 0 — «bot.services ничего не знает про aiogram» — умер
# вместе с каталогом bot/services/. Его наследник ниже: api-clients-know-no-telegram.


# ============================================================================
# ЭТАП 2 — перенос модулей. Контракт включается в том же коммите, что и модуль:
# правило без кода под ним ничего не защищает, код без правила разъезжается.
# ============================================================================

[importlinter:contract:domain-is-pure]
name = core.domain не знает ни транспорта, ни базы, ни фреймворка
# Причина: единственный слой, тесты которого не требуют ни сети, ни БД, ни
# моков. Любой из этих импортов отнимает ровно это свойство.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.domain
forbidden_modules =
    httpx
    aiogram
    aiosqlite
    sqlalchemy
    asyncpg
    fastapi

[importlinter:contract:config-is-a-leaf]
name = core.config ничего не импортирует из проекта
# Причина: конфиг читают все три точки входа, поэтому он внизу. И это
# единственное место, где разрешено читать окружение — вторая половина правила
# грепом в CI, потому что os.environ линтеру не выразить (§12.7 components.md).
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.config
forbidden_modules =
    bot
    core.domain
    core.i18n
    core.texts
    aiogram
    httpx
    aiosqlite

[importlinter:contract:i18n-is-a-leaf]
name = core.i18n и core.texts ничего не импортируют из проекта
# Причина: их импортирует почти всё дерево (14 модулей на момент переноса), и
# любая их зависимость немедленно становится зависимостью всего дерева. Тексты
# нужны и боту, и кабинету — §9 документа, — поэтому они внизу, а не в боте.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.i18n
    core.texts
forbidden_modules =
    bot
    core.domain
    aiogram
    httpx
    aiosqlite

[importlinter:contract:parsers-are-pure]
name = разборщики ответов не знают про транспорт
# Причина: вся ценность отделения parse от client в том, что тесты парсеров
# идут на сохранённых фикстурах и не требуют мока сети. До разделения разбор
# конверта сидел внутри `async with httpx.AsyncClient`, и покрыт был только
# тот кусок, ради которого кто-то написал мок транспорта.
#
# Модули добавляются сюда по одному, вместе со своим коммитом переноса.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.adapters.keycrm.parse
    core.adapters.shopify.parse
    core.adapters.novaposhta.parse
forbidden_modules =
    httpx

[importlinter:contract:adapters-do-not-know-their-callers]
name = core.adapters не знает ни точек входа, ни базы
# Причина: один и тот же адаптер обслуживает бота, воркер и веб. Зависимость от
# любого из них приколачивает его к одному процессу. База — не его зона: адаптер,
# который сам пишет в базу, делает запись невидимой для транзакции сценария.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.adapters
forbidden_modules =
    bot
    aiosqlite

[importlinter:contract:api-clients-know-no-telegram]
name = клиенты внешних API ничего не знают про aiogram
# Причина: наследник контракта ЭТАП 0 «bot.services ничего не знает про
# aiogram», умершего вместе с каталогом bot/services. Импорт aiogram здесь
# означает, что клиент внешнего API начал знать про транспорт бота.
#
# Правило перечисляет клиентов поимённо, а не весь core.adapters: адаптер
# Telegram (v4 §3, core/adapters/telegram/) обязан импортировать aiogram, и
# запрет на весь пакет пришлось бы снимать в тот же день, когда он появится.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.adapters.keycrm
    core.adapters.shopify
    core.adapters.novaposhta
forbidden_modules =
    aiogram

[importlinter:contract:repos-do-not-know-their-callers]
name = core.repos не знает ни точек входа, ни сети
# Причина: репозиторий обслуживает бота, воркер и веб одновременно, поэтому
# зависимость от любого из них его к одному процессу приколачивает. А
# репозиторий, ходящий во внешний API, делает время транзакции равным времени
# сетевого вызова — на SQLite это блокировка базы на десять секунд таймаута.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.repos
forbidden_modules =
    bot
    httpx
    aiogram

[importlinter:contract:usecases-do-not-know-their-callers]
name = core.usecases не знает ни бота, ни его фреймворка
# Причина: сценарий существует ровно затем, чтобы его можно было вызвать и из
# воркера, и из кабинета, и проверить без Telegram. Первый импорт aiogram здесь
# возвращает его туда, откуда его вынули, — в хендлер.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.usecases
forbidden_modules =
    bot
    aiogram

[importlinter:contract:ports-are-only-signatures]
name = core.ports не знает ничего, кроме домена
# Причина: порт — это Protocol и ничего больше. Любой его импорт немедленно
# становится импортом всех, кто через него разговаривает, а разговаривают через
# него оба конца: и сценарий, и адаптер.
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.ports
forbidden_modules =
    bot
    aiogram
    httpx
    aiosqlite
    core.adapters
    core.repos
    core.usecases
    core.config

[importlinter:contract:core-siblings-are-independent]
name = core: usecases, adapters и repos не видят друг друга
# Причина: сценарий, знающий конкретную реализацию, нельзя протестировать без
# сети и БД — это и есть смысл существования core.ports. Адаптер, знающий
# репозиторий, делает запись невидимой для транзакции сценария; репозиторий,
# знающий адаптер, делает время транзакции равным времени сетевого вызова.
#
# **Целевая формулировка, достигнутая серией портов (коммиты 1–22).** До неё
# здесь стояли два сиблинга вместо трёх, а `core.usecases` держали одиннадцать
# временных правил: запрет на `core.adapters`, список семейств
# `core.repos.*`, растущий по строке на коммит, и восемь правил вида
# «сценарий X не знает ни одного репозитория». Все они запрещали подмножество
# того, что запрещает эта строка, и все снесены здесь.
#
# Чего временные правила не запрещали, а это — запрещает: обратное направление.
# `core.repos`, импортирующий сценарий, и `core.adapters`, импортирующий
# сценарий, до сих пор были разрешены; независимость двусторонняя.
#
# И последнее, ради чего стоило дойти: список больше не надо дописывать. Новый
# файл в `core/repos` защищён этим правилом в момент создания, а не в момент,
# когда кто-то вспомнит про строчку — что за серию забывали дважды
# (`f55ed31`, и там же `core.repos.support`, пропущенный ещё на `6208af4`).
type = independence
modules =
    core.usecases
    core.adapters
    core.repos

[importlinter:contract:domain-does-not-know-its-callers]
name = core.domain не знает про точки входа
# Причина: домен обслуживает бота, воркер и веб одновременно. Импорт любого из
# них приколачивает его к одному процессу и ломает «один образ, три команды».
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.domain
forbidden_modules =
    bot

# ЭТАП 2+ — остальной целевой контракт. Раскомментировать вместе с модулями.

[importlinter]
root_package = src

# Enforce the intended dependency direction: api (transport) -> core
# (orchestration) -> services (integrations) -> database. A lower layer must
# never import a higher one. This contract now passes with NO exceptions —
# keep it that way. Shared value types live in leaf modules (e.g. src.usage)
# that any layer may import; never add an ignore_imports entry to paper over a
# new upward import — invert the dependency instead.
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = api -> core -> services -> database layering
type = layers
layers =
    src.api
    src.core
    src.services
    src.database

# The deprecated tool_manager shim must not gain new first-party importers —
# new code imports src.services.tools directly.
[importlinter:contract:tool_manager_shim]
name = tool_manager shim is deprecated
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.core
    src.api
forbidden_modules =
    src.services.tool_manager
ignore_imports =
    src.core.prompt_router -> src.services.tool_manager
    src.core.agent_auth -> src.services.tool_manager
    src.api.routes.auth -> src.services.tool_manager
    src.api.routes.tools -> src.services.tool_manager

# Import contracts.
#
# Enforced in CI (`lint-imports`) so the layering cannot quietly regress.
#
# Every contract below holds with NO ignored imports and no per-contract
# exceptions, including the full tiered layering the restructuring work was
# aimed at. Getting there took removing four upward edges: two when transforms stopped receiving the whole ExecutionContext,
# one when the transform registry stopped naming the type it holds, and the last
# when the execution context moved out of `core` into `runtime`, a tier above
# the config and adapters it names.

[importlinter]
root_package = pipeplan

# An `if TYPE_CHECKING:` import is erased before the module ever runs: it forms
# no cycle and imposes no load order, so it is not the kind of coupling these
# contracts exist to constrain. `config.graph` annotates the task types it is
# handed without depending on the schema module that defines them, which is what
# keeps the graph derivable below the model rather than beside it.
exclude_type_checking_imports = True

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the whole stack, in order. Imports may only point downward.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

[importlinter:contract:tiers]
name = Tiered layering
type = layers
layers =
    pipeplan.cli
    pipeplan.integrations
    pipeplan.orchestrator
    pipeplan.runtime
    pipeplan.settings
    pipeplan.config
    pipeplan.transforms : pipeplan.adapters
    pipeplan.contracts
    pipeplan.ast
    pipeplan.core
    pipeplan.domain

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# tier 0 -- the shared vocabulary
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

[importlinter:contract:domain-is-the-bottom]
name = The shared vocabulary depends on nothing else in PipePlan
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    pipeplan.domain
forbidden_modules =
    pipeplan.core
    pipeplan.config
    pipeplan.adapters
    pipeplan.transforms
    pipeplan.ast
    pipeplan.runtime
    pipeplan.orchestrator
    pipeplan.cli

[importlinter:contract:errors-are-independent]
name = The exception hierarchy depends on nothing
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    pipeplan.core.exceptions
forbidden_modules =
    pipeplan.domain
    pipeplan.core.registry
    pipeplan.core.state
    pipeplan.config
    pipeplan.adapters
    pipeplan.transforms
    pipeplan.ast
    pipeplan.runtime
    pipeplan.orchestrator
    pipeplan.cli

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the pluggable surface is authorable without the blueprint schema or the engine
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

[importlinter:contract:transforms-are-self-contained]
name = A transform sees a dataframe and a frame resolver, nothing else
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    pipeplan.transforms
forbidden_modules =
    pipeplan.config
    pipeplan.adapters
    pipeplan.runtime
    pipeplan.orchestrator
    pipeplan.cli

[importlinter:contract:adapters-are-self-contained]
name = An adapter speaks the vocabulary, not the schema or the engine
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    pipeplan.adapters
forbidden_modules =
    pipeplan.config
    pipeplan.transforms
    pipeplan.ast
    pipeplan.runtime
    pipeplan.orchestrator
    pipeplan.cli

# A contract is written in the blueprint's own predicate language -- `checks:`
# and `rules:` are predicate trees -- so it belongs *above* that language, not
# beside the registries and the exception hierarchy. It sat in `core` for as
# long as a check was a comparison operator and could be its own two-line
# implementation; widening it to what a `filter` can say is what made the
# position wrong, because `core` cannot see `ast`.

[importlinter:contract:dsl-is-self-contained]
name = The expression/predicate AST knows nothing about I/O or orchestration
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    pipeplan.ast
forbidden_modules =
    pipeplan.config
    pipeplan.adapters
    pipeplan.transforms
    pipeplan.runtime
    pipeplan.orchestrator
    pipeplan.cli

[importlinter:contract:engine-is-the-top]
name = Nothing below the engine imports the engine or the CLI
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    pipeplan.core
    pipeplan.config
    pipeplan.contracts
    pipeplan.domain
forbidden_modules =
    pipeplan.orchestrator
    pipeplan.cli
    pipeplan.runtime

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# inside the config package
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

[importlinter:contract:graph-does-not-know-the-schema]
name = The task graph is derived from tasks, not from the blueprint schema
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    pipeplan.config.graph
forbidden_modules =
    pipeplan.config.models
    pipeplan.config.compile
    pipeplan.config.validation

[importlinter:contract:compile-stages-are-independent]
name = The compile stages do not reach sideways into each other
type = independence
modules =
    pipeplan.config.assembly
    pipeplan.config.parameters
    pipeplan.config.graph

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "pipeplan"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "A declarative, configuration-driven batch ETL framework on pandas."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "PipePlan" }]
keywords = ["etl", "pandas", "pipeline", "declarative", "data-engineering"]
classifiers = [
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Topic :: Database",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
    # The package ships `py.typed`; without this a consumer has no way to know
    # the annotations are there before installing it.
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
# The three below carry an upper bound; the rest do not. The rule is not
# "cap everything" -- a cap the maintainer forgets to lift is how a package
# becomes unresolvable in someone else's environment. It is "cap what this
# framework is built *on top of*", where a major release is a redesign rather
# than a deprecation cycle: pandas owns the data model, pydantic owns every
# schema, SQLAlchemy owns the whole relational family. A major of any of the
# three is a version of PipePlan, not a free upgrade.
#
# The floor is proved by CI (the `floor` job resolves every minimum). Nothing
# proved the *ceiling* until the matrix grew a column that tracks the newest
# interpreter and therefore the newest pandas -- which is what a cap is for:
# to say where the tested range stops, rather than to guess where it breaks.
dependencies = [
    "pandas>=2.0,<4",
    "pydantic>=2.5,<3",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0,<3",
    # 2.8.2, not 2.8: pandas 2.0 -- our own floor -- already requires it, so the
    # lower bound was never actually installable and nobody could have noticed
    # until the floor was pinned in CI. Nothing new is asked of any user.
    "python-dateutil>=2.8.2",
    "requests>=2.28",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Excel/parquet file support.
files = ["openpyxl>=3.1", "pyarrow>=14.0"]
# Database drivers. Access additionally needs the OS-level ODBC driver.
postgres = ["psycopg2-binary>=2.9"]
access = ["pyodbc>=5.0", "sqlalchemy-access>=2.0"]
mysql = ["pymysql>=1.1"]
# MongoDB / DocumentDB resources.
mongo = ["pymongo>=4.6"]
# REST/HTTP API resources.
rest = ["requests>=2.28"]
# High-performance fuzzy matching (falls back to stdlib difflib without it).
fuzzy = ["rapidfuzz>=3.0"]
# Ship run events as OpenTelemetry spans and metrics. The API only: an
# exporter and its configuration belong to the deployment, not to us.
otel = ["opentelemetry-api>=1.20"]
# Scheduler shims (`pipeplan.integrations`). PipePlan runs a DAG and does not
# schedule one, so these are the glue every deployment would otherwise write by
# hand -- and get the degraded-run mapping wrong in the same way.
airflow = ["apache-airflow>=2.7"]
dagster = ["dagster>=1.6"]
prefect = ["prefect>=2.16"]
# Everything for local development and the test-suite.
dev = [
    "openpyxl>=3.1",
    "pyarrow>=14.0",
    "rapidfuzz>=3.0",
    "pymongo>=4.6",
    # In-process MongoDB stand-in: the conformance suite runs the whole adapter
    # contract against it. Not a substitute for a real server -- see the module
    # docstring of `pipeplan.adapters.mongo`.
    "mongomock>=4.1",
    "pytest>=7.0",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "mypy>=1.10",
    "ruff>=0.5",
    # Property-based tests (tests/property) and mutation testing (mutation.toml).
    "hypothesis>=6.100",
    "cosmic-ray>=8.3",
    # The reference event sink is only testable with the API installed.
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.20",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20",
]

[project.scripts]
pipeplan = "pipeplan.cli:main"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Extensibility: third-party packages contribute transforms / expressions by
# declaring entry points in these groups. The core never imports them directly.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

[project.entry-points."pipeplan.transforms"]
# example_action = "your_package.module:YourTransform"

[project.entry-points."pipeplan.expressions"]
# geodistance = "your_package.module:geodistance"

[project.entry-points."pipeplan.load_strategies"]

[project.entry-points."pipeplan.sql_dialects"]
# firebird = "your_package.module:FirebirdDialect"

[project.entry-points."pipeplan.adapters"]
# example = "your_package.module:YourAdapter"

[project.entry-points."pipeplan.stages"]
# sensor = "your_package.module:SensorExecutor"

[project.entry-points."pipeplan.middleware"]
# tracing = "your_package.module:TracingMiddleware"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/pipeplan"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["src", "."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config"
markers = [
    "requires_odbc: needs an OS-level ODBC driver (MS Access); skipped by default",
    # Each of these spawns a Python interpreter, which on Windows means a full
    # re-import of pandas per worker. Marked so they can be excluded from a
    # fast local loop; CI runs them.
    "slow_process: spawns worker processes",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["pipeplan"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "^\\s*\\.\\.\\.$",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "UP", "B", "C4"]
ignore = [
    "E501",   # line length is enforced by the formatter, not the linter
    "B008",   # function call in default arg -- pydantic Field() is idiomatic
    "UP042",  # str+Enum -> StrEnum changes str() semantics; not a safe swap here
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests deliberately import for side effects and shadow names in fixtures.
"tests/*" = ["F401", "B011"]

[tool.mypy]
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_configs = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
no_implicit_optional = true

# Strictness applies to the whole package, not a list. It was scoped to nine
# modules while the package was being made to type-check at all; that is done,
# so the list is gone rather than kept as a standing exemption nobody revisits.
#
# `disallow_untyped_defs` is the one that pays: an unannotated function is not
# merely undocumented, it is *unchecked* -- mypy skips the body -- so the gap
# hid errors rather than merely tolerating them.
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
warn_return_any = true

# Which code may import which: the import rules of docs/design/architecture.md (#282).
#
# Run by tests/repository/test_import_contracts.py, so the ordinary test run checks them on every
# host and in CI. By hand: `.venv/bin/lint-imports` from the repository root, with the package
# installed (`pip install -e .`). In a worktree sharing that virtualenv, run it with
# `PYTHONPATH=src`, or it reads the checkout the virtualenv was installed from.
#
# Where today's code breaks a rule, the import is listed under `ignore_imports` with the issue
# that will remove it. A listed import that no longer exists fails the run, so each list can
# only get shorter: remove an import and its line in the same commit. An entry marked
# "permanent" is not a breach but a stated exception, with its reason.
#
# `allow_indirect_imports` limits a rule to direct imports, so one listed breach is not
# reported again through every chain that passes through it.
#
# The code is one package with a folder for core and one for each module, and inside each a
# folder per kind of code (architecture.md, "How the code is laid out"). A `*` stands for any
# one of those folders, so `leaguebot.*.services` is every module's services and core's.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    leaguebot
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:nothing-below-the-cogs-imports-a-cog]
name = Nothing below the cogs imports a cog
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    leaguebot.*.services
    leaguebot.*.utils
    leaguebot.*.models
    leaguebot.core.db
forbidden_modules =
    leaguebot.*.cogs
allow_indirect_imports = True
ignore_imports =
    # #283: the in-memory state reaches for the seasons being set up and for pending reasons
    # (the reasons are signup's to publish, #286).
    leaguebot.core.services.in_memory_state -> leaguebot.signup.cogs.admin_review_cog
    leaguebot.core.services.in_memory_state -> leaguebot.core.cogs.season_cog
    # #285: the check-in rules live in the cog.
    leaguebot.attendance.services.rsvp_service -> leaguebot.attendance.cogs.attendance_cog
    # #286: signup's forced close lives in the module cog, and its views in its cogs.
    leaguebot.signup.services.wizard_service -> leaguebot.signup.cogs.admin_review_cog
    leaguebot.signup.services.wizard_service -> leaguebot.signup.cogs.signup_cog

[importlinter:contract:models-use-no-discord-and-no-database]
name = Models use no Discord and no database
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    leaguebot.*.models
forbidden_modules =
    discord
    aiosqlite
    sqlite3
    leaguebot.core.db
    leaguebot.*.services
    leaguebot.*.cogs

[importlinter:contract:the-database-code-imports-nothing-else-of-the-bots]
name = The database code imports nothing else of the bot's
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    leaguebot.core.db
forbidden_modules =
    leaguebot.*.cogs
    leaguebot.*.services
    leaguebot.*.utils
    leaguebot.*.models
    leaguebot.__main__

[importlinter:contract:utilities-use-no-services]
name = Utilities use no services
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    leaguebot.*.utils
forbidden_modules =
    leaguebot.*.services
allow_indirect_imports = True
ignore_imports =
    # Permanent: the bot's type names every service it carries, for the type checker only
    # (under TYPE_CHECKING). Services stay typed attributes on the bot (architecture.md).
    leaguebot.core.utils.league_bot -> leaguebot.*.services.*

[project]
name = "tg-agent"
version = "0.2.4.1"
description = "Telegram automation dependency for coding agents — tg-agent CLI + skill for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex"
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    {name = "Axisrow"}
]
keywords = ["telegram", "agent", "automation", "assistant", "telethon", "content"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Environment :: Web Environment",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Communications :: Chat",
]
dependencies = [
    "telethon>=1.43.2",
    "telethon-floodgate>=0.1.2,<0.2",
    "telethon-cli>=0.1.1",
    # Telethon's SOCKS/HTTP proxy path (TG_PROXY) needs python-socks with the
    # asyncio extra; without it Telethon silently ignores `proxy=` (warns only).
    "python-socks[asyncio]>=2.0",
    # Live dialog history reads (`dialogs read` / GET /dialogs/history, #1234
    # follow-up) reuse tg_messenger's StandaloneTelegramClient.history() for its
    # model mapping and flood-wait retry — see tg_agent/telegram/dm_history.py for why
    # it never opens a second connection. Note its per-instance history TTL cache
    # does NOT apply here: we build a throwaway client per call, so every read
    # hits Telegram. Caching happens one level up, in runtime_snapshots.
    "tg-messenger>=0.1.0",
    "fastapi>=0.136.3,<0.144",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.48.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.6",
    "aiosqlite>=0.22.1",
    "apscheduler>=3.11.3",
    "pydantic>=2.13.4",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14.1",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.2",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.29",
    # CLI framework (epic #959, argparse→Typer migration). Typer was already in
    # the tree transitively; pinning it directly makes the dependency explicit
    # for the Wave-0 scaffold (tg_agent/cli/typer_app.py). 0.12 is the first release
    # with the modern click 8.x API the scaffold relies on.
    "typer>=0.12.0",
    "cryptography>=48.0.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.5",
    "aiohttp>=3.13.5",
    "numpy>=2.4.6",
    "scikit-learn>=1.8.0",
    "jieba>=0.42.1",
    "langdetect>=1.0.9",
    "textual[syntax]>=8.2.8",
    "claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.87",
    "deepagents>=0.6.4",
    "huggingface_hub>=1.16.4",
    # Image-generation SDKs (issue #958): the OpenAI/Together/Replicate image
    # adapters use these instead of raw aiohttp. ``openai`` was already in the
    # tree transitively via ``langchain-openai``; pinning it directly makes the
    # dependency explicit. Together's images endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so it
    # reuses the ``openai`` SDK with a custom ``base_url`` (no heavy ``together``
    # SDK). ``replicate`` is lightweight (httpx + pydantic, both already present)
    # and removes the hand-rolled prediction-polling loop. HuggingFace stays on
    # raw aiohttp on purpose — its SDK returns a PIL.Image (a Pillow dependency)
    # whereas the raw path saves the image/* bytes directly.
    # openai 3.x adopted (the deliberate revisit the #1300 cap promised): 3.x
    # replaced the default httpx transport with the httpx2 package, so every
    # httpx.Client/AsyncClient monkeypatch in the test suite silently misses —
    # tests stop mocking the real request and hit the live provider. The
    # interception tests now patch BOTH httpx and httpx2 (guarded import), so
    # 2.x and 3.x stay sealed.
    "openai>=3.19.2,<4",
    "replicate>=1.0.7",
    "langchain>=1.3.2",
    "langchain-core>=1.4.0",
    "langchain-ollama>=1.1.0",
    "langchain-openai>=1.2.2",
    "tenacity>=9.1.4",
    "pybreaker>=1.4.0",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.14.3",
    "orjson>=3.10.0",
    "itsdangerous>=2.2.0",
    # ReDoS guard for user-supplied notification regexes: the `regex` engine's
    # `timeout=` aborts catastrophic backtracking inside its C matching loop,
    # which the stdlib `re` cannot (#1240). Present transitively (dateparser,
    # tiktoken) but declared here because it is now a direct runtime import.
    "regex>=2024.11.6",
    # QR login in the web panel (#1551): renders the tg://login token as an
    # inline SVG (SvgPathImage) — no PIL pull, unlike the PNG factories.
    "qrcode>=8.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [

    "pytest>=9.0.3",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.4.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "ruff>=0.15.14",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",

# Static security analysis config for `bandit -c pyproject.toml -r tg_agent` (#1053).
# The CI step (static-checks) runs it advisory (continue-on-error) for now; this
# scopes the scan to tg_agent/ and skips the test tree. Findings are triaged into a
# skip-list / `# nosec` here before the step is ever made blocking.
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests"]

# Dead-code scan whitelist (vulture, #1136). vulture auto-reads this section,
# so it applies both to `python -m vulture tg_agent/` and to scripts/code_health.py.
# Every name here is a VERIFIED false-positive — do not delete the code it
# refers to; each entry must say why it is intentionally "unused".
[tool.vulture]
ignore_names = [
    # tg_agent/utils/json.py safe_json_dumps(ensure_ascii=...): intentional
    # call-site-compatibility parameter after the orjson migration (#956) —
    # orjson is always UTF-8, the flag is accepted so existing
    # `safe_json_dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=True)` calls don't break, but has
    # no effect. Removing it would break call sites. See issue #1136.
    "ensure_ascii",
]

# Doc-coverage (interrogate, #1072). scripts/doc_coverage.py and the advisory
# CI step read this. `fail_under` is a SOFT baseline — a ratchet floor that
# surfaces regressions without forcing a docstring-everything sprint. Raise it
# as coverage climbs. interrogate ignores things that don't need a docstring
# (magic/init/nested/private, overloads).
# Ratchet history: 23 (#1072 floor) → 35 (#1134: documented the public-API
# facade — tg_agent/models.py Pydantic models, db.repos bundles, repository CRUD —
# lifting coverage 27% → 40.6%; floor set to 35 to lock in the win with a
# margin below the measured 40.6% so a stray docstring loss doesn't trip the
# gate). Doc-coverage is NOT a CI gate (#1097) — stays a local script.
[tool.interrogate]
fail_under = 35
ignore_init_method = true
ignore_init_module = true
ignore_magic = true
ignore_nested_functions = true
ignore_private = true
ignore_semiprivate = true
ignore_property_decorators = true
ignore_overloaded_functions = true
exclude = ["tests", "scripts", "build", "dist", "site", "mutants"]
verbose = 1

# Mutation testing (mutmut 3.8). Root-caused 07.10.26: stock mutmut is
# incompatible with a FLAT layout whose import package is literally named
# `src` (as this repo's was before the #1448 rename to tg_agent) — it strips a
# `src.` prefix from module names (breaking the trampoline routing and stats
# keys) and asserts against `src.`-prefixed trampoline hits. With the rename
# stock mutmut works again; the strip_src_prefix knob stays until the upstream
# PR (boxed/mutmut, branch fix/strip-src-prefix-knob) lands on PyPI — the fork
# is installed editable from its local checkout. The sandbox ships
# everything tests read outside tg_agent/tests, both at collection time (root
# conftest.py, scripts/) and at run time (.github/workflows/ci.yml,
# docs/reference/*, adk/). data/ is deliberately NOT copied — it holds the
# live DB; sandbox tests run on tmp/in-memory databases. mutmut never prunes
# a stale sandbox (deleted files keep their old copies) — `rm -rf mutants`
# before a rerun.
[tool.mutmut]
source_paths = ["tg_agent"]
also_copy = [
    "conftest.py",
    "scripts",
    ".github/workflows",
    "docs/reference",
    "adk",
    "mkdocs.yml",
    "config.yaml",
    "docker-compose.yml",
]
strip_src_prefix = false
# The fork-isolated serial stats phase pushes the whole suite (~10.7k tests,
# collect-verified 08.10.26) serially through one process; full sandbox runs
# have not completed yet, so the observations are from partial runs: leaky
# leftovers from earlier tests (unclosed sqlite connections, destroyed-pending
# asyncio tasks) get finalized mid-run, and pytest's unraisable AND
# threadexception plugins attribute each to whichever test happens to run
# (seen at 1713 and 3673 green tests respectively) — both plugins are
# disabled for mutation runs; the normal suite still enforces strictness in
# CI. Known cost: a mutant whose only observable effect is a
# broken cleanup path (unclosed connection, uncancelled task) now survives
# silently — the score overstates resource-lifecycle code; such survivors
# need a manual look.
pytest_add_cli_args = [
    "-p", "no:unraisableexception",
    "-p", "no:threadexception",
    "-m", "not mutmut_skip",
]

    # WordNet through nltk: which words of a request typed as a sentence are things, places or

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Bundled royalty-free music, shipped as its own distribution so a plain install
# stays small. Published by the release workflow before the main wheel, so `all`
# can require it.
music = [
    "immich-memories-music>=0.1.0",
]
# Mac-specific: Metal tells the automatic tier that this Mac has a GPU.
mac = [
    "pyobjc-framework-Metal>=9.0; sys_platform == 'darwin'",
]
# OIDC authentication (only needed for SSO login)
auth = [
    "authlib>=1.9.1",
]
# Local Demucs stem separation (in-process, no API server needed)
# Model cache: ~/.cache/torch/hub/ (~80MB for htdemucs)
demucs = [
    "demucs>=4.0",
    "soundfile>=0.14.0",
]
# Local ACE-Step music generation (in-process, no API server needed)
# ⚠️  NOT a pip extra — ACE-Step is not published on PyPI.
#     Install the tested v0.1.8 tag with --no-deps, then its inference-only
#     dependencies. The upstream UI set conflicts with this app's Starlette.
#     See docs-site/docs/make/titles-maps-music.md for setup instructions.
# Required when preparing missing editorial public heads and detector facts.
# Weights and the compact-caption endpoint are separate setup dependencies.
#
# Every seat here is an ONNX graph on ONNX Runtime, so this extra is torch-free
# and resolves with no `nvidia-*` wheel at all. That is what the ONNX detector
# bought: the sensitive-content seat used to be a timm/torch model, which cost
# 920 MB in a CPU image, 11 s of interpreter start-up, and the whole class of
# bug where `torch` and `torchvision` resolve from different indexes (#805,
# #806).
editorial = [
    "onnxruntime>=1.31.0",
    "tokenizers>=0.23.3",
    "huggingface-hub>=1.33.0",
    "kaldi-native-fbank>=1.20",
]
# The same seats on a CUDA host. Split by device rather than by feature, the way
# immich-machine-learning splits its own image: only this variant pulls the CUDA
# wheels, and the CPU one must never contain them.
#
# It REPLACES `editorial`, never joins it: `onnxruntime-gpu` ships the CPU
# provider too, and installing both distributions puts two copies of the same
# import name in one environment. `all` and `all-mac` therefore keep the CPU
# variant, and the marker keeps a Linux-only wheel out of a macOS resolution.
editorial-cuda = [
    # 1.27+ requires CUDA 13; the supported image uses CUDA 12 / cuDNN 9.
    "onnxruntime-gpu>=1.26,<1.27; sys_platform == 'linux'",
    "tokenizers>=0.23.3",
    "huggingface-hub>=1.33.0",
    "kaldi-native-fbank>=1.20",
]

all = [
    "immich-memories[music]",
    "immich-memories[auth]",
    # demucs pulls sphn, which has no manylinux aarch64 wheel; building it there needs
    # Rust plus a C compiler. Skipped on that one platform; vocal separation degrades
    # gracefully without it (#2081).
    "immich-memories[demucs]; sys_platform != 'linux' or platform_machine != 'aarch64'",
    "immich-memories[editorial]",
]
# All features for macOS (adds the Metal probe)
all-mac = [
    "immich-memories[music]",
    "immich-memories[auth]",
    "immich-memories[demucs]; sys_platform != 'linux' or platform_machine != 'aarch64'",
    "immich-memories[mac]",
    "immich-memories[editorial]",
]
dev = [
    "tokenizers>=0.23.3",  # Real portable Laya tokenizer in the lightweight unit suite.
    "pytest>=9.0.3",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4.0",
    "pytest-benchmark>=5.3.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5",
    "pillow-heif>=1.8.1",  # Encodes HEIC test inputs; pi-heif decodes only. Never shipped.
    "mypy>=2.4.0",
    "ruff>=0.1",
    "pre-commit>=3.0",
    "commitizen>=4.19.2",
    "python-semantic-release>=10.7.0",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0",
    # Advanced quality gates
    "refurb>=2.0",
    "import-linter>=2.15",
    "grimp>=3.0",
    "deptry>=0.25.1",
    "diff-cover>=10.6.0",
    "oidc-provider-mock>=0.3",
    # E2E browser tests
    "pytest-playwright>=0.5",
    # Privacy audio tests (lightweight, no torch needed)
    "soundfile>=0.12",
    "hypothesis>=6.168.3",
]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# On non-tagged commits: 0.1.1.dev1+g1234567
# On tagged commits: 0.1.0

[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
# Exact releases have no local suffix. Unreleased builds keep their commit identity.
local_scheme = "node-and-date"
tag_regex = '^v(?P<version>\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-(?:rc|dev)\.\d+)?)$'
# WHY --exclude: a dev rehearsal (#1940) tags v0.0.0-dev.<run id> on main, and setuptools-scm cannot
# add a distance to a .devN version, so every later build failed to compute its version.
scm.git.describe_command = "git describe --dirty --tags --long --match v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]* --exclude *-dev.*"

[tool.hatch.build.hooks.vcs]
version-file = "src/immich_memories/_version.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/immich_memories"]
# The built web client is gitignored (#1580); artifacts ship it anyway, and hatch_build.py
# refuses a standard wheel that would go out without it.
artifacts = ["src/immich_memories/web/client"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.hooks.custom]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]

artifacts = ["src/immich_memories/web/client"]
include = [
    "/hatch_build.py",
    "/src",
    "/tests",
    "/web/src",
    "/web/package.json",
    "/web/package-lock.json",
    "/web/svelte.config.js",
    "/web/tsconfig.json",
    "/web/vite.config.ts",
]

# Semantic Release Configuration

[tool.semantic_release.branches.main]

match = "rc/*"
prerelease = true

[tool.semantic_release.changelog]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "analysis-stages-are-layered"
name = "Each analysis stage imports only the stages below it"
type = "layers"
containers = ["immich_memories.analysis"]
# Top to bottom: composition, then the film's structure down to the model transport.
layers = [
    "runtime",
    "structure",
    "polish",
    "selection",
    "stories",
    "film",
    "audience",
    "special_days",
    "reading",
    "preparation",
    "captions",
    "clips",
    "facts",
    "sources",
    "corpus",
    "places",
    "judgments",
    "llm",
]

    # Loading a config derives the caption identity from the caption contract, so config (which
    # every stage imports) reads two caption modules; that is not a stage depending on captions.
    "immich_memories.config.tiers -> immich_memories.analysis.captions.identity",
    "immich_memories.config.models.editorial -> immich_memories.analysis.captions.contract",
    # The shared timing policy is built from the run's GenerationParams and title settings,
    # imported lazily from the orchestrator modules above every stage.
    "immich_memories.processing.editorial_timing -> immich_memories.generate",
    "immich_memories.processing.editorial_timing -> immich_memories.generate_settings",
]

[tool.refurb]
# FURB184 (chained assignments) is a style preference — config + result = func(config)
# is more readable than result = func(MockConfig()) in tests
ignore = [
    "FURB184",  # chained assignments: config + result is more readable
    "FURB110",  # X if X else Y: false positive on Linux with similar variable names
]
# refurb sees src/ layout modules twice — only scan the package, not src/
python_version = "3.11"

testpaths = ["tests"]
# The inference service is its own top-level package: it runs in its own image,

# suite resolves it from the tree the same way.
pythonpath = ["services/inference"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
markers = [
    "integration: requires FFmpeg (deselect with '-m not integration')",
    "extras: needs the torch-family optional dependencies (demucs/editorial)",
    "e2e: Playwright E2E browser tests (deselect with '-m not e2e')",
    "slow: long-running tests (full generation pipeline, ~10min)",
    "perf: performance benchmarks (run with: make benchmark-perf)",
    "demo: renders a docs demo asset (run with: make demo-output)",
    "install_checks: meets the real pre-run install checks instead of an install that ran models fetch",
    "real_mounts: reads this machine's own mount table instead of the suite's local one",
    "container: runs the built image through docker compose (run with: make test-container)",
    "feature(id): checks an advertised feature, by its row id in tests/features/inventory.yaml (make feature-check)",
    "fake_immich_only(reason): a feature test only the fake Immich can drive; the real-Immich pass skips it with the reason",
    "real_immich_only: a feature test that needs a real Immich (make test-features-real-immich); the fake pass skips it",
]
# `-p no:quadrants`: the quadrants distribution registers a pytest11 plugin, so
# merely having it installed pulls its C++ runtime into every pytest session,
# including the thousands of tests that never touch a kernel. The app imports it
# in exactly one place and nowhere near collection time; blocking the plugin
# keeps it that way, and is a no-op where the wheel does not exist.
addopts = "-p no:quadrants -m 'not integration and not e2e and not container'"

source = ["src/immich_memories", "services/inference/immich_memories_inference"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]

# This floor prevents erosion — the REAL check is diff-cover at 80% per PR.
fail_under = 65
show_missing = true
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
    "\\.\\.\\.",  # Protocol stubs

    # every one of them as missed however hard the pixel tests exercise them.
    "@ti\\.kernel",

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter — enforces the boundary contracts declared in
# agent-policy.yaml (boundaries:). See AGENTS.md for the framing.
#
# Run:    python -m importlinter
# CI:     python scripts/run-import-linter.py --out build/import-linter-report.json
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["api", "app", "capabilities", "core", "providers", "redaction", "retrieval", "semantic", "storage"]
exclude_type_checking_imports = true
include_external_packages = false

# Every `forbidden` contract sets `allow_indirect_imports = true` to assert
# DIRECT boundaries only. The core ↔ semantic / core → capabilities tangle
# (see AGENTS.md "Known import-graph smells") would make transitive checks
# unsatisfiable (e.g. api → core → semantic).

# 1. providers is a leaf — never imports siblings.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "providers stays leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["providers"]
forbidden_modules = ["api", "app", "capabilities", "core", "retrieval", "semantic", "storage"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# 1b. redaction is a cross-cutting leaf utility — imports nothing internal.
# Homed as a top-level package (not under semantic) so providers/core/app/
# semantic can all depend on it without crossing a layer boundary.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "redaction stays leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["redaction"]
forbidden_modules = ["api", "app", "capabilities", "core", "providers", "retrieval", "semantic", "storage"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# 2. retrieval stays below orchestration.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "retrieval stays below orchestration"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["retrieval"]
forbidden_modules = ["api", "app", "capabilities", "semantic"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# 3. semantic stays below the runtime/HTTP entry layers.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "semantic stays below runtime"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["semantic"]
forbidden_modules = ["api", "app"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# 4. api stays thin — only depends on core.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "api stays thin"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["api"]
forbidden_modules = ["app", "capabilities", "semantic", "retrieval", "storage", "providers"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# 5. semantic.* submodules don't form import cycles.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "semantic siblings acyclic"
type = "acyclic_siblings"
ancestors = ["semantic"]

# 6. storage → app: no direct imports allowed.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "storage stays out of app"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["storage"]
forbidden_modules = ["app"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# 7. storage → capabilities: one baselined import. Adding a second offender
#    fails CI. The exception (storage.sqlite_workstream ->
#    capabilities.workstreams) is documented in AGENTS.md.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "storage stays out of capabilities (one baselined exception)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["storage"]
forbidden_modules = ["capabilities"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = ["storage.sqlite_workstream -> capabilities.workstreams"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 100
# docs/evidence is frozen verbatim records — data, not owned code (same standard
# as the markdown gate's exclusion list in .claude/verify.md). Excluding it here
# covers lint AND format, in both verify.sh modes, and ends the per-rule
# exemption creep (T20 -> C901 -> ... one per-file-ignores line per new rule).
# force-exclude extends this to explicitly-passed paths (the PostToolUse
# autofix hook invokes ruff on the edited file directly).
extend-exclude = ["docs/evidence"]
force-exclude = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Pin the rule set explicitly rather than inheriting ruff's defaults. The
# PostToolUse autofix hook resolves ruff from PATH/uvx while this repo locks
# its own version, and the two drifted: a wider default set fired UP/SIM/RUF
# on the files that happened to be edited, and `ruff check src/ tests/` at
# the locked version reported those same files clean — so the tree silently
# split into modernized and legacy halves. An explicit `select` makes the
# answer identical under both binaries (verified: 674 findings either way).
#
# E4/E7/E9/F are ruff's own defaults, restated here so nothing depends on
# what "default" means in a given release. Beyond them: B (bugbear —
# silent-truncation zip, mutable defaults), I (import sorting), T20 (no
# print in library code — use logging; rules/python/hooks.md), UP (pyupgrade
# — PEP 585/604 typing; the floor is py310 so `list[str]` / `X | None` are
# native at runtime). C901 (mccabe) is the complexity budget — a per-function
# ceiling so that "one more branch" has to be argued for rather than merged by
# default; its threshold and exemption ledger are configured below.
# ANN001-003/201 require explicit types at function boundaries and ANN401 bans
# bare `Any` there (LLM-first axis 4, 2026-08-31): a typed boundary is a
# machine-checkable spec — the frozen edge for regeneration and cross-session
# edits. Production code had zero missing annotations at adoption, and the 24
# bare-Any sites were drained the same day with no exemption and no inline
# noqa. ANN202/204-206 (private/dunder return types) stay unselected — the
# explicit-pin policy adds rules when argued for, not by family.
select = [
    "E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "B", "I", "T20", "UP", "C901",
    "ANN001", "ANN002", "ANN003", "ANN201", "ANN401",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Budget rule: drain, do not raise — any change to this number needs a dated
# reason in .claude/verify.md (harness ADR-0056). The exemption ledger in
# per-file-ignores is empty and stays empty: a function over the budget is a
# design question, not a config entry. When one cannot be drained the answer
# is to stop lowering the threshold, not to exempt the function.
# Distribution as-of 2026-08-31 (src/tests/scripts/evals): p50=1 / p90=3 /
# p95=5 / p99=9 / max=10. Introduced at 15 on 2026-08-28 (then p99=10 / max=35,
# 13 functions drained the same day) and walked down 15 -> 13 -> 11 -> 10 on
# 2026-08-31, draining 24 functions and exempting none. The budget now sits at
# p99: 26 functions are at 10, so the next branch added to any of them has to be
# argued for rather than merged by default.
# "10 was rejected" in the 2026-08-28 note meant rejected as an INTRODUCTION
# threshold, where it would have put 24 files on the exemption list and
# blinded the most-edited modules. Reached by draining instead, it exempts
# nothing — which is the road that was taken.
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# Keep explicit `X as X` re-export blocks (core/llm/__init__.py) compact
# instead of one import statement per name.
combine-as-imports = true
# Declare the first-party roots instead of letting ruff infer them from what
# happens to exist on disk. `.claude/verify.sh --staged` checks the *index*
# by materializing only the staged files into a tmpdir, so a commit that
# stages tests without src/ would leave `contemplative_agent` unresolvable
# there — inferred as third-party, and every test file then fails I001 on a
# section split that full mode considers correct (2026-07-31, 14 false
# positives). Declaring it makes staged and full mode agree by construction.
known-first-party = ["contemplative_agent", "tests", "evals"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Console-UI seams where print IS the interface, not stray logging.
"src/contemplative_agent/cli/**" = ["T20"]                      # CLI user output
"src/contemplative_agent/adapters/moltbook/agent.py" = ["T20"]  # ADR-0012 approval-gate TTY display
"src/contemplative_agent/adapters/dialogue/peer.py" = ["T20"]   # stderr turn progress
"src/contemplative_agent/testing/__main__.py" = ["T20"]         # ADR-0088 conformance CLI
# tests/ and the ANN family: test functions are not consumed boundaries (nothing
# regenerates against their signatures), and the corpus carries 5,810 missing
# annotations — cost with no LLM-first payoff. Permanent, not a drain ledger.
"tests/**" = ["T20", "ANN001", "ANN002", "ANN003", "ANN201", "ANN401"]
"scripts/**" = ["T20"]
"evals/**" = ["T20"]    # probe/CLI 系 (benchmark_distill と同じ扱い) — print が UI
# docs/evidence/** の免除行は 2026-08-31 に撤去 — [tool.ruff] の extend-exclude が
# ディレクトリごと検査対象から外した (凍結記録はデータであってコードではない)

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["glassbox"]
omit = ["tests/*", "examples/*", "glassbox/benchmarks/*"]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 80
show_missing = true

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_return_any = false
warn_unused_ignores = true

# The rebuilt layers are held to a stricter standard than the v1 code they replace.
#
# `warn_unreachable` is deliberately NOT enabled. The domain is a trust boundary:
# its `__post_init__` guards validate types that mypy already proves for typed
# callers, but which are NOT guaranteed for JSON deserialisation, untyped
# adapters or v1 code. mypy reports those guards as unreachable; deleting them to
# satisfy the checker would remove the validation the layer exists to provide.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["glassbox.domain.*", "glassbox.ports.*"]
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
warn_return_any = true
strict_equality = true

# Type debt register (GB-041): EMPTY as of Wave 6. All 30 originally-enumerated
# v1 modules now type-check cleanly with no ignore_errors override (verified
# via `mypy glassbox --ignore-missing-imports` in a clean venv containing only
# the pinned mypy, to rule out environment noise such as the stray-numpy
# issue below -- most of the original 144 errors were cascades from a handful
# of root causes: implicit-Optional defaults, unvalidated Optional bytes
# concatenation, and untyped dict/Queue literals). A module may only be
# RE-added here with the same review as any other invariant waiver.

# numpy is not a glassbox dependency (mandatory or optional) and is never
# imported anywhere in this package. Some typeshed stdlib stubs (array,
# ctypes) reference it under TYPE_CHECKING for buffer-protocol typing, so
# mypy loads whatever numpy happens to be on the host's Python path even
# though glassbox never imports it -- and a numpy version whose stubs use
# newer syntax (e.g. PEP 695 `type` statements) than this project's
# `python_version` target crashes the whole run before it reaches any
# glassbox module. Skip it explicitly rather than depending on the host
# environment not having a too-new numpy installed.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "numpy.*"
follow_imports = "skip"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.black]
line-length = 100
target-version = ["py313"]

[tool.isort]
profile = "black"
line_length = 100

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Architecture contracts (GB-004)
#
# The dependency rule `domain <- ports <- app <- adapters` is enforced three
# ways, deliberately:
#
#   1. import-linter, below, is the authoritative machine-checked contract;
#   2. tests/test_layering.py re-states the same rules as AST assertions, so the
#      architecture gate still runs when the optional tool is not installed and
#      so violations come with a readable, localised message;
#   3. tests/test_layering.py::TestContractConsistency asserts (1) and (2) agree,
#      so the two can never drift apart.
#
# `glassbox.adapters` as a whole is NOT a layer: only the rebuilt subtree
# `glassbox.adapters.outbound` (plus `glassbox.adapters.inbound`) participates.
# `glassbox.adapters.inbound` (the process entry points: http/, cli/) is the
# composition root -- it may freely import outbound adapters to wire concrete
# object graphs, but nothing may import it back: the "No rebuilt layer imports
# a concrete inbound adapter" contract below keeps that direction one-way, and
# it is held to the same v1-anchoring ban as every other rebuilt layer.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "glassbox"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture: domain <- ports <- app <- adapters.outbound"
type = "layers"
layers = [
  "glassbox.adapters.outbound",
  "glassbox.app",
  "glassbox.ports",
  "glassbox.domain",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The application layer never imports a concrete adapter"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["glassbox.app"]
forbidden_modules = ["glassbox.adapters"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "No rebuilt layer imports a concrete inbound adapter"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "glassbox.domain",
  "glassbox.ports",
  "glassbox.app",
  "glassbox.adapters.outbound",
]
forbidden_modules = ["glassbox.adapters.inbound"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The pure layers never reach forwards into orchestration or infrastructure"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["glassbox.domain", "glassbox.ports"]
forbidden_modules = ["glassbox.app", "glassbox.adapters"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Rebuilt layers are never anchored to the v1 code they replace"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "glassbox.domain",
  "glassbox.ports",
  "glassbox.app",
  "glassbox.adapters.outbound",
  "glassbox.adapters.inbound",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "glassbox.api",
  "glassbox.authoring",
  "glassbox.benchmarks",
  "glassbox.compliance",
  "glassbox.events",
  "glassbox.governance",
  "glassbox.integrations",
  "glassbox.orchestration",
  "glassbox.rag",
  "glassbox.rules",
  "glassbox.scenarios",
  "glassbox.security",
  "glassbox.store",
  "glassbox.telemetry",
  "glassbox.testing",
  "glassbox.workflow",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Invariant lint (GB-004)
#
# Deliberately narrow. black, isort and pylint already cover style; this gate
# exists only to make the non-negotiable invariants in the implementation plan
# mechanically unbreakable. Every selected rule maps to a named invariant.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py313"
extend-exclude = ["sdk", "docs", ".pytest-tmp"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E722",   # bare except .............................. I5 (never swallow)
  "S110",   # try-except-pass .......................... I5
  "S112",   # try-except-continue ...................... I5
  "B904",   # raise without `from` ..................... I5 (loses the cause)
  "B006",   # mutable default argument ................. I7 (bounded state)
  "B008",   # function call in a default argument ...... I7
  "TID251", # banned API ............................... I6, I10
]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"threading.local".msg = "Use contextvars.ContextVar; threading.local loses the tenant binding across executor boundaries (invariant I10, GB-023)."

# Lint debt register (GB-041/GB-004a). Empty as of Wave 5: every E722/S110/S112/
# B904/TID251 violation across the 17 originally-enumerated modules was fixed
# (bare except -> except Exception, try/except/pass -> logged or
# contextlib.suppress, raise-without-from -> raise ... from exc,
# threading.local -> contextvars.ContextVar). Tests still legitimately assert
# on swallowed-exception behaviour and construct deliberately broken objects.
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/*" = ["B904", "S110"]
