[project]
name = "prosperity"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Application de gestion des finances personnelles auto-hébergée pour un foyer."
requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
dependencies = [
    "alembic>=1.18.4",
    "asyncpg>=0.31.0",
    "email-validator>=2.2",
    "fastapi>=0.118",
    "ofxparse>=0.21",
    "pwdlib[argon2]>=0.2.1",
    "pydantic>=2.13.4",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14.2",
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.10",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9",
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.49",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.38",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.3",
    "httpx>=0.28",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.152.9",
    "testcontainers[postgres]>=4.14.2",
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9.10",
    "factory-boy>=3.3.3",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "coverage>=7.14.0",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "pyright>=1.1.405",
    "ruff>=0.14.0",
    "pre-commit>=4.0",
    "import-linter>=2.3",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "deptry>=0.25.1",
]

# `deptry` : cohérence des dépendances Python déclarées/importées (S-quality-gate-1/S07).
# `exclude` reprend l'exclusion par défaut de `tests/` (plus `client`, `htmlcov` et les
# caches) — volontairement, pour que DEP004 (une dépendance du groupe `dev` importée
# depuis `backend/` ou `alembic/`) reste détectée ; la contrepartie est qu'une dépendance
# `[project.dependencies]` consommée uniquement depuis `tests/` doit être ignorée en
# DEP002 avec motif (cas `email-validator`).
# `[dependency-groups].dev` (PEP 735) est déjà reconnu nativement comme groupe dev
# par deptry — aucune option supplémentaire n'est nécessaire pour ça.
[tool.deptry]
known_first_party = ["backend"]
# `exclude` REMPLACE la liste par défaut de deptry (qui contient `.git`) : sans `\.git` ici,
# un worktree du cycle (`.git/scd-worktrees/<ticket>/`) est scanné et fait rougir la gate.
exclude = ["\\.git", ".venv", "client", "htmlcov", "tests", "\\.hypothesis", "\\.pytest_cache", "\\.ruff_cache", "\\.mypy_cache", "__pycache__"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# DEP002 (déclarée mais jamais importée par son nom) : chargées à l'exécution par un
# mécanisme indirect, jamais par un `import` explicite dans backend/alembic/tests.
# - asyncpg : driver SQLAlchemy async résolu depuis l'URL de connexion (`postgresql+asyncpg://`).
# - python-multipart : parsing multipart/form-data fait par Starlette en interne (FastAPI File/Form).
# - uvicorn : serveur ASGI lancé en CLI/entrypoint, jamais importé en Python.
# - email-validator : chargé à l'exécution par pydantic.EmailStr (backend/modules/auth/schemas.py),
#   jamais importé par son nom hors tests/ (exclu du scan).
DEP002 = ["asyncpg", "python-multipart", "uvicorn", "email-validator"]

[tool.uv]
package = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Session-scoped loop so async tests share the same loop as the session-scoped
# testcontainers/db_engine/db_session fixtures (tests/integration/conftest.py).
# Without this, tests on the default function loop get "attached to a different
# loop" errors from asyncpg resources created on the fixture's session loop.
asyncio_default_test_loop_scope = "session"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"
markers = [
    "e2e: black-box HTTP user-journey tests (committed_client + real Postgres)",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["backend"]
branch = true
# SQLAlchemy's async stack and FastAPI's threaded sync routes both
# require explicit concurrency tracking — without these, route bodies
# and async-backed DB calls report uncovered even when fully exercised
# in tests (the bodies execute in worker threads/greenlets that
# coverage's default tracer doesn't see).
concurrency = ["greenlet", "thread"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py313"
extend-exclude = [".venv", "htmlcov", ".hypothesis", ".pytest_cache", "client"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# C90 (mccabe, max-complexity=10) : complexité cyclomatique. SIM/RET : idiomes de simplification
# et de retour anticipé. PERF : pièges de performance connus (boucles, comprehensions). PT :
# idiomes pytest (fixtures, raises, paramétrage). W : warnings pycodestyle. PLR déjà couvert par PL.
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "PL", "C90", "SIM", "RET", "PERF", "PT", "W"]
# PGH004 : pas de `# noqa` nu ; RUF100 : pas de `# noqa` mort. Le filet escape-hatches vit ici,
# pas dans un grep CI (cf. runbooks/ci.md § Escape-hatches).
extend-select = ["PGH004", "RUF100"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["backend"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = [
    "PLR2004", # 770 remontées : nombres magiques légitimes en test (codes HTTP, effectifs d'échantillon)
    "PT018",   # 53 remontées : assertions composites du patron arrange/act/assert (vérifs liées regroupées)
    "PT019",   # 16 remontées : fixtures `_`-préfixées injectées pour leur effet de bord (setup/teardown), jamais lues
]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"

# Type checker: pyright (cf. P01.3.1) — faster than mypy and better Pydantic v2 support.
# Strict on backend/ (production surface); standard on tests/ where third-party
# libs without stubs (testcontainers, factory_boy) would otherwise drown signal.
[tool.pyright]
include = ["backend", "tests"]
exclude = ["**/__pycache__", ".venv", "htmlcov", ".hypothesis", ".pytest_cache"]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
pythonPlatform = "Linux"
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
extraPaths = ["."]
reportMissingImports = "error"
reportMissingTypeStubs = "warning"
useLibraryCodeForTypes = true
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "tests"
reportMissingTypeStubs = "none"
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "none"

[importlinter]
# Enforces architectural boundaries defined in docs/local/ARCHITECTURE_CONTRACT.md.
# Run manually with:  lint-imports
# In CI, triggered by:  python scripts/check_architecture_sizes.py
root_packages =
    app
    core_ui
    plugin_marketplace
    servers
    studio
    web_ui
include_external_packages = True


# ─── Contract 1: agent_kernel must not import Django ORM ──────────────────────
# Goal: Keep the kernel pure Python so it can run in any environment
# (CLI, worker, cloud function) without a full Django stack.
[importlinter:contract:agent-kernel-no-django-orm]
name = agent_kernel must not import Django ORM models layer
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.agent_kernel
forbidden_modules =
    django

# ─── Contract 2: app/core must not import Django feature apps ─────────────────
# Goal: Shared infrastructure in app/core must remain dependency-free from
# feature apps so it can be reused across the whole project.
[importlinter:contract:app-core-no-django-apps]
name = app/core shared services must not import servers, studio, or core_ui
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.core
forbidden_modules =
    servers
    studio
    core_ui

# ─── Contract 3: app/tools must not import Django feature apps ────────────────
# Goal: Tool implementations must stay decoupled from feature apps.
# No legacy exceptions remain; feature-app behavior must be reached through
# app-level providers or gateway interfaces.
[importlinter:contract:app-tools-no-django-apps]
name = app/tools must not import servers, studio, or core_ui
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.tools
forbidden_modules =
    servers
    studio
    core_ui

# ─── Contract 4: app/tools must not import agent_kernel ───────────────────────
# Goal: Tools are leaf-layer utilities; importing the kernel would create a
# circular dependency risk and blur the kernel/tool boundary.
# Dependency direction must always flow: agent_kernel -> tools, never reversed.
[importlinter:contract:app-tools-no-agent-kernel]
name = app/tools must not import app/agent_kernel (dependency inversion)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.tools
forbidden_modules =
    app.agent_kernel

# ─── Contract 5: core_ui must not import servers or studio ────────────────────
# Goal: The UI layer should focus on session management and view aggregation;
# business logic lives in feature apps or app/.
[importlinter:contract:core-ui-isolation]
name = core_ui must not import servers or studio
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core_ui
forbidden_modules =
    servers
    studio


# ─── Contract 6: servers must not import studio directly ──────────────────────
# Goal: Feature-app isolation — servers communicates with studio via Django
# signals or app-level provider/gateway interfaces, never via direct imports.
[importlinter:contract:servers-no-studio]
name = servers must not import studio directly (use Signals or SkillProvider DI)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    servers
forbidden_modules =
    studio


# ─── Contract 7: studio must not import servers directly ──────────────────────
# Goal: Mirror of contract 6 — bidirectional isolation between feature apps.
[importlinter:contract:studio-no-servers]
name = studio must not import servers directly
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    studio
forbidden_modules =
    servers


# ─── Contract 8: plugin runtime must remain framework-free ───────────────────
# Goal: app/plugins exposes pure contracts for safe extensions. It must not
# import Django or feature apps that would pull runtime side effects.
[importlinter:contract:plugin-runtime-no-django-or-feature-apps]
name = app/plugins must not import Django or feature apps
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.plugins
forbidden_modules =
    django
    core_ui
    plugin_marketplace
    servers
    studio


# ─── Contract 9: plugin marketplace must not couple to feature apps ──────────
# Goal: marketplace storage and policy may use core_ui access/audit, but cannot
# reach directly into servers or studio feature implementations.
[importlinter:contract:plugin-marketplace-no-feature-apps]
name = plugin_marketplace must not import servers or studio
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    plugin_marketplace
forbidden_modules =
    servers
    studio

    "A",   # flake8-builtins
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "TCH", # flake8-type-checking
    "RUF", # ruff-specific
    "S",   # flake8-bandit
    "PT",  # flake8-pytest-style
    "ANN",     # flake8-annotations (codigo de prod; ignorado em tests/)
    "BLE001",  # blind except
    "FBT001",  # boolean-type-hint-positional-argument
    "C901",    # complex-structure (mccabe)
    "PLR2004", # magic-value-comparison
    "PLR0912", # too-many-branches
    "PLR0913", # too-many-arguments
    "PLR0915", # too-many-statements

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]

    "ANN",                                  # tests podem ser destipados
    "PLR2004",                              # magic values em asserts
    "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "PLR0912",        # fixtures e factories sao grandes
    "C901",                                 # tests podem ter setup complexo
    "FBT001",                               # callsites de stub/fake
    "BLE001",                               # tests as vezes capturam Exception
    "LOG014",                               # tests nao usam exc_info
    "PLW0603",                              # tests podem manipular singletons
    "PYI034",                               # FakeUnitOfWork etc sao stubs
]
"full-test/tests/**" = [
    "S101", "S105", "S106", "TCH", "SIM105", "PT012", "RUF059",
    "ANN", "PLR2004", "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "PLR0912",
    "C901", "FBT001", "BLE001", "LOG014", "PLW0603", "PYI034",
]
# Daemon do relay: `_drenar`/`processar_ciclo` expoem 6 parametros de
# proposito — engine + costuras injetaveis (handlers, nome_handler, lote,
# lease, relogio) que permitem teste unitario sem Postgres e sem relogio real.
# Quebrar em um objeto de config so para satisfazer o limite de 5 argumentos
# obscureceria as costuras; PLR0913 e ruido aqui.
"relay/**" = ["PLR0913"]
"**/exceptions.py" = ["N818"]
"**/interfaces/schemas.py" = ["S105", "TCH003"]
"**/interfaces/router*.py" = ["B008"]
"**/interfaces/middleware.py" = ["B008", "TCH002"]
"**/interfaces/dependencies.py" = ["B008"]
"migrations/**" = ["E402"]
"**/dtos.py" = ["S105"]
"migrations/env.py" = ["E402"]
# Script utilitario de build (gera o PDF de entrega). Chama binarios de dev
# conhecidos (gh/git/npx/pandoc) via subprocess com lista de args fixa, sem
# shell=True — nao ha superficie de injecao. S603 (subprocess) e S607 (partial
# path, resolvido via PATH de proposito p/ portabilidade) viram ruido aqui.
# Obs: este ignore e da ruff (regra "S"); o bandit "real" nao falha nesses
# porque sao severidade LOW e o gate roda com --severity-level high.
".claude/skills/entrega-tech-challenge/scripts/*.py" = ["S603", "S607"]

# Contratos de arquitetura (ADR-015 / RNF-017): a regra de dependencia da
# Clean Architecture e verificada por lint (`make lint-arch` / CI).
# `infraestrutura` (Frameworks & Drivers) fica fora do contrato de camadas
# porque importa `aplicacao`/`dominio` legitimamente — adapters implementam
# ports definidos pelas camadas internas; o sentido proibido (dominio e
# aplicacao -> infraestrutura) e coberto pelo contrato forbidden. `compartilhado`
# e shared kernel, nao contexto delimitado: fica fora dos containers de camadas,
# mas seu `dominio` e sua `aplicacao` entram no forbidden pelos mesmos motivos.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["src", "relay"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Camadas Clean por contexto (interfaces -> aplicacao -> dominio)"
type = "layers"
layers = ["interfaces", "aplicacao", "dominio"]
containers = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo",
    "src.catalogo_servicos",
    "src.estoque",
    "src.ordem_servico",
    "src.autenticacao",
    # Shared kernel tambem respeita a ordem interna de camadas (finding da
    # revisao arquitetural de fechamento: estava fora do lint de layers).
    "src.compartilhado",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Dominio e aplicacao nao importam infraestrutura de nenhum contexto"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo.dominio",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.dominio",
    "src.estoque.dominio",
    "src.ordem_servico.dominio",
    "src.autenticacao.dominio",
    "src.compartilhado.dominio",
    "src.cliente_veiculo.aplicacao",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.aplicacao",
    "src.estoque.aplicacao",
    "src.ordem_servico.aplicacao",
    "src.autenticacao.aplicacao",
    "src.compartilhado.aplicacao",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo.infraestrutura",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.infraestrutura",
    "src.estoque.infraestrutura",
    "src.ordem_servico.infraestrutura",
    "src.autenticacao.infraestrutura",
    "src.compartilhado.infraestrutura",
]

# `src` (a aplicacao) NUNCA importa o sidecar operacional `relay/`: o sentido
# legitimo e `relay -> src` (o relay consome dominio/infra de src). O sentido
# inverso (`src -> relay`) fecharia um ciclo de pacote `src -> relay -> src`,
# invisivel ao linter enquanto `relay` ficava fora de `root_packages`. Com
# `relay` agora graficado, este contrato torna o ciclo regressao-proof. As
# queries de DLQ que antes moravam em `relay/dlq.py` migraram para
# `src.compartilhado.infraestrutura.outbox_dlq`.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "src nao importa relay (relay e sidecar; so relay -> src e permitido)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src"]
forbidden_modules = ["relay"]

# Independencia entre bounded contexts (ADR-015 / DDD): o ``dominio`` e a
# ``aplicacao`` de cada um dos 5 contextos NAO importam o ``dominio``/
# ``aplicacao`` de nenhum outro — comunicacao entre contextos passa por

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    app

# Layer ordering (top may import bottom, never the reverse). Note that this
# contract only forbids UPWARD imports; the forbidden contracts below restrict
# specific downward edges that the ordering alone would allow.
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Layered architecture
type = layers
layers =
    app.web
    app.api
    app.domain
    app.db
    app.infrastructure
    app.shared
ignore_imports =
    # Intentional: app.db.tables aggregates the per-domain table definitions
    # into one metadata registry. Schema-only; no behaviour crosses here.
    app.db.tables -> app.domain.*.tables

[importlinter:contract:domain-independence]
name = Domain modules are independent (shared tables only)
type = independence
modules =
    app.domain.admin_accounts
    app.domain.agent_chat
    app.domain.booking_requests
    app.domain.courses
    app.domain.feedback
    app.domain.event_interest
    app.domain.groups
    app.domain.mobile_card
    app.domain.role_assignments
    app.domain.search
    app.domain.spotify
    app.domain.volunteer_applications
    app.domain.volunteers
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = none
# Tables are shared read models: a module may import another module's
# table definitions (for joins and read models), but never its service,
# repository, or workflow. That behavioural coupling is what this
# contract forbids; the schema seam below is the only allowed edge.
ignore_imports =
    app.domain.** -> app.domain.*.tables

# Domain must not depend on infrastructure (I/O adapters). Each exception
# below is a declared seam; add new ones only with justification, and prefer
# defining a protocol in the domain (or next to the adapter, like
# email.protocols) with the concrete adapter injected at wiring time
# in app/runtime.py.
[importlinter:contract:domain-infrastructure]
name = Domain does not import infrastructure (declared seams only)
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    app.domain
forbidden_modules =
    app.infrastructure
ignore_imports =
    # Intentional: protocol interfaces and pure template renderers.
    app.domain.admin_accounts.service -> app.infrastructure.email.protocols
    app.domain.admin_accounts.service -> app.infrastructure.email.admin_account_templates
    app.domain.mobile_card.service -> app.infrastructure.email.protocols
    app.domain.mobile_card.service -> app.infrastructure.email.mobile_card_templates
    app.domain.volunteer_applications.service -> app.infrastructure.media.protocols
    app.domain.volunteer_applications.service -> app.infrastructure.storage.protocols
    app.domain.volunteer_applications.side_effects -> app.infrastructure.storage.protocols
    app.domain.volunteers.service -> app.infrastructure.media.protocols
    app.domain.volunteers.service -> app.infrastructure.storage.protocols

# Web composes domain services and must not reach past them into
# infrastructure. Exceptions are exception types raised through domain
# calls.
[importlinter:contract:web-infrastructure]
name = Web does not import infrastructure (declared seams only)
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    app.web
forbidden_modules =
    app.infrastructure
ignore_imports =
    # Intentional: upload error types surface through domain service calls
    # and are translated to user-facing messages in the web layer.
    app.web.upload_helpers -> app.infrastructure.media.photo_processing
    app.web.routes.volunteers.actions -> app.infrastructure.media.photo_processing
    app.web.routes.volunteer_applications.actions -> app.infrastructure.media.photo_processing

; Architecture-contract gate for the canonical subsystems.
; Encodes inward-only dependency direction:
; dependencies flow inward only; same-level subsystems are independent.
;
; tokenpak/services/ is a regular package so grimp discovers all
; of services/* from the tokenpak root — no explicit extra roots needed.
;
; ignore_imports below is the declared debt ledger: one exact fully-qualified
; entry per real import edge on current staging. No wildcards. Every entry has
; a matching row in docs/import-debt-ledger.md (enforced by
; tests/lint/test_import_contracts.py). The ledger is monotonically shrinking:
; removing an edge from the graph removes it here and there; adding a NEW
; edge is a contract violation and fails the gate.
;
; Modules outside the configured tiers (config, models, platform, runtime, ...)
; are intentionally not layered here.

name = "tokenpak"
dynamic = ["version"]
# version sourced from tokenpak/__init__.py via [tool.setuptools.dynamic]
description = "Local proxy for coding agents that records each request and shows how far the session can go: measured usage, estimated cost, burn and runway."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
authors = [
    { name = "TokenPak", email = "hello@tokenpak.ai" },
]
maintainers = [
    { name = "TokenPak", email = "hello@tokenpak.ai" },
]
keywords = [
    "llm",
    "ai",
    "proxy",
    "token-optimization",
    "openai",
    "anthropic",
    "compression",
    "context",
    "context-window",
    "tokens",
    "cost-tracking",
    "routing",
]
classifiers = [
    # Alpha until a candidate build passes the beta gates end-to-end in
    # isolated environments. It claimed Production/Stable while `preview`
    # printed simulated numbers and `setup` reported success for a proxy
    # that had not started. Moves to "4 - Beta" when that candidate passes.
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Topic :: Internet :: WWW/HTTP :: HTTP Servers",
    "Topic :: System :: Networking",
    "Topic :: Utilities",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
# Slim core dependencies — keep the runtime footprint minimal.
# Anything that drags in torch / nvidia-* / scipy / pandas / a multi-hundred-MB
# transitive belongs in [project.optional-dependencies] below, not here.
# See proposals/2026-05-01-tokenpak-install-footprint-extras-split.md.
dependencies = [
    "aiohttp>=3.9.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "click>=8.1.0",
    "starlette>=0.36.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.27.0",
    "httpx>=0.26.0",
    "h2>=3,<5",
    "requests>=2.28.0",
    "watchdog>=3.0.0",
    "cryptography>=41.0.0",
    "urllib3>=2.0.0",
    # Version comparison for `tokenpak update` and doctor's update check. Was
    # imported unguarded at two callsites while undeclared, which crashed
    # `tokenpak update` with a bare ModuleNotFoundError traceback and silently
    # degraded the doctor check to a green "Unknown".
    "packaging>=23.0",
    # Native Codex sends Responses API request bodies with Content-Encoding:
    # zstd. TokenPak decodes them before inspection/optimization and forwards
    # a standards-compliant uncompressed JSON entity upstream.
    "zstandard>=0.23.0,<1",
    # TOML reader for permission-tier / creds config on Python < 3.11
    # (stdlib `tomllib` lands in 3.11; `tomli` is the tiny backport).
    "tomli>=2.0.1; python_version < '3.11'",
]

[project.license]
file = "LICENSE"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Heavy feature extras — opt-in. Every import site for these is wrapped in
# try/except ImportError with a clear "install tokenpak[<extra>]" message.
# See proposals/2026-05-01-tokenpak-install-footprint-extras-split.md.
retrieval = [
    # Pulls torch + nvidia/* (~5 GB) — opt-in only.
    "sentence-transformers>=2.2.0",
]
code-compression = [
    # tree-sitter-languages has no Python 3.13 wheel (dormant package);
    # pinned below 3.13 until a migration to modern per-language tree-sitter
    # bindings ships in 1.1.0. Features that import it will raise ImportError
    # on 3.13 installations — acceptable per graceful-degradation pattern.
    "tree-sitter-languages>=1.8.0; python_version < '3.13'",
]
intelligence = [
    # scipy is the only intelligence-tier dep currently imported (guarded in
    # tokenpak/intelligence/ab_optimizer.py). scikit-learn / sympy were
    # candidates in the proposal but no source file imports them today, so
    # adding them would violate the slim-core-deps policy ("New runtime deps require a
    # PR note explaining what they do, why stdlib won't work, and what
    # happens when they're missing"). Add them here when a real consumer
    # lands.
    "scipy>=1.10.0",
]
data = [
    "pandas>=1.3.0",
]
compression = [
    # llmlingua is the heavy compression engine; the slim default uses the
    # deterministic span_extractor pipeline. Guarded import in
    # tokenpak/compression/engines/llmlingua.py.
    "llmlingua>=0.1.0",
]
integrations-litellm = [
    # litellm router middleware. Guarded imports in
    # tokenpak/integrations/litellm/{proxy,middleware,__init__}.py.
    "litellm>=1.0.0",
]
dispatch = [
    # The Dispatch orchestration subsystem (tokenpak/orchestration/dispatch/**)
    # is pydantic-native: every record model subclasses pydantic.BaseModel, and
    # JSON Schema build/parse round-trips use jsonschema. Both are opt-in so the
    # slim core stays free of pydantic. The dispatch runtime is unbuilt as of
    # v0.1-alpha, so nothing in the slim install imports these yet.
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.0.0",
]
# Convenience meta-extra — `pip install tokenpak[full]` restores the legacy
# "everything bundled" install behavior for callers who don't want to pick
# extras individually.
full = [
    "tokenpak[retrieval,code-compression,intelligence,data,compression,integrations-litellm,dispatch]",
]
dev = [
    "pytest>=7.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
    "pytest-benchmark>=4.0.0",
    "pytest-mock>=3.12.0",
    # pytest-timeout makes the `timeout = 30` pyproject option + per-test timeout
    # marks actually enforce in CI (a hung subprocess fails fast instead of
    # stalling the job to the runner limit).
    "pytest-timeout>=2.1.0",
    "black>=24.0.0",
    # Formatter output is a release gate; pin it so a tool release cannot turn
    # an unchanged checkout red or silently rewrite the baseline.
    "ruff==0.16.5",
    # Artifact metadata validation is a release gate. Keep Twine in the
    # candidate lock so validation lanes can provision it with hashes and run
    # `twine check` offline against the exact wheel and sdist under review.
    "twine==7.0.0",
    # The build frontend and backend are also release gates. Pin both in the
    # candidate lock so offline validation does not depend on an unrecorded
    # host package or a network-enabled PEP 517 build environment.
    "build==1.6.0",
    "setuptools==84.0.0",
    # Architecture-contract gate (.importlinter) and its contract tests
    # under tests/lint/test_import_contracts.py.
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    # Subsystem test deps: the dispatch test suite imports pydantic/jsonschema.
    # Pulled via the [dispatch] extra so the standard `.[dev]` CI job collects
    # and runs those tests instead of erroring at import time.
    "tokenpak[dispatch]",
    # The strict-typed proxy subsystem (tokenpak/proxy/**) and the telemetry
    # dashboard/query/ingest HTTP surfaces it imports use fastapi/pydantic at
    # module level. Pulled via the [serve] extra so a plain `.[dev]` install
    # can import, test, and `mypy --strict` those modules instead of resolving
    # them to Any through ignore_missing_imports.
    "tokenpak[serve]",
]
tokens = [
    "tiktoken>=0.5.0",
]
docs = [
    "mkdocs>=1.5.0",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.5.0",
]
otel = [
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.24.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.24.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.24.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.24.0",
]
autogen = [
    "pyautogen>=0.2.0",
]
llamaindex = [
    "llama-index-core>=0.10.0",
]
serve = [
    "uvicorn>=0.27.0",
    "starlette>=0.36.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "fastapi>=0.100.0",
    # Dashboard HTML rendering and settings forms are imported when the
    # dashboard app is created, so both packages are part of the serve
    # runtime rather than development-only test dependencies.
    "jinja2>=3.1.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9",
    # Optional WebSocket proxy endpoint (tokenpak/proxy/websocket.py). The
    # import is guarded (try/except ImportError) and the WS server is simply
    # disabled when absent, so this is serve-only, not a core dependency.
    "websockets>=12.0",
]
telemetry = [
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "fastapi>=0.100.0",
    "flask>=3.0.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/tokenpak/tokenpak"
Documentation = "https://github.com/tokenpak/tokenpak/blob/main/README.md"
"Bug Reports" = "https://github.com/tokenpak/tokenpak/issues"
"Source Code" = "https://github.com/tokenpak/tokenpak"
Changelog = "https://github.com/tokenpak/tokenpak/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"

[tool.coverage.run]
# Test code is not production surface and must not sit in the coverage
# denominator. `--cov=tokenpak` measures the whole package, which contains an
# in-package test tree at `tokenpak/tests/`. Those files are never executed —
# `[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths` collects only the top-level `tests/`
# directory — so every statement in them counted as missed production code.
#
# That single directory was 32,005 statements, 40% of the reported coverage
# gap, understating the measured figure by roughly 12 points.
#
# The list below mirrors the `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] exclude` shapes
# above, deliberately and one-for-one. That is the principle: the coverage
# denominator is the *distributed* package, so anything packaging excludes from
# the distribution is excluded from the measurement too. An ad-hoc list drifts;
# a mirror of the packaging boundary does not.
#
# In-package example trees are NOT omitted. Unlike the test trees they are not
# excluded from the distribution, so they ship and are measured.
omit = [
    # One pattern covers all three exclude shapes. `**` is depth-unbounded, which
    # is what setuptools' `*.tests*` means; an explicit per-depth list silently
    # caps at whatever depth it was written for and misses trees added deeper.
    "tokenpak/**/tests/*",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# `testpaths = ["tests"]` means a bare `pytest` (and every CI invocation that
# runs `pytest tests/`) collects ONLY the top-level `tests/` directory. The
# in-package tree at `tokenpak/tests/` — excluded from the distribution by
# `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] exclude` above and from the coverage
# denominator by `[tool.coverage.run] omit` above — is NOT collected by
# default and is largely not CI-executed at all.
#
# `tokenpak/tests/` is legacy: a second, unmaintained test tree that predates
# (and partly duplicates) the canonical `tests/` directory. As of 2026-09-01
# it does not run as a whole — `pytest tokenpak/tests` hits 18 collection
# errors (imports of modules that no longer exist: `extraction`,
# `tokenpak.server`, `tokenpak.startup_validator`, `tokenpak.state_manager`,
# `tokenpak.timeline`, `tokenpak.tokens`, `tokenpak.version_check`, and
# others) plus additional failures in files that do collect. Making the
# whole directory CI-executed is a separate, larger cleanup, not something
# any one PR should fold in incidentally.
#
# The explicit exception is `.github/workflows/risk-selected-ci.yml`'s
# `python_proxy` job, which names individual `tokenpak/tests/` files it has
# verified pass (`test_custom_providers.py`, `test_proxy_config.py`,
# `test_savings_display.py`) — add a file there, by name, only after
# confirming it's green; do not glob the directory in.
testpaths = [
    "tests",
]
python_files = [
    "test_*.py",
]
norecursedirs = [
    "tests/archive",
    # Closed-source / `_internal`-dependent tests live in tests/_internal/
    # and are excluded from the default OSS gate. To run, invoke
    # `pytest tests/_internal/` explicitly on a daemon-equipped install
    # (or override-ini `norecursedirs=` in a Pro-side CI config). See
    # `tests/_internal/README.md`.
    "tests/_internal",
    ".git",
    "__pycache__",
    "*.egg-info",
    "dist",
    "build",
]
markers = [
    "quick: fast subset for CI and audit checks (<30s) — no live proxy or network",
    "integration: integration tests requiring external services or running proxy",
    "chaos: fault injection and chaos tests",
    "slow: tests that take longer than 5 seconds",
    "flaky: tests that may fail intermittently — run with --reruns",
    "needs_proxy: test requires a running tokenpak proxy (starts ProxyServer or subprocess)",
    "needs_webhook: test requires a live external API or webhook endpoint (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)",
    "needs_internal_alerts: test requires tokenpak._internal.alerts (internal-only module)",
    "needs_cali_env: test requires a specific dev-host filesystem layout (/home/<user>/tokenpak)",
    "needs_fast_host: test has timing-sensitive assertions that fail on slow hosts (benchmarks, latency targets)",
    # Test taxonomy markers (auto-applied by tests/conftest.py)
    "oss: public OSS surface; runs in slim/dev/full install shapes (default for tests/)",
    "optional: requires a named optional extra; runs in dev/full (tests/optional/)",
    "internal: internal/Pro/closed-source surface; runs in full only (tests/_internal/, excluded from OSS sdist)",
    "legacy: historical-compat tests; nightly only (tests/legacy/)",
]
timeout = 30

[tool.black]
line-length = 100
target-version = [
    "py310",
    "py311",
    "py312",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",
    "F",
    "W",
    "I",
]
ignore = [
    "E501",
    "E701",
    "E702",
    "E402",
    "E741",
    "F841",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# __init__.py files exist for re-export; "unused" imports are intentional
# public-surface symbols. Adding to __all__ would be a behavior change
# (makes them officially public); per-file-ignore is the idiomatic ruff
# convention for this pattern.
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]

# Test files use widespread `try: import dep except ImportError: pytest.skip`
# availability-check patterns where the import binding is never referenced
# but its presence is the test signal. Suppressing F401 globally for tests
# is safer than per-line noqa proliferation; tests are not production code.
"tests/**" = ["F401"]
"tokenpak/tests/**" = ["F401"]

[tool.mypy]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# Layering per 01-architecture.md §1.1. An import may only point downward.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "tor"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "tor layering"
type = "layers"
# Parenthesised layers are optional: they are modules the build order has not reached
# yet. Drop the parentheses as each lands, so the constraint is never retrofitted.
layers = [
    "(tor.cli) | (tor.api) | (tor.session)",
    "tor.rules",
    "tor.content",
    # 07.1 types every tor.rules.resources function `-> list[Event]`, while 17.4 defines
    # Event in tor.session at L5 — which a subsystem may not import. We keep 07.1's
    # signature and lift the record into tor.events, above tor.rolls because an Event
    # carries the RollResults that produced it. seq and timestamp are stamped at L5.
    # See the note in tor/events.py.
    "tor.events",
    # 01.1 lists these three as independent siblings, but 02.3.1 puts build_request in
    # tor.rolls and has it read the EffectBus. Both cannot hold; we follow 02.3.1 and
    # order rolls above effects. See the note in tor/rolls.py.
    "tor.rolls",
    "tor.effects | tor.tables",
    "tor.model",
    "tor.dice",
]
# tor.errors sits beneath everything and is deliberately unlayered.
exhaustive = false

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "rules subsystems are independent"
type = "independence"
# Shared leaves (resources, shadow, injury, contest) are excluded by design:
# every subsystem may depend on them, but they may depend on nothing at L4.
# 01.1's own example list omits creation and endeavour; each is a subsystem like any
# other and the constraint it states — no subsystem imports another — covers both.
# Uncomment each module as it lands; see 01-architecture.md §1.1.
modules = [
    "tor.rules.combat",
    "tor.rules.creation",
    "tor.rules.journey",
    "tor.rules.council",
    "tor.rules.endeavour",
    # "tor.rules.treasure",
    # "tor.rules.eye",
    # "tor.rules.fellowship",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "shared rules leaves"
type = "layers"
# 01.1 excludes the shared leaves from the independence contract above, but leaves their
# order among themselves unstated. This fixes it: the subsystems sit above the leaves,
# injury, contest and shadow may use resources, and resources uses only the context. As
# with the layering contract, parenthesised modules have not landed yet.
#
# shadow genuinely needs resources: every function in it moves Shadow, and only
# resources.recompute_conditions may write the Miserable flag derived from it (03.8, 11.6).
# injury needs it for injury.wound_hero alone — 01.1 names injury as the place a subsystem
# goes to inflict a Wound, and checking the Wounded box zeroes a Dying hero's Endurance.
layers = [
    "tor.rules.combat | tor.rules.journey | tor.rules.council | tor.rules.endeavour | (tor.rules.treasure) | (tor.rules.eye) | (tor.rules.progression) | (tor.rules.fellowship) | tor.rules.creation",
    "tor.rules.injury | tor.rules.contest | tor.rules.shadow",
    "tor.rules.resources",
    "tor.rules.context",
]
exhaustive = false

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    report_generator

# Rule: data flows one way through the generator layers
[importlinter:contract:generator-layers]
name = Generator layers — data flows one way
type = layers
layers =
    report_generator.generator.placeholders
    report_generator.generator.domain
    report_generator.generator.context
    report_generator.generator.utils

# Rule: domain/portfolio ↔ domain/system
[importlinter:contract:portfolio-system]
name = portfolio and system are independent
type = independence
modules =
    report_generator.generator.domain.portfolio
    report_generator.generator.domain.system

# Rule: domain/shared is a base — it cannot depend on system or portfolio
[importlinter:contract:domain-shared-isolation]
name = domain shared must not import system or portfolio
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    report_generator.generator.domain.shared
forbidden_modules =
    report_generator.generator.domain.system
    report_generator.generator.domain.portfolio

# Rule: placeholder implementation subdirectories must not import each other
[importlinter:contract:implementation-subdirs]
name = placeholder implementation subdirectories are independent
type = independence
modules =
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.implementations.text
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.implementations.charts
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.implementations.table
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.implementations.images
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.implementations.misc

# Rule: placeholders/formatting ↔ placeholders/rendering
[importlinter:contract:formatting-rendering]
name = formatting and rendering are independent
type = independence
modules =
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.formatting
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.rendering

# Rule: formatting → implementations
[importlinter:contract:formatting-implementations]
name = formatting must not import implementations
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.formatting
forbidden_modules =
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.implementations

# Rule: rendering → implementations
[importlinter:contract:rendering-implementations]
name = rendering must not import implementations
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.rendering
forbidden_modules =
    report_generator.generator.placeholders.implementations

# Rule: presets must only use the public API
[importlinter:contract:presets-isolation]
name = presets must not import generator internals
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    report_generator.presets
forbidden_modules =
    report_generator.generator.context
    report_generator.generator.domain
    report_generator.generator.placeholders
    report_generator.generator.utils
allow_indirect_imports = True

version = "1.4.0"

readme = "README.md"
license = { text = "MIT" }
requires-python = ">=3.13"
authors = [{ name = "Neuraaak" }]
maintainers = [{ name = "Neuraaak" }]
keywords = [
    "excel",
    "automation",
    "com",
    "openpyxl",
    "xlsx",
    "win32com",
    "spreadsheet",
    "office",
]
classifiers = [
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Build Tools",
    "Typing :: Typed",

    "polars>=1.0.0",
    "fastexcel>=0.11.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.0",
    "xlsxwriter>=3.0.0",
    "pywin32>=306; sys_platform == 'win32'",
    "pywinauto>=0.6.8; sys_platform == 'win32'",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "click>=8.0.0",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🛠️ OPTIONAL DEPENDENCIES
# Development tools, testing, and build dependencies
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[dependency-groups]
test = [
    "pytest>=7.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0.0",
    "pytest-mock>=3.10.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.0.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0.0",
]
docs = [
    "mkdocs>=1.6.0,<2.0.0",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.5.0",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.27.0",
    "mkdocs-section-index>=0.3.0",
    "mkdocs-coverage>=1.1.0",
    "mike>=2.0.0",
    # Floor set by PYSEC-2026-3654 / -3609 / -2999; capped below 12 because
    # 12.x changes the Highlight extension signature and breaks the

    "git-cliff>=2.7.0",

]

    # Tests (single source of truth, no duplication)
    { include-group = "test" },

    # Documentation (single source of truth, no duplication)
    { include-group = "docs" },

    # Development tools
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
    "ty>=0.0.13",
    "pyright>=1.1.0",
    "pre-commit>=3.0.0",

    # Task runner
    "poethepoet>=0.32",

    # Security
    "bandit>=1.7.0",
    "pip-audit>=2.7.0",

    # Build
    "build>=1.0.0",
    "twine>=4.0.0",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🔗 PROJECT URLS
# Links to repository, documentation, and package index
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/neuraaak/ezxl"
Documentation = "https://neuraaak.github.io/ezxl/"
Repository = "https://github.com/neuraaak/ezxl"
Issues = "https://github.com/neuraaak/ezxl/issues"
PyPI = "https://pypi.org/project/ezxl/"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🖥️ SCRIPTS
# Entry points for command-line tools
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[project.scripts]
"ezxl" = "ezxl.cli.main:cli"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# ⚡ POE TASKS
# Developer commands: run with `uv run poe <task>`
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[tool.poe.tasks]
lint = "ruff check src tests"
lint-fix = "ruff check --fix src tests"
format = "ruff format src tests"
format-check = "ruff format --check src tests"
security = { help = "Run Bandit and audit locked dependencies", sequence = [
    "bandit -c pyproject.toml -r src",
    "pip-audit",
], default_item_type = "cmd" }

test = "pytest"
# The `excel` marker drives a live Excel instance over COM: Windows-only,
# excluded from every CI run and from the coverage gate.
# Windows is the only OS where every module imports, so it is the only one
# where the total is meaningful: _com_utils and _pywintypes_compat are
# win32-only and score 0% on Linux. 01-ci picks the task per runner.
test-ci = "pytest -m 'not excel' --cov-fail-under=85"
test-ci-nogate = "pytest -m 'not excel' --cov-fail-under=0"
test-unit = "pytest -m unit"
test-fast = "pytest -n auto -m 'not slow and not excel'"
docs = "mkdocs serve"
docs-build = "mkdocs build --strict"
docs-coverage = "pytest -m 'not excel' --cov=src/ezxl --cov-report=html --cov-report=xml -q"
graph = "python .scripts/dev/generate_architecture_graph.py"
version = "python .scripts/dev/update_version.py"
# Single source for the version in CI: 02, 03 and 04 all read it this way
# instead of each re-implementing a grep/sed over pyproject.toml.
read-version = '''python -c "import tomllib, pathlib; print(tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))['project']['version'])"'''
build = "uv build"

[tool.poe.tasks.imports]
help = "Check import-linter layer contracts"
cmd = "lint-imports"
env = { PYTHONPATH = "src" }

[tool.poe.tasks.typecheck]
help = "Run pyright then ty"
sequence = ["pyright", "ty check"]
default_item_type = "cmd"

[tool.poe.tasks.check]
help = "Full local quality gate (mirrors CI)"
sequence = ["format-check", "lint", "typecheck", "imports", "test"]
default_item_type = "ref"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 📦 HATCHLING CONFIGURATION
# Package discovery and inclusion/exclusion patterns
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/ezxl"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
exclude = [
    # Dev tooling & scripts
    ".scripts",
    ".hooks",
    ".pre-commit-config.yaml",
    # Test & coverage
    "tests",
    "htmlcov",
    ".coverage",
    "coverage.xml",
    ".pytest_cache",
    # Documentation
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "mkdocs.yml",
    "cliff.toml",
    # VCS & caches
    ".git",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".mypy_cache",
    # Virtual envs
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    # Byte-compiled / optimized files
    "*.pyc",
    "*.pyo",
    "__pycache__",
    # Logs & temp
    "*.log",
    ".tmp",
    # Build artifacts
    "dist",
    "build",
    "*.egg-info",
    # IDE & OS
    ".cursor",
    ".DS_Store",
    "Thumbs.db",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🎨 CODE FORMATTING & LINTING TOOLS
# Auto-formatting, import sorting, and style checking
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 88

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "I",   # isort-compatible import sorting (via ruff)
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "S",   # bandit security
    "T20", # flake8-print
    "ARG", # flake8-unused-arguments
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
]
ignore = [
    "E501", # line too long, handled by ruff format
    "B008", # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "S101", # assert_used (for tests)
    "S106", # hardcoded_password_funcarg
    "T201", # print statements (for init.py and scripts)
    "S603", # subprocess.run without check=True
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*" = ["S101", "S311", "E501", "ARG002"]
"examples/**/*" = ["T201", "E501"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# ✅ TYPE CHECKING TOOLS
# Static type analysis with minimal and comprehensive modes
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# ty: Type checking with minimal configuration
[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.13"
root = ["src", "src/ezxl"]

[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src/ezxl/**/*.py"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
]

# Respect .gitignore
respect-ignore-files = true

[tool.ty.terminal]
output-format = "full"
error-on-warning = false

# win32com, pywintypes, and pywinauto are Windows-only (sys_platform == 'win32').
# They are absent on Ubuntu CI runners — pyright covers missing-import detection
# via reportMissingImports = true and its bundled pywin32 stubs.
[tool.ty.rules]
unresolved-import = "ignore"
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"

# Pyright: Comprehensive type checking with detailed reporting
[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
# Target Windows so that ctypes.windll and other platform-specific members resolve.
pythonPlatform = "Windows"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

# Include/exclude paths
include = ["src"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "**/node_modules",
    "**/.*",
    # pywinauto has no type stubs and is absent on non-Windows runners.
    # Attribute errors on its symbols are suppressed here; runtime coverage
    # is provided by the excel-marked integration tests on Windows.
    "src/ezxl/gui/pywinauto",
]

# Reporting rules: flag missing imports and duplicates
reportMissingImports = true
reportMissingModuleSource = false
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportUnusedImport = true
reportUnusedClass = true
reportUnusedFunction = true
reportUnusedVariable = true
reportDuplicateImport = true

# Optional type checking (None safety)
reportOptionalSubscript = true
reportOptionalMemberAccess = true
reportOptionalCall = true
reportOptionalIterable = true
reportOptionalContextManager = true
reportOptionalOperand = true

# Tolerance for decorators and complex types
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = false
reportUntypedClassDecorator = false
reportUntypedBaseClass = false
reportUntypedNamedTuple = false

# Override and consistency checks
reportPrivateUsage = false
reportConstantRedefinition = true
reportIncompatibleMethodOverride = true
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = true
reportInconsistentConstructor = true

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🧭 IMPORT LINTER CONTRACTS
# Layer dependency contracts enforced in CI
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["ezxl"]
# Note: import-linter 2.x ne supporte pas source_paths (feature pending PR #323).
# Le package doit être installé en mode editable (pip install -e .)
# ou lancer avec PYTHONPATH=src lint-imports

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "layer dependency flow"
type = "layers"
# core sits above gui: ExcelApp.gui builds a GUIProxy, while gui imports
# nothing from core (it types the app through the ExcelAppLike Protocol).
# Declaring them as independent siblings was only true because the import was
# hidden in an importlib string, which the linter cannot see.
layers = [
    "ezxl.cli",
    "ezxl.core",
    "ezxl.gui",
    "ezxl.io | ezxl.utils",
    "ezxl.exceptions",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🧪 TESTING & COVERAGE TOOLS
# Test execution, coverage analysis, and test configuration
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Pytest: Test runner with markers and coverage configuration
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "7.0"
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--cov=src/ezxl",
    "--cov-report=term-missing",
    "--cov-report=html",
    "--cov-report=xml",
    "--tb=short",
    "--color=yes",
    "--durations=10",
    "--maxfail=5",
]
console_output_style = "progress"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "unit: marks tests as unit tests (default)",
    "cli: marks tests related to CLI",
    "excel: marks tests requiring a live Excel installation (deselect with '-m not excel')",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/ezxl"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/site-packages/*",
    "*/.pytest_cache/*",
    "*/.benchmarks/*",
    "*/.vscode/*",
    "*/.egg-info/*",
    "*/.hooks/*",
    "setup.py",
    "build/*",
    "dist/*",
    ".venv/*",
    "venv/*",
    "htmlcov/*",
    "coverage.xml",
    ".coverage",
    "docs/*",
    "examples/*",
    "_temp/*",
    # COM/live-Excel modules — require a running Excel instance (excluded from
    # CI). Everything omitted here is invisible to the --cov-fail-under gate,
    # so keep the list to modules that genuinely cannot run without Excel:
    # _com_utils.py and cli/ were omitted and are not in that category.
    "*/core/_excel_app.py",
    "*/core/_workbook.py",
    "*/core/_sheet.py",
    # win32com GUI backends — require COM and a live Excel window
    "*/gui/win32com/*",
    "*/gui/_gui_proxy.py",
    # pywinauto GUI backends — require pywinauto and a live Excel HWND
    "*/gui/pywinauto/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
# Lines to exclude: comments, abstractions, unreachable code
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "if self.debug:",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if 0:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
    "if platform.system\\(\\) == \"Windows\":",
    "except ImportError:",
]
show_missing = true
precision = 2
# No `fail_under` here on purpose: it would apply to every coverage run,
# including `docs-coverage`, which only produces htmlcov/ as a docs input.
# The threshold belongs to the gate that wants it — see `test-ci`.

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🔒 SECURITY TOOLS
# Code security scanning and vulnerability detection
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Bandit: Security linter for identifying common security issues
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = [
    "tests",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "venv",
    ".venv",
    ".hooks",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    ".tmp",
    "_temp",
]
skips = ["B101", "B601"]

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    app

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Scopus API layered architecture
type = layers
containers = app
layers =
    routers
    services
    infrastructure
    interfaces
    models

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    CortexOS
    packs
# Required so contract 3 can forbid n8n/langchain/langflow/gencfsm without
# vendoring them. Contract 1 then also sees function-level packs imports that
# grimp previously skipped; those already live on the AST C2 allowlist.
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:1]
name = the engine never reaches into a pack (C2 boundary)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    CortexOS
forbidden_modules =
    packs
# Packs register into the engine; the engine only ever holds a port. Enforced at
# lint as well as in tests/contract/test_import_boundaries.py, because a single

pretty = true
# The contract package is distributed as top-level `cortex_contract`. Without
# this, mypy resolves packages/cortex_contract/*.py as both `cortex_contract.*`
# (the __init__.py walk-up) and `packages.cortex_contract.*` (as a namespace
# package from the root) and refuses to run at all.
mypy_path = "packages"
namespace_packages = false
# A setuptools build/ tree under the package is a *copy* of it, so mypy sees two
# modules named cortex_contract and stops with "errors prevented further
# checking" — exit 2, nothing type-checked, and it reads like an environment
# glitch rather than a disabled gate. Any `pip install -e .` or `python -m
# build` recreates it, so excluding it is the fix; deleting it is not.
exclude = '(^|/)build/'

]

pythonpath = ["."]

]
