    "pytest-xflaky>=1.0.3",
    "pytest-json-report>=1.5",
    # TRACE 0.2 Trust Record emitter tests.
    "agentrust-trace-tests>=0.6,<0.7",
    # Error-telemetry SDK for the operator-managed Sentry-protocol-compatible
    # error sink. Imported lazily in src/bernstein/cli/main.py and only
    # initialised when BERNSTEIN_TELEMETRY_DSN is set. Kept in dev so the
    # test-suite can exercise the no-op + initialised paths.
    "sentry-sdk[fastapi]>=2.20",
    # Cron expression parser. Optional at runtime - trigger_manager imports it
    # inside try/except ImportError and yields no events without it - but
    # required here so the cron-evaluation regression tests execute instead of
    # being skipped by importorskip. types-croniter below stubs the same
    # library for mypy.
    "croniter>=6.0",
    # Rendering-fetcher tests (#3120) exercise the headless browser against
    # a local fixture server. Runtime extra: bernstein[research-render].
    "playwright>=1.62.0",
    # NOTE: semgrep is intentionally NOT a dev dep. Its transitive pins
    # (click<8.2, opentelemetry-sdk<1.38) collide with our production
    # floors (click>=8.3.3, opentelemetry-sdk>=1.41.1). Install via
    # `uv tool install semgrep` (isolated env). See .github/workflows/ci.yml
    # and docs/contributing/testing.md.
    #
    # Type stubs for dependencies that ship no inline annotations. Mirror of
    # [dependency-groups].dev. Everything below is typeshed's own `types-*`
    # distribution except lxml-stubs (published by the lxml developers) and
    # boto3-stubs / botocore-stubs (published by the mypy_boto3 project).
    # Stub-only wheels: no runtime code, no import cost. They are dev-only
    # because they are consumed by `uv run mypy src`.
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12.20260724",  # pyyaml
    "types-jsonschema>=4.26.0.20260518",  # jsonschema
    "types-reportlab>=4.5.1.20260724",  # reportlab
    "types-defusedxml>=0.7.0.20260504",  # defusedxml
    "types-psutil>=7.2.2.20260518",  # psutil
    "types-croniter>=6.2.4.20260711",  # croniter
    "types-qrcode>=8.2.0.20260518",  # qrcode (gui extra)
    "types-grpcio>=1.82.1.20260724",  # grpcio (grpc extra)
    "types-grpcio-reflection>=1.0.0.20260508",  # grpcio-reflection (grpc extra)
    "lxml-stubs>=0.5.1",  # lxml, via signxml (SAML assertion parsing)
    "boto3-stubs>=1.43.56",  # boto3 (s3 / r2 extras), published by the mypy_boto3 project
    "botocore-stubs>=1.43.14",  # botocore, same publisher
]
grpc = ["grpcio>=1.68", "grpcio-tools>=1.68", "grpcio-reflection>=1.68", "protobuf>=7.35.1"]
voice = ["faster-whisper>=1.0.0", "sounddevice>=0.4.0", "numpy>=1.20.0"]
k8s = ["kubernetes>=35.0.0"]
# SPIFFE/SPIRE workload-identity integration
# (src/bernstein/core/identity/spiffe/workload_api.py). The py-spiffe SDK talks
# to a running SPIRE agent's Workload API to fetch X.509-SVIDs. Optional so the
# default self-contained Ed25519 identity path stays dependency-free and works
# with a truthy regression suite when the extra is absent. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[spiffe]'
spiffe = ["spiffe>=0.2"]
ml = ["scikit-learn>=1.5"]
# Browser activity driver (src/bernstein/core/orchestration/browser_driver.py).
# Declared empty (like `graphics` below) so a default install and the project
# lock stay lean and license-clean: the live `browser-use` backend pulls a large
# transitive tree with licenses outside the accepted set (see
# .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml), and vendoring it here would bind that
# surface onto every install. The recorded-tape driver runs every offline replay
# and verification path with no extra installed, and asking for a live driver
# without the backend raises a typed refusal naming the package to install.
# Enable the live driver on demand with: pip install 'browser-use>=0.7'.
browser = []
graphics = []  # term-image disabled: caps pillow<11, conflicts with CVE-2026-25990 fix
# OpenAI Agents SDK v2 integration (src/bernstein/adapters/openai_agents.py).
# Declared as an optional extra so users who don't spawn OpenAI Agents agents
# don't need the SDK installed.  Enable with: pip install 'bernstein[openai]'.
openai = ["openai-agents>=0.4.0"]
# Sandbox backend extras. Each pulls in the provider SDK for the
# corresponding SandboxBackend. Kept optional so minimal installs stay lean.
docker = ["docker>=7.1.0"]
e2b = ["e2b-code-interpreter>=1.0"]
modal = ["modal>=1.4.2"]
# Cloud artifact storage sinks. Each extra pulls in the provider SDK
# needed by the corresponding ArtifactSink. Kept optional so local-only
# installs stay lean. R2 reuses boto3 under the hood.
s3 = ["boto3>=1.43.6"]
gcs = ["google-cloud-storage>=3.10.1"]
azure = ["azure-storage-blob>=12.20"]
r2 = ["boto3>=1.43.6"]
# Chat-control bridge backends. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[telegram]'
# Standard Telegram bot integration via long-poll: configure the bot
# token (from @BotFather) and the chat id, no external services.
telegram = ["python-telegram-bot>=22.7"]
# Slack bidirectional driver over Socket Mode. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[slack]'
# Configure a Slack app with bot scopes (``chat:write``, ``commands``),
# enable Socket Mode, and set ``BERNSTEIN_SLACK_TOKEN`` (xoxb-...) plus
# ``BERNSTEIN_SLACK_APP_TOKEN`` (xapp-...) before invoking ``bernstein
# chat serve --platform=slack``.
slack = ["slack-sdk>=3.27", "aiohttp>=3.9"]
# Discord bidirectional driver over the gateway. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[discord]'
# Configure a Discord bot application in the developer portal, copy the
# bot token, and set ``BERNSTEIN_DISCORD_TOKEN`` before invoking
# ``bernstein chat serve --platform=discord``.
discord = ["discord.py>=2.4"]
# Microsoft Teams bidirectional driver over the Bot Framework. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[teams]'
# Register a bot in the Azure Bot Service, copy the app id and password, and
# set ``BERNSTEIN_TEAMS_TOKEN`` (app id) plus ``BERNSTEIN_TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD``
# (client secret) before invoking ``bernstein chat serve --platform=teams``.
teams = ["botbuilder-core>=4.15", "aiohttp>=3.9"]
# Contamination-resistant eval harness (SWE-bench Pro / Terminal-Bench 2.0 /
# SWE-rebench). Kept optional so production installs don't pull HuggingFace
# datasets unless the operator opts into the nightly leaderboard path.
# Enable with: pip install 'bernstein[eval]'
eval = ["datasets>=4.8.5", "huggingface-hub>=0.24"]
# Web GUI (Vite + React SPA + FastAPI mount). Static assets ship with the
# wheel under src/bernstein/gui/static/ (see artifacts). Python deps stay
# minimal so TUI users keep zero overhead. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[gui]'
# then: bernstein gui serve
gui = [
    "sse-starlette>=2.1.0",
    # Terminal QR rendering for ``bernstein gui qr`` and the
    # ``--tunnel`` flag of ``bernstein gui serve`` (#1218). Pure Python,
    # MIT-licensed, no native deps. The qr renderer ships a fallback
    # placeholder when this extra is absent so minimal installs do not
    # crash - they just print a "install qrcode" diagnostic.
    "qrcode>=7.4",
]
# OpenTelemetry OTLP/gRPC exporter for GenAI semantic conventions
# (src/bernstein/core/observability/otlp_exporter.py). The exporter is a
# no-op when this extra is absent or BERNSTEIN_OTEL_ENDPOINT is unset, so
# minimal installs do not pay the gRPC import cost. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[otel]'
otel = [
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.41.1",
]
# Error-telemetry SDK wired to an operator-managed Sentry-protocol-compatible
# error sink (src/bernstein/cli/main.py:_init_error_telemetry). The SDK is
# imported lazily and only initialises when BERNSTEIN_TELEMETRY_DSN is set, so
# minimal installs pay zero overhead. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[observability]'
observability = [
    "sentry-sdk[fastapi]>=2.20",
]
research-render = [
    "playwright>=1.62.0",
]
# TRACE 0.2 Trust Record emitter (src/bernstein/core/observability/trust_record.py).
# Optional so minimal installs stay dependency-free. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[trace]'
trace = ["agentrust-trace>=0.11,<0.12"]

[project.scripts]
bernstein = "bernstein.cli.main:cli"
bernstein-worker = "bernstein.core.worker:main"
bernstein-bench = "bernstein.eval.bench.bench_cli:bench_group"
verify-audit-receipt = "bernstein.core.verifier.audit_receipt_verifier:main"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.plugins"]
# Lifecycle/event plugins (hookimpl classes). Example:
# my_plugin = "my_package:MyPlugin"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.adapters"]
# Third-party CLI agent adapters (CLIAdapter subclasses). Example:
# myagent = "my_package.adapter:MyAgentAdapter"
# Then use: bernstein run --cli myagent plan.yaml

[project.entry-points."bernstein.gates"]
# Custom quality gates (GatePlugin subclasses). Example:
# my_gate = "my_package.gates:MyGate"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.triggers"]
# Custom trigger sources (normalize external events into tasks). Example:
# jira = "my_package.triggers:JiraTriggerSource"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.reporters"]
# Custom reporters (hookimpl classes that emit run summaries). Example:
# slack = "my_package.reporters:SlackReporter"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.sandbox_backends"]
# Sandbox backends (SandboxBackend protocol implementations).
# First-party backends (worktree, docker) ship in core and are registered
# by bernstein.core.sandbox.registry directly; plugin authors register
# additional backends (e2b, modal, cloud providers ...) via this group.
# Example:
# e2b = "bernstein.core.sandbox.backends.e2b:E2BSandboxBackend"
# modal = "bernstein.core.sandbox.backends.modal:ModalSandboxBackend"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.skill_sources"]
# Progressive-disclosure skill packs. Each entry resolves to a
# zero-arg factory returning a ``bernstein.core.skills.SkillSource``.
# Example:
# my-data-pack = "my_pack.skills:source"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.storage_sinks"]
# Pluggable artifact storage sinks. First-party sinks
# (local_fs, s3, gcs, azure_blob, r2) ship in core and are registered
# eagerly by bernstein.core.storage.registry; plugin authors register
# additional sinks (custom providers, domain-specific wrappers ...) via
# this group. Example:
# my_sink = "my_pkg.storage:MyArtifactSink"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.spec_quality_rules"]
# Spec-quality checklist rules (Rule factories). Each entry resolves to a
# zero-arg callable returning a
# ``bernstein.core.planning.spec_quality.Rule`` instance.
# Example:
# stakeholder = "my_pkg.spec_rules:stakeholder_factory"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.notification_sinks"]
# Outbound notification drivers (release 1.9). First-party drivers
# (telegram, slack, discord, email_smtp, webhook, shell) ship in core
# and are registered eagerly by bernstein.core.notifications.registry;
# plugin authors register additional drivers (PagerDuty, Opsgenie,
# Mattermost, ...) via this group. Each entry resolves to a callable
# whose signature is ``factory(config: dict[str, Any]) -> NotificationSink``
# and the entry name is the ``kind`` referenced from
# ``bernstein.yaml::notifications.sinks[*].kind``. Example:
# pagerduty = "my_pkg.notify:PagerDutySink"

[tool.hatch.build]
# NOTE: do NOT add src/bernstein/ entries here.  Every file under src/
# ships production code that the runtime imports -- either directly or
# via the _CoreRedirectFinder in core/__init__.py.  Previously 18 core/
# sub-packages plus three cli/run_*.py helpers were excluded (v1.8.7..
# v1.8.9 wheels on PyPI are all broken because of this); `pip install
# bernstein && bernstein --version` failed with `ModuleNotFoundError:
# No module named 'bernstein.core.config'` and similar because the
# redirect map / import chain points to files stripped from the wheel.
exclude = [
    ".sdd/",
    "tests/",
    "scripts/",
    "docs/",
    ".github/",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/bernstein"]
# Eval golden fixtures live INSIDE src/bernstein/eval/golden_data/ so they
# ship by virtue of being inside the package tree.  ``artifacts`` is listed
# explicitly to pin the *.md inclusion even if a future ``include`` /
# ``exclude`` rewrite tries to whitelist only *.py.  Loader:
# ``bernstein.eval.golden._packaged_tier_files`` (importlib.resources).
# .sdd/ MUST stay out of the repo (Repo hygiene CI gate); the operator
# override path .sdd/eval/golden/<tier>/*.md is still consulted first.
artifacts = [
    "src/bernstein/eval/golden_data/**/*.md",
    # Recipe golden traces - YAML fixtures that pin the resolved
    # workflow shape for each bundled recipe.  Loaded by the eval
    # harness to catch drift after refactors.
    "src/bernstein/eval/golden_data/**/*.yaml",
    # Web GUI built assets - Vite output committed to the package tree so
    # the wheel ships pre-built. Rebuild with: cd web && npm run build.
    "src/bernstein/gui/static/**/*",
    "src/bernstein/dashboard/static/**/*",
    # microVM launcher source. The libkrun monitor spawns one process per VM
    # and, on macOS, that process must carry the hypervisor entitlement, so the
    # binary is compiled and signed on the operator's host from this source
    # (`bernstein sandbox microvm-launcher`). Shipping the source rather than a
    # binary keeps the wheel platform-independent and lets the link step resolve
    # the local libkrun prefix. Loader:
    # bernstein.core.sandbox.backends._libkrun.launcher_source_dir.
    "src/bernstein/core/sandbox/backends/_libkrun_launcher/*.c",
    "src/bernstein/core/sandbox/backends/_libkrun_launcher/*.plist",
    # SDD ticket schemas. Shipped alongside the validator so downstream
    # projects can lint their .sdd/backlog tickets via importlib.resources
    # without a source checkout. Loader: bernstein.sdd.validator.load_schema.
    "src/bernstein/sdd/schema/*.json",
    # MCP per-tool input schemas (issue #1406). The orchestrator-side input
    # firewall loads them at startup to validate every incoming MCP tool
    # call. Loader: bernstein.mcp.input_validation.load_registry.
    "src/bernstein/mcp/tool_schemas/*.json",
    # OSCAL v1.1.0 assessment-results schema for compliance exports.
    "src/bernstein/compliance/oscal_schema/*.json",
    # Doctor doc-suggestion seed list. Curated list of common documentation
    # gaps surfaced by `bernstein doctor --suggest-docs`. Operator refreshes
    # it on each release. Loader:
    # bernstein.cli.doctor.suggest_docs.load_unanswered_topics.
    "src/bernstein/_default_templates/docs/*.json",
    # Tracker ingest event-type catalogue (#5132). Schema-validated YAML of
    # canonical event names; GitHub/GitLab parsers map through it only.
    # Loader: bernstein.core.trackers.event_catalogue.load_event_catalogue.
    "src/bernstein/core/trackers/event_catalogue.yaml",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"templates/prompts" = "bernstein/_default_templates/prompts"
"templates/bernstein.yaml" = "bernstein/_default_templates/bernstein.yaml"
# Progressive-disclosure skill packs - shipped alongside the wheel so
# installed packages get the index without requiring a checkout of
# templates/.
"templates/skills" = "bernstein/_default_templates/skills"
"templates/roles" = "bernstein/_default_templates/roles"
# Review pipeline DSL - built-in stage templates and the default 3-phase
# pipeline. Loaded by bernstein.core.quality.review_pipeline at runtime
# when users omit a pipeline path.
"templates/review" = "bernstein/_default_templates/review"
# Lethal-trifecta capability matrix declarations.  Bundled so the
# default-deny check can find tags right after pip install.
"templates/capabilities" = "bernstein/_default_templates/capabilities"
# Provenance trust-class source map (issue #2513). Bundled so tool-result
# taint classification resolves right after pip install.
"templates/provenance" = "bernstein/_default_templates/provenance"
# Stock YAML workflow manifests (#1108) shipped with the wheel so
# `bernstein workflow list` / `... run <name>` resolve immediately
# without requiring a source checkout.
"templates/workflows" = "bernstein/_default_templates/workflows"
# Plan templates (#4877) for `bernstein templates list|use`. They lived at
# the repo root under plans/, which is the user's own working directory, and
# so shipped in no wheel at all - the command was dead on every install.
"templates/plans" = "bernstein/_default_templates/plans"
# First-class recipe library - parameterised workflows for common
# operator tasks (refactor-glob, bump-dependency, add-tests-for-module,
# license-audit, regenerate-docs).  Shipped in the wheel so
# `bernstein recipes list|show|run` resolves immediately.
"templates/recipes" = "bernstein/_default_templates/recipes"
# Per-task criterion profile presets (issue #1346).  Shipped in the
# wheel so `bernstein run --criterion-profile safety-first` resolves
# without a source checkout, mirroring the mode_profile pattern.
"templates/criterion_profiles" = "bernstein/_default_templates/criterion_profiles"
# Blast-radius detector defaults (#1322) so the reversibility gate finds
# its rule list without requiring a source checkout.
"templates/blast-radius" = "bernstein/_default_templates/blast-radius"
# Built-in team manifests (#2248) so `team_manifest: python` and the
# `bernstein team` commands resolve right after pip install.
"templates/teams" = "bernstein/_default_templates/teams"
# Packaged scenario library for `bernstein scenario list|run` and
# `bernstein routine ...`. Resolved by
# bernstein.core.planning.scenario_library.packaged_scenarios_dir; without
# this entry the commands see an empty library on every pip install.
"templates/scenarios" = "bernstein/_default_templates/scenarios"
# Adapter admission evidence (#3547). The verdict `bernstein adapters
# verify --seal` derives is a projection of the pinned contract's bytes and
# the golden-transcript replay, so both have to be resolvable off a pip
# install or every adapter falls back to a skip-shaped refusal
# (`no_contract` / `no_transcript`) and the seal can never go green outside
# a dev checkout. Both trees are shipped verbatim rather than filtered, so
# an installed host derives the same replay fingerprint a checkout does.
# Loaders: bernstein.adapters._contract.CONTRACTS_DIR and
# bernstein.adapters.admission.golden_transcripts_dir.
"tests/contract/contracts" = "bernstein/_default_templates/adapter_contracts"
"tests/golden" = "bernstein/_default_templates/adapter_golden"
# Cross-vendor agent-plugin assets (#2369): the bernstein-run skill plus
# the plugin command/agent/rule files, so `bernstein skills package
# install` resolves the bundled tree right after pip install. Loader:
# bernstein.core.skills.packaging.packaged_asset_root.
"skills" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/skills"
"commands" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/commands"
"agents" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/agents"
"rules" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/rules"
".mcp.json" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/.mcp.json"
".plugin/plugin.json" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/.plugin/plugin.json"
# Standalone audit-receipt verifier. The `verify-audit-receipt` console
# script and `bernstein audit receipt verify` run this file as a subprocess
# (it imports only stdlib + cryptography + cbor2, never bernstein). It lives
# at the repo root under tools/, so without this entry every pip / uv / conda
# install exited 2 with "can't open file .../tools/verify_audit_receipt.py".
# Loader: bernstein.core.verifier.audit_receipt_verifier.VERIFIER_SCRIPT.
"tools/verify_audit_receipt.py" = "bernstein/_default_templates/tools/verify_audit_receipt.py"
# ascii_logo.md now lives in-package at src/bernstein/_default_templates/ -
# no force-include needed. The dev-repo copy at docs/assets/ascii_logo.md is
# the display fallback read by cli/display/splash_v2.py when running from a
# source checkout.

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist.force-include]
# Wheel force-include sources must also exist inside the sdist: `uv build`
# (and any pip install from the sdist) builds the wheel FROM the sdist, and
# hatchling hard-fails on a missing force-include source. Every other wheel
# force-include source above (templates/, skills, ...) survives into the
# sdist by default, but these two live under tests/, which the global
# [tool.hatch.build] exclude drops - so they are re-included here verbatim,
# at their checkout paths. Guard:
# tests/unit/test_adapter_verification_data_in_wheel.py.
"tests/contract/contracts" = "tests/contract/contracts"
"tests/golden" = "tests/golden"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 120
src = ["src"]
extend-exclude = [
    "src/bernstein/core/grpc_gen",
    "scripts/gen_tickets_*.py",
    "scripts/gen_roadmap_*.py",
    "scripts/convert_tickets_*.py",
    # Intentionally vulnerable synthetic codebase used by the
    # security-pentest eval scenario. Linting it makes no sense; the
    # files exist so the security role can find seeded findings.
    "tests/fixtures/eval/security_pentest/**",
    # Gate-evasion corpus fixtures containing intentional syntax errors,
    # broken code, and mock patterns used to evaluate quality gates.
    "src/bernstein/eval/cases/gate_evasion/**",
    # Cookiecutter source templates with Jinja-interpolated identifiers
    # ({{cookiecutter.X}}) that ruff cannot parse as Python.
    "templates/**",
]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "TCH", "RUF"]
# TC006: We use module-level string constants for cast() type args (Sonar S1192).
# Ruff cannot see through the indirection and flags them as "unquoted".
ignore = ["TC006"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# HTML/CSS template strings that cannot be wrapped without breaking structure
"src/bernstein/evolution/report.py" = ["E501"]
# Agent-generated modules with long inline strings and class-level lists
"src/bernstein/adapters/mock.py" = ["E501"]
"src/bernstein/compliance/eu_ai_act.py" = ["E501", "RUF012"]
"src/bernstein/core/differential_privacy.py" = ["RUF002"]
"src/bernstein/core/license_scanner.py" = ["E501"]
"src/bernstein/core/memory_integrity.py" = ["E501", "RUF003"]
"src/bernstein/core/seed_config.py" = ["TC001"]
"src/bernstein/core/server_models.py" = ["TC001"]
"src/bernstein/core/server_middleware.py" = ["TC002"]
"src/bernstein/core/orchestration/decomposition_emitter.py" = ["TC001"]
"src/bernstein/core/orchestration/decomposition_proposal.py" = ["TC001"]
"src/bernstein/core/spawner_merge.py" = ["TC003"]
"src/bernstein/core/spawner_worktree.py" = ["TC003"]
"src/bernstein/core/spawner_warm_pool.py" = ["TC003"]
"src/bernstein/core/server_supervisor.py" = ["TC003"]
"src/bernstein/core/runtime_state.py" = ["TC003"]
"src/bernstein/cli/frame_buffer.py" = ["TC003", "RUF002"]
"src/bernstein/cli/gradients.py" = ["TC003", "RUF002", "RUF003"]
"src/bernstein/cli/image_renderer.py" = ["TC003"]
"benchmarks/run_benchmark.py" = ["E501", "RUF002"]
"scripts/generate_roadmap_tickets.py" = ["E501", "RUF001"]
# Ticket/roadmap generators have long inline strings and unicode symbols
"scripts/gen_tickets_*.py" = ["E501", "RUF001"]
"scripts/gen_roadmap_*.py" = ["E501", "RUF001"]
"scripts/convert_tickets_*.py" = ["RUF001"]
"tests/pentest/*.py" = ["SIM105"]
"sdk/python/src/bernstein_sdk/adapters/github_actions.py" = ["E501"]
"sdk/python/src/bernstein_sdk/adapters/jira.py" = ["E501"]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["E402", "E501", "E741", "RUF002", "RUF003", "RUF012", "RUF043", "SIM108", "SIM117", "TC002", "TC003", "TC006"]
# Bug-hunt suite uses ambiguous unicode (homoglyphs, ZWS) intentionally for bypass tests
"tests/property/test_capability_matrix_bughunt.py" = ["RUF001", "RUF002", "RUF003"]
# Example plugins are worked-example packages; runtime imports survive
# ``TYPE_CHECKING`` blocks because tests rely on them at runtime (e.g.
# ``pytest.fail``) and the adapter code uses ``Path`` in concrete
# function signatures, not just hints.
"examples/plugins/**/*.py" = ["TC001", "TC002", "TC003"]

[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
typeCheckingMode = "strict"

[tool.mypy]
# Repo-wide mypy settings for the documented `uv run mypy src` command.
# This run is advisory: mypy has a large pre-existing backlog because it
# never actually parsed the tree (see the note on `python_version` below).
# The subset that gates CI lives in mypy.gate.ini, the same way the
# repo-wide pyright run is advisory and pyrightconfig.strict.json gates.
#
# `python_version` is pinned rather than inherited from whatever
# interpreter happens to run mypy. It matches [tool.pyright] pythonVersion
# and the `requires-python` floor. Note that this pins the *target*
# version only - PEP 695 `type` aliases (11 of them in src/) still need
# the interpreter running mypy to be >= 3.12, because mypy parses with the
# host `ast` module. That is why mypy is a declared dev dependency: an
# undeclared `uv run mypy` falls through to a PATH mypy that may be bound
# to an older interpreter, and the run then aborts on the first alias with
# `Invalid syntax` before checking anything.
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["src"]
namespace_packages = true
warn_unused_configs = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Legacy `bernstein.core.*` / `bernstein.cli.*` import paths are served at
# runtime by the `sys.meta_path` finders in src/bernstein/core/__init__.py
# and src/bernstein/cli/__init__.py, not by files on disk. No static
# checker can follow a meta-path redirect, so these resolve to nothing.
module = ["bernstein.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Installed dependencies that ship neither a `py.typed` marker nor a
# published stub distribution. Checked against PyPI: there is no
# `types-asn1crypto`, `types-kubernetes` or `types-e2b-code-interpreter`,
# and the `google.cloud` namespace package carries no marker of its own
# even though the individual `google-cloud-*` distributions do.
#
# Every other untyped import in the tree is resolved by a real stub
# package in [dependency-groups].dev instead - see the block there. This
# list is the residue, and it should shrink as upstream adds markers, not
# grow. Adding an entry here means "no type information exists anywhere";
# it is not a place to park a package we simply have not stubbed yet.
module = [
    "asn1crypto.*",  # RFC 3161 ASN.1 parsing, core/security/rfc3161_verifier.py
    "e2b_code_interpreter.*",  # `e2b` extra, core/sandbox/backends/e2b.py
    "google.cloud.*",  # `gcs` extra, core/security/secrets_broker.py
    "kubernetes.*",  # `k8s` extra, core/orchestration/operator.py
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Optional backends imported inside a function body behind a try/except
# ImportError, with a typed fallback when absent. They are absent from the
# environment `uv run mypy src` sees - the first group is not declared in
# [project] at all, the second is behind an extra that a plain `uv sync`
# does not install - so mypy reports `import-not-found`.
#
# `ignore_missing_imports` only applies to an import that fails to
# resolve. Where the package is present and ships inline annotations
# (`datasets`, `spiffe`, and most of the first group), mypy reads the real
# types and this override does nothing - so it silences the "not
# installed" noise without masking a typed surface.
#
# The first group is deliberately not installed rather than un-stubbed:
# pulling it into the dev group to read those annotations would add native
# toolchains (sounddevice/PortAudio, weasyprint/cairo+pango), multi-
# gigabyte ML runtimes (faster-whisper), and import-time-patching APM
# agents (ddtrace, newrelic) to every CI job.
module = [
    "asyncpg.*",  # core/persistence/store_postgres.py, cli/commands/status_cmd.py
    "ddtrace.*",  # core/observability/apm_integration.py
    "faster_whisper.*",  # cli/commands/voice_cmd.py
    "newrelic.*",  # core/observability/apm_integration.py
    "redis.*",  # core/persistence/store_redis.py
    "sigstore.*",  # core/security/{sigstore_attestation,audit_receipt}.py
    "sounddevice.*",  # cli/commands/voice_cmd.py
    "tiktoken.*",  # tui/context_tokens.py
    "weasyprint.*",  # core/observability/postmortem.py
    "zstandard.*",  # core/observability/trace_store.py
    # Declared extras, absent from a plain `uv sync`:
    "datasets.*",  # `eval` extra, benchmark/{swe_bench,programbench}.py
    "spiffe.*",  # `spiffe` extra, core/identity/spiffe/workload_api.py
    "sklearn.*",  # core/tokens/context_compression.py, core/planning/duration_predictor.py
    "z3.*",       # core/quality/formal_verification.py
    "playwright.async_api.*",  # core/orchestration/rendering_fetcher.py
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
# Tests use explicit @pytest.mark.asyncio - keep strict mode to avoid
# auto-collecting unmarked async tests and breaking existing suites.
asyncio_mode = "strict"
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
]
markers = [
    "ci: tests that run as part of CI for every release",
    "auth_enabled: opt out of the autouse auth-disabled shim (tests that exercise auth defaults)",
    "audit_key_real: opt out of the autouse audit-key path isolation (tests that exercise the real resolution logic)",
    "cluster_e2e: real-process cluster harness tests; skipped by default, run via the cluster-e2e workflow",
    "slow: long-running tests (> ~5s); skipped by default in fast feedback runs",
    "integration: end-to-end / subprocess-driven integration tests; selectable via -m integration in CI",
    "stress: resource-leak / memory-growth / deadlock stress tests (TC-C); gated off by default CI, run nightly via `-m stress`",
    "allow_network: opt out of the autouse unit no-network guard (rare; a genuine integration test belongs in tests/integration/ instead)",
    "protocol: protocol compatibility tests; applied to every item under tests/protocol/ by that directory's conftest, and run by the publish workflow's release gate",
    "auditor_question: binds one conformance vector under tests/integration/conformance/auditor/ to the question it answers; the argument is a question number registered in that suite's questions.py",
    "whole_tree_guard: asserts an invariant over the whole source tree by scanning it; no diff produces an import edge to these, so `scripts/run_tests.py --affected` selects them on every pull request regardless of what changed",
]
# Visible warnings without converting to errors; individual tests or runs
# can tighten via `pytest -W error::DeprecationWarning`.
filterwarnings = [
    "default",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::ResourceWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["bernstein"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*.py",
    "*/_default_templates/*",
    "*/__main__.py",
]

[tool.coverage.paths]
source = [
    "src/bernstein",
    "*/site-packages/bernstein",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "@overload",
    "\\.\\.\\.",
]

[tool.uv]
# The checked-in gRPC gencode under src/bernstein/core/grpc_gen/ carries
# `Protobuf Python Version: 7.35.1` and calls ValidateProtobufRuntimeVersion()
# at import time, which rejects any runtime from an older major. The modal SDK
# caps protobuf below 7.0, so the `grpc` and `modal` extras cannot share one
# environment. Declaring the conflict keeps the universal lock resolvable and
# turns a former import-time VersionError into an install-time resolution
# error, which is where a dependency conflict belongs.
#
# `otel` has the same shape as `grpc` here, not a different one:
# opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.41.1 pins protobuf==7.35.1 (same
# generated-code floor as the checked-in gRPC gencode above), which modal's
# <7.0 cap rules out just as directly. Undeclared, this doesn't fail as a
# known-incompatible pair - it fails as "your project's requirements are
# unsatisfiable" from the *whole* lockfile, which is what aborted every `uv`
# dependency-update run rather than just the two extras that actually clash
# (#4088).
conflicts = [[{ extra = "grpc" }, { extra = "modal" }], [{ extra = "otel" }, { extra = "modal" }]]
# spiffe 0.3.1 caps pyjwt below 2.14, but pyjwt 2.13 carries ten published
# advisories fixed in 2.14.0 and nothing in the spiffe extra depends on the
# behaviour that cap guards. The override lets the universal lock resolve
# pyjwt to a patched release; drop it once spiffe lifts its cap.
override-dependencies = ["pyjwt>=2.14"]

[tool.mutmut]
# Lineage v1 mutation testing - see scripts/mutmut_lineage.py for the
# focused runner that exercises only the three lineage modules. The
# project-wide conftest pulls heavyweight imports that mutmut 3's

# harness alongside the standard config for ad-hoc deep runs.

    "src/bernstein/core/lineage/tips.py",
    "src/bernstein/core/lineage/merge.py",

    "PLR0917",  # too-many-positional-arguments (public client ctor is positional by design)
    "TRY003",   # raise-vanilla-args (we want descriptive error messages)
    "TRY300",   # try-consider-else (sometimes the linear flow is clearer)
    "PLR2004",  # magic-number-comparison (HTTP status codes are well-known)
    "S105",     # hardcoded-password-string (the portal AccessKey is public)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"custom_components/eaux_marseille/_http.py" = [

    # object passed to `session.request()`, not a numeric deadline. Ruff's
    # ASYNC109 suggestion to use `asyncio.timeout()` does not apply.
    "ASYNC109",
]
"custom_components/eaux_marseille/_auth.py" = [
    # Same reason as _http.py: timeout is a ClientTimeout config object.
    "ASYNC109",
]
"tests/*" = [
    "S101",     # asserts are normal in tests
    "PLR2004",  # magic numbers are normal in tests
    "S106",     # hardcoded-password-func-arg (test fixtures use fake creds)

]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Cap cyclomatic complexity. The codebase currently sits well under this;
# the gate keeps a single function from quietly growing unmanageable.
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["custom_components.eaux_marseille"]
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mypy: static type checking
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true
# Types `voluptuous` as probatio, like HA core does (see stubs/voluptuous).
mypy_path = "stubs"
warn_unreachable = true
# Some `# type: ignore` comments target false positives that only appear
# when HA is actually installed (CI). Locally (Windows, HA stubbed) they
# look unused; that's expected and not a real problem.
warn_unused_ignores = false
disallow_untyped_decorators = false  # HA decorators aren't always typed
# HA / aiohttp / yarl don't ship type stubs in the form mypy expects,
# so subclassing or returning their values gets typed as ``Any``. That's
# fine in practice; we keep our own code strict but tolerate the gap
# at the integration boundary.
disallow_subclassing_any = false
disallow_any_unimported = false
plugins = []

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# We import a lot of HA helpers without strict types upstream.
module = ["homeassistant.*", "aiohttp.*", "yarl.*", "voluptuous.*", "aioresponses.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Tests use a lot of MagicMock / monkey-patching that is hard to type strictly.
module = ["tests.*"]
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
disable_error_code = ["no-untyped-def", "type-arg", "no-untyped-call"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter: enforce the documented module architecture
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "custom_components.eaux_marseille"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Auth/transport stack stays layered (api -> _auth -> _http -> _redirects)"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.api",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille._auth",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille._http",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille._redirects",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Leaf modules (const/exceptions/models) have no intra-package imports"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.const",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.exceptions",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.models",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.api",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille._auth",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille._mobile",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille._http",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille._redirects",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille._client_factory",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.coordinator",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.config_flow",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.sensor",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.statistics",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.diagnostics",
    "custom_components.eaux_marseille.services",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# deptry: dependency hygiene (unused / missing / misplaced imports)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.deptry]
# homeassistant, aiohttp, yarl and voluptuous are provided by the Home
# Assistant runtime; HA integrations import them without declaring them as
# requirements (manifest.json lists only tenacity). They are ignored
# whether deptry classifies them as missing (DEP001, when HA isn't
# installed in the run env) or transitive (DEP003, when it is). The
# residual signal deptry still provides: tenacity must stay used (DEP002)
# and no *other* undeclared third-party import may sneak in.
[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
DEP001 = ["homeassistant", "aiohttp", "yarl", "voluptuous"]
DEP003 = ["homeassistant", "aiohttp", "yarl", "voluptuous"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vulture: dead-code detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.vulture]
paths = ["custom_components/eaux_marseille"]
# Home Assistant framework hooks: called by HA (config-entry lifecycle,
# config-flow steps, the coordinator update method, the sensor platform
# entry point, entity attributes/properties), not by our own code, so they
# look "unused" to vulture. Matched by name; globs allowed. (Using
# ignore_names rather than a vulture_whitelist.py file, whose intentionally
# effect-free statements tripped CodeQL's "statement has no effect" rule.)
ignore_names = [
    "CONFIG_SCHEMA",
    "PARALLEL_UPDATES",
    "VERSION",
    "EauxDeMarseilleConfigFlow",
    "async_setup",
    "async_setup_entry",
    "async_unload_entry",
    "async_step_*",
    "async_get_config_entry_diagnostics",
    "_async_update_data",
    "native_value",
    "_attr_*",
    "config",
    "entry_data",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pylint: only the duplicate-code (copy/paste) checker is used; ruff
# covers everything else.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.pylint.similarities]
min-similarity-lines = 6
ignore-imports = true
ignore-signatures = true

# The one-way door. `vekna.trial` reaches into the lexicon's internals —
# `Grimoire`, `run_cast`, the rite contextvar — because a test harness has to
# drive a cast, and it is one module in one wheel versioned with the lexicon.
# Nothing may reach back: a rituals.py that could import the trial would have a
# route to the cast runtime, which is the thing that must not happen.
# `vekna.edges` is not a source here, and is the single exception: the pytest11
# plugin is the trial's own entry point, holds one fixture, and imports it
# inside that fixture's body so a coverage run does not see the package before
# it starts measuring.
# `src/rituals.py` is the one place the door is unguarded, and import-linter is
# why: `root_packages` takes packages, and rejects a lone module by name. Making
# it a package to satisfy a linter is the tail wagging the dog — `10-ritual-
# modules.md` has a directory and a file of the same name being an error — so
# the gap is named here instead of hidden.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "nothing-imports-trial"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "vekna.lexicon",
    "vekna.folio",
    "vekna.wire",
    "vekna.gates",
    "vekna.links",
    "vekna.inits",
    "vekna.mills",
    "vekna.pacts",
    "vekna.specs",
]
forbidden_modules = ["vekna.trial"]

[tool.mypy]

disallow_any_decorated = true
disallow_any_explicit = true
disallow_any_expr = true
disallow_any_generics = true
disallow_any_unimported = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_subclassing_any = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
exclude = []
explicit_package_bases = true
extra_checks = true
implicit_reexport = true
mypy_path = "src"
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
strict_equality = true
strict_equality_for_none = true
warn_incomplete_stub = true
warn_no_return = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unreachable = true
warn_unused_configs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true

[tool.pydantic-mypy]
init_forbid_extra = true
init_typed = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "vekna.folio.coding_claude._links"
disallow_any_expr = false
disallow_any_explicit = false

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "vekna.lexicon._mills._annotations"
disallow_any_expr = false
disallow_any_explicit = false

# Pydantic's own error report is a list of TypedDicts whose values are `Any`.
# Reading it is how `CodingOpts` and `ClaudeOptions` turn a refusal into a
# sentence, and a `pacts` module may import no internal layer, so the boundary
# lives here rather than in an adapter beside it.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["vekna.folio.coding._pacts", "vekna.folio.coding_claude._pacts"]
disallow_any_expr = false

# `@pytest.fixture` is an overloaded, Any-typed decorator from a framework we do
# not define. The plugin is one module holding one fixture, which is what keeps
# the exemption from spreading anywhere it could matter.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "vekna.edges.pytest_plugin"
disallow_any_expr = false

# `tomllib` hands back `dict[str, Any]`. Both ends read their config through one
# module, which hands the rest of the codebase `object` to validate.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "vekna.wire._toml"
disallow_any_expr = false

# RUFF

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
output-format = 'concise'
preview = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "COM812",  # Trailing comma missing
    "CPY",     # Missing copyright notice at top of file
    "D1",      # Missing docstring
    "PLC2701", # Private name import
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**.py" = [
    "ANN",                    # flake8-annotations
    "S",
    "pytest-fixture-autouse",
]
"src/vekna/lexicon/_mills/_annotations.py" = ["any-type"]
# The import is inside the fixture deliberately: pytest loads an entry-point
# plugin before coverage starts, and a top-level import would take the whole
# package with it. The module says so at length.
"src/vekna/edges/pytest_plugin.py" = ["PLC0415"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-annotations]
allow-star-arg-any = true

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"


# VULTURE

[tool.vulture]

# COVERAGE

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["src"]
omit = ["src/vekna/edges/*"]

[tool.coverage.report]

exclude_also = ["if TYPE_CHECKING:", "# pragma: no cover"]
precision = 2

# Project Metadata (PEP 621)
# Defines package metadata used for packaging,
# publishing, and dependency management.
# -------------------------------------------------
[project]
name = "Juris-AI"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Juris AI is a modern backend service for AI-powered legal assistance."
authors = [{ name = "Bharat Kumar", email = "kumar.bhart28@gmail.com" }]
readme = "README.md"
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
requires-python = ">=3.11,<4.0"
dynamic = ["dependencies"]
keywords = ["LangChain", "Legal", "AI", "FastAPI", "groq", "LangSmith", "Agent"]


# -------------------------------------------------
# Poetry Configuration
# Poetry-specific settings that control how the
# project is managed and packaged.
# -------------------------------------------------
[tool.poetry]
package-mode = false


# -------------------------------------------------
# Poetry Package Sources
# -------------------------------------------------
# PyTorch CPU wheels are used for the default
# CPU-based application/container environment.
#
# GPU deployments can use a separate environment/image
# with the appropriate CUDA-enabled PyTorch distribution.
# -------------------------------------------------
[[tool.poetry.source]]
name = "pytorch-cpu"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"
priority = "explicit"


# -------------------------------------------------
# Runtime Dependencies
# Packages required to run the application.
# -------------------------------------------------
[tool.poetry.dependencies]

# Web API framework and ASGI server
fastapi = "^0.141.1"
uvicorn = { extras = ["standard"], version = "^0.31.1" }

# Authentication and password hashing
pwdlib = { extras = ["argon2"], version = "^0.3.0" }
python-jose = "^3.5.0"

# Multipart form/file uploads
python-multipart = "^0.0.32"

# Data validation and application configuration
pydantic = { version = "^2.7.1", extras = ["email"] }
pydantic-settings = "^2.2.1"
python-dotenv = "^1.0.1"

# Database ORM and PostgreSQL driver
sqlalchemy = "^2.0.29"
psycopg = { version = "^3.1.19", extras = ["binary"] }
asyncpg = "^0.31.0"

# Database schema migrations
alembic = "^1.13.1"

# PDF parsing and text extraction
pypdf = "^6.15.0"
python-docx = "^1.2.0"
# HTML parsing (rag/ingestion/parsers/file.py's _parse_html) -- was
# previously present only as an untracked/incidental install, not a
# declared dependency; discovered and fixed while resolving an
# unrelated ragas/langchain-community conflict (`poetry install --sync`
# correctly removed it as untracked, which is what surfaced the gap).
beautifulsoup4 = "^4.12.3"

# -------------------------------------------------
# Embeddings / Vector Search
# -------------------------------------------------
pgvector = ">=0.3,<1.0"

# Embedding model:
# BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5
#
# sentence-transformers depends on PyTorch.
# Explicitly use the CPU PyTorch distribution for the
# default application environment.
sentence-transformers = "6.1.0"
torch = { version = "*", source = "pytorch-cpu" }
# Transitive (via sentence-transformers), declared only as a security
# floor: <5.3 has an RCE via config injection (CVE-2026-4372) and <5.10
# a path traversal in save_pretrained (CVE-2026-9856); neither is
# backported to 4.x.
transformers = "^5.10.0"

# Token counting for prompt budgeting (agentic/agents/prompts/token_budget.py).
# Not an exact tokenizer for the Llama/Qwen models actually in use --
# see that module's docstring for why cl100k_base is the best available
# approximation without a gated per-model tokenizer download.
tiktoken = "^0.14.0"

# -------------------------------------------------
# Output Guardrails / PII Detection
#
# agentic/guardrails/pii.py -- NER-based PII detection needs a real
# entity recognizer, not regex, which is what presidio-analyzer's
# spaCy-backed AnalyzerEngine provides; redaction itself is a plain
# span replacement in pii.py (presidio-anonymizer was dropped: its
# cryptography<49 pin blocked two HIGH CVE fixes). en-core-web-sm
# (not the default, larger en_core_web_lg) keeps this addition small relative to the
# torch/sentence-transformers stack already installed for embeddings
# -- see pii.py's module docstring for the full design reasoning.
# spaCy models aren't published to PyPI, hence the direct wheel URL
# (the same artifact `python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm`
# installs).
# -------------------------------------------------
# Same pattern as aws-sam-cli below: requires-python's declared upper
# bound (<4.0) is looser than presidio-analyzer's own (<3.15,
# Python 3.15 not yet released at time of writing) -- an explicit

# -------------------------------------------------
# Development Dependencies
# Tools used for testing, linting, formatting,
# static analysis, and local development.

# Testing

pytest-asyncio = "^1.4.0"

# Code quality

mypy = "^1.13.0"
pre-commit = "^4.0.0"
# No types-redis: redis>=5 ships its own inline types (py.typed), and
# the stale 4.x stubs shadowed them (e.g. hid Redis.aclose()).

# Layer-boundary contracts ([tool.importlinter] below; make lint-imports)
import-linter = "^2.15"

# Local AWS development tools

# -------------------------------------------------
# Ruff Configuration
# -------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"

exclude = [
  ".git",
  ".mypy_cache",
  ".ruff_cache",
  ".tox",
  ".venv",
  "build",
  "dist",
  "node_modules",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "W", "F", "I", "C4", "B", "UP"]
ignore = ["E501", "B008"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"


# -------------------------------------------------
# MyPy Configuration
# Static type checking rules.
# -------------------------------------------------
[tool.mypy]
# Pydantic's plugin: BaseSettings fields come from the environment, so
# e.g. Field(default_factory=SecuritySettings) is valid.
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_no_return = true
strict_equality = true

# Treat src/ as the source/import root.
explicit_package_bases = true
namespace_packages = true
mypy_path = ["src"]
exclude = ["src/.*/__pycache__", "src/__pycache__", ".venv", "venv", "env"]

# Work around missing type stubs for third-party libraries.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["faiss.*", "fitz.*", "sentence_transformers.*", "sklearn.*", "datasets.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true


# -------------------------------------------------
# Pytest Configuration
# Test discovery, execution, and custom markers.
# -------------------------------------------------
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]


asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"


python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]

addopts = "--strict-markers --tb=short -v -p no:langsmith_plugin"

markers = [
  "unit: Unit tests — no I/O, no DB, no external services",
  "integration: Integration tests — use real services",
  "slow: Tests that take more than 5 seconds",
  "smoke: smoke tests for critical application workflows",
  "e2e: API-level end-to-end tests — real FastAPI app, real Postgres/Redis",
  "live_messaging: real email/Slack delivery; only with RUN_LIVE_MESSAGING=1, never in CI",
]


# -------------------------------------------------
# Coverage Configuration
# -------------------------------------------------
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src"]
omit = ["tests/*", "scripts/*", "migrations/*"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
fail_under = 30

exclude_lines = [
  "pragma: no cover",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]


# -------------------------------------------------
# Release Versioning (python-semantic-release)
# Next version from Conventional Commits since the last v* tag. Used only
# by the release job in .github/workflows/ci-server.yml, which runs it
# with --no-commit/--no-tag/--no-push: main needs signed commits, so the
# workflow creates the tag + GitHub Release itself and syncs the version
# and CHANGELOG.md back to develop via a PR. See docs/release-process.md.
# -------------------------------------------------
[tool.semantic_release]
version_toml = ["pyproject.toml:project.version"]
tag_format = "v{version}"
commit_parser = "conventional"
# Stay on 0.x until a deliberate 1.0: breaking changes bump the minor.
allow_zero_version = true
major_on_zero = false
build_command = ""

[tool.semantic_release.branches.main]
match = "main"
prerelease = false

# Every develop build gets a release candidate: vX.Y.Z-rc.N.
[tool.semantic_release.branches.develop]
match = "develop"
prerelease = true
prerelease_token = "rc"

[tool.semantic_release.changelog]
# Regenerate the whole file from tags each release (deterministic; the
# sync PR carries it to develop).
mode = "init"

[tool.semantic_release.changelog.default_templates]
changelog_file = "../CHANGELOG.md"


# -------------------------------------------------
# Build System
# Backend used to build and manage the project.
# -------------------------------------------------
[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"

# -------------------------------------------------
# Import Linter (layer boundaries; make lint-imports)
# -------------------------------------------------
# Static analysis only (grimp), nothing is imported. Run from server/ with
# src/ on PYTHONPATH, like the rest of the tooling.
[tool.importlinter]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

source_modules = ["core"]
forbidden_modules = ["adapters", "agentic", "api", "application", "config", "rag", "wiring"]

name = "API routes don't import agentic directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["api.v1"]
forbidden_modules = ["agentic"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

package dev.kviklet.kviklet

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaModifier
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.methods
import dev.kviklet.kviklet.security.NoPolicy
import dev.kviklet.kviklet.security.Policy
import jakarta.annotation.PostConstruct
import jakarta.persistence.Entity

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = ["dev.kviklet.kviklet"], importOptions = [DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class ArchitectureTest {

    @ArchTest
    val entityRule = classes().that().areAnnotatedWith(Entity::class.java)
        .should().onlyBeAccessed().byAnyPackage("..db..")

    @ArchTest
    val policyAnnotationRule = methods()
        .that().arePublic()
        .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..service..")
        .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Service")
        .and().doNotHaveModifier(JavaModifier.SYNTHETIC)
        .and().areNotAnnotatedWith(PostConstruct::class.java)
        .should().beAnnotatedWith(Policy::class.java).orShould().beAnnotatedWith(NoPolicy::class.java)
}

package fcis.fcis

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture
import kotlin.test.Test

class LayeredArchitectureTest {
    val classes = ClassFileImporter().importPackages("fcis")

    @Test
    fun `layer dependencies are_respected`() {
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer("Imperative Shell")
            .definedBy("fcis.shell..")
            .layer("Functional Core")
            .definedBy("fcis.core..")
            .whereLayer("Imperative Shell")
            .mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("Functional Core")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Imperative Shell")
            .check(classes)
    }
}

[importlinter]
root_package = apps

[importlinter:contract:domain-independence]
name = Domain apps must not import from each other (cross-domain coupling)
type = independence
# Unmatched ignore expressions should not error — wildcards may cover future modules.
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = none
modules =
    apps.emr
    apps.billing
    apps.pharmacy
    apps.ai
    apps.whatsapp
    apps.hr
    apps.signatures
    apps.fhir
    apps.imaging
    apps.telemedicine
    apps.patient_portal
    apps.pharmacy_ai
    apps.smart_scheduling
    apps.triage
    apps.mobile
    apps.analytics

# ─── BASELINE (pre-existing cross-app imports — do NOT add new ones) ──────────
# These were grandfathered in on P1-01 (2026-06-13). Every pair here represents
# existing coupling that must eventually be refactored toward apps.core or an
# explicit service boundary. Adding new entries to this list is forbidden without
# a documented ADR.
#
# ALSO included: edges from apps.core into domain apps that create transitive
# paths (core is the permitted hub but also imports some domain models directly;
# those graph edges are masked here so they don't create phantom transitive
# violations between unrelated domain apps).
ignore_imports =
    # --- direct cross-domain baseline ---
    # ai -> emr
    apps.ai.** -> apps.emr.**
    # analytics -> ai
    apps.analytics.** -> apps.ai.**
    # analytics -> billing
    apps.analytics.** -> apps.billing.**
    # analytics -> emr
    apps.analytics.** -> apps.emr.**
    # analytics -> whatsapp
    apps.analytics.** -> apps.whatsapp.**
    # billing -> ai
    apps.billing.** -> apps.ai.**
    # billing -> emr
    apps.billing.** -> apps.emr.**
    # emr -> ai
    apps.emr.** -> apps.ai.**
    # emr -> pharmacy
    apps.emr.** -> apps.pharmacy.**
    # emr -> signatures
    apps.emr.** -> apps.signatures.**
    # emr -> whatsapp
    apps.emr.** -> apps.whatsapp.**
    # emr -> signatures (S32 Compliance: ICP-Brasil encounter signing — emr.services.
    # icp_brasil_integration bridges into the signatures domain to produce a
    # DigitalSignature. Consistent with the existing emr-> orchestration edges above;
    # tech-debt: extract a signatures service boundary so emr depends on an interface.)
    apps.emr.** -> apps.signatures.**
    # fhir -> emr
    apps.fhir.** -> apps.emr.**
    # fhir -> pharmacy
    apps.fhir.** -> apps.pharmacy.**
    # hr -> emr
    apps.hr.** -> apps.emr.**
    # hr -> whatsapp
    apps.hr.** -> apps.whatsapp.**
    # imaging -> emr
    apps.imaging.** -> apps.emr.**
    # patient_portal -> emr
    apps.patient_portal.** -> apps.emr.**
    # patient_portal -> whatsapp (M1-S5: reuse the slot engine for self-service scheduling)
    apps.patient_portal.** -> apps.whatsapp.**
    # patient_portal -> billing (M1-S5: view/pay own receivables via PIXCharge)
    apps.patient_portal.** -> apps.billing.**
    # pharmacy -> emr
    apps.pharmacy.** -> apps.emr.**
    # pharmacy_ai -> pharmacy
    apps.pharmacy_ai.** -> apps.pharmacy.**
    # smart_scheduling -> emr
    apps.smart_scheduling.** -> apps.emr.**
    # telemedicine -> emr
    apps.telemedicine.** -> apps.emr.**
    # triage -> emr
    apps.triage.** -> apps.emr.**
    # whatsapp -> emr
    apps.whatsapp.** -> apps.emr.**

    # --- core -> domain edges (mask transitive paths through the hub) ---
    # core.signals, core.views_onboarding, core.views_platform import domain models;
    # these are masked so that "domainA -> core -> domainB" is not reported as a
    # direct domainA -> domainB violation.
    apps.core.** -> apps.emr.**
    apps.core.** -> apps.billing.**
    apps.core.** -> apps.pharmacy.**
    apps.core.** -> apps.hr.**

ai-sonar-bot = "zeroone_ops.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/zeroone_ops"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.package-data]
"zeroone_ops" = ["prompts/*.txt", "py.typed"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
  "src/zeroone_ops/**/*.py",
  "src/zeroone_ops/prompts/*.txt",
  "src/zeroone_ops/py.typed",
  "README.md",
]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = ["dev"]
exclude-newer = "7 days"

[tool.uv.exclude-newer-package]
# Temporary security overrides; remove once these releases fall within the
# global exclude-newer window.

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "bandit>=1.9.4",
  "import-linter>=2.15",
  "pre-commit>=4.6.2",
  "mypy>=2.4.0",
  "pip==26.2.1",
  "pip-audit>=2.10.1",
  "pytest>=9.1.1",
  "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
  "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
  "ruff>=0.16.10",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "D",
  "E",
  "F",
  "I",
  "PLC0415",
  "UP",
  "B",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"samples/**/*.py" = ["E712"]
"samples/ruff_findings/**/*.py" = ["E712", "F841"]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["D"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
strict = true
packages = ["zeroone_ops"]
warn_unused_configs = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
addopts = "--cov=zeroone_ops --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80"

[build-system]
# setuptools>=77 is the floor for the PEP 639 ``license``/``license-files``
# form used below (the deprecated TOML-table form breaks on 2027-Feb-18).
requires = ["setuptools>=77", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "hyperloom-inference_optimizer"
version = "1.1.4"
description = "Inference Optimizer — two-role (Orchestration/Critic) autonomous LLM inference optimization runtime for AMD GPU platforms. Kernel optimization is handled by programmatic Python handlers."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
# PEP 639 SPDX expression. The former ``{ text = "MIT" }`` table is deprecated
# by setuptools and slated to become a hard error on 2027-Feb-18.
license = "MIT"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
# Intentionally empty: the bare wheel carries no third-party runtime deps, so a
# ``pip install --target`` workspace stays clean. Runtime deps come from the
# ``runtime`` extra, installed by the packaged install.sh.
dependencies = []

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom"
Source = "https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom"
Issues = "https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom/issues"
Changelog = "https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom/releases"
Security = "https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom/security/policy"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# LLM backend SDKs, lazy-imported by the Claude/Codex/critic/scorer roles.
# ``openai-codex`` is the agent runtime for the OpenAI side: Hyperloom makes no
# bare LLM API calls, so an OpenAI-only deployment needs it to run at all.
llm = [
    "claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.110",
    "openai-codex>=0.144",
    "openai>=1.50",
    "httpx>=0.27",
]
# Critic-agent web tools (web_search / web_fetch).
web = [
    "markdownify>=0.11",
    "cachetools>=5.3",
]
# The Experience KB service on a PostgreSQL server (``HYPERLOOM_KB_DATABASE_URL``), as a global KB runs; a workspace's
# service keeps its database in SQLite and needs none of this. The connection pool checks each connection it hands
# out, which needs psycopg-pool 3.2.
kb-service = [
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    "psycopg[binary]>=3.2,<4",
    "psycopg-pool>=3.2,<4",
]
# Full runtime dependency set installed by the packaged install.sh.
runtime = [
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    "hyperloom-inference_optimizer[llm,web,forge]",
]
# Built-in kernel-opt agent (``kernelforge``). ``torch`` is deliberately absent:
# the ROCm build is supplied by the container image and a bare specifier would
# resolve to the CUDA wheel from PyPI.
#
# ``llm`` is a hard requirement, not a convenience: forge's agent backends
# lazy-import ``claude_agent_sdk`` and ``openai_codex`` at the first agent turn,
# so a ``[forge]``-only install imports cleanly and then fails minutes into a
# campaign. It only looked self-contained because ``runtime`` happens to pull
# ``[llm,web,forge]`` together.
forge = [
    "click>=8.0",
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    "anthropic>=0.40",
    "hyperloom-inference_optimizer[llm]",
]
# ROCm Compute Profiler (rocprof-compute) Python requirements. Nothing in this
# repository imports them: they satisfy the profiler, whose binary is supplied
# by the ROCm image or system package. Without this extra, kernelforge
# profiling degrades to the lightweight PMC path.
forge-profiling = [
    # Exact pins required by ROCm 7.2.x rocprofiler-compute.
    "astunparse==1.6.2",
    "kaleido==0.2.1",
    "colorlover",
    "dash-bootstrap-components",
    "dash-svg",
    "dash>=3.0.0",
    "matplotlib",
    "numpy>=1.17.5",
    "plotext",
    "plotille",
    "plotly",
    "pymongo",
    "setuptools",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.42",
    "tabulate",
    "textual",
    "textual-plotext",
    "textual-fspicker>=0.4.3",
    "tqdm",
]
test = [
    "hyperloom-inference_optimizer[runtime]",
    "hyperloom-inference_optimizer[ci]",
    # The Experience KB tests run on PostgreSQL too when HYPERLOOM_KB_TEST_DATABASE_URL names a server.
    "hyperloom-inference_optimizer[kb-service]",
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.18",
    # Property-based tests over the bring-up ladder.
    "hypothesis>=6.0",
    "respx>=0.21",
    "requests>=2.28",
    # psutil-based live-compiler probe in _aiter_jit.
    "psutil>=5.9",
    # framework-agent patch-authoring / isolation paths.
    "libcst>=1.0",
    "patch-ng>=1.18",
]
# Coverage job deps: ``pip install -e ".[test,ci]"``.
ci = [
    "pytest-cov>=5.0",
    "coverage>=7.0",
    # In-runner parallelism (``-n`` in ``pytest_ci_args``).
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5",
    # Cross-job sharding for the coverage matrix (``--splits``/``--group``).
    "pytest-split>=0.8",
    "tomli>=2.0.1; python_version < '3.11'",
]
# Opt-in Langfuse trace sink (HYPERLOOM_LANGFUSE_ENABLE=1).
trace = [
    "langfuse>=2.0",
]
# framework-agent patch-authoring / isolation path.
ast = [
    "libcst>=1.0",
    "patch-ng>=1.18",
]
# Optional ``synthesize --with-llm`` KB-distillation backend.
claude = [
    "claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.110",
]
# Local dev tooling: pre-commit hooks, formatters, type checker.
dev = [
    "pre-commit>=4.0",
    "ruff>=0.8,<1",
    "mypy>=1.0",
    "reuse>=5.0",
]

[project.scripts]
hyperloom = "hyperloom.cli:main"
# Built-in kernel-opt agent. The orchestrator dispatches
# ``python -m kernelforge.cli`` directly; this is for interactive use.
kernelforge = "kernelforge.cli:main"
hyperloom-kb = "hyperloom_kb.cli:main"
hyperloom-kb-serve = "hyperloom_kb.http_service:main"
hyperloom-kb-collect = "hyperloom_kb.collect.cli:main"

[tool.setuptools]
# setuptools defaults this to true for pyproject-based config, which makes
# build_py sweep every file living under a package directory -- including
# subdirectories that are NOT packages. ``packages.find.exclude`` keeps
# ``*.tests`` out of the *package* list, but the sweep then re-added the very
# same files as package *data*: the wheel shipped 627 test entries before forge
# was vendored and 833 after (all under ``kernelforge/tests/``).
# ``scripts/check_wheel_contents.py`` has
# been reporting this; it is the ``packaging.yml`` wheel-contents job.
#
# Turning the sweep off makes ``[tool.setuptools.package-data]`` below the sole
# source of shipped non-module files, which is the state the two packaging
# checks already assume: ``test_packaging_lint.py`` walks tree -> declaration
# and check_wheel_contents.py walks declaration -> wheel, so nothing can now
# ship undeclared or be declared and missing.
include-package-data = false

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
# Test trees are not part of the distribution: their fixture data is not
# package-data, so a shipped copy could never run. Singular/gerund spellings
# are covered too; test_packaging_lint.py fails if a new one escapes.
exclude = [
    "*.tests",
    "*.tests.*",
    "tests",
    "tests.*",
    "*.test",
    "*.test.*",
    "test",
    "test.*",
    "*.testing",
    "*.testing.*",
    "testing",
    "testing.*",
    # KernelForge's examples and local-wiki resources contain .py reference
    # files. Keep those resource trees out of implicit namespace discovery;
    # they ship only through the package-data declarations below.
    "kernelforge.examples",
    "kernelforge.examples.*",
    "kernelforge.knowledge.local_wiki.resources",
    "kernelforge.knowledge.local_wiki.resources.*",
    # Scripted launch/specialist backends and a virtual clock: scaffolding a
    # test drives, not a runtime component. Nothing in the shipped tree imports
    # it, and the production launch boundary it substitutes
    # (``actions/executors/launch_backend.py``) ships as normal.
    "hyperloom.orchestrator.rehearsal",
    "hyperloom.orchestrator.rehearsal.*",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# One recursive glob covers every per-package tests/ dir under src/ --
# hyperloom and kernelforge alike.
# ``scripts/tests`` is listed separately because the operator scripts sit
# outside the package on purpose -- they have to run on hosts with no Hyperloom
# install -- so the glob above cannot reach them, and without this line their
# tests are collected by nobody and fail in silence.
testpaths = [
    "src/**/tests",
    "scripts/tests",
]
pythonpath = ["src", ".", "scripts"]
markers = [
    "targeted_build_e2e: end-to-end tests that run a real AITER compile on a ROCm host; skip with '-m \"not targeted_build_e2e\"' in CI.",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = false
# Relative paths so per-shard ``.coverage.*`` files from different CI runners
# combine into consistent totals.
relative_files = true
source = [
    "src/hyperloom",
    "src/kernelforge",
    "src/hyperloom_kb",
    "OOB",  # optional component; not always present in a clone

# Omitted: tests / package boilerplate, CLI drivers, subprocess wrappers, and

    "*/__init__.py",

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_also = [
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@overload",
]
skip_empty = true
precision = 2
# Tolerate dangling ``.coverage`` entries for transient CI-generated files so
# the standalone ``coverage report`` step does not fail on NoSource.
ignore_errors = true
# Line coverage across all ``[tool.coverage.run].source`` trees.
fail_under = 90

# GitHub Actions ``tests-coverage.yml`` reads this table with inline Python.
[tool.hyperloom.tests_coverage]
# Base trailing argv for ``pytest`` in CI; the workflow appends sharding
# (``--splits``/``--group``) and ``-n`` from the values below.
pytest_ci_args = [
    "-m", "not targeted_build_e2e",
    "--cov=.", "--cov-report=",
]
# In-runner pytest-xdist workers per shard job (``-n auto`` yields 1 on the
# 2-vCPU GitHub runner, so pin it).
xdist_workers = 2
# GitHub matrix shards the suite is split across (pytest-split).
total_shards = 6

# White-box code-metrics gate: ``scripts/code_metrics.py``, run by
# ``.github/workflows/code-metrics.yml``. Each number below carries its reason.
# Units already over a threshold are recorded in ``baseline`` (one line each) and
# may only go down; a file is judged only when a change touches it. CI refuses a
# change that loosens anything in this table relative to the base branch: a
# raised limit, a new ``exclude`` entry, a dropped root, a raised duplication,
# dead-code or warning parameter.
[tool.hyperloom.code_metrics]
baseline = "scripts/code_metrics_baseline.txt"
# Production Python: all of ``src`` (so a new package is in scope by default) and
# ``scripts``. Plain repository paths only; pathspec magic and globs are refused.
# Files under a ``tests/`` directory are exempt from every dimension but
# duplication, as in the style guide's "Size and complexity".
roots = ["src", "scripts"]
# Same vendored / shipped-example trees as ``[tool.ruff] extend-exclude``.
exclude = [
    "src/hyperloom/orchestrator/knowledge/remote_recipe/_vendor/kb_store_client.py",
    "src/kernelforge/examples",
    "src/kernelforge/knowledge/local_wiki/resources",
    "src/kernelforge/knowledge/kb_store/remote_client.py",
]
# SonarSource CPD defaults: a clone is at least 100 tokens and 10 lines (jscpd).
duplication-min-tokens = 100
duplication-min-lines = 10
# vulture's documented setting for CI: report only findings it is >= 80% sure of.
dead-code-min-confidence = 80
# A module over this many lines is listed in the report as a warning, never a
# failure: the size at which a reviewer asks for a split (the style guide's
# module-length review trigger).
module-lines-warning = 800
# Design checks (scripts/code_metrics_design.py), diff-only like the comment and
# literal checks. A1 takes its package units (root packages, layers and
# independent modules) from these import-linter contracts.
import-contracts = ".importlinter"
# A10 compares against the values of the enums defined here; A12 counts the
# implementations of a new ABC or Protocol here.
vocabulary-roots = ["src"]
# A9: a function returning a tuple of more elements than this fails; past two,
# positions stop naming themselves (the review rule's NamedTuple/dataclass line).
tuple-return-max-elements = 2

[tool.hyperloom.code_metrics.thresholds]
# Twice McCabe's 10 (the style guide's review trigger): at 20 a function has
# more paths than a reviewer can hold while reading it, so an explanation in the
# PR no longer makes it reviewable. Same number and the same two cases (added,
# or raised) as the style guide's "Complexity ceiling".
cyclomatic-complexity = 20
# Twice SonarSource's S3776 default of 15, the same step as the cyclomatic
# limit: cognitive complexity weights nesting, so a value past 30 is a function
# a reader has to re-read rather than read.
cognitive-complexity = 30
# Physical lines, ``def`` through the last line, decorators excluded, comments
# and docstrings included: a function no longer fits one screen past 80, and
# most of this tree's functions stay well under (the review trigger is ~60).
function-lines = 80
# pylint R1702 default: past five nested blocks, the innermost line depends on
# six conditions at once; extract the inner loop or invert a condition.
nested-blocks = 5
# pylint R0913 default: past five, a call site no longer reads as a sentence and the
# values travel together anyway -- pass the object they come from, or name them in a
# dataclass. ``self``/``cls`` and ``*args``/``**kwargs`` do not count; keyword-only
# parameters do.
function-args = 5
# Fails above 1200 physical lines: half again the review trigger of 800, the
# size at which a module almost always holds more than one job.
module-lines = 1200
# Any clone (see duplication-min-*) counts; the value is a file's duplicated lines.
duplicated-lines = 0
# Any vulture finding at dead-code-min-confidence counts.
dead-code = 0

# Exact versions: the script refuses to measure with any other, because each
# release can change what a metric counts. CI installs these same pins.
[tool.hyperloom.code_metrics.tools]
ruff = "0.16.2"
complexipy = "8.0.1"
vulture = "2.16"
jscpd = "5.4.1"

# Bandit security linter. ``B101`` (assert_used) is skipped repo-wide because

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 120
# Generated / vendored trees that ship their own linting.
extend-exclude = [
    "_audit_artifacts",
    "build",
    ".venv",
    "TraceLens-internal",
    "InferenceX",
    "src/hyperloom/orchestrator/knowledge/remote_recipe/_vendor/kb_store_client.py",
    # Local-wiki resources and example drivers are not source whose style this
    # repository owns.
    "src/kernelforge/examples",
    "src/kernelforge/knowledge/local_wiki/resources",
    "src/kernelforge/knowledge/kb_store/remote_client.py",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]

# math / parsing helpers where single-letter locals are idiomatic.
ignore = ["E501", "E741"]

# Principle rules held at zero: any new finding fails CI. See the style guide's
# "Formatting and lint" section for what each family enforces and why.
extend-select = [
    "G",  # logging calls take %-style args, not pre-formatted strings
    "TD001", "TD003", "TD004", "TD005", "TD006", "TD007",  # TODO hygiene (issue link required)
    "FIX001", "FIX003", "FIX004",  # no FIXME / XXX / HACK markers (TODO stays allowed)
    "PGH",  # no blanket `# noqa` / `# type: ignore`, no eval-like misuse
    "RSE",  # `raise X`, not `raise X()`
    "ERA",  # no commented-out code
    "PIE",  # no redundant pass / range start / lambda wrappers
    "RET",  # explicit, consistent returns
    "DTZ",  # timezone-aware datetimes
    "LOG",  # correct logging API use
    "A",  # do not shadow builtins
    "C4",  # comprehension / collection-call idioms
]
# Still off pending a team decision -- each rewrites hundreds of lines that the
# open PRs touch: "I" (import sorting), "UP" (pyupgrade). "B", "SIM" and the
# rest of "RUF" carry a backlog and belong behind a ratchet, not a hard gate.

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-builtins]
# ``aiter`` is AMD's kernel library, imported under its own name throughout;
# the builtin ``aiter`` (async iterator) is never used in this tree.
ignorelist = ["aiter"]

# C901 (mccabe) is the complexity trigger in the style guide's "Size and
# complexity" table. It stays off rather than on-and-ignored: the tree carries a
# backlog above the default max of 10, so selecting it would red the tree instead
# of gating new code. The code-metrics gate above measures it at 20 on the files a
# change touches. Measure on demand -- no config edit needed:
#   ruff check --select C901 --config "lint.mccabe.max-complexity=10" src/hyperloom src/kernelforge
# [tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests re-import inside function bodies (E402), redefine fixtures (F811), and
# bind setup values they assert on indirectly (F841). They build fixtures with
# ``dict(key=...)`` (C408), and fakes mirror the keyword names of the APIs they
# stand in for, builtins included (A002, A006).
"**/tests/**/*.py" = ["F811", "E402", "F841", "C408", "A002", "A006"]
# Modules whose imports sit below the module-level constants / helpers they
# close over (cycle-safe or lazy ordering).
"src/hyperloom/orchestrator/loop/coordinator.py" = ["E402"]
"src/hyperloom/orchestrator/state/shared_state.py" = ["E402"]
"src/hyperloom/inference_optimizer/cli/__init__.py" = ["E402"]

"src/hyperloom/inference_optimizer/multi_node/commands/infera.py" = ["E402"]

"src/hyperloom/inference_optimizer/roofline_ceiling.py" = ["E402"]
"src/hyperloom/orchestrator/prompts/specialist_prompt_builder.py" = ["E402"]
"src/hyperloom/agents/critic/runtime/decision_reviewer.py" = ["E402"]
# The import sits under the comment block explaining why the attribute name is

"src/kernelforge/fusion/llm_failure.py" = ["E402"]
# Sphinx reads the module-level name ``copyright``.
"docs/conf.py" = ["A001"]
# Keyword names that mirror a stdlib signature callers already use:
# ``subprocess.run(input=...)`` and ``BaseHTTPRequestHandler.log_message(format, ...)``.
# Renaming them would break keyword callers / the override.
"src/hyperloom/orchestrator/actions/executors/_git.py" = ["A002"]

"src/hyperloom_kb/http_service.py" = ["A002"]

"src/kernelforge/tracker/experiment.py" = ["DTZ005"]

"src/kernelforge/tracker/usage_ledger.py" = ["DTZ005"]
