# GeoSync architectural-boundary contracts.
#
# These rules describe the dependency direction the architecture intends.
# Each rule is enforced by `lint-imports`. Violations fail CI.
#
# When intentionally introducing a cross-layer import that breaks one of
# these rules, EITHER add a new public abstraction in the lower layer
# (preferred) or amend the contract here with a documented rationale.
#
# Discovered (audit 2026-04-26):
#   core           -> application: 0
#   core           -> apps:        0
#   core           -> execution:   0
#   core           -> runtime:     0
#   core/physics   -> execution:   0
#   core/physics   -> runtime:     0
#   core/kuramoto  -> application: 0
#   core/kuramoto  -> execution:   0
#   apps           -> core:        0  (apps/risk_guardian; apps/web is TS)
#
# The contracts below codify those independence facts so that a future
# accidental cross-layer import becomes a CI failure instead of a quiet
# drift.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    core
    application
    execution
    runtime
    apps
    interfaces
    libs
include_external_packages = False

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 1 — core is independent of every I/O / web / scheduling layer.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Pre-existing violations (TRACKED, not BLESSED — paid down by PRs):
#   - core.architecture_integrator.adapters reaches into application.system*
#   - core.integration.adapters reaches into application.microservices.*
#   - core.integration.system_integrator reaches into application.*
#   - core.agent.registry reaches into runtime.misanthropic_agent
#
# Each ignore entry MUST have a rationale comment. New entries get review
# pushback. The acceptable repayment is to introduce a public abstraction in
# core that the application/runtime layer can register itself with, then
# remove the ignore.
[importlinter:contract:core-independence]
name = core does not import from application / apps / execution / runtime
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core
forbidden_modules =
    application
    apps
    execution
    runtime
ignore_imports =
    # core ↔ application — pre-existing tight coupling in the integrator/
    # adapter modules; tracked for paydown:
    core.architecture_integrator.adapters -> application.system
    core.architecture_integrator.adapters -> application.system_orchestrator
    core.integration.adapters -> application.microservices.base
    core.integration.adapters -> application.microservices.registry
    core.integration.system_integrator -> application.microservices.registry
    core.integration.system_integrator -> application.system
    core.integration.system_integrator -> application.system_orchestrator
    # core ↔ runtime — registry shortcut to a runtime agent; tracked:
    core.agent.registry -> runtime.misanthropic_agent
    # core ↔ runtime — TYPE_CHECKING-only type-hint reference to the
    # RebusGate primitive (used solely for typing; not imported at runtime).
    # Tracked for eventual relocation of the RebusGate type into a shared
    # `core/types` module so the type hint stops crossing the boundary.
    core.neuro.epistemic_validation -> runtime.rebus_gate

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 2 — core.physics is hardened: no I/O, scheduling, or HTTP.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:core-physics-hardened]
name = core.physics does not import from application / apps / execution / runtime / interfaces / libs
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.physics
forbidden_modules =
    application
    apps
    execution
    runtime
    interfaces
    libs
ignore_imports =
    # No exemptions today.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 3 — core.kuramoto is hardened identically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:core-kuramoto-hardened]
name = core.kuramoto does not import from application / apps / execution
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.kuramoto
forbidden_modules =
    application
    apps
    execution
ignore_imports =
    # No exemptions today.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 4 — apps (Python apps; apps/web is TS and out of scope) do not
# reach down into core directly. They consume API / HTTP layers instead.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:apps-no-core]
name = apps do not import from core directly
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    apps
forbidden_modules =
    core
ignore_imports =
    # No exemptions today.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 5 — execution is independent of application (HTTP / API).
# It may consume core; it may not call up the stack.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:execution-no-application]
name = execution does not import from application
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    execution
forbidden_modules =
    application
ignore_imports =
    # No exemptions today.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 6 — leaf indicator math is import-light. core.indicators must not
# pull in the data/IO persistence layer (which transitively requires pydantic
# + cryptography), so that pure-numerical modules such as
# core.indicators.temporal_ricci import with only numpy/scipy/pandas/networkx.
# Regression guard for the B3 dependency-direction fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:indicators-no-feature-store]
name = core.indicators does not import core.data.feature_store
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    core.indicators
forbidden_modules =
    core.data.feature_store
ignore_imports =
    # No exemptions today.

# Analysis target is 3.12: recent numpy ships PEP 695 `type` statements in its
# bundled stubs (e.g. numpy/__init__.pyi), which mypy rejects with a syntax
# error under python_version < 3.12. Skipping numpy's stubs instead is not an
# option — that types numpy as Any and cascades 130+ strict errors through
# first-party array code. The 3.10 support floor (requires-python = ">=3.10")
# is guarded by the Verify CI matrix, which executes the suite on real 3.10 /
# 3.11 / 3.12 interpreters; mypy stays a pure type gate.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
warn_redundant_casts = false
disable_error_code = ["redundant-cast"]

    "N803",

    "N818",

]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  ruff — comprehensive Python linting
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"
# Frozen surfaces excluded from lint — scheduled for removal in v5.0
extend-exclude = [
  "src/mycelium_fractal_net/crypto/",
  "src/mycelium_fractal_net/signal/",

  "src/mycelium_fractal_net/analytics/legacy_features.py",
  "research/",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E",     # pycodestyle errors
  "W",     # pycodestyle warnings
  "F",     # pyflakes
  "I",     # isort
  "B",     # flake8-bugbear — opinionated bug detection
  "C4",    # flake8-comprehensions — unnecessary list/dict comprehension
  "UP",    # pyupgrade — modernize syntax for target Python
  "SIM",   # flake8-simplify — simplifiable constructs
  "PT",    # flake8-pytest-style — pytest best practices
  "RUF",   # ruff-specific rules
  "S",     # flake8-bandit — security checks
  "A",     # flake8-builtins — shadowing built-ins
  "C90",   # mccabe complexity
  "DTZ",   # flake8-datetimez — naive datetime usage
  "T20",   # flake8-print — print() in production code
  "PIE",   # flake8-pie — misc lints
  "PLC",   # pylint convention
  "PLE",   # pylint error
  "PLW",   # pylint warning
  "TID",   # flake8-tidy-imports — banned imports
  "TCH",   # flake8-type-checking — move imports to TYPE_CHECKING
  "PERF",  # perflint — performance anti-patterns
  "FLY",   # flynt — f-string conversion
  "FURB",  # refurb — modern Python idioms
]
ignore = [
  "E402",    # module-level import not at top (needed for conditional imports)
  "S101",    # assert usage (allowed in tests, banned in src via per-file)
  "S311",    # pseudo-random generators (acceptable for simulation seeds)
  "B008",    # function call in default argument (FastAPI Depends pattern)
  "UP007",   # X | Y union syntax (keep Optional for readability in complex signatures)
  "SIM108",  # ternary operator (readability over brevity for scientific code)
  "C901",    # too complex (handled by C90 mccabe with explicit threshold)
  "PLW2901", # loop variable overwritten (common in numeric code)
  "S603",    # subprocess call (needed in scripts)
  "S607",    # partial executable path (needed in scripts)
  "PLC0415", # import-outside-top-level (lazy imports by design for optional deps)
  "RUF002",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-docstring (μM, α, β are scientific notation)
  "RUF001",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-string (same)
  "RUF003",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-comment (same)
  "PLW0603", # global-statement (registry pattern for causal rules, detection config)
  "RUF043",  # pytest-raises-ambiguous-pattern (acceptable in test assertions)
  "PERF203", # try-except-in-loop (necessary for resilient iteration over scenarios)
  "PERF401", # manual-list-comprehension (readability over micro-optimization in scientific code)
  "PLW1510", # subprocess-run-without-check (scripts handle errors explicitly)
  "RUF012",  # mutable-class-default (dataclass fields with default_factory pattern)
  "SIM105",  # suppressible-exception (explicit try/except clearer than contextlib.suppress)
  "PT011",   # pytest-raises-too-broad (acceptable for integration tests)
  "PT012",   # pytest-raises-with-multiple-statements (test readability)
  "PT017",   # pytest-assert-in-except (intentional test pattern)
  "E741",    # ambiguous-variable-name (I, F, H, N are standard in scientific code)
  "S110",    # try-except-pass (intentional for optional features with fail-closed pattern)
  "T201",    # print (used in CLI, scripts, and cognitive functions)
  "E501",    # line-too-long (handled by formatter, allow in complex expressions)
  "A002",    # builtin-argument-shadowing (id= in rule_registry is domain convention)
  "B039",    # mutable-contextvar-default (logging config pattern)
  "S104",    # hardcoded-bind-all-interfaces (API server binds 0.0.0.0 by design)
  "S105",    # hardcoded-password-string (false positive on enum/config field names)
  "S112",    # try-except-continue (rate limiter resilience pattern)
  "SIM102",  # collapsible-if (readability over compactness in gate logic)
  "DTZ003",  # call-datetime-utcnow (UTC usage intentional in timestamps)
  "DTZ005",  # call-datetime-now-without-tzinfo (same)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"src/**/__init__.py" = [
  "F401",    # unused-import: __init__.py re-exports are intentional public API
]
"tests/**/*.py" = [
  "S101",    # assert is fine in tests
  "S105",    # hardcoded passwords in test fixtures
  "S106",    # hardcoded passwords in test arguments
  "T20",     # print in tests is acceptable
  "PLR2004", # magic values in tests are fine
]
"scripts/**/*.py" = [
  "T20",     # print is expected in CLI scripts
  "S603",    # subprocess calls in scripts
  "S607",    # partial path in scripts
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/cli.py" = [
  "T20",     # print is the correct output mechanism for CLI
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/__main__.py" = [
  "T20",     # print is the correct output for CLI entrypoint
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/integration/crypto_adapters.py" = [
  "B904",    # frozen adapter — exception chaining deferred to v5.0
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/experiments/**/*.py" = [
  "T20",     # print for experiment output
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/pipelines/reporting.py" = [
  "E501",    # HTML templates contain long lines by nature
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/pipelines/scenarios/**/*.py" = [
  "T20",     # print in __main__ blocks
]
"benchmarks/**/*.py" = [
  "T20",     # print for benchmark output
  "S101",    # assert in benchmarks
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 15

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["mycelium_fractal_net"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
extend-immutable-calls = ["fastapi.Depends", "fastapi.Query", "fastapi.Path"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bandit]
check-typed-exception = true

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  mypy — gradual strict typing
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
namespace_packages = true
pretty = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
show_error_codes = true
no_implicit_optional = true
strict_equality = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = true

# Core, analytics, neurochem: strict typing enforced — CI gate blocks merge
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "mycelium_fractal_net.types.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.security.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.core.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.analytics.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.neurochem.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.interpretability.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.self_reading.*",
]
disallow_untyped_defs = true
warn_return_any = true
no_implicit_optional = true
strict_equality = true

# Frozen / transport / ML modules: errors reported but not blocking
# Goal: remove this override entirely by v5.0
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "mycelium_fractal_net.model",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.signal.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.numerics.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.api",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.metrics",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.intelligence",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.pipelines.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.integration.*",
]
disallow_untyped_defs = false
# NOTE: ignore_errors removed — type errors are now visible and trackable

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  coverage — enforced minimum
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["mycelium_fractal_net"]
branch = true
parallel = true
omit = [
  "*/tests/*",
  "*/experiments/*",
  "*/load_tests/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
precision = 2
fail_under = 80
exclude_lines = [
  "pragma: no cover",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  "@overload",
  "\\.\\.\\.",
]

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "benchmarks", "scripts", "examples"]
skips = ["B101", "B311"]

[project]
name = "dagnam"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Official Python SDK for Dagnam.AI - datasets, training, model hub, deployments, and inference."
readme = { file = "README.md", content-type = "text/markdown" }
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE", "NOTICE"]
requires-python = ">=3.12"
authors = [
    { name = "Dagnam.AI", email = "dagnam@dagnam.ai" },
]
maintainers = [
    { name = "Dagnam.AI", email = "sdk@dagnam.ai" },
]
keywords = [
    "dagnam",
    "machine-learning",
    "deep-learning",
    "pytorch",
    "tensorflow",
    "jax",
    "flax",
    "datasets",
    "model-hub",
    "training",
    "inference",
    "mlops",
    "ai",
    "sdk",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    # License classifier intentionally omitted - PEP 639 SPDX expression
    # in `license = "Apache-2.0"` is the canonical source of truth and
    # newer setuptools/hatchling reject duplicate `License ::` classifiers.
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: CPython",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = [
    # >=2.32.0 is a security floor: it carries the credential/cert fixes
    # (CVE-2023-32681 Proxy-Authorization leak on redirect, CVE-2024-35195
    # cert-verify bypass on session reuse) and requests is the client that
    # carries the API key.
    "requests>=2.32.0",
    # numpy is imported eagerly by the dataset layer (dagnam.data.dataset.base),
    # so it is required for any dataset operation, not optional.
    "numpy>=1.24",
    # Pillow decodes images in the framework-agnostic system-dataset loaders, so
    # image datasets work from a plain ``pip install dagnam`` (no framework extra).
    # >=10.3.0 is a security floor: it excludes CVE-2023-50447 (ImageMath.eval
    # RCE, fixed 10.2) and CVE-2024-28219 (_imagingcms overflow, fixed 10.3),
    # and the SDK feeds dataset-supplied image bytes straight to the decoder.
    # 12.3.0 is the security floor: pillow 12.2.0 and below carry 13 known
    # advisories (PYSEC-2026-2253..2257, -3451..3454, -3493..3496).
    "pillow>=12.3.0",
    "polars>=1.0",
    "tqdm>=4.60",
    "typing_extensions>=4.12",
    "filelock>=3.13",
    # The canonical component/parameter validation contract, shared verbatim
    # with the backend and the Studio so all three reach identical verdicts.
    # Has ZERO runtime dependencies by design, so it costs this SDK no
    # transitive deps.
    # Capped below the next minor: the contract's PII class list and score
    # shape are a wire protocol with the platform, so a contract minor is only
    # ever picked up by an SDK release built and tested against it. An open
    # floor let a new contract reach an already published SDK whose platform
    # still ran the old one, and every audit stopped at its PII check.
    "dagnam-contracts>=0.4.1,<0.5",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
streaming = ["sseclient-py>=1.7"]
# The workload audit stores the customer's read-only observability key in the
# OS keychain; the readers themselves need nothing beyond polars.
audit = ["keyring>=25"]
# torchvision supplies ImageFolder + transforms for the PyTorch image loaders
# (dagnam.data.loaders.image_folder); it is a real runtime dep of this extra.
# torch>=2.13.0 is the validated security floor shared with the audio/all extras
# (2.12.1 and below carry GHSA-rrmf-rvhw-rf47); torchvision>=0.19 pairs with it.
pytorch = ["torch>=2.13.0", "torchvision>=0.19"]
# SoundFile decodes uploaded WAV/FLAC/MP3 files without a machine-global FFmpeg
# shared-library install. Torchaudio remains the framework transform dependency
# for generated MFCC/Mel nodes; TorchCodec is deliberately not a loader dep.
audio = ["torch>=2.13.0", "torchaudio>=2.0", "soundfile>=0.13"]
# TensorFlow added Python 3.12 support in 2.16 (2.12 tops out at 3.11), so the
# floor must be >=2.16 to be installable on the supported interpreters.
# keras is TensorFlow's own dependency (tensorflow declares only keras>=3.12.0),
# but it is named here as a security floor shared with the `all` extra: 3.15.0
# is the first release clearing all six 2026 model-loading advisories
# (GHSA-5gwj-m78q-7pq3 and GHSA-v2w2-w228-c444 code execution,
# GHSA-m8wh-29wm-52mv / GHSA-26c4-7vv6-867j local-file disclosure,
# GHSA-gh82-f9x8-5frx / GHSA-58hv-7753-xmfq path traversal). Those paths run
# whenever a user of this extra loads a `.keras`/`.h5` artifact, so the floor
# belongs in the published metadata rather than only in this repo's lockfile.
tensorflow = ["tensorflow>=2.16", "keras>=3.15.0"]
flax = [
    "jax>=0.4",
    "flax>=0.7",
]
aio = ["httpx>=0.27", "httpx-sse>=0.4"]
all = [
    "torch>=2.13.0",
    "torchvision>=0.19",
    "torchaudio>=2.0",
    "soundfile>=0.13",
    "tensorflow>=2.16",
    # Security floor, mirrors the `tensorflow` extra above.
    "keras>=3.15.0",
    "jax>=0.4",
    "flax>=0.7",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "httpx-sse>=0.4",
    "sseclient-py>=1.7",
]

[project.scripts]
dagnam = "dagnam.cli:main"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://dagnam.ai"
Documentation = "https://dagnam.ai/docs"
Repository = "https://github.com/Dagnam-AI/dag-lib"
Changelog = "https://github.com/Dagnam-AI/dag-lib/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"
Issues = "https://github.com/Dagnam-AI/dag-lib/issues"
Security = "https://github.com/Dagnam-AI/dag-lib/blob/main/SECURITY.md"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "hypothesis",
    "import-linter>=2.11",
    "pip-audit>=2.7",
    "poethepoet>=0.46.0",
    "pre-commit>=3.5",
    "pyright>=1.1.380",
    "pytest",
    "pytest-cov",
    "pytest-xdist",
    "requests-mock>=1.12",
    "respx>=0.20",
    "ruff",
    "truststore>=0.9",
]

[build-system]
# hatchling 1.32 (2026-08-11) made core metadata 2.5 the default, which the
# publish action's twine still rejects ("'2.5' is not a valid metadata
# version") -- the 0.11.0 release died on that check. Held below 1.32 (2.4)
# until pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish ships a twine that accepts 2.5.
requires = ["hatchling>=1.27,<1.32"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# Single source of truth for the version: hatchling reads ``__version__`` from
# ``dagnam/__init__.py`` at build time (default ``__version__ = "..."`` regex).
# Bump the version in that one file only — the built wheel/sdist metadata and
# ``importlib.metadata.version("dagnam")`` both derive from it, so there is no
# second place to keep in sync.
[tool.hatch.version]
path = "dagnam/__init__.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["dagnam"]
include = [
    "dagnam/py.typed",
    # Ship the Agent Skill payload + harness adapters as package data so
    # `dagnam agent install` can locate them via importlib.resources.
    "dagnam/_agent/skill/**",
    "dagnam/_agent/claude/**",
    "dagnam/_agent/codex/**",
]
force-include = { "NOTICE" = "dagnam/NOTICE" }

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
    "dagnam",
    "tests",
    "/scripts",
    "README.md",
    "LICENSE",
    "NOTICE",
    "CHANGELOG.md",
    "CONTRIBUTING.md",
    "SECURITY.md",
    "CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md",
    "pyproject.toml",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["dagnam"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
# Hard gate: the suite must keep dagnam at 100% statement AND branch coverage
# (branch = true in [tool.coverage.run] folds branch coverage into the total %
# that fail_under checks). Any regression fails `uv run poe check`. Genuinely
# non-coverable lines are excluded narrowly via exclude_also / `# pragma: no
# cover` / `# pragma: no branch`, each with an inline reason.
fail_under = 100
# Exclude only genuinely non-coverable lines (not whole files). These are
# boilerplate that can never execute in a normal test run, so counting them
# understates real coverage:
#   - TYPE_CHECKING-only import blocks (never run at runtime)
#   - abstract / Protocol method bodies (`raise NotImplementedError`, `...`)
#   - optional-dependency import guards (torch/tf/jax are installed, so the
#     `except ImportError: raise ImportError(...)` arms can't fire)
#   - script entry points
# Real but currently-untested logic (hub/projects facade delegations, the
# local-run streaming uploader, native dataset-conversion branches) is left
# visible on purpose — that is a test gap, not non-coverable code.
exclude_also = [
    "if\\s+TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "^\\s*\\.\\.\\.\\s*$",
    "if\\s+__name__\\s*==\\s*[\"']__main__[\"']:",
    "except\\s+ImportError(\\s+as\\s+\\w+)?:",
    # Defensive response-shape re-narrowing repeated across every client method.
    # The canonical narrowing logic lives in (and is tested via) the
    # `ensure_json_*` validators in `dagnam/_types.py`; these per-call-site
    # `raise TypeError("Expected JSON ...")` guards only fire when the backend
    # violates its own contract and would each need a contrived wrong-type wire
    # mock to hit. Excluded as boilerplate, not as a real test gap.
    "raise TypeError\\(f?\"Expected JSON",
]

[tool.pyright]
include = ["dagnam", "tests"]
exclude = ["**/__pycache__", ".venv"]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
reportMissingImports = "error"
reportMissingTypeStubs = "warning"
reportImplicitOverride = "error"
reportUnusedImport = "error"

# Strict mode minus its "completeness" family. The SDK consumes untyped
# third-party ML libraries (torch, torchaudio, tensorflow, jax/flax, numpy)
# and dynamic JSON server responses,
# which makes the reportUnknown*/reportMissing* diagnostics pervasive noise
# that cannot be resolved without sprinkling casts over every boundary. They
# are disabled deliberately; every *bug-catching* strict diagnostic
# (reportArgumentType, reportCallIssue, reportAttributeAccessIssue,
# reportReturnType, reportOptional*, reportIndexIssue, reportOperatorIssue,
# reportPrivateImportUsage, reportImplicitOverride, ...) stays enabled.
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportUnknownLambdaType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "none"
reportMissingTypeArgument = "none"

# Tests additionally reach into private (`_`-prefixed) attributes to assert on
# internal state; that is expected of unit tests, not a design smell.
[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "tests"
reportPrivateUsage = "none"
# Test modules import shared first-party helpers (`tests.typing_helpers`,
# `tests.data.loaders._*`) for annotations. `tests` is a namespace package with
# no `py.typed`, so pyright flags each such import as a missing stub. These are
# our own source files, not third-party libraries; scoping the rule off for the
# tests root removes the noise without weakening production type checking.
reportMissingTypeStubs = "none"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
src = ["dagnam", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W",
    "F",
    "I",
    "N",
    "UP",
    "B",
    "C4",
    "SIM",
    "PT",
    "RUF",
    "ASYNC",
    "S",
    "T20",
    "TID",
    "TCH",
    "D",
    "PERF",
    "FBT",
    "FA",
    "ARG",
]
ignore = [
    "E501",
    "D203", "D213", "D211", "D212",
    "D100", "D104", "D105",
    "S101",
    "S113",
    "B008",
    "ARG001",
    "ARG002",
    "ARG005",
    # Async SDK methods deliberately expose a `timeout` parameter that is
    # forwarded to the httpx transport (a network/socket timeout), not an
    # asyncio cancellation scope. This is the correct way to bound a single
    # request, so ASYNC109's "use asyncio.timeout() instead" does not apply.
    "ASYNC109",
    "ASYNC230",
    "B904",
    "D103",
    "D107",
    "D415",
    "D417",
    "E741",
    "FA100",
    "FA102",
    "FBT001",
    "FBT002",
    "PERF401",
    "PERF403",
    "RUF059",
    "S110",
    "S202",
    "S310",
    "S311",
    "SIM105",
    "SIM108",
    "SIM201",
    "TC001",
    "TC003",
    "UP006",
    "UP007",
    "UP028",
    "UP035",
    "UP045",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*" = [
    "S101", "S105", "S106", "S108",
    "D",
    "T20",
    "ARG",
    "FBT",
    "E741",
    "N806",
    "PERF401",
    "PT011", "PT012",
    "RUF059",
    "SIM117",
    # Test modules import shared type aliases from ``tests.typing_helpers``
    # purely for annotations; gating their placement behind TYPE_CHECKING in
    # tests adds churn with no runtime benefit (TC003 is already exempt here).
    "TC002",
    "TC003",
    "UP028",
]
# Framework-adapter modules are dominated by structural ``Protocol`` classes
# that mirror external ML library surfaces (torch, torchaudio, tensorflow,
# jax/flax, soundfile). Their stub methods intentionally
# mirror the external API and carry no behaviour, so per-method docstrings
# would be pure noise; the public API is the module-level loader functions.
"dagnam/data/loaders/**" = ["D102"]
"dagnam/cli/**/*" = ["T20"]
# The agent-integration runner and guard hook print to stdout by design: they
# back the skill's ``scripts/*.py`` shims and the PreToolUse hook protocol, both
# of which communicate via stdout. The script shims are equally print-by-design.
"dagnam/_agent/runner.py" = ["T20"]
"dagnam/_agent/guardhook.py" = ["T20"]
"dagnam/_agent/skill/scripts/**" = ["T20"]
# E402: the NullHandler must be attached BEFORE any subpackage import can log,
# so one non-import statement necessarily precedes the imports below it.
"dagnam/__init__.py" = ["F401", "E402"]
"dagnam/_core/__init__.py" = ["F401"]
"dagnam/aio.py" = ["F401"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["dagnam"]
combine-as-imports = true
force-sort-within-sections = true

[tool.ruff.lint.pep8-naming]
# These names intentionally violate snake_case because they mirror the exact
# public API surface of external ML libraries inside structural ``Protocol``
# definitions (and the test fakes that satisfy them). Renaming them would
# break the structural match against the real torch/torchaudio/tensorflow APIs
# they stand in for.
extend-ignore-names = [
    "Compose",
    "ToTensor",
    "Resize",
    "Normalize",
    "ImageFolder",
    "MNIST",
    "CIFAR10",
    "CIFAR100",
    "FashionMNIST",
    "OxfordIIITPet",
    "SPEECHCOMMANDS",
    "WikiText2",
    "MelSpectrogram",
    "Resample",
    "Tout",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
docstring-code-format = true

[tool.poe.tasks]
lint = { cmd = "ruff check", help = "Lint with ruff" }
format-check = { cmd = "ruff format --check", help = "Verify formatting" }
typecheck = { cmd = "pyright", help = "Static type check (pyright, strict)" }
lint-imports = { cmd = "lint-imports", help = "Verify the layer-first import contract" }
test = { cmd = "pytest tests -q -n 4 --dist=loadfile --cov=dagnam --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing", help = "Run the test suite in parallel with branch coverage (fails under 100%)" }
test-cov = { cmd = "pytest tests -q -n 4 --dist=loadfile --cov=dagnam --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html:htmlcov --cov-report=json:coverage.json --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml", help = "Run tests in parallel and generate terminal, HTML, JSON, and XML coverage reports" }
audit = { cmd = "python -c \"import sys, truststore; truststore.inject_into_ssl(); from pip_audit._cli import audit; sys.exit(audit())\"", help = "Audit Python dependencies for known vulnerabilities" }
build = { cmd = "uv build", help = "Build the source distribution and wheel" }
check = { sequence = [
    "lint",
    "format-check",
    "typecheck",
    "lint-imports",
    "test",
], help = "Run every quality gate (lint, format, types, import layering, tests)" }
release-check = { sequence = ["check", "audit", "build"], help = "Run quality gates, dependency audit, and package build" }

# Layer-first import contract for the SDK. The package keeps its layer-first
# layout by design: cli -> resources -> audit -> data -> _core, where a layer may import
# only the layers below it. Enforced (blocking) in CI via `uv run lint-imports`.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "dagnam"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "layered SDK: _core <- data <- audit <- resources/cli"
type = "layers"
# `_contracts` was the deepest layer until 0.10.0 removed it — the contract now
# ships as the separate `dagnam-contracts` distribution, which is a third-party
# dependency from this package's point of view and so is not a layer here.
# `audit` sits just above `data`: it imports `_core` (and may import `data`),
# and only `cli` reaches down into it.
layers = ["cli", "resources", "audit", "data", "_core"]
containers = ["dagnam"]

# §17.1057 — module-boundary contracts for the assist clusters (§17.856 split
# a 4,500-line agent into clusters held apart by deferred imports; nothing
# enforced the layering). grimp parses source, so this runs without app deps:
# `make lint-imports` (host) and in the CI smoke job.
[importlinter]
root_package = app
include_external_packages = False

[importlinter:contract:assist-leaves]
name = assist leaf modules import no assist orchestration
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.modules.assist_policy
    app.modules.assist_state_check
    app.modules.assist_replan
    app.modules.assist_decide
    app.modules.assist_notes
forbidden_modules =
    app.modules.assist_turn
    app.routers.assist

[importlinter:contract:policy-is-pure]
name = assist_policy is a pure gate module
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.modules.assist_policy
forbidden_modules =
    app.modules.assist_agent
    app.modules.assist_guide
    app.modules.assist_decide
    app.modules.assist_notes
    app.model_router

[project]
name = "scistudio"
version = "0.3.5a0"
description = "AI-native, inclusive workflow runtime for multimodal scientific data"
readme = "README.md"
license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    {name = "Jiazhen Zhang"},
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 2 - Pre-Alpha",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
]
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "fastapi>=0.110,<0.142",  # Starlette 1.3 nests included routers under _IncludedRouter; route-contract tests handle both layouts (#1769).
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.29",
    "numpy>=2.1",  # Core Array/storage/preview/plot paths import NumPy directly; numpy-2 baseline (#1809) — runtime + mypy stubs already assume 2.x.
    "zarr>=3.0",
    "pyarrow>=15.0",
    "watchdog>=4.0",
    "typer>=0.12",
    "xxhash>=3.4",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "psutil>=5.9",  # ADR-022: OS-level memory monitoring
    "filelock>=3.13",  # ADR-033 OQ7: file-locked atomic writes for MCP write tools
    "ruamel.yaml>=0.18",  # T-ECA-203: ruamel round-trip preserves comments/order in update_block_config
    "pywinpty>=2.0; sys_platform == 'win32'",  # ADR-034 Phase 1.2: PTY-based terminal embedding for claude/codex TUIs
    "platformdirs>=4.2",  # ADR-037 desktop/user-scoped config, cache, logs, and plugin directories
    "packaging>=24.0",  # Desktop package installer parses plugin dependency requirements.
    "fastmcp>=3.1,<5",  # ADR-040 §3.1: FastMCP migration — replaces hand-rolled JSON-RPC MCP server with FastMCP 3.x.
    "matplotlib>=3.8",  # ADR-048 SPEC 2: Python plot jobs import matplotlib in the core plot runtime.
    "pandas>=2.2",  # ADR-048 SPEC 2: Python plot jobs open DataFrame/Series inputs with pandas.
    "openpyxl>=3.1",  # #1810: core DataFrame/Series .xlsx read/write (pandas Excel engine).
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
ai = [
    "anthropic>=0.30",
    "openai>=1.30",
]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3",  # ADR-040 preflight: hard wall-clock kill for hung tests (Windows subprocess/asyncio edge cases)
    "hypothesis>=6.0",  # #1602: property-based tests (e.g. serializer path round-trip)
    "ruff>=0.11",
    "mypy>=1.15",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "griffe>=1.7",
    "pre-commit>=4.0",
    # ADR-042 Addendum 6 parity venvs must be able to run the local mirror of
    # ci.yml jobs. Keep build-system helpers in the dev extra so python_tests
    # and wheel_release_smoke do not fail as environment-parity gaps.
    "setuptools>=68.0",
    "build>=1.2",
    # The in-repo test fixture package (tests/fixtures/scistudio-blocks-fixture)
    # performs minimal real TIFF round-trips so core IO machinery
    # tests can exercise a package-owned capability. Keep this test-only helper
    # out of the core runtime dependency set.
    "tifffile>=2024.8",
    # #1340: vulture wires into full_audit as informational dead-code child
    # report (ADR-042 code-quality stack named vulture but never installed it).
    "vulture>=2.11",
]
docs = [
    # ADR-052 §7: the author-facing API reference is generated from docstrings +
    # the scistudio.stability decorators via mkdocstrings (griffe collector), so
    # the reference cannot drift from the code and tier/Since badges render
    # automatically. ``scripts/docs/build_reference.py`` emits the public surface
    # (the 9 canonical roots' ``__all__``) under ``docs/user/reference/`` and runs
    # ``mkdocs build --strict``. ``griffe`` is already pinned in the ``dev`` extra.
    "mkdocs>=1.6",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.26",
    "griffe>=1.7",
]

[project.scripts]
scistudio = "scistudio.cli.main:app"

# Issue #1779: core's own first-party blocks are NOT declared here. They are
# registered by direct import in ``scistudio.blocks.registry._scan._scan_builtins``
# so the palette is environment-independent. Entry-point discovery depends on
# installed ``*.dist-info`` metadata, which the desktop bundle does not carry
# (it ships core as raw source on PYTHONPATH and strips build metadata —
# ``desktop/scripts/stage-resources.sh``, #1775). Declaring first-party blocks
# here made the entire process/code/app palette disappear in packaged builds.
# This group is now reserved for third-party plugin packages only.
[project.entry-points."scistudio.blocks"]

# T-TRK-004 / ADR-028 §D4: the ``scistudio.adapters`` entry-point group
# has been removed. Plugin-owned IO blocks now register via the
# ``scistudio.blocks`` entry-point group as ``IOBlock`` subclasses
# (see ADR-028 §D1 + Addendum 1 §C). Core ``LoadData`` / ``SaveData`` are
# first-party blocks registered in ``_scan_builtins`` (#1779), not here.

# T-008 / ADR-027 D2: the previous entry-points here pointed at
# core ``Image``, ``Spectrum``, and ``PeakTable`` classes that were
# removed in T-006 and T-007. The classes now live in plugin
# packages (``scistudio-blocks-imaging``, ``scistudio-blocks-spectral``)
# which declare their own ``scistudio.types`` entry-points. The core
# repository contributes no built-in domain types via this group.
[project.entry-points."scistudio.types"]

# The ``scistudio.runners`` entry-point group was removed with the dead legacy
# CodeBlock runner layer: CodeBlock resolves interpreters through
# ``scistudio.blocks.code.backends`` / ``_backends_registry``, not the deleted
# ``runners/*`` modules. The group had no runtime consumer.
#
# ADR-053 FR-035: this note used to cite "ADR-052 §7A", which reads as a section
# of ``docs/adr/ADR-052.md`` — a document whose sections stop at §10 and which
# never mentions runners. The decision is real and is recorded one document
# over: ``docs/specs/adr-052-public-api-surface.md`` §7A, whose decision table
# carries the owner's 2026-06-27 ruling to delete ``runner_registry.py`` and
# ``runners/*`` as dead code with zero production importers, delivered in #1817.
# The citation is spelled in full here so a reader can follow it.
#
# The live entry-point groups are listed in exactly one place,
# ``src/scistudio/core/entry_points.py`` (ADR-053 FR-034). This group is not
# among them and must not be reintroduced by inference from this note.

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68.0", "setuptools-scm>=8.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
scistudio = [
    "api/static/**/*",
    "cli/templates/**/*.tpl",
    # ADR-040 §3.4: multi-skill source tree must ship in the wheel so
    # ``scistudio install --target claude|codex`` and the agent_provisioning
    # cross-installer can find canonical bodies.
    "_skills/scistudio/**/*.md",
    # ADR-040 §3.5-3.8: agent_provisioning template files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md,
    # codex_config.toml, 6 hook scripts) must ship with the wheel so
    # ``scistudio init`` / ``ApiRuntime.create_project`` can install them.
    "agent_provisioning/templates/**/*",
    # ADR-052 §7 / #1850: the in-project user guide + self-contained API
    # reference and the agent reference docs must ship in the wheel so
    # provisioning can copy them into each project (user-guide/ + agent docs).
    "_user_guide/**/*",
    "_agent_reference/**/*",
    # ADR-053 Learning Center: the published manifest schema and the shipped
    # core tutorials. Neither is reachable by ``packages.find``: the schema is
    # data, and a tutorial's ``assets/code/*.py`` sources live in directories
    # that are deliberately not importable packages (spec FR-020a keeps tutorial
    # material off every import path). Without these patterns an installed wheel
    # has a Learning Center whose schema fails to load and whose catalogue is
    # empty, and ``wheel-release-smoke`` would not notice because it inspects
    # the SPA bundle only. Same failure class as #824 and #2032.
    "panels/sdk/**/*",
    "panels/lib/**/*",
    "panels/builtin/**/*",
    "tutorials/schema/*.json",
    "tutorials/core/**/*",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 120
src = ["src"]
# #1340: vulture_allowlist.py is a vulture configuration file, not real code.
# The ``_.attr`` lookups are sentinels vulture reads; ruff would flag every
# line as B018 / RUF100 if it linted them.
extend-exclude = ["vulture_allowlist.py"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E",   # pycodestyle errors
  "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
  "F",   # pyflakes
  "I",   # isort
  "N",   # pep8-naming
  "UP",  # pyupgrade
  "B",   # flake8-bugbear
  "SIM", # flake8-simplify
  "RUF", # ruff-specific
  "C901", # mccabe complexity ceiling (#1602)
  "TD",  # flake8-todos: keep TODO markers well-formed + issue-linked (#1602)
  "FIX", # flake8-fixme: flag leftover FIXME/XXX/HACK markers (#1602)
]
ignore = [
  "E501", # line too long (handled by formatter)
  # flake8-todos rules we deliberately do NOT enforce, to fit the repo's
  # ``TODO(#NNN):`` convention (issue link lives in the author slot, not a
  # trailing URL) — issue-link enforcement is owned by scripts/deferral_scan.py
  # (#1602), which understands ``TODO(#NNN)`` exactly:
  "TD002", # missing author — our convention puts ``#NNN`` here, not a name
  "TD003", # missing issue link — deferral_scan owns the ``(#NNN)`` check
  # flake8-fixme FIX002 flags *every* TODO line; we allow tracked TODOs, so
  # bare-TODO blocking is owned by deferral_scan, not ruff:
  "FIX002", # line contains TODO
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Grandfathered ceiling (#1602): current worst is ``validate_workflow`` at 60,
# carried with an explicit ``# noqa: C901``. 30 blocks any *new* function from
# exceeding it while leaving the existing single offender visible. Ratchet down
# as complex functions are refactored.
max-complexity = 30

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["scistudio"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
# Respect per-module follow_imports="skip" for stub (.pyi) packages too, so the
# numpy/zarr/tifffile overrides below actually skip their 3.12-syntax stubs under
# our python_version = "3.11" target (otherwise stub parse errors leak through).
follow_imports_for_stubs = true
mypy_path = "src"
packages = ["scistudio"]
# The in-project documentation tree (#1850) ships example block files as data,
# not importable library modules. Several are named block.py and collide as
# duplicate top-level modules under type checking; exclude the whole docs tree.
#
# ADR-053 Learning Center: the same case. A core tutorial ships its block and
# plot sources under ``assets/code/`` as package data, and FR-020a keeps tutorial
# material off every import path deliberately — so these are files the product
# writes into a reader's project, not modules it imports. They are also written
# to be read and edited by a bench scientist, which is why ``def render(collection):``
# carries no annotations; requiring them would make the first Python a new user
# meets less like the Python they write.
exclude = ['/_user_guide/', '/tutorials/core/']

# zarr 3.2+ uses PEP 695 generic syntax (`class Foo[T]:`) which is only valid
# in Python 3.12+. Our mypy is pinned to python_version = "3.11", so it cannot
# parse zarr's source. Skip following imports into zarr to avoid syntax errors.
# See issue #693.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["zarr", "zarr.*"]
follow_imports = "skip"

# tifffile uses Python 3.12+ type-alias syntax in current releases. The package
# remains an optional/dev data-format helper for tests, while SciStudio's mypy
# target is still Python 3.11, so do not parse tifffile internals.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["tifffile", "tifffile.*"]
follow_imports = "skip"

# numpy 2.x ships PEP 695 type-alias syntax (`type X = ...`) in its stubs, valid
# only in Python 3.12+. mypy is pinned to python_version = "3.11" (see above), so
# it cannot parse numpy's stubs. Skip following imports into numpy to avoid the
# stub syntax error; SciStudio code does not rely on numpy's internal types.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["numpy", "numpy.*"]
follow_imports = "skip"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# TODO(#1540): Restore coverage gate to ≥80% once ADR-034 Phase 1-3 tests are
#   added back. Lowered temporarily during PR #808 rollback.
#   Out of scope per owner decision recorded in issue #1540.
#   Followup: https://github.com/zjzcpj/scistudio/issues/1540
addopts = "-ra -q --cov=scistudio --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=70"
# ADR-040 preflight: per-test 60s wall-clock kill via pytest-timeout. Without
# this, hung tests (Windows subprocess pipe issues, deadlocked asyncio) hang
# pytest forever which hangs agents forever. ``thread`` method works on Windows
# (signal method requires SIGALRM, POSIX-only).
timeout = 60
timeout_method = "thread"
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "requires_r: tests that need an R installation with Rscript on PATH",
    "requires_fiji: marks tests that need a local Fiji install at the master-plan §10 path (deselect with '-m \"not requires_fiji\"').",
    "serial: process/PTY/thread/timing-sensitive tests that must run OUTSIDE xdist (run with '-n0 -m serial'; the parallel batch deselects them via '-m \"not serial\"'). Under '-n auto' these can leak a thread/subprocess that hangs or crashes an xdist worker (#1867, #1896). See scistudio.qa.testing.run_python_tests.",
]
# filterwarnings policy (issue #1560):
#   - "error" is NOT applied globally — the suite uses third-party libraries
#     (zarr, fsspec, h5py, PIL, pytest-asyncio) that emit deprecation warnings
#     we do not own.  Turning those into errors would break CI on every upstream
#     release.  Instead we silence known third-party deprecations explicitly and
#     let unrecognised warnings from scistudio.* surface as errors so regressions
#     are visible.
#
#   Policy rationale:
#     1. Third-party DeprecationWarnings: ignore (not our responsibility to fix
#        until we upgrade the dependency; tracked via normal dependency updates).
#     2. PendingDeprecationWarning from third-parties: ignore (same rationale).
#     3. DeprecationWarning whose source is scistudio.*: error (we own it).
#     4. PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning: error (signals hidden async failures).
#
#   Conservative approach: we deliberately do NOT use "error::DeprecationWarning"
#   globally because zarr, h5py, and fsspec emit stdlib deprecations that would
#   make the suite fail today; that cleanup belongs in the dependency-upgrade
#   milestone (issue #1560).
filterwarnings = [
    # Surface first-party regressions as errors.
    "error::DeprecationWarning:scistudio.*",
    "error::PendingDeprecationWarning:scistudio.*",
    # Catch hidden async failures that would otherwise be swallowed.
    "error::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning",
    # Known third-party deprecations — ignore until upstream resolves.
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:zarr.*",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:fsspec.*",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:h5py.*",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:PIL.*",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:pkg_resources.*",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["scistudio"]
# Round-4 no-cycles: count only imports that execute at runtime. A
# ``TYPE_CHECKING``-guarded import is a type-annotation reference, not a real
# module-load dependency, so it can never cause an import cycle or a real
# layering inversion. Excluding it matches the project's agreed "no-cycles"
# definition (the failure mode we guard against is a circular *import*, i.e. a
# module-load crash) and keeps annotation back-references (e.g. a bound-method
# module typing its owner class) from being flagged.
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Core must not depend on blocks, engine, api, ai, or workflow"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["scistudio.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["scistudio.blocks", "scistudio.engine", "scistudio.api", "scistudio.ai", "scistudio.workflow"]
# ADR-038 §3.2: ``LineageRecorder`` (in core/lineage/) references the engine
# ``EventBus`` / ``EngineEvent`` types only under ``TYPE_CHECKING`` — event-name
# strings are hardcoded in core to avoid runtime coupling, and runtime objects
# arrive via constructor injection. That type-only edge no longer needs an
# ``ignore_imports`` carve-out: ``exclude_type_checking_imports`` (top of this
# section) already drops it from the graph.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Blocks must not depend on engine, api, or ai services"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["scistudio.blocks"]
forbidden_modules = ["scistudio.engine", "scistudio.api", "scistudio.ai"]
# Narrow carve-outs for engine-layer dispatch surfaces that block-layer
# code must call. Each entry cites the ADR that justifies the boundary
# crossing.
#
# ADR-035 §3.10: AIBlock.run() must call back to the engine to allocate
# a PTY tab and notify completion.
#
# ADR-028 §D8 (Phase -1 sprint, this PR + #1080): AppBlock's
# `_bin_outputs_by_extension` dispatches to
# `engine.materialisation.reconstruct_from_file` for typed DataObject
# reconstruction. The helper lives in `engine/` because it consumes
# `BlockRegistry` from `blocks/` (a `core/` placement would violate
# Core ↔ Blocks per the first contract above). Both ignore entries
# below are lazy function-body imports executed only inside the per-run
# AppBlock dispatch path.
#
# ADR-035 §3.8 (#1591) / ADR-034 (#1994): AIBlock lazily reaches the agent
# layer inside its per-run dispatch path. The edge used to terminate at
# `ai.agent.terminal` (`_ensure_mcp_config`, `_write_system_prompt_tempfile`)
# because the block composed its own spawn argv; ADR-034 FR-012 deleted that,
# so the block no longer writes MCP config or system-prompt files at all. What
# remains is a narrower read-only edge to `ai.agent.providers_registry` for the
# provider key set, descriptor lookup, and binary resolution (FR-005, FR-014,
# FR-015). The registry deliberately imports neither `scistudio.api` nor
# `scistudio.blocks` (spec §4.1) so both layers can depend on it. The crossing
# is intentional and lazy, so it stays carved out here rather than restructured.
ignore_imports = [
    "scistudio.blocks.ai.ai_block -> scistudio.engine.pty_control",
    "scistudio.blocks.ai.ai_block -> scistudio.ai.agent.providers_registry",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Engine must not depend on api or ai services"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["scistudio.engine"]
forbidden_modules = ["scistudio.api", "scistudio.ai"]
# ADR-035 §3.8 (#1591): the only engine->ai path is transitive through the
# block-registry scan — `engine.scheduler -> blocks.registry -> _spec ->
# blocks.ai.ai_block -> ai.agent.providers_registry`. The terminating edge is the same
# accepted lazy AIBlock->agent import carved out in the Blocks contract above
# (it became graph-visible once `ai/agent/` gained its `__init__.py`). Engine
# does not depend on ai services directly; it scans every block (incl. the AI
# block) via the registry. Carve out the same leaf edge here so the registry
# scan does not transitively trip this contract.
ignore_imports = [
    "scistudio.blocks.ai.ai_block -> scistudio.ai.agent.providers_registry",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Round-4 no-cycles: complete the reverse-dependency coverage. The three
# contracts above only checked core/blocks/engine as sources; the lower/側
# layers below were unchecked, which let real inversions slip through (e.g.
# the bottom ``utils`` layer importing ``core``/``engine``). These contracts
# close that gap.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Utils is the bottom layer — must not depend on higher layers"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["scistudio.utils"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "scistudio.core",
    "scistudio.engine",
    "scistudio.blocks",
    "scistudio.workflow",
    "scistudio.ai",
    "scistudio.api",
    "scistudio.panels",
]
# #1729: ``utils.axis_iter`` (ADR-027 D3 ``iterate_over_axes``) is documented
# public API consumed by the imaging plugin, so it stays in ``utils`` for now
# even though it lazily reads the core zarr backend. Tracked for relocation to
# ``core`` at #1729; carve out the edges until then.
ignore_imports = [
    "scistudio.utils.axis_iter -> scistudio.core.storage.zarr_backend",
    "scistudio.utils.axis_iter -> scistudio.core.storage.ref",
    "scistudio.utils.axis_iter -> scistudio.core.storage.flush_context",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Workflow must not depend on ai or api"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["scistudio.workflow"]
forbidden_modules = ["scistudio.ai", "scistudio.api"]
# Same accepted lazy leaf edge carved out in the Blocks and Engine contracts
# above: ``workflow.validator -> blocks.registry`` transitively reaches
# ``blocks.ai.ai_block -> ai.agent.providers_registry`` through the registry's per-run
# block scan. Workflow does not depend on ai services directly; it validates
# against the block registry, which scans every block (incl. the AI block).
ignore_imports = [
    "scistudio.blocks.ai.ai_block -> scistudio.ai.agent.providers_registry",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "AI must not depend on api"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["scistudio.ai"]

# mutant re-runs the selected tests, so cost scales with paths × suite time.

#   .venv/bin/mutmut run          # generate + test mutants

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture

@AnalyzeClasses(
    packages = ["br.com.rfasioli.bootstrap.api"],
    importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class],
)
class HexagonalArchitectureTest {
    @ArchTest
    val hexagonalArchitectureLayersIsRespected: ArchRule =
        layeredArchitecture().consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer("DomainServices").definedBy("..domain.usecase..")
            .layer("PortIn").definedBy("..port.input..")
            .layer("PortOut").definedBy("..port.output..")
            .layer("AdapterIn").definedBy("..adapter.input..")
            .layer("AdapterOut").definedBy("..adapter.output..")
            .whereLayer("AdapterIn").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("AdapterOut").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("DomainServices").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("PortIn").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("DomainServices", "AdapterIn")
            .whereLayer("PortOut").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("DomainServices", "AdapterOut")
            .allowEmptyShould(true)
}

# 现状说明：mypy 已可正常运行，但全库仍有数百处存量类型错误（check_untyped_defs
# 打开且历史代码从未被检查过）。因此它是【增量排查工具】而非 CI 门禁——
# CI 里不跑 mypy，避免引入一个永久失败的检查项。用法：`make typecheck`。
[tool.mypy]
# 按包名而非路径检查：xcash/ 自身也是包（有 __init__.py），若按路径传入，
# 同一文件会被同时解析为 xcash.common 和 common 两个模块名而直接报错中止。
packages = [
    "aml",
    "chains",
    "common",
    "config",
    "core",
    "currencies",
    "deposits",
    "evm",
    "invoices",
    "projects",
    "saas_api",
    "tron",
    "users",
    "webhooks",
]
# 只接受 x.y，写 x.y.z 会被 mypy 判为非法版本并放弃该配置。
python_version = "3.13"
# 各 app 以顶层包形式存在于 xcash/ 下（运行期由 base.py 的 sys.path.append 注入）。
# mypy 不认这个运行期 hack，必须显式告知，否则它解析不到 users.User 等模块：
# django-stubs 插件为 AUTH_USER_MODEL 解析 _AnyUser 时会无限 defer，
# 最终以 "Must not defer during final iteration" 崩溃（INTERNAL ERROR）而非报缺模块。
mypy_path = "xcash"
check_untyped_defs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_configs = true
plugins = [
    "mypy_django_plugin.main",
    "mypy_drf_plugin.main",
]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Django migrations should not produce any errors:
module = "*.migrations.*"
ignore_errors = true

[tool.django-stubs]
# 必须指向 test settings：django-stubs 插件会在启动时真实导入该 settings 模块，
# dev/production 依赖 POSTGRES_PASSWORD 等外部环境变量，缺失时插件直接构造失败
# （mypy 报 INTERNAL ERROR）。test settings 用 os.environ.setdefault 自带全部默认值，
# 无需任何环境变量即可导入，故是唯一能让 mypy 开箱可用的选择。
django_settings_module = "config.settings.test"

# ==== import-linter ====
# 模块分层契约：上层可以依赖下层，下层不得反向依赖上层。同一行里用 | 分隔的模块
# 互相独立（不得互相 import），用 : 分隔的可以互相 import。函数内延迟 import 同样
# 计入（这正是循环依赖最常藏身的地方）；仅 TYPE_CHECKING 下的类型导入不计入。
# 运行：make lint（CI 的 lint job 同步执行）。各 app 以顶层包形式位于 xcash/ 下，
# 必须带 PYTHONPATH=xcash 才能被解析到。
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = [
    "aml",
    "chains",
    "common",
    "core",
    "currencies",
    "deposits",
    "evm",
    "invoices",
    "projects",
    "saas_api",
    "tron",
    "users",
    "webhooks",
]
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "模块分层：依赖只能自上而下"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    # 入口与运维聚合层：SaaS 控制面 API、后台看板 / 巡检 / 初始化，可依赖一切。
    "saas_api : core.admin : core.dashboard : core.dashboard_metrics : core.default_data : core.health : core.management : core.monitoring : core.tasks",
    # 业务层：账单、充值。
    "invoices | deposits",
    # 业务支撑层：商户项目、AML、后台用户。
    "projects | aml | users",
    # 链族实现：在各自 AppConfig.ready() 里向 chains.registry 登记。
    "evm | tron",
    # 链引擎内核与币种目录（Transfer ↔ Crypto、CryptoOnChain ↔ Chain 在模型层互相引用）。
    "chains : currencies",
    # 出站投递基础设施：商户 Webhook。
    "webhooks",
    # 通用基础组件。
    "common",
    # 平台参数：SystemSettings / SystemWallet 模型与运行时参数读取。core 包内的其余模块
    # 属于最上层；包按模块分属两层，是因为模型迁移出 core 需要跨部署的数据迁移，收益不抵风险。
    "core.runtime_settings : core.models",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # 测试可以跨层组装夹具。平铺的测试模块无法用通配符表达（通配符只能替换整段模块名），需逐个登记。
    "**.tests -> **",
    "**.tests.** -> **",
    "chains.test_keys -> **",
    "chains.tests_constants -> **",
    "chains.tests_fixtures -> **",
    "chains.tests_models_refactor -> **",
    # ---- 以下为存量例外：待消化，新代码不得效仿。消化后删除对应行（残留行会让检查报错）。----
    # AML 筛查结果直接回写账单 / 充值；应改为业务层消费筛查结果。
    "aml.service -> invoices.models",
    "aml.service -> deposits.models",
    # 商户项目校验收款模式时直接查询账单侧的钱包直收地址 / 易支付商户。
    "projects.models -> invoices.models",
    "projects.service -> invoices.models",
    # Django admin 是展示组合层，按页面需要跨层取数。
    "projects.admin -> invoices.models",
    "webhooks.admin -> core.monitoring",
    # HTTP 签名鉴权中间件按 appid 解析商户项目，本属入口层，物理上仍在 common。
    "common.middlewares -> projects.models",
    # TVM 与 EVM 复用同一份 VaultSlot 合约字节码构造。
    "tron.contracts_codec -> evm.contracts_codec",
]

# ==== black ====
# 本项目唯一的格式化器。line-length 不配置：black 默认 88，与 [tool.ruff] 一致。
[tool.black]
# 必须与 ruff 的 exclude 和 .pre-commit-config.yaml 的 exclude 保持一致地排除迁移文件。

# codemem layer-boundary enforcement (M1 Task 1.11).
#
# Run locally: uv run lint-imports
# Run in CI: GitHub Actions `security.yml` (codemem-smoke job) runs
# `uv run lint-imports` after `uv sync` (diagram-generation M2).
#
# Contracts:
#
# 1. Layered architecture inside the codemem package: storage is the
#    leaf, parser sits above it, and the orchestrators + public API
#    sit on top. storage must not know anything about parser; parser
#    must not know anything about mcp_tools.
#
# 2. codemem.parser must not import from codemem.mcp_tools (back-edge
#    forbidden — the parser layer is pure and must stay reusable).
#
# 3. aa_ma.render is a leaf: derived views (lint, HTML) may import the
#    grammar and parsers, but nothing in aa_ma may import aa_ma.render
#    (plan-architecture-views M2, ADR-0010).
#
# 4. aa_ma never imports codemem: aa_ma.render.graph reads codemem's SQLite
#    file with stdlib sqlite3, so the coupling is the on-disk schema, not a
#    Python API (diagram-generation M2, ADR-0014). `source_modules = aa_ma`
#    is accepted here — the shared-descendants refusal noted in contract 3
#    applies only when source and forbidden share a root package.
#
# 5. aa_ma.analysis is a leaf both ways (codebase-analysis-skills M1): nothing in aa_ma imports it,
#    and it imports no other aa_ma module (stdlib + pydantic only). Both lists are explicit and
#    pinned by tests/render/test_leaf_contract.py.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    codemem
    aa_ma

[importlinter:contract:codemem-layers]
name = codemem layered architecture
type = layers
layers =
    codemem.mcp_tools : codemem.indexer : codemem.resolver : codemem.pagerank
    codemem.parser
    codemem.storage

[importlinter:contract:parser-is-pure]
name = parser must not depend on public API
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    codemem.parser
    codemem.parser.python_ast
    codemem.parser.ast_grep
forbidden_modules =
    codemem.mcp_tools
    codemem.indexer
    codemem.resolver
    codemem.pagerank

[importlinter:contract:render-is-leaf]
name = aa_ma.render is a leaf package
type = forbidden
# Every top-level aa_ma module except render. import-linter's `forbidden` type
# refuses `source_modules = aa_ma` ("shared descendants"), so the list is explicit
# and tests/render/test_leaf_contract.py fails when a module is added but not listed.
source_modules =
    aa_ma.analysis
    aa_ma.cli
    aa_ma.deps
    aa_ma.enforce
    aa_ma.forks
    aa_ma.gate
    aa_ma.goal_synthesis
    aa_ma.grammar
    aa_ma.logsetup
    aa_ma.plan_markers
    aa_ma.plan_parsers
    aa_ma.schemas
    aa_ma.tui
    aa_ma.validators
forbidden_modules =
    aa_ma.render

[importlinter:contract:aa-ma-never-imports-codemem]
name = aa_ma never imports codemem
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    aa_ma
forbidden_modules =
    codemem

[importlinter:contract:analysis-is-leaf]
name = analysis-is-leaf: aa_ma.analysis is a leaf package
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    aa_ma.cli
    aa_ma.deps
    aa_ma.enforce
    aa_ma.forks
    aa_ma.gate
    aa_ma.goal_synthesis
    aa_ma.grammar
    aa_ma.logsetup
    aa_ma.plan_markers
    aa_ma.plan_parsers
    aa_ma.render
    aa_ma.schemas
    aa_ma.tui
    aa_ma.validators
forbidden_modules =
    aa_ma.analysis

[importlinter:contract:analysis-is-self-contained]
name = analysis-is-self-contained: aa_ma.analysis imports no other aa_ma module
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    aa_ma.analysis
forbidden_modules =
    aa_ma.cli
    aa_ma.deps
    aa_ma.enforce
    aa_ma.forks
    aa_ma.gate
    aa_ma.goal_synthesis
    aa_ma.grammar
    aa_ma.logsetup
    aa_ma.plan_markers
    aa_ma.plan_parsers
    aa_ma.render
    aa_ma.schemas
    aa_ma.tui
    aa_ma.validators

[project]
name = "aa-ma"
# NOTE: version is owned by commitizen via scripts/release.sh (docs/runbooks/release.md).
# Do NOT hand-edit.
version = "0.17.0"
description = "Advanced Agentic Memory Architecture - structured external memory for AI coding agents"
readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    { name = "Stephen J Newhouse", email = "stephen.j.newhouse@gmail.com" },
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
]
# Runtime dependencies — created in aa-ma-tui-tracker M0 T0.1 (2026-05-17).
# Declared explicitly per L-055 (no implicit transitives for direct imports).
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2,<3",         # Typed model (Task/Milestone/Step). Promoted from transitive.
    "textual>=0.80,<1.0",     # Interactive TUI framework (M3).
    "rich>=13,<14",           # Snapshot mode + Textual renderer (M2). Declared explicitly per L-055.
    "watchfiles>=0.21,<1.0",  # Async file-watch for live refresh (M3). Already transitive via fastmcp.
    "markdown-it-py>=4,<5",   # Render (plan-architecture-views M4). Promoted from transitive via rich per L-055.
]

[project.scripts]
# CLI entry point — created in aa-ma-tui-tracker M0 T0.2 (2026-05-17).
aa-ma-tui = "aa_ma.tui.__main__:main"
# Gate questions from the Python SSoT — created in milestone-grammar-ssot M5 (2026-09-11).
aa-ma-gate = "aa_ma.gate:main"
# §13 Architecture View lint — created in plan-architecture-views M2 (2026-09-12).
aa-ma-lint-views = "aa_ma.render.cli:lint_main"
aa-ma-render = "aa_ma.render.cli:render_main"
# Codebase-analysis core (assess-codebase / understand-codebase) — created in codebase-analysis-skills M1 (2026-09-28).
aa-ma-analysis = "aa_ma.analysis.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.uv.workspace]
# codemem-mcp is a sibling standalone package; see packages/codemem-mcp/pyproject.toml.
# Rationale documented in .claude/dev/active/codemem/codemem-plan.md §3 #1 (Q1 + Q13).
members = ["packages/codemem-mcp"]

[tool.uv.sources]
codemem-mcp = { workspace = true }

[tool.ruff]
# Eval fixtures plant logging/style defects on purpose for the skills to find (ADR-0021).
extend-exclude = [
    "tests/fixtures/evals",
    "tests/fixtures/canary/canary_shell.py",  # why: a deliberate S602; tests/security/test_canary.py scans it explicitly
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Logging + comment hygiene (logging-and-comments standard). CI's `touched` job runs
# `ruff check` (via pre-commit) on every file a PR touches (ADR-0018).
# T201 has only an unsafe fix, so `ruff check --fix` reports prints and never deletes them.
extend-select = [
    "LOG",              # logger misuse: Logger() direct, getLogger without __name__, root-logger calls
    "G",                # eager log formatting (G004 = f-string in log call), .warn, exc_info misuse
    "T20",              # print/pprint left in library code
    "BLE",              # blind `except Exception`
    "S",                # flake8-bandit security rules, the Python security gate (M8, ruff-only); incl. S110/S112 silent swallows
    "TRY400", "TRY401", # use logger.exception in except; don't repeat the exception in the message
    "D",                # docstrings, google convention (incl. D417 undocumented Args) (T8)
    "TD",               # TODO format: TODO(owner/issue): text
    "ERA",              # commented-out code
    "RUF100",           # unused noqa: a suppression that suppresses nothing is removed (T8)
    "PGH003", "PGH004", # blanket `type: ignore` / `noqa`: name the code you silence (T8)
    "C901",             # cyclomatic complexity (KISS, T11 §3)
    "PLR0913",          # too many arguments (KISS, T11 §3)
    "W605",             # invalid escape sequence: a SyntaxWarning on Python 3.12+, an error later
]
# Touched files comply in full (D8): CI lints only the files a PR touches, so the
# pre-existing docstring gaps are paid down as files are edited, not all at once.
# PLR2004 (magic values) is deliberately not selected: constants are review-only (T8).
extend-ignore = [
    "D107",  # why: the class docstring documents __init__ args (google style, T8)
    "TD003", # why: wants an issue URL line; it rejects TODO(ADR-NNNN), which TODO001 accepts (T8)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10  # why: ruff/flake8 default; Ste's T11 §3 ceiling for one function

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 6  # why: one over ruff's 5 — leaves room for a keyword-only flag (T11 §3)

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# print IS the interface for CLIs (data -> stdout); tests need no docstrings.
"**/cli.py" = ["T20"]
"**/__main__.py" = ["T20"]
"src/aa_ma/forks.py" = ["T20"]  # run as `python -m aa_ma.forks`; stdout is its report
"src/aa_ma/deps.py" = ["T20"]   # run as `python -m aa_ma.deps` (aa_ma_deps helper); stdout is its report
"scripts/**" = ["T20"]
# tests run git/bash on purpose (S603/S607), write tmp fixtures (S108) and assert (S101) — approved M8.2.
"tests/**" = ["D", "T20", "S101", "S108", "S110", "S603", "S607"]

[tool.commitizen]
# Releases are cut by scripts/release.sh (docs/runbooks/release.md): it promotes the curated
# `## Unreleased` CHANGELOG section and the README "Current version" line, then `cz bump`
# updates version_files and commits everything (-a) under an annotated tag. cz never writes
# the CHANGELOG — update_changelog_on_bump=true replaced curated notes with commit subjects
# every release from v0.7.0 to v0.11.0 (lessons L-006/L-008).
name = "cz_conventional_commits"
version_provider = "pep621"
tag_format = "v$version"
update_changelog_on_bump = false
annotated_tag = true
bump_message = "bump: version $current_version → $new_version\n\n[ad-hoc]"
version_files = [
    "VERSION:__version__",
]
# uv.lock records the project version; re-lock after cz writes version_files so the -a
# commit (and the tag) carry a consistent lock. release.sh refuses to push otherwise.
pre_bump_hooks = ["uv lock --quiet"]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# pytest (M1 Task 1.13)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# The `perf` marker gates the performance-budget suite at
# `tests/perf/test_budgets.py`. Default test runs skip it (via the
# `addopts` filter below); run it locally with `-m perf` (CI does not run it).
[tool.pytest.ini_options]

# Import Linter configuration for Adapt
#
# Purpose:
# Enforce architectural boundaries so the codebase stays modular,
# testable, and free of accidental coupling.
#
# Run:
#   lint-imports
#
# Philosophy:
# - The layer stack below is the architecture. A package may import only
#   packages in layers BELOW its own; siblings on one layer (joined by |)
#   are independent and never import each other.
# - `exhaustive = true` means every top-level package under adapt MUST be
#   placed in a layer. Adding a new package fails this check until it is
#   deliberately assigned a home — that is the point.
# - This file is mirrored in ARCHITECTURE.md; tests/test_architecture.py
#   asserts the two stay identical and match the real source tree.
# - Scientific-module independence (adapt.modules.X never imports
#   adapt.modules.Y) is enforced by tests/test_architecture.py, which
#   auto-discovers module subpackages at runtime.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    adapt

include_external_packages = False

# ==========================================================
# 1. The layer stack
# ==========================================================
#
# cli            outermost shell; may import anything
# consumers      dashboards/TSE — read ONLY via adapt.api (see contract 2)
# visualization  plotting; core never imports it
# runtime        composition root: orchestrates everything below
# configuration  pydantic schemas + resolution; builds module configs
# api            StoreClient read facade over the store
# execution      graph + nodes: the one sanctioned wiring layer over modules
# modules        science; deterministic; no I/O to the store
# persistence    SQLite/NetCDF store; no science, no orchestration
# contracts      types + check_* validators; zero adapt imports
# downloaders    boto3/S3 isolation; zero adapt imports
# utils          shared pure functions; zero adapt imports

[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Adapt layer stack
type = layers
containers =
    adapt
exhaustive = true
layers =
    cli
    consumers | visualization
    runtime
    configuration
    api | execution
    modules | persistence
    contracts | downloaders | utils

# ==========================================================
# 2. Consumers speak only through the public API
# ==========================================================
#
# The layer stack alone would let consumers import any lower layer.
# Consumers (dashboard, target selection) must not reach persistence,
# runtime, or execution directly — reaching them THROUGH adapt.api is
# the sanctioned path, hence allow_indirect_imports. StoreClient is the
# only read surface (I/O side doors are closed by
# tests/test_architecture.py::test_consumers_read_only_through_the_store_api).

[importlinter:contract:consumers_use_public_api_only]
name = Consumers do not import persistence, runtime, or execution
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    adapt.consumers
forbidden_modules =
    adapt.persistence
    adapt.runtime
    adapt.execution
allow_indirect_imports = True

version = "0.3.16"
description = "Persatrix AI Agent Runtime"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
