# PR review: upper bounds prevent silent breakage from major version bumps.
# Caps are set at the next major (or next minor for 0.x) version to allow
# compatible updates while guarding against breaking API changes.
#
# CI installs these, and the `dev` extra below, at the exact versions in
# .github/python-constraints.txt. After changing a dependency here, run `make
# python-constraints` and commit the file with it: the Python CI job fails
# until the two agree.
dependencies = [
    "grpcio>=1.71.2,<2",
    # Pinned exactly because this is the program that emits the committed
    # `agents/generated/*_pb2.py` and `*_pb2_grpc.py`, and `make
    # proto-python-check` fails the build when they drift. Same reasoning as
    # the `mypy-protobuf` pin below, which covers the `.pyi` half — and the
    # same reasoning CI uses to pin protoc to an exact version.
    #
    # The pin is not a new restriction. Under the `protobuf<6` cap below,
    # every grpcio-tools from 1.72.1 to 1.83.1 is unresolvable (they all
    # require protobuf>=6), so `>=1.71.2,<2` could only ever resolve to
    # 1.71.2 anyway. What changes is that the generator now says so, instead
    # of being a side effect of a cap on a different package. Bump it the way
    # `mypy-protobuf` asks to be bumped: deliberately, regenerating the stubs
    # in the same change, with the toolchain CLAUDE.md pins.
    "grpcio-tools==1.71.2",
    # Load-bearing beyond ordinary compatibility: until the pin above existed,
    # this cap was the only thing holding the stub generator still, by
    # constraining what pip could resolve for it. Widening it turned every
    # generated file stale at once, not just the mypy-protobuf .pyi — PRs #870
    # and #879 each did exactly that. Lifting it now means moving the
    # generator pin with it, regenerating with the CI-pinned toolchain, and
    # dropping the matching `ignore` rules in `.github/dependabot.yml`.
    # Tracked in docs/issues/ISSUE-0145-proto-toolchain-pinned-to-protobuf-5x.md.
    "protobuf>=5.28.0,<6",
    "pyyaml>=6.0,<7",
    "aiohttp>=3.9.0,<4",
    # The <1 cap is load-bearing, not just cautious: anthropic 1.x removed
    # `temperature` from `messages.create`, and AnthropicProvider passes it to
    # every older model that takes it (agents/llm_providers.py),
    # claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-haiku-4-5 among them, so 1.x turns those
    # requests into a TypeError raised before the request is even sent. CI
    # cannot see it — the unit tests construct the provider (whose signature
    # did not change) and mock the client from there. Lifting this cap means
    # moving the provider to whatever 1.x replaced `temperature` with, in the
    # same change — and dropping the matching `ignore` rule in
    # `.github/dependabot.yml`, which stops the monthly sweep re-proposing the
    # widening this cap exists to refuse. The port is tracked in
    # docs/issues/ISSUE-0144-anthropic-sdk-pinned-below-1x.md.
    # The 0.83.0 floor is the first release whose `messages.create` takes the
    # request settings an alias can ask for (ISSUE-0169): `thinking` of type
    # adaptive and `output_config` (0.80.0), and the top-level `cache_control`
    # that `prompt_cache` sends (0.83.0); older releases raise a TypeError.
    "anthropic>=0.83.0,<1",
    # <4 admits openai 2.x and 3.x. Checked against 3.19.2 on the surface this
    # tree actually touches — AsyncOpenAI(api_key, base_url),
    # chat.completions.create(model, messages, max_tokens or
    # max_completion_tokens, temperature, tools, reasoning_effort), and the
    # fields _normalize reads back (choices[].message.tool_calls[].function,
    # finish_reason, usage.prompt_tokens/completion_tokens and
    # prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens/cache_write_tokens) — all present.
    # The 1.58.0 floor is the first release that takes `reasoning_effort`,
    # which an alias can ask for (ISSUE-0169); older ones raise a TypeError.
    "openai>=1.58.0,<4",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.28.0,<2",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.28.0,<2",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.28.0,<2",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc>=0.49b0,<1",
    # NOTE: ``opentelemetry-instrumentation-system-metrics`` is intentionally
    # NOT listed here. It is consumed only by the metrics work in RFC 0019
    # PR 3 (process & runtime metrics) and adding it now would bloat the
    # install closure for one PR cycle. PR 3 will reintroduce it alongside
    # its first consumer. See PR #163 review round 2 (Nit #3).
    "opentelemetry-semantic-conventions>=0.49b0,<1",
    "structlog>=24.1.0,<27",
    "jsonschema>=4.23.0,<5",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19.0,<1",
    # RFC 0021 P1 — agents/temporal/ and agents/clock.py read named
    # IANA zones via ``zoneinfo.ZoneInfo``.  Linux/macOS ship a system
    # tz database; Windows does not, so ``tzdata`` is required there
    # for any non-UTC zone to resolve.  Pinned for every platform so
    # the install closure does not branch on host OS.
    "tzdata>=2024.1",
    # RFC 0023 (LLM Call Leasing) Open Question §5 — promoted from the
    # former ``accurate-tokens`` optional extra to a hard runtime
    # dependency. The wallet client tokenises the prompt with
    # ``tiktoken.cl100k_base`` to fund the lease's provisional charge
    # (agents/wallet_client.py via agents/llm_client.py), so a single
    # tokeniser path must exist on every runtime install — not just
    # when an optional extra was selected.
    "tiktoken>=0.7.0,<1",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.24.0",
    "ruff>=0.8.0",
    "mypy>=1.13.0",
    "types-PyYAML",
    "types-protobuf",
    "types-grpcio",
    "pip-licenses>=5.0.0,<6",
    # ISSUE-0017: protoc plugin that emits *_pb2.pyi stubs at `make
    # proto-python` time, replacing the previously hand-maintained
    # `agents/generated/task_pb2.pyi`. Pinned to an exact version
    # because mypy-protobuf output differs across minor versions
    # (3.5 → 3.6 swapped `typing_extensions.final` for `typing.final`
    # and rewrote `Literal` references) — the same reason CI pins
    # protoc to an exact version (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` →
    # arduino/setup-protoc, version: "34.1"). Without an exact pin,
    # `make proto-python-check` flips red whenever pip resolves a
    # newer 3.x release. The 4.x line is excluded because it requires
    # protobuf>=6 while the runtime closure above caps protobuf<6
    # (see grpcio-tools constraint). Bump deliberately, regenerate the
    # *.pyi, and commit in the same change.
    "mypy-protobuf==3.6.0",
    # RFC 0045 §B — the MIT↛BUSL dependency-direction gate. import-linter's
    # `lint-imports` runs the `[tool.importlinter]` forbidden contract below as
    # a hard CI gate (`make imports-check`), failing the build if an
    # MIT-candidate primitive grows an import into orchestrator-coupled (BUSL)
    # code. Pinned `>=2` for the `forbidden`-contract + child-wildcard
    # (`<root>.*`) semantics the contract relies on.
    "import-linter>=2.0,<3",
]
# RFC 0053 (Gemini + watsonx.ai providers) OQ #4 — the provider SDKs ship as
# extras (`pip install 'persatrix-agents[gemini]'`), not base requirements, so a
# single-provider deployment carries no new runtime dependency. The
# `create_provider` gemini branch surfaces an actionable `ImportError →
# SystemExit` install hint when the extra is not present. The native
# `google-genai` SDK (RFC 0053 OQ #1 — not the OpenAI-compat endpoint).
# The 1.56.0 floor is the first release whose ThinkingConfig takes every
# `thinking_level` an alias can ask for (`minimal` and `medium` arrived then).
gemini = [
    "google-genai>=1.56.0,<3",
]
# watsonx.ai native SDK — the `create_provider` watsonx branch surfaces the
# actionable `ImportError → SystemExit` install hint when this extra is absent.
# watsonx has no broad OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so a native class over
# `ModelInference` is required (RFC 0053 §C), not a `base_url` reuse.
watsonx = [
    "ibm-watsonx-ai>=1.1.0,<2",
]
# RFC 0053 PR 3 (closeout) — a combined bundle of every optional provider SDK,
# so an operator standing up the four-vendor human-free brainstorm (RFC 0052
# PR 9) pulls them all in one step: `pip install 'persatrix-agents[providers]'`
# instead of naming each (`[gemini,watsonx]`). This is a **self-referencing
# extra**: it re-exports the individual provider extras by name rather than
# copying their pins, so a bumped SDK pin is inherited automatically and can
# never drift out of sync. Keep the bracket in step with the individual provider
# extras above — the drift guard
# `tests/unit/python/test_pyproject_provider_extras.py` fails if a new provider
# extra is added without folding its name in here. `anthropic` / `openai` are
# always-on base dependencies and Ollama reuses the base `openai` SDK, so they
# contribute nothing to this bundle.
providers = [
    "Persatrix-agents[gemini,watsonx]",
]

[project.scripts]
Persatrix-agent = "persatrix_agents.server_cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=75.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

# Map the agents/ directory to the 'persatrix_agents' import path.
# Without this, pip install would discover sub-packages (generated, memory, etc.)
# as top-level packages, and 'python -m persatrix_agents.server' would fail
# with ModuleNotFoundError since no 'persatrix_agents' package would exist.
#
# Packages are listed explicitly because 'packages.find' scans for directories
# literally named 'persatrix_agents*', which don't exist here (the mapping is
# agents/ → persatrix_agents). Auto-discovery would leave MAPPING empty in the
# editable install finder, silently breaking imports.
[tool.setuptools.package-dir]
persatrix_agents = "."

[tool.setuptools]
# MAINTAINER NOTE: this list is manually maintained because auto-discovery
# cannot resolve the agents/ → persatrix_agents mapping (see comment above).
# When adding a new sub-package (e.g. persatrix_agents.bridges), add it here
# or imports will silently fail in editable installs.
packages = [
    "persatrix_agents",
    "persatrix_agents.generated",
    "persatrix_agents.memory",
    "persatrix_agents.observability",
    "persatrix_agents.persona_runtime",
    "persatrix_agents.sub_agents",
    "persatrix_agents.temporal",
    "persatrix_agents.tests",
    "persatrix_agents.tools",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"
# Machine-generated protobuf/gRPC stubs — do not lint.
extend-exclude = ["generated"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# "TID251" is the specific banned-api rule, not the umbrella "TID" category:
# selecting "TID" would also enable TID252 (banned relative imports) and flag
# this package's pervasive `from .x import y` style. Keep the rule code.
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "TID251", "W", "UP"]

# RFC 0029 — the personal/society storage boundary. A direct aiosqlite
# import is allowed only inside agents/memory/ (see the per-file-ignore
# below); every other caller must go through the agents.memory.MemoryStore
# facade. TID251 flags the import; agents/memory/_boundary.py emits the
# matching DeprecationWarning on direct EpisodicMemory / RelationshipMemory
# construction — two halves of one guard rail.
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"aiosqlite".msg = "Direct aiosqlite access outside agents/memory/ breaks the RFC 0029 personal/society storage boundary — use the agents.memory.MemoryStore facade. See docs/rfcs/0029-personal-society-storage-split.md."

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# gRPC servicer methods use PascalCase per proto contract.
"server.py" = ["N802"]
# RFC 0029 — agents/memory/ IS the personal-tier storage boundary, so it
# is the one place a direct aiosqlite import is allowed; the TID251 ban
# applies everywhere else.
"memory/**" = ["TID251"]
# Grandfathered: participant.py's UserStore is a pre-existing direct-SQLite
# store (the `users` participant-identity table). Folding it behind the
# MemoryStore facade is out of RFC 0029 Phase 1 scope; the TID251 ban
# still blocks any *new* direct-aiosqlite caller elsewhere.
"participant.py" = ["TID251"]

[tool.mypy]
# ISSUE-0062: the repo-root `mypy.ini` duplicates these base settings to
# type-check the `tests/` tree, because mypy has no config-inheritance
# mechanism. Keep the two in sync — when changing a setting below, mirror it
# in `mypy.ini`, which deliberately carries all of these EXCEPT
# `warn_return_any` (test doubles return `Any` by design).
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# testpaths is not set here because test paths are specified explicitly
# in the Makefile targets.
#
# Python unit tests live in TWO trees, both CI-gated:
#   * tests/unit/python/ (repo root) — the bulk of the suite, run by
#     `make test-python`.
#   * agents/tests/      — run by `make test-agents`, from the repo root with
#     this config (`-c agents/pyproject.toml`).
# This comment previously asserted that tests live at tests/unit/python/ "not
# under agents/tests/". That was scaffold boilerplate: the note and
# agents/tests/ were added in the same commit (fb76bb80, "scaffold initial
# project structure"), so it never described a migration anyone performed —
# agents/tests/ grew to 422 tests underneath it. Because the note read as a
# deliberate convention while no job actually ran the tree, drift there stayed
# invisible. Add new tests to either tree; both run in CI.
markers = [
    "requires_compose: integration tests that require the docker-compose observability stack to be running (otel-collector, jaeger, prometheus, loki). Opt-in: run with `pytest -m requires_compose`.",
    "requires_orchestrator: integration tests that spawn the built `bin/persatrix-server` and `cli/target/release/persatrix` binaries. Opt-in: run with `pytest -m requires_orchestrator` after `make build-orchestrator build-cli`.",
    "requires_anthropic: integration tests that exercise a real Anthropic API call (probabilistic, billed). Opt-in: run with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... pytest -m requires_anthropic`. Tests under this marker auto-skip when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset.",
]
# RFC 0029 — the personal/society storage guard rail emits a
# DeprecationWarning on direct EpisodicMemory / RelationshipMemory
# construction (agents/memory/_boundary.py). ~25-30 per-tier test files
# construct those tiers directly by design — a tier cannot be unit-tested
# through the MemoryStore facade — so the warning is expected, permanent
# suite noise rather than an actionable signal; left unfiltered it buries
# genuine DeprecationWarnings. This scoped ignore silences exactly that
# message. It is mirrored in tests/conftest.py for repo-root runs
# (`make test-python` runs pytest from the root with no `-c`, so this
# file is not discovered) — same dual-declaration rationale as the
# markers above. test_memory_boundary.py's pytest.warns assertions still
# observe the warning: they install their own always-filter.
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore:Direct construction of:DeprecationWarning",
]

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# RFC 0045 §B — the MIT↛BUSL dependency-direction gate (Python half).
#
# Open-core rests on one load-bearing rule: imports may only point *down*-tier
# (`MIT ← BUSL ← Private`). A small, generically-useful "MIT-candidate"
# primitive must never import an orchestrator-internal (BUSL) module — on the
# next mirror/release that one-line diff would ship BUSL source under an MIT
# grant (RFC 0045 §M-4). This `forbidden` contract makes that a hard CI gate
# (`make imports-check`), seeded *before* any code physically moves.
#
# The candidates below are each already leaf on `main` (they import only
# stdlib, third-party SDKs, the generated wallet stubs, or a fellow MIT leaf),
# so the contract is green today and only a future up-import turns it red.
#
# `forbidden_modules` lists the *children* of the root (`persatrix_agents.*`),
# NOT the root itself: forbidding the ancestor package is silently vacuous —
# import-linter does not count a source importing a sibling under that same
# ancestor as a violation. The child wildcard also auto-covers any new
# top-level orchestrator module without a config edit.
# The regression suite is tests/unit/python/test_dependency_direction_imports.py.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "persatrix_agents"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "MIT-candidate primitives must not import orchestrator-coupled (BUSL) modules"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "persatrix_agents.wallet_client",
    "persatrix_agents.prompt_loader",
    "persatrix_agents.prompt_safety",
    "persatrix_agents.llm_types",
    "persatrix_agents.llm_offline",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "persatrix_agents.*",
]
# The only first-party imports a candidate may make: a fellow MIT leaf, or the
# generated wallet proto stubs (the published MIT wire contract, RFC 0046 §D).
# Every entry's right-hand side must stay an MIT leaf — never an
# orchestrator-coupled module (asserted by the regression suite).
ignore_imports = [
    "persatrix_agents.llm_offline -> persatrix_agents.llm_types",
    "persatrix_agents.wallet_client -> persatrix_agents.generated.wallet_pb2",
    "persatrix_agents.wallet_client -> persatrix_agents.generated.wallet_pb2_grpc",
]

[importlinter]
# Every first-party root is named here.  The source tree, separately shipped
# harness, repository-only tooling, documentation namespace, test support, and
# generated companion namespace are all part of the closed classification.
root_packages =
    cadrumo
    cadrumo_harness
    dev
    docs
include_external_packages = False
# Import form does not change the architectural verdict.  In particular,
# TYPE_CHECKING imports and function-local imports remain in the graph.
exclude_type_checking_imports = False

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Closed package classification
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[importlinter:contract:closed-cadrumo-classification]
type = layers
name = Every cadrumo source package has a declared lane
containers = cadrumo
layers =
    _data : adapters : application : conftest : core : domain : entrypoints : tests : (locales)
exhaustive = True

[importlinter:contract:closed-harness-classification]
type = layers
name = Every harness source package has a declared lane
containers = cadrumo_harness
layers =
    _resources : _skill_metadata : _workspace : mcp : resources : tests : (_data)
exhaustive = True

[importlinter:contract:closed-dev-classification]
type = layers
name = Every repository tooling package has a declared lane
containers = dev
layers =
    _paths : acceptance : actionlint : agent_eval : audit : cache_root : ci : ci_reports : conftest : corpus : deploy : docs : env : exit_codes : first_party_source : identity : ingest_harness : init : locales : packaging : product_environment : quality : readme : registry : release : report_storage : sanitizer : smoke : source_tree : test_runs : tests : tui
exhaustive = True

[importlinter:contract:closed-documentation-classification]
type = layers
name = Every documentation package has a declared lane
containers = docs
layers =
    conf
exhaustive = True

# ``cadrumo_data`` is an installed namespace rather than a local Python
# directory in this checkout.  Its resource lane is therefore represented by
# the static census gate, which also rejects undeclared generated-root imports.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Repository-only and separately shipped-root boundaries
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[importlinter:contract:shipped-code-never-reaches-repository-only]
type = forbidden
name = Shipped code never reaches repository-only roots
source_modules =
    cadrumo
    cadrumo_harness
forbidden_modules =
    dev
    docs
allow_indirect_imports = False

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inward dependency direction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[importlinter:contract:core-is-innermost]
type = forbidden
name = Core has no outward dependency
source_modules =
    cadrumo.core
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.domain
    cadrumo.application
    cadrumo.adapters
    cadrumo.entrypoints
    cadrumo_harness
    dev
    docs
allow_indirect_imports = False

[importlinter:contract:domain-is-inward]
type = forbidden
name = Domain has no outward dependency
source_modules =
    cadrumo.domain
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.application
    cadrumo.adapters
    cadrumo.entrypoints
    cadrumo_harness
    dev
    docs
allow_indirect_imports = False

[importlinter:contract:application-is-inward]
type = forbidden
name = Application has no concrete outer dependency
source_modules =
    cadrumo.application
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.adapters
    cadrumo.entrypoints
    cadrumo_harness
    dev
    docs
allow_indirect_imports = False

[importlinter:contract:shared-tests-are-core-only]
type = forbidden
name = cadrumo.tests remains core-only shared support
source_modules =
    cadrumo.tests
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.domain
    cadrumo.application
    cadrumo.adapters
    cadrumo.entrypoints
    cadrumo_harness
    dev
    docs
allow_indirect_imports = False

[importlinter:contract:resource-data-isolated]
type = forbidden
name = Resource data does not depend on product layers
source_modules =
    cadrumo._data
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.core
    cadrumo.domain
    cadrumo.application
    cadrumo.adapters
    cadrumo.entrypoints
    cadrumo_harness
    dev
    docs
allow_indirect_imports = False

[importlinter:contract:harness-has-no-entrypoint-or-repository-dependency]
type = forbidden
name = Separately shipped harness consumes inward code only
source_modules =
    cadrumo_harness
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.entrypoints
    dev
    docs
allow_indirect_imports = False

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outer peer boundaries
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[importlinter:contract:adapters-do-not-reach-composition]
type = forbidden
name = Adapters do not reach entrypoint composition
source_modules =
    cadrumo.adapters
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.entrypoints
    cadrumo_harness
    dev
    docs
allow_indirect_imports = False

[importlinter:contract:cli-does-not-reach-tui]
type = forbidden
name = CLI and TUI are independent entrypoint siblings
source_modules =
    cadrumo.entrypoints.cli
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.entrypoints.tui
allow_indirect_imports = False

[importlinter:contract:tui-does-not-reach-cli]
type = forbidden
name = TUI and CLI are independent entrypoint siblings
source_modules =
    cadrumo.entrypoints.tui
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.entrypoints.cli
allow_indirect_imports = False

[importlinter:contract:entrypoint-shared-code-does-not-reach-siblings]
type = forbidden
name = Shared entrypoint composition does not reach CLI or TUI
source_modules =
    cadrumo.entrypoints
forbidden_modules =
    cadrumo.entrypoints.cli
    cadrumo.entrypoints.tui
allow_indirect_imports = False

# The canonical public defining modules remain the only legal domain-to-domain
# surface.  Package-initializer and private-module enforcement is completed by
# the source census gate because Import Linter cannot distinguish an exported
# symbol from a module-level import after name resolution.

[project]
name = "cadrumo"
version = "0.6.0"
description = "Cadrumo is a deterministic Spanish tax calculation CLI that turns local financial records into checked, exportable modelo filing artifacts. Independent software; not affiliated with AEAT."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
license = "Apache-2.0"
# Explicit so the wheel/sdist always carry the Apache §4(d) attribution chain
# (dist-info/licenses/{LICENSE,NOTICE}), independent of hatchling's default
# license-file globs.
license-files = ["LICENSE", "NOTICE"]
authors = [
  { name = "Neve Nincs", email = "hello@neve.md" },
]
keywords = ["cadrumo", "aeat", "hacienda", "impuestos", "spain", "tax", "toolkit", "utility", "cli"]
classifiers = [
  "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Topic :: Office/Business :: Financial",
]

dependencies = [
  # The command-bearing distribution is complete by default. The three data
  # companions are separate files only to stay below the package-index
  # per-file cap; they are exact-version runtime dependencies because the CLI
  # cannot perform grounded tax work without every corpus slice.
  "anyio>=4.5,<5",
  "cadrumo-data-manuals==0.6.0", # x-release-please-version
  "cadrumo-data-official==0.6.0", # x-release-please-version
  "cadrumo-data-normatives==0.6.0", # x-release-please-version
  "mcp>=2,<3",
  # Rust-backed TOML parser behind the canonical `cadrumo.core.toml` boundary,
  # the only place TOML is parsed; several times faster than the stdlib parser.
  "rtoml>=0.13.0,<1",
  # Capability-gated integrations live in [project.optional-dependencies].
  # `anthropic` (Anthropic-API LLM provider), the `google-*` stack
  # (Drive/Sheets export), and `playwright*` (live AEAT browser) are lazily
  # imported and map to the `anthropic`, `google`, and `browser` extras below.
  # Argon2id KDF for the file-fallback master-key provider's
  # passphrase-to-KEK derivation. OWASP-current top-tier
  # password-hashing primitive; ships pre-built wheels for
  # Linux/macOS/Windows.
  "argon2-cffi>=23.1.0,<26",
  # HTML parsing for status readers. The `lxml` extra is load-bearing, not a
  # preference: every AEAT page read goes through one constructor
  # (`adapters/outbound/aeat/_html.py`) that names "lxml" as the parser
  # backend, and BeautifulSoup raises FeatureNotFound rather than falling back
  # when the named backend is absent. lxml does reach a default install today, but only
  # as a transitive of pikepdf -- incidental supply for a direct reliance, so a
  # pikepdf change would surface as a runtime failure on the first AEAT page
  # parsed. Declaring it turns that into a resolution failure instead.
  "beautifulsoup4[lxml]>=4.12,<5",
  # Direct first-party imports (CadrumoTyperGroup command suggestions,
  # wizard prompt types, click context helpers). typer>=0.26 no longer
  # declares click, so the dependency must be explicit here.
  "click>=8.1,<9",
  # PKCS#12 parsing for client-certificate auth.
  "cryptography>=50.0.0,<51",
  # XML parsing.
  "defusedxml>=0.7.1,<1",
  # HTTP client
  "httpx>=0.28.1,<1",
  # OS-keychain abstraction for the master-key provider (Windows
  # Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service via
  # libsecret). Pure-Python, gracefully degrades when no usable backend
  # is detected; the substrate's file fallback covers headless / CI.
  "keyring>=25.6.0,<26",
  # Native Secret Service protocol calls and encrypted session codec.
  "jeepney>=0.9,<0.10; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "secretstorage>=3.5,<3.6; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  # The Windows ACL hardening path imports pywin32 directly. Keep it in the
  # base runtime on Windows rather than relying on mcp's transitive supply.
  "pywin32>=311 ; sys_platform == 'win32'",
  "openpyxl>=3.1.5,<4",
  # PDF parsing for justificantes.
  "pdfplumber>=0.11.9,<1",
  # Fast text extraction from official AEAT manual PDFs for registry
  # source-citation validation.
  "pypdfium2>=5.7.1,<6",
  # PDF sanitiser; content-stream rewriter for PII redaction.
  # Upstream 10.14 wheels require macOS 15; retain the declared macOS 14 floor.
  "pikepdf==10.13.0.post1; sys_platform == 'darwin'",
  "pikepdf>=10.0.0,<11; sys_platform != 'darwin'",
  # Imaging primitive behind pypdfium2's `to_pil()` page rasterisation. Same
  # class as the `lxml` entry above and declared for the same reason: Pillow
  # DOES reach a default install today, but only as a transitive of pdfplumber
  # and pikepdf -- incidental supply for a direct reliance, since the
  # rasteriser calls `bitmap.to_pil()` and then `image.save(...)` itself. A
  # pdfplumber or pikepdf change dropping Pillow would surface as a runtime
  # failure on the first page rendered, misdiagnosed as a broken PDF by the
  # rasteriser's own error wrapping. Declaring it turns that into a resolution
  # failure instead. The `llm` extra declares it too; that declaration is
  # correct but not load-bearing, because the two PDF packages keep Pillow in
  # the base closure regardless.
  "pillow>=12,<13",
  # Data validation & models
  "pydantic>=2.12.5,<3",
  "pydantic-settings>=2.9.1,<3",
  # `pydantic` does not re-export `PydanticSerializationError`, so ten production
  # modules reach it at its own distribution. A direct import needs a direct
  # declaration; left unbounded above so `pydantic`'s exact pin stays the
  # resolver's authority.
  "pydantic-core>=2.46",
  # Interactive prompt backend for the wizard descriptor runtime.
  "questionary>=2.1.1,<3",
  # Direct prompt_toolkit imports support wizard console validation and tests.
  "prompt-toolkit>=3.0,<4",
  # Configuration
  "python-dotenv>=1.2.2,<2",
  # CLI localization backend.
  "python-i18n>=0.3.9,<1",
  "PyYAML>=6.0.3,<7",
  # Typer imports Rich at runtime for help/error rendering. Keep the direct
  # pin version-bounded here; application code should not import Rich directly.
  "rich>=14.2.0,<16",
  # Spanish Snowball stemmer for the grounding-search FTS5 stemmed column
  # (bundled-corpus retrieval and the command-search index). Small, pure-Python,
  # BSD, no transitive weight. Core rather than optional so the lexical index
  # has ONE shape on every install and carries no unstemmed degraded branch.
  "snowballstemmer>=2.2,<4",
  # Persistence
  "sqlalchemy>=2.0.36,<3",
  # CLI
  "typer>=0.20.0,<1",
  # IANA timezone data for Europe/Madrid, including Windows and minimal
  # Linux containers whose operating system carries no zoneinfo database.
  "tzdata>=2026.2",
  "xlrd>=2.0.1,<3",
  # Full-screen TUI framework for paged terminal flows (screens, focus,
  # reactive widgets, headless Pilot test driver). MIT; depends on rich
  # (shared pin above) and not on prompt_toolkit, so the line-mode and
  # full-screen stacks stay independent.
  "textual>=8.2.8,<9",
]

[project.scripts]
aeat = "cadrumo.entrypoints.cli.bootstrap:main"
cadrumo-mcp = "cadrumo_harness.mcp.main:main"
cadrumo-runtime = "cadrumo.entrypoints.runtime.bootstrap:main"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/nevenincs/cadrumo"
Issues = "https://github.com/nevenincs/cadrumo/issues"
Repository = "https://github.com/nevenincs/cadrumo"

[project.optional-dependencies]
workbook-windows = [
  "pywin32>=311 ; sys_platform == 'win32'",
]
# ── Capability-gated optional integrations ───────────────────────────────────
# Each extra maps to an operator-facing capability/feature. All are lazily
# imported, so `pip install cadrumo` (no extras) builds and runs the core CLI; the
# feature refuses with an install hint when its extra is absent (graceful
# degradation). `cadrumo config check` reports
# which extras are importable.
#
# Google Drive + Sheets export (the `google_export` capability). OAuth Desktop
# flow: loopback IP + PKCE via
# google-auth-oauthlib's InstalledAppFlow; the storage provider drives Drive v3
# / Sheets v4 through the discovery client. google-auth-httplib2 is intentionally
# NOT pinned — transport is satisfied by `requests` (transitive via google-auth).
google = [
  "google-auth>=2.50.0,<3",
  "google-auth-oauthlib>=1.3.1,<2",
  "google-api-python-client>=2.195.0,<3",
]
# Live AEAT browser automation (the `cadrumo app live ...` sede sessions).
browser = [
  "playwright>=1.58.0,<2",
  # Runtime browser evasion used by AEAT live browser sessions.
  "playwright-stealth>=2.0.3,<3",
]
# Direct Anthropic-API LLM classification provider (distinct from the
# subprocess CLI providers, which need no Python SDK).
anthropic = [
  "anthropic>=0.74.1,<1",
]
# OFX/QFX bank-statement import. ofxtools is the maintained, strict OFX-spec
# parser (ships py.typed), but it is GPL-3.0-only; gating it behind this extra
# keeps the CORE dependency closure free of strong copyleft. Lazily imported
# behind `require_optional_extra(OFX_EXTRA)`; an OFX source without the extra
# refuses with the `pip install cadrumo[ofx]` hint.
ofx = [
  "ofxtools>=1.1,<2",
]
# Local-inference document reading (the opt-in `cadrumo.adapters.outbound.llm`
# subpackage).
# Gates the probabilistic reading path: rasterising a scan-only invoice
# on-host and handing it to a local model runtime. Deliberately narrow, and
# the narrowness is the honest result rather than an oversight -- the local
# runtime is reached over HTTP on the already-declared `httpx`, page rendering
# runs on the already-declared `pypdfium2`, and the one direct third-party
# reliance the path adds beyond the core closure is Pillow, via `to_pil()`.
# The path carries no model weights, no GPU runtime and no inference library
# today. The extra exists so that stays a CHECKABLE property: a transformers-
# or vLLM-served model would land HERE rather than in [project.dependencies],
# which is the boundary this extra is for.
#
# Pillow is ALSO a direct base dependency above. Both declarations are
# deliberate: the base entry closes the undeclared-direct-reliance defect,
# this one declares what the inference path needs on its own terms.
llm = [
  "pillow>=12,<13",
  # NVML bindings, read-only. The local-inference contention check needs FREE
  # VRAM, not total: a 16 GB card shared with a resident service and a desktop
  # is not 16 GB of headroom, and a load admitted against the total is the
  # overflow this check exists to prevent. NVML gives per-device total AND free
  # figures; a whole-device `nvidia-smi` shell-out gives neither reliably nor
  # without a subprocess. Absent, the accelerator reads `unknown` and acting
  # fails closed -- so this extra widens what can be admitted, never what can
  # be refused.
  "nvidia-ml-py>=13,<14",
]
# The calculation-summary PDF destination (`aeat app modelo work report
# --document-format pdf`). ReportLab (BSD) lays out the pages; the tagging,
# attachment and metadata pass runs on the already-declared `pikepdf`, and
# verifying a summary needs no extra at all. ReportLab depends only on Pillow
# and charset-normalizer, both already in the core closure. Lazily imported
# behind `PDF_EXTRA`; without it the destination refuses before reading the
# store.
pdf = [
  "reportlab>=5.0.1,<6",
]
# Deliberately absent: an `agent` extra. The operator agent harness, its
# reviewed operating data, accessors, and MCP runtime are a separate
# `cadrumo_harness` package shipped alongside it in this distribution.
#
# Deliberately absent: a `search` extra. The on-host grounding search stack
# needs none — the lexical index (stdlib sqlite3 FTS5 plus the core
# `snowballstemmer` stemmed column) and the structured citation lookup run on
# every install. The runtime embedding stack the extra once gated (model2vec,
# huggingface-hub, numpy) was retired, so the product ships no semantic runtime
# and reaches no model host; semantic search is a dev-side precompile step whose
# laundered output ships with the documentation.

# Convenience aggregate: every capability-gated integration at once. The corpus
# companions need no entry here because every command-bearing install requires
# them through the base dependency closure.
all = [
  "cadrumo[google]",
  "cadrumo[browser]",
  "cadrumo[anthropic]",
  "cadrumo[ofx]",
  "cadrumo[llm]",
  "cadrumo[pdf]",
]

[build-system]
# The build hook compiles a missing source-tree authority before packaging it.
# Keep this closure aligned with the canonical compiler's direct import and
# official-source extraction requirements; normal runtime dependencies remain
# declared separately under project.dependencies.
requires = [
  "hatchling>=1.32.3,<2",
  "beautifulsoup4[lxml]>=4.12,<5",
  "defusedxml>=0.7.1,<1",
  "openpyxl>=3.1.5,<4",
  "pdfplumber>=0.11.9,<1",
  "pydantic>=2.12.5,<3",
  "pydantic-settings>=2.9.1,<3",
  "pypdfium2>=5.7.1,<6",
  "python-dotenv>=1.2.2,<2",
  "python-i18n>=0.3.9,<1",
  "PyYAML>=6.0.3,<7",
  "rtoml>=0.13.0,<1",
  "tzdata>=2026.2",
  "xlrd>=2.0.1,<3",
]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# Deny-by-default. Without an explicit target, hatchling packs every
# non-gitignored path into the sdist — which meant publishing the project's own
# development records and tooling (`.vault/`, `.vaultspec/`, `dev/`)
# inside the product's source distribution. The sdist carries what is needed to
# build the wheel and nothing else; anything absent from this list is not shipped.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
only-include = [
  "src/cadrumo",
  "src/cadrumo_harness",
  # The build hook that admits the published authority. It must travel in the
  # sdist: a wheel built from the sdist runs the same hook, and without the
  # hook module that rebuild would produce an authority-less wheel.
  "packaging/authority/hatch_build.py",
  "pyproject.toml",
  "README.md",
  "CHANGELOG.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "NOTICE",
  "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md",
  "SECURITY.md",
  "PRIVACY.md",
]
exclude = [
  ".vault",
  ".vault/**",
  ".vaultspec",
  ".vaultspec/**",
  "dev",
  "dev/**",
  # Publication lock sidecars and in-flight candidate staging are publication
  # machinery, never distributable content. Excluded explicitly rather than
  # left to the repository's ignore rules, so an unrelated ignore edit cannot
  # silently change what ships.
  "**/*.lock",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/authority/authority-candidate-*",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/authority/authority-candidate-*/**",
  "src/cadrumo/tests",
  "src/cadrumo/tests/**",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/tests",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/tests/**",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/**/tests",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/**/tests/**",
  "src/cadrumo/**/tests",
  "src/cadrumo/**/tests/**",
  # Pytest configuration is development-only, including package-root
  # conftests that sit outside the excluded test directories.
  "src/cadrumo/conftest.py",
  "src/cadrumo/**/conftest.py",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/conftest.py",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/**/conftest.py",
  # Registry TOML, source manifests, and cached compiler receipts are
  # development authoring inputs.  A released product consumes exactly one
  # published authority artifact, so no authored registry tree may reach an
  # sdist from which a downstream wheel could accidentally restore a compiler
  # fallback.
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/aeat",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/aeat/**",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.pdf",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.docx",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.xls",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.xlsm",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.xlsx",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.zip",
  # The registry verdict cache is written by a validating load, not by the
  # repository. Capturing it makes the build depend on whether local tooling
  # has run: a tree that has validated yields a distribution two files larger
  # than a clean checkout does, and the digests then disagree with the ones a
  # release actually promoted.
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/aeat-registry-identity.json",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/aeat-validation-verdict.json",
  # Runtime authoring inputs are development-only.  The profile schema is a
  # captured compiler input and is represented in the SQLite component store,
  # not shipped as a second loader-readable TOML source.
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/cadrumo",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/cadrumo/**",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/cadrumo", "src/cadrumo_harness"]
# Test modules and fixtures serve no installed consumer: the suites run from
# the repo tree, and nothing in the wheel imports `cadrumo.tests` at module load.
# This payload is shed from the distribution to bound its size.
exclude = [
  "src/cadrumo/tests",
  "src/cadrumo/tests/**",
  "src/cadrumo/**/tests",
  "src/cadrumo/**/tests/**",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/tests",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/tests/**",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/**/tests",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/**/tests/**",
  # Pytest configuration is development-only, including package-root
  # conftests that sit outside the excluded test directories.
  "src/cadrumo/conftest.py",
  "src/cadrumo/**/conftest.py",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/conftest.py",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/**/conftest.py",
  # The immutable published authority is the only registry payload a product
  # process may consume.  Its evidence projection is digest-verified inside the
  # same frame, so it needs no parallel corpus-quality or registry-source
  # payload in the wheel.
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/aeat",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/aeat/**",
  # The registry verdict cache is written by a validating load, not by the
  # repository, so capturing it makes the build depend on whether local tooling
  # has run. A tree that has validated otherwise yields a wheel two files
  # larger than a clean checkout does, whose digest then disagrees with the one
  # a release promoted -- which is exactly what an acquisition proof compares.
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/aeat-registry-identity.json",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/aeat-validation-verdict.json",
  # Captured profile declarations are authoring inputs, never installed
  # runtime resources.
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/cadrumo",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/cadrumo/**",
  # Publication lock sidecars and in-flight candidate staging are publication
  # machinery, never distributable content. Excluded explicitly rather than
  # left to the repository's ignore rules: those exist to keep bytes out of
  # history, and treating them as a packaging boundary means an unrelated
  # ignore edit silently changes what ships.
  "**/*.lock",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/authority/authority-candidate-*",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/registry/authority/authority-candidate-*/**",
  # Corpus source binaries (the AEAT/BOE manuals and workbooks) are 94% of the
  # wheel's compressed weight and serve only the always-on registry integrity
  # hash chain at runtime.
  # They ship in the three manuals, official, and normatives data companion
  # distributions (installed as mandatory base dependencies)
  # under a mirrored `cadrumo_data/_data/corpus` tree; the corpus locator resolves
  # either root. Every derived surface the
  # grounding search and legal gates read at runtime — extracted text
  # (`*.extracted.md`/`.json`), normative html, registry, terminology, and the
  # manual-PDF corpus text sidecars (`_data/manual_corpus_text/`, ~7.4 MB
  # compressed, generated by dev/corpus/extract_manual_corpus_text.py) — stays
  # in this wheel. Excluding only the source binaries keeps the slim `cadrumo`
  # wheel under PyPI's 100 MB cap with no file-size grant on the critical path.
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.pdf",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.docx",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.xls",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.xlsm",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.xlsx",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/corpus/**/*.zip",
]
# `py.typed` marks the package PEP 561 typed so consumers read the inline
# types; `external_constants.toml` carries the curated leaf constants.
include = [
  "src/cadrumo/py.typed",
  "src/cadrumo/core/external_constants.toml",
  "src/cadrumo/_data/local_runtime/**",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/py.typed",
  "src/cadrumo_harness/_data/**",
]

# The published authority — the `authority.current.json` descriptor and the one
# content-addressed SQLite database it names — is generated output that is also
# shipped runtime input, so it lives in a gitignored `.authority/` at the
# repository root rather than in the package source tree. A static `include` or
# `only-include` pattern cannot admit it: those patterns narrow the builder's
# file selection, and the selection never offers a path the repository's ignore
# rules exclude, so naming `.authority/` there yields an archive with no
# authority member and no error. `force_include` is the only selection-independent
# admission path, and a static force-include table cannot serve both layouts at
# once — in an sdist the pair already sits at the published path, and a table
# naming `.authority/` fails the sdist-to-wheel rebuild outright. Hence a hook
# on both targets. It selects exactly the descriptor and the database it names,
# never the directory, which always also holds the retained publication lock
# sidecar and may hold a superseded database whose retirement was deferred.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.hooks.custom]
path = "packaging/authority/hatch_build.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist.hooks.custom]
path = "packaging/authority/hatch_build.py"

# ── uv ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `cadrumo-data-manuals` (packaging/cadrumo_data_manuals/) and `cadrumo-data-official`
# (packaging/cadrumo_data_official/), plus `cadrumo-data-normatives`
# (packaging/cadrumo_data_normatives/), own NO source. Each is a project file plus a
# hatchling build hook that force-includes a disjoint slice of the ONE corpus tree at
# `src/cadrumo/_data/corpus` under a mirrored `cadrumo_data` namespace. They author
# nothing and only repackage the base product's mandatory corpus payload.
[tool.uv.sources]
# The three data companions are not yet on PyPI, so the development resolver builds
# each from its in-repo project. These source overrides never reach published wheel
# metadata, whose mandatory dependencies resolve the exact-version companion
# distributions from the configured package index.
cadrumo-data-manuals = { path = "packaging/cadrumo_data_manuals" }
cadrumo-data-official = { path = "packaging/cadrumo_data_official" }
cadrumo-data-normatives = { path = "packaging/cadrumo_data_normatives" }

[dependency-groups]
registry = [
  # Registry load-census tooling imports grimp directly for the executed import graph.
  "grimp>=3.15,<4",
  # Registry authoring preserves TOML comments and formatting through tomlkit directly.
  "tomlkit>=0.15,<1",
  # The indexed-authority benchmark measures process RSS directly.
  "psutil>=5.9",
  # libxml2 binding. Registry tooling imports `lxml.etree` directly to compile
  # the bundled AEAT record-design XSDs as validation oracles; declaring it makes
  # that reliance explicit rather than leaning on the transitive supply.
  #
  # This entry covers the XSD-compilation use ONLY. Nothing in src/cadrumo/
  # compiles a schema -- but that does not put lxml outside the runtime set:
  # production needs lxml as BeautifulSoup's parser BACKEND, declared as the
  # `beautifulsoup4[lxml]` extra. Two independent reliances, two declarations.
  "lxml>=6.0",
]
dev = [
  { include-group = "registry" },
  # Type-check and directly exercise the repository's three Hatch build hooks.
  "hatchling>=1.32.3,<2",
  # Alembic CLI for source-controlled schema migrations; development tooling only.
  "alembic>=1.16,<2",
  # Dependency declaration drift: missing, unused, transitive, and misplaced deps.
  "deptry>=0.25.1",
  # Import-linter for layered-architecture boundary enforcement.
  # Contract definition lives in `.importlinter` at repo root; activated by
  # the architecture boundary checks.
  "import-linter>=2.15",
  # Formatting-preserving syntax engine for the repository-owned, manifest-
  # bounded object-name rename transforms. Development tooling only.
  "libcst>=1.9.0",
  # Reads the repository's own .gitignore rules so development tooling can
  # enumerate the source tree in-process. Git is not a declared dependency, so
  # no dev tool may shell out to it to learn which files exist.
  "pathspec>=1.1,<2",
  # The capability-gated optional integrations (now in
  # [project.optional-dependencies]) are pulled into the dev/test/CI
  # environment here so the full test suite — which imports every adapter —
  # installs unchanged. Production `pip install cadrumo` stays lean without them.
  "google-auth>=2.50.0,<3",
  "google-auth-oauthlib>=1.3.1,<2",
  "google-api-python-client>=2.195.0,<3",
  "playwright>=1.58.0",
  "playwright-stealth>=2.0.3,<3",
  "anthropic>=0.74.1,<1",
  "ofxtools>=1.1,<2",
  # The `llm` extra's exclusive requirement, and therefore the module the
  # extra's probe resolves against. Without it here the probe reads ABSENT in
  # the dev environment, every `require_optional_extra(LLM_EXTRA)` guard fires,
  # and the inference test suite refuses instead of running. A pure-Python
  # `py3-none-any` wheel: importable with no NVIDIA driver and no accelerator.
  "nvidia-ml-py>=13,<14",
  "prek>=0.5.3",
  "pytest>=9.0.3",
  "pytest-asyncio>=1.0.0",
  # Coverage measurement + fail-under gate for unit tests.
  "pytest-cov>=6.0.0",
  # Live browser harness.
  "pytest-playwright>=0.6.0",
  # Parallel unit suite via opt-in `uv run pytest -n auto -m unit`.
  "pytest-xdist>=3.6.0",
  # Reproducible light-theme CLI GIFs for the repository README.
  "pillow==12.3.0",
  # Generates synthetic fixture PDFs in tests, and is the `pdf` extra's
  # exclusive requirement: without it here the extra's probe reads ABSENT in
  # the dev environment and the calculation-summary suite refuses instead of
  # rendering.
  "reportlab>=4.4.10",
  # Stubs for the registry group's `lxml`. `lxml.etree` is a C extension
  # shipping no inline types, so it is the tree's only unresolved-import under
  # `ty`; the stubs are dev-only because production never imports lxml, it
  # names the backend as a string.
  "types-lxml>=2025.3.30",
  "ruff>=0.16.7",
  # Repository-wide YAML syntax/style linting; TOML parsing goes through the rtoml-backed `cadrumo.core.toml` boundary.
  "yamllint>=1.38,<2",
  "ty>=0.0.81",
  # Vault tooling — contributor-only; not imported by src/cadrumo/ and never
  # shipped in a published product wheel.
  # 0.1.55 is the first version that understands the `body_hash` frontmatter
  # fingerprint; older versions drop unknown frontmatter keys on rewrite, so a
  # mixed-version corpus silently loses the stamp on exactly the documents
  # being edited (nevenincs/vaultspec-core#299). Operator directive: the
  # tooling tracks latest.
  "vaultspec-core>=0.1.55",
  "vaultspec-rag[mcp]>=0.3.8",
  # Sphinx documentation pipeline — `just docs-build` builds HTML + Markdown from
  # the Google-style + Sphinx-cross-referenced docstrings under src/cadrumo/.
  "sphinx>=8.1,<9",  # <9: sphinx-hoverxref 1.4.2 (latest) crashes on Sphinx 9's _Opt config repr at config-inited
  "sphinx-autodoc-typehints>=2.5",
  "sphinx-markdown-builder>=0.6",
  "furo>=2024.8",
  "myst-parser>=4.0",
  "sphinx-copybutton>=0.5.2",
  "sphinx-design>=0.6",
  "sphinx-notfound-page>=1.1",
  "sphinxext-opengraph>=0.9",
  # Hover tooltip cards on :term: cross-references. With hoverxref_roles=["term"],
  # every :term: reference to a generated glossary entry shows the definition on
  # hover - the curated short description surfaces without a page load. The
  # generated glossary's :term: anchors are the load-bearing part; this is the
  # presentation enhancement over them.
  "sphinx-hoverxref>=1.4",
  # Precompiled docs search backend (MIT). `pagefind` is the pure-Python API
  # wrapper; the `extended` extra pins `pagefind-bin-extended`, whose wheel
  # BUNDLES the platform Rust binary WITH the es/ca/hu/en Snowball stemmers
  # (the standard `bin` extra omits the non-English stemmers). Vendoring the
  # binary inside the pinned wheel keeps the docs build offline-hermetic: the
  # post-build index pass invokes the bundled binary and makes no network
  # fetch. The compiled index is an uncommitted build artifact, like docs/cli/.
  "pagefind[extended]>=1.5,<2",
  # Live-reloading docs dev server (`just docs-serve`): wraps the Sphinx build
  # with a filesystem watcher and a livereload websocket so edits to docs/ and
  # the src/cadrumo/ docstring surface refresh the browser without a manual rebuild.
  "sphinx-autobuild>=2024.10",
  # Documentation localization (`just docs-generate-catalogs` / `docs-langs`): sphinx-intl
  # manages the per-language `.po` catalogues under docs/locales/ from the
  # gettext POT templates, and babel parses catalogue statistics
  # (translated / fuzzy / untranslated) for the all-languages completeness gate.
  "sphinx-intl>=2.3",
  "babel>=2.16",
  # Documentation conformance enforcement: docstring presence/style,
  # signature-vs-docstring accuracy, and RST formatting.
  "pydoclint>=0.9.1",
  "interrogate>=1.7.0",
  "doc8>=2.0.0",
  "types-defusedxml>=0.7.0.20260504",
  "types-openpyxl>=3.1.5.20260408",
  "types-reportlab>=4.4.10.20260408",
  "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12.20260510",
  "types-xlrd>=2.0.0.20260408",
  "types-pywin32>=311.0.0.20260508",
  "google-api-python-client-stubs>=1.36",
  "pyrefly>=1.3.1",
  # Semgrep is invoked through `uvx --from semgrep==1.168.0 semgrep` instead of the
  # persistent dev group: the Windows Python package install does not expose a
  # working console command, while uvx resolves the supported standalone tool.
  "radon>=6.0.1",
  "complexipy>=8.0.1",
  "vulture>=2.16",
  "sphinxcontrib-mermaid>=1.0",
  "pytest-timeout>=2.3.1",
  "basedpyright>=1.40.1",
  "spylls==0.1.7",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 120
src = ["src"]
extend-exclude = [
  # Ruff 0.16 formats Python blocks embedded in Markdown. The `.vault/` corpus,
  # the `.vaultspec/` harness and `.agents/` handovers are removable
  # development scaffolding external to the codebase: their code blocks are
  # historical records of what a decision looked like when it was taken, and
  # reformatting them rewrites the record and is barred by the vaultspec
  # hand-edit rules. The harness owns its own gates and their style; linting
  # them with the product's rules judges one tree by another's standard.
  # Narrative docs under `docs/` stay in scope.
  ".vault",
  ".vaultspec",
  ".agents",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E",  # pycodestyle errors
  "W",  # pycodestyle warnings
  "F",  # pyflakes
  "I",  # isort
  "N",  # pep8-naming
  "UP",  # pyupgrade
  "B",  # flake8-bugbear
  "S",  # flake8-bandit (security)
  "T20",  # flake8-print
  "SIM",  # flake8-simplify
  "TID251",  # flake8-tidy-imports banned-api; enforces the table below
  "RUF",  # ruff-specific rules
  "D",  # pydocstyle (Google-style docstring conventions)
]
ignore = [
  # `Translatable as tr` is the canonical i18n alias across the codebase (45 of
  # the 47 N813 sites). The alias is the readable call form at every message
  # site; renaming it would churn the entire localized surface for no gain.
  "N813",
  # Mutable class defaults on pydantic models are safe: pydantic deep-copies

# RUF001/2/3 stay ARMED. A previous project-wide ignore justified itself on
# Spanish source fidelity -- accented glyphs and inverted punctuation from
# quoted BOE/AEAT text. That premise does not hold: ruff does not treat
# `a e i o u n` or the inverted marks as confusable, and zero of the ~298
# findings were Spanish letters. What the rule actually catches here is
# deliberate typography (below) plus the genuinely dangerous class it exists
# for -- fullwidth digits and Latin letters, which this project MUST keep
# detectable because it parses AEAT numerics.
#
# These five are prose typography the project uses on purpose in docstrings,
# comments, and rendered strings. Naming them individually keeps the fullwidth
# and no-break-space detections live.

  "×",  # MULTIPLICATION SIGN -- dimension/product notation in docstrings
  "−",  # MINUS SIGN -- signed monetary examples
  "–",  # EN DASH -- ranges and parenthetical prose
  "‘",  # LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK -- quoted prose
  "’",  # RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK -- apostrophes in prose
  "›",  # SINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK -- breadcrumb separator
  "∪",  # UNION -- set notation in explanatory comments

# ── Audience scoping ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# These entries scope a rule OUT OF A SURFACE IT WAS NEVER WRITTEN FOR. They
# are not deferred debt and carry no backlog: on the surfaces below the rule
# reports a property that is correct by design. Each is measured, not assumed.
#
# S101 (assert): pytest's entire assertion model IS the bare `assert`. 73,929 of
# the 74,220 S101 sites are test modules. Scoping to the test surface rather
# than ignoring project-wide is deliberate and STRENGTHENS the gate: it leaves
# S101 armed over production, where 262 real asserts remain visible as a
# genuine backlog (an assert standing in for a load-bearing runtime invariant
