"mock".msg = "Third-party 'mock' is banned for the same reason as unittest.mock. See src/cadrumo/tests/README.md."

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"

# ── ty ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.13"
# Pinned, not inherited. An unset target platform makes every checker assume the
# HOST, so the same tree reports zero diagnostics on Windows and 49 on Linux and
# macOS -- the gate's verdict becomes a function of the runner, the same defect
# class as the `pyrightconfig.json` that used to win discovery and the phantom
# `reportMissingImports` cascade `--pythonpath` closes. `linux` is the baseline
# because it is what the CI fleet runs; `dev/quality/types.py` overrides this
# per run and sweeps EVERY supported platform, so a Windows-only branch is
# still checked rather than traded away for determinism.
python-platform = "linux"
extra-paths = ["stubs"]

[tool.ty.rules]
all = "error"

[tool.ty.analysis]
# Hand-written stubs under `stubs/` cover packages without `py.typed` and
# without `types-*` distributions on PyPI: `pypdfium2`, `playwright_stealth`,
# and `snowballstemmer`. Other previously-listed unresolved imports (playwright,
# typer, rich, bs4) now ship `py.typed` themselves, and
# `google-api-python-client-stubs` (a dev dep) covers the googleapiclient
# surface. The empty list is the mandate: every unresolved import is a hard
# failure, so a new one is fixed with a stub, not an allowance.
allowed-unresolved-imports = []

# ── mypy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The project does not run mypy in CI (ty is the canonical checker) but
# external auditors do. Mirror ty's stance so a mypy invocation against
# this project picks up the same stub set.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
platform = "linux"
mypy_path = ["src", "stubs"]
explicit_package_bases = true
namespace_packages = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Only packages that still lack py.typed and have no community stubs.
# playwright, typer, rich, bs4 all ship py.typed; google-api-python-client
# is covered by google-api-python-client-stubs (installed as a dev dep).
module = ["i18n.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ── pyrefly ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The project's SECOND type checker, alongside ty. Two independent
# implementations are deliberate: ty is the canonical checker across all of
# `src` but is still pre-1.0, so a mature second opinion over the strict
# domain + application subset catches what a young checker misses. pyrefly is
# a native binary, so unlike the pyright it replaces it drags in no JavaScript
# runtime — the packaging lanes need nothing installed to run it.
#
# `search_path` also declares the stub policy, the same rationale as
# `[tool.mypy]`: resolve `pypdfium2` and `playwright_stealth` against `stubs/`
# rather than reporting them as unresolved imports.
#
# The checked subset lives HERE rather than in the harness's argv, because
# `project_excludes` filters `project_includes` but does NOT filter paths
# passed explicitly on the command line. A harness that named the two
# directions would silently re-admit everything this excludes.
[tool.pyrefly]
python_version = "3.13"
# Same pin, same reason as `[tool.ty.environment]`: the target platform is a
# declared input, never the host it happens to run on.
python_platform = "linux"
search_path = ["src", ".", "stubs"]
project_includes = ["src/cadrumo/domain", "src/cadrumo/application", "src/cadrumo/core", "src/cadrumo/adapters/outbound/llm"]
# Tests are excluded from this checker, not overlooked. pyright reported zero
# diagnostics across the test tree, so excluding it loses no signal that was
# previously enforced, while pyrefly's stricter inference finds ~24 fixture
# typing issues there that would have to be triaged before the checker could
# gate anything. Production code in the same subset IS checked, and that is
# where the swap immediately paid for itself.
project_excludes = ["**/.[!/.]*", "**/tests/**"]

# ── basedpyright ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A third, independent strict checker over the same production boundary as
# pyrefly. Tests stay outside this gate; ty remains the all-``src`` authority.
[tool.basedpyright]
# ``core`` joined this gate once it reached zero. The sequence is deliberate and
# is the only honest one available: burn a tree down, THEN admit it permanently.
# aeat-quality-gates bans baselines and ratchets, so a tree is never admitted
# with errors outstanding and never carries a per-tree exemption.
include = ["src/cadrumo/domain", "src/cadrumo/application", "src/cadrumo/core", "src/cadrumo/adapters/outbound/llm"]
exclude = ["**/tests"]
extraPaths = ["src", "stubs"]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
# Same pin, same reason as `[tool.ty.environment]`.
pythonPlatform = "Linux"
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
# A suppression that no longer suppresses anything is indistinguishable from one
# that does, and it silently widens as the code under it changes. Reporting the
# dead ones keeps this checker adversarial about its own escape hatches rather
# than trusting them. Note `# type: ignore` IS honoured here even though ty
# matches only its own rule names, so a mypy-shaped comment can hide a
# diagnostic from this checker while looking inert.
reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment = "error"
# A rule this project does not hold, in the same sense as Ruff's TID252 above:
# its premise -- that an annotation is enforced at run time -- is false in
# Python, while `no-silent-under-declaration` and
# `sensitive-financial-data-secure-storage-only` REQUIRE validation at exactly
# the boundaries it flags. All 42 sites were audited individually before this
# was set: 10 were genuinely dead and were REMOVED in code (a py.typed
# dependency or the language grammar already guaranteed the type, or earlier
# control flow did), and 2 were dispatch over a closed union, rewritten as
# `match` + `assert_never`. The 27 that remain guard something Python does not
# enforce: `__post_init__` checks on plain dataclasses, SQLAlchemy
# `process_bind_param` values, an untyped third-party return, a network
# response body, and the public redaction entry points. Satisfying the rule at
# those sites would mean widening an annotation to `object` -- deleting a
# static check to quiet a checker, which is the opposite of the intent.
reportUnnecessaryIsInstance = "none"

# ── Pytest ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = [
  "src/cadrumo",
  "src/cadrumo_harness",
]
pythonpath = ["src"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
# `-ra` replaces the per-lane `-rsf`: pytest's default `-r` value is `fE`, so
# a bare `-rs` REPLACES it and the short-summary `FAILED path::test` lines
# disappear - the triage path this repository documents greps the log for
# `^FAILED`. `a` reports every non-passing outcome, so nothing has to be
# re-added flag by flag, and the reporting decision stops being restated on
# every lane.
#
# `--strict-config` joins `--strict-markers`: an ini key no installed plugin
# owns is otherwise ignored in silence, exactly as an unregistered marker used
# to select nothing and exit 5.
#
# `--capture=sys` avoids pytest's fd-level dup2 capture, which dies silently
# under Git Bash / MinTTY on this project's primary platform.
# Plain assertions preserve failures without rendering expensive comparison diffs.
addopts = "-n auto --dist=loadfile -ra --tb=short --durations=10 -m 'unit and not perf and not external_tool and not os_keychain and not windows_only and not resident_service and not private_ingest_corpus' --strict-markers --strict-config --capture=sys --max-worker-restart=0 --assert=plain"
# Correctness tests run to completion independently of host speed. Callers
# can explicitly request a pytest-timeout deadline when investigating a hang.
# `--max-worker-restart=0` keeps a crashed worker terminal and visible rather
# than silently retrying its test.
# Drop a test's `tmp_path` as soon as that test PASSES; keep it when it fails.
# Measured on this box: `pytest-of-hello` reached 39.1 GB across 101 retained
# session directories, 85% of it a dozen packaging-lane runs at up to 4.4 GB and
# 100k files each -- the real-wheel smoke tests build wheels and pip venvs into
# `tmp_path`, which is inherent to what they verify, not waste to remove.
# `tmp_path_retention_count` does NOT bound this: pytest gates the numbered-dir
# rotation behind `_pytest.pathlib.LOCK_TIMEOUT`, which is 72 HOURS and is a
# module constant with no ini setting, so the retained population is bounded by
# three days of accrual rather than by the count. An isolated A/B on
# `test_three_wheel_cohort_installs_only_aeat_human_script` measured 1200.4 MB
# retained under the default `all` against 0.0 MB under `failed`.
# Failing tests keep their directories, which is where triage actually looks;
# module- and session-scoped `tmp_path_factory.mktemp` directories are NOT
# covered by this and still clear only at a green session's end.
tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed"
asyncio_mode = "strict"
markers = [
  "unit: deterministic offline tests scoped to one owner; owned local processes are allowed, external networks and services are not",
  "integration: deterministic in-process tests that cross architectural layers",
  "aeat_live: opt-in tests that read from a real external service; see src/cadrumo/tests/README.md",
  "hex_domain: exercises domain.* business model and computation",
  "hex_application: exercises application.* use-cases and orchestration",
  "hex_inbound_adapter: exercises adapters.inbound.* boundaries",
  "hex_outbound_adapter: exercises adapters.outbound.* boundaries",
  "hex_persistence_adapter: exercises adapters.persistence.* boundaries",
  "hex_entrypoint: exercises entrypoints.* command and presentation surfaces",
  "hex_core: exercises core.* foundational cross-cutting utilities",
  "docs: documentation build, stubs, and docstring structure verification",
  "serial: isolation-sensitive tests that must run without xdist workers (-n0); they mutate or read process-global state (e.g. the active master-key-provider singleton) and flake under -n auto worker interleaving. Run via the serial pass of `just test-integration`.",
  "perf: performance acceptance gates (CPU-time asserts, wall-clock advisory); excluded from every per-push lane and enrolled explicitly in the `test-ci-perf` recipe, which only a dispatch-triggered release run reaches, so a quiet machine makes the advisory wall numbers meaningful too. Named by selection rather than by workflow file: the workflow set has churned once already, and the previous wording here outlived the lane it named.",
  "external_tool: tests requiring heavy external tooling or data the dependency set does not install (LibreOffice, for binary .xls conversion and formula recalculation; the npm-installed Hunspell dictionaries, for locale orthography; a real PowerShell, which a POSIX host has only if `pwsh` was installed; a stock OpenSSL, for the calculation summary signature recipe). Carried ALONGSIDE an execution marker, since the marker-integrity contract requires exactly one of {unit, integration, aeat_live}; the default lane selects `unit and not external_tool`, so this marker -- not the path --ignore beside it -- is what holds these tests out. Enrolled explicitly by `just test-workbook-parity`, `just test-locale-spelling`, `just test-powershell-literal` and `just test-calculation-summary-pdf`.",
  "os_keychain: tests whose assertion subject is the OS credential store itself (that a profile login custodies a session key there, and that a later process resumes the record by unwrapping its DEK under that key). Carried ALONGSIDE an execution marker, like `external_tool`. The capability is a property of the LOGON SESSION, not of the dependency set: a headless CI runner and an agent's SSH network logon reach a real backend that then refuses every credential call, so no keychain-custodied session key can exist there at all. Every lane excludes this marker; `just test-os-keychain` enrols it, and it is meaningful only in an interactive desktop session. Cases provable WITHOUT custody stay in the default lanes. A case belongs under this marker when it cannot reach its subject without a minted acceleration receipt, because `resume_profile_session` leaves the login PROCESS-SCOPED when the keychain is unavailable and mints no receipt at all. Apply the marker at the narrowest scope whose assertion actually requires custody.",
  "windows_only: tests whose assertion subject exists only on Windows -- today the two console-launcher stubs (`aeat.exe`, `cadrumo-mcp.exe`) that a Windows install materialises and no POSIX install has at all. Carried ALONGSIDE an execution marker, like `os_keychain`. The precondition is a property of the OPERATING SYSTEM, not of the dependency set: on Linux or macOS there is no stub to project, so the subject of the assertion does not exist and no amount of installed tooling conjures it. Every lane excludes this marker; `just test-windows` enrols it, and it is meaningful only on a Windows checkout. Cases provable WITHOUT a launcher stub stay in the default lanes.",
  "resident_service: tests that query the resident vaultspec-rag search service over HTTP and assert on what it returns (golden-query retrieval, the live terminology sweep). Carried ALONGSIDE an execution marker, like `external_tool` and `os_keychain`. The precondition is a property of a RUNNING LOCAL SERVICE and the health of its index, not of the dependency set. The service is a separate development product rather than a Cadrumo runtime dependency. Every ordinary lane excludes this marker; `just test-resident-service` refreshes the index and enrols the tests serially, while the root conftest supplies their isolated pytest singleton scope. A degraded index remains a test failure rather than a reason to skip.",
  "private_ingest_corpus: tests that score the ingestion harness against the read-only ingestion measurement corpus, operator data held outside the checkout and located only through `CADRUMO_INGEST_CORPUS_ROOT`, which has no default path. Carried ALONGSIDE an execution marker, like `os_keychain`. The precondition is a property of the HOST'S DATA, not of the dependency set: nothing installs the corpus and no CI runner holds it. Every lane excludes this marker; `just test-ingest-corpus` enrols it, and its tests FAIL rather than skip when the variable is unset, names no corpus, or the corpus key is not the pinned one. Apply the marker at the narrowest scope that reads the corpus; cases provable without it stay in the default lanes.",
]

# ── Coverage (pytest-cov) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/cadrumo"]
branch = true
omit = [
  "*/test_*.py",
  "src/cadrumo/tests/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
# Starting floor. Ratchet upward after real measurement, and never lower
# without a documented architectural update.
fail_under = 60
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false

# ── doc8 (reStructuredText style for hand-authored docs) ─────────────────────
# Scope doc8 to hand-written documentation. The gitignored build output and the
# machine-generated API / CLI stub trees (long dotted module paths in headings)
# are excluded so `just docs-check` stays green in any working tree, including
# one that has already built the docs.
[tool.doc8]
ignore-path = [
  "docs/_build",
  "docs/_generated",
  "docs/_inventories",
  "docs/api",
  "docs/cli",
  # Vendored font and its licence, reproduced verbatim rather than authored.
  "docs/_static/readme/fonts",
]
max-line-length = 100

# ── Interrogate (docstring coverage) ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Without configuration interrogate counts every public symbol missing a
# Google-style docstring as a finding, and most of those are private helpers,
# magic methods, nested closures, and test fixtures that do not carry
# docstrings by convention. Filter those at the config layer so the measured
# surface is the public API that genuinely warrants prose documentation.
[tool.interrogate]
ignore-init-method = true
ignore-init-module = true
ignore-magic = true
ignore-nested-functions = true
ignore-private = true
ignore-semiprivate = true
ignore-property-decorators = true
ignore-module = false
fail-under = 80
exclude = [
  "stubs",
  "src/cadrumo/tests",
  "src/cadrumo/**/tests/test_*.py",
]

# ── pydoclint (docstring-vs-signature accuracy) ──────────────────────────────
# Verifies documented Args/Returns/Raises match the real signature - the
# true-to-reality docstring gate. Configured to the project convention: types
# live in signatures (rendered by autodoc_typehints="description"), so
# docstrings carry no arg type hints; pydantic Field(description=...) covers
# attribute docs, so class-attribute checks are off. Tests are out of scope.
[tool.pydoclint]
style = "google"
arg-type-hints-in-docstring = false
check-return-types = false
check-yield-types = false
check-class-attributes = false
skip-checking-short-docstrings = true
allow-init-docstring = true
exclude = 'tests|test_'

# ── Vulture (dead-code) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Vulture defaults to confidence threshold 60 which surfaces many
# false-positive "unused" guesses (decorators, dynamic dispatch, test
# fixtures, lazily-bound CLI entrypoints). Bump to 80 and exclude tests so
# the dashboard tracks code that is plausibly dead in production paths.
[tool.vulture]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["src/cadrumo"]
exclude = [
  "*/tests/*",
  "*\\tests\\*",
  "*/_data/*",
  "*\\_data\\*",
  "*/test_*.py",
  "*\\test_*.py",
  "*/_test_*.py",
  "*\\_test_*.py",
  "*/conftest.py",
  "*\\conftest.py",
]
ignore_decorators = [
  "@app.command",
  "@cli.command",
  "@click.command",
  "@click.group",
  "@app.callback",
  "@app.result_callback",
  "@pytest.fixture",
  "@field_validator",
  "@model_validator",
  "@field_serializer",
  "@classmethod",
  "@staticmethod",
  "@property",
]
# Textual dispatches message and event handlers by NAME, not by call site:
# posting `LedgerEntrySelected` invokes `on_ledger_entry_selected` through the
# framework's message pump, so the method has no caller any static analysis can
# see. Treating those as dead is not hypothetical here -- a working Ledger
# entry-to-classification path (handler, controller method, production
# submitter, installed wiring and both its tests) was removed in one 130-line
# commit because the convention-dispatched edge was invisible, and the
# resulting gap was then documented as a deliberate design constraint. The
# same shape covers Textual's `on_mount` / `on_key` lifecycle hooks and the
# `action_*` methods bound from key tables.
ignore_names = [
  "on_*",
  "action_*",
  "compose",
  "watch_*",
]

# ── Deptry (unused / transitive dependency lint) ─────────────────────────────
# Suppress the false positives surfaced by deptry's default heuristics. Every
# entry below is verified to actually fire against the configured scan (the
# `check-dependencies` recipe: `src/cadrumo` with the test tree excluded); an
# ignore that no longer suppresses anything is removed rather than carried, so
# this list stays an inventory of live false positives. The remaining
# diagnostics flag genuine drift and stay active.
[tool.deptry.package_module_name_map]
"PyYAML" = ["yaml"]
"pyyaml" = ["yaml"]
# pywin32 ships these modules across its distribution roots; deptry's package
# metadata cannot discover all of them. Keep the direct Windows ACL and COM
# dependencies visible to the declaration check.
"pywin32" = [
  "ntsecuritycon",
  "pythoncom",
  "pywintypes",
  "win32api",
  "win32com",
  "win32con",
  "win32event",
  "win32file",
  "win32job",
  "win32pipe",
  "win32process",
  "win32security",
  "win32ts",
]
# The NVML binding's distribution name and its import name differ, so the
# mapping is stated rather than guessed: deptry's fallback would be
# `nvidia_ml_py`, making the accelerator probe's `import pynvml` read as an
# undeclared dependency (DEP001) while the declaration itself reads as unused
# (DEP002) — one mapping closes both. Verified against the published wheel
# rather than asserted from memory: `nvidia_ml_py-13.610.43-py3-none-any.whl`
# ships a top-level `pynvml.py`.
"nvidia-ml-py" = ["pynvml"]
[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# `cadrumo`: the `all` convenience extra self-references the capability extras
# (`cadrumo[google]` etc.); deptry reads the self-reference as an unused dependency.
# `cadrumo-data-manuals` / `cadrumo-data-official` / `cadrumo-data-normatives`:
# three data-only companion
# distributions with no importable code the scanner can see; the corpus locator
# reaches their shared `cadrumo_data` namespace package dynamically through
# `importlib.resources` (the corpus-binary resolution seam).
# `pillow`: the one dependency here whose declaration is deliberately NOT
# backed by an import statement. The page rasteriser reaches Pillow from inside
# pypdfium2's `to_pil()` and then calls `save()` on the result, so the reliance
# is real while no module under `src/cadrumo/` writes `import PIL` — the exact
# asymmetry that let Pillow arrive as an incidental transitive of pdfplumber and
# pikepdf. Deptry sees only the absent import and reads both declarations (base
# and the `llm` extra) as unused. Suppressed here rather than resolved by
# deleting a declaration: the declaration is the fix, and
# `dev/packaging/tests/test_inference_imports_are_declared.py` asserts it
# directly for this reason.
DEP002 = [
  "cadrumo",
  "cadrumo-data-manuals",
  "cadrumo-data-official",
  "cadrumo-data-normatives",
  "pillow",
  "python-dotenv",
  # Typer imports Rich for runtime help/error rendering. The application
  # intentionally reaches it through Typer's public rich_utils boundary rather
  # than importing Rich directly, while the base declaration keeps that
  # runtime reliance independent of Typer's transitive metadata.
  "rich",
  "tzdata",
]
# `pydantic_core` is re-exported by pydantic — a legitimate transitive use.
DEP003 = ["pydantic_core"]
# Package-level `conftest.py` modules sit outside the excluded test tree, so the
# dev-only pytest import they carry reads as misplaced.
DEP004 = ["pytest"]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "ghdag"
version = "0.104.3"
description = "Generic DAG execution engine extracted from graph-watcher"
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = ["watchdog>=4.0.0", "pyyaml>=6.0"]
classifiers = [
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
  "pytest>=7.0.0",
  "pytest-cov>=4.0.0",
  "mypy>=1.10.0",
  "ruff>=0.4.0",
  "import-linter>=2.0",
  "types-PyYAML>=6.0",
]

[project.scripts]
ghdag = "ghdag.cli:main"

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/sumipan/ghdag"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"ghdag.ui" = ["static/*"]
"ghdag" = ["py.typed"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]

[tool.mypy]
strict = false
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
packages = ["ghdag"]
mypy_path = "src"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 120
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "W"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"src/ghdag/cli/**" = ["E501"]
"src/ghdag/dag/engine.py" = ["F841", "E501"]
"src/ghdag/dag/hooks.py" = ["E501"]
"src/ghdag/dag/parser.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/**" = ["E501"]
"tests/pipeline/test_audit_hooks.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/test_ghdag_parser.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/test_pipeline_status.py" = ["F401", "E402"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["ghdag"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Infrastructure must not import orchestration"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "ghdag.files",
  "ghdag.llm",
  "ghdag.metrics",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "ghdag.pipeline",
  "ghdag.workflow",
  "ghdag.ui",
  "ghdag.cli",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core は ghdag の他パッケージに依存しない"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ghdag.core"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "ghdag.io",
  "ghdag.files",
  "ghdag.llm",
  "ghdag.metrics",
  "ghdag.github_client",
  "ghdag.github_cli",
  "ghdag.dag",
  "ghdag.pipeline",
  "ghdag.workflow",
  "ghdag.cli",
  "ghdag.ui",
  "ghdag.cleanup",
  "ghdag.maintenance",
  "ghdag.tool",
  "ghdag.markdown",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "投入塔は実行塔を import しない（通信は exec.jsonl / done のみ）"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ghdag.pipeline", "ghdag.workflow"]
forbidden_modules = ["ghdag.dag"]
ignore_imports = [
  # AuditHooks extends dag.DefaultHooks — implementation must live in the dag layer.
  # pipeline.hooks is a re-export shim for public API backward-compat (pipeline.__init__).
  # Resolving this requires moving DefaultHooks to core — deferred to a separate issue.
  "ghdag.pipeline.hooks -> ghdag.dag.audit_hooks",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "実行塔は投入塔を import しない"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ghdag.dag"]
forbidden_modules = ["ghdag.pipeline", "ghdag.workflow"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "io / effects は塔と入口を知らない"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "ghdag.io",
  "ghdag.files",
  "ghdag.llm",
  "ghdag.metrics",
  "ghdag.github_client",
  "ghdag.vcs",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "ghdag.dag",
  "ghdag.pipeline",
  "ghdag.workflow",
  "ghdag.cli",
  "ghdag.ui",

/**
 * Enforces the import layering for @syncro/shared (issue #1307).
 *
 * Layers, and the only direction imports may flow:
 *
 *   types/  ->  logic/  ->  platform/
 *
 * A module may import from its own layer or any layer to its left. It
 * must never import from a layer to its right, and no cycle is allowed
 * anywhere in the graph. Run with `npm run check-imports` (see
 * package.json); wired into CI in .github/workflows/lint.yml.
 */
module.exports = {
  forbidden: [
    {
      name: 'no-circular',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        'Circular imports through the barrel are exactly what issue #1307 removes. ' +
        'If this fires, break the cycle by moving the shared piece down a layer ' +
        '(or into its own module) instead of importing back up.',
      from: {},
      to: { circular: true },
    },
    {
      name: 'types-layer-is-pure',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        'types/ is the pure-data layer: it must not depend on logic/ or platform/. ' +
        'If a type needs a helper function, the function belongs in logic/, and the ' +
        'type stays a type.',
      from: { path: '^src/types' },
      to: { path: '^src/(logic|platform)' },
    },
    {
      name: 'logic-does-not-import-platform',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        'logic/ must stay pure (deterministic, no I/O, no third-party SDK wiring). ' +
        'platform/ (the RPC client, Sentry config) depends on logic/ and types/, never ' +
        'the reverse — otherwise importing a pure helper drags in Sentry/RPC again, ' +
        'which is the exact bug this issue exists to fix.',
      from: { path: '^src/logic' },
      to: { path: '^src/platform' },
    },
    {
      name: 'root-barrel-is-types-only',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        'index.ts (the "@syncro/shared" barrel) may re-export only from types/. ' +
        'Anything from logic/ or platform/ must be imported via its own subpath ' +
        '(e.g. "@syncro/shared/crypto", "@syncro/shared/sentry") so that importing a ' +
        'type never pulls in Sentry or the RPC client.',
      from: { path: '^src/index\\.ts$' },
      to: { path: '^src/(logic|platform)' },
    },
  ],
  options: {
    tsPreCompilationDeps: true,
    tsConfig: { fileName: 'tsconfig.json' },
    doNotFollow: { path: 'node_modules' },
    exclude: { path: '__tests__' },
  },
};

# Architectural boundary enforcement (run: `lint-imports`).
#
# The codebase is organised in three trust rings (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md):
#
#   Ring 0  kernel    — the trusted computing base: the gate logic and the data
#                       it reasons over. A bug here can cause a wrong ALLOW.
#   Ring 1  runtime   — wires the kernel to an executor (capability boundary,
#                       node/worker orchestration, opt-in federation).
#   Ring 2  platform  — quality/cost/observability (budget, context, trace,
#                       extensions). A bug here wastes resources, not safety.
#
# The one guarantee that matters: the kernel must not depend on the runtime or
# the platform. A platform bug therefore cannot reach the decision. (Runtime is
# allowed to use the platform — node legitimately orchestrates budget/context/
# trace — so that edge is not forbidden; only the kernel boundary is.)

[importlinter]
root_package = axor_core

[importlinter:contract:kernel-purity]
name = Kernel (Ring 0) must not import runtime (Ring 1) or platform (Ring 2)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    axor_core.contracts
    axor_core.errors
    axor_core.taint
    axor_core.security
    axor_core.policy
    axor_core.kernel
    axor_core.degradation
    axor_core.governor
forbidden_modules =
    axor_core.capability
    axor_core.node
    axor_core.worker
    axor_core.federation
    axor_core.budget
    axor_core.context
    axor_core.trace
    axor_core.extensions

# T0 (producing process non-interpreting) — see docs/kernel-theorem.md §3.
#
# The functions that PRODUCE a trusted-path projection must be deterministic and
# structural, never a model reading the governed content (a steerable projector
# can emit a valid-but-unfaithful projection). This contract pins the structural
# half: a projection producer must not import the advisory/model layer
# (kernel.adjudicator — the only model-consumer surface in core). The external
# half (no provider SDK / network / subprocess in a producer) is pinned by
# tests/invariants/test_t0_producers_non_interpreting.py, because import-linter
# graphs only the root package by default. The adjudicator is a *consumer* of the
# projection (advisory, projection-only, tightening-only) and may itself be a
# model — T0 constrains the producer, not the consumer, which is why the rule is
# scoped to these producer modules, not to the whole kernel. The taint ledger and
# causal_root produce the provenance-label projection the taint gate reads
# (``driving_root``), and the trusted-origin index decides whether a value escapes
# the context root (context-default integrity), so they are producers too.
[importlinter:contract:t0-producers-non-interpreting]
name = T0 — projection producers must not import the advisory/model surface
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    axor_core.security.carrier
    axor_core.policy.consequence
    axor_core.policy.normalizer
    axor_core.node.canonicalizer
    axor_core.taint.ledger
    axor_core.taint.causal_root
    axor_core.taint.trusted
forbidden_modules =
    axor_core.kernel.adjudicator

# Authority/plan separation (RFC: task classification must not determine
# authority). Enforcement surfaces decide on AuthorityPolicy and structural
# facts only — an ExecutionPlan import there would be a channel through which
# an untrusted task classification could reach an allow/deny decision.
# (Extend source_modules with axor_core.planning when that package lands.)
[importlinter:contract:authority-plan-separation]
name = Enforcement surfaces must not import execution planning
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    axor_core.capability
    axor_core.security
    axor_core.governor
    axor_core.kernel
    axor_core.taint
    axor_core.degradation
forbidden_modules =
    axor_core.contracts.planning

# The reverse direction: the planning layer must not be able to construct
# authority. A planner that could import AuthorityPolicy could smuggle a
# classifier-derived authority object into the session wiring.
[importlinter:contract:planning-non-authoritative]
name = Planning layer must not import authority constructors
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    axor_core.contracts.planning
forbidden_modules =
    axor_core.contracts.authority

    @ArchTest

        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer("shared").definedBy(SHARED_PACKAGE)
            .layer("command").definedBy(COMMAND_PACKAGE)
            .layer("query").definedBy(QUERY_PACKAGE)
            .whereLayer("shared").mayNotAccessAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("command").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("query")
            .whereLayer("query").mayOnlyAccessLayers("shared", "command")
            .ignoreDependency(
                DescribedPredicate.alwaysTrue(),
                JavaClass.Predicates.resideOutsideOfPackages("$BASE_PACKAGE..")
            )
}

/**
 * ZX84 architecture boundary rules (dependency-cruiser).
 *
 * See docs/re-architecture.md §3.1 (import table) and §7 (enforcement).
 *
 * Phase 1 of the migration has relocated the code into the target layered
 * layout, so these rules now run against the real folders:
 *
 *   - src/cores/       commodity silicon; imports only cores + media types + utils.
 *   - src/media/       format/codec code; imports only media + utils (pure data).
 *   - src/machines/<name>/  one machine per folder; an island that may reach its
 *                      own folder, the shared machine substrate
 *                      (machine.ts / base-machine.ts / registry / shared),
 *                      cores, media, debug substrate (src/debug) and utils — but
 *                      never another machine folder, and never UI / reactive
 *                      state / settings store.
 *   - src/debug/       machine-agnostic debug tools + CPU-family debug substrate
 *                      (src/debug/<family>/); imports cores, utils, and the
 *                      machine SPI *types* only.
 *
 * All four rules currently pass with ZERO exceptions — the Phase 0 baseline
 * backlog (cores/ula.ts → keyboard.ts, cores/gate-array.ts → cpc/constants.ts)
 * was cleared by moving that custom silicon into its machine folder.
 *
 * Note: a `ui-no-concrete-machines` rule (§7) is intentionally NOT enforced yet
 * — UI panes still import concrete machines until Phase 6. It is added when the
 * shell/service seams land.
 */

module.exports = {
  forbidden: [
    {
      name: 'cores-know-nothing',
      comment:
        'src/cores/** models commodity silicon: it may import only other cores, ' +
        'media types (src/media), and src/utils. See re-architecture §3.1.',
      severity: 'error',
      from: { path: '^src/cores/' },
      to: {
        pathNot: '^(src/cores/|src/media/|src/utils/|node_modules/)',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'media-is-pure',
      comment:
        'Format/media code (src/media) parses into neutral models and must not ' +
        'import a machine, core, UI, or state — only other media and utils. §3.1/§4.',
      severity: 'error',
      from: { path: '^src/media/' },
      to: {
        pathNot: '^(src/media/|src/utils/|node_modules/)',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'machines-are-islands',
      comment:
        'A machine folder (src/machines/<name>/) is an island: it may import its ' +
        'own folder plus the shared substrate (machine.ts, base-machine.ts, ' +
        'registry, shared/), but never another machine folder. §3.1.',
      severity: 'error',
      from: { path: '^src/machines/([^/]+)/' },
      to: {
        path: '^src/machines/(?!$1/|machine|base-machine|registry|shared)',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'debug-is-cpu-substrate',
      comment:
        'src/debug holds machine-agnostic debug tools and CPU-family debug ' +
        'substrate (src/debug/<family>/: disassembler + DebugService provider). ' +
        'It may import cores, utils, and the machine SPI *types* (machine.ts) — ' +
        'never a concrete machine folder, UI, state, store, or shell.',
      severity: 'error',
      from: { path: '^src/debug/' },
      to: {
        pathNot: '^(src/debug/|src/cores/|src/utils/|src/machines/machine\\.ts$|node_modules/)',
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'machines-no-ui',
      comment:
        'A machine folder must not import UI, reactive state, the settings store, ' +
        'the shell, or solid-js; those bind to machines through services/registry, ' +
        'not vice-versa. §3.1.\n' +
        'EXCEPTION: a machine`s own `ui/` subfolder holds its Solid UI contributions ' +
        '(hardware-pane section, on-screen keyboard, sysvars) — the only machine files ' +
        'allowed to import solid-js and the shell/state/store they bind to. They are ' +
        'still islands (machines-are-islands forbids importing another machine).',
      severity: 'error',
      from: { path: '^src/machines/', pathNot: '^src/machines/[^/]+/ui/' },
      to: { path: '^(src/ui/|src/state/|src/store/|src/shell/|solid-js)' },
    },
    {
      name: 'ui-no-concrete-machines',
      comment:
        'Generic UI (src/ui) and reactive state (src/state) must not import a ' +
        'concrete machine folder (src/machines/<name>/). They bind to machines through ' +
        'the SPI (machine.ts), the registry, the descriptor`s `ui` capabilities, and ' +
        'services. §3.1/§7.\n' +
        'The SOLE sanctioned exception is the UI-side manifest ' +
        '`src/ui/machine-ui.ts`, which lazily maps a machine kind to its `ui/` ' +
        'contributions. The shell is governed separately by `shell-stays-above-machines`.',
      severity: 'error',
      from: { path: '^src/(ui|state)/', pathNot: '^src/ui/machine-ui\\.ts$' },
      to: { path: '^src/machines/[^/]+/' },
    },
    {
      name: 'shell-stays-above-machines',
      comment:
        'The shell (src/shell) may import the machine SPI + registry (machine.ts, ' +

        'Phase 8 dissolved the last two carve-outs: the shell-context `spectrum` ' +
        'narrowing shim (HMR/boot-trap/IF1-format now go through services + narrow ' +
        'SPI hooks) and the direct SZX import (now SnapshotService.saveSync/' +
        'restoreSync). ZERO exceptions remain — the boundary is a hard error.',
      severity: 'error',
      from: { path: '^src/shell/' },
      to: {
        path: '^src/machines/[^/]+/',
      },
    },
  ],
  options: {
    doNotFollow: { path: 'node_modules' },
    tsConfig: { fileName: 'tsconfig.json' },

import org.springframework.stereotype.Service

const val BASE_PACKAGE: String = "org.boro.gmailcleaner"

private const val DOMAIN = "Domain"
private const val ADAPTERS = "Adapters"
private const val INFRASTRUCTURE = "Infrastructure"

private const val DOMAIN_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.domain.."
private const val ADAPTER_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.adapter.."
private const val INFRASTRUCTURE_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.infrastructure.."
private const val REST_ADAPTER_PACKAGE = "$BASE_PACKAGE.adapter.rest.."
private const val CONTROLLER_SUFFIX = "Controller"

class ArchitectureTest {
    private val classes: JavaClasses =
        ClassFileImporter()
            .withImportOption(DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
            .importPackages(BASE_PACKAGE)

    @Test
    fun `classes should not throw generic exceptions`() = NO_CLASSES_SHOULD_THROW_GENERIC_EXCEPTIONS.check(classes)

    @Test
    fun `classes should be free of cycles`() =
        slices().matching("$BASE_PACKAGE.(*)..")
            .should().beFreeOfCycles()
            .check(classes)

    @Test
    fun `domain should be framework free`() =
        classes()
            .that().resideInAPackage(DOMAIN_PACKAGE)
            .should().onlyDependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage(
                "$BASE_PACKAGE..",
                "java..",
                "kotlin..",
                "jakarta.persistence..",
                "jakarta.transaction..",
                "jakarta.validation..",
                "org.jetbrains..",
                "org.hibernate..",
            )
            .check(classes)

    @Test
    fun `adapters should not depend on infrastructure`() =
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer(DOMAIN).definedBy(DOMAIN_PACKAGE)
            .layer(ADAPTERS).definedBy(ADAPTER_PACKAGE)
            .layer(INFRASTRUCTURE).definedBy(INFRASTRUCTURE_PACKAGE)
            .whereLayer(ADAPTERS).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(INFRASTRUCTURE)
            .whereLayer(INFRASTRUCTURE).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .check(classes)

    @Test
    fun `adapters should not depend on each other`() {
        val prefix = ADAPTER_PACKAGE.dropLast(2)
        val adapterPackages =
            classes
                .map { it.packageName }
                .filter { it.startsWith(prefix) }
                .distinct()

        adapterPackages.forEach { adapter ->
            noClasses()
                .that()
                .resideInAPackage("$adapter..")
                .should()
                .dependOnClassesThat()
                .resideInAnyPackage(*adapterPackages.filterNot { it == adapter }.map { "$it.." }.toTypedArray())
                .check(classes)
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `spring beans should be created only in configuration classes`() =
        classes()
            .should().notBeAnnotatedWith(Component::class.java)
            .andShould().notBeAnnotatedWith(Service::class.java)
            .andShould().notBeAnnotatedWith(Repository::class.java)
            .andShould().notBeAnnotatedWith(Controller::class.java)
            .check(classes)

    @Test
    fun `controller should have proper suffix`() =
        classes()
            .that().areAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java).and().resideInAPackage(REST_ADAPTER_PACKAGE)
            .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith(CONTROLLER_SUFFIX)
            .check(classes)
}

/**
 * Architecture boundaries, machine-checked.
 *
 * The layer diagram these rules encode (see also src/core/types.ts):
 *
 *   util, native            — leaves; import nothing above themselves
 *   storage                 — persistence; no core/backend/frontend imports
 *   core                    — the engine; no frontend/backend imports (types.ts:5)
 *   backend                 — agent-runtime adapters; no frontend imports
 *   frontend                — platform drivers; no direct backend imports
 *   cli, app, bootstrap     — composition roots; may import anything
 *
 * Severity discipline:
 *   error — the rule holds today; a violation is a regression and fails CI.
 *   warn  — the rule is the target state of an in-flight migration; each
 *           carries the migration that ratchets it to error. Never add new
 *           violations to a warn rule.
 */
module.exports = {
  forbidden: [
    // ── Ratified boundaries (error = CI gate) ────────────────────────────
    {
      name: "core-not-to-frontend",
      comment:
        "core/ imports nothing from frontend/ (src/core/types.ts:5). " +
        "Frontends register handlers with the engine at startup; the engine " +
        "never reaches into a platform.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/core/" },
      to: { path: "^src/frontend/" },
    },
    {
      name: "core-not-to-backend",
      comment:
        "core/ imports nothing from backend/ (src/core/types.ts:5). " +
        "Backends are bound through the agent-runtime seam, not imported. " +
        "core/doctor/ used to be carved out here; it no longer imports " +
        "backend/ and is covered like the rest of core.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/core/" },
      to: { path: "^src/backend/" },
    },
    {
      name: "backend-not-to-frontend",
      comment:
        "Backends speak to frontends only through the gateway action " +
        "protocol — never by import.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/backend/" },
      to: { path: "^src/frontend/" },
    },
    {
      name: "util-is-a-leaf",
      comment:
        "util/ is the bottom of the stack — anything it imported from the " +
        "layers above would be a cycle waiting to happen. util/ is the " +
        "kernel's lib/: leaf helpers only, nothing that knows what a chat, " +
        "a session or a model is (docs/structure.md, worklist item 4 moved " +
        "the rest to their owning subsystems). What is left has nothing to " +
        "carve out: both exemptions below are now vestigial guards rather " +
        "than live exceptions. The #prompt-assets subpath import is the " +
        "build-time asset seam (package.json `imports` switches " +
        "disk/embedded prompts per runtime) and not a layering edge — its " +
        "last util/ caller left with workspace.ts. metrics.ts left earlier, " +
        "for storage/metrics.ts. Both stay so the seam and " +
        "metrics-read-shape-moves-down keep speaking for their paths if " +
        "anything tries to come back.",
      severity: "error",
      from: {
        path: "^src/util/",
        pathNot: "^src/util/metrics\\.ts$",
      },
      to: {
        path: "^src/(core|backend|frontend|storage|cli|plugins)/",
        dependencyTypesNot: ["aliased-subpath-import"],
      },
    },
    {
      name: "native-is-a-leaf",
      comment: "native/ bricks are self-contained; same rule as util/.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/native/" },
      to: { path: "^src/(core|backend|frontend|storage|cli|plugins)/" },
    },
    {
      name: "storage-below-the-engine",
      comment:
        "storage/ persists; it never calls up into the engine or the " +
        "platform layers.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/storage/" },
      to: { path: "^src/(core|backend|frontend|cli)/" },
    },
    {
      name: "db-handle-stays-in-storage",
      comment:
        "Only stores open the SQLite handle — everything else goes through " +
        "a store's API. Composition roots (app, cli, bootstrap, index) are " +
        "exempt: they own process lifecycle, which includes the final " +
        "flushDatabase.",
      severity: "error",
      from: {
        pathNot: "^src/(storage/|cli/|app\\.ts$|bootstrap\\.ts$|index\\.ts$)",
      },
      to: { path: "^src/storage/db\\.ts$" },
    },
    {
      name: "no-circular",
      severity: "error",
      comment:
        "Import cycles make ownership ambiguous and break incremental " +
        "reasoning. Cycles closed only through a dynamic import() are " +
        "allowed: the lazy edge is the deliberate cycle-break (module " +
        "load order stays acyclic).",
      from: {},
      to: {
        circular: true,
        viaOnly: { dependencyTypesNot: ["dynamic-import"] },
      },
    },

    // ── Migration targets (warn = visible, ratchets to error) ────────────
    {
      name: "backend-sessions-move-to-thread",
      comment:
        "DEFERRED BY DESIGN — see docs/weaver.md 'Non-goals': session " +
        "writes still run through the store directly, because backends own " +
        "those callsites and `Thread.session` is a read handle for now. " +
        "Ratchets to error when QueryParams carries a write-capable " +
        "ThreadSession and nothing under backend/ imports the store " +
        "directly. That is ~88 callsites across six backends, so treat the " +
        "current warnings as a visible debt marker, not an imminent " +
        "migration. Do not add new importers. " +
        "(Renamed from sessions-owned-by-weaver: the old name claimed the " +
        "Weaver owns ALL session state, but `from` only covers backend/ " +
        "and core/engine/ — eleven frontend modules import the store too " +
        "and were never flagged. The name now matches what is checked.)",
      severity: "warn",
      from: {
        path: "^src/(backend|core/engine)/",
        // gateway.ts reads getActiveSessionCount() — fleet cardinality for
        // /status, not per-chat session ownership. The Thread migration
        // will not remove it: that count is of persisted rows, while
        // loom.activeContextCount() counts live Threads.
        pathNot: "^src/core/engine/gateway\\.ts$",
      },
      to: { path: "^src/storage/sessions\\.ts$" },
    },
    {
      name: "doctor-probes-move-behind-registry",
      comment:
        "DONE, now enforced: backends contribute their own checks through " +
        "`BackendFactory.doctor` and core/doctor/ composes whatever the " +
        "registry holds — it names no backend and imports none. The rule " +
        "stays as an error so a probe can't creep back into core: a new " +
        "backend gets doctor coverage by implementing the slot, not by " +
        "teaching doctor about itself.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/core/doctor/" },
      to: { path: "^src/backend/" },
    },
    {
      name: "config-belongs-in-core",
      comment:
        "DONE, now enforced: engine configuration lives in core/config/ " +
        "(it imports core/prompt and core/agent-runtime, so it was never a " +
        "leaf utility). A config module under util/ would be a regression.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/util/config" },
      to: {},
    },
    {
      name: "metrics-read-shape-moves-down",
      comment:
        "DONE, now enforced: the metrics read shape was a view over the " +
        "session store misfiled as a leaf utility — it imported nothing " +
        "except storage/sessions and was imported only from backend/ and " +
        "frontend/. It now lives at storage/metrics.ts, beside its data. " +
        "The rule stays as an error so nothing reintroduces a util/ module " +
        "that reaches up into the layers above it.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/util/metrics\\.ts$" },
      to: { path: "^src/(core|backend|frontend|storage|cli|plugins)/" },
    },
    {
      name: "frontend-not-to-backend",
      comment:
        "ENFORCED: frontends consume turn results through the engine, never " +
        "by importing backend/ directly. The last violation was " +
        "`extractSessionName`, a 41-line import-free string helper that was " +
        "simply misfiled under backend/runtime; it now lives in " +
        "core/weaver/session-name.ts (still re-exported from the " +
        "backend/runtime barrel, so backends keep one import site). " +
        "With that gone the " +
        "boundary is clean, so this is an error rather than a target.",
      severity: "error",
      from: { path: "^src/frontend/" },
      to: { path: "^src/backend/" },
    },
  ],
  options: {
    doNotFollow: { path: "node_modules" },
    exclude: { path: "(^|/)__tests__/|\\.test\\.ts$|\\.d\\.m?ts$" },
    // The repo compiles with typescript@7 (tsgo), whose API dependency-cruiser

    parser: "swc",
    tsConfig: { fileName: "tsconfig.json" },
    tsPreCompilationDeps: true,
    enhancedResolveOptions: {

      extensions: [".ts", ".mts", ".js", ".mjs"],
    },
    reporterOptions: {

@Tag("Architecture")
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = ["fr.sdecout.handson"])
class ArchitectureTest {

    @ArchTest
    val layers: ArchRule = layeredArchitecture()
        .consideringAllDependencies()
        .layer("rest").definedBy("..rest..")
        .layer("persistence").definedBy("..persistence..")
        .whereLayer("persistence").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
        .whereLayer("rest").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("persistence")
        .`as`("Layers should be clearly defined")
        .because("we want to work on a single layer with no impact on the other ones.")
