package org.danteplanner.backend.architecture; import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses; import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest; import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule; import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.methods; /** * Ratchets the test-method naming contract: a subject, a condition, and an expectation, separated * by underscores. * *

Enforced here rather than via Checkstyle {@code MethodName} on purpose: Checkstyle * cannot scope a name rule to annotated methods, so the strict regex would also reject the * suite's legitimate camelCase helpers ({@code createTestUser}, {@code setUp}, ...) and break * the zero-suppression baseline. ArchUnit is annotation-aware, so the rule targets exactly the * test methods and leaves helpers untouched.

* *

Config includes test classes ({@code @AnalyzeClasses} default) — a * {@code DoNotIncludeTests} import option would make this rule pass vacuously against zero * methods.

*/ @AnalyzeClasses(packages = "org.danteplanner.backend") class TestNamingConventionTest { /** * Every JUnit test method (anything meta-annotated {@code @Testable}: {@code @Test}, * {@code @ParameterizedTest}, {@code @RepeatedTest}, {@code @TestFactory}) carries three or * more underscore-separated parts, spelled {@code subject_WhenCondition_Expectation}: a * camelCase subject, a middle part opening with {@code When}, and PascalCase expectation parts * — {@code findById_WhenExists_ReturnsUser}. * *

The condition word is fixed rather than drawn from a set. {@code After}, {@code With} and * {@code Given} each read well in isolation, and admitting them is what let half the suite * settle into spellings that were neither mechanical nor invariant; a reader scanning a file * should not have to hold four shapes in mind at once.

* *

A name whose middle part reads as an outcome rather than a condition — * {@code cannotCreateComment}, {@code NoDeadlock} — is misnamed rather than exempt. The * condition belongs in the middle and the outcome at the end, and rewriting it that way * usually exposes that the two had been swapped.

*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule test_methods_follow_naming_convention = methods() .that().areMetaAnnotatedWith("org.junit.platform.commons.annotation.Testable") .should().haveNameMatching( "^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*_When[A-Z0-9][A-Za-z0-9]*(_[A-Z0-9][A-Za-z0-9]*)+$") .as("test methods are spelled subject_WhenCondition_Expectation"); }

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = [BOUNDED_CONTEXT_PACKAGE],
  importOptions = [DoNotIncludeTests::class, DoNotIncludeArchives::class])
class UtilLayerTest {

  companion object {
    const val UTIL = "Util"
  }

  @ArchTest
  fun utilClasses(classes: JavaClasses) =
    classes()
      .that().haveSimpleNameEndingWith(UTIL)
      .should().resideOutsideOfPackage("$BOUNDED_CONTEXT_PACKAGE.")
      .check(classes)
}

Closes the gap left by the * earlier field-only / domain-and-application-only rules: web, consumer, and producer adapters * could otherwise reach into jOOQ types directly and bypass the repository ports. */ @ArchTest static final ArchRule jooq_only_used_in_db = noClasses() .that() .resideOutsideOfPackages("..infrastructure.db..", "..jooq..") .should() .dependOnClassesThat() .resideInAnyPackage("org.jooq..", "..jooq..") .as("jOOQ (library and generated) may only be referenced from ..infrastructure.db..") .because( "jOOQ usage must be confined to repository adapters. Application orchestrates via" + " ports; controllers, consumers, producers, and cross-slice helpers must" + " never reach into jOOQ directly. The layered-architecture rule does not" + " catch this because generated jOOQ lives outside the three declared layers."); /** * OpenAPI-generated transport types — controller interfaces and DTO models under {@code * ..api.generated..} — are HTTP transport plumbing. They may only be referenced from {@code * ..infrastructure.web..} (controllers and web mappers, including {@code * shared.infrastructure.web} for the global exception handler) and from the generated package * itself. Domain, application, and the non-web infrastructure slices must exchange domain types, * not DTOs. */ @ArchTest static final ArchRule openapi_generated_only_used_in_web = noClasses() .that() .resideOutsideOfPackages("..infrastructure.web..", "..api.generated..") .should() .dependOnClassesThat() .resideInAPackage("..api.generated..") .as( "OpenAPI-generated transport types may only be referenced from ..infrastructure.web..") .because( "DTOs and generated controller interfaces are an HTTP transport concern. Other infrastructure slices (db, consumer, producer)" + " do not know HTTP exists."); @ArchTest static final ArchRule kafka_template_only_used_in_producer_or_config = noClasses() .that() .resideOutsideOfPackages("..infrastructure.producer..", "..config..") .should() .dependOnClassesThat() .areAssignableTo(KafkaTemplate.class) .as("KafkaTemplate may only be referenced from ..infrastructure.producer.. or ..config..") .because( "Kafka producer adapters belong in the producer slice. Infrastructure depends on application and" + " domain via ports."); } private static ArchRule ioSiblingMustNotDependOn(String mySlice, String... forbiddenSiblings) { String[] forbiddenPackages = Arrays.stream(forbiddenSiblings) .map("..infrastructure.%s.."::formatted) .toArray(String[]::new); return noClasses() .that() .resideInAPackage("..infrastructure." + mySlice + "..") .should() .dependOnClassesThat() .resideInAnyPackage(forbiddenPackages) .as( "Infrastructure.%s must not depend on sibling I/O slices: %s" .formatted(mySlice, String.join(", ", forbiddenSiblings))) .because( "Infrastructure I/O adapters communicate via application ports, not directly with" + " each other. Cross-slice helpers live in ..infrastructure.serialization..," + " ..infrastructure.metric.., ..infrastructure.id.."); } /** * Discovers bounded contexts by scanning imported classes for top-level segments that have a * {@code domain} subpackage. {@code shared} is naturally excluded (no {@code shared.domain}), as * is {@code WealthpayApplication} (top-level class with no sub-segments). Tests are excluded via * {@link ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests} on the class-level {@code @AnalyzeClasses}. */ private static SortedSet detectBoundedContexts(JavaClasses classes) { Map> bcLayers = new HashMap<>(); for (var javaClass : classes) { String pkg = javaClass.getPackageName(); if (!pkg.startsWith(BASE_PACKAGE + ".")) { continue; } String tail = pkg.substring(BASE_PACKAGE.length() + 1); String[] parts = tail.split("\\.", 3); if (parts.length < 2) { continue; } String bc = parts[0]; String layer = parts[1]; if (layer.equals("domain") || layer.equals("application") || layer.equals("infrastructure")) { bcLayers.computeIfAbsent(bc, ignored -> new HashSet<>()).add(layer); } } SortedSet result = new TreeSet<>(); for (Map.Entry> entry : bcLayers.entrySet()) { // A BC must have at least a domain subpackage (the defining trait of hexagonal architecture). if (entry.getValue().contains("domain")) { result.add(entry.getKey()); } } return result; } }

package org.gotson.komga.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import org.gotson.komga.Application

@AnalyzeClasses(packagesOf = [Application::class], importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class])
class DomainDrivenDesignRulesTest {
  @ArchTest
  val domainModelShouldNotAccessOtherPackages: ArchRule =
    noClasses()
      .that()
      .resideInAPackage("..domain..model..")
      .should()
      .dependOnClassesThat()
      .resideInAnyPackage(
        "..infrastructure..",
        "..interfaces..",
        "..domain.persistence..",
        "..domain.service..",
      )

  @ArchTest
  var classesNamedControllerShouldBeInAnInterfacesPackage: ArchRule =
    classes()
      .that()
      .haveSimpleNameContaining("Controller")
      .should()
      .resideInAPackage("..interfaces..")
}

package org.bazar.authorization.arch

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures

@AnalyzeClasses(
    packages = ["org.bazar.authorization"],
    importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class]
)
class ArchitectureTest {

    companion object {
        const val DOMAIN = "DOMAIN"
        const val APPLICATION = "APPLICATION"
        const val ADAPTER_INBOUND = "ADAPTER_INBOUND"
        const val ADAPTER_OUTBOUND = "ADAPTER_OUTBOUND"
        const val INFRASTRUCTURE = "INFRASTRUCTURE"

        val ARCHITECTURE: Architectures.LayeredArchitecture = Architectures.layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers()
            .layer(DOMAIN).definedBy("..domain..")
            .layer(APPLICATION).definedBy("..application..")
            .layer(ADAPTER_INBOUND).definedBy("..adapter.inbound..")
            .layer(ADAPTER_OUTBOUND).definedBy("..adapter.outbound..")
            .layer(INFRASTRUCTURE).definedBy("..infrastructure..")
    }

    @ArchTest
    val domain_layer_must_not_depend_on_any_layer: ArchRule = ARCHITECTURE
        .whereLayer(DOMAIN)
        .mayNotAccessAnyLayer()
        .`as`("Domain layer must not depend on any other layer")

    @ArchTest
    val application_layer_may_only_access_domain: ArchRule = ARCHITECTURE
        .whereLayer(APPLICATION)
        .mayOnlyAccessLayers(DOMAIN)
        .`as`("Application layer may only access Domain layer")

    @ArchTest
    val application_layer_whitelist: ArchRule = classes()
        .that().resideInAPackage("..application..")
        .should().onlyDependOnClassesThat().resideInAnyPackage(
            "..application..",
            "..domain..",
            "org.jetbrains.exposed..",
            "org.jetbrains.annotations..",
            "org.slf4j..",
            "java..",
            "kotlin.."
        )
        .`as`(
            "Application layer may only depend on Domain, itself, JDK/Kotlin, slf4j, JetBrains annotations and " +
                    "Exposed transaction DSL (pragmatic tradeoff)"
        )

    @ArchTest
    val adapter_inbound_may_only_access_domain_and_application: ArchRule = ARCHITECTURE
        .whereLayer(ADAPTER_INBOUND)
        .mayOnlyAccessLayers(DOMAIN, APPLICATION)
        .`as`("Inbound adapters may only access Domain and Application layers")

    @ArchTest
    val adapter_outbound_may_only_access_domain_application_and_infrastructure: ArchRule = ARCHITECTURE
        .whereLayer(ADAPTER_OUTBOUND)
        .mayOnlyAccessLayers(DOMAIN, APPLICATION, INFRASTRUCTURE)
        .`as`("Outbound adapters may only access Domain, Application and Infrastructure layers")

    @ArchTest
    val infrastructure_may_only_be_accessed_by_adapters: ArchRule = ARCHITECTURE
        .whereLayer(INFRASTRUCTURE)
        .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(ADAPTER_INBOUND, ADAPTER_OUTBOUND)
        .`as`("Infrastructure layer may only be accessed by adapters")

    @ArchTest
    val infrastructure_must_not_depend_on_outbound_adapters: ArchRule = noClasses()
        .that().resideInAPackage("..infrastructure..")
        .and().resideOutsideOfPackage("..infrastructure.di..")
        .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..adapter.outbound..")
        .`as`("Infrastructure must not depend on outbound adapters (DI wiring excluded)")
}

/*- * #%L * Cheshire :: Test Common * %% * Copyright (C) 2026 Halim Chaibi * %% * Licensed under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. * #L% */ package io.cheshire.architecture; import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes; import static com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition.slices; import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption; import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses; import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest; import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule; /** * Architecture tests using ArchUnit to validate the Cheshire framework structure. * *

Purpose: * *

Enforces architectural constraints and best practices across the Cheshire framework: * *

    *
  • Module Layering: SPI → Core → Server → Runtime dependency hierarchy *
  • No Circular Dependencies: Prevents cyclic dependencies between modules *
  • SPI Compliance: Query engines and source providers implement correct SPIs *
  • Factory Pattern: Factories implement appropriate SPI factory interfaces *
  • Exception Hierarchy: All exceptions extend Exception *
  • Naming Conventions: Consistent naming across the framework *
  • Immutability: Records for data carriers where applicable *
* *

Module Structure: * * 

 * ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
 * │           cheshire-runtime              │ (Top layer)
 * └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
 *                  ↓
 * ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
 * │           cheshire-server               │
 * └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
 *                  ↓
 * ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
 * │           cheshire-core                 │
 * └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
 *                  ↓
 * ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
 * │        SPI Modules (base layer)         │
 * │  • cheshire-pipeline-spi                │
 * │  • cheshire-query-engine-spi            │
 * │  • cheshire-source-provider-spi         │
 * └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
 *
* *

Design Principles Enforced: * *

    *
  • Dependency Inversion: High-level modules depend on abstractions (SPIs) *
  • Open/Closed Principle: Extensions via SPI, core closed for modification *
  • Single Responsibility: Each module has clear, distinct purpose *
  • Interface Segregation: Small, focused SPI interfaces *
* * @see ArchUnit Documentation * @since 1.0.0 */ @AnalyzeClasses( packages = "io.cheshire", importOptions = {ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class}) public class CheshireArchitectureTest { // ============================================ // Layer Rules (Module Dependencies) // ============================================ /** * Ensures SPI modules remain independent and don't depend on higher layers. * *

Rationale: SPI modules define contracts that implementations must follow. * They should be pure interfaces with no dependencies on concrete implementations (Core, Server, * Runtime). * *

Allowed Dependencies: * *

    *
  • Other SPI modules (for composition) *
  • Java standard library *
  • Common utilities (exceptions, config) *
*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule spi_Should_Not_Depend_On_Core_Server_Runtime = classes() .that() .resideInAPackage("..spi..") .should() .onlyDependOnClassesThat() .resideInAnyPackage("..spi..", "..common..", "java..", "lombok..", "org.slf4j..") .because( "SPI modules must remain independent and cannot depend on Core, Server, or Runtime modules"); /** * Ensures Core module only depends on SPIs and not on implementations. * *

Rationale: Core orchestrates the framework but should depend only on * abstractions (SPIs). This enables plugin-based architecture via ServiceLoader. * *

Allowed Dependencies: * *

    *
  • All SPI modules (abstractions) *
  • Common utilities *
  • Jackson (for configuration) *
  • SLF4J (for logging) *
*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule core_Should_Only_Depend_On_Spi_And_Common = classes() .that() .resideInAPackage("..core..") .should() .onlyDependOnClassesThat() .resideInAnyPackage( "..core..", "..common..", "..spi..", "java..", "lombok..", "org.slf4j..", "com.fasterxml.jackson..") .because("Core modules can depend on SPI and Common but not Server or Runtime"); /** * Ensures Server module respects layering: Server → Core → SPI. * *

Rationale: Server implementations handle protocol-specific concerns (HTTP, * stdio) and delegate to Core for business logic. * *

Allowed Dependencies: * *

    *
  • Core module (for orchestration) *
  • SPI modules (for contracts) *
  • Jetty (for HTTP server) *
  • MCP SDK (for MCP protocol) *
*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule server_Should_Only_Depend_On_Core_And_Spi = classes() .that() .resideInAPackage("..server..") .should() .onlyDependOnClassesThat() .resideInAnyPackage( "..server..", "..core..", "..common..", "..spi..", "java..", "lombok..", "org.slf4j..", "com.fasterxml.jackson..", "org.eclipse.jetty..", "io.modelcontextprotocol..") .because("Server modules can depend on Core and SPI only, not Runtime"); /** * Ensures Runtime module is the top layer with access to all modules. * *

Rationale: Runtime orchestrates startup, shutdown, monitoring, and * deployment. It's the only module that can depend on all lower layers. * *

Allowed Dependencies: * *

    *
  • All Cheshire modules (top-level orchestration) *
  • Standard dependencies (logging, configuration) *
*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule runtime_Should_Only_Depend_On_Server_Core_Spi = classes() .that() .resideInAPackage("..runtime..") .should() .onlyDependOnClassesThat() .resideInAnyPackage( "..runtime..", "..server..", "..core..", "..common..", "..spi..", "java..", "lombok..", "org.slf4j..", "com.fasterxml.jackson..") .because("Runtime is the top layer and can depend on all lower layers"); // ============================================ // SPI Implementation Rules // ============================================ /** * Ensures all query engine implementations properly implement the QueryEngine SPI. * *

Examples: * *

    *
  • JdbcQueryEngine implements QueryEngine ✓ *
  • CalciteQueryEngine implements QueryEngine ✓ *
*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule queryEngines_Should_Implement_Spi = classes() .that() .resideInAPackage("..query.engine..") .and() .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("QueryEngine") .and() .areNotInterfaces() .and() .areNotNestedClasses() .should() .implement("io.cheshire.spi.query.engine.QueryEngine") .because("Query engines must implement the QueryEngine SPI"); /** * Ensures all source provider implementations properly implement the SourceProvider SPI. * *

    *

  • RestApiProvider implements SourceProvider ✓ *
*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule source_Providers_Should_Implement_Spi = classes() .that() .resideInAPackage("..source..") .and() .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Provider") .and() .areNotInterfaces() .and() .areNotNestedClasses() .should() .implement("io.cheshire.spi.source.SourceProvider") .because("Source providers must implement the SourceProvider SPI"); // ============================================ // Factory Pattern Rules // ============================================ /** * Ensures query engine factories implement the QueryEngineFactory SPI. * *

Pattern: Factory classes in query.engine packages must implement {@code * io.cheshire.spi.query.engine.QueryEngineFactory}. * *

ServiceLoader Integration: These factories are discovered via Java's * ServiceLoader mechanism for plugin-based architecture. * *

{@code
   * public class JdbcQueryEngineFactory implements QueryEngineFactory {

Example: * * 

{@code
   * public class JdbcDataSourceProviderFactory implements SourceProviderFactory {

   *     public JdbcDataSourceProvider create(JdbcDataSourceConfig config) { ... }

   * }

   *   └─ RuntimeException
   *       └─ CheshireException (base)
   *           ├─ ConfigurationException
   *           ├─ ValidationException
   *           ├─ ExecutionException
   *           ├─ QueryEngineException
   *           ├─ SourceProviderException
   *           └─ CheshireRuntimeError

*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule exceptions_Should_Extend_Exception = classes() .that() .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Exception") .or() .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Error") .and() .resideInAPackage("io.cheshire..") .should() .beAssignableTo(Exception.class) .because("All exceptions should extend Exception for consistent error handling"); // ============================================ // Circular Dependency Detection // ============================================ /** * Prevents circular dependencies between modules. * *

   * core → server → core ✗ (circular!)
   *
*/ @ArchTest static final ArchRule no_Circular_Dependencies = slices() .matching("io.cheshire.(*)..") .should() .beFreeOfCycles() .because("No circular dependencies should exist between modules for maintainability"); // ============================================ // Naming Convention Rules // ============================================ /** * Ensures manager classes follow naming conventions. * *

Pattern: Classes ending with "Manager" should reside in manager packages * and handle lifecycle/registration concerns. * *

Examples: * *

* S8 wrote these rules in full against packages that were still empty, so every one of them * carried {@code allowEmptyShould(true)} — otherwise ArchUnit fails a rule that matches * nothing. package com.example.linksphere.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.methods
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.Modifying
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.Query
import org.springframework.data.repository.Repository

/**
 * Spring Data의 derived delete(`deleteBy…`)는 엔티티를 읽어 하나씩 지우고 Hibernate가 지운 행 수를
 * 검사해서, 같은 행을 동시에 지운 요청과 부딪히면 StaleObjectStateException(HTTP면 409, 비동기 작업이면
 * 롤백)을 낸다. 2026-10-13 좋아요 연타 500이 이 경로였다. 삭제 메서드는 일괄 DELETE(`@Modifying @Query`)로만
 * 만들게 강제한다. ArchitectureRulesTest와 달리 infra(FCM 등)까지 보려고 앱 전체를 분석한다.
 */
@AnalyzeClasses(
    packages = ["com.example.linksphere"],
    importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class],
)
class RepositoryDeleteRulesTest {

    @ArchTest
    val repositoryDeleteMethodsMustBeBulk: ArchRule =
        methods()
            .that().haveNameMatching("(delete|remove)([A-Z].*)?By.*")
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().areInterfaces()
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().areAssignableTo(Repository::class.java)
            .should().beAnnotatedWith(Modifying::class.java)
            .andShould().beAnnotatedWith(Query::class.java)
            .`as`("리포지토리의 delete/remove 메서드는 derived delete가 아니라 @Modifying @Query 일괄 DELETE로 만든다")
}

package ru.stankin.uits; import com.tngtech.archunit.base.DescribedPredicate; import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption; import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses; import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest; import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule; import ru.stankin.uits.common.storage.FileStorage; import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClass.Predicates.resideInAPackage; import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes; import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses; import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noFields; import static com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition.slices; /** * Архитектурные правила проекта (T-13). * *

Новое исключение добавляется только вместе * с объяснением, почему связь легальна. */ @AnalyzeClasses(packages = "ru.stankin.uits", importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class) class ArchitectureTest { /** * Правило 1. DTO не зависят от JPA-сущностей. * *

DTO — это контракт API из docs/API.md. Сущность в DTO означает, что смена * схемы БД молча меняет контракт, а сериализация ленивых полей тянет * LazyInitializationException наружу. import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter

import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture
import io.kotest.core.spec.style.DescribeSpec

class ArchitectureTest :
    DescribeSpec({

        val classes =
            ClassFileImporter()
                .withImportOption(ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests())
                .importPackages("io.clroot.snaplake")

        describe("레이어 의존성") {
            it("domain → application, adapter, config 의존 금지") {
                noClasses()
                    .that()
                    .resideInAPackage("io.clroot.snaplake.domain..")
                    .should()
                    .dependOnClassesThat()
                    .resideInAnyPackage(
                        "io.clroot.snaplake.application..",
                        "io.clroot.snaplake.adapter..",
                        "io.clroot.snaplake.config..",
                    ).check(classes)
            }

            it("application → adapter 의존 금지") {
                noClasses()
                    .that()
                    .resideInAPackage("io.clroot.snaplake.application..")
                    .should()
                    .dependOnClassesThat()
                    .resideInAPackage("io.clroot.snaplake.adapter..")
                    .check(classes)
            }

            it("layered architecture 검증") {
                layeredArchitecture()
                    .consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers()
                    .layer("Domain")
                    .definedBy("io.clroot.snaplake.domain..")
                    .layer("Application")
                    .definedBy("io.clroot.snaplake.application..")
                    .layer("Adapter")
                    .definedBy("io.clroot.snaplake.adapter..")
                    .layer("Config")
                    .definedBy("io.clroot.snaplake.config..")
                    .whereLayer("Domain")
                    .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Application", "Adapter", "Config")
                    .whereLayer("Application")
                    .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Adapter", "Config")
                    // Config는 composition root이므로 Adapter 참조 허용
                    .whereLayer("Adapter")
                    .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Config")
                    .check(classes)
            }
        }

        describe("domain 프레임워크 격리") {
            it("domain은 Spring에 의존하지 않는다") {
                noClasses()
                    .that()
                    .resideInAPackage("io.clroot.snaplake.domain..")
                    .should()
                    .dependOnClassesThat()
                    .resideInAPackage("org.springframework..")
                    .check(classes)
            }

            it("domain은 JPA/Hibernate에 의존하지 않는다") {
                noClasses()
                    .that()
                    .resideInAPackage("io.clroot.snaplake.domain..")
                    .should()
                    .dependOnClassesThat()
                    .resideInAnyPackage(
                        "jakarta.persistence..",
                        "org.hibernate..",
                    ).check(classes)
            }
        }

        describe("application port 격리") {
            it("inbound port는 외부 프레임워크에 의존하지 않는다") {
                noClasses()
                    .that()
                    .resideInAPackage("io.clroot.snaplake.application.port..")
                    .should()
                    .dependOnClassesThat()
                    .resideInAnyPackage(
                        "org.springframework..",
                        "jakarta.persistence..",
                    ).check(classes)
            }
        }
    })

@AnalyzeClasses(
    packages = ["com.team2.server"],
    importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class, ImportOption.DoNotIncludeJars::class],

    @ArchTest
    @ArchIgnore(reason = "Phase 2: party 4-레이어 재배치 후 활성화")

            .consideringAllDependencies()

            .definedBy("..api..")
            .layer("UseCase")
            .definedBy("..application.usecase..")
            .layer("Service")
            .definedBy("..application.service..")
            .layer("Domain")
            .definedBy("..domain..")
            .layer("Infrastructure")
            .definedBy("..infrastructure..")
            .whereLayer("Api")
            .mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("UseCase")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Api")
            .whereLayer("Service")
            .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("UseCase")
            .whereLayer("Infrastructure")

  "missing-trailing-comma",                    # Conflict with formatter

  "D",                                    # don't care about documentation in tests
  "FBT",                                  # don't care about booleans as positional arguments in tests
  "implicit-namespace-package",           # no implicit namespace
  "import-private-name",                  # private imports
  "legacy-type-comment",                  # we test for legacy `# type:` comments
  "magic-value-comparison",               # Magic value used in comparison, consider replacing with a constant variable
  "non-pep585-annotation",                # we test for old List/Tuple syntax
  "non-pep604-annotation-optional",       # we test for old Optional syntax
  "non-pep604-annotation-union",          # we test for old Union syntax
  "pytest-fixture-autouse",               # shared setup fixtures are meant to apply to every test
  "pytest-incorrect-pytest-import",       # names come from pytest like from any other module
  "subprocess-without-shell-equals-true", # `subprocess` call: check for execution of untrusted input
  "too-many-arguments",                   # any number of arguments in tests
  "too-many-positional-arguments",        # any number of arguments in tests
]

]
lint.per-file-ignores."tests/roots/test-attrs/attrs_lazy_mod.py" = [
  "missing-required-import",               # intentionally omits `from __future__ import annotations` to keep annotations lazy
  "runtime-import-in-type-checking-block", # the guarded import is the case under test
]
lint.per-file-ignores."tests/roots/test-integration/mod_eager.py" = [
  "missing-required-import",  # this file intentionally omits `from __future__ import annotations` to test non-deferred annotations
  "no-self-use",              # a subclass binds the type parameter of an inherited instance method
  "non-pep695-generic-class", # the type parameter must be a module global, as only the legacy spelling makes it
  "return-in-generator",      # the generator's return value is the type under test
]
lint.per-file-ignores."tests/roots/test-integration/mod_forward_ref.py" = [
  "missing-required-import", # intentionally omits `from __future__ import annotations` to test forward references
  "no-self-use",             # method must be instance method to test class forward refs
]
lint.per-file-ignores."tests/roots/test-public-api/public_module.py" = [
  "ANN",                                       # a type comment stands in for the annotations
  "lambda-assignment",                         # the lambda's source line holds a second statement
  "multiple-statements-on-one-line-semicolon", # the source of the lambda then parses to two nodes
  "no-self-use",                               # a method of a class local to a function
  "undefined-name",                            # the forward reference the warning reports
  "unused-import",                             # the guarded import that fails to run
]

  "missing-required-import", # intentionally omits `from __future__ import annotations`
  "no-self-use",             # method must be instance method to test stub resolution
  "unused-async",            # async function must be async to test async stub resolution
]

[project]
name = "petbot"
version = "2.1.0"
description = "A chatbot: a thin Discord frontend that dispatches to a compute service."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
authors = [{ name = "auzbuzzard" }]
# Base install is the shared kernel only. The runtime dependencies of each
# deployable live in an extra below, so a process installs just what it runs
# (the edge never pulls pydantic-ai; a worker never pulls discord.py).
# opentelemetry-api is the one always-present telemetry dep: it is a no-op until a
# process wires the SDK (the `observability` extra) in its entrypoint, so library
# code can instrument unconditionally.
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.13",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.42",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# OpenTelemetry SDK + OTLP exporter, wired once per entrypoint by
# `petbot.observability.configure_observability`. The AWS extension supplies the
# X-Ray id generator + propagator so an edge->core trace joins in X-Ray; botocore
# SigV4-signs the collector-less export to AWS's OTLP endpoints. Pulled by every
# deployable that emits telemetry (the frontend and the compute core).
observability = [
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.42",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.42",
    "opentelemetry-sdk-extension-aws>=2.0",
    "botocore>=1.40",
]
# The always-on Discord frontend: holds the gateway, dispatches to a compute
# service over HTTP (or a Lambda, with the `lambda` extra).
discord = [
    "petbot[observability]",
    "discord.py>=2.7,<2.8",
    "httpx>=0.28",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14",
]
# The core compute service: math + booru + web search/fetch + weather + the chat process.
compute-core = [
    "petbot[observability]",
    "httpx>=0.28",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14",
    "numexpr>=2.14",
    "numpy>=2.4",
    # Capped below the next major: 2.x changed `openai_model_profile` to return a
    # non-dataclass, breaking the `dataclasses.replace` in process/model.py. A rebuilt
    # image must not pull a new major out from under the pinned lock.
    "pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock,openai]>=1.107,<2",
    # Main-content extraction for the fetch skill: a page's article, not its navigation.
    "trafilatura>=2.0",
    # Keyless web-search fallback (metasearch over public result pages).
    "ddgs>=9.16",
]
# The music compute service: its own gateway plus voice playback.
compute-music = [
    "petbot[observability]",
    "discord.py[voice]>=2.7,<2.8",
    "yt-dlp>=2026.6",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14",
]
# Dispatch to a Lambda compute service (boto3) — used by the frontend in production.
lambda = ["boto3>=1.43"]
# Everything, for development and CI (so type-check and tests see all code).
dev = [
    "petbot[discord,compute-core,compute-music,lambda]",
    "ruff>=0.15",
    "mypy>=2.1",
    "import-linter>=2.11",
    "pytest>=9.1",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1",
    "respx>=0.23",
    "pre-commit>=4.6",
]

[project.scripts]
petbot-discord = "petbot.frontends.discord.__main__:main"
petbot-core = "petbot.services.core.__main__:main"
petbot-music = "petbot.services.music.__main__:main"

# Skills are discovered at runtime from this entry-point group.
[project.entry-points."petbot.skills"]
math = "petbot.skills.math:MathSkill"
derpi = "petbot.skills.booru:build_derpi"
e621 = "petbot.skills.booru:build_e621"

web_fetch = "petbot.skills.web:build_fetch"
weather = "petbot.skills.weather:build_weather"

src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "ASYNC", "RUF"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["petbot"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
mypy_path = "src"
files = ["src", "tests"]
# The root tests/conftest.py shares a module name with the package-local booru
# conftest; it is trivial env setup, so keep it out of the type graph.
exclude = ["tests/conftest\\.py$"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["numexpr.*", "yt_dlp.*", "nacl.*", "boto3.*", "botocore.*", "requests.*", "conftest"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.coverage.run]
omit = [
    # Live-connection bootstraps are smoke-tested manually, not in CI.
    "src/petbot/frontends/discord/bot.py",
    "src/petbot/frontends/discord/__main__.py",
    "src/petbot/services/core/__main__.py",
    "src/petbot/services/music/bot.py",
    "src/petbot/services/music/voice.py",
    "src/petbot/services/music/__main__.py",
]

# import-linter: enforce the layering. domain (center) <- everything; the process core
# and the frontends are adapters that never import each other or a concrete skill;
# services are the only composition roots (allowed to import anything).
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["petbot"]
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The domain kernel depends on nothing else first-party and no platform SDK"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["petbot.domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["petbot.types", "petbot.platform", "petbot.process", "petbot.skills", "petbot.frontends", "petbot.services", "discord", "httpx"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The typed surface depends only on the kernel"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["petbot.types"]
forbidden_modules = ["petbot.platform", "petbot.process", "petbot.skills", "petbot.frontends", "petbot.services", "discord"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The platform is generic plumbing: no skill, process, frontend, or service"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["petbot.platform"]
forbidden_modules = ["petbot.process", "petbot.skills", "petbot.frontends", "petbot.services", "discord"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Skills are tools: they never import the process, frontend, platform, or a service"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["petbot.skills"]
forbidden_modules = ["petbot.platform", "petbot.process", "petbot.frontends", "petbot.services", "discord"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The process core never imports a concrete skill, a frontend, or a service"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["petbot.process"]
forbidden_modules = ["petbot.skills", "petbot.frontends", "petbot.services", "discord"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The frontend dispatches to a service and never imports a skill or the process core"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["petbot.frontends"]
forbidden_modules = ["petbot.skills", "petbot.process", "petbot.services"]

    "pre-commit>=4.3.0",

    "pytest-cov>=7.0.0",

    "pytest-sugar>=1.1.1",

    "scipy-stubs>=1.18.1.1",

    "types-python-dateutil>=2.9.0.20250822",

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Coverage is deliberately not here, so it does not run on every local
# invocation. Ask for it with --cov.
#
# --disable-socket makes "the suite runs offline" enforced rather than
# aspirational; unix sockets stay allowed because SQLite and multiprocessing
# need them. It cannot see curl_cffi, which connects from libcurl, so the
# `no_curl_requests` fixture in tests/conftest.py refuses those instead.
addopts = """
--strict-markers
--strict-config
--disable-socket
--allow-unix-socket
-m 'not live and not slow'
"""
xfail_strict = true
markers = [
  "live: makes real requests to the FPL API; deselected by default, run with -m live",
  "slow: takes more than a couple of seconds; deselected by default, run with -m slow",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
exclude = ["notebooks"]

[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true  # code snippets in docstrings will be formatted

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", "F", "W", # flake8
  "B",           # flake8-bugbear
  "I",           # isort
  "ARG",         # flake8-unused-arguments
  "C4",          # flake8-comprehensions
  "EM",          # flake8-errmsg
  "ICN",         # flake8-import-conventions
  "ISC",         # flake8-implicit-str-concat
  "G",           # flake8-logging-format
  "PGH",         # pygrep-hooks
  "PIE",         # flake8-pie
  "PL",          # pylint
  "PT",          # flake8-pytest-style
  "RET",         # flake8-return
  "RUF",         # Ruff-specific
  "SIM",         # flake8-simplify
  "UP",          # pyupgrade
  "YTT",         # flake8-2020
  "EXE",         # flake8-executable
  "TC",          # flake8-type-checking
  "N",           # pep8-naming
  "TID251",      # flake8-tidy-imports: banned-api (see below)
  # pydocstyle: the rules that pin Google-style sections, and the ones that keep
  # a docstring's first line a summary. Not the whole D family - D1xx would
  # require a docstring on everything and D417 every parameter documented once
  # any are, both of which push towards docstrings that restate the signature.
  "D200", "D202", "D205", "D209", "D403", "D415",
  "D405", "D410", "D411", "D412", "D414", "D416", "D418",
]
ignore = [
  # Ignored is design advice about magic values and comparison style.
  # flake8-annotations (ANN) is deliberately not enabled: mypy's strict mode
  # already requires annotations.
  "PLR2004", "PLR0402", "PLR1702", "PLR5501", "PLR6301",
  "ISC001", # Conflicts with formatter
  "G004",   # f-strings with logger
]
flake8-unused-arguments.ignore-variadic-names = true  # allow unused *args/**kwargs

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"__future__.annotations".msg = "Quote the annotation, or import the name at runtime."

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

# Each value is the current worst offender. Lower them as improvements are made.
[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 12          # run_optimization, make_new_squad
max-positional-args = 12  # run_optimization
max-branches = 18      # Squad.get_actual_points
max-statements = 76    # test_deap_optimization_creates_valid_squad
max-returns = 8        # Player.get_gameweek_attributes

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"src/airsenal/cli/*.py" = [
	# Ignore too many argument rules for CLI commands
	"PLR0913",
	"PLR0917",
]
"tests/**" = [
	"B011",  # allow using assert statements in tests
	"ARG001"  # allow unused arguments in tests, e.g. for pytest fixtures
]

[tool.mypy]
files = ["src/airsenal", "tools"]
strict = true
show_error_codes = true
warn_unreachable = true
warn_unused_configs = true
enable_error_code = [
    "ignore-without-code",
    "redundant-expr",
    "truthy-bool",
    "possibly-undefined",
]

# Named rather than a blanket ignore_missing_imports, so a new untyped
# dependency is a decision rather than something that slips in unnoticed.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "bpl.*",
    "deap.*",
    "numpyro.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# Modules allowed to call into untyped libraries above. Everything else
# reaches them through our own typed wrappers.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "airsenal.prediction.team_models.dixon_coles",
    "airsenal.prediction.player_models.mcmc",
    "airsenal.optimization.squad_optimizers.genetic_algorithm",
]
disallow_untyped_calls = false
warn_return_any = false

# curl_cffi ships py.typed but leaves Response.json(), raise_for_status(),
# iter_content() and close() unannotated
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "airsenal.remote.download",
]
disallow_untyped_calls = false

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/airsenal"]
branch = true

# A floor, not a target, raise it as coverage improves.
[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 65

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "airsenal"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Stage packages form a one-way dependency chain"
type = "layers"
containers = ["airsenal"]
layers = [
    "cli",
    "pipeline",
    "apply",
    "optimization",
    "export",
    "ingest",
    "reporting",
    "squad",
    "prediction",
    "db",
    "remote",
    "core",
    "game",
]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = ["data"]
ignore_imports = [
    # Annotation only, under TYPE_CHECKING: a caller passes a fetcher when the
    # database has no fixtures to work the gameweek out from.
    "airsenal.db.queries.gameweeks -> airsenal.remote.fpl_api",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The database layer does not reach for the FPL API"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["airsenal.db"]
forbidden_modules = ["airsenal.remote.fpl_api", "airsenal.remote.fpl_auth"]
ignore_imports = [
    # Annotation only, under TYPE_CHECKING
    "airsenal.db.queries.gameweeks -> airsenal.remote.fpl_api",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The database layer neither renders nor talks to the network"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["airsenal.db"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "airsenal.core.console",
    "airsenal.reporting",
    "curl_cffi",
    "matplotlib",
    "requests",
    "rich",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Only the remote package talks to the network"
type = "protected"  # direct imports only
protected_modules = [
    "bs4",
    "curl_cffi",
    "requests",
]
allowed_importers = ["airsenal.remote"]

  "peakfit.io",

line-length = 100
target-version = "py314"

[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Selected high-value rules.
# Defaults (E, F) + imports (I) + upgrades (UP) + bugbear (B) +
# pytest (PT) + import hygiene (TID, ICN) + builtin-shadowing/unused-
# argument/raise/return/string/logging conventions (A, ARG, RSE, RET,
# ISC, G) + simplification/performance nits (PIE, PERF) + timezone-aware
# datetimes (DTZ) + NumPy (NPY) + type-checking imports (TC) +
# direct-print cleanup (T20) + stale-noqa cleanup (RUF100).
select = [
  "A",
  "ARG",
  "E",
  "W",
  "F",
  "I",
  "N",
  "UP",
  "B",
  "C4",
  "EXE",
  "G",
  "ICN",
  "ISC",
  "SIM",
  "PTH",
  "PL",
  "PT",
  "RET",
  "RSE",
  "RUF",
  "RUF100",
  "D",
  "DTZ",
  "NPY",
  "PERF",
  "PIE",
  "TC",
  "T20",
  "TID"
]
ignore = [
  "D100",
  "D104",
  "D107",  # Missing docstrings in public modules/init (optional)
  "PLR0913",  # Too many arguments
  "RUF001",
  "RUF002",
  "RUF003",  # Unicode (Greek letters)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# Disallow relative imports from parent directories (e.g. from ..utils import x)
# This forces package-qualified imports and makes architecture boundaries clear.
ban-relative-imports = "parents"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*" = [
  "D",  # Documentation not needed in tests
  "PLR2004",  # Allow magic values in tests (assert x == 5)
]
"src/peakfit/engine/domain/cluster.py" = ["TC001"]
"src/peakfit/auto_pick/algorithm.py" = ["PLR0912", "PLR0915"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]
runtime-evaluated-decorators = [
  "pydantic.validate_call",
  "pydantic.field_validator",
  "pydantic.model_validator",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pep8-naming]
classmethod-decorators = [
  # Allow Pydantic's `@validator` decorator to trigger class method treatment.
  "pydantic.validator",
  "pydantic.field_validator",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-boolean-trap]
extend-allowed-calls = ["pydantic.Field"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
extend-immutable-calls = ["pydantic.Field"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true

Documentation = "https://github.com/Kaoruha/GinkGO/blob/master/README.md"
Changelog = "https://github.com/Kaoruha/GinkGO/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md"
"Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/Kaoruha/GinkGO/issues"

# setuptools配置
[tool.setuptools]
package-dir = {"" = "src"}

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"*" = ["*.yaml", "*.yml", "*.json", "*.xml"]

# 工具配置
[tool.black]
line-length = 120
target-version = ['py311', 'py312']
include = '\.pyi?$'
extend-exclude = '''
/(
  # 排除的目录
  \.eggs
  | \.git
  | \.hg
  | \.mypy_cache
  | \.tox
  | \.venv
  | _build
  | buck-out
  | build
  | dist
)/
'''

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
check_untyped_defs = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = true
no_implicit_optional = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_no_return = true
warn_unreachable = true
strict_equality = true

# 第三方库缺少 type stubs，仅对这些模块放宽缺失导入检查
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "apscheduler.*",
    "asyncmy.*",
    "baostock.*",
    "clickhouse_sqlalchemy.*",
    "jose.*",
    "kafka.*",
    "mootdx.*",
    "plotext.*",
    "pymysql.*",
    "textual.*",
    "tushare.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# 测试发现配置
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
minversion = "7.0"
pythonpath = [".", "src", "api"]

# 运行配置
addopts = [
    "-v",                    # 详细输出
    "--strict-markers",      # 严格标记模式
    "--strict-config",       # 严格配置模式
    "--tb=short",           # 简短traceback
    "--color=yes",          # 彩色输出
    "--durations=10",       # 显示最慢的10个测试
    "--timeout=60",         # 单测试超时
]

# 标记定义 - 覆盖所有在用的高频 markers
markers = [
    "unit: 快速的单元级测试",
    "integration: 组件协同/端到端测试",
    "slow: 执行时间较长的测试",
    "database: 依赖数据库或持久化资源的测试",
    "network: 需要外部网络资源的测试",
    "performance: 性能或压力测试",
    "backtest: 回测场景相关测试",
    "live: 实盘场景相关测试",
    "db_cleanup: 需要数据库清理的测试（自动清理测试数据）",
    "tdd: TDD开发的测试用例",
    "enum: 枚举处理相关的测试用例",
    "financial: 金融精度测试（涉及金额计算）",
    "cli: 命令行接口测试",
    "risk: 风控管理测试",
    "e2e: 端到端测试（浏览器自动化）",
    "lab: 实验性功能测试",
    "critical: 关键路径测试",
    "indicator: 技术指标测试",
    "notifier: 通知系统测试",
    "asyncio: 异步相关测试",
    "selector: 选股器测试",
    "strategy: 策略测试",
    "sizer: 仓位管理测试",
    "protocol: Protocol接口测试",
    "benchmark: 基准测试",
    "kafka: Kafka消息队列测试",
    "error_handling: 错误处理测试",
    "infrastructure: 基础设施测试",
    "refactor: 重构验证测试",
    "engine: 引擎测试",
    "time_controlled: 时间控制引擎测试",
    "event_processing: 事件处理测试",
    "lifecycle: 生命周期测试",
    "clickhouse: ClickHouse数据库测试",
    "mysql: MySQL数据库测试",
    "bug: 回归 bug 守护测试(防已修 bug 复发)",
]

# 警告过滤
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::UserWarning:ginkgo.*",
]

# 日志配置
log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"
log_cli_format = "%(asctime)s [%(levelname)8s] %(message)s"
log_cli_date_format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"

timeout = 300
console_output_style = "progress"

# 所需插件
required_plugins = ["pytest-cov", "pytest-timeout"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "C4"]
ignore = ["E501"]
fixable = ["ALL"]

# CI 分层 import 门禁 (#6906 / ADR-002)：
# client + api 禁止直连 ginkgo.data.crud，须经 *_service 触达数据层。
# 两处 scheduler 启动期构造 RedisCRUD 注入 livecore.Scheduler 的 DI 边界（#6300 评估为合法）按站点白名单。
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["ginkgo", "api"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "client and api must not import crud directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ginkgo.client", "api"]
forbidden_modules = ["ginkgo.data.crud"]
# 仅拦直接 import；client→service→crud 的合法传递路径放行（allow_indirect_imports=true）。
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "ginkgo.client.scheduler_cli -> ginkgo.data.crud",
    "ginkgo.client.serve_cli -> ginkgo.data.crud",
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
url = "https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple"
default = true

[tool.uv]
override-dependencies = [
    "httpx>=0.27",
]

[build-system]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
requires = [ "hatchling>=1.27" ]

[project]
name = "biotapy"
version = "0.5.0"
description = "mia-style microbiome toolkit for Python on AnnData/TreeData"
readme = "README.md"
license = "BSD-3-Clause"
license-files = [ "LICENSE" ]
maintainers = [
  { name = "Pedro Ribeiro", email = "pedrocasalribeiro@gmail.com" },
]
authors = [
  { name = "Pedro Ribeiro" },
]
requires-python = ">=3.12"
classifiers = [
  "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
  "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Bio-Informatics",
]
dependencies = [
  "anndata",
  "biom-format>=2.1.16",
  # io.write_h5mu / read_h5mu write the trees into the file (decisions/multiomics-as-mudata); anndata's own floor.
  "h5py>=3.11",
  "matplotlib>=3.8",
  "mudata>=0.4",
  "networkx",
  "numpy",
  "pandas",
  "pooch",
  "rdata>=1.1,<2",
  "scikit-bio>=0.7.4,<0.8",
  "scikit-learn>=1.8",
  "scipy",
  # for debug logging (referenced from the issue template)
  "session-info2",
  "threadpoolctl>=3.5",
  "treedata>=0.3.1,<0.4",
  "xarray",
]
# MGM, ml.embed's reference model (decisions/optional-heavy-dependencies): a GPT-2 that transformers runs on torch.
optional-dependencies.mgm = [ "torch>=2.9", "transformers>=5" ]
# The ALDEx2 and MaAsLin 3 bridges (decisions/optional-heavy-dependencies); R and the R packages are the user's install.
optional-dependencies.r = [ "rpy2>=3.6.8" ]
# ml.to_torch (decisions/optional-heavy-dependencies); 2.9.0 is torch's first release with CPython 3.14 wheels.
optional-dependencies.torch = [ "torch>=2.9" ]
# https://docs.pypi.org/project_metadata/#project-urls
urls.Documentation = "https://biotapy.readthedocs.io/"
urls.Homepage = "https://github.com/pedrocr83/biotapy"
urls.Source = "https://github.com/pedrocr83/biotapy"
# ml.embed's models (decisions/embedding-plugins); biotapy registers its own reference model as any plugin would.
entry-points."biotapy.embeddings".mgm = "biotapy.ml._mgm:embed"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "asv>=0.6.6",
  "import-linter>=2.15",
  "mypy>=2.3.1",
  "pandas-stubs",
  "prek",
  "scipy-stubs",
  "twine>=4.0.2",
  "types-networkx",
]
test = [
  "coverage>=7.10",
  "hypothesis>=6.168.1",
  "pytest",
  "pytest-cov",          # For VS Code’s coverage functionality
  "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
]
doc = [
  "ipykernel",
  "ipython",
  "myst-nb>=1.1",
  "pandas",
  "scverse-misc[sphinx]>=0.1.2",
  "sphinx>=8.1",
  "sphinx-autodoc-typehints",
  "sphinx-book-theme>=1",
  "sphinx-copybutton",
  "sphinx-design",
  "sphinxcontrib-bibtex>=1",
  "sphinxcontrib-katex",
  "sphinxext-opengraph",
]

[tool.hatch]
# Development-only files (rules.md, plan.md, .knowledge/, tests/r/, scripts/, .github/)
# stay in the GitHub repo but are not part of what ships to PyPI. So do the tests that check
# the repository itself (CI config, knowledge bundle, staleness script): they read those files.
build.targets.sdist.include = [
  "/CHANGELOG.md",
  "/conftest.py",
  "/docs",
  "/src/biotapy",
  "/tests",
]
build.targets.sdist.exclude = [
  "/docs/_build",
  "/docs/generated",
  "/docs/jupyter_execute",
  "/tests/humann",
  "/tests/mgm",
  "/tests/r",
  "/tests/test_ci.py",
  "/tests/test_knowledge_bundle.py",
  "/tests/test_knowledge_stale.py",
]
envs.default.installer = "uv"
envs.default.dependency-groups = [ "dev" ]
envs.docs.scripts.build = "sphinx-build -M html docs docs/_build -W {args}"
envs.docs.scripts.clean = "git clean -fdX -- {args:docs}"
envs.docs.scripts.open = "python -m webbrowser -t docs/_build/html/index.html"
envs.docs.dependency-groups = [ "doc" ]
envs.hatch-test.matrix = [
  # Test every supported Python version with normal deps
  { deps = [ "stable" ], python = [ "3.12", "3.13", "3.14" ] },
  # Test the newest supported Python version also with pre-release deps
  { deps = [ "pre" ], python = [ "3.14" ] },
]
# If the matrix variable `deps` is set to "pre",
# set the environment variable `UV_PRERELEASE` to "allow".
envs.hatch-test.overrides.matrix.deps.env-vars = [
  { value = "allow", key = "UV_PRERELEASE", if = [ "pre" ] },
]
envs.hatch-test.dependency-groups = [ "dev", "test" ]

[tool.uv]
# CI and contributors get torch's CPU wheels (196 MB on Linux), not PyPI's Linux wheel (555 MB plus CUDA packages).
# explicit = true: only torch, named in sources, comes from this index; the published metadata is unchanged.
sources.torch = { index = "pytorch-cpu" }
index = [ { name = "pytorch-cpu", url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu", explicit = true } ]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
src = [ "src" ]
extend-include = [ "*.ipynb" ]
format.docstring-code-format = true
lint.select = [
  "B",      # flake8-bugbear
  "BLE",    # flake8-blind-except
  "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
  "D",      # pydocstyle
  "E",      # Error detected by Pycodestyle
  "F",      # Errors detected by Pyflakes
  "I",      # isort
  "RUF100", # Report unused noqa directives
  "TID",    # flake8-tidy-imports
  "UP",     # pyupgrade
  "W",      # Warning detected by Pycodestyle
]
# Size and complexity limits (rules.md R5)
lint.extend-select = [ "C90", "PLR0911", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "PLR0917", "T20" ]
lint.ignore = [
  "B008", # Errors from function calls in argument defaults. These are fine when the result is immutable.
  "D100", # Missing docstring in public module
  "D104", # Missing docstring in public package
  "D105", # __magic__ methods are often self-explanatory, allow missing docstrings
  "D107", # Missing docstring in __init__
  # Disable one in each pair of mutually incompatible rules
  "D203", # We don’t want a blank line before a class docstring
  "D213", # <> We want docstrings to start immediately after the opening triple quote
  "D400", # first line should end with a period [Bug: doesn’t work with single-line docstrings]
  "D401", # First line should be in imperative mood; try rephrasing
  "E501", # line too long -> we accept long comment lines; formatter gets rid of long code lines
  "E731", # Do not assign a lambda expression, use a def -> lambda expression assignments are convenient
  "E741", # allow I, O, l as variable names -> I is the identity matrix
]
lint.per-file-ignores."*/__init__.py" = [ "F401" ]
lint.per-file-ignores."docs/*" = [ "I" ]
lint.per-file-ignores."src/biotapy/_core/_tree.py" = [ "TID251" ]
lint.per-file-ignores."tests/*" = [ "D", "TID251" ]
# Tree access only through biotapy._core (contracts/tree-access)
lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api.networkx.msg = "Tree operations live in biotapy/_core/_tree.py (contracts/tree-access)."
lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api.treedata.msg = "Use the TreeData helpers in biotapy._core (contracts/tree-access)."
lint.mccabe.max-complexity = 8
lint.pydocstyle.convention = "numpy"
lint.pylint.max-args = 6
lint.pylint.max-branches = 8
lint.pylint.max-positional-args = 3
lint.pylint.max-returns = 4
lint.pylint.max-statements = 30

[tool.mypy]
files = [ "docs/extensions", "src/biotapy" ]
python_version = "3.12"
# biom-format, h5py and scikit-learn ship no type annotations at all, nor do scikit-bio's
# subsample_counts, tree_basis and ancombc2, threadpoolctl's threadpool_limits, mudata's MuData.update and pooch's
# Unzip; exempt only calls into them (not our own code) from strict's disallow_untyped_calls (mypy/checkexpr.py
# matches by callee fullname).
untyped_calls_exclude = [
  "biom",
  "h5py",
  "mudata",
  "pooch.processors.Unzip",
  "skbio.stats._subsample",
  "skbio.stats.composition._ancombc.ancombc2",
  "skbio.stats.composition._base.tree_basis",
  "sklearn",
  "threadpoolctl",
]
# rules.md R7.2: strict on the package; tests stay unannotated
strict = true
overrides = [
  # treedata 0.3.1 ships no py.typed marker (contracts/tree-access); type-check it anyway
  # instead of ignoring it, so `TreeData` stays a real type under strict mode.
  { module = "treedata", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  { module = "treedata.*", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  # scikit-bio 0.7.4 ships no py.typed marker either; same treatment.
  { module = "skbio", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  { module = "skbio.*", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  # biom-format 2.1.17 ships no py.typed marker either; same treatment.
  { module = "biom", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  { module = "biom.*", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  # h5py 3.16.0 ships no py.typed marker either; same treatment.
  { module = "h5py", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  { module = "h5py.*", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  # mudata 0.4.1 ships no py.typed marker either; same treatment.
  { module = "mudata", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  { module = "mudata.*", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  # pooch 1.9.0 ships no py.typed marker either; same treatment.
  { module = "pooch", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  { module = "pooch.*", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  # scikit-learn 1.9.1 ships no py.typed marker either; same treatment.
  { module = "sklearn", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  { module = "sklearn.*", follow_untyped_imports = true, implicit_reexport = true },
  # threadpoolctl 3.7.0 is a single module, which cannot carry a py.typed marker; same treatment.
  { module = "threadpoolctl", follow_untyped_imports = true },
  # torch is the extra `torch`: absent where prek runs mypy, present where a contributor synced the extra. Not
  # following it makes its names Any in both, so mypy gives one answer, and skips analysing 700 MB of torch.
  { module = "torch", ignore_missing_imports = true, follow_imports = "skip" },
  { module = "torch.*", ignore_missing_imports = true, follow_imports = "skip" },
]

[tool.pytest]
addopts = [
  "--import-mode=importlib",                         # allow using test files with same name
  "--doctest-modules",
  "-m",
  "not network and not r and not torch and not mgm",
]
markers = [
  "golden: compares against R or HUMAnN golden files (contracts/r-golden-parity)",
  "network: downloads data; runs only in the dedicated CI job",
  "r: needs R and rpy2 (extra `r`)",
  "torch: needs PyTorch (extra `torch`); runs only in the ml-extras CI job",
  "mgm: needs the extra `mgm` and downloads MGM's weights; runs only in the ml-extras CI job",
]
strict = true
testpaths = [ "tests", "src/biotapy" ]

[tool.coverage]
run.omit = [
  "**/test_*.py",
]
run.patch = [ "subprocess" ]
run.source = [ "biotapy" ]
# rules.md R11.6 through a line-coverage proxy: coverage.py has no per-function view, so the whole
# package (public and private modules) must reach 90%; CI's `coverage report` step fails below it.
report.fail_under = 90

[tool.cruft]
skip = [
  ".git",
  "tests",
  "src/**/__init__.py",
  "src/**/basic.py",
  "docs/api.md",
  "docs/changelog.md",
  "docs/references.bib",
  "docs/references.md",
  "docs/notebooks/example.ipynb",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "biotapy"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layers (contracts/module-boundaries)"
type = "layers"
containers = [ "biotapy" ]
layers = [
  "(pl) | (ml) | (da)",
  "(tl) | (fn)",
  "(pp)",
  "(datasets)",
  "(io)",
  "_core",
]

requires = ["hatchling>=1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/fake_winreg"]
include = [
    "src/fake_winreg/py.typed",
    "src/fake_winreg/adapters/config/defaultconfig.toml",
    "src/fake_winreg/adapters/config/defaultconfig.d/*.toml",
]

# An allowlist, never a denylist: hatchling reads only the root .gitignore, so tracked working
# files and files hidden through .git/info/exclude or a nested .gitignore (session records,
# review notes, helper scripts) would ship. tests/test_packaging.py builds the sdist and
# refuses any other top-level entry.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
    "/src/fake_winreg",
    "/tests/*.py",
    "/docs",
    "/README.md",
    "/LICENSE",
    "/CHANGELOG.md",
    "/pyproject.toml",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", "W",     # pycodestyle
  "F",           # pyflakes
  "I",           # isort
  "N",           # pep8-naming
  "UP",          # pyupgrade
  "B",           # bugbear
  "A",           # builtins shadowing
  "C4",          # comprehension simplification
  "C90",         # mccabe: cyclomatic complexity <= 10 (the house hard limit)
  "SIM",         # simplification
  "TCH",         # type-checking imports
  "RUF",         # ruff-specific
  "G",           # logging format (catches f-string in logger)
  "T20",         # print statements
  "PTH",         # pathlib preference
  "PLC", "PLE",  # pylint conventions/errors
  "S",           # flake8-bandit security checks
  "PERF",        # performance anti-patterns
  "ERA",         # eradicate dead/commented-out code
  "FBT",         # boolean trap (boolean positional args)
  "PLR",         # pylint refactor
  "PLW",         # pylint warnings
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

# Pydantic resolves field annotations at runtime, so TC00x must not move their imports
# into a TYPE_CHECKING-only block.
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Notebooks: unused imports are often intentional for side effects
"notebooks/*.ipynb" = ["F401", "T201", "PERF203"]
# Tests: assert is standard, test fixtures have passwords, magic values are clearer inline, temp paths are
# fine, deferred imports inside a test body are a deliberate idiom (exercising import/cache behavior)
"tests/*.py" = ["T20", "S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "FBT001", "FBT003", "PLR0913", "PLR2004", "PLC0415"]
# CLI: Click framework injects boolean params; commands have many options
"src/fake_winreg/adapters/cli/**/*.py" = ["FBT001", "FBT002", "PLR0913", "B904"]
# Protocols/adapters: many-param signatures by design
"src/fake_winreg/application/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/fake_winreg/adapters/config/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/fake_winreg/adapters/memory/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
# Persistence: .reg parser complexity, winreg compat errors, many-param backend methods
"src/fake_winreg/adapters/persistence/*.py" = ["PLR0913", "PLR0915", "PLR0911", "PLR2004", "B904", "PERF401", "PERF203", "SIM105", "PLW0602", "PLW2901", "ERA001", "RUF059"]
# Domain API: PascalCase names match winreg module, `type` param matches winreg API
"src/fake_winreg/domain/api.py" = ["N802", "A002", "PLR0913", "ARG001", "PLR2004", "B904", "S101", "PLW0603"]
# Domain registry: many-param functions, perf overhead acceptable, exception chaining not needed for compat
"src/fake_winreg/domain/registry.py" = ["PLR0913", "PERF203", "B904"]
# Domain handles: global statement needed for thread-safe handle counter
"src/fake_winreg/domain/handles.py" = ["PLW0603"]
# Domain memory backend: exception chaining not needed for winreg compat
"src/fake_winreg/domain/memory_backend.py" = ["B904", "PLR0913"]
# Domain validators: magic values from Windows API spec
# Domain validators: magic values from Windows API, sys._getframe for caller name (perf)
"src/fake_winreg/domain/_validators.py" = ["PLR2004", "SLF001"]

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
extraPaths = [
  "src",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = ["--doctest-modules"]
doctest_optionflags = ["ELLIPSIS", "NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
markers = [
  "os_agnostic: test runs on every supported operating system",
  "os_windows: test exercises Windows-only behavior",
  "os_macos: test exercises macOS-only behavior",
  "os_posix: test exercises behavior requiring POSIX semantics",
  "os_linux: test exercises Linux-only behavior",
  "local_only: tests that require the local dev environment (external resources, script composition); skipped in CI",
  "integration: tests requiring external resources (SMTP, databases, APIs); run via 'bmk ti' or 'mktesti.sh'",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
parallel = false
# Use a temp directory for the coverage database to avoid SQLite locking
# issues on network-mounted filesystems. The {envtmpdir} placeholder is
# not supported by coverage.py, so we use an environment variable with
# fallback to a cross-platform temp location via the pytest_configure
# hook in tests/conftest.py. CI also sets COVERAGE_FILE via workflow env.
#
# For local development, the pytest hook automatically redirects to
# tempfile.gettempdir() before pytest-cov creates its Coverage() object.
# This static fallback catches edge cases where coverage is run directly.
data_file = "/tmp/.coverage.fake_winreg"
source = ["src/fake_winreg"]

[tool.coverage.report]
omit = [
  "tests/*",
]
fail_under = 80
show_missing = true

[tool.coverage.json]
output = "coverage.json"
pretty_print = true

[tool.clean]
# Patterns to remove when running `make clean`
patterns = [
  "**/__pycache__",
  ".hypothesis",
  ".import_linter_cache",
  ".pytest_cache",
  ".ruff_cache",
  ".pyright",
  ".mypy_cache",
  ".tox",
  ".nox",
  ".eggs",
  "*.egg-info",
  "build",
  "dist",
  "htmlcov",
  ".coverage",
  "coverage.xml",
  "codecov.sh",
  ".cache",
  "result",
  ".data_arch_violations.json",
]

[tool.git]
# Default git remote for push/release commands
default-remote = "origin"

[tool.scripts.test]
# Configuration for CI/CD test runner
pytest-verbosity = "-vv"
coverage-report-file = "coverage.xml"
src-path = "src"

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "fake_winreg"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain is pure (no adapter dependencies)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "fake_winreg.domain",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "fake_winreg.adapters",
  "fake_winreg.composition",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Clean Architecture layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
  # Composition wires adapters - can import everything
  "fake_winreg.composition",
  # Adapters implement ports - can import application and domain
  "fake_winreg.adapters",
  # Application defines ports - can import domain
  "fake_winreg.application",
  # Domain is pure - bottom layer
  "fake_winreg.domain",
]

[tool.pip-audit]
# Known vulnerabilities to ignore (environment-level packages, not project dependencies)
# PYSEC-2022-42969: py library ReDoS — py 1.11.0 is installed in the development
#   environment but is not a dependency of this project; no fix available.
ignore-vulns = [
  "PYSEC-2022-42969",  # py 1.11.0 — ReDoS, env-only, no fix available
  "CVE-2025-8869",     # pip 24.3.1 — env-only, not a project dependency
  "CVE-2026-1703",     # pip 24.3.1 — env-only, not a project dependency
  "CVE-2026-25990",    # pillow 12.0.0 — env-only, fix in 12.1.1
  "CVE-2026-34515",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — NTLMv2 path info leak on Windows, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34513",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — unbounded DNS cache DoS, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34516",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — excessive multipart headers memory, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34517",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — multipart field read before size check, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34519",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — response reason header injection, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34518",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — cookie/proxy-auth leak on redirect, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34520",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — C parser null bytes in response headers, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34525",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — multiple Host headers allowed, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34521",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — permissive multipart content-type parsing, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-34514",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — bad chunk-ext handling in chunked encoding, fix in 3.13.4
  "CVE-2026-22815",    # aiohttp 3.13.3 — uncapped memory from header/trailer handling, fix in 3.13.4
]

[tool.bashate]
# bashate style settings for .sh files (E003 excluded: indent handled by shfmt)
max-line-length = 120
ignores = ["E003"]

[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "1 day"
exclude-newer-package = {lib-cli-exit-tools = false, lib-layered-config = false, lib-log-rich = false}

# Import Linter Configuration
# =============================
#
# This enforces architectural constraints to maintain code quality.
# Unlike ruff/flake8, import-linter does NOT support inline # noqa-style comments.
# To add exceptions, update the ignore_imports list below.
#
# ADDING EXCEPTIONS:
# -----------------
# If a data source needs to do something "strange" and bypass HTTP centralization:
#
# 1. Add to ignore_imports list in format: module.path -> forbidden_module
#    Example: bolster.data_sources.special_case -> requests
#
# 2. Document WHY in a comment above the ignore entry
#    Example:
#    # Special case: Legacy API requires custom SSL context not supported by shared session
#    bolster.data_sources.legacy_api -> requests
#
# 3. Consider if the "strange" thing should be added to utils.web instead
#
# COMMON EXCEPTIONS:
# -----------------
# - Testing/debugging: Add specific test modules
# - Legacy integrations: Document the technical constraint
# - Performance-critical paths: Explain why centralized session doesn't work
# - External library integration: When the library expects raw requests

[importlinter]
root_package = bolster
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:http-centralization]
name = HTTP centralization - prevent scattered HTTP clients
type = forbidden
source_modules = bolster
forbidden_modules =
    requests
    httpx
ignore_imports =
    # Central HTTP utilities module - allowed to import requests for session creation
    bolster.utils.web -> requests
    # Add exceptions here following the format above
    # Example: bolster.data_sources.special_case -> requests

# Note: urllib.request.urlretrieve is banned separately via ruff's TID251
# (flake8-tidy-imports banned-api, pyproject.toml) -- import-linter can't
# easily handle submodule imports like urllib.request.urlretrieve itself.

# Spawn-site guard (ADR-0050, E015-S01-001 AC 5): the post-export hook is the only process the
# package starts, so ADR-0049's root-mode trust rule on `postexportcommand` is the one gate on
# what root executes. ruff's default rule set is kept; TID251 and PGH004 are added to it.
#
# Coverage limit -- what this does NOT catch (global rule 3):
# - dynamic access: `getattr(os, "system")`, `importlib.import_module`, `__import__`,
#   `eval`/`exec` of source text. No static check resolves these; review is the only check.
# - attribute calls on runtime objects: `loop.subprocess_exec` / `loop.subprocess_shell` on an
#   event loop, `ctypes.CDLL(...).system` once a CDLL object exists. ruff resolves imports,
#   not the type of a value; the banned modules (`ctypes`, `asyncio.subprocess`) catch the
#   import, not a loop method. Review is the only check.
# - `noqa`: `libs/post_export.py` carries `# noqa: TID251` on its `import subprocess` line.
#   ruff reports a banned module only at its import, so that one `noqa` admits EVERY
#   `subprocess` call in post_export.py; a second call there is held by review. Other banned
#   names in that file are still reported. tests/libs/test_post_export.py runs the dev group's
#   ruff with `--select TID251 --ignore-noqa` over the package directory and fails on any
#   report but that import line: `--ignore-noqa` disregards every suppression comment ruff
#   honours (line `noqa`, file-level `ruff: noqa` / `flake8: noqa`, range `ruff: disable[...]`).
#   PGH004 (selected below) reports a blanket `# noqa` / `# ruff: noqa` / `# flake8: noqa`
#   with no code. A suppression outside the package directory is not checked.
# - configuration: tests/libs/test_post_export.py fails if `per-file-ignores` maps TID251
#   (or a prefix of it) to anything but `tests/**`, or if `ignore` / `extend-ignore` (top
#   level or under `lint`) holds TID251 or a prefix. A ruff `exclude` / `extend-exclude`, a
#   second ruff configuration file, or a CLI `--ignore` is not checked.
# - third-party code: what a dependency spawns (the Docker SDK's `ssh` transport, credential
#   helpers) is reviewed, not checked.
# - stdlib code that spawns internally (sprint closure 2026-10-12): tests/libs/test_post_export.py
#   AST-scans the runner's stdlib for modules that import `subprocess` / `_posixsubprocess` or
#   call an `os` spawn primitive, and fails on any such module that is neither banned (whole,
#   or through a parent) nor has a named entry here nor is in its reviewed list. That proves
#   the MODULE is accounted for, not every FUNCTION in it: which functions of `imaplib`,
#   `uuid`, `socketserver` and `http.server` are banned by name is review. The builtin
#   `help()` reaches the `pydoc` pager and is not caught; `asyncio` event-loop methods are the
#   runtime-object gap above. A module that hides the spawn behind another module's call
#   (not an import of `subprocess` or an `os.<spawn>` attribute) is not found by the scan.
# - re-export: `traefik_certificate_exporter.libs.post_export.subprocess` is banned, and ruff
#   resolves `from .post_export import subprocess`, `from . import post_export` then
#   `post_export.subprocess.<x>`, and the absolute forms to it (verified; the suppression test
#   plants them). NOT caught: another module's `subprocess` or `os` attribute
#   (`imaplib.subprocess.Popen`, `socketserver.os.fork`, a dependency's -- verified unreported),
#   and `getattr` / `vars` / `sys.modules` access.
#   Review is the only check for those.
# - the `os` names are hand-listed; tests/libs/test_post_export.py derives the spawn-capable
#   set from `dir(os)`, `dir(posix)` (`dir(nt)` on Windows) and `dir(asyncio)` on the runner
#   and fails on any name missing here (Windows-only `os.startfile` is listed by hand). The
#   modules `posix`, `nt`, `_posixsubprocess`, `asyncio.subprocess`,
#   `concurrent.futures.process`, `ctypes` and `webbrowser` are banned whole (ADR-0050,
#   amendment 2026-10-12) and are required by the same test.
# - the init resolver is Python embedded in an s6 shell script, which ruff does not lint.
[tool.ruff.lint]
extend-select = ["TID251", "PGH004"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
