# editor.formatOnSaveMode = "modificationsIfAvailable"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# The project's one logger lives in sysconst and is imported everywhere else.  Naming it
# here lets ruff see that 'logger.exception(...)' records the traceback -- without it, a
# broad except that does log its failure still trips BLE001.
logger-objects = ["maptasker.src.core.sysconst.logger"]
# PLW1514 (open() with no encoding=) is a preview rule.  On Windows the default encoding is
# the locale's (cp1252), not UTF-8, so an open() with no encoding garbles or rejects a
# non-ASCII Tasker name there and works fine on a Mac -- the kind of bug a Mac never shows.
# explicit-preview-rules keeps every OTHER preview rule off: a preview rule is enabled only
# when it is named in full below, never by a prefix such as 'PL'.
preview = true
explicit-preview-rules = true
select = [
    'A',    # Builtins
    'ANN',  # Annotations
    'ARG',  # Unused arguments
    'B',    # Bugbear
    'BLE',  # Blind except
    'C4',   # Comprehensions
    'C90',  # mccabe
    'COM',  # Commas
    'D1',   # Undocumented public elements
#    'D2',   # Docstring conventions
    'D3',   # Triple double quotes
#   'D4',   # Docstring text format
    'DTZ',  # Datetimes
    'EM',   # Error messages
#    'ERA',  # Commented-out code
#    'EXE',  # Executable
    'F',    # Pyflakes
    'FA',   # __future__ annotations
    'FLY',  # F-strings
    # 'FURB', # Refurb
    'G',    # Logging format
    'I',    # Isort
    'ICN',  # Import conventions
    'INP',  # Disallow PEP-420 (Implicit namespace packages)
    'INT',  # gettext
    'ISC',  # Implicit str concat
    # 'LOG',  # Logging
    'N',    # PEP-8 Naming
    'NPY',  # Numpy
    'PERF', # Unnecessary performance costs
    'PGH',  # Pygrep hooks
    'PIE',  # Unnecessary code
    'PL',   # Pylint
    'PLW1514',  # open() without an explicit encoding (a preview rule; see explicit-preview-rules)
    'PT',   # Pytest
    # 'PTH',  # Use Pathlib
    'PYI',  # Stub files
    'Q',    # Quotes
    'RET',  # Return
    'RUF',  # Ruff
    'RSE',  # Raise
    'S',    # Bandit
    'SIM',  # Code simplification
    'SLF',  # Private member access
    'SLOT', # __slots__
    'T10',  # Debugger
    'T20',  # Print
    'TCH',  # Type checking
    'TID',  # Tidy imports
    'TRY',  # Exception handling
    'UP',   # Pyupgrade
    'W',    # Warnings
    'YTT',  # sys.version
]

ignore = [
    "PLR2004",  # Constant value comparison
    "SIM115",   # Missing "with" on open file
    "S606",     # No shell
    "B009",     # Do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    # -- House style, not debt -------------------------------------------------
    # This project imports ElementTree as 'ET' (and as 'ETW' where a writer-side
    # alias is wanted). Ruff wants one specific alias and objects to the casing of
    # both. 16 occurrences, all deliberate.
    "ICN001",   # unconventional-import-alias
    "N814",     # camelcase-imported-as-constant
    "N817",     # camelcase-imported-as-acronym
    # The logger is written to with f-strings (100+ calls), and an EXPECTED failure --
    # an OSError writing a report, say -- is logged as one line with logger.error, not
    # as a traceback.  Both rules only woke up when logger-objects (above) let ruff
    # recognise the logger at all; nothing they report was newly introduced.
    "G004",     # logging-f-string
    "TRY400",   # error-instead-of-exception
    # -- Formatter conflict ----------------------------------------------------
    # Ruff emits a startup warning when COM812 is selected alongside its formatter,
    # because the two disagree about trailing commas. The formatter already adds
    # them, so the lint rule is redundant as well as conflicting.
    "COM812",   # missing-trailing-comma
    ]

[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
ignore-overlong-task-comments = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-quotes]
docstring-quotes = 'double'
multiline-quotes = 'double'

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# A ceiling, and as low as the code allows: the worst function sits at it.  The target for new code
# is lower; see [tool.complexity-ratchet] below and scripts/complexity_ratchet.py.
max-complexity = 15

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/
'__init__.py' = ['F401','F403','F405',]
'tests/*' = ['ANN', 'ARG', 'INP001', 'S101',]
# scripts/ holds maintainer command-line tools, not a package, and they report by printing.
'scripts/*' = ['INP001', 'T201']
# capture_screens.py imports MapTasker inside its functions on purpose: serve() puts the chosen
# checkout on sys.path (--root) and checks the keyring and HOME are isolated before anything of
# MapTasker's is loaded, and playwright is only there for the driver half of the one file.
# S603: the one subprocess it starts is this same script, from the project's own interpreter.
'scripts/capture_screens.py' = ['PLC0415', 'S603']
# complexity_ratchet.py runs ruff to measure the functions, and coverage_ratchet.py runs coverage,
# each from the project's own interpreter.
'scripts/complexity_ratchet.py' = ['S603']
'scripts/coverage_ratchet.py' = ['S603']

# There is no per-file backlog any more.  Every rule is enforced in every file; a new
# violation fails CI, and the fix belongs in the code rather than in a line added here.
# What is exempted above is exempted on purpose (tests, scripts, __init__.py), with the reason.

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Ceilings, not targets: each is as low as the code allows, so the worst function in the
# project sits right at it and a function any worse than that fails.  They were 15, 20, 10
# and 120 until the largest functions were split up.  What new code is held to is lower still:
# see [tool.complexity-ratchet] below and scripts/complexity_ratchet.py, which also keeps the
# functions that are over it from growing.
max-args = 9
max-branches = 15
max-returns = 9
max-statements = 60
max-locals = 20
max-nested-blocks = 10

# The targets scripts/complexity_ratchet.py holds every function to, as opposed to the ceilings
# above, which nothing may pass.  A function over a target is listed, with how far over it is,
# in scripts/complexity_baseline.json; that list can only shrink.  Fix a function and lower it
# with `uv run python scripts/complexity_ratchet.py --update`.
[tool.complexity-ratchet]
statements = 50  # ruff PLR0915, the pylint default
branches = 12  # ruff PLR0912, the pylint default
complexity = 12  # ruff C901
arguments = 8  # ruff PLR0913
lines = 100  # first line of the def to its last, which ruff has no rule for

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = 'all'

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
# indent-style = "tab"
docstring-code-format = true
# Like Black, automatically detect the appropriate line ending.
line-ending = "auto"
# Stable formatter style. Ruff's preview style is unstable by design -- it can
# change in any minor release -- which is a poor fit for the enforced
# `ruff format --check` gate in CI. Its only visible effect on this project was
# to break the first call of a method chain onto its own line, leaving a bare
# receiver ('ui', 'clean_text') stranded above it.
preview = false

# NOTE: a local, git-ignored pytest.ini used to shadow this block entirely --
# pytest.ini outranks pyproject.toml, so these settings never took effect on a
# developer machine and CI (which has no pytest.ini, it is not in the repo) would
# have run under different settings. This block is now the single source of truth;
# delete any leftover local pytest.ini so both run the same way.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# 52 tests are async and rely on the @pytest.mark.asyncio marker.
asyncio_mode = "strict"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["maptasker"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
# Set from what CI measures: a checkout with no XML/, since XML/ holds personal Tasker
# data and is not in the repository.  Every test that reads sample data reads
# tests/data/synthetic_backup.xml, with any backups in XML/ only as extra material, so a
# developer machine measures the same as CI, with or without XML/.  The floor is about two
# points under what is measured, so a per-Python-version difference cannot fail the build
# while a real regression does.
#
# Raise this as coverage improves -- it is meant to ratchet upward, never down.
#
# This is one number for the whole program, which lets a well-tested layer cover for a
# neglected one.  scripts/coverage_ratchet.py holds each layer (gui, core, mapgen ...) to its
# own floor in scripts/coverage_baseline.json as well; raise those with --update.
#
# History: 36 at 37.58% (754 tests) -> 44 at 45.41%, when the XML-parsing core
# (taskerd/tasks/profiles/projects/scenes/action/actargs) gained direct tests and
# went from 43% to 75% between them -> 42, recalibrated to CI's environment while
# tests still skipped without XML/ -> 56 at 57.5% (1847 tests), once they no longer did
# -> 60 at 62.25% (2300 tests), once the installer, backup fetch, Preferences, Task flags and the
# Fix, Restore and Impact dialogs had direct tests -> 66 at 68.5% (3114 tests), once the Profile, Project and
# Scene editors, label formatting, the AI analysis, the command-line setup and the small utilities did
# -> 73 at 75.8% (3507 tests), once the Edit Profile dialogs, the Find/Replace and Search dialogs and the
# Legacy and Version 2 Scene designers were driven through NiceGUI's user simulation
# -> 78 at 80.6% (3788 tests), once the editor event handlers and the Map/Diagram/Scene-preview/Tree views were too.
# -> 83 at 85.2% (4750 tests), once the start-up, crash handling, safety copies, AI model lists, condition and
# action wording, and the GUI's plain logic and navigation had direct tests.
# Set about two points under, as before.
fail_under = 83
exclude_also = [
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]

# Checks that the annotations ruff's ANN rules require are actually right.  Enforced by
# scripts/typecheck_ratchet.py against scripts/pyright_baseline.json, so only new errors fail.
[tool.pyright]
include = ["maptasker/main.py", "maptasker/src", "scripts"]
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
# Strict mode, file by file.  Basic mode is what the baseline ratchets (see above); these files are
# clean under strict as well, and tests/test_strict_typing.py keeps it that way for new ones: every
# module in maptasker/src is either listed here or in scripts/strict_exempt.json, and a new module
# may not be added to the second list -- it has to be written clean enough to be listed here.
# Moving a module out of the exempt list into this one is the whole of paying one off.  (A module
# whose dicts others index stays out, servicec for one: strict infers them more narrowly than basic.)
strict = [
    "maptasker/src/__init__.py",
    "maptasker/src/analysis/__init__.py",
    "maptasker/src/analysis/livemon.py",
    "maptasker/src/analysis/resrefs.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/__init__.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/actiont.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/assettext.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/caches.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/clock.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/config.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/deprecate.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/error.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/maputil3.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/mtexcept.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/nameattr.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/outdir.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/presave.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/resstore.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/taskervars.py",
    "maptasker/src/core/translator.py",
    "maptasker/src/device/__init__.py",
    "maptasker/src/device/devicecheck.py",
    "maptasker/src/device/devicefiles.py",
    "maptasker/src/device/deviceimport.py",
    "maptasker/src/device/devicemonitor.py",
    "maptasker/src/device/deviceresource.py",
    "maptasker/src/edit/__init__.py",
    "maptasker/src/edit/taskedit_model.py",
    "maptasker/src/gui/__init__.py",

# Import layering, checked by import-linter ('lint-imports') in CI.  The source is split into
# sub-packages of maptasker/src, each layer allowed to import only the ones below it:
#   entry points  -- mapit, progargs, runcli, rungui, clireports: start the program, CLI or GUI
#   gui           -- NiceGUI windows, dialogs and their event handlers
#   device        -- what is done on the Android device, through Tasker's HTTP server
#   mapops        -- bulk replace, refactor, repair, restore, draft; the TaskerNet and readiness tools
#   analysis      -- read-only questions asked of a configuration
#   mapgen : edit -- loading a backup and building the Map from it; the Task/Profile/Project/Scene
#                    editors and Undo.  Siblings: each needs a little of the other.
#   core          -- run state, the Tasker action tables, shared utilities
# so a GUI module cannot be pulled into the core by accident, the core stays usable by the CLI
# and the tests without a web server, and the Map builder never reaches up into an operation.
# Every module in maptasker.src must be in exactly one layer ("exhaustive"): a new package fails
# the check until it is placed.  Import cycles, and the imports deferred into functions to break
# them, are ratcheted separately by tests/test_import_structure.py.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "maptasker"
include_external_packages = true
# An import under "if TYPE_CHECKING:" never runs, so it can neither pull a module in at
# runtime nor close a cycle -- it is the sanctioned way to name a type from a module that
# must not be imported for real.
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Entry points above the GUI, the GUI above the operations, the operations above the core"
type = "layers"
containers = ["maptasker.src"]
exhaustive = true
layers = [
    "mapit : progargs : runcli : rungui : clireports",
    "gui",
    "device",
    "mapops",
    "analysis",
    "mapgen : edit",
    "core",
]

# A Scene is one of two kinds, and what a caller does with one should not depend on which.
# scenemodel is where that is decided (see its header): the analyses, the editing core
# (sceneedit), the Map output (scenes) and the bulk replace (mapswap) all ask it.  What is
# left importing a kind's editor directly is the code that edits that kind and nothing else --
# its designer, the property dialogs and the preview -- and this keeps it that list.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Only the Legacy Scene designer and its dialogs import the Legacy Scene editor"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["maptasker.src.edit.sceneedit_legacy"]
allowed_importers = [
    "maptasker.src.gui.guiwins",
    "maptasker.src.gui.guiwins_designer_legacy",
    "maptasker.src.gui.guiwins_legacyarg",
    "maptasker.src.gui.guiwins_sceneprops",
    "maptasker.src.edit.scenemodel",
    "maptasker.src.gui.userintr_editors",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Only the Version 2 Scene designer and its preview import the Version 2 Scene editor"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["maptasker.src.edit.sceneedit_v2"]
allowed_importers = [
    "maptasker.src.gui.guiwins_designer_v2",
    "maptasker.src.gui.guiwins_views",
    "maptasker.src.edit.scenemodel",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Only the GUI and the entry points import NiceGUI"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["nicegui"]
allowed_importers = [
    "maptasker.src.mapit",
    "maptasker.src.progargs",
    "maptasker.src.runcli",
    "maptasker.src.rungui",
    "maptasker.src.gui",
]
# restart_program_subprocess stops the GUI's own server when a restart is started from a
# button.  It imports NiceGUI only when an event loop is running -- that is, only when the
# GUI is up -- so the core still runs without it.
ignore_imports = [
    "maptasker.src.core.maputils -> nicegui",
]

# import-linter contracts for the cellcraft backend.
#
# Run (once import-linter is installed) from the backend/ directory:
#     lint-imports
#
# Purpose: define the architectural import contracts up front (during PR-1,
# the safety-net phase) so they can be switched on as the refactoring lands.
#
# STATUS: ACTIVATED in PR-2 (phase-1-app-assembly). `app.worker` now exists and the
# Celery worker boots via `celery -A app.worker.app worker` — it no longer imports
# the web layer (`app.main`). See the contract below.
#
# NOTE on scope: TIGHTENED in PR-4 (phase-2-domain-skeleton). The old
# `app.routes` web package was removed; the FastAPI app is now assembled in
# `app.api` from per-domain routers (`app.<domain>.router`). The worker must not
# depend on any of those web-facing modules. It may still import each domain's
# non-router modules (crud/utils/models/schemas), which is intentional.

[importlinter]
root_package = app

[importlinter:contract:no-web-in-worker]
name = worker must not depend on the web layer
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.worker
forbidden_modules =
    app.main
    app.api
    app.auth.router
    app.admin.router
    app.datatable.router
    app.file.router
    app.plugin.router
    app.task.router
    app.version.router
    app.workflow.router

[importlinter:contract:shared-is-domain-agnostic]
name = shared infrastructure must not depend on any domain
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    app.shared
forbidden_modules =
    app.auth
    app.user
    app.admin
    app.datatable
    app.file
    app.plugin
    app.task
    app.version
    app.workflow

[tool.importlinter]
# run with 'lint-imports' or 'import-linter lint'
# https://import-linter.readthedocs.io/en/stable/contract_types.html
root_package = "sedrila"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "SeDriLa layering"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    # Layers listed highest to lowest; 'a | b' means 'independent' (may not import), 'a : b' means 'siblings' (may import)
    # Modules not listed are unconstrained.
    "sedrila.__main__",  # L6: main
    "sedrila.cmd.author : sedrila.cmd.student : sedrila.cmd.instructor : sedrila.cmd.maintainer : sedrila.cmd.evaluator : sedrila.cmd.server : sedrila.cmd.cli",  # L5.2: commands
    "sedrila.subcmd.rename | sedrila.webapp",  # L5.1: subcommands
    "sedrila.course.course : sedrila.course.coursebuilder : sedrila.course.course_si : sedrila.course.participant : sedrila.course.programchecker : sedrila.course.repo : sedrila.course.glossary : sedrila.course.report",  # L4: course
    "sedrila.framework.macros : sedrila.framework.markdown : sedrila.framework.elements : sedrila.framework.directory : sedrila.framework.partbuilder : sedrila.framework.macroexpanders",  # L3: framework
    "sedrila.mech.replacements | sedrila.mech.snippetchecker | sedrila.mech.linkchecker | sedrila.mech.protocolchecker",  # L2.3: mechanisms
    "sedrila.base2.argparser",  # L2.2: mechanisms base 
    "sedrila.base2.constants : sedrila.base2.html",  # L2.1: domain base
    "sedrila.base.cache | sedrila.base.sgit | sedrila.base.mycrypt",  # L1: domain-independent utils
    "sedrila.base.base", # L0: generic utils
]
ignore_imports = [
    # Function-level ("lazy") imports violating the layering, ignored for now: import-linter sees them like any
    # top-level import, but they are mostly workarounds for import cycles. Top-level violations are NOT listed here.
    # If one of these entries stops matching (import removed), import-linter complains; delete the entry then.
    "sedrila.framework.directory -> sedrila.course.course",
    "sedrila.framework.directory -> sedrila.course.coursebuilder",
    "sedrila.framework.directory -> sedrila.course.glossary",
    "sedrila.framework.elements -> sedrila.course.course",
    "sedrila.framework.partbuilder -> sedrila.course.course",
    "sedrila.framework.partbuilder -> sedrila.course.coursebuilder",
    "sedrila.framework.macroexpanders -> sedrila.course.course",
    "sedrila.framework.macroexpanders -> sedrila.course.coursebuilder",
    "sedrila.framework.macroexpanders -> sedrila.course.programchecker",
    "sedrila.mech.snippetchecker -> sedrila.framework.macros",
]

include = [
    "/src",
    "/tests",
    "/README.md",

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Pytest's DEFAULT norecursedirs contains ``build``, which silently shadowed
# the real test package ``tests/build/`` — nothing in it was ever collected by
# a bare ``pytest`` (issue #776). This is the default list minus ``build``.
# If you add a test directory, make sure its name is not on this list.
norecursedirs = ["*.egg", ".*", "_darcs", "CVS", "dist", "node_modules", "venv", "{arch}"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "slow: mark tests as slow to run",
    "db_only: mark tests that use real database but not real workers",
    "integration: mark tests as integration tests requiring full worker setup",
    "e2e: mark tests as end-to-end tests that test full course conversion",
    "docker: mark tests that require Docker daemon (excluded by default)",
    "recordings: mark tests for the recordings module",
    # ``serial`` pins a test onto a single xdist worker (via the ``--dist
    # loadgroup`` scheduler below). Use it for tests that spawn heavyweight
    # external processes — a mitmdump proxy, a Jupyter kernel, a worker pool —
    # whose simultaneous startup across many xdist workers oversubscribes the
    # box and produces contention flakes (readiness ceilings expiring, worker
    # registration starvation, port races). An optional argument names the
    # RESOURCE CLASS: ``@pytest.mark.serial`` (default group) vs
    # ``@pytest.mark.serial("subproc")`` / ``("workerpool")`` / ``("port")``.
    # Same-class tests share one group (run one-at-a-time on one worker);
    # DIFFERENT classes get different groups that run on different workers
    # concurrently — so e.g. the subprocess-spawning family doesn't serialize
    # behind the worker-pool family. The marker -> xdist_group mapping lives in
    # ``tests/conftest.py`` (``pytest_collection_modifyitems``) via
    # ``tests/xdist_group_helpers.serial_group_name``.
    "serial: pin a heavy/contention-prone test to a single xdist worker (optional resource-class arg)",
    # ``flaky`` opts a test into pytest-rerunfailures' SCOPED rerun: there is
    # deliberately NO global ``--reruns`` in addopts (that would rerun every
    # test and mask real regressions), so only tests carrying
    # ``@pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=N, only_rerun=[...])`` are retried, and only
    # when the failure matches the contention exception signature. It is a thin
    # SAFETY NET over the structural fixes, not a substitute for them — a test
    # that reruns often (surfaced by ``-rR`` in the summary) is a signal to fix
    # the root cause, not to widen the net. Reserve it for the known
    # thread-starvation / subprocess-contention families.
    "flaky: scoped pytest-rerunfailures retry for known-contention tests",
    # ``load_sensitive`` tags whole suites whose runtime or correctness depends
    # on machine load — heavyweight-process spawners (worker pools, real
    # kernels) and wall-clock-timing asserters (busy-retry backoffs, threaded
    # shutdowns). The pre-push hook excludes them (``-m "not load_sensitive"``,
    # see scripts/run_pytest_hook.py) so the local gate stays a fast,
    # deterministic tier; CI and a plain ``uv run pytest`` run them
    # unconditionally. The directory set lives in ``tests/conftest.py``
    # (``LOAD_SENSITIVE_TEST_DIRS``); tagging there is automatic, so a test
    # added under one of those directories needs no marker of its own.
    "load_sensitive: heavyweight-process or wall-clock-timing suite, excluded from the pre-push gate only",
]
# Run fast unit tests by default, skip db_only, integration, slow, e2e, and docker tests.
# Use -n auto for parallel execution via pytest-xdist (pass -n0 to disable).
# --dist loadgroup keeps the default load-balancing scheduler but honours the
# ``xdist_group`` mark that the ``serial`` marker maps to, so contention-prone
# tests are serialized onto one worker instead of racing each other.
# ``-rR`` surfaces pytest-rerunfailures' rerun summary so a scoped ``flaky``
# retry is never silent (anti-masking: a frequently-rerun test is a signal to
# fix the root cause). There is intentionally no ``--reruns`` here — reruns are
# opt-in per test via ``@pytest.mark.flaky`` only.
addopts = "-n auto --dist loadgroup -rR -m 'not slow and not db_only and not integration and not e2e and not docker'"
# Per-test timeout — converts a hung test into a prompt, attributable failure
# instead of a 10-minute stall (the old 600s default, which turned a contention
# hang on the pre-push gate into a Ctrl-C + manual re-run). 120s matches CI's
# fast-suite ``--timeout=120`` (.github/workflows/ci.yml), the authoritative
# ceiling on 2-4 vCPU hardware: the slowest legitimate fast test measures ~5.5s
# (16-worker dev box) / ~11s (64-worker contention), so 120s is a >10x backstop,
# NOT a performance gate. The heavier non-fast suites need more headroom, so
# ``tests/conftest.py`` bumps their per-test timeout at collection time —
# integration -> 240, e2e/slow/docker -> 600, matching CI — so running them
# locally (a non-default ``-m`` selection) never false-kills against this
# fast-suite default. (A ``timeout`` marker takes precedence over this value.)
timeout = 120
timeout_method = "thread"  # Works better with asyncio tests
# Filter out deprecation warnings from third-party packages

    # ZMQ/Jupyter Windows-specific warning about Proactor event loop
    "ignore:Proactor event loop does not implement add_reader:RuntimeWarning",
]

]

# No local tag: the Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) creates the

# commit is never tagged. bump-my-version only produces the `Bump version …`
# commit that the workflow keys on. (tag_name documents the format the server
# uses; it is inert while tag = false.)

[[tool.bumpversion.files]]
# AGENTS.md is the single source of truth (CLAUDE.md is a thin @AGENTS.md
# pointer), so the version line that bump-my-version updates lives here.

search = "**Version**: {current_version}"
replace = "**Version**: {new_version}"

[[tool.bumpversion.files]]
filename = "docs/developer-guide/architecture.md"

[[tool.bumpversion.files]]

# uv.lock records the editable project's own version. If we don't update
# it here, `uv run` resyncs uv.lock on the next invocation, which lands
# during the bumpversion pre-commit hook and trips "files were modified
# by this hook". Scope the replacement to the project's own [[package]]
# block via the unique two-line name+version pair.
[[tool.bumpversion.files]]
filename = "uv.lock"
search = """name = "coding-academy-lecture-manager"
version = "{current_version}\""""
replace = """name = "coding-academy-lecture-manager"
version = "{new_version}\""""

[dependency-groups]
# PEP-735 dependency groups. uv auto-syncs the `dev` group on `uv run`
# and `uv sync`, so tools listed here are always present in `.venv`
# without any `--extra` flag. This group lists:
#   1. Dev tools (pytest, ruff, mypy, etc.) — a full mirror of
#      `[project.optional-dependencies] dev`, so that `pip install -e
#      ".[dev]"` and `pip install -e ".[all]"` keep working for non-uv
#      users. The [all] extra references [project.optional-
#      dependencies] dev via self-reference syntax, so the mirror must
#      stay in sync with this list.
#   2. Self-referencing extras needed for the fast test suite. The
#      notebook/plantuml/drawio/recordings/slides/mcp/voiceover/etc.
#      extras contain packages that several test modules import at
#      collection time (e.g. tests/workers/notebook imports nbformat
#      from the [notebook] extra), so without them `uv sync` would
#      leave the fast suite broken. The course-runtime ML stack is not
#      here (and is no longer a clm extra as of 1.19) — it's huge,
#      course-runtime-only, and lives in the separate course venv.
#      `replay` (mitmproxy + pyyaml + filelock) is included so the
#      HTTP-replay / cassette tests actually *run* in the fast suite
#      instead of silently `pytest.importorskip`-skipping: without it,
#      `uv sync` would leave the http-replay surface untested in the
#      pre-commit gate.
# See docs/proposals/PRE_COMMIT_HOOK_HARDENING.md (Fix 1) for rationale.
dev = [
    # This is the group `uv sync` installs by default (local dev / worktree
    # setup / pre-push gate). The course-runtime ML stack is absent (huge,
    # course-runtime-only, py3.14-blocked, and no longer a clm extra as of 1.19 —
    # it lives in the course venv, see course-runtime-requirements.txt), and
    # JupyterLite is not a clm extra at all — its build runs in an isolated `uvx`
    # tool env (Wave 2a), so nothing here pulls jupyterlite-core/empack into
    # clm's resolution.
    "coding-academy-lecture-manager[notebook,plantuml,drawio,recordings,slides,mcp,summarize,voiceover,replay,tui,web]",
    # Keep this environment on a modern Click (the CliRunner 8.2+ API).
    "click>=8.2",
    "pytest>=7.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.21",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0",
    "pytest-mock>=3.12.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.2.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5.0",
    "pytest-rerunfailures>=14.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.148.2",
    "mypy>=1.0",
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
    "import-linter>=2.3",  # layer contracts (Phase 8 S6, #802); run: uv run lint-imports
    "respx>=0.20.0",
    "pre-commit>=4.5.0",
]

[tool.uv]
# Only allow packages published before this instant (supply-chain safety).
# Update with: python scripts/update_exclude_newer.py [DATE]
# (also refreshes uv.lock; see scripts/check_exclude_newer.py for drift check)
# Must stay in uv's canonical `<date>T00:00:00Z` form and exactly equal
# uv.lock's [options].exclude-newer, or `uv sync --locked` rejects the
# lockfile on a clean checkout (issue #524).
exclude-newer = "2026-05-29T00:00:00Z"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import-linter: the layer contracts (Phase 8 S6, #802). The documented stack
# is core <- infrastructure <- workers <- extensions <- cli (each layer may
# import only BELOW itself); extensions and the CLI are unconstrained sources.
# The extension list is static here (import-linter cannot derive it): when a
# new top-level package is added under src/clm, add it to the forbidden list
# of the third contract. Runs in CI's lint job and as a pre-commit hook
# (`uv run lint-imports`). Grimp sees function-body and TYPE_CHECKING imports,
# so lazy imports cannot dodge these contracts; string-based importlib dodges
# are guarded by tests/test_architecture_contracts.py.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "clm"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered: core below infrastructure below workers below build"
type = "layers"
layers = ["clm.build", "clm.workers", "clm.infrastructure", "clm.core"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Constrained layers never import the CLI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["clm.core", "clm.infrastructure", "clm.workers", "clm.build"]
forbidden_modules = ["clm.cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Constrained layers never import extension packages"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["clm.core", "clm.infrastructure", "clm.workers", "clm.build"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "clm.cohort_calendar",
    "clm.mcp",
    "clm.notebooks",
    "clm.recordings",
    "clm.release",
    "clm.slides",
    "clm.snapshot",
    "clm.voiceover",
    "clm.web",
]

[project]
name = "sophios"
dynamic = ["version"]
authors = [{name = "Jake Fennick", email = "jake.fennick@axleinfo.com"}]
description = "DSL for inferring the edges of a CWL workflow DAG"
classifiers = [
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
]
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    # NOTE: This 'graphviz' refers to the python bindings to the underlying
    # system binary graphviz package (i.e. the `dot` executable) which we need to
    # install separately using either `conda install graphviz` or `sudo apt install graphviz`.
    # This 'graphviz' is equivalent to `conda install python-graphviz` or
    # `sudo apt install python3-graphviz` ONLY.
    # 3.1.20241217163858 names a singularity image with no tag `<name>_latest`, as
    # cwl-docker-extract does (it pulls `<name>:latest`); before it, the pulled
    # image is not found and a run with --disable-pull fails.
    "cwltool>=3.1.20241217163858",
    "graphviz",
    "jsonschema",
    "pyyaml",
    "ruamel.yaml",
    "requests",
    "mergedeep",
    "cwl-utils>=0.32",
    # CommandInputParameter attr changed from `type_` to `type` and back to `type_`
    # between versions 0.30, 0.31, 0.32
    # See https://github.com/common-workflow-language/cwl-utils/releases/
    #
    # No upper bound. 0.43+ will not read a document whose embedded process
    # declares a `cwlVersion` other than the root's, but the fix for that is
    # ours: inlining no longer copies the field into a `run:`, which is what
    # the spec says a packed document means anyway. Pinning would only hide
    # that, and an upper bound on a package whose parsers are regenerated from
    # an evolving schema costs more than it saves. See
    # https://github.com/common-workflow-language/cwl-utils/issues/470.
    "pydantic>=2.6",
    "pydantic[email]",
    "docker",
    # FYI also need uidmap to run podman rootless
    "podman",
    # We are using the official release for these packages for now
    "toil[cwl]",
    "fastapi",
    "uvicorn",
    "aiofiles"
]

[tool.setuptools_scm]
# A release is the tag vX.Y.Z that release-please puts on master.
tag_regex = "^v(?P<version>[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(?:[.-]dev[0-9]+)?)$"
version_scheme = "no-guess-dev"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"
# With no release tag in reach (a fork, a shallow clone, or master before its
# first tag), git builds count from this base: 0.6.0.post0.devN after 0.6.0.
# Without git at all it is the version itself. release-please moves it to each
# new release through the marker below, so it always names the last release.
fallback_version = "0.6.0.post0.dev0"  # x-release-please-version
# The version is also written beside the code, so sophios.__version__ describes
# the files that are running rather than whichever install the metadata names.
version_file = "src/sophios/_version.py"
version_file_template = """\"\"\"The version setuptools-scm resolved when this copy of Sophios was built.\"\"\"
__version__ = "{version}"
"""
write_to_source = true

# Disallows defining functions with incomplete type annotations.

# Warns about unneeded `# type: ignore` comments.
warn_unused_ignores = true

warn_return_any = true

# A regular expression that matches file names, directory names and paths which

[tool.pip-audit]

[tool.importlinter]
# Пакеты лежат в src/, но импортируются как верхний уровень (src в sys.path).
root_packages = ["cfg", "domain", "infrastructure", "parsers", "services"]

# Слои сверху вниз: композиционный корень → сервисы → парсеры → инфраструктура → домен.
# Внутри одного слоя (cfg и services) импорты разрешены, между слоями — только вниз.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Слои: cfg/services -> parsers -> infrastructure -> domain"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "cfg",
    "services",
    "parsers",
    "infrastructure",
    "domain",
]
broken_contract_guidance = "Импорт из слоя выше запрещён: развернуть зависимость или передать объект через параметр."

# Строгая форма правил: domain — чистый слой без IO.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain не зависит от инфраструктуры, парсеров, сервисов и композиционного корня"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["infrastructure", "parsers", "services", "cfg"]
broken_contract_guidance = "Домен не знает про внешние слои: описать порт в domain/protocols.py и внести реализацию в infrastructure."

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Инфраструктура не зависит от прикладных слоёв"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["infrastructure"]
forbidden_modules = ["parsers", "services", "cfg"]
broken_contract_guidance = "Инфраструктура — адаптеры: прикладные слои вызывают её, а не наоборот."

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Парсеры не знают про композиционный корень и сервисы"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["parsers"]
forbidden_modules = ["cfg", "services"]
broken_contract_guidance = "Зависимости парсера передаются аргументом или через порт домена; сборку делает src/cfg."

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

[project]
name = "smacc"
description = "Sleep manipulation and communication clickything"
readme = "README.md"
# Build/runtime Python is pinned to 3.13 via .python-version. The minimum OS is
# Windows 10, set by Qt 6 (see the PyQt6 dependency note below).
requires-python = ">=3.13"
license = { text = "GPL-3.0-or-later" }
authors = [{ name = "Remington Mallett", email = "mallett.remy@gmail.com" }]
dynamic = ["version"]
classifiers = [
    "Environment :: Win32 (MS Windows)",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows :: Windows 10",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows :: Windows 11",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: GNU General Public License v3 or later (GPLv3+)",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
]
dependencies = [
    # BlinkStick LED device (visual cues). Its backend, pywinusb, is Windows-only,
    # so scope to win32 to keep the cross-platform lock resolving everywhere.
    "blinkstick; sys_platform == 'win32'",
    # Validates a .smacc against the model-derived JSON Schema in `SMACC validate`
    # (#302). Imported lazily and optionally — the command degrades to the model's
    # own validators if it (or its rpds-py backend) isn't available in a build.
    "jsonschema>=4.26.0",
    "numpy",
    # Read-only view of the Windows volume mixer (Core Audio COM); Windows-only, so
    # scope to win32 like blinkstick. Pulls in comtypes.
    "pycaw; sys_platform == 'win32'",
    "pylsl",
    # Optional hardware TTL trigger output to a USB-serial trigger box (#28). Pure
    # Python and cross-platform, so it isn't platform-scoped; imported lazily and a
    # no-op unless a study enables serial triggers.
    "pyserial",
    "pyyaml",
    # Qt 6 GUI toolkit. Qt 6 requires Windows 10+, which is why SMACC's floor is
    # Windows 10 (Qt5/PyQt5 was the last line that still ran on Windows 8.1). PyQt6
    # pulls in PyQt6-Qt6 (the Qt libraries, incl. QtMultimedia) and PyQt6-sip. The
    # >=6.8 floor is for QStyleHints.unsetColorScheme (the "match system" theme, #315).
    "PyQt6>=6.8",
    "scipy",
    "sounddevice",
    "soundfile>=0.12",
    # The EEG Annotator (#136) ships inside the one SMACC binary — it is no longer
    # a separate optional exe — so its stack is a core dependency. MNE reads and
    # writes recordings (imported lazily, in smacc.eeg.io only); pyqtgraph renders
    # the traces; matplotlib backs figure export (#180). MNE is heavy, but the
    # onedir build imports it lazily off disk, so a session that never opens the
    # Annotator never loads it.
    "matplotlib>=3.7",
    "mne>=1.6",
    "pyqtgraph>=0.13",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# The docs site and the single-file PDF manual are built with Quarto (#259) — a
# standalone binary (installed separately, not from PyPI) that renders both the HTML
# site and the Typst PDF from docs/, with no plugin stack or system libraries. The
# only Python the docs build needs is:
docs = [
    # pdf check: scripts/check_manual.py reads the built manual to guard against a
    # renderer silently truncating it (#250). Was transitive via mkdocs-exporter;
    # now a direct dependency.
    "pypdf",
    # Markdown formatter (the docs counterpart to ruff), run in CI and pre-commit.
    # gfm covers tables/autolinks; frontmatter leaves YAML front matter alone. Lists
    # nest with standard two-space CommonMark indentation — Quarto/Pandoc renders that
    # natively, so the MkDocs-era four-space style (and the mdformat-mkdocs plugin that
    # enforced it) retired with MkDocs (#265). Base mdformat leaves Quarto `:::`
    # callouts and `{...}` attributes intact.
    "mdformat",
    "mdformat-gfm",
    "mdformat-frontmatter",
]
dev = [
    "pytest",
    # GUI tests run headless via the Qt "offscreen" platform (set in
    # tests/conftest.py); pytest-qt supplies the qtbot/qapp fixtures and manages
    # the QApplication lifecycle. pytest-cov reports coverage of the now-tested
    # Qt layer (see the test job in .github/workflows/ci.yml).
    "pytest-qt",
    "pytest-cov",
    "ruff",
    "mypy",
    # Enforces the hardware-free boundary of the Study Editor and its model: a
    # static import-graph contract (see [tool.importlinter]) that fails CI if
    # smacc.studyconfig ever reaches the session/panels/audio stack (#301).
    "import-linter",
    "pre-commit",
    "pyinstaller",
    "types-PyYAML",
]

# Optional automated sleep staging in the EEG Annotator (#226): YASA scores the
# night and SMACC shows it as a read-only overlay beside the manual hypnogram.
# Deliberately its OWN extra — NOT in core `dependencies`, NOT in `dev` — because
# YASA's tree is heavy and PyInstaller-hostile (lightgbm's compiled lib, numba +
# llvmlite's bundled LLVM ~120 MB, scikit-learn, pandas, plus ~35 MB of pretrained
# .joblib classifiers). A plain `uv sync` and a source checkout stay lean; only the
# frozen release build opts in (release.yml syncs `--extra yasa` and PyInstaller
# collects yasa's data + the lightgbm/llvmlite native libs). smacc.eeg.yasa_staging
# imports it lazily, so the Annotator hides the feature when it is absent. YASA
# pulls mne/numpy/scipy/matplotlib, which SMACC already bundles, so only the ML
# stack is marginal weight.
yasa = ["yasa"]

# A GUI launcher (no console window): exposes a `smacc` command after install.
# `python -m smacc` runs the same main(); see src/smacc/__main__.py.
[project.gui-scripts]
smacc = "smacc.__main__:main"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/remrama/smacc"
Source = "https://github.com/remrama/smacc"
"Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/remrama/smacc/issues"
"Release Notes" = "https://github.com/remrama/smacc/releases"

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = { attr = "smacc.__version__" }

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
smacc = ["assets/*", "assets/biocals/*", "assets/cues/*", "assets/surveys/*"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 88
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "W"]
# The formatter owns line length; it won't split string literals/comments,
# so leave E501 to the formatter rather than flagging unsplittable lines.
ignore = ["E501"]

[tool.ruff.format]
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "lf"
quote-style = "double"

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
ignore_missing_imports = true
files = ["src"]

# Static import-graph contracts (run by `lint-imports` in CI's quality job).
# These lock in architectural boundaries that a stray import would otherwise
# erode silently — caught here, before code review, not at runtime.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "smacc"
# Required so the external audio/marker libraries in the contract below
# (sounddevice, pylsl) are tracked in the graph; without it the contracts would
# only see smacc's own modules.
include_external_packages = true

# The Study Editor authors a study by editing the pure StudyConfig model; it must
# never be able to open an audio stream, meter a mic, or fire an LSL marker. We
# make that true *by construction* rather than by discipline: forbid both the model
# and the editor window from importing the run-time stack at all. With no import
# path to sounddevice/pylsl/the session, no code path can reach the hardware — the
# guarantee can't be forgotten in a future edit.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The Study Editor never reaches the hardware/run-time stack"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["smacc.studyconfig", "smacc.studyeditor"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "smacc.session",
    "smacc.gui",
    "smacc.panels",
    "sounddevice",
    "pylsl",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["smacc"]
# Store repo-relative paths so Codecov maps the Windows CI run onto the source
# tree (src/smacc/…) instead of dropping the report for unmatched paths.
relative_files = true
# Coverage gating (project/patch targets) lives in codecov.yml, not here.

requires = ["hatchling >= 1.32", "hatchling-autoextras-hook>=0.1.3"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build]
sources = ["src"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
only-include = ["src"]

[tool.hatch.metadata.hooks.autoextras]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import Linter: architectural contracts. Run with `make lint-imports`.
#
# The contracts describe the structure we want. If one breaks, change the import,
# not the contract. Any import that is deliberately exempt is listed under
# `ignore_imports` with a comment saying why. import-linter reports an entry that
# no longer matches anything as an error, so delete it when the import goes away.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "clientele"
include_external_packages = true

# --- Package-wide structure ------------------------------------------------

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "runtime-layers"
name = "Runtime layers: features -> api -> http"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "clientele.testing",
    "clientele.graphql | clientele.retries | clientele.cache",
    "clientele.api",
    "clientele.http",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
clientele.http is the transport: it sends requests and returns Responses. clientele.api builds
clients on top of it, and the optional features build on clientele.api. Lower layers must not
import higher ones. If you need something from a higher layer, move it down or pass it in.
"""

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "runtime-independent-of-codegen"
name = "The runtime doesn't depend on the code generator, CLI or mypy plugin"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "clientele.api",
    "clientele.http",
    "clientele.cache",
    "clientele.retries",
    "clientele.graphql",
    "clientele.testing",
    "clientele.schemas",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "clientele.cli",
    "clientele.generators",
    "clientele.mypy",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
Generated clients import the runtime, and are installed without the [cli] extra. The runtime
must work without the generator, so it can't import it.
"""

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "codegen-independent-of-runtime"
name = "The code generator and CLI don't depend on the runtime"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "clientele.cli",
    "clientele.generators",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "clientele.api",
    "clientele.http",
    "clientele.cache",
    "clientele.retries",
    "clientele.graphql",
    "clientele.testing",
    "clientele.schemas",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
The generator writes source code that imports the runtime; it never needs the runtime itself.
Keeping them apart lets either change without the other.
"""

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "runtime-base-dependencies"
name = "The runtime only imports its base (non-optional) dependencies"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "clientele.api",
    "clientele.http",
    "clientele.cache",
    "clientele.retries",
    "clientele.graphql",
    "clientele.testing",
    "clientele.schemas",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    # The [cli] extra
    "click",
    "rich",
    "cicerone",
    "jinja2",
    "yaml",
    # Optional HTTP clients, and mypy, which only runs our plugin
    "aiohttp",
    "requests",
    "niquests",
    "mypy",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # ALLOWED: each optional backend wraps its own client library. Nothing else may import these
    # backends (see the opt-in-modules contract), so `import clientele` never needs them.
    "clientele.http.aiohttp_backend -> aiohttp",
    "clientele.http.requests_backend -> requests",
    "clientele.http.niquests_backend -> niquests",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
`pip install clientele` only installs httpx2, pydantic, pydantic-settings and stamina. Anything
else imported by the runtime fails for users who didn't install the extra. Add the dependency to
[project.dependencies] if it's really needed, or keep the import inside an opt-in module.
"""

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "opt-in-modules"
name = "Opt-in modules are only imported by the user"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = [
    "clientele.http.aiohttp_backend",
    "clientele.http.requests_backend",
    "clientele.http.niquests_backend",
    "clientele.mypy",
]
allowed_importers = []
broken_contract_guidance = """
These modules import packages that aren't base dependencies (aiohttp, requests, niquests, mypy).
Users opt in by importing them directly, or mypy loads the plugin. Importing one from elsewhere in
clientele would make every user need that package.
"""

# --- Inside packages -------------------------------------------------------

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "api-layers"
name = "api: client -> request handling -> building blocks"
type = "layers"
containers = ["clientele.api"]
layers = [
    "client",
    "request_context | config",
    "stream | params | exceptions",
    "type_utils",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "http-layers"
name = "http: backends build on HTTPBackend and are independent"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "clientele.http.httpx_backend | clientele.http.aiohttp_backend | clientele.http.requests_backend | clientele.http.niquests_backend | clientele.http.fake_backend",
    "clientele.http.backends",
    "clientele.http.response",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
Each backend depends only on the HTTPBackend interface and Response, so backends can be added,
removed or swapped without touching each other.
"""

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "codegen-layers"
name = "Code generation: CLI -> generators -> shared -> OpenAPI compatibility"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "clientele.cli",
    "clientele.generators.api | clientele.generators.basic",
    "clientele.generators.shared",
    "clientele.generators.cicerone_compat",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
Code shared by the api and basic generators belongs in clientele.generators.shared, not in one
generator imported by the other.
"""

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "no-cycles"
name = "No import cycles inside subpackages"
type = "acyclic_siblings"
# The top level is covered by runtime-layers and the forbidden contracts above, so its known
# cycles are only listed once.
ancestors = [
    "clientele.api",
    "clientele.cache",
    "clientele.generators",
    "clientele.http",
]

name = "Layers Contract"
type = "layers"

    "src.tools",
    "src.models",

/**
 * Layer rules as a ratchet (#329). HACER's three layers — pure logic ← state ← rendering — were a
 * convention until now: the foundation audit found 16 production cross-layer edges and 3 cycles
 * passing a green `lint` (docs/research/2026-09-21-foundation-audit/REPORT.md §4-§6).
 *
 * The rules below are the wall. Today's violations live in `.dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json`
 * and are ignored at lint time; a *new* one fails. The baseline is only ever rewritten with
 * `--baseline-mode shrink-only` (`pnpm run lint:layers:shrink`), so a violation that has been fixed
 * can never be re-added. Run it, and read the count, with `pnpm run lint:layers`.
 *
 * Adding a RULE is the one exception: its existing violations have to enter the baseline before the
 * ratchet can hold them, which shrink-only cannot do. Record them once, with the rule, in the same
 * commit — `pnpm exec depcruise src --config .dependency-cruiser.cjs --baseline` — and say in the
 * commit message how many rows that added. From then on the rule shrinks like every other.
 *
 * That same command absorbs whatever *else* is broken in the tree at that moment, and no one reads
 * this baseline in a PR: `.gitattributes` keeps it `linguist-generated`, which is deliberate (#406
 * — a baseline write rewrites the whole file, so a line review sees churn, not meaning) but does
 * take it out of review. So this paragraph is not the fence; the fence is the `ratchet` rule in
 * `scripts/pr-hygiene.logic.mjs`, which compares the committed rows against the PR's merge base
 * and fails any row that arrives under a rule name **this file does not newly declare in the same
 * PR**, naming it — whatever the row *count* did, so fixing one violation while absorbing another
 * does not buy a pass.
 *
 * That the declaration has to be *here* is the guard, and it was the round-2 hole (#432): reading
 * "a new rule is being armed" off the baseline *rows* instead made every rule with zero rows a
 * silent free pass. `engine-no-ui-packages` below had 0 of 72 rows, so a real `zustand` import
 * under `src/core/` plus the documented baseline write read `PASS ratchet=armed` — no config edit,
 * no declaration, nothing for a reviewer to look at — and an invented rule name passed the same
 * way. The hole widened as the ratchet shrank, because driving a rule to zero rows is the goal.
 *
 * The rules themselves are guarded as well as their rows (#489). `pnpm run lint:layers` fails a
 * baseline row under a rule name no rule here reports — deleted, renamed without its rows, commented
 * out, set to `ignore` — where an emptied copy of this file read `0 known violations … 0 new`; and
 * `pr-hygiene` reads every PR that edits this file, failing a rule name the merge base declares and
 * the PR does not as `ratchet=disarmed`, rows or none. A rename gets past it only with all of its
 * rows moved to the new name, and still warns as `swapped`.
 *
 * What the rule still cannot see, stated rather than left implicit: a rule **declared here in the
 * same PR** to catch the edge being hidden — a rename, a copy under another name, a widened `to:`.
 * In the baseline a genuinely new rule and a renamed one are the same shape, so no comparison of
 * rows can separate them. What it does see is that rows *left* as well as arrived, which no real
 * arming does — that reads `swapped` and warns, pointing here. The fence on it is this file: the
 * declaration is an added line in a reviewed file, which is the cost round 2's hole did not carry.
 * A rule name inside a **comment** or a **string literal** here counts as declared too — the rule
 * reads this file as text and never runs it — so it also reaches `armed`. That is not a false pass:
 * dependency-cruiser matches `knownViolations` by rule name, so a baseline row under a name no real
 * rule emits suppresses nothing (measured on #432: still `1 new`, exit 1). It leans on the scan
 * finding every rule the merge base's copy declares: a copy of this file, on either side, that it
 * finds no names in fails closed (#438), and so does a missed rule that has baseline rows (#456). A
 * rule with **no** rows that keeps its name while it stops checking — commented out, set to
 * `ignore`, narrowed — or that is added in a form the scan cannot read is fenced by review alone
 * (#505). So keep every rule's name written out as a literal.
 *
 * A guard that cries wolf makes agents argue with it, so every rule here is deliberately narrow:
 * it names the directions the audit measured and nothing more. Widen it only with a measurement.
 *
 * `console.*` and DOM globals in the engine are NOT here: they are globals, not dependencies, and
 * dependency-cruiser only sees dependencies. ESLint carries those (eslint.config.js, "engine layer").
 */

/** pure logic — no React, no browser, no store. */
const ENGINE = '^src/(core|simulation)/'
/** the single Zustand store. */
const STATE = '^src/store/'
/** everything that draws: R3F components, the DOM shell, per-gate bodies, hooks, theme. */
const UI = '^src/(components|gates|nodes|hooks|theme|styles)/|^src/(App|main)\\.tsx$'
/** the mesh components that draw from props alone, named file by file: the renderers beside them
 *  in the same folders read the store and pass props down, so a folder pattern would flag them. */
const MESH_FILES = [
  'src/gates/common/BaseGate.tsx',
  'src/nodes/components/InputNode3D.tsx',
  'src/nodes/components/OutputNode3D.tsx',
  'src/nodes/BusComponent3D.tsx',
  'src/components/canvas/Wire3D.tsx',
]
const MESHES = `^(${MESH_FILES.map((file) => file.replaceAll('.', '\\.')).join('|')})$`
/** `preserveSymlinks` keeps these as `node_modules/<pkg>/…` under pnpm instead of
 *  `.pnpm/<pkg>@<version>/…`, so neither the pattern nor the baseline breaks on a version bump.
 *  Left unanchored so a nested or hoisted `node_modules` matches too. */
const RENDERING_PACKAGES = '(^|/)node_modules/(three|three-stdlib|@react-three/[^/]+|@react-spring/[^/]+)/'
const UI_PACKAGES = `${RENDERING_PACKAGES}|(^|/)node_modules/(react|react-dom|zustand|sonner|next-themes|lucide-react|framer-motion|leva|@radix-ui/[^/]+|@testing-library/[^/]+)/`

/** @type {import('dependency-cruiser').IConfiguration} */
module.exports = {
  forbidden: [
    {
      name: 'engine-no-state',
      severity: 'error',
      comment: 'Pure logic may not import the store. Pass the data in; return data out.',
      from: { path: ENGINE },
      to: { path: STATE },
    },
    {
      name: 'engine-no-ui',
      severity: 'error',
      comment: 'Pure logic may not import anything that renders.',
      from: { path: ENGINE },
      to: { path: UI },
    },
    {
      name: 'engine-no-ui-packages',
      severity: 'error',
      comment: 'No three, React, Zustand or toast libraries in the engine — it must run headless in Node.',
      from: { path: ENGINE },
      to: { path: UI_PACKAGES },
    },
    {
      name: 'state-no-ui',
      severity: 'error',
      comment: 'The store may not import rendering code: layout and node config belong below it.',
      from: { path: STATE },
      to: { path: UI },
    },
    {
      name: 'state-no-3d',
      severity: 'error',
      comment: 'The store may not import a 3D library; geometry types belong to the renderer.',
      from: { path: STATE },
      to: { path: RENDERING_PACKAGES },
    },
    {
      name: 'mesh-no-state',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        'A mesh component draws from its props alone: no store import, not even a type. Its plain data types come from src/types/scene.ts.',
      from: { path: MESHES },
      to: { path: STATE },
    },
    {
      name: 'core-through-index',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        "Code outside src/core imports the engine through src/core/index.ts, not past it into a module's internals.",
      from: { path: '^src/', pathNot: '^src/core/' },
      to: { path: '^src/core/', pathNot: '^src/core/index\\.ts$' },
    },
    {
      name: 'surfaces-through-core',
      severity: 'error',
      comment:
        'The CLI and MCP surfaces reach the engine only through src/core, never the store or anything that renders: they must run headless in Node.',
      from: { path: '^src/(cli|mcp)/' },
      to: { path: `${STATE}|${UI}` },
    },
    {
      name: 'src-no-e2e',
      severity: 'error',
      comment: 'Production code may not import test-harness types from e2e/.',
      from: { path: '^src/' },
      to: { path: '^e2e/' },
    },
    {
      name: 'no-circular',
      severity: 'error',
      comment: 'A cycle means neither module can be loaded, tested or moved on its own.',
      from: { pathNot: '^node_modules/' },
      to: { circular: true },
    },
  ],
  options: {
    // node_modules stays in the graph (the package rules need it) but is never walked into.
    doNotFollow: { path: 'node_modules' },
    // pnpm resolves node_modules/<pkg> through .pnpm/<pkg>@<version>; keeping the symlink keeps the
    // version out of every path, so a bump does not invalidate the baseline.
    preserveSymlinks: true,
    // `import type` counts: 4 of the audit's 16 production edges are type-only, and a type edge is
    // still a compile-time coupling that blocks a move.
    tsPreCompilationDeps: true,
    tsConfig: { fileName: 'tsconfig.app.json' },
    reporterOptions: { text: { highlightFocused: true } },
  },
}

# .importlinter – gpkit‑core architecture baseline (INI)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This file encodes a layered architecture that matches the current reality
# while aiming for the desired future state (clean separation of primitives,
# algebra, modelling API, solver adapters, and interactive helpers).
#
# code may depend **downward** (toward lower‑numbered layers) but never upward.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter]
root_package = gpkit

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 1: Layered architecture (highest first)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = layered dependencies
type = layers

layers =
    # Interactive/UI helpers (may import everything below)
    gpkit.interactive | gpkit.tools

    # Model eventually goes here? user-friendly interface to model and solvers
    gpkit.model

    # mathematical optimization models
    gpkit.programs

    # GP representation and solver interfaces
    gpkit.solvers : gpkit.solutions

    # Solution breakdown analysis (solutions imports from here)
    gpkit.breakdowns

    # Modelling primitives + indexing
    gpkit.constraints

    # Algebra + mathematical objects (including constraint primitives)
    gpkit.nomials

    # Variable containers (VarMap, VarSet) — depends on varkey
    gpkit.varmap

    # Variable identity and display context (VarKey, lineage_display_context)
    gpkit.varkey

    # Utilities (including globals, build)
    gpkit.util

    # Pure primitives & units (no gpkit imports allowed)
    gpkit.units | gpkit.exceptions

# goal is to eventually eliminate the ignore list below via refactoring
ignore_imports =
    # the following import patterns exist today but should be eliminated
    gpkit.units -> gpkit.nomials
    gpkit.tools.autosweep -> gpkit.interactive.plot_sweep
    gpkit.model -> gpkit.tools.autosweep

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 2: Keep test helpers independent of production code (optional)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:tests_are_isolated]
name  = tests must not be imported by src
type  = forbidden
source_modules      = gpkit.*
forbidden_modules   = tests.*

[project]
name = "{{cookiecutter.repo_name}}"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "{{cookiecutter.description}}"

{%- if cookiecutter.open_source_license != "No license file" %}
license = "{{ cookiecutter.open_source_license }}"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
{%- endif %}
requires-python = ">={{cookiecutter.python_version}}"
# Dependencies are split by where they are installed (see README > Dependencies):
# - base: what src/core, src/libs and src/utils import; installed everywhere
# - extras (optional-dependencies): runtime sets an image or a step environment
#   asks for, e.g. `uv sync --extra serving` or `pip install -e ".[pipeline]"`
# - groups (dependency-groups): only for working on the project (your machine
#   and CI); never in images
# Your .venv gets everything (`make venv` runs `uv sync --all-extras`).
dependencies = [
    "boto3",
    # The MLflow client (runs, models, projects) without the server's
    # dependencies; the full package is in the tracking-server extra
    "mlflow-skinny>=3",
    "omegaconf",
    "pandas",
    "pyarrow",
    "python-dotenv",
    "pyyaml",
    "scikit-learn",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Running the pipeline: main.py, run.py and the steps
pipeline = [
    "dask[dataframe]",
    "hydra-core",
    "hydra-joblib-launcher",
    "statsmodels",
]
# The API in src/serving
serving = [
    "fastapi",
    "uvicorn",
]
# The MLflow tracking server (the mlflow image, `make mlflow-server`) and local
# SQLite tracking (launcher.local=true), which need the full mlflow package
tracking-server = [
    "mlflow>=3",
    "psycopg[binary]",
]

[dependency-groups]
test = [
    "httpx",
    "moto[s3]",
    "pytest",
]
dev = [
    "cookiecutter",
    "import-linter",
    "pre-commit",
    "ruff",
]
notebook = [
    "ipywidgets",
    "jupyterlab",
    "jupyterlab-git",
]
eda = [
    "matplotlib",
    "seaborn",
    # ydata-profiling imports pkg_resources without declaring it; setuptools 81
    # removed it. Drop this pin once ydata-profiling stops using it.
    "setuptools<81",
    "ydata-profiling",
]
[tool.uv]
# `uv sync` and `uv run` install every group; `uv sync --no-group eda` skips one
default-groups = ["test", "dev", "notebook", "eda"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# Ship the shared packages in src/ so they can be imported from anywhere (main.py,
# notebooks, tests, the MLflow steps and serving). src/steps/ holds the steps,
# which MLflow runs as scripts, so it is not a package.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/core", "src/libs", "src/utils", "src/serving"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["serving", "libs", "core", "utils"]

[project]

license-files = ["LICENSE"]

default-groups = ["dev"]

[tool.uv.sources]
feedparser = { git = "https://github.com/Jenselme/feedparser.git", rev = "jen-release" }


# ==== pytest ====
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "6.0"
addopts = "--ds=config.settings --reuse-db --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket --allow-hosts=localhost"
python_files = [
    "tests.py",
    "test_*.py",
]
filterwarnings = [
    # We know and aren’t impacted.
    "ignore:To avoid breaking existing software while fixing issue 310",
]
env = [
    "LOGGING_RICH_TRACEBACK=False", # This slows downs test and we don’t need it.
    "ENABLE_DEBUG_TOOLBAR=False", # This messes up the test suite.
]
env_files = [
    "devops/envs/local/django"
]

# ==== Coverage ====
[tool.coverage.run]
include = ["legadilo/**"]
omit = ["*/migrations/*", "*/tests/*"]
plugins = []


# ==== Ruf ====
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py314"
exclude = [
    "docs/**",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
preview = true
select = [
    "F", "E", "W", "C", "I", "N", "UP", "ASYNC", "S", "BLE", "FBT", "B", "A", "COM", "DTZ", "T",
    "DJ", "ICN", "RSE", "PT", "ISC", "RET", "SIM", "INT", "PTH", "ERA", "PGH", "PL", "FLY",
    "FURB", "LOG", "G", "RUF", "D", "UP"
]
ignore = [
    "RUF012", # RUF012 Mutable class attributes should be annotated with `typing.ClassVar`
    "RUF067", # Non empty init module
    "COM812", # missing-trailing-comma (the formatter will do this)
    "ISC001", # single-line-implicit-string-concatenation (the formatter will do this)
    "PLR6301", # Method XXX could be a function, class method, or static method
    "D100", # Missing docstring in public module
    "D101", # Missing docstring in public class
    "D102", # Missing docstring in public method
    "D103", # Missing docstring in public function
    "D104", # Missing docstring in public package
    "D105", # Missing docstring in magic method
    "D106", # Missing docstring in public nested class
    "D107", # Missing docstring in __init__
    "D415", # First line should end with a period, question mark, or exclamation point
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"legadilo/**/tests/**/test_*.py" = [
    # at least this three should be fine in tests:
    "S101", # asserts allowed in tests...
    "ARG", # Unused function args -> fixtures nevertheless are functionally relevant...
    "FBT", # Don't care about booleans as positional arguments in tests, e.g. via @pytest.mark.parametrize()
    "PLR0904", # Too many public methods.
    "PLR2004", # Magic value used in comparison, ...
    "S311", # Standard pseudo-random generators are not suitable for cryptographic purposes
    "S106", # Possible hardcoded password
]
"legadilo/feeds/tests/test_utils/test_article_fetching.py" = [
    "E501",
    "RUF001", # String contains ambiguous `’`
]
"legadilo/**/factories.py" = [
    "FBT001", # Boolean-typed positional argument in function definition
    "ARG002", #  Unused method argument
    "RUF012", # Mutable class attributes should be annotated with `typing.ClassVar`
]
"legadilo/**/migrations/*.py" = [
    "E501", # Line too long.
    "RUF012", # Mutable class attributes should be annotated with `typing.ClassVar`
]
"config/wsgi.py" = [
    "ERA001", # Found commented-out code
]
"config/asgi.py" = [
    "ERA001", # Found commented-out code
]
"config/settings.py" = [
    "ERA001", # Found commented-out code
]

[tool.ruff.format]
preview = true
# Like Black, use double quotes for strings.
quote-style = "double"
# Like Black, indent with spaces, rather than tabs.
indent-style = "space"
# Like Black, respect magic trailing commas.
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
# Like Black, automatically detect the appropriate line ending.
line-ending = "auto"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = [
    "legadilo",
    "config",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 6
allow-dunder-method-names = ["__get_pydantic_core_schema__"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"


# ==== curlylint ====
[tool.curlylint.rules]
# All role attributes must be valid.
# See https://www.curlylint.org/docs/rules/aria_role.
aria_role = true
# Forms cannot be rendered with as_table, as_ul, or as_p
# See https://www.curlylint.org/docs/rules/django_forms_rendering.
django_forms_rendering = true
# The `lang` attribute must be present.
# See https://www.curlylint.org/docs/rules/html_has_lang.
html_has_lang = true
# The `alt` attribute must be present.
# See https://www.curlylint.org/docs/rules/image_alt.
image_alt = true
# Use tabs.
# See https://www.curlylint.org/docs/rules/indent.
indent = 4
# `user-scalable=no` must not be used, and `maximum-scale` should be 2 or above.
# See https://www.curlylint.org/docs/rules/meta_viewport.
meta_viewport = true
# The `autofocus` attribute must not be used.
# See https://www.curlylint.org/docs/rules/no_autofocus.
no_autofocus = true
# Avoid positive `tabindex` values, change the order of elements on the page instead.
# See https://www.curlylint.org/docs/rules/tabindex_no_positive.
tabindex_no_positive = true


# ==== mypy ====
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
check_untyped_defs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_configs = true
plugins = [
    "mypy_django_plugin.main",
]
exclude = [
    # mypy gets messed up when factories are used instead of models instances.
    "test.*\\.py$"
]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Django migrations should not produce any errors:
module = "*.migrations.*"
ignore_errors = true

[tool.django-stubs]
django_settings_module = "config.settings"


# ==== djLint ====
[tool.djlint]
blank_line_after_tag = "load,extends"
close_void_tags = true
format_css = true
format_js = true
# TODO: remove T002 when fixed https://github.com/Riverside-Healthcare/djLint/issues/687
ignore = "H006,H025,H030,H031,T002"
include = "H017,H035"
indent = 4
max_line_length = 119
profile = "django"
custom_blocks = "partialdef"

[tool.djlint.css]
indent_size = 4

[tool.djlint.js]
indent_size = 4


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "legadilo"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Enforce Django apps layering"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "legadilo.import_export",
    "legadilo.feeds",
    "legadilo.reading",
    "legadilo.users",
    "legadilo.core",

[build-system]

  { git = { commit = true, tags = true } },
]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# Last-resort sentinel: only used when a build sees neither a .git directory nor
# an expanded .git_archival.txt (e.g. an archive of a commit with no reachable
# tag). "0.0.0" reads clearly as "version could not be determined" rather than
# masquerading as a real early release. See .git_archival.txt + .gitattributes
# `export-subst` for the archive path that recovers the real tag-derived version.
