[tool.hatch.build]
hooks.vcs.version-file = "src/fastui_admin/_version.py"


[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "only-version"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true


[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The package uses a src layout, so the source tree lives under /src (not
# /fastui_admin); including /src ships the actual modules -- and, for
# C-extension projects, the .pyx/.pxd sources needed to compile from the sdist.
include = [
  "/README.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "/src",
  "/tests",
  "/docs/examples",
]


[tool.commitizen]
# Commit-authoring and message linting only. release-please owns version
# bumping, git tagging, and CHANGELOG.md (see .github/release-please-config.json),
# so the bump/tag/changelog settings are intentionally omitted here to avoid two
# tools competing over the same tags and changelog file.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# addopts = "-rXs --strict-config --strict-markers"
addopts = "-v --tb=short --doctest-glob=README.md"
# One marker per component, auto-applied by tests/conftest.py from each test's
# top-level tests/<dir>/. Enables `pytest -m web` locally and per-component CI
# jobs; `integration` is one axis of the scheme.
markers = [
  "core: core/shared component tests",
]
# Strict mode requires explicit @pytest.mark.asyncio annotations, making async
# test collection intentional instead of silently accepting unmarked coroutines.
asyncio_mode = "strict"
filterwarnings = [
  "error",
]
# The project README is the deliberately small Markdown doctest surface. Other
# Markdown files can use illustrative snippets without becoming pytest inputs.
testpaths = ["tests", "README.md"]
doctest_optionflags = "ELLIPSIS IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"
xfail_strict = true


[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
# Match `_version.py` wherever it resolves: `src/...` in editable dev installs and
# `.../site-packages/...` when tox/CI installs the built (non-editable) wheel. A
# `src/**`-only pattern silently misses the installed copy and reports it at 0%.
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
parallel = true
# Store data-file paths relative to the project root so `.coverage` files produced
# on different runners/OSes merge in the `coverage-combine` CI job without
# absolute-path mismatches. Complements the `[tool.coverage.paths]` remap below
# (which unifies the src/ vs site-packages layouts).
relative_files = true
source_pkgs = ["fastui_admin", "tests"]


[tool.coverage.paths]
# Unify coverage data across environments. tox installs the built wheel into
# each env's site-packages, so the same source file is measured under a different
# `.tox/<env>/.../site-packages/fastui_admin` path per interpreter. Without
# remapping those back to the canonical `src/` tree, `coverage combine` keeps a
# separate copy per env and a version-gated line covered in one interpreter but not
# another is wrongly counted as missed — silently failing the `fail_under` gate.
# `tests` needs no remapping: it is never installed, so every environment measures
# it at the same repo-local path.
fastui_admin = ["src/fastui_admin", "*/site-packages/fastui_admin"]


[tool.coverage.report]
# Untestable code is excluded per site with `# pragma: no cover`, not with blanket
# patterns here: a regex matching a `def` line excludes the *whole function body*,
# so a pattern like `def main\(` would silently un-measure any future `main()`
# with real logic (and did mask the tested GUI/TUI entrypoints). Pragmas carry the
# exclusion decision next to the code it affects.
exclude_lines = [
  "no cov",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]
fail_under = 99
# Patterns match both the `src/` (editable) and installed (`site-packages`)
# layouts (see [tool.coverage.run] omit).
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true


[tool.vulture]
# Framework-invoked handlers: Typer commands, FastAPI routes, FastStream
# lifecycle hooks, and the MCP tool dispatcher.
ignore_decorators = [
  "@app.command",
  "@app.get",
  "@app.after_startup",
  "@app.after_shutdown",
  "@server.call_tool",
]
# Public API surfaces vulture cannot see being used: ``main`` entry points are
# referenced only via pyproject scripts, ``model_config`` is consumed by
# pydantic-settings, ``logger`` is imported only by optional components, the MCP
# ``arguments`` parameter is mandated by the call_tool signature, the Textual
# names (CSS/compose/on_mount/title/BINDINGS) are invoked by the TUI framework,
# and ``pytestmark``/``pytest_*`` (conftest hooks) are consumed by pytest at
# collection time. ``annotation``/``field_info`` are the NamedTuple fields of
# the create_model definitions (consumed positionally); ``category``/``icon``
# are view ClassVars read only via the admin surface; ``setup_db`` is a
# side-effect fixture injected by name; ``BadView`` test doubles are never
# instantiated — defining them is what triggers the validation under test;
# the rest are SQLAlchemy-mapped test model attributes, referenced
# declaratively rather than by attribute access.
ignore_names = ["CONFIG_FILE_PATH", "logger", "main", "model_config", "pytest_*", "collect_ignore_glob", "annotation", "field_info", "category", "icon", "setup_db", "BadView", "id", "username", "email", "is_active", "created_at", "label"]
min_confidence = 60
paths = ["src", "tests"]


[tool.deptry]
# `known_first_party` is explicit because the tox `deps` env installs the built
# wheel, so without it deptry reads the project's own imports as a third-party
# transitive dependency (DEP003). Add further `per_rule_ignores` entries for the
# project's own findings, e.g. DEP003 for a package only importable through
# another declared one, or DEP002 for an optional import guarded by try/except.
# See https://deptry.com/rules-violations/.
# Excluded: the Sphinx config, the build hook (its imports belong to
# `[build-system].requires`, not the runtime dependencies), the benchmarks and the
# worker probe script (neither ships in the wheel; pytest and anyio come from
# the dev tooling).
extend_exclude = [
  "docs/conf.py",
]
known_first_party = ["fastui_admin"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# tools/build_docs.py imports `packaging`, pinned in the `docs` group for that
# script alone, so deptry reads it as a misplaced dev dependency.
DEP004 = ["packaging"]


[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "fastui_admin"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Flat modules over leaf utils"
type = "layers"
# This project keeps its runtime in flat modules (base/views/layout) that all
# depend downward on the `utils` leaf (helpers plus the Admin/View/Layout
# protocols). Layers are listed high -> low: `base` (the app, importing layout
# and utils) sits above the independent siblings `views | layout` (which must
# not import each other and only reach `base` through the utils protocols, so
# no import cycle exists; basedpyright's reportImportCycles gate enforces that),
# which sit above the leaf `utils` (imports nothing internal).
#
# `exhaustive` makes the contract fail when a subpackage of
# `fastui_admin` is not named in `layers` — so a new top-level
# subpackage is a deliberate architecture decision (add it to a layer here)
# rather than something that silently accretes at the package root. Feature code
# belongs inside an existing layer; see "Package structure" in `AGENTS.md`.
containers = ["fastui_admin"]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = [
  "_version",
]
layers = [
  "base",
  "views | layout",
  "utils",
]

fix = true
output-format = "full"
preview = true
show-fixes = true
src = ["src", "tests", "examples", "docs/examples"]
target-version = "py310"
unsafe-fixes = true


[tool.ruff.analyze]
detect-string-imports = true
preview = true

docstring-code-format = true
line-ending = "lf"
preview = true
skip-magic-trailing-comma = true

fixable = ["ALL"]
# Two opinionated ruff 0.16 preview rules are disabled: RUF105 would rewrite the
# portable `# noqa` comments into ruff's own `# ruff: ignore` syntax (its docs note
# `# noqa` is needed for cross-tool compatibility), and RUF201 would rewrite every
# rule *code* in this config's selectors into long rule *names*. Both are stylistic.
ignore = ["COM812", "CPY", "FIX", "RUF105", "RUF201", "TD"]
logger-objects = ["logging_setup.logger"]

combine-as-imports = true
# skip-magic-trailing-comma = true
split-on-trailing-comma = false

# Recursive glob so nested test packages (tests/cli, tests/gui, ...) are covered.
# Tests legitimately use asserts/magic values, reach into package internals, and
# don't need return-value documentation on their fixtures and helpers.
"src/fastui_admin/__init__.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC2701", "DOC201", "TID252"]
"examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001"]
# Documentation examples are importable modules tested by
# ``tests/test_docs_examples.py``; they are not application packages.
"docs/examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001"]
# The Sphinx config is a standalone module, not part of an importable package.
"docs/conf.py" = ["INP001"]
# The docs warning-allowlist gate is a standalone script (not an importable
# package) whose whole job is to print GitHub `::error::` annotations to stdout.
"docs/check_warnings.py" = ["INP001", "T201"]
# The versioned-docs build orchestrator is a standalone CLI script under tools/,
# not part of an importable package.
"tools/build_docs.py" = ["INP001"]


[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true


[tool.ruff.lint.ruff]
parenthesize-tuple-in-subscript = true


[tool.mypy]
files = ["src", "docs/examples"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true


[tool.basedpyright]
exclude = [".venv"]
include = ["src/fastui_admin", "docs/examples"]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
venv = ".venv"
# venvPath is the directory *containing* the venv, not the venv itself; ".venv"
# here would make basedpyright look for ".venv/.venv". Use "." so both the venv
# and basedpyright's strict ruleset resolve the project's installed deps.
venvPath = "."


[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "tests", "docs/examples"]
respect-ignore-files = false


[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.10"


[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true


[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.10"
project-includes = ["src", "docs/examples"]

[tool.pylint.main]
# pylint runs as an always-on gate that deliberately overlaps ruff's PL* rules.
# Its canonical invocation is `pylint src docs/examples`, so it never descends into tests; this
# ignore-paths is a defensive scope guard for broader invocations (`pylint .`,
# filename-passing hooks). Tests are linted by ruff, not pylint.
ignore-paths = ["^tests/.*$"]
# `.pyi` stubs (the c-extension type stub) are signature-only: their bodies are
# `...` and every parameter is unused by construction, so pylint's unused-argument
# check is a guaranteed false positive there. Stubs are type-checked by the
# type-checker gate, not pylint.
ignore-patterns = ['.*\.pyi$']

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
# Only formatter-owned checks, the docstring family, and too-few-public-methods
# are disabled so pylint is usable out of the box; everything else stays on.
disable = [
  "line-too-long", # C0301 — ruff-format owns line length
  "missing-module-docstring", # C0114
  "missing-class-docstring", # C0115
  "missing-function-docstring", # C0116
  "too-few-public-methods", # R0903 — trips dataclasses / config / Protocol classes
  # C0415 — the cli->tui/gui/web dispatch, and each component's own heavy or
  # platform-conditional import (tkinter, uvicorn, the worker's uvloop probe),
  # are deliberately lazy so import-linter's layering contract holds and a
  # framework is only imported when the code path that needs it actually runs.
  # Textual is the exception: the TUI imports it at module scope so `InfoApp`
  # can be defined there and driven by the headless pilot.
  "import-outside-toplevel",
  # W0706 — the generated TUI entry point explicitly re-raises
  # KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit ahead of a broad `except Exception` to make the
  # "let these propagate" intent obvious to readers, even though BaseException
  # subclasses wouldn't be caught by the Exception clause anyway.
  "try-except-raise",
  # R0801 — the component skeletons (gui/tui/mcp/worker) are deliberately
  # parallel: each fetches package metadata and formats the same info block the
  # same way. That structural symmetry is a feature of the layout, not
  # copy-paste debt, and R0801 cannot be suppressed inline at the call site.
  "duplicate-code",
]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10
max-positional-arguments = 10
max-branches = 20

[tool.typos.files]
# The answers file can record a `git describe` string (`v1.2.3-4-g<hash>`), and
# a fragment of the hex hash can read as a misspelled word, failing the check on
# a hash nobody chose. The file is machine-written with no prose to check. The prek hook passes
# `--force-exclude`, so the exclusion holds there as well as in `tox -e style`.
extend-exclude = [
  ".copier-answers.yml",
]

[tool.tox]
# The ``worker`` env is intentionally omitted: it starts a broker-bound process
# and would hang/fail under ``tox run`` in CI (where no broker is available).
# The worker is covered by its pytest TestBroker suite; run it on demand with
# ``tox -e worker`` when a broker is up (e.g. inside the devcontainer).
env_list = [
  "style",
  # Inline ``>>>`` snippets are part of the tested-documentation contract,
  # so run them in the default CI ``tox run`` invocation.
  "docs-doctest",
  "3.14",
  "3.13",
  "3.12",
  "3.11",
  "3.10",
]
requires = ["tox>=4"]


[tool.tox.env_run_base]
commands = [
  [
    "coverage",
    "run",
    "--module",
    "pytest",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the tests under {base_python}"
env_tmp_dir = "{toxworkdir}/tmp/{envname}"
# Arms coverage-enable-subprocess so xdist/subprocess workers are measured too;
# `coverage run` plus `parallel = true` writes per-env data files that the CI
# `coverage combine` step merges.
set_env = { COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = "{tox_root}/pyproject.toml" }
# Non-editable: `uv sync --no-editable` builds the project and installs it into
# site-packages, the layout `[tool.coverage.paths]` remaps and the per-component
# coverage gates measure.
package = "wheel"
# Every env installs from uv.lock (`uv sync --locked`), so tox tests and lints
# the exact versions the lockfile pins. The plain `uv-venv-runner` resolves the
# project's own dependencies fresh on every env creation (tox's
# `use_frozen_constraints` never reaches its `uv pip install`), so a newer
# release could float in and clash with a pinned tool such as semgrep.
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.style]
base_python = ["3.10"]
commands = [
  [
    "ruff",
    "check",
    "--no-fix",
  ],
  [
    "ruff",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.10",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.14",
  ],
  # Style runs once on Linux, so explicitly sweep platform-gated branches that
  # mypy would otherwise prune as unreachable on the host platform.
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "win32",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "darwin",
  ],
  [
    "basedpyright",
  ],
  [
    "ty",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "pyrefly",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "zuban",
    "check",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "pylint",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "python",
    "-m",
    "slotscheck",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "lint-imports",
  ],
  # Rules-database SAST. Deliberately style-env-only (like ty/pyrefly/zuban) and
  # not a prek hook: semgrep keeps no on-disk rule cache, so a pre-commit hook
  # would make a registry request on every `git commit`. The ruleset is named
  # explicitly rather than `--config auto` so rule selection does not depend on
  # language auto-detection; it is still fetched from the registry, which is why
  # this cannot be vendored. `--error` makes findings blocking;
  # silence a false positive with a trailing `# nosemgrep: <rule-id>`.
  #
  # Runs via `uvx` in an isolated env (not the style venv): semgrep<=1.180
  # needs opentelemetry-api<1.38 while this repo's floated fastapi>=0.143 needs
  # otel>=1.44 — mutually unsatisfiable in one env, so a shared install always
  # produces a broken mix (otel ImportError at startup). The isolated env
  # resolves semgrep's own compatible otel set. Keep the `@1.180.0` pin exact.
  [
    "uvx",
    "semgrep@1.180.0",
    "scan",
    "--config",
    "p/python",
    "--error",
    "--metrics=off",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "taplo",
    "lint",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  # A strict `--check` gate, not fix mode: a generated file that taplo would
  # rewrite fails its own CI on first push.
  # `.taplo.toml` disables array auto expand/collapse so the shipped layout is
  # the canonical one regardless of which components are enabled. The `*.toml`
  # glob is non-recursive, so it scopes taplo to this project's own root TOML
  # (pyproject/prek/mise/taplo) without walking vendored `.tox`/`.venv`/
  # site-packages trees — no `.taplo.toml` exclude config needed.
  [
    "taplo",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  [
    "typos",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "ec",
  ],
  [
    "sphinx-lint",
    "docs",
    "REPOSITORY_SETUP.rst",
  ],
  # Collects (does not run) the suite and flags fixtures that are never used --
  # cheap, deterministic, and a natural fit next to the other whole-program
  # analyzers above (lint-imports, slotscheck).
  [
    "pytest",
    "--dead-fixtures",
  ],
]
# `test` is included so the type checkers that scope tests (e.g. ty) can
# resolve pytest and other test-only imports.
dependency_groups = ["style", "test"]
description = "Run Checkers, Linters and Formatters"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


# On-demand and CI-only (not in env_list, like `integration`): the `deps` job in
# ci.yml runs it and `check` aggregates that job. `test` is included so deptry
# and creosote can resolve the project's own test-only imports. creosote needs
# the installed distributions to map import names, which the lock runner provides.
[tool.tox.env.deps]
commands = [
  [
    "deptry",
    ".",
  ],
  [
    "creosote",
    "--deps-file",
    "pyproject.toml",
    "--section",
    "project.dependencies",
    # Without this creosote skips imports inside functions, so a dependency used
    # only through a lazy import (the worker's uvloop) is reported as unused.
    "--include-deferred",
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["deps", "test"]
description = "Check dependency hygiene (deptry, creosote)"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.prek]
commands = [["prek", "run", "--all-files"]]
dependency_groups = ["prek"]
description = "Run prek hooks"
# The hooks that need the project call `uv run --locked`, which syncs it (and the
# groups they name) into this env through the runner's UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT;
# installing the wheel here too would only be swapped for that install each run.
package = "skip"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-build]
# Write the warning stream to a file (`-w`) instead of `-W` turning the first
# warning into a hard error, then let docs/check_warnings.py own the pass/fail:
# it diffs the emitted warnings against the docs/expected_warnings.txt allowlist,
# failing on both unexpected new warnings and expected ones that vanished.
commands = [
  ["sphinx-build", "-w", "docs/_build/warnings.txt", "-b", "html", "docs", "docs/_build/html"],
  ["python", "docs/check_warnings.py"],
]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Build Docs"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
# Keep build log output unbuffered/ordered. Reproducible builds pin Sphinx's
# "today"/copyright to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, which the CI docs steps
# (docs-preview.yml, release.yml) export from the last commit date before
# invoking sphinx-build directly. Local `tox` runs deliberately do NOT export
# it: an empty value ("{env:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:}") is *present but blank*, which
# breaks hatchling's get_reproducible_timestamp (`int("")`), so we leave it
# unset locally and conf.py falls back to the current year.
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-server]
# ``--ignore`` the machine-generated ``docs/_generated/`` tree: ``conf.py``
# rewrites it on every Sphinx build, so watching it would make each rebuild
# trigger the next in an endless live-reload loop.
commands = [["sphinx-autobuild", "--ignore", "*/_generated/*", "docs", "docs/_build/html"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Start the live-reloading docs server"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-doctest]
# ``literalinclude`` keeps complete examples in tested Python modules; this
# separate builder executes the occasional ``>>>`` snippet that belongs inline
# with prose.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "doctest", "docs", "docs/_build/doctest"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Run documentation doctests"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-linkcheck]
# On-demand link checker. Also run weekly (non-blocking) by docs-linkcheck.yml.
# Hits the network, so it is deliberately not part of the `style` env or PR CI.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "linkcheck", "docs", "docs/_build/linkcheck"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Check documentation for broken links"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }

# ── Project metadata ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    "pytest-rerunfailures>=14.0",

    "COM", # trailing-comma
    "C90", # mccabe
    "DTZ", # flake8-datetimez
    "T",   # flake8-print
    "ERA", # eradicate
    "PD",  # pandas-vet

    "PL",  # pylint

    "FLY", # flynt

    "RET505",  # superfluous-else-return: allow for clarity
    "RET506",  # superfluous-else-raise: allow for clarity
    "RET507",  # superfluous-else-continue: allow for clarity
    "RET508",  # superfluous-else-break: allow for clarity
    "SIM108",  # if-else-block-instead-of-if-exp: allow for clarity
    "SIM114",  # if-with-same-arms: allow for clarity
    "UP007",   # typing-union: allow Union for Python 3.9 compat
    "PTH123",  # pathlib-open: allow open() for simplicity
    "RUF012",  # mutable-class-default: allow for class-level defaults

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]

"scripts/**/*" = ["T20"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Maximum number of arguments
max-args = 10
# Maximum number of branches
max-branches = 20
# Maximum number of statements
max-statements = 50


# ── import-linter architecture contracts ──────────────────────────────────────
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["pages", "locators", "components", "utils", "config", "tests"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Pages must not import from tests"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pages"]
forbidden_modules = ["tests"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Locators must not import from tests or utils"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["locators"]
forbidden_modules = ["tests", "utils"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Components must not import from tests"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["components"]
forbidden_modules = ["tests"]

[importlinter]
root_package = src
include_external_packages = True

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract 1: レイヤ単方向依存
#
# 上位レイヤは下位レイヤのみ import 可。逆方向（下位→上位）は禁止。
# 順序: pipeline > operation > simulation > portfolio > training
#       > policies > preparing > preprocessing > constants
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = レイヤ単方向依存（上位は下位のみ import 可）
type = layers
layers =
    src.pipeline
    src.operation
    src.simulation
    src.portfolio
    src.training
    src.policies
    src.preparing
    src.preprocessing
    src.storage
    src.constants
exhaustive = false

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract 2: constants 純粋性
#
# constants は他のどの src レイヤにも依存しない基盤モジュール。
# ここに依存が入ると全レイヤに影響が波及する。
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[importlinter:contract:constants_purity]
name = constants は src 内の他レイヤに依存しない（基盤純粋性）
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.constants
forbidden_modules =
    src.preprocessing
    src.preparing
    src.policies
    src.training
    src.portfolio
    src.simulation
    src.operation
    src.pipeline

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract 3: policies 独立性
#
# policies（馬券・スコア戦略プリミティブ）は training 以上のレイヤに
# 依存しない。これにより training を差し替えても policies に変更が波及しない。
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[importlinter:contract:policies_independence]
name = policies は training / simulation 以上のレイヤに依存しない
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.policies
forbidden_modules =
    src.training
    src.simulation
    src.portfolio
    src.operation
    src.pipeline

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract 4: simulation は training に依存しない
#
# simulation（バックテスト・評価）は特定の training 実装を知らない。
# training の結果（確率・馬券候補）だけを受け取り、実装には依存しない。
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[importlinter:contract:simulation_no_training]
name = simulation は training 実装に依存しない
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    src.simulation
forbidden_modules =
    src.training

[project]
name = "openapipages"
description = "OpenAPI Spec-based pages (SwaggerUI, ReDoc, RapiDoc, Elements, Scalar) ready with configuration features."
license = "MIT"
readme = "README.md"
authors = [
  { name = "Hasan Sezer Taşan", email = "hasansezertasan@gmail.com" },
]
maintainers = [
  { name = "Hasan Sezer Taşan", email = "hasansezertasan@gmail.com" },
]
dynamic = ["version"]
keywords = [
  "openapipages",
  "fastapi",
  "flask",
  "litestar",
  "openapi",
  "swagger",
  "swagger-ui",
  "scalar",
  "elements",
  "redoc",
  "rapidoc",
  "api",
  "documentation",
  "specification",
  "spec",
]
classifiers = [
  "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
  "Environment :: Web Environment",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Intended Audience :: Information Technology",
  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Natural Language :: English",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: CPython",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: PyPy",
  "Programming Language :: Python",
  "Framework :: FastAPI",
  "Framework :: Flask",
  "Framework :: Litestar",
  "Topic :: Internet",
  "Topic :: Internet :: WWW/HTTP",
  "Topic :: Internet :: WWW/HTTP :: HTTP Servers",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Application Frameworks",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
  "Topic :: Software Development",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
  "typing-extensions>=4.8.0",
]

[project.urls]
changelog = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/openapipages/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"
homepage = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/openapipages"
issues = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/openapipages/issues"
releasenotes = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/openapipages/releases"
source = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/openapipages.git"


[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "tox==4.65.0",
  "tox-uv==1.36.1",
  "debugpy==1.8.22",
  { include-group = "style" },
  { include-group = "test" },
]
style = [
  "basedpyright==1.40.2",
  "detect-secrets==1.5.0",
  "editorconfig-checker==3.8.0",
  "import-linter==2.15",
  "mypy==2.4.0",
  "pylint==4.0.6",
  "pyrefly==1.2.0",
  "ruff==0.17.0",
  "slotscheck==0.21.0",
  "taplo==0.9.3",
  "ty==0.0.66",
  "typos==1.51.1",
  "zuban==0.9.1",
]
# Semgrep pins an older OpenTelemetry API than FastAPI. Keep its scan in a
# separate tox environment so test dependencies do not enter the SAST resolver.
sast = [
  "semgrep==1.181.0",
]
# Dependency hygiene gets its own group for the same reason `sast` does: it is
# only ever run by the on-demand `deps` tox env and the `deps` CI job, so a plain
# `uv sync` should not install it. deptry checks the imports against the declared
# dependencies (missing, transitive, misplaced or obsolete); creosote flags
# declared runtime dependencies that nothing imports.
deps = [
  "creosote==5.2.0",
  "deptry==0.25.1",
]
test = [
  "coverage-enable-subprocess==1.0",
  "coverage[toml]==7.16.2",
  "fastapi>=0.150.0,<0.151.0",
  "httpx>=0.28.1,<0.29.0",
  "pytest-mock==3.17.0",
  "pytest-playwright>=0.5.0",
  "pytest-randomly==5.0.0",
  "pytest-rerunfailures==16.7",
  "pytest-xdist[psutil]==3.8.0",
  "pytest==9.1.1",
  "pytest-sugar==1.1.1",
  "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
  "pytest-deadfixtures==3.1.0",
  "uvicorn>=0.30",
]
tool = [
  "commitizen==4.19.2",
]
prek = [
  "prek==0.5.5",
]


[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"


[tool.uv]
add-bounds = "exact"
conflicts = [
  [{ group = "sast" }, { group = "dev" }],
  [{ group = "sast" }, { group = "test" }],
]
cache-keys = [
  { file = "pyproject.toml" },
  { git = { commit = true, tags = true } },
]
package = true
trusted-publishing = "always"


[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# Last-resort sentinel: only used when a build sees neither a .git directory nor
# an expanded .git_archival.txt (e.g. an archive of a commit with no reachable
# tag). "0.0.0" reads clearly as "version could not be determined" rather than
# masquerading as a real early release. See .git_archival.txt + .gitattributes
# `export-subst` for the archive path that recovers the real tag-derived version.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"


[tool.hatch.build]
hooks.vcs.version-file = "src/openapipages/_version.py"


[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "only-version"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"


[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The package uses a src layout, so the source tree lives under /src (not
# /openapipages).
include = [
  "/README.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "/src",
  "/tests",
]


[tool.commitizen]
# Commit-authoring and message linting only. release-please owns version
# bumping, git tagging, and CHANGELOG.md (see .github/release-please-config.json),
# so the bump/tag/changelog settings are intentionally omitted here to avoid two
# tools competing over the same tags and changelog file.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# `-m "not e2e"` keeps a bare `pytest` off the browser suite, matching tox: the
# Playwright sync API holds a running event loop for the session, which breaks
# every pytest-asyncio test ordered after it. Run e2e with `-m e2e` (or `tox -e
# e2e`); a later `-m` overrides this one.
addopts = "-v --tb=short --doctest-glob=README.md -m \"not e2e\""
# `core` is auto-applied by tests/conftest.py to top-level tests; `e2e` by
# tests/e2e/conftest.py to every browser test.
markers = [
  "core: core/shared component tests",
  "e2e: end-to-end browser tests (Playwright + subprocess uvicorn)",
]
# Strict mode requires explicit @pytest.mark.asyncio annotations, making async
# test collection intentional instead of silently accepting unmarked coroutines.
asyncio_mode = "strict"
filterwarnings = [
  "error",
]
# The project README is the deliberately small Markdown doctest surface. Other
# Markdown files can use illustrative snippets without becoming pytest inputs.
testpaths = ["tests", "README.md"]
doctest_optionflags = "ELLIPSIS IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"
# Enables strict_config, strict_markers, strict_xfail and
# strict_parametrization_ids: an undeclared marker or unknown ini key is an error.
strict = true


[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
# Match `_version.py` wherever it resolves: `src/...` in editable dev installs and
# `.../site-packages/...` when tox/CI installs the built (non-editable) wheel. A
# `src/**`-only pattern silently misses the installed copy and reports it at 0%.
# e2e is excluded from the default run (`--ignore=tests/e2e` in env_run_base and
# `-m "not e2e"` in addopts); omit it so it does not depress coverage.
omit = ["*/_version.py", "tests/e2e/*", "*/tests/e2e/*"]
parallel = true
# Store data-file paths relative to the project root so `.coverage` files produced
# on different runners/OSes merge in the `coverage-combine` CI job without
# absolute-path mismatches. Complements the `[tool.coverage.paths]` remap below
# (which unifies the src/ vs site-packages layouts).
relative_files = true
source_pkgs = ["openapipages", "tests"]


[tool.coverage.paths]
# Unify coverage data across environments. tox installs the built wheel into
# each env's site-packages, so the same source file is measured under a different
# `.tox/<env>/.../site-packages/openapipages` path per interpreter. Without
# remapping those back to the canonical `src/` tree, `coverage combine` keeps a
# separate copy per env and a version-gated line covered in one interpreter but not
# another is wrongly counted as missed — silently failing the `fail_under` gate.
# `tests` needs no remapping: it is never installed, so every environment measures
# it at the same repo-local path.
openapipages = ["src/openapipages", "*/site-packages/openapipages"]


[tool.coverage.report]
# Untestable code is excluded per site with `# pragma: no cover`, not with blanket
# patterns here: a regex matching a `def` line excludes the *whole function body*,
# so a pattern like `def main\(` would silently un-measure any future `main()`
# with real logic. Pragmas carry the exclusion decision next to the code it
# affects.
exclude_lines = [
  "no cov",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]
fail_under = 99
# Patterns match both the `src/` (editable) and installed (`site-packages`)
# layouts (see [tool.coverage.run] omit).
omit = ["*/_version.py", "tests/e2e/*", "*/tests/e2e/*"]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true


[tool.vulture]
# The FastAPI test apps' route handlers are reached only through `@app.get`.
ignore_decorators = ["@app.get"]
# `id`/`name` are pydantic model fields in the e2e app; pytest consumes conftest
# hooks and `collect_ignore_glob` at collection time.
ignore_names = ["id", "name", "pytest_*", "collect_ignore_glob"]
min_confidence = 60
paths = ["src", "tests"]


[tool.deptry]
# `known_first_party` is explicit because the tox `deps` env installs the built
# wheel, so without it deptry reads the project's own imports as a third-party
# transitive dependency (DEP003). Add further `per_rule_ignores` entries for the
# project's own findings, e.g. DEP003 for a package only importable through
# another declared one, or DEP002 for an optional import guarded by try/except.
# See https://deptry.com/rules-violations/.
# Excluded: the Sphinx config, the build hook (its imports belong to
# `[build-system].requires`, not the runtime dependencies), the benchmarks and the
# worker probe script (neither ships in the wheel; pytest and anyio come from
# the dev tooling) and the framework examples (they import fastapi, litestar and
# uvicorn, which are deliberately not dependencies of the library).
extend_exclude = [
  "examples",
]
known_first_party = ["openapipages"]


[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "openapipages"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture with independent components"
type = "layers"
# Layers are listed high -> low: a layer may import lower layers but never a
# higher one. Renderers joined by ` | ` are independent siblings that may not
# import each other; all of them build on the shared `base`.
#
# `exhaustive` makes the contract fail when a module of `openapipages` is not
# named in `layers`, so a new module is a deliberate architecture decision. The
# `exhaustive_ignores` entries are the non-layer foundations: the metadata
# re-export and the hatch-vcs version module.
containers = ["openapipages"]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = [
  "__about__",
  "_version",
]
layers = [
  "elements | rapidoc | redoc | scalar | swaggerui",
  "base",
]


[tool.ruff]
fix = true
output-format = "full"
preview = true
show-fixes = true
src = ["src", "tests", "examples"]
target-version = "py310"
unsafe-fixes = true


[tool.ruff.analyze]
detect-string-imports = true
preview = true


[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true
line-ending = "lf"
preview = true
skip-magic-trailing-comma = true


[tool.ruff.lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
# Two opinionated ruff 0.16 preview rules are disabled: RUF105 would rewrite the
# portable `# noqa` comments into ruff's own `# ruff: ignore` syntax (its docs note
# `# noqa` is needed for cross-tool compatibility), and RUF201 would rewrite every
# rule *code* in this config's selectors into long rule *names*. Both are stylistic.
ignore = ["COM812", "CPY", "D", "DOC201", "E501", "FIX", "PLR6301", "RUF105", "RUF201", "TD"]
logger-objects = ["logging_setup.logger"]
preview = true
select = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
split-on-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-copyright]
author = "Hasan Sezer Taşan <hasansezertasan@gmail.com>"


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"


[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 5


[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
ignore-overlong-task-comments = true


[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"


[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Recursive glob so nested test packages (tests/unit, tests/e2e, ...) are covered.
# Tests legitimately use asserts/magic values, reach into package internals, and
# don't need return-value documentation on their fixtures and helpers.
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC2701", "DOC201"]
# The e2e server fixture intentionally manages a subprocess and its startup
# lifecycle in one fixture.
"tests/e2e/conftest.py" = ["S404", "S603", "C901", "PLR0915"]
"examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001"]


[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true


[tool.ruff.lint.ruff]
parenthesize-tuple-in-subscript = true


[tool.mypy]
files = ["src", "tests"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true


[tool.basedpyright]
exclude = [".venv"]
include = ["src/openapipages"]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
reportAny = false
reportExplicitAny = false
reportImplicitOverride = false
venv = ".venv"
# venvPath is the directory *containing* the venv, not the venv itself; ".venv"
# here would make basedpyright look for ".venv/.venv". Use "." so both the venv
# and basedpyright's strict ruleset resolve the project's installed deps.
venvPath = "."


[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "tests"]
respect-ignore-files = false


[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.10"


[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true


[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.10"
project-includes = ["src"]

[tool.pylint.main]
# pylint runs as an always-on gate that deliberately overlaps ruff's PL* rules.
# Its canonical invocation is `pylint src`, so it never descends into tests; this
# ignore-paths is a defensive scope guard for broader invocations (`pylint .`,
# filename-passing hooks). Tests are linted by ruff, not pylint.
ignore-paths = ["^tests/.*$"]

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
# Only formatter-owned checks, the docstring family, too-few-public-methods and
# duplicate-code are disabled so pylint is usable out of the box; everything else stays on.
disable = [
  "line-too-long", # C0301 — ruff-format owns line length
  "missing-module-docstring", # C0114
  "missing-class-docstring", # C0115
  "missing-function-docstring", # C0116
  "too-few-public-methods", # R0903 — trips dataclasses / config / Protocol classes
  # R0801 — each renderer ships its own self-contained HTML page template, so
  # the shared `<head>`/`<noscript>` boilerplate repeats by design, and R0801
  # cannot be suppressed inline at the call site.
  "duplicate-code",
]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10
max-positional-arguments = 10
max-branches = 20

[tool.typos.files]
# The answers file can record a `git describe` string (`v1.2.3-4-g<hash>`), and
# a fragment of the hex hash can read as a misspelled word, failing the check on
# a hash nobody chose. The file is machine-written with no prose to check. The prek hook passes
# `--force-exclude`, so the exclusion holds there as well as in `tox -e style`.
extend-exclude = [
  ".copier-answers.yml",
]

[tool.tox]
# `e2e` and `coverage` are on-demand envs, not part of the default run: e2e needs
# a browser and network access, and coverage combines data the matrix produced.
env_list = [
  "style",
  "sast",
  "3.14",
  "3.13",
  "3.12",
  "3.11",
  "3.10",
]
requires = ["tox>=4"]


[tool.tox.env_run_base]
commands = [
  [
    "coverage",
    "run",
    "--module",
    "pytest",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--ignore=tests/e2e",
    "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the tests under {base_python}"
env_tmp_dir = "{toxworkdir}/tmp/{envname}"
# Arms coverage-enable-subprocess so xdist/subprocess workers are measured too;
# `coverage run` plus `parallel = true` writes per-env data files that the CI
# `coverage combine` step merges.
set_env = { COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = "{tox_root}/pyproject.toml" }
# Non-editable: `uv sync --no-editable` builds the project and installs it into
# site-packages, the layout `[tool.coverage.paths]` remaps and the per-component
# coverage gates measure.
package = "wheel"
# Every env installs from uv.lock (`uv sync --locked`), so tox tests and lints
# the exact versions the lockfile pins. The plain `uv-venv-runner` resolves the
# project's own dependencies fresh on every env creation (tox's
# `use_frozen_constraints` never reaches its `uv pip install`), so a newer
# release could float in and clash with a pinned tool such as semgrep.
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.style]
base_python = ["3.10"]
commands = [
  [
    "ruff",
    "check",
    "--no-fix",
  ],
  [
    "ruff",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.10",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.14",
  ],
  # Style runs once on Linux, so explicitly sweep platform-gated branches that
  # mypy would otherwise prune as unreachable on the host platform.
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "win32",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "darwin",
  ],
  [
    "basedpyright",
  ],
  [
    "ty",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "pyrefly",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "zuban",
    "check",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "pylint",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "python",
    "-m",
    "slotscheck",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "lint-imports",
  ],
  [
    "taplo",
    "lint",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  # A strict `--check` gate, not fix mode: a generated file that taplo would
  # rewrite fails its own CI on first push.
  # `.taplo.toml` disables array auto expand/collapse so the shipped layout is
  # the canonical one regardless of which components are enabled. The `*.toml`
  # glob is non-recursive, so it scopes taplo to this project's own root TOML
  # (pyproject/prek/mise/taplo) without walking vendored `.tox`/`.venv`/
  # site-packages trees — no `.taplo.toml` exclude config needed.
  [
    "taplo",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  [
    "typos",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "ec",
  ],
  # Collects (does not run) the suite and flags fixtures that are never used --
  # cheap, deterministic, and a natural fit next to the other whole-program
  # analyzers above (lint-imports, slotscheck). `-m ""` overrides the addopts
  # `not e2e` filter so the e2e fixtures count as used.
  [
    "pytest",
    "--dead-fixtures",
    "-m",
    "",
  ],
]
# `test` is included so the type checkers that scope tests (e.g. ty) can
# resolve pytest and other test-only imports.
dependency_groups = ["style", "test"]
description = "Run Checkers, Linters and Formatters"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.sast]
commands = [["semgrep", "scan", "--config", "p/python", "--error", "--metrics=off", "src"]]
dependency_groups = ["sast"]
description = "Scan source with Semgrep in an isolated environment"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


# On-demand and CI-only (not in env_list, like `integration`): the `deps` job in
# ci.yml runs it and `check` aggregates that job. `test` is included so deptry
# and creosote can resolve the project's own test-only imports. creosote needs
# the installed distributions to map import names, which the lock runner provides.
[tool.tox.env.deps]
commands = [
  [
    "deptry",
    ".",
  ],
  [
    "creosote",
    "--deps-file",
    "pyproject.toml",
    "--section",
    "project.dependencies",
    # Without this creosote skips imports inside functions, so a dependency used
    # only through a lazy import (the worker's uvloop) is reported as unused.
    "--include-deferred",
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["deps", "test"]
description = "Check dependency hygiene (deptry, creosote)"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.prek]
commands = [["prek", "run", "--all-files"]]
dependency_groups = ["prek"]
description = "Run prek hooks"
# The hooks that need the project call `uv run --locked`, which syncs it (and the
# groups they name) into this env through the runner's UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT;
# installing the wheel here too would only be swapped for that install each run.
package = "skip"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.e2e]
base_python = ["3.14"]
commands = [
  ["playwright", "install", "chromium"],
  [
    "pytest",
    "tests/e2e",
    "-m",
    "e2e",
    "-v",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the end-to-end browser tests (Playwright + Chromium)"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
# e2e is excluded from coverage; don't arm subprocess measurement.
set_env = {}


[tool.tox.env.coverage]
commands = [["coverage", "combine"], ["coverage", "report"], ["coverage", "xml"]]
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Combine the matrix's coverage data and report it"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
skip_install = true

[tool.poetry]
name = "frontend"
version = "0.1.0"
description = ""
authors = ["Kaveh <kaveh.razavi@gmail.com>"]
readme = "README.md"

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.10"
nicegui = "^2.0"
vmx = "^2.6.0"
httpx = "^0.27"
pydantic = {extras = ["email"], version = "^2.6.3"}
pydantic-settings = "^2.2"
email-validator = "^2.1.1"
langdetect = "^1.0.9"
plotly = "^5.20.0"
pandas = "^2.2.2"
numpy = "^1.26.4"

[tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies]
pytest = "^8.1.1"
pytest-asyncio = "^0.23.6"
pytest-cov = "^5.0.0"
respx = "^0.21"
import-linter = "^2.0"
mypy = "^1.10"
ruff = "^0.5"

[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
pythonpath = ["."]

[tool.importlinter]
# Runtime imports are `models.X`, `viewmodels.X`, `views.X`, `core.X` — no `frontend.` prefix
# (pythonpath = ["."] from frontend/ makes these top-level packages).
root_packages = ["models", "viewmodels", "views", "core"]
# Required because the "forbidden_modules" contracts reference `nicegui` (external dep).
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "MVVM layering"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "views",
    "viewmodels",
    "models",
    "core",

  { file = "pyproject.toml" },
  { git = { commit = true, tags = true } },
]
package = true
trusted-publishing = "always"


[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# Last-resort sentinel: only used when a build sees neither a .git directory nor
# an expanded .git_archival.txt (e.g. an archive of a commit with no reachable
# tag). "0.0.0" reads clearly as "version could not be determined" rather than
# masquerading as a real early release. See .git_archival.txt + .gitattributes
# `export-subst` for the archive path that recovers the real tag-derived version.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"


[tool.hatch.build]
hooks.vcs.version-file = "src/opinionated_mixins/_version.py"


[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "only-version"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true


[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The package uses a src layout, so the source tree lives under /src (not
# /opinionated_mixins); including /src ships the actual modules -- and, for
# C-extension projects, the .pyx/.pxd sources needed to compile from the sdist.
include = [
  "/README.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "/src",
  "/tests",
  "/docs/examples",
]


[tool.commitizen]
# Commit-authoring and message linting only. release-please owns version
# bumping, git tagging, and CHANGELOG.md (see .github/release-please-config.json),
# so the bump/tag/changelog settings are intentionally omitted here to avoid two
# tools competing over the same tags and changelog file.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# addopts = "-rXs --strict-config --strict-markers"
addopts = "-v --tb=short --doctest-glob=README.md"
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# One marker per component, auto-applied by tests/conftest.py from each test's
# top-level tests/<dir>/. Enables `pytest -m web` locally and per-component CI
# jobs (issue #160, ADR-028); `integration` (ADR-008) is one axis of the scheme.
markers = [
  "core: core/shared component tests",
]
filterwarnings = [
  "error",
  "ignore:No uuidRepresentation is specified:DeprecationWarning",
]
# The project README is the deliberately small Markdown doctest surface. Other
# Markdown files can use illustrative snippets without becoming pytest inputs.
testpaths = ["tests", "README.md"]
doctest_optionflags = "ELLIPSIS IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"
xfail_strict = true


[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
# Match `_version.py` wherever it resolves: `src/...` in editable dev installs and
# `.../site-packages/...` when tox/CI installs the built wheel or sdist. A
# `src/**`-only pattern silently misses the installed copy and reports it at 0%.
# The RFC version compatibility shim is a one-line import and the generated
# module is intentionally excluded. ODMantic integration tests exercise
# framework and mongomock roundtrips, but coverage focuses on package code.
omit = ["*/_version.py", "*/__about__.py", "tests/odmantic/*_integration.py"]
parallel = true
# Store data-file paths relative to the project root so `.coverage` files produced
# on different runners/OSes merge in the `coverage-combine` CI job without
# absolute-path mismatches. Complements the `[tool.coverage.paths]` remap below
# (which unifies the src/ vs site-packages layouts). See ADR-026.
relative_files = true
source_pkgs = ["opinionated_mixins", "tests"]


[tool.coverage.paths]
# Unify coverage data across environments. tox installs the built wheel/sdist into
# each env's site-packages, so the same source file is measured under a different
# `.tox/<env>/.../site-packages/opinionated_mixins` path per interpreter. Without
# remapping those back to the canonical `src/` tree, `coverage combine` keeps a
# separate copy per env and a version-gated line covered in one interpreter but not
# another is wrongly counted as missed — silently failing the `fail_under` gate.
# `tests` needs no remapping: it is never installed, so every environment measures
# it at the same repo-local path.
opinionated_mixins = ["src/opinionated_mixins", "*/site-packages/opinionated_mixins"]


[tool.coverage.report]
# Untestable code is excluded per site with `# pragma: no cover`, not with blanket
# patterns here: a regex matching a `def` line excludes the *whole function body*,
# so a pattern like `def main\(` would silently un-measure any future `main()`
# with real logic (and did mask the tested GUI/TUI entrypoints). Pragmas carry the
# exclusion decision next to the code it affects. See ADR-008.
exclude_lines = [
  "no cov",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]
fail_under = 99
# Patterns match both the `src/` (editable) and installed (`site-packages`)
# layouts (see [tool.coverage.run] omit).
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true


[tool.vulture]
# Framework-invoked handlers: Typer commands, FastAPI routes, FastStream
# lifecycle hooks, and the MCP tool dispatcher.
ignore_decorators = [
  "@app.command",
  "@app.get",
  "@app.after_startup",
  "@app.after_shutdown",
  "@server.call_tool",
]
# Public API surfaces vulture cannot see being used: ``main`` entry points are
# referenced only via pyproject scripts, ``model_config`` is consumed by

paths = ["src", "tests"]


[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "opinionated_mixins"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture with independent components"
type = "layers"
# Layers are listed high -> low: a layer may import lower layers but never a
# higher one. The four framework integrations are independent sibling layers
# (SQLModel ships native Pydantic fields, not re-exported SQLAlchemy columns);
# they share no implementation imports and expose separate adapter APIs.
#
# `exhaustive` makes the contract fail when a subpackage of
# `opinionated_mixins` is not named in `layers` — so a new top-level
# subpackage is a deliberate architecture decision (add it to a layer here)
# rather than something that silently accretes at the package root. The
# `exhaustive_ignores` entries are the generated version module and the optional
# `python -m` dispatcher.

  "__about__",

  "enums",

  "PLC0415",

"src/opinionated_mixins/enums.py" = ["D100"]

# The versioned-docs build orchestrator is a standalone CLI script under tools/,
# not part of an importable package (ADR-027).
"tools/build_docs.py" = ["INP001"]


[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true


[tool.ruff.lint.ruff]
parenthesize-tuple-in-subscript = true


[tool.mypy]
files = ["src", "docs/examples"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "opinionated_mixins.contrib.sqlalchemy.*"
# Declarative mixins use Column() without Mapped[] annotations.
disable_error_code = ["var-annotated"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "opinionated_mixins.contrib.mongoengine.*"
disable_error_code = ["import-untyped"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "pymongo.*"
follow_imports = "skip"


[tool.basedpyright]
exclude = [".venv"]
include = ["src/opinionated_mixins", "docs/examples"]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
# Framework descriptor APIs intentionally use unannotated class attributes;
# MongoEngine and ODMantic also expose dynamic fields and incomplete stubs.
reportAny = false
reportExplicitAny = false
reportImplicitOverride = false
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportUnannotatedClassAttribute = false
reportUnknownVariableType = false
venv = ".venv"
# venvPath is the directory *containing* the venv, not the venv itself; ".venv"
# here would make basedpyright look for ".venv/.venv". Use "." so both the venv
# and basedpyright's strict ruleset resolve the project's installed deps.
venvPath = "."


[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "docs/examples"]
respect-ignore-files = false


[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.10"


[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true


[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.10"
project-includes = ["src", "docs/examples"]

[tool.pylint.main]
# pylint runs as an always-on gate that deliberately overlaps ruff's PL* rules.
# Its canonical invocation is `pylint src docs/examples`, so it never descends into tests; this
# ignore-paths is a defensive scope guard for broader invocations (`pylint .`,
# filename-passing hooks). Tests are linted by ruff, not pylint.
ignore-paths = ["^tests/.*$"]
# `.pyi` stubs (the c-extension type stub) are signature-only: their bodies are
# `...` and every parameter is unused by construction, so pylint's unused-argument
# check is a guaranteed false positive there. Stubs are type-checked by the
# type-checker gate, not pylint.
ignore-patterns = ['.*\.pyi$']

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
# Only formatter-owned checks, the docstring family, and too-few-public-methods
# are disabled so pylint is usable out of the box; everything else stays on.
disable = [
  "line-too-long", # C0301 — ruff-format owns line length
  "wrong-import-order", # C0411 — ruff/isort owns import grouping
  "useless-import-alias", # C0414 — aliases declare intentional public re-exports
  "unused-import", # W0611 — re-export imports are the public API
  "missing-module-docstring", # C0114
  "missing-class-docstring", # C0115
  "missing-function-docstring", # C0116
  "too-few-public-methods", # R0903 — trips dataclasses / config / Protocol classes
  # C0415 — the cli->tui/gui/web dispatch, and each component's own heavy or
  # platform-conditional import (tkinter, uvicorn, the worker's uvloop probe),
  # are deliberately lazy so import-linter's layering contract holds and a
  # framework is only imported when the code path that needs it actually runs.
  # Textual is the exception: the TUI imports it at module scope so `InfoApp`
  # can be defined there and driven by the headless pilot (ADR-035).
  "import-outside-toplevel",
  # W0706 — the generated TUI entry point explicitly re-raises
  # KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit ahead of a broad `except Exception` to make the
  # "let these propagate" intent obvious to readers, even though BaseException
  # subclasses wouldn't be caught by the Exception clause anyway.
  "try-except-raise",
  # R0801 — the component skeletons (gui/tui/mcp/worker) are deliberately
  # parallel: each fetches package metadata and formats the same info block the
  # same way. That structural symmetry is a feature of the scaffold, not
  # copy-paste debt, and R0801 cannot be suppressed inline at the call site.
  "duplicate-code",
]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10
max-positional-arguments = 10
max-branches = 20

[tool.typos.files]
# copier records `_commit` as a `git describe` string (`v1.2.3-4-g<hash>`) when
# the template is rendered from an untagged ref, and a fragment of the hex hash
# can read as a misspelled word, failing the check on a hash nobody chose. The
# file is machine-written with no prose to check. The prek hook passes
# `--force-exclude`, so the exclusion holds there as well as in `tox -e style`.
# CHANGELOG.md is release-please-generated: every entry embeds a short commit
# hash, and a fragment of any hash can read as a misspelled word (e.g. `ded`
# in `ded19db` flagged as `dead`), failing the check on bytes nobody chose and
# auto-"fixing" the link text out of sync with its commit URL. Same
# machine-written rationale as above, so it is excluded rather than allowlisted
# word by word.
extend-exclude = [
  ".copier-answers.yml",
  "CHANGELOG.md",
]

[tool.tox]
# The ``worker`` env is intentionally omitted: it starts a broker-bound process
# and would hang/fail under ``tox run`` in CI (where no broker is available).
# The worker is covered by its pytest TestBroker suite; run it on demand with
# ``tox -e worker`` when a broker is up (e.g. inside the devcontainer).
env_list = [
  "style",
  # Inline ``>>>`` snippets are part of the tested-documentation contract,
  # so run them in the default CI ``tox run`` invocation.
  "docs-doctest",
  "3.14",
  "3.13",
  "3.12",
  "3.11",
  "3.10",
]
requires = ["tox>=4"]


[tool.tox.env_run_base]
commands = [
  [
    "coverage",
    "run",
    "--module",
    "pytest",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
constrain_package_deps = true
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the tests under {base_python}"
env_tmp_dir = "{toxworkdir}/tmp/{envname}"
# Arms coverage-enable-subprocess so xdist/subprocess workers are measured too;
# `coverage run` plus `parallel = true` writes per-env data files that the CI
# `coverage combine` step merges.
set_env = { COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = "{tox_root}/pyproject.toml" }

package = "wheel"

runner = "uv-venv-runner"
use_frozen_constraints = true
wheel_build_env = ".pkg"


[tool.tox.env.style]
base_python = ["3.10"]
commands = [
  [
    "ruff",
    "check",
    "--no-fix",
  ],
  [
    "ruff",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.10",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.14",
  ],
  # Style runs once on Linux, so explicitly sweep platform-gated branches that
  # mypy would otherwise prune as unreachable on the host platform.
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "win32",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "darwin",
  ],
  [
    "basedpyright",
  ],
  [
    "ty",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "pyrefly",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "zuban",
    "check",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "pylint",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "python",
    "-m",
    "slotscheck",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "lint-imports",
  ],
  # Rules-database SAST. Deliberately style-env-only (like ty/pyrefly/zuban) and
  # not a prek hook: semgrep keeps no on-disk rule cache, so a pre-commit hook
  # would make a registry request on every `git commit`. The ruleset is named
  # explicitly rather than `--config auto` so rule selection does not depend on
  # language auto-detection; it is still fetched from the registry, which is why
  # this cannot be vendored (see ADR-032). `--error` makes findings blocking;
  # silence a false positive with a trailing `# nosemgrep: <rule-id>`.
  [
    "semgrep",
    "scan",
    "--config",
    "p/python",
    "--error",
    "--metrics=off",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "taplo",
    "lint",
    "--config",
    ".config/.taplo.toml",
    "*.toml",
    ".config/mise.toml",
    ".config/.taplo.toml",
  ],
  # A strict `--check` gate, not fix mode: a generated file that taplo would
  # rewrite fails its own CI on first push and drifts on every `copier update`.
  # `.config/.taplo.toml` disables array auto expand/collapse so the shipped
  # layout is the canonical one regardless of which components are enabled. The
  # `*.toml` glob is non-recursive, so it covers the root TOML
  # (pyproject/prek) without walking vendored `.tox`/`.venv`/
  # site-packages trees — no config exclude rules needed; the relocated
  # `.config/mise.toml` and `.config/.taplo.toml` are listed explicitly
  # because the glob does not reach into `.config/`. `--config` is
  # passed explicitly because taplo cannot read a repo-local `.config/` and
  # does not fold `[tool.taplo]` out of pyproject.toml.
  [
    "taplo",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
    "--config",
    ".config/.taplo.toml",
    "*.toml",
    ".config/mise.toml",
    ".config/.taplo.toml",
  ],
  [
    "typos",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "ec",
    "-config",
    ".config/.editorconfig-checker.json",
  ],
  [
    "sphinx-lint",
    "docs",
  ],
  # Collects (does not run) the suite and flags fixtures that are never used --
  # cheap, deterministic, and a natural fit next to the other whole-program
  # analyzers above (lint-imports, slotscheck).
  [
    "pytest",
    "--dead-fixtures",
  ],
]
# `test` is included so the type checkers that scope tests (e.g. ty) can
# resolve pytest and other test-only imports.
dependency_groups = ["sast", "style", "test"]
description = "Run Checkers, Linters and Formatters"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"


[tool.tox.env.prek]
commands = [["prek", "run", "--all-files"]]
dependency_groups = ["prek"]
description = "Run prek hooks"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-build]
# Write the warning stream to a file (`-w`) instead of `-W` turning the first
# warning into a hard error, then let docs/check_warnings.py own the pass/fail:
# it diffs the emitted warnings against the docs/expected_warnings.txt allowlist,
# failing on both unexpected new warnings and expected ones that vanished.
commands = [
  ["sphinx-build", "-w", "docs/_build/warnings.txt", "-b", "html", "docs", "docs/_build/html"],
  ["python", "docs/check_warnings.py"],
]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Build Docs"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"
# Keep build log output unbuffered/ordered. Reproducible builds pin Sphinx's
# "today"/copyright to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, which the CI docs steps
# (docs-preview.yml, release.yml) export from the last commit date before
# invoking sphinx-build directly. Local `tox` runs deliberately do NOT export
# it: an empty value ("{env:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:}") is *present but blank*, which
# breaks hatchling's get_reproducible_timestamp (`int("")`), so we leave it
# unset locally and conf.py falls back to the current year.
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-server]
# ``--ignore`` the machine-generated ``docs/_generated/`` tree: ``conf.py``
# rewrites it on every Sphinx build, so watching it would make each rebuild
# trigger the next in an endless live-reload loop.
commands = [["sphinx-autobuild", "--ignore", "*/_generated/*", "docs", "docs/_build/html"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Start the live-reloading docs server"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-doctest]
# ``literalinclude`` keeps complete examples in tested Python modules; this
# separate builder executes the occasional ``>>>`` snippet that belongs inline
# with prose.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "doctest", "docs", "docs/_build/doctest"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Run documentation doctests"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-linkcheck]
# On-demand link checker. Also run weekly (non-blocking) by docs-linkcheck.yml.
# Hits the network, so it is deliberately not part of the `style` env or PR CI.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "linkcheck", "docs", "docs/_build/linkcheck"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Check documentation for broken links"
runner = "uv-venv-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }

[project]

    "polars",
    "pydantic",
    "scikit-learn",

]

[project.optional-dependencies]

test = ["pytest", "pytest-cov", "httpx"]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["cardre*", "sidecar*"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["F", "W", "E", "I", "B", "C4", "UP", "SIM"]
ignore = ["SIM102", "SIM116", "E501"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"cardre/api/**" = ["B008"]
"tests/**" = ["ANN001", "ANN101", "ANN201", "ANN202", "S101", "PLR2004", "D100", "D101", "D102", "D103", "D107", "SIM117"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
no_implicit_optional = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
check_untyped_defs = true
packages = ["cardre", "sidecar"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "numpy",
    "numpy.*",
]
follow_imports = "skip"

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "polars.*",
    "sklearn.*",
    "scipy.*",
    "uvicorn.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_classes = ["Test*", "*Tests"]
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--cov=cardre",
    "--cov=sidecar",
    "--cov-report=term-missing",

    "slow: tests that take longer to run",
    "api: sidecar API integration tests",
    "e2e: end-to-end acceptance tests",

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["cardre"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain must not import internal packages"

forbidden_modules = [
    "cardre.application",
    "cardre.nodes",
    "cardre.adapters",
    "cardre.api",
    "cardre.bootstrap",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Application must not import adapters, api, or bootstrap"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["cardre.application"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "cardre.adapters",
    "cardre.api",
    "cardre.bootstrap",
]
ignore_imports = []

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Nodes must not import application, adapters, api, or bootstrap"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["cardre.nodes"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "cardre.application",
    "cardre.adapters",
    "cardre.api",
    "cardre.bootstrap",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = []

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Adapters must not import api, bootstrap, or nodes"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["cardre.adapters"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "cardre.api",
    "cardre.bootstrap",
    "cardre.nodes",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "API must not import adapters or nodes"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["cardre.api"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "cardre.adapters",
    "cardre.nodes",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[tool.importlinter.independent_modules]
modules = [
    "cardre._version",
    "cardre.modeling",
    "sidecar",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "laughtrack"

## NOTE: A strict layered contract is intentionally omitted at this stage.
## We start with targeted forbidden rules to establish a safe baseline,
## and will tighten to layers after refactors.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Ports do not depend on app/infra/scrapers/adapters"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["laughtrack.ports"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "laughtrack.app",
    "laughtrack.infrastructure",
    "laughtrack.scrapers",
    "laughtrack.adapters",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Scrapers cannot depend on app"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["laughtrack.scrapers"]
forbidden_modules = ["laughtrack.app"]

## Restores the entity-layer purity guarantee lost when the laughtrack.domain
## facade (and its forbidden contract) was deleted in TASK-3646. Scoped to
## core.entities rather than all of laughtrack.core because core.services
## legitimately reaches infrastructure today (e.g. metrics.reporter ->
## infrastructure.email.service). core/entities/__init__.py exists so this
## source is a regular package — import-linter rejects implicit namespace
## packages as sources. base_handler reaches the DB through the
## ports.database seam (adapters.db self-registers at import — TASK-3701),
## so no ignore_imports grandfathering remains.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Core entities do not depend on app/infra/scrapers/adapters"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["laughtrack.core.entities"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "laughtrack.app",
    "laughtrack.infrastructure",
    "laughtrack.scrapers",
    "laughtrack.adapters",
]

## laughtrack.domain was a pure re-export facade over laughtrack.core, deleted
## in TASK-3646. Import laughtrack.core directly; do not reintroduce the facade.
## Sources enumerate every laughtrack subpackage (not the root) because
## import-linter rejects a contract whose forbidden module is a descendant of a
## source module once that module exists again. When adding a new top-level
## laughtrack subpackage, add it to this source list too.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The deleted laughtrack.domain facade must not be reintroduced"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "laughtrack.adapters",
    "laughtrack.app",
    "laughtrack.core",
    "laughtrack.foundation",
    "laughtrack.infrastructure",
    "laughtrack.ports",
    "laughtrack.scrapers",
    "laughtrack.shared",
    "laughtrack.utilities",
]
forbidden_modules = ["laughtrack.domain"]

const RUNTIME_MODULES = ['daemon', 'data', 'transports', 'security', 'pairing', 'connect', 'tunnel', 'power', 'push']

const any = (parts) => `(?:${parts.join('|')})`

const LAYERS = [
  'kernel',
  `runtime/${any(RUNTIME_MODULES)}`,
  'workspace',
  'services',
  'client',
  'panels',
  'shells',
]

const layerName = (layer) => layer.split('/')[0]

const ROOT = `^src/${any(LAYERS)}`
const NEW = `${ROOT}/`
// A panel's definition.ts is a contract (pure); its session.ts and
// runtime.ts are its runtime side.
const PANEL_DEFINITION = '^src/panels/[^/]+/definition\\.ts$'
const CONTRACT = `(?:${ROOT}.*/contract(?:\\.ts$|/)|${PANEL_DEFINITION})`
// Sides are folders of the shared modules; a shell is one zone of its own.
const SHARED = `^src/${any(LAYERS.filter((layer) => layer !== 'shells'))}`
const side = (names) => `${SHARED}.*/${any(names)}/`
// The desktop shell, its UI included, and the iOS app's headless client core.
const DESKTOP_SHELL = '^src/shells/desktop/'
const MOBILE_SHELL = '^src/shells/mobile/'

const RUNTIME = [side(['runtime']), '^src/runtime/daemon/(?!node/|desktop/|client/)', '^src/panels/[^/]+/(?:session|runtime)\\.ts$']
// The daemon's composition root wires every module's runtime side.
const COMPOSITION_ROOT = '^src/runtime/daemon/(?:entry\\.ts$|main\\.ts$|compose/)'
const NODE = [side(['node'])]
const CLIENT = [side(['client']), '^src/client/', '^src/kernel/interaction/']
const DESKTOP = [side(['desktop']), DESKTOP_SHELL]

const SIDE_NAMES = ['runtime', 'client', 'desktop', 'node']
const PUBLIC_ENTRY = [
  `${ROOT}.*/contract(?:\\.ts$|/.*\\.ts$)`,
  `${ROOT}.*/${any(SIDE_NAMES)}/index\\.tsx?$`,
  // A desktop side splits by Electron process: desktop/{main,preload,renderer}/index.ts.
  `${ROOT}.*/desktop/[^/]+/index\\.tsx?$`,
  // The client layer's modules and kernel/interaction are client core as a
  // whole, with no side folders: their module index is their client side's.
  '^src/(?:client/[^/]+|kernel/interaction)/index\\.ts$',
  // The panel index: every panel's definition, and the daemon's panel runtimes.
  '^src/panels/(definitions|runtime|api|settings|capabilities)\\.ts$',
]

const IMPURE = `^(?:node_modules/)?(?:@types/)?${any([
  'electron',
  'electron-log',
  'react',
  'react-dom',
  '@xterm',
  'xterm',
  'monaco-editor',
  'y-monaco',
  'chokidar',
  'node-pty',
  'ws',
  'simple-git',
  'bonjour-service',
  'node-datachannel',
  '@parcel/watcher',
  'electron-updater',
  'lucide-react',
  '@phosphor-icons',
])}(?:/|$)`
const ELECTRON = `^(?:node_modules/)?(?:electron|electron-log)(?:/|$)`
// What draws: React and the libraries only a UI uses. The runtime's headless
// terminal (@xterm/headless, the serialize addon) and zustand/vanilla stores
// are not UI.
const UI_LIBRARY = `^(?:node_modules/)?(?:@types/)?${any([
  'react',
  'react-dom',
  'react-markdown',
  'zustand/(?:esm/)?(?:index|traditional|shallow|react)(?:\\.d)?\\.[cm]?[jt]s$',
  'lucide-react',
  '@phosphor-icons',
  '@xterm/xterm',
  '@xterm/addon-(?:fit|search|web-links|webgl)',
  'monaco-editor',
  'y-monaco',
  'pdfjs-dist',
  'mermaid',
])}(?:/|$)`


const forbid = (name, comment, from, to) => ({ name, comment, severity: 'error', from, to })

const sideRules = [
  forbid('runtime-side', 'runtime/ imports only contracts, runtime/ and node/',
    { path: RUNTIME, pathNot: [CONTRACT, COMPOSITION_ROOT] },
    { path: NEW, pathNot: [CONTRACT, ...RUNTIME, ...NODE] }),
  forbid('node-side', 'node/ imports only contracts and node/',
    { path: NODE, pathNot: CONTRACT },
    { path: NEW, pathNot: [CONTRACT, ...NODE] }),
  forbid('client-side', 'client/ imports only contracts and client/',
    { path: CLIENT, pathNot: CONTRACT },
    { path: NEW, pathNot: [CONTRACT, ...CLIENT] }),
  forbid('desktop-side', 'desktop/ and the desktop shell never import a runtime/ side',
    { path: DESKTOP },
    { path: RUNTIME, pathNot: CONTRACT }),
  forbid('portable-client', 'the client core runs on every client: no Node built-ins',
    { path: [...CLIENT, MOBILE_SHELL] },
    { dependencyTypes: ['core'] }),
  forbid('portable-client-electron', 'the client core runs on every client: no Electron',
    { path: [...CLIENT, MOBILE_SHELL] },
    { path: ELECTRON }),
  forbid('mobile-shell', 'the iOS core never imports a runtime/ side or the desktop shell',
    { path: MOBILE_SHELL },
    { path: [...RUNTIME, ...NODE, ...DESKTOP], pathNot: CONTRACT }),
  forbid('ui-only-in-desktop-shell', 'UI (React, the DOM libraries) lives only in the desktop shell; shared code holds no UI',
    { pathNot: DESKTOP_SHELL },
    { path: UI_LIBRARY }),
  forbid('daemon-no-electron', 'runtime/ and node/ run in the daemon, which has no Electron',
    { path: [...RUNTIME, ...NODE] },
    { path: ELECTRON }),
]

const contractRules = [
  forbid('contract-pure', 'contracts are pure: no Electron, React, DOM or I/O libraries',
    { path: CONTRACT },
    { path: IMPURE }),
  forbid('contract-no-core', 'contracts do not import Node built-ins',
    { path: CONTRACT },
    { dependencyTypes: ['core'] }),
  forbid('contract-only-contracts', 'contracts import only other contracts',
    { path: CONTRACT },
    { path: NEW, pathNot: CONTRACT }),
]

// The `cate` CLI: contracts, the rpc client and the panel index files.
const CLI = '^src/cli/'
const cliRules = [
  forbid('cli-zone', 'the cate CLI imports only contracts, kernel/rpc/client and the panel index files',
    { path: CLI },
    { path: '^src/', pathNot: [CLI, CONTRACT, '^src/kernel/rpc/client/index\\.ts$', '^src/panels/(definitions|api)\\.ts$'] }),
]

const higher = (index) => `^src/${any(LAYERS.slice(index + 1))}/`

const layerRules = LAYERS.slice(0, -1).flatMap((layer, index) => [
  forbid(`layer-${layerName(layer)}`, `${layerName(layer)} imports only its own layer or layers below`,
    { path: `^src/${layer}/`, pathNot: [CONTRACT, COMPOSITION_ROOT] },
    { path: higher(index), pathNot: CONTRACT }),
  forbid(`contract-layer-${layerName(layer)}`, `${layerName(layer)} contracts import contracts of their own layer or below`,
    { path: `^src/${layer}/.*/contract(?:\\.ts$|/)` },
    { path: higher(index) }),
])

const publicEntries = forbid('public-entries', "across modules, import a module's contract or a side's index.ts",
  { path: `^src/(${any(LAYERS.map(layerName))})/([^/]+)/`, pathNot: COMPOSITION_ROOT },
  { path: NEW, pathNot: ['^src/$1/$2/', ...PUBLIC_ENTRY] })

// Dependencies between services point one way (architecture 10.3): agents
// plugs into terminal's extension points, terminal never knows agents.
const serviceRules = [
  forbid('terminal-no-agents', 'the terminal service never imports agents; agents plugs into its extension points',
    { path: ['^src/services/terminal/', '^src/shells/desktop/ui/services/terminal/'] },
    { path: ['^src/services/agents/', '^src/shells/desktop/ui/services/agents/'] }),
]

module.exports = {
  forbidden: [...contractRules, ...sideRules, ...layerRules, publicEntries, ...serviceRules, ...cliRules],
  options: {
    doNotFollow: { path: ['node_modules'] },
    exclude: { path: ['\\.i?test\\.tsx?$', '^src/test/'] },
    tsPreCompilationDeps: true,
    tsConfig: { fileName: 'tsconfig.json' },
    enhancedResolveOptions: {
      exportsFields: ['exports'],
      conditionNames: ['import', 'require', 'node', 'default', 'types'],
      extensions: ['.ts', '.tsx', '.d.ts', '.js', '.cjs', '.mjs', '.json'],
    },
  },
}
