# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Style and typing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "A",    # shadowed builtins
    "ANN",  # mandatory annotations
    "ARG",  # unused arguments
    "B",    # bugbear, includes mutable default arguments
    "BLE",  # blind except
    "C4",   # comprehensions
    "D",    # docstrings
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors, includes bare except
    "ERA",  # commented-out code
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "I",    # import ordering: standard library, third party, internal
    "N",    # naming conventions
    "PL",   # pylint
    "PT",   # pytest style
    "PTH",  # prefer pathlib over os.path
    "RET",  # return consistency
    "RUF",  # ruff-specific, includes ambiguous unicode
    "SIM",  # simplification
    "TD",   # a TODO must carry an issue reference
    "TID",  # tidy imports
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
]
ignore = [
    "D203",  # conflicts with D211
    "D213",  # conflicts with D212
    # The port contracts under specs/001-cxr-vqa-vilt/contracts/ document every
    # method in the third person ("Returns the validated samples"). Code and
    # contract must read alike, so imperative mood is not enforced.
    "D401",
    # A constructor docstring restating the class docstring is the filler the
    # engineering standards prohibit. Classes must be documented; their __init__
    # is documented by the class.
    "D107",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# A test method's name is its documentation; a docstring restating it is filler.
# Test classes and modules do carry docstrings, so D101 and D100 stay enforced.
"tests/**" = ["D102", "D103", "PLR2004"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
warn_unreachable = true
# The pre-commit check scripts under tools/ guard the repository against committed
# radiographs and credentials, so they are held to the same strictness as the source.
files = ["src", "tests", "tools"]

# disallow_any_explicit is deliberately NOT enabled. Pydantic generates an
# __init__(**data: Any) on every BaseModel subclass, and Constitution II mandates
# Pydantic for every type crossing a boundary, so the setting would flag the
# architecture itself rather than any hand-written Any. The prohibition on Any in
# our own signatures is carried by strict mode's disallow_untyped_defs and
# disallow_any_generics, and by review.

# The test tree mirrors the source tree, so basenames repeat across packages
# (tests/unit/domain/constants/test_reporting.py and .../errors/test_reporting.py).
# Deriving module names from the full path relative to the repository root keeps
# them unique without scattering __init__.py files through the test tree.

    # is a general, first-class platform ingress the user wants always available

    # Three former extras folded into the core install (PACKAGING-INSTALL,

# Experimental controller shipped as ``sail-kd[agent]`` with kd 0.8.0. Install with
# ``uv sync --extra agent``; CI installs it too since 2026-08-14, so the kdagent
# suites actually run there. What stays pinned is that the PACKAGE ROOT is light:
# ``import kdagent`` runs only a lazy ``__getattr__`` and pulls in none of this
# (``pdeagent/tests/unit/kdagent/test_lazy_extra.py``). The modules below the root DO
# import the framework at module level — ``adapter``'s injected-argument
# annotations and ``state``'s channel schema both require it.
# deepagents was ruled OUT by the 2026-08 v0 (its filesystem/sub-agent middleware
# is non-excludable scaffolding, ~2.4k tokens of file-tool schema per turn) and
# back IN by the 2026-08-10 rewrite: the collaborator's ask #3 is the model
# writing its own analysis scripts, and ``execute`` ships only with that backend.
# langchain-openai provides the OpenAI-compatible chat model kd's convention
# targets (OPENAI_API_KEY / OPENAI_BASE_URL).
# langchain-anthropic covers the endpoints whose plan-tier keys are honored only
# on an Anthropic-protocol surface (Zhipu GLM); orchestration imports it lazily,
# inside that branch. Kept in step with pdeagent/pyproject.toml.
agent = [
    "deepagents>=0.7,<1",
    "langchain>=1.3,<2",
    "langchain-openai>=1.0",
    "langchain-anthropic>=1.5",
]
# Everything optional at once.
all = [
    "sail-kd[pysr,agent]",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=7.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.4.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.0",
    "mypy>=1.0",
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
    "pandas>=3.0.3",
    "scikit-learn>=1.9.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    # The EDL reference-oracle conftest imports tqdm at module load; without
    # it the fast tier drowns real failures in collection errors.
    "tqdm>=4.60",
    "memray>=1.19.3",
    "py-spy>=0.4.2",
    "ipykernel>=7.3.0",
    # Layering gate (.importlinter). Pinned to one minor so a cold runner
    # cannot drift gate semantics; lived behind `uv run --with` until 2026-09-13.
    "import-linter>=2.13,<2.14",
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
# Discover all `kd*` packages under src/. ``pdeagent/src`` is a second root
# because the controller moved out to its own subproject dir (2026-08-18): that
# whole directory is what ``git subtree push --prefix=pdeagent`` publishes to the
# PDEAgent repo, so its README / pyproject / test conftest live there and have
# exactly one home. Dropping this entry does not fail loudly -- ``import
# kdagent`` just stops resolving after the next sync.
where = ["src", "pdeagent/src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
# Bundle benchmark dataset files + report HTML template into the wheel so
# loaders / VizEngine.render_all work after `pip install` (no source-tree
# fallback needed). py.typed is the PEP 561 marker: without it a type
# checker treats an *installed* kd as Any (the tax kd itself pays for pysr,
# see the mypy overrides below), and setuptools ships only .py unless the
# marker is listed here -- an editable install hides the omission because it
# reads src/ directly.
"kd" = ["py.typed", "_assets/data/*"]
"kd.viz.templates" = ["*.html"]
"kd.search.eqgpt" = ["_assets/*.json"]
# Kept in step with pdeagent/pyproject.toml (package-data): the controller's
# instrument cards must ride the root wheel too, or a non-editable root install
# assembles its first SKILL.md from an empty glob (arch-audit WIRE-02).
"kdagent" = ["_assets/*.md", "_assets/instruments/*.md", "_assets/guidance/*.md", "_assets/skills/*/*.md", "_assets/task/*.md", "_assets/pinned-input/*.md", "_assets/experience/*.md", "_assets/fingerprint/*.json"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Two roots since 2026-08-18: the controller's tests moved with it into
# ``kdagent/``. Bare pytest must still collect both, or CI silently stops
# running the controller suite (CI runs `pytest tests/` -- see ci.yml, which
# names both paths for the same reason).
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Default = fast tier: bare pytest must never trip the
# slow/golden science-contract tests (multi-hour, golden also requires
# PYTHONHASHSEED=0). An explicit -m on the CLI REPLACES this filter:
# uv run pytest -m slow -> slow suite (nightly)
# uv run pytest -m "" -> full run, no marker filter
addopts = '-m "not slow"'
markers = [
    "smoke: quick sanity checks (run always)",
    "unit: isolated function tests",
    "integration: component interaction tests",
    "equivalence: comparison with reference implementations",
    "e2e: end-to-end pipeline tests",
    "benchmark: performance tests",
    "numerical: numerical stability tests",
    "slow: tests that take >10s",
    "validation: algorithm validation tests (fidelity + recovery)",
    "golden: golden-baseline regression tests (discover subsystem, very slow)",
    "mode2_aggregate: 3-seed STRICT MODE2 aggregate (discover §B.2 contract)",
    "phase3_e2e: full discover plugin e2e (slow, requires GPU; research suite)",
    "pysr: tests requiring the optional PySR/Julia backend (excluded from default smoke)",
    "pysindy: tests exercising the PySINDy backend",
    "eqgpt: tests requiring the EqGPT pretrained assets / reference source (skip gracefully when absent)",
    "exploration: open-question probes that are NOT quality gates — never run by default or nightly; run on demand with -m exploration",
    "v1_compare: kd vs v1 oracle recovery comparison; excluded from the weekly and full slow runs, run on demand with -m v1_compare",
]

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true

# pysr is an optional extra (sail-kd[pysr]); environments without it (CI) must
# not fail on the lazy import. Paired override: missing pysr is fine, and
# the import site's `type: ignore[import-untyped]` (used when pysr IS
# installed locally, since pysr ships no py.typed) is allowed to sit
# unused when pysr is absent.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "pysr"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "kd.search.pysr.backend"
warn_unused_ignores = false

# pysindy ships no py.typed; the adapter imports it inside fit under a
# ``type: ignore[import-untyped]`` that the paired backend override keeps valid.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "pysindy.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# The agent runtime is an optional extra (sail-kd[agent]) that kdagent's lower modules
# import at module level, so a bare ``uv sync`` must still type-check.
# CI installs the extra, so there these overrides are inert and the real types are
# checked; they only matter to a dev who skipped it. ``deepagents`` belongs in the
# list because ``kdagent.state`` imports ``DeepAgentState`` at module level.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["deepagents.*", "langchain.*", "langchain_core.*", "langgraph.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "kd.search.pysindy.backend"
warn_unused_ignores = false

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 88

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "A", "SIM"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# discover subsystem tests follow ML tensor-dim naming (B, L, N, T) and
# math-notation test names (test_R_e_*, test_baseline_R_*); idiomatic for
# this code class.
"tests/**/discover/**/*.py" = ["N806", "N802"]
"tests/integration/test_discover_*.py" = ["N806", "N802"]
"tests/helpers/discover_*.py" = ["N806", "N802"]
"tests/helpers/test_discover_noise.py" = ["N806", "N802"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["domain", "application", "infrastructure", "api"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered Architecture"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "api",
    "infrastructure",
    "application",
    "domain",
]

requires = ["setuptools>=64", "setuptools_scm[toml]>=8"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "py_launch_blueprint"
# ITM-070 — static version (ADR-06 cutover). release-please bumps this.

description = "CLI tools for interacting with Py, including project search functionality"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
license = "MIT" # PEP 639 license expression (ITM-070, round-19).
authors = [{ name = "Steve Morin", email = "steve.morin@gmail.com" }]
classifiers = [
  # ITM-070 — round-19. py3.13+ only (per ITM-033 floor); MIT classifier
  # intentionally omitted (PEP 639 license expression above is the single
  # source of truth — duplication would drift).
  "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
]
dependencies = [
  "click>=8.1.0",
  "pydantic>=2.0.0",   # structured result models (the JSON representation)
  "structlog>=24.1.0", # structured logging (human-friendly TTY / JSON otherwise)
  "tomli-w>=1.0.0",    # writing the TOML config file (`config set`)
  "requests>=2.31.0",
  "rich>=13.0.0",
]

# Single-distribution + extras strategy. The library (core/) and CLI always
# install; the web service ships behind the `web` extra:
#   uv sync --extra web   /   pip install py-launch-blueprint[web]

  "uvicorn[standard]>=0.29.0",

  "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp>=1.27.0",
  "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.48b0",
]

# ITM-063 — PEP 735 dependency-groups (round-13 decision). Replaces

  "pytest>=7.0.0",
  "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
  "ty>=0.0.1a16",        # per ADR-03 (pre-1.0; bump as needed)

# ITM-072 — package metadata URLs (round 19).

[tool.ruff]
# ITM-018 reconciled config (round-2). Merge: template's stricter rule
# selection + source's ignore rationale. target-version reflects ITM-033
# Python-floor bump.
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 88

lint.select = [
  "E",   # pycodestyle errors
  "F",   # pyflakes
  "I",   # isort
  "B",   # flake8-bugbear
  "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
  "UP",  # pyupgrade
  "N",   # pep8-naming
  "RUF", # Ruff-specific rules
  "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
  "YTT", # flake8-2020

  "W293", # whitespace on blank line (formatter owns trim_trailing)
]

  ".venv",
  "__pycache__",
  "build",
  "dist",
  "docs/source/conf.py",
  "src/py_launch_blueprint/_version.py",

]

[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"] # Ignore unused imports in __init__.py files
"tests/*" = [

  "S105",
  "S106",
  "ANN",
] # asserts + annotations optional in tests
# S101: assert statements removed under -O — security risk if assert is the only gate.
# S105/S106: hardcoded password strings/variables in code.

# ITM-018 — explicit format config (round-2; mirrors source). Values match Ruff
# defaults but being explicit prevents silent drift if defaults change.
[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"

# Pyright/Pylance (IDE) strict type checking — formerly pyrightconfig.json.
# CI typechecking runs ty (ADR-03); this section drives the VS Code Pyright
# extension and ad-hoc `pyright` runs.
[tool.pyright]
include = ["src/py_launch_blueprint", "tests"]
exclude = ["**/node_modules", "**/__pycache__"]
defineConstant = { DEBUG = true }
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
pythonVersion = "3.13"
useLibraryCodeForTypes = true
reportMissingImports = true
reportMissingTypeStubs = true
reportUnknownParameterType = true
reportUnknownArgumentType = true
reportUnknownLambdaType = true
reportUnknownVariableType = true
reportUnknownMemberType = true
reportMissingTypeArgument = true
reportInvalidTypeVarUse = true
reportUnnecessaryIsInstance = true
reportUnnecessaryCast = true
reportUnnecessaryComparison = true
reportDuplicateImport = true
reportPrivateUsage = "warning"
reportUnusedImport = true
reportUnusedVariable = true
reportUnusedFunction = true
reportUnusedClass = true

# ty (Astral) is the CI type-check authority (ADR-03). ty is rule-based, not
# strict-mode-based: its correctness core already defaults to `error`, so this
# block only promotes the handful of quality rules that ship below `error`.
# Each was verified against the pinned ty (see uv.lock, 0.0.61): running
# `ty check --error <rule> src/py_launch_blueprint/` passes for each.
# `error-on-warning` is set explicitly to false below (not left implicit): a
# dependency `deprecated` warning must not fail every fork's CI, and pinning the
# value keeps CI deterministic across ty upgrades (its default is version-
# sensitive pre-1.0). `strict-literal-narrowing` is left off as an optional
# stricter knob. See projects/P03-type-precision-uplevel.md.
[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.13" # matches requires-python floor; explicit for determinism

[tool.ty.rules]
ambiguous-protocol-member = "error"      # core/ports.py exposes Protocol ports
blanket-ignore-comment = "error"         # every `# ty: ignore` must name its rule
invalid-ignore-comment = "error"
ignore-comment-unknown-rule = "error"
ineffective-final = "error"
invalid-enum-member-annotation = "error"
invalid-named-tuple-override = "error"

[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = false # warnings (e.g. `deprecated`) inform; they don't gate CI

# ITM-027 — bandit config (round 3). Tests legitimately use `assert`
# (pytest convention) — exclude_dirs covers tests/.
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", ".venv", "build", "dist"]
skips = []                                         # No global skips; add with rationale only.

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
# Marker taxonomy (ITM-046, round-9 decision).
# `live` = requires external services; `slow` = takes >1s.
# Default `addopts` excludes both — run full suite with `pytest -m ""`.
markers = ["live: requires external services", "slow: takes >1s"]
addopts = "-m 'not live and not slow'"
strict_markers = true
# WL-009 — a hung test fails loudly instead of burning a CI slot. `thread`
# method (not the POSIX-only signal default) so the cap also holds on the
# Windows matrix leg. A genuinely slow test overrides via
# `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)`.
timeout = 60
timeout_method = "thread"
# WL-010 (pytest-randomly) reorders tests each run with a printed, replayable
# seed (`-p randomly --randomly-seed=…`) to surface hidden inter-test coupling;
# it needs no config. Parallelism (WL-008, `-n auto`) is opt-in per invocation
# (`just test -n auto`, and the CI full-suite + canary runs) rather than in
# default addopts, so the fast local inner loop keeps clean `-x`/pdb behaviour.

# Branch coverage (ADR-0019): count both-arms of every branch, not just line
# execution, so the Codecov gate (WL-005) catches untested conditionals.
[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true

# ITM-015 — codespell. US English baseline (default builtin="clear,rare"); empty
# ignore list — add terms only when intentional. Decided round 9.
[tool.codespell]
skip = ".git,.venv,build,dist,node_modules,uv.lock,bun.lock,*.lock,docs/_build,*.svg,*.cast,.ruff_cache,.pytest_cache,.mypy_cache,.ty_cache,*.log"
# *.log: raw run output, not prose.
ignore-words-list = "ans,porjects,unparseable"
# ans: variable name used in prompt-handling code; codespell wants to "fix"
# it to "and". Whitelist to keep the short variable name.
# porjects: intentional typo — the did-you-mean example in cli/groups.py and
# its test ("plbp porjects" must suggest "projects").
check-filenames = true
check-hidden = false

# HEX-30 — import-linter: enforce the hexagonal boundaries described in
# docs/design/0005-hexagonal-architecture-and-enforcement.md. Run via
# `uv run lint-imports` (locked dev group, WL-001); wired into `just check`
# and the pre-push hook. Contracts match the CURRENT layer-first layout
# (core / cli / web); the feature-first reshape (HEX-02) + tach come with the
# second capability.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "py_launch_blueprint"
# Required because the framework-bleed contract names external packages
# (fastapi/click/uvicorn) as forbidden imports.
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core never imports the front-ends (inward-only, HEX-01)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["py_launch_blueprint.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["py_launch_blueprint.cli", "py_launch_blueprint.web"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "cli and web are independent of each other"
type = "independence"
modules = ["py_launch_blueprint.cli", "py_launch_blueprint.web"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "composition root is not imported by core (HEX-04)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["py_launch_blueprint.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["py_launch_blueprint.composition"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core layering: models < services < adapters (HEX-01)"
type = "layers"
layers = [
  "py_launch_blueprint.core.adapters",
  "py_launch_blueprint.core.services",
  "py_launch_blueprint.core.models",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core does not import web/cli frameworks (framework-bleed, HEX-32)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["py_launch_blueprint.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["fastapi", "click", "uvicorn"]

[project]
name = "pyrpoc"
version = "3.1.4"
description = "Real-time Precision Opto-Control Toolkit"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "MIT"

authors = [
  { name = "Ishaan Singh", email = "sing1125@purdue.edu" }
]

dependencies = [
  "opencv-python",
  "pyqt6",
  "PyQt6Ads",
  "pyqtgraph",
  "nidaqmx",
  "tifffile",
  "swabian-timetagger>=2.22.6",
]

[project.scripts]
pyrpoc = "pyrpoc.main:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["pyrpoc*"]

# pyrpoc/assets/ is not a package, so its icons ship as data of pyrpoc.
[tool.setuptools.package-data]
pyrpoc = ["assets/*.svg", "assets/*.png", "assets/sdks/*.dll"]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "pyright",
  "ruff",
  "pre-commit",
  "import-linter>=2.15",
  "pytest>=9.1.1",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.pyright]
include = ["pyrpoc", "tests"]
exclude = [
  "docs/swabian_demos",
  "rpoc_env",
  "dist",
  "build",
  "**/__pycache__",
  "**/*.egg-info",
]
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"
pythonVersion = "3.13"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
# Problems get fixed, not silenced: `# type: ignore` has no effect, and the
# pre-commit hook rejects `# pyright: ignore` (which this setting cannot turn off).
enableTypeIgnoreComments = false

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
extend-exclude = ["docs/swabian_demos", "rpoc_env"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", "F",   # basic errors, unused imports and variables
  "I",        # import sorting, plus the required __future__ import (see below)
  "B",        # likely bugs
  "UP",       # modernize syntax; UP037 removes quoted annotations
  "FA",       # flags annotations that need the __future__ import
  "SIM",      # simplifiable code
]
# SIM118 assumes .keys() is a dict's; here it is Registry.keys() and
# catalog.keys(), which support neither `in` nor iteration.
ignore = ["SIM118"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Generated by the Qt resource compiler.
"pyrpoc/app/theme/breeze_all.py" = ["E501"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# Every file must start with this (rule I002, auto-fixable). Once it is there,
# quotes around a type name are never needed, and UP037 flags them.
required-imports = ["from __future__ import annotations"]

[tool.ruff.format]
line-ending = "lf"

# The architecture, checked by `uv run lint-imports`. Each ignore_imports list
# is a ledger of known debt: delete a line when its import is fixed, and never
# add one to make a new violation pass.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "pyrpoc"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layers: app > acquisition > data_library | device_inventory > plugins > qt_components > structs"
type = "layers"
containers = ["pyrpoc"]
layers = [
  "app",
  "acquisition",
  "data_library | device_inventory",
  "plugins",
  "qt_components",
  "structs",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Inside plugins: programs may use devices; programs and data panels never meet"
type = "layers"
containers = ["pyrpoc.plugins"]
layers = ["programs | data_panels", "devices"]

# Keyed on <name>/program.py, the file every program registers in, so the
# contracts never list the programs themselves.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Programs never import each other; they share through building_blocks"
type = "independence"
modules = ["pyrpoc.plugins.programs.*.program"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Building blocks never import a program"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pyrpoc.plugins.programs.building_blocks"]
forbidden_modules = ["pyrpoc.plugins.programs.*.program"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Subsystems never name a plugin; they find plugins through registries"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pyrpoc.acquisition", "pyrpoc.data_library", "pyrpoc.device_inventory"]
forbidden_modules = ["pyrpoc.plugins"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "structs is Qt-free, except plugins/data_panels.py"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "pyrpoc.structs.registry",
  "pyrpoc.structs.data_library",
  "pyrpoc.structs.plugins.devices",
  "pyrpoc.structs.plugins.params",
  "pyrpoc.structs.plugins.programs",
]
forbidden_modules = ["PyQt6", "pyqtgraph"]
ignore_imports = [
  # A type-only import, for the return type of Device.panel().
  "pyrpoc.structs.plugins.devices -> PyQt6",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The cores are Qt-free: running, the library's store and files, the session file"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "pyrpoc.acquisition.claims",
  "pyrpoc.acquisition.executor",
  "pyrpoc.acquisition.recording",
  "pyrpoc.data_library.store",
  "pyrpoc.data_library.saving",
  "pyrpoc.data_library.format",
  "pyrpoc.app.session.file",
]
forbidden_modules = ["PyQt6"]
# Direct imports only: structs.plugins.devices' type-only Qt import is already on the
# structs ledger above, and reaches these through structs, not through them.
allow_indirect_imports = true

# The application itself is left out: it is the composition root, and importing
# every plugin, display panels included, is how it registers them.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Subsystem models hold no widgets: they never import a panel or a widget"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "pyrpoc.acquisition.model",
  "pyrpoc.acquisition.host",
  "pyrpoc.acquisition.events",
  "pyrpoc.data_library.model",
  "pyrpoc.device_inventory.inventory",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "pyrpoc.acquisition.panel",
  "pyrpoc.data_library.panel",
  "pyrpoc.data_library.details",
  "pyrpoc.device_inventory.panel",
  "pyrpoc.qt_components",
  "pyqtgraph",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Inside app: session > window > menubar > theme | application"
type = "layers"
containers = ["pyrpoc.app"]
layers = ["session", "window", "menubar", "theme | application"]

[project]
name = "mixd"
version = "0.12.1.3"
description = "Music metadata integration and playlist management platform"
authors = [{name = "Ash Wright", email = "a@ashwright.net"}]
readme = "README.md"
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
requires-python = ">=3.14,<3.15"
# Floors track the lock: every `>=` below is the version `uv.lock` resolves to, raised
# in step on each dependency sweep. Mixd is an application deployed from its own
# lockfile, never a library someone else co-installs, so a tight floor costs nothing
# and buys an honest manifest — `pyproject.toml` states what we actually run against
# rather than the oldest version that once happened to work.
dependencies = [
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.54,<2.1",
    "alembic>=1.20.0",
    # Pydantic's stewarded continuation of httpx (encode/httpx has had no release
    # since 2024). Starlette's TestClient already prefers it and mcp v2 requires it,
    # so this is the line the ecosystem settled on. Plain httpx stays in the lock
    # only as an anthropic transitive; nothing in src/ or tests/ imports it.
    "httpx2>=2.13.0,<3",
    "structlog>=26.1.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.3",
    "rich>=15.0.0",
    "typer>=0.27.2",
    "attrs>=26.1.0",
    "tenacity>=9.1.4",
    "psycopg[binary]>=3.3.6",
    "rapidfuzz>=3.14.6",
    "pydantic>=2.13.5",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.15.0",
    "cryptography>=50.0.1",
    "fastapi>=0.141.1",
    # Imported directly by the ASGI middleware in src/interface/api/ and
    # src/interface/mcp/ (starlette.datastructures, .types, .routing,
    # .middleware.authentication — FastAPI does not re-export these), so it is a
    # real first-party dependency, not just a fastapi transitive.
    "starlette>=1.6.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.53.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.32",
    "jellyfish>=1.2.1",
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.14.0",
    "orjson>=3.12.0",
    "croniter>=6.2.4",
    "anthropic>=0.125.0,<1",
    # v0.9.3 MCP server, on the stable v2 SDK (2.0.0 released 2026-07-28).
    "mcp>=2.2.0,<3",
    # Imported directly by src/interface/mcp/server.py, so declared here; mcp itself
    # pins it to an exact matching version.
    "mcp-types>=2.2.0,<3",
    # Imported directly by src/interface/api/app.py (the shutdown drain sets
    # `AppStatus.should_exit`), so declared here; it otherwise arrives only as an
    # mcp transitive, which deptry rightly reports as DEP001.
    "sse-starlette>=3.4.11",
]

[project.scripts]
mixd = "src.interface.cli.app:main"
mixd-api = "src.interface.api.app:run_server"
export-openapi = "scripts.export_openapi:main"
export-status-matrix = "scripts.export_status_matrix:main"

Homepage = "https://github.com/w-ash/mixd"
Documentation = "https://github.com/w-ash/mixd/docs"
Repository = "https://github.com/w-ash/mixd"
"Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/w-ash/mixd/issues"

dev = [

    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",

    "hypothesis>=6.168.0",
    "mutmut>=3.8.0,<3.9",
]

[tool.uv]
# Single source of truth for the uv version. astral-sh/setup-uv reads required-version
# from pyproject.toml and installs the match, so CI tracks this automatically; the
# ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv tag in Dockerfile must be bumped by hand to stay in step.
required-version = ">=0.13,<0.14"

# Undeclared-import detection (`uvx deptry .`, run in CI's Python job). Catches the
# class of drift W1 fixed: code importing a package we only get transitively.
[tool.deptry]
# extend_exclude, not exclude — overwriting `exclude` would drop deptry's own
# defaults (notably `tests`, whose dev-only imports would then all trip DEP004).
# docs/dev-setup-guide is a vendored submodule, not our dependency contract.
extend_exclude = ["docs/dev-setup-guide"]

# Distributions whose import name differs from their PyPI name. Required, not
# belt-and-braces: `uvx` runs deptry in its own isolated environment, so it can
# never read our installed package metadata to infer these — without the map it
# guesses the PyPI name and reports a bogus DEP002/DEP001 pair for each.
[tool.deptry.package_module_name_map]
python-dotenv = ["dotenv"]
pyjwt = ["jwt"]
python-multipart = ["multipart", "python_multipart"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# DEP002 = declared but never imported. python-multipart is a runtime *plugin* of
# FastAPI, not a library we call: FastAPI's `UploadFile` form parsing
# (src/interface/api/routes/imports.py) imports it internally and raises at request
# time if it is absent. Base `fastapi` does not depend on it (only the `standard`
# extra does), so we must declare it — and no import graph will ever see it.
DEP002 = ["python-multipart"]
# DEP004 = dev dependency imported outside tests. scripts/mutmut_run.py is dev
# tooling that wraps the dev-group mutmut.
DEP004 = ["mutmut"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src"]

# Ruff configuration for version 0.15.4+ with Python 3.14 support
[tool.ruff]
# Basic settings
line-length = 88
target-version = "py314"
preview = true  # Enable latest lint rules and formatter improvements
# Python 3.14 specific: Enhanced version-aware parsing
output-format = "full"
extend-exclude = ["vulture_whitelist.py", "docs/dev-setup-guide"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Linting rules
select = [
    "E",     # pycodestyle errors
    "F",     # pyflakes
    "I",     # isort
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear
    "UP",    # pyupgrade - modernize syntax
    "N",     # pep8-naming
    "SIM",   # flake8-simplify
    "RUF",   # Ruff-specific rules
    "C4",    # flake8-comprehensions (optimizes list/dict comprehensions)
    "TCH",   # type-checking (better typing practices)
    "TID",   # tidy imports
    "S",     # flake8-bandit (security checks)
    "PIE",   # flake8-pie (misc. lints for code improvement)
    "PT",    # flake8-pytest-style (for better test patterns)
    "COM",   # flake8-commas (trailing comma usage)
    "DTZ",   # flake8-datetimez (timezone awareness)
    "PERF",  # Performance anti-patterns
    "ERA",   # Eradication of deprecated APIs
    "ASYNC", # Common async/await issues
    "FLY",   # String formatting issues
    "ARG",   # Function argument validation
    "FURB",  # Refurb - modernize Python code patterns
    "LOG",   # Logging best practices
    "TRY",   # Exception handling best practices
    "PL",    # Pylint (additional logic checks)
    "PTH",   # Use pathlib for path operations
    "RET",   # flake8-return — simplify return patterns
    # Added with the ruff 0.16 bump. The categories above already pick up new
    # rules automatically (they select whole prefixes, and `preview = true`), so
    # these are the 0.15/0.16 additions that fell *outside* an enabled category.
    "ISC",   # flake8-implicit-str-concat — ISC004 (stabilized in 0.16) catches
             # the missing-comma-in-a-list bug class
    "PYI",   # flake8-pyi — PYI041/PYI033 apply to .py, not just stubs
    "property-docstring-starts-with-verb",  # D421: a property documents a value,
             # not an action ("Import success rate", not "Returns the rate")
]

# Rule *names* rather than codes since ruff 0.16 (RUF201). `select` above is
# unaffected — it selects whole categories, which keep their prefix form.
ignore = [
    "line-too-long",          # Handled by the formatter
    "missing-trailing-comma", # Conflicts with the formatter
    "single-line-implicit-string-concatenation", # ISC001: also conflicts with the
                              # formatter — ruff's own docs say to disable it when
                              # the formatter is on. ISC003/ISC004 stay enabled.
    # PLR complexity suppressions re-censused at the v0.8.17 sweep closeout (2026-07-02,
    # spoke 26): none reached 0, so all seven stay off. Per-rule counts + rationale below;
    # ratchet policy: flip a rule only when its count genuinely hits 0 — no new noqa.
    "too-many-branches",      # 13 left (sync_likes, track/playlist repos, diff_engine)
    "too-many-statements",    # 9 left (sync_likes at 108, executor, play_dedup)
    "too-many-locals",        # 12 left (matching/algorithms at 29, sync_likes, executor)
    "too-many-nested-blocks", # 2 left (apply_playlist_assignments; apple_music tree is user-protected)
    "no-self-use",            # Method could be function — the DI pattern requires methods
    "import-outside-top-level", # Lazy imports for CLI startup performance
    "raise-vanilla-args",     # Long exception messages — clear errors are worth it
    "literal-membership",     # Tuples are fine for small static membership checks
    "import-private-name",    # _shared modules are internal API
    "too-many-arguments",     # 61: dominated by Typer command / FastAPI Query() entry
                              # points where every CLI/API option is a parameter (framework
                              # idiom, not debt); scoped-per-file-ignore vs keep-off decision
                              # documented in fable-sweep spoke 26
    "too-many-positional-arguments", # 20, tracks too-many-arguments
    "too-many-return-statements", # 5 left, all guard/classification chains (webhook
                              # verification, error classifiers) where each return is a
                              # distinct outcome: a log event name, HTTP status, or error
                              # category. Merging returns would collapse distinct observable
                              # outcomes — worse code to satisfy a count
    "error-instead-of-exception", # Use logging.exception — doesn't apply to Loguru
    "global-statement",       # Acceptable for library-style patterns in utilities
    # PEP 649 makes deferred annotations the default, so hoisting imports into a
    # TYPE_CHECKING block buys nothing, and quoting cast() is actively wrong on 3.14.
    "typing-only-first-party-import",
    "typing-only-third-party-import",
    "typing-only-standard-library-import",
    "runtime-cast-value",
]
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = []

# Per-file rule exceptions
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["unused-import", "non-empty-init-module"]   # Allow unused imports and non-reexport code (version reading)
"src/interface/api/**/*.py" = [
    "unused-async",   # FastAPI requires async handlers even without await (framework awaits them)
]
"src/infrastructure/connectors/musicbrainz/status.py" = [
    "unused-async",   # status_fn Protocol requires async callables even for stateless probes
]
"src/infrastructure/connectors/_shared/http_client.py" = [
    "unused-async",   # httpx2 AsyncClient always awaits its event hooks; a sync hook raises TypeError
]
"src/application/chat/tool_executor.py" = [
    "unused-async",   # ToolDispatch protocol requires async dispatchers even without await
    "unused-function-argument",   # dispatchers share one (tool_input, ctx) signature; not all use both
]
"src/application/chat/dispatchers/*_write.py" = [
    "unused-async",   # write dispatchers propose (no I/O) but ToolDispatch requires async
]
"src/application/chat/dispatchers/long_ops.py" = [
    "unused-async",   # long-op tools propose (no I/O) but ToolDispatch requires async
]
"src/interface/mcp/server.py" = [
    "unused-async",   # MCP SDK's request-handler protocol requires async handlers even
                # when a handler (tools/list) does no I/O
]
"src/application/chat/use_case.py" = [
    "yield-in-context-manager-in-async-generator", # streaming proxy MUST yield inside the LLM stream context; the SSE
                # bridge's try/finally cancels the task on disconnect, which closes
                # the context via GeneratorExit — cleanup is guaranteed cross-function
]
".claude/hooks/guard_test_edits.py" = [
    "suspicious-subprocess-import",     # runs one fixed git command to read the branch
    "subprocess-without-shell-equals-true",     # fixed git argv; only the edited file's directory varies, passed to -C
    "start-process-with-partial-path",     # trusts PATH for git like any dev tool
]
"scripts/check_test_vacuity.py" = [
    "suspicious-subprocess-import",     # --base-ref runs fixed git commands to read the base baseline
    "subprocess-without-shell-equals-true",     # fixed git argv; the ref is validated (no leading '-')
    "start-process-with-partial-path",     # trusts PATH for git like any dev tool
]
"tests/unit/scripts/test_check_test_vacuity.py" = [
    "start-process-with-partial-path",     # builds throwaway git repos to exercise --base-ref
]
"tests/unit/scripts/test_guard_test_edits.py" = [
    "start-process-with-partial-path",     # builds throwaway git repos to exercise the hook's branch check
]
"tests/**/*.py" = [
    "assert",     # Allow assert in tests
    "suspicious-subprocess-import",     # Allow subprocess import in tests (isolation guards run fixed commands)
    "subprocess-without-shell-equals-true",     # Allow subprocess calls in tests (input is sys.executable + literal code)
    "unused-function-argument",   # Allow unused function arguments (fixtures, mocks)
    "unused-method-argument",   # Allow unused method arguments (fixtures, mocks)
    "unused-async",   # Allow async functions without await (test setup functions)
    "unused-unpacked-variable",   # Allow unused unpacked variables (destructured test results)
    "float-equality-comparison",   # Allow float equality in assertions (exact test values)
    "blocking-open-call-in-async-function", # Allow sync file operations in async test functions (test data)
    "blocking-path-method-in-async-function", # Allow pathlib in async test fixtures (cleanup code)
    "commented-out-code",   # Allow commented-out code in tests (documentation, debugging)
    "invalid-function-name",     # Allow uppercase in function names (e.g., pgcode test names)
    "non-lowercase-variable-in-function",     # Allow uppercase variables for Mock classes
    "hardcoded-password-string",     # Allow hardcoded password strings (test tokens)
    "hardcoded-password-func-arg",     # Allow hardcoded password arguments (test tokens)
    "pytest-raises-too-broad",    # Allow broad pytest.raises without match (simpler test patterns)
    "assert-raises-exception",     # Allow pytest.raises(Exception) for general exception testing
    "type-comparison",     # Allow type() == comparisons for exact type checking in tests
    "magic-value-comparison",  # Allow magic numbers in tests (durations, counts, test data)
    "unused-variable",     # Allow assigned-but-unused variables (side-effect assertions)
    "multiple-with-statements",   # Allow nested with statements (patch + pytest.raises readability)
    "unused-lambda-argument",   # Allow unused lambda arguments (mock callbacks)
    "suspicious-non-cryptographic-random-usage",     # Allow non-cryptographic random (test data generation)
    "raise-vanilla-class",   # Allow raising vanilla Exception (test error simulation)
    "compare-to-empty-string",  # Allow comparison to empty string (explicit test assertions)
    "suspicious-xml-element-tree-usage",     # Allow XML parsing in tests (test data, not untrusted)
    "suspicious-xml-etree-import",     # Allow xml.etree imports in tests (test data parsing)
    "error-suffix-on-exception-name",     # Allow exception names without Error suffix (test helpers)
    "collapsible-if",   # Allow nested ifs in tests (readability with complex conditions)
    "enumerate-for-loop",   # Allow manual counters in tests (as_completed doesn't support enumerate)
    "ambiguous-unicode-character-string",   # Allow unicode characters in test strings (intentional test data)
    "ambiguous-unicode-character-comment",   # Allow unicode characters in test comments (readability)
]
"src/domain/repositories/connector.py" = [
    "too-many-public-methods",  # ConnectorRepositoryProtocol has many methods by design
]
"src/domain/repositories/uow.py" = [
    "too-many-public-methods",  # UnitOfWorkProtocol exposes all repository accessors — many by design
]
"src/infrastructure/persistence/unit_of_work.py" = [
    "too-many-public-methods",  # UoW exposes all repository accessors — many methods by design
]
"src/infrastructure/persistence/repositories/track/connector.py" = [
    "too-many-public-methods",  # Connector track repo implements a large Protocol interface
]
"src/infrastructure/connectors/spotify/client.py" = [
    "too-many-public-methods",  # One method per Spotify Web API endpoint — breadth tracks the API surface, not design complexity
]
"src/infrastructure/connectors/spotify/connector.py" = [
    "too-many-public-methods",  # Facade implements every capability protocol Spotify satisfies — breadth tracks the port surface, not design complexity
]
"src/application/use_cases/*.py" = ["unused-method-argument"] # Allow parameter forwarding patterns in orchestrators
"src/application/workflows/observers.py" = ["unused-method-argument"] # Protocol implementations must match signatures
"src/interface/api/oauth/provider.py" = ["unused-method-argument"] # SDK OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider protocol signatures
"alembic/versions/*.py" = [
    "hardcoded-sql-expression",     # SQL injection: table names from hardcoded constants, not user input
]
"scripts/**/*.py" = [
    "blocking-open-call-in-async-function", # Allow sync file operations in async scripts
    "blocking-input-in-async-function", # Allow blocking input() in async scripts (interactive CLI prompts)
    "unused-function-argument",   # Allow unused arguments in scripts
    "unused-async",   # Allow async functions without await in scripts
    "magic-value-comparison",  # Allow magic numbers in utility scripts
    "try-consider-else",   # Allow return in try blocks (simplicity over pedantry in scripts)

# Import sorting configuration
[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["mixd", "src"]
section-order = ["future", "standard-library", "third-party", "first-party", "local-folder"]
combine-as-imports = true
split-on-trailing-comma = true
force-single-line = false           # Allow multi-line imports
force-sort-within-sections = true   # Sort within sections
from-first = false                  # Put "from" imports after regular imports (not before)
detect-same-package = true          # Similar to grouping by package
order-by-type = true                # Organize by import type

# Python 3.13+ specific settings via pyupgrade
[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
# Keep typed versions of builtins for better type checking
keep-runtime-typing = true

# Configure typing practices
[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

# Formatter configuration (Ruff 0.14.6+ with Python 3.13 support)
[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"
# 2025 best practice: Format code in docstrings
docstring-code-format = true
# Enhanced Python 3.13 support
docstring-code-line-length = "dynamic"

# flake8-annotations settings
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-annotations]
allow-star-arg-any = true
suppress-none-returning = true

# Note: implicit string concatenation (ISC) enforcement via basedpyright reportImplicitStringConcatenation
# — ruff ISC001/ISC002 don't catch the parenthesized multi-line pattern that basedpyright does.

# Testing configuration (pytest 9+ native TOML)
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
addopts = "--strict-markers --tb=short -n auto -m 'not diagnostic and not slow and not performance'"
filterwarnings = [
    # Savepoint-rollback test isolation triggers this when UoW manages its own transactions
    "ignore:nested transaction already deassociated from connection:sqlalchemy.exc.SAWarning",
    # Live mappings with no primary are a writer defect that no read repairs
    # (v0.12.1 pre-flight 1) — the mapper's warning fails the test.
    "error::src.infrastructure.persistence.repositories.track.mapper.MissingPrimaryMappingWarning",
]
markers = [
    # Test Pyramid Layers (applied via pytestmark in conftest.py)
    "unit: unit tests - pure logic, no external dependencies (<100ms)",
    "integration: integration tests - real DB, mocked APIs (<1s)",
    "e2e: end-to-end tests - full system, critical user flows (<10s)",
    # Execution Filtering (skipped by default via addopts)
    "slow: tests that take longer than 1 second",
    "performance: performance and load testing with timing assertions",
    "diagnostic: diagnostic and profiling tests - for investigation only (skip by default)",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["mixd", "src"]
omit = [
    "tests/*",
    "src/interface/cli/*",
]

# Type checking configuration - BasedPyright (modern Python-focused type checker)
[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["src"]
exclude = ["tests", "**/__pycache__"]
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
reportMissingImports = true
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportUnusedImport = true
reportUnusedVariable = true
reportDuplicateImport = true
reportUntypedBaseClass = true
reportUntypedClassDecorator = true
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = true
reportUntypedNamedTuple = true
reportDeprecated = "error"
reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment = "warning"
reportImplicitOverride = "error"
# Keep: catches genuinely unknown types from missing annotations
reportUnknownParameterType = "error"
reportUnknownVariableType = "error"
reportUnknownMemberType = "error"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "error"
reportUnknownLambdaType = "error"
# Both reportAny and reportExplicitAny at error: no Any — explicit or implicit — allowed.
reportAny = "error"
reportExplicitAny = "error"
# basedpyright-specific: narrow TypeVars to their bound union under isinstance
# checks instead of collapsing to Unknown/Any. Helps BaseRepository generics.
strictGenericNarrowing = true
# Side-effect calls (raise_for_status, .pop, .discard) intentionally discard returns.
reportUnusedCallResult = "none"
# Intentional patterns that "recommended" mode would flag as errors:
# - bare list/dict generics are valid in Python 3.14 (equivalent to list[Any])
reportMissingTypeArgument = "error"
# - attrs @define classes initialize fields via __attrs_post_init__ (not __init__)
reportUninitializedInstanceVariable = "none"
# Python 3.14
enableTypeIgnoreComments = false
pythonVersion = "3.14"
pythonPlatform = "All"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

# Dead code detection (Vulture 2.14+)
[tool.vulture]
paths = ["src/", "alembic/", "vulture_whitelist.py"]
exclude = ["tests/"]
min_confidence = 60
ignore_decorators = [
    "@router.*",           # FastAPI route handlers
    "@app.command",        # Typer CLI commands
    "@*_app.command",      # Typer CLI sub-app commands (track_app, etc.)
    "@app.callback",       # Typer CLI callbacks
    "@app.exception_handler",  # FastAPI exception handlers
    "@field_validator",    # Pydantic field validators
    "@model_validator",    # Pydantic model validators
    "@computed_field",     # Pydantic computed fields
]
ignore_names = [
    "model_config",        # Pydantic class-level config
    "revision",            # Alembic migration variables
    "down_revision",
    "branch_labels",
    "depends_on",
    "upgrade",             # Alembic migration functions
    "downgrade",
    "do_GET",              # HTTP handler protocol
    "log_message",         # HTTP handler protocol
]

# Mutation testing. How to run it, and why the config looks like this: the
# scripts/mutmut_run.py docstring.
[tool.mutmut]
source_paths = ["src/"]
only_mutate = ["src/domain/*"]
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = ["tests/unit/domain/"]
# test_status_matrix_export imports scripts/ and reads the web fixture it renders.
also_copy = ["scripts/", "web/src/test/fixtures/"]
# -n 0 overrides addopts' `-n auto`: mutmut runs tests in-process and forces -x.
pytest_add_cli_args = ["-n", "0", "--hypothesis-profile", "mutmut"]
mutate_only_covered_lines = true

# Layer-boundary enforcement (import-linter 2.13+).
#
# Lives here rather than in a standalone `.importlinter` because every other tool in
# this repo (ruff, pytest, coverage, basedpyright, vulture, typer) is configured in
# pyproject.toml — there are no standalone tool config files to be consistent with.
#
# The contract is CLAUDE.md's "Interface → Application → Domain ← Infrastructure",
# split across five contracts because a single `layers` contract cannot express it:
# interface and infrastructure are siblings that must not see each other, yet only
# one of them (interface) may import application.
#
# Every `ignore_imports` entry below is an exception documented in `.claude/rules/`.
# Nothing gets added here to make the check pass — an undocumented violation is a
# finding to escalate, not a line to add.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["src"]
include_external_packages = false

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture: interface → application → domain"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "src.interface",
    "src.application",
    "src.domain",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain is a self-contained kernel"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.domain"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.application",
    "src.infrastructure",
    "src.interface",
    "src.config",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # domain-purity.md: TYPE_CHECKING-only import breaking a genuine circular
    # import (`operations.py` → `spotify/personal_data`).
    "src.domain.entities.operations -> src.infrastructure.connectors.spotify.personal_data",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Infrastructure depends inward only"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.infrastructure"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.application", "src.interface"]
# Direct imports only: a chain that passes *through* an approved bridge is the
# architecture working as designed, not a second violation of the same edge.
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    # infrastructure-patterns.md named exception: an adapter may import the
    # application-owned *port/type* modules it implements — never use cases,
    # never the runner. Importing them realises a contract, not orchestration.
    "src.infrastructure.chat.anthropic_adapter -> src.application.chat.events",
    "src.infrastructure.chat.anthropic_adapter -> src.application.chat.protocols",
    "src.infrastructure.connectors.lastfm.play_resolver -> src.application.connector_protocols",
    "src.infrastructure.persistence.unit_of_work -> src.application.connector_protocols",
    "src.infrastructure.services.base_play_importer -> src.application.connector_protocols",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Application reaches infrastructure only through the approved bridges"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.application"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.infrastructure"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    # application-patterns.md "Approved infrastructure bridges": DI wiring entry
    # points that intentionally import infrastructure for session/UoW creation.
    "src.application.runner -> src.infrastructure.persistence.database.db_connection",
    "src.application.runner -> src.infrastructure.persistence.database.user_context",
    "src.application.runner -> src.infrastructure.persistence.repositories.factories",
    # application-patterns.md: the `metric_config` protocol's concrete provider,
    # imported inside the function that needs it. It lives once, beside the
    # protocol it provides, so every consumer — a call-site construction or an
    # attrs `factory=` default — reaches it through `default_metric_config()`
    # and `interface/` never has to name the concrete class. Consumers reach it
    # indirectly, which this contract's `allow_indirect_imports` already covers.
    "src.application.use_cases._shared.metric_config -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.metric_registry",
    # Same bridge shape for the connector registry: the `connector_catalog`
    # protocol's concrete provider, imported inside the method that needs it.
    "src.application.use_cases._shared.connector_catalog -> src.infrastructure.connectors",
    # Same bridge module, second reader: the registry-declared external page
    # links, so the application layer stores a real playlist URL instead of a
    # guessed one. `_shared/external_urls` is the registry's single URL reader.
    "src.application.use_cases._shared.connector_catalog -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.external_urls",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Interface reaches infrastructure only through the credential/OAuth carve-out"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.interface"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.infrastructure"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    # interface-patterns.md, v0.6.5 credential/secret carve-out — connector
    # OAuth/token management shared by CLI + web so one `exchange_code` serves both.
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.token_storage",
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.connectors.discovery",
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.connectors.lastfm.client",
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.connectors.spotify.auth",
    # Same carve-out: the callbacks stamp the Spotify identity (display name +
    # account_id) onto the fresh grant via the connector's own status module.
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.connectors.spotify.status",
    # Same carve-out, v0.11.3: the Tidal OAuth callback shares the connector's
    # `exchange_code` (PKCE public client) exactly as Spotify's does.
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.connectors.tidal.auth",
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.persistence.database.db_connection",
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.persistence.database.models",
    # Same carve-out: state creation opens its session as the initiating user
    # (`user_context`), and state validation declares itself cross-tenant
    # (`system_context`) — the token is the credential, the row's user unknown
    # until read. Without these the default-user guard 500s every web auth flow
    # against a hosted database.
    "src.interface.api.routes.auth -> src.infrastructure.persistence.database.user_context",
    # Same carve-out, v0.11.x: the in-app Apple Music MusicKit flow — the SPA
    # fetches the developer token (musickit-config) and POSTs the Music User
    # Token its own authorize() call mints; the best-effort storefront
    # backfill lives in `apple_music/auth.py` (`backfill_storefront`).
    "src.interface.api.routes.apple_auth -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.token_storage",
    "src.interface.api.routes.apple_auth -> src.infrastructure.connectors.apple_music.auth",
    "src.interface.api.routes.connectors -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.connector_status",
    "src.interface.api.routes.connectors -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.token_storage",
    "src.interface.api.routes.connectors -> src.infrastructure.connectors.discovery",
    "src.interface.api.routes.connectors -> src.infrastructure.connectors.protocols",
    # Connector registry metadata, not a credential: each connector declares the
    # canonical web page for one of its tracks (`track_url`), and the track
    # detail read-model renders the link. Static config the registry already
    # publishes to `interface/` next door in `routes/connectors.py`; a port would
    # carry a callable through the domain to no benefit.
    "src.interface.api.schemas.tracks -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.external_urls",
    "src.interface.cli.discogs_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.token_storage",
    "src.interface.cli.discogs_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors.discogs.token_service",
    # Same carve-out, v0.11.3: `mixd tidal auth` — the device-code flow with
    # the localhost-redirect fallback shares `tidal/auth.py` + the token
    # store with the web callback, so one auth implementation serves both.
    "src.interface.cli.tidal_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.token_storage",
    "src.interface.cli.tidal_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors.tidal.device_auth",
    "src.interface.cli.connector_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.connector_status",
    "src.interface.cli.connector_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.token_storage",
    "src.interface.cli.connector_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors.discovery",
    "src.interface.cli.connector_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors.lastfm.client",
    "src.interface.cli.connector_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors.spotify.auth",
    "src.interface.cli.connector_commands -> src.infrastructure.connectors.spotify.status",
    # Same carve-out: `whoami` probes connectors exactly as `connector status`
    # does, and the probe reads (and silently refreshes) the stored grant.
    "src.interface.cli.app -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.connector_status",
    # Same carve-out: the startup prune of expired connector-OAuth CSRF state.
    # `routes/auth.py` evicts opportunistically on the next state creation; this
    # catches rows that expired while the server was down.
    "src.interface.api.app -> src.infrastructure.persistence.repositories.oauth_states",
    # Same carve-out, factored into the FastAPI dependency module that the
    # OAuth/assistant-key routes above depend on.
    "src.interface.api.deps -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.token_storage",
    # Same carve-out, narrowed: `connector_access` is the pure verdict predicate
    # both `deps` and the schedule schemas read, so it names `StoredToken` (the
    # credential TypedDict) and nothing else from infrastructure.
    "src.interface.api.connector_access -> src.infrastructure.connectors._shared.token_storage",
    "src.interface.api.deps -> src.infrastructure.chat.credentials",
    "src.interface.api.deps -> src.infrastructure.chat.anthropic_adapter",
    # interface-patterns.md, v0.9.0 assistant API-key carve-out — the acting
    # user's Anthropic key is a write-only per-user secret, not domain data.
    "src.interface.api.routes.assistant -> src.infrastructure.chat.credentials",
    "src.interface.api.routes.assistant -> src.infrastructure.chat.anthropic_adapter",
    "src.interface.cli.assistant_commands -> src.infrastructure.chat.credentials",
    "src.interface.cli.assistant_commands -> src.infrastructure.chat.anthropic_adapter",
    # interface-patterns.md, v0.9.5 in-app OAuth authorization server — the AS
    # owns its own token machinery and runs with no session user, so the
    # RLS/`user_context` path a use case assumes does not apply.
    "src.interface.api.oauth.cimd -> src.infrastructure.persistence.repositories.oauth_as",
    "src.interface.api.oauth.provider -> src.infrastructure.persistence.repositories.oauth_as",
    # interface-patterns.md, operational probes — the readiness check reads the
    # raw engine on purpose. Through `execute_use_case()` it would open and
    # commit a transaction, and would report ORM/UoW/RLS health rather than
    # connectivity, which is a broader claim than the endpoint makes.
    "src.interface.api.routes.health -> src.infrastructure.persistence.database.db_connection",
    # interface-patterns.md, composition root — process teardown of cached
    # httpx2 pools in the lifespan `finally`. No session, no data access;
    # nothing in application/ owns adapter lifetime.
    "src.interface.api.app -> src.infrastructure.chat.anthropic_adapter",
    "src.interface.api.app -> src.infrastructure.connectors.spotify.status",
]

# Sixth contract, v0.11.3 Tidal churn defense: the hand-written models derived
# from the vendored, SHA-pinned Tidal OpenAPI spec live in one isolated module
# (`tidal/oas_models.py`) that only the Tidal connector package may import.
# Tidal revises its API in place, so wire-format shapes must never leak past
# the adapter — when the spec drifts, the blast radius is exactly this package,
# not every module that found the models convenient. Direct imports only
# (`allow_indirect_imports`): reaching Tidal data through the connector's
# public surface is the adapter wrapping working as designed.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Tidal OAS-derived models are importable only inside the Tidal connector"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.**"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.infrastructure.connectors.tidal.oas_models"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "src.infrastructure.connectors.tidal -> src.infrastructure.connectors.tidal.oas_models",
    "src.infrastructure.connectors.tidal.* -> src.infrastructure.connectors.tidal.oas_models",

    "app.domains.sessions",

; Import-Linter contracts enforcing Cosmic Python layered architecture.
;
; Layer mapping (from architecture audit finding #7):
;   models       -> src.domain, src.models
;   adapters     -> src.infrastructure
;   services     -> src.application (components + services)
;   entrypoints  -> src.main, src.dashboard
;
; Cross-cutting (intentionally NOT layered):
;   src.utils, src.config, src.mappings, src.display, src.migration
;
; The cross-cutting modules are leaf-level utilities or top-level orchestrators
; that legitimately need to be imported from any layer; constraining them now
; would force an unrelated refactor. Revisit once the migration.py god-file is
; broken up.

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    src

; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
; Layered contract (top-down): higher layers may import from lower layers,
; never the reverse. import-linter's layers contract type implicitly forbids
; upward imports, so we don't need separate `forbidden` contracts to enforce
; the same rules (e.g. "models can't import infrastructure" falls out of the
; bottom→top relationship below).
;
; Delimiter semantics (per import-linter docs):
;   "|"  -> peers at the same level that MUST remain independent of each other
;   ":"  -> peers at the same level that MAY freely import from each other
;
; src.dashboard and src.main are the entrypoints; we keep them independent
; because the FastAPI dashboard and the CLI must not couple to one another.
;
; src.domain and src.models legitimately reference each other today
; (e.g. src.domain.results imports src.models.component_results, and
; several src.models.* modules import src.domain.ids). Treat them as a
; non-independent peer pair until the model/domain split is resolved.
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Cosmic Python layered architecture
type = layers
layers =
    src.dashboard | src.main
    src.application
    src.infrastructure
    src.domain : src.models

# Import layering, enforced by `lint-imports` (import-linter) in CI via the
# py-dev-gates python-health action. The package is flat (modules, not
# subpackages); the layering, high -> low, is:
#
#   client                          (high-level facade)
#   controls | secure_connection    (behaviour / SSL transport)
#   connection                      (WebSocket transport)
#   discovery | model               (leaves: SSDP scan, value objects)
#
# Higher modules may import lower ones; the reverse is forbidden, and siblings
# stay independent. Any accepted exception goes in `ignore_imports` with a
# why in the commit body -- the suppression list IS the audit trail.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["asyncwebostv"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "model is a dependency-free leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["asyncwebostv.model"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "asyncwebostv.client",
    "asyncwebostv.controls",
    "asyncwebostv.connection",
    "asyncwebostv.secure_connection",
    "asyncwebostv.discovery",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "discovery is a dependency-free leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["asyncwebostv.discovery"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "asyncwebostv.client",
    "asyncwebostv.controls",
    "asyncwebostv.connection",
    "asyncwebostv.secure_connection",
    "asyncwebostv.model",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "connection (transport) does not import behaviour"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["asyncwebostv.connection"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "asyncwebostv.client",
    "asyncwebostv.controls",
    "asyncwebostv.secure_connection",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "controls do not reach up into the facade or SSL transport"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["asyncwebostv.controls"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "asyncwebostv.client",
    "asyncwebostv.secure_connection",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "secure_connection does not import behaviour or the facade"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["asyncwebostv.secure_connection"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "asyncwebostv.client",
    "asyncwebostv.controls",
]

keywords = ["llm", "openai", "anthropic", "gateway", "litellm", "mixture-of-models"]

# Runtime dependencies. litellm is the provider transport (quarantined to
# adapters/litellm_client); langfuse backs the optional tracer.
#
# The litellm floor is a MODEL-CATALOG floor, not an API one. mom reads the catalog litellm
# bundles (see mom/__init__.py), so a model missing from it gets litellm's unknown-model
# defaults rather than its real limits — silently, with no error. Live on 2026-08-19: the
# catalog bundled with 1.93 predated claude-opus-5, so every Opus 5 call was capped at
# litellm's 4096-token default (all of it spent on thinking -> empty answers) and had the
# client's `top_p` forwarded to a model that rejects it (400, killing synthesis). 1.97 is the
# a release whose bundled catalog carries the models config.yaml pins (1.105 knows the
# Claude 5.5 line, GPT-6.x and Grok 4.7). Raise this floor whenever config.yaml adopts a
# model newer than the pinned catalog knows.
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.115",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30",
    "pydantic>=2.7",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.3",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "typer>=0.12",
    "structlog>=24.1",
    "aiosqlite>=0.20",
    "platformdirs>=4.2",
    "litellm>=1.105",
    "langfuse>=3.0",
    "mcp>=2.1",
    # Direct, not transitive: mom.runtime.secrets parses the discovered .env files itself rather
    # than relying on litellm's incidental import-time load_dotenv() (which resolves relative to
    # litellm's own install directory, not the cwd — see that module's docstring).
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
]

# Optional feature deps, imported lazily so a base install never requires them:
#   redis -> the cross-process progress event bus (settings.redis_url)
#   otel  -> the OpenTelemetry/OTLP tracer (observability.otel.enabled); grpc users also install
#            opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc and set protocol: grpc
[project.optional-dependencies]
redis = ["redis>=5.0"]
otel = [
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.25",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.25",
]

[project.scripts]
mom = "mom.cli:app"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ruff — the single linter + formatter.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
src = ["src"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W", "F", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "C4", "SIM",
    "S",     # flake8-bandit (this is an auth gateway)
    "ASYNC", # blocking-call-in-async — v1's worst runtime bug class
    "DTZ",   # naive datetimes
    "PT",    # pytest style
    "RET", "ARG", "PERF", "LOG", "G", "RUF",
]
ignore = [
    "B008",   # function call in argument defaults (FastAPI/Typer idiom)
]
fixable = ["ALL"]
dummy-variable-rgx = "^(_+|(_+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+?))$"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/*" = ["S101", "S105", "S106", "S107", "ARG"]  # asserts + dummy secrets + unused fixture args are fine in tests
"src/mom/domain/errors.py" = ["N818"]  # domain error vocabulary; base is MomError

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["mom"]
force-sort-within-sections = true
lines-after-imports = 2

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
docstring-code-format = true

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# mypy — strict, scoped to the mom package.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["src/mom"]
strict = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
warn_unused_configs = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_ignores = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["litellm", "litellm.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# Optional feature deps, imported lazily; treat as untyped so a base checkout type-checks too.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["redis.*", "opentelemetry.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# pytest
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
addopts = "-ra -q --strict-markers --strict-config --disable-socket --allow-hosts=127.0.0.1,::1"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"

[tool.coverage.run]
# Gate the core logic; api/runtime/store/cli are exercised but not chased to a number.
source = [
    "mom.domain",
    "mom.engine",
    "mom.adapters",
    "mom.config",
    # Config/secret resolution: gated because it decides which credentials and which config file
    # the process uses, which is the last thing that should go unmeasured.
    "mom.runtime.bootstrap",
    "mom.runtime.discovery",
    "mom.runtime.secrets",
]
branch = true
omit = ["*/tests/*"]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 88
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    'if __name__ == .__main__.:',
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter — enforce the layered architecture (grows as domain/ports/adapters land).
# Lower layers must not import higher ones: runtime cannot import api; api cannot import cli.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "mom"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture"
type = "layers"
layers = ["mom.cli", "mom.api", "mom.runtime"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain is pure"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["mom.domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["mom.api", "mom.runtime", "mom.store", "mom.config", "mom.cli"]

exclude_lines = [

    "if self.debug:",
    "if settings.DEBUG",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if 0:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
# Coverage is opt-in: use `make test`, CI, or `pytest --cov=src/codomyrmex --cov-fail-under=60`.
# [tool.coverage.report] fail_under still applies whenever pytest runs with --cov.
addopts = [
    "--import-mode=importlib",
    "-p",
    "pytest_pymupdf",
    "--verbose",
    "--tb=short",
    "--timeout=300",
    "--timeout-method=thread",
    # Exclude git submodule test dirs: separate dep sets (litellm, swerex, tinker)
    # and plugin-registration conflicts with the main suite's conftest.
    "--ignore=src/codomyrmex/agents/open_gauss/mini-swe-agent",
    "--ignore=src/codomyrmex/agents/open_gauss/tinker-atropos",
    "--ignore=src/codomyrmex/agents/open_gauss/tests",
    "--ignore=src/codomyrmex/agents/hermes/evolution",
]
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests (fast, isolated)",
    "integration: Integration tests (may require external services)",
    "smoke: Smoke tests that exercise code paths without explicit assertions",
    "slow: Slow tests (>10s execution time)",
    "bench: Opt-in benchmark and contention-sensitive timing tests",
    "benchmark: Opt-in pytest-benchmark tests",
    "performance: Performance and benchmarking tests",
    "examples: Example validation tests",
    "network: Tests requiring network access",
    "database: Tests requiring database access",
    "external: Tests requiring external services",
    "requires_ollama: Tests requiring a live Ollama service",
    "requires_docker: Tests requiring a live Docker daemon",
    "security: Security-related tests",
    "asyncio: Asynchronous tests",
    "crypto: Cryptography tests",
    "orchestrator: Orchestrator and workflow tests",
    "soul: soul module tests (persistent markdown-memory LLM agents)",
    "aider: Aider AI pair programming tests",
    "openfang: openfang Agent OS integration tests",
    "pai_pm: PAI Project Manager module tests (requires bun for server tests)",
    "google_workspace: Google Workspace API and gws CLI tests",
]
filterwarnings = [
    # Any warning not matched by a later rule becomes a test failure.
    "error",
    "ignore:builtin type Swig.*has no __module__ attribute:DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore:The verify_requirements argument is now a no-op:DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore:datetime\\.datetime\\.utcnow\\(\\) is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
    # Resource and collection warnings are actionable test failures.  Keep
    # only narrow third-party compatibility exceptions below.
    # requests warns on import when urllib3/chardet pins drift; do not use category path (imports requests during parse).
    "ignore:.*doesn't match a supported version.*:Warning",
    # google.api_core without grpcio-status; optional for storage client import chains during test collection.
    "ignore:Please install grpcio-status.*:ImportWarning",
    # google-genai 1.68 uses typing._UnionGenericAlias which Python 3.14 marks as deprecated.
    "ignore:'_UnionGenericAlias' is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
    # google-genai 1.68 with pydantic >= 2.12: model_validator mode='after' classmethod deprecation at import.
    "ignore:Using `@model_validator` with mode='after' on a classmethod is deprecated.*:",
    # matplotlib 3.10 date-axis default intervals use bare-integer timedelta
    # arithmetic that NumPy 2.5 deprecates; raised inside matplotlib, not here.
    "ignore:The 'generic' unit for NumPy timedelta is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
    # pytest-benchmark disables itself under pytest-xdist and says so with a
    # warning during configure; the CI suites run with xdist (-n auto).
    "ignore:Benchmarks are automatically disabled because xdist plugin is active",
]
