[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# --strict-markers turns an unregistered marker into a collection error. Without it,
# `gpu` sat unregistered and silently ungated for months: the modules using it carried no
# `integration` marker, so they ran in the fast suite AND in CPU-only CI, passing only on
# their own runtime skip guards, while the gate's `-m integration` phase never selected
# them. Register every marker you use — see scripts/run-integration-tests.sh for the phases.
# --durations surfaces the slow tail every run. Without it, a 40 s test that is really 40 s
# of lock queue is invisible; that is how one worker came to own 81% of the wall clock.
# --timeout converts a hang into a failure. DDL tests serialise behind a Postgres advisory
# lock that only covers connections opting into it, so a genuine cross-connection cycle is
# possible and would otherwise stall the run indefinitely. 300 s is ~5x the slowest observed
# test (54.6 s), so it cannot fire on a merely slow test — tighten it once the suite is fast.
# Both require pytest-timeout, which is therefore MANDATORY in requirements-dev/-ci: a
# missing plugin makes --timeout a collection error, not a no-op (issue #431).
# `-m 'not integration and not gpu'` is now load-bearing for CUDA device VISIBILITY, not
# only test selection (issue #719): tests/conftest.py's pytest_configure asks whether this
# exact expression can ever select a `gpu`-marked test and, since it cannot, sets
# CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 before any worker imports torch. Changing this default without
# checking tests/conftest.py's `_selection_may_run_gpu_tests` can silently re-open every
# GPU to the fast suite again.
addopts = "-n auto --dist loadgroup --tb=short -q --strict-markers --durations=25 --timeout=300 -m 'not integration and not gpu'"
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow",
    "unit: pure unit test, no external service",
    "pki: PKI certificate tests",
    "e2e: end-to-end browser tests",
    "integration: integration tests requiring running dev environment",
    "gpu: tests requiring a physical GPU — deselected from the fast suite, run by the gate, and the only selection that keeps CUDA devices visible (issue #719)",
    "models: tests requiring ML model weights (Presidio/GLiNER/toxicity) — skipped in fast CI",
    "ddl_exclusive: performs schema DDL (DROP/ALTER TABLE) needing full DB-wide exclusivity, not just self-consistency — see tests/conftest.py's advisory-lock isolation (issue #389)",
    "multi_gpu: needs a MULTI-WORKER GPU topology (--gpu-scale / --gpu-split), i.e. a running celery-worker-gpu-scaled or celery-worker-gpu-diarize container — NOT merely a second card. run-integration-tests.sh deselects these when that topology is absent and selects them when it is present, so they are visibly absent from the count rather than inflating it as skips",
    "export_capability: the diar-native model-export check specifically. A SECOND marker on top of opt_in_gate so `--export-capability` can select THAT test without un-deselecting every other opt-in one — it used to clear the whole `not opt_in_gate` filter, which re-selected RUN_INDEX_AUDIT's deployment audit, and that then skipped and pushed the phase over its ceiling",
    "opt_in_gate: deliberately not part of any default run — an expensive or deployment-scoped check behind its own RUN_* variable (RUN_EXPORT_CAPABILITY_TEST, RUN_INDEX_AUDIT). The marker exists so the gate can DESELECT them rather than count them as skips: a permanently-skipping test inflates the skip total toward the ceiling and buries the skips that mean something",
]
norecursedirs = ["tests/e2e"]

# Coverage runs via `pytest --cov=app` (CI backend-tests job + the local gate's
# --coverage flag). fail_under is a RATCHET FLOOR set just below the measured
# baseline (36.6% on 2026-06-04) — raise it as coverage grows, never lower it.
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["app"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "app/alembic/*",
    "app/scripts/*",
    "tests/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_empty = true
precision = 1
fail_under = 37

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mutation testing (opt-in — NEVER part of the default gate or CI).
#
# Coverage says a line RAN. Mutation testing says a line MATTERS: it edits the
# source (flips a comparison, drops a condition, changes a constant) and asks
# whether any test notices. A surviving mutant is a line the suite executes but
# does not actually check — for a security predicate that means the control can
# be silently removed with the suite still green.
#
# Scoped to security-critical modules ONLY. A whole-codebase run on ~40k lines is
# hours of GPU-idle CPU and is not what this is for; the point is a small set where
# a survivor is unambiguously a bug. `scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh` reads
# `paths_to_mutate` from here, so this list is the single source of truth.
#
# `runner` deliberately carries NO test paths and NO -n: the script supplies both
# through PYTEST_ADDOPTS, which pytest prepends to the command line. That is how a
# per-module test subset is selected, and how the project's `-n auto` is overridden
# to `-n0` — a mutant run that forks 24 xdist workers per mutant is slower than
# serial and, against this repo's single shared Postgres, deadlock-prone
# (the advisory-lock/system_settings collisions of issues #389 and #431).
[tool.mutmut]
# source_paths must be the WHOLE package, not just the targets. mutmut copies it
# into backend/mutants/ and runs pytest THERE; listing only the six files left
# mutants/app/ holding 6 modules out of hundreds, and tests/conftest.py died with
# ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'app.core.config'. Narrow the MUTATION set
# with only_mutate — that is also what scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh reads to build
# its per-module list.
source_paths = ["app"]
only_mutate = [
    "app/services/redaction/spans.py",
    "app/auth/password_policy.py",
    "app/core/security.py",
    "app/api/endpoints/auth/dependencies.py",
    "app/auth/lockout.py",
    "app/auth/session.py",
]
# Test SELECTION is per-module and comes from scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh via
# PYTEST_ADDOPTS, not from here: mutating spans.py should only run the redaction
# tests, and one static list cannot express that.
#
# Do NOT reintroduce `tests_dir` or `runner`. In mutmut 3.x `tests_dir` is
# deprecated and must be a LIST (a string crashes config loading with
# "can only concatenate list (not str) to list"), and `runner` is not a
# recognized key at all — it is read by nothing, so flags put there are silently
# dropped. Runner flags belong in pytest_add_cli_args.
# mutmut supplies its own --tb=native -x -q -p no:randomly, so runner flags here
# would only duplicate them. Its own timeout is timeout_constant (seconds), NOT a
# pytest --timeout flag: mutmut runs pytest IN-PROCESS, and pytest-timeout's
# thread method plus the inherited addopts is what made the first run die with
# BadTestExecutionCommandsException.
timeout_constant = 120

requires = ["pdm-backend~=2.4"]  # pdm-backend 2.4 supports project.license-files.

[dependency-groups]
dev = [

# BLACK

# CODESPELL

[tool.codespell]
# The two legal documents are published Polish text, skipped for the same reason
# as the *.po catalogs above: an English dictionary flags ordinary Polish words.
# Named individually rather than by directory, so anything else added under
# content/ stays checked.
# `./.claude` only matches when codespell is handed the repo root; hk and CI
# pass explicit paths, so the vendored skills need a glob that matches the
# path as given too.
skip = 'node_modules,tests/e2e,*.po,*.lock,package-lock.json,vendor,src/ludamus/gates/web/django/theme/static_src/package-lock.json,CLAUDE.md,./.claude,./.agents,.claude/*,.agents/*,*/.claude/*,*/.agents/*,zagrajmy-landing-notes.md,aube-lock.yaml,src/ludamus/client/package-lock.json,src/ludamus/static/vite,src/ludamus/content/privacy-policy.md,src/ludamus/content/terms-of-service.md'
# 'fallow' is the frontend analysis tool, not a misspelling of 'follow'.
# 'adres' is Polish for 'address' — real localized sheet headers ("Adres e-mail").
# 'afterall' is bun:test's afterAll hook.
# 'blok' is Polish for 'track' — the agreed translation, see the copy reference.
ignore-words-list = 'fallow,adres,afterall,blok'

# COVERAGE

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["src"]
omit = [
    "src/ludamus/edges/*",
    "src/ludamus/links/db/django/migrations/*",
    "src/ludamus/client/*",
    # Static HTML is served as files (the browser renders it; Django never does),
    # and django_coverage_plugin measures every .html under src, so it would
    # read as 0% forever.
    "src/ludamus/static/*",
    "tests/template_checks.py",
]
sigterm = true
plugins = ["django_coverage_plugin"]
core = "ctrace"

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
precision = 2
exclude_also = [
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    # An exhaustiveness guard is unreachable by construction: mypy rejects the
    # code that would enter it. Matched across both lines so the `case _:` goes
    # with it — a bare `case _:` pattern would also silence the several real
    # fallbacks that carry logic.
    """case _:\\n\\s*assert_never\\([^)]*\\)""",
]

[tool.coverage.django_coverage_plugin]
template_extensions = 'html'

# DJLINT

[tool.djlint]

warn_no_return = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_return_any = true

# RUFF

[tool.ruff]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    # Unused
    "COM",
    "CPY",
    "D1",
    "DOC",   # No docstring param/return spec
    "FIX",
    "TD003",
    # Left to fix
    "PLR0911",                       # Too many return statements
    "PLR0912",                       # Too many branches
    "PLR0915",                       # Too many statements
    "PLR0914",                       # Too many local variables
    "PLR1702",                       # Too many nested blocks
    "EM101",                         # Exception must not use a string literal, assign to variable first
    "TRY003",                        # Avoid specifying long messages outside the exception class
    "too-many-public-methods",
    "too-many-positional-arguments",
]
allowed-confusables = ["–", "×"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"*/migrations/**.py" = [
    "ANN",    # flake8-annotations
    "ARG001", # Unused arguments
    "E501",   # Line too long
    "RUF012", # ClassVar
]
"tests/**.py" = [
    "ANN",                   # flake8-annotations
    "ARG002",                # unused-method-argument
    "INP001",                # implicit namespace package
    "PLR0913",               # too-many-arguments
    "PLR0917",               # too-many-positional-arguments
    "S",                     # bandit
    "PLR0904",               # Too many public methods
    "PLR6301",               # Method could be a function
    "private-member-access",
]
# DI registries are intentionally wide: their whole job is to expose one leaf
# per repository/service. Bucketing them (see the class docstrings) is a
# separate refactor, not a per-leaf concern. `pacts/services.py` is the protocol
# mirror of the services registry, so it carries the same width by definition.
"*/inits/repositories.py" = ["PLR0904"]
"*/inits/services.py" = ["PLR0904"]
"*/pacts/services.py" = ["PLR0904"]
"scripts/*.py" = ["T201", "S404", "S603", "S607"]
# Standalone Django seed script: imports must follow django.setup(), and it
# prints a summary line when run directly.
"tests/e2e/scripts/*.py" = [
    "unsorted-imports",
    "module-import-not-at-top-of-file",
    "print",
]
# `pytest-fixture-autouse` (preview) flags `autouse=True`, but these two
# conftest.py files exist specifically to apply cross-cutting setup — DB
# access, English locale, tmp media root, template/N+1 error detection,
# sphere/site bootstrap, PostHog stubbing — to every test under their
# directory. No `pytest.mark.usefixtures` scoping replaces that: the mark
# only reaches tests declared in the same module, never a whole tree. Ruff's
# own docs for the rule name conftest.py as the one legitimate use.
"**/conftest.py" = ["pytest-fixture-autouse"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-public-methods = 12
max-args = 12

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-pytest-style]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-unused-arguments]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-annotations]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"

# PYTEST

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = "ludamus.edges.settings"

[tool.mutmut]
# NOTE: two layers only. `mills` is the one the unit suite owns
# (docs/TESTING_STRATEGY.md), and `specs` is the pure constants those same
# tests reach through it. A mutant in any other layer survives whatever only
# the integration suite could have killed, so mutating `src` wholesale reports
# noise instead of gaps.
source_paths = ["src/ludamus/mills", "src/ludamus/specs"]
# NOTE: mutmut runs the suite twice in one process (stats pass, then clean
# pass); DBOS refuses to register the same workflow twice, so its smoke test
# stays out.

    "tests/unit",
    "--ignore=tests/unit/test_dbos_smoke.py",
]

# dependencies and nothing else. `uv lock` after editing dependencies; the

[tool.ruff]
src = ["src"]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py313"
extend-exclude = ["alembic/versions", "backups"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Chosen for defect-finding, not style. Every rule here has either caught a
# real bug in this codebase or guards a class of bug we have actually shipped:
#   DTZ  - naive datetime.now() wrote ai_queries.created_at in local time and
#          shifted every window query by the container's UTC offset.
#   ASYNC- synchronous work inside async def stalls the worker's event loop.
#   F    - the missing UniqueViolation import that `compileall` waved through.
#   B    - mutable defaults, unused loop vars, except-without-raise.
#   S    - subprocess/SSRF/secret shapes; we shipped a real SSRF.
#   SIM/PIE/RUF - small correctness-adjacent simplifications.
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "I", "B", "S", "ASYNC", "DTZ", "SIM", "PIE", "RUF", "PLW", "UP"]

# UP* (pep585/604 modernisation) is on. It is cosmetic, but a codebase that
# mixes typing.Dict with dict makes the inconsistency itself a thing to think
# about at every edit. Applied as one mechanical commit so it is reviewable
# separately from behaviour.
ignore = [
    # FastAPI's whole idiom is `x = Depends(...)` / `Query(...)` in defaults.
    "B008",
    # Broad excepts are load-bearing here: a scrape or an AI call failing must
    # not kill a sweep. Reviewed individually rather than banned.
    "BLE001",
    # asserts are used as invariant checks after db.query_one, not as
    # validation of untrusted input.
    "S101",
    # f-string SQL. Audited: every interpolated fragment is a whitelist
    # (_SORTABLE, column-name constants) or a re.escape'd literal - there is
    # no user-controlled path into a query. Flagging 31 verified-safe sites
    # would train us to skip the finding when a real one appears.
    "S608",
    # Assigning a lambda is how the check dispatch tables read most clearly
    # (verdict_of = lambda p: ...); a def per branch is worse here.
    "E731",
    # Module-level mutable state in the worker is deliberate (_current_task_id
    # for the signal handler); the alternative is a global object wrapper.
    "PLW0603",
    # `timeout` is our own parameter name on AI wrappers, not asyncio.timeout
    # misuse; renaming it would change a public-ish signature for a lint.
    "ASYNC109",
    # Nested ifs here read as "guard, then condition" and flattening them makes
    # the two separate concerns harder to see.
    "SIM102",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests legitimately use hardcoded credentials-shaped strings and sleeps.
# conftest deliberately shells out to initdb/pg_ctl to build a scratch
# database; the arguments are literals, not untrusted input.
"tests/*" = ["S105", "S106", "S311", "ASYNC251", "S603", "S607", "PLW1510", "DTZ005", "DTZ011"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
markers = [
    "corpus: runs against the generated corpus (tests/corpus.py), built on demand",
    "integration: needs a synced copy of REAL production; skipped without one",
    "no_board_recompute: the client fixture must not recompute the board before a read",
]
# No marker filter. `pytest tests` runs everything: the hermetic suite on a
# truncated database, the corpus suite on generated data measured out of
# production, and the integration suite skipped unless the database actually
# holds a synced copy. That is what lets CI run the whole thing on a pull
# request with no production credential anywhere.

# The layering, enforced. `core` is the bottom: fetching, scraping, providers,
# the catalog and the stores, none of which may reach up into the API layer.
# The one violation when this was added was core/devseed.py, which seeded a
# development database through api.db and has moved to api/ where it belongs.
#
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["api", "core", "tasks"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core does not depend on api"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["core"]
forbidden_modules = ["api"]

# The second layer. `tasks` is the work the worker runs, and it uses `api`;
# `api` must not reach back.
#
# One line only because `tasks` is a SIBLING of `api` rather than a child:
# import-linter's `forbidden` skips a target sitting inside its source, so
# while the handlers lived at api.tasks this rule passed whatever the code
# did. Verified before the move by adding a violation and watching it stay
# green.
#
# Nine imports were ignored here, in three causes. Five were one smell wearing
# five hats: something in `api` reaching past a handler for a SHAPE or a
# CONSTANT, never for behaviour. Those five are gone.
#
# What each task declares is now core/shapes.py, so api.budget prices a fleet
# cycle and api.routers.task_models configures one without importing the code
# that runs it. `configured_model` is api/task_config.py and `load_config` is
# api/budget.py; both were reading the database on behalf of the services from
# inside the task runtime. What a draft is written from is
# api/apply/drafting.py, so the two routers that draft one live no longer
# borrow it from the sweep that batches them.
#
# Two of the five were called impossible here, and the reading was wrong. The
# claim was that mail_classify BUILDS its two shapes in a function so its
# declaration cannot invert, and that application reads its purpose from
# another module. A factory moves down exactly as well as a literal does, and
# api.apply.writes now reads its purpose off the shape rather than spelling it
# a second time.
#
# The worker is the task runner and sits above handlers by definition. Its
# entry point and the claim, scheduling and execution modules load the handler
# registry or runtime to dispatch work. These explicit edges are the only
# service-to-handler imports allowed by this contract.
#
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the services do not reach into the handlers"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["api"]
forbidden_modules = ["tasks"]
ignore_imports = [
    "api.worker -> tasks",
    "api.worker -> tasks.runtime",
    "api.worker_lifecycle.claims -> tasks",
    "api.worker_lifecycle.execution -> tasks",
    "api.worker_lifecycle.execution -> tasks.runtime",
    "api.worker_lifecycle.scheduling -> tasks",
]

    # client.proxy accepts. (0.27.0 also percent-encoded a `\` in a URL path,
    # `/a%5Cb`, so a URL the plugin sends as written did not reach the server
    # as written.) No upper bound, but before taking a new httpx: the built-in
    # digest auth (request_builder._DigestAuth) builds on DigestAuth's private
    # state, which its unit tests in tests/unit/test_request_builder.py pin.
    "httpx[http2]>=0.28.0",
    # The parser pytest reads its ini files with: `validate` reads
    # httpchain_suffix from one (validation.discovery) as pytest would. The
    # floor pytest 9.0 itself requires.
    "iniconfig>=1.0.1",
    "jmespath>=1.0.0",

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 180
target-version = "py313"

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",  # pycodestyle errors
    "W",  # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",  # pyflakes
    "I",  # isort
    "B",  # flake8-bugbear
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP", # pyupgrade
    "PT", # flake8-pytest-style
    "TID252", # flake8-tidy-imports: ban relative imports
]
ignore = []

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["tests"]

[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.13"

[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true

# Test suites (especially the models package) deliberately construct models with
# invalid types to assert ValidationError, and access attributes on unions/mocks
# the checker can't narrow. Relax those specific rules for test code only; src/
# stays strict and uses pinpoint `# ty: ignore[...]` comments instead.
[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["tests/**"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"
unknown-argument = "ignore"
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
not-subscriptable = "ignore"
missing-argument = "ignore"

[tool.pytest]
minversion = "9.0"
# pytest 9 umbrella: strict_config, strict_markers, strict_xfail,
# strict_parametrization_ids — unknown ini keys and unregistered markers
# become errors instead of warnings.
strict = true
# Logs are captured and shown only for failing tests (pytest's default). Streaming
# live INFO for every passing test buried real output ~10-27x; opt back in per-run
# with `-o log_cli=true --log-cli-level=INFO` when debugging.
log_cli = false
log_cli_level = "INFO"
norecursedirs = ["examples"]
pytester_example_dir = "tests/integration/examples"
addopts = ["--log-disable=werkzeug", "--import-mode=importlib"]
pythonpath = [
    ".",
]
testpaths = ["tests"]
markers = [
    "slow: subprocess-spawning or sleep-bound integration test; deselect with -m 'not slow'",
]
# Treat warnings as errors so dependency deprecations (e.g. across the 3.13/3.14
# and lowest-floor matrix) fail loudly instead of rotting. The plugin's own
# ScenarioValidationWarning is intentional behavior that many tests assert on,
# so it stays a warning; individual tests still escalate it via -W when needed.
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    "default::pytest_httpchain.ScenarioValidationWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src"]
branch = true
# Measure pytester subprocess children too (runpytest_subprocess families):
# `patch` injects startup into every child with this config serialized —
# data_file/source absolutized, so children report into this project's data
# files regardless of their CWD. Requires the pid-suffixed parallel data
# files; run `coverage combine` before `coverage report`.
parallel = true
patch = ["subprocess"]

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
# Regression floor for the CI `coverage report` step (full suite under
# `coverage run -m pytest`, ~98%). Kept a few points below the real number to
# tolerate platform/Python-version branch differences; ratchet upward as
# coverage improves rather than letting it silently erode.
fail_under = 96

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "pytest_httpchain"

# Exhaustive vertical layering: every top-level module must appear in exactly one
# layer; a new module fails lint-imports until it is placed. Modules on the same
# layer (separated by ":") are additionally kept mutually independent.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "package layering"
type = "layers"
containers = ["pytest_httpchain"]
exhaustive = true
layers = [
    "plugin : cli",
    "factory",
    # importers is the cli's `import` command, beside carrier and independent
    # of it: it builds on validation, templates and redaction, and nothing on
    # a lower layer, the domain packages included, may import it.
    "carrier : dataflow : schema : importers",
    "validation : har_writer : report_formatter : request_builder : response_steps : parallel_stats",
    "body_schema",
    # scoping reads stage marks with utils.make_marker (scoping.SkipCause).
    "scoping",
    "utils : redaction",
    "userfunc",
    "models",
    "templates : jsonref",
    "wire_codec",
    "errors : constants : warnings",
]

# Horizontal refinement the layers contract cannot express: models sits above the
# domain trio and may import templates/userfunc, but must never import jsonref.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "models does not import jsonref"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pytest_httpchain.models"]
forbidden_modules = ["pytest_httpchain.jsonref"]

    "pytest>=9.0.3",
    "pytest-cov>=7.0.0",
    "networkx>=3.6.1",
    "matplotlib>=3.10.8",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",
    "debugpy>=1.8.19",
    "ruff>=0.14.10",
    "pre-commit>=4.5.1",
    "mypy>=1.19.1",  # Static type checking
    "types-python-dateutil>=2.9.0.20251115",  # Type stubs for dateutil
    "types-bleach>=6.3.0.20251115",  # Type stubs for bleach
    "websocket-client>=1.9.0",  # WebSocket client for testing connection termination
    "bandit>=1.9.2",  # Python security linter
    "pylint>=4.0.4",  # Python code quality linter
    "pylint-per-file-ignores>=3.2.0",  # Per-file ignore support for pylint (matches ruff per-file-ignores)
    "sqlfluff>=4.2.0",  # SQL linting; >=4.1.0 CVE-2026-46373, >=4.2.0 CVE-2026-46374
    "lizard>=1.19.0",  # Code complexity analyzer (used by Codacy)
    "vulture>=2.11",  # Dead code finder (unused functions, classes, variables)
    # sqlint>=0.2.1 - REMOVED: Conflicts with click>=8.1.8 (sqlint requires click==7.0)
    # Use sqlfluff instead, which provides comprehensive SQL linting
    "asyncpg-stubs>=0.31.0",
    "import-linter>=2.5",  # Enforces ADR-001 layer direction as CI-checked contracts (#757)
    "basedpyright==1.40.1",  # #784 gate; exact pin: the baseline is checker-version specific. CI installs .[dev], not [dependency-groups] dev
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["server*"]

[tool.vulture]
paths = ["server"]
# graphify-out/.venv under server/ is a local tool dump, not app code (matches ruff extend-exclude).
exclude = [
    "server/tests",
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/graphify-out/*",
    "*/.venv/*",
    "*/site-packages/*",
]
# Ignore FastAPI/router convention: route handlers receive request (or _request) for side effect
ignore_names = ["_request", "request", "app", "_", "db", "_db"]
min_confidence = 80

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py314"
# line-length checks disabled project-wide; formatter may still use this for wrap
line-length = 120
# Generated graphify extract/wiki trees (and any nested **/graphify/** dumps).
extend-exclude = ["graphify-out", "**/graphify-out", "**/graphify"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",  # pycodestyle errors
    "W",  # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",  # pyflakes
    "I",  # isort
    "B",  # flake8-bugbear
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "C90", # mccabe complexity (includes C901: too complex)
    "UP", # pyupgrade
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long - line-length checks disabled globally
    "B008",  # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    # py314 (PEP 649/749) modernization deferred from #748 to #988; remove these when it lands.
    "UP037",  # quoted annotations (420 sites); safe to unquote only with runtime-resolver review
    "UP043",  # unnecessary default type args
]
# Cyclomatic complexity threshold: 11 (matches Codacy threshold)
# Functions with complexity > 10 will trigger C901 violation
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 11

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/**/*" = ["B011"]
"docs/**/*" = ["F821", "F841", "F811", "B904", "E402"]
# Codacy's containerised PyLintPython3 uses a pre-3.12 parser and fails to parse PEP 695 type
# parameter lists ("Parsing failed: expected '('"). Keep the TypeVar spelling used by the
# repo's other 12 generics until that runtime catches up. See #784.
"server/tests/support.py" = ["UP047"]
"server/main.py" = ["E402"]  # Reason: Imports must come after load_dotenv() to ensure env vars are loaded before any modules that depend on them are imported
# ast.NodeVisitor dispatches to visit_<NodeType> (e.g. visit_Import, visit_ImportFrom, visit_Call); names fixed by API
"scripts/verify_enhanced_logging_compliance.py" = ["N802", "N815"]

[tool.isort]
profile = "black"
line_length = 120
multi_line_output = 3
include_trailing_comma = true
force_grid_wrap = 0
use_parentheses = true
ensure_newline_before_comments = true
known_first_party = ["server"]
known_third_party = [
    "fastapi",
    "pydantic",
    "uvicorn",
    "argon2",
    "jose",
    "faker",
    "dotenv",
    "sqlalchemy",
    "structlog",
    "fastapi_users",
    "pytest",
    "jsonschema",
    "bleach",
    "tqdm",
    "click",
    "passlib",
    "nats",
    "psutil",
    "ftfy",
    "strip_ansi",
    "playwright",
    "prometheus_client",
]
sections = ["FUTURE", "STDLIB", "THIRDPARTY", "FIRSTPARTY", "LOCALFOLDER"]
skip_glob = ["**/node_modules/**", "**/__pycache__/**", "**/.git/**"]
force_sort_within_sections = true
lines_after_imports = 2

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["server/tests"]
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_functions = "test_*"

# Test discovery patterns
norecursedirs = [".git", ".tox", "dist", "build", "*.egg", "__pycache__", "node_modules"]

# Markers for test categories
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests",
    "integration: Integration tests",
    "e2e: End-to-end tests",
    "security: Security tests",
    "performance: Performance tests",
    "slow: Slow running tests",
    "regression: Bug fix regression tests",
    "coverage: Coverage improvement tests",
    "monitoring: Monitoring tests",
    "verification: Verification tests"
]

# Coverage settings
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--cov=server",
    "--cov-branch",
    "--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered",
    "--cov-report=html",
    "--cov-report=xml",
    "--cov-config=.coveragerc",
]

# Async support
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["server"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/stubs/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]
fail_under = 63

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
files = ["server"]
plugins = ["sqlalchemy.ext.mypy.plugin", "pydantic.mypy"]

# Gradual strictness: Enable checks incrementally for established codebase
strict = true # NOTE: revealed 962 errors. Enabling selectively instead.
warn_unreachable = true

# Performance optimizations (best practices)
cache_dir = ".mypy_cache"
namespace_packages = false  # Changed: server is not a namespace package
explicit_package_bases = false  # Changed: not using explicit package bases

# Discovery settings
follow_imports = "normal"
ignore_missing_imports = false

# Display options
show_error_codes = true
show_column_numbers = true
show_error_context = true
pretty = true

# Exclude patterns (directories that should never be type-checked)
exclude = [
    "^data/",
    "^client/",
    "^scripts/",
    "^docs/",
    "^tools/",
    "^monitoring/",
    "^\\.cursor/",
    "^\\.claude/",
    "^graphify-out/",
    ".*[\\\\/]graphify-out[\\\\/].*",
    ".*[\\\\/]graphify[\\\\/].*",
    "^server/tests/",
    ".*[\\\\/]__tests__[\\\\/].*",
    "^server/time/",  # Exclude server/time to avoid conflict with stdlib time module
    ".*[\\\\/]time[\\\\/]__init__\\.py$",  # Also exclude time/__init__.py specifically (Windows and Unix paths)
    "^server/persistence/__init__\\.py$",  # Exclude to avoid duplicate module conflict (matches pre-commit exclude)
    ".*[\\\\/]conftest\\.py$",  # Exclude all conftest.py files to avoid duplicate module conflicts (pytest-specific, don't need type checking)
]

# Per-module options - Third-party libraries without stubs or with incomplete stubs
# NOTE: analyze_error_logs and error_monitoring are in scripts/ which is excluded from mypy
# NOTE: prometheus_client is used in server.time which is excluded, so this override is unused but kept for future use
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "aiofiles",
    "bleach",
    "strip_ansi.*",
    "asyncpg",
    "ftfy.*",
    "statemachine.*",
    "prometheus_client.*",
    "psycopg2.*",
    "jsonschema.*",
    "psutil.*",
    "networkx.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# NOTE: nats / structlog / fastapi_users previously pointed at hand-written stubs under
# server/stubs/ via mypy_path. All three ship py.typed inline types upstream, and basedpyright
# never read those stubs at all (no stubPath was set), so the two checkers disagreed about the
# same libraries -- which is what produced the `redundant-cast` conflicts. Stubs deleted in #784;
# the global `ignore_missing_imports = false` already covers these modules.

# Core libraries - use their official types
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["fastapi.*", "pydantic.*", "uvicorn.*", "starlette.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = false

# SQLAlchemy - enable strict checking with plugin support
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["sqlalchemy.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = false
warn_return_any = false

# Logging module - use targeted error code disabling instead of blanket ignore_errors
# NOTE: Module is actually server.structured_logging, not server.logging
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "server.structured_logging.*",
]
# Disable specific error codes instead of ignore_errors = true
disable_error_code = ["var-annotated", "no-untyped-def", "no-untyped-call"]
disallow_untyped_defs = false
check_untyped_defs = false

# Player GUID formatter relies on dynamic logging context; allow untyped for now
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "server.structured_logging.player_guid_formatter",
]
disallow_untyped_defs = false
check_untyped_defs = false

# Modules with remaining no-untyped-def violations; relax strictness until fully annotated.
# Human: Gradual typing; we fix critical paths first, then annotate these modules.
# AI: Override disallow_untyped_defs for specific server modules with many untyped defs.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "server.services.nats_service",
    "server.persistence.repositories.*",
    "server.game.player_state_service",
    "server.game.emote_service",
    "server.game.mechanics",
    "server.game.player_respawn_wrapper",
    "server.game.player_search_service",
    "server.game.player_schema_converter",
    "server.game.player_creation_service",
    "server.game.player_service",
    "server.services.combat_turn_processor",
    "server.services.combat_event_handler",
    "server.services.combat_attack_handler",
    "server.services.exploration_service",
    "server.services.schedule_service",
    "server.services.holiday_service",
    "server.services.user_manager",
    "server.services.combat_messaging_integration",
    "server.services.combat_messaging",
    "server.services.combat_death_handler",
    "server.services.combat_cleanup_handler",
    "server.services.combat_persistence_handler",
    "server.services.passive_lucidity_flux_service",
    "server.realtime.event_handlers",
    "server.realtime.message_filtering",
    "server.realtime.connection_manager",
    "server.realtime.connection_manager_utils",
    "server.npc.npc_base",
    "server.npc.shopkeeper_npc",
    "server.npc.passive_mob_npc",
    "server.npc.idle_movement",
    "server.npc.aggressive_mob_npc",
    "server.auth.users",
]
disallow_untyped_defs = false
check_untyped_defs = true

# Based Pyright (IDE / CLI): scope checks to this repo; do not analyze stdlib sources
# or dependency trees under .venv. If you still see diagnostics on
# pyenv-win/.../Lib/*.py, that file is outside the project: close it and set the
# interpreter to this workspace's .venv.
[tool.basedpyright]
pythonVersion = "3.14"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"
# Repo root on path so scripts/*.py can import the top-level `server` package (same as runtime sys.path).
extraPaths = ["."]
# Scope: server/** only (prod + tests). Mirrors `files = ["server"]` under [tool.mypy].
# A no-argument `basedpyright` run -- which is what the pre-commit gate and CI run -- checks
# exactly this set, so the baseline in .basedpyright/baseline.json stays meaningful. See #784.
include = ["server"]
# `# type: ignore[code]` is a mypy comment. basedpyright honours a bare `# type: ignore` by
# suppressing EVERY rule on that line and ignoring the mypy rule code, so 372 such comments
# under server/ were blanket-laundering Any findings. Rule-specific `# pyright: ignore[rule]`
# is the only suppression this project accepts, and it must carry the justification comment
# enforced by scripts/lint_pyright_suppressions.py. See #784.
enableTypeIgnoreComments = false
exclude = [
    "**/.venv",
    "**/node_modules",
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/.git",
    "**/htmlcov",
    "**/.mypy_cache",
    "**/.pytest_cache",
    "**/.ruff_cache",
    "**/graphify-out",
    "**/graphify",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "ruff>=0.14.10",
    "mypy>=1.19.1", # Static type checking
    "types-python-dateutil>=2.9.0.20251115", # Type stubs for dateutil
    "websocket-client>=1.9.0", # WebSocket client for testing connection termination
    "types-bleach>=6.3.0.20251115",
    "types-psutil>=7.2.1.20251231",
    "types-jsonschema>=4.25.1.20251009",
    "types-psycopg2>=2.9.21.20251012",
    "types-networkx>=3.6.1.20251220",
    "asyncpg-stubs>=0.31.0", # Type stubs for asyncpg (basedpyright reportMissingTypeStubs)
    "bandit>=1.9.2", # Python security linter
    "pylint>=4.0.4", # Python code quality linter
    "pylint-per-file-ignores>=3.2.0", # Per-file ignore support for pylint (matches ruff per-file-ignores)
    "sqlfluff>=4.2.0", # SQL linting and formatting; >=4.1.0 CVE-2026-46373, >=4.2.0 CVE-2026-46374
    "lizard>=1.19.0", # Code complexity analyzer (used by Codacy)
    "vulture>=2.11", # Dead code finder (unused functions, classes, variables)
    # sqlint>=0.2.1 - REMOVED: Conflicts with click>=8.1.8 (sqlint requires click==7.0)
    # Use sqlfluff instead, which provides comprehensive SQL linting
    "basedpyright==1.40.1",  # keep in lockstep with [project.optional-dependencies] dev
    "import-linter>=2.5", # Enforces ADR-001 layer direction as CI-checked contracts (#757)
]

[tool.uv]
# Suppress hardlink warning on Windows when cache and project are on different filesystems
# Using "copy" mode ensures files are always copied instead of hardlinked
link-mode = "copy"
# Force python-multipart>=0.0.22 for CVE-2024-53981/CVE-2024-24762; fastapi-users 15.0.3 pins ==0.0.21
override-dependencies = ["python-multipart>=0.0.27"]

version = "2.7.3"
description = "A collection of custom and reusable Qt widgets for PySide6. Provides advanced, reusable, and stylish graphical components to facilitate the development of modern and user-friendly interfaces."

requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "Neuraaak" }]
maintainers = [{ name = "Neuraaak" }]
keywords = [
    "qt",
    "pyside6",
    "widgets",
    "gui",
    "interface",
    "components",
    "ui",
    "desktop",
]

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",

    "pre-commit>=3.0.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0.0",

    "venv",

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🎨 CODE FORMATTING & LINTING TOOLS
# Auto-formatting, import sorting, and style checking
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Ruff: All-in-one linter with comprehensive rule sets
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 88

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "I",   # isort-compatible import sorting (via ruff)
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "S",   # bandit security
    "T20", # flake8-print
    "ARG", # flake8-unused-arguments
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
]
ignore = [
    "E501", # line too long, handled by ruff format
    "B008", # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "S101", # assert_used (for tests)
    "S106", # hardcoded_password_funcarg
    "T201", # print statements (for init.py and scripts)
    "S603", # subprocess.run without check=True
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*" = ["S101", "S311", "E501", "ARG002", "S105", "S602", "S603"]
"examples/**/*" = ["T201", "E501"]
"src/ezqt_widgets/cli/**/*" = ["T201", "E501", "S603"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# ✅ TYPE CHECKING TOOLS
# Static type analysis with minimal and comprehensive modes
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Ty: Type checking with minimal configuration
[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.11"
root = ["src", "src/ezqt_widgets"]

[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src/ezqt_widgets/**/*.py"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "docs",
]
respect-ignore-files = true

[tool.ty.terminal]
output-format = "full"
error-on-warning = false

[tool.ty.rules]
# Ignore PySide6 stub issues (isValid, setIcon, setText overloads)
no-matching-overload = "ignore"

# Pyright: Comprehensive type checking with detailed reporting
[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.11"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
include = ["src/ezqt_widgets"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "**/node_modules",
    "**/.*",
]
reportMissingImports = true
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportUnusedImport = true
reportUnusedClass = true
reportUnusedFunction = true
reportUnusedVariable = true
reportDuplicateImport = true
reportOptionalSubscript = true
reportOptionalMemberAccess = true
reportOptionalCall = true
reportOptionalIterable = true
reportOptionalContextManager = true
reportOptionalOperand = true
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = false
reportUntypedClassDecorator = false
reportUntypedBaseClass = false
reportUntypedNamedTuple = false
reportPrivateUsage = false
reportConstantRedefinition = true
# Disabled: Qt widgets intentionally override methods with properties
reportIncompatibleMethodOverride = false
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = true
reportInconsistentConstructor = true

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# � IMPORT LINTER CONTRACTS
# Layer dependency contracts enforced in CI
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["ezqt_widgets"]
# Note: import-linter 2.x ne supporte pas source_paths (feature pending PR #323).
# Le package doit être installé en mode editable (uv sync) ou lancer avec PYTHONPATH=src lint-imports

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "layer dependency flow"
type = "layers"
layers = ["ezqt_widgets.cli", "ezqt_widgets.widgets", "ezqt_widgets.utils"]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🧪 TESTING & COVERAGE TOOLS
# Test execution, coverage analysis, and test configuration
# /////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Pytest: Test runner with markers and coverage configuration
[tool.pytest.ini_options]

# =============================================================================
# Ruff - linting + formatting
# =============================================================================
# Replaces black, flake8, flake8-tidy-imports, flake8-cognitive-complexity
# and pydocstyle.
#
#   uv run ruff check .          # lint
#   uv run ruff check --fix .    # lint + apply safe fixes
#   uv run ruff format .         # format
#
# IMPORTANT - import boundaries: the `banned-modules` option of
# flake8-tidy-imports is expressed here as `banned-api`. Ruff matches banned
# paths COMPONENT-WISE (banning `a.b` also bans `a.b.c`) and does NOT
# understand flake8's `a.b.*` wildcard syntax. A key that contains a wildcard
# matches nothing at all and silently disables the whole boundary check, so
# keep the keys below wildcard-free.
#
# Deliberately NOT enabled yet (measured violation counts at migration time):
#   D    1919  docstring coverage - needs a documentation pass
#   PL    836  pylint - largely overlapping, high churn
#   S    5167  bandit rules - covered by the bandit + semgrep hooks instead
#   ARG   317  unused arguments - noisy against Qt slots / ABC overrides
#   T20   150  print - meaningful only per-package, see note below
#   C90    34  cyclomatic complexity - see note below
#   G      27  logging format - assumes %-style logging, this codebase uses structlog
#   DTZ    17  naive datetimes - fixing changes the on-disk journal format
#
# T20 note: the project requires stdout to stay clean for LB_EVENT streaming.
# Enforcing "no print in lb_runner/lb_app/lb_controller" is worthwhile but needs
# a per-package decision, since it is legitimate in CLI commands and scripts.
#
# C90 note: ruff has no implementation of flake8-cognitive-complexity, so the
# former CCR001 check cannot be migrated. The cyclomatic equivalent (C901) is
# dominated by Typer command-registration functions, which are long but linear
# (register_resume_command scores 63), so gating on it today would be noise
# rather than signal. Complexity is instead covered by the radon/xenon sweep in
# scripts/arch_audit.sh.

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = [
    # Vendored Ansible collections and generated molecule artifacts.
    "lb_controller/ansible/collections/ansible_collections",
    "molecule/*/controller_artifacts",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",     # pycodestyle errors
    "W",     # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",     # Pyflakes
    "I",     # isort
    "N",     # pep8-naming
    "UP",    # pyupgrade
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",    # flake8-comprehensions
    "SIM",   # flake8-simplify
    "TID",   # flake8-tidy-imports (import boundaries)
    "RUF",   # Ruff-specific rules
    "PERF",  # Perflint
    "PT",    # flake8-pytest-style
    "RET",   # flake8-return
    "PTH",   # flake8-use-pathlib
    "ERA",   # eradicate (commented-out code)
    "D",     # pydocstyle (replaces the pydocstyle tool)
]
ignore = [
    # Whitespace before ':' - conflicts with the formatter, which owns this.
    "E203",
    # "Split this assertion into multiple parts" - produces worse failure
    # diagnostics for compound assertions and is not worth the churn.
    "PT018",
    # Missing-docstring family. ruff flags far more of these than pydocstyle did
    # (891 vs 216 on the same scope) because its notion of "public" is broader.
    # Documenting the public API is its own task, tracked separately; the
    # docstring rules that remain enabled are the consistency ones (D2xx/D4xx),
    # which are auto-fixable and now actually enforced.
    "D100",  # missing docstring in public module
    "D101",  # missing docstring in public class
    "D102",  # missing docstring in public method
    "D103",  # missing docstring in public function
    "D104",  # missing docstring in public package
    "D105",  # missing docstring in magic method
    "D107",  # missing docstring in __init__
    # Mutually exclusive summary conventions. The project's pydocstyle config
    # ignored D203/D213, i.e. it opted into D212 semantics - kept identical.
    "D203",  # blank line before class docstring
    "D213",  # multi-line summary second line
    # Nitpicks with low signal.
    "D401",  # non-imperative mood
    "D417",  # undocumented-param
    # "Use StrEnum instead of class X(str, Enum)" - new in the ruff 0.16 series
    # and deliberately NOT applied. The two are not equivalent: verified on this
    # interpreter, str() and f-strings on a (str, Enum) member yield
    # "ControllerState.RUNNING" and on a StrEnum member "running". Five classes
    # here mix in str, and they are public API (lb_controller.api exports
    # SigintDecision), so the conversion would change what those enums render as
    # in logs, reports and any consumer that stringifies them. Nothing in this
    # repository interpolates them, so no test would catch it. Adopt it as its
    # own change, with the affected call sites checked, not as a side effect of
    # a version bump.
    "UP042",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Import boundaries: the .api-only rule is enforced by flake8-tidy-imports'
# banned-modules successor below (TID251), plus the layer contracts in
# [tool.importlinter] and tests/unit/lint/test_import_boundaries.py.
# Modules inside lb_controller are of course allowed to use their own internals.
"lb_controller/**" = ["TID251"]
"tests/unit/lb_controller/**" = ["TID251"]
"tests/unit/common/test_lb_events_callback.py" = ["TID251"]
"tests/unit/common/test_plugin_installer.py" = ["TID251"]

"tests/e2e/**" = ["E501"]

"lb_ui/cli/**" = ["B008"]

known-first-party = ["lb_common", "lb_plugins", "lb_runner", "lb_controller", "lb_app", "lb_analytics", "lb_provisioner", "lb_ui", "lb_gui"]

# Import boundary rule, ported from the .flake8 `banned-modules` list.

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"lb_controller.ansible" = { msg = "Use lb_controller.api instead." }
"lb_controller.ansible_executor" = { msg = "Use lb_controller.api instead." }

# =============================================================================
# basedpyright - type checking
# =============================================================================
# This replaces mypy, which was the last type checker in the sibling projects.
# The migration was a swap, not a relaxing:
#
#   - mypy's strict flags (disallow_untyped_defs, warn_return_any,
#     disallow_untyped_decorators, warn_unreachable and the rest) are what
#     basedpyright's "standard" mode enforces by default. It reports the same
#     class of problem on this codebase - the bulk of what it found is
#     reportReturnType, which is mypy's warn_return_any.
#   - `plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]` is gone because basedpyright understands
#     pydantic natively; the plugin was a mypy mechanism.
#   - mypy followed imports transitively, which is why type checking used to run
#     through scripts/mypy_{core,plugins,all}.sh with --follow-imports=silent to
#     keep it out of the vendored Ansible collections. basedpyright only checks
#     what `include` names, so the same scoping is expressed here as data and
#     the scripts are gone.
#   - the four [[tool.mypy.overrides]] blocks existed to silence missing-stub
#     and missing-import reports for third-party packages. basedpyright resolves
#     all of them against the venv, and reportMissingTypeStubs covers the rest,
#     so none of them needed a basedpyright equivalent.
#
# reportImplicitOverride is left off, as in the projects that support 3.11;
# turning it on would add findings across the tree for a rule unrelated to this
# migration.

[tool.basedpyright]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
pythonVersion = "3.12"
include = [
    "lb_analytics",
    "lb_app",
    "lb_common",
    "lb_controller",
    "lb_gui",
    "lb_plugins",
    "lb_provisioner",
    "lb_runner",
    "lb_ui",
]
exclude = [
    "molecule",
    "lb_controller/ansible/collections",
    "lb_plugins/plugins/_user",
]
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportPrivateUsage = false
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

# =============================================================================
# Bandit - security static analysis
# =============================================================================
# Run with: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r <package>
#
# The skips below are families that are correct by design in this project.
# Everything else is left enabled: a new shell=True or a new hardcoded
# credential must still fail. Sites that are individually justified carry an
# inline `# nosec Bxxx` with a reason instead of being skipped wholesale.

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "molecule", ".venv", "arch_report"]
skips = [
    # This project exists to shell out to benchmark binaries, so importing
    # subprocess and using partial paths is the normal mode of operation,
    # not a finding. B602 (shell=True) is deliberately NOT skipped.
    "B404",
    "B603",
    "B607",
    # try/except/pass. Ruff's SIM105 covers this pattern with better feedback
    # (contextlib.suppress), so bandit's copy is duplicate noise.
    "B110",
    # Benchmark servers (dfaas/peva_faas generators) intentionally bind all
    # interfaces: the controller connects to them from other hosts.
    "B104",
    # tempfile.gettempdir() under a fixed subdirectory is used for a stable
    # on-disk asset cache, which is the intent - not for secret material.
    "B108",
    # urllib is used for configured Grafana/Loki/webhook endpoints. The scheme
    # comes from the user's own config, not from remote input.
    "B310",
    # SQL built by f-string interpolation of a table name, in
    # lb_plugins/plugins/peva_faas/services/memory_checkpoint.py (3 sites).
    # The interpolated value is never user input: it is always one of the
    # hardcoded CORE_TABLES / DEBUG_TABLES class constants, and every data
    # value is passed as a `?` parameter. An inline `# nosec` is not usable
    # there because the comment pushes the already-long SQL line past the
    # 88-char lint limit; the rule is therefore documented here instead.
    "B608",
]

# =============================================================================
# Coverage
# =============================================================================
# Run with: uv run pytest --cov
#
# fail_under is a ratchet: it is set to the level the suite actually holds so
# it prevents regressions. Raise it as coverage improves; never lower it to
# make a build pass.

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["lb_common", "lb_plugins", "lb_runner", "lb_controller", "lb_app", "lb_ui", "lb_analytics"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
# Measured at 73.2% on `pytest tests/unit tests/integration -m "not slow and
# not slowest and not inter_docker"` (2026-10-09, lb_common and lb_plugins now
# in `source`). The gate sits a few points lower on purpose: CI runs a
# 3.12/3.13 matrix and branch coverage varies slightly by version, and a gate
# that flakes is worse than a gate that lags. Raise it as the suite improves;
# never lower it to make a build pass.
fail_under = 70
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "\\.\\.\\.",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=7.3.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0.0",
    "pytest-mock>=3.10.0",
    "psutil>=7.0.0",
    "fabric>=3.2.2",
    "invoke>=2.2.1",
    "duckdb>=1.1.0",
    "pyarrow>=17.0.0",
    "pandas-stubs>=2.2.0.240218",
    "rich>=13.7.0",
    "typer>=0.12.5",
    "rapidfuzz>=3.0.0",
    "prompt_toolkit>=3.0.0",
    "PySide6>=6.6.0",
    # Linting + formatting. ruff replaces black, flake8, flake8-tidy-imports,
    # flake8-cognitive-complexity and pydocstyle.
    #
    # Pinned exactly, not with >=: .pre-commit-config.yaml pins the matching
    # ruff-pre-commit revision, and a newer ruff in either place makes the hook
    # and the local run disagree about what a violation is. Bump both together.
    "ruff==0.16.6",
    # The shared type checker across these projects; mypy is no longer used
    # anywhere. See [tool.basedpyright] for what replaced which mypy setting.
    "basedpyright>=1.39.3",
    "pre-commit>=3.2.0",
    "ansible-runner>=2.4.0",
    "ansible-lint>=25.0.0",
    "yamllint>=1.35.0",
    "vulture>=2.10",
    "coverage>=7.13.0",
    "radon>=6.0.1",
    "xenon>=0.9.3",
    "lizard>=1.19.0",
    "grimp>=3.14",
    "import-linter>=2.9",
    "pydeps>=3.0.1",
    "pyan3>=1.2.0",
    "deptry>=0.24.0",
    "pip-audit>=2.9.0",
    "bandit>=1.9.2",
    "semgrep>=1.86.0",
    "tenacity>=9.1.2",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0.12.20250822",
    "types-psutil>=7.0.0.20250601",
]

[tool.deptry]
# scripts/bump_version is a self-contained project with its own pyproject.toml
# and uv.lock (it depends on questionary, which the root project does not).
# Scanning it against the root dependencies reports false DEP001 misses.
extend_exclude = ["molecule", "scripts/bump_version"]

per_rule_ignores = { DEP001 = [
    "controller_stop_runner",
], DEP002 = [
    # Build/docs tooling invoked as executables rather than imported.
    "pytest-cov",
    "vulture",
    "molecule",
    "molecule-plugins",
    "mkdocs",
    "mkdocs-material",
    "mkdocstrings",
    # Optional UI dependencies. They are imported lazily / via
    # importlib.import_module so that a headless controller install works
    # without a display, which deptry cannot see statically:
    #   plyer, desktop-notifier  -> lb_ui/notifications/providers/desktop.py
    #   pystray                  -> lb_ui/services/tray.py
    #   pillow (PIL.Image)       -> lb_ui/services/assets.py (icon rendering)
    #   rapidfuzz                -> lb_ui pickers (fuzzy matching)
    "plyer",
    "desktop-notifier",
    "pystray",
    "pillow",
    "rapidfuzz",
    # Not imported in Python at all, but required at runtime: duckdb uses
    # pyarrow for its parquet reader/writer, which the peva_faas memory
    # checkpoint relies on (read_parquet / COPY ... FORMAT PARQUET), and
    # pandas uses it as the to_parquet engine for lb_analytics exports.
    "pyarrow",
] }

# =============================================================================
# Import Linter - Enforces layered architecture import boundaries
# =============================================================================
# Run with: uv run lint-imports
#
# Architecture:
#   lb_common (base) <- lb_plugins <- lb_runner <- lb_controller <- lb_app <- lb_ui
#   lb_analytics and lb_provisioner are siblings at the lb_app level
#
# These contracts enforce that packages only import from allowed lower layers.
# The .api boundary enforcement is handled by scripts/check_api_imports.py
# because import-linter tracks transitive imports which don't work well with
# re-exports from .api modules.

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["lb_common", "lb_plugins", "lb_runner", "lb_controller", "lb_app", "lb_ui", "lb_gui", "lb_analytics", "lb_provisioner"]
include_external_packages = false

# Layered architecture contract - enforces the dependency hierarchy
# Note: lb_controller, lb_analytics, lb_provisioner are at the same level (can't import each other)
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "lb_ui : lb_gui",
    "lb_app",
    "lb_controller",
    "lb_runner",
    "lb_plugins",
    "lb_common",
]
# lb_plugins has a known dependency on lb_runner for log_manager services
# This is a design decision to allow plugins to use runner's logging facilities
ignore_imports = [
    "lb_plugins.plugins.dfaas.services.log_manager -> lb_runner.api",
    "lb_plugins.plugins.peva_faas.services.log_manager -> lb_runner.api",
]

# lb_analytics is isolated - only imports from lb_common
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "lb_analytics isolation"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lb_analytics"]
forbidden_modules = ["lb_plugins", "lb_runner", "lb_controller", "lb_app", "lb_ui", "lb_gui", "lb_provisioner"]

# lb_provisioner can only import from lb_common and lb_plugins
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "lb_provisioner layer restrictions"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lb_provisioner"]
forbidden_modules = ["lb_runner", "lb_controller", "lb_app", "lb_ui", "lb_gui", "lb_analytics"]

# Note: The "forbidden" contract type tracks transitive imports, which is not what
# we want for the .api boundary check. Use scripts/check_api_imports.py for that.
# The layers contract above handles the main architecture hierarchy.

# Tool configuration only. Runtime dependencies stay in requirements.txt and
# dev tools in requirements-dev.txt; `mise run install` installs both.

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 100
extend-exclude = ["docs", "typings"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W", "F",  # pycodestyle, pyflakes
    "I",            # import order
    "UP",           # modern syntax for the target version
    "B",            # likely bugs
    "SIM",          # simplifications
    "T20",          # print: use logging (see AGENTS.md)
    "TID251",       # banned APIs below
    "ICN003",       # function modules imported whole (see AGENTS.md: imports)
]
# The formatter owns line length; long strings and comments are allowed.
ignore = ["E501"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
# Every roll goes through an injected random.Random so tests can seed it.
"random.random".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.randint".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.randrange".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.uniform".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.choice".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.choices".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.sample".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.shuffle".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.gauss".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.triangular".msg = "Roll with an injected random.Random (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
"random.seed".msg = "Seed the injected random.Random instead (see AGENTS.md: randomness)."
# Game logic runs on the game clock, never the wall clock.
"time.time".msg = "Use the game clock (see AGENTS.md: time)."
"time.monotonic".msg = "Use the game clock (see AGENTS.md: time)."
"datetime.datetime.now".msg = "Use the game clock (see AGENTS.md: time)."
"datetime.datetime.today".msg = "Use the game clock (see AGENTS.md: time)."
"datetime.date.today".msg = "Use the game clock (see AGENTS.md: time)."

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions]
# Modules of plain functions: call them through the module
# (`units.per_hour_from_frame`), so a call says where it comes from.
banned-from = ["modules.units", "managers.carry", "managers.naming", "managers.combat.weapons"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# The outside world may read the wall clock (timestamps, timeouts).
"adapters/**" = ["TID251"]
"app.py" = ["TID251"]

[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["modules", "managers", "adapters", "data", "tests", "app.py", "config.py"]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
# Errors that predate the checker live in .basedpyright/baseline.json; only new
# ones fail. Shrink it with `basedpyright --writebaseline` after fixing some.

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["modules", "data", "managers", "adapters"]
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layers: each layer depends only on the ones below it"
type = "layers"
# app.py and config.py are single modules, which import-linter cannot list.
layers = ["adapters", "managers", "data", "modules"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The game model and logic know nothing about the outside world"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["modules", "data", "managers"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "adapters", "flask", "requests", "faiss", "numpy", "sentence_transformers",
    "yaml",
]
# managers/game.py reads tuning values through config, which parses YAML.
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The game model reads no configuration"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["modules", "data"]
forbidden_modules = ["config"]

# Import Linter 配置文件
# 用于强制执行分层架构规则
#
# 运行检查：
#   task arch-check
#   lint-imports
#   lint-imports --contract layered-architecture

[importlinter]
# 多个 root packages
root_packages =
    ditto_platform
    ditto_kernel
    ditto_data
    ditto_features
    ditto_analysis
    ditto_strategy
    ditto_portfolio
    ditto_risk
    ditto_execution
    ditto_backtest
    ditto_application
    ditto_agent
    ditto_apps

# 不包含外部包
include_external_packages = false

# TYPE_CHECKING 导入也是架构依赖，不得用于隐藏边界违规或循环
exclude_type_checking_imports = false

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 分层架构检查
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[importlinter:contract:layered-architecture]
name = Layered Architecture
type = layers
# Technical ordering for import-linter's `layers` contract.
# This is not the domain architecture model.
#
# Domain architecture is a diamond:
#   apps -> application -> {data, features, strategy, portfolio, risk, execution, backtest, analysis} -> kernel
#   platform is horizontal foundation.
#
# import-linter `layers` needs a sequence, so this contract only guards
# broad top-to-bottom imports. Parallel-plane isolation is enforced by
# the explicit forbidden contracts below.
layers =
    ditto_apps
    ditto_agent
    ditto_application
    ditto_portfolio
    ditto_analysis
    ditto_features
    ditto_data
    ditto_platform
# NOTE: ditto_strategy, ditto_risk, ditto_execution, and ditto_backtest not in
# layers — they have bidirectional or cross-layer dependencies with other packages.
# Isolation is enforced by explicit forbidden contracts below.

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Kernel 层隔离：禁止依赖其他层
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[importlinter:contract:kernel-isolation]
name = Kernel must not depend on other layers
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ditto_kernel.**
forbidden_modules =
    ditto_data.**
    ditto_apps.**
    ditto_application.**
    ditto_platform.**
    ditto_features.**
    ditto_analysis.**
    ditto_strategy.**
    ditto_portfolio.**
    ditto_risk.**
    ditto_execution.**
    ditto_backtest.**
    ditto_agent.**

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Platform 层隔离：禁止依赖业务层（允许依赖 kernel）
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[importlinter:contract:platform-isolation]
name = Platform must not depend on business layers (kernel allowed)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ditto_platform.**
forbidden_modules =
    ditto_data.**
    ditto_apps.**
    ditto_kernel.**
    ditto_features.**
    ditto_analysis.**
    ditto_strategy.**
    ditto_risk.**
    ditto_execution.**
    ditto_backtest.**
    ditto_application.**
# PlatformError 继承 DittoError（全局异常根），这是跨层共享的合法依赖
ignore_imports =
    ditto_platform.exceptions -> ditto_kernel.exceptions
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = warn

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Platform storage 纯技术基础设施：禁止包含业务逻辑
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    ditto_portfolio.**
    ditto_risk.**

    ditto_analysis.**
    ditto_application.**
    ditto_apps.**

# Apps 层边界：禁止直接依赖 Data 服务/模型（逐步收紧）

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[importlinter:contract:apps-service-isolation]
name = Apps must not directly depend on Data services/models (tightening)
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ditto_apps.**
forbidden_modules =
    ditto_data.services.**
    ditto_data.services
    ditto_data.models.**
    ditto_data.models
    ditto_data.errors.**
    ditto_data.errors
    ditto_data.quality.**
    ditto_data.quality
    ditto_data.config.**
    ditto_data.config
# Registry 豁免（Composition Root）

    ditto_apps.registry.** -> ditto_data.services.**
    ditto_apps.registry.** -> ditto_data.quality.**
    ditto_apps.registry.** -> ditto_data.config
    ditto_apps.registry.** -> ditto_data.config.**

    ditto_apps.jobs.tasks.monitoring -> ditto_data.quality.quality_types

unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = error

# 矩阵：

source_modules =

forbidden_modules =
    ditto_application.builders.**

name = R8: app.builders must not import app.queries
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ditto_application.builders.**
forbidden_modules =
    ditto_application.queries.**

[importlinter:contract:r8-queries-no-commands]
name = R8: app.queries must not import app.commands
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ditto_application.queries.**
forbidden_modules =
    ditto_application.commands.**

[importlinter:contract:r8-commands-no-queries]
name = R8: app.commands must not import app.queries
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ditto_application.commands.**
forbidden_modules =
    ditto_application.queries.**

[importlinter:contract:r8-commands-no-builders]
name = R8: app.commands must not import app.builders
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    ditto_application.commands.**
forbidden_modules =
    ditto_application.builders.**

# ===================================================================
# Ruff (Linter + Formatter)
# 核心代码质量工具，集成了数十种工具，速度极快。
# 负责：代码风格检查、自动格式化、导入排序、坏味道重构等。
# ===================================================================
[tool.ruff]
required-version = ">=0.6.0"
# 设置与 Black 兼容的行长。
line-length = 88
# 指定你的项目支持的最低 Python 版本。
target-version = "py313"

# 指定 Ruff 需要检查的源代码和测试目录。
src = ["packages", "apps/backend", "scripts", "tooling"]

# 全局排除不需要检查的文件和目录。
exclude = [
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".hg",
    ".nox",
    ".pants.d",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    "venv",
    "scripts/learning",
]

cache-dir = ".ruff_cache"
respect-gitignore = true
force-exclude = true

# --- Ruff Linter (检查器) 配置 ---
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",
    "F",
    "W",
    "C90",
    "I",
    "N",
    "UP",
    "B",
    "A",
    "C4",
    "SIM",
    "PTH",
    "PLC",
    "PLE",
    "PLR",
    "PLW",
    "RUF",
    "D",
    "PT",
    "ANN",
    "S",
    "T20",
]

ignore = [
    "B008",   # 允许函数调用作为默认参数（FastAPI Depends）
    "N803",   # 函数参数命名：第三方库适配（numpy 矩阵变量等）
    "N806",   # 函数内变量命名：数学/科学计算常量（X, XtX, CONVERGENCE_TOL 等）
    "N818",   # DittoException 基类命名是设计选择
    "RUF002", # 中文标点符号
    "RUF003", # 中文注释标点符号
    "D203",   # 与 Black 冲突
    "D212",   # 与 Black 冲突
    "D100",   # 模块必须有文档字符串
    "D107",   # __init__ 文档字符串
    "D400",   # 文档字符串句号结尾（中文不适用）
    "D415",   # 文档字符串首行标点
    "D401",   # 祈使语气
    "PT011",  # pytest.raises match 参数
    "SIM105", # contextlib.suppress
    "SIM117", # 嵌套 with 语句
]

unfixable = []

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# SignalDelivery - 环境变量名（非实际密钥）是 Bandit S105 已知误报
"apps/backend/src/ditto_apps/registry/infra/signal_delivery.py" = ["S105"]
# Prefect 装饰器 mock 包装任意可调用，签名必然 Any（与 stub 文件同理）

# ResearchDatasetFacade.export() - 表名来自系统 dataset_id，非用户输入
"apps/backend/src/ditto_apps/services/derived/research.py" = ["S608"]
# ResearchDatasetExport - dataset_id is validated by _sanitize_table_name
"packages/analysis/src/ditto_analysis/storage/sqlite/research/export.py" = ["S608"]
# Protocol 属性用 ``...`` 省略体是标准惯例，D102 不适用
"packages/portfolio/src/ditto_portfolio/rebalancing/report_views.py" = ["D102"]
# Protocol 接口方法用 ``...`` 省略体是标准惯例，D102 不适用
"packages/data/src/ditto_data/storage/base/protocols.py" = ["D102"]
# 第三方 stub 文件包含 Any 类型签名，无法修改
"typings/**/*.pyi" = ["ANN401"]

# 测试文件 - 最宽松（所有 tests/ 目录通用）
"**/tests/**/*.py" = [
    "PLR2004",
    "PLR0913",
    "S101",
    "S106",
    "S311",
    "S608",
    "ANN",
    "D",
    "PLC0415",
    "C901",
    "S105",
    "S108",
    "S110",
]
"**/conftest.py" = ["ANN", "D", "PLC0415"]

# 脚本文件
"scripts/**/*.py" = ["T201", "S101", "S603", "S607", "D", "ANN"]
"tooling/agent_harness/**/*.py" = ["T201", "S101", "S603", "S607", "D", "ANN"]
"tooling/dev/*.py" = ["T201", "S603", "S607", "D", "ANN"]
"tooling/quality/*.py" = ["T201"]
"apps/backend/tests/scripts/**/*.py" = ["T201", "S101", "S603", "S607", "D", "ANN", "RUF001", "PLR0912", "PLR0915", "E501"]
"**/cli.py" = ["T201"]
"**/cli/*.py" = ["T201"]
"**/main.py" = ["T201"]

# __init__.py
"__init__.py" = ["D104"]

# provider.py - 延迟导入避免循环依赖
"**/sources/provider.py" = ["PLC0415"]

# 中文 description 中使用全角标点
"packages/data/src/ditto_data/quality/golden.py" = ["RUF001"]
"packages/data/src/ditto_data/sources/tushare/adapters/index.py" = ["RUF001"]
"packages/data/src/ditto_data/sources/tushare/adapters/fundamental.py" = ["RUF001"]

# Kernel tracing — Protocol __call__ 和通用装饰器签名不可避免使用 Any

# E2E 测试
"apps/backend/tests/e2e/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "D", "ANN", "E501"]

# --- Ruff Formatter (格式化器) 配置 ---
[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

[tool.inline-snapshot]
format-command = "ruff format --stdin-filename {filename}"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-annotations]
suppress-none-returning = true
suppress-dummy-args = true

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-statements = 50
max-args = 7
max-branches = 12
max-returns = 6

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

# flake8-tidy-imports: 禁止特定 API 导入
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"pandas".msg = "Use polars instead"

# ===================================================================
# BasedPyright (类型检查) - Pyright fork，更严格的默认设置
#
# 策略：standard 打底 + 核心目录 strict
# 优势：
#   1. 避免全仓 strict 导致的噪音爆炸
#   2. 核心业务逻辑获得最严格检查
#   3. 边缘模块保持灵活性
#   4. 更多诊断规则默认启用，更好的 AI coding 支持
# ===================================================================
[tool.basedpyright]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
pythonPlatform = "All"
stubPath = "typings"

# 显式指定 uv 管理的虚拟环境，确保 VS Code 扩展和 CLI 都能正确定位
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

# 核心：standard 模式打底（比 basic 严格，比 strict 宽松）
typeCheckingMode = "standard"

# 源码目录（tests 用独立配置 pyright.tests.json）
include = ["packages/**/src", "apps/backend/src"]

# 排除目录（tests 用独立配置）
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/node_modules",
    ".venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "**/tests",
]

# VS Code 体验：tests 打开也不出红黄线（诊断被抑制）
ignore = [
    "tests",
    "tests/**",
    "**/tests/**",
    "packages/*/tests/**",
    "apps/backend/tests/**",
    # MarketQueryService: multi-line error message uses implicit string concatenation
    # (已迁移至 services/)
]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 关键：核心目录提升到 strict 模式
# 这些是最值钱的代码，值得最严格的检查
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
strict = ["packages/**/src"]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 规则微调：让 Ruff 管风格，Pyright 专注类型
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Ruff 已经管了这些
reportUnusedImport = "none"
reportUnusedVariable = "none"

# 第三方库 stub 不完整时的处理
reportMissingTypeStubs = "warning"

# 检测不必要的 type: ignore 注释
reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment = "error"

# 检测隐式字符串拼接
reportImplicitStringConcatenation = "error"

# 对于 standard 模式下的 Unknown 类型，降级为 warning
# 这样编辑器里能看到黄线提醒，但不会阻塞 CI
#reportUnknownMemberType = "warning"
#reportUnknownArgumentType = "warning"
#reportUnknownVariableType = "warning"

# 私有成员访问（测试和内部模块可能需要）
#reportPrivateUsage = "warning"

# 告诉 Pyright 源码根目录（解决 import 路径问题）
extraPaths = [
    "packages/platform/src",
    "packages/kernel/src",
    "packages/data/src",
    "packages/features/src",
    "packages/analysis/src",
    "packages/strategy/src",
    "packages/portfolio/src",
    "packages/risk/src",
    "packages/execution/src",
    "packages/backtest/src",
    "packages/application/src",
    "apps/backend/src",
]

# ===================================================================
# Pytest (测试框架)
# ===================================================================
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "7.0"
testpaths = ["packages/*/tests", "apps/backend/tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
pythonpath = [
    ".",
    "packages/platform/src",
    "packages/kernel/src",
    "packages/data/src",
    "packages/features/src",
    "packages/analysis/src",
    "packages/strategy/src",
    "packages/portfolio/src",
    "packages/risk/src",
    "packages/execution/src",
    "packages/backtest/src",
    "packages/application/src",
    "apps/backend/src",
]

filterwarnings = ["error", "ignore::UserWarning", "ignore::DeprecationWarning"]

markers = [
    "unit: Mark test as a unit test",
    "integration: Mark test as an integration test",
    "e2e: Mark test as an end-to-end test",
    "slow: Mark test as slow running (skip with -m 'not slow')",
    "serial: Mark test that must run serially",
    "capacity: Mark scheduler-capacity slow-lane test (dedicated CI job)",
    "snapshot: Mark test that uses inline-snapshot (must run serially)",
    "pit: Mark test as Point-in-Time validation (no future data leak)",
    "sandbox_live: Physical OCI sandbox acceptance requiring the approved runtime",
    "cli_test: CLI tests that disable observability auto-reset",
]

log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"
asyncio_mode = "strict"

# pytest-timeout 兜底防挂死；合法慢测试打 slow/capacity 标记进慢车道，不调大此值
timeout = 600

addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "-v",
    "--import-mode=importlib",
    "-n", "auto",           # 默认并行运行
    "--dist", "loadfile",   # 同文件测试串行（避免 snapshot 冲突）
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--durations=10",       # 报告最慢的 10 个测试
]

# ===================================================================
# Coverage
# ===================================================================
[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
patch = ["subprocess"]
source = [
    "apps/backend/src/ditto_apps",
    "packages/agent/src/ditto_agent",
    "packages/analysis/src/ditto_analysis",
    "packages/application/src/ditto_application",
    "packages/backtest/src/ditto_backtest",
    "packages/data/src/ditto_data",
    "packages/execution/src/ditto_execution",
    "packages/features/src/ditto_features",
    "packages/kernel/src/ditto_kernel",
    "packages/platform/src/ditto_platform",
    "packages/portfolio/src/ditto_portfolio",
    "packages/risk/src/ditto_risk",
    "packages/strategy/src/ditto_strategy",
]
omit = ["**/generated/**", "**/tests/**"]

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "def __str__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
    "@overload",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "if self\\.debug:",
]
fail_under = 0
partial_branches = ["pragma: no branch", "if TYPE_CHECKING:"]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

[tool.commitizen]

tag_format = "v$version"
update_changelog_on_bump = true
changelog_incremental = true

[build-system]

[dependency-groups]
