[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S101"]

# Architecture fitness check, run by `make lint` (`uv run lint-imports`).
# The contracts below are the single source of truth for the Runtime's
# dependency direction. Layers are listed top to bottom: a module may import
# its own layer or any layer below it ("a : b" siblings may import each
# other, "a | b" siblings may not). Both layers contracts are exhaustive, so a
# new top-level module or a new toolset fails until it is classified here. A
# forbidden contract keeps the Worker off the concrete toolsets, and two
# protected contracts declare the only chains between toolsets. No contract
# has ignore_imports entries (known violations); if one is ever added, keep a
# "reason; fix" comment on it. Imports under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` are excluded.
# See docs/development.md.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "contractor_runtime"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "runtime-layers"
name = "Runtime layers (top imports bottom, never the reverse)"
type = "layers"
containers = ["contractor_runtime"]
exhaustive = true
layers = [
  # entry: process entry points and the private HTTP server
  "__main__ : cli : server",
  # orchestration: allocation lifecycle, control-plane client, lease and process state
  "allocation : control_client : lease : state",
  # composition: the toolset/worker factory registry and startup capability discovery
  "capabilities : factories",
  # agent loop
  "worker",
  # tools: concrete toolsets and their shared base (see the toolsets contract)
  "toolsets",
  # platform: infrastructure clients, workspace, sandbox, settings and protocol
  # bindings, plus the workspace observations that tools report (the Worker
  # keeps only their reducer)
  "a2a_server : adapters : agent_skills : artifacts : finding_proposals : llm : observations : projectfs : sandbox : settings : telemetry : work_root_lock : workspace",
  # kernel: wire contracts and dependency-free helpers (core: target policy,
  # subprocess pipes, line splitting, tool metrics and input errors, and the
  # Worker completion protocol)
  "_https : backoff : contracts : core : digests : http_body : log : mtls : probe : redaction : strict_json : threads",
]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "error"
broken_contract_guidance = """
A lower layer imports a higher one, or a module is not classified.
- Invert the dependency: pass the higher-level object in (Protocol, callback or
  factory argument) instead of importing it.
- Move the shared type or helper down into the lower layer (for example into
  contracts or a kernel module).
- If the dependency is genuinely intended, move the module to another layer in
  runtime/pyproject.toml, or add an ignore_imports entry with a
  "reason; fix" comment.
An unlisted module must be added to one layer. "No matches for ignored import"
means a known violation is gone: delete that ignore_imports entry.
"""

# The layers above let the Worker import toolsets; it may use only
# toolsets.common. The composition root (factories) registers the concrete
# toolsets, and the Worker learns what it needs about them through its
# WorkerBuildContext (for example the sensitive-output tools that the
# registered toolset factories declare). Add a new toolset here too.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "worker-no-concrete-toolsets"
name = "The Worker imports no concrete toolset, only toolsets.common"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["contractor_runtime.worker"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.audit_results",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.caido",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.code_analysis",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.code_execution",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.edit_files",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.filesystem",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.http",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.likec4",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.memory",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.openapi",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.run_artifacts",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.scan",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.security_findings",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.source_analysis",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.taint_annotations",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.text_artifacts",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.workspace_changes",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
The Worker imports a concrete toolset. Declare what the Worker needs on the
toolset factory (see ToolsetFactory in factories.py), let the composition root
derive it from the registered factories and pass it in through
WorkerBuildContext, or move shared code into toolsets.common.
"""

# Toolsets are independent of each other and share code through
# toolsets.common, except for two declared chains in which one toolset builds
# on another:
#   taint_annotations -> code_analysis
#     (tree-sitter language support and the pinned-dependency check)
#   edit_files, workspace_changes -> filesystem
#     (the filesystem tool error type)
# The layers contract below puts the two chain bases in a layer under the other
# toolsets, so no base imports a toolset. The two protected contracts after it
# then admit, per base, only its declared consumers and the composition root
# that registers every toolset. Any other import of a base, from a toolset or
# from anywhere else in the Runtime, breaks a contract. A new toolset joins the
# top layer; it becomes a chain base only together with its own protected
# contract.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "toolsets"
name = "Toolsets are independent apart from declared chains and share code through toolsets.common"
type = "layers"
containers = ["contractor_runtime.toolsets"]
exhaustive = true
layers = [
  # concrete toolsets: independent of each other ("|")
  "audit_results | caido | code_execution | edit_files | http | likec4 | memory | openapi | run_artifacts | scan | security_findings | source_analysis | taint_annotations | text_artifacts | workspace_changes",
  # chain bases: independent of each other; each one is imported only by the
  # consumers its protected contract below declares
  "code_analysis | filesystem",
  # shared tool base
  "common",
]
unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = "error"
broken_contract_guidance = """
A toolset imports another toolset outside a declared chain, a chain base or
toolsets.common imports a toolset above it, or a toolset package is not
classified.
- Move the shared code into toolsets.common (or below toolsets).
- Add a new toolset to the concrete-toolsets layer in runtime/pyproject.toml.
- If one toolset genuinely builds on another, declare the chain: move the base
  to the chain-bases layer and give it a protected contract that names its
  consumers.
"""

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "toolsets-chain-code-analysis"
name = "Declared chain: only taint_annotations builds on code_analysis"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["contractor_runtime.toolsets.code_analysis"]
allowed_importers = [
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.taint_annotations",
  # composition root: registers every toolset
  "contractor_runtime.factories",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
Only taint_annotations (and the factory registry) may import code_analysis.
Move code that another toolset needs into toolsets.common, or extend the
declared chain here and in the comment above the toolsets contract.
"""

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "toolsets-chain-filesystem"
name = "Declared chain: only edit_files and workspace_changes build on filesystem"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["contractor_runtime.toolsets.filesystem"]
allowed_importers = [
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.edit_files",
  "contractor_runtime.toolsets.workspace_changes",
  # composition root: registers every toolset
  "contractor_runtime.factories",
]
broken_contract_guidance = """
Only edit_files and workspace_changes (and the factory registry) may import
filesystem. Move code that another toolset needs into toolsets.common, or
extend the declared chain here and in the comment above the toolsets contract.
"""

[project]

description = "Nomad Backup: An rsync-based backup tool for nomadic setups where sources and destinations aren't always available — laptops on the move, removable drives, home servers behind changing networks. Sentinel files ensure backups only run when volumes are genuinely present, with optional btrfs or hard-link snapshots for point-in-time recovery."
readme = "README.md"
# Floor is Ubuntu 24.04 LTS's python3; upper bound keeps installs off an untested
# Python. See common/guidelines/coding/python.md "Python Version Policy".
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
authors = [{ name = "Sami Dalouche", email = "sami.dalouche@gmail.com" }]
dependencies = [
  "fabric>=3.0,<4.0",
  "jinja2>=3.0,<4.0",
  "pydantic>=2.13.4,<3.0.0",
  "pyyaml>=6.0,<7.0",
  "typer>=0.27.0,<1.0.0",
  "platformdirs>=4.11.0,<5.0",
  "mermaid-ascii-diagrams>=0.1.1",
]
dynamic = ["version"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
docker = ["docker>=7.2.0,<8.0"]
keyring = ["keyring>=25.0,<26.0"]

[project.scripts]
nbkp = "nbkp.cli:main"
nbkp-demo = "nbkp.demo:main"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "ruff>=0.16,<0.17",
  "pyright>=1.1,<2.0",
  "pytest>=9.1.1,<10.0",
  "pytest-xdist>=3.5.0,<4.0",
  "testcontainers>=4.15.0,<5.0",
  "vermin>=1.8.0,<2.0",
  # The `python = ">=3.12,<4.0"` marker this carried under poetry is subsumed by
  # [project] requires-python, so it is dropped rather than translated.
  "pydeps>=3.0.7",
  # Also declared as the `keyring` extra above. The extra is the shipped contract
  # (`uv tool install 'nbkp[keyring]'`); this entry guarantees the test suite has it
  # regardless of which extras are synced. Identical constraints, so uv resolves both to
  # one entry in uv.lock.
  "keyring>=25.0,<26.0",
  "import-linter>=2.15,<3.0",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "uv-dynamic-versioning"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "uv-dynamic-versioning"

[tool.uv-dynamic-versioning]
# Required, not optional: Renovate runs `uv lock --upgrade-package`, which triggers a
# build with no git context, and without a fallback every such PR fails outright.
#
# The cost is that "no git history" becomes a *successful* build producing 0.0.0 rather
# than an error — nothing else in the publish path would catch that, and a version number
# cannot be reused once PyPI has it. `mise run build-verify` is what closes the gap.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"

# Explicit rather than relying on hatchling's <NAME>/__init__.py heuristic: when the
# heuristic misses, the failure mode is a silently empty wheel rather than an error.
# This also carries the non-Python payload that ships inside the package — the jinja2
# templates under nbkp/sh/templates/ and the Dockerfiles and shell scripts under
# nbkp/remote/testkit/dockerbuild/, which are read at runtime via importlib.resources and
# Path(__file__).parent respectively, so they must be real files in the installed tree.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["nbkp"]

# Hatchling's sdist default is "every file not ignored by the VCS", which would ship
# tests/, docs/, demo/, marketing/, build-scripts/, .github/ and the lockfiles. Poetry
# shipped the package plus README/LICENSE/pyproject.toml; this keeps that shape.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
only-include = ["nbkp"]

[tool.hatch.build]
# .gitignore is the only ignore file hatchling reads — not .git/info/exclude, not
# core.excludesfile. .gitignore now covers .DS_Store, so this is a guard that keeps the
# published artifact independent of ignore-file hygiene rather than the primary fix.
exclude = [".DS_Store"]

[tool.uv]
# Replaces the default [{ file = "pyproject.toml" }] rather than extending it, hence the
# explicit file entry. The git entry is what keeps `nbkp --version` honest: nbkp reads its
# version through importlib.metadata, which an editable install freezes into .dist-info at
# install time, so without this a new commit or tag leaves a stale version in place.
cache-keys = [{ file = "pyproject.toml" }, { git = { commit = true, tags = true } }]

# uv.lock does not cover PEP 517 build dependencies — `uv build` resolves them fresh from
# PyPI on a cold cache — so these constraints are the only pin on the build backend, and
# on dunamai in particular, which is what computes the version. Regenerate with:
#   printf '%s\n' hatchling uv-dynamic-versioning \
#     | uv pip compile - --no-annotate --no-header --quiet
# [build-system].requires is left unpinned so the two can never contradict each other.
build-constraint-dependencies = [
  "dunamai==1.26.2",
  "hatchling==1.32.0",
  "jinja2==3.1.6",
  "markupsafe==3.0.3",
  "packaging==26.3",
  "pathspec==1.1.1",
  "pluggy==1.6.0",
  "tomlkit==0.15.1",
  "trove-classifiers==2026.6.1.19",
  "uv-dynamic-versioning==0.14.0",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# Keep aliased re-imports in the same `from x import (a, b as c)` block instead of
# emitting a duplicate import statement per alias.
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = [
  "e2e_docker: End-to-end tests requiring Docker",
  "integration_docker: Component integration tests requiring Docker",
  "integration_fs: Component integration tests using local filesystem",
]

[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
# uv creates the project venv at .venv; restating it here is what lets editors and

# Module layering rules, enforced by `mise run boundaries-check` (part of `check`).

  "nbkp.config",
  "nbkp.credentials",
  "nbkp.disks",
  "nbkp.fsprotocol",
  "nbkp.ordering",
  "nbkp.policy",
  "nbkp.preflight",
  "nbkp.remote",
  "nbkp.run",
  "nbkp.sh",
  "nbkp.snapshots",
  "nbkp.sync",

  "typer",
  "nbkp.clidisplay",
  "nbkp.cliwiring",
  "nbkp.cli",
  "nbkp.*.cli",
]

  # Each module's cli/ sub-app and output (rendering) code sit above the core.
  "nbkp.*.cli.** -> **",
  "nbkp.*.cli -> **",
  "nbkp.**.output.** -> **",
  "nbkp.**.output -> **",
  # Test and demo fixtures, not runtime code.

  "nbkp.**.testkit -> **",

  "nbkp.preflight.cli",
  "nbkp.run.cli",

name = "Command wiring sits below the CLI sub-apps"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["nbkp.cliwiring"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The config schema is the base layer"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["nbkp.config"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "nbkp.credentials",
  "nbkp.demo",
  "nbkp.disks",
  "nbkp.ordering",
  "nbkp.preflight",
  "nbkp.remote",
  "nbkp.run",
  "nbkp.sh",
  "nbkp.snapshots",
  "nbkp.sync",

  "nbkp.config.testkit -> **",

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "clidisplay is a presentation leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["nbkp.clidisplay"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "nbkp.cli",
  "nbkp.cliwiring",
  "nbkp.config",
  "nbkp.credentials",
  "nbkp.demo",
  "nbkp.disks",
  "nbkp.ordering",
  "nbkp.preflight",
  "nbkp.remote",
  "nbkp.run",
  "nbkp.sh",
  "nbkp.snapshots",
  "nbkp.sync",
]

    apps.core

[importlinter:contract:core_must_not_depend_on_devtools]

    apps.core
forbidden_modules =
    apps.dev_tools

[importlinter:contract:config_must_not_depend_on_non_runtime_apps]
name = Config must not depend on dev tools
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    config
forbidden_modules =
    apps.dev_tools

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "B", "UP", "RUF"]
# RUF001/2/3: this repo's zh-TW comments always carry full-width punctuation — legitimate.
ignore = ["E501", "RUF001", "RUF002", "RUF003"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
ignore_missing_imports = true
# Gradual-adoption profile, NOT strict: this is a large pre-existing codebase (51 files under
# app/ alone) with no prior type-annotation discipline — `strict = true` would surface hundreds
# of findings unrelated to any single change and make the baseline meaningless busywork rather
# than a real signal. `disallow_untyped_defs` stays off so untyped legacy functions are not
# forced to gain annotations just to satisfy this gate; the gate still catches real type errors
# in code that already IS annotated (which is what all 15 baselined errors below actually are).
disallow_untyped_defs = false
warn_unused_configs = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# EXPLICIT scope — do NOT rely on pytest's default recursive discovery from the repo root. This
# repo has several gitignored scratch/working dirs at the root (download/, save/, data/, venv/)
# — pytest's built-in norecursedirs already skips venv/, but NOT download/save/data, so a stray
# test_*.py dropped there would otherwise be silently collected and could fail the gate on a
# file nobody meant to ship. `testpaths` pins collection to tests/ only, regardless of what else
# exists at the root (found & closed during this gate install, 2026-08-27; proof of both exit
# codes in .claude/CLAUDE.md -> `## Code quality gates`).
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["app"]

# G4 (import-linter) — layering contract derived from this package's ACTUAL current import graph
# (verified 2026-08-27 via `grep -rhoE "^\s*(from|import)\s+app\.[a-zA-Z_.]+"` per subpackage —
# see quality-gates/check_import_cycles.py's own docstring for the raw edges found). Unlike
# learningMachine's from-scratch clean layering, this repo's app.providers and app.services
# already import EACH OTHER in both directions (providers/*/provider.py calls
# services.path_service / services.token_service for filesystem/auth helpers; services/
# download_service.py calls providers.*.provider to actually invoke a download). That is a real,
# working dependency shape, not a bug to silently "fix" by picking layer order — so the 4
# providers->services edges below are pre-existing and BASELINED (import-cycle-baseline.json),
# not cleaned up. This gate only blocks a NEW cross-layer edge beyond what's already there.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "app"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "app.api",
    "app.services",
    "app.providers",
    "app.domain",
    "app.storage",
    "app.config",
]

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    cyberdyne_backend

# ── Hexagonal layer contract ──────────────────────────────────────────
# domain knows nothing. application knows domain. adapters know
# application and domain. infrastructure wires the rest. main is the
# only thing allowed to import from anywhere.
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Hexagonal layers
type = layers
layers =
    cyberdyne_backend.adapters.inbound
    cyberdyne_backend.adapters.outbound
    cyberdyne_backend.infrastructure
    cyberdyne_backend.application
    cyberdyne_backend.domain
# The Container is the composition root for adapter wiring — it must
# import concrete adapters by definition. Listed explicitly because
# import-linter ignore_imports doesn't support wildcards.

[project]
name = "cyberdyne-backend"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Backend for the Cyberdyne SvelteKit frontend — hexagonal FastAPI service"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
authors = [{ name = "Cyberdyne Corp" }]
license = { text = "BSD-2-Clause" }
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.115.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30.0",
    "pydantic>=2.7.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.6.1",
    "structlog>=24.4.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    # Persistence — Phase 1 forward.
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.30",
    "asyncpg>=0.29.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.30",
    "reportlab>=4.5.1",
    # Attachment text extraction for the AI tutor (issue #220): PDF, DOCX,
    # and XLSX. CSV + plain text use the stdlib.
    "pypdf>=5.0.0",
    "python-docx>=1.1.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.0",
    # Ed25519 certificate signing (keypair — for external verifiers).
    "cryptography>=43.0.0",
    # Local RS256 access-token verification against CyberdyneAuth's JWKS.
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.9.0",
    # YouTube source material for the chat agents: transcripts + playlist
    # listings. Both are pure-python; hand-rolling these over httpx is not
    # viable (YouTube's caption/playlist internals change constantly and
    # these libraries track them).
    "youtube-transcript-api>=1.0.0",
    "yt-dlp>=2025.1.26",
    # Error monitoring. Major-pinned: a 3.x bump renames options, and this is a
    # main (not dev) dependency because the production image installs --no-dev.
    "sentry-sdk[fastapi]>=2,<3",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.2.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0.0",
    "ruff>=0.5.0",
    "mypy>=1.10.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "respx>=0.21.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.20.0",  # in-memory SQLAlchemy backend for unit/integration tests
]

[project.scripts]
cyberdyne-backend = "cyberdyne_backend.main:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/cyberdyne_backend"]

# ── pytest ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Default test run skips integration tests so CI stays offline. Use
# `just test-integration` to opt in.
addopts = "-m 'not integration'"
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests (no I/O, no real HTTP, no DB)",
    "integration: Adapter-level tests that cross a process boundary",
]

# ── coverage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Gate only the hexagonal core (domain + application) at 90% — adapters
# are exercised by integration tests instead, same shape as the rest of
# the Cyberdyne stack. The whole tree is still imported when tests run,
# but coverage only counts the layers we care about gating.
[tool.coverage.run]
source = [
    "src/cyberdyne_backend/domain",
    "src/cyberdyne_backend/application",
]
omit = ["**/__init__.py"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 90
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]

# ── ruff ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = ["alembic/versions"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "I",   # isort
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "N",   # pep8-naming
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "RUF", # ruff-specific
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line length — handled by formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["N802", "N806"]  # allow test function naming flexibility

# ── mypy (strict) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
mypy_path = "src"
packages = ["cyberdyne_backend"]
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
exclude = ["alembic/versions"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false

# reportlab ships no type stubs.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "reportlab.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# openpyxl ships no type stubs.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "openpyxl.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# yt-dlp ships no type stubs.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "yt_dlp.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.commitizen]
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

major_version_zero = true
update_changelog_on_bump = true
changelog_incremental = true
annotated_tag = true

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/delta_engine"]

# -------------------- Ruff  --------------------
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100
extend-exclude = [
  ".venv",
  ".tox",
  "dist",
  "build",
  ".mypy_cache",
  ".ruff_cache",
  "docs",
]
fix = false
unsafe-fixes = false

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
docstring-code-format = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
# E,F: pyflakes/pycodestyle; N: pep8-naming; I: isort; UP: pyupgrade; B: bugbear; RUF: extras; TID: tidy-imports
select = ["E", "W", "F", "N", "I", "UP", "B", "RUF", "TID", "D"]
ignore = [
  "E203", # slice spacing (compatible with ruff-format/black)
  "E266", # allow long inline comments
  "D104", # don't require package docstrings in __init__.py
  "D105", # magic methods implement named protocols (len/iter/bool); the protocol documents them
  "D107", # don't require docstrings on __init__ methods
  "D212", # don't require multi-line docstring summary to start at the first line
  "D203", # no blank line before docstring
]

# isort behavior for import sorting
[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["delta_engine"]
force-sort-within-sections = true
combine-as-imports = true

# Tidy imports
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all" # enforce absolute imports (TID252)

# Test file exceptions (short fixture names etc.)
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = [
  "N802", # allow non-PEP8 function names
  "N803", # allow non-PEP8 argument names
  "N806", # allow non-PEP8 variable names
  "D101", # don't require docstring in public classes
  "D102", # don't require docstrings in public methods
  "D103", # don't require docstrings in public
  "D105", # don't require docstrings in magic methods
  "D100", # don't require module docstrings
  "D205", # don't require 1 blank line between summary line and description
  "N815", # allow variables in class scope to be mixedCase
  "N812", # allow uppercase variable names
]
# Value-object modules: each class is documented and the contract lives on the
# abstract method (Action.subject, Failure.format_lines) or the diff module's
# canonical action/blocker vocabulary. Concrete overrides only restate it, so
# we don't require a docstring on every override.
"src/delta_engine/domain/plan/actions.py" = ["D102"]
"src/delta_engine/application/failures.py" = ["D102"]
"src/delta_engine/domain/plan/diff.py" = ["D102"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
markers = [
  "local_e2e: local Spark/Delta end-to-end tests that run in default CI",
  "databricks_e2e: credentialed Databricks/Unity Catalog end-to-end tests",
]
# Credentialed live tests (tests/live) are opt-in: the default marker filter
# keeps every ordinary and CI run off the real warehouse. Run them explicitly
# with: uv run pytest tests/live -m databricks_e2e --no-cov
addopts = """
-m "not databricks_e2e"
--cov
--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered
--cov-report=xml:reports/coverage.xml
"""

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 70
show_missing = true

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["delta_engine"]


# -------------------- Import Linter --------------------

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "delta_engine"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "hexagonal-layers"
name = "Hexagonal package layers"
type = "layers"
containers = ["delta_engine"]
layers = ["cli", "databricks | schema | adapters | api | lint | generate", "application", "domain"]
exhaustive = true
ignore_imports = [
  # Public Databricks facade; implementation remains in adapters.
  "delta_engine.databricks -> delta_engine.adapters.databricks.spark.factory",
  "delta_engine.databricks -> delta_engine.adapters.databricks.spark.schema",
  "delta_engine.databricks -> delta_engine.adapters.databricks.warehouse.factory",
  "delta_engine.databricks -> delta_engine.adapters.databricks.log_config",
  # Public schema facade: DeltaTable/ForeignKey/Self live in api.delta_table
  # (same layer, so the facade edge is exempted). TableProperty is imported
  # downward from domain.model, which the layer order already permits.
  "delta_engine.schema -> delta_engine.api.delta_table",
  # Module generation renders declaration source and proves it round-trips by
  # constructing the DeltaTable it prints (same layer, so the edge is exempted).
  "delta_engine.generate.declaration -> delta_engine.api.delta_table",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "backend-imports-stay-in-adapters"
name = "Backend imports stay in adapters"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "delta_engine.schema",
  "delta_engine.api",
  "delta_engine.application",
  "delta_engine.domain",
  "delta_engine.lint",
  "delta_engine.generate",
]
forbidden_modules = ["delta", "pyspark"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "cli-stays-pyspark-free"
name = "CLI stays PySpark-free"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["delta_engine.cli"]
forbidden_modules = ["delta", "pyspark"]
ignore_imports = [
  # The facade lazily reaches the Spark backend at runtime; the CLI itself
  # must not. Also ignore the facade's TYPE_CHECKING-only PySpark imports
  # (never execute; they exist only for public type hints, but grimp's static
  # analysis cannot tell that from real imports). Together these exempt only
  # the facade's narrow static edges to Spark, keeping
  # indirect-import checking on for every other path (e.g. a future direct
  # cli -> adapters.databricks.spark import).
  "delta_engine.databricks -> delta_engine.adapters.databricks.spark.factory",
  "delta_engine.databricks -> delta_engine.adapters.databricks.spark.schema",
  "delta_engine.databricks -> pyspark",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "shared-sql-core-is-backend-free"
name = "Shared SQL core stays PySpark-free"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["delta_engine.adapters.databricks.sql"]
forbidden_modules = ["delta", "pyspark", "py4j"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "databricks-backends-above-shared-sql"
name = "Databricks backends sit above the shared SQL core"
type = "layers"
containers = ["delta_engine.adapters.databricks"]
layers = ["spark | warehouse", "sql"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "warehouse-backend-is-pyspark-free"
name = "Warehouse backend stays PySpark-free"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["delta_engine.adapters.databricks.warehouse"]
forbidden_modules = ["delta", "pyspark", "py4j"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "cli-framework-stays-in-cli"
name = "CLI framework imports stay in the CLI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "delta_engine.schema",
  "delta_engine.api",
  "delta_engine.application",
  "delta_engine.domain",
  "delta_engine.adapters",
  "delta_engine.databricks",
]
forbidden_modules = ["typer", "click", "rich"]


# -------------------- MyPy --------------------

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
disallow_untyped_defs = true
strict_equality = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["tests.*"]
ignore_errors = true

# CI type-checks in the dev environment, where the docs group (and therefore

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]

# `assert` and hardcoded test credentials are the expected idiom in tests.

"tests/*" = ["S101", "S105", "S106", "TC001", "TC002", "TC003"]

# imports used only in route signatures (e.g. datetime.date) must stay importable.

"src/dispensa/cli.py" = ["TC003"]

# ── import-linter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CLAUDE.md rule 22 / PLAN.md D9: api/scripts → app → storage|ai|instagram|images
# → domain. `include_external_packages` is what lets the domain-is-pure contract
# see third-party SDK imports, not just first-party ones.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["dispensa"]
include_external_packages = true

# Golden rule 5: the domain layer is pure. It imports no sibling layer and no
# I/O or SDK library. pydantic is deliberately absent — domain models are Pydantic.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "domain-is-pure"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["dispensa.domain"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "dispensa.storage",
    "dispensa.ai",
    "dispensa.instagram",
    "dispensa.images",
    "dispensa.app",
    "dispensa.api",
    "dispensa.api_auth",
    "dispensa.api_models",
    "dispensa.routers",
    "dispensa.mcp_server",
    "dispensa.asgi",
    "dispensa.deps",
    "dispensa.settings",
    "instagrapi",
    "openai",
    "cloudinary",
    "sqlmodel",
    "sqlalchemy",
    "fastapi",
    "pydantic_ai",
]

# Adapters are independent siblings: each wraps one external system and none may
# reach into another. Cross-adapter orchestration belongs in app/.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "adapters-are-independent"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "dispensa.storage",
    "dispensa.ai",
    "dispensa.images",
    "dispensa.instagram",
]

# asgi.py is the composition root: the one module allowed to import both entry
# siblings (api and mcp_server) to mount them together. Below it, api sits above
# routers (api.py wires the routers in), routers above app, and the adapters form
# one flat sibling layer above the pure domain. mcp_server is an entry point
# beside api: it reaches down through app but is imported only by asgi, so it
# shares that sibling layer with api.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "dispensa.asgi | dispensa.cli",
    "dispensa.api | dispensa.mcp_server",
    "dispensa.routers",
    "dispensa.app",
    "dispensa.storage | dispensa.ai | dispensa.images | dispensa.instagram",
    "dispensa.domain",
]

# import-linter contract — intra-core dependency-layering oracle (OMN-14216)
#
# Encodes the DIRECTION of imports between omnibase_core's architectural
# sub-packages, per ADR-001, ADR-005, and https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/architecture/onex-dependency-inversion.md.
# This is the enforcement oracle every later decoupling change verifies against:
# a new illegal back-edge fails `lint-imports`; the current known back-edges are
# frozen below as an explicit, annotated allowlist to be burned down under the
# Platform Tech Debt Reduction epic (OMN-3210).
#
# Doctrine layering (high -> low):
#   nodes                            (top: coordination shells)
#   services | validation            (behavioral layers)
#   models                           (domain models)
#   constants | enums | errors | types   (foundation primitives)
#
# WHY `forbidden` (direct) contracts and not a transitive `layers` contract:
# core's import graph is densely interconnected through hub modules (utils,
# mixins, protocols) that bridge nearly every sub-package, so a transitive
# `layers` contract cannot be expressed today without an unmaintainable bridge
# allowlist. These contracts therefore enforce DIRECT imports
# (allow_indirect_imports = True). Tightening to a transitive contract is a
# follow-up gated on slimming those hub modules.
#
# `protocols` is the seam layer (protocol source of truth; spi depends on core).
# It sits low — everything depends on protocol interfaces — so it must not import
# the domain/behavioral layers. It forms a real cycle with `models`
# (protocols -> models AND models -> protocols): the protocols -> models
# direction (protocol I/O type references) is frozen debt below and burned down
# under OMN-3210; the models -> protocols direction (domain referencing
# interfaces) is left permitted.
#
# Each ignore_imports line is a frozen current back-edge (fix later, OMN-3210).
# unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting defaults to ERROR, so when a back-edge class
# is fully removed its now-unmatched ignore line forces its own deletion (ratchet).

[importlinter]
root_packages =
    omnibase_core
# Required so the `core-no-kafka-transport` forbidden contract (invariant I2,
# OMN-14719) can name external packages (aiokafka / confluent_kafka / omnibase_infra):
# import-linter mandates this at the top level when any contract forbids external
# modules. It adds external packages that core actually imports as leaf nodes; it does
# not affect the intra-core forbidden/ratchet contracts (they name only omnibase_core.*).
include_external_packages = True

[importlinter:contract:core-foundation-no-upward]
name = Foundation primitives must not import higher layers (direct)
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    omnibase_core.constants
    omnibase_core.enums
    omnibase_core.errors
    omnibase_core.types
forbidden_modules =
    omnibase_core.models
    omnibase_core.services
    omnibase_core.validation
    omnibase_core.nodes
    omnibase_core.utils
ignore_imports =
    # OMN-3210 burn-down: types -> models — RETIRED (OMN-14337 + OMN-14339).
    # OMN-14337 retired 20 of 24 edges (ModelSemVer references repointed to the
    # structural ProtocolSemVer in types.type_semver; immovable domain-model
    # annotations widened; the dead ModelBase lazy re-export removed from types/).
    # OMN-14339 retired the final 4: the dead SchemaDict/StepOutputs alias module
    # (type_schema_aliases) was deleted (zero real importers); validator_info's
    # func return was widened to object with a consumer-side cast in
    # ServiceValidationSuite; the two model-constructor-kwargs shapes
    # (output_format_options_kwargs, lifecycle_event_fields) were widened to
    # covariant Mapping[str, object] / ProtocolSemVer and their sole consumers
    # switched from **-unpack to model_validate(dict(...)).
    # OMN-3210 burn-down: errors -> models — RETIRED (OMN-14335): ModelOnexError,
    # ModelFailFastDetails, and _ModelOnexErrorData were relocated DOWN into the
    # errors package (models.* paths keep re-export shims); the ModelOnexWarning/
    # ModelRegistryError/ModelCLIAdapter convenience re-exports were pruned from
    # errors/__init__.py.
    # OMN-3210 burn-down: constants -> models — RETIRED (OMN-14221):
    # constants_handler_capabilities no longer imports ModelOnexError; the
    # get_capabilities_by_node_kind boundary now raises the built-in ValueError.

[importlinter:contract:core-models-no-upward]
name = Models must not import behavioral/orchestration layers (direct)
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    omnibase_core.models
forbidden_modules =
    omnibase_core.services
    omnibase_core.validation
    omnibase_core.nodes
    omnibase_core.logging
ignore_imports =
    # OMN-3210 burn-down: models -> validation — RETIRED (OMN-14331): all 18
    # edges severed. Pure name/hex/topic-suffix validators relocated to
    # utils/ (util_name_validation, util_hex_color, util_topic_suffix), workflow
    # constants to constants/constants_workflow, the runtime-ops verb loader to
    # utils/util_runtime_ops_verb_loader; migration TypedDicts and re-exported
    # models now import their canonical types/ and models/validation/ sources.

[importlinter:contract:core-midtier-no-top]
name = Services and validation must not import nodes (direct)
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    omnibase_core.services
    omnibase_core.validation
forbidden_modules =
    omnibase_core.nodes

[importlinter:contract:core-protocols-no-upward]
name = Protocols (seam) must not import domain/behavioral layers (direct)
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    omnibase_core.protocols
forbidden_modules =
    omnibase_core.models
    omnibase_core.services
    omnibase_core.validation
    omnibase_core.nodes
ignore_imports =
    # OMN-3210 burn-down: protocols -> models (protocol I/O type references, 65 edges).
    # NOT a permanent exception (operator ruling 2026-07-10). This wildcard ignore is
    # permissive, so a monotonic-non-increasing RATCHET freezes the edge set at 65 and
    # hard-fails any NEW protocols -> models edge: scripts/ci/check_import_ratchet.py
    # (baseline scripts/ci/import_ratchet_baseline.yaml; wired as CI gate + pre-commit,
    # OMN-14340). Owner: RSD canonical rewrite epic. Retirement mechanism: the rewrite
    # regenerates these modules canonically (dissolving the protocols<->models cycle),
    # after which this line + the ratchet are deleted. The set only SHRINKS.
    omnibase_core.protocols.** -> omnibase_core.models.**

[importlinter:contract:core-execution-tier-no-nodes]
name = Execution-tier packages must not import nodes (direct)
# OMN-14961 (OMN-3210 family, closure-boundary lock completing the OMN-14216
# oracle's source coverage for the execution tier). `runtime`, `pipeline`, `cli`,
# and `validators` were absent from every .importlinter source set despite
# carrying real cross-subpackage traffic (runtime -> models 50 edges,
# validators -> models 26, all downward-legal per the 2026-07-22 readback).
# Their layer position existed only by convention; this block formalizes it.
#
# Honest framing: this contract changes no live edges for the four modules
# below — it is a closure-boundary LOCK, not a closure shrink, matching the
# ticket's precondition finding (live grimp re-verification, 2026-07-23).
#
# `infrastructure` is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from source_modules. The live
# grimp readback found 4 real direct edges, all in one file:
# src/omnibase_core/infrastructure/infra_bases.py imports ModelServiceCompute/
# ModelServiceEffect/ModelServiceOrchestrator/ModelServiceReducer from
# omnibase_core.nodes.node_service_{compute,effect,orchestrator,reducer}. That
# file has zero production consumers anywhere in the OmniNode org (verified by
# exhaustive grep across every canonical repo) but IS referenced as a
# documented "Service Wrappers" pattern from 6 architecture/tutorial docs
# (the omnibase_core overview, node class hierarchy, ecosystem directory
# structure, node-building tutorials, and service-wrappers reference, all in the
# OmniNode knowledge base). Severing the 4 edges means either
# relocating infra_bases.py into nodes/ or retiring the documented pattern —
# an architecture call out of scope for a lint-contract ticket, not a
# mechanical import removal. Per this ticket's own precondition contingency
# ("otherwise drop that source module from the contract and record why"),
# `infrastructure` is dropped from source_modules here; fast-follow tracked
# under OMN-14961's follow-up ticket. Never add an ignore line instead.
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    omnibase_core.runtime
    omnibase_core.pipeline
    omnibase_core.cli
    omnibase_core.validators
forbidden_modules =
    omnibase_core.nodes

[importlinter:contract:core-no-kafka-transport]
name = Core must not import Kafka transport (aiokafka/confluent_kafka/omnibase_infra) — invariant I2
# Invariant I2 of the single-runtime / transport-via-DI unification (epic OMN-14717,
# ticket OMN-14719, plan 2026-07-17-single-runtime-transport-di-unification-plan.md).
#
# The target architecture puts the ONE runtime in omnibase_core and the concrete
# Kafka transport in omnibase_infra, injected inward via the ProtocolTransport*
# abstractions. Dependency inversion therefore REQUIRES that core never import Kafka
# (aiokafka / confluent_kafka) nor reach "up" into omnibase_infra — that is what keeps
# the compat <- core <- spi <- infra layering true. This contract is the mechanical
# guard for that invariant.
#
# It is currently VACUOUS (grimp confirms core imports neither aiokafka,
# confluent_kafka, nor omnibase_infra statically) — that is expected: it is the fence
# that keeps the target true as the runtime moves into core, not a fix for a present
# violation.
#
# `include_external_packages` is required so grimp records imports of the external
# aiokafka / confluent_kafka / omnibase_infra packages. grimp attributes an external
# import to its TOP-LEVEL package, so `omnibase_infra` (not the .event_bus.event_bus_kafka
# submodule the plan names) is the checkable granularity — and forbidding all of
# omnibase_infra is the stronger, layering-correct fence.
#
# Plan-declared deferred exception (I2): src/omnibase_core/cli/cli_run_node.py loads
# confluent_kafka via importlib.import_module("confluent_kafka") (a DYNAMIC import).
# grimp's static graph does not see dynamic importlib calls, so this contract stays
# green without an ignore entry; cli_run_node.py is re-expressed over
# ProtocolTransportProducer in a follow-up (plan step S11).
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    omnibase_core
forbidden_modules =
    aiokafka
    confluent_kafka
    omnibase_infra

[importlinter:contract:core-no-legacy-onex-error-path]
name = Import ModelOnexError from canonical errors/, not the legacy models.errors shims (direct)
# OMN-14965 (OMN-3210 family). OMN-14335 relocated ModelOnexError / ModelFailFastDetails
# DOWN into the foundation-layer `errors` package, leaving `models/errors/*` as re-export
# shims. 119 files across 23 subpackages (plus the root module `topics`) still imported
# through the legacy `models.errors` path, dragging `models` into their static import
# closure for an error type whose canonical home is the foundation layer. This contract
# is the fence that keeps the repoint true.
#
# Justified on layering architecture ONLY (standing rule: never CI cost).
#
# MEASURED OUTCOME, recorded honestly (grimp, .200 runtime, 2026-07-29): this repoint
# severs 119 DIRECT edges (utils->models 79->62, mixins->models 151->131,
# all->models.errors 462->343, exactly as OMN-14965 predicted) but shrinks the
# TRANSITIVE reverse closure of `models` by ZERO modules: 551 -> 551 counting
# TYPE_CHECKING edges, 496 -> 496 with exclude_type_checking_imports=True.
# Root cause: the canonical target `errors.model_onex_error` is ITSELF downstream of
# `models` (errors.model_onex_error -> types.type_core -> protocols -> ... -> models),
# so a repointed file keeps `models` in its closure through the protocols<->models
# cycle. That cycle is RSD-canonical-rewrite-owned and must not be hand-burned, so it
# -- not this family -- is the binding constraint on the OMN-14921 file-grain selector.
# This contract is therefore a layering fence, NOT a selector win; do not re-derive a
# selector rationale from it.
#
# ZERO ignore lines by construction: the repoint severed every in-scope edge in the
# same PR, so there is no allowlist to burn down later.
#
# Sources DELIBERATELY EXCLUDE:
#   - constants / enums / errors / types — already fenced from models by
#     `core-foundation-no-upward`.
#   - protocols — RSD-canonical-rewrite-owned (65-edge wildcard ignore + frozen
#     ratchet); must not be touched here.
#   - models — owns the shims; its ~343 intra-package legacy-path imports are
#     deliberately out of scope (intra-package edges, zero cross-subpackage closure gain).
#   - the root package `omnibase_core` itself — src/omnibase_core/__init__.py was
#     repointed by this PR (2 function-local imports), but `omnibase_core` cannot be
#     named as a source module without also covering `models`, which would fail
#     immediately on the out-of-scope intra-models imports. Residual, recorded here:
#     the root __init__ is repointed but unfenced.
#   - top-level subpackages with zero legacy-path imports today (adapters, agents,
#     artifacts, context, contract_graph, discovery, doctor, factories, feature_flags,
#     integrations, logging, navigation, normalization, overlays, schemas, tools,
#     workflows). They are clean but therefore also unfenced — a currently-clean
#     subpackage can still add a legacy-path import without tripping this contract.
#     Honest residual; widening the source list is a free follow-up (no ignore lines
#     would be needed), deliberately not bundled into this bounded single-pattern PR.
type = forbidden
allow_indirect_imports = True
source_modules =
    omnibase_core.analysis
    omnibase_core.backends
    omnibase_core.cli
    omnibase_core.container
    omnibase_core.contracts
    omnibase_core.crypto
    omnibase_core.decorators
    omnibase_core.dispatch
    omnibase_core.event_bus
    omnibase_core.gate
    omnibase_core.infrastructure
    omnibase_core.merge
    omnibase_core.mixins
    omnibase_core.nodes
    omnibase_core.package
    omnibase_core.pipeline
    omnibase_core.rendering
    omnibase_core.resolution
    omnibase_core.runtime
    omnibase_core.services
    omnibase_core.topics
    omnibase_core.utils
    omnibase_core.validation
    omnibase_core.validators
forbidden_modules =
    omnibase_core.models.errors

[tool.mypy]
# Strict mode enables: warn_return_any, warn_unused_configs, disallow_untyped_defs,
# disallow_incomplete_defs, check_untyped_defs, disallow_untyped_decorators,
# no_implicit_optional, warn_redundant_casts, warn_unused_ignores, strict_equality, and more
strict = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
python_version = "3.12"
mypy_path = "src"
namespace_packages = true
explicit_package_bases = true

# Third-party libraries without type stubs
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "jsonpath_ng.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "sqlglot.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pydantic-mypy]
init_forbid_extra = true
init_typed = false
warn_required_dynamic_aliases = true
warn_untyped_fields = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src", "."]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests that test individual components in isolation",
    "integration: Integration tests that test multiple components together",
    "slow: Tests that take a long time to run (>1s)",
    "smoke: Quick smoke tests for basic functionality",
    "performance: Performance and benchmark tests",
    "cache: Cache-related tests",
    "nodes: Node architecture tests",
    "validation: Validation framework tests",
    "flaky: Marks tests as flaky and allows reruns (from pytest-rerunfailures)",
    "timeout: Timeout for individual tests using pytest-timeout plugin (e.g., @pytest.mark.timeout(60))"
]
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "-ra",
    "--tb=short",
    "-n4",  # Limit parallel workers to prevent OOM (was: auto)
    "--timeout=60",  # Prevent hanging tests (60s per test)
    # OMN-15977: signal-based timeout, NOT thread-based. pytest-timeout's
    # thread method spawns a watcher thread that fires SIGKILL-equivalent only
    # when the GIL is released -- a CPU-bound pure-Python loop holding the GIL
    # continuously (e.g. a runaway regex/compute path) never yields, so the
    # watcher thread never gets scheduled and the "timeout" never fires. This
    # was the unkillable-CPU config behind two 2026-08-12 runaways (46min,
    # 53min) that a health-tick had to SIGKILL manually. Signal method
    # delivers SIGALRM, which interrupts at the next Python bytecode boundary
    # regardless of GIL contention -- it can actually kill a CPU-bound loop.
    "--timeout-method=signal",

    "--dist=loadgroup",  # Group tests by @pytest.mark.xdist_group for better control
    "--reruns=2",  # Auto-retry failed tests twice (handles flaky tests)
    "--reruns-delay=1",  # 1 second delay between reruns
]
filterwarnings = [
    # === Deprecation Warning Capture (OMN-199, Phase 7) ===
    # Display deprecation warnings during test runs so developers can address them
    # before v0.5.0 when these will become errors
    "default::DeprecationWarning",
    "default::PendingDeprecationWarning",
    # Suppress asyncio "Task was destroyed but it is pending!" warnings
    # These are expected during test cleanup when fixtures cancel pending tasks
    # The cleanup fixtures (event_loop_cleanup, cleanup_service_tasks) properly
    # cancel tasks, so these warnings are cosmetic and don't indicate real issues
    "ignore:.*Task was destroyed but it is pending.*:RuntimeWarning",
    # NOTE: "coroutine was never awaited" warnings are NOT suppressed
    # These indicate real bugs where async functions were called but never executed
    # If you encounter this warning, FIX the test by properly awaiting the coroutine
]
# Memory optimization notes:
# - Limited to 4 workers to prevent OOM on machines with 16GB RAM
# - Use --timeout to prevent hanging tests accumulating memory
# - Use --dist=loadscope to group tests by module (reduces import overhead)
# Test execution strategies:
#   Fast iteration: -n 2 --timeout=30
#   Full suite: -n 4 --timeout=60 (default)
#   CI/Large machines: -n 8 --timeout=120
#   Debug single test: -n 0 (disable xdist)
#
# Intelligent test selection with pytest-testmon:
#   Run only affected tests: uv run pytest --testmon
#   Reset testmon database: uv run pytest --testmon-noselect
#   Disable testmon: uv run pytest --testmon-off
#   Note: .testmondata file is gitignored and stores test dependencies

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/omnibase_core"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/archived/*",
    "*/archive/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/site-packages/*"
]
branch = true
parallel = true

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
fail_under = 60
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "@abc.abstractmethod"
]

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.5",
    # <2.5: numpy 2.5.0 dropped Python 3.11 support and its bundled .pyi
    # stubs adopted PEP 695 syntax (the `type X = ...` statement), which is
    # a hard mypy parse error under python_version=3.11 (verified against
    # openbtk's actual floor -- see [tool.mypy] below, and
    # https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/18701). Revisit this bound when
    # openbtk's own minimum Python version moves to 3.12+.
    "numpy>=1.26,<2.5",
    "structlog>=24.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "httpx>=0.27",

]

text = [

    "medspacy>=1.0",
    "presidio-analyzer>=2.2",
    "presidio-anonymizer>=2.2",
    "transformers>=4.40",
    # openbtk.deid.recognizers.ner: general-purpose PERSON/GPE/LOC/FAC NER.
    # Deliberately spaCy's own small English pipeline, not a scispaCy
    # biomedical model -- see that module's docstring for why (scispaCy's
    # off-the-shelf models target scientific entities, not names/places).
    "spacy>=3.8",
    # openbtk.data.clinical_text.loaders.MIMICNotesLoader: chunked CSV
    # reading (docs/05_DATA_MODALITY_SPEC.md section 1.2). Also listed
    # under `ehr` (its own, larger reason there); duplicated here
    # deliberately since clinical_text must not depend on the ehr extra.
    "pandas>=2.2",
]
ehr = [
    "fhir.resources>=7.1",
    "pyarrow>=16.0",
    "pandas>=2.2",
    "hl7apy>=1.3",
]
retrieval = [
    "faiss-cpu>=1.8",
    "chromadb>=0.5",
    # openbtk.retrieval.qdrant: task 5.6's roadmap entry names FAISS,
    # Chroma AND Qdrant explicitly, but this extra never listed the
    # package the third one needs -- added here, not assumed present.
    "qdrant-client>=1.9",
]
llms = [
    "openai>=1.30",
    "anthropic>=0.30",
    # For HuggingFaceLocalProvider (task 5.2): transformers (the "text"
    # extra) needs a real tensor backend to run text generation, and does
    # not pull one in itself -- torch is deliberately absent from "text"
    # since that extra's own transformers usage (tokenization only, in
    # data.clinical_text.tokenization) never needs it.
    "torch>=2.0",
]

# First candidate for carve-out into its own distribution: its version must be

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fallback-version = "0.0.0"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/openbtk"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ruff
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py311"
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W",    # pycodestyle
    "F",         # pyflakes
    "I",         # isort
    "N",         # pep8-naming
    "UP",        # pyupgrade
    "ANN",       # flake8-annotations
    "B",         # flake8-bugbear
    "SIM",       # flake8-simplify
    "TC",        # flake8-type-checking
    "RUF",       # ruff-specific
    "PTH",       # flake8-use-pathlib
    "RET",       # flake8-return
    "ARG",       # flake8-unused-arguments
    "C4",        # flake8-comprehensions
    "DTZ",       # flake8-datetimez -- naive clinical timestamps are a real bug class
    "T20",       # flake8-print -- no print() in library code
]
ignore = [
    "ANN401",    # Any permitted where documented in docs/04_API_DESIGN.md section 11.4
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["ANN", "ARG"]
"notebooks/**" = ["ANN", "ARG", "T20", "E501"]   # tutorials print and read top-to-bottom
"src/openbtk/cli/**" = ["T20"]     # the CLI prints legitimately
"scripts/**" = ["T20"]             # repo maintenance scripts, not the package; print legitimately

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["openbtk"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mypy
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
warn_unreachable = true
files = ["src/openbtk"]
# Pydantic's official plugin, required for mypy to correctly understand
# default_factory=SomeModel and Field(None, ...)-style optional fields in
# synthesized __init__ signatures. Without it, mypy's generic stub-based
# inference produces false "missing argument" / "incompatible default_factory"
# errors on patterns that are entirely valid Pydantic v2 -- found the hard way
# in core/config.py, whose earlier models (dict/list default_factory only)
# never exercised this gap.
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "scispacy.*", "medspacy.*", "spacy.*",
    "presidio_analyzer.*", "presidio_anonymizer.*",
    "transformers.*", "fhir.*", "hl7apy.*",
    "faiss.*", "chromadb.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import boundaries -- makes the layering in docs/03_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2
# executable rather than aspirational.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "openbtk"
# Required so the forbidden-modules contract can see external packages.
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture -- imports go strictly downward"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "openbtk.cli",
    "openbtk.pipelines",
    "openbtk.data",
    "openbtk.deid",
    "openbtk.core",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Modalities are independent of one another"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "openbtk.data.clinical_text",
    "openbtk.data.ehr",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "LangChain confined to its adapter (ADR-0001)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "openbtk.core",
    "openbtk.data",
    "openbtk.deid",
    "openbtk.pipelines",
    "openbtk.guardrails",
    "openbtk.terminology",
    "openbtk.embeddings",
    "openbtk.llms",
    "openbtk.retrieval",
    "openbtk.eval",
    "openbtk.cli",
]
forbidden_modules = ["langchain", "langchain_core", "langgraph"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pytest
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers --strict-config"
markers = [
    "slow: requires model downloads (skipped unless OPENBTK_SLOW_TESTS=1)",
    "network: requires network access",
    "gpu: requires CUDA",
    "benchmark: performance test, nightly only (skipped unless OPENBTK_RUN_BENCHMARKS=1)",
    "credentialed: needs user-supplied restricted data (i2b2/MIMIC); always skipped in CI",
]
# Later entries win: third-party DeprecationWarnings are ignored, but Openbtk's own
# deprecation warning is an ERROR here, so nothing inside Openbtk (or its tests) may
# call a deprecated Openbtk API -- a deprecation is only ever exercised on purpose,
# under pytest.warns.
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "error::openbtk.core.deprecation.OpenBTKDeprecationWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["openbtk"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
]

    socratron.app

description = "A tool to collaborate with AI agents via a task board"
readme = { file = "README.md", content-type = "text/markdown" }
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.14"
license-files = [
  "LICENSE",
  "third_party_licenses/**",
]
authors = [
  { name = "Ototadana" },
]
keywords = ["agents", "multi-agent", "automation", "workflow"]
classifiers = [
  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Environment :: Console",
  "Topic :: Utilities",
]
dependencies = [
  "click>=8.1.8,<9.0",
  "pydantic>=2.11,<3.0",
  "python-dotenv>=1.0",
  "keyring>=25.0,<26.0",
  "PyYAML>=6.0",
  "httpx>=0.28,<1.0",
  "fastapi>=0.115,<1.0",
  "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30,<1.0",
  "mcp>=2.0,<3.0",
  "cryptography>=50,<51",
  "PyJWT>=2.15",
  "croniter>=3.0",
  "GitPython>=3.1.59",
  "python-i18n>=0.3",
  "langcodes[data]>=3.3",
  "tzdata>=2025.2",
  "tzlocal>=5.3",
  # Engines/brains
  "agno>=2.8,<3.0",
  "requests>=2.32",
  "google-genai>=2.17,<3.0",
  "openai>=1.106,<3.0",
  "anthropic>=0.40,<1.0",
  "jinja2>=3.1.6",
  "markdown-it-py>=4.0.0",
  "weasyprint>=70.0",
  "websockets>=15.0.1",
  "microsandbox==0.6.17",
  "wakepy>=1.0,<2.0",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/GuildBotics/GuildBotics"
Source = "https://github.com/GuildBotics/GuildBotics"
Issues = "https://github.com/GuildBotics/GuildBotics/issues"

[project.scripts]
guildbotics = "guildbotics.cli:main"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
  "black>=24.0",
  "mypy>=1.15",
  "pylint>=3.3",
  "ruff>=0.11",
  "types-requests>=2.32",
  "types-PyYAML>=6.0",
  "import-linter>=2.5",
]
test = [
  "grimp>=3.9",
  # 9.1.0 and 9.1.1 drop a directory's conftest fixtures for files collected
  # after it is revisited on the command line (pytest-dev/pytest#14964). Drop
  # the exclusions once they are no longer the newest releases.
  "pytest>=8.2,!=9.1.0,!=9.1.1",
  "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
  "pytest-cov>=5.0",
  "pytest-timeout>=2.3",
  "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
]
redis = [
  "redis>=5.0",
]


[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = [
  "real_device(opt_in): test using a real device with an explicit opt-in",
  "windows: exercises a host OS boundary that must also work on real Windows",
]
# A test that waits for something that never comes fails instead of stopping
# the suite. Far above what any test takes, even on the slowest CI runner;
# tests on the device's real agent environment say how long they may take.
timeout = 120


[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["guildbotics"]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"

[tool.hatch.build.hooks.vcs]
version-file = "guildbotics/_version.py"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = ["guildbotics/_version.py"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "F",
  "I",
  "B",
  "UP",
  "E",
  "SIM",
  "C4",
  "RUF005",
  "RUF001",
  "RUF002",
  "RUF009",
  "RUF010",
  "RUF012",
  "RUF021",
  "RUF022",
  "RUF059",
  "RUF100",
  "PLC0207",
  "PLR1711",
  "PLR1714",
  "PLR2004",
  "PLR5501",
  "PLW2901",
]
ignore = [
  "E501",
]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
packages = ["guildbotics"]
exclude = [
  "^tests/",
]
warn_unused_configs = true
check_untyped_defs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pylint.main]
py-version = "3.12"

[tool.pylint.messages_control]
disable = ["all"]
enable = ["duplicate-code"]

[tool.pylint.similarities]
ignore-comments = true
ignore-docstrings = true
ignore-imports = true
ignore-signatures = true

# The package map: every package is the host's, the guest's (what runs only
# inside a command's isolated environment), or shared by both. This is the
# source of truth for which side a package is on; a new package is classified
# here, and a package never mixes two sides.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "guildbotics"
include_external_packages = true

# host: the entries (cli, app_api), execution control (drivers), the
# workspace's setup, the isolated environment itself (microVM, credential
# gateway, the window's host side, member broker), member capabilities, the
# provider integrations, and the records, sync, Hub and Secret distribution.
# shared: what the guest runs and the host reads alike -- the command
# machinery, the brains and catalogs, the Context and its ports, the domain
# models and the utilities. Shared code imports neither the host nor the
# guest, and the host starts the guest by module name, never importing it.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "zones"
name = "Every package is the host's, the guest's, or shared; shared imports neither"
type = "layers"
containers = ["guildbotics"]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = ["_version"]
layers = [
  "guest",
  "cli : app_api : drivers : setup : environment : capabilities : integrations : observability : sync : hub : secrets : workspace",
  "commands : intelligences : runtime : loader : entities : utils",
]

# The host's layers, top down: each imports only those below it, and the
# packages on one line (`|`) import none of each other. The Desktop backend
# (app_api) runs the member CLI in its own process for the member brokers of
# the commands it runs, so it sits above cli. The isolated environment
# (environment) holds the member brokers; the member CLI they run is handed
# to them by the entries above (install_member_cli).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "host-layers"
name = "The host imports only downward"
type = "layers"
containers = ["guildbotics"]
layers = [
  "app_api",
  "cli",
  "drivers | setup",
  "environment",
  "capabilities",
  "integrations",
  "sync | secrets",
  "workspace | observability | hub",
]

# Below the layers above, the records and storage, the Hub, and the sync and
# Secret distribution built on them take from the shared packages only the
# utilities: none of them knows the domain model, the Context, a brain, or a
# command.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "host-foundations-build-on-utils"
name = "workspace, observability, hub, sync and secrets import no shared package but utils"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "guildbotics.workspace",
  "guildbotics.observability",
  "guildbotics.hub",
  "guildbotics.sync",
  "guildbotics.secrets",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "guildbotics.commands",
  "guildbotics.intelligences",
  "guildbotics.runtime",
  "guildbotics.loader",
  "guildbotics.entities",
]

# Two stacks share the bottom layer: sync turns shared writes into Git work on
# workspace storage and the records; Secret distribution reaches the Hub, which
# holds repositories and values without knowing what they mean. Neither
# crosses to the other.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "sync-does-not-reach-the-hub"
name = "sync imports workspace and observability, never hub"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["guildbotics.sync"]
forbidden_modules = ["guildbotics.hub"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "secrets-reach-only-the-hub"
name = "secrets imports hub, never workspace or observability"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["guildbotics.secrets"]
forbidden_modules = ["guildbotics.workspace", "guildbotics.observability"]

# The shared packages' layers, top down: the command machinery, the brains and
# catalogs, the Context and its ports, the loaders, the domain models, the
# utilities.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "shared-layers"
name = "The shared packages import only downward"
type = "layers"
containers = ["guildbotics"]
layers = [
  "commands",
  "intelligences",
  "runtime",
  "loader",
  "entities",
  "utils",
]

# Shared writes reach synchronization through the Workspace Sync Port
# (utils/workspace_sync_port.py); importing the sync package would bring back
# the dependency on Git the port removes. Only the composition roots import
# it: the process entries that install the queue or run one repository
# operation -- the Desktop backend, `guildbotics start`, the member CLI, and
# the secret transfers (which read the workspace's Hub and push the
# generations they publish on a device running no service).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "sync-composition-roots"
name = "Only the composition roots import the sync package"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["guildbotics.sync"]
allowed_importers = [
  "guildbotics.app_api.workspace_sync",
  "guildbotics.cli.service",
  "guildbotics.cli.member",
  "guildbotics.cli.secrets",
]

# A provider is chosen in one place: integrations/factory.py picks the one
# project.services names for each kind. Everything else reaches a provider
# through the ports (runtime), the provider-neutral host modules of
# integrations, and the descriptor -- its setup included.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "providers-behind-the-factory"
name = "Only the factory imports a provider's package"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = [
  "guildbotics.integrations.branvil",
  "guildbotics.integrations.github",
  "guildbotics.integrations.local",
  "guildbotics.integrations.slack",
]
allowed_importers = ["guildbotics.integrations.factory"]

# One module drives the microVM SDK: the access contract is enforced by one
# layer, and a second module importing the SDK would translate it its own way.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "one-sandbox-runtime"
name = "Only the environment's runtime drives the microVM SDK"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["microsandbox"]
allowed_importers = ["guildbotics.environment.runtime"]

# guest: the entry the host starts in a command's microVM, the working
# directory's copy, the AI CLI adapters and their turns, the AI CLI brain, and
# the client of the command's window. The microVM holds no credential and no
# host-only code: it asks the host through the window.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "guest-imports-no-host"
name = "The guest imports nothing of the host's"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["guildbotics.guest"]
forbidden_modules = [
  "guildbotics.cli",
  "guildbotics.app_api",
  "guildbotics.drivers",
  "guildbotics.setup",
  "guildbotics.environment",
  "guildbotics.capabilities",
  "guildbotics.integrations",
  "guildbotics.observability",
  "guildbotics.sync",
  "guildbotics.hub",
  "guildbotics.secrets",
  "guildbotics.workspace",
]

# What runs in a command's microVM (the guest and the shared packages) loads
# none of the libraries only the host uses: a server stack, the microVM SDK,
# the OS keychain, the inference SDK, the chat SDK. The keychain is reached
# only from functions a host caller runs; utils never imports one of these at
# module level.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "environment-loads-no-host-only-library"
name = "The guest and the shared packages import no host-only library"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "guildbotics.guest",
  "guildbotics.commands",
  "guildbotics.intelligences",
  "guildbotics.runtime",
  "guildbotics.loader",
  "guildbotics.entities",
  "guildbotics.utils",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "agno",
  "cryptography",
  "fastapi",
  "jwt",
  "keyring",
  "mcp",
  "microsandbox",
  "opentelemetry",
  "slack_sdk",
  "sse_starlette",
  "starlette",
  "uvicorn",
  "watchfiles",
]
ignore_imports = [
  "guildbotics.utils.keychain -> keyring",
  "guildbotics.utils.secret_store -> keyring",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "archinstoo"
version = "0.0.0"
description = "Arch Linux installer - guided, templates etc."
authors = [
    {name = "Anton Hvornum", email = "anton@hvornum.se"},
    {name = "Hadean Eon", email = "hadean-eon-dev@proton.me"},
]
license = "GPL-3.0-only"
requires-python = ">=3.14"  # renovate: arch=python
keywords = ["linux", "arch", "archinstoo", "installer"]
classifiers = [
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
]
dependencies = [
    "pyparted>=3.13.0",  # renovate: arch=python-pyparted
]

[project.urls]
Home = "https://archlinux.org/downloads"
Source = "https://github.com/h8d13/archinstoo"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# floors at the Arch repo versions: renovate moves each with its package,
# pre-commit revs pin the hooks
dev = [
    "mypy>=2.4.0",  # renovate: arch=mypy
    "pre-commit>=4.7.0",  # renovate: arch=pre-commit
    "ruff>=0.17.1",  # renovate: arch=ruff
    "pylint>=4.0.7",  # renovate: arch=python-pylint
    "pytest>=9.1.1",  # renovate: arch=python-pytest
]

[project.scripts]
archinstoo = "archinstoo:run_as_a_module"

[tool.setuptools]
include-package-data = true

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"archinstoo" = [
    "**/*.py",
    "**/*.json",
    "**/*.toml",
    "**/*.kdl",
    "**/*.lua",
    "**/*.xml",
    "**/sway/config",
    "**/labwc/autostart",
]

[tool.setuptools.package-dir]
archinstoo = "archinstoo"

[tool.mypy]
cache_dir = "~/.cache/archinstoo/mypy"
files = "."
mypy_path = "$MYPY_CONFIG_FILE_DIR/stubs"
exclude = "^build/"
disallow_any_explicit = false
disallow_any_expr = false
disallow_any_unimported = true
enable_error_code = [
    "deprecated",
    "exhaustive-match",
    "explicit-override",
    "ignore-without-code",
    "mutable-override",
    "narrowed-type-not-subtype",
    "possibly-undefined",
    "redundant-expr",
    "redundant-self",
    "truthy-bool",
    "truthy-iterable",
    "unimported-reveal",
    "unused-awaitable",
]
show_traceback = true
strict = true
warn_unreachable = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "archinstoo.lib.grimoire"
# tracked in its own repo
ignore_errors = true

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "archinstoo"
include_external_packages = false
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "No circular imports between sibling subpackages"
type = "acyclic_siblings"
ancestors = ["archinstoo", "archinstoo.**"]

[tool.pytest]
cache_dir = "~/.cache/archinstoo/pytest"
addopts = [
    "-s",
    "--strict",
]
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.pylint.main]
ignore-paths = [
    "^build/",
    "^docs/",
    "^node_modules/",
    ".*grimoire.py",
]
persistent = false
recursive = true

[tool.pylint.format]
indent-string = '\t'
max-line-length = 88

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
disable = [
    "C",                       # ruff covers style
    "R",                       # ruff covers refactors
    "broad-exception-caught",  # log-and-continue boundaries
    "fixme",                   # tracked in-code on purpose
    "unspecified-encoding",    # PEP 686: utf-8 is the default from 3.15
]

[tool.pylint.refactoring]
score = false

[tool.pylint.variables]
init-import = true

[tool.pylint.imports]
ignored-modules = ["parted"]

[tool.ruff]
cache-dir = "~/.cache/archinstoo/ruff"
line-length = 88
indent-width = 8
extend-exclude = ["**/lib/grimoire.py"]
# extensionless scripts pre-commit lints by shebang, so a plain `ruff .` agrees
extend-include = ["**/NVGEN"]

[tool.ruff.format]
indent-style = "tab"
quote-style = "single"
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# preview behaviour for the rules already selected below (C419 catching
# sum/min/max, ...), without pulling in unselected preview rules.
# a preview rule needs its exact code in `select`: a prefix like `RUF` will not
# reach it, and listing one in `ignore` alone suppresses nothing until it
# stabilizes. `ruff rule <CODE>` reports whether a rule is still preview.
preview = true
explicit-preview-rules = true

select = [
    "A",      # flake8-builtins
    "ANN",    # flake8-annotations
    "ASYNC",  # flake8-async
    "B",      # flake8-bugbear
    "B909",   # loop-iterator-mutation (preview)
    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "C90",    # mccabe
    "COM",    # flake8-commas
    "DTZ",    # flake8-datetimez
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "EXE",    # flake8-executable
    "F",      # Pyflakes
    "FA",     # flake8-future-annotations
    "FLY",    # flynt
    "FURB",   # refurb
    "FURB142", # for-loop-set-mutations (preview)
    "G",      # flake8-logging-format
    "I",      # isort
    "ICN",    # flake8-import-conventions
    "ISC",    # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "LOG",    # flake8-logging
    "N",      # pep8-naming
    "PERF",   # perflint
    "PGH",    # pygrep-hooks
    "PIE",    # flake8-pie
    "PLC",    # Pylint conventions
    "PLC1901", # compare-to-empty-string (preview)
    "PLE",    # Pylint errors
    "PLR1704", # redefined-argument-from-local
    "PLR1714", # repeated-equality-comparison
    "PLR1730", # if-stmt-min-max
    "PLR5501", # collapsible-else-if
    "PLR6104", # non-augmented-assignment (preview)
    "PLR6201", # literal-membership (preview)
    "PLW",    # Pylint warnings
    "PT",     # flake8-pytest-style
    "PTH",    # flake8-use-pathlib
    "PYI",    # flake8-pyi
    "RET",    # flake8-return
    "RSE",    # flake8-raise
    "RUF",    # Ruff-specific rules
    "RUF039", # unraw-re-pattern (preview)
    "S",      # flake8-bandit
    "SIM",    # flake8-simplify
    "SLOT",   # flake8-slot
    "T10",    # flake8-debugger
    "TC",     # flake8-type-checking
    "TID251", # banned-api (typing.cast)
    "TID252", # relative-imports
    "TRY004", # type-check-without-type-error
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "YTT",    # flake8-2020
]

# grouped by why, not alphabetically: the reason is what decides whether a
# future ruff release makes an entry worth revisiting
ignore = [
    # formatter-incompatible, per ruff's own documented list. these fight
    # `ruff format` under the tab + magic-trailing-comma style set above.
    "COM812",   # missing-trailing-comma
    "W191",     # tab-indentation
    "PLC0415",  # import-outside-top-level: models/ -> hardware, disk breaks
                # cycles; the rest defer optional/slow imports (parted, tui)
    "RUF067",   # non-empty-init-module: init hacks are on purpose.

]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 40

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["archinstoo"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"typing.cast".msg = "avoid cast(); annotate the binding or validate at the boundary (add # noqa: TID251 with a reason if truly needed)"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"**/stubs/**" = ["N"] # names mirror pyparted's own API
"**/NVGEN" = [
    "S603",   # dev tooling runs fixed local commands, not untrusted input
    "S607",   # nvchecker/pacman helpers resolved from $PATH by design
]
"**/scripts/dev/**" = [
    "S603",   # dev tooling runs fixed local commands, not untrusted input
    "S607",   # qemu/bsdtar/stty resolved from $PATH by design
]
"**/tests/**" = [
    "S101",   # pytest uses assert
    "S106",   # test fixtures use placeholder passwords
    "S108",   # /tmp paths are symbolic test values
]
