[tool.setuptools]
zip-safe = false
include-package-data = true
license-files = [
    "LICENSE",
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
namespaces = false

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"*" = [
    "*.pyi",
]
napari_builtins = [
    "builtins.yaml",
]


[tool.setuptools_scm]
write_to = "napari/_version.py"

[tool.check-manifest]
ignore = [
  ".cirrus.yml",
  ".pre-commit-config.yaml",
  "asv.conf.json",
  "codecov.yml",
  "Makefile",
  "napari/_version.py",  # added during build by setuptools_scm
  "tools/minreq.py",
  "tox.ini",
  "napari/_qt/qt_resources/_qt_resources_*.py",
  "*.pyi",  # added by make typestubs
  "binder/*",
  ".env_sample",
  ".devcontainer/*",
  "napari/resources/icons/_themes/*/*.svg"
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 79
exclude = [
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".pants.d",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "buck-out",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    "venv",
    "*vendored*",
    "*_vendor*",
]

fix = true

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "single"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "F", "W", #flake8
    "UP", # pyupgrade
    "I", # isort
    "YTT", #flake8-2020
    "TCH", # flake8-type-checing
    "BLE", # flake8-blind-exception
    "B", # flake8-bugbear
    "A", # flake8-builtins
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "ISC", # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "G", # flake8-logging-format
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "COM", # flake8-commas
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "INP", # flake8-no-pep420
    "PYI", # flake8-pyi
    "Q", # flake8-quotes
    "RSE", # flake8-raise
    "RET", # flake8-return
    "TID",  # flake8-tidy-imports # replace absolutify import
    "TRY", # tryceratops
    "ICN", # flake8-import-conventions
    "RUF", # ruff specyfic rules
    "NPY201", # checks compatibility with numpy version 2.0
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async
    "EXE", # flake8-executable
    "FA", # flake8-future-annotations
    "LOG", # flake8-logging
    "SLOT", # flake8-slots
    "PT", # flake8-pytest-style
    "T20", # flake8-print
]
ignore = [
    "E501", "TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003",
    "A003", # flake8-builtins - we have class attributes violating these rule
    "COM812", # flake8-commas - we don't like adding comma on single line of arguments
    "COM819", # conflicts with ruff-format
    "SIM117", # flake8-simplify - we some of merged with statements are not looking great with black, reanble after drop python 3.9
    "RET504", # not fixed yet https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2950
    "TRY003", # require implement multiple exception class
    "RUF005", # problem with numpy compatybility, see https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff/issues/2142#issuecomment-1451038741
    "B028", # need to be fixed
    "PYI015", # it produces bad looking files (@jni opinion)
    "W191", "Q000", "Q001", "Q002", "Q003", "ISC001", # https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/#conflicting-lint-rules
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"napari/_vispy/__init__.py" = ["E402"]
"**/_tests/*.py" = ["B011", "INP001", "TRY301", "B018", "RUF012"]
"napari/utils/_testsupport.py" = ["B011"]
"tools/validate_strings.py" = ["F401"]
"tools/**" = ["INP001", "T20"]
"examples/**" = ["ICN001", "INP001", "T20"]
"**/vendored/**" = ["TID"]
"napari/benchmarks/**" = ["RUF012", "TID252"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-quotes]
docstring-quotes = "double"
inline-quotes = "single"
multiline-quotes = "double"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# Disallow all relative imports.
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party=['napari']
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions]
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions.extend-aliases]
# Declare a custom alias for the `matplotlib` module.
"dask.array" = "da"
xarray = "xr"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# These follow standard library warnings filters syntax.  See more here:
# https://docs.python.org/3/library/warnings.html#describing-warning-filters
addopts = ["--maxfail=5",  "--durations=10",  "-ra", "--strict-markers", "--strict-config"]
console_output_style = "count"
minversion = "8"
# log_cli_level = "INFO"
xfail_strict = true
testpaths = ["napari", "napari_builtins"]


# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.
# napari deprecation and future warnings should NOT go in here.
# instead... assert the warning with `pytest.warns()` in the relevant test,
# That way we can clean them up when no longer necessary
filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:ipykernel",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",
  "ignore:Accessing zmq Socket:DeprecationWarning:jupyter_client",
  "ignore:pythonw executable not found:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:data shape .* exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE:UserWarning",
  "ignore:For best performance with Dask arrays in napari:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:numpy.ufunc size changed:RuntimeWarning",
  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",
  "ignore:Alternative shading modes are only available in 3D, defaulting to none",
  "ignore:distutils Version classes are deprecated::",
  "ignore:There is no current event loop:DeprecationWarning:",
  "ignore:(?s).*Pyarrow will become a required dependency of pandas:DeprecationWarning",  # pandas pyarrow (pandas<3.0),
]
markers = [
    "examples: Test of examples",
    "disable_qthread_start: Disable thread start in this Test",
    "disable_qthread_pool_start: Disable strarting QRunnable using QThreadPool start in this Test",
    "disable_qtimer_start: Disable timer start in this Test",
    "disable_qanimation_start: Disable animation start in this Test",
    "enable_console: Don't mock the IPython console (in QtConsole) in this Test",
]

[tool.mypy]
files = "napari"
# This file triggers an internal mypy error, so exclude collection
# TODO: fix this
exclude = "napari/utils/events/_tests/test_evented_model\\.py"
plugins =  "numpy.typing.mypy_plugin, pydantic.mypy"
ignore_missing_imports = true
hide_error_codes = false
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
disable_error_code = [
  # See discussion at https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2427;
  # mypy cannot run type checking on method assignment, but we use
  # that in several places, so ignore the error
  'method-assign'
]
# see `$ qtpy mypy-args` and qtpy readme. This will be used by `tox -e mypy`
# to properly infer with PyQt6 installed
always_false=['PYSIDE6', 'PYSIDE2', 'PYQT5']
always_true=['PYQT6']


# gloabl ignore error

module = [
  '*._tests.*',
  '*.experimental.*',
  '*._vendor.*',
  '*.benchmarks.*',

# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.
# napari deprecation and future warnings should NOT go in here.
# instead... assert the warning with `pytest.warns()` in the relevant test,
# That way we can clean them up when no longer necessary
filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:ipykernel",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",
  "ignore:Accessing zmq Socket:DeprecationWarning:jupyter_client",
  "ignore:pythonw executable not found:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:data shape .* exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE:UserWarning",
  "ignore:For best performance with Dask arrays in napari:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:numpy.ufunc size changed:RuntimeWarning",
  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",
  "ignore:Alternative shading modes are only available in 3D, defaulting to none",
  "ignore:distutils Version classes are deprecated::",
  "ignore:There is no current event loop:DeprecationWarning:",
  "ignore:(?s).*Pyarrow will become a required dependency of pandas:DeprecationWarning",  # pandas pyarrow (pandas<3.0),
  # TODO: remove once xarray is updated to avoid this warning
  # https://github.com/pydata/xarray/blame/b1f3fea467f9387ed35c221205a70524f4caa18b/pyproject.toml#L333-L334
  # https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/8939
  "ignore:__array__ implementation doesn't accept a copy keyword, so passing copy=False failed.",
]
markers = [
    "examples: Test of examples",
    "disable_qthread_start: Disable thread start in this Test",

[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-quotes]
docstring-quotes = "double"
inline-quotes = "single"
multiline-quotes = "double"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
# Disallow all relative imports.
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party=['napari']
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions]
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-import-conventions.extend-aliases]
# Declare a custom alias for the `matplotlib` module.
"dask.array" = "da"
xarray = "xr"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# These follow standard library warnings filters syntax.  See more here:
# https://docs.python.org/3/library/warnings.html#describing-warning-filters
addopts = ["--maxfail=5",  "--durations=10",  "-ra", "--strict-markers", "--strict-config"]
console_output_style = "count"
minversion = "8"
# log_cli_level = "INFO"
xfail_strict = true
testpaths = ["napari", "napari_builtins"]


# NOTE: only put things that will never change in here.
# napari deprecation and future warnings should NOT go in here.
# instead... assert the warning with `pytest.warns()` in the relevant test,
# That way we can clean them up when no longer necessary
filterwarnings = [
  "error:::napari", # turn warnings from napari into errors
  "error:::test_.*", # turn warnings in our own tests into errors
  "default:::napari.+vendored.+",  # just print warnings inside vendored modules
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:shibokensupport",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:ipykernel",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:tensorstore",
  "ignore:Accessing zmq Socket:DeprecationWarning:jupyter_client",
  "ignore:pythonw executable not found:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:data shape .* exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE:UserWarning",
  "ignore:For best performance with Dask arrays in napari:UserWarning:",
  "ignore:numpy.ufunc size changed:RuntimeWarning",
  "ignore:Multiscale rendering is only supported in 2D. In 3D, only the lowest resolution scale is displayed",
  "ignore:Alternative shading modes are only available in 3D, defaulting to none",
  "ignore:distutils Version classes are deprecated::",
  "ignore:There is no current event loop:DeprecationWarning:",
  "ignore:(?s).*Pyarrow will become a required dependency of pandas:DeprecationWarning",  # pandas pyarrow (pandas<3.0),
]
markers = [
    "examples: Test of examples",
    "disable_qthread_start: Disable thread start in this Test",
    "disable_qthread_pool_start: Disable strarting QRunnable using QThreadPool start in this Test",
    "disable_qtimer_start: Disable timer start in this Test",
    "disable_qanimation_start: Disable animation start in this Test",
    "enable_console: Don't mock the IPython console (in QtConsole) in this Test",
]

[tool.mypy]
files = "napari"
# This file triggers an internal mypy error, so exclude collection
# TODO: fix this
exclude = "napari/utils/events/_tests/test_evented_model\\.py"
plugins =  "numpy.typing.mypy_plugin, pydantic.mypy"
ignore_missing_imports = true
hide_error_codes = false
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
disable_error_code = [
  # See discussion at https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2427;
  # mypy cannot run type checking on method assignment, but we use
  # that in several places, so ignore the error
  'method-assign'
]
# see `$ qtpy mypy-args` and qtpy readme. This will be used by `tox -e mypy`
# to properly infer with PyQt6 installed
always_false=['PYSIDE6', 'PYSIDE2', 'PYQT5']
always_true=['PYQT6']


# gloabl ignore error
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
  '*._tests.*',
  '*.experimental.*',
  '*._vendor.*',
  '*.benchmarks.*',
  'napari_builtins.*'
]
ignore_errors = true

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ruff: format + lint
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 80
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Layered rule selection. D (docstrings) keeps the existing convention;
# F (pyflakes) catches real bugs; I (isort) keeps imports tidy; E/W
# (pycodestyle, minus E501 which ruff format already handles); B (bugbear)
# catches subtle correctness issues.
select = ["D", "E", "F", "I", "W", "B", "W505"]
ignore = [
    # Docstring rules we explicitly waive (see existing convention).
    "D100", "D102", "D104", "D105", "D107", "D203", "D213", "D401", "D402",
    # E501 (line-too-long) is handled by ruff format; flagging it again on
    # long URLs / strings only adds noise.
    "E501",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests don't need module/function docstrings or strict bugbear rules.
"tests/**/*.py" = ["D", "B"]
"**/__init__.py" = ["D104", "F401"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
max-doc-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# basedpyright: type checker
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every module in `quantmind/` is type-checked at "standard" mode. PR5
# deleted the transitional packages (`config/`, `flow/`, `llm/`,
# `models/`) so the exclude list is now down to the directories pyright
# always wants ignored.

[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["quantmind"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/.venv",
    "**/build",
]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
reportMissingImports = "error"
reportMissingTypeStubs = "none"
# Pydantic v2 discriminated unions tighten a `str` field to `Literal["..."]`
# in subclasses (e.g. `Paper.item_type: Literal["paper"]`). Python's variance
# rules say mutable attributes must be invariant, so basedpyright flags this
# even though Pydantic supports it. We use this idiom throughout knowledge/
# and configs/, so disable the diagnostic globally.
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = "none"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter: architectural boundary contracts
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Encodes the target architecture: utils, knowledge, and preprocess are
# leaves; configs depends only on knowledge; flows + magic is the apex
# layer (PR5). The transitional packages (config/, flow/, llm/, models/)
# were deleted in PR5; they remain in the forbidden lists as a tripwire
# against accidental re-introduction during future refactors.

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["quantmind"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "utils is a leaf (no inbound deps from quantmind packages)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["quantmind.utils"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "quantmind.configs",
    "quantmind.flows",
    "quantmind.knowledge",
    "quantmind.magic",
    "quantmind.preprocess",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "knowledge is a leaf (no inbound deps from quantmind packages)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["quantmind.knowledge"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "quantmind.configs",
    "quantmind.flows",
    "quantmind.magic",
    "quantmind.preprocess",
    "quantmind.utils",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "configs only depends on knowledge"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["quantmind.configs"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "quantmind.flows",
    "quantmind.magic",
    "quantmind.preprocess",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "preprocess only depends on utils (no inbound deps on configs/knowledge/flows)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["quantmind.preprocess"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "quantmind.configs",
    "quantmind.flows",
    "quantmind.knowledge",
    "quantmind.magic",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "flows + magic is apex (no transitional package imports)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "quantmind.flows",
    "quantmind.magic",
]
# These packages were deleted in PR5; the contract guards against any
# future code re-introducing them under the same names.
forbidden_modules = [
    "quantmind.config",
    "quantmind.flow",
    "quantmind.llm",
    "quantmind.models",
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# pytest: configuration + coverage gate
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Coverage floor 75% — PR5 deleted the transitional packages so every
# remaining module is in the target architecture and is well-tested.
addopts = [
    "--cov=quantmind",
    "--cov-report=term-missing",
    "--cov-fail-under=75",
    "-ra",
]
asyncio_mode = "auto"

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["quantmind"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]
# Branch coverage. Floor moves with the migration:

# =============================================================================
# RUFF CONFIGURATION (Modern Python Linter + Formatter, 2025)
# =============================================================================
# Ruff replaces: flake8, black, isort, pyupgrade, autoflake, and more
# Speed: 10-100x faster than traditional tools
# Documentation: https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/

[tool.ruff]
# Exclude common directories
exclude = [
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".git-rewrite",
    ".hg",
    ".ipynb_checkpoints",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".nox",
    ".pants.d",
    ".pyenv",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".pytype",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    ".vscode",
    "__pycache__",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "buck-out",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    "site-packages",
    "venv",
    "archive",
    "vulture_whitelist.py",
    # ruff 0.16 formats Python code blocks inside Markdown by default; keep the
    # dev-tool refresh (dev group + lock only) from rewriting docs content.
    "*.md",
]

# Line length: 100 (slightly longer than Black's 88 for readability)
line-length = 100
indent-width = 4

# Target Python 3.12 (aligned with requires-python floor and mypy python_version)
target-version = "py312"

# =============================================================================
# LINTING RULES
# =============================================================================

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Enable recommended rule sets (2025 best practices)
select = [
    "E",     # pycodestyle errors
    "W",     # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",     # Pyflakes (undefined names, unused imports, etc.)
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear (common bugs and design problems)
    "I",     # isort (import sorting)
    "UP",    # pyupgrade (modernize Python code)
    "SIM",   # flake8-simplify (simplify code)
    "C4",    # flake8-comprehensions (better list/dict/set comprehensions)
    "PIE",   # flake8-pie (misc lints)
    "T20",   # flake8-print (detect print statements)
    "RET",   # flake8-return (return statement issues)
    "ARG",   # flake8-unused-arguments
    "PTH",   # flake8-use-pathlib (prefer pathlib over os.path)
    "PERF",  # perflint (performance anti-patterns) - NEW 2025
    "RUF",   # Ruff-specific rules - NEW 2025
    "FURB",  # refurb (modernize Python idioms) - NEW 2025
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async (async/await best practices) - NEW 2025
    # #3448: naive-UTC constructors stay blocked natively after the removed
    # Semgrep python.no-datetime-utcnow contract (flake8-datetimez subset).
    "DTZ003", # datetime.utcnow() (naive UTC)
    "DTZ004", # datetime.utcfromtimestamp() (naive UTC)
]

# Ignore specific rules
ignore = [
    "E501",    # Line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",    # Function calls in argument defaults
    "T201",    # print() statements (we use them for logging)
    "PTH123",  # pathlib open() (we use built-in open())
    "PTH",     # os.path usage (pathlib migration not critical for this project)
    "ARG002",  # Unused method arguments (often required for interface compatibility)
    "B904",    # raise-without-from (context dependent, not always needed)
    "SIM113",  # enumerate-for-loop (minor optimization, not critical)
    # NEW 2025 rules - selective ignores
    "RUF001",  # ambiguous-unicode (false positives for Cyrillic/Ukrainian text)
    "RUF002",  # ambiguous-unicode-docstring (false positives for Cyrillic)
    "RUF003",  # ambiguous-unicode-comment (false positives for Cyrillic comments)
    "PERF203", # try-except-in-loop (acceptable for error handling in async)
    "PERF401", # manual-list-comprehension (readability over micro-optimization)
    "RUF012",  # mutable-class-default (dataclasses handle this correctly)
    "ASYNC230",# blocking-open-call (some files are small, async not always needed)
    "ASYNC240",# blocking-path-call (local filesystem ops are fast, async overhead not worth it)
]

# Allow auto-fix for all enabled rules
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = []

# Allow unused variables when underscore-prefixed
dummy-variable-rgx = "^(_+|(_+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+?))$"

# Per-file ignores
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401", "E402"]  # Allow unused imports and late imports
"test_*.py" = ["E402", "T201", "SIM117"]  # Allow late imports, print(), nested with in tests
"tests/**/*.py" = ["E402", "T201", "SIM117"]  # Same for tests/ directory

"*.py" = ["ARG001"]               # Allow unused function arguments (common in callbacks)

# Import sorting configuration (isort replacement)
[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["config", "src", "telegram_bot"]
force-single-line = false
lines-after-imports = 2

# =============================================================================
# FORMATTING
# =============================================================================

[tool.ruff.format]
# Use double quotes for strings (like Black)
quote-style = "double"

# Indent with spaces (4 spaces)
indent-style = "space"

# Respect magic trailing commas
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

# Auto-detect line endings (LF on Linux, CRLF on Windows)
line-ending = "auto"

# Format code examples in docstrings
docstring-code-format = true

# Docstring code line length (dynamic = same as main code)
docstring-code-line-length = "dynamic"

# =============================================================================
# MYPY CONFIGURATION (Type Checking)
# =============================================================================
# Uncomment to enable strict type checking
# Run: mypy .

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false  # Set to true for strict mode
ignore_missing_imports = true  # Ignore missing stubs for now
explicit_package_bases = true  # Resolve duplicate module names in services/

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "src.retrieval.topic_classifier"
disallow_untyped_defs = true

# =============================================================================
# IMPORT-LINTER CONFIGURATION (Architecture boundary enforcement)
# =============================================================================
# Contracts encode the key layering invariants documented in
# docs/designs/adr-2855-module-collapse.md. Run with: uv run lint-imports
#
# Layer model (strict, inner cannot import outer):
#   src/core  →  src/runtime  →  telegram_bot
# The archived surfaces (archive/, services/) must never be imported by src/.

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["src", "telegram_bot"]
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Core must not import telegram_bot"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["telegram_bot"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# src.core.assistant is the documented public entrypoint: it orchestrates
# src.runtime.pipeline by design (see README "Assistant core entrypoint").
# src.core.contracts and src.core.telemetry are shared contracts consumed by
# both core and runtime — bidirectional coupling is intentional.
# The real invariant to guard is that runtime must not import telegram_bot.
name = "Runtime must not import telegram_bot"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.runtime"]
forbidden_modules = ["telegram_bot"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Core contracts layer is import-independent"
type = "independence"
modules = ["src.core.contracts"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "src must not import archive"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src"]
forbidden_modules = ["archive"]

# =============================================================================
# BANDIT CONFIGURATION (Security Linting)
# =============================================================================
# Uncomment to enable security checks
# Run: bandit -r . -c pyproject.toml

# =============================================================================
# VULTURE CONFIGURATION (Dead-code detection)
# =============================================================================
# Moved from Makefile CLI flags so `uv run vulture` picks up config automatically.
# Suppress false positives with inline `# noqa: vulture` comments where needed.

[tool.vulture]
paths = ["src", "telegram_bot", "services", "scripts"]
exclude = [
    ".venv/*",
    "archive/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/site-packages/*",
    "*/dist-info/*",
]
min_confidence = 80
sort_by_size = true

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = [".venv", "tests", "archive", "__pycache__", "scripts"]
skips = ["B101"]  # Skip assert_used (common in tests)

# =============================================================================
# PYLINT CONFIGURATION (Comprehensive Linting)
# =============================================================================
# Run: pylint src/

[tool.pylint.main]
# Python version for compatibility checks
py-version = "3.12"

# Files/directories to exclude
ignore = ["tests", ".venv", "__pycache__"]

[tool.pylint.messages_control]
# Disable specific checks
disable = [
    "C0111",  # missing-docstring
    "C0103",  # invalid-name (sometimes OK for ML code)
    "R0913",  # too-many-arguments (common in ML)
    "R0914",  # too-many-locals
    "W0511",  # fixme/todo comments
    "C0301",  # line-too-long (handled by ruff)
]

[tool.pylint.format]
max-line-length = 100
indent-string = "    "  # 4 spaces

[tool.pylint.basic]
# Good variable names
good-names = ["i", "j", "k", "ex", "Run", "_", "id", "f", "e"]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10  # Allow more args (ML models need many params)
max-attributes = 15
max-branches = 15

# =============================================================================
# PYTEST CONFIGURATION
# =============================================================================

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
addopts = """
    -ra
    --strict-markers
    --strict-config
    --capture=sys
    --dist=worksteal
"""
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
timeout = 30
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests with mocks (fast, no external deps)",
    "integration: Integration tests (requires Docker/API keys)",
    "slow: Tests taking > 5 seconds",
    "chaos: Chaos/resilience tests (service failures, fallbacks)",
    "load: Load/performance tests (concurrent users, throughput)",
    "e2e: End-to-end pipeline tests (require live services)",
    "smoke: Smoke tests (requires running services)",
    "legacy_api: tests for pre-imperative API (may need rewrite)",
    "requires_extras: Tests needing optional deps (voice/ingest/eval); skipped in core tier",
    "xdist_group: Group tests onto same xdist worker (prevents global registry collisions)",
    "contract: Contract tests (span/trace/error contracts)",
    "baseline: Baseline comparison tests (regression guard)",
    "performance: Performance benchmarks (latency, throughput, resource usage)",
    "regression: Regression guard tests (baseline comparisons, golden sets)",
    "characterization: Characterization/golden tests — behavior snapshot before refactors",
    "no_services: Tests that do NOT require Docker or external services (mocks, pure logic, fixture-shape)",
    "requires_services: Tests that require Docker, service fixtures, network ports, or live-service guards",
    "kommo: Kommo CRM live integration tests (requires KOMMO_SUBDOMAIN + KOMMO_ACCESS_TOKEN + RUN_KOMMO_LIVE_WRITES=1)",
]
filterwarnings = [
]

# =============================================================================
# COVERAGE CONFIGURATION
# =============================================================================

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src", "telegram_bot"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/.venv/*",
    # Scripts directory (not production code)
    "scripts/*",
    "scripts/**/*",
    # Evaluation surface (archived; was src/evaluation, now archive/evaluation)
    "archive/evaluation/*",
    # Test/debug scripts in wrong location
    "telegram_bot/test_*.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 80
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
]

# =============================================================================
# DEPTRY CONFIGURATION — scoped to production code (src/ telegram_bot/)
# =============================================================================
# Run via: make deps-audit  (blocking, full audit; also part of `make audit`)
#
# Design notes:
# - experimental_namespace_package: src/ and telegram_bot/ are in-repo
#   namespace packages (not PyPI packages), so DEP001 on intra-repo imports
#   is a false positive suppressed by this flag.
# - extend_exclude: archived/reference code and non-package support trees
#   should not gate the production lint. services/bge-m3-api is a nested
#   package that owns its own manifest/lock; the retired starter/ tree was
#   deleted outright by #3399, so no starter-specific exclusion exists (#3280).
# - per_rule_ignores DEP001: remaining optional/conditional imports that are
#   not declared in pyproject.toml because they live in optional extras or
#   archived CRM paths (fluent_compiler).
# - per_rule_ignores DEP002: packages declared in pyproject.toml that deptry
#   cannot see used inside the src/+telegram_bot/ scan scope (see the inline
#   reason on the DEP002 entry).

[tool.deptry]
experimental_namespace_package = true
extend_exclude = [
    "scripts",
    "services",
    "archive",
    "tests",
]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# Optional/archived imports not in pyproject.toml dependencies
DEP001 = [
    "fluent_compiler",
]
# fastapi (bge-extras) is imported by services/bge-m3-api/app.py — a nested
# package that owns its own manifest — and by the root-venv
# tests/unit/test_bge_m3_endpoints.py + test_bge_m3_rerank.py, which import
# that app. Both the importer and the caller sit in extend_exclude trees, so
# the usage is invisible to this scan (#3280).
DEP002 = [
    "fastapi",
]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
ai_rag_info = ["py.typed"]

# Where each heavy third-party library may be imported (docs/framework.md, section 2). The Import Linter contracts
# below enforce it for the modules they list; tests/architecture/test_layers.py enforces it for EVERY module,
# so a package added later cannot quietly import elasticsearch.
[tool.architecture.confinement]
cv2 = ["src.parsing"]
docx = ["src.parsing"]
easyocr = ["src.parsing"]
elasticsearch = ["src.indexing"]
fastapi = ["src.api", "src.mcp_server"]
langchain_core = ["src.models"]
langchain_openai = ["src.models"]
langchain_text_splitters = ["src.chunking"]
mcp = ["src.mcp_server"]
numpy = ["src.parsing"]
openpyxl = ["src.parsing"]
prometheus_client = ["src.api", "src.runtime", "src.worker"]
pydantic_settings = ["src.core.config"]
pymupdf = ["src.parsing"]
redis = ["src.chat", "src.jobs", "src.runtime"]
sklearn = ["src.chunking"]
starlette = ["src.api"]
torch = ["src.parsing"]
typer = ["src.cli"]
uvicorn = ["src.api"]
watchdog = ["src.ingestion"]

# --- Architecture contracts (docs/framework.md, section 2; docs/adr/0002) ----------------------------------
# Run with `lint-imports`; enforced in CI and by tests/architecture/. Type-checking-only imports create no
# runtime coupling and are not counted.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["src", "ai_rag_info"]
include_external_packages = true
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture: dependencies point inward"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "ai_rag_info.embedded | ai_rag_info.extend | ai_rag_info.testing",
    "src.api | src.cli | src.worker",
    "src.mcp_server | src.evaluation",
    "src.application",
    "src.core.container",
    "src.core.bootstrap",
    "src.chat",
    "src.retrieval | src.ingestion",
    "src.indexing | src.jobs | src.chunking | src.parsing | src.models",
    "src.runtime",
    "src.core.registry",
    "src.ports",
    "src.core.config",
    "src.core.specs | src.core.kinds",
    "src.contracts",
    "src.core.types | src.core.errors | src.core.logger",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]

    "integration: needs a live Elasticsearch (see tests/conftest.py for the URLs)",

    "ocr: needs EasyOCR model weights (downloaded on first use)",
    "packaging: builds the wheel and installs it into a clean virtualenv (slow; needs uv)",
]
addopts = "-ra"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 110
target-version = "py312"
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "B", "UP", "SIM", "ASYNC", "RUF"]
ignore = ["E501", "B008", "RUF012"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/*" = ["B", "SIM", "RUF", "ASYNC"]
# `timeout` here is an HTTP request setting (passed to httpx), not an asyncio.timeout() scope
"ai_rag_info/*" = ["ASYNC109"]
# the engine-availability check must run before the engine imports, to give an install hint instead of a bare ModuleNotFoundError
"ai_rag_info/embedded.py" = ["E402"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
check_untyped_defs = true

# The public package is held to strict typing (docs/framework.md, section 6): its interface is the contract.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "ai_rag_info.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_any_generics = true
no_implicit_reexport = true
warn_return_any = true
strict_equality = true

# === Pytest Configuration ===
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
addopts = [
    "-v",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--tb=short",
]
console_output_style = "progress"
log_cli = false
log_cli_level = "ERROR"
markers = [
    "asyncio: Async tests using pytest-asyncio",
    "unit: Unit tests (minimal mocking, fast)",
    "integration: Integration tests (multiple components, real DB)",
    "e2e: End-to-end tests (full pipeline)",
    "slow: Slow tests (model loading, heavy computation)",
    "requires_models: Tests that need model files",
    "requires_audio: Tests that need audio files",
    "requires_database: Tests that need Arango to function",
    "requires_essentia: Tests that need Essentia library",
    "requires_tensorflow: Tests that need TensorFlow",
    "container_only: Tests designed to run in Docker container (includes GPU tests, skip in CI)",
    "code_smell: Architecture/style tests that dont indicate broken functionality (skip in CI)",
    "mocked: Test uses mocked dependencies (informational)",
]

# === Mypy Configuration ===
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false
check_untyped_defs = true
exclude = [
    "^tests/",
    "^scripts/",
    "^build_resources/essentia/",
]
show_error_codes = true
show_column_numbers = true
pretty = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
follow_imports = "normal"

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "scipy.*",
    "mutagen.*",
    "onnxruntime.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# === Ruff Configuration ===
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 120
fix = true
output-format = "json"
exclude = [
    "scripts/",
    ".github/skills/",
    "build_resources/essentia/",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # pyflakes
    "I",      # isort (import sorting)
    "N",      # pep8-naming
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "B",      # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "SIM",    # flake8-simplify
    "RUF",    # Ruff-specific rules
    "TID",    # flake8-tidy-imports (for banned-api)
    "ERA",    # eradicate (commented-out code)
    "PERF",   # Perflint (performance anti-patterns)
    "ASYNC",  # flake8-async (async anti-patterns)
    "PIE",    # flake8-pie (misc code quality)
    "RET",    # flake8-return (return statement issues)
    "LOG",    # flake8-logging (logging best practices)
    "FURB",   # refurb (modernization)
    "TC",     # flake8-type-checking (TYPE_CHECKING imports)
    "ARG",    # flake8-unused-arguments
]

ignore = [
    "E501",   # Line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",   # Do not perform function calls in argument defaults (FastAPI Depends pattern)
    "N802",   # Function name should be lowercase (allow CamelCase for classes)
    "SIM108", # Use ternary operator instead of if-else-block (sometimes less readable)
    "ERA001", # Commented-out code detection (too many false positives)
    # TODO: Fix these incrementally, then remove from ignore
    "ARG001", # Unused function argument (26 existing violations)
    "ARG002", # Unused method argument (10 existing violations)
    "TC001",  # Move import into TYPE_CHECKING block
    "TC002",  # Move third-party import into TYPE_CHECKING block
    "TC003",  # Move stdlib import into TYPE_CHECKING block
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"debug_vram.py" = ["E722"]
"nomarr/helpers/time_helper.py" = ["TID251"]
"nomarr/components/workers/worker_crash_comp.py" = ["TID251"]
# Migration files use V-prefix naming convention (V006_*, V007_*, etc.)
"nomarr/migrations/V*.py" = ["N999"]
# ML components use intentional lazy imports to avoid loading TF/numpy until needed
"nomarr/components/ml/*.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# DI wiring file uses lazy imports by design
"nomarr/app.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# FastAPI DI getters must import application lazily to avoid circular deps
"nomarr/interfaces/api/web/dependencies.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# Discovery workers run in separate processes - imports deferred until worker starts
"nomarr/services/infrastructure/workers/*.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# ML processing workflows defer imports to control TF/ML component loading order
"nomarr/workflows/processing/*.py" = ["PLC0415"]
# Calibration workflows are tightly coupled with ML layer
"nomarr/workflows/calibration/*.py" = ["PLC0415"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
docstring-code-format = true
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["nomarr"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"time.time".msg = "Use now_s() or now_ms() from nomarr.helpers.time_helper for wall-clock time"
"time.time_ns".msg = "Use now_s() or now_ms() from nomarr.helpers.time_helper for wall-clock time"
"time.monotonic".msg = "Use internal_s() or internal_ms() from nomarr.helpers.time_helper for monotonic time"
"time.monotonic_ns".msg = "Use internal_s() or internal_ms() from nomarr.helpers.time_helper for monotonic time"
"datetime.datetime.now".msg = "Use now_ms() from nomarr.helpers.time_helper, or format_wall_timestamp() for display"
"datetime.datetime.utcnow".msg = "Use now_ms() from nomarr.helpers.time_helper (utcnow is deprecated in Python 3.12)"
"builtins.print".msg = "Use logging (logger.info/debug/warning) instead of print() for proper log management"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

forbidden_modules = ["nomarr.services", "nomarr.workflows", "nomarr.interfaces", "nomarr.components", "nomarr.persistence"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

# the constant and cut the multiplier so a genuine hang still can't cost minutes.
#
# Known limitation: mutmut runs each mutant by forking a warm parent process, and
# our DB/TestClient-backed tests hang after that fork. Mutants whose covering
# tests reach one of those are therefore reported as "timeout" rather than
# "killed" - roughly a third of the run. A timeout is inconclusive, NOT a
# survivor: spot-checking them by hand (MUTANT_UNDER_TEST=<name> pytest <test>

[build-system]

requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]

build-backend = "hatchling.build"


[tool.uv]
add-bounds = "exact"
cache-keys = [
  { file = "pyproject.toml" },
  { git = { commit = true, tags = true } },
]
package = true
trusted-publishing = "always"


[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# Last-resort sentinel: only used when a build sees neither a .git directory nor
# an expanded .git_archival.txt (e.g. an archive of a commit with no reachable
# tag). "0.0.0" reads clearly as "version could not be determined" rather than
# masquerading as a real early release. See .git_archival.txt + .gitattributes
# `export-subst` for the archive path that recovers the real tag-derived version.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"


[tool.hatch.build]
hooks.vcs.version-file = "src/pun/_version.py"


[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "only-version"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true


[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The package uses a src layout, so the source tree lives under /src (not
# /pun); including /src ships the actual modules -- and, for
# C-extension projects, the .pyx/.pxd sources needed to compile from the sdist.
include = [
  "/README.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "/src",
  "/tests",
  "/docs/examples",
]


[tool.commitizen]
# Commit-authoring and message linting only. release-please owns version
# bumping, git tagging, and CHANGELOG.md (see .github/release-please-config.json),
# so the bump/tag/changelog settings are intentionally omitted here to avoid two
# tools competing over the same tags and changelog file.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# addopts = "-rXs --strict-config --strict-markers"
addopts = "-v --tb=short --doctest-glob=README.md"
# One marker per component, auto-applied by tests/conftest.py from each test's
# top-level tests/<dir>/. Enables `pytest -m web` locally and per-component CI
# jobs (issue #160, https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#per-component-markers-path-filtered-jobs-and-one-coverage-gate-per-component); `integration` (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/testing-strategy/#real-broker-integration-tests-testcontainers-locally-per-broker-ci-mechanism) is one axis of the scheme.
markers = [
  "core: core/shared component tests",
  "cli: CLI component tests",
  "tui: TUI component tests",
]
# Strict mode requires explicit @pytest.mark.asyncio annotations, making async
# test collection intentional instead of silently accepting unmarked coroutines.
asyncio_mode = "strict"
filterwarnings = [
  "error",
]
# The project README is the deliberately small Markdown doctest surface. Other
# Markdown files can use illustrative snippets without becoming pytest inputs.
testpaths = ["tests", "README.md"]
doctest_optionflags = "ELLIPSIS IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"
xfail_strict = true


[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
# Match `_version.py` wherever it resolves: `src/...` in editable dev installs and
# `.../site-packages/...` when tox/CI installs the built (non-editable) wheel. A
# `src/**`-only pattern silently misses the installed copy and reports it at 0%.
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
parallel = true
# Store data-file paths relative to the project root so `.coverage` files produced
# on different runners/OSes merge in the `coverage-combine` CI job without
# absolute-path mismatches. Complements the `[tool.coverage.paths]` remap below
# (which unifies the src/ vs site-packages layouts). See https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#a-single-union-coverage-gate-across-the-whole-matrix.
relative_files = true
source_pkgs = ["pun", "tests"]


[tool.coverage.paths]
# Unify coverage data across environments. tox installs the built wheel into
# each env's site-packages, so the same source file is measured under a different
# `.tox/<env>/.../site-packages/pun` path per interpreter. Without
# remapping those back to the canonical `src/` tree, `coverage combine` keeps a
# separate copy per env and a version-gated line covered in one interpreter but not
# another is wrongly counted as missed — silently failing the `fail_under` gate.
# `tests` needs no remapping: it is never installed, so every environment measures
# it at the same repo-local path.
pun = ["src/pun", "*/site-packages/pun"]


[tool.coverage.report]
# Untestable code is excluded per site with `# pragma: no cover`, not with blanket
# patterns here: a regex matching a `def` line excludes the *whole function body*,
# so a pattern like `def main\(` would silently un-measure any future `main()`
# with real logic (and did mask the tested GUI/TUI entrypoints). Pragmas carry the
# exclusion decision next to the code it affects. See https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/testing-strategy/#coverage-exclusions-are-per-site-pragmas-and-the-globs-must-match-the-installed-layout.
exclude_lines = [
  "no cov",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]
fail_under = 99
# Patterns match both the `src/` (editable) and installed (`site-packages`)
# layouts (see [tool.coverage.run] omit).
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true


[tool.vulture]
# Framework-invoked handlers: Typer commands, FastAPI routes, FastStream
# lifecycle hooks, and the MCP tool dispatcher.
ignore_decorators = [
  "@app.command",
  "@app.get",
  "@app.after_startup",
  "@app.after_shutdown",
  "@server.call_tool",
  # A fixture used through ``@pytest.mark.usefixtures("name")`` -- or from
  # another test module -- is only ever named in a string, which vulture cannot
  # see. Unused fixtures are caught properly by ``pytest --dead-fixtures`` in
  # the tox ``style`` env, so this delegates rather than suppresses.
  "@pytest.fixture",
]
# Public API surfaces vulture cannot see being used: ``main`` entry points are
# referenced only via pyproject scripts, ``model_config`` is consumed by
# pydantic-settings, ``logger`` is imported only by optional components, the MCP
# ``arguments`` parameter is mandated by the call_tool signature, the Textual
# names (CSS/compose/on_mount/title/BINDINGS) are invoked by the TUI framework,
# and ``pytestmark``/``pytest_*`` (conftest hooks) are consumed by pytest at
# collection time.
ignore_names = ["CONFIG_FILE_PATH", "logger", "main", "model_config", "pytest_*", "collect_ignore_glob", "CSS", "compose", "on_mount", "title", "BINDINGS"]
min_confidence = 60
paths = ["src", "tests"]


[tool.deptry]
# `known_first_party` is explicit because the tox `deps` env installs the built
# wheel, so without it deptry reads the project's own imports as a third-party
# transitive dependency (DEP003). Add further `per_rule_ignores` entries for the
# project's own findings, e.g. DEP003 for a package only importable through
# another declared one, or DEP002 for an optional import guarded by try/except.
# See https://deptry.com/rules-violations/.
# Excluded: the Sphinx config, the build hook (its imports belong to
# `[build-system].requires`, not the runtime dependencies), the benchmarks and the
# worker probe script (neither ships in the wheel; pytest and anyio come from
# the dev tooling).
extend_exclude = [
  "docs/conf.py",
]
known_first_party = ["pun"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# tools/build_docs.py imports `packaging`, pinned in the `docs` group for that
# script alone, so deptry reads it as a misplaced dev dependency.
DEP004 = ["packaging"]


[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "pun"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture with independent components"
type = "layers"
# Layers are listed high -> low: a layer may import lower layers but never a
# higher one. Modules joined by ` | ` on one line are independent SIBLINGS that
# may not import each other. `cli` is the orchestrator layer — the
# `pun` console root, whose subcommands launch the other
# components (web/gui/tui/mcp/worker) via lazy imports — so it sits ABOVE the
# independent component group, which sits above `core`, which sits above the leaf
# `utils`.
#
# `exhaustive` makes the contract fail when a subpackage of
# `pun` is not named in `layers` — so a new top-level
# subpackage is a deliberate architecture decision (add it to a layer here)
# rather than something that silently accretes at the package root. Feature code
# belongs inside an existing layer; see "Package structure" in `AGENTS.md`. The
# `exhaustive_ignores` entries are the non-layer foundations: the metadata and
# hatch-vcs version modules and the `python -m` dispatcher.
containers = ["pun"]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = [
  "__main__",
  "__metadata__",
  "_version",
]
layers = [
  "cli",
  "tui",
  "core",
  "utils",
]


[tool.ruff]
fix = true
output-format = "full"
preview = true
show-fixes = true
src = ["src", "tests", "docs/examples"]
target-version = "py310"
unsafe-fixes = true


[tool.ruff.analyze]
detect-string-imports = true
preview = true


[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true
line-ending = "lf"
preview = true
skip-magic-trailing-comma = true


[tool.ruff.lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
# Two opinionated ruff 0.16 preview rules are disabled: RUF105 would rewrite the
# portable `# noqa` comments into ruff's own `# ruff: ignore` syntax (its docs note
# `# noqa` is needed for cross-tool compatibility), and RUF201 would rewrite every
# rule *code* in this config's selectors into long rule *names*. Both are stylistic.
ignore = ["COM812", "CPY", "FIX", "RUF105", "RUF201", "TD"]
logger-objects = ["logging_setup.logger"]
preview = true
select = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
# skip-magic-trailing-comma = true
split-on-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-copyright]
author = "Hasan Sezer Taşan <hasansezertasan@gmail.com>"


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
# Pydantic evaluates annotations at runtime, so imports used only in model
# field annotations (e.g. `pathlib.Path`) must NOT be moved into a
# `TYPE_CHECKING` block — doing so breaks model construction.
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = [
  "pydantic.BaseModel",
  "pydantic_settings.BaseSettings",
]


[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 5


[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
ignore-overlong-task-comments = true


[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"


[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Recursive glob so nested test packages (tests/cli, tests/gui, ...) are covered.
# Tests legitimately use asserts/magic values, reach into package internals, and
# don't need return-value documentation on their fixtures and helpers.
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC2701", "DOC201"]
# Documentation examples are importable modules tested by
# ``tests/test_docs_examples.py``; they are not application packages.
"docs/examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001"]
# The Sphinx config is a standalone module, not part of an importable package.
"docs/conf.py" = ["INP001"]
# The docs warning-allowlist gate is a standalone script (not an importable
# package) whose whole job is to print GitHub `::error::` annotations to stdout.
"docs/check_warnings.py" = ["INP001", "T201"]
# The versioned-docs build orchestrator is a standalone CLI script under tools/,
# not part of an importable package (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/docs-versioning/#docs-publish-only-the-current-version-and-carry-older-built-versions-forward-from-gh-pages).
"tools/build_docs.py" = ["INP001"]


[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true


[tool.ruff.lint.ruff]
parenthesize-tuple-in-subscript = true


[tool.mypy]
files = ["src", "docs/examples"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true


[tool.basedpyright]
exclude = [".venv"]
include = ["src/pun", "docs/examples"]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
venv = ".venv"
# venvPath is the directory *containing* the venv, not the venv itself; ".venv"
# here would make basedpyright look for ".venv/.venv". Use "." so both the venv
# and basedpyright's strict ruleset resolve the project's installed deps.
venvPath = "."


[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "tests", "docs/examples"]
respect-ignore-files = false


[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.10"


[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true


[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.10"
project-includes = ["src", "docs/examples"]

[tool.pylint.main]
# pylint runs as an always-on gate that deliberately overlaps ruff's PL* rules.
# Its canonical invocation is `pylint src docs/examples`, so it never descends into tests; this
# ignore-paths is a defensive scope guard for broader invocations (`pylint .`,
# filename-passing hooks). Tests are linted by ruff, not pylint.
ignore-paths = ["^tests/.*$"]
# `.pyi` stubs (the c-extension type stub) are signature-only: their bodies are
# `...` and every parameter is unused by construction, so pylint's unused-argument
# check is a guaranteed false positive there. Stubs are type-checked by the
# type-checker gate, not pylint.
ignore-patterns = ['.*\.pyi$']

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
# Only formatter-owned checks, the docstring family, and too-few-public-methods
# are disabled so pylint is usable out of the box; everything else stays on.
disable = [
  "line-too-long", # C0301 — ruff-format owns line length
  "missing-module-docstring", # C0114
  "missing-class-docstring", # C0115
  "missing-function-docstring", # C0116
  "too-few-public-methods", # R0903 — trips dataclasses / config / Protocol classes
  # C0415 — the cli->tui/gui/web dispatch, and each component's own heavy or
  # platform-conditional import (tkinter, uvicorn, the worker's uvloop probe),
  # are deliberately lazy so import-linter's layering contract holds and a
  # framework is only imported when the code path that needs it actually runs.
  # Textual is the exception: the TUI imports it at module scope so `InfoApp`
  # can be defined there and driven by the headless pilot (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/testing-strategy/#interactive-components-expose-injected-driver-seams-so-headless-ci-measures-everything-but-the-blocking-call).
  "import-outside-toplevel",
  # W0706 — the generated TUI entry point explicitly re-raises
  # KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit ahead of a broad `except Exception` to make the
  # "let these propagate" intent obvious to readers, even though BaseException
  # subclasses wouldn't be caught by the Exception clause anyway.
  "try-except-raise",
  # R0801 — the component skeletons (gui/tui/mcp/worker) are deliberately
  # parallel: each fetches package metadata and formats the same info block the
  # same way. That structural symmetry is a feature of the scaffold, not
  # copy-paste debt, and R0801 cannot be suppressed inline at the call site.
  "duplicate-code",
]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10
max-positional-arguments = 10
max-branches = 20

[tool.typos.files]
# copier records `_commit` as a `git describe` string (`v1.2.3-4-g<hash>`) when
# the template is rendered from an untagged ref, and a fragment of the hex hash
# can read as a misspelled word, failing the check on a hash nobody chose. The
# file is machine-written with no prose to check. The prek hook passes
# `--force-exclude`, so the exclusion holds there as well as in `tox -e style`.
extend-exclude = [
  ".copier-answers.yml",
]

[tool.tox]
# The ``worker`` env is intentionally omitted: it starts a broker-bound process
# and would hang/fail under ``tox run`` in CI (where no broker is available).
# The worker is covered by its pytest TestBroker suite; run it on demand with
# ``tox -e worker`` when a broker is up (e.g. inside the devcontainer).
env_list = [
  "style",
  # Inline ``>>>`` snippets are part of the tested-documentation contract,
  # so run them in the default CI ``tox run`` invocation.
  "docs-doctest",
  "cli",
  "3.14",
  "3.13",
  "3.12",
  "3.11",
  "3.10",
]
requires = ["tox>=4"]


[tool.tox.env_run_base]
commands = [
  [
    "coverage",
    "run",
    "--module",
    "pytest",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the tests under {base_python}"
env_tmp_dir = "{toxworkdir}/tmp/{envname}"
# Arms coverage-enable-subprocess so xdist/subprocess workers are measured too;
# `coverage run` plus `parallel = true` writes per-env data files that the CI
# `coverage combine` step merges.
set_env = { COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = "{tox_root}/pyproject.toml" }
# Non-editable: `uv sync --no-editable` builds the project and installs it into
# site-packages, the layout `[tool.coverage.paths]` remaps and the per-component
# coverage gates measure (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#per-component-markers-path-filtered-jobs-and-one-coverage-gate-per-component).
package = "wheel"
# Every env installs from uv.lock (`uv sync --locked`), so tox tests and lints
# the exact versions the lockfile pins. The plain `uv-venv-runner` resolves the
# project's own dependencies fresh on every env creation (tox's
# `use_frozen_constraints` never reaches its `uv pip install`), so a newer
# release could float in and clash with a pinned tool such as semgrep.
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.style]
base_python = ["3.10"]
commands = [
  [
    "ruff",
    "check",
    "--no-fix",
  ],
  [
    "ruff",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.10",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.14",
  ],
  # Style runs once on Linux, so explicitly sweep platform-gated branches that
  # mypy would otherwise prune as unreachable on the host platform.
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "win32",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "darwin",
  ],
  [
    "basedpyright",
  ],
  [
    "ty",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "pyrefly",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "zuban",
    "check",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "pylint",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "python",
    "-m",
    "slotscheck",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "lint-imports",
  ],
  # Rules-database SAST. Deliberately style-env-only (like ty/pyrefly/zuban) and
  # not a prek hook: semgrep keeps no on-disk rule cache, so a pre-commit hook
  # would make a registry request on every `git commit`. The ruleset is named
  # explicitly rather than `--config auto` so rule selection does not depend on
  # language auto-detection; it is still fetched from the registry, which is why
  # this cannot be vendored (see https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/lint-orchestration/#semgrep-runs-in-the-style-env-against-a-named-registry-ruleset-never-vendored). `--error` makes findings blocking;
  # silence a false positive with a trailing `# nosemgrep: <rule-id>`.
  [
    "semgrep",
    "scan",
    "--config",
    "p/python",
    "--error",
    "--metrics=off",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "taplo",
    "lint",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  # A strict `--check` gate, not fix mode: a generated file that taplo would
  # rewrite fails its own CI on first push and drifts on every `copier update`.
  # `.taplo.toml` disables array auto expand/collapse so the shipped layout is
  # the canonical one regardless of which components are enabled. The `*.toml`
  # glob is non-recursive, so it scopes taplo to this project's own root TOML
  # (pyproject/prek/mise/taplo) without walking vendored `.tox`/`.venv`/
  # site-packages trees — no `.taplo.toml` exclude config needed.
  [
    "taplo",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  [
    "typos",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "ec",
  ],
  [
    "sphinx-lint",
    "docs",
  ],
  # Collects (does not run) the suite and flags fixtures that are never used --
  # cheap, deterministic, and a natural fit next to the other whole-program
  # analyzers above (lint-imports, slotscheck).
  [
    "pytest",
    "--dead-fixtures",
  ],
]
# `test` is included so the type checkers that scope tests (e.g. ty) can
# resolve pytest and other test-only imports.
dependency_groups = ["sast", "style", "test"]
description = "Run Checkers, Linters and Formatters"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


# On-demand and CI-only (not in env_list, like `integration`): the `deps` job in
# ci.yml runs it and `check` aggregates that job. `test` is included so deptry
# and creosote can resolve the project's own test-only imports. creosote needs
# the installed distributions to map import names, which the lock runner provides.
[tool.tox.env.deps]
commands = [
  [
    "deptry",
    ".",
  ],
  [
    "creosote",
    "--deps-file",
    "pyproject.toml",
    "--section",
    "project.dependencies",
    # Without this creosote skips imports inside functions, so a dependency used
    # only through a lazy import (the worker's uvloop) is reported as unused.
    "--include-deferred",
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["deps", "test"]
description = "Check dependency hygiene (deptry, creosote)"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.prek]
commands = [["prek", "run", "--all-files"]]
dependency_groups = ["prek"]
description = "Run prek hooks"
# The hooks that need the project call `uv run --locked`, which syncs it (and the
# groups they name) into this env through the runner's UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT;
# installing the wheel here too would only be swapped for that install each run.
package = "skip"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-build]
# Write the warning stream to a file (`-w`) instead of `-W` turning the first
# warning into a hard error, then let docs/check_warnings.py own the pass/fail:
# it diffs the emitted warnings against the docs/expected_warnings.txt allowlist,
# failing on both unexpected new warnings and expected ones that vanished.
commands = [
  ["sphinx-build", "-w", "docs/_build/warnings.txt", "-b", "html", "docs", "docs/_build/html"],
  ["python", "docs/check_warnings.py"],
]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Build Docs"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
# Keep build log output unbuffered/ordered. Reproducible builds pin Sphinx's
# "today"/copyright to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, which the CI docs steps
# (docs-preview.yml, release.yml) export from the last commit date before
# invoking sphinx-build directly. Local `tox` runs deliberately do NOT export
# it: an empty value ("{env:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:}") is *present but blank*, which
# breaks hatchling's get_reproducible_timestamp (`int("")`), so we leave it
# unset locally and conf.py falls back to the current year.
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-server]
# ``--ignore`` the machine-generated ``docs/_generated/`` tree: ``conf.py``
# rewrites it on every Sphinx build, so watching it would make each rebuild
# trigger the next in an endless live-reload loop.
commands = [["sphinx-autobuild", "--ignore", "*/_generated/*", "docs", "docs/_build/html"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Start the live-reloading docs server"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-doctest]
# ``literalinclude`` keeps complete examples in tested Python modules; this
# separate builder executes the occasional ``>>>`` snippet that belongs inline
# with prose.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "doctest", "docs", "docs/_build/doctest"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Run documentation doctests"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-linkcheck]
# On-demand link checker. Also run weekly (non-blocking) by docs-linkcheck.yml.
# Hits the network, so it is deliberately not part of the `style` env or PR CI.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "linkcheck", "docs", "docs/_build/linkcheck"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Check documentation for broken links"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }

[tool.tox.env.cli]
commands = [["pun", { replace = "posargs", default = ["version"], extend = true }]]
description = "Run the CLI application."
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"

# AI Service Python project configuration
# This file configures mypy for static type checking to maintain parity with
# the TypeScript codebase.

[project]
name = "ringrift-ai-service"
version = "0.1.0-beta"
description = "RingRift AI Service - Game analysis and self-play engine"
requires-python = ">=3.10"

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = [
    "pytest==9.0.1",
    "pytest-randomly==4.0.1",
    "pytest-asyncio==1.3.0",
    "pytest-timeout==2.4.0",
    "pytest-cov==7.0.0",
]

[tool.mypy]
# Start with a permissive configuration to establish baseline
# These settings can be tightened as type coverage improves
#
# Current baseline (2026-04-01): 277 errors in 152 files (down from 557 in 36 files)
# Strategy: Start with a passing config, then incrementally tighten:
# 1. Enable mypy with relaxed settings (this config)
# 2. Fix critical parity modules (board_manager, rules_engine, game_state)
# 3. Gradually enable stricter checks per-module

python_version = "3.10"

# Module discovery
files = ["app"]
exclude = [
    "tests",
    "venv",
    "__pycache__",
    ".hypothesis",
]

# Error handling - very permissive for initial integration
ignore_missing_imports = true  # Third-party libs without stubs
warn_return_any = false        # Too noisy initially
warn_unused_ignores = false    # Don't flag old type: ignore comments
show_error_codes = true
pretty = true

# Note: mypy will emit [annotation-unchecked] notes for untyped functions.
# These are informational and don't cause failure. Suppress with --no-error-summary
# or ignore them during initial integration.

# Type checking strictness - progressively tightening
strict = false
check_untyped_defs = true      # Enabled 2025-12-20 (16 errors manageable)
disallow_untyped_decorators = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
disallow_untyped_defs = false

# Suppress most error categories for initial integration
# These will be enabled incrementally as type coverage improves
# Last updated: 2025-12-19 (79 base errors after fixing exit-return and MarkerInfo)
disable_error_code = [
    "import-untyped",  # Missing type stubs
    "arg-type",        # Enable after type annotations added
    "call-arg",        # Enable after type annotations added
    "assignment",      # Enable after type annotations added
    "union-attr",      # Enable after Optional handling improved
    "attr-defined",    # Enable after type stubs added
    "dict-item",       # Enable later
    "valid-type",      # Enable later
    "no-redef",        # Enable later
    "list-item",       # Enable later
    "index",           # Enable later
    "type-var",        # numpy shape inference issue
    "misc",            # 262 errors - decorators/generics issues
    "operator",        # 90 errors - numeric type issues
    "var-annotated",   # Enable later
    "return-value",    # 69 errors - Optional/type mismatches (being fixed incrementally)
    "has-type",        # 16 errors - uninitialized attributes (from check_untyped_defs)
    "truthy-function", # 3 errors - function truthiness checks (from check_untyped_defs)
    # Fixed 2025-12-19: exit-return errors (bool->None), MarkerInfo import
    # Enabled 2025-12-20: check_untyped_defs globally
]

# Per-module overrides - stricter checking on critical parity modules
# Modules with return-value checking enabled (fixed 2025-12-19):
# - app.training.dynamic_export
# - app.training.value_calibration
# - app.training.gradient_surgery
# These modules must maintain type parity with TypeScript equivalents
# Note: check_untyped_defs is now enabled globally (2025-12-20)
# Per-module overrides can be used for stricter checks as needed
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["app.board_manager", "app.rules_engine", "app.game_state"]
# Future: enable stricter checks here as types improve
# disallow_untyped_defs = true

[tool.black]
line-length = 120
target-version = ["py310", "py311", "py312", "py313"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"

[tool.ruff]
# Target Python 3.10+
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 120

# Exclude common directories
exclude = [
    ".git",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "__pycache__",
    ".hypothesis",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "*.egg-info",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Enable these rule categories
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # Pyflakes
    "I",      # isort
    "B",      # flake8-bugbear
    "BLE",    # flake8-blind-except - catch broad exception handling (Phase 21.2)
    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "SIM",    # flake8-simplify
    "RUF",    # Ruff-specific rules
]

# Ignore rules that conflict with existing code style
ignore = [
    "E501",   # Line too long - handled by formatter
    "E402",   # Module import not at top - intentional lazy imports to prevent OOM
    "B008",   # Function call in default argument - common pattern in FastAPI
    "B904",   # Within except, raise from - too noisy
    "SIM108", # Use ternary operator - reduces readability
    "UP007",  # Use X | Y for Union - keep Optional for clarity
    "RUF012", # Mutable class attributes - false positives with Pydantic
    # TODO: Migrate to fire_and_forget() from app.utils.async_utils
    "RUF006", # Asyncio dangling task - intentional fire-and-forget patterns
    # Unicode in comments/docstrings - intentional for dimensions (8×8) and math notation
    "RUF001", # String contains ambiguous unicode
    "RUF002", # Docstring contains ambiguous unicode
    "RUF003", # Comment contains ambiguous unicode
]

# Allow fix for all enabled rules
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = []

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests can have unused imports and assertions
"tests/**/*.py" = ["F401", "F811", "B011"]
# Scripts may have broader imports
"scripts/**/*.py" = ["F401"]
# __init__.py files re-export symbols intentionally and group by migration status
"**/__init__.py" = ["F401", "I001"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["app"]
combine-as-imports = true
force-wrap-aliases = true

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

[tool.importlinter]
# Architecture tests - enforce dependency rules
# Run with: lint-imports
root_package = "app"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "AI layer should not import from training"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["app.ai"]
forbidden_modules = ["app.training"]
ignore_imports = [
    # Allow specific exceptions for cache utilities
    "app.ai.cache_invalidation -> app.training.eval_cache",
    "app.ai.cache_invalidation -> app.training.export_cache",
    # Legacy module - scheduled for deprecation (see DEPRECATION_AUDIT.md)
    "app.ai._neural_net_legacy -> app.training.encoding",
    "app.ai._neural_net_legacy -> app.training.model_versioning",
    # TODO: Move generate_data shared logic to app.core or app.data
    "app.ai.hybrid_gpu -> app.training.generate_data",
    "app.ai.nnue_policy -> app.training.generate_data",
    # Cache invalidation chain - uses config which imports training
    "app.ai.cache_invalidation -> app.distributed.data_events",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Models should be dependency-free"
type = "independence"
modules = ["app.models"]
# TODO: models.loader currently imports from ai and training for model loading
# This should be refactored to move loading logic to models layer
ignore_imports = [
    "app.models.loader -> app.ai.nnue",
    "app.models.loader -> app.ai.nnue_policy",
    "app.models.loader -> app.training.model_registry",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "app.main",
    "app.ai",
    "app.game_engine",
    "app.models",
]
# Allow same-layer imports and downward dependencies
# TODO: Refactor these dependencies to follow layered architecture
ignore_imports = [
    # Models layer importing from higher layers
    "app.models.loader -> app.ai.nnue",
    "app.models.loader -> app.ai.nnue_policy",
    "app.models.loader -> app.training.model_registry",
    # Legacy game engine imports caches from ai layer
    # TODO: Move cache modules to game_engine or core layer
    "app._game_engine_legacy -> app.ai.move_cache",
    "app.board_manager -> app.ai.territory_cache",
]

[tool.mutmut]
# Mutation testing configuration for mutmut 2.x
# Run with: mutmut run --paths-to-mutate=app/ai/neural_losses.py
# View results: mutmut results

# Source files to mutate (start with small, critical modules)
paths_to_mutate = "app/ai/neural_losses.py"

# Tests to run for mutation detection
runner = "python -m pytest tests/unit/ai/test_neural_losses.py -x -q --tb=no"

# Skip mutations in these patterns
dict_synonyms = "Struct, NamedStruct"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"
extend-exclude = [
    "venv",
    "data",
    "ds003969",
    "calibration_logs",
    "validation_logs",
    "database/migrations",
    "analytics/migrations",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# C901 = complejidad ciclomática (gate #6). E/F/W = pycodestyle+pyflakes base.
select = ["E", "F", "W", "C901"]
mccabe = { max-complexity = 10 }

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
explicit_package_bases = true
mypy_path = "."
exclude = [
    "venv",
    "data",
    "ds003969",
    "scripts",
