version = "0.124.0"
description = "DAZZLE — declarative SaaS framework with built-in compliance (SOC 2, ISO 27001), provable RBAC, and graph features"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = {text = "MIT"}
authors = [
    {name = "DAZZLE Contributors"}
]
maintainers = [
    {name = "DAZZLE Contributors"}
]
keywords = [
    "dsl",
    "saas",
    "compliance",
    "soc2",
    "iso27001",
    "rbac",
    "graph",
    "openapi",
    "llm",
    "domain-modeling",
    "application-framework"
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Code Generators",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Compilers",
    "Topic :: Internet :: WWW/HTTP :: Dynamic Content",
    "Topic :: Security",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "typer>=0.9",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "markdown>=3.5",
    # CLI entry + scene walks import httpx at load (walk.runner / session_manager).
    # Must be core so bare-wheel smoke (`dazzle --help` on Publish to PyPI) works.
    "httpx>=0.24.0",
    # psycopg3 is the single Postgres driver across the whole codebase (#1341):
    # the request-serving runtime (back/runtime/pg_backend.py), SQLAlchemy/Alembic
    # (postgresql+psycopg://), the tenant registry, AND the async `dazzle db` CLI
    # (dazzle.db.connection.get_connection → psycopg.AsyncConnection).
    "psycopg[binary]>=3.2",
    "psycopg-pool>=3.2",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0",
    "alembic>=1.14",
    "slowapi>=0.1.9",
    # faker is used by dazzle.demo_data (realistic seed fixtures)
    # AND by testing.ux seed/form-fill paths (see #809).
    # Was previously guarded with a try/except — promoted to a
    # required dep so qualitative trials and demo boots produce
    # realistic strings instead of "UX first_name 2f828c".
    "faker>=20.0",
    # segno renders the TOTP enrolment QR code server-side (DD-014). Pure-Python,
    # zero transitive deps. The pre-#829 flow loaded QR codes from api.qrserver.com,
    # leaking the TOTP secret to a third party; the QR never leaves the server.
    "segno>=1.5",
    # bleach sanitises rich-text widget input on the server side
    # (#977 cycle 4). The client-side schema enforcement in
    # dz-richtext.js is a UX layer; bleach is the security boundary.
    # Allowlist sourced from src/dazzle/core/ir/richtext.py — drift
    # gated by tests/unit/test_richtext_allowlist_parity.py.
    "bleach>=6.0",
    # itsdangerous is required by Starlette's SessionMiddleware, which
    # Authlib's `authorize_redirect` uses to stash the `state` parameter
    # between SSO initiate and callback. Previously gated behind the
    # `sso` extras (#1054) but its absence broke test collection for
    # tests/integration/test_sso_routes.py on every CI run that didn't
    # install the SSO extras. Tiny package (~7KB), no transitive deps —
    # promoted to core to make the SSO flow + its tests work out of
    # the box.
    "itsdangerous>=2.1",
    # PyJWT backs the default-mounted bearer-token routes (/auth/token et
    # al., #1105). It lived only in the [mobile] extras while jwt_auth.py
    # deferred `import jwt` into method bodies — so on a clean install the
    # routes mounted at boot and 500'd at request time on a public
    # endpoint (#1362). Default-on feature's deps belong in the default
    # install; pure-Python, no transitive deps beyond typing.
    "PyJWT>=2.8.0",
    # fastapi was historically in the [serve] extras, but dazzle.core
    # transitively imports dazzle.http.runtime (via appspec_loader →
    # back.runtime.renderers.init → back.runtime/server.py → file_routes,
    # search_routes, etc.) which all have unconditional `from fastapi
    # import ...` at module level. Without fastapi in core deps, even
    # `dazzle --help` and `dazzle validate` crash on a vanilla
    # `pip install dazzle-dsl`. Promoted to core so the PyPI wheel
    # smoke-test (which only installs core deps) can import and run
    # the CLI. Pre-existing breakage caught by `gh run list` showing
    # red PyPI publish on every release back to at least v0.67.70.
    # MAL-2026-4750 flagged fastapi 0.136.3 for the `fastar` transitive dep
    # in the [standard] extra. Investigation (#1278) confirmed `fastar` is
    # a legitimate Rust-tar binding used by fastapi-cloud-cli for zstd-tar
    # upload bundling — not a typosquat, not malicious. We don't take
    # fastapi[standard] anywhere, so we never install fastar regardless.
    # CI's pip-audit suppresses the false-positive advisory by ID; the
    # version pin here is unrestricted. If you need fastapi[standard]
    # features downstream, prefer fastapi[standard-no-fastapi-cloud-cli]
    # which upstream provides specifically as the opt-out variant.
    "fastapi>=0.100.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
llm = [
    "anthropic>=0.21.0",
    "openai>=1.0.0",
    "google-genai>=1.0.0",  # Vertex AI / Gemini (provider: google)
]
mcp = [
    # MCP Python SDK v2 — protocol 2026-07-28 (stateless core, on_* handlers).
    # See docs/reference/mcp-2026-07-28-opportunity.md and ADR-0002.
    "mcp>=2,<3",
]
graph = [
    "networkx>=3.0",
]
proof = [
    # z3-solver drives the RBAC meta-property prover (`dazzle rbac prove`,
    # WP-2) and the predicate-algebra SMT encoder (dazzle.rbac.encode_smt,
    # WP-1). Lazy-imported inside dazzle.rbac.encode_smt, so core installs
    # without [proof] are unaffected until `dazzle rbac prove` runs. See
    # docs/reference/rbac-proof-model.md for what the proof discharges.
    "z3-solver>=4.13",
]
e2e = [
    # Playwright drives the browser-based UX walks (`dazzle ux verify
    # --interactions`). Pinned >=1.40 for the sync-API shape used in
    # cli/ux_interactions.py. NOTE: after `pip install 'dazzle-dsl[e2e]'`
    # you still need `playwright install chromium` to fetch the browser. (#1376)
    "playwright>=1.40",
]
compliance = [
    "weasyprint>=60.0",
    "markdown>=3.5",
]
sso = [
    # Authlib drives the OIDC / OAuth2 dance for Google + Microsoft
    # SSO (Phase 1.C). Pinned >=1.3 for the modern starlette
    # integration; <2 because the API surface is still evolving and
    # we want to absorb breaking changes intentionally.
    "authlib>=1.3.0,<2",
    # itsdangerous moved to core deps in v0.67.96 (#1054) — required
    # by Starlette's SessionMiddleware whether or not authlib is
    # installed. Kept here for documentation; pip dedupes.
    # cryptography: AES-GCM secret-at-rest for enterprise Connections
    # (DD-013, dazzle.http.runtime.auth.connection_crypto) — lazy-imported,
    # so core installs without [sso] are unaffected until a connection is used.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    # dnspython: DNS TXT/CNAME checks for custom-domain host aliases
    # (ADR-0055, dazzle.http.runtime.tenant.aliases) and enterprise-connection
    # domain verification (DD-013) — lazy-imported inside the resolvers, so core
    # installs are unaffected until an alias or a domain is verified.
    "dnspython>=2.0",
]
signing = [
    # #1283 phase 2: native document signing primitive.
    # fpdf2 = pure-Python PDF generation (no system deps).
    # pyhanko = pure-Python PKCS#7 + PAdES B-T + RFC 3161 timestamps.
    # Pillow = signature PNG handling (pyhanko + fpdf2 both depend on it).
    # cryptography drives the ECDSA P-256 CA + signing cert chain in
    # dazzle.signing.cert (not in core deps — pulled in here).
    "fpdf2>=2.8.0",
    "pyhanko>=0.25.0",
    "Pillow>=12.3.0",
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
]
dev = [
    "pytest>=7.4",
    # starlette >=1.3 deprecates backing TestClient with httpx; httpx2 is the
    # successor it imports preferentially (StarletteDeprecationWarning otherwise).
    "httpx2>=2.12.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.3",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.2",
    "hypothesis>=6.82",
    "syrupy>=4.0",
    "mypy>=1.5",
    "ruff>=0.1",
    "radon>=6.0",          # framework structural-fitness: complexity (CC/MI)
    "import-linter>=2.0",  # framework structural-fitness: layer contracts
    "z3-solver>=4.13",     # RBAC meta-property prover gate (WP-1/WP-2); see [proof]
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0",
    "requests>=2.31",
    "mutmut>=2.4",
    # MAL-2026-4750 flagged fastapi 0.136.3 for the `fastar` transitive dep
    # in the [standard] extra. Investigation (#1278) confirmed `fastar` is
    # a legitimate Rust-tar binding used by fastapi-cloud-cli for zstd-tar
    # upload bundling — not a typosquat, not malicious. We don't take
    # fastapi[standard] anywhere, so we never install fastar regardless.
    # CI's pip-audit suppresses the false-positive advisory by ID; the
    # version pin here is unrestricted. If you need fastapi[standard]
    # features downstream, prefer fastapi[standard-no-fastapi-cloud-cli]
    # which upstream provides specifically as the opt-out variant.
    "fastapi>=0.100.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.24.0",
    "httpx>=0.24.0",
]
# On-demand local OpenTelemetry tracing for `dazzle perf` (#1153 follow-on).
# Local-only by design — the bundled SQLite span exporter writes traces to
# `.dazzle/perf/<run-id>.db`. No OTLP collector required; users who want
# upstream collectors can pair this extra with their own exporter config.
perf = [
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.27,<2",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.27,<2",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.48b0,<1",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-psycopg>=0.48b0,<1",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-asyncio>=0.48b0,<1",

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/manwithacat/dazzle"
Documentation = "https://github.com/manwithacat/dazzle/blob/main/docs"
Repository = "https://github.com/manwithacat/dazzle"
Issues = "https://github.com/manwithacat/dazzle/issues"
Changelog = "https://github.com/manwithacat/dazzle/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"

# Console script entry point for `dazzle` command.
# Package name on PyPI: dazzle-dsl  |  Import name: dazzle
[project.scripts]
dazzle = "dazzle.cli:main"

# Local + CI + Heroku (uv buildpack) all provision Python via uv.
# `only-managed` refuses system/pyenv interpreters so `.python-version` (3.14)
# is a single source of truth and a missing pyenv install cannot hijack sync.
# Floor remains requires-python >=3.12; CI still matrices 3.12/3.13/3.14.
[tool.uv]
python-preference = "only-managed"

# Transitive floor, not a dependency claim. weasyprint and fpdf2 also
# pull pillow. The Oct 2026 collection scatter
# (ImageColor, ImageFile, jwt, hypothesis — 3.12 and 3.13 only) was the uv
# runner deleting the job venv. Linux wheels of 12.3.0 import ImageColor and
# ImageFile on 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 (Actions run 37811834250), so the <12
# hold is gone. Keep the floor at the patched release.
constraint-dependencies = [
    "pillow>=12.3.0",
    # Transitive (pyhanko, aiobotocore). 3.14.4 patches
    # unbounded memory/CPU use, a missing initial request/header timeout and
    # an unenforced Secure cookie attribute (Dependabot alerts 62–64).
    "aiohttp>=3.14.4",
]

[tool.setuptools]
package-dir = {"" = "src"}

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
include = ["dazzle*"]
namespaces = false

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
dazzle = ["py.typed"]
# Alembic migration assets (#1308). The `dazzle db` CLI loads these by file
# path via `version_locations` / `script_location` — they are NOT importable
# modules, so without this entry they're dropped from the wheel: `script.py.mako`
# (autogenerate template → `revision --autogenerate` fails), `alembic.ini`, and
# crucially the framework BASELINE migrations under `versions/` (which has no
# `__init__.py`, so `packages.find` with `namespaces=false` never discovers it —
# every pip install was missing 0001–0004). The `versions/*.py` glob ships them
# as data files regardless of package status.
"dazzle.http.alembic" = ["*.mako", "*.ini", "versions/*.py"]
"dazzle.compliance" = ["css/*.css", "templates/*.html", "frameworks/*.yaml"]
# Workspace chrome static assets — literal HTML+JS blobs the typed
# Fragment renderer emits verbatim (e.g. WorkspaceDrawer markup +
# IIFE script). Read at module-import time, then cached.
"dazzle.render.fragment.static" = ["*.html"]
# Dazzle UI runtime static files. The tree lives under
# dazzle/page/runtime/static/, whose OWNING PACKAGE is dazzle.page.runtime
# (static/ has no __init__.py, so neither "dazzle.page" nor
# "dazzle.page.runtime.static" ever matched anything — both keys were removed
# 2026-10-16). This one key is kept in agreement with the MANIFEST.in
# recursive-include: JS/CSS/MJS bundles, the Geist fonts + OFL.txt (#1572; OFL
# 1.1 requires the licence to accompany font distribution), the default
# favicon (*.svg) and the theme manifests (css/themes/*.toml) that
# app_theme_registry reads at runtime.
"dazzle.page.runtime" = [
    "static/**/*.js",
    "static/**/*.css",
    "static/**/*.mjs",
    "static/**/*.woff2",
    "static/**/*.svg",
    "static/css/themes/*.toml",
    "static/fonts/OFL.txt",
]
# Agent-command TOML definitions (#1589): dazzle agent sync/seed load
# definitions/*.toml via Path relative to loader.py. definitions/ has no
# __init__.py so packages.find omits it — same class as #1032/#1308/#1572.
"dazzle.services.agent_commands" = ["definitions/*.toml"]
# API Knowledgebase pack TOMLs (#1616) — search_select fragment sources load
# packs via Path relative to loader.py (companies_house/lookup.toml etc.).
# Provider dirs have no __init__.py so packages.find omits them — same class
# as #1032/#1308/#1572/#1589 (asset exists in-repo, wheel drops it).
"dazzle.api_kb" = ["**/*.toml"]
# Scene walk + job claim JSON Schemas (#1638)
"dazzle.testing.walk" = ["schemas/*.json"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "-ra",
]
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests",
    "integration: Integration tests",
    "slow: Slow tests (subprocess spawning, full validation)",
    "e2e: End-to-end tests for Dazzle runtime",
    "story: User story tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "access_control: Permission/access control tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "state_machine: State transition tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "invariant: Business rule/invariant tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "computed: Computed field tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "personas: Persona-related tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "data_management: Data reset/regenerate tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "state: State persistence tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "display: Display/UI element tests (FieldTest Hub)",
    "corpus: Parser corpus golden snapshot tests",
    "visual: Playwright-driven visual smoke tests (requires Chromium)",
    "postgres: Tests requiring a live PostgreSQL connection (TEST_DATABASE_URL)",
    "migration_engine: DSL-snapshot migration engine (#1431) regression path — run with `pytest -m migration_engine`",
    "gate: Fast, DB-free structural/regression gate run by /ship pre-flight (`pytest -m gate`). Completeness enforced by test_gate_marker_complete.py.",
    # Auto-generated test markers — emitted by `dazzle test dsl-generate`
    # and `dazzle test tier2-generate` per CRUD operation, surface mode,
    # tier, and validation kind. Per-entity / per-persona marks are also
    # emitted dynamically (one per entity name / persona id) and can't
    # be enumerated here — they're ignored via the filterwarnings rule
    # on `PytestUnknownMarkWarning` below.
    "create: Auto-generated marker for create-operation tests",
    "read: Auto-generated marker for read-operation tests",
    "update: Auto-generated marker for update-operation tests",
    "delete: Auto-generated marker for delete-operation tests",
    "list: Auto-generated marker for list-surface tests",
    "view: Auto-generated marker for view-surface tests",
    "edit: Auto-generated marker for edit-surface tests",
    "crud: Auto-generated marker for combined CRUD test groups",
    "tier2: Auto-generated Tier 2 (Playwright) test marker",
    "playwright: Tests that drive a real browser via Playwright",
    "navigation: Auto-generated marker for navigation-flow tests",
    "transition: Auto-generated marker for state-machine transition tests",
    "transitions: Plural variant of `transition` from older generator",
    "invalid_transition: Auto-generated marker for state-transition negative tests",
    "valid: Auto-generated marker for happy-path validation tests",
    "invalid: Auto-generated marker for negative-validation tests",
    "validation: Auto-generated marker for validation-rule tests",
    "format: Auto-generated marker for field-format validation tests",
    "required: Auto-generated marker for required-field validation tests",
    "reference: Auto-generated marker for FK-reference validation tests",
    "denied: Auto-generated marker for access-denied tests",
    "high_priority: Auto-generated marker for high-priority test groups",
]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
filterwarnings = [
    # Harmless: DSLLever.construct is a domain term (DSL construct path)
    # that coincidentally shadows a deprecated BaseModel.construct method.
    # See src/dazzle/testing/ux/reconciler.py docstring.
    "ignore:Field name \"construct\" in \"DSLLever\" shadows an attribute in parent \"BaseModel\":UserWarning",
    # Auto-generated tests (`dazzle test dsl-generate`, `tier2-generate`)
    # emit per-entity / per-persona marks (`@pytest.mark.task`,
    # `@pytest.mark.engineer`, etc.) that can't be enumerated in the
    # static `markers` list above. Suppressing the unknown-mark warning
    # keeps generated-test output clean — the static
    # categorical marks (CRUD, surface mode, validation kind) ARE
    # registered above for completion.
    "ignore::pytest.PytestUnknownMarkWarning",
]
# Coverage is opt-in for faster local runs. Use: pytest --cov=src/dazzle --cov-report=term-missing
# Fast local run: pytest -m "not slow and not e2e"
# CI runs with coverage enabled via command line

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/dazzle"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_any_generics = true
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_no_return = true
follow_imports = "normal"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = false

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "dazzle.mcp.server"
# MCP SDK decorators are untyped
disallow_untyped_decorators = false

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "dazzle.rbac.encode_smt",
    "dazzle.rbac.prove",
]
# z3-solver ships no py.typed, so every z3 expression is Any. The RBAC SMT
# encoder/prover are a thin boundary over it; relax the Any-return warnings at
# that boundary (mirrors the mcp untyped-SDK override above). The predicate
# IR they consume is fully typed; only the z3 handles are Any.
warn_return_any = false
disallow_any_explicit = false

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "dazzle.http.runtime.island_routes",
    "dazzle.http.runtime.debug_routes",
    "dazzle.http.runtime.audit_routes",
    "dazzle.http.runtime.test_routes",
    "dazzle.http.runtime.social_auth",
    "dazzle.http.runtime.jwt_middleware",
    "dazzle.http.runtime.route_generator",
    # #1361 final slice: the CRUD/graph handler factories moved out of
    # route_generator into handlers/* — the override moves with the code.
    "dazzle.http.runtime.handlers.*",
    "dazzle.http.runtime.auth.routes",
    "dazzle.http.runtime.auth.routes_jwt",
]
# FastAPI app.get/post decorators on closure-scoped routes are untyped (app: Any),
# and the create/update route factories annotate the request body with dynamically
# generated per-entity Pydantic schema classes (runtime variables) — which mypy
# cannot treat as static types (valid-type). These are inherent to FastAPI's
# runtime-driven body binding, not the (now-removed) optional-import shim.
disallow_untyped_decorators = false
warn_return_any = false
disable_error_code = ["valid-type"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
src = ["src"]
exclude = [
    # Third-party packages accidentally installed into src/
    "src/PIL/",
    "src/contourpy/",
    "src/cycler/",
    "src/dateutil/",
    "src/fontTools/",
    "src/kiwisolver/",
    "src/matplotlib/",
    "src/mpl_toolkits/",
    "src/numpy/",
    "src/packaging/",
    "src/pyparsing/",
    "src/share/",
    "src/bin/",
    "src/*.dist-info/",
    "src/six.py",
    "src/pylab.py",
]

# ruff 0.16+ formats Markdown (fenced-code quote style). Keep README /
# docs examples author-owned; the CI format gate is for Python.
[tool.ruff.format]
exclude = ["**/*.md"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "I",    # isort
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",   # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "G004", # logging-f-string (use %-formatting for lazy evaluation)
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",  # function call in default arg - standard Typer pattern (typer.Option/Argument)
    "B904",  # raise from err - style preference, not critical
    "B027",  # empty method in abstract class - intentional default implementations
    "B011",  # assert False in tests - pytest uses -O mode differently
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["dazzle"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # Allow unused imports in __init__.py

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "build", "dist", "scripts"]
skips = [
    "B101",  # assert_used - we use asserts for type narrowing
    "B104",  # hardcoded_bind_all_interfaces - intentional for containerized apps
    "B110",  # try_except_pass - intentional for discovery patterns
    "B310",  # urllib_urlopen - we use with controlled localhost URLs only
    "B404",  # import_subprocess - we need subprocess for git, CLI tools
    "B601",  # shell injection - we use subprocess safely with list args
    "B602",  # subprocess_popen_with_shell_true - false positive, using for piping
    "B603",  # subprocess_without_shell - we intentionally avoid shell=True
    "B604",  # any_other_function_shell_true - using for npm/node commands
    "B607",  # start_process_with_partial_path - we use git/python which are in PATH
    "B608",  # hardcoded SQL - false positives on template strings
    "B311",  # random - used for demo simulation data, not security
]

# Post-#1044 (v0.67.92): djlint + jinja2 retired; the framework no
# longer ships any Jinja templates.

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["dazzle"]
include_external_packages = true

# Framework structural-fitness (B): lock the layer boundaries while they're still nearly
# clean. New cross-layer imports fail CI; the 2 pre-existing structural edges are
# allow-listed as documented known-debt (relocations tracked via the hotspot queue).
# Layer names: http → page → render → core (ADR-0041, renamed from back/ui 2026-06-20).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core stays http- and page-agnostic"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["dazzle.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["dazzle.http", "dazzle.page"]
# INDIRECT enforced (#1438): catches transitive core → … → http paths, not just direct
# imports. Flipped from allow_indirect once two spurious edges were removed — the package
# root `dazzle/__init__` is now lazy (no eager http), and the only indirect leaks were
# `core.discovery.engine`'s `import dazzle` (now derives its path from __file__) and a
# broken `core.ir.app_spec` typo in mcp/seed that grimp resolved to the root.
allow_indirect_imports = "false"
# core.process is the ADR-0008 runtime-bridge subsystem (not the pure IR/parser core);
# its eventbus adapter bridges to http's event framework. Tracked debt: inject instead.
ignore_imports = [
    "dazzle.core.process.eventbus_adapter -> dazzle.http.events.envelope",
    "dazzle.core.process.eventbus_adapter -> dazzle.http.runtime.auth.events",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "page must not reach into the http runtime"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["dazzle.page"]
forbidden_modules = ["dazzle.http"]
# INDIRECT enforced (#1438): no transitive page → … → http path either (the shared edges
# that leaked through the `dazzle` root were removed alongside the core contract).
allow_indirect_imports = "false"
# Allow-list driven to ZERO in the 2026-06-19 smells round: the lone violator,
# combined_server (the http+page composition root), relocated to http/runtime/ where it
# belongs (the composition root may import both layers). page ↛ http now holds absolutely.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "http is Postgres-only (ADR-0008)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["dazzle.http"]
forbidden_modules = ["sqlite3", "aiosqlite"]
# ADR-0008 forbids SQLite in http's RUNTIME, not transitive reaches into the MCP
# knowledge-graph / perf tracer (which legitimately use
# SQLite for their own stores, explicitly outside the app-data scope). So only DIRECT
# http imports of sqlite are a violation.
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "render is pure (ADR-0038)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["dazzle.render"]
forbidden_modules = ["dazzle.http", "dazzle.page"]
# render/ is the pure AppSpec→Fragment→HTML layer: it imports only render/core/stdlib,
# never up into http/page (top-level OR lazy in-function — grimp's graph catches both).
# Migrated here from the hand-rolled tests/unit/test_import_boundaries.py rule 4, which the
# back→http/ui→page rename silently turned VACUOUS (its regex still scanned for the gone
# `dazzle.back|ui`) — graph-based contracts survive renames; regex gates rot. INDIRECT
# enforced (#1438): render reaches only the pure parts of core, never core.process's
# eventbus bridge, so no transitive render → … → http path exists.
allow_indirect_imports = "false"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "http uses the core.ir facade, not concrete submodules"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["dazzle.http"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "dazzle.core.ir.appspec",
    "dazzle.core.ir.surfaces",
    "dazzle.core.ir.domain",
]
# #1086/#1092/#1093: http must import IR types via the `dazzle.core.ir` re-export facade
# (or `dazzle.core.ir.protocols`), not the concrete submodules — keeps the IR fan-in
# decoupled. Migrated from test_import_boundaries.py rule 3 (the one rule still real).
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core stays below the tooling layers (api_kb, mcp)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["dazzle.core"]
forbidden_modules = ["dazzle.api_kb", "dazzle.mcp"]
# core is the bottom layer; api_kb and mcp are tooling that sits ABOVE it (mcp imports
# core 144×, the correct direction). INDIRECT enforced, ZERO edges (#1438). Both
# inversions are registry-based: dazzle.mcp registers into core.docs_gen, and dazzle.api_kb
# registers its pack-ops provider into core.validation.surfaces (for the #996 `source=`
# typo check) — both at import time, so core never imports the tooling layers. The validate
# entry points import api_kb to activate the best-effort check.
allow_indirect_imports = "false"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.25"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "agentic-rag"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Retrieval-augmented question answering: HTTP service, Python SDK and in-process engine."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
license = { text = "MIT" }
dependencies = [
    "httpx>=0.27,<1",
    "pydantic>=2.7,<3",
]

[project.scripts]
agentic-rag = "agentic_rag.cli:main"

[project.optional-dependencies]
engine = [
    "pydantic-settings>=2.4,<3",
    "pymilvus>=2.5,<4",
    "openai>=1.60,<3",
    "numpy>=1.26",
]
parsers = [
    "pymupdf>=1.24",
    "python-docx>=1.1",
    "openpyxl>=3.1",
    "python-pptx>=1.0",
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.12",
    "lxml>=5",
]
server = [
    "agentic-rag[engine]",
    "fastapi>=0.115",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9",
    "prometheus-client>=0.20",
]
crewai = ["agentic-rag[engine]", "crewai>=1.14,<2"]
chroma = ["agentic-rag[engine]", "chromadb>=1.0"]
qdrant = ["agentic-rag[engine]", "qdrant-client>=1.12"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.24",
    "pytest-cov>=5",
    "ruff>=0.6",
    "mypy>=1.11",
    "import-linter>=2.1",
    "griffe>=1.5",
    "pip-audit>=2.7",
    "milvus-lite>=2.4; sys_platform == 'linux'",
]

[tool.hatch.version]
path = "src/agentic_rag/_version.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/agentic_rag"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers --strict-config"
markers = [
    "milvus: needs a Milvus engine (Milvus Lite locally, standalone in CI)",
    "slow: long-running tests, excluded from the default run",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error::agentic_rag.AgenticRagDeprecationWarning",
    "error::agentic_rag.AgenticRagFutureWarning",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "B", "UP", "S", "BLE", "RUF", "SIM", "C4", "PT"]
ignore = ["S101"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S", "B", "E501", "PT011", "PT012", "PT017", "PT018", "RUF005", "RUF059"]
"src/agentic_rag/testing/contracts.py" = ["PT018", "S"]
"scripts/**" = ["E501", "RUF005", "RUF059", "S603", "S607", "S101"]

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
python_version = "3.11"
mypy_path = "src"
packages = ["agentic_rag"]
explicit_package_bases = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["pymilvus.*", "pymupdf.*", "fitz.*", "docx.*", "pptx.*", "openpyxl.*", "bs4.*", "lxml.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.coverage.run]
source_pkgs = ["agentic_rag"]
branch = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["agentic_rag.adapters.parser_pdf"]
disallow_untyped_calls = false

# -- architecture contracts (framework section 2 and 12; run by `lint-imports`) --------------------------------

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "agentic_rag"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G1 layers: higher layers may import lower ones, never the reverse (exhaustive)"
type = "layers"
containers = ["agentic_rag"]
layers = [
    "cli",
    "server | embedded",
    "container",
    "config | api | client",
    "application | adapters | testing | sdk | models | extend | evaluation",
    "ports | contracts | registry",
    "errors | _compat | blocking",
    "_version",
]
exhaustive = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G1 adapters are independent of each other"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "agentic_rag.adapters.milvus",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.openai",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.lexical_bm25",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.chunker_recursive",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.parser_text",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.parser_html",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.parser_pdf",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.parser_docx",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.pipeline_direct",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.chroma",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.qdrant",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.crewai",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G4 routes reach the system only through the application service"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag.api"]
forbidden_modules = ["agentic_rag.ports", "agentic_rag.adapters", "agentic_rag.container", "agentic_rag.config"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 domain code imports no framework or adapter library"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag.ports", "agentic_rag.application", "agentic_rag.errors", "agentic_rag.registry"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "pydantic", "pydantic_settings", "fastapi", "starlette", "uvicorn", "httpx",
    "pymilvus", "openai", "crewai", "bs4", "lxml", "pymupdf", "fitz", "docx", "numpy", "torch",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 contracts import only the standard library and pydantic"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag.contracts"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "pydantic_settings", "fastapi", "starlette", "uvicorn", "httpx",
    "pymilvus", "openai", "crewai", "bs4", "lxml", "pymupdf", "fitz", "docx", "numpy", "torch",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 the thin client reaches only the standard library, httpx and pydantic (even indirectly)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag.client", "agentic_rag.sdk", "agentic_rag.models"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "pydantic_settings", "fastapi", "starlette", "uvicorn", "pymilvus", "openai", "crewai", "bs4", "lxml",
    "pymupdf", "fitz", "docx", "numpy", "torch", "chromadb", "qdrant_client", "agentic_rag.container",
    "agentic_rag.config", "agentic_rag.adapters", "agentic_rag.api", "agentic_rag.embedded",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 httpx is confined to the SDK"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag"]
forbidden_modules = ["httpx"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = ["agentic_rag.sdk.** -> httpx", "agentic_rag.client -> httpx"]

# One contract per heavy library: it may be imported only by its own package (direct imports only).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 pymilvus is confined to adapters.milvus"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag"]
forbidden_modules = ["pymilvus"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = ["agentic_rag.adapters.milvus.** -> pymilvus"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 openai is confined to adapters.openai"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag"]
forbidden_modules = ["openai"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = ["agentic_rag.adapters.openai.** -> openai"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 document libraries are confined to their parser"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag"]
forbidden_modules = ["bs4", "lxml", "pymupdf", "fitz", "docx"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "agentic_rag.adapters.parser_html -> bs4",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.parser_pdf -> pymupdf",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.parser_docx -> docx",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 web framework is confined to api and server"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag"]
forbidden_modules = ["fastapi", "starlette", "uvicorn"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "agentic_rag.api.** -> fastapi",
    "agentic_rag.api.** -> starlette",
    "agentic_rag.server -> fastapi",
    "agentic_rag.server -> uvicorn",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 prometheus_client is confined to api.metrics"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag"]
forbidden_modules = ["prometheus_client"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = ["agentic_rag.api.metrics -> prometheus_client"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 CrewAI and the other vector stores are confined to their adapters"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag"]
forbidden_modules = ["crewai", "chromadb", "qdrant_client"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "agentic_rag.adapters.crewai.** -> crewai",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.chroma -> chromadb",
    "agentic_rag.adapters.qdrant -> qdrant_client",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "G2 settings library is confined to config"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["agentic_rag"]
forbidden_modules = ["pydantic_settings"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = ["agentic_rag.config -> pydantic_settings"]

[project]
name = "knik"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "AI-powered voice assistant with async TTS processing"
authors = [{name = "Amreet Kumar Khuntia", email = "amreetleo123@gmail.com"}]
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = {text = "ISC"}
dependencies = [
    "croniter>=6.0.0",
    "nest-asyncio>=1.6.0",
    "psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.3.3",
]

# Note: Ruff configuration is in .ruff.toml

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["src"]
testpaths = ["tests"]

# Dependency rules, checked by `lint-imports` (run with PYTHONPATH=src).
# Apps sit on top and never import each other; lib never imports an app or the app-only hub.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["backend", "bot", "console", "worker", "lib"]
# `imports` is a single module, so it is checked as an external module rather than a root package.
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Apps are independent of each other"
type = "independence"
modules = ["backend", "bot", "console", "worker"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Library code never imports apps or the app import hub"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lib"]
forbidden_modules = ["backend", "bot", "console", "worker", "imports"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Integration services are independent of each other (services.db is the shared foundation)"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "lib.services.ai_client",
    "lib.services.browser",
    "lib.services.shell",
    "lib.services.telegram",
    "lib.services.tts",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The database service imports no other service"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["lib.services.db"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "lib.services.ai_client",
    "lib.services.browser",
    "lib.services.shell",
    "lib.services.telegram",
    "lib.services.tts",
]

# Higher layers may import lower ones, never the reverse. workflows and commands sit side by side and
# do not import each other; services never reach up to tools, workflows or commands.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "lib layers: tools over workflows and commands (independent) over services over utils over core"
type = "layers"
containers = ["lib"]
layers = [
    "tools",
    "workflows | commands",
    "services",
    "utils",
    "core",
]

[project]
name = "ritam"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Cost-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation service for measuring and controlling LLM inference spend."
readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [
  { name = "Vishal Bhargava", email = "vish.bhargava91@gmail.com" }
]
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
  "contextvars>=2.4",
  "fastapi>=0.139.0",
  "fastembed>=0.8.0",
  "google-genai>=2.10.0",
  "pydantic>=2.13.4",
  "pydantic-settings>=2.14.2",
  "pytest-mock>=3.15.1",
  "qdrant-client>=1.18.0",
  "sqlalchemy>=2.0.51",
  "sqlmodel>=0.0.39",
  "starlette>=1.3.1",
  "typer>=0.26.8",
  "uvicorn[standard]>=0.51.0",
]

[project.scripts]
ritam = "ritam:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build>=0.9.12,<0.10.0"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "httpx>=0.28.1",
  "import-linter>=2.1",
  "ruff>=0.15.16",
  "mypy>=2.1.0",
  "pytest>=9.0.3",
  "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ruff
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py314"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", # pycodestyle errors
  "F", # pyflakes
  "UP", # pyupgrade — use modern Python syntax (the main ask)
  "B", # flake8-bugbear — real bugs and design issues
  "SIM", # flake8-simplify — unnecessarily verbose patterns
  "I", # isort — import ordering
  "C90", # McCabe complexity
  "RUF", # Ruff-specific rules
]
ignore = [
  "E501", # line too long — ruff-format handles this
  "B008", # function calls in default arguments — FastAPI Depends() uses this
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["ritam"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mypy
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true
warn_unused_configs = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# google-genai ships no py.typed marker or bundled stubs
module = ["google.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pytest
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--cov=src/ritam --cov-report=term-missing"
testpaths = ["tests"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "ritam"
source_paths = ["src"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Enforce layered architecture"
type = "layers"
# Each line is one layer. A module may only import from layers below it.
# Modules on the same line (separated by |) are independent of each other.
layers = [
  "ritam.api",
  "ritam.core",
  "ritam.document_source",
  "ritam.retrieval",
  "ritam.vector_store",
  "ritam.llm",
  "ritam.cost",
  "ritam.observability | ritam.config",
]

[project]
name = "pyproj_dep_analyze"
version = "4.0.9"
description = "Python project dependency analyzer"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
    "rich-click>=1.9.9",
    # click is imported directly (cli.py subclasses click.ParamType), so declare it rather
    # than free-riding on rich-click, which only requires click>=8. The floor is 8.4:
    # ParamType became generic there, and EnumChoice subscripts it (TypeError on click<8.4).
    "click>=8.5.0",
    "lib_cli_exit_tools>=2.4.1",
    "lib_log_rich>=6.5.3",
    "lib_layered_config>=7.1.9",
    "httpx2>=2.13.1",
    "pydantic>=2.14.1",
    "rtoml>=0.14.0",
]
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "bitranox", email = "bitranox@gmail.com" }]
keywords = ["dependency", "analyzer", "pyproject", "outdated", "version", "cli"]
classifiers = [
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.15",
  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Environment :: Console",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]

# System packages required for CI runners (read by GitHub Actions workflow template)
# Format: "apt_package_name" for Ubuntu, future: {"apt": "...", "brew": "...", "choco": "..."}
[tool.ci]
system-dependencies-ubuntu = []
system-dependencies-macos = []
system-dependencies-windows-pip = []
system-dependencies-windows-choco = []
os = ["ubuntu-latest", "windows-latest", "macos-latest"]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/bitranox/pyproj_dep_analyze"
Repository = "https://github.com/bitranox/pyproj_dep_analyze.git"
Issues = "https://github.com/bitranox/pyproj_dep_analyze/issues"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
  "pytest>=9.1.1",
  "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
  "ruff>=0.17.0",
  "pyright[nodejs]>=1.1.414",
  "bandit>=1.9.4",
  "build>=1.6.1",
  "hatchling>=1.32.4",
  "twine>=7.0.0",
  # codecov-cli is disabled, not dropped: it requires click<8.3.0, which holds click at
  # 8.2.1 (CVE-2026-7246). Worse, bmk requires click>=8.4.2, so uv cannot satisfy both and
  # silently BACKTRACKS bmk to 3.1.7 - this repo stopped receiving bmk updates entirely,
  # with no error. Verified nothing is lost: CI uploads coverage via codecov/codecov-action
  # (.github/workflows/default_cicd_public.yml) and nothing here invokes the CLI.
  # Re-enable once codecov-cli relaxes its click<8.3.0 pin.
  # "codecov-cli>=11.3.1",
  "pip-audit>=2.10.1",
  "textual>=8.2.8",
  "import-linter>=2.15"
]

[project.scripts]
pyproj_dep_analyze = "pyproj_dep_analyze.cli:main"
pyproj-dep-analyze = "pyproj_dep_analyze.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"



[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/pyproj_dep_analyze"]
include = ["src/pyproj_dep_analyze/py.typed", "src/pyproj_dep_analyze/defaultconfig.toml"]

# An allowlist, never a denylist: hatchling reads only the root .gitignore, so tracked working
# files and files hidden through .git/info/exclude or a nested .gitignore (session records,
# review notes, helper scripts) would ship. tests/test_packaging.py builds the sdist and
# refuses any other top-level entry.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
    "/src/pyproj_dep_analyze",
    "/tests",
    "/docs",
    "/README.md",
    "/LICENSE",
    "/CHANGELOG.md",
    "/pyproject.toml",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 160
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", "W",     # pycodestyle
  "F",           # pyflakes
  "I",           # isort
  "N",           # pep8-naming
  "UP",          # pyupgrade
  "B",           # bugbear
  "A",           # builtins shadowing
  "C4",          # comprehension simplification
  "C90",         # mccabe: cyclomatic complexity <= 10 (the house hard limit)
  "SIM",         # simplification
  "TCH",         # type-checking imports
  "RUF",         # ruff-specific
  "G",           # logging format (catches f-string in logger)
  "T20",         # print statements
  "PTH",         # pathlib preference
  "PLC", "PLE",  # pylint conventions/errors
  "S",           # flake8-bandit security checks
  "PERF",        # performance anti-patterns
  "ERA",         # eradicate dead/commented-out code
  "FBT",         # boolean trap (boolean positional args)
  "PLR",         # pylint refactor
  "PLW",         # pylint warnings
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
# The Pydantic models across config.py/models.py/schemas.py/repo_resolver.py/cli.py
# resolve their field annotations at model-build time, so their field-type imports
# must stay at runtime. Telling ruff about the Pydantic base keeps TC001/TC002/TC003
# from moving those imports into a TYPE_CHECKING block and breaking model construction.
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# ignore the "unused import sys" in the jupyter notebook - which we need (it is a linter hickup)
"notebooks/*.ipynb" = ["F401"]
# Tests: assert is standard, test fixtures have passwords, magic values are clearer inline, temp paths are fine.
# PLC0415: local/deferred imports are a deliberate test idiom - several tests import inside the test
# body to exercise import-time and cache behaviour, so moving them to module top would defeat intent.
# PERF203: a couple of tests loop over ~100 real-world pyproject.toml fixtures and skip the
# handful with deliberately-invalid TOML per item - test runtime, not production hot-path perf.
"tests/*.py" = ["S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "T20", "PLR2004", "PLR0913", "FBT001", "FBT003", "PLC0415", "PERF203"]
# CLI: Click commands legitimately need many options; Click injects them by keyword
# (all other boolean params in this file are already keyword-only - see cli_analyze).
"src/pyproj_dep_analyze/cli.py" = ["PLR0913"]

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
extraPaths = [
  "src",
]
exclude = [
  "scripts/menu.py",
  ".venv",
  ".venv-win",
  ".venv-bmk",
  ".venv*",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = ["--doctest-modules", "-m", "not slow"]
doctest_optionflags = ["ELLIPSIS", "NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
markers = [
  "os_agnostic: test runs on every supported operating system",
  "os_windows: test exercises Windows-only behavior",
  "os_macos: test exercises macOS-only behavior",
  "os_posix: test exercises behavior requiring POSIX semantics",
  "os_linux: test exercises Linux-only behavior",
  "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
  "e2e: end-to-end tests with real API calls (implies slow)",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
parallel = false
data_file = ".coverage.unit"
source = ["src/pyproj_dep_analyze"]

[tool.coverage.report]
omit = [
  "tests/*",
]
fail_under = 84
show_missing = true

[tool.coverage.json]
output = "coverage.json"
pretty_print = true

[tool.clean]
# Patterns to remove when running `make clean`
patterns = [
  "**/__pycache__",
  ".hypothesis",
  ".import_linter_cache",
  ".pytest_cache",
  ".ruff_cache",
  ".pyright",
  ".mypy_cache",
  ".tox",
  ".nox",
  ".eggs",
  "*.egg-info",
  "build",
  "dist",
  "htmlcov",
  ".coverage",
  "coverage.xml",
  "codecov.sh",
  ".cache",
  "result",
]

[tool.git]
# Default git remote for push/release commands
default-remote = "origin"


[tool.scripts.test]
# Configuration for scripts/test.py test runner
pytest-verbosity = "-vv"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

  "pyproj_dep_analyze.analyzer",
  "pyproj_dep_analyze.index_resolver | pyproj_dep_analyze.repo_resolver | pyproj_dep_analyze.version_resolver",
  "pyproj_dep_analyze.dependency_extractor | pyproj_dep_analyze.python_version_parser",

[tool.pip-audit]
# Known vulnerabilities to ignore (unfixable or accepted risk)
# GHSA-4xh5-x5gv-qwph: py library ReDoS (no fix available, low risk)
# PYSEC-2022-42969: same as above (alias)
# CVE-2025-66418, CVE-2025-66471: urllib3 vulnerabilities (pending upstream fix)
# PYSEC-2022-43012, PYSEC-2025-49, CVE-2024-6345: setuptools vulnerabilities (CI uses older version)
# CVE-2026-25990: Pillow OOB write via crafted PSD image (transitive dev/build dep; fixed upstream in 12.1.1)
# CVE-2026-26007: pyca cryptography small-subgroup attack on SECT curves (transitive via twine/keyring; fixed in 46.0.5)
# CVE-2026-4539: Pygments AdlLexer ReDoS, local-only DoS (transitive via rich; low risk)
# CVE-2026-25645: requests extract_zipped_paths temp-file reuse; helper unused by us (fixed upstream in 2.33.0)
# CVE-2026-44405: paramiko allows SHA-1 for RSA keys; NOT a dependency of this project (shared-venv audit noise), no fix available
ignore-vulns = ["GHSA-4xh5-x5gv-qwph", "PYSEC-2022-42969", "CVE-2025-66418", "CVE-2025-66471", "PYSEC-2022-43012", "PYSEC-2025-49", "CVE-2024-6345", "CVE-2026-25990", "CVE-2026-26007", "CVE-2026-4539", "CVE-2026-25645", "CVE-2026-44405"]

[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "1 day"
exclude-newer-package = {lib-cli-exit-tools = false, lib-layered-config = false, lib-log-rich = false}

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "6.2"
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Fail on unknown markers/config so marker discipline is enforced from the start.
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers --strict-config"
# pytest-asyncio: run `async def test_*` without per-test decoration.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
markers = [
    "unit: fast, isolated tests with no I/O or external services",
    "integration: tests that exercise multiple components or external resources",
    "e2e: end-to-end tests that run full workflows/runners",
    "contract: adapter<->port conformance tests",
]

# --- E6.T1: Import-linter contracts encoding dependency rules R1-R6 ---
# Authoritative source: docs/reports/phase2-target-architecture.md (§4 Dependency Rules).
# Run locally / in CI with: lint-imports
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = [
    "domain",
    "application",
    "infrastructure",
    "interface",
    "bootstrap",
    "shared",
]

# Layered architecture. Each layer may import only the layers BELOW it; siblings
# joined by "|" are independent (may not import each other). This single contract
# encodes:
#   R2  application -> domain only        (not infrastructure/interface/bootstrap)
#   R3  infrastructure -> domain only     (not application/interface/bootstrap)
#   R4  nothing imports bootstrap except interface
#   R5  domain pure (imports nothing above it; stdlib + shared only)
#   R6  shared -> nothing (bottom layer; everyone may use it, it uses no layer)
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture (R2, R3, R4, R5, R6)"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "interface",
    "bootstrap",
    "application | infrastructure",
    "domain",
    "shared",
]
# Pre-existing debt owned by DEFERRED tasks. Allowlisted so the contract stays green
# today while still failing on any NEW violation. Remove each entry as its owning task
# lands. This ledger was re-baselined in E6 graph-coverage: adding the missing
# __init__.py files raised grimp coverage from 142 -> 412 modules, surfacing 79 layered
# edges that were always present but invisible while their subpackages were skipped.
# Each block below is retired wholesale by the named task.
ignore_imports = [
    # --- E1.T4/T5: settings-injection bridge ---------------------------------------
    # Modules read bootstrap settings directly instead of receiving them via
    # constructor injection. Retired when E1.T4/T5 lands the injection seam.
    "application.configs.symbol_config -> bootstrap.settings.loaders",
    "application.configs.sync_settings -> bootstrap.settings.loaders",
    "application.symbol_management.centralized_symbol_manager -> bootstrap.settings.loaders",
    "infrastructure.strategies.strategy_config -> bootstrap.settings.loaders",
    "infrastructure.data.wfo_config -> bootstrap.settings.loaders",
    # --- E5-B: risk / execution / position-sizing wiring (golden-gated) ------------
    # E5-B.T1 (composition-root injection): strategy_adapters/risk_engine_adapter/
    # position_sizing_engine_adapter no longer import the canonical application
    # engines — the engine is built by bootstrap and injected (parity-gated by
    # test_risk_decisions + test_position_sizing characterization). Remaining
    # advanced_execution_service edge is INHERITANCE across layers (RiskAwareExecution
    # extends application ExecutionService) — needs a layer/composition design
    # decision, deferred.
    "infrastructure.execution.advanced_execution_service -> application.services.execution_services",
    "application.risk_management.enterprise_risk_manager -> infrastructure.tracking.trade_tracker",
    "application.risk_management.enterprise_risk_manager -> infrastructure.market_regime.regime_detector",
    "application.risk_management.enterprise_risk_manager -> infrastructure.logging.forensic_logger",
    # --- E5-B: backtest / walk-forward / optimization wiring (golden-gated) --------
    "application.walk_forward.wfo_orchestrator -> infrastructure.backtest.realistic_backtester",
    "application.walk_forward.wfo_orchestrator -> infrastructure.backtest.adapters.walk_forward",
    "application.walk_forward.wfo_orchestrator -> infrastructure.data.csv_history_loader",
    "application.walk_forward.wfo_orchestrator -> infrastructure.optimization.hyperopt_space",
    "infrastructure.backtest.adapters.walk_forward -> application.walk_forward.sliding_window_splitter",
    "shared.optimization_service -> infrastructure.optimization.hyperopt_space",
    # --- E4-deferred: data-ingestion / DTO wiring (infra.data -> application) -------
    "infrastructure.data.csv_history_loader -> application.dto",
    "infrastructure.data_sync.data_downloader_adapter -> application.dto",
    "infrastructure.data_sync.data_downloader_adapter -> application.configs.sync_settings",
    "infrastructure.data_sync.data_downloader_adapter -> application.configs.symbol_config",
    "infrastructure.data_sync.file_repository_adapter -> application.data_sync.ports",
    "infrastructure.data.configurable_historical_data_provider -> application.symbol_management.centralized_symbol_manager",
    "infrastructure.data._edp_pricing -> application.data_sync.sync_manager",
    "infrastructure.data._edp_availability -> application.data_sync.sync_manager",
    "infrastructure.data.enhanced_data_provider -> application.data_sync.sync_manager",
    # --- E5: data-sync / watcher-retune / workflow wiring (application -> infra) ----
    "application.services.watcher_services -> infrastructure.data.market_data_feed",
    # --- E5-A: reporting relocations awaiting dependency inversion (T1/T10) ---------
    "infrastructure.orchestrators.production_trading_orchestrator -> interface.reporting.live_dashboard",
    # --- E1-pattern: settings read directly (relocated event_system) ----------------
    # event_system was relocated shared/ -> infrastructure/messaging/ in E8.T4(b),
    # retiring its 5 R6 up-edges (-> domain/infrastructure). The remaining edge is the
    # E1 settings shim: SignalProcessor reads load_settings() on its trade-execution
    # path. Retired when settings injection reaches this singleton (E1-style; the
    # module-level singleton has no container seam yet).
    "infrastructure.messaging.event_system -> bootstrap.settings.loaders",
]

# R1: interface is user/operator-facing and must reach adapters only through the
# composition root, never by importing infrastructure directly. allow_indirect_imports
# keeps the legitimate interface -> bootstrap -> infrastructure path (the composition
# root wiring) from tripping the rule.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Interface must not import infrastructure directly (R1)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["interface"]
forbidden_modules = ["infrastructure"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
# Pre-existing debt surfaced by E6 graph-coverage (portfolio subpackage was invisible
# until its __init__.py was added). Three CLIs import the portfolio backtester's
# load_sample_strategies directly instead of routing through the composition root.
# Retired by E5.T6 CLI fat-wiring cleanup (route via bootstrap factory).
ignore_imports = [
    "interface.cli.comprehensive_portfolio_backtest -> infrastructure.portfolio.comprehensive_portfolio_backtester",
    "interface.cli.comprehensive_validation -> infrastructure.portfolio.comprehensive_portfolio_backtester",
    "interface.cli.extended_horizon_validation -> infrastructure.portfolio.comprehensive_portfolio_backtester",
]

[project]
name = "issue-orchestrator"
version = "0.10.0"
description = "Orchestrate AI agents working on GitHub issues in parallel"
readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    { name = "Bruce Gordon" }
]
keywords = ["ai", "github", "orchestration", "claude", "automation"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
]

dependencies = [
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "rich>=13.0",      # Nice terminal UI
    "textual>=0.40",   # TUI framework with keyboard input
    "fastapi>=0.104",  # Web dashboard
    "uvicorn>=0.24",   # ASGI server
    "jinja2>=3.1",     # HTML templates
    "sse-starlette>=1.6",  # Server-Sent Events for real-time updates
    "pluggy>=1.3",     # Plugin architecture (same as pytest uses)
    "transitions>=0.9",  # Lightweight state machine library
    "httpx>=0.27",     # GitHub HTTP client
    "PyJWT[crypto]>=2.10",  # GitHub App JWT signing
    "keyring>=25.0",   # OS keychain for secure token storage
    "pydantic>=2.0",   # Data-driven settings schema with validation
    "tenacity>=8.0",   # Retry with exponential backoff
    "pexpect>=4.8",    # Robust PTY handling for subprocess output capture
    "mcp>=1.0.0",      # MCP server support
    "pystray>=0.19",   # System tray icon (macOS menu bar / Windows tray)
    "Pillow>=10.0",    # Image handling for tray icon
    "defusedxml>=0.7",  # Harden XML parsing for untrusted reports
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
    "pytest-mock>=3.12",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.0",  # For e2e test timeouts
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5",  # Parallel test execution
    "pyright>=1.1.408",
    "ruff>=0.9",  # Fast Python linter
    "import-linter>=2.0",  # Architecture boundary enforcement
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.12",  # HTML parsing for template tests
    "lxml>=6.1.0",  # Fast HTML parser for BeautifulSoup
    "playwright==1.57.0",  # Pinned to avoid 250MB browser re-downloads on version bumps
    "pytest-playwright>=0.7",  # Playwright pytest integration
    "hypothesis>=6.0",  # Property-based testing
]

[project.scripts]
issue-orchestrator = "issue_orchestrator.entrypoints.cli:main"
coding-done = "issue_orchestrator.entrypoints.cli_tools.coding_done:safe_main"
reviewer-done = "issue_orchestrator.entrypoints.cli_tools.reviewer_done:safe_main"
exchange-respond = "issue_orchestrator.entrypoints.cli_tools.exchange_respond:safe_main"
verify-agent-sandbox = "issue_orchestrator.execution.sandbox_verify:main"
prepush-check = "issue_orchestrator.entrypoints.cli_tools.prepush_check:main"
# `main`, not a `safe_main` wrapper: `lane_run.main` is itself total over the
# lane exit-code contract (124 deadline, 78 configuration, 70 dispatcher fault,
# otherwise the lane's own code). A wrapper would guard this path only, so the
# contract would differ from `python -m ...lane_run`, which the Makefile uses.
# The agent-completion `safe_main`s exist to write a CompletionRecord on crash,
# an obligation lane-run does not have; `exchange-respond`'s exits 1, which
# here is a lane result code.
lane-run = "issue_orchestrator.entrypoints.cli_tools.lane_run:main"
issue-orchestrator-mcp = "issue_orchestrator.entrypoints.mcp_server:main"

# Plugin entry points - third-party packages can add their own
[project.entry-points."issue_orchestrator.plugins"]
# Built-in plugins are loaded directly, but listed here for reference
# tmux = "issue_orchestrator.adapters.terminal_tmux:TmuxPlugin"
# iterm2 = "issue_orchestrator.adapters.terminal_iterm:ITermPlugin"

# Optional packages can contribute API-key metadata without hardcoding
# provider-specific key names in the core package.
[project.entry-points."issue_orchestrator.ai_provider_keys"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/issue_orchestrator"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests", "packages/agent_runner/tests"]
pythonpath = ["src", "packages/agent_runner/src"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"
log_cli_format = "%(message)s"
# Emit per-testcase <system-out>/<system-err>/log records in the JUnit XML so
# the dashboard's captured-output viewer (validation_viewer.js) can render
# stdout/stderr/log per case instead of "not captured". Default pytest
# behaviour is junit_logging = "no", which strips captured output entirely.
junit_logging = "all"
filterwarnings = [
    # Python 3.14 warns about forkpty in multi-threaded processes.
    # Our PTY tests (pexpect.spawn) trigger this but run sequentially in xdist_group("pty"),
    # so deadlock risk is minimal. Safe to ignore until pexpect provides an alternative.
    "ignore:This process.*is multi-threaded, use of forkpty:DeprecationWarning",
]
markers = [
    "e2e: End-to-end tests with real GitHub (requires gh auth and E2E_TEST_REPO)",
    "heavy_e2e: Expensive journey-level tests for onboarding or full-stack orchestration flows",
    "improver_exam: Live improver exam (#7490) — runs the real improver model on a planted improver-data fixture and grades its findings; run via make test-improver-exam, never in PR validation",
    "tech_lead_exam: Live tech-lead exam (#7304) — plants known faults, runs the real engine and tech lead, grades the outcome; run via make test-tech-lead-exam, never in PR validation",
    "integration: Integration tests that may exercise external adapters",
    "live: Tests that require network access and external services",
    "live_agent: Tests that make real model calls; excluded from deterministic PR validation",
    "live_codex: Live Codex CLI smoke tests collected by e2e or dedicated live lanes",
    "live_deepseek: Live DeepSeek smoke tests (real API spend) — excluded from PR validation, run in the budgeted live lane",
    "xdist_group(name): Group tests to run serially under pytest-xdist --dist=loadgroup",
    "gh_activity_limit: Enforce GH API activity limits per test (test_gh_activity_limit, system_gh_activity_limit)",
    "requires_infra: Tests requiring external infrastructure (GitHub token, running services). Run in CI, excluded from pre-push.",
    "requires_backoff_pool: Live tests that need a pool started with IO_CONDOR_LOAD_BACKOFF=1; run only by the dedicated CI acceptance job.",
]

[tool.pyright]
include = ["src", "packages/agent_runner/src"]
pythonVersion = "3.14"

# Architectural import contracts (#149), enforced by `lint-imports` in CI.
# The package layering is routes -> services -> config -> serialization/models;
# higher layers may import lower ones, never the reverse. The only declared
# back-edge is serialization -> config, which exists purely under
# TYPE_CHECKING so config.py can import serialization at runtime without a
# cycle; exclude_type_checking_imports keeps those annotations-only edges out
# of the graph so the contracts describe runtime dependencies.

root_package = "nanoidp"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

name = "serialization has no runtime package imports"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["nanoidp.serialization"]

# runtime import from the package at all" (models included - today it is a
# TYPE_CHECKING import, and turning it into a runtime one is the likeliest
# regression). Wildcards need import-linter >= 2.1.
forbidden_modules = ["nanoidp.*"]

# Full ring layering (ADR 0034). Higher layers may import lower, never the
# reverse: adapters -> application -> ports -> domain. This subsumes the two
# targeted forbidden contracts that previously guarded application->adapters
# and ports->{adapters,application}, and adds the domain ring (domain may not
# name ports, application, or adapters). Packages outside the four rings
# (observability, testing) are deliberately unconstrained here. Note this
# catches by-name dependencies the
# Tier 0 sqlalchemy contract cannot: e.g. ports/readmodels importing
# eventsource.adapters.sql.readmodel_schema would break layering even though
# readmodel_schema itself imports no sqlalchemy (ADR 0029 gap, closed here).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Ring layering: adapters over application over ports over domain"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "eventsource.adapters",
    "eventsource.application",
    "eventsource.ports",
    "eventsource.domain",
]

# Out-of-ring settlement (ADR 0040). observability/ is the cross-cutting
# telemetry toolkit (OTel optional/guarded), consumed by application and
# adapters by design — but the two innermost rings must stay free of it:
# domain entities and port contracts carry no telemetry. testing/ is the
# public test toolkit; it imports adapters by design and no ring may ever
# import it back.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain and ports must not import observability"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "eventsource.domain",
    "eventsource.ports",
]
forbidden_modules = ["eventsource.observability"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Rings must not import the testing toolkit"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "eventsource.domain",
    "eventsource.ports",
    "eventsource.application",
    "eventsource.adapters",
]
forbidden_modules = ["eventsource.testing"]

# repositories.dlq) is resolved: projections/ and repositories/{checkpoint,dlq}.py were
# deleted in favor of eventsource.ports.{checkpoints,dlq} (pure) and
# eventsource.adapters.{sql,memory}.{checkpoints,dlq} (sqlalchemy-backed). See the
# projections-ring slice report for detail. The outbox slice went further and deleted
# eventsource.repositories/ outright: its sole remaining member (the transactional outbox)
# moved to eventsource.ports.outbox (pure) and eventsource.adapters.{memory,postgresql,
# sqlite}.outbox (backend-specific), so "eventsource.repositories" no longer exists to
# forbid above.

# eventsource.readmodels.schema (now eventsource.adapters.sql.readmodel_schema) lost its
# "must not import sqlalchemy" Tier 0 guard by design when it moved (ADR 0029 SS2.3): the
# guard asserted the wrong property. The module has never imported sqlalchemy -- it
# hardcodes POSTGRESQL_TYPE_MAP/SQLITE_TYPE_MAP and emits dialect-specific DDL text as
# plain strings -- but dialect knowledge is an adapter concern regardless of whether the
# code happens to avoid the sqlalchemy import to express it. The guard was not silently
# dropped; the property it should have been asserting (does this module encode
# backend-specific knowledge) was never "imports sqlalchemy" to begin with.

]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 160
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Explicit select pins the lint policy: ruff 0.16.0 widened its own default rule set from
# ~213 to ~920 rules when no select is configured, which is what turned this repo's CI red
# (a ruff-version regression, not a code regression). Matches the curated list used by the
# bitranox py-cli template and sibling repos derived from it.
select = [
  "E", "W",     # pycodestyle
  "F",           # pyflakes
  "I",           # isort
  "N",           # pep8-naming
  "UP",          # pyupgrade
  "B",           # bugbear
  "A",           # builtins shadowing
  "C4",          # comprehension simplification
  "C90",         # mccabe: cyclomatic complexity <= 10 (the house hard limit)
  "SIM",         # simplification
  "TCH",         # type-checking imports
  "RUF",         # ruff-specific
  "G",           # logging format (catches f-string in logger)
  "T20",         # print statements
  "PTH",         # pathlib preference
  "PLC", "PLE",  # pylint conventions/errors
  "S",           # flake8-bandit security checks
  "PERF",        # performance anti-patterns
  "ERA",         # eradicate dead/commented-out code
  "FBT",         # boolean trap (boolean positional args)
  "PLR",         # pylint refactor
  "PLW",         # pylint warnings
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# ignore the "unused import sys" in the jupyter notebook - which we need (it is a linter hickup)
# T201: notebooks are demonstrations - printing results to the cell output is the whole point.
"notebooks/*.ipynb" = ["F401", "T201"]
# Tests: assert is standard, test fixtures have passwords, magic values are clearer inline, temp paths are fine.
# PLC0415: local/deferred imports are a deliberate test idiom - several tests import inside the test
# body to exercise import-time and cache behaviour, so moving them to module top would defeat intent.
"tests/*.py" = ["T20", "S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "FBT001", "FBT003", "PLR0913", "PLR2004", "PLC0415"]
# CLI: Click framework injects many options per command; PLR0917 (positional count) is fixed via
# keyword-only params, but the total-argument-count rule PLR0913 still fires by design.
"src/finanzonline_databox/cli/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
# Application use cases: orchestration methods naturally take several collaborators/flags.
"src/finanzonline_databox/application/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
# Adapters: SOAP/email adapters carry many diagnostic/delivery fields by design.
"src/finanzonline_databox/adapters/**/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
# mail.py: send_email's options are already keyword-only (no PLR0917); the many named
# parameters mirror btx_lib_mail's own send() surface.
"src/finanzonline_databox/mail.py" = ["PLR0913"]
# i18n.py: N_ is the gettext/xgettext extraction convention (alongside `_`) for marking a
# string for translation without translating it now; renaming it breaks recognition by
# standard gettext/pybabel extraction tooling, which looks for the literal name `N_`.
"src/finanzonline_databox/i18n.py" = ["N802"]

    # same path ``developers.openai.com/codex/sdk`` documents — pinned to
    # ``rust-v0.129.0`` (matching the Codex CLI runtime version this integration
    # currently targets; earlier tags carry older generated app-server models,
    # and pre-0.126 tags carry the prior name ``codex-app-server-sdk`` and uv
    # refuses the rename mismatch). Replace with a normal version specifier once
    # the SDK is on PyPI.
    "openai-codex-app-server-sdk @ git+https://github.com/openai/codex@rust-v0.129.0#subdirectory=sdk/python",
    "typer>=0.9.0",

# that name; see the dependency comment above). Hatchling refuses direct
# references by default for safety; enabling it scoped to this project is the
# documented escape hatch
# (``hatch.pypa.io/latest/config/metadata/#allowing-direct-references``).
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src"]
artifacts = ["src/scripts/*.sh"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
# Ship the bundled Amp safety plugin inside the wheel next to the installer
# module so AmpPluginInstaller can resolve it after `uv tool install`.
# AmpPluginInstaller's resolver prefers this wheel-data path and falls back
# to the repo-root plugins/amp/ location for source/editable installs.
"plugins/amp/mala-safety.ts" = "src/infra/clients/_amp_plugin_data/mala-safety.ts"
# Ship the bundled Codex safety plugin tree inside the wheel next to the
# installer module so CodexPluginInstaller can resolve it after
# `uv tool install`. The resolver prefers this wheel-data path and falls
# back to the repo-root plugins/codex/ location for source/editable installs.
"plugins/codex/mala-safety/.codex-plugin/plugin.json" = "src/infra/clients/_codex_plugin_data/plugin.json"
"plugins/codex/mala-safety/.codex-plugin/hooks.json" = "src/infra/clients/_codex_plugin_data/hooks.json"
"plugins/codex/mala-safety/.codex-plugin/.mcp.json" = "src/infra/clients/_codex_plugin_data/.mcp.json"

invalid-type-form = "error"

unknown-argument = "error"

conflicting-declarations = "error"
conflicting-metaclass = "error"
cyclic-class-definition = "error"
duplicate-base = "error"
inconsistent-mro = "error"
invalid-base = "error"
unsupported-base = "error"

not-iterable = "error"

[tool.ruff.lint]
