    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
]

# =============================================================================
# Import Linter Configuration
# =============================================================================
# Enforces architectural boundaries between layers.
# Run with: uv run lint-imports (or: uvx --from import-linter lint-imports)
#
# Architecture:
#   cli -> orchestration -> pipeline -> domain -> infra -> core
#
# Contract categories:
# - Layered Architecture: enforces layer ordering
# - SDK/Typer confinement: external packages restricted to specific layers
# - Module isolation: hooks, telemetry, clients, tools boundaries
# - Leaf modules: models, log_events have no src imports
# - Aspirational contracts (commented out): future refactoring targets
# =============================================================================

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["src"]
include_external_packages = true

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 1: Layered Architecture
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enforces that higher layers cannot import from lower layers.
# This replaces most of the old layer-specific contracts.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered Architecture"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "src.cli",
    "src.orchestration",
    "src.pipeline",
    "src.domain",
    "src.infra",
    "src.core",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 14: CLI cannot bypass orchestration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI should go through orchestration layer, not directly to pipeline/domain.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "CLI cannot bypass orchestration"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.cli"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.pipeline", "src.domain"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 11: Domain subpackages independent
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Domain concepts should not depend on each other (except validation which is shared).

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain subpackages independent"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "src.domain.deadlock",
    "src.domain.lifecycle",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 12: Infra clients isolated
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Client wrappers should not depend on IO, hooks, or telemetry abstractions.
# Coder-backend providers (claude_provider, future amp_provider) are the
# documented exception: they bundle SDK + runtime + log-provider for a coder
# and necessarily reach into agent_runtime / session_log_parser. The
# whitelist is intentionally narrow so simple HTTP clients stay isolated.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Infra clients isolated"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.infra.clients"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.infra.io", "src.infra.hooks", "src.infra.telemetry"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "src.infra.clients.claude_provider -> src.infra.io.session_log_parser",
    "src.infra.clients.amp_log_provider -> src.infra.io.session_log_parser",
    # CodexEvidenceProvider reuses ``JsonlEntry`` from
    # session_log_parser as the structural carrier for parsed JSONL lines
    # (parity with AmpLogProvider, plan 2026-05-07-codex-provider-plan.md
    # F2/F3). The class is the single source of truth for the
    # JsonlEntryProtocol shape gate consumers expect.
    "src.infra.clients.codex_evidence_provider -> src.infra.io.session_log_parser",
    # AmpRuntime carries a LintCache for protocol parity with the Claude
    # runtime so AgentSessionRunner._build_session can read
    # ``runtime.lint_cache`` without branching on the active coder
    # (plan ``L165``: pipeline is coder-agnostic). Mirrors the Claude
    # path's AgentRuntimeBuilder, which lives outside src.infra.clients
    # and so does not need an exception.
    "src.infra.clients.amp_runtime -> src.infra.hooks.lint_cache",
    # CodexRuntime carries a LintCache for the same cross-coder parity
    # reason (plan 2026-05-07-codex-provider-plan.md L429).
    "src.infra.clients.codex_runtime -> src.infra.hooks.lint_cache",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 13: Agent runtime pure
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Runtime should only depend on core + low-level infra (hooks, mcp, tools.env).

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Agent runtime pure"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.infra.agent_runtime"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.pipeline", "src.domain", "src.orchestration", "src.infra.clients"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 14: SDK confined to infra
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# External SDKs (anthropic) and their wrappers should only be
# imported by CLI/orchestration/infra layers. Pipeline/domain/core cannot
# import either SDKs or their wrappers directly.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "SDK confined to infra"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "src.pipeline",
    "src.domain",
    "src.core",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "anthropic",
    "claude_agent_sdk",
    "src.infra.clients.anthropic_client",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 11: Only CLI imports typer
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# typer is only for CLI argument parsing.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Only CLI imports typer"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "src.orchestration",
    "src.pipeline",
    "src.domain",
    "src.infra",
    "src.core",
]
forbidden_modules = ["typer"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 12: Pipeline modules acyclic
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No circular imports within pipeline modules.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Pipeline modules acyclic"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "src.pipeline.agent_session_runner",
    "src.pipeline.gate_runner",
    "src.pipeline.review_runner",
    "src.pipeline.run_coordinator",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 13: Hooks isolated
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hook modules should not import from pipeline/domain/orchestration layers.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Hooks isolated"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.infra.hooks"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.pipeline",
    "src.domain",
    "src.orchestration",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 14: Telemetry abstraction pure
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Telemetry module should only contain protocols and null implementations.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Telemetry abstraction pure"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.infra.telemetry"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.infra.clients",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 11: Validation result minimal
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation result should not directly import heavy dependencies.
# Layers would allow domain->infra, but this needs stricter isolation.
# TYPE_CHECKING imports for type annotations are allowed via indirect imports.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Validation result minimal"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.domain.validation.result"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.infra.tools",
    "src.infra.io.config",
    "src.infra.io.log_output",
]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 12: Models is leaf
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Models should only contain data classes with no internal dependencies.
# Leaf modules: constraint is no-src-imports (stdlib is allowed).

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Models is leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.core.models"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.cli",
    "src.orchestration",
    "src.pipeline",
    "src.domain",
    "src.infra",
    "src.core.log_events",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contract 13: Log events is leaf
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Log events are pure data structures.
# Leaf modules: constraint is no-src-imports (stdlib is allowed).

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Log events is leaf"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.core.log_events"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.cli",
    "src.orchestration",
    "src.pipeline",
    "src.domain",
    "src.infra",
    "src.core.models",
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strict Additions: Expected to Pass
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain does not import infra"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.infra"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Pipeline does not import infra.clients"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.pipeline"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.infra.clients"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IO does not import clients"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.infra.io"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.infra.clients"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "IO does not import hooks"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.infra.io"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.infra.hooks"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Only session_log_parser imports core.log_events"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.core.log_events"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "src.infra.io.session_log_parser -> src.core.log_events",
    "src.infra.clients.amp_log_provider -> src.core.log_events",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Infra clients do not import IO, hooks, or telemetry"
type = "forbidden"

    "src.infra.io",
    "src.infra.hooks",
    "src.infra.telemetry",

allow_indirect_imports = true
ignore_imports = [
    "src.infra.clients.claude_provider -> src.infra.io.session_log_parser",
    "src.infra.clients.amp_log_provider -> src.infra.io.session_log_parser",
    # CodexEvidenceProvider reuses ``JsonlEntry`` from
    # session_log_parser as the structural carrier for parsed JSONL lines
    # (parity with AmpLogProvider).
    "src.infra.clients.codex_evidence_provider -> src.infra.io.session_log_parser",
    # AmpRuntime carries a LintCache for protocol parity with the Claude
    # runtime so AgentSessionRunner._build_session can read
    # ``runtime.lint_cache`` without branching on the active coder
    # (plan ``L165``: pipeline is coder-agnostic). Mirrors the Claude
    # path's AgentRuntimeBuilder, which lives outside src.infra.clients
    # and so does not need an exception.
    "src.infra.clients.amp_runtime -> src.infra.hooks.lint_cache",
    # CodexRuntime carries a LintCache for the same cross-coder parity

    "src.infra.clients.codex_runtime -> src.infra.hooks.lint_cache",

name = "Infra hooks do not import clients, IO, or telemetry"

[project]
name = "b3datetime"
version = "2.1.1"
description = "API REST para consultar horários de operação e dias de negociação da B3"
requires-python = ">=3.14"

# NOTA: este projeto NÃO deve ser instalado como pacote (nem com `pip install -e .`).
# Layout src: o pacote é `src/b3datetime/` e os testes o importam da árvore de trabalho
# via `pythonpath = ["src", "."]` (o `.` é para `tests.*`).
# Instalar faria o coverage registrar caminhos em site-packages, que não casam com
# `sonar.sources=src`, e o SonarQube reportaria 0% de coverage.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# pytest
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src", "."]
addopts = """
    -ra
    --strict-markers
    --strict-config
    --import-mode=importlib
    --cov
    --cov-report=term-missing
    --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
    --junitxml=junit.xml
    -m "not e2e and not diagramas"
"""
asyncio_mode = "auto"
markers = [
    "integration: depende de recurso real — Redis em localhost:6379 (db 15), calendário BVMF real ou lifespan real",
    "slow: constrói calendários reais do exchange_calendars",
    "api_fuzz: fuzzing da API inteira pelo contrato (Schemathesis); fica fora da mutação",
    "tempo: asserção sobre tempo de execução; fica fora da mutação (com N processos em paralelo, estoura e \"mata\" mutante por engano)",
    "e2e: ponta a ponta contra a imagem (E2E_IMAGE) ou uma URL (E2E_BASE_URL); fora da execução padrão, rode com -m e2e",
    "diagramas: render dos diagramas Mermaid no Chromium e Agentic Mermaid (precisam de `npm ci` em tests/docs); fora da execução padrão, rode com -m diagramas",
]
# Warnings viram erro: é o que impede deprecações do pydantic de voltarem.
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:dateutil",
]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# coverage
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.coverage.run]
include = ["src/b3datetime/*", "src/b3datetime/**/*"]
branch = true
# CRÍTICO: sem relative_files, os caminhos gravados no coverage.xml são absolutos
# (/home/runner/work/...), não casam com sonar.sources e o SonarQube mostra 0%.
relative_files = true
omit = ["src/b3datetime/__main__.py"]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 90
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_also = [
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# ruff
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py314"
line-length = 100
extend-exclude = [".history", "htmlcov", ".venv", "venv", "mutants"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",     # pycodestyle errors
    "W",     # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",     # pyflakes
    "I",     # isort
    "N",     # pep8-naming
    "UP",    # pyupgrade
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear (inclui B904: raise ... from e)
    "A",     # flake8-builtins
    "C4",    # flake8-comprehensions
    "SIM",   # flake8-simplify
    "RUF",   # ruff-specific
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async — detecta chamada bloqueante dentro de async def
    "S",     # flake8-bandit
    "PT",    # flake8-pytest-style
    "LOG",   # flake8-logging
    "G",     # flake8-logging-format (G004: f-string em log)
    "TRY",   # tryceratops
    "DTZ",   # flake8-datetimez
    "PL",    # pylint (convenções, refatoração, erros e avisos)
    "C90",   # mccabe: complexidade ciclomática (ver max-complexity)
    "FAST",  # FastAPI: response_model redundante (FAST001 = python:S8409 do Sonar), Depends sem Annotated
    "ARG",   # argumentos não usados
    "PTH",   # pathlib em vez de os.path
    "ERA",   # código comentado (código morto que sobreviveu como comentário)
    "PERF",  # anti-padrões de desempenho
    "FURB",  # modernizações (refurb)
    "RET",   # retornos inconsistentes ou redundantes
    "PIE",   # construções desnecessárias
    "BLE",   # except Exception cego
    "T20",   # print esquecido
    "PGH",   # type: ignore / noqa sem código
    "TID",   # banned-api: o relógio passa por get_current_datetime()
    "FLY",   # join estático → f-string
    "ISC",   # concatenação implícita de strings
]
# Avaliadas e deixadas de fora:
# - TC (flake8-type-checking): com as anotações adiadas do 3.14, mover imports para
#   `if TYPE_CHECKING:` quebra a resolução de anotações em runtime do FastAPI/pydantic.
# - D (pydocstyle): só estilo; as docstrings são em pt-BR e o Sonar já cobre o essencial.
# - FBT, EM, INP: estilo (booleans posicionais, mensagem de exceção em variável) ou
#   intencional (tests/ e scripts/ não são pacotes: --import-mode=importlib).
ignore = [
    "TRY003", # mensagens longas em raise: as mensagens em pt-BR são deliberadamente descritivas
    "E501",   # comprimento de linha: o formatter já cuida
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"datetime.datetime.now".msg = "Use get_current_datetime() (b3datetime.config): todo 'agora' passa pelo timezone das settings."
"datetime.date.today".msg = "Use get_current_datetime().date(): todo 'hoje' passa pelo timezone das settings."
"time.time".msg = "Para medir duração use time.perf_counter(); para 'agora', get_current_datetime()."

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = [
    "S101",    # assert é o ponto dos testes
    "S105",    # "senhas" hardcoded em fixtures
    "S106",
    "PLR2004", # números mágicos em asserts
    "PLR0913", # fixtures do pytest chegam como argumentos: o limite de 5 não se aplica
    "PLR0917",
    "PLC0415", # import local para referenciar o módulo exato que o monkeypatch altera
    "TID251",  # o relógio real é legítimo em testes (ex.: "hoje" do E2E contra a produção)
]
"scripts/**" = ["T201"]  # scripts de CI: a saída no terminal é o propósito
"src/b3datetime/main.py" = ["S104"]  # bind 0.0.0.0 é intencional em container
"src/b3datetime/config.py" = ["TID251"]  # get_current_datetime() é o único dono do relógio

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["b3datetime"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# mypy
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
# Strict em tudo — código, scripts de CI e testes: um teste mal tipado também é um
# teste que pode estar testando a coisa errada.
files = ["src", "scripts", "tests"]
mypy_path = "src"
explicit_package_bases = true
strict = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
warn_unreachable = true
show_error_codes = true
pretty = true

[tool.pydantic-mypy]
init_forbid_extra = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["exchange_calendars.*", "pandas.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# bandit
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", ".history", ".venv", "venv"]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# import-linter — arquitetura como contrato (job "Arquitetura")
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Camadas, de cima para baixo: entrypoint → composição (main) → routers → dependências →
# serviços → configuração. Uma camada só importa as de baixo. Os módulos-folha

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "camadas"
name = "Camadas: __main__ > main > routers > dependencies > services > config"

    "b3datetime.dependencies",

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "dominio-sem-web"

type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["b3datetime.services", "b3datetime.config"]
forbidden_modules = ["fastapi", "starlette", "uvicorn"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "redis-so-no-servico"

type = "forbidden"

    "b3datetime.services.calendar_service",
    "b3datetime.config",
    "b3datetime.middleware",

# Direto, não transitivo: routers chegam ao redis_service pela injeção de dependência,

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

type = "acyclic_siblings"
ancestors = ["b3datetime", "b3datetime.routers", "b3datetime.services"]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# código morto — job "Código morto"
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.vulture]
paths = ["src", "tests/dead_code/vulture_whitelist.py"]
# 60 é o mínimo do vulture: inclui funções, classes e atributos sem uso, que é onde
# está o valor (imports e argumentos mortos o ruff já pega com F401 e ARG).
min_confidence = 60
# Registrados no framework por decorador; o vulture não enxerga essa chamada.
ignore_decorators = ["@router.get", "@app.get", "@app.exception_handler"]
sort_by_size = true
# deptry: configuração em tests/dead_code/deptry.toml (ver o comentário de lá).

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# mutmut — teste de mutação (job "Mutação · mutmut")
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.mutmut]
# Layout src: o mutmut tira o prefixo "src." do nome do módulo — com o pacote em
# src/b3datetime, os mutantes se chamam b3datetime.*, igual ao __module__ (#52).
source_paths = ["src/"]
# Além de tests/ e pyproject.toml (copiados por padrão): o que os testes leem do disco.
# Faltar um aqui reprova a execução limpa e o job inteiro — .github/ faltou no push de
# #67; tests/architecture/test_convencoes.py agora confere.
also_copy = ["scripts/", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md", ".env.example", ".github/", "Dockerfile"]
do_not_mutate = [
    "src/b3datetime/__main__.py",                 # entrypoint de desenvolvimento
    "src/b3datetime/routers/openapi_examples.py", # só dados de documentação
    "src/b3datetime/static/*",                    # constantes e assets
]
# Mensagens de log: mutá-las gera mutantes que nenhum teste razoável mata.
do_not_mutate_patterns = ['logger\.(debug|info|warning|error|exception)\(']
# --no-cov: sem ele, cada execução parcial reprova no fail_under da cobertura e TODO
# mutante conta como "morto" — um score falso de 100%. -p no:randomly: a mesma ordem
# em toda execução, para o veredito de um mutante não depender de sorteio.
pytest_add_cli_args = ["--no-cov", "-p", "no:randomly", "-p", "no:cacheprovider"]
# Fora, para o veredito de cada mutante depender só do comportamento:
# - E2E (imagem) e o fuzzing da API inteira (`api_fuzz`: todas as rotas a cada exemplo);
# - arquitetura (lê o código-fonte, e o código mutado tem os trampolins do mutmut);
# - testes com asserção de tempo (`tempo`): com N processos em paralelo eles estouram;
# - integração: os N processos dividem o mesmo Redis (db 15), e o flushdb de um apaga os
#   dados do outro — "mortes" aleatórias. O que ela toca de src/ tem teste determinístico.
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = [
    "-m", "not e2e and not api_fuzz and not tempo and not integration",
    "tests/unit", "tests/api", "tests/property",
]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Limiares de qualidade do projeto (lidos pelos scripts de gate do CI)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
[tool.b3datetime.quality]
# Score mínimo do teste de mutação (scripts/mutation_gate.py). Ratchet: só sobe.
# Medido em #65/#66: 99,59% (730 de 733), idêntico em runs repetidos; os 3 sobreviventes são equivalentes documentados
# (allow_credentials=False explícito no CORS — o default do Starlette — e
# redirect_slashes=False trocado por None, que também é falso).
mutation_min_score = 99.0
# Headers de segurança da borda (Cloudflare) conferidos na produção pelo job de
# pós-deploy (scripts/cabecalhos_da_borda.py). `true` desde 2026-10-07, quando a borda
# passou a enviar as três regras do README (#77): uma regra desfeita no Cloudflare reprova
# o job. `false` só avisaria — o modo usado até a borda ser configurada.
edge_headers_required = true

# `sentence-transformers` is the ONLY package in this tree that requires torch,
# and it is needed by exactly one code path: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=huggingface, which
# runs a local model instead of calling an API. Everything else -- including the
# huggingface *chat* provider, which is an HTTP endpoint -- works without it.
#
# It is a group rather than a plain dependency because torch is not free. Measured
# 2026-08-31 on a cold interpreter: `import sentient.api.app` is 305 MB of RSS and
# 20 s with torch present, and 147 MB and 3.3 s without it. That gap decides whether
# the service fits a 512 MB host with room left for ingestion.
#
# It stays in `default-groups` so a fresh clone still behaves like main: `uv sync`
# installs it, and the huggingface embedding fallback (core/config.py's default when
# no EMBEDDING_PROVIDER is set) keeps working with no extra step. The deployed image
# opts out with `uv sync --no-default-groups`.
local-embeddings = [
    "sentence-transformers>=5.2.0",
]

# Error tracking and tracing. Deliberately NOT in `default-groups`, unlike
# `local-embeddings`: both integrations ship OFF, and a fresh clone that installs
# them anyway has not made them optional, it has only made them quiet. The
# deployed image opts in with `--group observability` on top of
# `--no-default-groups`.
#
# Both are guarded by a lazy import at the point of use, so a machine with the
# group missing and the DSN or key set logs one warning and carries on. An
# observability tool must never be a startup dependency of the thing it observes.
observability = [
    "sentry-sdk[fastapi]>=2.44.0",
    "langfuse>=3.11.0",
]
pgvector = [
    "psycopg[binary]>=3.2.10",
]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = ["dev", "local-embeddings"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/sentient"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM"]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line length is enforced by the formatter, not the linter
    # FastAPI *requires* calls in argument defaults: Depends(), File(), Form(),
    # Header() are sentinels the framework reads out of __defaults__ to build the
    # OpenAPI schema and pick a body parser. B008 is right about Python and wrong
    # about FastAPI, so it is off for the whole project rather than noqa'd per route.
    "B008",
]

# Strict typing is scoped to core/ and adapters/ on purpose (spec §9). Strict
# everywhere across a LangChain codebase produces hundreds of findings from
# untyped third-party surfaces, and a check that noisy gets disabled within a
# day. These two layers hold the Protocol seams, where type drift costs
# something.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["sentient.core.*", "sentient.adapters.*"]
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
warn_return_any = true

# The layer rule (spec §5): dependencies point one way only. A violation is an
# architectural regression, not a style nit -- if this fails, move the code, do
# not weaken the contract.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "sentient"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layers are one-directional: api -> services -> adapters -> core"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "sentient.api",
    "sentient.services",
    "sentient.adapters",
    "sentient.core",
]

[project]
name = "backend"
version = "0.1.0"

requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.14.3",
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    "html2text>=2025.4.15",
    "imap-tools>=1.11.0",

    "openai>=1.82.0",
    "pydantic>=2.12.5",

    "python-dotenv>=1.2.1",
    "requests>=2.33.0",
    "resend>=2.19.0",
    "supabase>=2.27.0",
    "tzdata>=2025.3",
    "urllib3>=2.8.0",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "coverage>=7.13.1",
    "import-linter>=2.15",
    "mypy>=1.13.0",
    "pip-audit>=2.10.0",
    "ruff>=0.14.14,<0.15",
    "tiktoken>=0.12.0",
]

[tool.ruff]
# Pinned: an unbounded version lets two environments lint the same tree differently.
required-version = ">=0.14,<0.15"
target-version = "py313"
# line-length stays at the default 88: the formatter already owns it, and changing it reformats every file.

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "F", "W",      # pycodestyle, pyflakes
    "I",                # isort
    "UP",               # pyupgrade (enforces the modern type hints CLAUDE.md asks for)
    "B",                # bugbear
    "C4",               # comprehensions
    "SIM",              # simplify
    "RUF",              # ruff-specific
    "ARG",              # unused arguments
    "PTH",              # pathlib
    "PIE", "N", "ERA",  # misc, naming, commented-out code
    "T20",              # no stray prints outside CLI surfaces
    "DTZ",              # naive datetimes (the app reasons in Chicago calendar days)
    "BLE",              # blind except
    "C901", "PLR0911", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR0915",  # size ceilings (see below)
    "FURB", "PERF",
]
ignore = [
    "E501",    # the formatter owns line length; what remains is long strings and URLs
    "SIM108",  # a ternary is not always clearer
    "SIM905",  # word lists written as one "...".split() string read better than a list literal
]
# Newsletter text uses typographic quotes and dashes; console output uses the info sign.
allowed-confusables = ["–", "‘", "’", "ℹ"]
# DS: tools/lint/check_docstrings.py, so ruff accepts `# noqa: DSNNN`.
external = ["DS"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests: mock signatures, fixture datetimes, factories with many fields.
"tests/*" = ["ARG001", "ARG002", "DTZ001", "DTZ005", "T20", "PLR0913"]
# CLI surfaces: printing is the job.
"utils/*" = ["T20"]
"tools/*" = ["T20"]
"ingest/email/process_emails.py" = ["T20"]
"ingest/scraper/process_scraped_newsletters.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/process_notification_queue.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/weekly_notification_queue.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/test_matcher.py" = ["T20"]
# Library modules that use print as logging. This list only shrinks: moving one to `logging` removes its line.
"ingest/email/email_parser.py" = ["T20"]
"ingest/scraper/newsletter_scraper.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/digest_data.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/rule_matcher.py" = ["T20"]
"processing/llm_client.py" = ["T20"]
"processing/llm_processor.py" = ["T20"]
"processing/weekly_report_generator.py" = ["T20"]
"shared/utils.py" = ["T20"]
# Pydantic fields use these aliases; a `type` statement makes a TypeAliasType,
# which Pydantic turns into a named schema reference instead of the plain type.
"models/types.py" = ["UP040"]
# One-shot maintenance scripts, ratcheted separately from the product.
"utils/calculate_token_costs.py" = ["C901", "PLR0912", "PLR0915"]
"utils/migrate_topics.py" = ["C901", "PLR0912", "PLR0915"]
"utils/cost_report_generator.py" = ["PLR0915"]

# Budget ceilings, not contracts: lower them freely, never raise them.
# Each sits at today's worst function, named in its comment; walk them down by
# splitting that function. tests/unit/test_lint_budgets.py holds them in place.
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 21   # ingest/email/email_parser.sanitize_content

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 8          # analytics/terms.compute_distinctive_terms, compute_rising_terms
max-returns = 9       # processing/weekly_report_generator.generate_weekly_topic_report
max-branches = 21     # ingest/email/email_parser.sanitize_content
max-statements = 65   # notifications/process_notification_queue.process_digests


[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["analytics", "config", "ingest", "models", "notifications", "processing", "prompts", "shared", "tools", "utils"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["."]
omit = ["tests/*", "tools/*", ".venv/*", "samples/*", "migrations/*"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 1
# Erosion backstop, not a target: raise it as coverage rises, keep ~2 pts under.
fail_under = 59
exclude_also = ["if TYPE_CHECKING:", "if __name__ == .__main__.:", "raise NotImplementedError"]

[project]

version = "0.1.0"

]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]

include_external_packages = False

; 合同1：models 层不得依赖 services/api 层。

forbidden_modules =
    app.services
    app.api

; 合同2：services 层不得依赖 api 层。

    app.services
forbidden_modules =
    app.api

# Opt-in tool-result compression engine (Rust ext: headroom._core). We call the
# SmartCrusher / LogCompressor transforms directly — never headroom.compress — so
# the engine's heavy core deps (litellm, ast-grep-cli) are neutralized below via
# [tool.uv] exclude-dependencies. Base install omits this group, so the import in
# app/llm/headroom_compress.py fails safe and compression no-ops.

    "headroom-ai==0.35.0",
]
dev = [
    # Testing - Core
    "pytest>=9.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=7.0.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    # Testing - Essential Plugins
    "pytest-mock>=3.15.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.4.0",
    "pytest-randomly>=3.16.0",
    # Linting & Type Checking
    "ruff>=0.15.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0.0",
    "ty>=0.0.17",
    "types-jsonschema>=4.26.0",
    "types-redis>=4.6.0",
]

exclude-dependencies = ["litellm", "ast-grep-cli"]

    "aiohttp>=3.14.3",

# ===========================================================================
# Architecture & hygiene gates (DEV/CI only — never imported by the runtime).
#
# These three tools are keyless OSS and live exclusively in the `dev` extra.
# They are NOT runtime dependencies and require no API key.
#
#   import-linter  — machine-checks the package layering contract
#   vulture        — dead-code detector
#   deptry         — dependency-hygiene checker
#
# All three are authored to pass on `main` TODAY. They gate *future* drift:
# a new back-edge, a new import of a deprecated shim, dead code, or an
# undeclared dependency turns CI red. Run locally with:
#
#   lint-imports
#   vulture src/na0s .vulture_whitelist.py --min-confidence 80
#   deptry src
# ===========================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter — package layering contract
#
# The contracts below were derived from the REAL import graph on `main`
# (grimp build_graph), not a guessed design. Two facts shaped them:
#
#  1. detectors / rules / validation are a true import CYCLE (an SCC):
#       rules.rules_registry  -> detectors.{recon,privacy_probe}
#       detectors.*           -> rules.{result,context}
#       validation.positive   -> rules ; detectors.multi_turn -> validation
#     They therefore CANNOT be split across layers. They are modeled as one
#     cohesive tier using the ':' (non-independent) operator, which permits
#     intra-tier imports while still forbidding the tier from importing any
#     layer above it.
#
#  2. predict.py / cascade.py are orchestrator HUBS that import almost the
#     whole stack. A handful of leaf modules import a hub back (e.g.
#     detectors.visual_injection -> predict). Those 4 specific back-edges are
#     ignored so the layers contract reflects the intended dependency
#     direction rather than the transitive hub cycle. Each ignored edge is an
#     existing, known seam — not a license to add more.
#
#  3. na0s.integrations and na0s.mcp are ORCHESTRATION CONSUMERS: thin adapters
#     that sit ABOVE the whole stack and call the top-level public API
#     (na0s.scan / na0s.scan_output / na0s.predict.scan_tools). Like predict /
#     cascade they import downward into many tiers, so they are deliberately
#     NOT listed as a layer and NOT in the independence contract — constraining
#     them would re-create the hub cycle. They ARE still gated by the
#     forbidden-shims contract below (no re-importing deprecated layerN names).
#     na0s.mcp's own internal detector (detectors.mcp_supply_chain) lives in the
#     detectors tier and is fully bound by the layers contract; it copies the
#     worm rug-pull primitives down rather than importing worm (a tier 6 -> 3
#     upward back-edge the contract would reject).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["na0s"]
include_external_packages = false

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Semantic detection layering (high imports low, never the reverse)"
type = "layers"
# Listed HIGH -> LOW. A higher layer may import lower layers; a lower layer
# may never import a higher one. '|' = independent siblings (may NOT import
# each other); ':' = cohesive tier (may import each other).
layers = [
    "na0s.output",
    "na0s.conversation",
    "na0s.fusion | na0s.judge | na0s.eval | na0s.worm",
    "na0s.dataset | na0s.ml",
    "na0s.integrity | na0s.structural",
    "na0s.detectors : na0s.rules : na0s.validation",
    "na0s.input | na0s.obfuscation | na0s.threat_intel | na0s.models",
]
# Existing back-edges through the predict/cascade orchestrator hubs. These are
# the only sanctioned upward seams; the contract gates any NEW one.
ignore_imports = [
    "na0s.detectors.visual_injection -> na0s.predict",
    "na0s.fusion.ensemble -> na0s.predict",
    "na0s.conversation.scan_bridge -> na0s.predict",
    "na0s.output.propagation -> na0s.predict",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Standalone subsystems are independent"
type = "independence"
# These subsystems must not import one another (they only depend on top-level
# core modules / external libs). Keeps optional features decoupled.
modules = [
    "na0s.rag",
    "na0s.canary",
    "na0s.parsers",
    "na0s.agents",
]
ignore_imports = [
    "na0s.agents.input_guard -> na0s.predict",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "No new imports of the deprecated layerN shims"
type = "forbidden"
# Bans any first-party module from importing the deprecated sys.modules-alias
# shims. ZERO current violations in src/ (verified on main) — this gates the
# numbered->semantic rename so new code can't re-grow a dependency on the old
# layer0/1/2/15/16 names. Tests still use the shims by design (test suite is
# not scanned by import-linter, which analyzes the `na0s` package only).
source_modules = [
    "na0s.input", "na0s.rules", "na0s.obfuscation", "na0s.threat_intel",
    "na0s.conversation", "na0s.output", "na0s.structural", "na0s.validation",
    "na0s.fusion", "na0s.dataset", "na0s.eval", "na0s.integrations", "na0s.mcp",
    "na0s.canary", "na0s.detectors", "na0s.judge", "na0s.ml", "na0s.rag",
    "na0s.worm", "na0s.parsers", "na0s.integrity", "na0s.agents", "na0s.models",
    "na0s.predict", "na0s.cascade", "na0s.config", "na0s.cli", "na0s.scan_result",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "na0s.layer0", "na0s.layer1", "na0s.layer2", "na0s.layer15", "na0s.layer16",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# vulture — dead-code detector
#
# min-confidence = 80 is calibrated against the real tree: confidence 60
# yields ~385 reports (every unused-looking *assignment*, including framework
# callback args and the in-flight rag_poison_weight); confidence 80 yields 13
# high-signal reports (100%-confidence dead locals + 90%-confidence unused
# imports). 80 keeps the gate actionable without drowning it in noise.
# The whitelist file documents intentional "unused" names (entrypoints,
# plugin-registered hooks, branch-owned WIP).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.vulture]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["src/na0s", ".vulture_whitelist.py"]
sort_by_size = true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# deptry — dependency hygiene
#
# Config (not src edits) reconciles deptry's static scan with this package's
# intentional design: optional features are lazily imported under
# try/except ImportError and declared in optional extras under their PyPI
# names. package_module_name_map resolves PyPI-name -> import-name; the
# per-rule ignores cover modules supplied by optional extras / transitive
# deps that deptry cannot statically attribute. NOTE: these are dependency
# *declarations*, not code changes — no src churn (per task constraint).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.deptry]
known_first_party = ["na0s"]
optional_dependencies_dev_groups = ["dev"]

[tool.deptry.package_module_name_map]
pymupdf = ["fitz"]
python-docx = ["docx"]
python-pptx = ["pptx"]
sentence-transformers = ["sentence_transformers", "torch", "transformers"]
faiss-cpu = ["faiss"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# DEP001 (missing): modules provided by optional extras / not pip-installed in
# the CI base, all imported under try/except ImportError guards.
DEP001 = ["pdfplumber", "PyPDF2", "pytesseract", "re2", "lxml", "olefile", "oletools", "xlrd", "claude_agent_sdk", "mcp", "openclaw", "redis"]
# DEP002 (declared-but-unused): optional-extra + data-pipeline deps used only
# via guarded/lazy imports that deptry's static scan does not see.
DEP002 = ["datasets", "huggingface-hub", "cleanlab", "datasketch", "dvc", "tqdm", "pyarrow", "easyocr", "Pillow", "striprtf", "openai", "groq", "langdetect"]
# DEP003 (transitive): pulled transitively by declared deps (sklearn->scipy/joblib)
# or by optional integrations.
DEP003 = ["scipy", "joblib", "redis", "cryptography", "openclaw", "lxml"]

requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "portolan-cli"
version = "0.8.0"
description = "A CLI tool for managing cloud-native geospatial data"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [
    { name = "Nissim Lebovits", email = "nlebovits@pm.me" },
]
keywords = ["cloud-native", "geospatial", "gis", "io"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: GIS",
]
dependencies = [
    "antimeridian>=0.3.11", # RFC 7946 compliant antimeridian handling for STAC bbox
    "click>=8.4,<8.6", # PYSEC-2026-2132 fix; 8.4 makes ParamType generic (temporal.FlexibleDateTime subscripts it)
    "defusedxml>=0.7.1", # Safe XML parsing (XXE protection) for CSW/ISO 19139 metadata
    "duckdb>=1.5.6,<1.5.7", # Floor skips 1.5.5, which segfaults in ST_Read_Meta on malformed input (duckdb/duckdb-spatial#860)
    "geopandas>=0.14.0", # Reads GeoParquet for the thumbnail floor, which every collection needs (Issue #683)
    "geoparquet-io>=1.6.0", # One write facade keeps CRS, native geometry and bbox covering on every write path (gpio#990, #1009)
    "httpx>=0.27.0", # HTTP client for ArcGIS REST API discovery
    "matplotlib>=3.8.0", # Renders the deterministic thumbnail floor. Core, not optional: PTL-VIZ-001 is an ERROR, so a default install must be able to produce a conformant catalog (#518 Track 1, #683)
    "obstore>=0.8.2", # Cloud object storage (S3, GCS, Azure) via Rust bindings
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.0", # Load .env files for credentials (Issue #356)
    "numpy>=1.24.0", # Array ops (transitive via rasterio, but we import directly for thumbnails)
    "pyarrow>=12.0.0,<26.0.0",
    "pyproj>=3.0.0", # CRS transformations (transitive via rasterio, but we import directly)
    "pystac>=1.10.0", # STAC catalog/collection/item creation
    "stac-geoparquet>=0.6.0", # Generate items.parquet for efficient STAC queries (optional)
    "pyyaml>=6.0", # YAML config file support
    "rasterio>=1.3.0", # Raster I/O (transitive via rio-cogeo, but we import directly)
    "cryptography>=46.0.7", # CVE-2026-39892 fix (transitive via httpx/certifi, pinned for security)
    "lxml>=6.1.0", # CVE-2026-41066 fix (transitive via owslib, pinned for security)
    "pillow>=12.3.0", # PYSEC-2026-2253..2257 fix (transitive via rasterio, pinned for security)
    "pmtiles>=3.0.0", # PMTiles metadata reading (header, bounds, zoom levels)
    "pluggy>=1.5.0", # Plugin hooks (#947). Pure Python, no dependencies. 1.5 adds warn_on_impl_args for hook deprecation
    "pyogrio>=0.7.0", # FlatGeobuf metadata reading (transitive via geoparquet-io, but we import directly)
    "pygments>=2.20.0", # CVE-2026-4539 fix (transitive via rich, pinned for security)
    "requests>=2.33.0", # CVE-2026-25645 fix (transitive, pinned for security)
    "rich>=13.0.0", # Terminal progress bars (transitive via geoparquet-io, but we import directly)
    "rio-cogeo>=5.0.0", # COG creation/validation (includes rasterio)
    "rashid>=0.2.0,<0.3.0", # Conformance validator behind `portolan check`; ships its own STAC + Portolan profile schemas, so validation runs offline. 0.2.0 is the floor for PTL-LIV-006, which `check --live` uses to report a linked file the publish host does not serve (issue #935). Earlier floors: 0.1.5 added the catalog-logo rules PTL-LNK-007/008/009 (PORTO-CORE-074..077) and PTL-AST-006, whose absence in 0.1.4 let a wrong COG media type mask PTL-COL-004 and PTL-MIR-001. The conformance gate asserts all four, so this is a hard floor, not a preference
    "typing_extensions>=4.0.0; python_version < '3.11'",
    "lerc>=4.0.1", # Decodes the LERC tiles that hosted tiled imagery layers cache. GDAL 3.12 fails on LERC2 version 6 with "MRF: Error decoding Lerc", so `extract arcgis` cannot read a TilesOnly ImageServer without it (Issue #870). The wheel ships binaries for Windows x64, macOS, and Linux x86-64, so tilecache.py imports it lazily and explains the failure on other platforms
]

[project.scripts]
portolan = "portolan_cli:cli"

# Built-in commands that use the plugin path (#947). An entry point that
# portolan-cli declares always loads, whatever PORTOLAN_PLUGINS says.
[project.entry-points."portolan.commands"]
"version.rollback" = "portolan_cli.backends.iceberg.cli:rollback"
"version.prune" = "portolan_cli.backends.iceberg.cli:prune"

[project.urls]
"Homepage" = "https://github.com/portolan-sdi/portolan-cli"
"Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/portolan-sdi/portolan-cli/issues"
"Documentation" = "https://github.com/portolan-sdi/portolan-cli#readme"
"Source" = "https://github.com/portolan-sdi/portolan-cli"

[project.optional-dependencies]
iceberg = [
    "pyiceberg[sql-sqlite]>=0.8.0",
    "shapely>=2.0.0",
    "pygeohash>=1.2.0",
]
e2e = [
    "boto3>=1.35.0",
]
aws = [
    # obstore.auth.boto3 wraps a botocore session, which reads every credential
    # mechanism an AWS profile can name. Optional, because a static key pair and
    # the environment variables need none of it (Issue #872).
    "boto3>=1.35.0",
    # boto3 installs botocore. The profile errors live there, and the upload
    # path reads ProfileNotFound to tell a missing profile from a failed one.
    "botocore>=1.35.0",
]
dev = [
    "codespell>=2.4.1",
    "deptry>=0.25.1", # Dependency checker (unused, missing, transitive deps)
    "gitingest>=0.1.0", # Auto-fetch API docs for core dependencies
    "import-linter>=2.0", # Architecture enforcement via import contracts
    "commitizen>=4.13.4",
    "hypothesis>=6.151.5",
    "mutmut>=3.4.0",
    "mypy>=1.19.1",
    "pip-audit>=2.10.0",
    "pytest>=9.0.3",
    "pytest-benchmark>=5.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3.1",
    "ruff>=0.14.11",
    "types-defusedxml>=0.7.0", # Type stubs for defusedxml
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0", # Type stubs for PyYAML
    "vulture>=2.14",
]
# PMTiles generation now comes from core geoparquet-io (>=1.4.0), which owns
# create_pmtiles. The extra stays declared, and empty, so an existing
# `pip install portolan-cli[pmtiles]` still resolves (Issue #754).
pmtiles = []
# Rendering itself is core (matplotlib, geopandas). What stays optional here is
# the extra fidelity: basemap tiles under a vector thumbnail, and the MVT decode
# that only the PMTiles render path uses. Both are lazily imported and guarded,
# so a default install renders without them.
thumbnails = [
    "contextily>=1.5.0", # Basemap tiles for vector thumbnails
    "mapbox-vector-tile>=2.0.0", # MVT decoding for PMTiles thumbnail generation
]
docs = [
    # Pinned exactly: zensical is alpha with a compiled core, so a floor
    # constraint is not a constraint. Dependabot offers reviewable bumps.
    "zensical==0.0.67",
    "mkdocstrings-python>=1.0.0", # pulls mkdocstrings itself as its own dependency
    "pymdown-extensions>=11.0", # zensical requires >=11.0; fixes filename=None in highlight
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["portolan_cli"]

# ---------- commitizen ----------

[tool.commitizen]
name = "cz_conventional_commits"
version = "0.8.0"
version_files = ["pyproject.toml:^version"]
tag_format = "v$version"
update_changelog_on_bump = true
# The project is pre-1.0. A breaking change bumps the minor number, so the
# major number stays at zero until the interface settles.
major_version_zero = true

# ---------- testing ----------

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_functions = "test_*"
addopts = "--tb=short"
markers = [
    "unit: Fast, isolated, no I/O (< 100ms each)",
    "integration: Multi-component, may touch filesystem",
    "network: Requires network access (mocked locally, real in CI nightly)",
    "refused_hosts: The network guard refuses these hosts without failing the test (child-process requests only)",
    "realdata: Uses real-world fixtures from tests/fixtures/realdata/ (tests orchestration, not geometry)",
    "snapshot: Compares output against golden files",
    "plugin: Needs the example plugin installed (tests/plugins/portolan_example)",
    "benchmark: Performance measurement, tracked over time",
    "slow: Takes > 5 seconds",
    "e2e: End-to-end tests requiring Docker (REST catalog + RustFS)",
    "e2e_slow: Extended E2E tests (concurrency stress, large datasets) - nightly only",
    "source_scan: Static source-tree guard incompatible with mutmut instrumentation",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["portolan_cli"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "portolan_cli/__init__.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 0
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]

# ---------- linting & formatting ----------

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"
# .claude/ holds tooling that portolan-ops syncs into every repo. This repo does
# not own those files, and a sync run overwrites any fix made here. Raise a rule
# change in portolan-ops instead.
extend-exclude = [".claude"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Ruff owns complexity, security, and docstring linting for this repo. It
# replaces three separate tools that each re-walked the same source tree:
# xenon/radon (C901), bandit (S), and pylint R0801 (now jscpd, see prek.toml).
select = [
    "E", # pycodestyle errors
    "W", # pycodestyle warnings
    "F", # pyflakes
    "I", # isort
    "B", # flake8-bugbear
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP", # pyupgrade
    "A", # flake8-builtins - shadowing a builtin hides it for the whole scope
    "ARG", # flake8-unused-arguments - an unused argument is a stale contract
    "C901", # mccabe complexity - replaces xenon's --max-absolute
    "D", # pydocstyle - see [tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle] for the convention
    "DTZ", # flake8-datetimez - a naive datetime in a STAC temporal extent is a bug
    "ERA", # eradicate - commented-out code
    "EXE", # flake8-executable
    "FURB", # refurb - modern idiom upgrades
    "G", # flake8-logging-format
    "ICN", # flake8-import-conventions
    "INT", # flake8-gettext
    "ISC", # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "LOG", # flake8-logging
    "N", # pep8-naming
    "PERF", # perflint
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "PTH", # flake8-use-pathlib - this repo passes paths everywhere; os.path invites str/Path drift
    "PYI", # flake8-pyi
    "Q", # flake8-quotes
    "RET", # flake8-return
    "RSE", # flake8-raise
    "S", # flake8-bandit - replaces the standalone bandit hook
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "SLOT", # flake8-slots
    "T20", # flake8-print - output goes through output.py, never bare print
    "TC", # flake8-type-checking
    "YTT", # flake8-2020
]
ignore = [
    "E501", # line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008", # do not perform function calls in argument defaults (Click uses this)
    "ISC001", # conflicts with the formatter
    # Google style documents the constructor arguments in the class docstring.
    # A separate __init__ docstring repeats them. errors.py alone holds 28
    # two-line constructors whose class docstring already states the contract.
    "D107", # missing docstring in __init__
    # Every hit is a loop that isolates one item's failure and continues. It
    # writes a file, reads a catalog, or calls a remote store. The handler
    # cannot move out of the loop, because that aborts the loop on the first
    # failure. The setup cost is free from Python 3.11 and negligible before it.
    "PERF203", # try-except within a loop
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]
# Tests assert, reach into private helpers, and carry fixture literals that
# would be magic values in library code. They are still held to the import,
# naming, and simplification rules.
"tests/**/*.py" = [
    "S101", # assert is the point of a test
    "S105", # "password"-shaped fixture literals
    "S106",
    "S108", # /tmp paths in fixtures
    "D", # test names carry the description; docstrings are optional
    "ARG", # pytest fixtures are injected and often unused by name
    "SLF001", # tests may reach into private helpers
    "T20", # a test may print for diagnostics
    "PTH123", # open() is fine in a fixture
    "ERA001", # commented-out fixture variants are deliberate
    "S603", # a harness starts docker or uv with a literal argument list
    "S607", # the harness resolves docker and uv from PATH
    "S310", # a test opens an https URL it writes itself
    "S311", # random builds test data, not a secret
    "S608", # a test builds a DuckDB query from a literal path
]
"scripts/**/*.py" = [
    "T20", # scripts are CLIs of their own and print by design
    "S310", # a script opens an https URL it writes itself
    "S603", # a script starts a tool or pytest with a literal argument list
    "S607", # the script resolves its tools from PATH
]
"examples/**/*.py" = ["T20"] # an example prints its result for the reader

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-builtins]
# STAC names a collection field "license". The ArcGIS REST API and the schema
# sidecar name a field "format". The keyword arguments carry the same names, so
# the Python API matches the specification it writes. No function that takes
# them calls the shadowed builtin.
builtins-ignorelist = ["license", "format"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pep8-naming]
# "ET" is the alias the stdlib documentation gives for xml.etree.ElementTree.
# "InterruptException" mirrors duckdb.InterruptException. convert.py matches
# that class name as a string, so a test double must use the same name.
extend-ignore-names = ["ET", "InterruptException"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["portolan_cli"]
# Every module defers annotation evaluation. This is what makes the TC rules
# safe here: moving an import into a TYPE_CHECKING block cannot break a runtime
# annotation when no annotation is evaluated at runtime.
required-imports = ["from __future__ import annotations"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
# Without an explicit convention ruff enables every D rule, including D413,
# which alone accounted for 1069 of 1233 D violations. Google is the style the
# existing docstrings already follow.
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# The removed xenon hook allowed any block up to grade C (complexity 20). It
# also checked the module average and the repo average. A single complex
# function cannot move an average. This is the per-function ceiling instead.
max-complexity = 15

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
docstring-code-format = true

# ---------- type checking ----------

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true # Enables all strict flags at once
# The example plugin (#947) is a separate package. This path lets mypy check
# its tests and its code without installing it.
mypy_path = "tests/plugins/portolan_example/src"
# pyarrow >=24 ships py.typed but leaves pyarrow.parquet helpers untyped, so
# strict's disallow_untyped_calls trips on every read_table/write_table/
# ParquetFile/read_metadata/read_schema call. Scope the suppression to pyarrow
# instead of relaxing strictness globally.
untyped_calls_exclude = ["pyarrow"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["pyarrow.*", "rasterio.*", "gitingest.*", "matplotlib.*", "pyiceberg.*", "shapely.*", "pygeohash.*", "mutmut.*", "geopandas.*", "contextily.*", "jsonschema.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# markdown ships no inline types. types-Markdown exists on PyPI, so mypy
# reports the missing stub even under ignore_missing_imports, and it reports it
# against the importing file. One docs test imports markdown's slugify to prove
# that the anchors the generator writes match the anchors MkDocs renders. The
# suppression therefore names that one test module.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["markdown.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["docs.test_reference_generation"]
disable_error_code = ["import-untyped"]

# ---------- spell check ----------

[tool.codespell]
# "Nd" is a Unicode category code for "Number, decimal digit" used in Hypothesis tests
# French words from Belgian ISO 19139 test fixture (tests/fixtures/csw/belgium_buildings_iso19139.xml)
# "BU" is the INSPIRE theme code for Buildings (used in test fixtures)
# "disjointness" is a real set-theory term (codespell wants "disjointedness")
# "lod" is the ArcGIS tile cache term for a level of detail (the tileInfo "lods" array)
ignore-words-list = "nd,bu,ue,adresse,projet,environnement,copie,explicite,connexion,objets,visibles,issus,fonction,mesures,informations,disjointness,lod"

# ---------- dead code ----------

[tool.vulture]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["portolan_cli", "tests", "vulture_whitelist.py"]
exclude = [
    "portolan_cli/backends/protocol.py", # Protocol method params are intentionally unused
    "portolan_cli/backends/json_file.py", # Stub methods raise NotImplementedError
    "portolan_cli/backends/iceberg/backend.py", # Protocol methods + lifecycle hooks
]
sort_by_size = true
verbose = false

# ---------- mutation testing ----------

[tool.mutmut]
paths_to_mutate = ["portolan_cli/"]
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = ["tests/"]
# The `scripts/` package is imported by a few tests (test_scripts,
# test_pip_audit_ignores, test_fetch_lib_docs_integration). mutmut runs the
# suite from a copied `mutants/` sandbox, so scripts/ must be copied in too or
# collection dies with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts'` — which
# used to sink the whole stats phase silently (see nightly.yml's zero-mutant
# guard).
# scripts/ (imported by a few tests) and the data files those tests read must
# be present in the sandbox, or collection/execution dies there.
# (spec/ used to be copied here for the spec_compliance suite; both are gone —
# the spec moved to portolan-spec and validation to rashid, which ships its own
# schemas inside its wheel, so nothing reads a schema by repo-root path now.)
# `.mutation-shards.json` joins `.mutation-baseline` here because
# TestShardBaselines::test_repo_baseline_file_parses reads it by repo-root path:
# inside the copied sandbox that root is `mutants/`, so an uncopied file is a
# FileNotFoundError that fails the in-mutation pytest run and aborts the gate.
also_copy = [
  "scripts/",
  ".pip-audit-ignores",
  ".mutation-baseline",
  ".mutation-shards.json",
]
# The stats/baseline run must mirror the fast CI test job, not the whole suite:
# - --no-cov: keeps coverage instrumentation off even when a caller or config
# adds --cov (it conflicts with mutmut's); addopts no longer injects it.
# - --tb=short: a stats-phase failure must show WHERE it broke.
# - --ignore=tests/docs: the docs tests check docs/, mkdocs.yml, and README.md,
# not portolan_cli behavior. The sandbox holds none of those files (#997).
# - marker filter: exclude network/slow/benchmark/e2e (mutation of portolan_cli
# is validated by the fast, offline suite; e2e needs Docker, network needs a
# live server).
#
# The sandbox rule (#997): a test that mutmut runs reads only paths that
# mutmut copies into mutants/. tests/mutation_sandbox.py enforces it in every
# ordinary pytest run. It reads this table and fails a test in the selection
# that opens any other repo-root path. A test that checks repository files goes
# in tests/docs/. A test of portolan_cli behavior reads a fixture under tests/.
# Add a path to also_copy only when such a test must read it from the root.
# The guard reads the -m filter only in the form "not a and not b".
pytest_add_cli_args = [
    "--no-cov",
    "--tb=short",
    "--ignore=tests/docs",
    "-m", "not network and not slow and not benchmark and not e2e and not e2e_slow and not source_scan",
]

# ---------- architecture enforcement ----------
# Stricter layered contracts are aspirational - the current architecture has some coupling
# that would need refactoring to support full layered enforcement.

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["portolan_cli"]
# The layer contracts forbid click and rasterio.
# import-linter adds those external packages to the graph only with this flag.
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "cli-no-storage"
name = "CLI cannot import storage backends directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["portolan_cli.cli"]
forbidden_modules = ["portolan_cli.backends"]
# Allow intermediate modules to access backends (CLI wraps API).
# cli.py uses these modules as a clean interface; direct cli->backends is still forbidden.
ignore_imports = [
    "portolan_cli.catalog -> portolan_cli.backends",
    # finalize_items routes version snapshots to the active backend (#624 moved
    # this edge out of add.py into finalization.py); cli reaches it only via the
    # library layer, so the direct cli->backends ban still holds.
    "portolan_cli.finalization -> portolan_cli.backends",
    "portolan_cli.version_ops -> portolan_cli.backends",
    "portolan_cli.version_ops -> portolan_cli.backends.protocol",
    "portolan_cli.hookspecs -> portolan_cli.backends.protocol", # TYPE_CHECKING only
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "validation-is-an-adapter"
name = "Validation is a rashid adapter and must not import the CLI"
type = "forbidden"
# The extraction seam is gone: rashid ships as a package and
# portolan_cli.validation is the adapter in front of it. What
# remains worth locking is direction. The adapter builds rashid's config,
# calls it, and returns plain data (validation.report emits dicts, never
# Click/Rich output), so cli.py depends on validation and never the reverse.
source_modules = ["portolan_cli.validation"]
forbidden_modules = ["portolan_cli.cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "utilities-are-foundational"
name = "Utilities must not import other portolan modules"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "portolan_cli.output",
    "portolan_cli.errors",
    "portolan_cli.constants",
    "portolan_cli.json_output",
    # input sanitization. A stdlib-only leaf (re, pathlib, urllib):
    # it hardens agent-supplied arguments, which is not catalog validation, so
    # it sits at the top level rather than inside validation/.
    "portolan_cli.input_hardening",
]

# ---------- feature-package boundaries (#625) ----------
# The scan/, sync/, and viz/ subpackages group the modules that used to sit
# flat in the root. Their real dependency DAG is: sync (top orchestration) may
# reach down into scan (its `sync` orchestrator drives check/scan); scan and viz
# are independent peers, and neither reaches back up into sync. These two
# contracts lock that shape so the grouping can't silently erode.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "viz-is-a-leaf"
name = "viz must not import the scan or sync layers"
type = "forbidden"
# viz/ only produces/classifies visual + tiling artifacts (thumbnails, Mapbox GL
# styles, PMTiles). It is a leaf: it depends on neither scanning nor sync.
source_modules = ["portolan_cli.viz"]
forbidden_modules = ["portolan_cli.scan", "portolan_cli.sync"]
ignore_imports = [
    # PORTO-CORE-069 makes `file:size`/`file:checksum` on a style asset a claim
    # about the style file's bytes, so `viz.style` must stamp them. It reuses
    # `stac_parquet.stamp_file_fields`/`sync_file_extension` rather than hashing
    # on its own terms, and those reach `sync.checksums` — a stdlib+rashid leaf,
    # not the sync orchestration this contract exists to keep out of viz. The
    # same reasoning is written into the scan contract below.
    "portolan_cli.viz.style -> portolan_cli.stac_parquet",
    # Same reasoning for the PMTiles writer, which was the one visual artifact
    # shipping without file:size/file:checksum until issue #746.
    "portolan_cli.viz.pmtiles -> portolan_cli.stac_parquet",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "scan-below-sync"
name = "scan must not directly import the sync or viz layers"
type = "forbidden"
# scan/ (directory scanning, classification, inference, check) sits below sync
# and is independent of viz. sync may import scan, never the reverse.
#
# Direct-only: `scan.check` is a command-level orchestrator that legitimately
# fans out through shared root modules (catalog, metadata, convert), which in
# turn depend on sync.checksums and viz.*. Those transitive chains are the
# existing architecture, not a scan->sync/viz coupling. What we lock here is
# the boundary that actually matters: no scan module may *directly* import the
# sync or viz packages. (viz-is-a-leaf stays transitive because viz truly is.)
source_modules = ["portolan_cli.scan"]
forbidden_modules = ["portolan_cli.sync", "portolan_cli.viz"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

# ---------- layers (#944, #947) ----------
# The package has three layers. A library caller (a Cloud Run job, a notebook,
# a plugin) imports the read and manage layers without the CLI shell.
#
#   read    catalog, collection, and item access. No Click, no rasterio,
#           no module that writes a catalog.
#   manage  STAC builders, conversion, extraction, versions.json, sync,
#           backends. No Click.
#   cli     cli, cli_types, emit, add_progress, scan.progress. Click and Rich.
#
# Each check follows transitive imports, and an import inside a function body
# counts too.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "layer-read"
name = "Read layer: no click, rasterio, or write modules"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "portolan_cli.versions",
    "portolan_cli.json_io",
    "portolan_cli.bbox",
    "portolan_cli.models",
    "portolan_cli.query",
    "portolan_cli.status",
    "portolan_cli.catalog_list",
    "portolan_cli.agents_md",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "click",
    "rasterio",
    "portolan_cli.cli",
    "portolan_cli.add",
    "portolan_cli.convert",
    "portolan_cli.preparation",
    "portolan_cli.finalization",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "layer-manage"
name = "Manage layer: no click"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["portolan_cli", "portolan_cli.**"]
forbidden_modules = ["click"]
ignore_imports = [
    # The CLI layer is the one place Click belongs.
    "portolan_cli.cli -> click",
    "portolan_cli.cli_types -> click",
    "portolan_cli.emit -> click",
    "portolan_cli.plugins.commands -> click",
    "portolan_cli.backends.iceberg.cli -> click",
    "portolan_cli.extract.*.cli -> click",
    "portolan_cli.extract.common.cli_helpers -> click",
    "portolan_cli.extract.common.layer_cli -> click",
    # The Extractor protocol names click.Command for type checkers only.
    "portolan_cli.plugins.extractors -> click",
    "portolan_cli.plugins.builtin.extractors -> click",
    "portolan_cli.extract.common.source -> click",
    # check_extractor runs in a plugin's test suite and checks for a Click command.
    "portolan_cli.testing -> click",
    # The package root names the Click group for type checkers only. It loads
    # the group lazily through __getattr__.
    "portolan_cli -> portolan_cli.cli",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "layer-cli"
name = "CLI layer: only the CLI layer imports it"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = [
    "portolan_cli.cli",
    "portolan_cli.cli_types",
    "portolan_cli.emit",
    "portolan_cli.add_progress",
    "portolan_cli.scan.progress",
    "portolan_cli.plugins.commands",
    "portolan_cli.backends.iceberg.cli",
    "portolan_cli.extract.*.cli",
    "portolan_cli.extract.common.cli_helpers",
    "portolan_cli.extract.common.layer_cli",
]
allowed_importers = [
    "portolan_cli.cli",
    "portolan_cli.cli_types",
    "portolan_cli.emit",
    "portolan_cli.add_progress",
    "portolan_cli.scan.progress",
    "portolan_cli.plugins.commands",
    "portolan_cli.backends.iceberg.cli",
    "portolan_cli.extract.*.cli",
    "portolan_cli.extract.common.cli_helpers",
    "portolan_cli.extract.common.layer_cli",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # The package root names the Click group for type checkers only. It loads
    # the group lazily through __getattr__.
    "portolan_cli -> portolan_cli.cli",
]

# ---------- dependency checking ----------
# deptry detects unused, missing, and transitive dependencies
# Rules: DEP001 (missing), DEP002 (unused), DEP003 (transitive), DEP004 (imported as dev)

[tool.deptry]
# Treat optional-dependencies groups as dev dependencies
optional_dependencies_dev_groups = ["dev", "docs"]
# Extend default exclusions (venv, .venv, tests, .git already excluded)
extend_exclude = [
    "scripts", # Standalone scripts may use external tools
    ".claude", # Claude Code worktrees and temp files
]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# Stability and security constraints for transitive dependencies (not directly
# imported)
# - cryptography: CVE-2026-39892
# - duckdb: 1.5.5 segfaults in ST_Read_Meta on malformed input. See
#   duckdb/duckdb-spatial#860
# - lxml: CVE-2026-41066
# - pillow: CVE-2026-40192
# - pygments: CVE-2026-4539
# - requests: CVE-2026-25645
DEP002 = [
    "cryptography",
    "duckdb",
    "lxml",
    "pillow",
    "pygments",
    "requests",
    "pyiceberg",
    "shapely",
    "pygeohash",
    "boto3",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "fastembed>=0.8.0",

    # raster v2.0.0 schema. jsonschema arrives transitively through rashid, but

    "jsonschema>=4.0.0",
    "moto[s3,server]>=5.0.0",

]

[tool.coverage.run]

clihelp = "nagioscli --help"
cliproblems = "nagioscli problems"

# publish.sh variant (pattern semacli ken #1131): progress dots only, full
# traceback of any failure. `-o addopts=` drops the project-wide -v;
# --cov-report= keeps the .coverage file the metrics gate reads without
# printing the per-file table.
test-publish = "env PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/ -o addopts= -q --tb=long -rfE -p no:cacheprovider --cov=nagioscli --cov-report="
test-unit = "env PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/ -v"
test-integration = "env PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/integration/ -v"

format-check = "black --check nagioscli/ tests/"
interrogate = "interrogate nagioscli/"
vulture = "vulture"
refurb = "refurb nagioscli/"

metrics-gate = "python scripts/quality_metrics.py --gate"

# The workspace root, not a member: it builds no package.

requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [

    "mael-common",
    "mael-agent",
    "mael-domain",
    "mael-agent-daemon",
    "mael-orchestrator",
]

# The one dev list. CI installs it with `uv sync --extra dev`, so anything a
# gate needs belongs here — `bin/lint` runs ruff, pyright and vulture, and the
# suite needs pytest-asyncio to collect an `async def` test at all.
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.0.2",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.0",
    "ruff>=0.15,<0.17",
    "pyright>=1.1",
    "vulture>=2.14,<3",
    "import-linter>=2.1",
]

[tool.uv]
package = false

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = [
    "cli",
    "lib/common",
    "lib/agent",
    "lib/domain",
    "agent-daemon",
    "orchestrator-api",
]

[tool.uv.sources]
sminnee-maelstrom = { workspace = true }
mael-common = { workspace = true }
mael-agent = { workspace = true }
mael-domain = { workspace = true }
mael-agent-daemon = { workspace = true }
mael-orchestrator = { workspace = true }

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = [
    "cli/tests",
    "lib/common/tests",
    "lib/agent/tests",
    "lib/domain/tests",
    "agent-daemon/tests",
    "orchestrator-api/tests",
    "tests",
]
# The domain and daemon suites' support modules. `cli/tests/` imports them too, so
# they must be on the path whichever suite pytest collects first.
pythonpath = ["lib/domain/tests", "agent-daemon/tests"]
# Async tests are plain `async def`, with no per-test decorator: an awaiting
# test is the normal case now, not the exception.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Pinned rather than left to the default, which pytest-asyncio plans to change.
# One loop per test keeps a fixture's loop-bound state from leaking into the
# next one.
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
markers = [
    "e2e: end-to-end tests that spawn real processes or use real git repos",
    "slow: tests that take >10s (skip with -m 'not slow')",
    "binds_socket: needs bind() on a Unix socket or a loopback TCP port, which an agent sandbox denies",
]

[tool.pyright]
include = [
    "cli/src",
    "lib/common/src",
    "lib/agent/src",
    "lib/domain/src",
    "agent-daemon/src",
    "orchestrator-api/src",
]
exclude = [".vulture_whitelist.py"]
pythonVersion = "3.11"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
useLibraryCodeForTypes = true
reportUnusedImport = true
reportUnusedVariable = true
reportDuplicateImport = true
reportMissingTypeStubs = false

[tool.ruff]
# Every workspace member's package is first-party, so isort groups them together.
src = [
    "cli/src",
    "lib/common/src",
    "lib/agent/src",
    "lib/domain/src",
    "agent-daemon/src",
    "orchestrator-api/src",
]
# The vulture whitelist is a list of bare names, not a program. Every line is
# an undefined name by design, so ruff and pyright must both skip it.
extend-exclude = [".vulture_whitelist.py"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "I"]

[tool.vulture]
# Configures the production pass alone. Run the gate through bin/vulture-check,
# never bare — the test pass needs the flags that script adds.
# See docs/dev/dead-code.md.
paths = [
    "cli/src",
    "lib/common/src",
    "lib/agent/src",
    "lib/domain/src",
    "agent-daemon/src",
    "orchestrator-api/src",
    ".vulture_whitelist.py",
]
min_confidence = 60

# A framework holds the reference to these, so no call site exists to find.
ignore_decorators = [
    # Click. Every command and group is reached through the CLI tree. This one
    # family removes about half of all findings, which is why it belongs here
    # and not in the whitelist: a whitelist would need a line per command, and
    # every new command would break the gate.
    "@click.*",
    "@*.command",
    "@*.group",
    "@*.result_callback",
    # Descriptors and generated methods.
    "@property",
    "@dataclass",
    "@staticmethod",
    "@classmethod",
    "@overload",
    # aiohttp: the router holds the handler.
    "@routes.*",
]

# Names a framework resolves at run time, or that name a repository convention.
ignore_names = [
    # Textual resolves these off the widget by name: compose builds the widget
    # tree, on_* handle events, action_* back the key bindings. They carry no
    # decorator, so only a name pattern reaches them.
    "compose",
    "on_*",
    "action_*",
    "BINDINGS",
    "CSS",
    # Click calls these on a Group subclass when it renders help.
    "list_commands",
    "get_command",
    # Click reads these off a Group/Command subclass to decide what class a
    # decorator builds. `AsyncGroup` sets both so its subcommands are async
    # too; nothing calls them by name.
    "command_class",
    "group_class",
    # The storage layer's test seam. docs/dev/architecture-patterns.md makes
    # the in-memory backend a convention, so the gate follows the convention.
    "InMemory*",
]

# The dependency graph between the packages: mael_agent imports mael_common;
# mael_domain imports both; mael_daemon imports mael_agent and mael_common;
# mael_orchestrator and mael_cli import the three libraries. Nothing imports
# either service, mael_daemon or mael_orchestrator.
# Run by `bin/lint` as `lint-imports`. See docs/dev/architecture-patterns.md.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = [
    "mael_common",
    "mael_agent",
    "mael_domain",
    "mael_daemon",
    "mael_orchestrator",
    "mael_cli",
]
# So a contract can name click, which is not one of the packages above.
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "mael_common imports no other maelstrom package"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["mael_common"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "mael_agent",
    "mael_domain",
    "mael_daemon",
    "mael_orchestrator",
    "mael_cli",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "mael_agent imports only mael_common"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["mael_agent"]
forbidden_modules = ["mael_domain", "mael_daemon", "mael_orchestrator", "mael_cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "mael_domain imports only mael_agent and mael_common"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["mael_domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["mael_daemon", "mael_orchestrator", "mael_cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The daemon imports neither the domain nor the mael CLI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["mael_daemon"]
forbidden_modules = ["mael_domain", "mael_orchestrator", "mael_cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The orchestrator server imports neither the daemon nor the mael CLI"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["mael_orchestrator"]
forbidden_modules = ["mael_daemon", "mael_cli"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The mael CLI meets the services only on the wire"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["mael_cli"]
forbidden_modules = ["mael_daemon", "mael_orchestrator"]

# The domain is click-free, so the CLI and the orchestrator server can share it.
# The async click group is the one library module allowed to import click.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "The libraries import no click, bar the async click group"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["mael_common", "mael_agent", "mael_domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["click", "mael_common.cli_async"]
ignore_imports = ["mael_common.cli_async -> click"]
