[tool.uv.sources]
insightscli = { workspace = true }
insights-owners = { workspace = true }
# github.com/hanzo-ds/orm answers 404 to anyone without a GitHub credential, and the
# image build carries none — it mounts FORGE_TOKEN, for git.hanzo.ai. So this address
# could only ever resolve from a warm uv cache, and the first build on a cold one died
# on "could not read Username for 'https://github.com'". The forge carries the same
# commit, cloneable without a credential at all. Its three siblings below are still
# reachable on github.com and stay where they are until they are not.
datastore-orm = { git = "https://git.hanzo.ai/hanzoai/datastore-orm", rev = "56c46e4bc6a424fd68b12df2afbacea4090b2dbb" }
datastore-driver = { git = "https://github.com/hanzo-ds/driver", rev = "119df3f" }
datastore-connect = { git = "https://github.com/hanzo-ds/connect", rev = "ccbd4b5" }
datastore-pool = { git = "https://github.com/hanzo-ds/pool", rev = "7260d56" }
insightsql-parser = { path = "common/insightsql_parser" }
insightsql-parser-rs = { path = "rust/insightsql/parser" }
# The forge is where this SDK lives. The github.com/hanzoai mirror is archived and
# therefore frozen a commit behind, and uv resolves a github.com URL through the
# GitHub API rather than git — so a url.insteadOf redirect cannot reach past it and
# the build would silently keep resolving the stale commit. Naming the forge
# directly is the only address that answers with the code that exists. The forge
# needs a credential: the image build mounts FORGE_TOKEN (see Dockerfile), the same
# way every other Hanzo image consumes our own packages.
hanzo_insights = { git = "https://git.hanzo.ai/hanzoai/insights-python", branch = "main" }
# pytest-split: pinned to Insights's fork (immutable tag) for the order-preserving
# optimal_chunks split. Fork: Insights/pytest-split (of jerry-git/pytest-split).
# To pull upstream fixes: rebase the fork's feat branch onto upstream, cut the next
# v0.11.0-insights.N tag, and bump this pin.
pytest-split = { git = "https://github.com/PostHog/pytest-split", tag = "v0.11.0-posthog.6" }

# protoletariat generates .pyi stubs with re-exports (e.g. `from . import person_pb2`)
# that type checkers need to resolve the package structure.
# protobuf 5.x _pb2.py files have side-effect-only imports that load dependency
# descriptors into the pool before AddSerializedFile() — ruff must not strip them.
"insights/personinsights_client/proto/generated/**/*.pyi" = ["F401"]
"insights/personinsights_client/proto/generated/**/*_pb2.py" = ["F401", "E402"]
# deltalite's test suite bootstraps its harness/planner via sys.path (the package is a
# maturin-built extension living under rust/, not part of the Django app), so imports
# are necessarily lazy / post-path-insert (PLC0415, E402); the planner's small CLI
# prints its report (T201).
"rust/deltalite/python/**" = ["PLC0415", "E402", "T201"]
# Django settings aggregator: star imports are how settings modules merge into one namespace.
# Not portable to explicit re-exports without losing the settings-loading semantics.
"insights/settings/**" = ["F403", "F405"]

# PLC0415 exemptions. products/ and services/llm-gateway/ have their own ruff configs.

[tool.ty.rules]
# Import resolution - ty can't always find all modules/stubs
unresolved-import = "ignore"

# Django-related rules - ty doesn't support Django's metaprogramming yet
# See: https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/291
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"  # Django model fields, relationships, auto-generated attributes
invalid-argument-type = "ignore"  # Django querysets, managers, form fields
unknown-argument = "ignore"  # Django kwargs, queryset filters, manager methods
invalid-base = "ignore"  # Django model metaclasses (e.g., models.Model)
missing-argument = "ignore"  # Django auto-generated __init__, managers
too-many-positional-arguments = "ignore"  # Django metaprogramming signatures

# Dual mypy+ty — mypy still runs, so its artifacts are legitimate
redundant-cast = "ignore"  # casts needed by mypy that ty resolves
unused-type-ignore-comment = "ignore"  # type: ignore comments required by mypy

# Django lazy imports and settings indirection
possibly-missing-submodule = "ignore"

# DRF serializer pattern — validate/update/create overrides are idiomatic
invalid-method-override = "ignore"

# Conditional base classes (e.g. EnterpriseEventQuery | EventQuery pattern)
unsupported-base = "ignore"

# Protobuf generated code + Django lazy references
unresolved-reference = "ignore"

# Third-party library overload stubs (Anthropic SDK, Django, re, etc.)
no-matching-overload = "ignore"

# Framework metaclass magic — ty can't resolve dynamic callables
call-top-callable = "ignore"
call-non-callable = "ignore"

# Django querysets typed as `object` — ty can't narrow through managers
not-iterable = "ignore"

# `in` operator on Django/framework `object` types
unsupported-operator = "ignore"

# Subscript on `object`/`None` from unresolved Django types
not-subscriptable = "ignore"

# mypy already catches deprecations; ty is a fast preflight, not the authority
deprecated = "ignore"

# ty disagrees with mypy on some existing code — baselined, not suppressed.
# These rules catch real bugs in new code, so they stay enabled.
# invalid-type-form is the exception: generated code + ty limitations on valid patterns.
invalid-type-form = "ignore"

[tool.ruff.lint]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter — the boundaries of the engine, enforced rather than described.
#
#   substrate                 the engine: everything needed to run an agent
#   substrate.types    what the engine needs from outside (pure)
#   substrate.integrations             adapters over the abstractions (heavy services are reached by URL: integrations/services)
#   substrate.server / console / cli   the HTTP server and the terminal
#
# Run with: uv run lint-imports
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["substrate"]
# An import made only for type checking never runs, so it cannot make a layer drag another along.
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the core imports nothing outside it"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "substrate.types",
    "substrate.telemetry",
    "substrate.tools",
    "substrate.models",
    "substrate.stores",
    "substrate.documents",
    "substrate.workspace",
    "substrate.safety",
    "substrate.context",
    "substrate.middleware",
    "substrate.runtime",
    "substrate.agents",
    "substrate.testing",
    "substrate.version",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "substrate.evals",
    "substrate.integrations",
    "substrate.server",
    "substrate.console",
    "substrate.cli",
    "substrate.logger",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the server is the engine over HTTP, and imports only the engine"
type = "forbidden"
# substrate.server is what `create_app(agent)` gives a downstream project: it sits on Runtime and the contracts, with
# FastAPI as its one framework. It must not reach an adapter, the reference deployment, or how an agent is built.
source_modules = ["substrate.server"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "substrate.agents",
    "substrate.integrations",
    "substrate.console",
    "substrate.cli",
    "substrate.evals",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the core's concepts only import downward"
type = "layers"
# Top first. tests/_layout.py holds the same order for the register row.
layers = [
    "substrate.testing",
    "substrate.agents",
    "substrate.runtime",
    "substrate.middleware",
    "substrate.context",
    "substrate.safety",
    "substrate.workspace",
    "substrate.documents",
    "substrate.stores",
    "substrate.models",
    "substrate.tools",
    "substrate.telemetry",
    "substrate.types",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "adapters depend on the contracts and the engine's support libraries, not how it runs an agent"
type = "forbidden"
# What an adapter (integrations/) may use from the core: the contracts it implements, and
#   models            capability registry, modality fitting, tool-argument parsing, error classification
#   workspace         object-key layout, content-addressed store, scope
#   stores            the folder stores that the cloud stores wrap or reuse, tenant binding
#   safety            text normalisation shared by the guardrail and the classifiers
#   tools, runtime    Toolbox / ToolInvoker (the chain and pipeline tools) and Runtime / RunContext / the
#                     SQL runtime store (triggers, human input, the Postgres store)
#   telemetry         spans and metrics
# These are pure or reusable by design. What it may not reach is how the engine runs an agent — the
# agents, the context window, middleware — because depending on those is how an adapter ends up coupled
# to behaviour that is free to change.
source_modules = ["substrate.integrations"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "substrate.agents",
    "substrate.context.builder",
    "substrate.context.compaction",
    "substrate.context.context",
    "substrate.context.history",
    "substrate.context.tokens",
    "substrate.middleware._contracts",
    "substrate.middleware.audit_logger",
    "substrate.middleware.cache",
    "substrate.middleware.content_truncator",
    "substrate.middleware.file_validator",
    "substrate.middleware.guardrails",
    "substrate.middleware.history_truncator",
    "substrate.middleware.pipeline",
    "substrate.middleware.rate_limiter",
    "substrate.middleware.retry",
    "substrate.middleware.schema_validator",
]
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

# Not part of this package at all: the multi-tenant platform (apps/substrate-cloud — it carries its own import contract) and
# the heavy services (apps/, packages/ — reached by URL through integrations/services).

[project]
name = "substrate-cloud"
version = "0.2.0"
description = "The multi-tenant Substrate platform: the monolith API, the nine microservices behind its gateway, and the composition root that picks backends. A consumer of the agent-substrate library."
requires-python = ">=3.13"
# Everything the library keeps optional is chosen here, because this is where backends are chosen: the library's extras
# for the vendors, stores and tools the platform wires up, plus the web, ORM, auth and observability it owns.
dependencies = [
    "agent-substrate[serve,openai,anthropic,gemini,postgres,redis,scheduler,mcp,tts,tools,logging,web,code,data,safety,sandbox]",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.12.0",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.46",
    "greenlet>=3.2.4",
    # SQLAlchemy resolves a `postgresql+psycopg://` DATABASE_URL dynamically — nothing imports it by name
    "psycopg[binary]>=3.3.0",
    # The engine only imports opentelemetry-api (a no-op until something configures an SDK); the SDK, the OTLP exporter
    # and the FastAPI instrumentation are what the platform wires up.
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi<0.60b1",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.34.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9",
    # one verifier for every entry point (Keycloak access tokens); the per-run data token is signed with pyjwt + cryptography
    "substrate-identity[fastapi]",
    "pyjwt>=2.12.0",
    "cryptography>=46.0.6",
    # the upload route counts a PDF's pages before accepting it
    "pypdf>=6.13.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = ["pytest>=9.0.3", "pytest-asyncio>=1.4.0", "httpx>=0.27.0", "pillow>=12.0.0", "import-linter>=2.11", "pytest-xdist>=3.6", "pytest-timeout>=2.3"]

[project.scripts]

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build>=0.11.16,<0.12"]

module-name = "substrate_cloud"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
# Tests marked ``heavy`` load real models (several GB, tens of seconds) and are left out of a plain run.
addopts = ["-m", "not heavy and not slow"]
markers = ["slow: Postgres-backed or minutes-long; left out of the default run (CI and `make test-slow` run them)", "heavy: loads real models"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["substrate_cloud", "substrate"]
# An import made only for type checking never runs, so it cannot make a layer drag another along.
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the platform routes cannot import the engine's internals"
type = "forbidden"
# substrate_cloud.factory and .research_orchestrator are deliberately NOT
# listed here — they're substrate_cloud/'s own composition root (formerly
# infrastructure/serving_factory.py, an orthogonal module outside the layer
# stack entirely), whose whole job is building the DI graph across every
# layer. This contract restricts the rest of substrate_cloud/ (routes, services)
# from reaching past that composition root directly.
source_modules = [
    "substrate_cloud.monolith",
    "substrate_cloud.services",
    "substrate_cloud.shared",
    "substrate_cloud.stream",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    # the engine — serving's routes use the contracts; building the engine is factory.py's job
    "substrate.agents",
    "substrate.context.builder",
    "substrate.context.compaction",
    "substrate.context.context",
    "substrate.context.tokens",
    "substrate.middleware._contracts",
    "substrate.middleware.audit_logger",
    "substrate.middleware.cache",
    "substrate.middleware.content_truncator",
    "substrate.middleware.file_validator",
    "substrate.middleware.guardrails",
    "substrate.middleware.history_truncator",
    "substrate.middleware.pipeline",
    "substrate.middleware.rate_limiter",
    "substrate.middleware.retry",
    "substrate.middleware.schema_validator",
    "substrate.models.client",
    "substrate.models.errors",
    "substrate.models.modalities",
    "substrate.models.registry",
    "substrate.models.tool_arguments",
    "substrate.runtime.cancellation",
    "substrate.runtime.context",
    "substrate.runtime.journal",
    "substrate.runtime.resolver",
    "substrate.runtime.runtime",
    "substrate.runtime.persistence.store",
    "substrate.runtime.tail",
    "substrate.runtime.tool_invoker",
    "substrate.runtime.worker",
    "substrate.safety.normalize",
    "substrate.stores.scoped",
    "substrate.tools.toolbox",
    # substrate.workspace.layout is deliberately NOT listed: it is the one place object keys are built (pure stdlib, no engine state),
    # so every route that touches the file store is meant to import it.
    "substrate.workspace.branching",
    "substrate.workspace.cas",
    "substrate.workspace.materialize",
    "substrate.workspace.scope",
    "substrate.workspace.snapshots",
    # These are the former `capabilities/` submodules, now merged into
    # `integrations/` (Phase G of the layer-charter pass). substrate_cloud/ was
    # always freely allowed to import `integrations.llm`/`.events`/`.tts`/
    # `.tools.mcp` directly (they were never under the old "capabilities"
    # restriction) — deliberately NOT listed here, so that stays true.
    "substrate.integrations.tools",
    "substrate.integrations.knowledge",
    "substrate.integrations.memory",
    "substrate.integrations.history",
    "substrate.integrations.data",
    "substrate.integrations.pipeline",
    "substrate.integrations.triggers",
    "substrate.integrations.safety",
    "substrate.integrations.artifacts",
]
# substrate_cloud/'s own factory.py is orthogonal — it may cross-cut to agents/integrations by design.
# We only want to catch DIRECT imports from substrate_cloud/'s routes to agents/former-capabilities.
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
ignore_imports = [
    # WebHITLBridge delivers human-input events; must know the capability type
    "substrate_cloud.monolith.sse.bridge -> substrate.integrations.tools.human_input",
    # pipelines/triggers routes need DTOs defined in integrations (PipelineDef, TriggerDef, ConditionDef)
    "substrate_cloud.monolith.routes.pipelines -> substrate.integrations.pipeline.engine",
    "substrate_cloud.monolith.routes.triggers -> substrate.integrations.triggers.conditions",
    "substrate_cloud.monolith.routes.triggers -> substrate.integrations.triggers.scheduler",
    # tool_executor IS a capability executor by design
    "substrate_cloud.services.tool_executor.app -> substrate.integrations.tools.code_interpreter",
    "substrate_cloud.services.tool_executor.app -> substrate.integrations.tools.code_interpreter.code_interpreter.runtimes.factory",
    "substrate_cloud.services.tool_executor.app -> substrate.integrations.tools.task_manager.tool",
    "substrate_cloud.services.tool_executor.app -> substrate.integrations.tools.web.surfer",
]

  "flax",
  "generative-models",
  "jax"
]
license = {file = "LICENSE"}
name = "avitai-artifex"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
version = "0.1.15"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Platform-specific installation:
# - Linux with GPU: uv pip install "avitai-artifex[cuda12]"
# - macOS (Apple Silicon): uv pip install avitai-artifex[all-macos]
# - macOS/Linux CPU-only: uv pip install avitai-artifex[all-cpu]
all = [
  "avitai-artifex[cuda-dev,docs]"
]
all-cpu = [
  # CPU-only installation (no GPU acceleration)
  # Use this for macOS or Linux without CUDA
  "avitai-artifex[dev,docs,test]"
]
all-macos = [
  # macOS with Metal acceleration (Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3+)
  "avitai-artifex[dev,docs,metal,test]"
]
analysis = [
  # artifex.generative_models.utils.code_analysis renders import graphs with graphviz.
  "graphviz>=0.20"
]
benchmarks = [
  # Only artifex.benchmarks needs these. datasets and huggingface-hub are imported lazily;
  # the mesh datasets and the benchmark CLI import trimesh and typer at module level.
  "avitai-artifex[cli,geometric]",
  "datasets>=2.14.0",
  "huggingface-hub>=0.25.0"
]
cli = [
  # The `artifex` console script and the benchmark runner are Typer applications.
  "typer>=0.7"
]
cuda-dev = [
  # Complete Linux CUDA development environment
  "avitai-artifex[dev,test,cuda12]"
]
cuda12 = [
  # Linux CUDA runtime managed through the official JAX extra.
  # jax, jaxlib and the NVIDIA wheels are pinned together because this extra exists to freeze
  # one validated stack, not to set a floor. Loosening any single line breaks that guarantee.
  #
  # These pins are not confined to GPU installs. uv resolves ONE universal lockfile across
  # every extra, so the jax named here is the jax that dev, test, docs and CI receive as
  # well; while this said 0.9.1 the whole repository resolved jax 0.9.1, flax 0.12.3 and
  # optax 0.2.6 no matter which extra was installed. Moving it moves everything.
  #
  # Validated 2026-08-28 on an RTX 4090 (sm_89, driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2): this stack installs
  # through `./setup.sh --backend cuda12`, scripts/verify_gpu_setup.py reports the device, and
  # 4143 generative-model and convolution tests pass on GPU in 775s. One pre-existing GPU-only
  # failure remains and is not from this stack: test_flash_attention_compatibility.py::
  # TestTransformations::test_jit_is_stable compares a jitted call against an eager one at
  # atol=1e-6 and they differ by about 7e-6 on GPU; it fails identically on the previous jax.
  #
  # CI cannot re-check any of this. Every runner is GitHub-hosted with no GPU, this extra is
  # installed by no workflow, and the GPU-only tests carry the `accelerator` marker, so they
  # skip there. The pin is therefore held by manual validation alone: re-run the check above on
  # comparable hardware before moving any version here, and record the new date.
  "jax[cuda12]==0.11.1; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "jaxlib==0.11.1; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cublas-cu12==12.9.2.10; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cuda-cccl-cu12==12.9.27; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cuda-cupti-cu12==12.9.79; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cuda-nvcc-cu12==12.9.86; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cuda-nvrtc-cu12==12.9.86; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12==12.9.79; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.24.0.43; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cufft-cu12==11.4.1.4; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cusolver-cu12==11.7.5.82; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-cusparse-cu12==12.5.10.65; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-nccl-cu12==2.31.2; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-nvjitlink-cu12==12.9.86; sys_platform == 'linux'",
  "nvidia-nvshmem-cu12==3.7.2; sys_platform == 'linux'"
]
dev = [
  "avitai-artifex[analysis]",
  "build>=1.0.3",
  "coverage>=7",
  "bandit[toml]>=1.8.6",
  "deadcode>=2.4",
  "deptry>=0.23",
  "flake8>=7.0",
  "flake8-functions-names>=0.4",
  "import-linter>=2.0",
  "interrogate>=1.5",
  "ipykernel>=6.29.5",
  "jupyter>=1.1.1",
  "jupytext>=1.16.6",
  "nbconvert>=7.16.4",
  "pydeps>=1.12.17",
  "pyright>=1.1.336",
  "pylint>=3.3",
  "pytest>=8.3.5",
  "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
  "pytest-benchmark>=4",
  "pytest-cov>=6.1.1",
  "pytest-env>=1.0.1",
  "pytest-json-report>=1.5.0",
  "pytest-randomly>=3.15",
  "pytest-timeout>=2.1",
  "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
  "python-dotenv>=1",
  "radon>=6.0",
  "ruff>=0.1.5",
  "tensorboard>=2.16",
  "vulture>=2.14",
  "wemake-python-styleguide>=1.0",
  "twine>=4.0.2",
  "pip-audit>=2.10.1",
  "xenon>=0.9.3",
  "pydoclint>=0.9.1",
  "detect-secrets>=1.5.0"
]
docs = [
  "griffe>=1.7.3",
  "hippogriffe>=0.2",
  "mkdocs>=1.6.1,<2",
  "mkdocs-include-exclude-files>=0.1",
  "mkdocs-ipynb>=0.1",
  "mkdocs-jupyter>=0.24",
  "mkdocs-material>=9.6.7,<10",
  "mkdocstrings>=0.28.3",
  "mkdocstrings-python>=1.1.2",
  "pymdown-extensions>=10.14.3"
]
geometric = [
  # ShapeNet-style mesh datasets under artifex.benchmarks.datasets.
  "trimesh>=3.30.1"
]
logging = [
  "mlflow>=2",
  "tensorboard>=2.16",
  "wandb>=0.15"
]
metal = [
  # Metal acceleration for Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2/M3+)
  # Provides GPU-like acceleration on macOS
  "jax-metal>=0.1.0; sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'"
]
test = [
  # The tracker callback tests patch `wandb.init`, and patching an attribute imports the real
  # module, so the suite needs the logging stack even though src/ imports it lazily. Declared
  # here rather than in a workflow so `uv sync --extra test` is enough to run the tests
  # anywhere, and so the macOS jobs get it through all-cpu/all-macos.
  "avitai-artifex[analysis,cli,geometric]",
  "avitai-artifex[logging]",
  "beartype>=0.14.1",
  "mock>=5.2",
  "coverage>=7",
  "hypothesis>=6.100",
  "pytest>=8.3.5",
  "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
  "pytest-benchmark>=4",
  "pytest-cov>=6.1.1",
  "pytest-env>=1.0.1",
  "pytest-json-report>=1.5.0",
  "pytest-split>=0.11",
  "pytest-timeout>=2.1",
  "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
  # The substrax pytest plugin and fresh-interpreter helpers the suite runs on.
  "substrax[testing]>=0.1.16"
]

[project.scripts]
artifex = "artifex.cli.__main__:main"

[project.urls]
repository = "https://github.com/avitai/artifex"

[tool.artifex.ci]
blocking_workflows = [
  ".github/workflows/ci.yml",
  ".github/workflows/build-verification.yml",
  ".github/workflows/security.yml"
]
compatibility_python = ["3.12", "3.13"]
informational_workflows = [
  ".github/workflows/quality-checks.yml",
  ".github/workflows/upstream-compat.yml"
]
pyright_enforcement = "blocking"
smoke_exports = ["generative_models"]
smoke_package = "artifex"
tooling_python = "3.12"

[tool.artifex.ci.security]
mode = "blocking"
reviewed_ignores = [
]

[tool.artifex.repo_standards]
line_length = 100

[tool.artifex.repo_standards.coverage]
# The repo-wide floor stays honest about current enforcement while new work
# is still expected to meet the stronger per-change target.
new_code_target = 80
project_fail_under = 80

[tool.artifex.repo_standards.docs]
development_strict = false
main_strict = true
rtd_fail_on_warning = true

[tool.artifex.repo_standards.interpreter]
docs = "3.12"
minimum_supported = "3.12"
tooling = "3.12"

[tool.artifex.repo_standards.typing]
pyright_mode = "standard"

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "examples", "notebooks", "scripts"]
skips = ["B101", "B404", "B603", "B607", "B110"]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"
skip_covered = false
skip_empty = false

[tool.coverage.paths]
source = [
  "src",
  "*/work/artifex/artifex/src"
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
  "pragma: no cover",
  "def __repr__",
  "if self.debug:",
  "if settings.DEBUG",
  "raise AssertionError",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  "if 0:",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
  "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
  "pass",
  "raise ImportError"
]
# Canonical values live in [tool.artifex.repo_standards.coverage].
fail_under = 80
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
omit = [
  "*/tests/*",
  "*/conftest.py",
  "*/__pycache__/*",
  "*/scripts/*",
  "*/examples/*",
  "*/benchmark/*"
]
parallel = true
relative_files = true
source = ["src"]

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
  "src/artifex",
  "README.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "pyproject.toml"
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/artifex"]

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["artifex"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
forbidden_modules = ["artifex.generative_models.models"]
name = "Core config must not import concrete models"
source_modules = ["artifex.generative_models.core.configuration"]
type = "forbidden"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
forbidden_modules = ["artifex.generative_models.models"]
name = "Backbone layers must not import concrete models"
source_modules = ["artifex.generative_models.core.layers"]
type = "forbidden"

[tool.interrogate]
exclude = ["tests", "scripts", "examples", "notebooks"]
fail-under = 80
ignore-init-method = true
ignore-init-module = true
ignore-magic = true

[tool.pydoclint]
allow-init-docstring = true
arg-type-hints-in-docstring = false
# Instance attributes are documented under Attributes per the Google style; pydoclint would
# compare them with class-level attributes only.
check-class-attributes = false
# Annotations are the source of truth for types; docstrings carry the prose.
check-return-types = false
check-yield-types = false
# `# noqa: DOC...` is read from the def line, where propagated exceptions are annotated.
native-mode-noqa-location = "definition"
skip-checking-short-docstrings = true
style = "google"

[tool.pyright]
exclude = ["tests"]
include = ["src"]
# Canonical values live in [tool.artifex.repo_standards.interpreter] and
# [tool.artifex.repo_standards.typing].
pythonVersion = "3.12"
reportFunctionMemberAccess = false
reportIncompatibleMethodOverride = false
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = false # Incompatible with eqx.AbstractVar
reportMissingImports = false
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
typeCheckingMode = "standard"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Configuration with smart parallel execution and coverage
# Note: -n auto removed to prevent GPU conflicts. Removed --maxfail=1 to run all tests
# Canonical coverage values live in [tool.artifex.repo_standards.coverage].
addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config --verbose --tb=short --color=yes --durations=10 --disable-warnings --cov=src/artifex --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html --cov-fail-under=80 --timeout=300 --json-report --json-report-file=temp/test-results.json --json-report-indent=2"
cache_dir = ".pytest_cache"
# Additional settings
console_output_style = "progress"
filterwarnings = [
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:pkg_resources.*",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:jax.*",
  "ignore:jax.interpreters.xla.pytype_aval_mappings is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
  "ignore::pytest.PytestCollectionWarning:cannot collect test class 'TestFileAnalysis'",
  "ignore::pytest.PytestCollectionWarning:cannot collect test class 'TestStructureAnalyzer'",
  # CUDA-related warnings (automatically handled by conftest.py)
  "ignore::UserWarning:jax._src.xla_bridge",
  "ignore:.*cuSPARSE.*",
  "ignore:.*CUDA-enabled jaxlib.*"
]
log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"
markers = [
  "blackjax: marks tests that use BlackJAX integration",
  "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
  "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
  "unit: marks tests as unit tests",
  "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests",
  "benchmark: marks tests as performance benchmarks (requires pytest-benchmark)",
  "performance: marks tests as performance tests (alias for benchmark)",
  "contract: marks tests as contract tests"
]
# Minimum version
minversion = "6.0"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_functions = "test_*"
# Main pytest configuration
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.pytest-benchmark]
compare = [
  "last",
  "base"
]
disable_gc = true
histogram = "histogram.svg"
min_rounds = 5
min_time = 0.1
save = "benchmark-results"
save_data = true
warmup = true
warmup_iterations = 3

[tool.pytest_env]
JAX_ENABLE_X64 = "0"
PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION = "python"
TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL = "1"
XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION = "0.75"
XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE = {skip_if_set = true, value = "false"}

[tool.ruff]
extend-include = ["*.ipynb"]
# Canonical value lives in [tool.artifex.repo_standards].
line-length = 100
src = []
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.format]
exclude = ["*.ipynb"]
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"
quote-style = "double"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Add W291, W292, W293 to fixable to handle whitespace issues
fixable = ["I001", "F401", "E", "W", "W291", "W292", "W293", "F841", "UP006", "UP007", "UP035"]
ignore = [
  "E402", # Module level import not at top of file
  "E721", # Do not compare types directly
  "E731", # Do not assign a lambda expression, use a def (we can refactor these later)
  "E741", # Ambiguous variable name
  "F722", # Forward annotation syntax error
  "W391", # Blank line at end of file
  "E203", # Whitespace before ':'
  # --- Documented exemptions from the adopted rule set (shared with datarax) ---
  "ANN401", # `Any` is legitimate for JAX pytree leaves and dynamic data payloads
  "TRY003", # inline exception messages are the established, readable style here
  "TRY300", # return-in-`else` restructuring adds no safety to guard-heavy flow
  "TRY004", # validation intentionally raises ValueError for structural incompatibility
  "PLR2004" # magic-value comparisons pervade numeric/array/scientific code
]
# The shared rule set. C90 (mccabe, max-complexity 10) is active; files that carried
# findings when the set was adopted are listed in the generated per-file-ignores table
# below, which scripts/check_ruff_baseline.py keeps shrinking.
select = [
  "E",
  "F",
  "I",
  "W",
  "D",
  "F841",
  "UP006",
  "UP007",
  "UP035",
  "BLE001",
  "T201",
  "ANN",
  "ARG",
  "B",
  "C90",
  "PLR",
  "PTH",
  "RET",
  "TRY"
]

[tool.ruff.lint.extend-per-file-ignores]
# Policy exemptions. The families ANN/ARG/B/C90/PLR/PTH/RET/TRY are enforced on the
# library under src/; tests, examples, scripts, docs, deployment probes and notebooks
# keep the correctness rules (E/F/I/W) and drop production-only strictness.
"*.ipynb" = ["D", "F821", "F541", "T201", "UP006", "UP035", "BLE001", "ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "TRY"] # Notebooks are generated tutorial artifacts with markdown cells and cross-cell context
"conftest.py" = ["ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "TRY"]
"deploy/**/*.py" = ["T201", "BLE001", "ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "TRY"] # Remote GPU launchers and probes report to stdout and deliberately catch whatever a backend raises
"docs/**/*.py" = ["D", "T201", "ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "TRY"] # Docs examples are tutorial sources; Ruff D is enforced on maintained src/ APIs
"examples/**/*.py" = ["D", "T201", "BLE001", "ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "TRY"] # Examples are executable tutorials with user-facing output and demo error wrappers
"scripts/**/*.py" = ["ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "TRY"] # Developer tooling; not shipped as library API
"tests/**/*.py" = ["D", "E501", "T201", "BLE001", "ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "TRY"] # Tests allow readable fixture names, debugging output, broad assertion wrappers, and long fixtures
"tests/*.py" = ["D", "E501", "T201", "BLE001", "ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "TRY"] # Tests allow readable fixture names, debugging output, broad assertion wrappers, and long fixtures
"tests/artifex/generative_models/core/sampling/test_blackjax_samplers.py" = ["E501", "E402", "T201", "BLE001"] # BlackJAX tests use custom imports and debug-style assertions

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
extra-standard-library = ["typing_extensions"]
known-first-party = ["artifex"]
lines-after-imports = 2
order-by-type = false

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Rule 2 (SRP/KISS): cyclomatic complexity ceiling; matches the radon rank-B boundary
# behind quality/complexity_baseline.json.
max-complexity = 10
