[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.uv]
python-preference = "only-managed"

[project]
name = "litestar_faststream"
description = "Litestar integration for FastStream message brokers"
license = "MIT"
readme = "README.md"
authors = [
  { name = "Hasan Sezer Taşan", email = "hasansezertasan@gmail.com" },
]
maintainers = [
  { name = "Hasan Sezer Taşan", email = "hasansezertasan@gmail.com" },
]
dynamic = ["version"]
keywords = [
  "litestar",
  "faststream",
  "asyncapi",
  "kafka",
  "rabbitmq",
  "nats",
  "redis",
  "mqtt",
  "framework",
  "message brokers",
]
classifiers = [
  "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
  "Environment :: Web Environment",
  "Framework :: AsyncIO",
  "Framework :: Pydantic :: 1",
  "Framework :: Pydantic :: 2",
  "Framework :: Pydantic",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Intended Audience :: Information Technology",
  "Intended Audience :: System Administrators",
  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Natural Language :: English",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: Implementation :: CPython",
  "Programming Language :: Python",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Application Frameworks",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
  "Topic :: Software Development",
  "Topic :: System :: Distributed Computing",
  "Topic :: System :: Networking",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]
requires-python = ">=3.10"
# Runtime dependencies restored from the pre-adoption manifest: the plugin
# imports faststream + litestar at module scope, typing_extensions for
# Python 3.10 compatibility.
dependencies = [
  "click>=8.0",
  "faststream>=0.7.1",
  "litestar>=2.24.0",
  "typing_extensions>=4.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
otel = ["opentelemetry-api>=1.20", "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20"]

[project.urls]
changelog = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/litestar-faststream/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"
documentation = "https://hasansezertasan.github.io/litestar-faststream"
homepage = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/litestar-faststream"
issues = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/litestar-faststream/issues"
releasenotes = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/litestar-faststream/releases"
source = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/litestar-faststream.git"


[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "tox==4.65.0",
  "tox-uv==1.36.1",
  "debugpy==1.8.22",
  { include-group = "style" },
  { include-group = "test" },
]
style = [
  "basedpyright==1.40.2",
  "detect-secrets==1.5.0",
  "editorconfig-checker==3.8.0",
  "import-linter==2.15",
  "mypy==2.4.0",
  "pylint==4.0.6",
  "pyrefly==1.2.0",
  "ruff==0.17.1",
  "slotscheck==0.21.0",
  "sphinx-lint==1.0.2",
  "taplo==0.9.3",
  "ty==0.0.66",
  "typos==1.51.1",
  "zuban==0.9.1",
]
# semgrep is deliberately its own group rather than part of `style`: `dev`
# includes `style` wholesale, so a plain `uv sync` — and every Windows/macOS
# cell in ci.yml, which runs `uv run --locked tox run` — would download and
# unpack ~215 MB (the wheel bundles a native semgrep-core) for a tool that only
# ever executes in the Linux-only `style` job. The tox `style` env lists this
# group explicitly. Still a single version source, same as every other pin.
sast = [
  "semgrep==1.181.0",
]
# Dependency hygiene gets its own group for the same reason `sast` does: it is
# only ever run by the on-demand `deps` tox env and the `deps` CI job, so a plain
# `uv sync` should not install it. deptry checks the imports against the declared
# dependencies (missing, transitive, misplaced or obsolete); creosote flags
# declared runtime dependencies that nothing imports.
deps = [
  "creosote==5.2.0",
  "deptry==0.25.1",
]
test = [
  "coverage-enable-subprocess==1.0",
  "coverage[toml]==7.16.2",
  "pytest-mock==3.17.0",
  "pytest-rerunfailures==16.7",
  "pytest-xdist[psutil]==3.8.0",
  "pytest==9.1.1",
  "pytest-sugar",
  "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
  "dirty-equals",
  "inline-snapshot",
  "pytest-deadfixtures==3.1.0",
  # Project test dependencies restored from the pre-adoption manifest: the
  # suite drives real Litestar apps (litestar[standard]), every FastStream
  # broker extra, MQTT via zmqtt, and the OTel instrumentation tests.
  "faststream[rabbit,kafka,confluent,nats,redis]>=0.7.1,<0.8",
  "httpx==0.28.1",
  "litestar[standard]",
  "opentelemetry-api>=1.20",
  "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20",
  "PyYAML==6.0.3",
  "zmqtt>=0.0.5; python_version >= '3.11'",
]
docs = [
  "sphinx==8.1.3",
  "shibuya==2026.7.12",
  "sphinx-autobuild==2024.10.3", # 2025.x drops Python 3.10 (requires-python >= 3.11)
  "sphinx-copybutton==0.5.2",
  "sphinx-design==0.6.1", # 0.7.0 drops Python 3.10 (requires-python >= 3.11)
  "sphinx-togglebutton==0.4.5",
  "sphinx-paramlinks==0.6.0",
  "auto-pytabs[sphinx]==0.5.0",
  "myst-parser==4.0.1",
  # Per-page "last updated" footer sourced from git commit dates;
  # offline, no network. Works from full history (docs CI checks out depth 0).
  "sphinx-last-updated-by-git==0.3.8",
  # PEP 440 version parsing/sorting used by tools/build_docs.py to order
  # published versions and pick the `latest` alias. Also a Sphinx
  # transitive dependency; pinned here for the explicit direct use.
  "packaging>=24.0",
]
tool = [
  "commitizen==4.17.0",
  # "marimo==0.15.2",
  # "inflection==0.5.1",
]
prek = [
  "prek==0.4.12",
]


[build-system]

requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]

build-backend = "hatchling.build"


[tool.uv]
add-bounds = "exact"
cache-keys = [
  { file = "pyproject.toml" },
  { git = { commit = true, tags = true } },
]
package = true
trusted-publishing = "always"


[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# Last-resort sentinel: only used when a build sees neither a .git directory nor
# an expanded .git_archival.txt (e.g. an archive of a commit with no reachable
# tag). "0.0.0" reads clearly as "version could not be determined" rather than
# masquerading as a real early release. See .git_archival.txt + .gitattributes
# `export-subst` for the archive path that recovers the real tag-derived version.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"


[tool.hatch.build]
hooks.vcs.version-file = "src/litestar_faststream/_version.py"


[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "only-version"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true


[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The package uses a src layout, so the source tree lives under /src (not
# /litestar_faststream); including /src ships the actual modules -- and, for
# C-extension projects, the .pyx/.pxd sources needed to compile from the sdist.
include = [
  "/README.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "/src",
  "/tests",
  "/docs/examples",
]


[tool.commitizen]
# Commit-authoring and message linting only. release-please owns version
# bumping, git tagging, and CHANGELOG.md (see .github/release-please-config.json),
# so the bump/tag/changelog settings are intentionally omitted here to avoid two
# tools competing over the same tags and changelog file.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# addopts = "-rXs --strict-config --strict-markers"
# `-p no:unraisableexception`: FastStream's TestBroker + AsyncMock teardown
# leaves un-awaited internal coroutines that GC finalizes after the test, and
# pytest groups repeated GC-timing artifacts into an `ExceptionGroup: multiple
# unraisable exception warnings` that NO warning filter can match (it is
# raised, not warned) — red on some OSes, green on others, for identical code
# (seen: ubuntu fails, macOS/Windows pass). The plugin detects GC timing, not
# bugs; every other warning class still errors via `filterwarnings` below.
addopts = "-v --tb=short --doctest-glob=README.md -p no:unraisableexception"
# One marker per component, auto-applied by tests/conftest.py from each test's
# top-level tests/<dir>/. Enables `pytest -m web` locally and per-component CI
# jobs; `integration` is one axis of the scheme.
# The broker markers below are the project's own: integration + example tests
# select brokers with @pytest.mark.rabbit() etc., so they must stay registered
# alongside the template's component markers under --strict-markers.
markers = [
  "core: core/shared component tests",
  "rabbit: RabbitMQ broker tests",
  "kafka: Kafka broker tests",
  "confluent: Confluent Kafka broker tests",
  "nats: NATS broker tests",
  "redis: Redis broker tests",
  "mqtt: MQTT broker tests",
]
# Strict mode requires explicit @pytest.mark.asyncio annotations, making async
# test collection intentional instead of silently accepting unmarked coroutines.
asyncio_mode = "strict"
filterwarnings = [
  "error",
]
# The project README is the deliberately small Markdown doctest surface. Other
# Markdown files can use illustrative snippets without becoming pytest inputs.
# `examples` is the project's own: per-broker demo apps ship testing.py suites
# (collected via python_files below) that must keep running.
testpaths = ["tests", "examples", "README.md"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "testing.py"]
doctest_optionflags = "ELLIPSIS IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"
xfail_strict = true


[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
# Match `_version.py` wherever it resolves: `src/...` in editable dev installs and
# `.../site-packages/...` when tox/CI installs the built (non-editable) wheel. A
# `src/**`-only pattern silently misses the installed copy and reports it at 0%.
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
parallel = true
# Store data-file paths relative to the project root so `.coverage` files produced
# on different runners/OSes merge in the `coverage-combine` CI job without
# absolute-path mismatches. Complements the `[tool.coverage.paths]` remap below
# (which unifies the src/ vs site-packages layouts).
relative_files = true
# Gate on `src` only, matching codecov's `paths: [src]`: handler stubs in tests
# (`async def h(): ...`) are never called and would drag the figure down.
source_pkgs = ["litestar_faststream"]


[tool.coverage.paths]
# Unify coverage data across environments. tox installs the built wheel into
# each env's site-packages, so the same source file is measured under a different
# `.tox/<env>/.../site-packages/litestar_faststream` path per interpreter. Without
# remapping those back to the canonical `src/` tree, `coverage combine` keeps a
# separate copy per env and a version-gated line covered in one interpreter but not
# another is wrongly counted as missed — silently failing the `fail_under` gate.
# `tests` needs no remapping: it is never installed, so every environment measures
# it at the same repo-local path.
litestar_faststream = ["src/litestar_faststream", "*/site-packages/litestar_faststream"]


[tool.coverage.report]
# Untestable code is excluded per site with `# pragma: no cover`, not with blanket
# patterns here: a regex matching a `def` line excludes the *whole function body*,
# so a pattern like `def main\(` would silently un-measure any future `main()`
# with real logic (and did mask the tested GUI/TUI entrypoints). Pragmas carry the
# exclusion decision next to the code it affects.
exclude_lines = [
  "no cov",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]
fail_under = 99
# Patterns match both the `src/` (editable) and installed (`site-packages`)
# layouts (see [tool.coverage.run] omit).
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true


[tool.vulture]
# Framework-invoked handlers: Typer commands, FastAPI routes, FastStream
# lifecycle hooks, and the MCP tool dispatcher.
ignore_decorators = [
  "@app.command",
  "@app.get",
  "@app.after_startup",
  "@app.after_shutdown",
  "@server.call_tool",
]
# Public API surfaces vulture cannot see being used: ``main`` entry points are
# referenced only via pyproject scripts, ``model_config`` is consumed by
# pydantic-settings, ``logger`` is imported only by optional components, the MCP
# ``arguments`` parameter is mandated by the call_tool signature, the Textual
# names (CSS/compose/on_mount/title/BINDINGS) are invoked by the TUI framework,
# and ``pytestmark``/``pytest_*`` (conftest hooks) are consumed by pytest at
# collection time.
#
# Project additions (verified): ``TracebackType`` is used in quoted
# `__aexit__` annotations under TYPE_CHECKING, which vulture cannot resolve.
# min_confidence stays at the pre-adoption 80: the 60%-confidence findings are
# all framework-invoked surfaces vulture cannot see (Litestar route handlers
# like html_view/json_schema/yaml_schema, Click subcommands like
# status/drain, the FastStream after_processed middleware hook, pytest fixtures
# referenced by string via usefixtures, and test doubles exercised through
# Litestar/FastStream rather than called directly).
ignore_names = ["CONFIG_FILE_PATH", "logger", "main", "model_config", "pytest_*", "collect_ignore_glob", "TracebackType"]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["src", "tests"]


[tool.deptry]
# `known_first_party` is explicit because the tox `deps` env installs the built
# wheel, so without it deptry reads the project's own imports as a third-party
# transitive dependency (DEP003). Add further `per_rule_ignores` entries for the
# project's own findings, e.g. DEP003 for a package only importable through
# another declared one, or DEP002 for an optional import guarded by try/except.
# See https://deptry.com/rules-violations/.
# Excluded: the Sphinx config, the build hook (its imports belong to
# `[build-system].requires`, not the runtime dependencies), the benchmarks and the
# worker probe script (neither ships in the wheel; pytest and anyio come from
# the dev tooling).
extend_exclude = [
  "docs/conf.py",
  # The per-broker example apps ship pytest-collected `testing.py` suites (see
  # `python_files` in [tool.pytest.ini_options]); like tests/ they may import
  # dev-only `pytest`, so deptry must not audit them for misplaced dev imports.
  "examples/confluent/testing.py",
  "examples/kafka/testing.py",
  "examples/mqtt/testing.py",
  "examples/multiple_plugins_host/testing.py",
  "examples/nats/testing.py",
  "examples/rabbit/testing.py",
  "examples/redis/testing.py",
]
known_first_party = ["litestar_faststream"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# tools/build_docs.py imports `packaging`, pinned in the `docs` group for that
# script alone, so deptry reads it as a misplaced dev dependency.
DEP004 = ["packaging"]
# The `otel` extra is imported in a try/except with no-op stub fallback (see
# src/litestar_faststream/_otel_typing.py); deptry does not count guarded
# imports as usage, so the optional pair reads as unused.
DEP002 = ["opentelemetry-api", "opentelemetry-sdk"]


[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "litestar_faststream"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# Tests and runtime code must stay decoupled in the import graph.
# (Restored from the pre-adoption manifest. The template renders a `layers`
# contract over `core`/`utils` packages, but the adoption removes that skeleton:
# this package is flat modules with mutual imports — plugin/host/lifespan,
# decorators/discovery, di, asyncapi/cli/info, instrumentation — which no layer
# ordering expresses without a redesign. If layers are introduced later, replace
# this contract with the template's and update AGENTS.md in the same PR.)
name = "src does not import tests"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["litestar_faststream"]
forbidden_modules = ["tests"]


[tool.ruff]
fix = true
output-format = "full"
preview = true
show-fixes = true
src = ["src", "tests", "examples", "docs/examples"]
target-version = "py310"
unsafe-fixes = true


[tool.ruff.analyze]
detect-string-imports = true
preview = true


[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true
line-ending = "lf"
preview = true
skip-magic-trailing-comma = true


[tool.ruff.lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
# Two opinionated ruff 0.16 preview rules are disabled: RUF105 would rewrite the
# portable `# noqa` comments into ruff's own `# ruff: ignore` syntax (its docs note
# `# noqa` is needed for cross-tool compatibility), and RUF201 would rewrite every
# rule *code* in this config's selectors into long rule *names*. Both are stylistic.
#
# Restored from the pre-adoption manifest (deliberate project policy, kept so the
# adoption does not rewrite the codebase to satisfy the stricter template gate):
# - ANN401 — broker payloads, handler registries, and decorator passthroughs are
#   structurally `Any` across the whole package (53 sites in 12 modules).
# - DOC201 + D100/D101/D102/D103/D104/D107 — google-style docstrings without
#   `Returns` sections and without per-symbol docstrings on every public name.
ignore = ["COM812", "CPY", "FIX", "RUF105", "RUF201", "TD", "ANN401", "DOC201", "D100", "D101", "D102", "D103", "D104", "D107"]
logger-objects = ["logging_setup.logger"]
preview = true
select = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
# skip-magic-trailing-comma = true
split-on-trailing-comma = false

# Restored from the pre-adoption manifest: the suite uses `@pytest.mark.asyncio()`
# *with* parentheses (and parenthesized fixtures / tuple-style parametrize), so the
# template's PT023/PT001/PT007 defaults are flipped to match instead of rewriting
# ~90 decorations.
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-pytest-style]
fixture-parentheses = true
mark-parentheses = true
parametrize-names-type = "tuple"
parametrize-values-type = "tuple"
parametrize-values-row-type = "tuple"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-copyright]
author = "Hasan Sezer Taşan <hasansezertasan@gmail.com>"


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"


[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 5


[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
ignore-overlong-task-comments = true


[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"


[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Recursive glob so nested test packages (tests/cli, tests/gui, ...) are covered.
# Tests legitimately use asserts/magic values, reach into package internals, and
# don't need return-value documentation on their fixtures and helpers.
# Project tests are white-box by design: they drive private plugin internals
# (SLF001), import fixtures inside test functions (PLC0415), declare async tests
# without awaits (RUF029), leave hook/fixture args unused (ARG001/ARG002/ARG005),
# and use untyped/defensive signatures (ANN001/ANN401); grouping helpers stay
# methods rather than staticmethods (PLR6301).
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "PLC2701", "DOC201", "ANN001", "ANN401", "ARG001", "ARG002", "ARG005", "PLC0415", "PLR6301", "RUF029", "SLF001"]
# Example apps are runnable demos, not libraries: they are not application
# packages (INP001), relative imports keep them executable as scripts (TID252),
# handlers stay methods (PLR6301), inline asserts and magic values are the test
# style (S101/PLR2004), docstrings are prose-light, and a few long lines are URLs
# (E501); one white-box access (SLF001) and async demo endpoints without awaits
# (RUF029) are intentional.
"examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001", "TID252", "PLR6301", "S101", "PLR2004", "RUF029", "E501", "SLF001"]
# Documentation examples are importable modules tested by
# ``tests/test_docs_examples.py``; they are not application packages.
"docs/examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001"]
# The Sphinx config is a standalone module, not part of an importable package.
"docs/conf.py" = ["INP001"]
# The docs warning-allowlist gate is a standalone script (not an importable
# package) whose whole job is to print GitHub `::error::` annotations to stdout.
"docs/check_warnings.py" = ["INP001", "T201"]
# The versioned-docs build orchestrator is a standalone CLI script under tools/,
# not part of an importable package.
"tools/build_docs.py" = ["INP001"]

# --- Project source: load-bearing patterns (verified per-file, not blanket) ---
# Broker client imports stay lazy so `litestar_faststream` imports without any
# broker extra installed; only the code path that needs a broker imports it
# (PLC0415 for cli/host/plugin). Lifespan/shutdown paths must never fail because
# telemetry or a hook did: errors are logged and teardown continues (BLE001 for
# cli/host/instrumentation — the documented lifespan composition). host.py drives
# the package's own composer internals and the README-documented
# broker._subscribers introspection (SLF001). Litestar route/hook handlers must
# stay methods: `self` is the shared Controller singleton between HTTP and stream
# handlers, so PLR6301's staticmethod rewrite would break the documented binding
# semantics. hooks.py lifespan banners are async by protocol without awaits
# (RUF029) and hooks.py/instrumentation.py keep protocol-mandated unused args
# (ARG001/ARG002). Discovery, CLI orchestration, and lifespan composition are
# inherently branched; the pre-adoption policy capped nothing here (C901).
"src/litestar_faststream/asyncapi.py" = ["PLR6301", "C901"]
"src/litestar_faststream/cli.py" = ["PLC0415", "BLE001", "C901"]
"src/litestar_faststream/discovery.py" = ["C901"]
"src/litestar_faststream/hooks.py" = ["PLR6301", "RUF029", "ARG001"]
"src/litestar_faststream/host.py" = ["PLC0415", "BLE001", "SLF001", "C901"]
"src/litestar_faststream/instrumentation.py" = ["BLE001", "ARG002", "PLR6301", "C901"]
"src/litestar_faststream/lifespan.py" = ["C901"]
"src/litestar_faststream/plugin.py" = ["PLC0415", "PLR6301", "PLR0912", "C901"]


[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true


[tool.ruff.lint.ruff]
parenthesize-tuple-in-subscript = true


[tool.mypy]
files = ["src", "docs/examples"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.10"
strict = true


[tool.basedpyright]
exclude = [".venv"]
include = ["src/litestar_faststream", "docs/examples"]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
venv = ".venv"
# venvPath is the directory *containing* the venv, not the venv itself; ".venv"
# here would make basedpyright look for ".venv/.venv". Use "." so both the venv
# and basedpyright's strict ruleset resolve the project's installed deps.
venvPath = "."


[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "tests", "docs/examples"]
respect-ignore-files = false


[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.10"


[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true


[[tool.ty.overrides]]
# Restored from the pre-adoption manifest: tests assert on dynamically-attached
# attributes — FastStream's Test brokers expose `.mock` at runtime and the
# `@subscriber`/`@publisher` markers stash `__faststream_*__` metadata via
# assignment — which no checker can resolve statically.
include = ["tests/**/*.py"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
empty-body = "ignore"


[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.10"
project-includes = ["src", "docs/examples"]

[tool.pylint.main]
# pylint runs as an always-on gate that deliberately overlaps ruff's PL* rules.
# Its canonical invocation is `pylint src docs/examples`, so it never descends into tests; this
# ignore-paths is a defensive scope guard for broader invocations (`pylint .`,
# filename-passing hooks). Tests are linted by ruff, not pylint.
ignore-paths = ["^tests/.*$"]
# `.pyi` stubs (the c-extension type stub) are signature-only: their bodies are
# `...` and every parameter is unused by construction, so pylint's unused-argument
# check is a guaranteed false positive there. Stubs are type-checked by the
# type-checker gate, not pylint.
ignore-patterns = ['.*\.pyi$']

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
# Only formatter-owned checks, the docstring family, and too-few-public-methods
# are disabled so pylint is usable out of the box; everything else stays on.
disable = [
  "line-too-long", # C0301 — ruff-format owns line length
  "missing-module-docstring", # C0114
  "missing-class-docstring", # C0115
  "missing-function-docstring", # C0116
  "too-few-public-methods", # R0903 — trips dataclasses / config / Protocol classes
  # C0415 — the cli->tui/gui/web dispatch, and each component's own heavy or
  # platform-conditional import (tkinter, uvicorn, the worker's uvloop probe),
  # are deliberately lazy so import-linter's layering contract holds and a
  # framework is only imported when the code path that needs it actually runs.
  # Textual is the exception: the TUI imports it at module scope so `InfoApp`
  # can be defined there and driven by the headless pilot.
  "import-outside-toplevel",
  # W0706 — the generated TUI entry point explicitly re-raises
  # KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit ahead of a broad `except Exception` to make the
  # "let these propagate" intent obvious to readers, even though BaseException
  # subclasses wouldn't be caught by the Exception clause anyway.
  "try-except-raise",
  # R0801 — the component skeletons (gui/tui/mcp/worker) are deliberately
  # parallel: each fetches package metadata and formats the same info block the
  # same way. That structural symmetry is a feature of the layout, not
  # copy-paste debt, and R0801 cannot be suppressed inline at the call site.
  "duplicate-code",
]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10
max-positional-arguments = 10
max-branches = 20

[tool.typos.files]
# The answers file can record a `git describe` string (`v1.2.3-4-g<hash>`), and
# a fragment of the hex hash can read as a misspelled word, failing the check on
# a hash nobody chose. The file is machine-written with no prose to check. The prek hook passes
# `--force-exclude`, so the exclusion holds there as well as in `tox -e style`.
extend-exclude = [
  ".copier-answers.yml",
]

[tool.typos.default.extend-words]
# `mosquitto` is the MQTT broker's real name (examples/mqtt), not a misspelling
# of `mosquito`. Mapping a word to itself marks it as valid.
mosquitto = "mosquitto"

[tool.tox]
# The ``worker`` env is intentionally omitted: it starts a broker-bound process
# and would hang/fail under ``tox run`` in CI (where no broker is available).
# The worker is covered by its pytest TestBroker suite; run it on demand with
# ``tox -e worker`` when a broker is up (e.g. inside the devcontainer).
env_list = [
  "style",
  # Inline ``>>>`` snippets are part of the tested-documentation contract,
  # so run them in the default CI ``tox run`` invocation.
  "docs-doctest",
  "3.14",
  "3.13",
  "3.12",
  "3.11",
  "3.10",
]
requires = ["tox>=4"]


[tool.tox.env_run_base]
commands = [
  [
    "coverage",
    "run",
    "--module",
    "pytest",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the tests under {base_python}"
env_tmp_dir = "{toxworkdir}/tmp/{envname}"
# Arms coverage-enable-subprocess so xdist/subprocess workers are measured too;
# `coverage run` plus `parallel = true` writes per-env data files that the CI
# `coverage combine` step merges.
set_env = { COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = "{tox_root}/pyproject.toml" }
# Non-editable: `uv sync --no-editable` builds the project and installs it into
# site-packages, the layout `[tool.coverage.paths]` remaps and the per-component
# coverage gates measure.
package = "wheel"
# Every env installs from uv.lock (`uv sync --locked`), so tox tests and lints
# the exact versions the lockfile pins. The plain `uv-venv-runner` resolves the
# project's own dependencies fresh on every env creation (tox's
# `use_frozen_constraints` never reaches its `uv pip install`), so a newer
# release could float in and clash with a pinned tool such as semgrep.
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.style]
base_python = ["3.10"]
commands = [
  [
    "ruff",
    "check",
    "--no-fix",
  ],
  [
    "ruff",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.10",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.14",
  ],
  # Style runs once on Linux, so explicitly sweep platform-gated branches that
  # mypy would otherwise prune as unreachable on the host platform.
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "win32",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "darwin",
  ],
  [
    "basedpyright",
  ],
  [
    "ty",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "pyrefly",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "zuban",
    "check",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "pylint",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "python",
    "-m",
    "slotscheck",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "lint-imports",
  ],
  # Rules-database SAST. Deliberately style-env-only (like ty/pyrefly/zuban) and
  # not a prek hook: semgrep keeps no on-disk rule cache, so a pre-commit hook
  # would make a registry request on every `git commit`. The ruleset is named
  # explicitly rather than `--config auto` so rule selection does not depend on
  # language auto-detection; it is still fetched from the registry, which is why
  # this cannot be vendored. `--error` makes findings blocking;
  # silence a false positive with a trailing `# nosemgrep: <rule-id>`.
  [
    "semgrep",
    "scan",
    "--config",
    "p/python",
    "--error",
    "--metrics=off",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "taplo",
    "lint",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  # A strict `--check` gate, not fix mode: a generated file that taplo would
  # rewrite fails its own CI on first push.
  # `.taplo.toml` disables array auto expand/collapse so the shipped layout is
  # the canonical one regardless of which components are enabled. The `*.toml`
  # glob is non-recursive, so it scopes taplo to this project's own root TOML
  # (pyproject/prek/mise/taplo) without walking vendored `.tox`/`.venv`/
  # site-packages trees — no `.taplo.toml` exclude config needed.
  [
    "taplo",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  [
    "typos",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "ec",
  ],
  [
    "sphinx-lint",
    "docs",
    "REPOSITORY_SETUP.rst",
  ],
  # Collects (does not run) the suite and flags fixtures that are never used --
  # cheap, deterministic, and a natural fit next to the other whole-program
  # analyzers above (lint-imports, slotscheck).
  [
    "pytest",
    "--dead-fixtures",
  ],
]
# `test` is included so the type checkers that scope tests (e.g. ty) can
# resolve pytest and other test-only imports.
dependency_groups = ["sast", "style", "test"]
description = "Run Checkers, Linters and Formatters"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


# On-demand and CI-only (not in env_list, like `integration`): the `deps` job in
# ci.yml runs it and `check` aggregates that job. `test` is included so deptry
# and creosote can resolve the project's own test-only imports. creosote needs
# the installed distributions to map import names, which the lock runner provides.
[tool.tox.env.deps]
commands = [
  [
    "deptry",
    ".",
  ],
  [
    "creosote",
    "--deps-file",
    "pyproject.toml",
    "--section",
    "project.dependencies",
    # Without this creosote skips imports inside functions, so a dependency used
    # only through a lazy import (the worker's uvloop) is reported as unused.
    "--include-deferred",
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["deps", "test"]
description = "Check dependency hygiene (deptry, creosote)"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.prek]
commands = [["prek", "run", "--all-files"]]
dependency_groups = ["prek"]
description = "Run prek hooks"
# The hooks that need the project call `uv run --locked`, which syncs it (and the
# groups they name) into this env through the runner's UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT;
# installing the wheel here too would only be swapped for that install each run.
package = "skip"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-build]
# Write the warning stream to a file (`-w`) instead of `-W` turning the first
# warning into a hard error, then let docs/check_warnings.py own the pass/fail:
# it diffs the emitted warnings against the docs/expected_warnings.txt allowlist,
# failing on both unexpected new warnings and expected ones that vanished.
commands = [
  ["sphinx-build", "-w", "docs/_build/warnings.txt", "-b", "html", "docs", "docs/_build/html"],
  ["python", "docs/check_warnings.py"],
]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Build Docs"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
# Keep build log output unbuffered/ordered. Reproducible builds pin Sphinx's
# "today"/copyright to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, which the CI docs steps
# (docs-preview.yml, release.yml) export from the last commit date before
# invoking sphinx-build directly. Local `tox` runs deliberately do NOT export
# it: an empty value ("{env:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:}") is *present but blank*, which
# breaks hatchling's get_reproducible_timestamp (`int("")`), so we leave it
# unset locally and conf.py falls back to the current year.
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-server]
# ``--ignore`` the machine-generated ``docs/_generated/`` tree: ``conf.py``
# rewrites it on every Sphinx build, so watching it would make each rebuild
# trigger the next in an endless live-reload loop.
commands = [["sphinx-autobuild", "--ignore", "*/_generated/*", "docs", "docs/_build/html"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Start the live-reloading docs server"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-doctest]
# ``literalinclude`` keeps complete examples in tested Python modules; this
# separate builder executes the occasional ``>>>`` snippet that belongs inline
# with prose.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "doctest", "docs", "docs/_build/doctest"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Run documentation doctests"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-linkcheck]
# On-demand link checker. Also run weekly (non-blocking) by docs-linkcheck.yml.
# Hits the network, so it is deliberately not part of the `style` env or PR CI.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "linkcheck", "docs", "docs/_build/linkcheck"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Check documentation for broken links"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🔨 BUILD SYSTEM
# Defines the build backend and requirements
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[build-system]
# Capped below 1.32: from that version hatchling emits Metadata-Version 2.5,
# which the twine bundled in pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish still rejects
# ("'2.5' is not a valid metadata version"). 1.31.x emits 2.4.
requires = ["hatchling>=1.27,<1.32"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 📦 PROJECT METADATA
# Package information, version, authors, and classifiers
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[project]
name = "ezcompiler"
version = "4.1.2"
description = "Project compilation and distribution framework for Python projects"
readme = { file = "README.md", content-type = "text/markdown" }
requires-python = ">=3.13"
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "Neuraaak" }]
maintainers = [{ name = "Neuraaak" }]
keywords = [
    "compilation",
    "packaging",
    "distribution",
    "cx_freeze",
    "pyinstaller",
    "versioning",
]
classifiers = [
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Build Tools",
    "Environment :: Console",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 📚 DEPENDENCIES
# Core production dependencies for runtime
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

dependencies = [
    "InquirerPy>=0.3.0",
    "requests>=2.28.0",
    "click>=8.0.0",
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    "ezplog>=2.0.2",
    "jinja2>=3.1.0",
    "tomli-w>=1.0.0",
    "packaging>=23.0",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🛠️ OPTIONAL DEPENDENCIES
# Development tools, testing, and build dependencies
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[project.optional-dependencies]
cx-freeze = ["cx_Freeze>=7.0,<9.0"]
pyinstaller = ["PyInstaller>=5.0"]
nuitka = ["Nuitka>=2.4"]
all-compilers = [
    "cx_Freeze>=7.0,<9.0",
    "PyInstaller>=5.0",
    "Nuitka>=2.4",
]
tufup = ["tufup>=0.10,<1.0"]
r2 = ["boto3>=1.34,<2.0"]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🧰 DEPENDENCY GROUPS (PEP 735)
# Development tooling. Unlike [project.optional-dependencies] above, these
# are NOT published in the wheel metadata: `pip install ezcompiler[dev]`
# is no longer a valid command, and the PyPI page only advertises the
# product extras. Install with `uv sync --group dev`.
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[dependency-groups]
test = [
    "pytest>=7.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0.0",
    "pytest-mock>=3.10.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.0.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0.0",
]
docs = [
    "mkdocs>=1.6.0,<2.0.0",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.5.0",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.27.0",
    "mkdocs-section-index>=0.3.0",
    "mkdocs-coverage>=1.1.0",
    "mike>=2.0.0",
    "pymdown-extensions>=10.7",
    "git-cliff>=2.7.0",
    "grimp>=2.3.0",

    # Task runner: 04-docs runs `poe docs-coverage|imports|graph` and syncs
    # only `docs` + `test`, so poethepoet must be reachable from this group.
    "poethepoet>=0.32",
]
dev = [
    # Tests (single source of truth, no duplication)
    { include-group = "test" },

    # Documentation (single source of truth, no duplication)
    { include-group = "docs" },

    # Development tools
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
    "ty>=0.0.13",
    "pyright>=1.1.0",
    "pre-commit>=3.0.0",

    # Task runner
    "poethepoet>=0.32",

    # Security
    "bandit>=1.7.0",
    "pip-audit>=2.7.0",

    # Compilers (all, for testing)
    "cx_Freeze>=7.0,<9.0",
    "PyInstaller>=5.0",
    "Nuitka>=2.4",

    # Build and distribution
    "build>=1.0.0",
    "twine>=4.0.0",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🔗 PROJECT URLS
# Links to repository, documentation, and package index
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/neuraaak/ezcompiler"
Documentation = "https://neuraaak.github.io/ezcompiler/"
Repository = "https://github.com/neuraaak/ezcompiler"
PyPI = "https://pypi.org/project/ezcompiler/"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🖥️ SCRIPTS
# Entry points for command-line tools
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[project.scripts]
ezcompiler = "ezcompiler.interfaces.cli_interface:main"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# ⚡ POE TASKS
# Developer commands: run with `uv run poe <task>`
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[tool.poe.tasks]
lint = "ruff check ."
lint-fix = "ruff check --fix ."
format = "ruff format ."
format-check = "ruff format --check ."
typecheck = "ty check src/ezcompiler/"
build = "uv build"
docs = "mkdocs serve"
docs-build = "mkdocs build --strict"
docs-coverage = "pytest --cov=src/ezcompiler --cov-report=html --cov-report=xml -q"
graph = "python .scripts/dev/generate_architecture_graph.py"
version = "python .scripts/dev/update_version.py"
# Machine-readable version for CI: the single source the workflows read,
# instead of each one re-implementing a grep/sed on pyproject.toml.
read-version = '''python -c "import tomllib, pathlib; print(tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))['project']['version'])"'''

test = "pytest"
test-ci = "pytest --cov=src/ezcompiler --cov-fail-under=70"
test-unit = "pytest -m unit"
test-fast = "pytest -n auto -m 'not slow'"

[tool.poe.tasks.imports]
help = "Check import-linter layer contracts"
cmd = "lint-imports"
env = { PYTHONPATH = "src" }

[tool.poe.tasks.security]
help = "Run Bandit and audit locked dependencies"
sequence = [
    "bandit -r src/ezcompiler -ll",
    "pip-audit --ignore-vuln GHSA-qp9x-wp8f-qgjj",
]
default_item_type = "cmd"

[tool.poe.tasks.check]
help = "Full local quality gate (mirrors CI)"
sequence = ["format-check", "lint", "typecheck", "imports", "test-ci"]
default_item_type = "ref"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 📦 HATCHLING CONFIGURATION
# Package discovery and inclusion/exclusion patterns
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/ezcompiler"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
exclude = [
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "htmlcov",
    ".hooks",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    ".git",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".cursor",
    ".tmp",
    "*.pyc",
    "*.pyo",
    "*.log",
    ".coverage",
    "coverage.xml",
    ".DS_Store",
    "Thumbs.db",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🎨 CODE FORMATTING & LINTING TOOLS
# Auto-formatting, import sorting, and style checking
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Ruff: All-in-one linter with comprehensive rule sets
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 88
# Markdown code blocks are authored for readability (aligned comments),
# not as formatted source.
extend-exclude = ["docs"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "I",   # isort-compatible import sorting (via ruff)
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "S",   # bandit security
    "T20", # flake8-print
    "ARG", # flake8-unused-arguments
    "PIE", # flake8-pie
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
]
# S101 (assert), T201 (print) and S603 (subprocess) are NOT ignored
# globally: the AGENTS.md rules "never print() in library code" and "no
# invariant assert in production" must stay enforceable on src/. Legitimate
# exemptions live in per-file-ignores, or in a one-off `# noqa` on the
# subprocess call concerned.
ignore = [
    "E501", # line too long, handled by ruff format
    "B008", # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "S106", # hardcoded_password_funcarg
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*" = ["S101", "S311", "E501", "ARG002"]
"examples/**/*" = ["T201", "E501"]
".scripts/**/*" = ["T201", "E501"]
"src/ezcompiler/interfaces/**/*" = ["T201", "E501"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# ✅ TYPE CHECKING TOOLS
# Static type analysis with minimal and comprehensive modes
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# ty: Type checking with minimal configuration
[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.13"
root = ["src", "src/ezcompiler"]

[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src/ezcompiler/**/*.py"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
]

# Respect .gitignore
respect-ignore-files = true

[tool.ty.terminal]
output-format = "full"
error-on-warning = false

# Pyright: powers the IDE (Pylance). Not a CI gate — `ty` is the single
# type-checking gate, in the pre-commit hook and in 01-ci. This config is kept
# so editor diagnostics match the checked scope.
[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

# Include/exclude paths
include = ["src/ezcompiler"]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "**/node_modules",
    "**/.*",
]

# Reporting rules: flag missing imports and duplicates
reportMissingImports = true
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportUnusedImport = true
reportUnusedClass = true
reportUnusedFunction = true
reportUnusedVariable = true
reportDuplicateImport = true

# Optional type checking (None safety)
reportOptionalSubscript = true
reportOptionalMemberAccess = true
reportOptionalCall = true
reportOptionalIterable = true
reportOptionalContextManager = true
reportOptionalOperand = true

# Tolerance for decorators and complex types
reportUntypedFunctionDecorator = false
reportUntypedClassDecorator = false
reportUntypedBaseClass = false
reportUntypedNamedTuple = false

# Override and consistency checks
reportPrivateUsage = false
reportConstantRedefinition = true
reportIncompatibleMethodOverride = true
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = true
reportInconsistentConstructor = true

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🧭 IMPORT LINTER CONTRACTS
# Layer dependency contracts enforced in CI
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["ezcompiler"]
# Note: import-linter 2.x does not support source_paths (feature pending PR #323).
# The package must be installed in editable mode (pip install -e .)
# or run with PYTHONPATH=src lint-imports

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "layer dependency flow"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "ezcompiler.interfaces",
    "ezcompiler.services",
    "ezcompiler.adapters",
    "ezcompiler.utils",
    "ezcompiler.shared",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "types is import-only (no upward deps)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ezcompiler._types"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ezcompiler.interfaces",
    "ezcompiler.services",
    "ezcompiler.adapters",
    "ezcompiler.utils",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "assets has no upward deps"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ezcompiler.assets"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ezcompiler.interfaces",
    "ezcompiler.services",
    "ezcompiler.adapters",
]

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🧪 TESTING & COVERAGE TOOLS
# Test execution, coverage analysis, and test configuration
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Pytest: Test runner with markers and coverage configuration
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "7.0"
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--cov=src/ezcompiler",
    "--cov-report=term-missing",
    "--cov-report=html",
    "--cov-report=xml",
    # No --cov-fail-under here: it would make any partial run (one file, a
    # -k, a marker) exit with code 1. The threshold is carried by the CI
    # command: `pytest --cov=src/ezcompiler --cov-fail-under=70`.
    "--tb=short",
    "--color=yes",
    "--durations=10",
    "--maxfail=5",
]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "requires_iscc: needs a real ISCC.exe (Inno Setup 6) on the machine",
    "requires_gh: needs a real, authenticated gh CLI on the machine",
    "unit: marks tests as unit tests (default)",
    "cli: marks tests related to CLI",
    "compiler: marks tests related to compilers",
    "uploader: marks tests related to uploaders",
    "robustness: marks tests for robustness and edge cases",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
]

# Coverage: Code coverage measurement and reporting
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/ezcompiler"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/site-packages/*",
    "*/.pytest_cache/*",
    "*/.benchmarks/*",
    "*/.vscode/*",
    "*/.egg-info/*",
    "*/.hooks/*",
    "setup.py",
    "build/*",
    "dist/*",
    ".venv/*",
    "venv/*",
    "htmlcov/*",
    "coverage.xml",
    ".coverage",
    "docs/*",
    "examples/*",
    "_temp/*",
    # Modules non testables unitairement (TUF signing / TTY interactif).
    # Les adaptateurs de compilation restent mesures : leur construction de
    # ligne de commande est du code testable (cf. _cx_freeze_compiler).
    "*/adapters/_tufup_releaser.py",
    "*/interfaces/cli_interface.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
# Lines to exclude: comments, abstractions, unreachable code
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "if self.debug:",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if 0:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
    "if platform.system\\(\\) == \"Windows\":",
    "except ImportError:",
]
show_missing = true
precision = 2
fail_under = 70

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
# 🔒 SECURITY TOOLS
# Code security scanning and vulnerability detection
# ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

# Bandit: Security linter for identifying common security issues
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = [
    "tests",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "venv",
    ".venv",
    ".hooks",
    "docs",
    "examples",
    "_temp",
]
skips = ["B601"]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "src"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "routers",
    "views",
    "services",
    "repositories",
    "models"
]
containers = [
    "src.modules.users",
    "src.modules.appointments",
    "src.modules.doctors",
    "src.modules.medical_records",
    "src.modules.notification"
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Service independence"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "src.modules.users.services",
    "src.modules.appointments.services",
    "src.modules.doctors.services",
    "src.modules.medical_records.services",
    "src.modules.notification.services"
]


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Views independence"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "src.modules.users.views",
    "src.modules.appointments.views",
    "src.modules.doctors.views",
    "src.modules.medical_records.views",
    "src.modules.notification.views"
]

[tool.pylint.master]
init-hook = "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, './')"

[tool.pylint.main]
ignore = ["venv"]
jobs = 2

[tool.pylint.messages_control]
disable = [
    "C0114", # missing-module-docstring
    "C0115", # missing-class-docstring
    "C0116", # missing-function-docstring
    "C0103", # invalid-name
    "R0903", # too-few-public-methods
    "W0718", # broad-exception-caught
    "R0801",
    "W1203", # logging-fstring-interpolation
    "E1102",
    "C0121", # singleton-comparison
    "I1101"
]

[tool.pylint.format]
max-line-length = 120

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 7
max-positional-arguments = 7
max-attributes=8
max-locals = 17
max-returns = 8
max-branches = 13
max-statements = 50

[tool.pylint.basic]
good-names = ["i", "j", "k", "ex", "Run", "_"]

[tool.pylint.reports]
output-format = "colorized"
reports = false
score = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "-v --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=50"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/bitranox_template_py_cli"]
include = [
    "src/bitranox_template_py_cli/py.typed",
    "src/bitranox_template_py_cli/adapters/config/defaultconfig.toml",
    "src/bitranox_template_py_cli/adapters/config/defaultconfig.d/*.toml",
]

# An allowlist, never a denylist: hatchling reads only the root .gitignore, so tracked working
# files and files hidden through .git/info/exclude or a nested .gitignore (session records,
# review notes, helper scripts) would ship. tests/test_packaging.py builds the sdist and
# refuses any other top-level entry.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
    "/src/bitranox_template_py_cli",
    "/tests/*.py",
    "/docs",
    "/README.md",
    "/CONFIG.md",
    "/LICENSE",
    "/CHANGELOG.md",
    "/pyproject.toml",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E", "W",     # pycodestyle
  "F",           # pyflakes
  "I",           # isort
  "N",           # pep8-naming
  "UP",          # pyupgrade
  "B",           # bugbear
  "A",           # builtins shadowing
  "C4",          # comprehension simplification
  "C90",         # mccabe: cyclomatic complexity <= 10 (the house hard limit)
  "SIM",         # simplification
  "TCH",         # type-checking imports
  "RUF",         # ruff-specific
  "G",           # logging format (catches f-string in logger)
  "T20",         # print statements
  "PTH",         # pathlib preference
  "PLC", "PLE",  # pylint conventions/errors
  "S",           # flake8-bandit security checks
  "PERF",        # performance anti-patterns
  "ERA",         # eradicate dead/commented-out code
  "FBT",         # boolean trap (boolean positional args)
  "PLR",         # pylint refactor
  "PLW",         # pylint warnings
]
[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
# The Pydantic models (EmailConfig, LoggingConfigModel)
# resolve their field annotations at model-build time, so their field-type imports
# must stay at runtime even though the file uses ``from __future__ import annotations``.
# Telling ruff about the Pydantic base keeps TC001/TC002/TC003 from moving those
# imports into a TYPE_CHECKING block and breaking model construction.
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Notebooks: unused imports are often intentional for side effects
"notebooks/*.ipynb" = ["F401"]
# Tests: assert is standard, test fixtures have passwords, magic values are clearer inline, temp paths are fine.
# PLC0415: local/deferred imports are a deliberate test idiom - several tests import inside the test
# body to exercise import-time and cache behaviour, so moving them to module top would defeat intent.
"tests/*.py" = ["T20", "S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "FBT001", "FBT003", "PLR0913", "PLR2004", "PLC0415"]
# CLI: Click framework injects boolean params; commands have many options
"src/bitranox_template_py_cli/adapters/cli/**/*.py" = ["FBT001", "FBT002", "PLR0913"]
# Protocols/adapters: many-param signatures by design
"src/bitranox_template_py_cli/application/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/bitranox_template_py_cli/adapters/config/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/bitranox_template_py_cli/adapters/email/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]
"src/bitranox_template_py_cli/adapters/memory/*.py" = ["PLR0913"]

[tool.pyright]
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
extraPaths = [
  "src",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = ["--doctest-modules"]
doctest_optionflags = ["ELLIPSIS", "NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
markers = [
  "os_agnostic: test runs on every supported operating system",
  "os_windows: test exercises Windows-only behavior",
  "os_macos: test exercises macOS-only behavior",
  "os_posix: test exercises behavior requiring POSIX semantics",
  "os_linux: test exercises Linux-only behavior",
  "local_only: tests that require the local dev environment (external resources, script composition); skipped in CI",
  "integration: tests requiring external resources (SMTP, databases, APIs); run via 'bmk ti' or 'mktesti.sh'",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
parallel = false
# The coverage database lives outside the checkout, because SQLite needs file
# locking that a network-mounted tree does not reliably give it. It is one path
# for the whole machine, so every run that leaves COVERAGE_FILE unset shares it:
# pytest-cov erases it when a run starts and combines the data files beside it
# when a run ends. bmk and CI each point COVERAGE_FILE at a directory of their
# own; set it the same way before running pytest --cov beside another run.
data_file = "/tmp/.coverage.bitranox_template_py_cli"
source = ["src/bitranox_template_py_cli"]

[tool.coverage.report]
omit = [
  "tests/*",
]
fail_under = 80
show_missing = true

[tool.coverage.json]
output = "coverage.json"
pretty_print = true

# Patterns to remove when running `make clean`
patterns = [
  "**/__pycache__",
  ".hypothesis",
  ".import_linter_cache",
  ".pytest_cache",
  ".ruff_cache",
  ".pyright",
  ".mypy_cache",
  ".tox",
  ".nox",
  ".eggs",
  "*.egg-info",
  "build",
  "dist",
  "htmlcov",
  ".coverage",
  "coverage.xml",
  "codecov.sh",
  ".cache",
  "result",
  ".data_arch_violations.json",
]

[tool.git]
# Default git remote for push/release commands
default-remote = "origin"

[tool.scripts.test]
# Configuration for CI/CD test runner
pytest-verbosity = "-vv"
coverage-report-file = "coverage.xml"
src-path = "src"

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "bitranox_template_py_cli"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain is pure (no adapter dependencies)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
  "bitranox_template_py_cli.domain",
]
forbidden_modules = [
  "bitranox_template_py_cli.adapters",
  "bitranox_template_py_cli.composition",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Clean Architecture layers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
  # Composition wires adapters - can import everything
  "bitranox_template_py_cli.composition",
  # Adapters implement ports - can import application and domain
  "bitranox_template_py_cli.adapters",
  # Application defines ports - can import domain
  "bitranox_template_py_cli.application",
  # Domain is pure - bottom layer
  "bitranox_template_py_cli.domain",
]

[tool.pip-audit]
# Known vulnerabilities to ignore (environment-level packages, not project dependencies)
# PYSEC-2022-42969: py library ReDoS - py 1.11.0 is installed in the development
#   environment but is not a dependency of this project; no fix available.
ignore-vulns = [

  "CVE-2025-8869",     # pip 24.3.1 - env-only, not a project dependency
  "CVE-2026-1703",     # pip 24.3.1 - env-only, not a project dependency

  "opifex[cuda12,dev]"

cuda12 = [
  # Named for the CUDA major version, as JAX names its own extras (cuda12, cuda12-local,
  # cuda13). "gpu" was wrong twice over: this repo also ships a `metal` extra, and Metal is
  # a GPU, and JAX already publishes cuda13, which "gpu" could not name without changing

  # `cuda12`, not `cuda12_local`. They are not spellings of one thing: cuda12 resolves
  # jax-cuda12-plugin[with-cuda], which delivers the CUDA wheels, while cuda12_local resolves

  "nvidia-nvtx-cu12>=12.8"

license = "MIT"
keywords = ["rename", "project", "cli"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",

]
dependencies = [

dev = [

    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",

    "pyright>=1.1.414",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # Pyflakes
    "I",      # isort
    "B",      # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "ARG",    # flake8-unused-arguments
    "SIM",    # flake8-simplify
    "TCH",    # flake8-type-checking
    "PTH",    # flake8-use-pathlib
    "ERA",    # eradicate
    "PL",     # Pylint
    "RUF",    # Ruff-specific rules
]
ignore = [
    "PLR0913",  # Too many arguments
    "PLR2004",  # Magic value comparison
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["rename_project"]

[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.10"
pythonPlatform = "All"
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
include = ["src", "tests"]
exclude = ["**/__pycache__"]
reportMissingTypeStubs = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "-q",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/rename_project"]
branch = true
parallel = true

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
]

  ".nox",

  "build",
  "dist",
  "htmlcov",
  ".coverage",
  "coverage.xml",
  "codecov.sh",
  ".cache",
  "result",
]
