    "ANN",     # flake8-annotations (mypy handles this)
    "COM812",  # missing-trailing-comma (conflicts with formatter)
    "ISC001",  # single-line-implicit-string-concatenation (conflicts with formatter)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = [
    "S101",    # assert allowed in tests
    "PLC0415", # import not at top level (common in tests for isolation)
    "PLR2004", # magic values allowed in tests
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "src"
exclude_type_checking_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Bounded contexts are independent (ADR-009, ADR-024)"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "src.modules.catalog_requests",
    "src.modules.collections",
    "src.modules.identity",
    "src.modules.library",
    "src.modules.media",
    "src.modules.metadata",
    "src.modules.notifications",
    "src.modules.preferences",
    "src.modules.settings",
    "src.modules.streaming",
    "src.modules.watch_progress",
]
ignore_imports = [
    "src.modules.*.infrastructure.acl.** -> src.modules.**",
    "src.modules.*.presentation.** -> src.modules.identity.presentation.public",
    "src.modules.*.presentation.** -> src.config.containers",
    # Known debt, frozen (ADR-037): catalog use cases still import the
    # MetadataProvider port owned by `metadata` (ADR-032 extraction). Listed
    # one by one so the set can only shrink.
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases._localized_metadata_helpers -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases._metadata_field_merge -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases.enrich_movie_metadata -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases.enrich_series_metadata -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases.get_movie_tmdb_suggestions -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases.get_related_movies -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases.get_related_series -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases.get_series_tmdb_suggestions -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
    "src.modules.media.application.use_cases.promote_movie_to_series -> src.modules.metadata.application.ports.metadata_provider_port",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layers inside each bounded context (ADR-008)"
type = "layers"
containers = [
    "src.modules.catalog_requests",
    "src.modules.collections",
    "src.modules.identity",
    "src.modules.library",
    "src.modules.media",
    "src.modules.metadata",
    "src.modules.notifications",
    "src.modules.preferences",
    "src.modules.settings",
    "src.modules.streaming",
    "src.modules.watch_progress",
]
layers = [
    "presentation",
    "infrastructure",
    "application",
    "domain",
]

[project]
name = "olink"
description = "A CLI tool that opens external URLs related to your project."
license = "MIT"
readme = "README.md"
authors = [{ name = "Hasan Sezer Taşan", email = "hasansezertasan@gmail.com" }]
maintainers = [
  { name = "Hasan Sezer Taşan", email = "hasansezertasan@gmail.com" },
]
dynamic = ["version"]
keywords = [
  "cli",
  "tui",
  "developer-tools",
  "git",
  "github",
  "gitlab",
  "bitbucket",
  "pypi",
  "npm",
  "open-url",
]
classifiers = [
  "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
  "Environment :: Console",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
  "Topic :: Software Development",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Version Control :: Git",
  "Topic :: Utilities",
  "Topic :: Terminals",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = ["typer==0.27.2", "defusedxml>=0.7.1"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
tui = ["textual>=3.0.0", "pyperclip==1.11.0", "rich>=13.3.3"]
all = ["textual>=3.0.0", "pyperclip==1.11.0", "rich>=13.3.3"]


[project.urls]
changelog = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/olink/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"
documentation = "https://hasansezertasan.github.io/olink"
homepage = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/olink"
issues = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/olink/issues"
releasenotes = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/olink/releases"
source = "https://github.com/hasansezertasan/olink.git"

[project.scripts]
olink = "olink.cli:main"


[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "olink[all]",
  "tox==4.64.4",
  "tox-uv==1.36.0",
  "debugpy==1.8.22",
  { include-group = "style" },
  { include-group = "test" },
]
style = [
  "basedpyright==1.40.1",
  "detect-secrets==1.5.0",
  "editorconfig-checker==3.11.1",
  "import-linter==2.15",
  "mypy==2.3.1",
  "pylint==4.0.9",
  "pyrefly==1.3.1",
  "ruff==0.16.10",
  "slotscheck==0.21.0",
  "sphinx-lint==1.0.2",
  "taplo==0.9.3",
  "ty==0.0.84",
  "typos==1.50.3",
  # actionlint, validate-pyproject, and vulture moved to prek upstream hooks
  # (see prek.toml); the tox `style` run no longer invokes them, so they are no
  # longer part of this group.
  # "zuban==0.9.0",  # removed from the style gate: panics on untyped pyperclip (see [tool.tox.env.style])
  # "google-yamlfmt",
  # "shellcheck-makefile>=1.27.3",
  # "shellcheck-py>=0.10.0.1",
  # "types-PyYAML",
  # "types-setuptools",
  # "types-ujson",
  # "yamlfix>=1.18.0",
  # "yamlfmt>=1.1.1",
  # "yamllint>=1.37.1",
]
# semgrep is deliberately its own group rather than part of `style`: `dev`
# includes `style` wholesale, so a plain `uv sync` — and every Windows/macOS
# cell in ci.yml, which runs `uv run --locked tox run` — would download and
# unpack ~215 MB (the wheel bundles a native semgrep-core) for a tool that only
# ever executes in the Linux-only `style` job. The tox `style` env lists this
# group explicitly. Still a single version source, same as every other pin.
sast = [
  "semgrep==1.178.0",
]
# Dependency hygiene gets its own group for the same reason `sast` does: it is
# only ever run by the on-demand `deps` tox env and the `deps` CI job, so a plain
# `uv sync` should not install it. deptry checks the imports against the declared
# dependencies (missing, transitive, misplaced or obsolete); creosote flags
# declared runtime dependencies that nothing imports.
deps = [
  "creosote==5.2.0",
  "deptry==0.25.1",
]
test = [
  "coverage-enable-subprocess==1.0",
  "coverage[toml]==7.16.2",
  "pytest-mock==3.16.0",
  "pytest-rerunfailures==16.7",
  "pytest-xdist[psutil]==3.8.0",
  "pytest==9.1.1",
  "pytest-sugar",
  "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
  "dirty-equals",
  "inline-snapshot",
  "pytest-deadfixtures==3.1.0",
  "lupa==2.8",
]
docs = [
  "sphinx==9.1.0",
  "shibuya==2026.7.12",
  "sphinx-autobuild==2025.8.25", # 2025.x drops Python 3.10 (requires-python >= 3.11)
  "sphinx-copybutton==0.5.2",
  "sphinx-design==0.7.0", # 0.7.0 drops Python 3.10 (requires-python >= 3.11)
  "sphinx-togglebutton==0.4.5",
  "sphinx-paramlinks==0.6.0",
  "auto-pytabs[sphinx]==0.5.0",
  "myst-parser==5.1.0",
  "sphinx-click==6.2.0",
  # Per-page "last updated" footer sourced from git commit dates (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/docs-versioning/#per-page-last-updated-comes-from-git-history);
  # offline, no network. Works from full history (docs CI checks out depth 0).
  "sphinx-last-updated-by-git==0.3.8",
  # PEP 440 version parsing/sorting used by tools/build_docs.py to order
  # published versions and pick the `latest` alias (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/docs-versioning/#docs-publish-only-the-current-version-and-carry-older-built-versions-forward-from-gh-pages). Also a Sphinx
  # transitive dependency; pinned here for the explicit direct use.
  "packaging>=24.0",
]
tool = [
  "commitizen==4.19.0",
  # "marimo==0.15.2",
  # "inflection==0.5.1",
  # "copier==9.11.0",
]
prek = ["prek==0.5.4"]


[build-system]

requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]

build-backend = "hatchling.build"


[tool.uv]
add-bounds = "exact"
cache-keys = [
  { file = "pyproject.toml" },
  { git = { commit = true, tags = true } },
]
package = true
trusted-publishing = "always"


[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# Last-resort sentinel: only used when a build sees neither a .git directory nor
# an expanded .git_archival.txt (e.g. an archive of a commit with no reachable
# tag). "0.0.0" reads clearly as "version could not be determined" rather than
# masquerading as a real early release. See .git_archival.txt + .gitattributes
# `export-subst` for the archive path that recovers the real tag-derived version.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"


[tool.hatch.build]
hooks.vcs.version-file = "src/olink/_version.py"


[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "only-version"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true


[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The package uses a src layout, so the source tree lives under /src (not
# /olink); including /src ships the actual modules -- and, for
# C-extension projects, the .pyx/.pxd sources needed to compile from the sdist.
include = [
  "/README.md",
  "LICENSE",
  "/src",
  "/tests",
  "/docs/examples",
]


[tool.commitizen]
# Commit-authoring and message linting only. release-please owns version
# bumping, git tagging, and CHANGELOG.md (see .github/release-please-config.json),
# so the bump/tag/changelog settings are intentionally omitted here to avoid two
# tools competing over the same tags and changelog file.
name = "cz_conventional_commits"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# addopts = "-rXs --strict-config --strict-markers"
addopts = "-v --tb=short --doctest-glob=README.md"
# One marker per component, auto-applied by tests/conftest.py from each test's
# top-level tests/<dir>/. Enables `pytest -m web` locally and per-component CI
# jobs (issue #160, https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#per-component-markers-path-filtered-jobs-and-one-coverage-gate-per-component); `integration` (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/testing-strategy/#real-broker-integration-tests-testcontainers-locally-per-broker-ci-mechanism) is one axis of the scheme.
markers = [
  "core: core/shared component tests",
  "cli: CLI component tests",
  "tui: TUI component tests",
]
# Strict mode requires explicit @pytest.mark.asyncio annotations, making async
# test collection intentional instead of silently accepting unmarked coroutines.
asyncio_mode = "strict"
filterwarnings = [
  "error",
]
# The project README is the deliberately small Markdown doctest surface. Other
# Markdown files can use illustrative snippets without becoming pytest inputs.
testpaths = ["tests", "README.md"]
doctest_optionflags = "ELLIPSIS IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE"
xfail_strict = true


[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
# Match `_version.py` wherever it resolves: `src/...` in editable dev installs and
# `.../site-packages/...` when tox/CI installs the built (non-editable) wheel. A
# `src/**`-only pattern silently misses the installed copy and reports it at 0%.
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
parallel = true
# Store data-file paths relative to the project root so `.coverage` files produced
# on different runners/OSes merge in the `coverage-combine` CI job without
# absolute-path mismatches. Complements the `[tool.coverage.paths]` remap below
# (which unifies the src/ vs site-packages layouts). See https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#a-single-union-coverage-gate-across-the-whole-matrix.
relative_files = true
source_pkgs = ["olink", "tests"]


[tool.coverage.paths]
# Unify coverage data across environments. tox installs the built wheel into
# each env's site-packages, so the same source file is measured under a different
# `.tox/<env>/.../site-packages/olink` path per interpreter. Without
# remapping those back to the canonical `src/` tree, `coverage combine` keeps a
# separate copy per env and a version-gated line covered in one interpreter but not
# another is wrongly counted as missed — silently failing the `fail_under` gate.
# `tests` needs no remapping: it is never installed, so every environment measures
# it at the same repo-local path.
olink = ["src/olink", "*/site-packages/olink"]


[tool.coverage.report]
# Untestable code is excluded per site with `# pragma: no cover`, not with blanket
# patterns here: a regex matching a `def` line excludes the *whole function body*,
# so a pattern like `def main\(` would silently un-measure any future `main()`
# with real logic (and did mask the tested GUI/TUI entrypoints). Pragmas carry the
# exclusion decision next to the code it affects. See https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/testing-strategy/#coverage-exclusions-are-per-site-pragmas-and-the-globs-must-match-the-installed-layout.
exclude_lines = [
  "no cov",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]
fail_under = 99
# Patterns match both the `src/` (editable) and installed (`site-packages`)
# layouts (see [tool.coverage.run] omit).
omit = ["*/_version.py"]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true


[tool.vulture]
# Framework-invoked handlers: Typer commands, FastAPI routes, FastStream
# lifecycle hooks, and the MCP tool dispatcher.
ignore_decorators = [
  "@app.command",
  "@app.get",
  "@app.after_startup",
  "@app.after_shutdown",
  "@server.call_tool",
  # A fixture used through ``@pytest.mark.usefixtures("name")`` -- or from
  # another test module -- is only ever named in a string, which vulture cannot
  # see. Unused fixtures are caught properly by ``pytest --dead-fixtures`` in
  # the tox ``style`` env, so this delegates rather than suppresses.
  "@pytest.fixture",
]
# Public API surfaces vulture cannot see being used: ``main`` entry points are
# referenced only via pyproject scripts, ``model_config`` is consumed by
# pydantic-settings, ``logger`` is imported only by optional components, the MCP
# ``arguments`` parameter is mandated by the call_tool signature, the Textual
# names (CSS/compose/on_mount/title/BINDINGS) are invoked by the TUI framework,
# and ``pytestmark``/``pytest_*`` (conftest hooks) are consumed by pytest at
# collection time.
ignore_names = [
  "CONFIG_FILE_PATH",
  "logger",
  "main",
  "model_config",
  "pytest_*",
  "collect_ignore_glob",
  "CSS",
  "DEFAULT_CSS",
  "compose",
  "on_*", # Textual message handlers dispatched by name (on_mount, on_input_submitted, ...)
  "action_*", # Textual key actions dispatched by name (action_toggle_pin, ...)
  "title",
  "BINDINGS",
]
# 60 surfaces Textual's dynamic style assignments (self.styles.background = ...)
# and framework hooks as false positives; 70 is the project's long-standing floor.
min_confidence = 70
paths = ["src", "tests"]


[tool.deptry]
# `known_first_party` is explicit because the tox `deps` env installs the built
# wheel, so without it deptry reads the project's own imports as a third-party
# transitive dependency (DEP003). Add further `per_rule_ignores` entries for the
# project's own findings, e.g. DEP003 for a package only importable through
# another declared one, or DEP002 for an optional import guarded by try/except.
# See https://deptry.com/rules-violations/.
# Excluded: the Sphinx config, the build hook (its imports belong to
# `[build-system].requires`, not the runtime dependencies), the benchmarks and the
# worker probe script (neither ships in the wheel; pytest and anyio come from
# the dev tooling).
extend_exclude = [
  "docs/conf.py",
]
known_first_party = ["olink"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# tools/build_docs.py imports `packaging`, pinned in the `docs` group for that
# script alone, so deptry reads it as a misplaced dev dependency.
DEP004 = ["packaging"]


[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false


[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "olink"


[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Layered architecture with independent components"
type = "layers"
# Layers are listed high -> low: a layer may import lower layers but never a
# higher one. Modules joined by ` | ` on one line are independent SIBLINGS that
# may not import each other. `cli` is the orchestrator layer — the
# `olink` console root, whose subcommands launch the other
# components (web/gui/tui/mcp/worker) via lazy imports — so it sits ABOVE the
# independent component group, which sits above `core`.
#
# `exhaustive` makes the contract fail when a subpackage of
# `olink` is not named in `layers` — so a new top-level
# subpackage is a deliberate architecture decision (add it to a layer here)
# rather than something that silently accretes at the package root. Feature code
# belongs inside an existing layer; see "Package structure" in `AGENTS.md`. The
# `exhaustive_ignores` entries are the non-layer foundations: the metadata and
# hatch-vcs version modules and the `python -m` dispatcher.
containers = ["olink"]
exhaustive = true
exhaustive_ignores = [
  "__main__",
  "__metadata__",
  "_version",
]
layers = [
  "cli",
  "tui",
  "core",
]


[tool.ruff]
fix = true
line-length = 100
output-format = "full"
preview = true
show-fixes = true
src = ["src", "tests", "docs/examples"]
target-version = "py314"
unsafe-fixes = true


[tool.ruff.analyze]
detect-string-imports = true
preview = true


[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true
line-ending = "lf"
preview = true
skip-magic-trailing-comma = true


[tool.ruff.lint]
fixable = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
  # Template defaults: the formatter owns trailing commas; no copyright/TODO gating.
  "COM812",
  "CPY",
  "FIX",
  "TD",
  # Two opinionated ruff 0.16 preview rules: RUF105 would rewrite the portable
  # `# noqa` comments into ruff's own `# ruff: ignore` syntax (its docs note
  # `# noqa` is needed for cross-tool compatibility), and RUF201 would rewrite
  # every rule *code* in this config's selectors into long rule *names*. Both are
  # stylistic.
  "RUF105",
  "RUF201",
  # Line length is enforced by the formatter (line-length = 100); the residual
  # E501 hits are unsplittable URLs/strings in code and are acceptable.
  "E501",
  # Docstring maximalism that conflicts with the project's convention (document
  # "why", not every method): per-method/dunder/__init__ docstrings and the
  # Returns/Yields/Raises sections. Module- and class-level docstrings still apply.
  "D102",
  "D105",
  "D107",
  "DOC201",
  "DOC402",
  "DOC501",
  # Exception messages are composed at the raise site with runtime context.
  "TRY003",
  # no-self-use: Typer callbacks and Textual handlers/test methods are bound by
  # the framework/pytest and legitimately do not touch self.
  "PLR6301",
  # Deliberate lazy imports (cli -> tui/textual, browser) keep the base install
  # light and match the import-linter "lazy imports" layering.
  "PLC0415",
  # Textual BINDINGS/CSS are framework-owned mutable class attributes.
  "RUF012",
]
logger-objects = ["logging_setup.logger"]
preview = true
select = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
# skip-magic-trailing-comma = true
split-on-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-copyright]
author = "Hasan Sezer Taşan <hasansezertasan@gmail.com>"


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"


[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Git-remote/URL parsing has irreducible branching; 5 would force artificial
# helper-splitting that hurts readability more than it helps.
max-complexity = 12


[tool.ruff.lint.pycodestyle]
ignore-overlong-task-comments = true


[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "pep257"


[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Recursive glob so nested test packages (tests/cli, tests/tui, ...) are covered.
# Tests legitimately assert, use magic values, reach into package internals, and
# their fixtures/helpers do not need annotations or return-value docs.
"tests/**/*.py" = [
  "S101", # asserts are the point of a test
  "PLR2004", # magic values read clearly inline in assertions
  "PLC2701", # white-box tests import private modules
  "SLF001", # white-box tests access private members
  "ANN", # test functions and fixtures are untyped by convention
  "ARG", # pytest injects fixtures a given test may not reference
  "RUF043", # pytest.raises match patterns are literal, not regexes, here
  "DOC201",
  "S404", # fixtures shell out to a real `git` to build test repos
  "S603",
  "S607", # `git` is invoked by name, resolved from PATH in the test env
  "S108", # fixtures reference throwaway temp paths
  "PLR0904", # grouping many cases in one Test* class is intentional
  "PTH118", # os.path is fine in test scaffolding
  "D104", # test packages need no package docstring
]
# Documentation examples are importable modules tested by
# ``tests/test_docs_examples.py``; they are not application packages.
"docs/examples/**/*.py" = ["INP001"]
# The Sphinx config is a standalone module, not part of an importable package.
"docs/conf.py" = ["INP001"]
# The docs warning-allowlist gate is a standalone script (not an importable
# package) whose whole job is to print GitHub `::error::` annotations to stdout.
"docs/check_warnings.py" = ["INP001", "T201"]
# The versioned-docs build orchestrator is a standalone CLI script under tools/,
# not part of an importable package (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/docs-versioning/#docs-publish-only-the-current-version-and-carry-older-built-versions-forward-from-gh-pages).
"tools/build_docs.py" = ["INP001"]
# Typer drives the CLI signature: bool options are declared as positional-style
# parameters with typer.Option defaults, and the top-level dispatch callback is
# necessarily branchy (it routes every target/subcommand).
"src/olink/cli/app.py" = [
  "FBT001",
  "FBT002",
  "FBT003",
  "C901",
  "PLR0912",
  "PLW0717",
]


[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
keep-runtime-typing = true


[tool.ruff.lint.ruff]
parenthesize-tuple-in-subscript = true


[tool.mypy]
files = ["src", "docs/examples"]
pretty = true
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true

# typer ships its own types; pyperclip and defusedxml do not publish stubs, so
# strict mypy would flag their imports as untyped without this override.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["pyperclip", "defusedxml.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true


[tool.basedpyright]
exclude = [".venv"]
include = ["src/olink", "docs/examples"]
pythonVersion = "3.14"
venv = ".venv"
# venvPath is the directory *containing* the venv, not the venv itself; ".venv"
# here would make basedpyright look for ".venv/.venv". Use "." so both the venv
# and basedpyright's strict ruleset resolve the project's installed deps.
venvPath = "."
# basedpyright layers opinions on top of standard strict typing that fight
# idiomatic dataclass/Typer/Textual code. Standard strict type-safety stays on;
# these purely-stylistic strict-only diagnostics are turned off:
reportUnannotatedClassAttribute = "none" # dataclass/Textual attrs (name=, BINDINGS=) are inferred
reportImplicitOverride = "none" # framework subclasses don't decorate every override
reportUnusedCallResult = "none" # Textual APIs return awaitables/Text routinely discarded
reportAny = "none" # narrow Any at boundaries (parsed JSON/XML) is deliberate
reportCallInDefaultInitializer = "none" # typer.Option()/Argument() defaults are the Typer idiom
reportImplicitStringConcatenation = "none"


[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src", "tests", "docs/examples"]
respect-ignore-files = false


[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.14"


[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true


[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.14"
project-includes = ["src", "docs/examples"]

[tool.pylint.main]
# pylint runs as an always-on gate that deliberately overlaps ruff's PL* rules.
# Its canonical invocation is `pylint src docs/examples`, so it never descends into tests; this
# ignore-paths is a defensive scope guard for broader invocations (`pylint .`,
# filename-passing hooks). Tests are linted by ruff, not pylint.
ignore-paths = ["^tests/.*$"]
# `.pyi` stubs (the c-extension type stub) are signature-only: their bodies are
# `...` and every parameter is unused by construction, so pylint's unused-argument
# check is a guaranteed false positive there. Stubs are type-checked by the
# type-checker gate, not pylint.
ignore-patterns = ['.*\.pyi$']

[tool.pylint."messages control"]
# Only formatter-owned checks, the docstring family, and too-few-public-methods
# are disabled so pylint is usable out of the box; everything else stays on.
disable = [
  "line-too-long", # C0301 — ruff-format owns line length
  "missing-module-docstring", # C0114
  "missing-class-docstring", # C0115
  "missing-function-docstring", # C0116
  "too-few-public-methods", # R0903 — trips dataclasses / config / Protocol classes
  # C0415 — the cli->tui/gui/web dispatch, and each component's own heavy or
  # platform-conditional import (tkinter, uvicorn, the worker's uvloop probe),
  # are deliberately lazy so import-linter's layering contract holds and a
  # framework is only imported when the code path that needs it actually runs.
  # Textual is the exception: the TUI imports it at module scope so `InfoApp`
  # can be defined there and driven by the headless pilot (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/testing-strategy/#interactive-components-expose-injected-driver-seams-so-headless-ci-measures-everything-but-the-blocking-call).
  "import-outside-toplevel",
  # W0706 — the generated TUI entry point explicitly re-raises
  # KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit ahead of a broad `except Exception` to make the
  # "let these propagate" intent obvious to readers, even though BaseException
  # subclasses wouldn't be caught by the Exception clause anyway.
  "try-except-raise",
  # R0801 — the component skeletons (gui/tui/mcp/worker) are deliberately
  # parallel: each fetches package metadata and formats the same info block the
  # same way. That structural symmetry is a feature of the scaffold, not
  # copy-paste debt, and R0801 cannot be suppressed inline at the call site.
  "duplicate-code",
]

[tool.pylint.design]
max-args = 10
max-positional-arguments = 10
max-branches = 20

[tool.typos.files]
# copier records `_commit` as a `git describe` string (`v1.2.3-4-g<hash>`) when
# the template is rendered from an untagged ref, and a fragment of the hex hash
# can read as a misspelled word, failing the check on a hash nobody chose. The
# file is machine-written with no prose to check. The prek hook passes
# `--force-exclude`, so the exclusion holds there as well as in `tox -e style`.
extend-exclude = [
  ".copier-answers.yml",
]

[tool.tox]
# The ``worker`` env is intentionally omitted: it starts a broker-bound process
# and would hang/fail under ``tox run`` in CI (where no broker is available).
# The worker is covered by its pytest TestBroker suite; run it on demand with
# ``tox -e worker`` when a broker is up (e.g. inside the devcontainer).
env_list = [
  "style",
  # Inline ``>>>`` snippets are part of the tested-documentation contract,
  # so run them in the default CI ``tox run`` invocation.
  "docs-doctest",
  "cli",
  "3.14",
]
requires = ["tox>=4"]


[tool.tox.env_run_base]
# The TUI ships as the optional `tui` extra; without it pylint/mypy/Sphinx
# autodoc and the TUI tests cannot import textual.
extras = ["all"]
commands = [
  [
    "coverage",
    "run",
    "--module",
    "pytest",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}",
    { replace = "posargs", default = [
    ], extend = true },
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["test"]
description = "Run the tests under {base_python}"
env_tmp_dir = "{toxworkdir}/tmp/{envname}"
# Arms coverage-enable-subprocess so xdist/subprocess workers are measured too;
# `coverage run` plus `parallel = true` writes per-env data files that the CI
# `coverage combine` step merges.
set_env = { COVERAGE_PROCESS_START = "{tox_root}/pyproject.toml" }
# Non-editable: `uv sync --no-editable` builds the project and installs it into
# site-packages, the layout `[tool.coverage.paths]` remaps and the per-component
# coverage gates measure (https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/ci-topology/#per-component-markers-path-filtered-jobs-and-one-coverage-gate-per-component).
package = "wheel"
# Every env installs from uv.lock (`uv sync --locked`), so tox tests and lints
# the exact versions the lockfile pins. The plain `uv-venv-runner` resolves the
# project's own dependencies fresh on every env creation (tox's
# `use_frozen_constraints` never reaches its `uv pip install`), so a newer
# release could float in and clash with a pinned tool such as semgrep.
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.style]
# The TUI ships as the optional `tui` extra; without it pylint/mypy/Sphinx
# autodoc and the TUI tests cannot import textual.
extras = ["all"]
base_python = ["3.14"]
commands = [
  [
    "ruff",
    "check",
    "--no-fix",
  ],
  [
    "ruff",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--python-version",
    "3.14",
  ],
  # Style runs once on Linux, so explicitly sweep platform-gated branches that
  # mypy would otherwise prune as unreachable on the host platform.
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "win32",
  ],
  [
    "mypy",
    "--platform",
    "darwin",
  ],
  [
    "basedpyright",
  ],
  [
    "ty",
    "check",
  ],
  [
    "pyrefly",
    "check",
  ],
  # NOTE: `["zuban", "check", "src"]` is temporarily removed — zuban 0.9.0 panics
  # (RefCell already mutably borrowed) following the import into the untyped
  # `pyperclip` dep and ignores mypy's ignore_missing_imports override. mypy
  # (strict), basedpyright (strict), ty, and pyrefly already cover typing.
  [
    "pylint",
    "src",
    "docs/examples",
  ],
  [
    "python",
    "-m",
    "slotscheck",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "lint-imports",
  ],
  # Rules-database SAST. Deliberately style-env-only (like ty/pyrefly/zuban) and
  # not a prek hook: semgrep keeps no on-disk rule cache, so a pre-commit hook
  # would make a registry request on every `git commit`. The ruleset is named
  # explicitly rather than `--config auto` so rule selection does not depend on
  # language auto-detection; it is still fetched from the registry, which is why
  # this cannot be vendored (see https://hasansezertasan.github.io/copier-pyproject/context/lint-orchestration/#semgrep-runs-in-the-style-env-against-a-named-registry-ruleset-never-vendored). `--error` makes findings blocking;
  # silence a false positive with a trailing `# nosemgrep: <rule-id>`.
  [
    "semgrep",
    "scan",
    "--config",
    "p/python",
    "--error",
    "--metrics=off",
    "src",
  ],
  [
    "taplo",
    "lint",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  # A strict `--check` gate, not fix mode: a generated file that taplo would
  # rewrite fails its own CI on first push and drifts on every `copier update`.
  # `.taplo.toml` disables array auto expand/collapse so the shipped layout is
  # the canonical one regardless of which components are enabled. The `*.toml`
  # glob is non-recursive, so it scopes taplo to this project's own root TOML
  # (pyproject/prek/mise/taplo) without walking vendored `.tox`/`.venv`/
  # site-packages trees — no `.taplo.toml` exclude config needed.
  [
    "taplo",
    "format",
    "--check",
    "--diff",
    "*.toml",
  ],
  [
    "typos",
    "--diff",
  ],
  [
    "ec",
  ],
  [
    "sphinx-lint",
    "docs",
  ],
  # Collects (does not run) the suite and flags fixtures that are never used --
  # cheap, deterministic, and a natural fit next to the other whole-program
  # analyzers above (lint-imports, slotscheck).
  [
    "pytest",
    "--dead-fixtures",
  ],
]
# `test` is included so the type checkers that scope tests (e.g. ty) can
# resolve pytest and other test-only imports.
dependency_groups = ["sast", "style", "test"]
description = "Run Checkers, Linters and Formatters"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


# On-demand and CI-only (not in env_list, like `integration`): the `deps` job in
# ci.yml runs it and `check` aggregates that job. `test` is included so deptry
# and creosote can resolve the project's own test-only imports. creosote needs
# the installed distributions to map import names, which the lock runner provides.
[tool.tox.env.deps]
commands = [
  [
    "deptry",
    ".",
  ],
  [
    "creosote",
    "--deps-file",
    "pyproject.toml",
    "--section",
    "project.dependencies",
    # Without this creosote skips imports inside functions, so a dependency used
    # only through a lazy import (the worker's uvloop) is reported as unused.
    "--include-deferred",
  ],
]
dependency_groups = ["deps", "test"]
description = "Check dependency hygiene (deptry, creosote)"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.prek]
commands = [["prek", "run", "--all-files"]]
dependency_groups = ["prek"]
description = "Run prek hooks"
# The hooks that need the project call `uv run --locked`, which syncs it (and the
# groups they name) into this env through the runner's UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT;
# installing the wheel here too would only be swapped for that install each run.
package = "skip"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"


[tool.tox.env.docs-build]
# The TUI ships as the optional `tui` extra; without it pylint/mypy/Sphinx
# autodoc and the TUI tests cannot import textual.
extras = ["all"]
# Write the warning stream to a file (`-w`) instead of `-W` turning the first
# warning into a hard error, then let docs/check_warnings.py own the pass/fail:
# it diffs the emitted warnings against the docs/expected_warnings.txt allowlist,
# failing on both unexpected new warnings and expected ones that vanished.
commands = [
  ["sphinx-build", "-w", "docs/_build/warnings.txt", "-b", "html", "docs", "docs/_build/html"],
  ["python", "docs/check_warnings.py"],
]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Build Docs"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
# Keep build log output unbuffered/ordered. Reproducible builds pin Sphinx's
# "today"/copyright to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, which the CI docs steps
# (docs-preview.yml, release.yml) export from the last commit date before
# invoking sphinx-build directly. Local `tox` runs deliberately do NOT export
# it: an empty value ("{env:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:}") is *present but blank*, which
# breaks hatchling's get_reproducible_timestamp (`int("")`), so we leave it
# unset locally and conf.py falls back to the current year.
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-server]
# The TUI ships as the optional `tui` extra; without it pylint/mypy/Sphinx
# autodoc and the TUI tests cannot import textual.
extras = ["all"]
# ``--ignore`` the machine-generated ``docs/_generated/`` tree: ``conf.py``
# rewrites it on every Sphinx build, so watching it would make each rebuild
# trigger the next in an endless live-reload loop.
commands = [["sphinx-autobuild", "--ignore", "*/_generated/*", "docs", "docs/_build/html"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Start the live-reloading docs server"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-doctest]
# The TUI ships as the optional `tui` extra; without it pylint/mypy/Sphinx
# autodoc and the TUI tests cannot import textual.
extras = ["all"]
# ``literalinclude`` keeps complete examples in tested Python modules; this
# separate builder executes the occasional ``>>>`` snippet that belongs inline
# with prose.
commands = [["sphinx-build", "-b", "doctest", "docs", "docs/_build/doctest"]]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Run documentation doctests"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }


[tool.tox.env.docs-linkcheck]
# On-demand link checker. Also run weekly (non-blocking) by docs-linkcheck.yml.
# Hits the network, so it is deliberately not part of the `style` env or PR CI.
commands = [
  [
    "sphinx-build",
    "-b",
    "linkcheck",
    "docs",
    "docs/_build/linkcheck",
  ],
]
extras = ["all"]
dependency_groups = ["docs"]
description = "Check documentation for broken links"
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"
set_env = { PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1" }

[tool.tox.env.cli]
commands = [
  [
    "olink",
    # olink exposes version via the --version flag (not a `version` subcommand);
    # bare args are treated as targets. Smoke-test with --version by default.
    { replace = "posargs", default = ["--version"], extend = true },
  ],
]
description = "Run the CLI application."
runner = "uv-venv-lock-runner"

[project]
name = "gts"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Guitar Tone Shootout - Tone comparison platform"

readme = "README.md"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
# Root package is a workspace meta-package — no Python source to ship.
# Point to README.md to satisfy hatchling's file discovery requirement.
only-include = ["README.md"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "ruff==0.15.1",
    "mypy>=1.14.0",
    "pytest>=8.3.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.24.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.0.0",

[tool.uv]
# CPU-only PyTorch — no GPU on this server, saves ~3GB of NVIDIA CUDA packages

[[tool.uv.index]]

[tool.uv.sources]

torchaudio = { index = "pytorch-cpu" }

[tool.uv.workspace]

    "apps/audio_worker",
    "apps/shootout_orchestrator",
]

# =============================================================================
# Import Linter - Dependency Enforcement
# =============================================================================

[tool.importlinter]

    "gts",
    "messaging",
    "audio",
    "video",
    "source_t3k",
    "webapp",
    "t3k_sync",
    "audio_worker",
    "shootout_orchestrator",
]
include_external_packages = true

# gts domain has zero dependencies on other project packages
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "gts-isolation"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["gts"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "messaging",
    "audio",
    "video",
    "source_t3k",
    "webapp",
    "t3k_sync",
    "audio_worker",
    "shootout_orchestrator",
]

# messaging has zero dependencies on other project packages
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "messaging-isolation"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["messaging"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "gts",
    "audio",
    "video",
    "source_t3k",
    "webapp",
    "t3k_sync",
    "audio_worker",
    "shootout_orchestrator",
]

# gts domain models must remain framework-agnostic.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

    "starlette",
    "pydantic",
    "redis",
    "taskiq",
    "httpx",
    "pedalboard",
    "torch",

# gts ports must remain framework-agnostic.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["gts.ports"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "sqlalchemy",
    "fastapi",
    "starlette",
    "pydantic",
    "redis",
    "taskiq",
    "httpx",
    "pedalboard",
    "torch",
]

# gts records should remain transport contracts, not framework adapters.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "gts-records-no-adapter-frameworks"

forbidden_modules = [
    "sqlalchemy",
    "fastapi",
    "starlette",
    "redis",
    "taskiq",
    "httpx",
    "pedalboard",
    "torch",
]

# gts services may use SQLAlchemy/pydantic for domain logic, but not web frameworks.

    "redis",
    "taskiq",

    "pedalboard",

    "webapp",
    "t3k_sync",

# Source adapters can only depend on gts domain

    "webapp",
    "t3k_sync",
    "audio_worker",

# =============================================================================
# Ruff Configuration
# =============================================================================

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # Pyflakes
    "I",      # isort
    "B",      # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "ARG",    # flake8-unused-arguments
    "SIM",    # flake8-simplify
    "TCH",    # flake8-type-checking
    "RUF",    # Ruff-specific rules
]
ignore = [
    "E501",   # line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",   # do not perform function calls in argument defaults (FastAPI Depends)
    "B904",   # raise from err (too noisy)
    "ARG001", # unused function argument (common in protocols/interfaces)
    "UP042",  # replace-str-enum (codebase uses str, Enum pattern)
    "RUF003", # ambiguous-unicode-character-comment (intentional unicode in comments)
    "RUF002", # ambiguous-unicode-character-docstring (intentional unicode in docstrings)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = [
    "gts",
    "messaging",
    "audio",
    "video",
    "source_t3k",
    "webapp",
    "t3k_sync",
    "audio_worker",
    "shootout_orchestrator",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["ARG001", "ARG002", "E402", "B017", "B011", "RUF043", "TCH001"]
# SQLAlchemy models need runtime imports for Mapped[] annotations — cannot move to TYPE_CHECKING
"apps/webapp/src/webapp/adapters/persistence/models/*.py" = ["TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003"]
"apps/webapp/src/webapp/adapters/persistence/unit_of_work.py" = ["TCH002"]
"apps/webapp/src/webapp/services/*.py" = ["TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003"]
"apps/webapp/src/webapp/api/**/*.py" = ["TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003"]
"apps/webapp/src/webapp/auth/*.py" = ["TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003"]
"apps/webapp/src/webapp/dependencies.py" = ["TCH001", "TCH002", "TCH003"]
"tests/unit/webapp/test_job_model.py" = ["TCH003"]
"infrastructure/migrations/**/*.py" = ["E501", "F401", "E402", "F811", "F821"]

# =============================================================================
# MyPy Configuration
# =============================================================================

[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.14"

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
check_untyped_defs = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = true
no_implicit_optional = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
exclude = [
    "infrastructure/migrations/",
]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "pedalboard.*",
    "nam.*",
    "pyloudnorm.*",
    "torch.*",
    "pgmq.*",
    "soundfile.*",
    "scipy.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# =============================================================================
# Pytest Configuration
# =============================================================================

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "-q",
    "--strict-markers",
]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests",
    "smoke: marks tests as smoke tests",
    "host_only: marks tests that must run on host, not in Docker",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["model", "infra", "sources", "apps"]
branch = true
omit = ["*/tests/*", "*/__pycache__/*"]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "@abc.abstractmethod",
]

# Ruff configurations

# =============================================================================
# Import Linter
# =============================================================================
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["src", "workers"]
include_external_packages = true

# Глобальные слои: workers -> src
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Global layers"
type = "layers"
layers = ["workers", "src"]

# Ядро MCP — второй composition root над тем же src: фабрики свои, бот и ядро друг друга не знают
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "bot and mcp core are independent composition roots"
type = "independence"
modules = ["workers.bot", "workers.mcp"]

# Контексты src не импортируют друг друга: связывает их только composition root
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "src contexts independence"
type = "independence"
modules = ["src.chat", "src.ai_tools", "src.voice_recognition", "src.gmail", "src.agent_notifications", "src.colleague_mail", "src.scheduled_runs"]

# Рабочая папка, папка «Personal Assistant» и уборка не знают реализаций соседних
# контекстов: Dropbox им отдаёт composition root через Protocol
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "files work folder, overflow and sweeper stand alone"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.files.work_folder", "src.files.overflow", "src.files.sweeper"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.dropbox", "src.gmail", "src.chat", "src.ai_tools"]

# Контракт источника переписки не знает ни реализаций, ни потребителей
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "conversations contract stands alone"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.conversations"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.todoist", "src.voice_recognition", "src.telegram_user", "src.whatsapp", "src.wiki"]

# Коннекторы WhatsApp из соседей знают только контракт src.conversations
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "whatsapp depends only on conversations contract"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.whatsapp"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.todoist", "src.voice_recognition", "src.wiki"]

# Коннектор Telegram (аккаунт владельца) из соседей знает только контракт src.conversations
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "telegram_user depends only on conversations contract"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.telegram_user"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.cases", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.colleague_mail", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.task_mirror", "src.todoist", "src.voice_recognition", "src.whatsapp", "src.wiki"]

# Telethon держит ключ от всего аккаунта владельца: клиент живёт только внутри src.telegram_user,
# наружу — объект с методами чтения протоколов src.conversations. Запрещён прямой импорт telethon;
# цепочка composition root -> src.telegram_user -> telethon и есть задуманный путь
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "telethon only inside telegram_user"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = true
source_modules = ["workers", "src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.cases", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.colleague_mail", "src.conversations", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.task_mirror", "src.todoist", "src.voice_recognition", "src.whatsapp", "src.wiki"]
forbidden_modules = ["telethon"]

# Клиент сервиса кейсов не знает ни соседей, ни потребителей: инструменты берут у него модели и ошибки
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "cases client stands alone"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.cases"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.conversations", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.task_mirror", "src.todoist", "src.voice_recognition", "src.whatsapp", "src.wiki"]

# Клиент сервиса расписаний не знает ни соседей, ни потребителей: инструменты берут у него модели и ошибки
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "scheduler client stands alone"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.scheduler"]
forbidden_modules = ["ai_framework", "bot_framework", "src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.cases", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.colleague_mail", "src.conversations", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.scheduled_runs", "src.task_manager", "src.task_mirror", "src.telegram_user", "src.todoist", "src.voice_recognition", "src.whatsapp", "src.wiki"]

# Порт задачника: только модели, ошибки и Protocol-ы — не знает ни реализаций, ни потребителей
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "task manager contract stands alone"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.task_manager"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.cases", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.colleague_mail", "src.conversations", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.task_mirror", "src.telegram_user", "src.todoist", "src.voice_recognition", "src.whatsapp", "src.wiki"]

# Todoist — реализация порта задачника: из соседей знает только src.task_manager
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "todoist depends only on task manager contract"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.todoist"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.cases", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.colleague_mail", "src.conversations", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.task_mirror", "src.telegram_user", "src.voice_recognition", "src.whatsapp", "src.wiki"]

# Отражение задач знает только клиента сервиса кейсов и порт задачника; реализацию (Todoist) подставляет бот
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "task mirror bridges only cases and task_manager"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.task_mirror"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.access", "src.agent_notifications", "src.ai_tools", "src.app_migrations", "src.chat", "src.checkup", "src.colleague_mail", "src.conversations", "src.dropbox", "src.files", "src.flows", "src.gmail", "src.memory", "src.telegram_user", "src.todoist", "src.voice_recognition", "src.whatsapp", "src.wiki"]

# Инструменты модели знают порт задачника, а не его реализацию (Todoist) и не отражение:
# задачник и подвязку к кейсу им подставляет composition root через Protocol-ы
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ai tools know task manager port, not todoist or task mirror"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.ai_tools"]
forbidden_modules = ["src.todoist", "src.task_mirror"]

# Почта ассистентов — слой без модели и без Telegram: входящее от коллег только ложится в журнал,
# до модели и владельцу его доносят инструменты и сводка, собранные в composition root
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "colleague mail knows neither the model nor Telegram"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.colleague_mail"]
forbidden_modules = ["ai_framework", "bot_framework"]

# Исполнитель расписаний — без модели и без Telegram: прогон, кейс и владельца ему подставляет

type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src.scheduled_runs"]

[project]
name = "wb-alert-bot"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Telegram bot for Ozon and Wildberries price monitoring and alerts"
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    "aiogram==3.26.0",
    "alembic>=1.18.4",
    "asyncpg>=0.31.0",
    "fastapi==0.135.1",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "loguru>=0.7.3",
    "playwright==1.64.0",
    "pydantic>=2.12.5",
    "pydantic-settings==2.13.1",
    "redis>=7.3.0",
    "sqlalchemy==2.0.48",
    "uvicorn==0.42.0",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "factory-boy>=3.3.3",
    "import-linter>=2.15",
    "mypy>=1.19.1",
    "pre-commit>=4.5.1",
    "pytest>=9.0.2",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "ruff>=0.15.7",
    "testcontainers>=4.15.0",
]


[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py314"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",
    "W",
    "F",
    "I",
    "B",
    "C4",
    "UP",
    "SIM",
    "ASYNC",
    "T20",
    "DTZ"
]

ignore = ["UP037"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
force-single-line = true


[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]

# Third-party packages without stubs/py.typed, named individually (measured
# by running `mypy app tests` without a global `ignore_missing_imports`, not
# guessed) — a global override would also silence a missing module of our own
# package, e.g. a commit deleting an imported `app/**` module (PAB-065,
# попытка 3, AC 4).
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["asyncpg", "asyncpg.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pydantic-mypy]
init_forbid_extra = true
init_typed = true
warn_untyped_fields = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "strict"
testpaths = ["tests"]
strict_markers = true
strict_config = true
filterwarnings = ["error::pytest.PytestConfigWarning"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["app"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
exclude_also = [
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]

# Layer boundaries, see PROJECT.md §4 "Механическая проверка границ".
# Contract composition is an architect decision; new client/service modules
# are added by the ticket that creates them.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "app"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "L1: layer order"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "app.main",
    "app.scheduler",
    "app.handlers : app.bot",
    "app.services",
    "app.repositories",
    "app.models",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "L2: bot and handlers do not reach repositories directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "app.bot",
    "app.handlers",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "app.repositories",
]
# The legitimate app.handlers -> app.services -> app.repositories path is an
# indirect import and must not break this contract; only a *direct* import of
# app.repositories from app.bot/app.handlers is forbidden (PAB-065, попытка 2).
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "L3: marketplace clients do not know about persistence or application services"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "app.services.base_client",
    "app.services.wb_client",
    "app.services.ozon_client",
    "app.services.client_factory",
    "app.services.wb_access",
    "app.services.wb_browser",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "app.repositories",
    "app.models",
    "app.core.database",
    "sqlalchemy",
    "app.services.price_service",
    "app.services.notification",
    "app.services.tracking",
]
ignore_imports = [
    "app.services.client_factory -> app.models.enums",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "L4: schemas and domain stay free of infrastructure"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "app.schemas",
    "app.domain",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "app.main",
    "app.scheduler",
    "app.bot",
    "app.handlers",
    "app.services",
    "app.repositories",
    "app.core",
    "sqlalchemy",
    "httpx",
    "aiogram",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "L5: core is a foundation, not a consumer of upper layers"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "app.core",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "app.main",
    "app.scheduler",
    "app.bot",
    "app.handlers",
    "app.services",
    "app.repositories",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "L6: playwright is imported only by the WB browser module"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = [
    "playwright",
]
allowed_importers = [
    "app.services.wb_browser",
]

The mapping is part of what is checked: a handler that survives a refactoring * but stops being an endpoint retires its guard just as quietly as a rename does. */ @ArchTest static void every_listed_entrypoint_names_an_existing_endpoint(JavaClasses classes) { List unresolved = TX_SCOPED_ENTRYPOINTS.stream().filter(entry -> !resolves(classes, entry)).sorted().toList(); assertTrue( unresolved.isEmpty(), "Entries of TX_SCOPED_ENTRYPOINTS naming no existing request-mapped method, rename or" + " remove them: " + unresolved); } private static boolean resolves(JavaClasses classes, String entry) { int separator = entry.indexOf('#'); String owner = entry.substring(0, separator); String method = entry.substring(separator + 1); return classes.contain(owner) && classes.get(owner).getMethods().stream() .anyMatch(m -> m.getName().equals(method) && isRequestMapped(m)); } /** Whether the method carries one of Spring's {@code @*Mapping} annotations. */ private static boolean isRequestMapped(JavaMethod method) { return method.getAnnotations().stream() .map(annotation -> annotation.getRawType().getName()) .anyMatch( name -> name.startsWith("org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.") && name.endsWith("Mapping")); } }

# DES-031 v2 I1 — the client/engine package boundary, enforced structurally.
#
# A *client process* (any process whose entry point is not `quarryd`) and the
# two client-tier libraries it rests on (`quarry.client`, `quarry.api`) must
# never pull the engine — `quarry.db`, `quarry.embeddings`, `quarry.ingestion`,
# `quarry.retrieval`, `quarry.sync`, `quarry.daemon` — into their import graph.
# A violating import fails CI (`make check-imports`), not review.
#
# The engine's own entry point (`quarry.daemon.launcher`, the `quarryd` console
# script) lives INSIDE `quarry.daemon`, so it is engine-side and never a source
# here. The runtime engine-sabotage test (tests/test_init.py) is the companion
# guard that no engine leaks to a client module's MODULE scope — import-linter
# checks the static graph, the sabotage test checks the eager import behaviour.

[importlinter]
root_package = quarry

[importlinter:contract:client-never-imports-engine]
name = Client processes and libraries must never import the engine
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    quarry.__main__
    quarry.hooks
    quarry.mcp_server
    quarry.client
    quarry.api
forbidden_modules =
    quarry.db
    quarry.embeddings
    quarry.ingestion
    quarry.retrieval
    quarry.sync
    quarry.daemon
# The one sanctioned exception: the host-admin diagnostic commands (`quarry
# doctor` / `quarry install` / `quarry uninstall`) inspect the LOCAL engine
# environment — model cache, GPU runtime, on-disk LanceDB — so they can report
# WHY a daemon is unhealthy even when it is down. `quarry.__main__` reaches
# these only through function-body (lazy) imports, so the heavy engine is
# deferred to those rare, explicit invocations and never loaded on the hot
# CLI/hook path (the sabotage test proves module-scope engine-freeness). The
# `quarry.doctor` edges are lazy `__main__`-side touches; the
# `quarry.doctor_inference` edge is eager, but reachable only through the lazy
# `__main__` -> `quarry.doctor` boundary, so the engine still loads only when a
# diagnostic command runs. A NEW engine import from any other client-reachable
# module still fails the contract.
ignore_imports =
    quarry.doctor -> quarry.db.facade
    quarry.doctor -> quarry.db.schema
    quarry.doctor -> quarry.embeddings
    quarry.doctor_inference -> quarry.ingestion.provider
    quarry.doctor_captures -> quarry.db.facade
    quarry.doctor_memory -> quarry.db.facade
    quarry.doctor_memory -> quarry.db.schema

[importlinter:contract:api-sits-below-client]
name = The wire contract (quarry.api) sits below the transport client
type = layers
layers =
    quarry.client
    quarry.api

    "starlette>=1.3.1",

    "ultimate-sitemap-parser>=1.8.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.0",
    "cryptography>=46.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",

    # subclasses watchdog's PRIVATE internals (Inotify._add_dir_watch/
    # _add_watch, InotifyBuffer.__init__, InotifyEmitter.on_thread_start --
    # see quarry/daemon/inotify_prune.py, inotify_prune_chain.py), and that
    # subclassed surface was verified only against the installed 6.0.0 (the
    # CI pin test, test_pins_the_watchdog_internals_this_module_subclasses,
    # never ran against an older release). The floor was previously >=4.0,
    # which was ALSO wrong independent of a naming issue Copilot separately
    # caught: fs_watchdog.py imports UnsupportedLibcError unconditionally,

# FastAPI resolves handler annotations at runtime (get_type_hints), so the

disallow_untyped_decorators = true

warn_unused_ignores = true

module = "quarry.code_processor"

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]

    "lancedb.*",
    "openpyxl",
    "openpyxl.*",
    "pptx",
    "pptx.*",
    "pyarrow",
    "pyarrow.*",
    "rapidocr",
    "rapidocr.*",

# The old `fitz` alias was unresolvable, so ignore_missing_imports was enough;
# pymupdf ships a real package, which mypy follows into unannotated source and
# then reports every call into it as untyped. Skipping the follow restores the
# treatment the stub-less libraries above already get — Any at the boundary,
# with our own annotations checked on our side of it.

pythonVersion = "3.13"

# and pyarrow ship no type stubs. Every value returned from these libraries
# is Unknown, cascading 591 errors across the codebase. The alternative is

reportUnknownMemberType = false
reportUnknownParameterType = false
reportUnknownVariableType = false
reportUnknownArgumentType = false
reportUnknownLambdaType = false

reportPrivateUsage = false
reportUnusedFunction = false
reportMissingParameterType = false

addopts = "-ra -q -m 'not slow and not embedding and not hook_integration'"
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
timeout = 30
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (run with -m slow)",
    "resource: long-lived-process resource-invariant tests (fd/memory leak guards)",
    "integration: real-socket/live-server tests, also slow so excluded from the fast CI suite and run via -m integration",

[tool.semantic_release]
tag_format = "v{version}"
version_toml = ["pyproject.toml:project.version"]
commit_parser = "conventional"
# 0.x stays 0.x: a breaking change bumps the minor, never to 1.0.0 on its own.
# Both are spelled out rather than left to the defaults, which have moved
# between python-semantic-release majors.
allow_zero_version = true
major_on_zero = false
# The default release commit message is not a conventional commit, so it would
# fail any later check over the range.
commit_message = "chore(release): {version}"
# A release only moves the version and the tag; it builds no artifact, because
# nothing publishes one. This hook exists solely to keep uv.lock honest:
# uv.lock carries its own cveta2 version entry, which version_toml does not
# touch, so without the re-lock the tagged commit ships a lockfile that
# disagrees with pyproject.toml and the next `uv run` silently re-locks.
# `git add` is what puts the lockfile inside the release commit instead of
# leaving it dirty after.
build_command = """
uv lock --upgrade-package "$PACKAGE_NAME"
git add uv.lock
"""

[tool.semantic_release.changelog]
# The release commit itself, and the two types that describe no change a reader
# of the changelog can act on.
exclude_commit_patterns = [
    '''chore(?:\([^)]*?\))?: .+''',
    '''style(?:\([^)]*?\))?: .+''',
]

[tool.ruff]
# Conservative syntax/lint baseline; runtime support is declared by requires-python.
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 88
# vendor/ and local/ need no entry here: both are gitignored, and ruff
# respects .gitignore. mutants/ is gitignored too but must stay listed --
# ruff would otherwise see mutmut's copy of the tree when it is passed
# explicitly. mypy needs all three, since it ignores .gitignore.
exclude = ["mutants/**"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "COM812",  # missing-trailing-comma - conflicts with ruff formatter
    "EM",      # flake8-errmsg - overly pedantic for small projects
    "TRY003",  # raise-vanilla-args - same as EM
    "D213",
    "D203",
    "RUF001",  # ambiguous-unicode-character - project uses Russian (Cyrillic) strings
    "CPY001",  # missing-copyright-notice - this project ships no per-file headers
]
fixable = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# Development scripts use stdlib tomllib on the supported Python >=3.12;
# the conservative py310 lint baseline needs this classification explicitly.
extra-standard-library = ["tomllib"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S101", "S105", "S106", "ANN401", "PLR2004", "PLC0415", "D101", "D102", "D103", "S311", "SLF001"]
# Standalone operator scripts: `print` is their output and their helpers are
# not an API surface. What only one script trips is suppressed at that site,
# where RUF100 retires the suppression once the site is fixed.
"scripts/*.py" = ["T201", "D103", "ANN401", "PLR2004"]

[tool.ruff.format]
docstring-code-format = true

[tool.mypy]
# Analyze against the minimum supported package interpreter.
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
# mutants/ holds mutmut's copy of the tree; without it mypy sees two `cveta2`
# packages and fails with a duplicate-module error. vendor/ is only a leftover
# CVAT checkout in older clones - mypy, unlike ruff, ignores .gitignore.
exclude = ["vendor/", "local/", "mutants/"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["cvat_sdk.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]

# `-n 0` is mandatory: mutmut runs pytest.main() inside each forked child and
# the global addopts `-n auto` would spawn a full xdist pool per mutant. These
# args are appended last, so this `-n` wins.
pytest_add_cli_args = ["-n", "0", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", "--no-cov"]
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = ["tests/"]
# Presentation is not behaviour. Log lines, progress bars and the text of a
# `sys.exit` are things a person reads, and the only test that can kill a
# mutation of them is one that pins their wording - a change-detector that
# makes every copy edit a test edit.
#
# These patterns are the ONE place that exclusion is declared. Do not instead
# restructure source to hide a literal from the mutation gate: hoisting a
# progress-bar caption into a module-level constant works (mutmut only mutates
# code inside a top-level function), but it buys a green gate by making the
# code worse, and every later feature pays the cost of the indirection.
# Presentation surface belongs here; if a new one appears, add it here.
#
# Matching is `re.search` per line, and a matched line skips every *expression*
# starting on it together with its children - so `for x in tqdm(items, ...)`
# suppresses the bar and its keywords without touching the loop body. The
# logger pattern stays line-anchored because a bare `logger.` can appear
# mid-expression; `tqdm(`/`sys.exit(` cannot.
#
# Individual equivalent mutants still go in [tool.cveta2.mutation.equivalent] -
# both suppression mechanisms key on the first line of the mutated node, so
# neither can single out one argument of a multi-line call.
do_not_mutate_patterns = [
    "^\\s*logger\\.[a-z_]+\\(",
    "\\btqdm\\(",
    "\\bsys\\.exit\\(",
    # Progress-bar captions. `\btqdm(` covers the single-line bars, but the
    # shared fan-out takes its caption as one argument of a multi-line
    # `run_concurrent` / `run_s3_transfers` call, which starts on a line of
    # its own. Patterns are re.search per line and skip every expression
    # starting on the matched line, so naming the argument reaches exactly
    # the caption and nothing else. Every `desc=`/`unit=` in the package is
    # a bar caption; grep before adding a third meaning.
    "^\\s*desc=",
    "^\\s*unit=",
    # Same family: the progress bar's own advance call.
    "^\\s*bar\\.update\\(",
]
# mutmut caches a mutant's verdict against the *source* function's text, so a
# changed test does not invalidate it: weakening an assertion otherwise leaves
# the gate green on stale results. Hashing the test tree and rerunning on any
# change is what makes the cached run trustworthy.
cache_invalidation_files = ["tests/**/*.py", "conftest.py"]
on_dependency_change = "rerun"
# mutate_only_covered_lines is deliberately left off: its coverage pre-pass
# leaves a half-imported numpy in sys.modules, so the following stats run dies
# with "Unable to import required dependency numpy". Not needed here anyway -
# the scoped modules report zero no-tests mutants without it.

# Which mutants each hook runs. `fast` is the pre-commit subset; `full` is
# empty on purpose, meaning "no positional filter" - mutmut honours a cached
# verdict only when no mutant name is passed, so spelling it '*' would
# re-execute the whole scope every time instead of reusing the cache.
#
# Membership is chosen so `fast` stays meaningfully quicker than `full` -
# putting every gated module in `fast` once measured the same as `full`, i.e.
# the split bought nothing. mutation_test.sh prints the count and elapsed time
# of each run; when a newly gated module erases the gap again, leave it to
# `full`.
[tool.cveta2.mutation.profiles]
fast = [
    "cveta2.domain.partition.*",
    "cveta2.adapters.cvat.connection.*",
    "cveta2.composition.runtime.*",
    "cveta2.application.use_cases.whats_new.*",
    "cveta2.domain.baseline.*",
    "cveta2.adapters.files.dataset.x_read_baseline_siblings__mutmut_*",
    "cveta2.application.use_cases.resolve.*",
    "cveta2.composition.workflows.x_project_cloud_storage__mutmut_*",
    "cveta2.composition.workflows.x_apply_sync_root_override__mutmut_*",
    "cveta2.application.client.assembly.*",
    "cveta2.domain.models.*",
    "cveta2.adapters.config.projects_cache.*",
]

# mutants land on the keyword arguments of one BBoxAnnotation constructor
# and die on pydantic validation rather than on any assertion, so they cost a
# full suite run each and say nothing about test quality.
full = []

# Mutants that no test can kill because the mutation genuinely cannot change
# behaviour. scripts/mutation_gate.py subtracts these from the survivor set and
# fails if an entry stops matching a live survivor, so a stale justification

[tool.vulture]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["cveta2", "main.py", "tests", "scripts"]
exclude = ["cveta2/adapters/s3/types.py"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["cveta2"]
branch = true
omit = [
    "cveta2/__main__.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 90
show_missing = true
skip_empty = true
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "\\.\\.\\.",
]

[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["cveta2"]
include_external_packages = true
exclude_type_checking_imports = false

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Every runtime module belongs to an inward layer"
type = "layers"
containers = ["cveta2"]
exhaustive = true
layers = [
    "__main__ | api | cli | client | config | dataset_partition | exceptions | fs_utils | image_downloader | image_uploader | models | projects_cache | s3_types | s3_utils | task_cache | upload_manifest",
    "interfaces",
    "composition",
    "adapters",
    "application",
    "domain | presets",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Application orchestration depends on neutral contracts"
type = "layers"
containers = ["cveta2.application"]
exhaustive = true
layers = ["use_cases", "client", "ports", "settings | results"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Outgoing adapters remain independent"
type = "layers"
containers = ["cveta2.adapters"]
exhaustive = true
layers = ["cvat | s3 | config | clearml | class_api", "files | execution"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Adapters implement contracts without application orchestration"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["cveta2.adapters"]
forbidden_modules = ["cveta2.application.client", "cveta2.application.use_cases"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Canonical packages cannot import the public root"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["cveta2.domain", "cveta2.application", "cveta2.adapters", "cveta2.composition", "cveta2.interfaces"]
forbidden_modules = ["cveta2"]
as_packages = false

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "CVAT SDK belongs to its adapter"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["cvat_sdk"]
allowed_importers = ["cveta2.adapters.cvat"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "S3 SDK belongs to its adapter"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["boto3", "botocore"]
allowed_importers = ["cveta2.adapters.s3"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ClearML SDK belongs to its adapter"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["clearml"]
allowed_importers = ["cveta2.adapters.clearml"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Prompt toolkit belongs to incoming interactive interfaces"
type = "protected"
protected_modules = ["questionary"]
allowed_importers = ["cveta2.interfaces.commands.interactive"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Canonical package siblings are acyclic"
type = "acyclic_siblings"
ancestors = ["cveta2.domain", "cveta2.application", "cveta2.adapters", "cveta2.composition", "cveta2.interfaces"]
depth = 10

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # pyflakes (unused imports, undefined names, etc.)
    "I",      # isort

    "PERF",   # perflint
    "PLW",    # pylint warnings
    "RUF",    # ruff-specific rules
]
ignore = [
    # Line length — many lines are intentionally wide (Rich markup, byte tables)
    "E501",
    # Multiple statements on one line — used intentionally for compact channel init
    "E701", "E702",
    # Module-level import not at top — sys.path manipulation before imports is intentional
    "E402",
    # Ambiguous variable names (l, O, I) — e.g. loop indices in SMPS parsing
    "E741",
    # Magic value comparisons — byte values ($81, $E0, etc.) are self-documenting constants
    "PLR2004",
    # Complexity thresholds — conversion engine is inherently complex
    "C901", "PLR0912", "PLR0915", "PLR0913",
    # Boolean positional args — existing API; not worth breaking callers
    "FBT001", "FBT002",
    # Import-outside-toplevel — conditional sys.path inserts in subpackages
    "PLC0415",
    # Non-lowercase variable in function — SETTINGS_FILE, SMPS_ constants are fine
    "N806",
    # os.path → pathlib migration — not a priority; keep os.path for consistency
    "PTH100", "PTH102", "PTH103", "PTH107", "PTH110", "PTH111",
    "PTH112", "PTH113", "PTH116", "PTH117", "PTH118", "PTH119",
    "PTH120", "PTH122", "PTH123",
    # Private member access — sfx/chips.py and tools/ reuse a few private helpers
    "SLF001",
    # Typing-only imports — not restructuring imports right now
    "TC001", "TC002", "TC003",
    # Implicit namespace package — tools/ scripts don't need __init__.py
    "INP001",
    # Ambiguous Unicode in strings/docstrings/comments — musical symbols are intentional
    "RUF001", "RUF002", "RUF003",
    # Missing trailing comma — style preference; not enforced here
    "COM812",
    # No-explicit-stacklevel for warnings.warn — minor
    "B028",
]

# cannot stand in for core where a runner puts tests/ first on sys.path

# are the shared vocabulary.  As in MAME, a chip is a device (core/chips/<chip>: the emulator and its
# facts) that any driver can drive; core/synth drives it with a song's voices for the converter.  Directly below only where it keeps drivers swappable: the layers

name = "backend"
