[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "django-stubs-ext>=6.1",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "django-stubs[compatible-mypy]>=6.1",
    "import-linter>=2.15",
    "libcst>=1.9",
    "mypy>=2.3.1",
    "pytest>=9.1.1",
    "pytest-django>=4.14",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "ruff>=0.16.6",
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12.20260906",
]

[tool.ruff]
# Not just a floor: makes ruff itself refuse to run if it predates this config.
required-version = ">=0.16.6"
# `extend-exclude`, not `exclude`: `exclude` would drop ruff's own defaults.
extend-exclude = [
    "__pycache__",
    "*/migrations/*",
    "/media",  # MEDIA_ROOT at backend/media — anchored so apps/media/ is still linted
    ".pytest_cache",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",      # pycodestyle errors
    "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",      # pyflakes
    "I",      # isort
    "N",      # pep8-naming
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "B",      # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "DJ",     # flake8-django
    "S",      # flake8-bandit (security)
    "T20",    # flake8-print
    "DTZ",    # flake8-datetimez (naive datetime bugs)
    "SIM",    # flake8-simplify
    "PT",     # flake8-pytest-style
    "LOG",    # flake8-logging
    "G",      # flake8-logging-format
    "PGH",    # pygrep-hooks (blanket noqa/type-ignore)
    "ISC",    # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "ANN401", # no Any/object in annotations
    # Rules with no violations in the tree: enabled as ratchets, so the first
    # one written is caught in review rather than accumulating into a backlog.
    "PL",     # pylint — see the code carve-outs in `ignore`
    "ASYNC",  # flake8-async (blocking calls inside async defs)
    "T10",    # flake8-debugger (a stray breakpoint() reaching main)
    "YTT",    # flake8-2020 (sys.version comparisons that break on 3.10+)
    "FA",     # flake8-future-annotations
    "FLY",    # flynt (static str.join of literals -> f-string)
    "ICN",    # flake8-import-conventions
    "INP",    # flake8-no-pep420 (implicit namespace packages)
    "INT",    # flake8-gettext (f-strings in translation calls)
    "TC",     # flake8-type-checking — see the TC001/2/3 carve-out in `ignore`
    "A",      # flake8-builtins (shadowing builtins)
    "BLE",    # flake8-blind-except
    "FBT",    # flake8-boolean-trap
    "FURB",   # refurb
    "PERF",   # perflint
    "PIE",    # flake8-pie
    "PTH",    # flake8-use-pathlib
    "PYI",    # flake8-pyi
    "RET",    # flake8-return
    "RSE",    # flake8-raise
    "RUF",    # ruff-specific
    "SLF",    # flake8-self (private member access)
    "SLOT",   # flake8-slots
    "TRY",    # tryceratops
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # Line too long — handled by formatter
    "DJ001", # Avoid nullable CharField — common Django pattern
    "S101",  # assert — mypy type-narrowing in app code, and free rein in tests
    "S311",  # Use of random — not cryptographic in this app
    "PT019", # Underscore-prefix fixtures are the pytest idiom for side-effect-only fixtures
    "SIM118", # Django SessionStore has .keys() but non-dict iteration
    "RUF012", # ClassVar for mutable defaults — fights Django's Meta/field idiom
    "PLW0603", # global — the model-driven registries are lazily-warmed module caches
    "PLW2901", # loop-var rebinding is how the claim-value pipeline normalizes in place
    # Function-level imports are the standard Django answer to app-loading and
    # circular-import order, not a deferred-cost optimization.
    "PLC0415",
    "PLR2004", # magic-value comparison — mostly HTTP status codes and test literals
    # Size gates. A threshold can only say "long", which review already sees,
    # and any value either fires on code nobody wants to split or sits above
    # everything and never fires.
    "PLR0911", # too many returns
    "PLR0912", # too many branches
    "PLR0913", # too many arguments
    "PLR0915", # too many statements
    "PLR0917", # too many positional arguments
    # The four rules that push a type out of the runtime namespace: TC001-003
    # move imports into a TYPE_CHECKING block, TC006 quotes the cast() target so
    # the name needn't be imported at all. Django and Pydantic evaluate
    # annotations at runtime, and the docs treat TYPE_CHECKING as a typing smell
    # to justify, so that trade buys nothing here — and `cast("Foo", x)` reads
    # worse than `cast(Foo, x)` for it. The rest of TC, which catches what a
    # TYPE_CHECKING block gets *wrong*, stays on.
    "TC001",
    "TC002",
    "TC003",
    "TC006",
    # Call-site rule: fires on Pydantic's `Field(False, ...)` and on booleans
    # passed as claim *values*, not as flags. FBT001/FBT002 still guard the
    # definition side, which is where a boolean trap actually gets built.
    "FBT003",
    "TRY003", # error copy belongs at the raise site, not in an exception class
    # Pydantic field validators must raise ValueError to become a 422; a
    # TypeError escapes as a 500.
    "TRY004",
]

# The confusables the codebase uses on purpose, so RUF001-003 can stay on for
# the rest: a Cyrillic `а` or a Greek `ο` in an identifier, a URL or a
# comparison literal is a real bug.
allowed-confusables = ["–", "∪", "×", "›", "’"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"*/tests/*.py" = ["S106", "S603", "S607", "TRY301", "SLF001"]  # hardcoded test passwords, subprocess, raise-in-try as the test subject, reaching into internals
"manage.py" = ["T20"]
"apps/*/management/commands/*.py" = ["T20", "S603", "S607", "B904"]  # print, subprocess, raise-from in commands
"scripts/*.py" = ["T201"]
"tests/*.py" = ["SLF001"]  # the `*/tests/*.py` glob above does not reach the top-level suite
"apps/catalog/tests/benchmark_game_rows.py" = ["T201"]  # a __main__ CLI harness, not a test
# Django system checks accumulate Error objects with long multi-line messages
# behind a guard. Folding those into a generator expression puts the condition
# after the six-line message, for no measurable gain at startup.
"**/checks.py" = ["PERF401"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-self]
# Django's introspection API. The model-driven catalog is built on walking it.
extend-ignore-names = ["_meta", "_default_manager"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-builtins]
# `type` and `id` are django-ninja query-parameter names, so they're the wire
# contract rather than a local naming choice; `license` mirrors Claim.license.
# `credits` is the domain noun, and the builtin it shadows is the REPL's help
# object — irrelevant in server code.
ignorelist = ["credits", "id", "license", "type"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["apps", "config"]
section-order = ["future", "standard-library", "third-party", "first-party", "local-folder"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
strict = true
extra_checks = true
plugins = ["mypy_django_plugin.main"]
explicit_package_bases = true
exclude = [
    "migrations/",
    "\\.venv/",
    "^media/",  # MEDIA_ROOT at backend/media — anchored so apps/media/ is still type-checked
    "^cache/",
]
# Four workers is the knee of the curve on an 8-core laptop; above gets no faster.
num_workers = 4
enable_error_code = [
    # Guards the model-driven catalog: a match that misses a new entity type.
    "exhaustive-match",
    "explicit-override",
    "possibly-undefined",
    "unused-awaitable",
    "redundant-self",
    "ignore-without-code",
    "truthy-iterable",
    "truthy-bool",
    "unimported-reveal",
    "deprecated",
    # A cast or assert that claims a type the checker knows the value can't have.
    "narrowed-type-not-subtype",
]
# Keeps the Any from the `ignore_missing_imports` overrides below inside
# function bodies: an unfollowed import reaching a signature is an error.
disallow_any_unimported = true

[tool.django-stubs]
django_settings_module = "config.settings"
strict_settings = true

# Relax annotation requirements for fixtures. Type correctness of the code under
# test still matters; per-function annotations in tests do not.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["*.tests.*", "tests.*", "conftest"]
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
disallow_untyped_decorators = false
disallow_untyped_calls = false

# Third-party libraries without py.typed markers or upstream stubs.
# Suppresses import-untyped errors at the import site; the libraries themselves
# are still treated as Any at use sites. They also declare no explicit
# re-exports, so the strict check is relaxed for them alone.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["pillow_heif", "constance", "constance.*", "publicsuffixlist", "publicsuffixlist.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true
implicit_reexport = true

# ===========================================================================
# Import boundary enforcement
# See docs/AppBoundaries.md for the prose spec.
# Run with `lint-imports` (wired into scripts/lint).
# ===========================================================================
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["apps"]

# ===========================================================================
# Cross-app boundaries
# ===========================================================================

# The vertical dependency spine. Higher tiers may import lower ones; lower may
# not import higher; pipe-separated names are independent siblings at one level.
# Media is NOT listed here — its peer-isolation rule is asymmetric (provenance
# may import citation, but media internals may import neither) and is enforced
# by the two forbidden contracts below.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "App layer tiers"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "apps.kiosk",
    "apps.catalog",
    "apps.claim_edit",
    "apps.provenance",
    "apps.citation",
    "apps.accounts",
    "apps.actors",
    "apps.core",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # --- Tests are exempt (mirrors the frontend's test-file boundary policy) ---
    # A test for one app routinely imports another app's models and factories.
    "apps.*.tests.** -> apps.**",
    # --- Page-API carve-out (permanent) ---------------------------------
    # Page endpoints intentionally cross tiers to compose a route's full
    # render payload. See docs/AppBoundaries.md § Exception: Page API endpoints.
    "apps.accounts.api.* -> apps.provenance.**",
    "apps.core.api.admin_dashboard_page -> apps.**",
    # --- BASELINE: existing violations to fix; do NOT add to this list ---
    "apps.core.api_helpers -> apps.accounts.models",
    "apps.core.middleware.sentry_scope -> apps.accounts.models",
]

# --- Inter-app boundaries outside the linear spine ---

# The ingest system (apps.claim_ingest) is the bulk catalog write path — a
# top-level consumer, not a dependency. The whole catalog domain must not import
# it; the sole sanctioned edge is the ingest_patches / pull_patches management
# commands, which drive the pipeline (with catalog cache invalidation) as the
# orchestration entrypoint. Whole-app source + an ignore for that one edge is
# both more concise and more complete than enumerating the domain modules — it
# now catches a new coupling from ANY catalog submodule, not just the listed ones.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Catalog domain does not import the ingest system"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = ["apps.catalog"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.claim_ingest"]
ignore_imports = [
    "apps.catalog.management.** -> apps.claim_ingest.**",
    "apps.catalog.tests.** -> apps.claim_ingest.**",
    "apps.catalog.*.tests.** -> apps.claim_ingest.**",
]

# The forward direction (mirror of the contract above): the ingest system must
# not reach back into the catalog domain. claim_ingest depends only on core,
# provenance and citation; its catalog couplings (the model-type bound and the
# resolution dispatch) were severed step by step (Steps 1-2) before it moved to
# its own app. A single "apps.catalog" forbid suffices now that claim_ingest is
# a separate top-level app (not a descendant of catalog): it catches a NEW
# coupling to ANY catalog package — catalog.api included — not just today's
# (zero) offenders. The reverse contract above must enumerate its source instead,
# because it has to exclude apps.catalog.management (the ingest commands
# legitimately import the pipeline); the forward direction has no such carve-out.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Ingest system does not import the catalog domain"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = ["apps.claim_ingest"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.catalog"]

# The two claim-write engines are independent peers: claim_edit (interactive
# HTTP edits) and claim_ingest (the bulk patch pipeline) share no code — only the
# provenance/core substrate both write through. "Never each other" is a headline
# property, and the layer spine covers neither direction (claim_ingest is out of
# the spine), so both edges are forbidden explicitly — one contract per direction,
# mirroring the catalog↔ingest pair above. See docs/AppBoundaries.md.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Interactive engine does not import the bulk ingest system"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = ["apps.claim_edit"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.claim_ingest"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Bulk ingest system does not import the interactive engine"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = ["apps.claim_ingest"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.claim_edit"]

# The single claim-mint chokepoint. ``apps.provenance.claim_writer._assert_claim``
# is the one sanctioned non-ingest place a Claim is minted; only claim_edit (the
# generic interactive write engine) may reach it. Every other app is forbidden,
# so a new write path can't quietly grow a second mint primitive. Media routes
# its attach/detach mutations through claim_edit's execute_claims, so it is
# forbidden here too — leaving execute_claims as the single non-ingest mint
# caller. (provenance itself is not a source — intra-app imports of claim_writer
# are governed by the internal-stack layers contract instead.)
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Only the interactive write surfaces import the claim-mint primitive"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = [
    "apps.core",
    "apps.accounts",
    "apps.actors",
    "apps.citation",
    "apps.catalog",
    "apps.claim_ingest",
    "apps.kiosk",
    "apps.media",
]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.provenance.claim_writer"]

# The resolution-engine primitives (apps.catalog.resolve._engine — the shared
# winner-pick kernel) are deliberately movable to apps.provenance.resolution, so
# they may import only what provenance already can (provenance/citation/accounts/
# actors/core/stdlib). Forbid every tier provenance cannot reach — not just a
# concrete model name — so a stray `from ..engine import X` or `from
# ._relationships import Y` is caught too, since either equally blocks the hoist.
# Direct-only (allow_indirect_imports): the module's own imports are the
# invariant; a transitive provenance -> catalog chain is provenance's baseline,
# and travels with the module when it moves.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Resolution engine primitives stay catalog-free"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = ["apps.catalog.resolve._engine"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "apps.catalog",
    "apps.media",
    "apps.claim_edit",
    "apps.claim_ingest",
    "apps.kiosk",
]

# --- Media peer-isolation ---

# Media internals are peer-isolated from the citation/provenance data apps.
# The one sanctioned crack is media.models -> provenance.models for ClaimControlledModel;
# because this is a forbidden contract (indirect imports counted), the ignore_imports below
# severs that edge for every source — including selectors/helpers, which reach
# media.models transitively.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Media internals do not reach into the data apps"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "apps.media.selectors",
    "apps.media.processing",
    "apps.media.storage",
    "apps.media.schemas",
    "apps.media.helpers",
    "apps.media.models",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "apps.provenance",
    "apps.citation",
]
ignore_imports = [
    # Surgical exception: media_attachment is a claim field, so every
    # MediaSupportedModel is structurally a ClaimControlledModel.
    "apps.media.models.base -> apps.provenance.models",
]

# The reverse direction: the data apps must not depend on media. Direct-only:
# the indirect chain provenance -> catalog -> media is the provenance -> catalog
# baseline issue above, not a provenance -> media dependency.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Data apps do not depend on media"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = [
    "apps.provenance",
    "apps.citation",
    "apps.claim_edit",
    "apps.claim_ingest",
]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.media"]

# --- Cross-cutting invariants ---

# Domain models are the bottom of each app's internal stack: they must not reach
# up into the HTTP/serialization layer. Direct-only — an indirect models -> X ->
# api chain is X's problem, caught by the api-leaf contract below.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain models do not import the api/schema layer"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = [
    "apps.core.models",
    "apps.accounts.models",
    "apps.catalog.models",
    "apps.provenance.models",
    "apps.citation.models",
    "apps.media.models",
    "apps.kiosk.models",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "apps.core.api",
    "apps.accounts.api",
    "apps.catalog.api",
    "apps.provenance.api",
    "apps.citation.api",
    "apps.media.api",
    "apps.kiosk.api",
    "apps.core.schemas",
    "apps.accounts.schemas",
    "apps.citation.schemas",
    "apps.media.schemas",
    "apps.provenance.schemas",
]

# Test-only helpers must never be imported by production code. test_factories
# encode test-fixture invariants; importing them from app code ships test
# scaffolding into the runtime path. One contract per factory: a forbidden
# module cannot be a descendant of its source, so each sources all apps EXCEPT
# the one that owns the factory (which covers every cross-app leak; a same-app
# self-import is the only residual gap and is trivially caught in review).
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Production code does not import accounts test factories"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "apps.core",
    "apps.catalog",
    "apps.claim_edit",
    "apps.claim_ingest",
    "apps.citation",
    "apps.provenance",
    "apps.media",
    "apps.kiosk",
]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.accounts.test_factories"]
# Tests import it freely; the second ignore lets another test factory reuse it
# (citation's default_actor() delegates here) — both are test-only helpers, not
# production code. apps.provenance.Source sits a tier above citation, so a
# user-backed default actor is the one the citation factory can reach.
ignore_imports = [
    "apps.*.tests.** -> apps.accounts.test_factories",
    "apps.**.test_factories -> apps.accounts.test_factories",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Production code does not import provenance test factories"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "apps.core",
    "apps.accounts",
    "apps.catalog",
    "apps.claim_edit",
    "apps.claim_ingest",
    "apps.citation",
    "apps.media",
    "apps.kiosk",
]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.provenance.test_factories"]
# apps.**.tests.** (not apps.*.tests.**) so nested test packages like
# apps.catalog.resolve.tests are covered — the commit that routed tests through
# make_claim means deeply-nested test packages now import this factory too.
ignore_imports = ["apps.**.tests.** -> apps.provenance.test_factories"]

# ===========================================================================
# Per-app internal structure (dependency order: consumers first, core last)
# ===========================================================================

# ----- catalog -----

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Catalog app internal stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true # so a new submodule left unplaced fails the build
exhaustive_ignores = ["apps", "migrations", "tests"]
containers = ["apps.catalog"]
layers = [
    "api | admin | management",
    "claims | resolve | signals",
    "_walks | cache | services",
    "models | authz",
    "engine", # domain-neutral; will eventually be moved out of catalog
]

# The generic resolver core — claim projection (_entities), its
# coercion/FK/constraint helpers (_helpers), and the read-side payload
# vocabulary (_claim_values) — is domain-agnostic substrate that merely lives
# in catalog: it names no concrete model and drives entirely off claim-field
# introspection (get_claim_fields, _meta).
#
# This will eventually be hoisted to the substrate, but the model-driven resolver
# engine is still coupled: it awaits the deferred relationship declaration
# vocabulary. The relationship/dispatch resolvers (_relationships, _dispatch,
# __init__) still bind MachineModel. See
# docs/plans/model_driven_metadata/ModelDrivenClaimResolution.md.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Generic resolver core does not import the catalog domain"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = [
    "apps.catalog.resolve._entities",
    "apps.catalog.resolve._helpers",
    "apps.catalog.resolve._claim_values",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "apps.catalog.models",
    "apps.catalog.claims",
    "apps.catalog.services",
    "apps.catalog.cache",
    "apps.catalog.engine.naming",
    "apps.catalog.signals",
    "apps.catalog.authz",
]

# The domain-neutral engine — the generic HTTP-surface substrate plus the generic
# bases (AliasModel, the wire schema bases, naming, the model-registry walk) the
# concrete domain mounts and subclasses — must never reach back up into the
# catalog domain.
#
# This is the in-app mirror of the resolver-core rule and the load-bearing invariant
# behind the deferred app extraction: once enforced, lifting `engine/` to its own
# top-level app is a `git mv`. The "Catalog internal layers" contract already forbids
# this structurally (engine is the bottom layer), but the explicit forbid is a
# durable, self-documenting ratchet that survives any future layer reshuffle.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Engine does not import the catalog domain"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = ["apps.catalog.engine"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.catalog"]
# Whole-package source with a wildcard
# ignore for engine's own internal edges (e.g. aliases → models) is more concise
# and more complete than enumerating the sibling domain modules — it catches a
# new coupling to ANY catalog domain module, present or future.
ignore_imports = ["apps.catalog.engine.** -> apps.catalog.engine.**"]

# The catalog engine's own internal stack.
# TODO: `entity_api ⊄ export_api` seam joins this contract when the public
# export surface (`export_api`) is extracted alongside `entity_api`.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Catalog engine internal stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true # so new submodule left unplaced fails build
exhaustive_ignores = ["tests"]
containers = ["apps.catalog.engine"]
layers = [
    "entity_api",
    "query | aliases",
    "schemas | models | naming | rich_text | walks",
]

# ----- claim_ingest -----

# The apply engine is the source-agnostic IR consumer: it turns an IngestPlan
# (apps.claim_ingest.plan) into DB writes and must not know which front end built
# it. apps.claim_ingest.patches is the patch adapter — format parsing and
# PatchError live there. The engine raises plain ValidationError and never imports
# the adapter, keeping apply source-agnostic.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Apply engine stays source-agnostic (no patch adapter)"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = ["apps.claim_ingest.apply"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.claim_ingest.patches"]

# The patch system is a compiler front end: it lowers YAML patches to an
# IngestPlan (the IR), which the ingest back end (apply/) executes. The split is
# load-bearing — new patch behavior belongs in the front end against the IR, not
# as a fork of apply_plan. See docs/DataArchitecture.md.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Patch front end does not depend on the ingest back end"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["apps.claim_ingest.patches"]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.claim_ingest.apply"]

# ----- provenance -----

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Provenance app internal stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true # so new submodule left unplaced fails build
exhaustive_ignores = ["apps", "migrations", "tests", "test_factories"]
containers = ["apps.provenance"]
layers = [
    "api | admin",
    "page_endpoints",
    "sources | history",
    "claim_citations",
    "helpers",
    "claims | claim_writer | citation_writer | display | revert",
    "changeset_writer",
    "validation | schemas | claim_ranking_in_db | licensing | resolution | rate_limits",
    "attribution",
    "models | claim_presence | constants | parked_fields | entity_links | pagination | authz",
    # The abstract claim-control bases every claim-controlled model inherits.
    # Pinned to the bottom so it can't reach UP into the provenance domain
    # (Claim, ChangeSet, Source). Its core-only-leaf guarantee — no cross-app
    # imports either — is enforced separately by the forbidden contract below,
    # since the global tiers would otherwise let it import down into citation /
    # accounts. Together they keep the package lift-out-ready (below citation).
    "model_bases",
    "types",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Claim-control bases stay a core-only leaf"
type = "forbidden"
# model_bases is the substrate every claim-controlled model inherits, meant to
# lift out to a top-level app below citation; it must import nothing but
# apps.core. The other boundaries are already covered — the internal-stack layer
# blocks reaching up into the provenance domain, the global tiers block the apps
# above provenance, and "Data apps do not depend on media" blocks media. The one
# gap is the apps the tiers let provenance import DOWNWARD (citation, accounts):
# a bare tiers check would allow model_bases -> citation, which would later cycle.
source_modules = ["apps.provenance.model_bases"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "apps.citation",
    "apps.accounts",
]

# ----- citation -----

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Citation app internal stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true # so new submodule left unplaced fails build
exhaustive_ignores = ["apps", "migrations", "tests", "management", "test_factories"]
containers = ["apps.citation"]
layers = [
    "api | admin",
    "url_extraction",
    "extractors | extraction | source_upsert | schemas | deep_links | locators",
    "models",
    "scheme_validation",
    "psl | deliverers",
    # The shared-CDN host table: consulted by models' clean(), extractors'
    # matcher and psl's derive funnel, itself importing only hosts — so it
    # sits alone between them and the pure bottom layer.
    "shared_hosts",
    "hosts | citation_types | safe_fetch | authz | source_node | isbn",
]

# Inside the citation_types package, the layers ARE the audience walls of
# the two plugin frameworks. Bottom-up: vocabulary (shared enum/aliases) and
# plugin_discovery (the generic module-export discovery helper), both importing
# nothing from the package; citation_scheme_specs (scheme-author declarations, pure
# configuration); citation_type_specs (type-author declarations; imports
# scheme specs only for the scheme_spec_type cross-reference — the
# composition contract's static face); the type modules (first-party type
# programming); then the two framework modules (citation_scheme_driver,
# citation_type_driver) beside the scheme modules; registry aggregates and
# weaves at the top. Exhaustive, so a new submodule must be placed.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Citation types plugin-package stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true
containers = ["apps.citation.citation_types"]
layers = [
    "registry",
    "schemes | citation_scheme_driver | citation_type_driver",
    "book | document | periodical | video | web",
    "citation_type_specs",
    "citation_scheme_specs",
    "vocabulary | plugin_discovery",
]

# The audience walls, enforced. Plugin modules — what an author writes — may
# import only declarations, never the framework machinery that drives them;
# and a citation-scheme author never sees citation-type authoring (a scheme
# module importing citation_type_specs directly fails the build). Direct-only,
# because the sanctioned door exists: a scheme imports its owning type's
# module for the per-type scheme contract (video's VideoSchemeSpec), and that
# module legitimately imports the type declarations.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Citation scheme modules see only declarations"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = ["apps.citation.citation_types.schemes"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "apps.citation.citation_types.citation_scheme_driver",
    "apps.citation.citation_types.citation_type_driver",
    "apps.citation.citation_types.citation_type_specs",
    "apps.citation.citation_types.registry",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Citation type modules see only declarations"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "apps.citation.citation_types.book",
    "apps.citation.citation_types.periodical",
    "apps.citation.citation_types.video",
    "apps.citation.citation_types.web",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "apps.citation.citation_types.citation_scheme_driver",
    "apps.citation.citation_types.citation_type_driver",
    "apps.citation.citation_types.registry",
]

# psl.py is the lone Public Suffix List gateway. The pure hosts module must stay
# dependency-free, and the recognition read path (extractors) must resolve by
# exact-stored-host suffix match only — never by consulting the PSL. So neither
# may import psl. Direct-only: models.py legitimately imports psl for the
# write-time clean() guard, and extractors imports models, so the indirect
# extractors -> models -> psl edge is fine — only a *direct* dependency is the
# leak this forbids.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "hosts and the recognition read path stay PSL-free"
type = "forbidden"
allow_indirect_imports = "true"
source_modules = [
    "apps.citation.hosts",
    "apps.citation.extractors",
]
forbidden_modules = ["apps.citation.psl"]

# ----- accounts -----

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Accounts app internal stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true # so new submodule left unplaced fails build
exhaustive_ignores = ["apps", "migrations", "tests", "test_factories"]
containers = ["apps.accounts"]
layers = [
    "api | admin | management | middleware",
    "models | schemas | auth_errors",
    "backends | pending | reserved | usernames | workos_client",
    # Imports nothing, so it sits at the bottom where every layer can reach it.
    "types",
]

# ----- actors -----

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Actors app internal stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true # so new submodule left unplaced fails build
exhaustive_ignores = ["apps", "migrations", "tests"]
containers = ["apps.actors"]
layers = [
    "admin | registry | checks",
    "models",
    "types",
]

# ----- core -----

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Core app internal stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true # so new submodule left unplaced fails build
exhaustive_ignores = ["apps", "migrations", "tests"]
containers = ["apps.core"]
layers = [
    "api | management",
    "markdown",
    "cache_control | wikilinks | middleware",
    "admin | admin_notifications | api_helpers | authz | autocomplete | checks | entity_types | licensing | rate_limits | sitemap | soft_delete",
    "exceptions | models",
    "admin_apps | admin_site | fetch_guard | response_cache | schemas | search | site_origin | types | user_agent | validators",
]

# ----- media -----

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Media app internal stack"
type = "layers"
exhaustive = true # so new submodule left unplaced fails build
exhaustive_ignores = ["apps", "migrations", "tests"]
containers = ["apps.media"]
layers = [
    "api | admin | checks",
    "authz",
    "selectors", # selectors gets its own tier above the storage/schemas/helpers peers because it composes storage + schemas into wire schemas, which helpers may not.
    "processing | storage | schemas | helpers",
    "models",
    "constants",
]

# Tenant-only migration/shadow composition. Sub's incumbent payment writers

# First composed domain module. Its `so` lineage is registered in

# Selectable tenant-plane schema composed for verification/shadow preparation

dotmac-subscriptions = { version = "0.1.0a3", source = "forgejo" }
# Dormant payment email backfill and read-only parity only. Sub's legacy live
# writer and renderer retain authority until a separate sealed cutover.
dotmac-template-studio = { version = "0.2.0a5", source = "forgejo" }
# Released atomic tenant-only Tax storage; no runtime caller or policy activation.

# the `ib` lineage is registered in alembic.ini so `mod_inbox` exists, and Sub
# declares its channel traits against it. Sub's own `public.inbox_*` tables
# remain the authority for every conversation, message and read cursor; no Sub
# service imports the module's service or writes a `mod_inbox` row. The
# authority move is ruled by docs/adr/0013-inbox-conversation-authority.md and
# is gated on evidence that does not exist yet. a1 is the published release;

# rewrites a JSON file with a trailing comma before the closing `}`/`]`,
# which `json.load` then refuses (confirmed directly against this repository
# — `ruff format` on a copy of kernel-runtime-composition.json produces
# "Illegal trailing comma before end of object"). This is pre-existing and
# not specific to the composition record: docs/kernel-runtime-readiness.json,
# untouched by this change, reports the identical "Would reformat". Their
# validity is enforced instead by tests/architecture/

    "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",     # pyupgrade
    "S",      # flake8-bandit (security)

    "E501",   # line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",   # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "S101",   # use of assert (OK in tests)
    "B007",   # loop control variable not used
    "B017",   # assert raises Exception in tests/legacy code
    "B904",   # raise without explicit cause in except
    "B905",   # zip strict parameter not explicitly set
    "C401",   # unnecessary generator for set
    "C408",   # unnecessary collection() call
    "C416",   # unnecessary comprehension
    "E402",   # import not at top of file
    "E712",   # boolean comparison against True/False
    "E741",   # ambiguous variable names in legacy/tests
    "F841",   # assigned but unused local variable
    "S105",   # possible hardcoded password string — too noisy on field
              # names and enum members; the real shape is gated by
              # tests/architecture/test_credential_literals.py
    "S110",   # try/except/pass
    "S112",   # try/except/continue

# Tests intentionally use asserts (S101) / hardcoded creds in fixtures
# (S105/S106), bind to 0.0.0.0 to simulate listener defaults (S104), and

"tests/**" = ["S101", "S104", "S105", "S106", "E731"]
"scripts/**" = ["S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "S608"]
# Alembic migrations: data-shape SQL is by design ``text()``-built and
# imports often sit below module-level helpers, so the standard ruff
# rules don't apply cleanly.
"alembic/**" = ["E402", "S608"]
"alembic/versions_archive/**" = ["S104", "S608"]
[tool.ruff.format]

    "orca_auto.systemd_plan",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Worker process supervision stays below CLI assembly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["orca_auto.cli_worker_supervision"]
forbidden_modules = ["orca_auto.cli_workers"]

# ORCA input handling is layered: line syntax, then geometry/%block structure,
# then external-file reference scanning and resource directives side by side,
# then whole-input validation. Syntax and blocks never see the layers above;
# nothing here reaches runtime consumers.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ORCA input syntax and blocks never import reference scanning, resources or validation"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "orca_auto.orca.input_validation",
    "orca_auto.orca.input_references | orca_auto.orca.resource_directives",
    "orca_auto.orca.input_blocks",
    "orca_auto.orca.input_syntax",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ORCA input reference scanning and validation stay below runtime consumers"
type = "forbidden"

    "orca_auto.orca.input_syntax",

# The top-level CLI modules are the outermost layer: they compose the domain

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain packages never import the top-level CLI layer"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["orca_auto.core", "orca_auto.orca"]
forbidden_modules = [

# ....................... #
# Pytest

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore:Deprecated call to `pkg_resources.declare_namespace`:DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::FutureWarning",
    "ignore::pytest.PytestCollectionWarning",
]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_functions = "test_*"
pythonpath = ["src", "tests"]
addopts = ["--tb=short", "--strict-markers", "--strict-config"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Safety net: no test may hang the run indefinitely. On timeout, dump all thread
# stacks and kill the process (the `thread` method guarantees the run can't stick).
# Defense-in-depth, not a fix — it's how the Temporal-sandbox/coverage-sysmon deadlock
# (see CI's COVERAGE_CORE=ctrace) was diagnosed: the dumped stack pinpointed the wedge.
# Generous enough to cover container/session-fixture startup on a cold runner.
timeout = 300
timeout_method = "thread"
markers = [
    "perf: Performance benchmark (excluded from default just test; not all perf tests need Docker)",
    "perf_gate: In-process, deterministic benchmark gated for regressions in CI (same-runner A/B vs merge-base)",
    "fuzz: Extended DST fuzz over many seeds (excluded from default just test; run via just fuzz, e.g. nightly)",
    "integration: Integration test",
    "unit: Unit test",
    "asyncio: Async test",
    "conformance(plane, engine): A differential conformance leg — this test runs the named plane's shared scenario against the named engine. Censused by .github/scripts/conformance_manifest.py; both kwargs are required",
    "mongo_atlas_search: Integration test requiring mongodb/mongodb-atlas-local",
    "yc_kms: Integration test requiring real Yandex Cloud KMS credentials (no emulator exists; skipped unless FORZE_YC_KMS_KEY_ID is set)",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src"]
branch = true
# Relative paths so per-shard data files combine cleanly across CI jobs.
relative_files = true
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__init__.py",
    "*/_version.py",
    "*/_compat.py",
    "*/_logging.py",
    # Temporal worker interceptors are exercised with a full SDK runtime.
    "*/forze_temporal/interceptors/*",
    # Redis deps module is exercised with a full SDK runtime.
    "*/forze_redis/execution/deps/module.py",
    "*/forze_meilisearch/execution/deps/module.py",
    "*/forze_neo4j/execution/deps/module.py",
    "*/forze_kafka/execution/deps/module.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
sort = "cover"
precision = 1
# Global floor: enforced in CI (see .github/workflows/ci.yml). Per-package
# floors are enforced on top of it — see [tool.coverage_floors] below.
fail_under = 80
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    # ``@overload`` stubs (and their ``...`` bodies) are type-checker-only: the
    # runtime impl follows them, so they are never executed. Excluding them keeps
    # branch coverage honest instead of penalizing typed overloaded signatures.
    "@overload",
    "@(typing\\.)?overload",
    "^\\s*\\.\\.\\.$",
    # Inline ellipsis stub bodies (``def f(...) -> T: ...``, including the closing
    # line of a multi-line signature) are the same type-checker-only stubs as the
    # own-line ``...`` above. The formatter collapses Protocol/overload bodies to
    # this inline form, so match the terminating ``: ...`` to keep branch coverage
    # honest for inline-stub Protocols (e.g. forze.base.serialization.model_codec).
    ": \\.\\.\\.\\s*$",
]

# ....................... #
# Per-package coverage floors
#
# Enforced by .github/scripts/coverage_floors.py in the CI coverage job, on top
# of the global fail_under gate above (a thin new package must not hide behind
# the well-covered core). Every top-level forze* package under src/ is gated:
# packages get `default` unless listed in `exceptions`, so a brand-new package
# is enforced automatically. Locally: `just coverage-floors` (full suite +
# check) or `just coverage-floors-check` (existing .coverage data).
#
# Calibration: floors gate the COMBINED unit+integration coverage that CI
# measures (all test shards merged) — a unit-only run reports far lower numbers
# for integration-heavy packages and must not be used to tune this table.

[tool.coverage_floors]
default = 80

# Exceptions ratchet reality, not aspiration: one entry per package that
# legitimately sits below the default TODAY (package = its current floor, with
# a trailing reason). Raise or delete entries as coverage improves.
# Empty as of 2026-07-13: combined CI coverage has every package >= 82%.
[tool.coverage_floors.exceptions]

# ....................... #
# Docs floors (.github/scripts/docs_floors.py)
#
# The coverage-floors move, applied to documentation. A public contract symbol that no
# page mentions is the debt that recurred through six audits: the plane ships, the docs
# follow a release or three later, and nothing fails in between. Here it fails.
#
# Three properties: every public DepKey/*Spec under contracts/ is mentioned somewhere in
# pages/docs; the nav resolves both ways (no dangling entry, no orphan page); every
# relative link between docs resolves.
#
# Exemptions are grouped and reasoned, like the conformance manifest's declared gaps —
# and they are checked in BOTH directions: an exempt symbol that no longer exists fails,
# and so does one that has since been documented. The table can only shrink.
#
# Locally: `just docs-check` (offline, ~5s) — part of `just quality`.

[tool.docs_floors]
docs_root = "pages/docs"
nav_config = "pages/zensical.toml"
# The capability index whose last column names each capability's dep keys. A key some
# `ctx` accessor resolves must appear in a row that shows that accessor, so a key
# cannot be documented under the wrong capability.
dep_key_index = "reference/contracts.md"
# Snippet includes pulled into other pages with `--8<--`; they are content, not
# destinations, so they are deliberately absent from the nav.
orphan_allow = ["dst/_generated/*.md"]

# `just build-diagrams` renders pages/diagrams/*.d2 into a gitignored output tree, so a
# fresh checkout links to SVGs that do not exist yet. Such a link is checked against the
# .d2 that generates it instead of the rendered file: CI passes without running the build,
# and a renamed or deleted diagram still fails.
[tool.docs_floors.generated_links]
prefix = "_diagrams"
source_dir = "pages/diagrams"
source_suffix = ".d2"

[[tool.docs_floors.exempt_groups]]
kind = "identity-plane-undocumented"
symbols = [
    "ApiKeyLifecycleDepKey",
    "AuthnEventSinkDepKey",
    "DelegationDepKey",
    "DelegationGrantDepKey",
    "GrantQueryDepKey",
    "PasswordAccountProvisioningDepKey",
    "PasswordLifecycleDepKey",
    "PasswordResetDepKey",
    "PrincipalDeactivationDepKey",
    "PrincipalEligibilityDepKey",
    "PrincipalRegistryDepKey",
    "RoleAssignmentDepKey",
    "TokenLifecycleDepKey",
]
reason = """
The identity plane splits its surface across many small lifecycle ports, and the docs \
teach it through the presets and recipes that wire them together rather than port by \
port. The gap is real for anyone replacing one port (a custom password lifecycle, an \
external principal registry), which is exactly the audience the identity reference page \
does not yet serve. `PasswordResetDepKey` joined its siblings when dep keys stopped \
counting as documented on a substring of their wire name: it had been passing on \
`authn_password_reset` appearing somewhere rather than on any page naming the key.\
"""

[[tool.docs_floors.exempt_groups]]
kind = "structural-base-types"
symbols = [
    "AggregateTruncSpec",
    "BaseSpec",
    "IngestSpec",
    "QuerySortKeySpec",
    "TenancyRouteSpec",
]
reason = """
Not application-facing vocabulary: `BaseSpec` is the shared base every documented spec \
inherits, and the rest are structural parts of a documented surface (an aggregate \
truncation unit, a sort-key declaration, an ingest target, a tenancy route) that the \
pages describe by behaviour rather than by type name. Documenting the type would add a \
name to learn without adding a decision to make — the one case where the gate's bar is \
worth declining rather than meeting.\
"""

# ....................... #
# Conformance manifest (.github/scripts/conformance_manifest.py)
#
# The differential ratchet, built on the same shape as the coverage floors above.
# DST proves invariants against the mock; a conformance leg is what makes "passed
# on the mock" mean "matches the real engine". This table is the one place that
# says which planes have such a leg, against which engines — and the checker
# derives the engines that ACTUALLY register each plane's ports from the
# integration packages, so a backend that registers a manifested port without
# running the leg fails CI. Every DepKey under contracts/ must be claimed exactly
# once: by a plane, by a declared gap, or by a categorised exemption.
#
# Locally: `just conformance-check` (offline, ~10s) or `just conformance` (the
# Docker-backed legs themselves).

[tool.conformance_manifest]
divergence_catalog = "forze_dst.conformance.catalog:PLANE_DIVERGENCES"

# Engines whose name does not map to `forze_<engine>`. Used to attribute a derived
# provider package to the leg that covers it.
[tool.conformance_manifest.engines]
mock = { package = "forze_mock" }
local = { package = "forze" }
subprocess = { package = "forze" }
container = { package = "forze_sandbox" }
kserve_v2 = { package = "forze_inference" }
mlflow = { package = "forze_inference" }

# ....................... #
# Planes with a leg

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.counter]
scenario = "forze_dst.conformance.counters:run_counter_allocation"
dep_keys = ["counter", "counter_admin"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "redis", "mongo", "firestore"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.storage]
scenario = "forze_dst.conformance.storage:run_container_probes"
dep_keys = ["storage_command", "storage_query", "storage_uploads"]
engines = ["mock", "s3", "gcs"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.search]
scenario = "tests.support.search_conformance:SEARCH_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["search_query", "hub_search_query", "federated_search_query"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "mongo", "meilisearch"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.search_write]
scenario = "tests.support.search_conformance:SEARCH_WRITE_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["search_command", "search_management"]
engines = ["mock", "meilisearch"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.graph]
scenario = "forze_dst.conformance.graph:run_bounded_neighbors"
dep_keys = ["graph_command", "graph_query"]
engines = ["mock", "neo4j"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.hlc_checkpoint]
scenario = "tests.support.hlc_checkpoint_conformance:HLC_CHECKPOINT_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["hlc_checkpoint"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "mongo"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.graph_management]
scenario = "tests.support.graph_management_conformance:GRAPH_MANAGEMENT_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["graph_management"]
engines = ["mock", "neo4j"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.idempotency]
scenario = "tests.support.idempotency_conformance:IDEMPOTENCY_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["idempotency"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "redis", "mongo"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.inference]
scenario = "forze_dst.conformance.inference:run_capability_gates"
dep_keys = ["inference_query"]
engines = ["mock", "local", "kserve_v2", "mlflow"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.dynamic_read]
scenario = "tests.support.dynamic_read_conformance:DYNAMIC_READ_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["dynamic_read_query"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.rotating_credentials]
scenario = "tests.support.rotating_credentials:ROTATING_STORE_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["rotating_credentials", "rotating_credentials_admin"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "mongo"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.isolation]
scenario = "forze_dst.conformance.anomalies:BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["transaction_manager", "document_command", "document_query"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "mongo"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.isolation.waivers]
firestore = """
Firestore transactions are not a general isolation surface: the client exposes optimistic \
read-then-commit retries over a single document set, with no session-per-participant model, \
so the N-independent-sessions ConformanceBackend the anomaly battery requires cannot be \
built against it. The document adapter is covered by its own suite; a real isolation leg \
needs a different harness, not this one.\
"""
neo4j = """
Neo4j registers the transaction manager for the graph plane, which has no document store \
for the Adya anomalies to act on — the battery's read/write sets are document rows. Graph \
transactional behaviour is covered by the graph mock conformance suite instead.\
"""

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.owned_reads]
scenario = "tests.support.owned_reads_conformance:OWNED_READS_BATTERY"
dep_keys = []
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "mongo", "firestore"]
# The document ports are claimed by the isolation plane; this battery is one more claim on
# them — whoever provides a document query port owes a leg showing a foreign row is not found.
derive_from = ["document_query"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.delivery]
scenario = "forze_dst.conformance.delivery:run_crash_recovery_delivery"
dep_keys = ["outbox_command", "outbox_query", "outbox_admin", "inbox"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "mongo"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.realtime_delivery]
scenario = "forze_dst.conformance.realtime:run_gateway_crash_delivery"
dep_keys = [
    "stream_command",
    "stream_query",
    "stream_group_admin",
    "stream_group_query",
]
engines = ["mock", "redis"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.realtime_delivery.waivers]
kafka = """
Kafka registers stream_command as the offset-log delivery model, whose commit-stream group \
contract is a different one: consumers advance an offset instead of acking individual \
messages, so the gateway's store-then-forward crash windows do not map onto it. Covered by \
the commit_stream gap, which names it explicitly.\
"""

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.realtime_cursor]
scenario = "forze_kits.integrations.realtime.conformance:run_capped_replay_boundary"
# No dep_keys of its own: the offline mailbox is kit code over the document ports, which
# the isolation plane already claims. What this plane gates is the kit's own invariant —
# a capped replay interleaved with a live cumulative ack — across the document stores
# behind it, so its engines are declared rather than derived.
dep_keys = []
engines = ["mock", "postgres", "mongo"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.misuse_transfer]
scenario = "forze_dst.conformance.transfer:run_transfer"
dep_keys = []
engines = ["postgres"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.dlock]
scenario = "tests.support.dlock_conformance:DLOCK_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["distributed_lock_command", "distributed_lock_query"]
engines = ["mock", "redis"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.sandbox]
scenario = "tests.support.sandbox_conformance:SANDBOX_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["sandbox_run"]
engines = ["mock", "subprocess", "container"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.fleet]
scenario = "tests.support.fleet_conformance:FLEET_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["fleet"]
engines = ["mock", "redis"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.revocation_states]
scenario = "tests.support.revocation_states_conformance:STATES_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["authn_revocation_states"]
engines = ["mock", "redis"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.principal_epoch]
scenario = "tests.support.revocation_states_conformance:EPOCH_BATTERY"
dep_keys = ["authn_principal_epoch"]
engines = ["mock", "postgres"]

# ....................... #
# Declared gaps: planes with real providers and no leg yet. Listed so "not covered"
# is data a reviewer sees, never an absence they have to notice.

[tool.conformance_manifest.gaps.queue]
dep_keys = ["queue_command", "queue_query"]
engines = ["rabbitmq", "sqs"]
reason = """
Two independent brokers implement the queue port and nothing compares them. The \
failure-path review already found their poison/retry dispositions differ; a battery over \
publish, consume, nack and redelivery is the leg this gap is waiting for.\
"""

[tool.conformance_manifest.gaps.analytics]
dep_keys = ["analytics_ingest", "analytics_query"]
engines = ["bigquery", "clickhouse", "duckdb", "postgres"]
reason = """
Four engines answer the analytics ports and no shared scenario runs against more than one. \
Scoping is the work here, as it was for search: most of what an analytics engine does is \
meant to differ, so the battery must assert the structural contract (row shape, typed \
scalars, empty results, parameter binding) and nothing about the plan or the dialect.\
"""

[tool.conformance_manifest.gaps.durable_function]
dep_keys = [
    "durable_function_step",
    "durable_function_run_store",
    "durable_function_run_admin",
    "durable_function_schedule_store",
    "durable_function_event_command",
]
engines = ["postgres", "mongo", "inngest"]
reason = """
Postgres, Mongo and Inngest implement the durable-function ports with materially different \
execution models (in-process replay against a step store versus a hosted event-driven \
runner). The two self-hosted stores are each pinned against the mock oracle by a scenario \
battery (tests/support/durable_conformance.py), which is what keeps them agreeing with each \
other; Inngest is compared to nothing. Step idempotency, replay determinism and JSON-only \
step results across the hosted runner are what a differential still has to pin.\
"""

[tool.conformance_manifest.planes.field_encryption]
scenario = "tests.support.field_encryption_conformance:FIELD_ENCRYPTION_BATTERY"
dep_keys = [
    "crypto.keyring",
    "crypto.deterministic",
    "crypto.aead",
    "crypto.key_directory",
]
engines = ["postgres", "mongo", "firestore"]
# Nobody REGISTERS the crypto keys — they are bound once in core and consumed by each
# adapter that seals values — so deriving from this plane's own keys would find no engines
# and require nothing. The document ports answer the same question exactly: this battery
# is document-plane specific, so whoever provides a document port needs a leg here.
derive_from = ["document_command", "document_query"]

[tool.conformance_manifest.gaps.kms]
dep_keys = ["crypto.kms"]
engines = ["vault"]
reason = """
Vault is the only KMS the provider census can see, but forze_kms ships AWS, GCP, Yandex and \
a self-hosted local backend behind the same port without an execution/deps module, so they \
are invisible here. Wrap/unwrap/rotate under one AAD is a sharp equivalence relation and \
deserves a battery across all of them.\
"""

# ....................... #
# Exemptions: contract keys with no differential to run. Each states a claim about
# the world, and the two structural kinds are CHECKED against the provider census —
# `single-engine` fails the moment a second backend registers the key, which is the
# exact event that turns "nothing to compare" into "nothing is comparing".

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "single-engine"
keys = [
    "cache",
    "pubsub_command",
    "pubsub_query",
    "search_result_snapshot",
]
reason = """
Redis is the only backend that registers these, so there is no second implementation to \
compare it against; the mock stands in for it in unit tests and any divergence would be \
mock-vs-Redis alone. A second cache, pub/sub or snapshot backend turns this claim false \
and fails the checker.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "single-engine"
keys = ["commit_stream_group_admin", "commit_stream_group_query"]
reason = """
Kafka alone implements the commit-stream (offset-log) delivery model. The contract is not \
shared with the ack-stream ports, so there is nothing to run a cross-engine differential \
against until a second offset-log broker lands.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "single-engine"
keys = ["graph_raw_query"]
reason = """
The raw-query hatch is Cypher by definition — there is no shared contract for a second \
engine to answer differently, so nothing about it is comparable. The graph data ports it \
sits beside are covered by the `graph` plane above. Tenant-aware traversal stays out of \
reach by construction — a cross-tenant edge is unrepresentable in the mock, so a \
mock-backed proof there would prove nothing.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "single-engine"
keys = [
    "durable_workflow_command",
    "durable_workflow_query",
    "durable_workflow_schedule_command",
    "durable_workflow_schedule_query",
]
reason = """
Temporal is the only workflow engine behind these ports, and its semantics (deterministic \
replay inside a sandboxed worker) are not reproduced by any second implementation, including \
the mock. The durable-function step port is the shared surface, and it has its own gap entry.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "single-engine"
keys = ["secrets", "secrets_admin", "secrets_lease"]
reason = """
Vault is the only registered secrets backend; the local file/env presets are wiring for \
development rather than a second engine. The lifecycle plane's own batteries already run the \
mock against Vault for the fetch/rotate/verify-before-promote sequence.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "single-engine"
keys = ["procedure_command", "http_service"]
reason = """
One implementation each (Postgres for the procedure port, forze_http for the outbound \
service port) and no second backend to disagree with. Each is exercised directly against \
its real server; there is simply no second party to a differential.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "no-engine-matrix"
keys = [
    "authn",
    "authn_api_key_lifecycle",
    "authn_api_key_verifier",
    "authn_event_sink",
    "authn_password_account_provisioning",
    "authn_password_lifecycle",
    "authn_password_reset",
    "authn_password_verifier",
    "authn_principal_deactivation",
    "authn_principal_eligibility",
    "authn_principal_resolver",
    "authn_token_lifecycle",
    "authn_token_verifier",
    "authz_decision",
    "authz_delegation",
    "authz_delegation_grant",
    "authz_grant_query",
    "authz_principal_registry",
    "authz_role_assignment",
    "authz_scope",
    "tenant_management",
    "tenant_resolver",
]
reason = """
The identity plane's ports are implemented in forze_identity over whichever document store \
the app already wired — there is no backend-specific adapter for them, so no engine axis \
exists to run a differential along. Their storage-level behaviour is inherited from the \
document plane, which the isolation plane does compare. The checker verifies the claim: any \
integration package registering one of these fails here.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "no-engine-matrix"
keys = [
    "domain_event_dispatcher",
    "saga_executor",
    "resilience_admin",
    "resilience_executor",
    "resilience_port_policies",
    "embeddings_provider",
]
reason = """
Kernel-side ports with a single in-process implementation registered by the execution layer \
itself, not by an integration package. There is no backend behind them to diverge, and the \
checker fails if one ever appears.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "no-engine-matrix"
keys = ["audit"]
reason = """
The audit port is implemented once, in forze_kits, over whichever document store the app \
already wired: an audit row is a document, so its storage-level behaviour is the document \
plane's, which the isolation plane compares. The checker verifies the claim: any integration \
package registering the key fails here.\
"""

[[tool.conformance_manifest.exempt_groups]]
kind = "no-engine-matrix"
keys = ["document_command_hook"]
reason = """
A hook around one document's command port, registered by the plane that owns the document \
(forze_identity.authz for the policy principal) and applied to whichever backend's port the \
document resolves to. No backend implements it, so there is no engine axis; the checker fails \
if an integration package ever registers the key.\
"""

[tool.conformance_manifest.exemptions."crypto.required_reach"]
kind = "config-value"
reason = """
A declared EncryptionReach value read by outbox and transport wiring rather than a port with \
behaviour, so there is nothing for a conformance leg to observe.\
"""

# Mypy configuration

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
warn_return_any = false
warn_unused_ignores = false

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["aiokafka.*", "grpc.*", "zstandard"]
ignore_missing_imports = true


[[tool.mypy.overrides]]

module = ["yandexcloud", "yandexcloud.*", "yandex.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true
implicit_reexport = true

# ....................... #
# Mock-server catalog gate
#
# Every operation in the driving example's catalog must resolve, and must answer against
# seeded data. A plane the seeder cannot fill therefore fails CI instead of shipping green.
# The exemptions below are operations that cannot be driven blind — not planes that are
# unsupported — and the table is checked BOTH ways: an exemption whose operation starts
# passing must be deleted, so it can only ever shrink.

[tool.mock_gate]
app = "examples.recipes.mock_workspace.served:mock_app"

[[tool.mock_gate.exempt]]
op = "attachments.complete_upload"
reason = "needs a live multipart session id; a seed has no way to leave one open"

[[tool.mock_gate.exempt]]
op = "attachments.list_parts"
reason = "needs a live multipart session id; a seed has no way to leave one open"

[[tool.mock_gate.exempt]]
op = "attachments.download"
reason = "the catalog carries no input type for this operation, so a blind sweep has nothing to author"

[[tool.mock_gate.exempt]]
op = "attachments.head"
reason = "the catalog carries no input type for this operation, so a blind sweep has nothing to author"

[[tool.mock_gate.exempt]]
op = "attachments.download_stream"
reason = "the catalog carries no input type for this operation, so a blind sweep has nothing to author"

[[tool.mock_gate.exempt]]
op = "attachments.download_range"
reason = "a byte range only means something against a known object length; the sweep has no size to range over"

[[tool.mock_gate.exempt]]
op = "projects.agg_list"
reason = "an aggregate request names functions and fields the caller chooses; a blind sweep cannot author one"

[[tool.mock_gate.exempt]]
op = "tasks.agg_list"
reason = "an aggregate request names functions and fields the caller chooses; a blind sweep cannot author one"

    "E402", # module-import-not-at-top: deferred/guarded imports are an established pattern here
    "E501", # line length is owned by `ruff format` (code is wrapped at 100); the remaining long
    # lines are unwrappable prose — single-token Sphinx :class: refs, minified embedded
    # HTML/JS assets, and `type: ignore`/`nosec` justification comments
    "ISC001",   # single-line implicit concat: conflicts with `ruff format`
    "ASYNC109", # ports/adapters deliberately expose `timeout` parameters as API surface
    "RUF001",   # ambiguous unicode: docs deliberately use typographic/math notation (×, −, ∪, –)
    "RUF002",   # see RUF001
    "RUF003",   # see RUF001
    "RUF022",   # __all__ is deliberately grouped by category (mirrors lazy-export tables), not sorted
    "UP040",    # PEP 695 type aliases/generics: migration is a separate arc — the framework does
    "UP046",    # heavy runtime type introspection (codecs/specs) and mechanical conversion of
    "UP047",    # ~80 generic declarations is not behavior-neutral enough to adopt via lint fixes

# expresses version *requirements*, not the build you run). The exact runtime pin
# lives in backend/.python-version and mise.toml. Tying this to the latest patch
# made a trailing .python-version — whose pyenv/docker datasource lags the CPython

    "aiogram>=3.31.0",

    "pydantic[email,timezone]>=2.13.5",
    "python-calamine>=0.8.2",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.4",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.32",

# .github/workflows/ci.yml; bump all five together.
required-version = "==0.12.24"
# Ignore releases younger than this when resolving, mirroring Renovate's
# `minimumReleaseAge` in renovate.jsonc. Renovate applies the cooldown when it
# *picks* a target version, but when it then calls uv to relock a bumped `>=`
# floor, uv would otherwise resolve to the newest release available — which may
# still be inside the cooldown — and Renovate rejects the lockfile as a pending
# version (the `renovate/artifacts` failure seen on PR #310). Matching the two
# keeps uv's own resolution inside the same window. Keep this in sync with
# renovate.jsonc `minimumReleaseAge`.
exclude-newer = "7 days"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Change both to session-scope so one loop is used for the whole run
asyncio_default_test_loop_scope = "session"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"
addopts = ["--strict-markers"]
# Any warning fails the run, so a new deprecation surfaces when it is introduced
# instead of hiding in a summary. A third-party warning that cannot be fixed here
# gets a narrow `ignore::` entry below, with a comment saying why.
filterwarnings = ["error"]
markers = [
    "integration: tests that use real infrastructure such as PostgreSQL or Redis containers",
    "unit: fast, pure tests with no infrastructure (no DB, Redis, or DI container)",
]
testpaths = ["tests"]

# Type checking (run via `just backend-typecheck`). Configured here rather than
# in a ty.toml because it is short enough not to earn its own file — ruff is the
# exception, in backend/ruff.toml, because its config is mostly prose. The
# convention is in AGENTS.md "Staying in sync".
#
# The paths live here rather than on the command line so the justfile,
# .pre-commit-config.yaml and CI cannot drift apart: `ty check` with no
# arguments means the same thing everywhere.
#
# `tests` is in scope so type checking catches doubles that drift from the ports
# they stand in for. Suppressions there use `# ty: ignore[<rule>]` and state why:
# mypy's bracketed `# type: ignore[code]` suppresses nothing in ty, which skips a
# code without a `ty:` prefix by design so several checkers can share one comment
# (https://docs.astral.sh/ty/suppression/).
[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src/fanfan", "tests", "scripts"]

# Opt-in rules, from ty's own "stricter than mypy/pyright --strict" recipe
# (https://docs.astral.sh/ty/coming-from-mypy-or-pyright/). Everything listed
# here costs nothing today — the codebase satisfies all of it — so each entry is
# a ratchet against future drift rather than a debt to pay down.
#
# `blanket-ignore-comment` is the load-bearing one: it rejects a bare
# `# ty: ignore` with no rule code, the escape hatch that silences a whole line
# instead of one diagnostic. Ruff already refuses the other three (PGH003 for a
# bare `# type: ignore`, PGH004 for a bare `# noqa`, RUF100 for one that no
# longer suppresses anything); this closes the one ruff cannot see.
#
# Note `terminal.error-on-warning` defaults to true, so "warn" would fail CI
# exactly as "error" does — these say "error" so the config means what it reads.
[tool.ty.rules]
blanket-ignore-comment = "error"
division-by-zero = "error"
dynamic-function-decorator-return = "error"
missing-type-argument = "error"
possibly-missing-attribute = "error"
possibly-missing-import = "error"
possibly-unresolved-reference = "error"
unsound-return-statement = "error"
unsound-yield = "error"
unsupported-dynamic-base = "error"

[tool.ty.analysis]
# Narrow conservatively: `==` between disjoint types is a bug, not a False, and a
# generic's type argument is checked rather than assumed compatible.
strict-equality-semantics = true
strict-generic-narrowing = true

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["fanfan"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true

# Dead-code sweep — a manual aid, NOT a CI gate (run via `just backend-deadcode`).
# Vulture finds globally-unused code that ruff's local rules (F401/F841) can't,
# but the framework-driven half of this app looks "unused" to a static pass:
# DI providers, route handlers and DTO fields are all invoked by reflection or
# by the framework, never by a call site vulture can see. So this config quiets
# the known-safe patterns and the remaining findings are for a human to judge —
# see docs/backend.md "Dead-code sweep". Anything vulture is wrong about that a
# decorator/name rule can't express goes in vulture_whitelist.py.
[tool.vulture]
paths = ["src/fanfan", "vulture_whitelist.py"]
# 60 surfaces unused attributes too but drowns in DTO/ORM-field false positives;
# 80 keeps imports, functions, classes and variables — the actionable slice.
min_confidence = 80
exclude = [
    # Alembic-owned: env.py hook signatures (include_object's `obj`, the
    # process_revision_directives args) and autogenerated revision files are
    # framework contracts, not dead code.
    "src/fanfan/adapters/db/migrations/",
]
ignore_decorators = [
    # FastAPI/FastStream routers — handlers are dispatched by the framework.
    # Every router in this app is named `*_router` (see presentation/web,
    # presentation/faststream); .get/.post/.subscriber/… all match.
    "@*_router.*",
    # Dishka DI — providers are resolved by the container, not called directly.
    "@provide",
    "@inject",
    # Click CLI entrypoints.
    "@click.*",
    "@async_command",
    # Pydantic hooks fired during (de)serialisation.
    "@field_validator",
    "@model_validator",
    # SQLAlchemy declarative helper.
    "@declared_attr",
    "@declared_attr.*",
]

[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-name = "fanfan"

# Architectural boundary enforcement (run via `just backend-import-lint`).
# Keeps the Clean/Hexagonal layering from docs/backend.md honest: inner layers

root_package = "fanfan"

name = "core stays pure (no outward imports)"

source_modules = ["fanfan.application"]

[importlinter]

    cobol_asg
    cobol_memory

# The reason cobol_asg is a sibling of interpreter rather than a subpackage of
# it: an import of interpreter.anything runs interpreter/__init__.py, which
# loads the VM. A consumer that only reads COBOL -- cobble's knowledge-graph
# extractor -- imports cobol_asg and nothing else, so this contract is what
# keeps that promise true. cobol_asg parses; interpreter.cobol lowers.
# cobol_memory holds storage algebra rather than ASG nodes, and it is a sibling
# for the same reason -- a consumer that only computes byte ranges must not
# load the VM.
[importlinter:contract:cobol-asg-is-a-leaf]

type = forbidden
source_modules =

forbidden_modules =
    interpreter

[importlinter:contract:cobol-memory-is-a-leaf]
name = The byte-extent algebra must not import the interpreter
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    cobol_memory
forbidden_modules =
    interpreter

[importlinter:contract:cobol-numeric-is-a-leaf]
name = The COBOL numeric boundary must not import the interpreter
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    cobol_numeric
forbidden_modules =
    interpreter

[importlinter:contract:vm-no-frontend]
name = VM must not import frontend lowering code
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    interpreter.vm
    interpreter.handlers
forbidden_modules =
    interpreter.frontends
ignore_imports =
    interpreter.vm.executor -> interpreter.frontends.symbol_table

[importlinter:contract:ir-is-leaf]
name = IR module must not import other interpreter modules
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    interpreter.ir
forbidden_modules =
    interpreter.vm
    interpreter.handlers
    interpreter.cfg
    interpreter.frontends
    interpreter.run
    interpreter.llm

[importlinter:contract:project-no-vm-internals]
name = Project module must not import VM internals
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    interpreter.project
forbidden_modules =
    interpreter.vm
    interpreter.handlers

[importlinter:contract:frontend-independence]
name = Language frontends must not import each other
type = independence
modules =
    interpreter.frontends.python
    interpreter.frontends.java
    interpreter.frontends.go
    interpreter.frontends.rust
    interpreter.frontends.csharp
    interpreter.frontends.kotlin
    interpreter.frontends.scala
    interpreter.frontends.ruby
    interpreter.frontends.php
    interpreter.frontends.lua
    interpreter.frontends.pascal
ignore_imports =
    interpreter.frontends.cpp.frontend -> interpreter.frontends.c.frontend
    interpreter.frontends.cpp.expressions -> interpreter.frontends.c.expressions
    interpreter.frontends.cpp.expressions -> interpreter.frontends.c.declarations
    interpreter.frontends.cpp.control_flow -> interpreter.frontends.c.declarations
    interpreter.frontends.cpp.declarations -> interpreter.frontends.c.declarations
    interpreter.frontends.c.declarations -> interpreter.frontends.cpp.node_types
    interpreter.frontends.c.declarations -> interpreter.frontends.cpp.control_flow

[importlinter:contract:cobol-isolation]
name = COBOL module only imported by frontend factory
type = forbidden
source_modules =
    interpreter.vm
    interpreter.handlers
    interpreter.project
    interpreter.run
forbidden_modules =
    interpreter.cobol
# Three exceptions used to live here -- interpreter.frontend reaching for
# cobol_parser and subprocess_runner, and project.cobol_compile for ast_store.
# They existed only because parsing and lowering shared interpreter.cobol; the
# parsing half is cobol_asg now, which this contract does not police.

classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",

    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Atmospheric Science",

# Depends ONLY on the substrate (legoesm-core) — NOT on the other Earth-system
# components, NOR on the coupler/driver/training above it.  Both invariants are
# machine-enforced by the import-linter contracts ("Earth-system components are
# independent of each other" + "Components must not import the coupler, driver,
# or training"), which is what lets `pip install legoesm-atmosphere` run standalone.

    "jaxlib>=0.5.3",

# ml), so the component stays standalone; this extra declares the install path
# for the SFNO/U-Cast neural dynamical cores + ML physics parameterization, which
# import the neural primitives at top level:

legoesm-ml = { workspace = true }

# This component PROVIDES the FV3 shallow-water barotropic dycores that the ocean
# component's barotropic solver resolves BY NAME through
# legoesm.registry.SW_BAROTROPIC_REGISTRY (importlib.metadata entry points — NOT a
# static import).  Declaring them here means installing legoesm-atmosphere makes
