[tool.setuptools]
py-modules = []

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["application*", "domain*", "infrastructure*", "interfaces*", "pipeline*"]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# deptry : détection de dépendances manquantes / inutiles / transitives
# Lit [project.dependencies] (PEP 621) et [dependency-groups] (PEP 735).
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.deptry]
known_first_party = ["application", "domain", "infrastructure", "interfaces", "pipeline"]
# `scripts/` outille le dépôt sans être distribué : ses imports relèvent de l'environnement de
# développement, pas des dépendances de l'application. `data/` est un répertoire de travail local,
# hors du dépôt. L'estimation des poids du modèle des groupes d'auteurs tourne sur le poste de
# développement : elle importe Splink, DuckDB et pyarrow, dépendances de développement.
extend_exclude = [
    "frontend",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "scripts",
    "data",
    "interfaces/cli/dev/estimate_residual_weights.py",
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# import-linter : vérifie les règles de dépendance entre couches DDD.
# Lancement : `lint-imports`
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["domain", "application", "infrastructure", "interfaces", "pipeline"]
# Nécessaire aux contrats qui ciblent des modules externes.
include_external_packages = true
# Type de contrat maison, défini dans `scripts/contrats_import.py`.
contract_types = ["purete_du_noyau: scripts.contrats_import.PureteDuNoyau"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Couches DDD (layered)"
type = "layers"
layers = ["interfaces", "infrastructure | application", "domain"]
# `application` n'importe pas `infrastructure` : toute nouvelle
# dépendance doit passer par un port.
#
# Exception : `application.ports.*` est zone neutre. `infrastructure`
# peut en importer les dataclasses de transport pour typer ses
# signatures. Les Protocols restent implémentés via duck typing.
ignore_imports = [
    "infrastructure.** -> application.ports.**",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Pipeline : hors des couches hexagonales"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["pipeline"]
forbidden_modules = ["application", "interfaces"]
# Le pipeline importe `domain/` et les modules techniques d'`infrastructure/` (connexion,
# réglages, journalisation, fragments SQL), jamais `application/` ni `interfaces/`.
# Exception : `infrastructure/` importe `application.ports` (voir le contrat des couches).
ignore_imports = [
    "infrastructure.** -> application.ports.**",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Pipeline : importé par interfaces seulement"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["domain", "application", "infrastructure"]
forbidden_modules = ["pipeline"]
# L'API et les scripts en ligne de commande (`interfaces/`) sont les seuls clients du pipeline.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Routers : pas d'import direct de infrastructure"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["interfaces.api.routers"]
forbidden_modules = ["infrastructure"]
# Les routers FastAPI pilotent des use-cases applicatifs et reçoivent
# leurs dépendances via `Depends(...)` (factories dans
# `interfaces.api.deps`, composition root). La construction des
# adapters et l'accès direct à l'infra (queries, repos, pool, engine)
# y sont interdits. Cf. docs/architecture/01-vue-d-ensemble.md.
#
# Imports transitifs autorisés : `routers → deps → infrastructure` est
# le chemin attendu (composition root), donc on n'interdit que les
# imports directs.
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Composition root : Pg* concrets uniquement dans app et deps"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["interfaces.api"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "infrastructure.repositories",
    "infrastructure.read_models",
]
# Verrouillage d'une règle de docs/architecture/01-vue-d-ensemble.md :
# seul `interfaces/api/deps.py` instancie les `Pg*` concrets ; les routers et autres modules
# sous `interfaces.api/` passent par un port via `Depends(...)`. L'interface publique du
# pipeline relève de son propre contrat.
ignore_imports = [
    "interfaces.api.deps -> infrastructure.repositories.**",
    "interfaces.api.deps -> infrastructure.read_models.**",
    "interfaces.api.** -> pipeline.public",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "API : le pipeline par son interface publique"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["interfaces.api"]
forbidden_modules = ["pipeline"]
# L'API importe seulement `pipeline/public.py`, qui exporte l'ordre des phases et les recalculs
# ciblés.
ignore_imports = ["interfaces.api.** -> pipeline.public"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Adapters : la connexion se reçoit, elle ne s'ouvre pas"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["infrastructure.read_models", "infrastructure.repositories"]
forbidden_modules = ["infrastructure.db.engine"]
# Un adapter travaille sur la connexion que son appelant lui remet : c'est elle qui porte la
# transaction de la requête, et les caractéristiques que la composition root y a posées — la
# lecture seule sur une méthode HTTP sans effet de bord. Atteindre l'engine ouvrirait une
# connexion en marge de cette règle, et l'écriture qu'un point d'entrée de lecture émettrait
# par ce chemin aboutirait.
#
# L'adapter dont la lecture se répartit sur plusieurs connexions — les facettes de
# publications, calculées en parallèle — reçoit une fabrique de connexions à sa construction,
# comme il reçoit sa connexion.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "API : aucune requête réseau sortante"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["interfaces.api"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "httpx2",
    "httpx",
    "socket",
    "http",
    "requests",
    "aiohttp",
    "urllib3",
    "ftplib",
    "smtplib",
    "poplib",
    "imaplib",
    "telnetlib",
    "socketserver",
]
# L'API n'émet aucun appel sortant : elle lit et écrit dans PostgreSQL, et rien d'autre. Tout
# le trafic sortant appartient au pipeline, exécuté hors du cycle web. Ce contrat en fait une
# garantie mécanique plutôt qu'un constat : aucun module servant une requête HTTP ne peut
# atteindre un client réseau, fût-ce par un import indirect (les chaînes sont vérifiées, pas
# seulement les imports directs).
#
# `httpx2` est le client HTTP unique du projet, et `httpx` l'autre nom de publication de la même bibliothèque : les deux sont fermés.
# `socket` ferme la porte à un repli sur la
# primitive de la bibliothèque standard, et `socketserver` à l'ouverture d'un service à
# l'écoute. Les autres noms couvrent les clients tiers et les protocoles que la bibliothèque
# standard sert : courrier, transfert de fichiers, terminal distant.
#
# `urllib.request` échappe seul à ce contrat : l'outil ne sait pas viser le sous-module d'un
# paquet qu'il tient pour externe, et interdire `urllib` entier écarterait `urllib.parse`, dont
# le domaine se sert pour manipuler des URL sans rien émettre. Il se ferme par la règle
# `banned-api` d'`interfaces/api/ruff.toml`.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "API : aucun lancement de programme"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["interfaces.api"]
forbidden_modules = ["subprocess", "multiprocessing", "pty"]
# Le code servant les requêtes HTTP ne lance aucun programme externe.
# L'analyse statique signale les appels de lancement partout dans le dépôt, mais elle
# ne voit qu'un appel écrit dans un fichier : ce contrat établit qu'aucun module atteignable
# depuis la couche API ne joint un lanceur, fût-ce par une chaîne d'imports.
#
# `subprocess` est le module de lancement de la bibliothèque standard ; `multiprocessing` et
# `pty` en lancent aussi, et échappent à l'analyse statique. `os.posix_spawn` reste hors de
# portée des deux outils : l'un ne connaît pas cet appel, l'autre ne sait pas viser l'attribut
# d'un module, et interdire `os` entier écarterait tout le reste de son usage.

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain : rien hors bibliothèque standard"
type = "purete_du_noyau"
paquet = "domain"
# `_typeshed` est fourni par les vérificateurs de types et n'existe pas à l'exécution.
autorises = ["_typeshed"]
# Le domaine ne dépend de rien : pas d'ORM, pas de validation Pydantic, pas de framework web,
# pas de driver de base. Les modèles d'entrée-sortie JSONB vivent dans
# `infrastructure/jsonb_models/`.

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# Paquets que rien n'importe, et qui restent des dépendances de production.
# - python-dotenv : pydantic-settings l'appelle en interne dès qu'on utilise
#   `env_file=...`.
# - uvicorn : serveur ASGI lancé en ligne de commande (`CMD uvicorn ...` du
#   Dockerfile, `start.sh`, systemd ou pm2 hors Docker). C'est lui qui importe
#   l'application, jamais l'inverse — deptry ne lit que les imports.
DEP002 = ["python-dotenv", "uvicorn"]

# Paquets de développement qu'un module de production importe sous `try`.
# - tqdm : les barres de progression ne s'affichent qu'en terminal. Son absence conduit au
#   même repli que l'absence de terminal, celui des runs en conteneur.
DEP004 = ["tqdm"]

# Alias paquet distribué → nom de module importé (les noms peuvent différer).
[tool.deptry.package_module_name_map]
pydantic-settings = "pydantic_settings"
pyahocorasick = "ahocorasick"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ruff : linter + formateur (remplace flake8, isort, pyupgrade, black)
# Mode permissif au début — voir `ruff check .` et `ruff format --check .`
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = [
    # Les extraits de code de la documentation illustrent un propos : ils ne sont pas du code
    # à maintenir, et les fiches archivées sont un compte rendu qu'on ne réécrit pas.
    "*.md",
    ".claude",                   # hooks du harnais de développement, hors code applicatif
    "data",                      # répertoire de travail local, hors du dépôt
    "interfaces/frontend",
    "bibliometrie_uca.egg-info",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Règles activées — on démarre permissif, à durcir au fil du temps.
select = [
    "E",     # pycodestyle errors
    "W",     # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",     # pyflakes (undefined names, unused imports, etc.)
    "I",     # isort (ordre des imports)
    "UP",    # pyupgrade (syntaxe obsolète)
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear (pièges courants)
    "C901",  # complexité cyclomatique
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async : I/O bloquantes dans une async def, etc.
    "S",     # flake8-bandit : 73 règles de sécurité (cf. per-file-ignores pour les exceptions)
    "A",     # flake8-builtins : un nom qui masque une fonction de base
    "C4",    # flake8-comprehensions : compréhensions et appels de collection superflus
    "DTZ",   # flake8-datetimez : instants sans fuseau (cf. `domain.dates.today`)
    "G",     # flake8-logging-format : message de journalisation formaté à l'émission
    "ISC",   # flake8-implicit-str-concat : concaténation implicite de littéraux
    "LOG",   # flake8-logging : usage du module de journalisation
    "PERF",  # Perflint : boucles réécrivables en compréhension
    "PIE",   # flake8-pie : tournures inutiles
    "Q",     # flake8-quotes : cohérence des guillemets
    "RET",   # flake8-return : chemins de retour superflus
    "TID",   # flake8-tidy-imports : imports relatifs remontants
]
# RUF029 (async def sans await) serait utile mais reste en preview chez
# ruff à ce jour : l'activer exigerait `preview = true` qui allume
# d'autres règles preview non évaluées. À ajouter quand elle stabilise.
# Ignorés le temps d'assainir progressivement
ignore = [
    "E501", # ligne trop longue — à durcir plus tard
    "E402", # module-level import not at top — quelques cas légitimes
    "B008", # function call in default argument — FastAPI Depends() idiomatique
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Seuil à 15 après décomposition de publications_facets (25 → <10),
# _build_list_conditions (17 → <15), refresh_from_sources (24 → <15),
# export_publications_csv (23 → <15). Prochaine cible : 10.
max-complexity = 15

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
# `httpx2` est le client HTTP unique du projet. `urllib.request` ouvrirait un second chemin
# sortant, hors des délais d'expiration, des tentatives bornées et du disjoncteur qui
# encadrent le premier — et hors de la liste blanche d'hôtes qu'un test confronte au code.
#
# L'interdiction vaut pour tout le dépôt plutôt que pour la seule couche API : le contrat
# d'architecture qui ferme les autres modules réseau à cette couche ne sait pas nommer le
# sous-module d'un paquet qu'il tient pour externe. Fermer la source obtient la même
# transitivité, sans avoir à suivre les chemins.
"urllib.request".msg = "Le client HTTP du projet est httpx2, et le trafic sortant appartient au pipeline (pipeline/ingestion)."

# Le projet n'a qu'un engine, construit par `infrastructure/db/engine.py`, seul endroit d'où
# une connexion peut naître. C'est lui qui choisit l'identité de connexion selon le processus
# et qui installe le suivi du DML ; un second engine fabriqué ailleurs porterait ni l'une ni
# l'autre, et ouvrirait des connexions hors des caractéristiques que la composition root de
# l'API pose sur les siennes — la lecture seule d'une requête de lecture, en particulier.
#
# L'interdiction porte sur tout le dépôt, les exceptions se lisant dans `per-file-ignores` :
# le constructeur lui-même, et les tests, qui montent leur propre engine sur la base de test.
"sqlalchemy.create_engine".msg = "L'engine du projet se construit dans infrastructure/db/engine.py, et s'obtient par get_sync_engine."

# Le type JSONB de SQLAlchemy écrit `None` en JSON `null` plutôt qu'en NULL SQL. Les deux se
# relisent en `None` côté Python, mais SQL les distingue : une colonne qui mélange les deux
# formes échappe aux contraintes et aux index qui raisonnent sur NULL. `infrastructure/db/jsonb.py`
# en pose la variante du projet, seule autorisée, et l'interdiction empêche l'autre de revenir.
"sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.JSONB".msg = "Le type JSONB du projet est Jsonb, dans infrastructure/db/jsonb.py : il écrit None en NULL SQL."

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
# Les couches du projet, déclarées pour que leur classement en premier rang ne dépende
# pas de l'inférence de ruff, qui varie d'une version à l'autre.
known-first-party = ["application", "domain", "infrastructure", "interfaces", "pipeline"]
# Regroupe les imports d'un même module en un seul bloc, alias inclus
# (sinon chaque `from x import (a as b)` aliasé occupe son propre bloc).
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# `S101` : une assertion est le propos d'un test. `S105`/`S106` : les fixtures posent des
# identifiants factices, nommés pour ce qu'ils sont. `S608` : les tests composent du SQL de
# jeu de données.
# `TID251` : les tests montent leur propre engine sur la base de test.
"tests/*" = ["E402", "S101", "S105", "S106", "S108", "S324", "S608", "TID251"]
# Les sites légitimes de ce qui est interdit ailleurs : le constructeur de l'engine, et le
# module qui pose le type JSONB du projet.
"infrastructure/db/engine.py" = ["TID251"]
"infrastructure/db/jsonb.py" = ["TID251"]
# `S608` signale toute interpolation dans une chaîne SQL. Ces couches ont pour métier de
# composer des requêtes à partir de fragments pris dans des listes blanches écrites en dur
# (tris, dimensions, colonnes) ; les valeurs issues d'une requête HTTP, elles, passent
# toujours par des paramètres liés. La règle reste active partout ailleurs — un SQL composé
# à la main dans `interfaces/api` ou `application` doit se signaler.
"infrastructure/read_models/*" = ["S608"]
"pipeline/*" = ["S101", "S608"]
"infrastructure/repositories/*" = ["S608"]
"infrastructure/sql_fragments.py" = ["S608"]
"alembic/versions/*" = ["S608"]
# Scripts de développement : `dump_schema` lance `pg_dump`, dont il compose lui-même les
# arguments.
"interfaces/cli/dev/*" = ["S603", "S607"]
# Génération d'illustrations : la disposition d'un graphe tire au sort des positions.
"docs/img/graphs/*" = ["S311"]
# `S101` vise l'assertion qui porte une décision de sécurité, effacée par l'interpréteur en
# mode optimisé. Ces couches et le pipeline s'en servent pour des invariants internes — cohérence d'un
# registre au chargement, resserrement d'un type — sans qu'aucune autorisation en dépende.
# La règle reste active sur `interfaces/` et `application/services/`, où une décision
# d'autorisation pourrait naître.
"domain/*" = ["S101"]
"infrastructure/*" = ["S101"]
"application/pipeline/normalize/normalize_hal.py" = ["S101"]
# Scripts en ligne de commande et orchestrateur du pipeline : imports tardifs, et SQL
# composé à partir de fragments écrits en dur.
"interfaces/cli/*" = ["E402", "S608"]
"application/pipeline/*" = ["S101"]
"interfaces/api/routers/*" = ["E402"] # imports tardifs fréquents

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pytest + coverage
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Mode d'import `importlib` : le nom de module dérive du chemin complet,
# ce qui autorise des fichiers de test homonymes dans des répertoires
# distincts sans exiger un `__init__.py` dans chacun.
addopts = "-q --import-mode=importlib"
# pytest-asyncio mode auto — les fonctions `async def test_*` sont
# reconnues automatiquement sans décorateur. Loop scope par fonction
# (défaut) : chaque test async a sa propre boucle.
asyncio_mode = "auto"

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["application", "domain", "infrastructure", "interfaces", "pipeline"]
omit = [
    "tests/*",
    "*/__init__.py",
    # Backfills jetables : écrits pour une exécution, lancés à la main, puis conservés
    # comme trace de ce qui a été fait. Les autres scripts en ligne de commande — imports
    # de fichiers, maintenance, outils de développement — restent mesurés : ils écrivent
    # en base et se rejouent.
    "interfaces/cli/oneshot/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
skip_empty = true
show_missing = true
# Seuil progressif : ne jamais régresser. À faire remonter au fur et à
# mesure qu'on ajoute des tests.
fail_under = 90
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mypy : type checker
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.mypy]
# Version des images de production (cf. `scripts/versions-des-images.sh`) : le typage se
# vérifie sur la sémantique de l'interpréteur qui exécute, non sur un plancher de compatibilité.
python_version = "3.14"
# Système des images de production, pour la même raison. Sans cette ligne, mypy analyse pour la
# plateforme qui le lance : depuis un poste Windows, il rejette les appels POSIX que le code
# exécute en production (`signal.SIGKILL`).
platform = "linux"
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
# Imports : ignorer les libs tierces non typées plutôt que de polluer
ignore_missing_imports = true
# Mode strict : toutes les fonctions doivent être annotées, et leur corps
# est vérifié.
check_untyped_defs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
# `Any` explicite interdit. Les exceptions se lisent dans les overrides plus bas, où chacune
# porte son motif en regard du module.
disallow_any_explicit = true
disallow_any_generics = true
# Une fonction ne rend pas un `Any` sous une déclaration qui promet autre chose : le contrôle
# se fait à l'endroit où la valeur entre, non chez l'appelant qui la croira acquise.
warn_return_any = true
# Afficher les codes d'erreur pour pouvoir ignorer précisément au besoin
show_error_codes = true
# Un paramètre qui accepte `None` le déclare : `x: str | None = None`, jamais `x: str = None`.
implicit_optional = false
# Ignorer les erreurs dans les tests (focus sur le code de prod)
exclude = [
    "^tests/",
    "^frontend/",
    "^bibliometrie_uca\\.egg-info/",
    "^\\.venv/",
    "^build/",
    # Code Alembic : `op` et `context` sont ajoutés dynamiquement au
    # module `alembic` à l'import, mypy ne les détecte pas. Cohérent
    # avec l'exclusion `tests/` : code framework, pas du métier.
    "^alembic/",
    # Copie de travail de mutmut : double les paquets du projet.
    "^mutants/",
    # Répertoire de travail local : données brutes et scripts jetables, hors du dépôt.
    "^data/",
    # Scripts jetables (audits, rattrapages), exécutés une fois.
    "^interfaces/cli/oneshot/",
]

# Désactivation d'`explicit-any`, tenue au plus juste : une entrée qui ne couvre plus aucune
# erreur est retirée, et le motif se lit en regard du module.
#
# Un JSON de forme libre ne se décrit pas par l'alias récursif `JsonValue` : le schéma OpenAPI
# qui en découlerait produit un type TypeScript circulaire, que le compilateur refuse, et
# `schema.ts` dérive du contrat.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "application.ports.read_models.config_queries",        # `value` : JSON de forme libre
    "application.ports.read_models.pipeline_runs_queries", # `details` : JSON de forme libre
    "interfaces.api.models.config",                        # `value` : JSON de forme libre
    "infrastructure.read_models.publications.facets",      # facette appelée par son nom (`getattr`)
]
disallow_any_explicit = false

# Les deux réglages tiennent ensemble : `init_typed` type le constructeur synthétisé,
# `init_forbid_extra` lui retire son `**kwargs: Any`. Sans l'un des deux, ce `Any` est écrit
# dans chaque classe de modèle et génère des erreurs `explicit-any`.
[tool.pydantic-mypy]
init_forbid_extra = true
init_typed = true

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pyrefly : second vérificateur de types, lancé à la demande.
# Lancement : `uv run --with pyrefly pyrefly check`
#
# Mypy reste la référence, seul branché au pre-commit et à l'intégration.
# Celui-ci sert à comparer les deux lectures du même code : il voit des
# choses que l'autre laisse passer, et l'inverse.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.pyrefly]
python-version = "3.14.0"
# Système des images de production, comme pour mypy : depuis un autre système, les appels POSIX
# que le code exécute en production seraient rejetés.
python-platform = "linux"
# Le code des tests, du frontend, d'Alembic et du répertoire de travail local reste hors du champ,
# comme pour mypy.
project-excludes = [
    "**/tests/",
    "**/frontend/",
    "**/bibliometrie_uca.egg-info/",
    "**/.venv/",
    "**/build/",
    "**/alembic/",
    "**/data/",
]
# Libs tierces non typées : ignorées plutôt que déclarées une à une.
ignore-missing-imports = ["*"]

[tool.pyrefly.errors]
# Les deux règles qui portent la discipline déclarée à mypy : `Any` explicite interdit,
# et pas de valeur `Any` rendue sous une déclaration qui promet autre chose.
explicit-any = "error"
no-any-return = "error"

# Modules exemptés d'`explicit-any`, les mêmes qu'à mypy et pour les mêmes motifs.
[[tool.pyrefly.sub-config]]
matches = "application/ports/read_models/config_queries.py"
[tool.pyrefly.sub-config.errors]
explicit-any = false

[[tool.pyrefly.sub-config]]
matches = "application/ports/read_models/pipeline_runs_queries.py"
[tool.pyrefly.sub-config.errors]
explicit-any = false

[[tool.pyrefly.sub-config]]
matches = "interfaces/api/models/config.py"
[tool.pyrefly.sub-config.errors]
explicit-any = false


[[tool.pyrefly.sub-config]]
matches = "infrastructure/read_models/publications/facets.py"
[tool.pyrefly.sub-config.errors]
explicit-any = false

# L'appariement d'une ligne de relevé avec le type qu'elle alimente se fait par dépaquetage de
# clés qu'aucune analyse statique ne connaît, le relevé étant une chaîne de caractères. Le module
# porte ce contrôle à l'exécution, et les tests d'intégration l'exercent sur chaque relevé.
[[tool.pyrefly.sub-config]]
matches = "infrastructure/db/rows.py"
[tool.pyrefly.sub-config.errors]
bad-unpacking = false

# `Scope`, le type que Starlette donne au contexte d'une requête ASGI, est un alias de
# `MutableMapping[str, Any]`. Pyrefly compte l'alias importé comme un `Any` écrit ; le nommer
# autrement reviendrait à renoncer au type de l'interface qu'on implémente.
[[tool.pyrefly.sub-config]]
matches = "interfaces/api/route_path.py"
[tool.pyrefly.sub-config.errors]
explicit-any = false

[[tool.pyrefly.sub-config]]
matches = "interfaces/api/spa.py"
[tool.pyrefly.sub-config.errors]
explicit-any = false

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# mutmut : tests de mutation du domaine.
# Lancement, à la demande : `uv run --with mutmut mutmut run`, puis
# `mutmut results` pour la liste et `mutmut show <mutant>` pour le diff.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.mutmut]
# Seule couche mutée : ses règles sont pures, et une règle fausse ne s'y voit
# qu'au résultat. Les tests unitaires y répondent sans base de données.
source_paths = ["domain"]

# Toute la suite unitaire répond, pas seulement `tests/unit/domain` : les tests
# d'une règle du domaine vivent parfois sous la couche qui l'appelle.
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = ["tests/unit"]

# mutmut copie le code muté dans `mutants/` et y lance les tests. Ce qu'ils lisent
# hors de la couche mutée s'y copie tel quel : modules importés et fichiers du
# repository que les tests de conformité relisent.
also_copy = [
    "application",
    "infrastructure",
    "interfaces/api",
    "interfaces/cli",
    "interfaces/frontend/src/lib",
    "interfaces/frontend/Dockerfile",
    "scripts",
    ".github",
    "Dockerfile",
    "docker-compose.prod.yml",
    "docker-compose.yml",
    "pyproject.toml",
    "start.sh",
]

[project]

description = "A Graph Neural Network that learns to play chess via PPO self-play."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = { file = "LICENSE" }
authors = [{ name = "Lucas Tabary" }]
keywords = ["chess", "graph-neural-network", "reinforcement-learning", "ppo", "pytorch-geometric"]

dependencies = [
    "chess>=1.11",
    "torch>=2.4,<2.5",
    "torch-geometric>=2.5",
    "numpy>=1.24",
    "pygame>=2.6",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.1",
    "tensorboard>=2.12",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "ruff==0.16.5",  # same pins as requirements-dev.txt
    "mypy==2.3.1",
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5",
    "import-linter>=2.1",
    "pre-commit>=3.7",
]
notebooks = [
    "jupyter>=1.0",
    "matplotlib>=3.7",
    "pandas>=2.0",
]

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/lucastabary/kAIsparov"

[project.scripts]
kaisparov = "kaisparov.cli:main"

# ---- Package discovery (src/ layout) ----
[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
include = ["kaisparov*"]

# ---- Version: read off the latest `vX.Y.Z` tag (1.0.1.devN+g<sha> between tags) ----
[tool.setuptools_scm]
fallback_version = "0.0.0"  # a source tree without git metadata

# ---- Ruff: linter + formatter ----
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 100
extend-exclude = ["notebooks"]  # exploratory notebooks aren't held to the lint bar

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM"]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line length is handled by the formatter
    "B008",  # function calls in argument defaults (torch idioms)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # re-exports

# ---- mypy: gradual typing (informational for now) ----
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.10"
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
check_untyped_defs = true
# game_interface (pygame UI) fights the pygame stubs; not worth typing strictly.
exclude = ["build/", "dist/", "game_interface.py"]

# ---- import-linter: the architecture rules of CLAUDE.md, checked (`lint-imports`) ----
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "kaisparov"
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "python-chess stays inside the engine (core/game, move, rules)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "kaisparov.agents", "kaisparov.analysis", "kaisparov.bench", "kaisparov.cli",
    "kaisparov.envs", "kaisparov.eval", "kaisparov.insights", "kaisparov.models",
    "kaisparov.play", "kaisparov.tracking", "kaisparov.train", "kaisparov.training",
    "kaisparov.core.bitboard_batch", "kaisparov.core.coords", "kaisparov.core.draw",
    "kaisparov.core.game_interface", "kaisparov.core.material", "kaisparov.core.notation",
    "kaisparov.core.pieces", "kaisparov.core.utils",
]
forbidden_modules = ["chess"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "the engine depends on nothing above it"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["kaisparov.core"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "kaisparov.agents", "kaisparov.analysis", "kaisparov.bench", "kaisparov.cli",
    "kaisparov.envs", "kaisparov.eval", "kaisparov.insights", "kaisparov.models",
    "kaisparov.play", "kaisparov.tracking", "kaisparov.train", "kaisparov.training",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "torch-free: the engine, the benchmark, the run registry"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["kaisparov.core", "kaisparov.bench", "kaisparov.tracking.registry"]
forbidden_modules = ["torch", "torch_geometric"]
# A `run:<id>` contestant loads its network on first use, inside a function: the

    "kaisparov.bench.contestants -> torch",
    "kaisparov.bench.contestants -> kaisparov.models.factory",
    "kaisparov.bench.contestants -> kaisparov.agents.minimax_agent",
    "kaisparov.bench.contestants -> kaisparov.agents.neural_agent",
    "kaisparov.bench.contestants -> kaisparov.agents.neural_analyzer",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "pygame only in the UI (play, core/game_interface)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "kaisparov.agents", "kaisparov.analysis", "kaisparov.bench", "kaisparov.cli",

[project.optional-dependencies]
# The embedder backend — ``sentence-transformers`` (and, transitively,
# ``torch``). Split out of ``paper`` (ADR 0020/0021) so the torch-free
# serve / worker images can omit it and reach the model over HTTP via
# ``RemoteEmbedder`` instead. The embedder *service* image installs this
# extra; single-process PyPI installs that want an in-process model get
# it via ``[all]`` or an explicit ``[embed]``.
#
# Without an embedder (no ``[embed]`` and no remote URL) the ``search()``
# verb on every embedder-backed kind crashes with -32603 even though
# tools/list advertises it (MCP critic CRITICAL). ``[all]`` includes
# ``embed`` so the single-process install keeps working.
embed = ["sentence-transformers>=3.0"]
# asa — the Discord bridge that runs Asa as a Claude Code agent backed by
# precis (folded in from the standalone asa-bot repo). A sibling package
# (`src/asa_bot`) + the `asa-bot` entry point, like `precis_web` + `precis
# web`. Deliberately NOT in `[all]`: asa is an operational daemon, not a
# precis capability, and its only extra deps are discord.py + aiohttp
# (psycopg + pyyaml are already core). asa keeps talking to `precis serve`
# over stdio at runtime — the merge shares the code, not the process
# boundary. Install target: `precis-mcp[asa]` on the asa host (melchior).
asa = ["discord.py>=2.4", "aiohttp>=3.9"]
# asa-slack — a Slack bridge to Asa, sibling to `asa` (`src/asa_slack` +
# the `asa-slack` entry point). Unlike the Discord bridge it doesn't hand-
# roll its own `claude -p` subprocess: it calls
# `precis.utils.llm.router.dispatch()` in-process (forced to the sonnet
# tier + a hard kind-allowlist), so its only extra deps are the Slack SDK
# itself — psycopg/pyyaml/precis-mcp's own claude wrappers are already
# core. Socket Mode (a persistent outbound WebSocket), so no HTTP/ingress
# deps needed. Install target: `precis-mcp[asa-slack]` on the same host
# `asa` runs on.
asa-slack = ["slack_bolt>=1.20", "slack_sdk>=3.27"]
# tts — local text-to-speech for the audio-export renderer (voice drafts +
# the morning brief). Kokoro (per-language native voices, Apache) via
# kokoro-onnx; soundfile for WAV I/O; numpy rides along. Heavy + host-specific
# (installed on the inference node with the model files), so it's opt-in and
# the engine import is lazy — non-tts builds never load it.
tts = ["kokoro-onnx>=0.4", "soundfile>=0.12"]
# Paper ingest — PDF → layout (marker-pdf) → chunks + metadata
# lookup (CrossRef / Semantic Scholar). The full pipeline lives in
# :mod:`precis.ingest` as of the v7 rewrite (was previously farmed out
# to ``acatome-extract``).
#
# ``marker-pdf`` is gated on ``sys_platform != 'win32'`` because
# Marker's surya / torch stack doesn't support Windows; on Windows
# the install resolves but PDF layout extraction will error out at
# call time with a clear ``ModuleNotFoundError: marker``.
#
# Dependabot #44/#45 (transformers <5.3.0 RCE) are FIXED as of 2026-07:
# ``marker-pdf`` 2.0.0 lifted its ``transformers<5.0.0`` cap, so
# ``transformers`` now resolves freely (currently 5.14.x) — no pin needed
# here anymore. Note ``anthropic``/``openai``/``google-genai`` also ride in
# transitively via marker-pdf (its own LLM-assisted-OCR fallback path) —
# precis never imports them directly (``router.dispatch`` talks to LLM
# backends over raw ``httpx``/``urllib``), so their versions float freely
# too.
#
# Pillow: marker-pdf caps Pillow<11; we override it to >=12.3.0 via
# [tool.uv] override-dependencies (see that table for why and when to drop).
paper = [
    "marker-pdf>=1.0; sys_platform != 'win32'",
    "pymupdf>=1.24.10",     # ``fitz`` — page-level PDF text + metadata.
                            # >=1.24.10 picks up the heap-corruption
                            # fixes shipped in the 1.24 maintenance
                            # series; agent-supplied PDFs reach
                            # fitz.open via the OA cascade so we keep
                            # the floor tight.
    "rapidfuzz>=3.0",       # title/author fuzzy match in verify_metadata
    "fonttools>=4.40",      # embedded-font outlines for glyph recovery
                            # (ingest/glyph_outline.py, gr228652); also
                            # pulled in by matplotlib.
    # NOTE: ``habanero`` and ``semanticscholar`` moved to the core
    # ``dependencies`` block (gr489310): gateway-served paths import them.
    # NOTE: ``tenacity`` moved to the core ``dependencies`` block — its
    # ``@retry`` decorators run at import of ``workers/fetch_oa`` (on the
    # always-on ``cli.main`` parser-build path), so gating it here broke
    # the torch-free ``serve-embeddings`` venv. See the core-deps note.
    # NOTE: ``pysbd`` moved to the core ``dependencies`` block — it is a
    # pure-Python ~50 KB rules engine imported at module top by
    # ``utils/sentences`` (verifier + chunker fallback), so gating it
    # behind ``[paper]`` made non-paper test collection ImportError.
    # NOTE: ``sentence-transformers`` is NOT here — it moved to the
    # ``embed`` extra (ADR 0021). Marker still pulls ``torch`` for surya,
    # so the ingest image is heavy regardless; serve / worker, which omit
    # both ``paper`` and ``embed``, are the ones that go torch-free.
]
# NOTE: calc, tex, docx, plot, cad-export, dft, and mermaid were promoted
# from extras into the core ``dependencies`` block (2026-08-12) — see the
# "Deterministic, pure-code, no-API tool deps" policy note there. The
# extras no longer exist; their kinds ship with every install.
# The rented MLIP relax rung (ADR 0043 §9, `fidelity='ml'`): ASE + a machine-
# learned potential (MACE-MP-0). torch is heavy — gated out of the default
# install; rung-0 `clean` geometry repair needs none of this. GPAW/DFT
# (`dft-gpaw`) runs as a cluster job, not inline.
dft-ml = ["ase>=3.22", "mace-torch>=0.3", "torch-dftd>=0.4"]

catalyst = ["autocatpath>=0.31.0"]

# backends + this repo's own dormant `dft-ml` torch extra targeting the same

cad-step = ["cadquery-ocp-novtk>=7.8"]
# guide — the annotated user-guide capture/render pipeline

guide = ["Pillow>=10.0"]
# NOTE: [pcb] deleted (2026-08-27) — it was only ``easyeda2kicad``, and Flow-B

# (slice 2) — and lands here when that slice does. Kept out of `[all]` (heavy,

chem = ["rdkit>=2023.9"]
# NOTE: [import] deleted (2026-08-16) — both of its deps (``ase``,
# ``httpx``) are core now, so it gated nothing. The ``structure/
# importers/`` adapter registry stays dependency-free by design (ADR

# own extra when it lands.

# see the "Deterministic, pure-code, no-API tool deps" note above.

# mendeleev (element property DB), pymatgen (ChemEnv/CrystalNN/
# StructureMatcher — slice 2), tblite (GFN-xTB — slice 2) are all light,
# PyPI-resolvable, torch-free — but kept as an extra (not core, not `[all]`)
# because they aren't installed in every venv yet: a fresh prod deploy needs
# `[estimate]` explicitly before `get(kind='estimate', ...)` works. The
# `precis_estimate` handler imports them lazily (module import never touches
# them) so an `[estimate]`-less venv still boots every other kind cleanly.
# tblite ships NO linux-aarch64 wheel (macOS arm64/x86_64 + manylinux x86_64
# only) and won't build from source in the dev container — the platform
# marker keeps `--all-extras` image rebuilds green on Apple-Silicon Docker
# and aarch64 cluster nodes; the xtb tier (slice 2) degrades gracefully
# where it's absent. The aarch64 compute hosts (where xtb struct_relax jobs
# pin) get tblite from the wheelhouse instead: scripts/build-tblite-wheel
# builds it, roles/autocatpath's wheelhouse.yml installs it (gr488907).
# Drop the marker and that channel when upstream ships the wheel.
estimate = [
    "mendeleev>=1.2.0",
    "pymatgen>=2026.5",
    "tblite>=0.7 ; sys_platform == 'darwin' or platform_machine == 'x86_64'",
]
# `chain` — nucleic-acid secondary-structure prediction for the `se` chain
# domain's fold checks (`precis_se.chain.fold`:
# `fold_layout`, `chain_fold_disagree`, `chain_offtarget`). ViennaRNA is a

# `estimate` — a real capability that isn't in every venv yet.
#
# The item's "promote to core when the wheel resolves on every CI/deploy
# platform" condition is MET as of 2026-09-29 (measured: viennarna 2.7.2
# resolves for manylinux x86_64, manylinux aarch64, win_amd64 and darwin, on

# every install carrying a compiled RNAlib, not a platform-availability one.
# A promotion must also add `viennarna -> RNA` to
# `scripts/lib/check-core-deps.py`'s IMPORT_NAME_OVERRIDES: the module the

chain = ["ViennaRNA>=2.7"]
# `pourbaix` — the bulk Pourbaix verdict job (`pourbaix_bulk`,
# src/precis_dft/pourbaix_bulk.py): pymatgen's PourbaixDiagram
# (same pin as `[estimate]`) over Materials Project entries fetched with
# mp-api. Installed into every venv that runs the `claude_inproc` pass
# (deploy roles `mcps` and `precis_worker`); `precis_dft.pourbaix_bulk`
# imports both lazily, so a venv without the extra still imports it.
pourbaix = [
    "pymatgen>=2026.5",
    "mp-api>=0.45",
]
all =["precis-mcp[embed,paper,web]"]

[project.scripts]
precis = "precis.cli:main"
asa-bot = "asa_bot.__main__:main"
asa-slack = "asa_slack.__main__:main"
hexfold = "hexfold.cli:main"

# Core kinds use an in-tree `BUILTINS` registry (V2 dropped entry-point
# discovery for them). The three groups below are the THIRD-PARTY / plugin
# seam (precis.dispatch._load_plugins + Migrator.discover_sources +
# workers.job_types._discover_job_type_plugins) — a tool-pack snaps in
# through them with zero core churn (ADR 0056). `precis_chem` is the
# first-party chem tool-pack, bundled in this repo but loaded as a plugin:
# the `route` kind, the `retrosynth` job_type, and its migrations
# (namespace `precis_chem`). It ships dark behind PRECIS_CHEM_ENABLED.
# `precis_bio` is its protein sibling (slice 4): the `protein` kind, the
# `fold` job_type (AlphaFold3 on the GPU node), and its migrations
# (namespace `precis_bio`), dark behind PRECIS_BIO_ENABLED.
# `precis_pathway` is the catalyst reaction-pathway sibling (bundle-pathway-
# in-tree proposal): the `pathway` kind, the `autocatpath_explore` job_type
# (autocatpath in-process on the GPU node), and its migrations — kept under
# the `autocatpath` namespace (matches the value already applied in prod from
# when the glue lived in the external autocatpath package). The kind is
# gated on the `[catalyst]` extra being installed, not on a feature flag.
# `precis_se` is the fourth keystone kind (docs/backlog/se-kind.md): the
# `se` (structural envelope) kind — scale-agnostic block trees with
# cad-DSL envelopes in metres, first-class arrays, manufacturing modes,
# and the `se_propose_atomic`/`se_simp` job_types. It absorbed the retired `nm`
# (nanomachine) kind as its `atomic` mode (docs/backlog/nm-se-merge.md):
# `precis_nm`'s handler/ops/persist/migrations and its one `nm_propose`
# job type are gone — the domain layer lives in `precis_se.atomic`, and
# nm's tables are dropped by `precis_se/migrations/0008`.
[project.entry-points."precis.handlers"]
route = "precis_chem.route:RouteHandler"
protein = "precis_bio.protein:ProteinHandler"
pathway = "precis_pathway.handler:PathwayHandler"
estimate = "precis_estimate.handler:EstimateHandler"
se = "precis_se.handler:SeHandler"

[project.entry-points."precis.job_types"]
retrosynth = "precis_chem.jobs:RETROSYNTH_SPEC"
fold = "precis_bio.jobs:FOLD_SPEC"
# autocatpath_explore: kept registered so pre-existing queued/legacy rows
# don't error-loop; dispatch_autocatpath no longer mints it (§B-1,
# gr180096 — see precis_pathway/job.py's docstring). autocatpath_seed /
# autocatpath_aggregate are the fan-out replacement.
autocatpath_explore = "precis_pathway.job:SPEC"
autocatpath_seed = "precis_pathway.seed_job:SPEC"
autocatpath_aggregate = "precis_pathway.aggregate_job:SPEC"
# surface_coverage_scan: one MLIP model's coverage anchors on a slab + the
# inner CHE sweep (docs/backlog/surface-pourbaix-staircase-optimizer.md,
# slice 1). Same ssh_node/target_node seam as autocatpath_seed.
surface_coverage_scan = "precis_pathway.coverage_job:SPEC"
se_propose_atomic = "precis_se.atomic.propose:SPEC"
# se_simp: the enqueued half of realize(kind='se', strategy='simp') — a
# SIMP topology solve over one block's envelope, bound back as a cad
# field-leaf design (docs/backlog/structural-solution-space.md slice 4).
se_simp = "precis_se.simp_job:SPEC"
# se_manufacture: the enqueued half of realize(kind='se',
# strategy='manufacture') — a print-in-place fuse of one print group,
# bound back as a cad field-leaf design on the group root (same item,
# round B2). Small groups fuse inline; this job takes the rest.
se_manufacture = "precis_se.manufacture_job:SPEC"
# hexfold_relax: assembled-hexfold-block relax on the compute group —
# whole-block polish + GFN2 on H-capped junction fragments, strain
# before/after stored on the scene (hexfold H3,
# docs/backlog/hexfold-nanoreactor-tube.md). Plugin spec, not a core
# builtin: the core must never import precis_se.
hexfold_relax = "precis_se.hexfold_relax_job:SPEC"

[project.entry-points."precis.migrations"]
precis_chem = "precis_chem.migrations"
precis_bio = "precis_bio.migrations"
autocatpath = "precis_pathway.migrations"
precis_estimate = "precis_estimate.migrations"
precis_se = "precis_se.migrations"

# Skill roots a plugin ships with itself (plugin-split step 3). Each value is
# a package holding *.md skills; precis.handlers.skill walks it after the
# built-ins, which win any slug clash.
[project.entry-points."precis.skills"]
precis_pathway = "precis_pathway.skills"

[project.entry-points."precis.handle_codes"]
pathway = "precis_pathway.handles"
estimate = "precis_estimate.handles"
se = "precis_se.handles"
route = "precis_chem.handles"
protein = "precis_bio.handles"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8",
    # Parallel test execution. The suite is CPU-bound and single-threaded
    # without this; ``addopts = -n auto`` (below) fans it across cores. Safe
    # because each xdist worker is its own process and so runs the
    # session-scoped ``_initialise_test_db`` fixture independently — every
    # worker gets its OWN ``precis_test_<uuid>`` clone, so the per-test
    # TRUNCATE isolation never races across workers (see tests/conftest.py).
    "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
    # Impact selection for the inner dev loop: `scripts/test --impacted` runs
    # only the tests a working-tree change affects (testmon maps test↔code).
    # Not in the ship gate (which runs the full suite); scripts/test pulls it
    # in via `uv run --with` too, so this entry just bakes it into the image
    # and documents the dep.
    "pytest-testmon>=2.1",
    "ruff>=0.11",
    "mypy>=1.15",
    "pre-commit>=4",
    # FastAPI's TestClient (starlette) needs httpx; used by the
    # precis_web route tests under tests/precis_web/.
    "httpx>=0.27",
    # Module-level import graph for `scripts/coderef imports|importers` (the
    # structural-retrieval verbs). Lazy-imported inside those verbs so coderef's
    # stdlib core (resolve/anchor/check/deps/callers) stays dep-free and
    # host-runnable; grimp only needs to be present under `uv run` / in the dev
    # image. Needs a dev-image rebuild to activate the grimp verbs in-container;
    # until then their tests `importorskip("grimp")`.
    "grimp>=3",
    # ViennaRNA (the `[chain]` extra) in the dev image, so the `se` fold
    # checks' *installed* branch is exercised by CI and not only the
    # `chain_fold_unavailable` degradation. Needs a dev-image rebuild to
    # activate in-container; until then those tests `importorskip("RNA")`.
    "ViennaRNA>=2.7",
    # Architecture contracts (`uv run lint-imports`, wired into the ship
    # gate): mechanises the layering conventions that used to live only in
    # prose — see [tool.importlinter] below. Built on grimp (already here).
    "import-linter>=2.1",
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12.20260724",
    "lxml-stubs>=0.5.1",
    "types-tqdm>=4.70.0.20260805",
    "types-xmltodict>=1.0.1.20260518",
    "types-networkx>=3.6.1.20260728",
    # Diff-coverage gate: the full-suite ship gate (scripts/ship without
    # --impacted) runs pytest under coverage and diff-cover then fails the
    # ship if changed src lines aren't executed by a test. Also feeds
    # scripts/mutate-diff its per-test contexts (--cov-context=test) so each
    # mutant runs only its covering tests. Not used by /land or scripts/test.
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
]

# autocatpath is release-gated off PyPI past 0.13.0; resolve it from the
# private repo, pinned to a release REV (not branch main: catpath main runs
# ahead of its tags, and an untagged bump that moves energies — 0.24.0's
# gas/H* corrections — must not enter through a plain re-lock). To take a
# new engine: change `rev` to the release commit, then `uv lock -P
# autocatpath`; the engine token the quest keys margins by follows. Auth:
# git credential helper locally, gh_token BuildKit secret in the image build.
# tool.uv.sources applies only to THIS project's lock/sync — cluster
# `uv pip install precis-mcp[...]` never reads it (wheelhouse covers those).
# Pillow security override (Reto 2026-10-11). marker-pdf 2.0.0 hard-caps
# Pillow<11; the override replaces that requirement so the lock takes
# pillow>=12.3.0, clearing Dependabot #56-67. The reachable ones: paste/crop
# out-of-bounds write, JPEG2000 decode DoS, ImageCms out-of-bounds write —
# paper ingest (Marker + pymupdf) decodes images from untrusted PDFs.
# Overrides only bind THIS project's lock/sync; cluster `uv pip install`s
# pass `--overrides /opt/precis/overrides.txt`, which
# deploy/playbooks/03-precis-constraints.yml derives from the exported
# lock's `pillow==` line. Marker's runtime path was smoke-tested on 12.3.0.
# Drop this table (and the 03-precis-constraints overrides step, and every
# `--overrides /opt/precis/overrides.txt`) once marker-pdf lifts its cap.
[tool.uv]
override-dependencies = ["pillow>=12.3.0"]

[tool.uv.sources]
autocatpath = { git = "https://github.com/retospect/catpath", rev = "4291094d9793f75c01a54dc2644dde1e22f6a4d3" }  # v0.31.1

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/precis", "src/precis_web", "src/asa_bot", "src/asa_slack", "src/precis_chem", "src/precis_bio", "src/precis_pathway", "src/precis_dft", "src/precis_estimate", "src/precis_se", "src/hexfold", "src/precis_surface", "src/precis_chain"]

# Note: hatchling ≥ 1.20 already includes non-Python files inside a
# packaged directory (Jinja .j2 templates under
# ``src/precis_web/templates`` ship automatically with the
# ``src/precis_web`` package). Earlier versions of this file carried
# a ``[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]`` block that
# duplicated the templates path; the newer hatchling detects the
# duplicate and refuses to build with
# "A second file is being added to the wheel archive at the same
# path". The block was deleted in this commit.
#
# Workspace templates (LaTeX / Markdown scaffolds copied verbatim
# into a freshly-initialized workspace by
# ``precis.utils.workspace.ensure_initialized``) ship as package
# data under ``src/precis/data/workspace_templates/``. The ``.tex``
# / ``.md`` files come along automatically, but hatchling skips
# dotfiles by default — so we widen the artifact pattern below to
# include them. Without this, ``importlib.resources`` on a wheel
# install finds ``main.tex`` but not ``.gitignore`` and the
# initializer silently writes a workspace with no ignore file.

[tool.hatch.build]
artifacts = [
    "src/precis/data/workspace_templates/**/.gitignore",
]

# Source distribution includes docker/ so packagers / downstream image
# builders get the Dockerfile and entrypoint alongside the Python source
# (`pip download --no-binary precis-mcp` lands a tarball with both).
# tests/ ships so downstream can verify; docs/ ships so the ADRs travel
# with the release. The wheel above stays src/precis only — Dockerfiles
# aren't useful inside an installed package and would just bloat
# every `pip install`.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
  "src/",
  "tests/",
  "docker/",
  "docs/",
  "scripts/",
  "*.md",
  "*.toml",
  "LICENSE",
  "CITATION.cff",
]

# Architecture contracts (`uv run lint-imports`; ship-gate step). Each
# contract mechanises a layering rule that previously lived only in prose
# (CLAUDE.md / package docstrings). Contracts must pass on today's graph —
# a new violation is a design regression, not style noise. Static analysis
# via grimp: nothing is imported, so optional/uninstalled deps are safe.
# The smaller plugin-ish packages (asa_slack, precis_chem, precis_bio,
# precis_pathway) are roots too so their edges are visible to contracts.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = [
    "precis",
    "precis_web",
    "asa_bot",
    "asa_slack",
    # `precis_chain` is a root so its (deliberately empty) outbound edge to the
    # rest of the tree is visible to the contract below — the kernel is a
    # numpy-only package destined for its own pip, like `hexfold`.
    "precis_chain",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "core is surface-free: precis never imports web/discord/slack daemons"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["precis"]
forbidden_modules = ["precis_web", "asa_bot", "asa_slack"]
# The one sanctioned edge: the `precis web` CLI subcommand is the web
# app's composition root/launcher.
ignore_imports = [
    "precis.cli.web -> precis_web.app",
    "precis.cli.web -> precis_web.config",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "surface daemons stay independent (web vs discord bridge)"
type = "independence"
modules = ["precis_web", "asa_bot"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "precis_chain is a standalone numpy kernel: no precis/asa imports"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["precis_chain"]
forbidden_modules = ["precis", "precis_web", "asa_bot", "asa_slack"]
# Direct AND transitive: unlike the two intra-precis contracts below, there is
# no dense graph to indict here — the kernel's whole point is that its import
# closure is numpy and the standard library. `tests/
# test_precis_chain_import_boundary.py` is the belt to this braces (it catches a
# `precis_se`/`precis_chem` plugin import too, which is not a root package here).

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "slack bridge shares asa_bot runtime but never the web app"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["asa_slack"]
forbidden_modules = ["precis_web"]

# The two intra-precis contracts are direct-import only: the package's
# transitive graph is dense (utils → liveness → workers chains reach almost
# everything), so a full-chain ban would indict every module. The convention
# they encode — and the regression they catch — is a module *reaching for*
# the higher layer by name.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "ingest below workers: the embedding/summary cascade is worker-owned"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["precis.ingest"]
forbidden_modules = ["precis.workers"]
allow_indirect_imports = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "store is the bottom layer of precis"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["precis.store"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
forbidden_modules = [
    "precis.workers",
    "precis.handlers",
    "precis.tools",
    "precis.jobs",
    "precis.ingest",
    "precis.cli",
    "precis.server",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 88
# Don't descend into Claude Code worktrees — sibling sessions live under
# .claude/worktrees/<name>/ (nested copies of the repo) and would
# otherwise be scanned twice and trip the format/lint gate on unrelated
# in-flight work.
extend-exclude = [".claude"]

[tool.ruff.format]
# ruff 0.16 formats python fences inside markdown by default; our LLM-facing
# docs deliberately use compact single-quote snippets (mirroring MCP call
# style), so keep the formatter out of prose.
exclude = ["*.md"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "RUF", "PLW1514"]
# PLW1514 (unspecified-encoding) is still a preview rule in ruff 0.16, so it
# needs `preview` on to fire at all. `explicit-preview-rules` keeps that from
# being a blanket opt-in: preview rules arrive only when named by their exact
# code, so the prefix selectors above (E/F/I/UP/B/SIM/RUF) stay stable-only and
# a ruff upgrade can't silently redden the gate with unrelated preview rules.
preview = true
explicit-preview-rules = true
ignore = [
    "B008",    # function-call-in-default-argument (typer pattern)
    "E501",    # line-too-long (formatter handles what it can)
    "E741",    # ambiguous-variable-name
    "RUF001",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-string
    "RUF002",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-docstring
    "RUF003",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-comment
    "RUF012",  # mutable-class-default (SQLAlchemy/Pydantic models)
    "SIM102",  # collapsible-if
    "SIM103",  # needless-bool
    "SIM105",  # suppressible-exception
    "SIM108",  # if-else-block-instead-of-if-exp
    "SIM110",  # reimplemented-builtin
    "SIM117",  # multiple-with-statements
    "B007",    # unused-loop-control-variable
    "B905",    # zip-without-explicit-strict
    "RUF005",  # collection-literal-concatenation
    "RUF006",  # asyncio-dangling-task
    "RUF013",  # implicit-optional
    "RUF043",  # match-metacharacter-unescaped
    "UP036",   # outdated-version-block
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["B007", "E402", "E731", "E741", "F841", "RUF012", "RUF015", "RUF059", "UP036"]
"src/**" = ["E402", "RUF059"]
# The U+00D7 repeat marker is required by the hexfold notation format.
"src/hexfold/text.py" = ["RUF001", "RUF002"]
"tests/hexfold/*" = ["RUF001", "RUF002"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
warn_unused_configs = true
check_untyped_defs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
# `mypy src tests` (the gate's scope) never passes `scripts/` as a target,
# but tests/test_guide_scripts.py imports scripts/guide_lib.py at runtime
# via a sys.path insert (scripts/*.py isn't a package under src/ — see the
# CLAUDE.md scripts convention). mypy_path only widens import RESOLUTION
# for files it's already checking; it doesn't add scripts/*.py to the
# checked set, so the rest of scripts/ stays outside gate scope as before.
# `scripts/mine-sessions` is listed too because tests/test_mine_sessions_*.py
# import its modules the same way (`sys.path` insert; the directory is
# hyphenated, so it can never be a package). Resolution only — the miner's
# own files still aren't in the checked set.
mypy_path = "scripts:scripts/mine-sessions"
# Burn-down complete 2026-08-02: every once-disabled error code
# (no-any-return, valid-type, dict-item, method-assign, var-annotated,
# union-attr, type-var, assignment, operator, index) is now enforced.
# Don't reintroduce a disable_error_code list — fix or narrowly ignore
# at the site instead.

# The genuinely-untyped (or genuinely-optional-and-uninstalled) third-party
# surface: no upstream py.typed marker and no widely-used types-* stub
# package worth the dev-dep weight for what's usually a single call site
# (contrast with yaml/lxml/tqdm/xmltodict/networkx above, which got real
# stub packages instead — see the dev dependency group). Some of these
# (anki, chgnet, pdf2doi, acatome_store, acatome_extract) aren't even
# installed in the container image — they're optional runtime deps behind
# try/except ImportError guards, never resolvable regardless of extras.
# Replaces the old blanket ``ignore_missing_imports = true``: first-party
# modules now get real import-resolution checking, so a broken/first-party
# import path surfaces as an error instead of silently becoming ``Any``.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "acatome_extract.*",
    "acatome_store.*",
    "agox",
    "agox.*",
    "anki",
    "anki.*",
    "autocatpath",
    "autocatpath.*",
    "chgnet.*",
    "epo_ops",
    "epo_ops.*",
    "fitz",
    "fontTools",  # no py.typed marker (ingest/glyph_outline.py)
    "fontTools.*",
    "gpaw",
    "gpaw.*",
    "habanero",
    "manifold3d",
    "marker.*",
    "mendeleev",
    "mendeleev.*",
    "mermaidx",
    # mp-api (the [pourbaix] extra) ships no py.typed marker.
    "mp_api",
    "mp_api.*",
    "num2words",
    "numba",  # core dep (pcb/maze.py) that ships no py.typed marker
    "numba.*",
    "OCP",
    "OCP.*",
    "opentimestamps.*",
    "pdf2doi",
    "pylatexenc.*",
    "pymatgen",
    "pymatgen.*",
    "pysbd",
    "ray",  # pulled by [struct-search] (agox); absent from the gate image like agox itself
    "ray.*",
    "rdkit",
    "rdkit.*",
    # present in every install transitively (core dep ase requires it);
    # ships no stubs for scipy.spatial (precis_se/atomic/clearance.py).
    "scipy",
    "scipy.*",
    # ViennaRNA's module is `RNA` and ships no stubs; it is the `[chain]`
    # extra, absent from the dev image until it is rebuilt, and imported
    # lazily (precis_se/chain/fold.py::rna_module).
    "RNA",
    "semanticscholar",
    "semanticscholar.*",
    "shapely",
    "shapely.*",
    "sklearn.*",
    "soundfile",
    "surya.*",
    "sympy",
    "sympy.*",
    "tblite",
    "tblite.*",
    "torch_dftd",
    "torch_dftd.*",
    "wolframalpha",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# These modules touch heavy optional deps (kokoro-onnx, torch/transformers,
# ase, slack SDK, starlette task plumbing) whose types only resolve where
# the extras are installed — the container gate. There, their site ignores
# are load-bearing; on a host/CI run without the extras the same ignores
# read as unused. Exempt exactly these modules from unused-ignore warnings
# so one mypy config is green in both environments; the suppressions
# themselves still apply everywhere.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "tests.test_tts_kokoro",
    "tests.precis_web.test_todo",
    "tests.test_asa_slash",
    "precis.ingest.marker",
    "precis.structure.relax",
    "precis.structure.preflight",
]
warn_unused_ignores = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Fan the suite across cores. It is CPU-bound and was single-threaded
# (~36s host / minutes in the container gate); -n auto roughly halves
# wall-clock on a multi-core box. Each worker is a separate process and
# gets its own per-session DB clone (see tests/conftest.py), so DB
# isolation holds. For a clean single-test debug session
# (pdb / -s output), override with ``-n0``.
# --max-worker-restart=0 (gr346941): xdist otherwise replaces a crashed
# (OOM-killed) worker, and under --cov-context the replacement errored
# every test it ran (~1400 ERRORs + INTERNALERROR). With 0 the run stops
# at once with one failure naming the crashed worker.
addopts = "-n auto --max-worker-restart=0"

[tool.coverage.run]
# relative_files: coverage runs INSIDE the gate container (/app) but
# diff-cover runs on the HOST (the warm gate container has no .git — source
# arrives via `git archive` — so it can't compute the diff). Relative paths
# (src/precis/…) make one coverage.xml valid in both places.
relative_files = true

[tool.coverage.report]
# Defensive-only lines a diff-coverage gate must not force tests for.
exclude_also = [
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "@overload",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "workers import store and utils, never handlers"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["precis.workers"]
forbidden_modules = ["precis.handlers"]
allow_indirect_imports = true
# Ratchet: the remaining edges are legacy; migrate them to store/utils
# helpers and delete the line — never add one.
ignore_imports = [
    "precis.workers.briefing -> precis.handlers.news",
    "precis.workers.executors._common -> precis.handlers.skill",
    "precis.workers.executors._context -> precis.handlers.job",
    "precis.workers.executors._sandbox_harvest -> precis.handlers.plaintext",
    "precis.workers.job_types.draft_export -> precis.handlers.draft",
    "precis.workers.job_types.draft_refresh -> precis.handlers.draft",
    "precis.workers.job_types.reground_claim -> precis.handlers.draft",
    "precis.workers.job_types.struct_search -> precis.handlers.structure",
    "precis.workers.job_types.taproot_backfill -> precis.handlers.draft",
    "precis.workers.news_poll -> precis.handlers.news",
    "precis.workers.orcid_enrich -> precis.handlers.orcid",
    "precis.workers.planner_prompt -> precis.handlers.skill",
]

[project]
name = "pytstop"
version = "0.2.0"
description = "Sistema Integrado de Atendimento e Execucao de Servicos"
# Alinhado ao runtime real (3.14: .python-version, Dockerfiles, CI e mypy
# abaixo): manter >=3.12 fazia o resolver carregar wheels/markers de versoes
# que nada no projeto executa.
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.141.1",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.52.1",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0,<2.1",
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9",
    "alembic>=1.14",
    "pyjwt>=2.9",
    "pwdlib[bcrypt]>=0.3.0",
    "brutils>=2.3,<3",
    "pydantic[email]>=2.13.4,<3",
    "structlog>=24.0",
    "slowapi>=0.1",
    "redis>=8.1.0,<9",
    # Piso 50: PYSEC-2026-3552/CVE-2026-69247 (HIGH) na 49.x — pip-audit e
    # trivy (--exit-code 1) derrubam o CI com qualquer resolucao < 50.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.0",
    # Timeout de sessao (config em [tool.pytest.ini_options]): os testes de
    # concorrencia do relay fazem ``t.join()`` sem limite — uma regressao de
    # lock (deadlock/lock perdido) penduraria o job em vez de falhar. O timeout
    # transforma "pendurado" em falha visivel e limitada no tempo.
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3",
    "testcontainers[postgres,redis]>=4.15.0",
    "polyfactory>=2.0",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "ruff>=0.16.1",
    "mypy>=2.3.0",
    "bandit>=1.7",
    "import-linter>=2.13",
    # Lido por scripts/codeql_quality.py (gate de Code Quality) para parsear o
    # codeql-config.yml. Declarado explicitamente aqui (dev-tooling, junto de
    # ruff/mypy/bandit): hoje so funciona porque bandit o puxa transitivamente,
    # fragil em fresh venvs. Nao e dependencia de runtime.
    "pyyaml>=6",
]
ui = [
    "nicegui>=3.15.0,<4",
    # httpx e usado direto por ui/cliente_api.py (wrapper HTTP da UI). NiceGUI
    # 3.x nao puxa httpx transitivamente, entao precisa estar declarado aqui.
    # Sem isso, `uv run --extra ui` (incluindo make ui, make seed-demo,
    # scripts/seed_demo.py) explode com ModuleNotFoundError em fresh venv.
    "httpx>=0.27",
    # Necessarios para a fixture `screen` de nicegui.testing executar os testes
    # lentos de browser em vez de marca-los como skipped por dependencia ausente.
    "pytest-selenium>=4.1",
    "selenium>=4.46.0",
]
full-test = [
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "pytest>=8",
    # timeout global em [tool.pytest.ini_options] + --strict-markers: qualquer
    # ambiente que rode pytest precisa do plugin, senao a coleta morre com
    # "'timeout' not found in markers" (CI full-test sincroniza SO este extra).
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0",
]
# Observabilidade OTLP (ADR-020, diferencial opcional). Fora do extra `test`
# de proposito: o CI nao paga o custo de instalar SDK + grpcio, e o codigo
# que consome estes pacotes (observability.py / relay/metrics.py) importa lazy
# dentro da funcao com try/ImportError — flag ligada sem o extra instalado
# degrada para warning + no-op, nunca quebra o boot. Exporter gRPC (porta 4317)
# escolhido para casar com o endpoint default http://jaeger:4317 do
# manifest/compose. O par Prometheus (TD-022/ADR-024) instrumenta o relay:
# MeterProvider + PrometheusMetricReader expoem /metrics scrapeado pelo
# k8s/prometheus.yaml.
otel = [
    # Par compativel: SDK 1.42.x <-> instrumentation 0.63bx (o sdk exige
    # semantic-conventions ==0.63bx). Atualizar os 4 juntos, em milestones.
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.42,<1.43",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.42,<1.43",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.63b1,<0.64",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.63b1,<0.64",
    # Metricas do relay (TD-022/ADR-024): o reader registra os instrumentos do
    # MeterProvider no REGISTRY default do prometheus_client; start_http_server
    # serve /metrics. Versionado junto do SDK 1.42.x.
    "opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus>=0.63b1,<0.64",
    "prometheus-client>=0.26.0",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=75.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
# UI e dev-only: NAO e empacotada em wheels/sdists distribuiveis.
# Docker do UI copia `ui/` e `src/` diretamente (ver `ui/Dockerfile`) e
# roda via `python -m ui` com CWD no path, sem depender de `pip install`.
include = ["src*"]

[tool.ruff]
# Runtime e 3.14 (requires-python/mypy), mas o target do ruff fica em py313
# DE PROPOSITO: com py314 o `ruff format` remove os parenteses de
# `except (A, B):` (PEP 758), sintaxe que tooling externo ainda nao parseia --
# SonarQube do scan de fechamento (ADR-011) e revisores automaticos a acusam
# como SyntaxError. Manter py313 preserva `except (A, B):`, compativel com todo
# o tooling, sem impacto no runtime 3.14.
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 88

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "I",   # isort
    "N",   # pep8-naming
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "A",   # flake8-builtins
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "TCH", # flake8-type-checking
    "RUF", # ruff-specific
    "S",   # flake8-bandit
    "PT",  # flake8-pytest-style
    "ANN",     # flake8-annotations (codigo de prod; ignorado em tests/)
    "BLE001",  # blind except
    "FBT001",  # boolean-type-hint-positional-argument
    "C901",    # complex-structure (mccabe)
    "PLR2004", # magic-value-comparison
    "PLR0912", # too-many-branches
    "PLR0913", # too-many-arguments
    "PLR0915", # too-many-statements
    "PLW0603", # global-statement
    "PYI034",  # non-self-return-type
    "LOG014",  # exc-info-outside-except-handler
]
fixable = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
# Campos de modelos Pydantic sao avaliados em runtime: mover o import da
# annotation para TYPE_CHECKING quebraria a validacao (TC001 falso-positivo).
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["src", "ui", "relay"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = [
    "S101", "S105", "S106", "TCH", "SIM105", "PT012", "RUF059",
    "ANN",                                  # tests podem ser destipados
    "PLR2004",                              # magic values em asserts
    "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "PLR0912",        # fixtures e factories sao grandes
    "C901",                                 # tests podem ter setup complexo
    "FBT001",                               # callsites de stub/fake
    "BLE001",                               # tests as vezes capturam Exception
    "LOG014",                               # tests nao usam exc_info
    "PLW0603",                              # tests podem manipular singletons
    "PYI034",                               # FakeUnitOfWork etc sao stubs
]
"full-test/tests/**" = [
    "S101", "S105", "S106", "TCH", "SIM105", "PT012", "RUF059",
    "ANN", "PLR2004", "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "PLR0912",
    "C901", "FBT001", "BLE001", "LOG014", "PLW0603", "PYI034",
]
# Daemon do relay: `_drenar`/`processar_ciclo` expoem 6 parametros de
# proposito — engine + costuras injetaveis (handlers, nome_handler, lote,
# lease, relogio) que permitem teste unitario sem Postgres e sem relogio real.
# Quebrar em um objeto de config so para satisfazer o limite de 5 argumentos
# obscureceria as costuras; PLR0913 e ruido aqui.
"relay/**" = ["PLR0913"]
"**/exceptions.py" = ["N818"]
"**/interfaces/schemas.py" = ["S105", "TCH003"]
"**/interfaces/router*.py" = ["B008"]
"**/interfaces/middleware.py" = ["B008", "TCH002"]
"**/interfaces/dependencies.py" = ["B008"]
"migrations/**" = ["E402"]
"**/dtos.py" = ["S105"]
"migrations/env.py" = ["E402"]
# Script utilitario de build (gera o PDF de entrega). Chama binarios de dev
# conhecidos (gh/git/npx/pandoc) via subprocess com lista de args fixa, sem
# shell=True — nao ha superficie de injecao. S603 (subprocess) e S607 (partial
# path, resolvido via PATH de proposito p/ portabilidade) viram ruido aqui.
# Obs: este ignore e da ruff (regra "S"); o bandit "real" nao falha nesses
# porque sao severidade LOW e o gate roda com --severity-level high.
".claude/skills/entrega-tech-challenge/scripts/*.py" = ["S603", "S607"]

# Contratos de arquitetura (ADR-015 / RNF-017): a regra de dependencia da
# Clean Architecture e verificada por lint (`make lint-arch` / CI).
# `infraestrutura` (Frameworks & Drivers) fica fora do contrato de camadas
# porque importa `aplicacao`/`dominio` legitimamente — adapters implementam
# ports definidos pelas camadas internas; o sentido proibido (dominio e
# aplicacao -> infraestrutura) e coberto pelo contrato forbidden. `compartilhado`
# e shared kernel, nao contexto delimitado: fica fora dos containers de camadas,
# mas seu `dominio` e sua `aplicacao` entram no forbidden pelos mesmos motivos.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["src", "relay"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Camadas Clean por contexto (interfaces -> aplicacao -> dominio)"
type = "layers"
layers = ["interfaces", "aplicacao", "dominio"]
containers = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo",
    "src.catalogo_servicos",
    "src.estoque",
    "src.ordem_servico",
    "src.autenticacao",
    # Shared kernel tambem respeita a ordem interna de camadas (finding da
    # revisao arquitetural de fechamento: estava fora do lint de layers).
    "src.compartilhado",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Dominio e aplicacao nao importam infraestrutura de nenhum contexto"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo.dominio",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.dominio",
    "src.estoque.dominio",
    "src.ordem_servico.dominio",
    "src.autenticacao.dominio",
    "src.compartilhado.dominio",
    "src.cliente_veiculo.aplicacao",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.aplicacao",
    "src.estoque.aplicacao",
    "src.ordem_servico.aplicacao",
    "src.autenticacao.aplicacao",
    "src.compartilhado.aplicacao",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo.infraestrutura",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.infraestrutura",
    "src.estoque.infraestrutura",
    "src.ordem_servico.infraestrutura",
    "src.autenticacao.infraestrutura",
    "src.compartilhado.infraestrutura",
]

# `src` (a aplicacao) NUNCA importa o sidecar operacional `relay/`: o sentido
# legitimo e `relay -> src` (o relay consome dominio/infra de src). O sentido
# inverso (`src -> relay`) fecharia um ciclo de pacote `src -> relay -> src`,
# invisivel ao linter enquanto `relay` ficava fora de `root_packages`. Com
# `relay` agora graficado, este contrato torna o ciclo regressao-proof. As
# queries de DLQ que antes moravam em `relay/dlq.py` migraram para
# `src.compartilhado.infraestrutura.outbox_dlq`.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "src nao importa relay (relay e sidecar; so relay -> src e permitido)"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["src"]
forbidden_modules = ["relay"]

# Independencia entre bounded contexts (ADR-015 / DDD): o ``dominio`` e a
# ``aplicacao`` de cada um dos 5 contextos NAO importam o ``dominio``/
# ``aplicacao`` de nenhum outro — comunicacao entre contextos passa por
# ports/adapters (ACL), nunca por acoplamento direto no nucleo. Modelado como 5
# contratos ``forbidden`` (um por contexto) em vez de um unico ``independence``:
# ``independence`` sobre os 5 pacotes-raiz proibiria tambem infraestrutura/
# interfaces de cruzarem (adapters e composition roots cruzam LEGITIMAMENTE, por
# isso ficam FORA); e listar as camadas separadas dentro de um contexto quebraria
# o ``aplicacao -> dominio`` do PROPRIO contexto. ``compartilhado`` (shared
# kernel) fica de fora: e o nucleo compartilhado por desenho.
# Passa com 0 violacoes hoje — o codigo ja cumpre a regra.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "cliente_veiculo nao acopla no nucleo de outros contextos"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo.dominio",
    "src.cliente_veiculo.aplicacao",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.catalogo_servicos.dominio",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.aplicacao",
    "src.estoque.dominio",
    "src.estoque.aplicacao",
    "src.ordem_servico.dominio",
    "src.ordem_servico.aplicacao",
    "src.autenticacao.dominio",
    "src.autenticacao.aplicacao",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "catalogo_servicos nao acopla no nucleo de outros contextos"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "src.catalogo_servicos.dominio",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.aplicacao",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo.dominio",
    "src.cliente_veiculo.aplicacao",
    "src.estoque.dominio",
    "src.estoque.aplicacao",
    "src.ordem_servico.dominio",
    "src.ordem_servico.aplicacao",
    "src.autenticacao.dominio",
    "src.autenticacao.aplicacao",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "estoque nao acopla no nucleo de outros contextos"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "src.estoque.dominio",
    "src.estoque.aplicacao",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "src.cliente_veiculo.dominio",
    "src.cliente_veiculo.aplicacao",
    "src.catalogo_servicos.dominio",

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ruff: lint + format.  The full rule set applies to the application package
# (src/website); tests, scripts and the seed CLI keep a lighter baseline.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 88
extend-exclude = [".specify", "specs"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W", "F",  # pycodestyle, pyflakes
    "I",            # isort
    "UP",           # pyupgrade
    "B",            # bugbear
    "SIM",          # simplify
    "C4",           # comprehensions
    "N",            # pep8 naming
    "ANN",          # type annotations on every signature
    "D",            # docstrings (google convention)
    "RUF",          # ruff-specific
    "PL",           # pylint (complexity / size limits)
    "C90",          # mccabe complexity
    "FAST",         # FastAPI idioms (Annotated dependencies)
    "PERF",         # performance anti-patterns
    "S",            # bandit security rules
    "T20",          # no print()
    "TID",          # tidy imports (no relative imports)
    "PTH",          # pathlib over os.path
    "RET",          # return statements
    "ARG",          # unused arguments
    "BLE",          # no blind `except Exception`
    "ERA",          # no commented-out code
]
ignore = [
    "D105",  # magic methods
    "D107",  # __init__ (documented on the class)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"src/website/**/__init__.py" = ["D104"]
"src/website/repository/*.py" = ["S608"]  # SQL built only from constant fragments
"tests/**" = [
    "ANN", "D", "S", "PL", "N", "ARG", "PTH", "ERA", "BLE", "T20", "C90",
    "RET", "SIM", "PERF", "RUF", "FAST", "B017", "E501", "TID252",
]
"scripts/**" = [
    "ANN", "D", "S", "PL", "N", "ARG", "PTH", "ERA", "BLE", "T20", "C90",
    "RET", "SIM", "PERF", "RUF", "FAST", "E501", "B",
]
"src/cli/**" = [
    "ANN", "D", "S", "PL", "N", "ARG", "PTH", "ERA", "BLE", "T20", "C90",
    "RET", "SIM", "PERF", "RUF", "E501",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 8
max-branches = 12
max-returns = 6
max-statements = 50

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

    "website.integrations | website.repository",

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "uv-dynamic-versioning"]
