[tool.hatch.version]
source = "uv-dynamic-versioning"

[tool.uv-dynamic-versioning]
# Required, not optional: Renovate runs `uv lock --upgrade-package`, which triggers a
# build with no git context, and without a fallback every such PR fails outright.
#
# The cost is that "no git history" becomes a *successful* build producing 0.0.0 rather
# than an error — nothing else in the publish path would catch that, and a version number
# cannot be reused once PyPI has it. `mise run build-verify` is what closes the gap.
fallback-version = "0.0.0"

# Explicit rather than relying on hatchling's <NAME>/__init__.py heuristic: when the
# heuristic misses, the failure mode is a silently empty wheel rather than an error.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["photree"]

# Hatchling's sdist default is "every file not ignored by the VCS", which would ship
# tests/, docs/, demo/, build-scripts/, .github/ and the lockfiles. Poetry shipped the
# package plus README/LICENSE/pyproject.toml; this keeps that shape.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
only-include = ["photree"]

[tool.hatch.build]
# .gitignore is the only ignore file hatchling reads — not .git/info/exclude, not
# core.excludesfile. .gitignore now covers .DS_Store, so this is a guard that keeps the
# published artifact independent of ignore-file hygiene rather than the primary fix.
exclude = [".DS_Store"]

[tool.uv]
# Replaces the default [{ file = "pyproject.toml" }] rather than extending it, hence the
# explicit file entry. The git entry is what keeps `photree --version` honest: photree
# reads its version through importlib.metadata, which an editable install freezes into
# .dist-info at install time, so without this a new commit or tag leaves a stale version
# in place indefinitely.
cache-keys = [{ file = "pyproject.toml" }, { git = { commit = true, tags = true } }]

# uv.lock does not cover PEP 517 build dependencies — `uv build` resolves them fresh from
# PyPI on a cold cache — so these constraints are the only pin on the build backend, and
# on dunamai in particular, which is what computes the version. Regenerate with:
#   printf '%s\n' hatchling uv-dynamic-versioning \
#     | uv pip compile - --no-annotate --no-header --quiet
# [build-system].requires is left unpinned so the two can never contradict each other.
build-constraint-dependencies = [
  "dunamai==1.26.2",
  "hatchling==1.32.0",
  "jinja2==3.1.6",
  "markupsafe==3.0.3",
  "packaging==26.3",
  "pathspec==1.1.1",
  "pluggy==1.6.0",
  "tomlkit==0.15.1",
  "trove-classifiers==2026.6.1.19",
  "uv-dynamic-versioning==0.14.0",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"

# Ruff 0.16 turned on a much larger default rule set (413 rules, up from 59). We take
# the new defaults; the exceptions below are rules that conflict with a deliberate
# design decision in this codebase rather than rules we have not gotten around to.
[tool.ruff.lint]
ignore = [
  # Photo capture times are naive wall-clock instants: EXIF DateTimeOriginal carries
  # no offset, so attaching a tzinfo would invent information we do not have. DTZ005
  # (datetime.now() without tz) stays enabled — that one is a real bug.
  "DTZ001",
  "DTZ007",
  # Batch commands deliberately isolate per-item failures: one album that fails to
  # export/fix/refresh must not abort the whole run, so the exception is captured into
  # the batch result and reported to the user instead of propagating.
  "BLE001",
]
# PLW1514 (open/read_text/write_text without an explicit encoding) is still a preview
# rule in ruff 0.16. explicit-preview-rules opts into that one rule alone, so the rest
# of the rule set keeps its stable behavior. It enforces the UTF-8-everywhere guideline:
# without it the locale encoding is used silently. Drop the preview flags once ruff
# stabilizes PLW1514.
preview = true
explicit-preview-rules = true
extend-select = ["PLW1514"]

# pytest 9's native table; it cannot coexist with [tool.pytest.ini_options].
#
# --import-mode=importlib is the mode pytest recommends for new projects. pytest itself
# no longer inserts test directories into sys.path, so a module has one name: a test file
# is imported as `tests.test_x`, derived from the rootdir. The flag has no ini key, hence
# addopts.
#
# "." (resolved against this file's directory, the repo root) is the one sys.path entry
# the suite needs. It makes `scripts.*` and `tests.*` importable in this process from any
# test file run alone. Neither directory has an __init__.py, so both are namespace
# packages; tests/conftest.py stops a session that could merge another tree's `tests/`
# or `scripts/` into them (#207).
#
# pytest's docs recommend putting test utilities with the library code instead. They
# stay under tests/ (tests/_helpers/) because cs2rl ships in the wheel (the

# child interpreter never inherits that, so code that launches one keeps setting
# PYTHONPATH and the cwd itself (tests/conftest.py:29-32).
[tool.pytest]

# among the dots, and hid the fast-math guard for a whole refactor wave).
# PITFALL: -r chars REPLACE pytest's default `fE`, they do not add to it. `-rs` alone
# drops every FAILED/ERROR line from the summary, so keep the f and the E.
# CLI -m training selects real integration; -m "" restores complete coverage.
addopts = ["--import-mode=importlib", "-rfEs", "-m", "not slow and not training"]
pythonpath = ["."]

line-length = 100

select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "TID251"]
# E501 (line-too-long) disabled: YAPF's `spaces_before_comment` aligner pushes
# trailing comments past column 100 when the preceding code is long, producing
# fights between the formatter and the linter. YAPF's column_limit=100 still
# keeps lines reasonable for actual code; we just stop policing trailing comments.
ignore = ["E501"]

# one misses the other. Each entry bans the spelling that is NOT canonical; the
# runtime half is the session guard in tests/conftest.py.

"scripts.analyze_tplant".msg = "import `cs2rl.experiment.analyze_tplant`"

[tool.complexipy]
# Cognitive-complexity limit of the hook ratchet (#216); the hooks also pass it explicitly.
max-complexity-allowed = 40

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "lf"

[tool.yapf]
based_on_style          = "pep8"
column_limit            = 100
# Snap trailing comments to the first column stop > longest line in the block.
# Tune these stops to match typical line lengths in the codebase.
spaces_before_comment   = "40, 56, 72"
indent_width            = 4

# The package's layering (#205), checked by tests/integration/test_import_layers.py on every suite
# run; by hand: `lint-imports --no-cache --no-logo` from the repo root with
# PYTHONPATH=<checkout>/src. Without that PYTHONPATH a worktree checks MAIN's tree and
# passes: import-linter finds cs2rl with find_spec, which never runs the package's
# foreign-checkout guard.
#
# import-linter counts function-local imports as edges, and an ignore_imports entry names
# a module PAIR, never a line or a scope: it hides every site of that pair, a future
# module-scope one included. No contract has one since #205 part 3, and
# tests/integration/test_import_layers.py::test_no_contract_ignores_imports fails if one is added.
# The same file fails if a module is invisible to the graph (a directory without
# __init__.py).
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "cs2rl"

# Higher layers may import lower ones, never the reverse. exhaustive: every module
# directly under cs2rl must be named here, so a new module fails until it gets a layer.
# `|` members may not import each other; `:` members may, so this contract does not
# reject a cycle among them. The acyclic contract below does. A package (spec, env,
# eval, viz, train) is one member here; the `cs2rl.env layers` and `cs2rl.train layers`
# contracts order their own modules.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "cs2rl layers"
type = "layers"
containers = ["cs2rl"]
exhaustive = true
layers = [
    "experiment | deploy",
    # train is the run application (#205 part 3): its driver uses eval (the
    # --eval-interval BaselineEvaluator) and viz (--record), so it sits above them.
    # eval, viz and BC use only the policy, which sits below them. Every edge that
    # needed an ignore_imports entry before (#92) points down now;
    # tests/integration/test_import_layers.py::test_train_sits_above_eval_and_viz_and_policy_below_them
    # pins the order.
    "train",
    "train_bc : bc_demos : profile_step : viz : eval",
    "policy",
    # The nn.Module (torch at module scope); build_policy above imports it lazily.
    "policy_net",
    "env",
    "spec",
]
broken_contract_guidance = "Give a new module a layer in pyproject.toml. Move an upward import down: never add an ignore_imports entry (#205 part 3 retired the last ones)."

# Inside env/: config is the stdlib-only contract that env.c.cs2_env and
# `python -m cs2rl.train --dump-config` import, so it may import neither nav (awpy, shapely) nor map.
# The package-wide contract above cannot say so: all of env is one member there. c (the C
# env's Python side) imports config, map and nav at module scope; factory imports
# c.cs2_env inside build_env_for, so factory sits above c.
# exhaustive: a new module in env/ fails until it gets a layer here.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "cs2rl.env layers"
type = "layers"
containers = ["cs2rl.env"]
exhaustive = true
layers = ["factory", "c", "map : nav", "config"]
broken_contract_guidance = "Keep cs2rl.env.config stdlib-only: move the import into its caller. Give a new env/ module a layer here."

# Inside train/: the CLI on top, then the run driver, then the three things it composes
# (the --record and --eval modes and the PuffeRL trainer), then the parts, then config.
# The imports of trainer (torch, pufferlib) and of eval/viz stay function-local for
# `--dump-config`'s lightness (tests/train/test_w1_modules.py), except config's import of
# cs2rl.eval.duel_bot (numpy and cs2rl.spec only;
# tests/eval/test_duel_bot.py::test_importing_the_module_pulls_no_heavy_module), not for this
# contract.
# exhaustive: a new module in train/ fails until it gets a layer here.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "cs2rl.train layers"
type = "layers"
containers = ["cs2rl.train"]
exhaustive = true
layers = [
    "__main__",
    "loop",
    "compose",
    "record : evaluate : trainer",
    "selfplay : envs : update : rewards : entropy : resume : metrics : duel_opponent",
    "config",
]
broken_contract_guidance = "Give a new train/ module a layer here. Move an upward import down, or the shared code to a lower module."

# No cycles among the children of cs2rl, or of any package inside it (env.nav and
# env.map included), at any scope (import-linter sees function-local imports too).
# #205 part 3 removed the last cycles (through {env, eval, train, trainer, viz}): the policy
# moved below eval and viz, build_selfplay_manager moved up from env.factory into
# train.selfplay, and trainer became train.trainer, which imports no module above it.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "cs2rl acyclic siblings"
type = "acyclic_siblings"
ancestors = ["cs2rl"]
broken_contract_guidance = "Break the cycle: move the shared code down a layer. Never add an ignore_imports entry (#205 part 3 retired the last ones)."

# if the symbol is new).

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
timeout = 60
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"
minversion = "9.0"
# Cap xdist auto scheduling to keep the async/ASGI-heavy suite stable on macOS.
# The suite is clean at 8 workers and below, but `-n auto` on 12 logical CPUs
# reproducibly triggers unraisable socket/event-loop teardown warnings.
addopts = "-ra -q --strict-markers --maxprocesses=8"
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    "error:::litestar_auth",
    "ignore::litestar_auth.totp.SecurityWarning",
    # AA's own Litestar plugin calls the deprecated set_async_context/reset_async_context
    # during provide_session; we cannot remove these until AA 2.0. Scoped to the exact
    # messages so any other advanced_alchemy deprecation (incl. our own misuse) still fails.
    "ignore:Call to deprecated function '(set|reset)_async_context':DeprecationWarning",
]
markers = """
    imports: mark a test as an imports test
    integration: mark a test as an integration test
    e2e: end-to-end tests using real persistence and full plugin stack
    unit: mark a test as a unit test
"""

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["litestar_auth"]
branch = true
parallel = true
concurrency = ["multiprocessing", "thread"]
sigterm = true

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 1
fail_under = 100
include = ["litestar_auth/*"]
omit = [
    "tests/*",
]
exclude_lines = [
    # Have to re-enable the standard pragma
    "pragma: no cover",
    # Don't check obviously not implemented
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    # We don't really care what happens if fail
    "except ImportError:",
    # Don't check for typing-only code
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    # Don't check overload-only signatures
    "^\\s*@overload\\b",
    "@(typing\\.)?overload",
    # Don't check placeholder bodies used by overload and structural typing declarations
    "^\\s*\\.\\.\\.\\s*$",
    # Don't check Protocol class bodies; they are pure type contracts
    "^\\s*class \\w+(\\[.*\\])?\\(.*Protocol\\b.*\\):",
    # Don't check multiline Protocol class bodies; they are pure type contracts
    "^\\s*class \\w*Protocol(\\[.*\\])?\\(",
    # Don't check TypedDict class bodies; they are pure type contracts
    "^\\s*class \\w+\\(.*TypedDict\\b.*\\):",
    # Don't check PEP 695 type aliases; they are pure type contracts
    "^\\s*type \\w+\\s*=",
    # Don't check for code that only runs itself
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]
show_missing = true

[project]
name = "cas"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Clif's Agentic System: SAGE, ROOT Harness, and CAS Application"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    # Hosted abstraction provider (Claude). Cross-platform pure-Python SDK with
    # no Apple-Silicon constraint, so it stays in the base dependency set and the
    # SAGE core can run a hosted-abstraction deployment on any target (CAS-ADR-042).
    # Floor at 0.86: the hosted input-length guard reads the configured model's
    # maximum input size from the Models API, a ModelInfo field that first appears
    # in that release (0.85 carries the resource without the field; 0.40 carries
    # no Models resource at all). Below the floor the lookup degrades to an
    # unchecked call and the guard is silently inert -- which is the failure mode
    # it exists to remove, so the floor is a capability bound rather than a
    # security one. Resolves to 0.107.1 today (no version move).
    "anthropic>=0.86",
    "fastapi>=0.136.3",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.32",
    "pydantic>=2.13.4",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    # XML sources are parsed with entity expansion and external references refused.
    "defusedxml>=0.7",
    # Ceiling below the 2.x major: mcp 2.0 removes `mcp.server.fastmcp`, which
    # the entire MCP server surface is built on (the FastMCP subclass tools are
    # registered against, and the private ArgModelBase carrying strict
    # unknown-kwarg rejection, CAS-ADR-037). Crossing it is a ModuleNotFoundError
    # at import, so the bound turns a future unscoped resolve across 2.0 into a
    # reviewable lock-time conflict instead of a broken build. Resolves to
    # 1.30.0 today.
    "mcp>=1.0,<2",
    "sentence-transformers>=5.5.1",
    # Transitive via sentence-transformers / mlx-lm, but pinned directly to hold a
    # forward-looking ceiling: transformers 5.12 removes get_extended_attention_mask,
    # which nomic-embed-text's remote modeling code still calls at load time. The
    # bound turns a future float across 5.12 into a reviewable lock-time conflict
    # instead of a startup AttributeError. Resolves to 5.11.0 today.
    "transformers>=5.9,<5.12",
    # Imported directly to fetch pinned model and remote-code snapshots before
    # they are loaded. Transitive via transformers; declared so the import is
    # not an accident of another package's dependencies. Resolves to 1.17.0
    # today (no version move).
    "huggingface-hub>=1.0",
    # Direct so [tool.uv.sources] can route it through the CPU wheel index on
    # Linux (the default PyPI build there is CUDA). Resolved exactly by uv.lock.
    "torch>=2.11.0",
    "einops>=0.8",
    "python-docx>=1.1",
    "python-pptx>=1.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.5",
    "pdfplumber>=0.11",
    "pypdf>=6.11.0",
    "markdown-it-py>=3.0",
    "mdit-py-plugins>=0.4.0",
    # Postgres storage engine: async driver + connection pool (`pool` adds
    # psycopg_pool's AsyncConnectionPool) and pgvector type registration
    # (CAS-ADR-042). Serving-path runtime dependencies since the local
    # profile's durable-storage binding defaults to the Postgres adapters;
    # the embedded SQLite/LanceDB fallback needs neither.
    "psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.2",
    "pgvector>=0.3",
    # Confidential-client OIDC sign-in and delegated (on-behalf-of) downstream
    # token acquisition for the application backend-for-frontend auth flow
    # (cloud profile, CAS-ADR-042). Microsoft first-party; cross-platform pure
    # Python, so it stays in the base set like the hosted abstraction SDK.
    "msal>=1.28",
    # Outbound HTTP client the backend-for-frontend uses to reach SAGE with a
    # forwarded delegated token. Already an indirect dependency (the hosted
    # abstraction SDK and the Starlette test client both use it); pinned
    # directly here because the BFF imports it as a first-class runtime client.
    "httpx>=0.27",
    # OAuth resource-server token validation (CAS-ADR-042): RS256 JWT signature
    # and claim verification against the issuer's published JWKS. Pure-Python
    # with no Apple-Silicon constraint, so it stays in the base set; the
    # [crypto] extra pulls `cryptography` for the asymmetric verification path.
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.10",
    # Authenticated encryption (Fernet, with an HKDF-derived key) of the
    # backend-for-frontend's stored token caches. Already present through
    # pyjwt[crypto]; named here because the session store imports it directly.
    "cryptography>=46",
    # Managed-identity secret resolution for the cloud profile (CAS-ADR-042):
    # azure-identity mints the workload's managed-identity tokens (Key Vault
    # data-plane reads and the Postgres Entra access token), and
    # azure-keyvault-secrets reads the hosted abstraction key from the vault at
    # runtime so no secret lives in the environment, image, or repository.
    # Microsoft first-party; cross-platform pure Python, so they stay in the
    # base set like the other hosted-target SDKs. Imported lazily, so an on-box
    # local-profile install never loads them.
    "azure-identity>=1.19",
    "azure-keyvault-secrets>=4.9",
    # Async HTTP transport for the cloud Postgres managed-identity credential
    # (CAS-ADR-042). The cloud storage path authenticates with the asynchronous
    # azure.identity.aio.DefaultAzureCredential, which builds an aiohttp-backed
    # azure-core transport at construction; azure-core is otherwise pulled in only
    # for its synchronous (requests) transport, so the async peer must be declared
    # explicitly or a `uv sync --locked` image omits it and the credential raises
    # ImportError on first use. The [aio] extra tracks whichever async transport
    # azure-core requires.
    "azure-core[aio]>=1.30",
]

[tool.ruff.per-file-target-version]
# The deploy probes are invoked as a bare `python3` — by `cloud-preflight.sh`'s
# default probe command and by the SharePoint validation workflow — in jobs that
# provision no interpreter, so they run on the runner image's system Python
# rather than the one `versions.json` declares. They are written to depend on
# nothing for exactly that reason.

# The target here is a floor, not a claim about the runner: it keeps the
# formatter from rewriting these two files into syntax a system interpreter
# older than the declared version cannot parse. `except (A, B):` becoming the
# PEP 758 `except A, B:` under a 3.14 target is the live instance — it would
# turn the deploy preflight into a SyntaxError on the runner. The formatter

# `--dist loadfile` is load-bearing: a few modules depend on file order

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

# modules reach storage only through the service layer, as the routers do.
# Module-granular: a storage or adapter name re-exported through another module

name = "MCP tool modules do not import storage or adapters directly"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

    "sage.source_adapters",

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# CAS-ADR-042: the layer above the deployment-profile ports is profile-invariant,
# and the binding factories are the sole owners of any environment-specific import.
# The profile core (the generic profile mechanism) and the BFF server entry point
# carry no cloud import at all, so this contract fences them statically: a cloud SDK
# or cloud-binding module named directly in either would pass a Linux/local-profile
# CI run and surface only on the next on-box restart. azure and psycopg are external
# packages, graphed via the top-level include_external_packages. allow_indirect_imports
# keeps the fence on imports written into these modules, not the indirect chains they
# reach through the lazy bindings. psycopg is fenced here only because these modules
# reach durable storage through the binding seam, never the driver directly; the
# storage layer's own use of psycopg (local Postgres password auth) is a shared
# dependency and is unaffected. The SAGE application factory (sage.app) is not listed:
# it carries legitimate lazy, profile-guarded imports for the BFF session store's
# managed-identity path that import-linter cannot distinguish from a module-scope
# hoist, so its local-boot cloud-freeness is enforced at runtime by the deployment-
# profile guardrail tests, and its azure use is fenced by the confinement contract below.
name = "Profile core and server entry import no cloud dependency directly"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "sage.profiles",
    "app.backend.asgi",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "azure",
    "psycopg",
    "sage.secrets.key_vault",
    "sage.storage.postgres.managed_identity",
    "sage.vault_source_document_store",
]
allow_indirect_imports = "true"

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
# CAS-ADR-042/043: the cloud SDKs stay confined to the binding modules that own
# them -- the Key Vault secret reader, the managed-identity Postgres auth path, and
# the SharePoint/Graph document-store vault-source adapter -- so an azure import
# hoisted into any new call site fails the build. These owner edges are the only
# legitimate importers of azure, so ignoring them severs every remaining chain;
# psycopg is deliberately not forbidden here because it is a shared dependency of
# both the local and cloud Postgres paths.
name = "Azure SDKs are confined to the cloud binding modules"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "sage",
    "app",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "azure",
]
ignore_imports = [
    "sage.secrets.key_vault -> azure",
    "sage.storage.postgres.managed_identity -> azure",
    "sage.vault_source_document_store -> azure",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=75.0", "setuptools-scm>=8.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

# VCS-derived versioning: the version is computed from git tags + commits,
# single-sourcing it from the repository instead of a hand-edited literal. The
# running version (sage.build_info.RELEASE_VERSION) is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with
# PATCH = commit distance since the last vMAJOR.MINOR.0 tag, read live from git
# at import; a build-time-baked SAGE_BUILD_VERSION env stamp and then this
# setuptools-scm metadata are the successive no-git fallbacks, where
# ``no-guess-dev`` keeps the commit distance in the ``.devN`` segment that
# build_info parses. The committed OpenAPI info.version tracks only MAJOR.MINOR,
# so it does not churn between minor releases. No ``version_file`` is written: a
# generated, tracked module would leave the working tree perpetually dirty.
# ``fallback_version`` mirrors build_info's runtime ``unknown`` degradation when
# built outside a git checkout.
[tool.setuptools_scm]
version_scheme = "no-guess-dev"
local_scheme = "node-and-date"
fallback_version = "0.0.0"

    # database spans (test_mcp_observability.py fails). Lift the cap — and drop
    # the sqlalchemy[mypy] extra and the [tool.mypy] plugin with it, since 2.1
    # removed sqlalchemy.ext.mypy — once the instrumentation supports 2.1
    # (open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-contrib #5118 / PR #5120).
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.0,<2.1",
    "asyncpg>=0.29.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0",

    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.24.0",

    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.45b0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-redis>=0.45b0",
    "aiokafka>=0.11.0",

    # drops or vendors httpx, the image stops importing and the webhook is

    "httpx>=0.27.0",

    # Deliberately unversioned — fastapi already constrains starlette and

# Integration tests live in backend/tests/integration/ and are deliberately
# outside testpaths: they require Docker, so a bare `pytest` stays fast and
# service-free. They are NOT optional coverage — the `integration` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml runs them on every PR (and fails if any of the five
# files skips). Locally: `make test-integration`, which exports the three
# RUN_* gates. Running `pytest backend/tests/integration/` by hand without
# those variables collects the files and skips most of them while still
# exiting 0.

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
python_version = "3.12"
plugins = ["sqlalchemy.ext.mypy.plugin"]
exclude = ["alembic/"]
mypy_path = "backend"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP", "RUF006"]
ignore = ["N818", "UP046"]

[tool.coverage.run]
omit = ["*/tests/*", "*/alembic/*"]

# ADR 0006 says the MCP server is a standalone process that calls the service
# layer directly, and that an import-linter rule in CI keeps that one
# directional. Three places in the repo claimed the rule existed (CLAUDE.md,
# app/mcp/__init__.py, the ADR) while import-linter was not a dependency, had
# no config, and ran in no job — the invariant held by convention alone, which
# is exactly the state a "locked in" design decision must not be in.
#
# Run by the `Import contracts` step of the `lint` CI job, and locally with
# `make lint-imports`. Needs `app` importable, which the editable install
# provides in CI and PYTHONPATH provides from a worktree.
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "app"

# The rule as ADR 0006 states it. A layers contract is directional: a higher
# layer may import a lower one, never the reverse. Only these two packages are
# ordered here — `exhaustive` is off deliberately, because the rest of the app
# has no layering claim to make and pretending otherwise would produce a
# contract nobody could keep green.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "app.mcp depends on app.services, never the reverse"
type = "layers"
layers = ["app.mcp", "app.services"]

# The other half of the same ADR sentence: "nothing imports app.mcp". The MCP
# surface is a leaf, so that collapsing it back into the API (the ADR's own
# revisit trigger) stays the one-line change the ADR promises rather than an
# untangling.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Nothing outside app.mcp imports app.mcp"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "app.api",
    "app.core",
    "app.lab",
    "app.models",
    "app.repositories",
    "app.schemas",
    "app.services",
    "app.utils",
    "app.workers",
    "app.config",
    "app.dependencies",
    "app.main",
]
forbidden_modules = ["app.mcp"]

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noFields

/**
 * Guards the hexagon: the domain sits in the middle and knows nothing about the world around it.
 *
 * These rules are what stop the architecture from quietly eroding — an accidental `@Autowired` in
 * a domain service or a controller reaching straight into a repository fails the build.
 */
@AnalyzeClasses(
    packages = ["be.gerard.lifestarter"],
    importOptions = [ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests::class],
)
class HexagonalArchitectureTest {

    @ArchTest
    val domainIsFrameworkFree: ArchRule = noClasses()
        .that().resideInAPackage("..domain..")
        .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAnyPackage(
            "org.springframework..",
            "jakarta.persistence..",
            "jakarta.servlet..",
            "com.fasterxml.jackson..",
            "tools.jackson..",
            "org.apache.poi..",
        )
        .because("the domain must stay independent of frameworks and infrastructure")

    @ArchTest
    val domainDoesNotDependOnOuterLayers: ArchRule = noClasses()
        .that().resideInAPackage("..domain..")
        .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAnyPackage("..api..", "..repository..", "..mapper..")
        .because("dependencies point inwards: only adapters may know the domain")

    @ArchTest
    val controllersDoNotUseRepositoryAdapters: ArchRule = noClasses()
        .that().resideInAPackage("..api..")
        .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..repository..")
        .because("controllers talk to domain services, never to persistence adapters")

    @ArchTest
    val persistenceRecordsStayInsideRepositories: ArchRule = classes()
        .that().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Record")
        .should().resideInAPackage("..repository.model..")
        .because("persistence records must not leak past the repository boundary")

    @ArchTest
    val controllersAreNamedConsistently: ArchRule = classes()
        .that().resideInAPackage("..api..")
        .and().areAnnotatedWith("org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController")
        .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Controller")

    @ArchTest
    val noFieldInjection: ArchRule = noFields()
        .should().beAnnotatedWith("org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired")
        .because("constructor injection only")
}

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77.0", "wheel"]

[project]

version = "1.3.2"

readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
authors = [
    { name = "Michael Blaess" },
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Intended Audience :: End Users/Desktop",
    "Topic :: Office/Business",
]
dependencies = [
    "textual>=0.40",
    "rich>=13.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1",
    "holidays>=0.40",
    # Speichern-Dialog des Exports (Formatwahl ueber den Dateifilter).
    "textual-fspicker>=0.4.0",
    "textual-themes[textual]>=0.15.1",
    "textual-widgets>=0.32.1",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Web-Oberflaeche (christo.web): python -m christo.web

    "python-fasthtml>=0.12",
]
dev = [
    # Damit die Web-Tests auch in der CI laufen
    "christophorus[web]",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5",
    "mypy>=1.8",
    "poethepoet>=0.29",
    "ruff>=0.3",
    # Prueft die Schichtgrenzen. Ohne ihn ist "der Kern kennt keine

    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "types-openpyxl>=3.1.5.20260518",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/michaelblaess/christophorus"
Repository = "https://github.com/michaelblaess/christophorus"
Issues = "https://github.com/michaelblaess/christophorus/issues"

[project.scripts]
christophorus = "christo.__main__:main"
christo = "christo.__main__:main"
christo-web = "christo.web.__main__:main"

[tool.poe.tasks]
run = { cmd = "python -m christo", help = "Startet Christophorus" }
web = { cmd = "python -m christo.web", help = "Startet die Web-Oberflaeche (Arbeitskopie)" }
test = { cmd = "pytest", help = "Tests sequentiell (schnell bei Unit-Tests)" }
test-parallel = { cmd = "pytest -n auto", help = "Tests parallel (fuer langsame Test-Suiten)" }
cov = { cmd = "pytest --cov=christo --cov-report=term-missing", help = "Tests + Coverage" }
typecheck = { cmd = "mypy src", help = "mypy strict ueber src/" }
lint = { cmd = "ruff check .", help = "Ruff Linting" }
fmt = { cmd = "ruff format .", help = "Ruff Formatting" }
fix = { cmd = "ruff check --fix .", help = "Ruff Auto-Fix" }
layers = { cmd = "lint-imports", help = "Prueft die Schichtgrenzen (import-linter)" }

[tool.importlinter]
root_package = "christo"
# Fuer die Regel "der Kern zieht kein Textual" muss der Linter auch Pakete
# ausserhalb des Projekts sehen.
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Schichten von oben nach unten"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "christo.app",
    "christo.screens",
    "christo.widgets",
    "christo.services",
    "christo.models",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Der Kern kennt keine Oberflaeche"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "christo.services",
    "christo.models",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "christo.app",
    "christo.screens",
    "christo.widgets",
    "christo.web",
    "textual",
    "textual_widgets",
    "fasthtml",
]

# TUI und Web sind zwei Oberflaechen ueber demselben Kern. Kennen sie einander, laesst sich
# die eine nicht mehr aendern, ohne die andere anzufassen. Zwei gerichtete Regeln, kein
# independence-Vertrag: der wuerde auch verbieten, dass die TUI ihre eigenen Masken importiert.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Die Web-Oberflaeche kennt die TUI nicht"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["christo.web"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "christo.app",
    "christo.screens",
    "christo.widgets",
    "textual",
    "textual_widgets",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Die TUI kennt die Web-Oberflaeche nicht"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "christo.app",
    "christo.screens",
    "christo.widgets",
]
forbidden_modules = [
    "christo.web",
    "fasthtml",
]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]

# FastHTML liefert keinen py.typed-Marker.

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.ruff]

[project.entry-points."ter.capabilities"]

markers = [
    "req(id): links a test to the EARS requirement it verifies (see docs/ter4)",
    "embeddings: runs the real sentence-transformers model; skipped without the embeddings extra (see conftest.py)",

[tool.ruff]

target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true

# TER 4 code is held to strict typing from its first line.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["ter", "ter.*"]
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
disallow_untyped_calls = true
disallow_any_generics = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = true
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_reexport = true
strict_equality = true
warn_unused_ignores = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["anthropic", "sentence_transformers", "tiktoken"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["ter_calculator", "ter"]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 90
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
exclude_also = [
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

# TER 4 architecture rules, enforced by `lint-imports` in CI and by
# tests/architecture. See docs/ter4/architecture.md.
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["ter", "ter_calculator"]
include_external_packages = true

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "hexagon-layers"
name = "TER 4 hexagon: dependencies point inward"
type = "layers"
layers = [
    "ter.bootstrap",
    "ter.adapters",
    "ter.application",
    "ter.ports",
    "ter.domain",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "pure-domain"
name = "The domain is pure: no IO, no vendors, no TER 3 internals"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ter.domain"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ter_calculator",
    "tiktoken",
    "sentence_transformers",
    "anthropic",
    "rich",
    "sqlite3",
    "subprocess",
    "socket",
    "urllib",
    "http",
    "yaml",
    "pytest",
    # External capabilities (ADR 0005): adapters read their files by schema
    # name; the core never imports their packages or their stacks.
    "gare",
    "pydantic",
    "httpx",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "vendor-free-core"
name = "Ports and use cases know no vendors and no TER 3 internals"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ter.ports", "ter.application"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ter_calculator",
    "tiktoken",
    "sentence_transformers",
    "anthropic",
    "rich",
    "sqlite3",
    "yaml",
    "pytest",
    # External capabilities (ADR 0005), as in pure-domain.
    "gare",
    "pydantic",
    "httpx",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "report-renderers"
name = "Report renderers read only the view-model, never TER 3 results"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = [
    "ter.adapters.driving.reports.palette",
    "ter.adapters.driving.reports.svg",
    "ter.adapters.driving.reports.html",
    "ter.adapters.driving.reports.a3",
    "ter.adapters.driving.reports.control",
]
forbidden_modules = ["ter_calculator"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "behaviour-blind-to-outcome"
name = "No behaviour measure reads the outcome verdict (point 5)"
type = "forbidden"
# Measurement of agent behaviour and judgement of the result stay apart: the
# modules that compute behaviour never import ter.domain.outcome. Reports (the
# A3 view-model) and use cases show the verdict beside the measures.
source_modules = [
    "ter.domain.events",
    "ter.domain.pricing",
    "ter.domain.report",
    "ter.domain.scoring",
    "ter.domain.stream",
    "ter.domain.lean.analysis",
    "ter.domain.lean.control",
    "ter.domain.lean.countermeasures",
    "ter.domain.lean.detectors",
    "ter.domain.lean.facts",
    "ter.domain.lean.graph",
    "ter.domain.lean.model",
    "ter.domain.lean.steps",
    "ter.domain.lean.wip",
    "ter.domain.lean.concepts",
]
forbidden_modules = ["ter.domain.outcome"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "intervention-reads-signals"
name = "The Intervention Engine reads only structured detector signals (TER-INT-006)"
type = "forbidden"
# Observation and intervention are separate engines (points 121, 161, 162):
# the engine sees ter.domain.intervention.Signal values, never the events,
# steps or findings the Analysis Engine works on.
source_modules = [
    "ter.domain.effectiveness",
    "ter.domain.intervention",
    "ter.domain.ledger",
    "ter.domain.policy_set",
]
forbidden_modules = ["ter.domain.lean", "ter.domain.stream", "ter.domain.events"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "analysis-knows-no-intervention"
name = "The Analysis Engine never imports the Intervention Engine (P121)"
type = "forbidden"
# Both engines share only ter.domain.signal.Signal.
source_modules = ["ter.domain.lean", "ter.domain.stream", "ter.domain.signal"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ter.domain.effectiveness",
    "ter.domain.intervention",
    "ter.domain.ledger",
    "ter.domain.policy_set",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "independent-adapters"
name = "Driven adapters do not import each other"
type = "independence"
modules = [
    "ter.adapters.driven.claude_code",
    "ter.adapters.driven.control_limits",
    "ter.adapters.driven.critical_evidence",
    "ter.adapters.driven.embedders",
    "ter.adapters.driven.gare",
    "ter.adapters.driven.event_log",
    "ter.adapters.driven.tokenizers",
    "ter.adapters.driven.dependency_cruiser",
    "ter.adapters.driven.import_linter",
    "ter.adapters.driven.in_memory",
    "ter.adapters.driven.intervention_channel",
    "ter.adapters.driven.intervention_ledger",
    "ter.adapters.driven.intervention_policies",
    "ter.adapters.driven.junit",
    "ter.adapters.driven.pricing",
    "ter.adapters.driven.repository",
    "ter.adapters.driven.requirements_yaml",
    "ter.adapters.driven.routing_profiles",
    "ter.adapters.driven.ter3",
]
# TER 3 sits outside the hexagon and reads its prices through the pricing
# adapter. A chain that passes through TER 3 is not one adapter depending on
# another, so those edges are exempt here (and only here).
ignore_imports = ["ter_calculator.** -> ter.adapters.driven.pricing"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "provider-neutral-evidence"
name = "Repository evidence depends on no model provider (P054, TER-EVD-001)"
type = "forbidden"
# The evidence values and every repository engine import no model SDK,
# tokenizer, embedder, TER 3 internals or external capability stack: what a
# repository says never depends on which model reads it.
source_modules = ["ter.domain.repository", "ter.adapters.driven.repository"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "ter_calculator",
    "tiktoken",
    "sentence_transformers",
    "anthropic",
    "gare",
    "pydantic",
    "httpx",
    "ter.adapters.driven.embedders",
    "ter.adapters.driven.tokenizers",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
id = "ter3-uses-hexagon-edges"
name = "TER 3 uses TER 4 only through domain, ports or adapters, never bootstrap"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["ter_calculator"]
forbidden_modules = ["ter.bootstrap", "ter.application"]
# The TER 3 `ter` command hands `ter a3` and `ter explain` to the TER 4
# command line, whose services only the composition root builds. That one
# lazy delegation in the TER 3 CLI entry point is exempt (and only it).
ignore_imports = ["ter_calculator.cli -> ter.bootstrap"]

[tool.mutmut]
# Mutation score of the pure domain (scripts/mutation.py, TER-TST-015).
# The tests that reach ter.domain (tests/requirements: the EARS and points
# rules); the embedding model never runs here.

package no.nav.eessi.pensjon.architecture

import com.tngtech.archunit.base.DescribedPredicate
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.*
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.*
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.dependencies.SlicesRuleDefinition.slices
import no.nav.eessi.pensjon.EessiFagmodulApplication
import no.nav.eessi.pensjon.metrics.MetricsHelper
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Disabled
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Scope
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController
import java.util.*

class ArchitectureTest {

    companion object {

        @JvmStatic
        private val root = EessiFagmodulApplication::class.qualifiedName!!.replace("." + EessiFagmodulApplication::class.simpleName, "")

        @JvmStatic
        lateinit var allClasses: JavaClasses

        @JvmStatic
        lateinit var productionClasses: JavaClasses

        @JvmStatic
        lateinit var testClasses: JavaClasses

        @BeforeAll @JvmStatic
        fun `extract classes`() {
            allClasses = ClassFileImporter().importPackages(root)

            assertTrue(allClasses.size in 350..1300, "Sanity check on no. of classes to analyze (is ${allClasses.size})")

            productionClasses = ClassFileImporter()
                    .withImportOption(ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests())
                    .withImportOption(ImportOption.DoNotIncludeJars())
                    .importPackages(root)

            assertTrue(productionClasses.size in 140..300, "Sanity check on no. of classes to analyze (is ${productionClasses.size})")

            testClasses = ClassFileImporter()
                    .withImportOption{ !ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests().includes(it) }
                    .importPackages(root)

            assertTrue(testClasses.size in 200..800, "Sanity check on no. of classes to analyze (is ${testClasses.size})")
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `check architecture in detail`() {

        // components
        val bucSedApi         = "fagmodul api"
        val prefill           = "fagmodul prefill"
        val pesys             = "fagmodul pesys"
        val euxService        = "fagmodul euxservice"
        val euxBucModel       = "fagmodul euxBucModel"
        val config            = "fagmodul config"
        val geoApi            = "api geo"
        val personApi         = "api person"
        val pensjonApi        = "api pensjon"
        val pensjonService    = "services pensjon"
        val statistikk    = "services statistikk"
        val utils             = "utils"
        val vedlegg           = "vedlegg"
        val packages: Map<String, String> = mapOf(
            "$root.fagmodul.api.." to bucSedApi,
            "$root.fagmodul.api.vedlegg.." to vedlegg,
            "$root.fagmodul.prefill.." to prefill,
            "$root.fagmodul.eux" to euxService,
            "$root.fagmodul.eux.bucmodel.." to euxBucModel,
            "$root.fagmodul.config.." to config,
            "$root.fagmodul.pesys.." to pesys,
            "$root.api.geo.." to geoApi,
            "$root.api.person.." to personApi,
            "$root.api.pensjon.." to pensjonApi,
            "$root.config.." to config,
            "$root.services.statistikk" to statistikk,
            "$root.services.pensjonsinformasjon" to pensjonService,
            "$root.metrics.." to utils,
            "$root.utils.." to utils,
            "$root.logging.." to utils,
            )

        // packages in each component - default is the package with the component name
        fun packagesFor(layer: String) = packages.entries.filter { it.value == layer }.map { it.key }.toTypedArray()

        // mentally replace the word "layer" with "component":
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringOnlyDependenciesInAnyPackage(root)
                .layer(geoApi).definedBy(*packagesFor(geoApi))
                .layer(personApi).definedBy(*packagesFor(personApi))
                .layer(pensjonApi).definedBy(*packagesFor(pensjonApi))
                .layer(bucSedApi).definedBy(*packagesFor(bucSedApi))
                .layer(pesys).definedBy(*packagesFor(pesys))
                .layer(prefill).definedBy(*packagesFor(prefill))
                .layer(euxService).definedBy(*packagesFor(euxService))
                .layer(euxBucModel).definedBy(*packagesFor(euxBucModel))
                .layer(pensjonService).definedBy(*packagesFor(pensjonService))
                .layer(config).definedBy(*packagesFor(config))
                .layer(utils).definedBy(*packagesFor(utils))
                .layer(vedlegg).definedBy(*packagesFor(vedlegg))
                .layer(statistikk).definedBy(*packagesFor(statistikk))

                .whereLayer(geoApi).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
                .whereLayer(bucSedApi).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
                .whereLayer(pensjonApi).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()

                .whereLayer(prefill).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(bucSedApi, pensjonApi)
                .whereLayer(pesys).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(euxService)
                .whereLayer(vedlegg).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(bucSedApi, prefill)

                .whereLayer(euxService).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(bucSedApi, pesys, prefill, personApi)
                .whereLayer(pensjonService).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(pensjonApi, prefill, bucSedApi, personApi)

                .whereLayer(euxBucModel).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(euxService, bucSedApi, pesys, personApi)

                .whereLayer(config).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
                .check(productionClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `main layers check`() {
        val frontendAPI = "Frontend API"
        val fagmodulCore = "Fagmodul Core"
        val services = "Services"
        val vedlegg ="Vedlegg"
        val support = "Support"
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringOnlyDependenciesInAnyPackage(root)
                .layer(frontendAPI).definedBy(      "$root.api..")
                .layer(fagmodulCore).definedBy(     "$root.fagmodul..")
                .layer(services).definedBy(         "$root.services..", "$root.kodeverk..", "$root.pensjonsinformasjon..")
                .layer(vedlegg).definedBy(          "$root.fagmodul.api.vedlegg..")
                .layer(support).definedBy(
                        "$root.metrics..",
                        "$root.config..",
                        "$root.logging..",
                        "$root.utils.."
                )
                .whereLayer(frontendAPI).mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
                .whereLayer(fagmodulCore).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                        frontendAPI,
                        services)
                .whereLayer(services).mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers(
                        frontendAPI,
                        fagmodulCore,
                        vedlegg)
                .withOptionalLayers(false)
                .check(productionClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `no cycles on any level for production classes`() {
        slices()
                .matching("$root.(*)..")
                .should().beFreeOfCycles()
                .check(productionClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `controllers should have RestController-annotation`() {
        classes().that()
                .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Controller")
                .should().beAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java)
                .check(allClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `RestControllers should not call each other`() {
        classes()
            .that().areAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java)
            .should().onlyHaveDependentClassesThat().areNotAnnotatedWith(RestController::class.java)
            .because("RestControllers should not call each other")
            .check(allClasses)
    }
    @Test
    fun `Methods in RestControllers should only call be get, post, patch and delete`() {
        val rule = methods()
            .that().arePublic()
            .and(dontAccessInstanceMethods())
            .and(dontAccessMemberVariables())
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat()
            .resideInAPackage("..no.nav.eessi.pensjon.fagmodul.api..")
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Controller")
            .should().beAnnotatedWith(RequestMapping::class.java).orShould().beAnnotatedWith(GetMapping::class.java)

        rule.check(productionClasses)

    }
    private fun dontAccessMemberVariables(): DescribedPredicate<JavaMethod?> {
        return object : DescribedPredicate<JavaMethod?>("don't access member variables") {
            override fun test(input: JavaMethod?): Boolean {
                return !input!!.fieldAccesses.stream().filter { access: JavaFieldAccess ->
                    val optionalField = access.target.resolveMember()
                    if (!optionalField.isPresent) {
                        return@filter false
                    }
                    !optionalField.get().modifiers
                        .contains(JavaModifier.STATIC)
                }
                    .findAny().isPresent
            }
        }
    }

    private fun dontAccessInstanceMethods(): DescribedPredicate<JavaMethod?> {
        return object : DescribedPredicate<JavaMethod?>("don't access instance methods") {
            override fun test(input: JavaMethod?): Boolean {
                return !input!!.callsFromSelf.stream().filter { access ->
                    val targets: Optional<out JavaCodeUnit>? = access.target.resolveMember()
                    if (targets == null || !targets.isPresent) {
                        return@filter false
                    }
                    val target = targets.get()
                    target.owner == input.owner && !target.modifiers.contains(JavaModifier.STATIC)
                }
                    .findAny().isPresent
            }
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `tests should assert, not log`() {
        noClasses().that().haveNameNotMatching(".*\\.logging\\..*") // we allow using slf4j in the logging-package
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("org.slf4j.LoggerFactory")
                .because("Test should assert, not log; after you made your test the logs will not be checked")
                .check(testClasses)
    }


    @Test
    fun `Spring singleton components should not have mutable instance fields`() {

        class SpringStereotypeAnnotation:DescribedPredicate<JavaAnnotation<*>>("Spring component annotation") {
            override fun test(input: JavaAnnotation<*>?) = input != null &&
                    (input.rawType.packageName.startsWith("org.springframework.stereotype") ||
                            input.rawType.isEquivalentTo(RestController::class.java))
        }

        val springStereotype = SpringStereotypeAnnotation()

        noMethods().that()
            .haveNameMatching("set[A-Z]+.*")
            .and().doNotHaveRawParameterTypes(MetricsHelper.Metric::class.java)
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().areNotAnnotatedWith(Scope::class.java) // If scope is not singleton it might be ok
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().haveNameNotMatching(".*(STSService|Template|Config|GcpStorageService)") // these use setter injection
            .should().beDeclaredInClassesThat().areAnnotatedWith(springStereotype)
            .because("Spring-components (usually singletons) must not have mutable instance fields " +
                    "as they can easily be misused and create 'race conditions'")
            .check(productionClasses)

        noFields().that()
            .areNotFinal()
            .and().doNotHaveRawType(MetricsHelper.Metric::class.java)
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().areNotAnnotatedWith(Scope::class.java)// If scope is not singleton it might be ok
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().haveNameNotMatching(".*(STSService|Template|Config|GcpStorageService)") // these use setter injection
            .should().beDeclaredInClassesThat().areAnnotatedWith(springStereotype)
            .because("Spring-components (usually singletons) must not have mutable instance fields " +
                    "as they can easily be misused and create 'race conditions'")
            .check(productionClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `No test classes should use inheritance`() {
        class TestSupportClasses:DescribedPredicate<JavaClass>("test support classes") {
            override fun test(input: JavaClass?) = input != null &&
                    (!input.simpleName.endsWith("Test") &&
                            (!input.simpleName.endsWith("Tests")
                                    && input.name != "java.lang.Object"))
        }

        noClasses().that().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Test").or().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Tests")
                .should().beAssignableTo(TestSupportClasses())
                .because("it is hard to understand the logic of tests that inherit from other classes.")
                .check(testClasses)
    }
}

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "inaki"
version = "2.1.1"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "aiosqlite>=0.20",
    "sqlite-vec>=0.1",
    "onnxruntime>=1.18",
    "numpy>=1.26",
    "python-telegram-bot>=21.0",
    "markdown-it-py>=3.0",
    "fastapi>=0.111",
    "uvicorn>=0.30",
    "croniter>=2.0",
    "exchangelib>=5.0",
    "cryptography>=42.0",
    "typer>=0.12",
    "rich>=13.0",
    "tzlocal>=5.0",
    "pypdf>=4.0",
    "ruamel.yaml>=0.18",
    "Pillow>=10.0",
    "tokenizers>=0.15",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Reconocimiento facial (photos.enabled). Aparte porque insightface compila en ARM
# y una instalación sin fotos no tiene por qué pagarlo: pip install "inaki[faces]".
faces = ["insightface"]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
    "pytest-mock>=3.14",
    "freezegun>=1.5",
    "respx>=0.21",
    "ruff>=0.4",
    "mypy>=1.10",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0",
    "types-croniter>=2.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
]

[project.scripts]
inaki = "inaki.cli:app"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["inaki*"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
# La UI web de config viaja dentro del paquete: sin build step ni CDN.
"inaki.channels.rest" = ["static/*.html"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"

[tool.mypy]
# ext/ es territorio de extensiones de usuario (gitignored, ver CLAUDE.md).
# Cada usuario gestiona su propio código de extensión — no versionamos ni
# type-checkeamos. Si una extensión tiene errores, son responsabilidad del
# usuario, no del proyecto.
exclude = ["^ext/"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# ruamel.yaml no expone py.typed marker — third-party sin stubs.
module = "ruamel.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# sqlite_vec no expone py.typed marker — third-party sin stubs.
# Wrapper de extensión SQLite para vectores; usado en outbound/memory y faces.
module = "sqlite_vec"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# exchangelib no expone py.typed marker — third-party sin stubs.
# Usado por el ext de ms_exchange.
module = "exchangelib.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# insightface no expone py.typed marker — third-party sin stubs.
# Modelo de reconocimiento facial cargado lazy en el adapter de visión.
module = "insightface.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# onnxruntime no expone py.typed marker — third-party sin stubs.
# Usado por el embedder e5-small ONNX (adapters/outbound/embedding/e5_onnx).
module = "onnxruntime"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# tokenizers (HuggingFace) no expone py.typed marker — third-party sin stubs.
# Usado por el embedder e5-small ONNX (adapters/outbound/embedding/e5_onnx).
module = "tokenizers"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ley de dependencias entre capas — verificada por `lint-imports`.
#
# Codifica las reglas de tests/unit/test_architecture.py de forma declarativa.
# grimp incluye imports locales y bajo TYPE_CHECKING: un import "solo de tipos"
# también acopla. Regla 2 (allowlist de terceros en core/) sigue en el test de
# pytest: import-linter solo sabe PROHIBIR paquetes, no permitir una lista cerrada.
#
# Refactor modular (2026-09): cada fase agrega o endurece un contrato acá. NUNCA se resuelve una violación con ignore_imports —
# es la lista DEUDA_* con otro nombre. ÚNICA excepción, por diseño: el `wiring.py` de un módulo es
# su factory (config → adapters) y puede conocer `inaki.config` y el `wiring.py` de otro módulo;
# se declara como `ignore_imports` en su contrato para que el borde quede escrito, no supuesto.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["inaki"]

# La ley de capas. `inaki.shared` (primitivas) la consumen todos; el kernel
# (`inaki.kernel`: el turno y los ports que consume) no conoce a ningún módulo;
# cada módulo conoce el kernel, shared y lo que su contrato permite; solo el
# composition root (`inaki.app`, `inaki.cli`) conoce a todos.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "el kernel no conoce ningún módulo salvo shared"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["inaki.kernel"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "inaki.cli",
    "inaki.app",
    "inaki.observability",
    "inaki.config",
    "inaki.channels",
    "inaki.perception",
    "inaki.embedding",
    "inaki.memory",
    "inaki.knowledge",
    "inaki.skills",
    "inaki.tools",
    "inaki.llm",
    "inaki.extensions",
    "inaki.scheduler",
    "inaki.agents",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "inaki/shared no conoce a nadie del proyecto"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["inaki.shared"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "inaki.kernel",
    "inaki.cli",
    "inaki.app",
    "inaki.observability",
    "inaki.config",
    "inaki.channels",
    "inaki.perception",
    "inaki.embedding",
    "inaki.memory",
    "inaki.knowledge",
    "inaki.skills",
    "inaki.tools",
    "inaki.llm",
    "inaki.extensions",
    "inaki.scheduler",
    "inaki.agents",
]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "inaki/observability solo conoce el kernel (ports) y shared"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["inaki.observability"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "inaki.cli",
    "inaki.app",
    "inaki.config",
    "inaki.channels",
    "inaki.perception",
    "inaki.embedding",
    "inaki.memory",
    "inaki.knowledge",
    "inaki.skills",
    "inaki.tools",
    "inaki.llm",
    "inaki.extensions",
    "inaki.scheduler",
    "inaki.agents",
]


# inaki/config es un módulo de feature: conoce shared y los ports de core, nada más.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "inaki/config solo conoce el kernel (ports) y shared"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["inaki.config"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "inaki.cli",
    "inaki.app",

# Un canal conoce el kernel (core), shared, observability, config (su sección se

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]

    "inaki.cli", "inaki.app", "inaki.channels",

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "memory, knowledge y skills son independientes entre sí"

# tools conoce el kernel, shared y embedding (routing semántico); nunca a otro módulo.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "inaki/tools solo conoce el kernel, shared y embedding"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["inaki.tools"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "inaki.cli", "inaki.app", "inaki.channels",
    "inaki.config", "inaki.observability", "inaki.perception",
    "inaki.memory", "inaki.knowledge", "inaki.skills", "inaki.llm", "inaki.extensions",
    "inaki.scheduler", "inaki.agents",
]
ignore_imports = ["inaki.tools.wiring -> inaki.config"]

# llm es un gateway puro: recibe ResolvedLLMConfig del wiring y no conoce a nadie más.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "inaki/llm solo conoce el kernel y shared"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["inaki.llm"]

    "inaki.cli", "inaki.app", "inaki.channels",
    "inaki.config", "inaki.observability", "inaki.perception", "inaki.embedding",
    "inaki.memory", "inaki.knowledge", "inaki.skills", "inaki.tools", "inaki.extensions",
    "inaki.scheduler", "inaki.agents",
]
ignore_imports = ["inaki.llm.wiring -> inaki.config"]

# extensions solo DESCUBRE manifests: devuelve clases, paths y factories sin
# instanciar nada, así que no conoce ni a tools, ni a skills, ni a knowledge.
[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "inaki/extensions no conoce a nadie del proyecto"
type = "forbidden"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]

# Every test carries exactly one of these, and a CI job is a marker expression
# over them and nothing else -- so no test can fall between two jobs or land in
# both. See `.system_design/TEST_SUITE.md` section 8 for the job/marker matrix.
#
# The marker is assigned by PATH DEFAULT in `tests/conftest.py`, not by hand;
# a file only names its own layer where the default is wrong. `tests/layers.py`
# owns both the vocabulary and the default map, and this list is checked against
# it by `tests/test_layer_markers.py`.
markers = [
    "l1: component and property tests -- a unit's logic, in milliseconds",
    "l2: contract tests -- two artifacts that must agree, checked statically",
    "l3: subsystem tests -- one service against real sockets, files and processes",
    "acceptance: Gherkin scenarios over the product's stated promises",
    "agent_smoke: a real agent binary starts and reaches the bridge",
    "agent_live: a real agent binary against live provider credentials",
    "eval: answer-quality evaluation -- nondeterministic, alerts and never gates",
    "load: load and endurance runs",
]

# IMPORTANT: `-m` here is a DEFAULT, not a policy: a command-line `-m` replaces it
# outright (verified against pytest 9.0.3, and the reason `tests.yml` can name
# its own expression). It exists so a bare `pytest` -- a developer's local run,
# or a future caller that forgets an expression -- does not try to launch four
# real agent CLIs against live credentials.
#
# The string is asserted equal to `layers.default_marker_expression()`, derived
# from `RESOURCE_DEPENDENT_LAYERS`. Do not edit one without the other; two
# hand-maintained copies of one list is how a layer gets excluded in the module
# and keeps running locally anyway.
#
# It replaces a `--runslow` flag that attached `pytest.mark.skip` to those tests
# instead. The difference is the whole point: this run reports "32 deselected",
# a statement about what was SELECTED, where the old one reported "32 skipped",
# a statement about tests that were supposed to run and did not. section 8: "Skips are
# failures in a gating job."
#
# IMPORTANT: `--strict-markers` is deliberately NOT here, and must not be added.
# pytest 9.0 regressed so that `--strict-markers` given through `addopts` is
# silently ignored; the fix landed in 9.1.0 (upstream issue 14442). Verified
# against 9.0.3: from `addopts` a bogus marker is a warning and the run exits 0,
# from the command line it is a collection error and the run exits 2.
#
# A strictness setting that depends on the patch version of pytest a contributor
# happens to have is worse than no setting: it is a gate that reports differently
# to two people looking at the same tree. So `tests.yml` passes the flag on the
# command line, where every supported version honours it, and
# `tests/test_layer_selection.py` proves the flag works rather than assuming it.
addopts = ["-m", "not agent_smoke and not agent_live and not eval and not load"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py310"
# The review system under `.github/review/` is carried from the repository this
# system was adopted from, byte for byte apart from `select_rules.py`, so that a
# fix made in either place can be copied to the other. Reformatting those files
# to this project's lint settings would make every one of them a fork, and the
# next carried-across fix would arrive as a conflict. `.github/review/rules/ci.md`
# records the same rule for anyone reviewing a change there.
#
# NOTE: this is not "that code is unchecked". `ci.yml` runs its 738-case suite
# on every pull request, and that suite carries guards this linter could not
# express - the private-reference sweep, the runner-ceiling pairing, the
# aggregate's dependency set.
#
# Deliberately ASCII, and NOT because the file is: line 8's description carries
# an em-dash and always has. The reason is narrower. `tests/test_pypi_packaging.py`
# reads this file with `Path.read_text()` and no encoding, so on a machine whose
# locale is not UTF-8 any non-ASCII byte fails the release-gating version check.
# The em-dash is grandfathered and would fail the same way; adding more is what
# this note is about. (The claim above used to say "like the rest of this file",
# which was simply wrong - caught by this repository's own automated review.)
exclude = [".github"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "I",    # isort
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify
]

# KBR-152 acceptance canary: the file's `assert False` is deliberate (the
# file's own docstring says it must be red so KBR-152's `--require-category`
# guard has something to fail on). The pytest runner exercises it under the
# dedicated acceptance job; the ruff gate here only needs to tolerate the
# specific B011 violation that an `assert False` raises.
"tests/test_kbr152_throwaway_canary.py" = ["B011"]

[tool.mypy]

    "kitty.bridge",

# kitty.bridge_runner -- so it has to sit below every layer. That is the whole
# reason it is its own module rather than a function in cli/main.py: a
# bridge_runner -> kitty.cli import would invert the direction the contract
# above enforces, and would NOT be caught, because kitty.bridge_runner is a
# sibling top-level module rather than a descendant of kitty.bridge. This
# contract pins the property the module docstring claims.

# This list names EVERY sibling, not the seven kitty.io_encoding's contract

# would have omitted: kitty.providers already imports kitty.auth, so a

    "kitty.tui",
    "kitty.profiles",
    "kitty.credentials",
    "kitty.providers",
]

# Mutation testing -- T-H1 (KBR-88).
#
# `source_paths` is the whole importable package: mutmut removes the original
# `src/` from `sys.path` and runs tests against `mutants/`, so anything not in
# `source_paths` (or in `also_copy`) is unimportable. TEST_SUITE.md section 6.1
# narrows the scope to specific functions; that narrowing cannot live here --
# mutmut treats wildcard entries as filesystem paths and silently drops them
# (its `walk_all_files` only follows directories and files, not globs). The
# function-level narrowing lives in `tests/mutmut_scope.py` (the registry) and
# in the positional patterns the recorded invocation in
# `.system_design/MUTATION_BASELINE.md` passes to `mutmut run`.
#
# `only_mutate` is file-level and bounds mutant generation to the files that
# carry any section 6.1 target -- CLI, TUI, auth and `kitty.io_encoding` are
# out of scope and never generate mutants. The `providers/*` glob was
# intentionally narrowed to per-file globs (the round-1 review caught that
# it matched `__init__.py`, `registry.py` and `model_context_sync.py`,
# none of which are named by section 6.1). `tests/test_mutmut_scope.py`'s
# `test_every_registry_file_is_covered_by_only_mutate` guard keeps this
# list in sync with the registry: any registry target whose file is not
# in this list fails
# the gate.
#

# `pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection` is array form -- mutmut's TOML reader
# requires it (its config schema validates the array shape explicitly).
#
# The `--ignore` below is mutmut-only, not a gate change. The internal-keys
# guard fails against mutmut's mutated source: mutmut-generated string
# mutations in MessagesTranslator._translate_assistant_message write
# `_THINKING_BLOCKS` in upper case, and the test's `startswith("_")` scan
# sees the uppercase key as leaked before the strip test runs. Every
# parametrized case of test_no_internal_key_reaches_upstream fails for the
# same reason -- one `--deselect` only shifts the failure to the next case.
# Deselecting the whole file removes ~111 tests from mutmut's selection
# only; the L1 gate still runs them. Investigating the trampoline
# interaction further is its own ticket, not T-H1 scope.
#
# `also_copy` carries files outside `source_paths`/`tests/` that the L1
# selection reads from the repo root. README.md is the one such file today:
# `tests/bridge/test_compaction_failure_response.py` (an L1 test) reads it.
# `scripts` is the second: the L2 test
# `tests/test_aggregate_mutation_baseline.py` imports
# `scripts/aggregate_mutation_baseline.py` by filesystem path at module
# level (added in KBR-88 review round 7, after the recorded b680edd run;
# every mutmut run on main needs this copy or test collection fails
# before the clean run starts). `openapi` is the third: the L2 schemathesis
# conformance test (KBR-82) loads `openapi/kitty-bridge.yaml` at module
# import, which happens at collection even under `-m l1`, so every mutmut
# run needs the copy since that file landed (after the KBR-266 run). The
# whole directory is copied, not the
# single file, because mutmut 3.8.0's file branch (`shutil.copy2`) does
# not create the destination's parent directory and dies on a fresh
# `mutants/` tree; the directory branch (`copytree(dirs_exist_ok=True)`)
# does.
# This file must stay ASCII (see the ruff note above): section 6.1 is written
# out rather than using the section sign.
[tool.mutmut]
source_paths = ["src/kitty"]
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = [
    "-m",
    "l1",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/test_internal_keys_not_sent_upstream.py",
    # KBR-290: deselect the section-8.2 socket/process-binding modules from
    # mutmut's nightly so it never depends on loopback socket timing. The set
    # is held against the registry in `tests/socket_binding_l1_modules.py` by
    # `tests/test_socket_binding_l1_mutation_exclusion.py`; both are edited
    # together -- never the one without the other. The Fast job's
    # `pytest -m "l1 or l2"` selection still collects every module here.
    "--ignore",
    "tests/bridge/test_tls_certs.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_recorder.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_recorder_falsification.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_bridge.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_bridge_falsification.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_vertical_slice.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_provider_aiohttp.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_containment.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/bridge/test_responses_string_input.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/bridge/test_bridge_management.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/cli/test_bridge_state_location.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/test_egress_https_proxy.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_connect_proxy.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/bridge/test_crash_resilience.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_oracle_botocore_slice.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/harness/test_oracle_provider_aiohttp_slice.py",
    "--ignore",
    "tests/cli/test_stream_encoding.py",
]
only_mutate = [
    "src/kitty/bridge/messages/*",
    "src/kitty/bridge/responses/*",
    "src/kitty/bridge/gemini/*",
    "src/kitty/bridge/engine.py",
    "src/kitty/bridge/tool_audit.py",
    # ``server.py`` carries the section-6.1 registry-named targets: the
    # seven ``compaction_and_pairing`` methods plus KBR-285's two content
    # predicates (``_cc_chunk_carries_content`` and
    # ``BridgeServer._is_empty_cc_response``); every other def/class in it
    # is suppressed by ``# pragma: no mutate block`` (mutmut's block pragma)
    # so generation stays fast and the scope narrows to the registered
    # targets. The guard
    # ``tests/test_mutmut_scope.py::test_server_py_pragma_scheme_marks_everything_but_the_registered``
    # (KBR-266, generalised by KBR-285) pins the marker scheme against drift.
    "src/kitty/bridge/server.py",
    # Every adapter file carrying one of the three provider hooks
    # (translate_to_upstream / normalize_request / build_upstream_headers)
    # -- per-file rather than `providers/*` so the three un-scoped
    # modules (`__init__.py`, `registry.py`, `model_context_sync.py`)
    # generate no mutants. `tests/test_mutmut_scope.py` asserts the file
    # set equals the union of the files carrying a registry target, so
    # a new adapter lands in this list when its registry row lands.
    "src/kitty/providers/anthropic.py",

python_functions = [ "test_*",]

asyncio_mode = "auto"
markers = [
  "e2e: end-to-end tests that start a real server (run with `pytest -m e2e`)",
  "mock: unit tests using mocks only, no real I/O (default, always run)",
  "integration: integration tests with real DB/H5 (run on push to main)",
  "llm: tests requiring real LLM API (gated by GHA secret, only main + nightly)",
